title: Evaluate Lauren Tan's pstack for Eon's agent workflow
description:
## Why

Lucca asked (2026-10-21) for an evaluation of pstack, Lauren Tan's (poteto) agent-workflow kit, for
work on Eon. pstack targets two weak spots this repository already has:

- **Verification.** Its `create-verification-skill` and `create-formal-verification-skill` write
  project-local skills that check a change against the real app or a formal property, and they show
  the check failing before handing off. Eon's installed proofs depend on recipes kept in agent
  memory (isolated capture, an Ubuntu VM with seat sway, wdotool priming), not on a skill in the
  repository. Orbit's Rust host, which owns the PTY, signals, reaping and the worker fault path, is
  the unproved half of Orbit (`eon-fony`).
- **Review.** Its `/interrogate` sends one diff to several models and sorts the findings. Eon's
  review loop runs through Starcompass's `converge` skill with Opus and Codex.

Decide which parts, if any, would make Eon's agents more correct or cheaper than what Eon already
has.

## Evidence

- Source: `https://github.com/cursor/plugins/tree/main/pstack` at `190d28736eff128ec94f502a22c7fe0c4b56cd37`
  (HEAD on 2026-10-21). MIT, Copyright (c) 2026 Lauren Tan. 172 files: about 50 skills
  (workflow skills, `principle-*` skills, `poteto-mode` playbooks), 2 agents (`poteto-agent`,
  `comment-sicko`), an optional `automations/benny` pack, and TypeScript helpers run under Bun in
  `skills/poteto-mode/scripts/` (`orch`, `watch-pr`, `check-plan`).
- Overview: https://flaviocopes.com/pstack. Its official target is Cursor. Claude Code and Codex
  load the `SKILL.md` files when they are copied in, but lose `/add-plugin`, `/setup-pstack`,
  per-subagent model roles and `/loop`. Community port for Claude Code and Codex:
  https://github.com/michael-denyer/pstack-claude.
- The skills that already cover the same ground live in Starcompass (`~/pjs/lab/starcompass/skills`):
  `converge`, `fresh-pass`, `fresh-eyes`, `fix-or-bead`, `prime`, `create-beads`, `handoff` and
  `stop-slop`. Repository policy lives in `AGENTS.md` and `docs/AGENT-PROTOCOLS.md`.
- Constraint: `AGENTS.md` "Implementation Languages" lets Eon add no TypeScript of its own, so
  pstack's helpers cannot be checked in here.

## Scope

In scope:
- Read pstack at the pinned commit. Classify each relevant piece as **adopt in Eon**, **propose to
  Starcompass**, or **reject**, with the reason and, where one exists, the Eon or Starcompass
  equivalent it would replace or extend. Priority pieces:
  1. `create-verification-skill` and `maintain-verification-skill`: would a generated `verify-eon`
     skill replace the memory-held installed-proof recipes?
  2. `create-formal-verification-skill`: on Orbit's host and worker fault and reap races (for
     example a TLA+ model). How would it sit beside `LAWS.bend` and `PROOF.bend`?
  3. `interrogate` and `arena` against `converge` and the Opus-plus-Codex review history.
  4. The `principle-*` skills and playbooks against `AGENTS.md` and the Starcompass protocols:
     report only gaps and conflicts, not overlap.
  5. `show-me-your-work` and `blast-radius` against Beads proof records.
- At most one trial, with Lucca's authorization: run the strongest candidate as a fresh agent on a
  representative, already-closed Eon task in a scratch worktree. Report how it behaved, without
  supplying the expected conclusion (AP-TEST-001).

Out of scope:
- Installing pstack into `~/.claude`, `.cursor` or this repository, checking in its TypeScript, or
  running Benny automations.
- Editing `AGENTS.md`, Starcompass skills or protocol imports. Adoption is a separate bead that
  Lucca approves.
- Model-routing defaults (Grok, Sol). They don't apply to this setup.

## Acceptance

- A verdict table on this bead covering at least the five priority pieces: piece, verdict, reason,
  equivalent, and proposed follow-up.
- A recommendation, with its reason, on whether anything is adopted, and where (Eon-local skill or
  Starcompass).
- Follow-up beads are proposed, not filed, until Lucca chooses.

## Verification

- Planning only: `br show` on this bead with the verdict comment, and `.beads/` after
  `br sync --flush-only`. A trial, if one runs, records its worktree revision, prompt and outcome.
  No runtime proof or profile refresh.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop for Lucca before installing anything, running a trial agent, or filing adoption beads.
- Stop if `main` of `cursor/plugins` has moved materially from the pinned commit. Evaluate at the
  pin and note the drift.

## Maintenance Notes

- Lucca chose Eon over Starcompass as this bead's home (2026-10-21), so the focus is Eon's own
  workflow. A piece worth spreading to other repositories goes to Starcompass as a proposal.

title: Make click interval and word separators configurable
description:
## Why

Approved as "configurable later" (`eon-configurability-audit-twdr`, Lucca, 2026-10-23). The
double-click interval and the word-selection separators are fixed. ORB-C9 explicitly excludes
making them configurable, so this changes ORB-C9 under the Happy Users rule.

## Why deferred

It is a contract reversal, and no user has asked yet.

title: Move create-column from Alt+Shift+M to Ctrl+Alt+M
description:
## Why

Lucca decided on 2026-10-22 to free Alt+Shift+M for the Eon command runner
(`eon-command-runner-uctp`). Nova users already press Alt Shift M for Nova's
command menu, and Eon's Alt+Shift popups already match Nova's (J Git, L Agent).
Creating a column moves to Ctrl+Alt+M. Ctrl+Alt is Eon's layout group: H/J/K/L
move panes, Ctrl+Alt+Shift+H/L move tabs, and at a tab's edge Ctrl+Alt+H/L
already opens a new column. Eon has no users yet, so the move costs no one any
muscle memory.

Rejected options:
- Keep Alt+Shift+M and give the runner Ctrl+Shift+M (the runner bead's
  original plan). The runner key would then match neither Nova nor any
  convention.
- Ctrl+Shift+P, the VS Code, Ghostty, WezTerm and Windows Terminal palette
  key, either alone or as a second key. It helps users from those tools,
  but Eon's first users come from Nova. A second key for one action adds a
  row to the shortcut viewer and hints bar and takes a key that popup
  configuration could otherwise use.
- Ctrl+Alt+P. No app uses it as a palette key, and it sits among Eon's
  pane-moving keys.

## Contract (approved by Lucca, 2026-10-22)

- EON-C8 (`docs/CONTRACTS.md`, "Venus maps Alt+Shift+M to it" in the
  create-column clause) and VEN-C8 (`venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md`, "Alt+Shift+M
  sends one non-repeating `CreateColumn`" and "Alt+Shift+M's
  40-terminal-column refusal") change only the key, from Alt+Shift+M to
  Ctrl+Alt+M. Behavior stays the same: one non-repeating `CreateColumn`, the
  40-terminal-column refusal, and Eon's four-column capacity refusal.
- Until `eon-command-runner-uctp` lands, nothing in Eon binds Alt+Shift+M, so
  it reaches the terminal program. The command runner bead then claims it.

## Evidence

- `venus/src/application/shortcuts.rs:187-193`: the fixed `Create column`
  binding (`KeyCode::KeyM`, `ALT_SHIFT`, `NativeShortcutAction::CreateColumn`).
  `CTRL_ALT` is defined at line 98. No Ctrl+Alt+M binding exists.
- `venus/src/application/shortcuts.rs:~837`: the test that maps Alt+Shift+M to
  `WorkspaceAction::CreateColumn`.
- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/managed_environment.rs:1225`: the test that
  a popup may take a fixed Venus key lists "Alt+Shift+M" as its example.
- User docs: `README.md:51`, `docs/USAGE.md:115`,
  `venus/docs/INTERACTION.md:62`, `venus/docs/PRESENTATION.md:41`.
- `demo/record.rs` never presses Alt+Shift+M, so it needs no change.

## Scope

In scope:
- The fixed binding and its test in `venus/src/application/shortcuts.rs`. The
  shortcut viewer and hints bar take their key text from that table.
- The example key in the `managed_environment.rs` test, changed to Ctrl+Alt+M
  so it still names a fixed binding.
- EON-C8 and VEN-C8 text, the docs listed above, `CHANGELOG.md`, and
  `venus/CHANGELOG.md`.

Out of scope:
- The command runner and any Alt+Shift+M binding (`eon-command-runner-uctp`).
- `CreateColumn` semantics, EONW, and the 40-column or capacity refusals.
- Historical CHANGELOG entries, which stay as written.

## Acceptance

- In installed Eon, Ctrl+Alt+M creates a column right of the selected one,
  with the same refusals as before. Alt+Shift+M no longer creates a column.
- The shortcut viewer (Alt+/) and the hints bar show Ctrl+Alt+M for
  "Create column".
- A popup configured with `keybinding = "Ctrl+Alt+M"` takes the key, as it can
  take any other fixed Venus key.
- No current-state doc names Alt+Shift+M as the create-column key.

## Implementation Notes

1. The shared tree is busy. `eon-claude-chip-split-u3ik` had uncommitted edits
   in `venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md`, `docs/USAGE.md`, both CHANGELOGs and
   `demo/record.rs` on 2026-10-22, and `eon-zoom-selected-pane-e2pv` is
   adding a key. Check `git status` and coordinate before editing those files.
   Commit through a private index.
2. Change `ALT_SHIFT` to `CTRL_ALT` in the `Create column` entry and update
   its test. Update the managed_environment test example.
3. Change the contract text and docs. Add one Unreleased entry each to
   `CHANGELOG.md` and `venus/CHANGELOG.md`.

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-venus` and
  `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime` pass.
- `cargo fmt --check` and
  `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings` pass for Venus.
- Refresh the profile, then make one isolated installed dogfood observation:
  Ctrl+Alt+M adds a column, Alt+Shift+M does not, and Alt+/ lists Ctrl+Alt+M.
  Do not restart the live supervisor.
- Finish with converge and the Codex review that AGENTS.md requires.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if a Ctrl+Alt+M binding or reservation already exists.
- Stop if the change needs any EONW or `CreateColumn` change.
- Stop if verification fails twice for the same reason after a reasonable fix.
close_reason: Ctrl+Alt+M creates a column (3c77cd0); proven by eon-test, fmt/clippy and isolated installed dogfood; profile refreshed

title: Move a live window to a new Eon build without losing terminals
description:
## Why
herdr hands its server over live on upgrade, so terminals survive an update. Eon needs a supervisor restart to pick up a new build, which ends live terminals' clients (eon-newer-build-notice-byd2 only notifies). Source: competitor audit eon-r6yt (2026-10-29), reports in ~/pjs/refs/competitor-audit-2026-10/. Lucca, 2026-10-29: "file the beads". Filing only; no work is approved yet beyond planning.

## Contract
Lifecycle boundary (consequential): ORB/EON contracts for supervisor replacement. Needs approval.

## Change (to plan)
Investigate exec-in-place or handoff of the supervisor and Venus while Orbit hosts keep running; Orbit terminals already persist.

## Acceptance
Upgrading the profile and running one command moves a live window to the new build with every terminal intact.

## Scope
Investigation and plan first.
close_reason: Duplicate of eon-1bq8 (richer: evidence, re-exec shape, open contract questions). herdr evidence and this bead's acceptance recorded as a comment on eon-1bq8.

title: Keep a pane attached when a burst of output overflows Venus's Orbit event queue
description:
## Report

Lucca, 2026-10-22 16:53 -03, installed eon ckisr53k (EONW 15, Venus k2fg2dbk, Orbit 1r1090ww), generation
g1-caca13d0…, Venus PID 251298. In tab t4 (~/pjs/lab/tide), pane p8 (Orbit session-11) ran Codex
TUI (GPT-6.1 Sol). It printed a large burst of output, roughly a screen of escaped JSON from an
Algolia search result, in one go. Venus then showed "p8 unavailable" in the pane header, with the
footer notice "Orbit connection lost: Orbit event queue exceeded its bounded capacity". Lucca: "it
froze". A minute or two later: "it recovered on it's own". Screenshot in the coordinator session.

## Evidence (coordinator, 16:54 -03)

- Orbit still listed p8 as live (`eon workspace --json`). The session-11 sockets existed, and the
  Codex process kept running. Only Venus's attachment dropped.
- Venus wasn't hung: STAT S, ep_poll, about 20% CPU. Load average was about 2 (dyfd's nix build was
  starting), so machine load is unlikely to be the cause.
- The generation log (~/.local/state/eon/logs/g1-caca13d0…log) has no entry for it.
- Source (edge 1ce839f): `venus/src/transport.rs:484-504`. When the per-attachment event queue goes
  past `EVENT_QUEUE_CAPACITY` (256 events), `FRAME_QUEUE_CAPACITY` (2 unreplaced frames), or
  `EVENT_QUEUE_BYTE_CAPACITY` (3 max payloads), the queue is cleared and replaced with
  `TransportEvent::Lost`, and the transport stops. Recovery afterwards presumably came from the
  workspace column retry (`retry_column_views`, VEN-C3). Confirm it.

## Unknown, to establish first

- Which bound tripped: event count, unreplaced frames, or bytes. Why the queue filled at all: the
  Venus event loop falling behind the reader thread (for example while laying out a large frame),
  or a burst of non-frame events that coalescing doesn't replace.
- How long p8 stayed unavailable, and whether input typed meanwhile was lost.
- Reproduce in isolation: a headless Venus attached to an Orbit terminal that prints a few MB of
  long wrapped lines in one write (and a Codex-like full-screen TUI redraw). Record which bound trips.

## Expected

A burst of output never costs a pane its connection. Venus applies backpressure or drops
superseded frames and catches up from Orbit's current state (the latest revision), without a
"connection lost" notice or a visible freeze. The bounds stay, because they protect memory, but
reaching them leads to a resync to the current frame, not a loss.

## Contract

VEN-C3 (transient client recovery) and VEN-C4 (bounded explicit failure UX). The Orbit side,
ORB-C slow-consumer behavior, needs checking too. Making queue saturation resync instead of lose
the connection is a contract change: bring Lucca the exact wording before code.

## Portability disposition

neutral (transport queue and client state; no platform API).

## Scope

In scope: diagnosing which bound trips and why; the Venus transport/queue change, so that
saturation resyncs to the newest state; the contract text; a Venus suite regression test that
floods the queue and checks the attachment survives and shows the latest revision;
`venus/CHANGELOG.md` and `CHANGELOG.md`. Out of scope: Orbit wire changes, unless the diagnosis
shows Orbit must send a checkpoint on request (then stop and bring Lucca the wire change).

## Acceptance

- The isolated reproduction no longer shows "Orbit connection lost". The pane keeps updating and
  ends on the terminal's final screen.
- Memory stays bounded: queue bytes never exceed the existing byte bound.
- One isolated installed dogfood observation with a burst-printing program.
close_reason: Venus applies backpressure when its Orbit event queue is full; burst-while-scrolling no longer drops the attachment (VEN-C3/VEN-C4)

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Diagnosis (2026-10-22, edge f033767, code trace; no isolated run yet):
- Bound: FRAME_QUEUE_CAPACITY (2 unreplaced frames), venus/src/transport.rs:485-495. Output alone cannot trip it, because a newer frame replaces the queued one when only Accepted or WheelOutcome::TerminalRouted sit between them. Orbit sends no Metadata on the attachment.
- Cause: during an active Venus scroll (wheel, trackpad or momentum), drive_terminal_scroll runs after every drain (application.rs:3479). Each drained Frame rebases the scroll and clears the preview (scroll.rs:216-224, 266; model.rs:333), so Venus sends a new PreviewVertical per frame revision. Orbit answers each with VerticalPreview between its frames. With the event loop busy, the queue then holds Frame, VerticalPreview, Frame, VerticalPreview, and the next Frame becomes Lost. ScrollOutcome, SelectionFinished, CopiedText, ClipboardWrite (OSC 52) and Failure also block replacement. With enough of them, the 256-event cap does the same.
- Recovery: Lost resets the retry (application.rs:1371), so no timer re-attaches. A workspace change re-attached it: tab or pane selection, a popup, the column set, or the pane's live/endpoint changing (application.rs:1507-1522, 1302-1306). Which one Lucca hit is unknown.
- Orbit side: ORB-C7 already handles a slow reader. Its OutputQueue replaces unstarted frames and previews (socket.rs:246-266) and detaches only past output_bound, which Venus sees as RetryableLoss and retries.
- Proposed shape: backpressure. When a push would exceed a bound, the Venus reader stops reading until the event loop drains, and Orbit's ORB-C7 coalescing keeps the newest frame. No wire change. Awaiting Lucca's approval of the VEN-C3/VEN-C4 wording.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Lucca approved (2026-10-22): 1) the VEN-C3 Result bullet 'A burst of Orbit output never costs the attachment. When Venus's bounded event queue is full, Venus stops reading from Orbit until its event loop drains the queue. Orbit's bounded slow-reader handling (ORB-C7) then delivers the newest frame, so the pane resumes at the current terminal state.' and dropping 'queue' from VEN-C4's terminal failures; 2) backpressure only, with no Venus preview replacement; 3) proof is a Venus-suite red/green regression plus one isolated installed burst-while-scrolling observation, with no headless Venus harness; 4) the one-preview-per-frame flood while scrolling goes to a separate follow-up bead.

On installed ckisr53k, the same script ended with 'p1 unavailable' and 'Orbit connection lost: Orbit event queue exceeded its bounded capacity'.
- Rebases from f033767 to 2a3ed97, 6a3b231 and c1fa8ef conflicted only on changelog ordering.

title: Decide: update a running window in place without losing its terminals or layout
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-10-24: "maybe we should open a bead to consider 'in-place' updating. supposedly, if a
eon update does not touch orbit, could we not replace the window without losing information from the
old window?" Today every profile refresh leaves running windows on the old build until the user
closes them, which ends their terminals; this session alone asked him to restart windows after each
of six landings.

## Today (evidence)

- EON-C11 (docs/CONTRACTS.md:1080): a generation's identity is the `g1-` hash of Eon's source tree,
  so any change makes a new generation. Older live generations stay discoverable and presentable only
  with the exact same EONW and component graph; otherwise `eon attach GENERATION` delegates to the old
  build. Present never replaces the live Venus process, Orbit attachment or terminal.
- Terminals live in per-session Orbit host processes (`yazelix-orbit serve <gen dir>/session-N.sock
  --management-v2 ...`), children of the supervisor, which reaps them (Orbit owns direct-child
  reaping). Their sockets live in the generation's runtime directory.
- Recovery after a supervisor restart (EON-C8) keeps terminals but projects them all into `t1`, so the
  layout (tabs, columns, popups, selection) is lost.
- Terminals carry `EON_TERMINAL` and `EON_SESSION_BIN` (their build's `eon`), so CLI calls from old
  terminals talk with the old build's EONW (memory: CLI accepts same-version supervisors).
- eon-newer-build-notice-byd2 (P2) tells a window that a newer Eon is installed; this bead would be
  the action behind that notice.

## The idea, refined

The real condition is not "Orbit untouched" but "the running Orbit hosts stay compatible": they keep
running their old binary anyway, so what matters is that the new supervisor and Venus still speak the
running hosts' management and terminal protocols (ORB versions), and that the supervisor can take over
their ownership.

Candidate shape (to compare at the reference gate):
1. Re-exec in place: the old supervisor serializes its state (workspace set and layout, ID allocator,
   attention, run records, Venus presentation state) to an inherited fd, then `execve`s the new
   build's supervisor binary with a resume flag. Same PID, so the Orbit hosts stay its children (no
   reaping gap) and listening sockets can be inherited. Comparable: nginx binary upgrade, systemd
   `daemon-reexec`, HAProxy seamless reload.
2. Venus restarts on the new build and presents the restored layout (on Wayland a new process means a
   new surface, so the window closes and reopens; terminals, scrollback and layout survive).
3. Refuse and fall back to today's behaviour (keep the old window, show the notice) when the protocols
   differ, with a clear reason.

## Open questions (user-owned or contract)

- EON-C11 identity: a generation whose supervisor binary changes in place. Contract change.
- EONW: old terminals' `eon` (old build) talking to a new supervisor; version negotiation or a
  terminal-environment refresh.
- Trigger: automatic on profile refresh, a notice button, or `eon update` per window.
- Platform: execve and fd inheritance are POSIX; keep it out of Venus (portability disposition).

## Next step

A decision bead: reference gate (re-exec designs above; how Orbit hosts and the generation directory
move), a written contract proposal for Lucca, then a spike behind it. Split before any implementation.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Line-drift refresh, 2026-10-27 (prime-beads pass 3): EON-C11 docs/CONTRACTS.md:1080 -> :1219. 'Recovery into t1' is EON-C15 behaviour (docs/CONTRACTS.md ~1436-1451, :545), not EON-C8. Other references hold. Related now linked: eon-agent-parity-a9g0.7 (re-read config by replacing Venus) and eon-reboot-restore-im8y (layout serialization).

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Competitor evidence (audit eon-r6yt, 2026-10-29; ~/pjs/refs/competitor-audit-2026-10/herdr.md): herdr hands its server over live on upgrade, so terminals survive an update. eon-0o5d ('Move a live window to a new Eon build without losing terminals', filed from that audit) was closed as a duplicate of this bead; its acceptance carries over as a candidate check: upgrading the profile and running one command moves a live window to the new build with every terminal intact.

title: Fix the intermittent quota worker isolation test
description:
## Defect

eon-runtime's quota::tests::workers_isolate_failure_and_bound_output_timeout_and_shutdown failed once in an 80-run loop of `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime --lib` (2026-10-21, x86_64 Linux, 1-minute load about 2-13, while working eon-p8cq on base 9e0bb86 with an earlier p8cq candidate). It panicked at quota.rs:447:37 on that revision (now quota.rs:448, after cbe397c added a line): `quotas.codex.snapshot().unwrap()` found None after the test's 2 s wait. It passed in the 110 other full-suite runs that session.

## Suspected cause (unproved)

Linux refuses to exec a file while any process holds it open for writing (ETXTBSY), and Rust's Command::spawn does not retry. The test writes its fake backend with fs::write and execs it right after. Other tests in the same process spawn children; a child forked during that fs::write inherits the write descriptor until it execs, so the backend is briefly "text file busy". The first fetch (claude, 50 ms timeout) expects an error anyway, so an ETXTBSY there fails instantly instead of after 50 ms, and Quotas::start then spawns the codex worker microseconds later, still inside the window. That fetch also fails, the worker waits its 60 s interval, and the snapshot is still None at 2 s. This is the same fork-inheritance class as eon-p8cq.

The later rewrite of the backend before the output-bound fetch (quota.rs:468) has the same race; there ETXTBSY yields the expected Err, so it cannot fail the test but can skip the output-bound check it means to exercise. claude_waits_300_units_after_a_failed_read_while_codex_reads_every_60 writes and execs its backend the same way (quota.rs:490).

Alternative to rule out: plain scheduling delay under load (sh startup plus printf exceeding 2 s).

## Contract

No contract change. The test protects EON-C27 quota worker isolation, the output bound, timeout and shutdown.

## Acceptance

- Name the cause from evidence: a reproduction under the full suite (or a focused one, e.g. a concurrent fork loop around the fs::write), showing the failing spawn's error kind.
- A test-only fix that makes the backend's spawn deterministic without weakening what the test checks, for example writing the script to a temporary name and renaming it into place, or writing it once before any other test can fork, rather than retrying the spawn in product code. The output-bound fetch must exercise the bound, not fail at spawn.
- Red/green from the reproduction; `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime --lib` looped under the full suite.
- cargo fmt --check and clippy -D warnings clean.

## Scope boundary

The quota tests that write and exec a backend script. No product change unless the reproduction shows a product defect; then stop and record it.
close_reason: Quota test script helper now has a child sh write each script, so no forked child inherits a write descriptor; ETXTBSY red/green 107-135/2000 to 0/2000, suite 30/30

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
From eon-ven-new-window-test-flake-66gm (2026-10-27), which asked whether one shared test-helper pattern fixes both. What I found by reading the code at 6a3ee78; nothing here is proved in eon-runtime.

- The quota test helper `script` (runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/quota.rs:522-530) still writes the backend with `fs::write` in the test process, then chmods it. Its callers exec it right away: lines 629 and 674 in workers_isolate_failure_and_bound_output_timeout_and_shutdown, and 687, 759 and 848 in other tests.
- bd7fa29 moved the callers to fresh paths ("callers use a fresh path for each one (eon-1fxc)"). A fresh path does not close the race. The descriptor that a concurrently forked child inherits refers to the new file and stays open until that child execs or exits.
- 66gm's standalone reproduction of exactly this pattern (~/.cache/eon-agents/66gm-work/repro/main.rs: four threads forking while the main thread writes, chmods and execs a fresh script) failed 162/2000 and 758/10000 rounds with "Text file busy (os error 26)".
- The pattern 66gm adopted had 0 failures in 20000 rounds: a child shell writes the file (`sh -c 'printf %s "$1" > "$0"' <path> <body>`) and the test process only chmods by path. The same pattern applies here, using the `sh` that the helper already finds on PATH.
- It cannot be one shared helper: Venus depends only on the protocol crates, and there is no shared test crate, so each crate keeps a local copy.
- eon-1fxc's acceptance still needs its own red/green in eon-runtime, including ruling out plain scheduling delay.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Cause and red/green (eon-50, 2026-10-27, x86_64 Linux, base abdbfd0, `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime --lib zz_repro -- --test-threads=1 --nocapture`, 1-minute load 7-13). The reproduction is kept outside the repository at ~/.cache/eon-agents/1fxc-work/repro.rs, with logs red*.log and green.log next to it. It adds two temporary tests to quota.rs `mod tests`, both run while four threads fork and exec /bin/sh in a loop.

- Spawn error kind. In each of 2000 rounds the test writes a fresh script with the `script` helper and spawns it at once. Old helper: ETXTBSY in 107, 135, 44 and 49 of 2000 rounds across four runs (the last with fork-forcing pre_exec forkers), and no other spawn error. When the first spawn hit ETXTBSY, an immediate second spawn hit it again in 46/135, 20/44 and 24/49 of those rounds. Fixed helper: 0/2000.
- The failing test's prefix, 1500 rounds: script, the 50 ms claude fetch timed, then Quotas::start_every for codex and the test's 2 s wait. Old helper: the claude spawn failed (the read ended before its 50 ms timeout) in 12/1500 rounds; the codex snapshot was missing at 2 s in 0/1500. Fixed helper: 0/1500 failed claude spawns, 0/1500 missing snapshots, slowest snapshot 25 ms.
- Conclusion. The helper's own write makes an immediate exec fail with ETXTBSY under concurrent forks; that is the proved cause class. The full failure needs the codex worker's spawn to fail too (it then waits its 60 s interval), which happened once in 191 suite runs and 0/1500 times in this focused loop; it was not reproduced end to end. Plain scheduling delay is not supported: across 1500 rounds at load about 10 the slowest snapshot was 25 ms, against the 2 s budget.
- Fix (test-only, quota.rs `script`): a child `sh` writes the script (`printf '%s' "$1" > "$0"`), so the test process never holds a write descriptor that a forked child could inherit; it then only chmods by path. All five callers already use fresh paths, which the redirect needs. The output-bound fetch (flood) now spawns, so it exercises the bound.

comments.text:
Proof (eon-50, 2026-10-27, x86_64 Linux, base abdbfd0, candidate tree 94557da93203d81d6dea8e7c6ba65ffed16d0322; this commit changes only this bead record beyond it).

comments.text: Review ledger: 2 Claude passes and 2 Codex passes. Claude 1 (tree 94557da) found one wrong count in the 03:52 comment (191 suite runs); the 04:02 comment corrects it. Claude 2 (tree 60fcc9f) was clean. Codex full review of 94557da: clean. Codex narrow re-check of 94557da to 60fcc9f: clean. title: Keep the link hover steady while the terminal is printing output
description:
## Report

Lucca, 2026-10-22 ~16:30 -03, installed eon ckisr53k (EONW 15): "hovering on links while a program
or agent is outputing makes it flicker on and off a lot". The link highlight and its Open/Copy hint
blink while the terminal keeps receiving output (for example a Claude Code agent streaming), even
though the pointer stays still on the link.

## Contract

VEN-C5 (native hyperlinks), Failures: "Revision, attachment, geometry, presentation, focus,
occlusion, or scroll changes retire link actions." Scene re-detects plain-text targets on every
frame's visible rows.

## Hypothesis (inference, not yet evidence)

Each new terminal revision retires the hovered target, and the highlight only returns once hover is
re-derived (on the next pointer event or frame). Streaming output produces revisions many times a
second, so the highlight toggles at that rate. First check: confirm it in the Venus scene/input code
and reproduce it in isolation. Use a headless Venus with the pointer on a plain-text URL and an OSC 8
link, while the terminal prints a line every ~50 ms on rows away from the link. Count how often the
highlight changes state.

## Expected

While the pointer stays still and the same target (same URI, same visible cells) remains under it,
the highlight and hint stay steady across revisions. They change only when the target under the
pointer actually changes or goes away (scrolled, overwritten, rewrapped, retired by focus or
presentation). Activation safety stays as it is: Ctrl+click still opens only a target that is
current at both press and release.

## Contract change (needs Lucca's approval before code)

Keeping hover across revisions narrows VEN-C5's "revision changes retire link actions" for the
hover highlight. Proposal to bring him: a revision re-validates the hovered target instead of
retiring it. If the same URI still occupies the same cells, the hover is kept. Activation still
requires press and release on the same current target. Bring the exact wording first.

## Portability disposition

neutral (scene and hover state; no platform API).

## Scope

In scope: Venus hover persistence across revisions for OSC 8 and plain-text targets; the VEN-C5
text; a Venus suite regression test; `venus/CHANGELOG.md` if the contract changes; `CHANGELOG.md`
(user-visible).

Out of scope: link detection rules, open/copy behavior, the AccessKit target list (unless it
flickers for the same cause, then note it).

## Acceptance

- In the isolated reproduction, the highlight stays on for the whole streaming run while the
  pointer is still and the target is unchanged.
- When the line under the pointer is overwritten or scrolls away, the highlight follows within one
  frame.
- One isolated installed dogfood observation: hover a link while an agent streams output, with no
  flicker.

## Verification

A Venus suite regression test for hover across revisions, through `nix develop -c eon-test -p
venus` (or Venus's documented harness), plus `cargo fmt --check` and clippy for venus. One isolated
installed observation per venus/docs/DEVELOPMENT.md.
close_reason: Hover and hint stay steady under output, and Ctrl+click survives output that keeps its target. VEN-C5 updated with Lucca's approved wording. Proof is in the comments; the profile refresh is left to the coordinator.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Cause, from code at edge 1ce839f (venus/src/application.rs). The bead's hypothesis was close but not exact.

- Every plain output frame bumps the presentation generation (`content_changed`, ~2052). Eon workspace focus changes and invalidations bump it too.
- `render()` (~2731) takes the highlight from `focused_link()`, and `status()` takes the hint from it through `link_status()`. Both go through `link_scene()`, which requires `presentation.is_current(candidate)`. The candidate being drawn is not yet published, so a frame that presents a new revision is drawn with no highlight, no hint, and a 1.5-row notice box instead of 3 rows.
- After `Presented`, `inspect_pointer_link()` re-derives focus against the newly published identity. The identity differs, so it calls `refresh_client_view()`, and the next frame draws the highlight again.
- Result: each revision gives one frame off, then one frame on. With output arriving every frame, the highlight stays off most of the time. The ignored live test (~4961) asserts the unpresented half: `handle_transport(linked_frame(7)); assert!(focused_link().is_none())`.
- Same mechanism for Ctrl+click: press at revision R and release at R+1 are different `LinkFocus` identities, so a Ctrl+click during streaming output is consumed without opening (test "a captured click cannot cross a frame replacement").
- AccessKit's link list is replaced per presented revision, not cleared in between, so it does not flicker from this cause.

Proposed shape (pending Lucca's approval of the VEN-C5 text): render derives the highlight and hint from the candidate scene it is drawing (the same pointer hit test, with `scroll_offset == 0` for unshifted). Actions keep requiring a published current target. When focus moves to a new identity at the same cells with the same URI, it updates without a second redraw.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Lucca approved the VEN-C5 change in this session on 2026-10-22, around 16:50 -03 ("1 ok, 2 ok"). Both items are in this bead's scope:

1. Hover: add to Result: "The highlight and hint are derived from the frame being presented, so a target that stays under a still pointer stays highlighted while output arrives." Change Failures to: "Attachment, geometry, presentation, focus, occlusion, or scroll changes retire link actions. A revision retires them too; the hovered target is re-derived in the new frame."
2. Ctrl+click: replace "Opening requires a press and release on the same current presented target" with "Opening requires a press and release on the same target: the same URI over the same cells, presented at both; output revisions between them keep the press, and every other change in Failures retires it."

The regression test covers both: the hover flicker, and Ctrl+click failing while output streams.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Lucca approved the reconciled Failures text in this session on 2026-10-22, around 17:30 -03 ("ok"). The approved sentence "A revision retires them too" conflicted with item 2, which says output revisions keep the press. The new text: "Attachment, geometry, presentation, focus, occlusion, or scroll changes retire link actions. An output revision keeps a target that stays over the same cells with the same URI and retires any other; the hovered target is re-derived in the new frame."

comments.text:
Candidate observations, not accepted proof, at edge 587563d4323e667c76d0062c9e5df645696dc10d plus the candidate tree 3a550e3d1b244173a8c6a6fb5ff15b586a7c043d.

- Green: with the candidate, every new link assertion in that test passes: hover and hint steady over revisions 8-10, Ctrl+click across them activates, a replaced target retires the press, an overwritten target loses its hover.
- Environment: private headless Sway 1.12 (`WLR_BACKENDS=headless`, 1280x800), with the installed Venus wrapper's LD_LIBRARY_PATH and FONTCONFIG_FILE, on this x86_64 Linux host.
- Pre-existing failure, not from this change: later in the same test, the tab-strip hit test fails (`Some(Control(NewTab))` vs `None`). Unmodified edge 587563d4323e667c76d0062c9e5df645696dc10d fails at the same assertion in this environment, so the remaining steps of that test do not run here. Accepted gap for this bead: it predates the change and does not touch link code.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Review ledger: 1 Codex round, 6 Claude passes and 1 narrow Codex re-check, converged on tree d9cf9d9 (rebased onto edge 2a3ed97).
- Round 1, Codex plus a fresh Claude reviewer on candidate tree 3a550e3:
  - Both found that a Ctrl+click press was not retired for good when output replaced its target and then restored it before a redraw.
  - Codex also found that a hovered target which was already presented could not be pressed until its highlight had been drawn.
  - Both fixed: the new `LinkPress::{Live, Retired}` retires the press, and `presented()` accepts the current scene or the highlighted target.
- Converge round 2: removed the test-only `Renderer::hyperlink()` getter (the test reads `links.shown`), merged `pointer_target` into `pointer_link(unshifted)`, and made the unpresented-inertness assertion meaningful.
- Converge round 3: trimmed the `LinkPress` derive and fixed the epoch comment.
- Converge round 4: the notice-box hit test uses the scroll state of the frame being drawn.
- Converge round 5: the release branch assigns focus once.
- Rebased onto 2a3ed97 (root CHANGELOG conflict resolved). Converge round 6: clean.
- Narrow Codex re-check of the change between candidate 3a550e3 and fixed tree d9cf9d9: nothing blocking.
- Accepted, not fixed:
  - A plain ReturnToLive frame that lands the same URI on the same cells keeps the hover. A pill click or wheel input still retires a held press.
  - A held press stays live after an invalidation until the next view refresh. Its release cannot activate, because the epochs differ.

comments.text:
Proof, 2026-10-22, on base edge 6a3b231. Code tree bafddb40d404dabc6dbd0259e604aacf70a50aca; the committed tree adds only the VEN-C5 proof text and this bead line. This commit is the proof's revision.
- Source checks, x86_64 Linux, run with CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=6:
  - `nix develop -c bash -c 'cargo fmt -p yazelix-venus --check && cargo clippy --locked -p yazelix-venus --all-targets -- -D warnings'`: clean.
  - `nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-venus`: 108, 55 and 18 passed, 0 failed.
  - Venus's ignored `live_output_keeps_application_input_admitted_before_repaint` on a private headless Sway 1.12 (1280x800, with the installed Venus wrapper's LD_LIBRARY_PATH and FONTCONFIG_FILE): passed in full. Its link steps cover:
    - hover and hint steady over revisions 8-10;
    - a Ctrl+click held across them activating;
    - a target that is replaced and then returns before a redraw retiring the press;
    - hover following a successor while a retired press is held;
    - invalidation retiring a press;
    - plain output overwriting a target removing its hover.
- Red, at edge 587563d: base code plus only the hover assertion failed with `left: None, right: Some((0, 0))`.
- Installed build: `nix build .#default` from the code tree produced /nix/store/0irplm13r9km7bm30fc0kx8spayd2fd8-eon-0.1.1 (eon g1-38744629ff605dd79c08b2f64efe2b3a, EONW 17).
- Installed observation setup: a private headless Sway 1.12 (1280x720, pixman), fresh HOME/XDG dirs, Anima off, and a recording `gio` first on PATH. A pane created with `eon pane create -- sh stream.sh` printed https://example.invalid/eon-1u9e on row 1 and then rewrote row 5 every 50 ms.
- Installed observation results:
  - Link row, 20 grim captures 0.1 s apart: one hash with the pointer away and one different hash while hovered, so the outline stayed steady.
  - Hint box: 20 of 20 captures identical. They show the target and "Ctrl+click Open · Ctrl+Shift+C Copy".
  - Ctrl+click (wtype holding Ctrl, Sway seat cursor press, 0.4 s or about 8 output frames, release): dispatched `gio open -- https://example.invalid/eon-1u9e`, with the notice "Link handed to the desktop handler.".

title: Show the directory the shell used, not the resolved one, for a tab on macOS and symlinks
description:
## Why

On macOS `/tmp` is a symlink to `/private/tmp`. Eon reports a terminal's directory from the
process's physical cwd (getcwd), so a tab opened from `/tmp/x` shows `/private/tmp/x`, unlike the
path the person typed and the shell shows. Found by kz4p.25 (its workspace_control.rs test now
expects the physical path for 8 cwd-derived assertions). The same happens on Linux for any
symlinked directory.

Lucca, 2026-10-28, agreeing to the recommendation: show the path the shell used.

## Contract

The tab/pane directory Eon shows and reports (`eon workspace --json` `directory`, tab labels). Check
docs/CONTRACTS.md for the owning EON-C text before code; if a contract names "the working
directory" precisely, propose the wording change to Lucca first.

## Change

Prefer the logical directory: when Eon learns a directory and a logical `$PWD` is available (the
launching environment, or the shell's reported cwd such as OSC 7), use it only if it resolves to
the same physical directory (same device and inode); otherwise keep the physical path. One owner
for this choice in Eon Runtime.

## Acceptance

- Launching from a symlinked directory on Linux shows the symlink path; a stale or lying `$PWD`
  falls back to the physical path (tests for both).
- workspace_control.rs's 8 macOS-adjusted expectations go back to the raw path where they derive
  from such a launch.
- `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime -p eon`, fmt, clippy on Linux and darwin.

## Scope

Eon Runtime directory reporting only. Not part of the macOS CI blockers. Codex review per
AGENTS.md.

title: Let the CLI act on the calling terminal's own workspace when another generation is current
description:
## Why

Found 2026-10-24 by the overseer (agent in Lucca's live Eon window, g1-712f) when Lucca asked to
run Codex workers "live on this stack" (pane stack of his window). The window's terminals carry
`EON_TERMINAL=session-1.338547-...` for generation g1-712f, but another live generation
(g1-7241..., started 16:44 in the default runtime root with no Venus window) had become the
"current" one. Then, from a terminal of Lucca's window:

    $ eon workspace --json
    {... "tabs":[{"id":"t1","directory":"/home/lucca/pjs/games/machines_vs_aliens", ...}]}
    # the other generation's workspace, silently, not the caller's

    $ eon pane create --json --no-focus -- tail -F <log>
    {"error":{"code":"unknown-caller","detail":"the calling terminal is not live in this Eon workspace"}}

So an agent in a perfectly live Eon terminal cannot act on its own window, and reads another
window's state without any sign that it is not its own. AGENTS.md "Humans and Agents": every
window action has a CLI path an agent in an Eon terminal can use, naming its target by ID.

## Goal

The CLI targets the calling terminal's own workspace when it runs inside an Eon terminal,
whatever generation is current, and otherwise has an explicit way to name the target
(generation or window ID). `workspace --json` says which generation/window it describes. Owner:
Eon's CLI target resolution (eon crate) over Eon Runtime's caller identity.

## Acceptance

- Reproduce first: two live generations, the caller's not current; `eon workspace --json` and
  `eon pane create --no-focus` from the caller's terminal act on the caller's workspace.
- Outside Eon, the current generation stays the default; an explicit target flag (name chosen in
  the contract) reaches a non-current one.
- Contract wording to Lucca before code (EON-C CLI clause).

Related: eon-agent-parity-a9g0, eon-89ho (pane create --tab), eon-agent-terminal-control-n8ic and
eon-pane-send-research-fo4p (sending input to a pane; the other limit hit the same day: an agent
cannot drive a TUI such as a live Codex session running in a pane).
close_reason: Landed: CLI targets the caller's own workspace

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Approval (Lucca, 2026-10-25 ~05:40 -03, direct to the overseer, answering its numbered list item 3): "approval to all". Approved: inside an Eon terminal the CLI resolves the terminal's own supervisor and workspace through EON_TERMINAL whichever generation the invoked build would pick, with no fallback to another workspace; outside Eon, explicit `--generation G` / `--window ID`; workspace JSON gains `generation` and `window`. The draft's choices stand as it recommends (separate flags; explicit targets constrain rather than override the caller; window-only selection follows `window attach`'s rule; bounded validated discovery; incompatible builds fail explicitly). Drafted wording (Codex draft reviewed by the overseer, 2026-10-25):

**3. eon-2gk7 — Resolve the caller’s supervisor and workspace**

**Current clauses → proposed replacements**

EON-C10, `docs/CONTRACTS.md`, caller-targeting sentence:
> When set, it makes `pane create`, `edit`, `pane close PANE`, `pane move` and `tab move` act on that terminal's tab instead of the active tab: `pane create` adds to the caller's column, the moves move the caller's own pane or tab, and `pane close` resolves PANE in the caller's tab.

Replace with:
> For workspace control, `EON_TERMINAL` selects the live supervisor and workspace that own that exact terminal, independently of the invoked CLI build’s current generation. Within that workspace, `pane create`, `edit`, `pane close PANE`, `pane move` and `tab move` retain their calling-tab, column and pane rules: creation uses the caller’s column, moves act on its pane or tab, and pane close resolves its target in the caller’s tab.

EON-C10, remaining-command sentence:
> Other commands, and commands run outside Eon terminals, ignore it.

Replace with:
> Other workspace-scoped commands use the caller’s workspace and retain their existing per-tab rules. Without a calling terminal or explicit target, workspace control uses the invoked build’s current generation in the selected runtime namespace and its shown workspace. Launch, lifecycle and local information commands retain their existing targeting.

EON-C10, build-mismatch failures:
> This includes a caller whose CLI build has no supervisor in that terminal's window, as when an `eon` from another build runs inside an Eon terminal: its detail names that build's generation and points to the terminal's own `eon`, never to running `eon` first. Other commands run inside an Eon terminal that find no supervisor of their build still exit 4, with the same detail.

Replace with:
> Absence of this CLI build’s supervisor does not prevent control of the caller’s compatible supervisor. Caller resolution uses the complete opaque terminal identity and never falls back to another workspace. A malformed or stale caller exits 3; failed or ambiguous resolution changes nothing. An unavailable or incompatible selected supervisor fails explicitly without starting, presenting or restarting it.

EON-C11, default-generation clause:
> Eon and eonbase use separate runtime namespaces and default to their exact current generation.

Replace with:
> Eon and eonbase use separate runtime namespaces. Launch and lifecycle defaults use their exact current generation; Eon workspace control follows EON-C10’s caller and explicit-target rules.

**Add to EON-C10 Result:**
> Workspace commands accept `--generation GENERATION` and `--window ID` before any `--` operand separator. `--window` selects an independent window’s runtime namespace; otherwise the existing runtime namespace applies. `--generation` selects an exact generation there. With only `--window`, selection follows `window attach`’s current-or-sole-live-generation rule. If `EON_TERMINAL` is set, the selected supervisor must validate that caller; explicit targeting does not waive caller validation. Workspace CLI results name the described `generation` and `window`, with `window` null for the default namespace, and identify the projected workspace through shn4.3’s workspace discriminator.

**Wire:** no additional EONW change is required for generation routing or the CLI’s `generation`/`window` fields. Existing `Request.caller: Option<String>` carries the opaque identity; the selected supervisor validates the exact live run. Generation IDs retain `g1-` plus 32 lowercase hex digits; independent window IDs retain eight lowercase hex digits. Caller-scoped snapshot projection needs shn4.3’s work, including distinguishing the described workspace from the shown one. Unknown explicit targets exit 3, unavailable supervisors exit 4, malformed flags/IDs exit 2, and ambiguous window selection exits 1.

**Open choices**
1. Flags: separate `--generation`/`--window`, one `--target`, or positional targets. **Recommend separate flags**, reusing the nouns and validation already used by `attach GENERATION` and `window attach ID`.
2. Explicit target precedence: constrain the caller or override it. **Recommend constraining it**; `env -u EON_TERMINAL eon ...` already expresses acting without caller context and preserves command-pane caller validation.
3. Window-only selection: current-or-sole-live, or require a generation. **Recommend the existing `window_generation` rule**, with `--generation` resolving ambiguity.
4. JSON: `generation`/`window` or `generation_id`/`window_id`. **Recommend `generation`/`window`**, matching lifecycle results and `window stop all --json`.
5. Discovery: validate candidate supervisors in the inherited namespace, or add an exported routing locator. **Recommend bounded validated discovery first**; the current identity is opaque, and `Runtime.sessions` contains local session IDs rather than complete caller identities. Never match only `session-N`.
6. Incompatible builds: fail explicitly or delegate workspace commands to the retained old executable. **Recommend explicit failure**, preserving the existing EONW boundary; delegation currently belongs to attach.

**Conflicts/splits:** “current” in the report is misleading: `current_generation()` hashes the invoked build’s immutable assembly; a newer live generation does not become a mutable global current. The actual owner is Runtime’s `cli.rs`/`generation.rs`/`windows.rs`, as EON-C10 already states; the Eon crate supplies inputs and exit handling. Update the bead’s ownership claim accordingly. Preserve same-EONW control across component-graph differences without weakening presentation admission. Cross-window discovery, incompatible-command delegation, lifecycle retargeting and terminal input automation are separate scope. Future proof must exercise both reads and `pane create --no-focus` from a non-current caller, explicit outside targets, and stale callers without fallback.

title: Show the Eon icon in the Eon Bar
description:
## Decision
Lucca, 2026-10-19: show the Eon icon in the Eon Bar.

## Contract (provisional; needs Lucca's approval before code)
- Consumer: a full-Eon user on native x86_64 Linux Wayland.
- Result: the Eon Bar shows the Eon icon (the shipped `assets/eon.png` mark, the same one the
  desktop entry uses) at a fixed size that fits the existing tab-strip height, at a fixed position.
- Failures: a missing or undecodable icon shows no icon and leaves no gap, hit target or accessible
  node; the icon never displaces required tabs, controls or drag space under width pressure
  (VEN-C21 priority); it stays sharp at integer scales.
- Contracts: an extension of EON-C21 (native workspace header) and VEN-C21 (native Eon Bar
  workspace header); stop for approval of the text first.

## Ownership
Eon owns product identity and the icon asset. Venus owns the bar's geometry, painting and AccessKit
projection. Venus must not hard-code Eon's brand, so the slice decides how the asset reaches Venus
(decision 1).

## Open decisions (recommendations)
1. Delivery: Eon's launch passes the icon to Venus as a launch input the way other product inputs
   travel (recommended, keeps Venus brand-neutral); or Venus embeds it at build time (cheaper, but
   puts Eon's brand inside Venus); or EONW carries it (a protocol revision for a static image; not
   recommended).
2. Position: at the bar's leading edge before the first tab (recommended, where app marks usually
   sit).
3. Behavior: decorative only, with no click or hover action (recommended); a click target such as
   an About or menu is a separate feature.
4. Accessibility: no accessible node, since it is decorative (recommended); or one static label
   "Eon".
5. Width pressure: drop the icon first, before quota chips (recommended).

## Reference gate
Consequential only if decision 1 adds a launch-input or protocol field: then record the existing
launch-input path in Eon and Venus, a comparable header (e.g. Ghostty's or WezTerm's tab bar), the
rejected delivery options, and the check before code.

## Prerequisites
None.

## Acceptance
Venus layout test: icon present, its size and position, and absent with no gap or node when the
asset is missing or under width pressure; affected Rust tests through `nix develop -c eon-test`;
fmt and clippy for the changed Venus crate; nix build; one isolated installed capture showing the
icon in the bar; review loop; profile refresh.

## Scope boundary
The static icon only: no animation, menu, click action, theming variants or new icon design. Linux
Wayland only; no macOS claim.

title: Centralize Venus chrome colors in one role-named palette
description:
Contracts: Venus chrome presentation (VEN-C8, VEN-C18, VEN-C30 colors as drawn); no contract text change expected, since this is a behavior-preserving refactor.

Decision (Lucca, 2026-10-26): centralize Venus's colors in one palette and use it everywhere.

Problem: Venus has about 84 inline `SceneColor { r, g, b }` literals across venus/src/render/chrome.rs, render.rs and render/cells.rs, and only two named constants (`CARD_OUTLINE`, `DEFAULT_BACKGROUND` in render.rs). Shades repeat by hand (bright label 239,244,248; dim label 162,174,190; accent 126,231,185 defined locally inside `build_border_title`), so contrast drifts per call site; eon-furp's tab contrast bug came from that.

Change: one Venus palette module with role-named colors (for example surface, bar, pill idle/hover/selected, text primary/secondary, outline neutral/focus, accent, danger, attention states), each defined once; every draw site uses the role. Keep test-only literals (fixtures like 255,0,0) where they are test inputs. `focus_color` stays the configured value Runtime sends; the palette holds Venus's own fixed chrome colors.

Acceptance: identical rendering: no pixel changes (prove with the existing Venus render tests plus a before/after capture or golden comparison of the chrome at one size and scale). Record each role's contrast ratio against its background in the bead, flagging any below 4.5:1 for text or 3:1 for UI edges as follow-up candidates (do not change colors in this bead). Venus tests, fmt and clippy green.

Scope boundary: no user-configurable theme (Eon Runtime would own parsing; separate decision), no color changes, no Orbit terminal palette (cells.rs ANSI defaults stay unless they are chrome colors). Prerequisite: eon-furp landed (955df93).

title: Make eonbase-closure absence checks fail on a match
description:
## Why

The eonbase-closure flake check asserts that the eonbase closure excludes Eon's managed tools
and the full eon package, and that the eonbase wrapper does not name libexec/eon/bin. Both
absence assertions are written as `! grep ...` (flake.nix:542, :546). Under the stdenv builder's
errexit, a command negated with `!` never stops the script, so the check passes even when grep
finds a forbidden path. Found during eon-zti4.2 review.

## Scope

title: Prove Yazelix Eon as a thin orchestrator
description:
## Current planning disposition — 2026-09-08

This is an unclaimed, deferred product-horizon container. The user authorized reconciliation of the Eon backlog after benchmark/focus-policy commit `418c388`; no implementation child, runtime change, new issue, platform, consumer cutover or distribution channel is activated. EON-C7 and `eon-linux-wayland-product-wr0` govern Linux/native-Wayland-only scope with exact x86_64 alpha proof. The Nova transition below remains a separately gated consumer plan; its historical macOS path cannot block unrelated Eon Linux work. Organizational epic links use `related`; real outcome prerequisites retain `blocks`. Exact contract phases and defaults belong to `docs/CONTRACTS.md` and README.

## Goal and permanent product hierarchy

Keep Eon a thin orchestrator with one canonical exact component graph and one owner for each behavior.

- **Eon** is the full managed experience and permanent product name; command/package `eon`.
- **EonTerm** is the reusable terminal product in this repository; command/package `eonterm`.
- **Nova** remains an independent full Yazelix/Zellij product and currently uses its accepted minimal Rio surface. Any later adoption of exact EonTerm instead of Rio requires fresh Nova-owned acceptance; it is not an Eon alpha requirement.
- **Eonova** remains private transition dogfood and is retired after Nova acceptance.

Do not use `Eon Terminal`, `eon-term`, `terminal-host`, `bare`, `minimal`, or `Eon Workspace` as public product identities. This epic is a deferred planning container and must never be claimed for implementation.

The executable EonTerm transition issues are associated through this recorded sequence, labels, external references, and real `blocks` dependencies rather than parent-child edges. In this tracker parent-child edges are treated as prerequisites; retaining them would make children wait for an epic that may close only after those children. Closed historical relationships retain their proof history; uncompleted organizational relationships are non-blocking.

## Accepted current state

Eon has accepted activation, one canonical manifest, a Nix-only Linux alpha, Eon-owned workspace topology, managed environment, generation/lifecycle behavior, and proved EON-C12 exact-command terminal hosting, EON-C13 opacity, EON-C14 blur, EON-C16 application identity, and EON-C19 typography/initial geometry. EON-C8 workspace is Partially proved; EON-C11 generations and EON-C15 same-boot recovery are Proven on x86_64 Linux native Wayland, each only within its recorded proof and limitations. Private Eonova proved exact Eon plus Nova-no-Mars composition. `docs/CONTRACTS.md` remains authoritative for exact proof phases.

## Ownership boundary

Orbit owns generic terminal Sessions, PTYs, attachment, transport, authoritative terminal state, and any accepted graphics resource plane. Venus owns native graphical materialization, input, clipboard effects, presentation settings application, and native window identity. Eon owns product lifecycle policy, workspace topology, configuration schema, composition, diagnostics, updates, and distribution; Eon Runtime owns reusable runtime mechanisms and canonical EONW packages. EonTerm reuses the Eon lifecycle and Orbit/Venus boundary without Eon workspace or managed-tool policy. Nova owns `yzx`, branding, tools, Ratconfig integration, Zellij workspace/layout/keys, its current Rio surface, and any later migration to EonTerm. Eonova owns only temporary pins, wrapper, package, namespace, desktop metadata, and dogfood proof.

Cross-repository consumers pin exact proof commits and contract IDs. No repository copies child schemas or behavior, creates a second compatibility graph, or adds a generic terminal-provider abstraction.

## Deferred Nova transition sequence

1. `eon-4is.4` changes and proves EON-C12 under permanent `eonterm` identity while preserving full `eon`.
2. `eon-4is.5` advances temporary Eonova and proves exact EonTerm plus Nova on x86_64 Linux.
3. Venus `ven-native-clipboard-paste-uas`, `ven-lq4`, `ven-terminal-presentation-settings-5y7`, `ven-wayland-background-blur-e06`, and `ven-caller-application-identity-dcb` prove native paste, hyperlinks, presentation application, compositor blur, and caller identity at their owning boundaries.
4. Eon `eon-eonterm-presentation-e4f`, `eon-consume-venus-background-blur-k8o`, and `eon-eonterm-application-identity-xwi` publish EON-C13 opacity, EON-C14 blur and EON-C16 application identity without duplicating Venus policy.
5. Nova `yazelix-5vl-map-eonterm-presentation-0kd6` and `yazelix-5vl-eonterm-nova-identity-e8ra` consume those exact interfaces. `yazelix-5vl-eonterm-kitty-graphics-decision-totz` decides required Kitty/Yazi parity or an explicitly bounded regression.
6. Nova `yazelix-5vl-wmg` is the deferred EonTerm dogfood gate, but its pinned-Mars comparison is stale after Nova accepted minimal Rio. Before reactivation, Nova must refresh that bead against its exact current Rio surface under one predeclared functional/performance envelope and must recommend promotion.
7. `eon-4is.6` first requires a fresh user platform/consumer decision: Eon is Linux-only, and Nova's advertised systems cannot be silently narrowed. Only then can an approved target set receive exact package and native proof.
8. After successful dogfood, Nova must create and accept a Nova-owned EonTerm cutover issue. Closed `yazelix-5vl-eonterm-only-graphical-surface-q5w4` accepted Rio and is historical comparison evidence, not an EonTerm prerequisite.
9. `eon-4is.7` retires Eonova from active use after exact Nova cutover. Destructive repository disposition remains a fresh user choice.

Existing full-Eon workspace, direct/public distribution, Home Manager, editor, isolation, AgentRun, provider-attention, and extension work stays in its current owners. Public distribution is independent of a future private Nova cutover. Any consumer target mismatch remains an explicit decision, not implicit Eon portability work.

## Success Criteria

Eon stays the complete experience and EonTerm stays the small reusable terminal product. Nova may remain on Rio; any later exact-EonTerm adoption is Nova-owned and Eonova disappears from active products only after that cutover or another explicit retirement decision. The result retains one manifest, lifecycle owner, terminal authority, renderer owner, settings inventory, application identity policy per product, and no compatibility aliases or speculative provider framework.
notes: Repository-wide prime — 2026-09-17: reconciled the deferred consumer sequence with Nova's accepted Rio cutover. This is planning correction only; it does not reactivate Nova integration, retire Eonova, or change Eon's product frontier.

Every outcome child (.1, .2, .3, eon-ax4, eon-omq, eon-68v) and the sequence beads .4-.7 are closed; Eon ships as the thin orchestrator in this repository.

title: Expose an Eon single-surface terminal-host lifecycle
description:
## Why

Eon Desktop already has a native one-Orbit-socket mode in which Venus presents one terminal surface and forwards terminal input without EONW workspace shortcuts. Eon always launches Venus with the workspace socket, so an external composition cannot use that accepted child capability through an Eon-owned lifecycle. Nova inside the current workspace mode also loses its Zellij Alt navigation to Eon.

The smallest generally useful groundwork is one explicit Eon terminal-host mode. It belongs in Eon because Eon owns launch, generation, cleanup, and component selection. A private Eonova wrapper must not bypass Eon by starting Orbit and Venus itself.

## Contract routing

- Proposes additive EON-C12 because a separately released composition needs a stable Eon-owned contract. Stop before implementation until the user explicitly approves adding EON-C12 to docs/CONTRACTS.md.
- Changes and reproves EON-C1 through EON-C4 only where the canonical component graph and launch policy gain the accepted mode.
- Consumes and preserves EON-C9 managed command semantics, EON-C10 lifecycle actions and bounded unavailable-action failures, and EON-C11 generation identity, selection, attach, stop, and cleanup.
- Preserves EON-C8 workspace behavior unchanged. Terminal-host mode does not expose or mutate workspace topology.
- Current planning evidence: Eon f4303e2181ccc7ebf7a44bbe333a36e8e3d3eaaa; component manifest Orbit 64db581445bafca1a08a6530f8e44f9c1edbc169 with ORBF v1 and ORBS v2 proof 9d6d2bb37f20ab4ad9e186c7bc715eabef43e757; Venus 6ef19afddaedcbe2b9ed0996e31bc02df5d854ac with VEN-C1 proof e7bda96822274727faacb51731ae19181295e1cd and standalone-capable VEN-C3/VEN-C4 at that revision. Rebaseline all identities before implementation.

## Proposed EON-C12 observable contract

- Consumer: one local user or local composition that asks Eon to host exactly one command in one native terminal surface.
- Trigger: an explicit terminal-host invocation supplies a non-empty argv. The final CLI spelling is approved in the contract index before code; do not overload bare launch or the existing eon run meaning.
- Result: Eon selects the exact current component generation, starts or attaches one compatible terminal-host instance in the selected runtime namespace, owns exactly one Orbit Session for the supplied command, and launches Venus with the Orbit endpoint but no EONW workspace endpoint. Venus therefore sends terminal input, including Alt-h/j/k/l, Alt-m, and Ctrl-t, to Orbit rather than interpreting Eon workspace actions. Reopening the same compatible namespace attaches the existing instance instead of creating a second hidden Session. Command exit closes the terminal surface and supervisor through the existing bounded lifecycle.
- Important failures: an empty command, unsafe runtime namespace, incompatible or wrong-mode live supervisor, component mismatch, child startup failure, stale endpoint, or partial launch returns a bounded explicit error. It never attaches a workspace instance as a terminal host, mutates an EON-C8 topology, substitutes a different generation, or leaves an unsafe endpoint or newly orphaned child.
- Ownership: Eon owns mode selection, exact component set, process orchestration, generation policy, and cleanup. Orbit remains sole owner of the process, PTY, terminal state, attachment, and transport. Venus remains sole owner of native presentation and input collection. The caller owns only the command choice and runtime namespace.
- Boundary: no Nova or Zellij dependency, preset framework, configurable keymap, second workspace model, split layout, terminal parser, compatibility window, remote behavior, macOS proof, or Kitty graphics work.

## Evidence-first reference gate

Required before code:
1. Complete current AGENTS.md, docs/CONTRACTS.md, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, components/eon-alpha-v1.json, the supervisor and launcher flow, and their focused tests.
2. Exact accepted Orbit contracts and proof named by the implementation baseline.
3. Exact accepted Venus contracts and the one-socket startup/input path at the selected revision. Confirm that direct Eon shortcuts are conditional on a valid EONW snapshot and that standalone mode sends the same keys to Orbit.
4. Nova at exact comparison revision 6c7174b4efca5f139a461d204186c5001d6457bd: yzx enter, yazelix-no-mars, and fixed Zellij keybindings. This is required comparison evidence only; copy no Nova code or schema.
5. Current runtime-generation and installed Nix proof paths.

Rejected surrounding reference scope: Nova package ownership, Mars, Nova shell/configuration policy, Zellij compatibility promises, and all terminal-emulator features unrelated to input pass-through.

Record the required Execution baseline and Reference gate comments before production, test, manifest, or generated-fixture edits. No new crate or direct dependency is expected; stop for the crate gate and user approval if evidence requires one.

## Implementation shape

1. Reuse the current supervisor, generation namespace, component manifest, child-spec helpers, and lifecycle cleanup.
2. Add one explicit mode value at the existing launch owner. Do not create a second orchestrator, adapter process, or generic preset system.
3. In terminal-host mode, start one Orbit Session and invoke Venus with only that Orbit endpoint. Keep workspace actions unavailable rather than allowing invisible tabs or panes.
4. Keep the supplied command as exact argv and preserve eon run as the existing escape hatch.
5. Update the contract index first after approval, then current help, README, architecture/component documentation, changelog if user-visible, focused tests, and the README LOC scorecard.
6. Classify the slice as isolated Linux platform integration; name any newly discovered macOS blocker and stop rather than building a platform framework.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The user explicitly approves EON-C12 and the exact CLI spelling before production edits.
2. One focused deterministic test proves the terminal-host child graph contains one Orbit Session and Venus receives the Orbit endpoint without an EONW endpoint; workspace mode remains unchanged.
3. Focused lifecycle tests prove same-namespace reopen attaches the compatible terminal host, wrong-mode or wrong-generation instances are rejected explicitly, command exit closes the last surface, and partial startup cleanup leaves no new child or unsafe endpoint.
4. A focused input proof at the exact Venus revision demonstrates Alt-h/j/k/l, Alt-m, and Ctrl-t reach the Orbit Session in terminal-host mode and do not invoke EON-C8 actions.
5. The canonical manifest, versions output, runtime identity, and Nix composition remain one exact component graph with no new dependency or duplicate schema.
6. Locked Rust format, check, tests, Clippy, exact Nix build/check, manifest validation, README LOC check, and git diff --check pass.
7. Installed x86_64 Linux dogfood launches Zellij or an equivalent key-reporting command, exercises the conflicting keys, closes and reopens the terminal host, and records the exact package, revisions, environment, and result.
8. docs/CONTRACTS.md records the exact proof-bearing commit only after all canonical checks and dogfood pass.

## Out of scope and stop conditions

Out of scope: creating Eonova, changing Nova, publishing a repository, remapping Zellij, a named preset or profile system, multiple simultaneous terminal-host Sessions, distinct application identity, desktop integration, Kitty graphics, general configuration, macOS implementation, and public compatibility promises.

Stop if standalone Venus requires an unproved Orbit or Venus contract, if lifecycle reuse would duplicate EON-C10/EON-C11 ownership, if invisible workspace mutation is required, if a new dependency or protocol change is needed without its gate and approval, or if the chosen CLI would change bare launch or eon run semantics.
close_reason: Proven and published: Eon owns optional terminal-host decorations, Eonova requests no decorations, installed native dogfood shows no title bar, and both profiles resolve the accepted artifacts.

comments.text:
Reference gate

Question:
What is the smallest Eon-owned way to host one exact command in Venus without EONW workspace shortcuts, while preserving authoritative generation, attach, stop, and cleanup behavior?

Contracts:
Add EON-C12; change and reprove EON-C1 through EON-C4 for the additional launch mode; consume and preserve EON-C9, EON-C10, and EON-C11; preserve EON-C8 unchanged.

Sources and exact revisions:
- Eon 178c0d247a2bf8fcbcb7ebd5ac978fb2a5546254: complete AGENTS.md, docs/REFERENCES.md, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, docs/CONTRACTS.md, components/eon-alpha-v1.json, crates/eon/src/main.rs, crates/eon/tests/workspace_control.rs, crates/eon-manifest, flake.nix, and flake.lock.
- Orbit source 64db581445bafca1a08a6530f8e44f9c1edbc169 and its complete AGENTS.md, contracts, and reference map. Consumed ORB-C1 through ORB-C9, ORBF v1, and ORBS v2 proof 9d6d2bb37f20ab4ad9e186c7bc715eabef43e757 plus ORB-C10 proof 292b2451c9a1d99390334771a681c7f481c996f2 are sufficient. No Orbit contract gap exists.
- Venus published source 690b038e2b58a0e7761023ac7e004e92327ac901, complete current contracts/reference route, and exact src/main.rs. socket_arguments accepts ORBIT_SOCKET with an optional EON_WORKSPACE_SOCKET; create_window starts direct Orbit transport when the workspace socket is absent; handle_workspace_key returns false until an authoritative workspace snapshot exists; workspace_shortcut owns the six Eon bindings only in workspace mode. VEN-C8 proof 33a3d9af9f4c6015301ad6829fe733413c5b683d records exact standalone pass-through bytes. VEN-C3 and VEN-C4 runtime proof remains 6ef19afddaedcbe2b9ed0996e31bc02df5d854ac; 690b038 changes only their authoritative contract record.
- Nova 6c7174b4efca5f139a461d204186c5001d6457bd, comparison only: runtime/yzx/cli.rs launches Zellij directly through yzx enter; flake.nix exposes yazelix-no-mars and proves it excludes Mars; defaults/zellij/config.kdl retains its own Ctrl-t, Alt-m, horizontal Alt navigation, default vertical navigation, and move bindings. Nova remains Apache-2.0 and independent.
- Installed Eon candidate baseline: /nix/store/dirnp4ri16smqcr2vd00wkp454b27kcg-eon-0.1.0, generation g1-b7dd7734e2788946626f05700421056e, with three live current-generation Sessions and one live legacy workspace. These must survive profile refresh.

Constraints preserved:
- Eon remains the only composition, launch-mode, generation, and cleanup owner.
- Orbit remains the sole process, PTY, Session, terminal-state, attachment, and transport owner.
- Venus remains transient and owns native presentation/input only.
- EONW remains the authoritative control and lifecycle boundary; Venus need not receive its endpoint.
- Bare eon and eon run retain their current workspace meanings.
- One runtime namespace and generation has at most one live supervisor and one mode. A wrong-mode launch is rejected explicitly.
- Terminal-host mode has no Workspace value and cannot create an invisible tab or pane.
- The exact child argv remains unmanaged and non-empty.

Decision and code shape:
- Add one small LaunchMode value at the existing runtime owner.
- Reuse the current supervisor and mode-0600 EONW control listener for InspectRuntime and Stop in both modes.
- In terminal mode hold no Workspace and return the structured workspace-unavailable failure for any EON-C8 request. A mode probe uses that owner-authored response or a normal snapshot; no marker file, state inference, protocol field, schema fork, or compatibility window is added.
- Centralize Venus argv construction once: workspace mode passes Orbit plus EONW; terminal mode passes only Orbit. Startup, reopen, concurrent-launch recovery, and explicit attach consume the same mode decision.
- Advance the Venus source pin from 6ef19af to published 690b038 so Eon is not stale. Record that this is contract-proof metadata only; retain the exact VEN-C3/VEN-C4 runtime proof at 6ef19af and make no new Venus behavior claim.
- No direct dependency, crate feature, service, daemon, or implementation language changes. No crate gate is required. Nova inspection is comparison-only and no source is copied. The already accepted Orbit/Venus Nix consumption boundary and user-directed Apache-2.0 licensing are unchanged by this slice.

Rejected alternatives and failure conditions:
- Starting Orbit and Venus in an Eonova wrapper: duplicates Eon lifecycle ownership.
- Launching workspace Venus and remapping or forwarding shortcuts: keeps hidden workspace behavior and creates keymap policy.
- An invisible one-pane Workspace in terminal mode: violates the no-topology contract.
- A mode marker file or pathname inference: violates EON-C11 fresh owner authority.
- A new EONW mode field or version: unnecessary protocol and consumer change.
- Separate terminal generation trees, a preset framework, multiple terminal-host Sessions, Nova/Zellij changes, Kitty graphics, distinct app identity, remote behavior, and macOS implementation: outside scope.

First contract checks:
1. A focused unit check proves the one Venus command owner emits two endpoints for workspace mode and only Orbit for terminal mode.
