title: Let eon commands target the calling pane by default
description:
## Why
Workspace commands act on the active tab or selected column (`eon pane create` "creates a pane in
the active tab's selected column", docs/USAGE.md:218; `pane close PANE` targets "a pane of the
active tab"). An agent running in a background tab therefore changes the tab the user is looking at.
tmux (`TMUX_PANE`), WezTerm (`WEZTERM_PANE`, `wezterm cli --pane-id`), kitty (`KITTY_WINDOW_ID`,
`--match`) and Rex (`REX_SESSION`/`REX_BLOCK`, ambiguous targets change nothing) let the CLI target
its caller. See the parent epic for context.

## Evidence (edge 38cb1ea)
- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/managed_environment.rs:660-725`: the runtime builds each
  terminal's environment (`EON_CONFIG_HOME`, `EON_SHELL_*`) but exports no tab, pane or terminal
  identity.
- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/cli.rs:646-660`: `pane create` maps to
  `WorkspaceAction::CreatePane` with no target; `tab move`, `pane move` act on the active selection.
- `runtime/crates/eon-workspace-protocol/src/{v2,v3,v11}.rs`: identity-naming actions include `ClosePane`, `CloseTab`,
  `FocusId` and `SetTabDirectory`; `CreatePane` and the moves name none.
- EON-C10 target safety (docs/CONTRACTS.md:674-681): the runtime validates targets against its
  current Snapshot; identities are not reused after recovery.

## Contract (provisional, needs Lucca's approval before code)
- Consumer: a command run inside an Eon terminal (agent, script, editor).
- Trigger: a workspace command without an explicit target, run from an Eon terminal.
- Result: it acts on the caller's own tab/pane (resolved from an immutable terminal identity the
  runtime exports at spawn), not the active one; an explicit target overrides; outside Eon,
  behavior is unchanged. Focus is not stolen unless the command is `focus`.
- Important failures: ended or older-generation caller identity, closed caller pane, or ambiguous
  target change nothing and return the "target missing" status from the sibling exit-code child.
- Owner: Eon Runtime (identity export, resolution, validation); EONW carries any new target field
  under its versioning rules; Orbit and Venus unchanged.

## Reference gate (consequential: environment contract, likely EONW change)
Read docs/REFERENCES.md routes and inspect at exact revisions: tmux `TMUX_PANE` and `-t` resolution,
WezTerm `WEZTERM_PANE`/`cli --pane-id`, kitty `KITTY_WINDOW_ID` and `--match`. Record adopted and
rejected shapes (e.g. exporting mutable tab IDs vs the immutable terminal identity), the EONW
classification, and the cheapest falsifying check before code.

## Scope
In: terminal environment export, CLI target resolution and an explicit target flag, EONW target
fields if required, EON-C10 text after approval, USAGE/help, CHANGELOG.md.
Out: sending input or reading screens (`eon-agent-terminal-control-n8ic`, `orb-p92`), discovery
and wait (`eon-cli-action-discovery-ogzi`), popups' own targeting rules, Venus.

## Acceptance
- From a pane in an inactive tab, `eon pane create --json` adds a pane to that tab and leaves the
  active tab and desktop focus unchanged; from outside Eon it behaves as today.
- A stale identity (closed pane, stopped generation) changes nothing and exits with the documented
  target-missing status.
- Full affected Rust and Nix surfaces plus one isolated installed dogfood observation; converge
  review loop; ledger line here.

## Stop conditions
- Stop for Lucca's design and contract approval before code.
- Stop if the change would require exporting mutable identities or a Nix store path.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Reference gate (edge b18f2cd). Contract proposal follows; needs Lucca's approval before code.

Behavior owners: Eon Runtime owns the identity export (sessions.rs orbit_command), the caller resolution and its validation (workspace.rs dispatch, today hard-wired to `self.active` and the selected column/pane), and the CLI projection (cli.rs parse_control_arguments, control.rs failure_status). EONW owns the request field. Orbit and Venus are unchanged; Venus sends no caller.

Routes read: docs/REFERENCES.md has no CLI-targeting route; the "agent-readable actions" route (TUIOS 0047c409185f) applies only as "one registry, stable errors". Read EON-C10, EON-C28, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md EONW boundary, runtime/AGENTS.md.

Comparables (read at these revisions):
- tmux 6f655f487338c0a49a3ec2052e559f73f4419c8a: TMUX_PANE=%N from a never-reused counter (spawn.c:415, window.c:61,1474) that follows the pane through join/break-pane. With no -t, a command from inside a pane uses TMUX_PANE only to pick the session, then targets that session's current window and active pane (cmd-find.c:913-928); a gone pane falls back silently (932-935). TMUX_PANE is not checked against the server.
- WezTerm e2a98e1b8af156988ad0ac778658ac27b60a55fb: WEZTERM_PANE at spawn (mux/src/domain.rs:479-482), monotonic IDs (mux/src/pane.rs:24-28), the mux server strips it from its own environment (wezterm-mux-server/src/main.rs:190-201). resolve_pane_id: --pane-id, else WEZTERM_PANE, else the focused pane (wezterm-client/src/client.rs:1314-1339). split-pane splits the caller's pane; a gone pane is an error ("no such pane"). spawn quietly opens a new window when the caller is unknown (lib.rs:1334-1352).
- kitty cda133cd26a573474d7cf2eb3cf04dd9684aafb0: KITTY_WINDOW_ID (tabs.py:858). The default depends on the command: those with a --self option default to the active window, the rest to the caller (rc/base.py:366-410); a stale ID falls back to the active window.

Kept: a pane-level (terminal-level) identity that is never reused and follows its terminal, resolved to a tab at request time; the server strips the variable from its own environment; a present but stale caller is an error, never a fallback (WezTerm split-pane).
Rejected:
- Exporting tab or pane IDs. Tab membership is mutable, and pane IDs are renumbered on same-boot supervisor replacement (workspace.rs with_recovered_sessions: p{session number}), so a pane ID can name a different pane later.
- Kernel-attested identity (tmux tty match, kitty tty transport). The runtime does not know PTY devices: Orbit owns them. This would need an Orbit management field plus Linux /proc lookups (AP-PORTABILITY-001), for a same-user tool that has no trust boundary to defend.
- tmux's session-only use, kitty's per-command split, and every silent fallback.

Identity: Orbit session ID plus Orbit run ID (supervisor request_id(): pid-nanos-seq, sessions.rs:809), already in the management record. It is unique across generations, windows and fresh supervisors in the same generation, and it survives same-boot replacement, which keeps exact Orbit runs. So no generation or window field is needed: a foreign caller simply names no live terminal of the supervisor addressed. Windows already route through the inherited EON_WINDOW_RUNTIME_DIR.

EONW: every frame carries exactly v12 (v12.rs:1451-1453), with no negotiation. An optional caller on the request needs v13, and Venus moves with it in the same commit. Cost: the new eon cannot list or stop v12 generations, the same accepted cost as eon-igae.12.4. Only Lucca's own sessions run v12 (v0.1.1 ships an older version anyway), and EON-C28's lifecycle-codec promise binds only from 1.0.

Cheapest falsifiers: a Runtime unit test (caller in an inactive tab: pane create lands there and the active tab is unchanged; a stale caller changes nothing), an eon workspace_control integration test through the CLI with EON_TERMINAL set, and one isolated installed dogfood from a background tab.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Lucca, 2026-10-21: approved the proposed contract with all three recommendations. (1) Every Eon terminal carries opaque EON_TERMINAL (Orbit session plus run identity); the supervisor strips it from its own environment. With it set, pane create, pane move, tab move and pane close PANE act on the caller's tab (pane create in the caller's column; moves move the caller's own pane or tab; pane close resolves PANE in the caller's tab); a popup caller resolves to its tab and that tab's selected column and pane. Within that tab each action behaves as today (pane create selects the new pane and dismisses that tab's popup); the active tab and desktop focus never change. workspace, tab create, tab close, tab directory and focus are unchanged, as is everything outside Eon terminals. A caller naming no live terminal of the addressed supervisor changes nothing and exits 3 (unknown-caller), with no fallback. (2) No explicit target flag in this slice (additive, 1.x); env -u EON_TERMINAL restores active-tab behavior. (3) EONW v13 adds an optional bounded caller to requests; Venus sends none; the new eon cannot list or stop v12 generations, so Lucca stops his v12 generations with the current eon before the profile refresh.

title: Stop shipping Zsh and Fish as Eon managed shells
description:
## Why

User decision (Lucca, 2026-10-18): "we should not ship zsh and fish, makes no sense". Eon's managed environment (EON-C9) ships four shells. Zsh and Fish add maintenance, test and closure weight for little product value: Nushell is the default (`command = ["eon-nu"]`) and Bash covers the POSIX case. Users who want Zsh or Fish can still run their host shell as the direct argv command.

The bundle redesign (eon-zti4, decision record on eon-zti4.1) found a concrete cost. Fish pulls python3 (134 MB), coreutils, man-db, groff, gettext and util-linux into the closure, and Zsh links ncurses 6.6. Both raise the host glibc floor of the namespace-free bundle to GLIBC_2.42. Dropping them shrinks the payload and leaves ncurses 6.6 (libncursesw and tset, used by bash-interactive, readline and bc) as the only GLIBC_2.42 objects, so the later floor-2.39 work becomes an ncurses fix.

This decision authorizes removing Zsh and Fish from EON-C9's managed shell list. Any other EON-C9 change still needs separate approval.

## Evidence

- `components/eon-alpha-v3.json:10` lists `zsh` and `fish` in `tools`; their component entries start at :195 and :212.
- `flake.nix:130-131` (identities), `:317-321` (packages), `:336-344` (shell environment inputs), `:350-351` and `:479-480` (licences), `:456-463` (session command farm), `:500-510` (EON_ZSH, EON_FISH, EON_ZSH_CONFIG, EON_FISH_INIT wrapper env), `:562` (eonbase closure forbidden list) and `:572-579` (managed-command check).
- `nix/shell-environment.nix:3-54` (per-shell init generation), `:163-229` (zsh env/rc, ZDOTDIR config and its build check), plus the fish init.
- `eon/crates/eon/src/product.rs:115-124`: the `EON_ZSH`, `EON_FISH`, `EON_ZSH_CONFIG` and `EON_FISH_INIT` inputs.
- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/managed_environment.rs` (38 matches), `sessions.rs` (2) and `fixtures.rs` (4): managed shell selection and its tests.
- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/managed_environment.rs:214-215` maps bare `zsh`/`fish` to managed tools today; `managed_invocation_names_are_bounded` (:1315-1326) covers that mapping.
- `docs/REFERENCES.md:277-285` names Zsh and Fish as references.
- `docs/CONTRACTS.md:553-589` (EON-C9 consumer, result and proof mention Zsh and Fish); `docs/CONFIGURATION.md:134` (`eon-zsh`, `eon-fish`).

## Scope

In scope:
- Remove Zsh and Fish from the component manifest, the Nix composition (packages, licences, wrapper env, session commands `eon-zsh`, `eon-fish`, `zsh`, `fish`, the shell-init and config generation and their checks), the Eon product inputs, the runtime's managed-shell handling and its tests and fixtures.
- Bare `zsh`/`fish` stop mapping to managed tools (managed_environment.rs:214-215).
- Trim docs/REFERENCES.md:277-285 to what still applies to Nushell and Bash.
- Update EON-C9 to Nushell and Bash only, with the proof note that names the removed shells; also docs/CONFIGURATION.md and README if it lists them, and a CHANGELOG entry (user-visible: commands and packaged tools removed).

Out of scope:
- Nushell, Bash, Starship, Zoxide, Atuin, Carapace, Helix, Yazi and LazyGit behavior, and any other EON-C9 semantics.
- The bundle mechanism (eon-zti4 children), Orbit and Venus.
- A compatibility shim or migration for configs that name `eon-zsh` or `eon-fish`; they take EON-C9's existing explicit shell-launch failure path.

## Acceptance

- `eon versions` and the component manifest no longer list zsh or fish, and the eon closure contains no zsh or fish store paths (`nix path-info -r` of `.#default` has no `-zsh-` or `-fish-` entries).
- `eon-zsh`, `eon-fish` and the unprefixed `zsh`/`fish` managed commands no longer exist. A config with `command = ["eon-zsh"]` fails explicitly without a replacement terminal, as EON-C9 already specifies for a missing artifact; a host shell given as the direct command (for example `["zsh"]` from the host PATH) still launches as an unmanaged command.
- Nushell and Bash managed shells keep their EON-C9 behavior: Starship, Zoxide, Atuin and Carapace integration, and native user configuration loading.
- EON-C9 and docs describe exactly two managed shells.

## Implementation Notes

1. Start from the manifest and `flake.nix`; let manifest validation and the Nix build show every remaining consumer.
2. Remove the runtime and product handling, then the tests that only exercised Zsh or Fish; keep the Nushell and Bash coverage.
3. Edit EON-C9 (docs/CONTRACTS.md:550-600) to the two-shell set, plus CONFIGURATION, README and CHANGELOG.

## Verification

- `managed_invocation_names_are_bounded` asserts `None` for `zsh` and `fish`, so a host shell given as the direct command runs unmanaged.
- `nix develop -c eon-test` exits 0 (workspace and installer suites; never run inside a live Eon session's environment without that sandbox).
- `nix build .#default` and `nix flake check` exit 0; `nix path-info -r` of the result has no zsh or fish paths.
- Refresh the active `eon` profile element from the working tree and check that it resolves to the new store path. In one isolated installed dogfood observation, `eon versions` shows no zsh or fish, `eon-bash` and `eon-nu` start with their integrations, and a config naming `eon-zsh` fails explicitly. Do not restart the running supervisor; report that a restart is needed.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if removal requires changing EON-C9 semantics beyond dropping the two shells.
- Stop if another component or contract depends on Zsh or Fish (for example a Carapace, Atuin or Helix integration that needs them).
- Stop if verification fails twice for the same reason after a reasonable fix attempt.

## Maintenance Notes

- Rejected: keeping Zsh and Fish as optional managed shells. The user decided they should not ship at all.
- Effect on eon-zti4: the namespace-free bundle's GLIBC_2.42 floor then comes only from Bash (ncurses 6.6), so the floor-2.39 work becomes an ncurses fix. Record this on eon-zti4.1 when this bead lands.
close_reason: Zsh and Fish removed from the managed shell set; proof and review ledger in comments

title: Decide: pane labels that say what runs in the pane
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-10-24, asked the overseer "what do you think of our pane naming protocol", and on its
proposal: "your plan is good". Today each pane label is `pN`, two spaces, and a compact working
directory (EON-C8). In his screenshots every pane in a tab shows the same directory as the tab
(`~/pjs/games/machines_vs_aliens` four times), nothing says what runs in each pane, and workspace-
wide IDs grow (`p14 p15 p16` in a three-pane tab).

## Proposal to research (nothing decided)

- Keep `pN` (the ID agents use with `eon focus`, `eon pane close`) but dim it: the same label, the
  ID drawn in a lower-contrast colour than the rest, so the eye lands on the name.
- Then the terminal title the program sets (OSC 0/2; Claude Code sets its session name), falling
  back to the foreground command name.
- The working directory only when it differs from the tab's directory, written relative to it.
- `eon pane rename pN "<name>"` (and the matching window action) to pin a name; CLI parity per
  AGENTS.md "Humans and Agents".
- Examples: `p14  claude · eon-6ros review`, `p15  hx src/main.rs`, `p16  ../other-repo · cargo test`.

## Research path (overseer runs it, Lucca decides)

1. What Orbit already gives Eon for collapsed (unattached) panes: the metadata reply (working
   directory today), and whether the terminal title (ORB-C15, already on EONW v19 as
   attention.name) and the foreground command are available without attaching; contracts that
   would change (EON-C8 label clause, ORB-C metadata, EONW).
2. References at exact revisions: Zellij pane names and frames, tmux pane titles and
   automatic-rename, WezTerm/kitty tab and pane titles (local clones in ~/pjs/refs).
3. Mockups of 2-3 label styles over a real capture of a stacked tab.
4. Recommendation and contract wording for Lucca.

## Scope

Pane label content and the rename path. Out: tab labels, sidebar rows (they already use the
title), protocol work beyond what the chosen style needs.

Portability: neutral.
close_reason: Decided: PINNED labels without the process fallback; implemented by eon-a7xd

title: Prove every EONW v2 request action
description:
## Contract Routing

This hardens the existing EON-C10 EONW v2 compatibility proof. It must not add an action, change a wire tag or field encoding, widen accepted input, or create a new protocol version.

Consumer: an EONW v2 client or legacy Eon supervisor.

Trigger: the client encodes or decodes any request action supported by EONW v2.

Result: every supported action has independently checked canonical bytes and decodes to the same typed request; incompatible versions, unknown tags, malformed presentation values, invalid identities/directories, and trailing payload remain rejected.

## Why

The 2026-08-28 coverage-aware audit found the largest actionable CRAP score in the repository here: `decode_request` has cyclomatic complexity 33, cognitive complexity 4, 37.21% line coverage, and CRAP 302.60. `encode_request` has cyclomatic complexity 19, cognitive complexity 1, 38.24% coverage, and CRAP 104.06. The low cognitive scores show exhaustive wire matching rather than a design problem; the missing proof is the issue.

Impact HIGH, effort S, implementation risk LOW, confidence HIGH.

## Evidence

- `crates/eon-workspace-protocol/src/v2.rs:169`: `encode_request` owns tags 0 through 12 for all v2 request actions.
- `crates/eon-workspace-protocol/src/v2.rs:208`: `decode_request` mirrors those tags and validates field-specific payloads.
- `crates/eon-workspace-protocol/src/v2.rs:811`: the only v2 request round-trip exercises `SetTabDirectory`; most action arms are uncovered.
- `crates/eon-workspace-protocol/src/v3.rs:306`: v3 already has a compact all-action corpus that demonstrates the repository pattern.
- `docs/CONTRACTS.md:311`: EON-C10 names EONW v2 codec/version rejection as accepted evidence.

## Scope

In scope:
- `crates/eon-workspace-protocol/src/v2.rs` tests.
- One compact golden request corpus covering every v2 action and both valid presentation values.
- Focused malformed-request cases needed to exercise v2-specific rejection branches.
- A before/after cargo-crap observation using cargo-crap 0.4.3 and the same LCOV workload.

Out of scope:
- Production codec refactoring merely to reduce a metric.
- EONW v3/v4 behavior, new actions, protocol negotiation, compatibility adapters, dependencies, CI thresholds, or contract-status changes.
- Tests that only mirror implementation trivia without independently constraining the wire contract.

## Implementation Notes

1. Re-read the v2 action enum, frame helpers, EON-C10, and the existing v3 corpus at the implementation revision.
2. Add one data-driven golden corpus that constrains canonical bytes as well as typed decode; paired round trips alone cannot detect matching encoder/decoder tag swaps.
3. Cover unknown action tag, invalid presentation byte, incompatible version, and trailing payload only where the current v2 suite does not already prove them.
4. Leave production code unchanged unless the golden contract exposes a real defect. If it does, stop and record the exact mismatch before changing accepted wire behavior.
5. Rerun the identical coverage-aware report and record the score change as diagnostic evidence, not a repository quality gate.

## Verification

- `cargo test --locked -p eon-workspace-protocol` should exit 0 and prove the complete v2 golden corpus and existing v3/v4 compatibility checks.
- `cargo clippy --locked -p eon-workspace-protocol --all-targets -- -D warnings` should exit 0.
- `cargo llvm-cov --workspace --all-features --lcov --output-path /tmp/eon-quality.lcov` should exit 0 and emit the shared LCOV workload.
- `cargo-crap --workspace --lcov /tmp/eon-quality.lcov --format json --output /tmp/eon-crap.json` with cargo-crap 0.4.3 should report materially higher v2 request coverage without source/LCOV mismatch diagnostics.
- `git diff --check` should exit 0.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if current EON-C10 evidence or an accepted downstream v2 consumer disagrees with the encoded bytes.
- Stop before changing a production wire tag, accepted field, version, frame bound, or downstream consumer.
- Stop before adding a dependency, generated corpus, broad test abstraction, or CI threshold.

## Maintenance Notes

Prefer exhaustive data over helper layers. The CRAP result is a prioritization signal, not an architectural requirement; do not split the two wire matches solely to lower cyclomatic complexity.

## Acceptance Criteria

- One compact corpus independently constrains the canonical v2 request bytes and typed decode for every action tag 0 through 12, including every direction and both valid presentation values.
- Focused cases retain rejection of incompatible versions, unknown action tags, invalid presentation bytes, invalid bounded fields, and trailing payload without duplicating equivalent existing proof.
- The v2 codec package tests and Clippy pass. Production codec bytes and EON-C10 behavior remain unchanged unless a separately scoped confirmed defect is recorded.
- The repeated cargo-crap 0.4.3 report records higher coverage for both v2 request functions and no source/LCOV mismatch; it creates no threshold or CI policy.
- No dependency, generated fixture system, compatibility adapter, or EONW v3/v4 change is introduced.

title: Reopen Eon across last-Session exit
description:
## Contract

For a local Linux native-Wayland user, invoking Open Eon after the last Session exits converges on one fresh current-generation supervisor, Orbit Session, and Venus surface. A launch overlapping supervisor teardown waits for exact generation ownership. Before Eon forks any new Orbit process, Eon waits within the existing five-second Session-start deadline until Eon itself occupies a validated user-owned cgroup-v2 directory suitable for Orbit to inherit. Existing live Session recovery does not wait or restart anything.

The launch-readiness policy is independent of compositor, init, and service-manager APIs. Orbit remains the enforcement owner for Session containment. A system without systemd is supported by the implementation when its Linux environment provides Orbit’s existing documented delegated cgroup-v2 capability; non-systemd installed proof remains pending under EON-C7.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Close the Eon presentation, reopen the existing Session, and exit the last Session.
2. Invoke Open Eon through a launcher that starts Eon in a non-delegated login cgroup and relocates only Eon asynchronously.
3. Observe Eon fork Orbit before relocation; Orbit inherits the root-owned cgroup, fails ORB-C12 before Ready, and no surface opens.

## Prerequisites

EON-C11 runtime-generation and presentation ownership; EON-C15 exact same-boot Orbit recovery; ORB-C12 containment; current accepted Orbit and Venus pins.

## Acceptance Criteria

A focused red/green regression proves cgroup readiness is retried before the Orbit spawn boundary and fails boundedly if readiness never arrives. Existing generation-overlap regression remains green. Locked Eon Rust checks, governance, manifest validation, and affected Nix build pass. The refreshed installed profile preserves live Sessions and an ordinary Open Eon launch proves a fresh Orbit inherits Eon’s exact validated cgroup before creating its per-Session containment.

## Scope Boundary

Eon’s existing Orbit lifecycle adapter and current-generation supervisor lifecycle only. No systemd, D-Bus, compositor detection, launcher wrapper, daemon, new dependency, timeout expansion, relaxed Orbit checks, PID inference, automatic cleanup of unverified state, child-project edit, unrelated generation change, or claim that non-systemd dogfood has occurred.

comments.text:
Reference gate (shutdown/reopen overlap):
Question: How does an attach-capable launch distinguish a retiring generation from a reusable live owner without overlapping teardown?
Contract: EON-C11; launching the current generation during its clean last-Session exit must wait for that generation to finish and then start fresh. Other generations remain independently attachable.
Sources and revisions: TUIOS 0047c409185f37e568933a566e0253b2a6e96a96 docs/SESSIONS.md, internal/session/daemon.go, daemon_startlock.go, daemon_shutdown_test.go; Ghostty d760ee96e54657416eb427b793c7e839f003df7d src/apprt/gtk/class/application.zig and Config.zig; Rio/Canario 3e41b8b19a1cad9cd9bdfc8f7900cf61ce5a9098 CanarioApp.swift, AppModel.swift, SessionStore.swift; Herdr 3c7327c267a352023797c8a13fd0b7f4a7a40591 server/autodetect.rs, ipc.rs, api/server.rs, server/headless.rs; Linux unix(7)/accept(2) and Rust UnixListener documentation inspected 2026-08-23.
Constraints preserved: one owner per generation; live detach remains attachable; clean owner exit means fresh Session; socket-path removal is identity-checked; independent generations must not serialize each other; no systemd dependency.
Options compared: native application uniqueness; reconstruction-only app lifecycle; socket probe plus stale cleanup; root-wide startup lock; per-generation lifetime lock.
Decision: retain one stable per-generation lock for the supervisor lifetime, close/unlink its listener and finish runtime cleanup before releasing it, then let a waiting launch re-probe and start. Never unlink the lock file because replacing its inode defeats advisory-lock serialization.
Rejected: GTK/macOS native uniqueness does not own Eon's multi-generation process lifecycle; Canario restores fresh shells rather than process continuity; Herdr's socket-only check-then-spawn remains vulnerable to the demonstrated overlap; a root-wide lifetime lock blocks valid cross-generation use; intermittent startup/shutdown locking allowed queued connections to outlive the proof; sleeps, systemd scopes, and socket deletion without ownership are not lifecycle truth.
Cheapest proof: existing launch_overlapping_last_session_exit_starts_a_fresh_session regression plus exact installed isolated overlap dogfood.
Exit condition: the replacement remains blocked while the retiring owner holds the generation lock, then starts one fresh Session after teardown.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Reference-driven implementation candidate — 2026-08-23 America/Sao_Paulo

Shape: each exact generation owns one stable advisory lock outside its removable runtime directory. The winning supervisor retains that file descriptor from endpoint recovery through common listener, Venus, and runtime cleanup. A missing endpoint uses nonblocking lock attempts so concurrent starters keep probing and attach when the winner becomes ready; an unresponsive endpoint waits a bounded six seconds for the retiring owner to release the lock. Dead-generation cleanup uses the same per-generation lock. Lock files are not unlinked, preserving inode identity. No systemd, launcher wrapper, daemon, dependency, child change, or cross-generation serialization was added.

Reference result: TUIOS supplied the applicable lifetime-lock and teardown ordering. Ghostty delegates single-instance ownership to GTK/GApplication and uses systemd only as optional child resource isolation. Rio/Canario delegates application lifecycle to macOS and reconstructs metadata with fresh shells. Herdr's identity-checked socket removal is useful, but its socket-only check-then-spawn path does not serialize this overlap and was rejected for Eon.

Regression proof: launch_overlapping_last_session_exit_starts_a_fresh_session now also asserts the generation lock remains contended during steady state; it freezes the old owner, ends the last Session, overlaps a replacement, resumes teardown, and observes exactly one fresh Orbit. concurrent_launches_converge_and_generation_stop_is_owner_routed guards startup contention. Both focused checks pass.

Mechanical proof on the unchanged candidate: cargo fmt --all -- --check; cargo test --locked --workspace (46 passed); cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings; canonical manifest validation; complete nix flake check --no-update-lock-file path:. including exact Eon/EonTerm builds, managed command path, and EonTerm closure. title: Retire Eon's dependency forks (accesskit, winit 0.30, libghostty-rs)
description:
## Why

Lucca asked on 2026-10-21 to get rid of Eon's dependency forks by whatever route fits each one: accept the upstream bug, land upstream PRs, or another way. Each fork is a second owner of upstream code, a Git pin outside crates.io, and extra work on every bump.

## Contract

No new contract. The consumer is Eon's build: every fork in `Cargo.toml` `[patch.crates-io]` or in a Git dependency has a recorded disposition, and is removed once its exit condition holds.

## The forks

1. **Yazelix/accesskit `0f9d186`**, based on upstream `c88605b`.
   - What it fixes: the Linux AT-SPI cache adapter's shared signal helper. The fork wraps each cache structure as one D-Bus argument, which keeps libatspi's cache contract.
   - It pins four crates together: `accesskit`, `accesskit_consumer`, `accesskit_atspi_common` and `accesskit_unix`.
   - Where it is recorded: `Cargo.toml`, `venus/docs/CRATES.md` (AccessKit section) and `venus/docs/REFERENCES.md:373`.
   - Its proof: Venus's one wire regression, which checks the encoded signal headers and values.
2. **Yazelix/winit-0.30 `7c209ec`**: winit v0.30.13 plus a backport of upstream `c4afadbf`.
   - What it adds: Venus prefers `ext-background-effect-v1` for compositor blur and keeps the KDE fallback.
   - Where it is recorded: `Cargo.toml`, `venus/docs/CRATES.md` (Native host section) and `venus/docs/REFERENCES.md:729`.
   - Its exit is already written down: the first accepted stable winit that contains the fix.
3. **Yazelix/libghostty-rs**, arriving with `eon-a9tr.2`: upstream master `0ef8041` plus 4 commits.
   - What it adds: Ghostty 8c425a7 and Zig 0.17, plus the program-status and semantic-prompt wrappers.
   - Its exit condition is in `eon-a9tr.1`.
   - The reviewed series is in `~/pjs/refs/agent-sidebar-research/a9tr1-libghostty-rs-series`.
   - libghostty-rs does not let agents open PRs, so Lucca opens that one.

## Acceptance

- For each fork, Lucca chooses one disposition, recorded here with its evidence:
  - an upstream PR, with its link and status;
  - an accepted upstream bug, with the user-visible consequence named;
  - or keep the fork, with its exit condition and a date to look again.
- A fork whose fix has reached an upstream release is replaced by that exact release. The proof is the owning check: Venus's AT-SPI wire regression and an installed Orca observation for accesskit, an installed blur observation for winit, and the Orbit suites plus the real-PTY checks for libghostty-rs.
- Afterwards, `[patch.crates-io]` and the Git dependencies hold only forks that have a recorded reason.

## Scope boundary

- In scope: Eon's dependency forks.
- Out of scope:
  - Yazelix-owned inputs that are products rather than dependency patches: nova-helix, anima, kinestra and ratconfig. Include them only if Lucca adds them.
  - New forks.
  - Releases.
- Outward-facing steps need Lucca: opening PRs and creating or deleting fork repositories.

## Notes

This is too big for one session. When work starts, split it into one child bead per fork; the forks are independent. The libghostty-rs part waits for `eon-a9tr.2`.

title: Label panes with a pinned name, the program title or the directory, and rename them from the CLI
description:
## Why

eon-8rdi decision (Lucca, 2026-10-24: "ok, the pane labels are fine"): pane labels say what runs
in the pane. Research and mockups: ~/.cache/eon-agents/8rdi/research/ (frame PINNED,
mock/png/labels-zoom.png; recommendation.md has the ownership split, trust bounds and contrast
numbers).

## Behaviour

- Label = `pN` (drawn slightly dimmer than the name, contrast >= 4.5:1 over the resolved card
  fill at the configured opacity) + two spaces + name, where name = the pinned name if set, else
  the program's terminal title (sanitized as Orbit already sanitizes management titles, bounded),
  else the compact working directory, else nothing; plus ` · <directory>` context when the
  terminal's directory differs from the tab's launch directory (lexical, relative: `subdir`,
  `../other-repo`, or the compact path when shorter). States offline/connecting/unavailable stay.
- `eon pane rename pN NAME` sets the pin; `eon pane rename pN --clear` (exact flag in the
  contract) clears it; a matching window action. Pins live in the Runtime workspace state.
- Runtime composes the label (one owner) and sends it on EONW; Venus draws it (ID styled by the
  known `pN  ` prefix), fits it as today, and exposes the full label to AccessKit; `eon workspace
  --json` includes each pane's label and pin.
- Ships in the same next EONW version as eon-workspace-switching-shn4.3 (one bump, one window
  restart).

## Contract

EON-C8 pane-label bullet, EON-C10 (CLI), EON-C28 if fields freeze, VEN-C8, the EONW revision.
Exact wording to Lucca before code. Reference gate: consequential (wire change).

## Prerequisites

eon-workspace-switching-shn4.3 (same EONW revision; implement together or immediately after in
the same unreleased EONW version).

## Acceptance

- Runtime tests: precedence (pin > title > directory), context rules, sanitizing and bounds,
  rename set/clear over CLI and JSON.
- Venus test: dimmed ID colour and contrast, fitting keeps the ID, AccessKit name.
- Isolated capture: a 4-pane stack with claude, hx, a test in another repo and an idle shell.

Portability: neutral.
close_reason: Landed: pane labels and rename

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Approval (Lucca, 2026-10-25 ~05:40 -03, direct to the overseer, answering its numbered list item 1): "approval to all". Approved: the label shape and the drafted contract wording below, with the overseer's recommendations: (a) clearing by both `--clear` and an empty NAME; (b) JSON fields `label` + `pinned_name`; (c) order `NAME · DIRECTORY` as in this bead (the 8rdi mock's directory-first order is not used); (d) label policy fixed, no `terminal.pane_label_style`/`pane_id_dim` settings (Configurability reason: one more style setting costs more support than users differing would gain); (e) no executable/process-name fallback (eon-6heq stays deferred). The draft's remaining choices stand as it recommends: window action as Commands entries; metadata from the existing ORBS observers; contrast as a 4.5:1 target against the resolved fill. Ships on EONW v20 together with eon-workspace-switching-shn4.3. Drafted wording (Codex draft reviewed by the overseer, 2026-10-25):

**1. eon-a7xd — Pane labels and rename**

**Current clauses → proposed replacements**

EON-C8, `docs/CONTRACTS.md`, Trigger:
> Launch, create or close a tab, create or close a pane, create a column, traverse focus, reorder the active tab or selected pane, move the selected pane into a neighbouring column, zoom the selected pane, receive terminal exit, or recover accepted same-boot runs.

Replace with:
> Launch, create or close a tab, create, close or rename a pane, create a column, traverse focus, reorder the active tab or selected pane, move the selected pane into a neighbouring column, zoom the selected pane, receive terminal exit, or recover accepted same-boot runs.

EON-C8, pane-label result:
> Each pane is identified as `pN`, two ASCII spaces, and a compact working-directory label; home uses `~`, descendants use `~/`, and external paths remain absolute.

Replace with:
> Each pane retains its stable `pN` identity. Runtime supplies its label: the identity, two ASCII spaces, then the pinned name, otherwise the sanitized terminal title, otherwise the compact working directory, otherwise no name. The default style appends ` · DIRECTORY` when the terminal directory differs lexically from the tab’s launch directory, without repeating a directory already used as the name. Context uses a relative path, or the compact path when shorter; compact paths use `~` for home and `~/` for its descendants. Labels preserve explicit offline, connecting and unavailable states. Program metadata is untrusted display text, never identity or command input.

VEN-C8, `venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md`, metadata observer:
> Every visible live pane endpoint has one bounded read-only metadata observer.

Replace with:
> Runtime supplies labels for every workspace pane, including collapsed panes and panes in background tabs. Venus consumes those labels without reconstructing their naming policy.

VEN-C8, label clauses:
> Headers and AccessKit names show the opaque `pN` identity, two ASCII spaces, and one compact working-directory label.
>
> Home displays `~`; descendants use `~/`; paths outside home remain absolute; overlong paths elide from the left to preserve the leaf; an unset or empty `HOME` keeps absolute paths.
>
> Terminal title remains available to the selected window and is not repeated in pane chrome. Empty, offline, unavailable, or incompatible metadata falls back to pane identity without exposing mapped Session identity.

Replace those three bullets with:
> Headers show Runtime’s bounded pane label. Fitting retains the literal pane identity whenever it fits and middle-elides the remaining text at shaping-cluster boundaries; AccessKit and final-close pane listings retain the full bounded label. The ID may be dimmer than the name, with 4.5:1 contrast as the target against the resolved fill at the configured opacity; when dimming compromises readability, it uses the name’s colour. Terminal title remains available for selected-window compositor semantics. Labels never expose mapped Session identity.

VEN-C8, observation lifecycle:
> Hidden tabs have no observers, obsolete observations retire, and a 250 ms reinspection exposes accepted external workspace changes without native input.

Replace with:
> Venus opens no separate workspace-label metadata observers. Removed panes retire their label projections, and a 250 ms reinspection exposes accepted external workspace changes without native input.

VEN-C8, Owner:
> Venus workspace materialization, bounded metadata observation, clipping, and accessibility projection; Eon owns topology and Orbit owns terminal metadata and Session lifetime.

Replace with:
> Venus owns workspace materialization, label fitting, rendering and accessibility; Runtime owns semantic pane labels and pins; Orbit owns terminal metadata and Session lifetime.

VEN-C8, Consumes:
> Eon `EON-C10`, `EON-C17`, `EON-C18`, canonical EONW through the in-tree `eon-workspace-protocol` 0.1.0, and Orbit metadata observation in ORBS v13 through the in-tree `orbit-protocol` 0.1.0.

Replace with:
> Eon `EON-C10`, `EON-C17`, `EON-C18`, canonical EONW through the in-tree `eon-workspace-protocol` 0.1.0, and Orbit terminal presentation in ORBS v13 through the in-tree `orbit-protocol` 0.1.0.

VEN-C7, related fitting sentence:
> The selected pane header reserves space for the count and fits its directory label into the remaining width using the existing cluster-safe header fitter.

Replace “its directory label” with “its pane label”.

**Add to EON-C8 / EON-C10 Result; no existing rename clause:**
> `eon pane rename PANE NAME [--json]` pins a name; `eon pane rename PANE --clear [--json]` restores automatic naming. `--` permits an option-looking NAME. Names are trimmed; an empty result clears the pin. Invalid names fail without mutation. Rename addresses an explicit pane anywhere in the addressed workspace and changes no workspace, tab, pane or popup selection or desktop focus. Window rename and clear actions use the same mutation. Pins follow pane moves, survive presentation detach and reattach, and end with the pane or supervisor; recovery does not restore them. Workspace inspection and action replies expose each pane’s `label` and nullable `pinned_name`, independently of attention records.

**EONW proposal:** one v20 with shn4.3: `Pane.label: String` ≤450 UTF-8 bytes, containing the existing ≤128-byte ID and a name/context portion ≤80 Unicode scalars; `Pane.pinned_name: Option<String>` and `RenamePane { pane: String, name: Option<String> }`, with names ≤80 scalars/320 bytes, excluding controls and the format characters Orbit’s management-title cleaner removes. Reject oversized pins; visibly elide composed display text. Preserve the 2 MiB frame and existing aggregate limits. shn4.3 adds `workspaces: Vec<WorkspaceSummary>` of 1–32 entries, each `id: String` (canonical `wN`, ≤128 bytes), `name: Option<String>` (1–64 scalars/256 bytes), `tab_count: u16` (1–64), and `active_workspace: String`. Recommend also `workspace: String` identifying whose `tabs`/`active_tab` the reply projects; `active_workspace` continues to identify the shown workspace. These are proposed bounds and names, not fields already approved by shn4.3.

**Open choices**
1. Clear syntax: `--clear`; empty NAME only; both. **Recommend both**, with `--` handling like the existing command-pane parser; empty-name clearing also agrees with approved EON-C33 workspace rename.
2. JSON: `pinned_name`/`label` or `name`/`label`. **Recommend `pinned_name`/`label`**: existing attention `name` already means terminal title.
3. Context order: `NAME · DIRECTORY` or `DIRECTORY · NAME`. **Recommend the bead’s appended directory**; the mock uses the opposite order and needs reconciliation.
4. Configuration: fixed policy with a recorded rationale, or `terminal.pane_label_style = "title-directory"` (`directory`, `title`, `title-directory`) plus `terminal.pane_id_dim = true`. **Recommend the settings**, following existing terminal presentation settings; Runtime resolves them and Venus parses no config.
5. Window action: Commands entries or a pane-header menu. **Recommend Commands entries**, using the existing command surface without adding a shortcut.
6. Metadata: move existing ORBS observers to Runtime, or add management metadata. **Recommend existing observers for this slice**: they already carry title and CWD; `attention.record.name` alone cannot cover ordinary panes.
7. Contrast: a resolved-fill target or an opaque backing that guarantees contrast. **Recommend the target**; arbitrary translucent compositor backdrops cannot support the bead’s unconditional ≥4.5:1 guarantee.

**Conflicts/splits:** omit the research’s executable fallback, process lookup and ORB-C12/C13 management changes: the bead specifies title → directory, and those additions need separate approval. Preserve EON-C31 attention meanings. Pin persistence beyond supervisor life is separate. Label-only updates must preserve zoom, navigation, scroll and attachments. EON-C28 needs no field-specific amendment: its existing 1.0 fixture rule covers whichever fields ship. The shared bump also replaces the current EONW references: EON-C8’s “Current EONW v19 workspace/popup values, Orbit terminal identities/endpoints and Venus `VEN-C8`.” → the same clause with v20; EON-C10’s “Current EONW v19 and accepted Orbit management operations.” → v20; its package sentence’s “v19 bytes” → “v20 bytes”; Venus’s index preamble likewise moves canonical EONW v19 to v20. Historical proof/version references remain.

title: Bump Orbit's Ghostty to a revision with OSC 7501 support
description:
## Why

Lucca decided on 2026-10-21 (eon-agent-sidebar-yx8.1) to bump Orbit's Ghostty now, at P1. This
replaces the alternative of adding an OSC 7501 pre-scanner to Orbit.

- **What the sidebar needs:** the agent attention sidebar (yx8) takes its state from OSC 7501,
  the Program Status Protocol
  (https://www.superlogical.com/rex/docs/build/program-status, rev 0.4). Claude Code >= 2.1.295
  and Codex >= 0.163 emit it natively.
- **What libghostty-vt provides:**
  - From Ghostty a4aacd91 (#14560) it parses OSC 7501 and answers the `OSC 7501;?` probe. Claude
    reports only after that answer arrives before DA1.
  - Rev 0.4 support lands in 9cd19b40d (#14630).
  - Malformed-id and length validation land in 8c425a7bd (#14793).
- **Where Eon is:** Eon pins Ghostty a887df42 (2026-07-11), about 1,700 commits older.
- **What else the bump brings:** the semantic-prompt (OSC 133) and reset options, and probably the
  key-release fix that the deferred bead orb-ze3 is waiting for (bd647035; ancestry not yet
  checked).

Rejected: an OSC 7501 pre-scanner in the Orbit host. It is smaller, but it would be a second OSC
parser beside libghostty. Lucca preferred the bump.

## Acceptance

- Orbit builds and ships through the flake against an exact Ghostty revision at or after
  8c425a7bd.
- Every ORB-C real-PTY and lifecycle check passes again on the new revision.
- Orbit's Rust host can reach the program-status callback, through a safe wrapper or a minimal
  binding, ready for the yx8 Orbit-records slice. Storing the records is not part of this epic.

## Children

1. Spike: measure the bump and choose the binding route. The output is a decision record;
   nothing merges.
2. Land the bump with full Orbit proof.

## Related

- orb-ze3 (the deferred adoption of a released crate) loses its purpose if this lands.
- Its stop conditions forbid unpublished Git dependencies and copied bindings. Whether to relax
  that is the policy question the spike must put to Lucca.
close_reason: Both children closed: the bump landed in 03afe53 with the full Orbit proof (eon-a9tr.2), after the eon-a9tr.1 spike.

title: Spike: measure the Ghostty bump to OSC 7501 and choose the binding route
description:
## Why

This is the first child of the Ghostty bump epic. Three unknowns decide how big the bump is: the
Zig toolchain, the Rust binding, and drift in the C ABI. Measure them before changing the
shipping tree.

## Evidence

**Current pins in this repository**

- `flake.nix:31` pins the Ghostty input at a887df42c56f6de86c0fe6da9c4eeca37931e083, and `:246`
  asserts that rev.
- `flake.nix:216`, `:271` and `:803` use `zig_0_15`.
- `orbit/Cargo.toml:9` pins `libghostty-vt = "=0.2.2"`.
- The sys crate's build.rs compiles the flake's Ghostty through `GHOSTTY_SOURCE_DIR`
  (`flake.nix:225-229`). Its checked-in bindings must match that source.
- Code that calls libghostty: `orbit/src/{cli,frame,input,pointer,pty}.rs`.

**Research from 2026-10-21**

The report is `~/pjs/refs/agent-sidebar-research/research-orbit-7501.md`; the clones are
`~/pjs/refs/ghostty-7501` and `~/pjs/refs/libghostty-rs-7501`.

- **Zig:** Ghostty 8c425a7bd needs Zig 0.17.0. Eon's nixpkgs (567a49d) has 0.16; nixpkgs master has
  0.17.
- **Rust binding:**
  - crates.io libghostty-vt 0.2.2 pins a887df42.
  - libghostty-rs master (0ef80413) pins 3425025e, which is older than #14560. It already
    carries the breaking PRs #84, #85 and #87.
  - It has no wrapper for program status, semantic prompt or reset.
- **C API at 8c425a7bd:**
  - `GHOSTTY_TERMINAL_OPT_PROGRAM_STATUS = 46`, with callback `GhosttyTerminalProgramStatusFn`.
  - The callback receives a sized struct with borrowed strings; progress is -1 when absent.
  - The probe is answered only when both that callback and WRITE_PTY are set
    (stream_terminal.zig:972).
- **ABI changes found so far:**
  - `GhosttyTerminalOptions` is removed, and `terminal_new` now takes `(cols, rows)`.
  - Scrollback is set through `OPT_SCROLLBACK_MAX_BYTES`. This touches Orbit's byte budget at
    `orbit/src/frame.rs:19` (ORB-C8).
  - The clipboard write callback now returns void and replies through a function (ORB-C11).
  - `mode_get/set` are removed.
  - The render-state colors call is removed.
- **Behaviour changes found so far:** CHA/VPA origin, DECRQM, DECXCPR, CSI 19 t, pulling
  scrollback on resize, and paste CR handling.

## Scope

In scope:
- A throwaway worktree or branch, never `edge`, that builds Orbit against Ghostty at or after
  8c425a7bd.
- Ways to get Zig 0.17: bump the nixpkgs input, or add a second pinned input used only for Zig.
- Ways to bind the new API:
  - (a) Send libghostty-rs an upstream PR that adds the wrapper and bumps Ghostty, and consume it
    as an exact git pin until it is released.
  - (b) Pin libghostty-rs master by git and add one minimal local FFI call through
    `libghostty-vt-sys`.
  - (c) Wait for a release.

  orb-ze3 forbids unpublished Git dependencies and copied bindings, so Lucca must choose the
  route.
- A list of every compile break, and of every behaviour change the ORB-C real-PTY suite detects.
- A check of whether bd647035 (orb-ze3's key-release fix) is an ancestor of the chosen revision.

Out of scope:
- Merging anything to `edge`, refreshing the profile, editing contracts, storing 7501 records, and
  Venus.

## Acceptance

- A bead comment records:
  - the chosen Ghostty revision;
  - the Zig route;
  - the binding route, with Lucca's decision;
  - the list of breaks, with an estimate for fixing each;
  - which ORB-C checks failed or changed on the candidate;
  - a recommendation on whether the bump fits one landing bead or needs splitting. Update the
    second child to match.
- A minimal proof on the candidate build:
  - the program-status callback fires for `ESC]7501;state=working:app=x ESC\`;
  - `ESC]7501;?` gets its reply before the DA1 answer.

## Implementation Notes

1. Check load first (`/proc/loadavg`, `free`), because many agents share the machine. Run one
   heavy build at a time.
2. Prefer the flake route (`GHOSTTY_SOURCE_DIR`) so the result matches the shipping build.
3. Record the reference-gate facts that AGENTS.md requires for a consequential code shape, since
   this is a dependency change.

## Verification

- Build the Orbit host crate on the candidate with `nix develop -c cargo build`. Record the
  outcome; it does not have to be green.
- Run `nix develop -c eon-test` on the Orbit suites for the candidate and record the failures.
- Run the callback and probe proof from Acceptance.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop and ask Lucca before choosing a binding route that orb-ze3's stop conditions forbid.
- Stop if Zig 0.17 cannot be obtained without bumping nixpkgs for the whole product. Report the
  blast radius instead.

## Maintenance Notes

Portability disposition: neutral. Ghostty and Zig are cross-platform, and macOS stays deferred.
close_reason: Spike done: Ghostty 8c425a7bd, Zig 0.17 via a Zig-only nixpkgs input, binding route (a) approved by Lucca (Yazelix/libghostty-rs fork, upstream PR offered); patch reviewed to convergence (ledger comment); eon-a9tr.2 updated.

comments.text: From eon-agent-sidebar-yx8.1 (approved contract, 2026-10-21): the spike must also choose the binding route for libghostty's semantic-prompt (OSC 133) option, and confirm whether RIS arrives as a program-status CLEAR with an empty id. If it does, a reset binding is needed only for Bend to tell RIS apart and reset its 'ever sent OSC 133 A' flag, and the spike decides whether that is worth it. Next consumer: eon-agent-sidebar-yx8.4 (ORB-C15).

ORB-C15 keeps the 'ever sent OSC 133 A' latch permanent for the run, and RIS reaches Orbit as a program-status CLEAR with an empty id. The spike only confirms that CLEAR behavior; the semantic-prompt binding is still needed.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Spike record (eon-a9tr.1, 2026-10-21). Throwaway detached worktree from edge 7cc7156; nothing merged; edge, profile and contracts untouched.

Ghostty revision: 8c425a7bd57de848aa83cb9b003b1ecd6037c56a (#14793, 2026-10-20), 1,767 commits after a887df42 and 297 after libghostty-rs master's 3425025e. It is the minimum with the 7501 malformed-id and length checks; 18 newer upstream commits add nothing the sidebar needs. bd647035 (orb-ze3's key-release fix) IS an ancestor (git merge-base --is-ancestor).

Zig route: a second flake input nixpkgs-zig = NixOS/nixpkgs 02c087f3fe673c9e317f206a627cb6b910336dbe (nixos-unstable, 2026-10-20), used only for zig_0_17 (0.17.0). Product nixpkgs stays at 567a49d, so no whole-product bump (stop condition not hit). Three Zig 0.17 breaks, each with a small fix:
1. nixpkgs' Zig 0.17 hook sets ZIG_GLOBAL_CACHE_DIR only in its configurePhase, which buildRustPackage replaces: orbitPackage needs preBuild 'export ZIG_GLOBAL_CACHE_DIR=$(mktemp -d)'.
2. Zig 0.17 fetchDeps stores packages as .tar.gz, but 'zig build --system' wants them unpacked: one runCommand that untars each archive (each holds its package directory). Deps hash sha256-Q0ZgKPVtXbiTbJqrMlGPJBnNpmaXNLUAk0VcqLBFGFI=. Trap: with the old hash still in the store, the fixed-output derivation is silently reused; change the hash to fakeHash to refetch.
3. Zig 0.17 removed 'zig build --global-cache-dir': libghostty-vt-sys build.rs (master and 0.2.2) must pass ZIG_GLOBAL_CACHE_DIR through the environment instead. This is a binding change, so no route consumes master unmodified.

Binding (libghostty-rs master 0ef8041 plus a local patch, 4 files, +628/-36):
- build.rs: GHOSTTY_COMMIT -> 8c425a7bd; the --global-cache-dir fix above.
- bindings.rs regenerated (gen-bindings); the C API diff from 3425025e is additive except OscCommandType CONTEXT_SIGNAL (renamed upstream in 079f5d202; unused).
- gen_bindings.rs: prefixes for SemanticPromptKind/SemanticPromptPromptKind (master leaves them as GHOSTTY_SEMANTIC_PROMPT_*; the OSC 133 types already exist at 3425025e).
- terminal.rs: ProgramStatus{State,Kind}, ProgramStatus<'t>, SemanticPromptKind, SemanticPrompt<'t>, and on_program_status/on_semantic_prompt handlers in the existing handlers! macro, plus 5 tests.
The master wrapper otherwise builds unchanged on 8c425a7bd, and libghostty-rs's whole suite passes on it (117 tests incl. 4 of the new ones; the fifth, probe-without-callback, ran after).

Orbit breaks (crates.io 0.2.2 -> master; all API, none ABI), each fixed in the spike, ~0.5 h total:
- Terminal::new(TerminalOptions{..}) -> Terminal::new(cols, rows) + set_scrollback_max_bytes(Some(SCROLLBACK_BUDGET_BYTES)) (pty.rs; 8 test sites in frame/input/pointer/pty). ORB-C8's byte budget maps 1:1 onto OPT_SCROLLBACK_MAX_BYTES.
- on_clipboard_write: the closure now answers with write.reply(result, false) instead of returning it, and ClipboardContent.data is &[u8], so Orbit rejects non-UTF-8 itself as InvalidData (before: it arrived as empty text and was rejected as InvalidData; same outcome) (ORB-C11).
- Key is repr(i32): Key::try_from(i32::from(raw)) (input.rs).
- mode_get/set and render-state colors removals did not reach Orbit: master's wrapper already absorbs them.

Checks on the candidate (wt dev shell, Zig 0.17, Ghostty 8c425a7bd):
- cargo build -p yazelix-orbit --all-targets: green after the fixes above.
- nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-orbit: unit 32/32, lifecycle 18/18 pass; real_pty is ignored there.
- all orbit-* flake checks (38 real-PTY + boundary, laws, terminfo, unsupported): all 42 build and pass (nix build --keep-going of every checks.x86_64-linux.orbit-* attribute, exit 0; the flake asserts ghostty.rev 8c425a7bd). No ORB-C check failed or changed.
- Spike proof (libghostty-vt tests on 8c425a7bd): ESC]7501;state=working:app=x ESC\ reaches on_program_status as (Working, id "", app "x"); ESC]7501;? ESC\ ESC[c writes '\e]7501;?:states=idle,working,done,blocked,error:kinds=permission,question,auth\e\\' before DA1 '\e[?62;22c'; RIS after a working record reports Clear with an empty id (confirms the yx8.1 correction: no reset binding needed); ESC]133;A ESC\ reaches on_semantic_prompt as PromptStart. Without the callback the probe gets no reply and DA1 still answers (tested), so Orbit answers the probe only once it registers the callback (ORB-C2).

Binding route (Lucca decides; orb-ze3 forbids unpublished Git deps and copied bindings):
(a) Upstream PR plus exact git pin until release. libghostty-rs's AGENTS.md forbids agents from opening issues or PRs, so Lucca would submit the prepared patch by hand. No upstream branch or open PR moves past 3425025e (PR #93 recognizes new OSC commands but keeps that pin), so release timing is unknown.
(b) Pin master by git plus a minimal local FFI call: not viable as specified, because master's build.rs fails under Zig 0.17 with GHOSTTY_ZIG_SYSTEM_DIR (break 3) and its checked-in bindings lack the program-status types, so Orbit would copy bindings.
(c) Wait for a release: blocks yx8 indefinitely.
Recommendation: (a) in the shape this repository already uses for accesskit and winit: a Yazelix/libghostty-rs fork at an exact rev, consumed through [patch.crates-io] (or a direct git dependency), carrying exactly this patch, with the same patch offered upstream; exit condition: replace with the first crates.io release whose GHOSTTY_COMMIT contains 8c425a7bd and whose API carries the program-status and semantic-prompt wrappers. It needs Lucca's approval because it relaxes orb-ze3's no-unpublished-Git rule for this dependency.

Landing recommendation: one bead (a9tr.2) fits once the route is approved: flake (Zig input, deps unpack, preBuild), the fork pin, the four Orbit adaptations, docs that name a887df42 (orbit/docs/CRATES.md, TERMINAL.md, CONTRACTS.md header and ORB-C proof identity lines, venus/docs references stay historical), Cargo.lock, then the full orbit-* proof plus Eon's downstream build. Recording the program-status callback in Orbit stays with yx8.4.

Reference gate: nixpkgs 02c087f3's Zig 0.17 consumers were read for the deps shape (ly links the archives as $ZIG_GLOBAL_CACHE_DIR/p; zls and kiesel use unpacked linkFarms with --system); Eon keeps --system with an unpacked runCommand because the binding's build.rs runs Zig inside the read-only Ghostty source. Fork-pin precedent: Cargo.toml's [patch.crates-io] Yazelix/accesskit and Yazelix/winit-0.30 at exact revs. Rejected: bumping the product nixpkgs for Zig (whole-product blast radius); option (b) (see above). Version policy: exact Ghostty rev and exact fork rev, moved only by a bead; exit as stated in the recommendation.
Spike artifacts (scratch, disposable): worktree and patches under this session's scratchpad (wt/, lgrs/); the libghostty-rs patch can be regenerated from this record.

comments.text: Review ledger (libghostty-rs patch, 2026-10-21): base upstream master 0ef8041, final series 6313a9b = ec1a18b vt-sys: update to Ghostty 8c425a7 and Zig 0.17 / 76a8210 vt-sys: strip the semantic prompt and resize window enum prefixes / 821c498 vt/terminal: add program status and semantic prompt callbacks / 6313a9b vt: resync docs with 8c425a7. Codex: 2 passes (round 1: 1 blocking, iOS Zig 0.17 needs Ghostty's zig-0.17-ios-process-replace.patch, fixed in the dev shell's zigPkg; narrow re-checks 975f5d3..c1fd118 and 975f5d3..6313a9b: 0 blocking). Claude: 5 rounds (1: sized_field! bypass; 2: docs stale vs 8c425a7, resynced in a 4th commit; 3: clean; 4 after a test fix: wrong breaking-change claim in a commit message, reworded, text-only restart 1 of 2; 5: clean). Every round ran upstream's 8 flake checks per commit (bindings-fresh, cargo-check, clippy -D warnings, doc, doctest, fmt, test, test-dynamic), plus the examples workspace and Miri; the offline GHOSTTY_ZIG_SYSTEM_DIR path was exercised by hand. Not run anywhere: iOS, macOS, Windows CI (Linux host). Open nits, not taken: size-truncation tests for ProgramStatus/SemanticPrompt; build.rs:234 comment wording; example/ghostling_rs/src/main.rs:140 'CSI 14/16/18 t'; tests cover only some ProgramStatusState variants; the probe test hard-codes Ghostty's reply list. Series saved as ~/pjs/refs/agent-sidebar-research/a9tr1-libghostty-rs-series/000{1..4}-*.patch (supersedes a9tr1-libghostty-rs-8c425a7bd.patch). Upstream commits carry Signed-off-by; Lucca adds his own when he opens the PR (agents may not open PRs there).

title: Land the Ghostty bump with full Orbit proof
description:
## Why

This is the second child of the Ghostty bump epic. It lands the bump that the spike measured, so
the yx8 Orbit program-status slice can build on it.

## Scope

In scope:
- In `flake.nix`: the Ghostty input, its rev assert, and the Zig toolchain.
- The binding in `orbit/Cargo.toml` and `Cargo.lock`.
- The libghostty call sites in `orbit/src/`.
- The ORB-C fixes the spike listed.
- The dependency identity in `orbit/docs/CRATES.md`, and `orbit/CHANGELOG.md` if behaviour
  changes.
- Exposing the program-status callback (and semantic-prompt, if it comes for free) to the host as
  an unused hook point with a test.

Out of scope:
- Storing or publishing 7501 records, management Status, EONW, Venus, and new contracts. yx8 owns
  those.
- Changes to ORB-C contract text beyond what the bump forces. Those need Lucca.

## Acceptance

- Orbit on `edge` uses the Ghostty revision and binding route the spike chose.
- All Orbit suites and ORB-C real-PTY checks pass on the new revision.
- `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings` are green for the
  Orbit crates.
- The full Nix build of the eon package succeeds.
- The profile is refreshed, and running supervisors are left untouched.

## Implementation Notes

Read the spike's decision comment first. It replaces the estimates here.

## Verification

- Run `nix develop -c eon-test` (Orbit and workspace suites), `nix flake check`, and the Nix
  package build.
- Get the Codex review AGENTS.md requires, since this changes a dependency and Nix.
- After the profile refresh, make one installed dogfood observation of ordinary terminal use.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if the work clearly exceeds the spike's estimate. Split it rather than let it grow.
- Stop for Lucca on any ORB-C behaviour change that is not purely a fix.
close_reason: Bump landed in 03afe53 with the full Orbit and Nix proof; profile refreshed and dogfooded

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Updated from eon-a9tr.1 (Lucca approved route (a) on 2026-10-21; read a9tr.1's spike record, decision and review ledger first).
Prerequisite (outward-facing, Lucca's call): Yazelix/libghostty-rs exists with the reviewed 4-commit series (~/pjs/refs/agent-sidebar-research/a9tr1-libghostty-rs-series) on upstream master 0ef8041, and the same series is offered upstream. Stop if the fork is not there.
Shape:
- orbit/Cargo.toml: libghostty-vt as a git dependency on Yazelix/libghostty-rs at the exact fork rev (as Cargo.toml already pins Yazelix/accesskit and winit-0.30); flake.nix workspaceCargoLock.outputHashes gains its hash.
- flake.nix: ghostty input -> 8c425a7bd57de848aa83cb9b003b1ecd6037c56a (and its rev assert); a nixpkgs-zig input at 02c087f3 used only for zig_0_17; ghosttyDeps = the fetchDeps archives unpacked (runCommand untar; hash sha256-Q0ZgKPVtXbiTbJqrMlGPJBnNpmaXNLUAk0VcqLBFGFI=, refetch with fakeHash if in doubt); orbitPackage preBuild exports ZIG_GLOBAL_CACHE_DIR; dev shell uses the same Zig. Zig's iOS patch is not needed for Eon (Linux only).
- orbit/src: Terminal::new(cols, rows) + set_scrollback_max_bytes(Some(SCROLLBACK_BUDGET_BYTES)) in pty.rs and 8 test sites; clipboard write answers via write.reply(result, false) and rejects non-UTF-8 data as InvalidData; Key::try_from(i32::from(raw)). Spike version: ~/pjs/refs/agent-sidebar-research/a9tr1-eon-orbit-flake.patch (its Cargo dependency points at a spike-only path; replace with the fork pin).
- Host hook points: register on_program_status and on_semantic_prompt as unused hooks with a test; registering on_program_status also makes Orbit answer the OSC 7501;? probe (ORB-C2 behaviour change: stop for Lucca if that needs contract text).
- Docs naming a887df42: orbit/docs/CRATES.md (dependency identity, fork rationale and exit condition: drop the fork for the first crates.io release whose GHOSTTY_COMMIT contains 8c425a7bd and whose API has both wrappers), orbit/docs/TERMINAL.md, orbit/docs/CONTRACTS.md header identity lines; venus/docs references stay historical.
Spike evidence on this shape: all 42 orbit-* flake checks, unit 32/32, lifecycle 18/18 green.

Pin Orbit to that exact rev. Upstream issue: https://github.com/Uzaaft/libghostty-rs/issues/111 (asks whether they take it as a PR or do the bump themselves).

comments.text: Decision (Lucca, 2026-10-21): a9tr.2 lands only the bump and registers no new callbacks. Registering on_program_status, even as a no-op, makes libghostty answer the OSC 7501;? probe, so Orbit would advertise states it discards. yx8.4 registers on_program_status together with storing the records, and on_semantic_prompt waits for its first consumer. The fork's own tests prove that both callbacks fire. Work is in a detached worktree because other agents share the main tree.

comments.text:
Profile refresh and dogfood (2026-10-21, after 03afe53): scheduled with the other sessions. eon-2e moved its uncommitted v14 work out of the main tree. The eon element was briefly pointed at a clean git-archive export of 03afe53, then returned to path:/home/lucca/pjs/eon/eon once that tree was clean, under its usual name. Both builds gave the same store path. eon resolves to /nix/store/qhx385rwsy7yy24w5m8rh7wj00n1kzh3-eon-0.1.1, and eonbase was upgraded to /nix/store/sbn54w1l66v1y6mk9l1sny880jbzjn5f-eonbase-0.1.1. Both carry Orbit /nix/store/id5h8rjqg62i2fxslmwb4zlzb47k1ars-yazelix-orbit-0.1.0. No running supervisor was stopped, so live Eon sessions run the old Orbit until restarted.
Dogfood: the installed eon ran on a private headless Sway (isolated HOME and XDG_RUNTIME_DIR). From the startup picker, Enter opened ~/work in nushell. Bold red, reverse-video green, a wide 界, a combining é and 'term size' (124x33) all rendered and answered correctly, and Return submitted. Negative, not from this change: wdotool 'type' with several characters drops a few letters per call and the Return after it. The old package (l5ss1z32, Ghostty a887) drops the same letters (s, d) on the same input, so this is a driver artifact. Typing one character per call delivers every key.

title: Restore Accelerando frame cadence with ordered bundled fonts
description:
Goal and contract
Restore Accelerando rendering at its existing 55ms animation cadence in newly opened Eon and EonTerm terminals. Preserve the real alien alphabet, same font/size/grid/trails, alien-only default and opt-in --symbols. Ordinary text and Nerd Font icons must remain correct. Preserve explicit user font_fallbacks overrides and all live supervisors/terminals. This is a corrective follow-up to published Anima 1d02919 and Eon e02a2e1, prompted by the user reporting approximately half-second ticks.

Evidence and owner
Installed Anima hyfiac2 emits steady frames every55-58ms at80x24 and180x55; release producer p95 <=1.4ms at320x90. Private installed EonTerm1920x1080 scale1 with pixman software compositing (Venus GPU adapter unrecorded) reproduces roughly333ms graphical updates (11 updates in3.13s), while Matrix produces54 in3.1s. Cosmic-text matching bench with installed fontconfig:8192 ordinary shapes14.5ms, alien fallback1268ms cold and1262ms warm, explicitly named alien face22ms. Missing fallback ordering, rather than Anima simulation speed, is the measured bottleneck.
Eon crates/eon/src/product.rs supplies default font_fallbacks. Existing Eon Runtime TerminalConfig override/forwarding owns mechanics; Venus FontSetup::resolve installs OrderedFallback and resolves the existing monospace primary. Private config [Symbols Nerd Font Mono, Accelerando Terminal] yields52 visible updates in3.13s (capture resolution33.3ms; p50 gap66.7ms, p95 100ms), preserving glyphs/size. Eon owns the bundled-font default; no child renderer change or new dependency is needed.

Reference gate and decision

title: Accept Eon same-boot Orbit recovery
description:
## Outcome and contract routing

Accept the exact installed EON-C15 consumer of Orbit ORB-C13. This issue changes no source behavior, protocol, dependency, or compatibility promise.

Consumer: one local Eon or EonTerm user on x86_64 Linux.

Trigger: an installed exact Eon generation launches managed Orbit runs, then its supervisor is abruptly lost after Ready while the Orbit runs and PTY work remain live.

Result: replacement Eon validates and acquires the same runs, reconstructs the bounded deterministic workspace, and presents the same authoritative terminal state through the exact accepted managed Venus. Owner-routed Stop then completes ORB-C12 for every run. EON-C15 and the composed half of ORB-C13 become Proven only from this exact observation plus their owner proofs.

Important failures: profile refresh stops no live supervisor; no old generation is relabeled; Busy, stale/corrupt state, partial recovery, ambiguous ownership, transport uncertainty, orphaned presentation, or failed Orbit cleanup remains visible and cannot become success. macOS, logout, reboot, prior topology, Eonova rollout, and remote continuity remain outside this acceptance.

- Exact Eon manifest, lock, packages, installed profile artifacts, current instructions, and owner proof records.

## Scope boundary

In scope: isolated installed Eon and EonTerm same-boot supervisor loss, old managed-Venus release, immediate replacement presentation, one-winner lease recovery, PTY continuity, multi-Session management Stop, authority negatives, exact identities, proof metadata, and contract status after user acceptance.

Out of scope: source fixes; Eonova rollout; prior topology; durable records; logout/reboot/machine loss; macOS; promotion; direct distribution; service management; remote access; public protocol; compatibility adapters. A defect returns to one separately authorized owner issue.

title: Venus panics in AccessKit on a pane-less tab with no visible terminal
description:
## Defect (found during eon-jqxr, read-only code hunt; confirmed by reading, not run)

`venus/src/accessibility.rs:325` always puts the terminal-content node (CONTENT) in the AccessKit
tree update. In workspace mode it gets a parent only at `:432-441`: under the pane panel when the
tab has no panes and a terminal is visible or the status is non-empty, or under the selected pane.
When the active tab has no panes, no visible terminal and an empty status, CONTENT is in the update
with no parent. accesskit_consumer 0.38.0 `tree.rs:306-310` then panics on the next update ("TreeUpdate
includes N nodes which are neither in the current tree nor a child"), or on the first tree if that
state is the initial one, and Venus exits.

Reachable state: EONW permits a popup-only tab with no selected popup (`validate_workspace`, and
`remove_empty_tab` keeps a tab that still has popups, `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/workspace.rs:1309`);
a kept-alive popup dismissed after the tab's last pane exited leaves `selected_popup = None`
(`workspace.rs:681`). Only fires while AccessKit's AT-SPI adapter is active (`update_if_active`,
`accessibility.rs:648`), e.g. with a screen reader running.

The existing unit test `accessibility.rs:2785-2790` asserts the node exists while the pane panel
has no children, but never feeds the update through AccessKit's tree, so it misses the panic.

## Contract

VEN-C18 (popup-only tabs with an empty body) and Venus accessibility: Venus must not exit in that state.

## Acceptance

Red/green: a Venus unit test that feeds successive tree updates for an empty popup-only tab through
accesskit_consumer's Tree (or an equivalent existing harness) panics before and passes after; fix
parents CONTENT (or omits it) consistently. Venus fmt/clippy green.

## Scope boundary

Only this orphan. A second, less likely AccessKit panic (focus on a header button dropped for width
<= 0, `accessibility.rs:380` vs `:519`) may share the fix only if trivially; otherwise file it.
close_reason: Venus omits CONTENT only when it holds no terminal and no status, and parents it otherwise; red/green through accesskit_consumer::Tree

comments.text:
Reference gate (consequential: adds a dev-dependency).
- Behavior and owner: with an AT-SPI adapter active, Venus no longer exits when the active tab is popup-only with no shown popup and no status. Venus's accessibility snapshot (`Snapshot::tree`, venus/src/accessibility.rs) is the one owner of the AccessKit tree; it now omits the terminal-content node (CONTENT) whenever the pane panel does not parent it, and the panel stays labeled "Empty tab" with no children. Focus never named CONTENT in that state (it falls back to the selected tab without a visible terminal).
- References read: venus/docs/CRATES.md "Accessibility" (the shared Yazelix/accesskit pin); accesskit_consumer at that pin, rev 0f9d186ec6f5e66fe4ccc131ca318dc2725c12f5: consumer/src/tree.rs:306-317 (orphan node / dangling child panics), :546 (focus unwrap), and its own tests' no-op ChangeHandler pattern (tree.rs:751), which the Venus test mirrors as `IgnoreChanges`. docs/REFERENCES.md has no accessibility route.
- Dependency: `accesskit_consumer = "=0.38.0"` as a venus dev-dependency only. It is already in the graph through accesskit_winit's Unix adapter under the same [patch.crates-io] pin, so Cargo.lock gains only the venus edge; no new package, source, feature or build tool. Version policy: follows the shared AccessKit pin in CRATES.md. Exit: it goes when Venus stops using AccessKit. It removes the "hand-checked node list" responsibility from tests by applying AccessKit's own validation.
- Rejected: always parenting CONTENT under an empty panel (exposes an empty, boundless "Tab content" container to screen readers); a hand-written parent check in tests (a second, weaker copy of AccessKit's validation).
- Decision check: popup_and_empty_body_expose_only_visible_accessibility_targets feeds popup -> empty -> status-alert updates through accesskit_consumer::Tree.
