comments.text:
## Parity audit: gap ranking, rule draft, proposed beads (eon-70, 2026-10-23; pending Lucca)

### Gaps ranked by value to an agent working with a person
1. **Send input to a running pane or popup.** Use: drive a Codex/Grok/OpenCode/Pi agent, answer a
   prompt, rerun a command in a live shell. Existing: eon-pane-send-research-fo4p, then
   eon-agent-terminal-control-n8ic.
2. **Read a pane's output, title and cwd.** Use: check what a Codex agent did, read a build's error.
   Without it, sending input is blind. Existing: orb-p92 (deferred P1; phase 1 is the minimum
   observer).
3. **Create a tab at a directory, optionally running a command, with no picker and no focus
   change.** Use: start an agent in another project's tab (hit 2026-10-23). Existing:
   eon-tab-create-launch-8tl4.
4. **Popups from the CLI.** Show, hide or toggle a catalog popup (Agent, Git, Files, custom) in a
   tab, and focus a popup by ID. Use: "open lazygit on t2 for me"; start the Agent popup in a project
   tab. EONW `InvokePopup` exists; `DismissPopup` exists with no sender. New.
5. **Sidebar detail in the JSON.** The attention title and needs-input message, kind, progress,
   `changed_at`, stale and `others`, plus the quota chips and popup labels. Use: the overseer sees
   "Claude in t3 asks to run rm" without the person relaying it. EON-C31 Q8 cut these on purpose.
   New (related: yx8.11).
6. **Act on any tab by ID without moving focus.** `tab close` refuses a non-active tab, `pane close`
   refuses another tab, `pane create` reaches only the caller's tab, and `edit` always focuses. Use:
   the overseer closes a finished agent's tab without changing the person's view. Existing for pane
   create: eon-89ho. The rest is new.
7. **Pane facts.** The running command and the exit status of an ended pane. Use: did the build pane
   exit 0? New. Title and cwd belong with gap 2.
8. **Wait and discovery.** Today an agent can only poll. Use: wait until an agent needs input.
   Existing: eon-cli-action-discovery-ogzi (deferred).
9. **Prompts that fail quietly.** Without `--json`, `eon stop` prompts; non-TTY stdin reads as "no",
   prints "cancelled" and exits 0, so a script thinks it succeeded. New, small.
10. **Thin wrappers for EONW actions only Venus sends.** `CreateColumn`, `ToggleSidebar`,
    `Next/PreviousAttention`, `FocusAttention` (popup targets included). Low value, cheap. New.
11. **Apply `[terminal]`/`[bar]` config without detaching.** A person detaches and runs
    `eon attach`; an agent can't detach. Use: "make the font bigger". Touches EON-C11/VEN-C14 and
    the EON-C32 "no live reload" exclusion. New, P3.

Human-only by nature (proposed exceptions): Venus view state (Alt+Shift+Z zoom, F6/Tab/Escape
chrome focus, sidebar row stepping, the Shortcuts viewer, the hints bar, hover and tooltips,
tab-strip and scrollback viewport scrolling, selection), pointer mechanics (mouse reporting to
programs, window drag; links work through `xdg-open`), detaching the person's window, and desktop
focus. Relative navigation (Alt+H/L/K/J, Ctrl+Tab) counts as covered when an equivalent that names
its target exists (`eon focus ID`).

### Rule draft
For AGENTS.md, a new section "Humans and Agents" after "Happy Users":

> Eon is the terminal for humans and agents to work together. Every action a person can take on
> the workspace in an Eon window, over its tabs, panes, popups, terminals, agent attention, windows
> and configuration, has an `eon` CLI path that an agent in an Eon terminal can use. That path names
> its target by ID and leaves the person's active tab, selection, shown popup and desktop focus as
> they are unless the agent asks to move them. Everything a person can see about that workspace, an
> agent can read from the CLI as data. Reading or writing terminal contents goes through the
> authorization its owner defines. The exceptions are Venus-local view state (zoom, keyboard focus
> in the chrome, the Shortcuts viewer, the hints bar, hover, scroll position and selection),
> pointer mechanics, and detaching the person's window. A change that adds a window action ships
> its CLI path in the same change, or names the open bead that adds it. Open gaps:
> `eon-agent-parity-audit-t31r`.

For `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, under "CLI and executable boundary", an "Agent parity" bullet: the CLI
is the agent's projection of every Runtime workspace action. Each EONW `Action` a client can send
has a CLI command or a named exception. Venus-local view state is listed as an exception and has no
EONW action.

Notes on the draft:
- It states what the product guarantees going forward and points at open gaps. Today's CLI doesn't
  meet it for gaps 1 to 7, so it can't claim parity yet.
- It is a rule, not an EON-C contract. Each gap bead amends its owning contract.

### Proposed beads (file only after approval)
| # | Bead | Contract owner | Pri | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | eon-pane-send-research-fo4p → eon-agent-terminal-control-n8ic | new EON-C + ORB-C | P2 → P1? | existing |
| B | orb-p92 phase 1, minimum observer (visible text, title, cwd) | ORB-C3 change + new EON-C | P1 | existing, deferred |
| C | eon-tab-create-launch-8tl4 (also let `tab directory` commit a pending tab) | EON-C18, EON-C10 | P2 | existing |
| D | `eon popup show/hide/toggle ENTRY [--tab T] [--json]` + `eon focus uN` | EON-C10 (+EON-C8) | P2 | new |
| E | Full attention record, quotas and popup label in `eon workspace --json` | EON-C31 Q8, EON-C10 | P2 | new |
| F | `tab close` / `pane close` on any tab by ID, `edit --no-focus`; sibling of eon-89ho | EON-C10, EON-C8 | P2 | new |
| G | Pane command and last exit status in the snapshot | EON-C8, EON-C10 | P3 | new |
| H | Non-TTY confirmation fails non-zero (or `--yes`) instead of silent cancel | EON-C11, EON-C10 | P2 | new |
| I | `eon column create`, `eon sidebar toggle`, `eon attention next/previous/focus` | EON-C10, EON-C31 | P3 | new |
| J | eon-cli-action-discovery-ogzi (discovery + `wait`) | EON-C10 | P2 | existing, deferred |
| K | Re-present the window to apply `[terminal]`/`[bar]` without detaching | EON-C11, VEN-C14, EON-C32 | P3 | new |
| L | Parity check: an exhaustive `match` over EONW `Action` maps each variant to its CLI command or a named exception, so a new variant fails to compile without one | EON-C10 | P2, after the rule | new |
| M | Docs mismatches (VEN-C30 label and Space, USAGE zoom wording, INTERACTION drag and stray line) | VEN-C30 | P3 | new, docs-only |
Related reliability: eon-cli-old-window-after-upgrade-mno4 (P1, in-window `eon` breaks after an upgrade).

title: Investigate the Agent popup's resume behaviour in folders with no history
description:
## Problem

Lucca, 2026-10-27: "if i open the agent in a empty folder, it cant resume anything. if i press esc, the
agent quits. looks like a claude bad UI imo?" His Agent popup ran `claude --resume` (also the last
entry of the built-in `auto` list, eon/crates/eon/src/product.rs:138-144; docs/CONFIGURATION.md:334-335).
In a folder with no Claude history the resume picker is empty; Esc quits Claude, the popup's
program ends and the popup disappears.

Coordinator checks (Claude Code 2.1.303, throwaway PTY, no Eon, empty folder):
- `claude --continue` prints "No conversation found to continue" and exits 1 at once: in the popup
  that would close it immediately.
- `sh -c 'claude --continue || exec claude'` prints the same line, then opens a fresh session.
  Lucca's config now uses this as a stopgap (~/.config/eon/config.toml `[popups.agent].command`).

Upstream (anthropics/claude-code, read only; never post):
- #78586 "'- c' flag silently starts new session when no prior session resolves instead of erroring"
  (bug, closed completed 2026-08-21): erroring is the intended behaviour.
- #78748 "`claude -c` should gracefully start a new session when no previous conversation exists"
  (enhancement, closed not planned 2026-09-18).
So Claude will not fall back by itself; a launcher must. No upstream issue was found about the
empty `--resume` picker quitting on Esc.

## Investigate

1. For each agent in the `auto` list (`codex resume`, `grok`, `opencode`, `pi`, `claude --resume`),
   record in a throwaway PTY what happens in a folder with and without history: picker, error, or
   fresh session; what Esc and Ctrl+C do; exit codes. Note the comparable `opencode --continue`
   already in runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/managed_environment.rs:1764.
2. Decide the built-in behaviour per agent: "continue the folder's last session, else start fresh"
   (Claude: `--continue`, falling back on exit 1 with "No conversation found"), versus a picker.
   Prefer a check that does not read another tool's private session files; if a fallback on exit
   status is used, make it exact (only that first-run failure), so a continued session that later
   exits non-zero does not respawn.
3. Where the fallback lives: a built-in command shape (Runtime-resolved, no shell) or a tiny Eon
   launcher; no new language (AGENTS.md Implementation Languages).
4. Popup exit: today a popup whose program exits disappears. Consider showing "exited — Enter to
   restart" for keep_alive popups instead (a contract change; propose only).
5. Propose to eon-overseer (numbered, with recommendations, exact contract and CONFIGURATION.md
   text) and stop for Lucca.

## Contract

The Agent popup's built-in command and `auto` list (docs/CONFIGURATION.md; the popup contract that
owns built-in popups, find it in docs/CONTRACTS.md and venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md). Any change to
contract text or defaults needs Lucca's approval.

## Acceptance (after approval)

- In an empty folder the Agent popup opens a fresh Claude session; in a folder with history it
  continues the last one; Esc inside Claude never leaves an empty popup flash.
- Tests for the command resolution; one isolated installed observation with real Claude in both
  folders.
- docs/CONFIGURATION.md and CHANGELOG.md updated; review per AGENTS.md.

## Scope boundary

The Agent popup's launch and exit behaviour only. Not: changes to any agent's own UI, posting to
upstream trackers.

Only a new window (new supervisor) picks it up, and docs/CONFIGURATION.md does not say so. title: Add a source-aware agent attention sidebar
description:
## Outcome
A user supervising coding agents across Eon tabs can see which project needs input, which agent is working, and which result awaits review, then jump to the exact tab/pane. The sidebar can be hidden without affecting agents.

## Contract routing and ownership
Refine the provider-attention horizon of eon-pxn and propose the minimum additions to EON-C8/EON-C10 and Venus VEN-C8. Eon owns agent/session associations, normalized attention, evidence source/freshness and navigation actions; provider adapters own provider-native event meanings; Venus owns the rail and accessible interaction; Orbit retains sole terminal and process authority. An AgentRun identity, if needed, is distinct from a pane, PTY or provider thread.

## Prerequisites and reference gate
Planning-only selection on 2026-09-09, not implementation activation. Deferred product container; first settle one provider-backed workflow and its contract, then split provider/Eon ownership, Venus display and downstream acceptance into non-epic children.
Required before code: eon-pxn's preserved decisions; current accepted Eon/Orbit/Venus contracts; docs/REFERENCES.md agent-work routes. Inspect the user-named Nova, zj-radar and Herdr at exact source revisions, including licenses, producer events, stale-state handling and jump-to-attention behavior. Discovery inspected Nova e476ca8065cc8b2c02ea611ae7edeeb0989c0c23 and local zj-radar 0b1672606ca118f6241df687889142c8b52d03fe; Nova pins Radar 166626879b2067561915d7c60781932c809939d2, so resolve that distinction at activation. Herdr https://herdr.dev/docs/agents/ distinguishes full lifecycle-hook authority from screen-manifest inference; pin source before adopting a mechanism.

## Success Criteria
One real supported agent workflow produces useful, source-labeled attention and reliable navigation in an optional native Eon sidebar.

## Acceptance Criteria
- First slice shows project/agent identity, working/needs-input/done/unknown-or-stale state, and click/keyboard jump to the exact live target.
- Select the first provider from the user's actual workflow; unsupported providers remain usable terminals with unknown semantic state. No universal compatibility promise.
- Define source precedence, freshness expiry, completion acknowledgement, tab rollup, missing hooks, process exit, provider restart and stale identity behavior.
- Prefer explicit provider reports. Output growth, process names, terminal screenshots and elapsed silence never become authoritative semantic status; absence of evidence does not mean idle or done.
- Bound event input, retained metadata and refresh work; reuse existing Eon actions/snapshot mechanisms unless measured needs justify more. No generic event bus or polling every terminal screen by default.
- Toggle/collapse, keyboard traversal, narrow-window layout and screen-reader labels preserve terminal focus and navigation. Status updates never steal desktop focus.
- Isolated installed proof uses a real working/input-needed/completed workflow plus missing/stale/out-of-order signals; unavailable integration degrades visibly without blocking or terminating work.
- Hook/config installation is explicit and reversible, preserves user configuration and remains quiet outside Eon.

## Scope boundary
No adoption of Zellij or Herdr as another multiplexer, screen-scraping authority, agent launch/resume framework, token dashboard, chat UI, MCP, remote orchestration or automatic focus changes. Popups and broader eon-pxn horizons are related, not hard prerequisites.

## Planning status
Recorded in the user-authorized planning-only batch on 2026-09-09. No implementation, contract-index edit, dependency adoption, runtime refresh or proof advancement is authorized by this record; select the issue and settle its named contract choices before implementation.

title: Settle the agent attention source and contract for Claude and Codex
description:
## Why

`eon-agent-sidebar-yx8` requires an approved non-epic child before implementation and says to
"first settle one provider-backed workflow and its contract". Lucca put the agent attention
sidebar in 1.0 on 2026-10-20 (competitors Herdr, Rex and Nova already show agent status).
The hard part is a trustworthy state source, not the rail.

## Plan agreed 2026-10-20

Two slices after this one: (1) the attention state pipeline for Claude and Codex launched in
the tab's Agent popup, shown as a working / needs-input / done / unknown marker on tab headers;
(2) the sidebar rail with jump-to-agent. Eon launches the Agent popup itself, so it already knows
which pane holds an agent; start there.

## Scope

In: the reference gate from `eon-agent-sidebar-yx8` (Nova, zj-radar, Herdr at pinned revisions:
producer events, stale-state handling, jump behavior, licenses); the provider mechanisms (Claude
hooks, Codex notify) and how they are installed explicitly and reversibly; the proposed contract
additions to EON-C8/EON-C10 and VEN-C8, the EONW revision if any, and the change to the
`venus/` rule that puts sidebars outside Venus (edit `venus/.agent-protocols.local.md` and
render, never `venus/AGENTS.md` directly).
Out: implementation code.

## Acceptance

- The bead records the reference gate (sources, revisions, kept constraints, rejected
  approaches) and a contract proposal Lucca approves.
- The two implementation beads below are updated with the approved contract.

## Verification

Planning route: beads state and changed Markdown paths; render/check the agent-protocol import
if the Venus rule changes (`starcompass check-consumer`).

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Research record, 2026-10-21 (Claude session; Lucca asked for research only, nothing approved). Copy of ~/pjs/refs/agent-sidebar-research/DESIGN.md; per-source reports and clones under ~/pjs/refs/.

# Agent sidebar: research and design proposal (eon-agent-sidebar-yx8.1)

Research for the decision bead `eon-agent-sidebar-yx8.1`, done 2026-10-21 against Eon `edge`
`cd1f4cf`. Nothing here is approved yet: every decision below is a recommendation that waits for
Lucca. The per-source reports sit next to this file (`research-*.md`), and clones live in
`~/pjs/refs/`.

## 1. Summary

- **Hashimoto's protocol is OSC 7501, the Program Status Protocol** (Superlogical; draft rev 0.4,
  2026-10-10). The program *reports* its state to the terminal through the PTY, and the terminal
  stores the records. Nothing can query or read a record back; the only exchange is a support
  probe (`OSC 7501;?`).
- **Both of Lucca's agents already emit it with no hooks and no config edits.**
  - **Codex 0.163.0** (installed) emits `idle|working|blocked` on any TTY; 0.164 adds `done`,
    `error` and `kind`.
  - **Claude Code ≥ 2.1.295** emits `working|blocked(kind)|done|error`, but only after the
    terminal answers its probe before DA1. The installed version, 2.1.293, is too old.
- **That changes the plan.** The state source becomes "Orbit reads OSC 7501", not "install hooks".
  It is provider-neutral; Pi, OpenCode, Grok, Crush and Herdr reportedly speak it too.
- **Main obstacle: getting 7501 into Orbit.** Ghostty's library parses it from `a4aacd91`
  (2026-10-06), but Eon's Ghostty pin is from 2026-07, about 1,700 commits behind. That bump
  needs Zig 0.17 and breaks parts of the C ABI Orbit uses.
  - Recommendation: for 1.0, Orbit scans for OSC 7501 itself in its Rust host, with an exit
    condition to switch to libghostty's callback once the pin moves. (D2)
- **Sidebar shape:** one key toggles open ↔ closed, always one press. "Small" is not a third
  toggle state:
  - With horizontal tabs, the Eon Bar *is* the small mode: tab index plus an attention mark.
  - A later "vertical tabs" layout moves the tabs into the sidebar. Only there does closing
    collapse to an icon rail instead of hiding.

## 2. What the references do

| | Layout | Toggle | State source | "Done" clearing |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Herdr** `herdrdev/herdr@143bf5fd` (Apache-2.0) | Sidebar = workspaces (≈ Eon tabs) + all agents; separate per-workspace tab bar without state | `prefix+b` expanded ↔ collapsed; setting `sidebar_collapsed_mode = compact\|hidden` | Screen-manifest scraping for Claude/Codex (fallback = idle, so blocked can show idle); hooks only report session id; socket report API with `seq` for other agents | done = finished-and-unseen, cleared when the tab is viewed with window focus |
| **Rex** (closed; docs `llms-full.txt` sha256 `fc17b069…`) | Horizontal tabs; "vertical tabs already work" (mitchellh, 2026-08-04); `client.sidebar.toggle` | on/off only documented | OSC 7501 natively, no inference | terminal decides; badges on unfocused tabs, picker badge; "priority inbox" planned |
| **zj-radar** `0b167260` / Nova pin `3ad74c18` (MIT) | Pinned 32-col left pane; no collapse of its own; Nova toggles via `Alt Shift H` by swapping 32→1 col | n/a | Claude plugin hooks + Codex `hooks.json`, `zellij pipe` JSON, no seq | explicit ✓ ack; done clears on new event / prompt return / close; focus is not ack |
| **Nova** `3325ef5d` (Apache-2.0) | Deleted activity from tab labels (TAB-ACTIVITY-REMOVAL-001) "because of stale markers" | — | consented `yzx radar-setup` | — |
| **cmux, Warp, Zed, VS Code, browsers, agent-deck, workmux, Conductor, Nimbalyst** (see `research-ux-survey.md`) | Either vertical tabs *replace* the strip (Warp, Firefox, Edge, cmux), or an agent list sits at a different level beside tabs (Zed, VS Code, Conductor). None shows the same list twice. | Always one key, one press for show/hide; compact rail is a separate key or setting; **no product cycles 3 states on one key** | hooks, OSC 9/99/777 | clear on focus; needs-input clears only when the agent resumes |

Lessons kept:

- **One state owner with thin views.** Nova and Radar learned this from per-tab plugin cost and
  from the smart-tabs polling meltdown.
- **Shape + colour, never colour alone** (WCAG 1.4.1). Herdr's default dots and zj-radar's
  waiting/error pair both break this.
- **Bounded, deadline'd producers.** Radar once crashed a session with EMFILE.
- **Explicit acknowledgement semantics.** "Done" is a finished-and-unseen fact, not a provider
  state.
- **A one-key jump to the next agent needing attention.** Herdr leaves it unbound; cmux,
  workmux and Conductor ship one.

Lessons rejected:

- **Screen scraping as authority.** Herdr's Claude rules changed about 10 times in 3 months and
  can show blocked as idle.
- **Rules fetched at runtime from a vendor site.**
- **Hooks that rewrite agents' settings**, which cause Codex trust re-approval churn.
- **The trailing-`?` heuristic.**
- **Event-order trust without sequence numbers.**

Nova's stale-tab-marker lesson came from writing activity *into tab names* through a plugin. Eon
recomputes marks from one snapshot on every 250 ms poll, so that failure class does not apply.
The rule that survives: never write status into tab *names*.

## 3. Decisions, each with a recommendation

### D1. State source

- **Recommended:** OSC 7501 only, read by Orbit. Install no hooks and edit no agent config.
  Terminals that never report show no state; the Agent popup shows "status unavailable" (D8).
- **Alternatives:**
  - Claude `--settings` hooks + Codex `-c notify`. This needs no Ghostty work, but it creates a
    second owner of the same state and only covers Eon-launched agents.
  - Herdr-style scraping. Rejected by the epic.
- **Why:** both agents already emit 7501, it needs zero user config, it is provider-neutral via
  `app=`, and it is the standard Rex, Zellij main and libghostty are converging on.
- **Requirements for users:**
  - Claude ≥ 2.1.295. Lucca's profile has 2.1.293, so update it.
  - Codex ≥ 0.163, which is installed. Codex `done`/`error` need 0.164, and Eon covers the gap
    in D4.
  - Agents inside tmux report nothing. Zellij support exists only on unreleased main. Document
    both.

### D2. How OSC 7501 reaches Orbit

- **Recommended for 1.0:** a small Orbit-host pre-scanner.
  - A bounded byte state machine finds `ESC ] 7501 ; … (BEL|ESC \)` in PTY output before the
    bytes go to libghostty, with a 4096-byte cap.
  - On `?` it writes the support reply to the PTY immediately, so the reply precedes
    libghostty's DA1 answer.
  - Otherwise it parses `key=value` pairs per spec rev 0.4.
  - Libghostty ignores the unknown OSC at the current pin, so there is no double handling.
  - **Exit condition:** replace the scanner with `GHOSTTY_TERMINAL_OPT_PROGRAM_STATUS` when the
    Ghostty pin passes `8c425a7b` (rev 0.4 plus id/length validation).
- **Alternative:** bump Ghostty to ≥ `8c425a7b` now. This needs Zig 0.17 (not in pinned
  nixpkgs) and libghostty-rs master with breaking changes and no 7501 wrapper. The ABI changes
  touch `terminal_new`, scrollback budget (ORB-C8), the clipboard reply (ORB-C11) and
  `mode_get/set`, so every ORB-C real-PTY check must be re-proved.
- **Why:** the bump is a multi-week, high-risk dependency slice unrelated to the sidebar. The
  scanner is about 200 lines, owned by the terminal-state owner, and red/green testable with
  recorded Claude/Codex output.
- Both options are consequential shapes needing a reference record. The scanner adds no
  dependency.

### D3. Who owns what

**Recommended:**

- **Orbit host** owns the raw records per terminal, applying spec limits and lifetime rules:
  - limits: ≤ 256 records with least-recently-updated eviction, 4096-byte cap, bidi/control
    characters stripped from `title`/`msg`;
  - `state=clear`, and `clear` on RIS;
  - drop `working`/`blocked` when the child exits, or when the PTY foreground process group
    returns to the shell (`tcgetpgrp == child`). This stands in for OSC 133 `A`, which Eon's
    shells don't reliably emit. It is a lifetime rule from the spec, not a state inference.
- **Orbit management Status (ORB-C13 v2)** returns a bounded summary: the most urgent record,
  counts, and a per-terminal report sequence. Eon Runtime already holds a management lease per
  terminal. Leave ORBS and ORB-C3 alone, because Venus only observes visible panes.
- **Eon Runtime** owns normalization, the finished/unseen bit, tab rollup, sidebar visibility
  and navigation. It projects an optional bounded `attention` on EONW `Pane` and `Popup`
  (EONW v13). Venus keeps polling `Inspect` every 250 ms, so EON-C10's "no event stream"
  holds.
- **Venus** renders tab marks and the sidebar from the snapshot and sends actions. It never
  interprets providers.

### D4. Normalized states, priority, glyphs

**Recommended**, in priority order:

| Eon state | From the record | Glyph | Colour role |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| needs input | `blocked` (+ `kind` permission/question/auth) | ◆ | amber, bold |
| error | `error` | ✕ | red |
| finished | `done`, **or** a `working → idle` transition (covers Codex 0.163), and not yet seen | ✓ | green |
| working | `working` (+ `progress`) | spinner (static ⠿ when the animation is off) | accent |
| idle | `idle`, or finished and seen | ○ | dim |
| unavailable | Agent popup with no record | · | dim |

- The tab rollup is the highest-priority state among the tab's panes and popups.
- Labels carry the state word for screen readers, e.g. "Needs input: Claude in tab 3, eon".

### D5. Acknowledgement ("seen")

- **Recommended:** Eon Runtime marks a finished/error record seen when its exact terminal
  becomes the focused target: the selected pane of the active tab, or the shown popup. Eon
  already knows this through `FocusId` and `InvokePopup`.
- A new `working` report resets the record. Needs-input never clears by viewing; only the
  agent's next report clears it.
- **Accepted gap for 1.0:** Eon does not know desktop window focus. A done agent in the active
  tab is marked seen even while Eon is behind another window. Venus could later send
  window-focus with its poll.
- **Alternatives:**
  - Clear on input to the terminal (Orbit-owned; it matches the spec's example). Users who read
    the result without typing keep a stale ✓.
  - An explicit ✓ click (Radar). Extra work for every finish.

### D6. Sidebar states and the toggle-key problem

**Recommended:**

- **Two runtime states, open and closed, and one key: `Alt+Shift+H`** (free today; it matches
  Nova muscle memory and a left-edge sidebar). It is always one press to either state.
- **"Small" is not a toggle state with horizontal tabs.** The Eon Bar already shows each tab's
  index, name and attention mark, which is exactly what a small rail would show. A rail beside
  the bar would duplicate it.
- **"Off" is a setting**, `[sidebar] enabled = false`. It removes the sidebar and frees
  `Alt+Shift+H`, while tab marks in the bar stay.
- **Later "vertical tabs" layout (post-1.0):** `[tabs] position = "sidebar"` removes the tab
  pills from the Eon Bar, and the sidebar becomes the tab list.
  - The same key then toggles full ↔ compact rail (index + mark + glyph).
  - Tabs may never be fully hidden in this layout; that is the Firefox/Herdr pattern of one key
    with a setting choosing the pair.
- **Rejected:** a 3-state cycle on one key, which no surveyed product does. A second key for
  "small" is unnecessary.

### D7. Tabs in the Eon Bar vs the sidebar

- **Recommended for 1.0:** keep horizontal tabs, which hold project identity and navigation.
  The sidebar lists **agents grouped by tab**:
  - group header `3  eon`, then one row per reporting terminal;
  - tabs without agents are omitted;
  - the sidebar is an attention inbox, not a second tab strip.
- Later, vertical tabs *replace* the bar's tabs rather than duplicating them (D6). This matches
  the evidence: no surveyed product shows both, and Rex supports both layouts.

### D8. Row content

**Recommended:** in each row:

- glyph;
- app name (`claude-code` shown as Claude, `codex` as Codex, others verbatim but sanitized);
- the record `title` if present, else the pane's cwd leaf;
- age since the last change ("4m");
- for needs input, a second line with the sanitized, single-line, truncated `msg`
  (e.g. "Allow Bash: cargo test?");
- subagent child records folded into "+2 subagents" under their parent.

Also:

- The Agent popup of every tab appears even without a record, as "status unavailable". This
  makes old Claude and other unsupported agents visible and honest.
- **Order:** stable tab order. Priority comes from the jump key (D9), so rows never reshuffle
  under the pointer.
- **Not in 1.0:** git branch, tokens, cost, chat preview.

### D9. Navigation

**Recommended:**

- Click or `Enter` on a row jumps to the exact pane (`FocusId`) or popup (`InvokePopup`).
  Arrows traverse rows, `Esc` returns to the terminal, and `F6` cycles into the sidebar.
- **New key `Alt+Shift+U`** ("unread", as in cmux; free today) jumps to the next terminal
  needing attention, ordered needs input → error → finished, oldest first.
  - Repeated presses walk the queue.
  - It works with the sidebar closed.
- Status updates never move focus or open the sidebar.

### D10. Layout behaviour

**Recommended:**

- Left side, pushes the columns (no overlay). Fixed width of about 28 cells in 1.0; column
  resizing stays out of Venus scope.
- Default **closed** on first run, so terminals keep full width and the bar marks already
  announce state. The visibility choice is remembered per window as Eon workspace state.
  - Alternative: open by default, for discoverability in an agent-focused product.
- Below a minimum terminal width, the sidebar auto-hides without changing the stored choice
  (VS Code's narrow-window pattern).
- Opening or closing it causes one PTY resize. That is accepted.

### D11. Eon Bar

- **Recommended:** tab pills gain the rollup glyph before the label, e.g. `◆ 3  eon`.
  - The accessible name says the state.
  - Width priority is unchanged: the glyph is part of the tab identity and yields last.
- **Close `eon-agent-attention-eon-bar-jm0` as superseded:** per-tab marks plus `Alt+Shift+U`
  cover its "1 needs input" chip, and jm0 explicitly forbade per-tab marks, which yx8.2 needs.

### D12. Out of scope for 1.0

- Notifications and sound (`eon-iwmz` stays separate and consumes the same state).
- Hooks fallback.
- OSC 133 shell integration.
- The Ghostty bump.
- Vertical tabs.
- Remote or MCP.
- Automatic focus.

## 4. Contract changes to approve (IDs free as of 2026-10-21)

- **ORB-C15 Program status records (new):**
  - scanning, the probe reply before DA1, the bounded store, lifetime rules and sanitization;
  - fixtures from recorded real Claude 2.1.306 / Codex 0.163 output plus malformed, oversized,
    split-chunk and out-of-order input.
- **ORB-C13:** management v2 `Status` gains the bounded attention summary.
- **EON-C31 Agent attention (new):**
  - normalization, finished/seen, rollup, the EONW v13 fields (under EON-C10), sidebar
    visibility state and `[sidebar]` config;
  - the jump-next action and `Alt+Shift+U`;
  - unavailable/unsupported behaviour.
- **EON-C21 / VEN-C21:** allow the tab attention glyph; both now exclude agent status.
- **VEN-C29 Agent sidebar (new):** rendering, traversal, AccessKit labels, narrow-window
  behaviour and no focus theft.
- **Venus rule:** remove "sidebars" from the excluded list in `venus/.agent-protocols.local.md`
  for an Eon-authored sidebar, then render with `starcompass`.

## 5. Proposed bead split (small beads; replaces yx8.2/yx8.3 bodies after approval)

1. **yx8.1 (this):** approve D1–D12 and the contract text.
2. **Spike: 7501 in Orbit.**
   - A pre-scanner prototype answers the probe.
   - Prove that real Claude ≥ 2.1.295 and Codex 0.163 report through Orbit in an isolated
     session; record their bytes as fixtures.
   - Blocks 3.
3. **Orbit records:** ORB-C15 store and lifetime, plus the ORB-C13 v2 Status summary.
4. **Runtime projection:** EON-C31 normalization, seen, rollup, EONW v13.
5. **Eon Bar tab marks** (rewritten yx8.2): Venus glyph and accessibility, plus the EON-C21 and
   VEN-C21 amendment.
6. **Sidebar** (rewritten yx8.3): open/closed, `Alt+Shift+H`, `[sidebar]` config, rows,
   traversal, jump.
7. **Jump-next attention:** `Alt+Shift+U` and the action. Could fold into 6 if small.
8. **Deferred:** vertical-tabs layout with compact rail.
9. **Deferred:** Ghostty ≥ `8c425a7b` bump; delete the scanner (the D2 exit condition).
10. Close jm0 as superseded.

## 6. Pinned evidence

- **OSC 7501 spec:** https://www.superlogical.com/rex/docs/build/program-status (rev 0.4,
  2026-10-10); announcement https://mitchellh.com/writing/program-status-osc7501.
- **Ghostty:**
  - 7501 parsing `a4aacd918ba9e79929ff608034c60a4341773ef0` (#14560);
  - rev 0.4 `9cd19b40d` (#14630);
  - validation `8c425a7bd` (#14793);
  - Eon pin `a887df42` (flake.nix:31).
- **libghostty-rs:** crates.io 0.2.2 (pins `a887df42`), master `0ef80413` (pins `3425025e`, no
  7501).
- **Codex:**
  - `rust-v0.163.0` = `83086188ae0614bd882818ff1aa23f3194962012`,
    `codex-rs/tui/src/terminal_program_status.rs:236`;
  - done/error/kind in #54114 `dec54912` (0.164.0-alpha.1+);
  - clone `~/pjs/refs/codex-0163`.
- **Claude Code:**
  - CHANGELOG 2.1.295 "Added Program Status Protocol (OSC 7501) support";
  - 2.1.306 bundle: probe `ESC]7501;?BEL` followed by DA1, 2000 ms deadline, reports
    `state=…:app=claude-code[:id][:kind][:progress][:title][:msg]`.
- **Herdr:** `143bf5fd4781d164260c63fe28e7dc08054ad32f`, clone `~/pjs/refs/herdr`.
- **zj-radar:** local `0b1672606ca118f6241df687889142c8b52d03fe`, bead pin `1666268`, Nova pins
  `3ad74c18e44cf97cdd8c6ea9121f93c5c7135dd0`.
- **Nova:** `3325ef5df0f86251a03ecac64d2187ba9506d4b9`. nova-bar:
  `4199371380a99892b50bee3e1e6243ad4b16fa5f`.
- **tmux:** `6f655f48` drops 7501. **Zellij:** main `bfcdf7ac` (#5734, unreleased) handles it;
  0.45.1 drops it.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Lucca, 2026-10-21, on the research record above:
- Accepted: D1 (OSC 7501 only, read by Orbit), D3 (owners), D4 (states/priority/glyphs), D5 (seen on focus), D6 (one key, open/closed; off is a setting; small is not a toggle state), D7 (keep bar tabs; sidebar = agents grouped by tab; vertical tabs later replace bar tabs), D10 (left, push, ~28 cells, closed until the user first opens it, remembered).
- D2 changed: bump Ghostty rather than add an Orbit pre-scanner. Route through orb-ze3 (deferred "adopt a qualifying libghostty release"; also brings key-release fix bd647035 and the semantic-prompt API). Constraints found: Ghostty >= 8c425a7bd needs Zig 0.17 (pinned nixpkgs has 0.16); libghostty-rs 0.2.2 pins a887df42 and master (0ef80413) has no program-status wrapper; ABI changes touch terminal_new, scrollback budget (ORB-C8), clipboard reply (ORB-C11), mode_get/set. Plan: spike first, then the bump as its own proven slice, then 7501.

# Contract proposal for the agent attention sidebar (eon-agent-sidebar-yx8.1)

Draft 15, 2026-10-21, revised after fourteen fresh-eyes reviews against `edge` `2e4a914`.

- **Approval:** Lucca approves this text before anything lands. Each contract enters its index
  as Planned in the slice that first implements it, and becomes Proven in the slice that proves
  it.
- **IDs:** ORB-C15, EON-C31 and VEN-C29 were free at `2e4a914`. Recheck them when landing.
- **Decisions:** those referenced here (D1–D11, Alt+G, tab markers) are recorded on yx8.1.
- **Status:** every new contract starts as **Planned**.
- **Open choices:** eight items need Lucca, marked **[Q1]** to **[Q8]** and collected at the end.

---

## ORB-C15 — Program status records (new, Orbit)

- **Status:** Planned. Needs eon-a9tr, including its semantic-prompt binding.
- **Consumer:**
  - a program in an Orbit terminal that speaks the Program Status Protocol (OSC 7501, rev 0.4),
    such as Claude Code ≥ 2.1.295 or Codex ≥ 0.163;
  - Eon Runtime, which reads the records through management (ORB-C13).
- **Trigger:**
  - PTY output carries `OSC 7501 ; ? ST` or a report `OSC 7501 ; pairs ST`;
  - an OSC 133 `A` prompt mark arrives;
  - the PTY foreground process group changes;
  - the child exits;
  - RIS arrives, as libghostty reports it (eon-a9tr.1 settles whether through the program-status CLEAR or the reset option);
  - a management `ProgramStatus` request arrives.
- **Result:**
  - **Probe.** While Orbit sets libghostty's program-status callback and `WRITE_PTY`, the library
    answers the probe. The answer is written before the reply to a DA1 query that follows the
    probe.
  - **Reports.** They follow spec rev 0.4, with these deviations (a third, CLI read-back, is under
    EON-C31 **[Q8]**):
    - the foreground-group drop under Lifetime. Eon adds it under D3; it is not a spec event.
    - child exit ends the Orbit run, so `done` and `error` records end with it, although the
      spec says they survive process exit. EON-C31 accepts this.
    - An unknown key, or a malformed pair, is skipped; the rest of the report applies.
    - Orbit discards the whole report if any of these holds:
      - it breaks a spec limit:
        - key over 16 bytes;
        - `msg` over 2732 encoded or 2048 decoded bytes;
        - `title` over 256 encoded or 192 decoded bytes;
        - `app` over 32 bytes;
        - `id` over 128 bytes, a segment over 32, or more than 8 levels;
      - a base64 value fails to decode;
      - the decoded `title` or `msg` contains control characters;
      - the `id` is invalid (Orbit never falls back to the root record);
      - `state` is missing or unknown.
    - Some invalid values are treated as absent and do not discard the report: an `app` with
      characters outside its set, an unknown `kind`, and an out-of-range `progress`.
    - Orbit disarms bidi-override and invisible format characters.
    - A valid report replaces the record with its `id`; an absent `id` means the root record.
      - A record holds `state` (`idle | working | done | blocked | error`), `kind` (blocked
        only), `progress`, `app`, `title` and `msg`.
      - A record without `app` inherits the `app` of its nearest ancestor when Orbit answers.
    - OSC 7501 is the sole source of program status, so no precedence among sources applies.
  - **Clearing.** `state=clear:id=X` removes X and every record beneath it. `state=clear` with no
    `id` removes all records, and so does RIS.
  - **Neutral per-record facts.** Orbit derives no attention meaning.
    - **Update sequence.** One counter per terminal increases by one on each accepted report,
      clear and lifetime drop, so the Runtime sees removals.
    - **Change sequence.** The update sequence at which the record's state last changed.
      Creating a record counts as a change. A same-state re-report keeps it, because the spec
      allows duplicates. Codex itself sends `state=clear` before re-reporting after a handoff or
      suspend, so its re-report creates a new record.
    - **Previous state.** The state before that change, or none for a newly created record.
    - **Ages.** The Orbit-monotonic ages, in milliseconds, of the last update and of the last
      state change.
  - **Lifetime.** Orbit removes `working` and `blocked` records on any of these:
    - the child exits. This ends the run and every record with it (a deviation listed under
      Reports), so it needs no Bend decision;
    - an OSC 133 `A` prompt mark arrives;
    - the PTY foreground process group *changes to* the child's own group from a different group.
      - This applies only on terminals that have never sent OSC 133 `A`. The latch is
        permanent, so one nested `nu` in a Bash pane turns the rule off for the rest of that
        run. This is accepted for 1.0.
      - It is edge-triggered. It is sampled at the start of each PTY read, before that read's
        bytes are processed, and on each `ProgramStatus` request. A report in the same read
        therefore comes after the edge and survives it.
      - A popup tool that *is* the child never triggers it while it keeps the foreground group.
      - With prompt marks (Nushell emits them natively), a shell script that reports its own work
        (`status working; rsync …; status done`) keeps its record until the prompt.
      - Without prompt marks (Eon's managed Bash today), `status working; make; make test` loses
        its `working` record when a job returns to the shell. Sampling can miss a short return,
        so this happens unpredictably. This is accepted for 1.0. Shipping OSC 133 for Bash is a
        follow-up after eon-a9tr.

    **Stream order.** Lifetime drops apply in byte-stream order. A prompt mark or foreground edge
    drops only the `working`/`blocked` records that exist at that point in the stream; a report
    that arrives after it, even in the same PTY read, survives. However bead 1 shapes the facts
    sent to Bend, they must preserve this order.

    `done`, `error` and `idle` records remain until the program replaces or clears them, or the
    run ends. Orbit uses no expiry and no heartbeat. The spec forbids requiring re-sends and
    leaves to the terminal when to stop showing `done` or `error`; EON-C31 decides that.
  - **ProgramStatus reply.** One request gets one reply of at most 4 KiB.
    - It carries the record count, the terminal's latest update sequence, and the count of
      records omitted for size.
    - It includes as many records as fit, about 7 at full field sizes, in a neutral fill order:
      - first `blocked`, `error` and `done`, the spec states that wait on the user, most recent
        change first;
      - then every other record, most recent change first. Previous state plays no part, so the
        fill order stays independent of how EON-C31 defines finished.
    - Each record carries:
      - its full `id`, up to 128 bytes. Orbit never truncates it, because it is identity.
      - `state`, `kind` and `progress`;
      - `app` (≤ 32 bytes), `title` (≤ 96) and `msg` (≤ 256);
      - its update sequence, change sequence, previous state and both ages.
    - Orbit truncates only `title` and `msg`, at UTF-8 boundaries.
- **Important failures:**
  - Orbit ignores any report over 4096 bytes.
  - Past 256 records, Orbit evicts the least-recently-updated one.
  - Status work never blocks PTY reading. A report causes no frame or metadata publication
    beyond what the PTY read that carried it already causes (ORB-C4 unchanged).
- **Owner:**
  - **Orbit host** owns raw observation and mechanism, and `orbit/docs/HOST.md` is amended to
    name this store. It:
    - parses reports (through libghostty);
    - stores records with their neutral facts;
    - applies the spec's eviction;
    - assembles reply content by the fixed fill order, as it assembles Status fields today.
  - **Bend worker** decides from one-line numeric facts:
    - whether a prompt mark or foreground-group edge drops the `working`/`blocked` records;
    - whether to answer a `ProgramStatus` request or refuse it with Busy. It never defers.
      - Orbit targets an answer within 250 ms.
      - The hard cap is the existing worker-stall bound: the host counts the worker as stalled
        after 2 s (orbit/docs/HOST.md:46-51).
      - The Runtime's own 250 ms poll deadline covers a miss, which only makes the attention
        stale.

    Bend also holds the state that its decisions read: whether the terminal has ever sent
    OSC 133 `A`, and the last sampled foreground group. The host keeps no session state that Bend
    decides from (orbit/docs/HOST.md:202-203).

    These decisions get laws in LAWS.bend, proofs in PROOF.bend and a `boundary.schema` update.
    Lucca sees each new or changed law before its proof is relied on (orbit/AGENTS.md). Bead 1
    settles the exact fact shape. This refines D3, which had put the lifetime rules in the host
    **[Q5]**.
  - **The program** owns what its report means.
- **Consumes:** libghostty-vt at the eon-a9tr revision, with its program-status and
  semantic-prompt option (and the reset option if eon-a9tr.1 needs it); ORB-C2's terminal authority.
- **Boundary:**
  - no inference from the screen, process names or elapsed silence;
  - no change to ORBS or ORB-C3;
  - no event stream, no reading back by the program, and no notifications;
  - no OSC 9, 99 or 777 handling;
  - no records across Orbit restarts.
- **Portability:** neutral. `tcgetpgrp` and the PTY are POSIX; macOS stays deferred.

## ORB-C13 — amendment

- **Result.** "Management carries only bounded identity, live status, and explicit Stop" becomes
  "…bounded identity, live status, the ORB-C15 `ProgramStatus` request, and explicit Stop".
  Requests on a lease stay one at a time.
- **Bounds.** ORB-C13's "Bounds are explicit" list (orbit/docs/CONTRACTS.md:684-689) is
  unchanged. A `ProgramStatus` answer is capped by the existing 2 s worker-stall bound
  (orbit/docs/HOST.md:46-51), and 250 ms is only a target.
- **Generation.** Management generation 2 is a breaking orbit-protocol change. Its known
  consumers are:
  - Eon Runtime, and Eon's `eon/crates/eon/tests/workspace_control.rs`;
  - Orbit's own `tests/lifecycle.rs`, `tests/real_pty/management_lease.rs`,
    `management_record.rs`, `descendant_exit.rs` and `observer_finish.rs`;
  - `orbit/crates/protocol/tests/management.rs`.

  Venus does not use management.
  The change also gets an `orbit/CHANGELOG.md` entry. **[Q1]** decides compatibility.
- **Consumes.** ORB-C13's "management v1" line becomes v2. The same slice amends three more
  references:
  - EON-C11's "management v1";
  - EON-C15's "management v1";
  - ORB-C13's proof line "Eon consumes management v1".

---

## EON-C31 — Agent attention (new, Eon)

- **Status:** Planned.
- **Consumer:** One person supervising coding agents across the tabs of one full-Eon window.
  eonbase has no poller and no sidebar; its `sidebar` is `Off`.
- **Trigger:**
  - the attention poller's timer fires;
  - focus moves to a pane or popup;
  - a Venus attaches;
  - an attention action arrives: `FocusAttention`, `NextAttention`, `PreviousAttention` or
    `ToggleSidebar`.
- **Result:**
  - **Polling.** A Runtime attention poller runs off the request path, on its own timer, at no
    more than 2 Hz.
    - It polls only pane and popup terminals, never directory-picker sessions.
    - It polls peers concurrently, each with a 250 ms deadline.
    - Each lease has exactly one reader and at most one request in flight. The EOF probe and
      Stop first drain or await an in-flight `ProgramStatus` reply, so no reply is ever read as
      an unsolicited or stop result.
    - Replies are tagged by type, so a late reply can never be mistaken for a Stop result.
    - A slow poll never drops or replaces a lease.
    - A Stop or EOF probe that waits for an in-flight reply is delayed by Orbit's answer time:
      normally well under 250 ms, and never beyond the existing 2 s worker-stall bound. There is
      no new failure path.
    - A peer that misses the poll deadline only goes stale. Its lease stays as it is.
    - A lease with a Stop pending is not polled.
    - Inspect and actions read only the poller's latest cached result and never wait on a peer.
  - **Stale.** A missed deadline keeps the last good result, which avoids flicker.
    - Once a terminal's last good result is older than 3 s, its attention is marked stale. It is
      shown in its last state, dimmed, with "status stale" in its accessible name, and it stays
      in the Alt+G queue.
    - Stale clears on the next good reply.
    - When the run ends or the target is removed, the attention is removed.
  - **Identity and time.** State is keyed by the exact Orbit run ID plus record `id`.
    - A new run starts empty.
    - A reply whose update sequence is lower than the cached one for the same run is discarded.
    - On first sight of a (run, `id`, change sequence), the Runtime fixes the change time on its
      own monotonic clock: receipt time minus the change age. Polls never move that time, so
      queue keys and row ages stay stable across polls, and ages from different terminals share
      one clock.
  - **Raise.** Attention meaning is derived here, not in Orbit. A record *raises* at its change
    sequence in these cases:
    - it changes into `done` or `error`, including being created in them;
    - it changes into `idle` from `working`, as D4 decided.

    An `idle` from `blocked` (for example, a declined permission prompt) does not raise **[Q6]**.
    - An `idle` from `done` keeps the cached raise of that `done`. If the Runtime never saw the
      `done`, the `idle` raises at its own change sequence.
    - An `idle` from `error` does not raise: the program has moved on.
    - Same-state re-reports never raise.
    - An `idle` raised from `working` covers Codex 0.163, which has no `done`. It also counts an
      interrupted turn as finished, which D4 accepted.
  - **Normalization.** Each record maps to one state, in this priority order:

    | State | Source |
    | --- | --- |
    | needs input | `blocked`, with its `kind` |
    | error | `error` whose raise is unseen |
    | finished | `done`, or a raised `idle`, whose raise is unseen |
    | working | `working`, with `progress` |
    | idle | any other `idle`; or `done`/`error`/raised `idle` whose raise has been seen |
    | unavailable | an Agent popup with no records |

  - **Seen.** Seen is keyed by (run, `id`, raise). A raise becomes seen when a Venus is attached
    and its exact terminal is the focused target (the selected pane of the active tab, or the
    shown popup) at one of these moments:
    - focus arrives on that terminal, including via `FocusAttention` to a terminal that
      already has focus;
    - a new raise arrives while that terminal is focused;
    - a Venus attaches while that terminal is focused.

    A focus action applies seen to the raise cached when the action was handled, and a poll in
    flight cannot undo it. Needs input is never cleared by viewing.
  - **Rollup.** A tab's rollup is the highest-priority state among its terminals. A stale
    terminal counts with its last state, and its badge is dimmed.
  - **Sidebar visibility [Q3].** The Runtime keeps one value per window: `Open` (the default),
    `Closed`, or `Off` (when `[sidebar] enabled = false`).
    - The value lives in memory while the supervisor runs, so it survives detach and reattach.
      It resets to `Open` after a supervisor restart.
    - `ToggleSidebar` flips `Open` and `Closed`. A toggle, rather than a set, cannot race a stale
      snapshot. In `Off` it is a no-op.
  - **EONW v14** (amends EON-C10) adds:
    - an optional `attention` on `Pane` and `Popup`, holding:
      - `state`: the *normalized* EON-C31 state of the terminal's most urgent record, one of
        needs input, error, finished, working, idle or unavailable. Venus never normalizes,
        and seen is already folded into this state;
      - from that record: kind, progress, `app`, `title` and `msg`;
      - its `changed_at`, as wall-clock Unix milliseconds. The Runtime computes it once from its
        fixed change time, so the snapshot does not change as time passes, and Venus computes
        the age shown;
      - the stale flag;
      - the count of other records.

      For unavailable, only `state` is present.

      Its bounds are those of the ORB-C15 reply: `app` ≤ 32, `title` ≤ 96 and `msg` ≤ 256
      bytes. A whole snapshot still fits the 2 MiB frame.
    - `attention_rollup` on `Tab`;
    - `sidebar` (`Open | Closed | Off`) on `Snapshot`;
    - the actions `ToggleSidebar`, `FocusAttention { tab, target }`, `NextAttention` and
      `PreviousAttention`;
    - the same fields in the CLI JSON, except that **[Q8]** decides whether `title` and `msg`
      are included. If v14 ships in 1.0, EON-C28 makes the included fields stable 1.x fields.
      - A program inside an Eon terminal can run `eon workspace --json`, so it can read its own
        records and other terminals' `title`/`msg`. The spec says records are never sent back.
        This is a third deviation **[Q8]**.
  - **FocusAttention** is what sidebar rows send. It goes to the exact pane or popup under the
    covered-target rule. Rows do not use `FocusId`, because `FocusId` dismisses a shown popup.
    - Its target names the exact pane id, or the exact popup instance (the `expected_instance`
      used by `InvokePopup`).
    - A stale target is rejected as an EONW action rejection, with no fallback, as EON-C10
      target safety requires (docs/CONTRACTS.md:744-751). Venus shows it as a VEN-C8 notice.
  - **NextAttention and PreviousAttention.**
    - **The queue** holds every terminal whose most urgent record is needs input, an unseen
      error, or finished. Its total order is:
      1. class: needs input, then error, then finished;
      2. the fixed change time, oldest first (for needs input, the time it entered `blocked`;
         otherwise the raise's time);
      3. tab position;
      4. terminal position.
    - **The cursor.** The Runtime keeps one cursor per window: the order key of the last jump
      target.
      - `NextAttention` goes to the first entry whose key is greater than the cursor, wrapping
        to the smallest key. `PreviousAttention` does the reverse.
      - The cursor advances even when the jump only selected a tab.
      - The cursor keeps working after its entry leaves the queue, so repeated presses walk
        every entry.
      - **Reset [Q7].** The cursor resets, so the next press starts at the front of the queue,
        in two cases:
        - focus moves by any other means;
        - an entry of a higher class than the cursor's appears, for example a needs input
          while the cursor sits on a finished entry.

        This keeps D9's rule that the most urgent work comes first.
    - Seen raises leave the queue.
    - An empty queue is EON-C10's unchanged-snapshot no-op.
  - **Covered-target rule.** It applies to `FocusAttention` and both queue actions, for pane and
    popup targets alike. If the target's tab is showing a popup that is not the target:
    - a keep-alive popup is hidden (it survives), and then the target is focused or shown;
    - a transient popup (one whose dismissal stops its terminal, docs/CONTRACTS.md:734), or a
      pending directory picker, is left alone. The action only selects the tab and never stops a
      terminal.
  - **Configuration.** `[sidebar] enabled = true` is the default. Setting it to `false` sets
    `sidebar` to `Off`:
    - Venus shows no sidebar;
    - Alt+Shift+H is unbound;
    - tab markers always show.
- **Important failures:**
  - **No attention.** Before its first good reply, a peer gives no attention. A terminal without
    records also gives none, except an Agent popup, which gives unavailable, including before its
    first good reply. After the first good
    reply, slowness only makes a peer stale. The poller never guesses a state.
  - **Failures stay contained.** A poll failure never blocks Inspect or actions. It delays Stop
    by at most Orbit's answer time, which is capped by the existing 2 s worker-stall bound.
  - **Removed targets.** A removed pane or popup's records disappear with it.
  - **Restarts.**
    - A supervisor restart or recovery loses the seen bits and visibility, so `done` and `error`
      records reappear unseen. This is accepted for 1.0.
    - A provider that restarts in the same pane replaces its records with new reports.
  - **Leftover idle records.** An agent killed by SIGKILL in a shell pane can leave an `idle`
    record, which shows as an idle row until the run ends or the record is replaced. The spec
    allows dropping `idle` on exit, but keeping it lets a finish raise. This is accepted for 1.0.
  - **Finishes that vanish with their record.** An unseen finish disappears with its record in
    these cases:
    - Claude Code clears its records on exit, and Codex clears its record on exit, on suspend,
      and when it hands the terminal to another program such as an editor;
    - in the Agent popup the agent is the PTY child, so its exit ends the Orbit run, and its
      `done` and `error` records end with the run, even though the spec says they survive
      process exit;
    - the ProgramStatus reply holds about 7 records, so a terminal with 7 or more `blocked`,
      `error` or `done` records (Claude subagents, for example) can crowd out a raised `idle`
      from the reply. That finish never shows.

    All three are accepted for 1.0. In the first two the user is usually interacting with that
    terminal; the third needs an unusual number of records.
  - **Window focus.** Eon does not know desktop window focus, so a raise in the focused terminal
    counts as seen even while the window sits behind another app. This is accepted under D5.
  - **Detached windows.** While no Venus is attached, nothing becomes seen. The supervisor knows
    this because it holds the control stream (VEN-C14).
  - **Older peers.** If EONW v14 ships after 1.0, EON-C28's previous-generation Stop test covers
    the predecessor generation.
  - **No side effects.** Status changes never change focus, open the sidebar, raise the window or
    send terminal input.
- **Owner:**
  - **Eon Runtime** owns the poller, raise, normalization, seen, rollup, the queue and cursor,
    sidebar visibility and `[sidebar]` configuration.
  - **Orbit** owns the records and their neutral facts.
  - **Venus** owns presentation and hiding for width (VEN-C29).
- **Consumes:** ORB-C15, ORB-C13 generation 2, EON-C8 topology, and EON-C10 (EONW v14, still
  request and response, with no event stream).
- **Boundary:**
  - no hooks and no edits to agent configuration;
  - no provider parsing; the Runtime passes `app` through unchanged, and Venus maps it for
    display (VEN-C29);
  - no notifications or sound (eon-iwmz consumes this later);
  - no agent launching, orchestration or worktrees;
  - agents under tmux report nothing; this is documented.

## EON-C10 — amendment

- **Accepted bytes.** "Accepted v13 bytes" and "v13 bytes" (docs/CONTRACTS.md:723) become v14,
  with the EON-C31 fields and actions.
- **Provider selection.** "Commands, provider selection, cwd and lifetime … never cross EONW"
  (:759-760) keeps its rule and gains one clarifying sentence: the `app` that crosses is the
  program's own report, not Eon's provider selection.
- **Status report text.** "No terminal contents cross EONW" (docs/CONTRACTS.md:756) and the
  Boundary's "terminal content" (:719) each gain one exception. A program's own status report
  text (`app`, `title`, `msg`) may cross. It is not screen content: Orbit has validated,
  sanitized and bounded it under ORB-C15.
- **Other v13 references.** These become v14 in the same slice:
  - EON-C10's own "Consumes: Current EONW v13" (docs/CONTRACTS.md:716);
  - EON-C8's "Consumes: Current EONW v13" (docs/CONTRACTS.md:499). EON-C8's Boundary exclusion
    of "provider state" (:501-506) gains the same exception for the EON-C31 attention values;
  - the EONW v13 reference at venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md:8. The ":1132" reference is ORBS v13,
    not EONW, and stays.
- **Component graph.** It requires EONW 14.

## EON-C21 / VEN-C21 — amendment

- **Boundary.** EON-C21's "agent status, polling, configuration, protocol change" and VEN-C21's
  "status/quota data … configuration … polling … protocol change" each gain one exception: the
  EON-C31 tab attention marker, read from the EONW v14 snapshot that Venus already polls.
- **VEN-C21 Result, added.** These rules apply while the agent sidebar is not visible (`Closed`,
  `Off`, or hidden for width):
  - every tab whose rollup is needs input, error, finished or working shows a corner badge (◆,
    ✕, ✓, or a spinner), the active tab included. A stale tab's badge is dimmed;
  - Eon has no animation-off setting, so the spinner always animates. Under AP-PERF-001 it
    repaints at no more than 5 Hz, and only the badge;
  - the badge changes neither the tab's width nor its label text;
  - with tab overflow, the scroll edge shows the most urgent hidden badge;
  - a tab's accessible name appends its state, for example "Tab 3 of 5, site, needs input";
  - clicking a badged tab behaves like any tab click **[Q2]**.

## VEN-C29 — Agent sidebar (new, Venus)

- **Status:** Planned.
- **Consumer:** One person using a Venus window attached to a full Eon workspace. The sidebar
  itself needs `sidebar` other than `Off`. Alt+G and Alt+Shift+G work under `Off` too.
- **Trigger:**
  - Alt+Shift+H;
  - a new EONW v14 snapshot;
  - the pointer, keyboard or AccessKit acts on the sidebar;
  - the window is resized.
- **Result:**
  - **Visibility.** The sidebar shows while the snapshot's `sidebar` is `Open`, on every tab of
    the window. Alt+Shift+H sends `ToggleSidebar`, so one press always flips the choice
    between open and closed. That shows on screen unless the window is too narrow (see Layout).
  - **Layout.**
    - A left sidebar 28 cells wide sits below the Eon Bar **[Q4]**. The bar keeps its full
      width, its controls and its drag region.
    - It pushes the tab columns, so opening or closing it resizes the visible terminals once.
    - Venus hides it when the total remaining column area would drop below 80 cells. This leaves
      `sidebar` unchanged, and VEN-C21's markers then show.
    - Above that threshold, individual columns may still drop below 40 cells, as VEN-C8 already
      allows when the window shrinks.
    - While the sidebar is hidden for width, Alt+Shift+H still toggles `sidebar`. The new value
      applies once the window is wide enough.
    - **VEN-C8 and VEN-C18 amendment.** While the sidebar is visible:
      - the side gaps and the 40-column CreateColumn check are measured from the content area
        to its right;
      - the first tab pill keeps its window-edge position, and its alignment with the first
        card is suspended;
      - VEN-C18's popup card area is that content area, so popups never cover the sidebar.
  - **Contents.**
    - It lists, in tab order, only tabs that have attention or an Agent popup.
    - Each such tab gets a header (`3  site`), followed by one row per terminal with attention.
    - A row shows:
      - the state glyph;
      - the app icon or name. Venus maps `app=claude-code` to the Claude splat (VEN-C26) and
        `app=codex` to the Codex mark (VEN-C22), and shows any other `app` verbatim;
      - the record title, or the tab's directory leaf when there is none (EONW panes carry no
        cwd);
      - the age;
      - the source terminal, by the pane's `pN` identity as in pane headers and AccessKit
        (VEN-C8), or, for a popup, its catalog label such as "Agent popup", because the spec says shown
        status should name its source terminal.
    - A stale record is dimmed and labelled "status stale".
    - A needs-input row adds one plain-text, truncated `msg` line.
    - Other records of a terminal fold into "+N".
    - Rows never reorder by priority.
  - **Navigation.**
    - Activating a row sends `FocusAttention`, and keyboard focus moves to the target
      terminal, or stays on the tab when the covered-target rule only selects the tab. It never
      stops a terminal.
    - F6 cycles Terminal → Sidebar → Tabs → Panes, and skips Sidebar while it is not visible.
      Today F6 cycles Terminal → Tabs → Panes. This amends VEN-C18 and the F6 label in
      `venus/src/application/shortcuts.rs`.
    - Arrows traverse rows, Enter activates and Esc returns focus to the terminal.
    - **Focus rule.** Alt+Shift+H never moves keyboard focus into the sidebar; focus stays on
      the terminal. Keyboard focus returns to the terminal in three cases:
      - the sidebar closes while it holds focus;
      - it is hidden for width while it holds focus;
      - the focused row's target is removed.
    - Alt+G and Alt+Shift+G send `NextAttention` and `PreviousAttention`, whether the sidebar is
      visible or not.
  - **Accessibility.** Each row's accessible name gives the state word, app, tab, source
    terminal and message.
- **Important failures:**
  - With no attention, the sidebar shows an explanatory empty state.
  - The sidebar never takes desktop focus and never changes Orbit state.
  - Record text renders only as plain text, never as markup or links.
- **Owner:**
  - **Venus** owns layout, hiding for width, rendering, input and accessibility.
  - **Eon** owns state, visibility and actions (EON-C31).
- **Attention-only refreshes.** A snapshot that differs only in attention or `sidebar` keeps
  rejected-action notices (VEN-C8) and disturbs no navigation, scroll, attachment or resize, as
  quota-only refreshes already do (VEN-C22). VEN-C8 and VEN-C22 gain this clause, and so does
  EON-C8's "a changed workspace retires the notice" (docs/CONTRACTS.md:494-496).
- **Consumes:** EONW v14 and the VEN-C22 and VEN-C26 icons. VEN-C22's boundary ("no …
  provider parsing … click action, focus target") gains one exception: the Codex mark may sit
  in clickable, focusable sidebar rows. VEN-C26's "No … module" boundary and its "static
  no-action behavior" (venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md:1350-1353) gain the same exception, for reuse
  of the Claude splat in those rows.
- **Boundary:**
  - no interpretation of provider events, terminal output or process data, except mapping the
    reported `app` identifier to an icon;
  - no drag resizing, compact rail or vertical tabs;
  - no previews, no priority reordering and no notifications.

These replace the yx8.2 and yx8.3 bodies.

## Open choices for Lucca

- **[Q1] Management generation 2: a breaking bump with no compatibility window?**
  - A new package never adopts Orbit runs from an older one anyway. EON-C15 recovers only the
    same exact generation, and EON-C11 rules out PTY handoff. Old runs stay with their own
    supervisor, so the bump loses no terminals.
  - A compatibility window would never be exercised, and orbit/docs/CONTRACTS.md disfavors
    such windows.
  - orbit/AGENTS.md still requires your explicit choice for a breaking change.
  - Alternative: keep management v1 and add `ProgramStatus` under a new component generation
    tag. The handshake already requires exact component and management generations, so this
    works too, but it hides a wire change behind an unchanged version.
  - **Recommendation:** breaking bump, no window.
- **[Q2] What clicking a badged tab does.**
  - **Recommendation:** select the tab, as today. Alt+G is the jump to the exact terminal.
- **[Q3] Where sidebar visibility lives.**
  - **Recommendation:** in Runtime memory per window, as drafted.
    - It honors D3 (Runtime owns visibility). It honors D10 ("remembered") only while the
      supervisor runs: a supervisor restart or recovery resets the window to `Open`.
    - It survives detach and reattach, and it costs one toggle action plus a field v14 already
      needs. Nothing is written to disk.
  - Alternative: Venus-local, like the hints footer. That is simpler, but every reattach starts
    open again.
  - Alternative: persist the choice per window across a supervisor restart or recovery. This is
    the strongest reading of D10's "remembered" wording, since recovery keeps the window and its
    terminals (EON-C15). It crosses EON-C10's "durable restoration" exclusion
    (docs/CONTRACTS.md:719) and needs durable per-window state.
  - Alternative: store the per-window choice in the saved workspace state that
    `eon-reboot-restore-im8y` (in 1.0 scope) will add. This is the cheapest way to honor D10
    fully, once im8y exists.
  - Recommendation refined: Runtime memory now, and move it into im8y's saved state when im8y
    lands.
- **[Q4] Where the sidebar sits.**
  - **Recommendation:** below the Eon Bar. The bar keeps its full width, controls and drag
    region; the first tab pill's alignment with the first card is suspended while the sidebar
    is open.
  - Alternative: full window height, with the Eon Bar starting to its right. This keeps the
    alignment but moves the tabs, controls and drag region.

- **[Q5] Refinements of D3, D8 and D9.**
  - **Lifetime rules.** D3 put them in the Orbit host. orbit/AGENTS.md says the Bend worker
    decides every answer, so this draft gives Bend the drop decisions and the answer-or-refuse
    decision, with laws you review.
  - **Status shape.** D3 had management `Status` return a bounded summary around the most urgent
    record. This draft adds a separate `ProgramStatus` request instead:
    - it returns up to about 7 records with neutral facts;
    - urgency, raise and normalization move to the Runtime, so Orbit derives no attention
      meaning.
  - **Row contents.** D8 was proposed but never accepted as a whole; only the icon reuse and
    "any reporter is listed" were. Approving this text approves D8's row contents, the
    unavailable rows and the "+N" fold. One change from D8: it said rows fall back to the
    pane's cwd leaf, but EONW panes carry no cwd, so rows fall back to the tab's directory
    leaf.
  - **Row jumps.** D9 had rows jump through `FocusId` or `InvokePopup`. `FocusId` dismisses a
    shown popup, and dismissing a transient popup stops its terminal. So rows send a new
    `FocusAttention` under the covered-target rule:
    - keep-alive popups are hidden;
    - when a transient popup or a pending picker is in the way, the jump only selects the tab.
  - **Recommendation:** accept all four. The first is required by the repository rule; the
    others keep ownership single and never stop a terminal.
- **[Q6] Is a declined permission prompt "finished"?** D4 makes finished come from `done` or
  `working → idle`. A `blocked → idle` change, such as pressing Esc on Codex's approval, would
  otherwise show ✓. Either answer leaves ORB-C15, including its fill order, as it is; only EON-C31's
  raise rule changes.
  - **Recommendation:** no. A declined prompt shows idle, because you just interacted with that
    agent.
- **[Q8] Status text readable through `eon workspace --json`.** Programs in Eon terminals can
  run `eon`, so they could read every terminal's `title` and `msg`, for example another tab's
  permission prompt. The spec says records are never sent back.
  - **Recommendation:** accept the deviation, but keep `title` and `msg` out of the CLI JSON.
    Only state and `app` go there, so EON-C28 does not freeze agent text.
    - Venus still gets the text over EONW.
    - Any same-UID process could read raw EONW anyway, so this narrows exposure rather than
      sealing it.
  - Alternative: include them for scripting, and accept the wider read-back.
- **[Q7] When the Alt+G cursor resets.** Without a reset, a new needs input can wait behind
  later finished entries until the walk wraps.
  - **Recommendation:** reset the cursor when focus moves by other means, or when an entry of a
    higher class appears.
  - Alternative: never reset, a simple round-robin.

Approving this text also approves the agent sidebar as a new Venus module. venus/AGENTS.md says
"A new Venus module is product scope".

Draft 15 (approved), 2026-10-21, revised after fourteen fresh-eyes reviews against `edge` `2e4a914`.
