---

## ORB-C15 — Program status records (new, Orbit)

- **Status:** Planned. Needs eon-a9tr, including its semantic-prompt binding.
- **Consumer:**
  - a program in an Orbit terminal that speaks the Program Status Protocol (OSC 7501, rev 0.4),
    such as Claude Code ≥ 2.1.295 or Codex ≥ 0.163;
  - Eon Runtime, which reads the records through management (ORB-C13).
- **Trigger:**
  - PTY output carries `OSC 7501 ; ? ST` or a report `OSC 7501 ; pairs ST`;
  - an OSC 133 `A` prompt mark arrives;
  - the PTY foreground process group changes;
  - the child exits;
  - RIS arrives, which libghostty reports as a program-status CLEAR with an empty id (eon-a9tr.1
    confirms this);
  - a management `ProgramStatus` request arrives.
- **Result:**
  - **Probe.** While Orbit sets libghostty's program-status callback and `WRITE_PTY`, the library
    answers the probe. The answer is written before the reply to a DA1 query that follows the
    probe.
  - **Deviations from spec rev 0.4.** There are three:
    - the foreground-group drop under Lifetime. Eon adds it under D3; it is not a spec event.
    - child exit ends the Orbit run, so `done` and `error` records end with it, although the
      spec says they survive process exit. EON-C31 accepts this.
    - CLI read-back, covered under EON-C31 **[Q8]**.
  - **Reports.** Everything else follows spec rev 0.4:
    - An unknown key, or a malformed pair, is skipped; the rest of the report applies.
    - Orbit discards the whole report if any of these holds:
      - it breaks a spec limit:
        - key over 16 bytes;
        - `msg` over 2732 encoded or 2048 decoded bytes;
        - `title` over 256 encoded or 192 decoded bytes;
        - `app` over 32 bytes;
        - `id` over 128 bytes, a segment over 32, or more than 8 levels;
      - a base64 value fails to decode;
      - the decoded `title` or `msg` contains control characters;
      - the `id` is invalid (Orbit never falls back to the root record);
      - `state` is missing or unknown.
    - Some invalid values are treated as absent and do not discard the report: an `app` with
      characters outside its set, an unknown `kind`, and an out-of-range `progress`.
    - Orbit disarms bidi-override and invisible format characters.
    - A valid report replaces the record with its `id`; an absent `id` means the root record.
      - A record holds `state` (`idle | working | done | blocked | error`), `kind` (blocked
        only), `progress`, `app`, `title` and `msg`.
      - A record without `app` inherits the `app` of its nearest ancestor when Orbit answers.
    - OSC 7501 is the sole source of program status, so no precedence among sources applies.
  - **Clearing.** `state=clear:id=X` removes X and every record beneath it. `state=clear` with no
    `id` removes all records, and so does RIS.
  - **Neutral per-record facts.** Orbit derives no attention meaning.
    - **Update sequence.** One counter per terminal increases by one on each accepted report,
      clear and lifetime drop, so the Runtime sees removals.
    - **Change sequence.** The update sequence at which the record's state last changed.
      Creating a record counts as a change. A same-state re-report keeps it, since the spec
      implies re-reports are harmless. Codex itself sends `state=clear` before re-reporting after a handoff or
      suspend, so its re-report creates a new record.
    - **Previous state.** The state before that change, or none for a newly created record.
    - **Ages.** The Orbit-monotonic ages, in milliseconds, of the last update and of the last
      state change.
  - **Lifetime.** Orbit removes `working` and `blocked` records on any of these:
    - the child exits. This ends the run and every record with it (a deviation listed under
      Deviations), so it needs no Bend decision;
    - an OSC 133 `A` prompt mark arrives;
    - the PTY foreground process group *changes to* the child's own group from a different group.
      - This applies only on terminals that have never sent OSC 133 `A`. The latch is
        permanent, so one nested `nu` in a Bash pane turns the rule off for the rest of that
        run. This is accepted for 1.0.
      - It is edge-triggered. It is sampled at the start of each PTY read, before that read's
        bytes are processed, and on each `ProgramStatus` request. A report in the same read
        therefore comes after the edge and survives it.
      - A popup tool that *is* the child never triggers it while it keeps the foreground group.
      - With prompt marks (Nushell emits them natively), a shell script that reports its own work
        (`status working; rsync …; status done`) keeps its record until the prompt.
      - Without prompt marks (Eon's managed Bash today), `status working; make; make test` loses
        its `working` record when a job returns to the shell. Sampling can miss a short return,
        so this happens unpredictably. This is accepted for 1.0. Shipping OSC 133 for Bash is a
        follow-up after eon-a9tr.

    **Stream order.** Lifetime drops apply in byte-stream order. A prompt mark or foreground edge
    drops only the `working`/`blocked` records that exist at that point in the stream; a report
    that arrives after it, even in the same PTY read, survives. However bead 1 shapes the facts
    sent to Bend, they must preserve this order.

    `done`, `error` and `idle` records remain until the program replaces or clears them, or the
    run ends. Orbit uses no expiry and no heartbeat. The spec forbids requiring re-sends and
    leaves to the terminal when to stop showing `done` or `error`; EON-C31 decides that.
  - **ProgramStatus reply.** One request gets one reply of at most 4 KiB.
    - It carries the record count, the terminal's latest update sequence, and the count of
      records omitted for size.
    - It includes as many records as fit, about 7 at full field sizes, in a neutral fill order:
      - first `blocked`, `error` and `done`, the states that persist or ask for the user, most recent
        change first;
      - then every other record, most recent change first. Previous state plays no part, so the
        fill order stays independent of how EON-C31 defines finished.
    - Each record carries:
      - its full `id`, up to 128 bytes. Orbit never truncates it, because it is identity.
      - `state`, `kind` and `progress`;
      - `app` (≤ 32 bytes), `title` (≤ 96) and `msg` (≤ 256);
      - its update sequence, change sequence, previous state and both ages.
    - Orbit truncates only `title` and `msg`, at UTF-8 boundaries.
- **Important failures:**
  - Orbit ignores any report over 4096 bytes.
  - Past 256 records, Orbit evicts the least-recently-updated one.
  - Status work never blocks PTY reading. A report causes no frame or metadata publication
    beyond what the PTY read that carried it already causes (ORB-C4 unchanged).
- **Owner:**
  - **Orbit host** owns raw observation and mechanism, and `orbit/docs/HOST.md` is amended to
    name this store. It:
    - parses reports (through libghostty);
    - stores records with their neutral facts;
    - applies the spec's eviction;
    - assembles reply content by the fixed fill order, as it assembles Status fields today.
  - **Bend worker** decides from one-line numeric facts:
    - whether a prompt mark or foreground-group edge drops the `working`/`blocked` records;
    - whether to answer a `ProgramStatus` request or refuse it with Busy. It never defers.
      - Orbit targets an answer within 250 ms.
      - The worker-stall bound (orbit/docs/HOST.md:46-51) caps each fact/decision exchange at
        2 s, and a `ProgramStatus` answer needs at most two exchanges: a foreground-edge drop
        decision, then the answer. Host turn scheduling (HOST.md:42-44) can add to that.
      - A stalled worker ends that terminal's run (HOST.md:22-31), exactly as it does today.
      - Bead 2 measures the real answer time under PTY load.
      - The Runtime's own 250 ms poll deadline covers a miss. A miss keeps the last good result,
        and attention becomes stale only after 3 s without a good reply.

    Bend also holds the state that its decisions read: whether the terminal has ever sent
    OSC 133 `A`, and the last sampled foreground group. The host keeps no session state that Bend
    decides from (orbit/docs/HOST.md:202-203).

    These decisions get laws in LAWS.bend, proofs in PROOF.bend and a `boundary.schema` update.
    Lucca sees each new or changed law before its proof is relied on (orbit/AGENTS.md). Bead 1
    settles the exact fact shape. This refines D3, which had put the lifetime rules in the host
    **[Q5]**.
  - **The program** owns what its report means.
- **Consumes:** libghostty-vt at the eon-a9tr revision, with its program-status and
  semantic-prompt option; ORB-C2's terminal authority.
- **Boundary:**
  - no inference from the screen, process names or elapsed silence;
  - no change to ORBS or ORB-C3;
  - no event stream, no reading back by the program in Orbit, and no notifications;
  - no OSC 9, 99 or 777 handling;
  - no records across Orbit restarts.
- **Portability:** neutral. `tcgetpgrp` and the PTY are POSIX; macOS stays deferred.

## EON-C31 — Agent attention (new, Eon)

- **Status:** Planned.
- **Consumer:** One person supervising coding agents across the tabs of one full-Eon window.
  eonbase has no poller and no sidebar; its `sidebar` is `Off`.
- **Trigger:**
  - the attention poller's timer fires;
  - focus moves to a pane or popup;
  - a Venus attaches;
  - an attention action arrives: `FocusAttention`, `NextAttention`, `PreviousAttention` or
    `ToggleSidebar`.
- **Result:**
  - **Polling.** A Runtime attention poller runs off the request path, on its own timer, at no
    more than 2 Hz.
    - It polls only pane and popup terminals, never directory-picker sessions.
    - It polls peers concurrently, each with a 250 ms deadline.
    - Each lease has exactly one reader and at most one request in flight. The EOF probe and
      Stop first drain or await an in-flight `ProgramStatus` reply, so no reply is ever read as
      an unsolicited or stop result.
    - Replies are tagged by type, so a late reply can never be mistaken for a Stop result.
    - A slow poll never drops or replaces a lease.
    - A Stop or EOF probe that waits for an in-flight reply is delayed by Orbit's answer time:
      normally well under 250 ms, and at most two worker exchanges plus host turn scheduling.
      There is no new failure path. Bead 2 asserts this under PTY load.
    - A Busy refusal counts as a missed poll deadline.
    - A peer that misses the poll deadline only goes stale. Its lease stays as it is.
    - A lease with a Stop pending is not polled.
    - Inspect and actions read only the poller's latest cached result and never wait on a peer.
  - **Stale.** A missed deadline keeps the last good result, which avoids flicker.
    - Once a terminal's last good result is older than 3 s, its attention is marked stale. It is
      shown in its last state, dimmed, with "status stale" in its accessible name, and it stays
      in the Alt+G queue.
    - Stale clears on the next good reply.
    - When the run ends or the target is removed, the attention is removed.
  - **Identity and time.** State is keyed by the exact Orbit run ID plus record `id`.
    - A new run starts empty.
    - A reply whose update sequence is lower than the cached one for the same run is discarded.
    - On first sight of a (run, `id`, change sequence), the Runtime fixes the change time on its
      own monotonic clock: receipt time minus the change age. Polls never move that time, so
      queue keys and row ages stay stable across polls, and ages from different terminals share
      one clock.
  - **Raise.** Attention meaning is derived here, not in Orbit. A record *raises* at its change
    sequence in these cases:
    - it changes into `done` or `error`, including being created in them;
    - it changes into `idle` from `working`, as D4 decided.

    An `idle` from `blocked` (for example, a declined permission prompt) does not raise **[Q6]**.
    - An `idle` from `done` keeps the cached raise of that `done`. If the Runtime never saw the
      `done`, the `idle` raises at its own change sequence.
    - An `idle` from `error` does not raise: the program has moved on.
    - Same-state re-reports never raise.
    - An `idle` raised from `working` covers Codex 0.163, which has no `done`. It also counts an
      interrupted turn as finished, which D4 accepted.
  - **Normalization.** Each record maps to one state, in this priority order:

    | State | Source |
    | --- | --- |
    | needs input | `blocked`, with its `kind` |
    | error | `error` whose raise is unseen |
    | finished | `done`, or a raised `idle`, whose raise is unseen |
    | working | `working`, with `progress` |
    | idle | any other `idle`; or `done`/`error`/raised `idle` whose raise has been seen |
    | unavailable | an Agent popup with no records |

  - **Seen.** Seen is keyed by (run, `id`, raise). A raise becomes seen when a Venus is attached
    and its exact terminal is the focused target (the selected pane of the active tab, or the
    shown popup) at one of these moments:
    - focus arrives on that terminal, including via `FocusAttention` to a terminal that
      already has focus;
    - a new raise arrives while that terminal is focused;
    - a Venus attaches while that terminal is focused.

    A focus action applies seen to the raise cached when the action was handled, and a poll in
    flight cannot undo it. Needs input is never cleared by viewing.
  - **Rollup.** A tab's rollup is the highest-priority state among its terminals. A stale
    terminal counts with its last state, and its badge is dimmed.
  - **Sidebar visibility [Q3].** The Runtime keeps one value per window: `Open` (the default),
    `Closed`, or `Off` (when `[sidebar] enabled = false`).
    - The value lives in memory while the supervisor runs, so it survives detach and reattach.
      It resets to `Open` after a supervisor restart.
    - `ToggleSidebar` flips `Open` and `Closed`. A toggle, rather than a set, cannot race a stale
      snapshot. In `Off` it is a no-op.
  - **EONW v14** (amends EON-C10) adds:
    - an optional `attention` on `Pane` and `Popup`, holding:
      - `state`: the *normalized* EON-C31 state of the terminal's most urgent record, one of
        needs input, error, finished, working, idle or unavailable. Venus never normalizes,
        and seen is already folded into this state;
      - from that record: kind, progress, `app`, `title` and `msg`;
      - its `changed_at`, as wall-clock Unix milliseconds. The Runtime computes it once from its
        fixed change time, so the snapshot does not change as time passes, and Venus computes
        the age shown;
      - the stale flag;
      - the count of other records.

      For unavailable, only `state` is present.

      Its bounds are those of the ORB-C15 reply: `app` ≤ 32, `title` ≤ 96 and `msg` ≤ 256
      bytes. A whole snapshot still fits the 2 MiB frame.
    - `attention_rollup` on `Tab`;
    - `sidebar` (`Open | Closed | Off`) on `Snapshot`;
    - the actions `ToggleSidebar`, `FocusAttention { tab, target }`, `NextAttention` and
      `PreviousAttention`;
    - **CLI JSON.** It carries exactly three things (Q8):
      - `attention: { state, app }` on panes and popups;
      - `attention_rollup` on tabs;
      - `sidebar` on the snapshot.

      It leaves out `kind`, `progress`, `title`, `msg`, `changed_at`, the stale flag and the
      record count. v14 ships in 1.0, because yx8.9 gates eon-igae.7, .8 and .11, so EON-C28
      freezes exactly these fields.
      - A program inside an Eon terminal can run `eon workspace`, so it can read every
        terminal's attention `state` and `app`. `title` and `msg` never appear through `eon workspace`, though
        any same-UID process can read them over raw EONW (Q8). The spec says
        records are never sent back, so this is a third deviation **[Q8]**.
  - **FocusAttention** is what sidebar rows send. It goes to the exact pane or popup under the
    covered-target rule. Rows do not use `FocusId`, because `FocusId` dismisses a shown popup.
    - Its target names the exact pane id, or the exact popup instance (the `expected_instance`
      used by `InvokePopup`).
    - A stale target is rejected as an EONW action rejection, with no fallback, as EON-C10
      target safety requires (docs/CONTRACTS.md:744-751). Venus shows it as a VEN-C8 notice.
  - **NextAttention and PreviousAttention.**
    - **The queue** holds every terminal whose most urgent record is needs input, an unseen
      error, or finished. Its total order is:
      1. class: needs input, then error, then finished;
      2. the fixed change time, oldest first (for needs input, the time it entered `blocked`;
         otherwise the raise's time);
      3. tab position;
      4. terminal position.
    - **The cursor.** The Runtime keeps one cursor per window: the order key of the last jump
      target.
      - `NextAttention` goes to the first entry whose key is greater than the cursor, wrapping
        to the smallest key. `PreviousAttention` does the reverse.
      - The cursor advances even when the jump only selected a tab.
      - The cursor keeps working after its entry leaves the queue, so repeated presses walk
        every entry.
      - **Reset [Q7].** The cursor resets, so the next press starts at the front of the queue,
        in two cases:
        - focus moves by any other means;
        - an entry of a higher class than the cursor's appears, for example a needs input
          while the cursor sits on a finished entry.

        This keeps D9's rule that the most urgent work comes first.
    - Seen raises leave the queue.
    - An empty queue is EON-C10's unchanged-snapshot no-op.
  - **Covered-target rule.** It applies to `FocusAttention` and both queue actions, for pane and
    popup targets alike. If the target's tab is showing a popup that is not the target:
    - a keep-alive popup is hidden (it survives), and then the target is focused or shown;
    - a transient popup (one whose dismissal stops its terminal, docs/CONTRACTS.md:734), or a
      pending directory picker, is left alone. The action only selects the tab and never stops a
      terminal.
  - **Configuration.** `[sidebar] enabled = true` is the default. Setting it to `false` sets
    `sidebar` to `Off`:
    - Venus shows no sidebar;
    - Alt+Shift+H is unbound;
    - tab markers always show.
- **Important failures:**
  - **No attention.** Before its first good reply, a peer gives no attention. A terminal without
    records also gives none, except an Agent popup, which gives unavailable, including before its
    first good reply. After the first good
    reply, slowness only makes a peer stale. The poller never guesses a state.
  - **Failures stay contained.** A poll failure never blocks Inspect or actions. It delays Stop
    by at most Orbit's answer time for one in-flight request (see Polling).
  - **Removed targets.** A removed pane or popup's records disappear with it.
  - **Restarts.**
    - A supervisor restart or recovery loses the seen bits and visibility, so `done` and `error`
      records reappear unseen. This is accepted for 1.0.
    - A provider that restarts in the same pane replaces its records with new reports.
  - **Leftover idle records.** An agent killed by SIGKILL in a shell pane can leave an `idle`
    record, which shows as an idle row until the run ends or the record is replaced. The spec
    allows dropping `idle` on exit, but keeping it lets a finish raise. This is accepted for 1.0.
  - **Finishes that vanish with their record.** An unseen finish disappears with its record in
    these cases:
    - Claude Code clears its records on exit, and Codex clears its record on exit, on suspend,
      and when it hands the terminal to another program such as an editor;
    - in the Agent popup the agent is the PTY child, so its exit ends the Orbit run, and its
      `done` and `error` records end with the run, even though the spec says they survive
      process exit;
    - the ProgramStatus reply holds about 7 records, so a terminal with 7 or more `blocked`,
      `error` or `done` records (Claude subagents, for example) can crowd out a raised `idle`
      from the reply. That finish never shows.

    All three are accepted for 1.0. In the first two the user is usually interacting with that
    terminal; the third needs an unusual number of records.
  - **Window focus.** Eon does not know desktop window focus, so a raise in the focused terminal
    counts as seen even while the window sits behind another app. This is accepted under D5.
  - **Detached windows.** While no Venus is attached, nothing becomes seen. The supervisor knows
    this because it holds the control stream (VEN-C14).
  - **Older generations.** The new `eon` treats a still-running v13 generation as incompatible,
    exactly as it has since eon-igae.12.4. Nothing changes here. Bead 4's rollout follows
    igae.12.4's precedent.
  - **No side effects.** Status changes never change focus, open the sidebar, raise the window or
    send terminal input.
- **Owner:**
  - **Eon Runtime** owns the poller, raise, normalization, seen, rollup, the queue and cursor,
    sidebar visibility and `[sidebar]` configuration.
  - **Orbit** owns the records and their neutral facts.
  - **Venus** owns presentation and hiding for width (VEN-C29).
- **Consumes:** ORB-C15, ORB-C13 generation 2, EON-C8 topology, and EON-C10 (EONW v14, still
  request and response, with no event stream).
- **Boundary:**
  - no hooks and no edits to agent configuration;
  - no provider parsing; the Runtime passes `app` through unchanged, and Venus maps it for
    display (VEN-C29);
  - no notifications or sound (eon-iwmz consumes this later);
  - no agent launching, orchestration or worktrees;
  - agents under tmux report nothing; this is documented.

## VEN-C29 — Agent sidebar (new, Venus)

- **Status:** Planned.
- **Consumer:** One person using a Venus window attached to a full Eon workspace. The sidebar
  itself needs `sidebar` other than `Off`. Alt+G and Alt+Shift+G work under `Off` too.
- **Trigger:**
  - Alt+Shift+H;
  - a new EONW v14 snapshot;
  - the pointer, keyboard or AccessKit acts on the sidebar;
  - the window is resized.
- **Result:**
  - **Visibility.** The sidebar shows while the snapshot's `sidebar` is `Open`, on every tab of
    the window. Alt+Shift+H sends `ToggleSidebar`, so one press always flips the choice
    between open and closed. That shows on screen unless the window is too narrow (see Layout).
  - **Layout.**
    - A left sidebar 28 cells wide sits below the Eon Bar **[Q4]**. The bar keeps its full
      width, its controls and its drag region.
    - It pushes the tab columns, so opening or closing it resizes the visible terminals once.
    - Venus hides it when the total remaining column area would drop below 80 cells. This leaves
      `sidebar` unchanged, and VEN-C21's markers then show.
    - Above that threshold, individual columns may still drop below 40 cells, as VEN-C8 already
      allows when the window shrinks.
    - While the sidebar is hidden for width, Alt+Shift+H still toggles `sidebar`. The new value
      applies once the window is wide enough.
    - **VEN-C8 and VEN-C18 amendment.** While the sidebar is visible:
      - the side gaps and the 40-column CreateColumn check are measured from the content area
        to its right;
      - the first tab pill keeps its window-edge position, and its alignment with the first
        card is suspended;
      - VEN-C18's popup card area is that content area, so popups never cover the sidebar.
  - **Contents.**
    - It lists, in tab order, only tabs that have attention or an Agent popup.
    - Each such tab gets a header (`3  site`), followed by one row per terminal with attention.
    - A row shows:
      - the state glyph;
      - the app icon or name. Venus maps `app=claude-code` to the Claude splat (VEN-C26) and
        `app=codex` to the Codex mark (VEN-C22), and shows any other `app` verbatim;
      - the record title, or the tab's directory leaf when there is none (EONW panes carry no
        cwd);
      - the age;
      - the source terminal, by the pane's `pN` identity as in pane headers and AccessKit
        (VEN-C8), or, for a popup, its catalog label such as "Agent popup", because the spec says shown
        status should name its source terminal.
    - A stale record is dimmed and labelled "status stale".
    - A needs-input row adds one plain-text, truncated `msg` line.
    - Other records of a terminal fold into "+N".
    - Rows never reorder by priority.
  - **Navigation.**
    - Activating a row sends `FocusAttention`, and keyboard focus moves to the target
      terminal, or stays on the tab when the covered-target rule only selects the tab. It never
      stops a terminal.
    - F6 cycles Terminal → Sidebar → Tabs → Panes, and skips Sidebar while it is not visible.
      Today F6 cycles Terminal → Tabs → Panes (venus/docs/INTERACTION.md:72-73). This amends that
      order, VEN-C18 and the F6 label in
      `venus/src/application/shortcuts.rs`.
    - Arrows traverse rows, Enter activates and Esc returns focus to the terminal.
    - **Focus rule.** Alt+Shift+H never moves keyboard focus into the sidebar; focus stays on
      the terminal. Keyboard focus returns to the terminal in three cases:
      - the sidebar closes while it holds focus;
      - it is hidden for width while it holds focus;
      - the focused row's target is removed.
    - Alt+G and Alt+Shift+G send `NextAttention` and `PreviousAttention`, whether the sidebar is
      visible or not.
  - **Accessibility.** Each row's accessible name gives the state word, app, tab, source
    terminal and message.
- **Important failures:**
  - With no attention, the sidebar shows an explanatory empty state.
  - The sidebar never takes desktop focus and never changes Orbit state.
  - Record text renders only as plain text, never as markup or links.
- **Owner:**
  - **Venus** owns layout, hiding for width, rendering, input and accessibility.
  - **Eon** owns state, visibility and actions (EON-C31).
- **Attention-only refreshes.** A snapshot that differs only in attention or `sidebar` keeps
  rejected-action notices (VEN-C8) and disturbs no navigation, scroll, attachment or resize, as
  quota-only refreshes already do (VEN-C22). VEN-C8 and VEN-C22 gain this clause, and so does
  EON-C8's "a changed workspace retires the notice" (docs/CONTRACTS.md:494-496).
- **Consumes:** EONW v14 and the VEN-C22 and VEN-C26 icons. VEN-C22's boundary ("no …
  provider parsing … click action, focus target") gains one exception: the Codex mark may sit
  in clickable, focusable sidebar rows. VEN-C26's "No … module" boundary and its "static
  no-action behavior" (venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md:~1314 and :1355) gain the same exception, for reuse
  of the Claude splat in those rows.
- **Boundary:**
  - no interpretation of provider events, terminal output or process data, except mapping the
    reported `app` identifier to an icon;
  - no drag resizing, compact rail or vertical tabs;
  - no previews, no priority reordering and no notifications.

   - eon-igae.7, eon-igae.8 and eon-igae.11 are blocked by this bead rather than by yx8.3,
     so the 1.0 candidate proofs and the EON-C28 freeze include the keys and the CLI JSON.
   - eon-iwmz is blocked by bead 4 rather than yx8.2, since a sound needs only the state.
9. **Other notes for the beads.**
   - Add the semantic-prompt (OSC 133) binding to the acceptance of eon-a9tr.1 and eon-a9tr.2.
     Today a9tr asks only for the program-status callback. The spike also confirms that RIS
     arrives as a program-status CLEAR with an empty id (research-orbit-7501.md:24). No reset
     binding is needed: the "ever sent OSC 133 `A`" latch stays permanent for the run, RIS
     included.
   - Recheck "EONW v14" when landing. Other open Eon Bar beads may take that version first.
   - Bead 2 also renames or retires Orbit's `--management-v1` CLI flag, and updates every use
     of it across `orbit/`, `runtime/` and their docs (`rg -- --management-v1`).
   - Beads 1, 2, 5 and 7 each record a portability disposition. Bead 1 is neutral, since
     `tcgetpgrp` is POSIX; the others are neutral too.
   - Older "EONW v7" mentions in EON-C17, C18, C20, C21, C23 and C24 stay as historical
     consumption records, as venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md:9-11 treats them. Only contracts this work
     changes move to v14.
   - The poller is a new Runtime mechanism, `attention`, beside `quota`. EON-C4's count of
     "nine runtime mechanisms" (docs/CONTRACTS.md:232, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:285) becomes ten.
   - ORB-C15 enters its index as Planned in bead 1, which first implements it. It becomes Proven
     in bead 2, where its reply text can be proved.
   - Whether `ToggleSidebar` and the attention actions get `eon` CLI commands is left out of
     1.0. They are EONW actions only, so EON-C28 gains no new commands.
   - Within one terminal, ties between records in the same state go to the most recent change.
   - In the AccessKit tree, the sidebar comes after VEN-C21's header and before the panes,
     following the visual order. F6 starts from the terminal and visits Sidebar → Tabs →
     Panes, so the sidebar is the first region away from the terminal.
   - **Q3 follow-up.** eon-reboot-restore-im8y and bead 4 both block eon-igae.7, and either can
     land first. Whichever lands second moves `sidebar` visibility into im8y's saved per-window
     state. Both beads carry this note. That move amends EON-C31's visibility text and needs
     an exception to EON-C10's "durable restoration" exclusion (docs/CONTRACTS.md:719). Since
     im8y's design is still open, that step needs Lucca's sign-off when it lands. Note that
     bead 4 blocks igae.7 only through bead 8.
10. **jm0.** Close as superseded.

## Open choices for Lucca

- **[Q1] Management generation 2: a breaking bump with no compatibility window?**
  - A new package never adopts Orbit runs from an older one anyway. EON-C15 recovers only the
    same exact generation, and EON-C11 rules out PTY handoff. Old runs stay with their own
    supervisor, so the bump loses no terminals.
  - A compatibility window would never be exercised, and orbit/docs/CONTRACTS.md disfavors
    such windows.
  - orbit/AGENTS.md still requires your explicit choice for a breaking change.
  - Alternative: keep management v1 and add `ProgramStatus` under a new component generation
    tag. The handshake already requires exact component and management generations, so this
    works too, but it hides a wire change behind an unchanged version.
  - **Recommendation:** breaking bump, no window.
- **[Q2] What clicking a badged tab does.**
  - **Recommendation:** select the tab, as today. Alt+G is the jump to the exact terminal.
- **[Q3] Where sidebar visibility lives.**
  - **Recommendation:** in Runtime memory per window, as drafted.
    - It honors D3 (Runtime owns visibility). It honors D10 ("remembered") only while the
      supervisor runs: a supervisor restart or recovery resets the window to `Open`.
    - It survives detach and reattach, and it costs one toggle action plus a field v14 already
      needs. Nothing is written to disk.
  - Alternative: Venus-local, like the hints footer. That is simpler, but every reattach starts
    open again.
  - Alternative: persist the choice per window across a supervisor restart or recovery. This is
    the strongest reading of D10's "remembered" wording, since recovery keeps the window and its
    terminals (EON-C15). It crosses EON-C10's "durable restoration" exclusion
    (docs/CONTRACTS.md:719) and needs durable per-window state.
  - Alternative: store the per-window choice in the saved workspace state that
    `eon-reboot-restore-im8y` (in 1.0 scope) will add. This is the cheapest way to honor D10
    fully, once im8y exists.
  - Recommendation refined: Runtime memory now, and move it into im8y's saved state when im8y
    lands.
- **[Q4] Where the sidebar sits.**
  - **Recommendation:** below the Eon Bar. The bar keeps its full width, controls and drag
    region; the first tab pill's alignment with the first card is suspended while the sidebar
    is open.
  - Alternative: full window height, with the Eon Bar starting to its right. This keeps the
    alignment but moves the tabs, controls and drag region.

- **[Q5] Refinements of D3, D8 and D9.**
  - **Lifetime rules.** D3 put them in the Orbit host. orbit/AGENTS.md says the Bend worker
    decides every answer, so this draft gives Bend the drop decisions and the answer-or-refuse
    decision, with laws you review.
  - **Status shape.** D3 had management `Status` return a bounded summary around the most urgent
    record. This draft adds a separate `ProgramStatus` request instead:
    - it returns up to about 7 records with neutral facts;
    - urgency, raise and normalization move to the Runtime, so Orbit derives no attention
      meaning.
  - **Row contents.** D8 was proposed but never accepted as a whole; only the icon reuse and
    "any reporter is listed" were. Approving this text approves D8's row contents, the
    unavailable rows and the "+N" fold. One change from D8: it said rows fall back to the
    pane's cwd leaf, but EONW panes carry no cwd, so rows fall back to the tab's directory
    leaf.
  - **Row jumps.** D9 had rows jump through `FocusId` or `InvokePopup`. `FocusId` dismisses a
    shown popup, and dismissing a transient popup stops its terminal. So rows send a new
    `FocusAttention` under the covered-target rule:
    - keep-alive popups are hidden;
    - when a transient popup or a pending picker is in the way, the jump only selects the tab.
  - **Recommendation:** accept all four. The first is required by the repository rule; the
    others keep ownership single and never stop a terminal.
- **[Q6] Is a declined permission prompt "finished"?** D4 makes finished come from `done` or
  `working → idle`. A `blocked → idle` change, such as pressing Esc on Codex's approval, would
  otherwise show ✓. Either answer leaves ORB-C15, including its fill order, as it is; only EON-C31's
  raise rule changes.
  - **Recommendation:** no. A declined prompt shows idle, because you just interacted with that
    agent.
- **[Q8] Status text readable through `eon workspace --json`.** Programs in Eon terminals can
  run `eon`, so they could read every terminal's `title` and `msg`, for example another tab's
  permission prompt. The spec says records are never sent back.
  - **Recommendation:** accept the deviation, but keep `title` and `msg` out of the CLI JSON.
    Only state and `app` go there, so EON-C28 does not freeze agent text.
    - Venus still gets the text over EONW.
    - Any same-UID process could read raw EONW anyway, so this narrows exposure rather than
      sealing it.
  - Alternative: include them for scripting, and accept the wider read-back.
- **[Q7] When the Alt+G cursor resets.** Without a reset, a new needs input can wait behind
  later finished entries until the walk wraps.
  - **Recommendation:** reset the cursor when focus moves by other means, or when an entry of a
    higher class appears.
  - Alternative: never reset, a simple round-robin.

Approving this text also approves the agent sidebar as a new Venus module. venus/AGENTS.md says
"A new Venus module is product scope".

title: Read ProgramStatus replies on Runtime leases without misreading Stop or EOF
description:
## Why

Lucca split eon-agent-sidebar-yx8.5 in two on 2026-10-22. yx8.5 keeps the Orbit side
(management generation 2 serving `ProgramStatus`). This bead takes the Runtime half: the
one-reader-per-lease change that lets the yx8.6 attention poller send `ProgramStatus` on a lease
without the EOF probe or Stop ever misreading the reply.

**Contract:** EON-C31's Polling rules ("Each lease has exactly one reader and at most one request
in flight. The EOF probe and Stop first drain or await an in-flight `ProgramStatus` reply, so no
reply is ever read as the wrong result"; "A slow poll never drops or replaces a lease"; "A Busy
refusal counts as a missed poll deadline"; "A lease with a Stop pending is not polled"). Approved
on 2026-10-21 (draft 15 on eon-agent-sidebar-yx8.1). No new contract text lands here; EON-C31
enters the index with yx8.6.

## Scope

In scope, in `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/sessions.rs`:
- Per-lease in-flight request state: at most one `ProgramStatus` request, its partial reply
  bytes, and its deadline.
- A non-blocking send and a non-blocking read of the reply, tagged by message type, for the
  yx8.6 poller to call. A reply decodes to the records, or to Busy, which the caller treats as
  a missed deadline.
- `session_finished` (the EOF probe) reads an in-flight reply's bytes into its buffer instead of
  calling them an unsolicited result; bytes with no request in flight stay an error.
- `stop_managed_sessions` awaits an in-flight reply, within the stop deadline, before it writes
  Stop, so Orbit never sees a pipelined request and the Stopped answer is never confused with a
  `ProgramStatus` reply.
- A slow or missed reply never drops or replaces the lease.

Out of scope: the poller, its timer and deadlines, attention meaning (yx8.6), EONW, Venus, and
any Orbit change (yx8.5).

## Acceptance

- A focused test races Stop, and the EOF probe, against an in-flight `ProgramStatus` reply from
  a real Orbit and shows neither misreads it, with a sensitivity check that removing the drain
  makes it fail.
- A test asserts the delay Stop sees while a reply is in flight under PTY load, bounded by
  Orbit's answer time (target 250 ms, never beyond the 2 s worker-stall bound per exchange).
- Existing lifecycle, recovery and stop behaviour is unchanged when no request is in flight.

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test` (Runtime and Eon suites).
- fmt and clippy for eon-runtime.
- Converge plus a Codex review.

## Prerequisites

Blocked by eon-agent-sidebar-yx8.5, which serves `ProgramStatus` over management generation 2.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if one reader per lease needs a Runtime restructuring beyond `sessions.rs` (for example
  moving leases to another thread). Split it out instead.

## Maintenance Notes

Portability disposition: neutral (Unix sockets only). Reference gate: the yx8.1 research and
contract record (comment "Contract proposal, draft 15") covers the poller and reader shape;
record any new comparable read here before code.
close_reason: Profile refreshed with Lucca's go to /nix/store/ckisr53k62ald5ipdhf0fqkg2l86rrai-eon-0.1.1, built from the main tree at b6bb78a, which includes 7267b8a. That is the artifact eon-a9 proved; per its proof there is no observable installed change until yx8.6's poller. Closed by the orchestrator, because eon-a9's session ended in the restart.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Design and harness (eon-3c session 3, 2026-10-22). Reference gate: no new comparable read; the yx8.1 draft 15 record and yx8.5's gate (TUIOS one request in flight per connection; Herdr/Zellij refusal shapes) cover the reader shape.
- RunningSession gains program_status: Option<ProgramStatusRequest{unsent, reply, deadline}> and stop_sent. One step, advance_program_status, finishes the request write and reads the reply without reading past its end (Complete / WouldBlock / Closed). send_program_status (non-blocking; refuses while in flight, after Stop was sent, or after the run ended), read_program_status (Pending / Missed / Reply; Busy and a passed deadline are Missed, a late reply stays in flight until read; EOF leaves it for the EOF probe). session_finished reads an in-flight reply into its buffer, and only bytes after it are unsolicited. stop_managed_sessions awaits an in-flight reply within the stop deadline, then marks stop_sent and writes Stop. A short write is kept and finished, never dropped. No lease is dropped or replaced by a slow poll. The poller API is dead code until yx8.6 (cfg_attr(not(test), expect(dead_code)), the dd8b9ab pattern).
- Real Orbit in tests: leased_orbit uses ORBIT_BIN, else the workspace build's target/debug/yazelix-orbit beside the test binary (Runtime keeps no Cargo dependency on Orbit). The eon package check sets ORBIT_BIN to orbitPackage.
- Finding: a debug Orbit under a yes flood answers once per ~100 s (3 rounds: 102, 105, 115 s), and even Acquire times out if the flood starts before the lease; the release Orbit answers in ~0.1 ms. So the load test is #[ignore]d with a reason and requires ORBIT_BIN; the eon package check runs it with checkFlags --include-ignored (no other ignored tests exist in eon or eon-runtime), like Orbit's real-PTY checks run ignored tests from Nix. The race test runs in eon-test against the debug Orbit.
- Sensitivity: removing Stop's await made the race test fail with 'terminal returned the wrong stop result'; removing the EOF probe's in-flight read made it fail with 'terminal sent an unsolicited management result'.

    - Claude reviewer, who ran the checks: 1 blocking, fixed: a serial drain let one silent Orbit keep Stop from every later terminal. Stop now writes each Stop once that lease's reply is drained, in one non-blocking loop with 1 ms sleeps. Nits: the load-test distribution was lost to capture (now written straight to stderr); the stop_sent guard was untested (now tested).
  - Converge round 1: removed an unreachable TimedOut arm and corrected the ORB-C15 claim in a comment. Round 2: clean, on tree 73be958.
  - Narrow Codex re-check of 69be608..73be958: clean, no nits.
  - Then a mechanical rebase onto EONW v15 (eon-n6ga), changing the import v14 -> v15.

title: Show the agent's session name on sidebar rows
description:
## Why

Lucca decided on 2026-10-22 that sidebar agent rows show the agent's session name (for example
`eon-9a`), so he and the coordinator can tell agents apart. Claude Code never sends that name in
OSC 7501. It sets it only as the terminal window title (OSC 0). Claude Code 2.1.308 sets the title
to `--name`/`/rename`, then its AI session title, then "Claude Code". The format is `✳ eon-b6`,
with a ◐/◑ prefix while busy, and plain `eon-b6` when the terminal speaks OSC 7501.
`CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_TERMINAL_TITLE` turns it off. Orbit already tracks the title
(orbit/src/pty.rs `title_and_directory`) and publishes it to attached clients, but the management
`ProgramStatus` reply (ORB-C15) does not carry it. The Runtime polls only that reply.

**Contracts:** amendments to ORB-C15 (reply content), EON-C31 (attention `name`), EON-C10 (the
EONW field and the CLI projection) and VEN-C29 (row text). These are contract changes: bring Lucca
the exact wording before code.

## Scope

In scope:
- Orbit adds the terminal's current window title to the `ProgramStatus` reply: sanitized like
  `title` and truncated at a UTF-8 boundary to a fixed bound (proposed 64 bytes). Orbit records
  the codec change in orbit/CHANGELOG.md.
- Eon Runtime caches it per terminal and passes it through unchanged as the attention's `name`.
- EONW carries `name` on pane and popup attention.
- Venus leads a sidebar row with `name` and falls back to the VEN-C29 app label when it is empty.

Out of scope:
- Stripping Claude's ✳/◐/◑ prefix in the Runtime (no provider parsing, EON-C31 Boundary).
  Venus may decide its display under VEN-C29.
- Setting session names, and any agent configuration or hooks.

## Prerequisites

eon-agent-sidebar-yx8.3 (the sidebar row exists). The EONW part lands with or after
eon-agent-sidebar-yx8.7.

## Reference gate

Consequential: wire format and contracts. Record the routes read in the bead before code.

## Acceptance

- An Orbit management round-trip test covers the title in the reply, its bound and its
  sanitizing.
- A Runtime test shows the name passing through unchanged.
- An installed observation: a Claude Code session started with `--name` shows that name on its
  sidebar row.
close_reason: Done in the graph commit that carries this close, on commit A 4ca7347 (edge 006e79a). Proof is in the bead's comments.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Contract ID: the agent sidebar contract is VEN-C30, not VEN-C29 (Lucca, 2026-10-22; see eon-agent-sidebar-yx8.3).

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Reference gate and contract wording (eon-63, 2026-10-23). Base: yx8.13 candidate commit e0cd8a8 (tree 68d6f1a) on edge f4408bc.

Decisions taken under Lucca's sidebar approval of 2026-10-23, relayed by the overseer ("work autonomously so we can get the sidebar done. open agents as needed. everything is autoaproved regarding the sidebar"; the epic's approval comment names yx8.11 and the ORB-C15, EON-C31 and VEN-C30 amendments its children name). Recorded as relayed, 2026-10-23.

Behavior and owners:
- Orbit owns the fact: the terminal's current window title (the ORBS metadata title, OSC 0/2), sanitized and bounded, carried once in the ProgramStatus reply header as `terminal_title`.
- Eon Runtime caches it per terminal with the last good reply, so a stale terminal keeps its last name, and passes it through unchanged as the attention record's `name`.
- EONW v18 (unreleased since v0.1.1, amended in place as yx8.7 left it) carries `name` on AttentionRecord. The CLI JSON adds `name` beside `app`; the human projection adds `name=`.
- Venus owns the row text: `name` leads the row's first line in place of the app's name, and an empty `name` falls back to the VEN-C30 app label. The app icon stays.

Routes read: docs/REFERENCES.md "agent-readable actions and source-labeled attention" (TUIOS 0047c409185f; kept: explicit source, no screen classification). Comparable implementation: herdr 143bf5fd4781d164260c63fe28e7dc08054ad32f, src/ui/sidebar/tokens.rs, whose sidebar rows can show the raw `terminal_title` or a spinner-stripped `terminal_title_stripped`. Kept: the title is a terminal fact shown as-is. Rejected: stripping spinner or status prefixes (provider parsing, EON-C31 Boundary; Claude Code omits its ✳/◐/◑ prefix when the terminal answers the OSC 7501 probe, which Orbit does). Rejected: a separate management request for the title (a second request per lease per poll for one string). Rejected: the title on every record (it is per terminal, and seven copies cost reply room).

Wire: management generation 2 stays (unreleased since v0.1.1). The reply gains `terminal_title` (u16 length plus at most 64 UTF-8 bytes) after the update sequence and moves from server tag 70 to 71, so an older generation-2 peer's reply is refused by tag instead of misdecoded (yx8.12's precedent); stop and recovery are unaffected. Consumers: Eon Runtime only. Breaking for the reply only, no compatibility window. Bend, the worker boundary and the laws are unchanged, since the host assembles reply content.

Portability disposition: neutral (libghostty's title, no platform mechanics).

Exact contract wording:

ORB-C15 Status: append "; `eon-agent-sidebar-yx8.11` adds the terminal title to the reply".
ORB-C15 ProgramStatus reply: "It carries the record count, the terminal's latest update sequence, the terminal title, the creation sequence of each record omitted for size, and as many records as fit ..." plus: "The terminal title is the window title that ORBS metadata publishes (OSC 0 and 2), empty when the terminal has none. Orbit removes its control characters and the invisible characters it removes from record text, and cuts it to 64 bytes at a UTF-8 boundary. It is a neutral terminal fact, not a record, and Orbit gives it no status meaning." The bounds sentence becomes: "With every record and the terminal title at their bounds, a reply carries up to 7 records while the terminal holds 14 or fewer, and at least 3 when it holds 256."
ORB-C15 Owner (Rust host): "... and assembles reply content, the terminal title included, by the fixed fill order."

EON-C31 EONW v18 bullet, after "from that record: kind, progress, `app`, `title` and `msg`;":
"- `name`: the terminal title from the same reply (ORB-C15), passed through unchanged, so rows can tell agents apart. Claude Code sets it to its session name (`--name` or `/rename`), else to its session title. It is empty when the terminal has none;"
Bounds: "`app` ≤ 32, `name` ≤ 64, `title` ≤ 96 and `msg` ≤ 256 bytes."
CLI JSON: "`attention: { state, app, name }` on panes and popups;" v18 freezes these fields as before.
Boundary: "no provider parsing; the Runtime passes `app` and `name` through unchanged, and Venus maps `app` for display (VEN-C30);"
Owner: "Orbit owns the records, their neutral facts and the terminal title."

EON-C10: the CLI exclusion line stays (`name` is not excluded). Bounds/failures: "except a program's own status report text (`app`, `title`, `msg`) and its terminal title (`name`), which are not screen content: Orbit has validated, sanitized and bounded them under ORB-C15." Boundary: "(except a program's own EON-C31 status report text and terminal title)".

VEN-C30 Status: append "; `eon-agent-sidebar-yx8.11` adds the name".
VEN-C30 Contents, the row's app bullet becomes:
"- the app icon: Venus maps `app=claude-code` to the Claude splat (VEN-C26) and `app=codex` to the Codex mark (VEN-C22);
 - the attention `name`, such as Claude Code's session name, or, when it is empty, the app's name when no icon stands for it, shown verbatim;"
Accessibility: "Each row's accessible name gives the state word, app, name, tab, source terminal and message."

Checks: the Orbit protocol round trip and bounds test (title at 64 bytes, 7 and 3 records at the bounds); a host unit test on a real libghostty terminal for the title's sanitizing and UTF-8 cut in the reply; a Runtime test that `name` passes through unchanged and is kept while stale; a Venus scene test for name-led rows and the fallback; then the installed observation (a `claude --name` session's row).

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Relayed decisions (overseer, 2026-10-23, under Lucca's 2026-10-23 approvals on eon-agent-sidebar-yx8):
1. EONW 19 instead of amending v18 in place. Reason (found by eon-63): the CLI accepts any supervisor that reports EONW 18 (runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/control.rs probe_generation_runtime), and live terminals run the profile's eon, so a refreshed eon would misdecode a running v18 supervisor's attention records; the snapshot codec has no optional fields. The lifecycle codec carries no snapshot or attention. Overseer: "Bump to EONW 19 ... with the rename, VERSION 19 and the component graph together, so no tree has a mismatched graph. Your contract text is approved: EON-C31 \"EONW v19 adds name\", EON-C10 and VEN-C30 consume v19, and the 1.0 line follows."
2. Order: "you land after yx8.13 and yx8.8"; yx8.14 and yx8.15 rebase onto this.
3. Profile refresh after landing goes ahead; old windows get the clean "requires EONW 19" failure (filed as eon-cli-old-window-after-upgrade-mno4); the CHANGELOG says a restart is needed.
Pending with the overseer: the graph goes in a second commit that cites the first (a commit cannot cite its own hash; docs/ARCHITECTURE.md says interface versions change only after the consumer proof), both landed by one update-ref so edge never points at a mismatched graph.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Relayed (overseer, 2026-10-23): "A+B landed in one update-ref is fine." Commit A carries the code and contracts with EONW 19; commit B moves components/eon-v4.json to EONW 19 citing A; one update-ref lands both. title: Let the Runtime retire omitted program-status records exactly
description:
## Why

Lucca accepted a gap in eon-agent-sidebar-yx8.6 for 1.0 (2026-10-22) and asked for this follow-up.
The management `ProgramStatus` reply (ORB-C15) carries about 7 records per terminal and counts the
rest as `omitted`. Eon Runtime remembers omitted records so their fixed change times and seen
raises survive until they return (EON-C31). It cannot tell an omitted record from a cleared one,
so it caps that memory at Orbit's 256 records and evicts entries without a seen raise first. A
seen finish lights up again as finished only if one terminal churns about 250 more
seen-then-cleared records while that record stays crowded out of the reply.

**Contracts:** ORB-C15 (reply content) and EON-C31 internals. Changing ORB-C15 is a contract
change: bring Lucca the exact wording before code.

## Scope

In scope:
- Orbit gives the Runtime enough to retire remembered records exactly. One option is listing every
  record's id and change sequence (bounded by ORB-C15's 256 records) without its text. Another is a
  per-terminal removal sequence the Runtime can compare.
- Eon Runtime drops remembered records that Orbit no longer holds, and removes the 256 cap and its
  eviction order.

Out of scope:
- Raising the reply's 4 KiB bound, and any change to what the sidebar shows.

## Prerequisites

eon-agent-sidebar-yx8.6 (the Runtime memory exists).

## Reference gate

Consequential: wire format and contract. Record the routes read in the bead before code.

## Acceptance

- An Orbit management round-trip test covers the new fact and its bound.
- A Runtime unit test churns more than 256 seen-then-cleared records while one seen record stays
  omitted, and the seen record stays seen when it returns.
close_reason: Done in 6bd4f02 (pushed to origin/edge). The eon profile element was refreshed from the main tree at edge 6bd4f02 and resolves to /nix/store/b2n3yaksdnks733yyfzzd7gxy1147r8m-eon-0.1.1 (eon versions: eon 0.1.1 g1-8e4e55026979eb685fab1e4363283c8f, eonw 18). Its Orbit /nix/store/a4qvg9wqwx4qq5scnmhfkqaxha6rxqcl-yazelix-orbit-0.1.0 passed the program_status real-PTY check through sandboxed eon-test with ORBIT_BIN set: ProgramStatus answer under PTY load, median 0.14 ms. Running supervisors are untouched; they keep their old Orbit until restarted, and a new Runtime reading an older generation-2 Orbit's tag-69 reply leaves that terminal's attention stale. The eonbase profile element was not refreshed.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Reference gate and decision (2026-10-23, at edge 22915af), relayed under Lucca's 2026-10-23 epic approval to eon-a8 ("work autonomously so we can get the sidebar done. open agents as needed. everything is autoaproved regarding the sidebar"; scope per the approval comment on eon-agent-sidebar-yx8, which names yx8.12's contract wording and design choices).

- User-visible behavior: a seen finish stays seen while its record is crowded out of the ProgramStatus reply, however many other records churn. Owners: Orbit owns the records and the new neutral fact (ORB-C15); orbit-protocol owns the one wire schema; Eon Runtime owns memory and meaning (EON-C31, text unchanged).
- Routes read: docs/REFERENCES.md "How should Eon expose agent-readable actions and source-labeled attention..." and the yx8.5 gate (Herdr, TUIOS, Zellij). Comparable: Herdr 143bf5fd4781 agent.list returns every agent with state_change_seq and revision (src/api/schema/agents.rs:243-251), so a reader reconciles against a full identity listing. Kept: reconcile against an identity listing; ours is bounded, so it lists only identities, never text.
- Rejected: (a) listing every record's id: 256 x 128-byte ids exceed the 4 KiB bound. (b) a per-terminal removal sequence: under churn every reply shows a removal and cannot say which record went, so not exact. (c) listing omitted records' change sequences: a remembered seen `done` that turns `idle` while omitted would lose its memory, and its `idle` from `done` would raise again.
- Decision: each record gains a creation sequence (unique per live record: one report creates one record, and the update sequence never repeats), and the reply lists the creation sequence of every omitted record (8 bytes each, inside the 4 KiB). The Runtime keeps a remembered record exactly while its creation sequence is listed; the 256 cap and its eviction order go. Cost: with every record at its bounds a reply still fits 7 records up to 22 held, and at least 3 at 256 held.
- Wire: still management generation 2 (unreleased since v0.1.1). The reply moves from server tag 69 to 70, so an old generation-2 peer's reply is refused by tag (the Runtime keeps its last good result, then stale) instead of possibly misdecoding; stop and recovery are unaffected. Consumers: Eon Runtime only (Venus and Eon do not read ProgramStatus). Breaking for the reply only, no compatibility window.
- ORB-C15 wording decided:
  - Neutral per-record facts, new bullet after Update sequence: "**Creation sequence.** The update sequence of the report that created the record. Later reports keep it, so a record that is cleared, dropped or evicted and then reported again gets a new one."
  - ProgramStatus reply: "It carries the record count, the terminal's latest update sequence, the creation sequence of each record omitted for size, and as many records as fit in a neutral fill order: ..." and "... its update sequence, creation sequence, change sequence, previous state and both ages." plus "The omitted creation sequences count toward the 4 KiB and let a reader tell a record omitted for size from one Orbit no longer holds. With every record at its bounds, a reply carries 7 records while the terminal holds 22 or fewer, and at least 3 when it holds 256."
- Checks: protocol round trip with omitted creation sequences and the 256-record bound; status.rs fill test; Runtime unit test churning >256 seen-then-cleared records while one seen record stays omitted.
- Portability: neutral.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Review round 1 (2026-10-23) on candidate tree 629d69b6 (base 22915af): Codex and a fresh Claude reviewer both found the fill loop consuming the first record that did not fit (reply counts disagreed, so encoding failed and the Orbit host would exit; the fill unit test failed red). Fixed: the omitted list is built from order[records.len()..]. Codex also found the changelog overclaiming stale attention for a Runtime that never had a good reply; reworded. Other fixes from nits: Runtime memory is capped at the reply's omitted count (guards a peer that repeats creation sequences), wrap and wording fixes.

Decision (relayed under the 2026-10-23 epic approval): ORB-C15 says "a reply carries up to 7 records while the terminal holds 22 or fewer, and at least 3 when it holds 256" (was "carries 7"), and EON-C31's third vanishing-finish gap now reads "the ProgramStatus reply holds up to 7 records, and as few as 3 when a terminal holds many, so a terminal with as many `blocked`, `error` or `done` records as fit (Claude subagents, for example) can crowd out a raised `idle` from the reply. That finish never shows."

Out of scope, not beaded (rare, pre-existing): a returning record is matched to its cached raise by id, not creation sequence, so a seen `done` cleared, recreated as `done` and turned `idle` within one 500 ms poll inherits the old seen raise. Rebased the worktree onto edge d6fa09c (docs-only, clean merge).

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Decision text as committed (relayed under the 2026-10-23 epic approval; supersedes the wording in the round-1 comment after review found "up to 7" unqualified wrong, since shorter records fit more):
- EON-C31, third vanishing-finish gap: "the ProgramStatus reply holds 7 records at their bounds, more when they are shorter, and as few as 3 when a terminal holds many, so a terminal with as many `blocked`, `error` or `done` records as fit (Claude subagents, for example) can crowd out a raised `idle` from the reply. That finish never shows."
- ORB-C15 Creation sequence: "The update sequence of the report that created the record. Later reports keep it; a record that is cleared, dropped or evicted and then reported again is a new record with a new one."
- ORB-C15 reply bound sentence: "With every record at its bounds, a reply carries up to 7 records while the terminal holds 22 or fewer, and at least 3 when it holds 256."

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Proof (2026-10-23) on tree 1f3bc55a489d6846db69667a3b2958ead3dbeeb7 over edge b3be179 (this commit's tree apart from .beads), x86_64 Linux, load 5.8 to 11.4 with other agents' builds running:
- `nix build -L --no-link --max-jobs 2 --cores 6` of all 42 `checks.x86_64-linux.orbit-*` (orbit-laws: ALL PROOFS CHECK; orbit-boundary; orbit-terminfo; every orbit-<name> real-PTY check, including orbit-program-status): exit 0.
- `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=8 nix develop -c eon-test` (workspace and installer, sandboxed): exit 0, 24 suites, 415 passed, 0 failed, 45 ignored. Includes records_keep_neutral_facts, replies_fill_by_group_then_most_recent_change, program_status_replies_keep_their_bounds, the management round trip, and the Runtime churn test (identity_fixes_change_times_and_discards_older_replies_until_a_new_run: 512 seen-then-cleared records while `a` stays omitted; memory holds only `a`, and `a` returns seen).
- Red: the churn test fails against the old cap-and-evict code (cap 256 evicts the oldest seen record, `a`), as each review round confirmed by reading; the fill test caught the round-1 fill bug red.
- fmt and clippy -D warnings clean for orbit-protocol, yazelix-orbit, eon-runtime (Claude rounds 2 and 3).
Ledger: round 1 = Claude reviewer with checks + Codex in parallel on 629d69b6: 1 code bug (fill loop dropped the first non-fitting record: counts disagreed, encode failed, Orbit host would exit), 1 changelog overclaim, nits (Runtime memory guard against repeated creation sequences, wording). Claude converge rounds: 1 text-only fixes, 2 clean, then Codex narrow re-check: 2 text overclaims (EON-C31 "up to 7" unqualified; changelog Agent popup unavailable), Claude round 3 clean, Codex narrow re-check of 6ec26570..16bb1c0b clean. 3 Codex passes, 4 Claude passes. A /tmp wipe mid-loop was recovered from the recorded candidate tree.

title: Add the agent sidebar rows and their navigation (VEN-C30)
description:
## Why

The second half of the original yx8.3 (agent sidebar), split by Lucca on 2026-10-22: the sidebar's
rows and their navigation, inside the frame that eon-agent-sidebar-yx8.3 adds.

**Contract:** VEN-C30 (approved as VEN-C29 in "Contract proposal, draft 15" on
eon-agent-sidebar-yx8.1; renumbered, see the ID recheck comment on yx8.3). yx8.3 lands the text.
This bead implements the row and navigation parts and sets the Status.

## Prerequisites

eon-agent-sidebar-yx8.3 (the frame) and eon-agent-sidebar-yx8.2 (tab badges).

## Scope

In scope:
- **Rows.**
  - Listed: only tabs that have attention or an Agent popup, in tab order.
  - Each row shows the glyph and the app icon: the VEN-C26 splat for `claude-code`, the VEN-C22
    mark for `codex`, or the `app` name verbatim.
  - Then the title, or the tab's directory leaf when there is no title.
  - Then the age, computed from `changed_at`, and the source terminal (`pN`, or the popup's
    label).
  - Needs-input rows add a plain-text `msg` line. Extra records fold into "+N", and stale rows
    are dimmed.
- **Navigation.**
  - Activating a row sends `FocusAttention`, and focus follows the result.
  - Arrows move between rows, Enter activates, and Esc returns to the terminal.
  - Focus goes back to the terminal when a row's target is removed.
- **Accessibility:** AccessKit names for every row.

Out of scope: the agent's session name on rows (eon-agent-sidebar-yx8.11); Alt+G, Alt+Shift+G and
F6 (yx8.8).

## Acceptance

- Scene goldens cover row contents: both icons, an unknown `app`, the `msg` line, "+N" and a
  stale row.
- Row activation and keyboard navigation focus the exact target.
- One isolated installed dogfood with two tabs running agents, after the profile refresh, on the
  final revision of the sidebar batch (yx8.3 and this bead).

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test -p venus`, plus fmt and clippy for Venus.
- The profile refresh, and a dogfood observation on isolated Sway.
- A Codex review, including the VEN-C30 status and proof record.

## Maintenance Notes

Portability disposition: neutral.
close_reason: Sidebar rows, navigation, F6 and row accessibility landed with installed proof (rows and icons, click/F6/Enter jumps with terminal focus, Alt+Shift+H, width hide, idle age repaint, pane-matched translucent card framed and frameless, empty state); Alt+G/Alt+Shift+G remain yx8.8; profile refresh scheduled by the overseer after landing.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Decisions (eon-a0, 2026-10-23), relayed by the overseer eon-a8 under Lucca's 2026-10-23 approvals on eon-agent-sidebar-yx8 ("work autonomously so we can get the sidebar done ... everything is autoaproved regarding the sidebar"):
1. Scope: the F6 order change moves here from yx8.8: Terminal -> Sidebar -> Tabs -> Panes, skipping Sidebar while it is not visible, with its label in venus/src/application/shortcuts.rs and the docs rows. Alt+G and Alt+Shift+G stay in yx8.8 (eon-a8 recorded the move there).
2. Ages read "now" under a minute, then "4m", "2h", "3d", and refresh at their minute (hour, day) boundaries, not every second.
3. Rows that overflow the card are clipped; the keyboard-focused row scrolls into view. No wheel scroll in this bead. Follow-up: wheel scrolling of the sidebar list, which users with many agents will reach for.
4. Focus after activating a row (my decision under the same approval, weighing eon-a8's note): focus stays on the activated row until the result arrives, then goes straight to the terminal when the snapshot shows the exact target focused. If the result only selected the target's tab (VEN-C30's covered-target case), focus ends on the tab strip. A rejection leaves focus on the row with the VEN-C8 notice. This avoids a screen reader announcing the tab strip and focus flicker. Venus does not predict the covered-target rule; it reads the result from the snapshot.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Decisions and reference gate (eon-a0, 2026-10-23), taken under the relayed 2026-10-23 approvals on eon-agent-sidebar-yx8.
5. VEN-C30 text: F6 'skips Sidebar while it is not visible' becomes 'skips Sidebar while it is not visible or has no rows, since the empty state holds no focus target'. Status names yx8.13 as implementing contents, row navigation, F6 and row accessibility; Alt+G/Alt+Shift+G stay on yx8.8.
6. Rows: each tab with an attention rollup gets its heading (the tab pill label, '3  site'), then a row per pane (column order) and popup with attention. Line 1: glyph (VEN-C21 quads, plus a ring for idle and a dot for unavailable), the splat/mark for claude-code/codex or '<app> · ' verbatim, then the record title, the tab's directory leaf, or 'status unavailable'. Line 2: '<age> · <pN or popup label>[ · +N][ · status stale]'. Line 3, needs input only: the msg, single line, clipped. Stale rows dim text and glyph. Accessible name: '<State word>: <Claude|Codex|app|agent> in tab <n>, <leaf>, <source>[, <title>][, changed <age> ago][, N more records][, status stale][: <msg>]'; needs input names its kind (permission, question, sign-in). Rows are AccessKit Buttons (Click jumps, Focus focuses) after a Heading per tab, inside the Complementary region.
7. Keyboard: Enter or Space on the focused row jumps; Up/Down step and stop at either end; footer hint 'agents' for Up/Down while the sidebar is focused; Escape is the existing return-to-terminal. A click also puts focus on the row before jumping, so the jump result decides focus the same way for pointer, keyboard and AccessKit.
8. The yx8.3 nits: an attention-only refresh while the sidebar is visible now invalidates the presentation (rows are hit targets, as eon-e8 noted), and a snapshot that flips 'sidebar' cancels the pointer sequence, as the hints and zoom toggles do.

Reference gate: consequential only through the VEN-C30 text and status; no dependency, protocol or wire change. Owners as recorded on yx8.3 (Runtime: attention state and FocusAttention's covered-target rule, EON-C31; Venus: rows, input, focus, accessibility). Routes read: yx8.1 research record section 2 and D7-D9 (Herdr herdrdev/herdr@143bf5fd, rows grouped under their tab; cmux unread jump). Kept: rows never reorder, plain text only, no previews. Rejected: Venus predicting the covered-target result from the snapshot (it would duplicate EON-C31's rule); FocusId/InvokePopup for rows (EON-C31 already rejected them). Check: scene goldens agent_sidebar_rows_show_attention_in_tab_order_and_reveal_the_focused_row and agent_sidebar_ages_count_whole_minutes_hours_and_days, the accessibility region test, and sidebar_rows_take_f6_focus_step_by_arrow_and_follow_their_jump. Portability disposition: neutral.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Review round 1 (eon-a0, 2026-10-23), candidate tree 70d7171 on base 519dead (eon-e8's yx8.2 tree 3f62a1f on ec13ba6). Codex and a fresh Claude reviewer ran in parallel; the Claude reviewer's checks passed (fmt, clippy, eon-test -p yazelix-venus 115+58+18 passed), and the tree was unchanged afterwards.
Blocking, all fixed:
- Codex 1: row ages are absent from the renderer's content key, so the age timer's refresh would not repaint. Fixed: the tick marks presentation content changed; the next wake is computed in refresh_client_view from the scene it already builds, so every path (startup, snapshot, resize) schedules it.
- Codex 2 = Claude B2: a jump counted 'at most two responses' to find its answer, but up to 32 actions can be queued. Fixed in the transport: WorkspaceTransport::send returns a ticket, and the worker emits WorkspaceEvent::Answered { ticket, accepted } right after that action's response. A jump moves focus to the terminal on any snapshot that focuses its exact target; only its own accepted answer moves focus to the tab strip (covered-target case); a rejected or lost answer leaves focus on the row. The worker test asserts tickets and Answered events.

title: Match returning program-status records to their cached raise by creation sequence
description:
## Why

When a program-status record comes back in a reply, the Runtime looks up its cached record by the record `id` alone. If within one 500 ms poll a program clears a seen `done` record, re-creates it as `done` and then turns it `idle`, the new record arrives as `idle` from `done`. It then inherits the old record's seen raise, so its finish never lights up. The new record is a different record: Orbit gives it a new creation sequence (ORB-C15, since eon-agent-sidebar-yx8.12, commit 6bd4f02). The yx8.12 reviewers found this and recorded it as out of scope there. Lucca asked for it to be filed (2026-10-23). It is rare, because it needs a clear and a re-create inside one poll.

## Evidence

- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/attention.rs:261`: `known` finds the cached record by `record.record.id == id`.
- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/attention.rs:271`: `let cached = known(&record.id);`.
- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/attention.rs:291`: `(Idle, Some(Done))` takes `cached`'s raise when the cached record's state is `Done`, with no check that it is the same record.
- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/attention.rs:563`: the test helper `record()` sets `created: changed`, so a test record gets a new creation sequence at each state change.
- `docs/CONTRACTS.md:2178` (EON-C31 Identity and time) keys state by run plus record `id`. `docs/CONTRACTS.md:2191` says an `idle` from `done` keeps the cached raise "of that `done`".
- `orbit/docs/CONTRACTS.md` (ORB-C15 Neutral per-record facts, Creation sequence): a cleared and re-reported record is a new record with a new creation sequence.

## Scope

In scope:
- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/attention.rs`: match a returning record to its cached record only when the creation sequence matches too (id and `created`, or `created` alone, since it is unique per live record in a run), and the unit tests that cover it.

Out of scope:
- Orbit, orbit-protocol, the wire, EONW and Venus.
- Any other raise, seen or normalization rule of EON-C31.

## Acceptance

- A Runtime unit test shows a seen `done` record, then a reply whose record has the same `id`, a new creation sequence, state `idle` and previous `done`. The terminal shows finished (an unseen raise), and the test fails against the id-only lookup.
- The existing raise and seen tests still pass, including `idle` from `done` keeping the cached raise of the same record.

## Implementation Notes

1. Change `known` to also require `record.record.created == created` (pass the returning record's `created`).
2. Fix the test helper first: `created: changed` would break every existing test where one record changes state. Give each test id a fixed creation sequence, or add a way to set it per record, so a state change keeps it the way Orbit's `put` does.
3. Add the red/green case from Acceptance to the attention tests.
4. Decide whether EON-C31's "keyed by the exact Orbit run ID plus record `id`" needs an amendment. It is a contract text change: stop and bring Lucca the exact wording, unless he decides that the current text ("that `done`") already covers it.

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime` should exit 0, including the new case.
- `nix develop -c cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -p eon-runtime -- -D warnings` and `nix develop -c cargo fmt --check -p eon-runtime` should exit 0.
- After landing, refresh the eon profile per AGENTS.md (no supervisor restart).

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if the cited code has drifted materially, for example yx8.11 reshaping `apply`.
- Stop if the fix needs Orbit or wire changes.
- Stop before any EON-C31 text change until Lucca approves the exact wording.
- Stop if verification fails twice for the same reason after a reasonable fix attempt.

## Maintenance Notes

- Consequential? No new dependency, wire or lifecycle boundary. It changes only the Runtime's internal record identity, so it needs the cheapest check (the unit test) and a Codex review under AGENTS.md.
- eon-agent-sidebar-yx8.11 also edits `attention.rs`, adding the session name. Land them in sequence, not in parallel.

title: Stop the working-badge spinner from costing a third of a core on software rendering
description:
## Why

eon-e8 measured the yx8.2 tab-badge working spinner (5 Hz) on 2026-10-23. Under a software compositor (pixman, as in VMs and GPU-less machines), every tick re-rasterizes the frame: 738 frames against 51 ticks over 20 s, about 34% of one core. On the Intel GPU it costs about 0.4% (14 frames against 6 ticks). A user running agents in a VM, or on battery without GPU acceleration, pays a third of a core for an animation. Users are not happy paying that.

## Decision (overseer, 2026-10-23, under Lucca's 2026-10-23 approvals)

On a CPU (software) wgpu adapter, the working badge shows a static working glyph with no animation. On hardware adapters it keeps the 5 Hz spinner. Accessible state is unchanged either way. Record the exact VEN-C21 (and EON-C21 if it names the animation) text as relayed.

## Scope

In scope: detect the adapter type that Venus already selects (wgpu `AdapterInfo::device_type == Cpu`), and render the working badge statically there. No timer ticks or redraws for the spinner on that path. VEN-C21 presentation text, the Venus CHANGELOG, and a scene or render test.

Out of scope: other animations (cursor spring and Anima have their own owners), a user setting, and pausing the spinner when the window is unfocused (file separately if wanted).

## Acceptance

- A test shows that a software adapter schedules no spinner ticks and draws the static glyph.
- Measured on pixman, the same 20 s workload: the spinner's added redraws are gone (idle-level CPU). Record frames per second against ticks.

## Verification

`nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-venus`, Venus fmt and clippy, converge plus Codex, and one isolated headless-Sway measurement with the pixman renderer.

Portability disposition: neutral.
close_reason: Software adapters draw a still working badge with no ticks; the installed pixman measurement shows idle-level CPU (62 vs 65 ticks over 20 s, from 545-605).

title: Mark a shown popup in the agent sidebar
description:
## Why

Each tab keeps its own shown popup: EONW v18 `Tab::selected_popup` is "retained when another tab is active" (`runtime/crates/eon-workspace-protocol/src/v18.rs:343`). From another tab, nothing tells the user that tab 3 has its Agent or Git popup open; they find out when they switch and the popup covers the panes. An agent row whose source is "Agent popup" also doesn't say whether that popup is open now. Lucca proposed a sidebar marker for a popup that is "on" (2026-10-23) and chose its shape (2026-10-23, answering the overseer's numbered items "1. yeah 2. yeah 3. yeah"):

1. "On" means shown (the tab's `selected_popup`), not a hidden keep-alive popup, which is the normal state.
2. One glyph on the tab's sidebar header, plus the same glyph after the catalog label on rows whose source is the shown popup. Tabs the sidebar does not list (no attention and no Agent popup) get no marker, so no new rows.
3. Filed under the sidebar epic and built after eon-agent-sidebar-yx8.9 proves the current sidebar.

## Contract (VEN-C30 Contents, proposed; needs Lucca's approval of this exact text before code)

Add to VEN-C30 Result, Contents:

"- **Shown popup.** When a listed tab shows a popup (its snapshot `selected_popup` is set), its header ends with one popup marker glyph, and a row whose source terminal is that popup adds the same glyph after its catalog label. A hidden popup gets no marker. The header's and the row's accessible labels add "popup shown"."

No EONW, Runtime or Orbit change: Venus already receives `selected_popup` for every tab.

## Scope

In scope:
- `venus/`: the header and row marker, the accessible labels, the VEN-C30 text above once approved, `venus/CHANGELOG.md`, `docs/USAGE.md`'s sidebar description if it lists header contents, and the sidebar scene golden.
- The glyph: one cell, drawn in the existing badge or icon style, distinct from the attention state glyphs. Record the choice in the bead.

Out of scope:
- Listing tabs that have only a non-Agent popup.
- Eon Bar tab pills, popup behavior, and any wire or Runtime change.

## Acceptance

- A Venus scene or unit test: a non-active listed tab with `selected_popup` set shows the marker on its header, and a row sourced from that popup shows it after its label. The same tab with `selected_popup` unset shows neither. The test fails without the change.
- One installed dogfood observation: open the Agent popup in tab 2, switch to tab 1, and see the marker on tab 2's header and its agent row.

## Verification

`nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-venus`, Venus fmt and clippy, converge plus Codex, then the profile refresh and one isolated installed observation.

Portability disposition: neutral.
close_reason: Shown-popup marker implemented and proved: scene and RTL tests, converge + Codex, isolated installed observation
