title: Show agent attention badges on Eon Bar tabs
description:
## Why

This is the fifth slice of epic eon-agent-sidebar-yx8. Tabs in the Eon Bar show agent attention whenever
the sidebar is not visible. Lucca decided this on 2026-10-21 (D11).

**Contract:** the EON-C21/VEN-C21 amendment. Approved on 2026-10-21; the text is the "Contract
proposal, draft 15" comment on eon-agent-sidebar-yx8.1.

## Scope

In scope:
- In Venus, draw a corner badge on each tab whose rollup is needs input (◆), error (✕), finished
  (✓) or working (spinner). This includes the active tab.
  - Show badges while the sidebar is `Closed`, `Off`, or hidden for width. Until the sidebar bead
    lands, treat the sidebar as never visible.
  - A badge never changes tab width or label text.
  - A stale tab's badge is dimmed.
  - The spinner repaints only the badge, at no more than 5 Hz (AP-PERF-001).
  - With tab overflow, the scroll edge shows the most urgent hidden badge.
  - The accessible name appends the tab's state.
  - Clicking a badged tab selects the tab, as any tab click does (Q2).
- Attention-only refreshes keep notices and disturb no navigation, scroll, attachment or resize.
  This is the VEN-C8/VEN-C22 clause.
- Contract text: amend the EON-C21 and VEN-C21 Boundary and Result sections.

Out of scope:
- The sidebar, the keys, and any provider interpretation in Venus.

## Acceptance

- Scene goldens show the badges for each state, the stale dimming, overflow, and unchanged tab
  widths.
- AccessKit labels carry the tab's state.
- One isolated installed dogfood shows a real Claude or Codex run badging a background tab.

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test -p venus`, plus fmt and clippy for Venus.
- The profile refresh, and one dogfood observation on isolated Sway.
- A Codex review.

## Maintenance Notes

Portability disposition: neutral. eon-agent-attention-eon-bar-jm0 is superseded by this bead.
close_reason: Tab attention badges landed with installed proof (real Codex turn badging a background tab, all four states, overflow edges, sidebar gating); profile refresh scheduled by the overseer after landing.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Design and reference gate (eon-e8 session, 2026-10-23, base edge 22915af). Coordinator eon-a8.

Behavior and owners: Eon Runtime owns the attention state and tab rollup (EON-C31, EONW 18). Venus Scene (`WorkspaceTab`) owns badge projection, geometry, stale dimming, the overflow edges and the state suffix on the tab's accessible name. The chrome renderer draws them, and AccessKit and the tab tooltip read the same scene label. Hit testing is unchanged, so a badged tab click selects the tab (Q2).

References: the yx8.1 research (Rex: badges on unfocused tabs; Nova `3325ef5d`: remove activity text from tab names because markers went stale) and the docs/REFERENCES.md "direct human attention" route (cmux `a35880b1031e`, inspected under eon-pxn). Kept: a badge beside the name, never written into it, and the exact state from the snapshot with no inference. Rejected: label text markers, and a font glyph for each state (font coverage of ◆ ✕ ✓ varies by system).

Decisions:
- A badge is drawn from rectangle quads (◆ one quad, ✕ and ✓ two bars each, the spinner eight ring segments). It sits on a header-colored disc over the pill's top-right corner. It lies outside the label's text box and inside the tab viewport, so tab width and label are unchanged.
- Stale dimming: the rollup comes from the tab's terminals in that state, and the badge is dimmed only when every one of them is stale. A fresh terminal in the same state keeps the badge bright.
- Spinner: the static vertex buffer is rebuilt only when the content key changes. A spinner tick rewrites only the spinner segments' bytes in place (`queue.write_buffer` at their recorded offsets; the vertex count is the same in every phase). It never rebuilds the scene, the text or the terminal geometry. The frame is still presented whole, as cursor-trail frames already are, since Venus has no partial present. Ticks run every 200 ms (5 Hz) while a spinner is shown and the window is not occluded.
- Overflow: a tab whose badge is not fully inside the tab viewport counts as hidden on that side. Each scroll edge shows the most urgent hidden badge (state order, then undimmed first). The edge badge is not interactive.
- Accessible name: ", needs input" / ", error" / ", finished" / ", working", plus ", status stale" when dimmed.
- Sidebar visible: agreed with eon-62 (yx8.3). It owns `WorkspaceScene::sidebar() -> Option<SceneRect>`, computed in from_snapshot_with_zoom before the tab map. yx8.2 stubs `let sidebar_visible = false;` there, and whoever lands second replaces the stub with `sidebar.is_some()`.
- The attention-only refresh clause (VEN-C8/VEN-C22) and its model test already landed with yx8.7 (4b150d5). This slice checks that a badge-only change keeps notices and leaves the attachment alone.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Relayed approval, recorded 2026-10-23. eon-a8 relayed Lucca's words of 2026-10-23: "work autonomously so we can get the sidebar done. open agents as needed. everything is autoaproved regarding the sidebar". It covers contract wording and IDs, scope and design choices within this bead, and reference-gate decisions. It excludes host permission prompts, restarting the live supervisor or window, promotion, and work outside the epic. Decisions taken under it:
1. Stale dimming: a tab's badge is dimmed only when every terminal in the tab's rollup state is stale.
2. Spinner: "repaints at no more than 5 Hz, and only the badge" means that a tick (every 200 ms or longer, and only while the window is not occluded) rewrites only the spinner's own vertex bytes, while scene, text and terminal layers stay cached. The frame is still presented whole, as cursor-trail frames are.
3. Overflow: a badge crossing a tab-viewport edge counts as hidden past it. Each edge shows the most urgent such badge (state order, then undimmed first), drawn just inside that edge and not interactive.
4. VEN-C21 accessible-name example: the draft-15 wording "Tab 3 of 5, site, needs input" becomes `Tab 3 of 5  /home/me/site, needs input`, to match the existing tab accessible label format ("Tab N of M  <full path>"). The state suffix is ", <state>", plus ", status stale" when dimmed.
5. EON-C21's Consumes line: "current EONW v7" becomes "EONW v7 (v18 for the EON-C31 tab attention marker)". The Open proof names this bead's dogfood as the marker's installed proof.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Review round 1 (candidate tree 5fb22ee on 22915af), recorded 2026-10-23. A fresh Claude reviewer reported 1 blocking finding and ran the checks: fmt, clippy and eon-test -p yazelix-venus all green (185 passed); the tree was unchanged. Codex reported 4 blocking findings. Dispositions:
1. Edge badges were drawn under tab label text (both reviewers). Fixed: `WorkspaceScene::tab_label_clip` is the tab viewport less the edge badges' columns, and the label text clips to it. The scene test asserts that no edge badge intersects it.
2. An attention-only refresh bumped the presentation epoch, which retired a held link press (Codex). Fixed: the new `model::attention_only_change` (the exhaustive Snapshot destructure fails to compile when the snapshot gains a field) makes the application bump only the content generation for such a refresh. A sidebar-only change still invalidates, since the sidebar moves the content area. The model test covers both cases.
3. A spinner on a badge clipped away entirely kept ticking (Codex). Fixed: `push_badge` draws and registers nothing for a badge outside the clip.
4. A spinner tick redraw re-projects WorkspaceScene and re-emits the cursor trail (Codex). Recorded decision 2 overstated this. Corrected decision 2, taken under the relayed approval: a spinner tick rewrites only the spinner's vertex bytes in the cached static buffer. The static rectangle and text layers are not rebuilt, and no glyph is prepared. The redraw it requests still re-projects the workspace scene from the cached snapshot (tab text widths are cached) and, with the cursor trail on, re-emits the trail's few dynamic vertices, as every presented frame does. Installed evidence: two captures 300 ms apart differ only in the 8x8 spinner box (cap1, candidate 5fb22ee).
Nits taken: a 1 px badge ring (10 px glyph at 1x, after the capture showed 8 px), and VEN-C21 Open proof wording. Nits left: tooltips show the state suffix (same label as AccessKit, intended); occlusion stops ticks only when winit reports it; overhang pixels outside the pill are not hit targets.

title: Add the agent sidebar frame (VEN-C30)
description:
## Why

This is the sixth slice of epic eon-agent-sidebar-yx8: the agent sidebar's frame. Lucca split the
original yx8.3 on 2026-10-22 ("do it", answering the overseer: split into a frame and a rows bead,
and start the frame alongside yx8.2). The rows are eon-agent-sidebar-yx8.13.

**Contract:** VEN-C29, plus the VEN-C8/VEN-C18 layout amendment, the Alt+Shift+H part of the
EON-C20/VEN-C20 and EON-C24/VEN-C24 amendments, and the Venus rule change. Approved on
2026-10-21; the text is the "Contract proposal, draft 15" comment on eon-agent-sidebar-yx8.1.
Approval also covers the sidebar as a new Venus module. The ID is now VEN-C30 (see the ID recheck
comment); recheck it when landing. This bead lands the whole contract text; the Status says which
parts are implemented until yx8.13 lands.

## Prerequisites

eon-agent-sidebar-yx8.7 (sidebar state and attention on EONW 18, including the graph commit). Not
yx8.2: the frame does not use the tab badges. yx8.2 runs in parallel and touches the Eon Bar, so
whichever lands second rebases through any Venus layout conflict.

## Scope

In scope:
- **Visibility** follows `sidebar == Open`, the same on every tab. Alt+Shift+H sends
  `ToggleSidebar`.
- **Layout.**
  - The sidebar is 28 cells wide, sits below the Eon Bar (Q4), and pushes the columns.
  - It hides for width when the remaining column area would fall below 80 cells.
  - While it is visible: side gaps and the CreateColumn check are measured from the content area,
    the first tab pill's alignment with the first card is suspended, and popups use the content
    area.
- **Focus rule:** Alt+Shift+H never takes focus. Focus goes back to the terminal when the sidebar
  closes or is hidden for width.
- **Accessibility:** the sidebar region has an AccessKit name and comes after the header and
  before the panes.
- **Empty state:** shown when there is no attention.
- **Contract text:**
  - Add VEN-C30 (draft 15 text) to `venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md`.
  - Amend VEN-C8/VEN-C18 for the layout, and VEN-C22/VEN-C26 for the icon exceptions.
  - Apply the Alt+Shift+H amendments. The viewer and the hints derive from `FIXED_SHORTCUTS` and
    omit the key under `Off`.
  - Change the Venus rule: in `venus/.agent-protocols.local.md`, "sidebars" becomes "other
    sidebars" and "agent sidebar" is added. Render it with starcompass; never edit
    venus/AGENTS.md by hand.

Out of scope: row contents and row navigation (yx8.13); Alt+G, Alt+Shift+G and F6 (yx8.8); drag
resizing, a compact rail, vertical tabs, and notifications.

## Acceptance

- Scene goldens cover the layout, narrow-window hiding and the empty state.
- Toggling preserves terminal focus, including when the window narrows past the hide threshold.
- The contract index and the rendered Venus rule match the approved text.

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test -p venus`, plus fmt and clippy for Venus.
- `starcompass check-consumer` for the Venus import.
- A Codex review. The installed dogfood runs once, in yx8.13, on the final revision of the
  sidebar batch.

title: Store OSC 7501 program-status records in Orbit (ORB-C15)
description:
## Why

This is the first implementation slice of the agent attention sidebar (epic eon-agent-sidebar-yx8). Orbit
stores the OSC 7501 Program Status records that Claude Code (2.1.295 and later) and Codex (0.163 and
later) emit natively. It is the only source of agent state.

**Contract:** ORB-C15, approved by Lucca on 2026-10-21. The authoritative text is the "Contract
proposal, draft 15" comment on eon-agent-sidebar-yx8.1, with the approval comment after it. A
working copy is at ~/pjs/refs/agent-sidebar-research/CONTRACT-PROPOSAL.md.

## Scope

In scope:
- The Orbit host record store in `orbit/src/`, fed by libghostty's program-status callback, which
  eon-a9tr lands. It includes:
  - spec rev 0.4 parsing results: the discard rules, treat-as-absent values, disarming and `app`
    inheritance;
  - clear, RIS and least-recently-updated eviction at 256 records;
  - the neutral per-record facts: update sequence, change sequence, previous state and ages.
- Bend lifetime decisions for the prompt-mark drop and the foreground-group edge.
  - The edge is sampled at read start; the latch is "has this terminal ever sent OSC 133 A".
  - Drops keep stream order.
  - Bend holds that state. Add laws in LAWS.bend, proofs in PROOF.bend and the
    `boundary.schema` change.
  - **Show Lucca every new or changed law before relying on its proof.**
- Amend `orbit/docs/HOST.md` to name the store.
- Add ORB-C15 to `orbit/docs/CONTRACTS.md` as Planned.
- Fixtures recorded through Orbit:
  - real Claude Code ≥ 2.1.295 and Codex 0.163 bytes, including what Claude sends before its
    first prompt and whether either agent sends `done` and then `idle`;
  - malformed, oversized, split-chunk and discard-rule cases.

Out of scope:
- Management and `ProgramStatus` (the next bead), EONW, Venus, and any attention meaning such as
  raise, seen or finished.

## Acceptance

- Records follow ORB-C15's Result and Important failures sections exactly.
- The probe is answered before DA1. Show this with a real Claude Code ≥ 2.1.295 in an isolated
  Orbit session.
- Bend laws for the drop decisions pass PROOF.bend, including its sensitivity check.

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test` on the Orbit suites.
- PROOF.bend.
- `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings` for the Orbit crates.
- A Codex review, per AGENTS.md.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if libghostty's callback, at the eon-a9tr revision, cannot keep stream order between
  reports and prompt marks.
- Stop if the approved contract proves insufficient. Return to Lucca rather than widen it.

## Maintenance Notes

Portability disposition: neutral, since `tcgetpgrp` and the PTY are POSIX. Claude Code on this machine
is 2.1.293, so upgrade it before the live probe check.

title: Serve program status over management generation 2 (Orbit side)
description:
## Why

This is the second slice of epic eon-agent-sidebar-yx8. Eon Runtime reads Orbit's program-status records
through a new management request, `ProgramStatus`.

**Contract:** the ORB-C13 amendment and the ORB-C15 reply. Approved on 2026-10-21; the text is
the "Contract proposal, draft 15" comment on eon-agent-sidebar-yx8.1.

Lucca chose (Q1) management generation 2 as a breaking bump, with no compatibility window.

## Scope

In scope:
- Management generation 2: the `ProgramStatus` request and its reply of at most 4 KiB.
  - The reply has a fixed fill order: `blocked`, `error` and `done` come first, then the rest by
    most recent change.
  - It carries the full ids and the neutral facts.
- Bend decides to answer or refuse with Busy, and never defers.
  - The target is an answer within 250 ms.
  - The worker-stall bound caps each fact/decision exchange at 2 s, and an answer takes at most
    two exchanges.
  - Measure the real answer time under PTY load.
  - Laws go in LAWS.bend and are shown to Lucca.
- The Runtime side, with one reader per lease:
  - The EOF probe and Stop drain or await an in-flight reply, and replies are tagged by type.
  - A slow poll never drops a lease, and a Busy refusal counts as a missed poll deadline.
  - A test asserts the delay Stop sees under PTY load.
- Amend the "management v1" wording in ORB-C13, EON-C11 and EON-C15, and the ORB-C13 proof line.
- Rename or retire `--management-v1` and update every use (`rg -- --management-v1`).
- Add an `orbit/CHANGELOG.md` entry.
- Move ORB-C15 to Proven once its reply is proved.

Out of scope:
- The attention poller and its meaning (the next bead), EONW, and Venus.

## Acceptance

- Generation-2 handshakes work end to end. A generation-1 peer is refused, exactly as today's
  exact-generation rule refuses it.
- A Stop or EOF probe racing an in-flight `ProgramStatus` reply never misreads it. Show this with
  a focused test.

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test` (Orbit, Runtime and the protocol crate tests).
- PROOF.bend.
- fmt and clippy for the changed crates.
- A Codex review.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if one reader per lease needs a Runtime restructuring beyond `sessions.rs`. Split it out
  instead.

## Maintenance Notes

Portability disposition: neutral. Known consumers:
- Eon Runtime;
- `eon/crates/eon/tests/workspace_control.rs`;
- `orbit/tests/lifecycle.rs`;
- `orbit/tests/real_pty/{management_lease,management_record,descendant_exit,observer_finish}.rs`;
- `orbit/crates/protocol/tests/management.rs`.

Its Orbit /nix/store/w45pfnb7xgs563y5d342c7lrjxlsawmf-yazelix-orbit-0.1.0 passed the program_status real-PTY check: ProgramStatus over a --management-v2 lease, median 0.10 ms. Running supervisors are untouched and keep the old generation-1 Orbit until they are stopped; eon-5a stops them with the retained old eon.

(2) Busy rule for the law: under the lease Bend answers ProgramStatus while the child runs (lifecycle Detached or Attached) and answers Busy once a stop has begun or the child exited (Stopping or Stopped), since the records end with the run; outside the lease the existing slot rules apply (Negotiating rejects, Free and Closing stay quiet). title: Derive agent attention in Eon Runtime (EON-C31 model)
description:
## Why

This is the third slice of epic eon-agent-sidebar-yx8. Eon Runtime turns raw program-status records
into attention: what needs input, what has finished, and what has been seen.

**Contract:** EON-C31 internals. Approved on 2026-10-21; the text is the "Contract proposal,
draft 15" comment on eon-agent-sidebar-yx8.1.

## Scope

In scope:
- **The poller:** a new Runtime mechanism, `attention`, beside `quota`.
  - It runs off the request path, at no more than 2 Hz, and polls peers concurrently with a
    250 ms deadline.
  - It polls only pane and popup terminals, and skips leases with a Stop pending.
  - Inspect reads its cache.
- **Stale handling:** keep the last good result; mark it stale after 3 s.
- **Identity and time:** keys are (run ID, record `id`), and change times are fixed on first
  sight.
- **Raise:**
  - into `done` or `error`, including on creation;
  - `working` → `idle`;
  - `done` → `idle` keeps the earlier raise;
  - `error` → `idle` and `blocked` → `idle` do not raise (Q6).
- **Normalization:** needs input, error, finished, working, idle, or unavailable (an Agent popup
  with no records).
- **Seen:** set while a Venus is attached and the exact terminal has focus, at focus arrival, at a
  new raise, or at attach.
- **Rollup** and the queue's total order.
- **The cursor**, which resets on any other focus move and on a higher-class entry (Q7).
- **Sidebar visibility** per window in Runtime memory: `Open` by default, `Closed`, or `Off` (Q3).
- Amend EON-C4's mechanism count from nine to ten (docs/CONTRACTS.md:233, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:285).
- Add EON-C31 to `docs/CONTRACTS.md` as Planned.

Out of scope:
- EONW wire changes, actions, configuration parsing, the CLI, and Venus (the next bead).
- Persisting visibility. That moves into eon-reboot-restore-im8y's saved state when that bead
  lands.

## Acceptance

- Runtime unit tests cover every EON-C31 Result and Important-failure case:
  - stale data, out-of-order sequences, an Orbit process restart, a provider restart, removed
    targets, and detached windows;
  - raises lost when a record clears, a raise after a re-report, and the cursor walk and reset.

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime`.
- A Codex review.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if seen tracking needs window focus data, which EON-C31 accepts as a gap under D5.
- Stop if the poller cannot stay off the supervisor's request loop without restructuring it.

comments.text: Gap recorded (implementation, 2026-10-22): if a record goes done, working, done, then idle between two polls (500 ms), the idle keeps the cached raise of the first done (EON-C31: 'an idle from done keeps the cached raise of that done'). If that raise was already seen, the second finish is not shown. Orbit's facts can't tell this case apart: previous state is only the last one, and the update sequence counts reports across the whole terminal. Rare, not fixable without a new Orbit fact. Left as is.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Gap recorded (implementation, 2026-10-22), awaiting Lucca's acceptance: the Runtime remembers records the ProgramStatus reply omits for size, so their change times and seen raises survive until they return. It cannot tell an omitted record from a cleared one, so that memory is capped at Orbit's 256 records. Entries without a seen raise are evicted first, least recently updated first, and forgetting those changes nothing visible. A seen finish is lost, and shows as finished again, only if one terminal churns about 250 more seen-then-cleared records while that record stays crowded out of the reply. Closing this exactly would need a new Orbit fact.

title: Put agent attention on EONW v18
description:
## Why

This is the fourth slice of epic eon-agent-sidebar-yx8. It puts the attention model on the wire, so
Venus and the CLI can show it.

**Contract:** EON-C31's EONW part and the EON-C10 amendment. Approved on 2026-10-21; the text is
the "Contract proposal, draft 15" comment on eon-agent-sidebar-yx8.1.

## Scope

In scope:
- EONW v14, landed as one wire change. Recheck that v14 is still free first.
  - `attention` on `Pane` and `Popup`. It holds:
    - the normalized `state`, plus the record's kind, progress, `app`, `title` and `msg`;
    - `changed_at` in wall-clock milliseconds, the stale flag, and the count of other records.
  - `attention_rollup` on `Tab`.
  - `sidebar` (`Open | Closed | Off`) on `Snapshot`.
  - Actions:
    - `ToggleSidebar`;
    - `FocusAttention { tab, target }`, which takes an exact pane id or popup instance. A stale
      target is rejected as an EONW action rejection;
    - `NextAttention` and `PreviousAttention`.
  - All of these actions follow the covered-target rule: a keep-alive popup is hidden; a
    transient popup or a pending picker is left alone, and the action only selects the tab.
- `[sidebar] enabled` configuration. eonbase is always `Off`.
- CLI JSON (Q8) carries exactly:
  - `attention: { state, app }` on panes and popups;
  - `attention_rollup` on tabs;
  - `sidebar` on the snapshot.

  Add the EON-C10 projection exception for the EONW fields that the CLI leaves out.
- The Venus decoder, with no rendering yet.
- Contract and doc updates:
  - The EON-C10 amendment: v14 bytes; exceptions for report text and for terminal content; a
    clarifying sentence on provider selection.
  - EON-C8's v14 Consumes line, its provider-state exception, and its attention-only notice
    clause.
  - Other v13 references in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, runtime/README.md,
    venus/docs/PRESENTATION.md, venus/docs/CRATES.md and venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md:8.
  - The component graph moves to EONW 14.

Out of scope:
- Rendering: tab markers and the sidebar (the next beads).
- New `eon` CLI commands.

## Acceptance

- The protocol crate round-trips every v14 field and action.
- A snapshot with the maximum attention fields fits the 2 MiB frame.
- Runtime tests cover the action semantics, including the covered-target rule and stale
  rejection.

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test` (the protocol, Runtime and Venus decoder suites).
- The component-graph check.
- A Codex review.

## Maintenance Notes

Portability disposition: neutral. This also unblocks eon-iwmz, the completion sound.

- **Prerequisite (eon-igae.12.4):** ask Lucca to stop older v13 generations before the profile
  refresh. The new `eon` cannot stop them.
- **Q3 follow-up:** if eon-reboot-restore-im8y has landed first, move `sidebar` visibility into
  its saved per-window state here. Otherwise im8y does that move.

title: Jump to agents with Alt+G and Alt+Shift+G
description:
## Why

This is the seventh slice of epic eon-agent-sidebar-yx8: jumping to the agent that needs you.
Lucca decided the keys on 2026-10-21 (D9): Alt+G goes to the next agent, Alt+Shift+G to the
previous one.

**Contract:** the Alt+G/Alt+Shift+G part of the EON-C20/VEN-C20 and EON-C24/VEN-C24 amendments,
and the VEN-C18 F6 amendment. Approved on 2026-10-21; the text is the "Contract proposal,
draft 15" comment on eon-agent-sidebar-yx8.1.

## Scope

In scope:
- Fixed bindings in `FIXED_SHORTCUTS`: Alt+G sends `NextAttention` and Alt+Shift+G sends
  `PreviousAttention`.
  - Both work whether the sidebar is visible or not, including when it is `Off`.
  - A configured popup may take either key.
  - The shortcut viewer and the hints list both keys.
- F6 cycles Terminal → Sidebar → Tabs → Panes, skipping the sidebar when it is not visible.
  Update the F6 label in `venus/src/application/shortcuts.rs`.
- `docs/USAGE.md`'s shortcut table, plus a CHANGELOG entry.

Out of scope:
- New `eon` CLI commands.
- Notifications.

## Acceptance

- Tests show Alt+G walking the queue, the cursor reset, and a configured popup overriding the
  keys.
- The F6 order is shown with the sidebar both visible and hidden.

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test -p venus`, plus fmt and clippy.
- One dogfood observation.
- A Codex review.

## Maintenance Notes

Portability disposition: neutral. Evidence that Alt+G is free was gathered on 2026-10-21:
- Nothing Eon ships binds it, and neither do Claude Code, Codex or tmux.
- Minor losses: Emacs's `M-g`, bash `glob-complete-word`, zsh `get-line`, and micro's key menu.
close_reason: Alt+G and Alt+Shift+G shipped and proved on the installed package (proof comment)

- Shape: Venus-only. Alt+G and Alt+Shift+G join FIXED_SHORTCUTS (Navigate group) as NextAttention and PreviousAttention, and workspace_shortcut maps them to EONW v18 NextAttention and PreviousAttention. The Runtime already owns the queue and cursor (yx8.6, yx8.7, supervisor.rs NextAttention dispatch). This adds no wire, dependency, lifecycle or protocol change, so no reference gate is needed. Portability: neutral.
- Acceptance mapping: the queue walk and the cursor reset are proved by Runtime `the_queue_walks_its_total_order_and_its_cursor_resets` (attention.rs), which this slice reuses rather than duplicating. The Venus tests cover the rest: `direct_workspace_shortcuts_use_stable_eon_actions` shows both keys under Open, Closed and Off; `configured_popups_take_fixed_bindings_except_reserved_keys` shows a popup on Alt+G taking it, with the viewer marking it overridden and Alt+Shift+G kept; `shortcut_hints_follow_bindings_catalog_and_native_focus` shows the viewer rows and hints under every `sidebar`. F6 moved to yx8.13 (comment above).
- Decisions taken under Lucca's 2026-10-23 sidebar approval, relayed by the overseer eon-a8 ("everything is autoaproved regarding the sidebar"):
  - Viewer labels "Jump to the next agent needing attention" and "Jump to the previous agent needing attention"; hint labels "next agent" (priority 2) and "previous agent" (priority 3), so width pressure drops them before the core navigation hints.
  - Alt+G behaves like the other fixed workspace actions: it does not move keyboard focus itself. From the terminal, focus follows the attached terminal. From chrome, focus stays in chrome, unless the sidebar's focused row disappears. Only row activation (yx8.13) moves focus to the target.
  - Contract text: the approved EON-C20/VEN-C20 and EON-C24/VEN-C24 amendments for Alt+G and Alt+Shift+G go in now, together with the VEN-C30 status line. The installed rows and hints stay under Open proof until this bead's dogfood.

title: Let authorized agents send input to Eon terminals
description:
## Decision
Lucca, 2026-10-15: plan agent-facing commands that read and drive Eon terminals, the way agents use
tmux `capture-pane` and `send-keys`. Rescoped the same day (prime-beads pass): reading is already
planned in deferred epic `orb-p92`, so this bead owns only sending input, built on that observer's
identity, authorization and Eon policy. Design and contract are not chosen yet.

## Contract (provisional)
- Consumer: an AI coding agent or script running as the same local user, inside or outside Eon.
- Trigger: an Eon CLI command with machine-readable output.
- Result: an explicitly authorized caller sends text or keys to one selected live terminal while
Venus stays the only interactive attachment and the user's focus is untouched.
- Important failures: unknown, ended or older-generation terminals are reported, never guessed;
input to an ended terminal is rejected, not queued; revoked or expired authority sends nothing.

## Already available or planned elsewhere
- Listing: `eon workspace --json` (docs/USAGE.md:202) maps tabs, panes, popups and terminals.
- Reading: `orb-p92` phase 1 (explicitly authorized, bounded, read-only visible text, title, CWD,
active screen and revision; lossy text labelled). It excludes synthetic input and points mutating
actions here (its `astra-db8.9` reference is a pre-consolidation ID).
- Agent-driven terminal testing boundary: decision `eon-pxn.7`.

## Open design decisions
Command shape and identity; semantic keys encoded by Orbit (as Venus input is) versus pasted text;
whether input requires a visible indicator, per-terminal consent or an AgentRun capability from
`eon-pxn`; rate and size bounds; interaction with the user typing at the same time.

## Evidence (edge dc937b7)
Orbit's management protocol (`orbit/crates/protocol/src/management.rs:75-91`) offers only Acquire,
Status and Stop, and exactly one client may attach (`orbit/AGENTS.md`), so input from a second
party needs a new Orbit capability: an `orbit-protocol` change to classify as compatible or
breaking, with consumers Venus, Eon Runtime, Eon and bend-orbit. Orbit already encodes semantic
input against its authoritative state.

## Owners
Orbit owns input encoding and enforcement of the granted capability. Eon owns consent, terminal
selection, capability issuance, expiry and revocation (shared with `orb-p92`'s Eon policy
contract). Eon Runtime owns the CLI. Venus is unchanged.

## Prerequisites and reference gate
Blocked by `orb-p92` (observer identity, authorization owner and Eon policy contract). Consequential:
new EON and ORB contracts, a wire change and a trust boundary (injecting input into a user's
terminal). Inspect at exact revisions tmux `send-keys`, WezTerm `cli send-text`, kitty remote control
`send-text` and Zellij `write-chars`, plus `orb-p92`'s reference set. Stop for Lucca's design and
contract approval before code.

## Acceptance
- Design: Lucca approves the design and contracts.
- Implementation: in installed Eon, an authorized command from one pane sends a command to another
pane and the result is observable through the accepted observer; denial, expiry, revocation,
ended-terminal and oversized-input failures behave as specified. Full affected Rust and Nix surfaces
plus one isolated installed dogfood observation.

## Stop boundary
No remote or MCP exposure, multi-client interactive attachment, raw PTY access, process control,
scripting framework or plugin system. No code, contract or protocol change before approval.

title: Give one real agent workflow an Eon AgentRun identity
description:
## Origin
Split from closed `eon-pxn` on 2026-10-16 at Lucca's request. That epic's design, rejected
alternatives and comparison comments (cmux, Unpeel, TUIOS, Zeron, Herdr, Amp Orbs, VS Code Agent
Host) remain the evidence record.

## Contract (provisional)
For one real coding-agent workflow chosen from Lucca's use, Eon gives each agent run an explicit
AgentRun identity that links to, but never equals, its pane, Orbit terminal, process or provider
thread. Eon owns its launch, resume and stop policy. Execution state (from Orbit), provider semantic
state (from an explicit provider report, otherwise unknown) and Eon attention state stay distinct,
and each semantic value carries its source and freshness.

## Evidence (edge 798ab79)
- Agent popups already start the first installed of Codex, Grok, OpenCode, Pi or Claude with their
own resume commands (`eon/crates/eon/src/product.rs`), but Eon has no AgentRun owner.
- `eon-pxn.9` deferred Bend for the AgentRun transition kernel until Bend ships a supported native
embedding target; the kernel stays Rust-owned for now.
- `docs/REFERENCES.md` agent-work routes require explicit provider evidence and distinct
work/attempt/provider/terminal/process identities.

## Owners
Eon Runtime owns AgentRun identity, relationships and lifecycle policy; provider adapters own
provider-native meanings; Orbit keeps terminal and process authority; Venus only presents.

## Prerequisites and reference gate
Consequential (new contract, identity and lifecycle). Pick the provider workflow first. Read EON-C8,
EON-C10 and the agent-work routes; re-inspect Herdr and one provider's hook surface at exact
revisions. Stop for Lucca's contract approval before code.

## Acceptance
An isolated installed check runs the chosen workflow through start, hide, resume and stop with the
AgentRun linked to its terminal; an unsupported provider stays a usable terminal with unknown
semantic state.

## Stop boundary
No terminal-text, process-name or silence heuristics as provider truth, no provider compatibility
promise, no persistence, MCP or event stream.

title: Allow one picker to remain bound to an inactive tab in EONW v4
description:
## Contract

Consumer: exact Eon workspace producers and Venus consumers of private EONW v4.

Trigger: one live directory picker remains bound to a tab while another durable tab is active, including after leaving a pane-free pending tab.

Result: EONW v4 accepts and round-trips the existing snapshot shape without a new field, action, version, or dependency. The picker tab must remain live. It may be inactive. Its endpoint remains unique. At most one pane-free tab exists, and it must be the picker tab; the active tab must have a selected live pane unless it is that pane-free picker tab.

Important failures: a missing picker tab, a pane-free tab without the picker, multiple pane-free tabs, an active durable tab without a selected pane, aliased endpoints, duplicate identities, or existing bounds remain invalid.

Ownership: Eon owns EONW validation and workspace topology. Venus consumes the accepted state and decides which active-tab endpoint to present. Orbit is unchanged.

## Prerequisites and reference gate

User authorized the cross-repository expansion on 2026-08-27 after the original Eon-only gate was disproved. Read EON-C8 and EON-C18; complete EONW v4 encode/decode validation and tests; the original picker-first Bead eon-start-tabs-with-yazi-picker-1az; current Workspace snapshot production; and exact accepted Venus bdd8b3628452b1dba8c4d4b2ad9bc2e802659d29 only to confirm consumer requirements.

Preserve one picker, exact tab binding, existing wire bytes, pending-tab ownership, endpoint uniqueness, stable limits, and exact-version rejection. Reject hiding the picker from snapshots, moving it between tabs, a second schema, EONW v5, a generic modal, or Orbit changes.

## Scope boundary

Only EONW v4 state validity, its focused regression proof, EON-C18 wording, current protocol documentation, LOC, and the exact proof revision. No Venus production edit, Eon workspace dispatch change, component pin, profile refresh, keybinding, picker lifecycle change, or platform expansion.

## Acceptance Criteria

The structured acceptance criteria field is canonical.
design:
1. Update the EON-C18 contract before implementation to distinguish picker ownership from active presentation.
2. Add one v4 codec regression containing both inactive durable-picker and inactive pending-picker snapshots, plus constraining invalid cases.
3. Delete only the active-picker equality and active-pending requirement from validate_snapshot; replace them with one live-picker-tab and sole-pending-tab invariant using the existing validation loop. Add no helper unless it reduces the validator.
4. Run the focused protocol check and complete locked protocol package checks. Commit the proof seed before Venus consumes its exact revision.
5. Update only current protocol documentation and the README LOC scorecard; do not claim native behavior.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A v4 snapshot with one inactive picker-owning durable tab and an active durable tab round-trips unchanged.
2. A v4 snapshot with one inactive picker-owning pane-free pending tab and an active durable tab round-trips unchanged.
3. Returning the picker tab to active requires no state translation and retains the exact picker identity and endpoint.
4. Missing or duplicate picker ownership, any other pane-free tab, invalid active selection, aliased endpoints, invalid identities, and all existing bounds remain rejected.
5. Existing EONW v1 through v3 behavior and exact-version rejection remain unchanged; no field, action, version, crate, or dependency is added.
6. Focused red/green codec proof plus the complete locked protocol package checks, EON-C18/current docs, README LOC scorecard, Beads state, and final diff pass succeed on one candidate revision.
notes:
Execution baseline: edge 65a32269566eb72d0eaeaf064b0a7612e0ae1557; pre-existing dirty .beads/issues.jsonl contained only the user-authorized three-Bead split. Changed owners: EONW v4 validation/tests, EON-C18/architecture wording, and README LOC.

Reference gate: EON-C8 and EON-C18, complete EONW v4 codec/validator/tests, original picker-first Bead eon-start-tabs-with-yazi-picker-1az, Workspace snapshot production, and accepted Venus bdd8b3628452b1dba8c4d4b2ad9bc2e802659d29 model/application behavior were inspected. Preserved one picker, exact live-tab binding, sole picker-owned pane-free tab, endpoint uniqueness, bounds, and v1-v3 exact rejection. Rejected hiding/moving the picker, EONW v5, new fields/actions/helpers/dependencies, a second schema, generic modal, and Orbit changes.

Implemented shape: removed only the active-tab equality and active-pending requirement; added one live picker-tab validation after the existing tab loop. One focused regression round-trips inactive durable and pending picker tabs and rejects a missing picker tab. Existing invalid pending and alias checks remain authoritative.

Mechanical proof on x86_64 Linux candidate: focused red failed with InvalidSnapshot directory picker tab; focused green passed both v4 tests. cargo fmt --all -- --check, cargo check --locked --workspace, cargo test --locked --workspace (27 Eon unit, 25 process integration, 4 manifest, 4 EONW), cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings, and nix flake check path:. --print-build-logs all exited 0. Nix rebuilt accepted Venus against the local widened protocol and passed 112 Venus tests plus Eon/EonTerm checks. README LOC is exact at 15,243. No profile, process, Session, manifest, child source, dependency, or runtime behavior changed.
close_reason: Accepted EONW v4 owner proof 963bdaf4d9816f27a26c7bdb6ee122855566a222 admits one inactive live picker tab while preserving sole pending-tab ownership, bounds, endpoint uniqueness, exact older-version rejection, and zero new fields/actions/dependencies; complete locked Rust and Nix checks passed.

title: Allow multiple pending Eon tabs with independent pickers
description:
## Contract
Consumer: full Eon user creating tabs from the bar, keyboard shortcut, or CLI while a new-tab Project picker is open. Trigger: CreateTab with an existing pending tab. Result: create a distinct active pending tab and exact Project picker; earlier pending tabs and their pickers remain selectable and independently completable. Alt+Shift+W closes only the selected pending tab and stops its exact picker; no new cancel protocol is added. Failures: capacity or picker launch must not leave a partial tab; stale picker completion or close must not mutate another tab; pending tabs remain bounded and valid across tab switching.

## Prerequisites and reference gate
Preserve accepted Orbit f8ad14e, current Venus VEN-C18/VEN-C21 source 6aa79f6, and EONW v6 source 3103a00. Review EON-C10/EON-C18 and docs/REFERENCES.md picker-first/shared-popup routes, Eon workspace/control/supervisor and v2-v6 codecs, comparable v3/v4 protocol seeds, and Venus model/transport/Scene/input. The widened snapshot state requires an explicit next EONW version and exact Venus consumption; do not silently change the v6 validator.

## Scope
Eon-owned pending-tab policy, per-tab picker lifecycle, EONW validity and version, exact Venus consumer adaptation, and composed Eon pin/profile. Reuse existing picker and CloseTab actions. No new cancellation opcode, picker UI, process owner, generic tab framework, dependency, platform promise, or live-supervisor restart.

## Acceptance
Focused red/green owner and codec checks prove two pending tabs with distinct picker identities, independent switching/completion/Alt+Shift+W close, rollback on launch failure, stale-target safety, old-version rejection and bounds. Affected locked Rust and Nix checks pass. One isolated installed native Wayland run exercises New tab while the first picker is visible, tab switching, close and remaining picker. Refresh the named profile while preserving live Sessions; record exact revisions and proof limits.
close_reason: Background picker exit now preserves selected tab; exact installed private native proof passed

comments.text:
Reference gate — alternate desktop identity under EON-C1

Question: How should Eon package a second launcher identity without creating a second runtime owner or duplicating the canonical desktop-entry policy?
Contract: EON-C1 only. Selecting “Eon (Alternate Icon)” must invoke the same `eon` executable and retain `StartupWMClass=yazelix-venus`; only desktop-file ID, display name, and icon name differ.
Sources and revisions: current `flake.nix` desktop owner at Eon HEAD 2b8fef19bb09d7ea0d1e891720eb36c838cbd237; Nixpkgs `pkgs/build-support/make-desktopitem/default.nix` at pinned revision 567a49d1913ce81ac6e9582e3553dd90a955875f; Nixpkgs RustDesk package at that revision as a comparable multiple-`desktopItems` implementation; user-owned source `assets/icon-concepts/icon_eon_3.png`, SHA-256 1bc63f18c821520e9a3b5e09f1c8bd5e33b5a87da85179523cb22bc1fb0d9786, 1254x1254 RGB.
Constraints preserved: `makeDesktopItem` renders and runs `desktop-file-validate`; it is explicitly `lib.makeOverridable`, so the established canonical derivation can own all shared fields and a sibling override can change only `name`, `desktopName`, and `icon`. `copyDesktopItems` accepts a list. Both launchers retain `Exec=eon`, categories, keywords, terminal policy, and WM grouping. The canonical `assets/eon.png` and `eon.desktop` remain unchanged.
Options compared: no second entry (rejects the explicit request); duplicate a full `makeDesktopItem` attrset (works but creates duplicate launcher policy); add a desktop action to the canonical entry (not a separate desktop entry and cannot supply an independently selectable application icon); override the existing derivation (selected).
Decision: prepare one transparent `assets/eon-alternate.png`; create `eon-alternate.desktop` by overriding the canonical desktop item only at the three identity fields; install both icons through the existing Nix package.
Rejected alternatives and failure conditions: replacing the canonical icon violates the requested sibling identity; a second executable/configuration/product duplicates runtime ownership; SVG tracing or new icon tooling adds unsupported geometry and dependencies.
Cheapest proof: image metadata/alpha checks, exact generated desktop-file field comparison plus `desktop-file-validate`, pinned flake evaluation/build, installed-icon comparison, and `git diff --check`.
Exit condition: the second entry and prepared icon validate and package while canonical entry/icon metadata and the Eon component graph remain unchanged.

title: Diagnose mise trust errors in Claude Code SessionStart hooks inside Eon
description:
## Report
Lucca, 2026-10-19 (screenshot): starting Claude Code v2.1.293 in ~/pjs/evo/evo-clinica printed four
non-blocking `SessionStart:startup hook error` lines, each "mise ERROR error parsing config file:
~/pjs/evo/evo-clinica/mise.toml". Lucca is dogfooding Eon (the "Eon (Bend Orbit)" entry).

## Evidence (2026-10-19, not yet a diagnosis)
- Two mise binaries: ~/.local/bin/mise 2026.7.0 and ~/.nix-profile/bin/mise 2026.5.12.
- In evo-clinica, ~/.local/bin/mise parses mise.toml (java temurin-25, npm 8.19.4, node 16.20.2).
  ~/.nix-profile/bin/mise fails with the screenshot's error and the reason: "Config files in
  ~/pjs/evo/evo-clinica/mise.toml are not trusted".
- The hooks are plugin SessionStart hooks (vercel, zj-radar, codex), not a project hook; one of them
  runs through a mise shim or activation that resolves the Nix-profile mise.
- Open question: whether Eon's session environment puts ~/.nix-profile/bin before ~/.local/bin (an
  Eon PATH-ordering difference from Lucca's login shell, which would make this Eon's) or whether
  any shell would hit it (Lucca's environment: two mise installs with separate trust).

## Scope
In: find which hook calls mise and with which PATH, inside Eon and outside it; decide the owner.
If Eon's environment changes which tool resolves, propose the fix on Eon's launch environment and
stop for Lucca's approval. Otherwise recommend the user-side fix (one mise, or `mise trust` with
the other) and let Lucca apply it.
Out: changing evo-clinica's mise.toml or trusting configs on Lucca's behalf.

## Acceptance
The cause and its owner recorded here, with the observation that shows it, and the fix applied or
handed to its owner.
close_reason: Trusted the moved evo-clinica config for the shims' mise; not an Eon issue

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Diagnosis and fix (2026-10-19): not Eon's. The mise shims in ~/.local/share/mise/shims (codex, copilot, ...) link to ~/.nix-profile/bin/mise 2026.5.12, so a plugin SessionStart hook that runs e.g. codex goes through the old mise, which reads ./mise.toml only when trusted. Trust is per path: the trust store had ~/pjs/elfo/evo-clinica but not ~/pjs/evo/evo-clinica (the project moved). ~/.local/bin/mise 2026.7.0 accepts the tools-only config without trust, which hid it in direct use. Fix, with Lucca's go-ahead ('if you can fix it easily, please do so'): ~/.nix-profile/bin/mise trust ~/pjs/evo/evo-clinica/mise.toml. Check: that mise's 'config ls' in evo-clinica now lists mise.toml (java, npm, node) with no error, and the codex shim runs (codex-cli 0.163.0). Not done (Lucca's choice): reshim with the newer mise or remove one of the two installs; other moved projects would hit the same error until trusted. Not re-observed in a fresh Claude Code start.

title: Integrate Anima startup, eon anima, and Alt+Shift+A popup
description:
## Outcome
A fresh full-Eon interactive workspace plays one short, dismissible native Anima animation after Venus readiness and before its initial Project picker. `eon anima [STYLE] [CHILD OPTIONS...]` delegates to the same pinned child in the caller terminal. Alt+Shift+A opens or closes a tab-scoped transient Anima popup.

## Contract and owners
EON-C1/C2/C3/C4/C11/C18 and accepted EONW v7. Eon owns exact component selection, startup eligibility/defaults, CLI delegation and popup policy. Anima owns styles, random choice, browsing, rendering, duration and terminal cleanup. Orbit owns the PTY Session; Venus owns native input, presentation and shortcut dispatch. No copied animation, renderer or child schema in Eon.

## Reference and dependency gate
Anima 0.2.0 source b3133f057fa0029b3e06c85301161168c48bb799 and Nova e476ca8065cc8b2c02ea611ae7edeeb0989c0c23 were inspected with Eon launch, readiness, picker and popup owners. Manifest Orbit b6cecf8f2ee35570b41cfdc578b095889d917fe2 and Venus 773c6bab7d3e21e0b0d7d942c9bba72260a08b42 matched latest accepted revisions at activation. The decision and rejected mechanisms are recorded in comments and docs/REFERENCES.md.

## Chosen defaults and boundary
The user selected startup enabled, random style, three seconds and a disable setting on 2026-09-24, then added the Alt+Shift+A popup. Startup runs only for a fresh interactive full-Eon workspace. Exact-command EonTerm, attachment, recovery and later tabs are outside this trigger. Rich Kitty/image graphics, new animation styles and other platforms remain outside scope. The related deferred popup-decision issue is a planning duplicate for later reconciliation.

## Proof
Implementation and installed native observations are recorded under EON-C18 in docs/CONTRACTS.md. Native captures are retained at ~/.local/state/eon/proofs/eon-anima-startup-5el-2026-09-24/.
acceptance_criteria:
- The component manifest and Nix package resolve exact Anima b3133f057fa0029b3e06c85301161168c48bb799; EonTerm closure remains free of Anima.
- `eon anima` forwards child arguments/help and exit status in the caller terminal without launching a workspace.
- Valid `[anima]` settings default to enabled/random/3 seconds; invalid settings fail before launch. Startup waits for Venus ready-v1, plays once in the initial Project Session, hands off to the picker, and never replays on attach, reconnect, recovery or later tabs.
- Dismissal consumes its key and restores the terminal before the picker. Missing, failed or stuck playback reports briefly and continues to the picker within a bound.
- Alt+Shift+A is the installed Anima popup shortcut. Invoking it displays pinned Anima in one transient Orbit Session; closing, replacing or dismissing the popup stops playback and returns focus to the tab.
- Focused Rust contract checks, full affected Rust/Nix checks, exact profile refresh and isolated installed native Wayland startup, disabled, popup/dismiss and reattach observations are recorded with limits. README, help, configuration and LOC are current.
notes: 2026-09-24 user expansion: also ship a built-in transient Anima popup on Alt+Shift+A in this same integration. It runs pinned Anima random in its own Orbit popup Session through the accepted Eon popup owner; Anima handles browsing/dismissal; closing or replacing the popup stops the Session; focus returns to the tab. This supersedes the original no-popup scope boundary for this issue only. The related deferred decision bead is a planning duplicate to reconcile in a later writing run.

title: Draw the working badge as an antialiased open arc
description:
## Why

Lucca found the working badge hard to read (2026-10-23). The research bead eon-spinner-research-pinn compared candidates at real size (contact sheet: ~/.cache/eon-agents/eon-fd/spinner/contact-sheet-x3.png). The cause: today's 8-segment ring isn't antialiased (`MultisampleState::default`), and its 0.11-alpha faded segments vanish at a 10 px glyph. Lucca picked C2, a coverage-antialiased 270° arc with no track whose still form is the same arc ("1. approve"), and approved the VEN-C21 wording ("2. approve"), both on 2026-10-23 and recorded on the research bead.

## Contract (approved text)

In venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md VEN-C21, "Attention badges (EON-C31)", the CPU-adapter bullet becomes exactly:
"- on a software (CPU) graphics adapter the working badge is a still open arc that never repaints to animate; otherwise the arc turns, repainting at no more than 5 Hz under AP-PERF-001, and only the badge;"
Nothing else changes ("corner badge (◆, ✕, ✓, or a spinner)" and the existing proof records stay).

## Implementation note (from the research)

Draw C2 as a fixed grid of 1x1 coverage quads over the glyph box, keeping zero-alpha pixels: 100 quads at scale 1, 400 at scale 2, against 8 today. The vertex count stays fixed per phase, so today's in-place alpha-only rewrite and the 5 Hz badge-only tick hold. There are 8 phases in 45° clockwise steps, with the arc trailing its head. The research harness's coverage math, in ~/.cache/eon-agents/eon-fd/spinner/, is the reference. The still form on CPU adapters (yx8.15) is the same arc at a fixed phase. The same drawing serves Eon Bar tab badges and VEN-C30 sidebar rows.

## Scope

In scope: the Venus badge drawing, the approved VEN-C21 text, venus/CHANGELOG.md and the root CHANGELOG, and the scene goldens or tests that pin the badge.

Out of scope: other badge states (◆ ✕ ✓ idle), and antialiasing elsewhere in Venus.

## Acceptance

- A scene or render test pins the arc at scale 1 and 2 and the still form.
- CPU measurement on the yx8.15 setup (isolated headless Sway, pixman, then a hardware adapter): no regression against the yx8.15 baseline (62 ticks/20 s still on lavapipe) and the yx8.2 hardware baseline (about 0.4% of a core).
- One installed observation: a working agent's badge reads as a turning arc on the hardware adapter.

## Verification

`nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-venus`, Venus fmt and clippy, converge plus Codex, the nix build, the isolated measurement, and the profile refresh.

Portability disposition: neutral.
close_reason: The working badge is an antialiased open arc (C2): it turns at 5 Hz on hardware adapters and is still on CPU adapters. VEN-C21 has the approved text. Scale 1 and 2 goldens and the still form are pinned. Isolated pixman and GPU CPU measurements match the yx8.15/yx8.2 baselines.

title: Audit the canonical Eon component graph
description:
## Contract routing

This is a read-only repository audit. It changes no EON product contract, implements no feature or fix, and authorizes no dependency, compatibility surface, or public behavior. Audit one exact accepted revision and preserve all pre-existing worktree state.

## Why

Feature-local fresh-eyes and simplification passes can converge while stable identities, compatibility edges, validation, and consumers can drift into duplicate graphs. This subsystem owns a distinct invariant and failure domain, so it needs one bounded whole-subsystem review that includes direct callers and consumers.

## Evidence

- `components/eon-alpha-v1.json:1`: one distribution-neutral graph records the alpha composition
- `crates/eon-manifest/src/lib.rs:129`: the validator is the graph acceptance owner
- `crates/eon-manifest/src/lib.rs:171`: semantic compatibility validation is centralized
- `flake.nix:52`: Nix consumes the canonical JSON graph

## Prerequisites and reference gate

- There is no planning dependency beyond a stable in-scope subject. Do not start while another issue or agent is changing an in-scope surface.
- Route each architecture, dependency, portability, or ownership question through `docs/REFERENCES.md`; read the relevant primary sources and at least one comparable implementation when one exists. Also read the applicable contract proofs and dependency or flake decisions. Record the question, exact source revisions, preserved constraints, rejected approaches, decision, and cheapest check in this Bead. Reuse prior evidence only when the question and exact revision still match.

## Scope

In scope:
- `components/eon-alpha-v1.json`, the complete `eon-manifest` crate, and focused graph tests.

1. Record governing instructions, tracker state, accepted contract proofs, and immutable subject identity: clean HEAD, or HEAD plus a SHA-256 of the tracked binary diff and hashes of every in-scope untracked file. Preserve the exact dirty paths.
2. Read every in-scope owner, its direct callers and consumers, meaningful tests, contract rows, reference decisions, and dependency decisions.
3. Trace the observable flow end to end and audit correctness, failures, bounds, security boundaries, performance, tests, ownership, dependencies, portability, DX, and documentation.
4. Run a fresh-eyes correctness pass, then a separate simplification and ownership pass. Reject style preferences, speculative features, accepted tradeoffs, and duplicates of existing Beads.
5. Vet each remaining finding against exact file:line evidence and record impact, effort (S/M/L), implementation risk, confidence, the cheapest falsifying check, and why it merits action.

- Every finding is concrete, reproducible or directly evidenced, ownership-routed, and checked against existing Beads.
- No tracked project file or preserved untracked user artifact changes during the audit; generated build outputs do not alter the recorded subject snapshot.

- The final pass reports convergence under the declared lenses without widening that claim to runtime or platform behavior not exercised.
- Findings remain recommendations until the user chooses separate remediation work.

## Verification

- `cargo check --locked --workspace` should exit 0 on the audited revision.
- `cargo test --locked --workspace` should exit 0 on the audited revision.
- `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` should exit 0 on the audited revision.

- `br sync --flush-only` should persist the audit record without changing implementation.

## Stop conditions

title: Audit Eon managed-environment ownership
description:
## Contract routing

This is a read-only repository audit. It changes no EON product contract, implements no feature or fix, and authorizes no dependency, compatibility surface, or public behavior. Audit one exact accepted revision and preserve all pre-existing worktree state.

## Why

Feature-local fresh-eyes and simplification passes can converge while dispatch names, environment isolation, defaults, and package wiring can create a second owner for child behavior. This subsystem owns a distinct invariant and failure domain, so it needs one bounded whole-subsystem review that includes direct callers and consumers.

## Evidence

- `crates/eon/src/main.rs:96`: managed command construction owns the runtime environment projection
- `crates/eon/src/main.rs:326`: managed program inputs are explicit
- `defaults/nushell/config.nu:1`: the managed shell consumes sparse native initialization
- `flake.nix:198`: exact managed packages and generated native defaults are resolved in Nix

## Prerequisites and reference gate

- There is no planning dependency beyond a stable in-scope subject. Do not start while another issue or agent is changing an in-scope surface.
- Route each architecture, dependency, portability, or ownership question through `docs/REFERENCES.md`; read the relevant primary sources and at least one comparable implementation when one exists. Also read the applicable contract proofs and dependency or flake decisions. Record the question, exact source revisions, preserved constraints, rejected approaches, decision, and cheapest check in this Bead. Reuse prior evidence only when the question and exact revision still match.

## Scope

In scope:
- Managed invocation detection and command construction in `crates/eon/src/main.rs`.
- `defaults/` plus symlink, wrapper, PATH, configuration, license, and tool-version wiring in `flake.nix`.
- Unit/integration tests and EON-C9 proof claims for ambient PATH, native overrides, relative roots, and explicit argv.
- Native child schemas only as boundaries; do not audit or replace child behavior.

Out of scope:
- Implementing, fixing, refactoring, or editing repository files.
- Adding or changing product contracts, dependencies, compatibility promises, or deferred features.
- Auditing behavior owned by another repository beyond verifying the consumed boundary.
- Creating remediation Beads unless the user separately authorizes a planning-only batch.

## Audit method

1. Record governing instructions, tracker state, accepted contract proofs, and immutable subject identity: clean HEAD, or HEAD plus a SHA-256 of the tracked binary diff and hashes of every in-scope untracked file. Preserve the exact dirty paths.
2. Read every in-scope owner, its direct callers and consumers, meaningful tests, contract rows, reference decisions, and dependency decisions.
3. Trace the observable flow end to end and audit correctness, failures, bounds, security boundaries, performance, tests, ownership, dependencies, portability, DX, and documentation.
4. Run a fresh-eyes correctness pass, then a separate simplification and ownership pass. Reject style preferences, speculative features, accepted tradeoffs, and duplicates of existing Beads.
5. Vet each remaining finding against exact file:line evidence and record impact, effort (S/M/L), implementation risk, confidence, the cheapest falsifying check, and why it merits action.
6. Repeat the complete review after any material planning correction or subject-snapshot change. Converge only when a final full pass over one unchanged recorded snapshot finds no additional actionable finding beyond the recorded set.
7. Record either the vetted findings or an explicit no-finding result in this Bead with the audited revision, commands, failures, and remaining proof limits.

## Acceptance

- The audit covers the complete stated subsystem and adjacent boundaries, not only recent diffs.
- Every finding is concrete, reproducible or directly evidenced, ownership-routed, and checked against existing Beads.
- No tracked project file or preserved untracked user artifact changes during the audit; generated build outputs do not alter the recorded subject snapshot.
- The final record identifies the exact subject snapshot; any in-scope subject change invalidates prior completion and requires a complete new pass.
- The final pass reports convergence under the declared lenses without widening that claim to runtime or platform behavior not exercised.
- Findings remain recommendations until the user chooses separate remediation work.

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --all --check` should exit 0 on the audited revision.
- `cargo check --locked --workspace` should exit 0 on the audited revision.
- `cargo test --locked --workspace` should exit 0 on the audited revision.
- `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` should exit 0 on the audited revision.
- `git diff --check` should exit 0 on the audited revision.
- `nix flake check --no-build --no-update-lock-file path:.` should exit 0 on the audited revision.
- A prior verification result may be cited instead of rerun only when its recorded subject snapshot, environment, command, and exercised surface match exactly; otherwise rerun it.
- `br sync --flush-only` should persist the audit record without changing implementation.
- Final status and diff inspection should show only the pre-existing worktree plus authorized Beads mutations.

## Stop conditions

- Stop if an active implementation owns or materially changes an in-scope surface.
- Stop if evidence requires a new contract, dependency decision, cross-repository owner change, or scope expansion.
- Stop and report rather than compensating for an upstream or downstream contract gap.

title: Audit Eon runtime and lifecycle ownership
description:
## Contract routing

This is a read-only repository audit. It changes no EON product contract, implements no feature or fix, and authorizes no dependency, compatibility surface, or public behavior. Audit one exact accepted revision and preserve all pre-existing worktree state.

## Why

Feature-local fresh-eyes and simplification passes can converge while CLI, process, socket, and cleanup policies can drift across individually correct commands. This subsystem owns a distinct invariant and failure domain, so it needs one bounded whole-subsystem review that includes direct callers and consumers.

## Evidence

- `crates/eon/src/main.rs:141`: one dispatcher selects the public command flow
- `crates/eon/src/main.rs:415`: the foreground supervisor owns child observation and lifecycle
- `crates/eon/src/main.rs:580`: the private control listener owns stale-socket and cleanup policy
- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:84`: the runtime and lifecycle boundary is now explicit

## Prerequisites and reference gate

- Final convergence is deliberately blocked by `eon-5rp`, which transitively follows the accepted lifecycle corrections and changes an in-scope surface. Preserve pre-refactor evidence only as discovery; start the final pass after every blocker closes and one stable revision can be reread completely.
- Route each architecture, dependency, portability, or ownership question through `docs/REFERENCES.md`; read the relevant primary sources and at least one comparable implementation when one exists. Also read the applicable contract proofs and dependency or flake decisions. Record the question, exact source revisions, preserved constraints, rejected approaches, decision, and cheapest check in this Bead. Reuse prior evidence only when the question and exact revision still match.

## Scope

In scope:
- `crates/eon/src/main.rs` command, configuration/runtime directory, process, socket, timeout, and shutdown paths.
- `crates/eon/tests/workspace_control.rs` and unit tests that exercise those paths.
- README commands and EON-C1, EON-C3, EON-C4, EON-C8, EON-C9, and EON-C10 claims consumed by the runtime.
- Direct calls into workspace, manifest, EONW, Orbit, and Venus boundaries without auditing child internals.

Out of scope:
- Implementing, fixing, refactoring, or editing repository files.
- Adding or changing product contracts, dependencies, compatibility promises, or deferred features.
- Auditing behavior owned by another repository beyond verifying the consumed boundary.
- Creating remediation Beads unless the user separately authorizes a planning-only batch.

## Audit method

1. Record governing instructions, tracker state, accepted contract proofs, and immutable subject identity: clean HEAD, or HEAD plus a SHA-256 of the tracked binary diff and hashes of every in-scope untracked file. Preserve the exact dirty paths.
2. Read every in-scope owner, its direct callers and consumers, meaningful tests, contract rows, reference decisions, and dependency decisions.
3. Trace the observable flow end to end and audit correctness, failures, bounds, security boundaries, performance, tests, ownership, dependencies, portability, DX, and documentation.
4. Run a fresh-eyes correctness pass, then a separate simplification and ownership pass. Reject style preferences, speculative features, accepted tradeoffs, and duplicates of existing Beads.
5. Vet each remaining finding against exact file:line evidence and record impact, effort (S/M/L), implementation risk, confidence, the cheapest falsifying check, and why it merits action.
6. Repeat the complete review after any material planning correction or subject-snapshot change. Converge only when a final full pass over one unchanged recorded snapshot finds no additional actionable finding beyond the recorded set.
7. Record either the vetted findings or an explicit no-finding result in this Bead with the audited revision, commands, failures, and remaining proof limits.

## Acceptance

- The audit covers the complete stated subsystem and adjacent boundaries, not only recent diffs.
- Every finding is concrete, reproducible or directly evidenced, ownership-routed, and checked against existing Beads.
- No tracked project file or preserved untracked user artifact changes during the audit; generated build outputs do not alter the recorded subject snapshot.
- The final record identifies the exact subject snapshot; any in-scope subject change invalidates prior completion and requires a complete new pass.
- The final pass reports convergence under the declared lenses without widening that claim to runtime or platform behavior not exercised.
- Findings remain recommendations until the user chooses separate remediation work.

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --all --check` should exit 0 on the audited revision.
- `cargo check --locked --workspace` should exit 0 on the audited revision.
- `cargo test --locked --workspace` should exit 0 on the audited revision.
- `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` should exit 0 on the audited revision.
- `git diff --check` should exit 0 on the audited revision.
- A prior verification result may be cited instead of rerun only when its recorded subject snapshot, environment, command, and exercised surface match exactly; otherwise rerun it.
- `br sync --flush-only` should persist the audit record without changing implementation.
- Final status and diff inspection should show only the pre-existing worktree plus authorized Beads mutations.

## Stop conditions

- Stop if an active implementation owns or materially changes an in-scope surface.
- Stop if evidence requires a new contract, dependency decision, cross-repository owner change, or scope expansion.
- Stop and report rather than compensating for an upstream or downstream contract gap.

Reference gate
- Question: do EON-C10/EON-C11 lifecycle actions bind observation, presentation, destructive confirmation, concurrent launch, and cleanup to the same fresh supervisor owner without inferring Orbit or Venus state?
- Exact Eon evidence: complete runtime owner, focused tests, README, architecture, EON-C1/C3/C4/C8/C9/C10/C11/C12, component manifest, and related Beads at 1b8836e.
- Exact child boundaries: Orbit source 64db581445bafca1a08a6530f8e44f9c1edbc169 with ORB-C1 through ORB-C9 / ORBS v2 proof 9d6d2bb37f20ab4ad9e186c7bc715eabef43e757 and ORB-C10 proof 292b2451c9a1d99390334771a681c7f481c996f2; Venus runtime source 90988f6ebcde68338e202a9c637c59398aafe93d with VEN-C3/VEN-C4 proof 6ef19afddaedcbe2b9ed0996e31bc02df5d854ac, VEN-C8 proof 33a3d9af9f4c6015301ad6829fe733413c5b683d, and VEN-C9 proof 90988f6ebcde68338e202a9c637c59398aafe93d.
- Comparable primary source: Ghosthub 0.7.0 at 072cc83559bd590ed5d759af05ec0a1868dbf359, docs/architecture.md, docs/terminal-sessions.md, and docs/threat-model.md. Preserve backend authority, detach-only presentation, fresh attach, exact destructive-target revalidation, and process-owned socket namespaces. Reject tmux/Herdr/kwt adoption, remote scope, restored inventories, process-name/PID inference, and copied AGPL source.
- Decision: Eon already has the sufficient local SocketIdentity mechanism for presentation. Destructive stop and listener acquisition must preserve that same owner invariant. No EONW field, persisted marker, daemon, compatibility window, new dependency, or child change is justified.

Vetted finding 1 — human stop confirmation can terminate a replacement supervisor
- Evidence: crates/eon/src/main.rs:840-879 inspects and displays one GenerationRecord, then waits without retaining a socket identity. Lines 881-898 open a fresh connection and accept any Stopped response whose generation string matches. Session identities restart at session-1, so generation plus session labels do not identify the observed supervisor instance.
- Reproduction on exact HEAD with real target/debug/eon and Orbit 64db581: in an isolated private runtime, start supervisor A with terminal child /bin/sleep 300; start human eon stop and leave its one-Session prompt waiting; stop A through the JSON owner action; start supervisor B in the same generation with /bin/sleep 301; answer y at the old prompt. The waiting command exited 0, reported session-1, and supervisor B exited. All isolated processes and paths were then cleaned.
- Contract and impact: EON-C11 says confirmation names affected live Sessions and failure preserves Sessions. The confirmed observation can instead stop newer unconfirmed work. Impact HIGH; effort S/M; implementation risk MEDIUM; confidence HIGH.
- Cheapest falsifying check: a real-process test pauses at the human prompt, replaces the exact supervisor socket with a new same-generation supervisor, answers y, and requires an explicit owner-changed refusal while the replacement and its Session remain live.
- Fix boundary: bind stop confirmation to the validated SocketIdentity and fail closed if it changes. Reuse the existing owner mechanism; do not add protocol state unless local identity proves insufficient.

Vetted finding 2 — concurrent launches do not reliably converge
- Evidence: crates/eon/src/main.rs:1830-1861 checks connectability, separately inspects/removes an owned socket path, then binds. The absence/refusal observation and removal/bind are not serialized or identity-bound, so two launchers can both enter stale cleanup and unlink a newly bound peer. The replacement-safe Drop guard at lines 1812-1827 does not protect acquisition.
- Reproduction: repeated the existing exact test with: for audit_run in $(seq 1 100); do cargo test --locked -p eon --test workspace_control concurrent_launches_converge_and_generation_stop_is_owner_routed --quiet || exit 1; done. Runs 1-7 passed; run 8 failed at crates/eon/tests/workspace_control.rs:615 because one concurrent Eon process exited unsuccessfully. The failed fixture recorded one Orbit launch and left one dead mode-0600 eon.sock after process cleanup; that isolated fixture was moved to trash.
- Contract and impact: EON-C11 requires a concurrent launch to produce a bounded result without a second Session; EON-C12 requires current-generation convergence. The observed launch fails instead of attaching, and the acquisition race can detach the pathname from the live listener. Impact MEDIUM; effort M; implementation risk MEDIUM; confidence HIGH.
- Cheapest falsifying check: make the existing concurrent-start check deterministic at the stale-observation/bind boundary, then require exactly one listener/Orbit owner, one successful attached launcher, a reachable unchanged control socket, and clean shutdown. A repeated stress check remains supplementary, not the sole proof.
- Fix boundary: serialize or identity-bind control-listener acquisition inside the existing runtime owner. No new crate is expected; reject a broad supervisor abstraction.

Existing routed finding
- eon-generated-runtime-identity-h4g already owns the managed-audit finding that Nix-generated runtime behavior is absent from current_generation(). Do not duplicate it here. It blocks the corrections that would otherwise retain an old supervisor environment.

Rejected observations and simplification pass
- File size alone is not a finding. eon-5rp already owns the one justified extraction of the distinct managed-environment owner. A further runtime module split would move lines without deleting policy or reducing owners.
- Unexpected std::process observation errors could drop live Child handles, but no ordinary supported trigger or reproducible contract failure was established; reject as speculative.
- Relative EON_RUNTIME_DIR behavior, immediate Venus detach after spawn, and a stale Orbit socket after failed startup did not clear the contract/payoff bar on this snapshot.
- No dependency, duplicate lifecycle owner, child-contract gap, unbounded protocol allocation, or additional actionable simplification was found in this pre-refactor pass.

Verification and proof limits
- Passed on exact HEAD: cargo fmt --all --check; cargo check --locked --workspace; cargo test --locked --workspace (30 tests); cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings; git diff --check.
- The ordinary suite passes once while the explicit stress repetition above exposes finding 2. No Nix build, native compositor, macOS, signal-injection, crash-recovery, or performance claim is made.
- Final completion remains blocked by eon-5rp. After that in-scope refactor, rebaseline hashes, recheck existing remediation Beads, rerun both reproductions and the complete correctness/simplification pass, and only then claim convergence or close this audit.

title: Audit Eon workspace state invariants
description:
## Contract routing

This is a read-only repository audit. It changes no EON product contract, implements no feature or fix, and authorizes no dependency, compatibility surface, or public behavior. Audit one exact accepted revision and preserve all pre-existing worktree state.

## Why

Feature-local fresh-eyes and simplification passes can converge while topology, liveness, identity, action, and failure invariants can disagree across state transitions. ## Evidence

- `crates/eon/src/workspace.rs:30`: Workspace is the live topology owner

## Prerequisites and reference gate

- Route each architecture, dependency, portability, or ownership question through `docs/REFERENCES.md`; read the relevant primary sources and at least one comparable implementation when one exists. Also read the applicable contract proofs and dependency or flake decisions. Record the question, exact source revisions, preserved constraints, rejected approaches, decision, and cheapest check in this Bead. Reuse prior evidence only when the question and exact revision still match.

## Scope

In scope:
- `crates/eon/src/workspace.rs` state, transitions, projections, request history, capacity, liveness, and failure atomicity.
- Supervisor call sites and the real workspace control integration test.
- EON-C8 and EON-C10 ownership and proof claims.
- EONW values as consumed types, while codec internals remain in their own audit.

Out of scope:
- Implementing, fixing, refactoring, or editing repository files.
- Adding or changing product contracts, dependencies, compatibility promises, or deferred features.
- Auditing behavior owned by another repository beyond verifying the consumed boundary.
- Creating remediation Beads unless the user separately authorizes a planning-only batch.

## Audit method

1. Record governing instructions, tracker state, accepted contract proofs, and immutable subject identity: clean HEAD, or HEAD plus a SHA-256 of the tracked binary diff and hashes of every in-scope untracked file. Preserve the exact dirty paths.
2. Read every in-scope owner, its direct callers and consumers, meaningful tests, contract rows, reference decisions, and dependency decisions.
3. Trace the observable flow end to end and audit correctness, failures, bounds, security boundaries, performance, tests, ownership, dependencies, portability, DX, and documentation.
4. Run a fresh-eyes correctness pass, then a separate simplification and ownership pass. Reject style preferences, speculative features, accepted tradeoffs, and duplicates of existing Beads.
5. Vet each remaining finding against exact file:line evidence and record impact, effort (S/M/L), implementation risk, confidence, the cheapest falsifying check, and why it merits action.
6. Repeat the complete review after any material planning correction or subject-snapshot change. Converge only when a final full pass over one unchanged recorded snapshot finds no additional actionable finding beyond the recorded set.
7. Record either the vetted findings or an explicit no-finding result in this Bead with the audited revision, commands, failures, and remaining proof limits.

## Acceptance

- The audit covers the complete stated subsystem and adjacent boundaries, not only recent diffs.
- Every finding is concrete, reproducible or directly evidenced, ownership-routed, and checked against existing Beads.
- No tracked project file or preserved untracked user artifact changes during the audit; generated build outputs do not alter the recorded subject snapshot.
- The final record identifies the exact subject snapshot; any in-scope subject change invalidates prior completion and requires a complete new pass.
- The final pass reports convergence under the declared lenses without widening that claim to runtime or platform behavior not exercised.
- Findings remain recommendations until the user chooses separate remediation work.

## Verification
