title: Let agents subscribe to Eon events and discover its API
description:
## Why
herdr has an event stream that tools subscribe to, Rex a self-describing JSON-Schema server API, T3
Code an MCP server so outside agents can drive workspaces. Eon's CLI lets agents act and read state,
but they must poll; there is no subscription, no machine-readable description of the API, and no MCP
entry point. Source: competitor audit eon-r6yt (2026-10-29), reports in
~/pjs/refs/competitor-audit-2026-10/ (herdr.md, rex.md, t3code.md). Lucca, 2026-10-29: "file the
beads". Filing only; no work is approved yet beyond planning.

## Contracts
- EON-C10 (Typed workspace control): today each EONW connection carries exactly one
  length-delimited request and response, so a subscription is a new connection shape, an EONW
  version bump and a new or amended EON-C. Consequential (wire, lifecycle).
- EON-C31 (Agent attention): attention changes are the first events agents want; its Q8 rule limits
  what the CLI may show (`title` and `msg` never appear through `eon workspace`).
- EON-C28 (1.x stability): CLI commands and JSON fields freeze at 1.0, so a schema and an event
  format are cheaper to settle before 1.0.
- No new contract text without Lucca's approval.

## Children (each self-contained)
1. eon-ciwn.1: research an event subscription and draft its contract (planning only). The event
   stream's implementation beads are filed after Lucca approves that draft.
2. eon-ciwn.2: publish a JSON Schema for every `eon` command and its `--json` reply. Builds on
   eon-cli-action-discovery-ogzi (blocked by it; one action registry, no second schema).
3. eon-ciwn.3: decide whether Eon ships an MCP server over the CLI, and draft it if yes (blocked by
   .2, since MCP tool definitions must come from the same schema).

## Relationship to existing beads (one owner each)
- eon-cli-action-discovery-ogzi owns action discovery and the bounded `wait` for one named outcome;
  its stop boundary excludes "a general event stream, MCP server". This epic owns those two. The
  Runtime event source must have one owner: whichever of ogzi's `wait` and ciwn.1's stream lands
  first defines it, and the other consumes it.
- eon-agent-terminal-control-n8ic (send input) excludes "remote or MCP exposure"; MCP exposure of any
  terminal input goes through eon-ciwn.3 and only after n8ic's authorization exists.
- eon-agent-parity-a9g0 owns the CLI parity gaps; eon-pxn.7 excludes an MCP server from its
  terminal-testing decision.
- eon-ix6 (extension system, deferred) prefers external programs over accepted actions to plugins;
  an event stream is that path.

## Acceptance (epic)
- All children closed or explicitly dropped by Lucca.
- Overall outcome: an agent can wait for "pane X needs attention" without polling, discover every
  command and reply shape from the schema, and (if ciwn.3 decides yes) drive Eon from an MCP client.

## Scope
Planning container. Reference gate on each consequential child (docs/REFERENCES.md "How should Eon
expose agent-readable actions and source-labeled attention without creating another terminal or
action owner?" (TUIOS), plus the comparables each child names).

title: Research an Eon event subscription and draft its contract
description:
## Why
Agents in Eon must poll `eon workspace --json` to notice changes (a pane needing attention, a tab
closing). herdr ships an event stream (`events` CLI and socket subscription); Rex ships `rex events`.
Parent: eon-ciwn (competitor audit eon-r6yt, 2026-10-29).

## Evidence (edge fb7fe98)
- docs/CONTRACTS.md EON-C10 (from :793): "Each connection carries one length-delimited request and
  response and does not use EOF as framing." No subscription exists.
- docs/CONTRACTS.md EON-C31 (from :2400): the Runtime poller owns attention state at up to 2 Hz; the
  CLI JSON (Q8) carries only `attention{state, app, name}`, `attention_rollup` and `sidebar`.
- eon-cli-action-discovery-ogzi plans a bounded `wait` for one named outcome; ogzi excludes a
  general event stream.

## Deliverable (research and contract draft only; no product code)
Recorded on this bead:
1. References at recorded revisions: herdr's event stream and socket subscription, Rex `events`,
   tmux control mode (`-C`), Zellij `subscribe`, kitty/WezTerm if they have one, and the TUIOS
   route in docs/REFERENCES.md. What to take and reject (delivery guarantees, backpressure,
   reconnect, filtering, snapshot-then-deltas).
2. Owner and path: Runtime as the one event source; how a long-lived subscription fits EONW (new
   connection mode, version bump) and how ogzi's `wait` consumes the same source.
3. Event set for v1: workspace, tab, pane and popup lifecycle, attention changes (within EON-C31
   Q8's visibility rule), focus/selection changes if any. Bounds: queue size, slow-consumer policy
   (drop with a gap marker vs disconnect), multi-workspace (EON-C33) and generation (EON-C11)
   targeting, `EON_TERMINAL` selection.
4. Trust: same-UID socket permissions as today; anything more needs a reason.
5. Contract draft (new or amended EON-C, EONW version, CLI shape such as `eon events --json`, exit
   codes), plus a proposed implementation split into fresh-session beads. Bring both to Lucca.

## Acceptance
- The bead records the reference findings with sources and revisions, the owner and path trace,
  and the event set, bounds and trust decisions with reasons.
- Lucca approves or revises the contract draft and the implementation split; implementation beads
  are filed only after that.

## Verification
Planning route (AGENTS.md Verification table): bead state and the recorded research; no runtime
profile refresh.

## Stop conditions
- Stop for Lucca before any contract, EONW or code change.

title: Publish a JSON Schema for every eon command and its --json reply
description:
## Why
Rex exposes a self-describing API with JSON Schema, so an agent learns every command and reply shape
without reading docs. Eon's `--json` replies are documented in docs/USAGE.md and EON-C10 prose only.
Parent: eon-ciwn (competitor audit eon-r6yt, 2026-10-29).

## Contracts
EON-C10 (Typed workspace control) amendment; EON-C28 (1.x stability) freezes CLI JSON at 1.0, so
the schema should exist before 1.0 or be generated from the same source as the EON-C28 fixtures
(eon-igae.11.2, related).

## Scope
In scope: one machine-readable description (JSON Schema) of every `eon` command's arguments and
its `--json` reply and error result, emitted by the CLI (for example `eon schema --json`) and
generated from the same Runtime action registry that eon-cli-action-discovery-ogzi introduces, so
there is one schema owner.
Out of scope: a second action registry or hand-written schema; event formats (eon-ciwn.1); MCP
(eon-ciwn.3).

## Prerequisites
Blocked by eon-cli-action-discovery-ogzi (the action registry). Reference gate (contract change):
Rex's `api` schema output, kitty `@` / WezTerm `cli` JSON shapes, and the docs/REFERENCES.md TUIOS
route; record kept and rejected choices.

## Acceptance
- `eon schema --json` (name settled at the contract step) emits a JSON Schema document that
  validates the real `--json` output of every command, checked by a focused test that runs each
  command's projection through the schema.
- Contract text approved by Lucca before code.

## Verification
- `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime` (and the CLI crate if separate) exits 0 with the schema
  validation test; one-owned-logic route plus affected build.

title: Decide whether Eon ships an MCP server over the eon CLI
description:
## Why
T3 Code exposes an MCP server so outside agents can drive its workspaces. Agents inside Eon can
already run the `eon` CLI from a shell, so an MCP server adds value only for MCP-only clients or if
typed tools prove more reliable than CLI calls. Parent: eon-ciwn (competitor audit eon-r6yt,
2026-10-29).

## Decision question
Should Eon ship a local MCP server (stdio) that exposes `eon` actions as tools? Compare: no MCP
(CLI plus the Eon skill, eon-ed9d.1), a thin MCP adapter that projects the eon-ciwn.2 schema into
tools and calls the same action registry, or documenting a generic CLI-to-MCP bridge.

## Constraints
- One owner: tools derive from the eon-ciwn.2 schema; the adapter owns no behaviour.
- Trust boundary (consequential): local stdio only; no network listener. Terminal input tools only
  after eon-agent-terminal-control-n8ic's authorization exists (n8ic excludes MCP exposure).
- Dependency gate (AP-DEPENDENCY-001) if an MCP SDK crate is proposed; Rust only (AGENTS.md
  Implementation Languages).
- Contract: a new EON-C if yes. Reference gate: T3 Code's MCP server and one Rust MCP
  implementation at recorded revisions.

## Acceptance
- Decision recorded with reasons and rejected options. If yes: contract draft and a fresh-session
  implementation bead proposed to Lucca, not filed before approval.

## Verification
Planning route: bead state only.

title: Show the elapsed window position on the Claude quota chip
description:
## Decision
Lucca, 2026-10-16: keep one Claude chip (not one per window) and show progress like Codex, e.g. `3d2h/7d`.

## Contract (VEN-C26 wording change, approved by Lucca)
The Claude chip labels each window as `<elapsed>/<duration> <remaining>%` when Claude reports a reset, exactly as Codex does; a window without a reset keeps `<duration> <remaining>%` with no invented position. Wide shows both windows joined by ` · `; compact shows the window with the least remaining. Hover and the accessible label use Codex's wording: `observed <elapsed> into <duration>`, or `reset time unavailable`.

## Owner and scope
Venus scene text only (venus/src/scene.rs quota_window_text and quota_text). No EONW, Runtime, CodexBar or layout-policy change.

## Acceptance
Focused accessibility/scene test asserts the Claude label and description with and without a reset; Venus fmt, clippy and test suite; Nix build and profile refresh. Installed visual glance is Lucca's next fresh Eon launch, recorded as pending until observed.

title: Split the Claude quota chip into five-hour and seven-day chips
description:
## Decision
Lucca, 2026-10-17: split the Claude quota chip in two, one chip for the five-hour window and one for
the seven-day window, instead of one chip showing both (`[splat] 3h/5h 74% · 6d4h/7d 42%`).

## Contract (change needs Lucca's approval before code)
- Consumer: a full-Eon user with a Claude quota observation.
- Result: the Eon Bar shows up to two read-only Claude chips, five-hour then seven-day, each with
  the Claude splat, its elapsed position when a reset is known, and remaining percentage. Hover and
  each static accessible label name Claude, that window, freshness and reset availability.
- Failures: a window Claude does not report has no chip, gap or accessible node; stale text keeps
  `old` on every chip; transport loss removes both; quota-only changes keep attachments, scroll and
  navigation as today.
- Contract edits: VEN-C26 (one chip becomes one chip per window, compact/hide order) and EON-C27's
  "existing native chips" wording; changelogs. No EONW change: the observation already carries each
  window.

## Ownership
Venus Scene owns the per-window chips, geometry, hover and AccessKit through the existing quota chip
owner. Runtime facts, CodexBar collection and Codex's chip stay unchanged.

## Open decisions (recommendations)
1. Width pressure: today the single chip compacts to the lowest-remaining window. Recommend: both
   chips compact first, then the chip with more remaining disappears, keeping that rule; order stays
   five-hour then seven-day.
2. Mark: the splat on both chips (recommended; a bare `7d 42%` chip would not say whose quota it is).
3. Codex: stays one chip (Lucca asked for Claude only); split it too only by a separate decision.

## Prerequisites
None.

## Acceptance
Venus chip test covering two windows, one window, stale, compact and hiding order, and per-chip
accessible labels (update `two_provider_chips_share_layout_without_losing_identity_or_freshness`
rather than adding a mirror); `eon-test -p yazelix-venus`, fmt, clippy; nix build; isolated capture
with both chips, their hover and a narrow width; review loop; profile refresh.

## Scope boundary
Claude chip presentation only: no collection, cadence, EONW, Codex, color or icon change.

title: Deliver trustworthy Claude quota in the Eon Bar
description:
## Contract

A full-Eon user who uses authenticated Claude Code can see a compact Claude quota chip beside the existing Codex chip when the selected supported source supplies usable subscription facts. The chip identifies Claude and shows remaining percentages for the available five-hour and seven-day windows, with provider reset details on hover and in its accessible description. Missing or unsupported data remains absent or explicitly unavailable; failed or expired observations never look fresh or imply zero usage. Quota collection must not block startup, workspace actions, terminal attachment or shutdown.

## Ownership and prerequisites

Eon owns the product outcome and exact composition; Eon Runtime owns the provider adapter, observation lifecycle and normalization; the canonical EONW crate owns the typed boundary; Venus owns native layout, icon, tooltip and accessibility. Claude owns authentication and quota meaning. Orbit remains terminal authority.

The accepted Codex delivery and EON-C21/EON-C22 supply the bar and comparison baseline. EON-C22 is currently Codex-only and EONW v7 carries a Codex-specific optional field; neither is already a multi-provider contract. Before code, index the chosen Claude contract and select the smallest compatible canonical EONW change. Follow one active frontier, with accepted Runtime/EONW and Venus slices before downstream Eon delivery; establish owner-specific children only when this outcome is activated.

## Evidence and reference gate

Reviewed on 2026-10-11:
- Official Claude documentation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/statusline. Its status-line JSON documents rate_limits.five_hour and rate_limits.seven_day with used_percentage and resets_at. Fields are conditional on supported subscription/auth modes and appear only after a session response. Convert reported used percentage to remaining percentage explicitly; context usage and session cost are separate facts.
- PATH discovery found Claude Code 2.1.159. This is discovery, not proof that this installed executable emits those fields.
- Current local source owners: ../eon-runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/codex_quota.rs and supervisor.rs; canonical eon-workspace-protocol v6/v7; docs/CONTRACTS.md EON-C21/EON-C22; exact Codex source/delivery beads.
- Nova e7d8d6ffe9994413944bac388620b9f9f61669d7, docs/configuration.md and flake.nix, consumes Nova Bar 7295e9976803de8d912f766f1b00ad12652e3e9b and tokenusage. Preserve useful quota labels and width discipline; Nova's command-widget/cache composition is comparison evidence, not an Eon implementation.

Before choosing code, inspect the exact selected Claude release's status-line/auth/lifecycle behavior and license, one comparable quota implementation, and the current accepted Eon/Venus contracts. Compare the documented status-line adapter, any supported standalone query, and no integration. Resolve observation freshness, source binding/account changes, multiple sessions and missing fields. A status-line adapter does not imply always-on reads; never launch an inference turn merely to refresh quota. Any setup must be explicit and reversible and preserve an existing user status-line command.

## Scope and stop boundary

One read-only Claude quota outcome on the accepted Linux Wayland alpha. Match Codex's remaining-percentage convention and visual language; preserve provider-specific period labels and optional windows. Keep a single row, tab/control priority and a usable drag region. Optional chips yield space before required controls.

No generic provider/widget framework, arbitrary command widgets, charts, chat/activity UI, new bar row, provider bundling, login/account management, transcript/history parsing, token-to-quota estimates, quota mutation or platform/distribution expansion. Credentials and raw status-line payloads never enter EONW, Venus or logs. Any new dependency or auth access beyond the selected provider-owned route needs its normal explicit gate.

If the exact source cannot supply trustworthy quota, record the blocker and keep delivery incomplete. Unavailable data is an honest runtime fallback, not grounds to close the feature as delivered.

## Validation

Record exact provider, Eon Runtime/EONW, Venus, Orbit, manifest, package and environment identities. Use focused parser/source red-green checks for meaningful malformed/missing/stale cases, then the full affected Rust/Nix route for shared protocol or dependency changes. Refresh the installed eon profile and observe one isolated native x86_64 Linux Wayland workflow with real provider facts plus bounded failure substitutes, preserving live terminals and desktop focus. Inspect responsive width, hover and AccessKit labels together; do not treat accessibility structure alone as screen-reader qualification.
acceptance_criteria:
1. An exact supported authenticated Claude workflow supplies real five-hour and/or seven-day subscription quota; the source and auth scope are recorded, and remaining percentages/reset labels agree with the same observation. Conditional absence is handled without invented values.
2. The chosen source has bounded input, lifecycle and refresh work, explicit observation age/expiry and account/source invalidation, and graceful missing/incompatible/unauthenticated/malformed/failed behavior. Existing Claude configuration and status-line output are preserved; no paid turn is started to obtain quota.
3. Canonical EONW carries only bounded normalized presentation facts. Venus presents the Claude icon/name, available remaining percentages, reset details and honest stale/unavailable states; no credentials, account identity, transcript or raw payload crosses into the client or logs.
4. Codex and Claude coexist in the existing single-row bar. Wide, compact and hidden layouts retain active tabs, fixed controls, dragging, terminal focus and accessible provider/window/freshness labels.
5. Exact accepted child revisions are composed and the affected Rust/Nix, profile refresh and isolated installed observation pass at the changed boundaries. Current docs/changelog/LOC describe only proved behavior; live user terminals are preserved.
notes: Implementation activated by the user on 2026-10-13. Fresh review fixed the investigation: disableAllHooks had suppressed the tested statusline; a corrected isolated startup now receives Claude Code 2.1.159 JSON with rate_limits=null, without a submitted prompt. Earlier no-callback evidence is inconclusive and must not block the documented route. Existing authorization covers that integration; direct OAuth credential access remains unselected and requires its separate gate. Collector output is private per run, size/type/numeric bounded and whitelisted; raw-screen parsing/logging removed; early-exit/hang cleanup verified. Exact proof and review: /home/lucca/.local/state/eon/proofs/eon-claude-quota-2026-10-13-ioqmp2y4/fresh-review-2/report.txt. title: Let the eon CLI report available actions and wait on outcomes
description:
## Origin
Split from closed `eon-pxn` on 2026-10-16 (its CLI and action boundary and acceptance item 7).

## Contract (provisional)
An agent or script can ask the running supervisor which workspace actions are valid now, with
stable action IDs, typed arguments, current targets and owner-authored reasons an action is
unavailable, and can `wait` with a bound for one named outcome. Structured mode prints data on
stdout, diagnostics on stderr, stable symbolic error codes, and never prompts.

## Evidence (edge 798ab79)
`eon --help` already ships `workspace`, `tab create|close|directory|move`, `pane create|move` and
`focus` with `--json` through the supervisor's private EONW endpoint. Discovery, symbolic error
codes and `wait` are absent.

## Owners
Eon Runtime's action registry owns availability and results; the CLI is a projection. EONW changes,
if any, follow its versioning rules.

## Prerequisites and reference gate
Consequential if it changes EONW. Re-read EON-C8 and the TUIOS and Unpeel action evidence on
`eon-pxn`. Stop for Lucca's contract approval before code.

## Acceptance
Focused process tests on the real binary cover discovery, an unavailable action's reason, a symbolic
error and a bounded `wait` timeout.

## Stop boundary
No general event stream, MCP server, plugin API or second action schema.

title: Keep eon commands working inside a window after a profile upgrade
description:
## Report (overseer, 2026-10-23 ~02:45 -03)

After a profile refresh, `eon` commands run inside an existing window's terminals stop working. The overseer runs in a window on generation g1-8e4e55… (store b2n3yaksdnks…-eon-0.1.1). Once the `eon` profile was refreshed to g1-6c7787… (i0j3p4bd…), `eon pane create --no-focus --json -- true` from that window's Agent popup returned `{"error":{"code":"missing-supervisor","detail":"endpoint /run/user/1000/eon/generations/g1-6c778755…/eon.sock is missing; run \`eon\` first"}}` with exit 4. It worked with the window's own binary, `/nix/store/b2n3…-eon-0.1.1/bin/eon`.

Users and agents upgrade while windows run (the documented flow keeps running windows until restart). Every `eon` call in those windows, including `pane create`, `edit`, `pane close`, `tab move` and agent scripts, breaks with a misleading "run `eon` first" until the window restarts. Users are not happy with that.

## Expected

Inside an Eon terminal (`EON_TERMINAL` set), `eon` acts on that terminal's own window and generation, whatever profile is installed, or it tells the user exactly what to do. "run `eon` first" is wrong: that would start a new window.

## Candidate shapes (decide at the reference gate)

- The terminal environment puts the window's own `eon` first on PATH (`EON_SESSION_BIN` already holds the generation's tools, but not `eon`).
- Or the CLI resolves the target from `EON_TERMINAL` and, on a generation mismatch, re-execs the binary for that generation, which the supervisor would have to advertise without constructing store paths (AGENTS.md forbids constructing them).
- Or it fails with exit 3 and a message naming the cause and a fix.

## Contract

EON-C10 or EON-C11 (CLI and generation boundary) and the EON_TERMINAL rule in docs/CONTRACTS.md (calls that land in another generation exit 3). Today the missing-supervisor path wins first. Bring the exact wording under the overseer's 2026-10-23 approval, or to Lucca.

## Related

eon-reattach-after-upgrade-n5qv (windows and generations after an upgrade). Fold this in there if that bead's shape covers it.

## Acceptance

- After a profile refresh, a test (or an isolated installed check) shows `eon pane create` from an older window's terminal either working on that window or failing with exit 3 and a correct message.
- The installed check covers both the old and the new window.
close_reason: CLI inside an older window acts on its own window via its own eon on PATH; another build by path exits 3 with a correct message. Proven installed across two builds.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Evidence (eon-63, yx8.11, 2026-10-23): runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/control.rs:270 (probe_generation_runtime) accepts any supervisor that reports the same EONW version, then decodes its Snapshot. Live terminals run the profile's `eon`, not their generation's own binary. So after a refresh with an unchanged EONW version, a new CLI talks to an older running supervisor. A snapshot change that keeps the version number would then misdecode instead of failing. yx8.11 bumps to EONW 19 to avoid that. When fixing this bead, make the CLI inside an Eon terminal use its own generation's binary or codec, so that same-version drift cannot misdecode either.

The new window w/b640477a (05:01) runs supervisor g1-8e4e… with the same Venus (gsxywm9j…), so it has the old code: no sidebar rows. Its generations/g1-00d891… dir is empty. Lucca believed he was 'in the new runtime'. Users expect 'new window' after an upgrade to open the installed version, or at least to be told it didn't. Decide in this bead whether Alt+Shift+N and the launcher's New Eon Window open the installed generation or say which version opened.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Lucca, 2026-10-23 ~05:10, on the Alt+Shift+N evidence above: "have it consider if this behavior is not actually a good call. a window splitting up with the same runtime". So the new-window part is an open question, not a bug yet. Weigh both before choosing:
- Same-generation new window (today): every window a supervisor opens shares one known-good build. There's no mixed-version session, and the window's Agent popup, pane create and CLI keep working, because they match. Upgrades take effect only when the user starts Eon fresh, which is predictable.
- Installed-generation new window: users get the upgrade without restarting. But the opener and the new window then run different builds, which can't talk to each other over the window boundary, and the user may not know which window runs which version.
- A middle path: keep the same generation, but say so when a newer build is installed, e.g. a one-line notice or a version marker on the bar, with the way to get it (launcher or `eon window new` from a shell).
Record the reference gate (how Zellij, WezTerm and kitty behave after an upgrade) and the decision with its reason. The CLI-inside-an-old-window failure (exit 4 'run eon first') stays a bug either way: at minimum its message must be right.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Reference gate (2026-10-23, edge ad64d81). Consequential: changes the terminal launch environment and a CLI failure path (lifecycle boundary).

Cause (E): control() (runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/cli.rs:743) always addresses the CLI binary's own current_generation inside runtime_directory() (the window dir when EON_WINDOW_RUNTIME_DIR is set). A newer profile `eon` in an older window finds no socket, and unreachable_supervisor (cli.rs:813) reports missing-supervisor "run `eon` first", exit 4. EON-C10 already says a caller from another generation exits 3, so the code breaks the contract. A side effect: prepare_generation_runtime (supervisor.rs:671) creates an empty generations/<new> dir in the old window. That is the empty-dir evidence in comment 2 and feeds eon-reattach-after-upgrade-n5qv's listing.

Owners: Nix composition supplies the terminal's session bin dir (flake.nix:643,701-716, EON_SESSION_BIN), which sessions.rs:1204 prepends to every Orbit terminal's PATH. Runtime owns CLI failures. libexec/eon/bin already holds the generation's own eon under other names (eon-commands, eon-files, eon-directory-picker), and Files gets EON_FILES_CLI = current_exe, "this same Eon build" (managed_environment.rs:748).

References (subagent, from source): zellij v0.45.1 efd8fd5a, wezterm e2a98e1b, kitty b2cb8712 (0.49.2), tmux 3.8 7f2a35ad.
- All four find the instance through an inherited env var that names a per-instance socket (ZELLIJ_SESSION_NAME, WEZTERM_UNIX_SOCKET/WEZTERM_PANE, KITTY_LISTEN_ON, TMUX). Only Zellij scopes the socket dir, and by contract version (contract_version_1), not by release.
- On a mismatch, tmux prints "protocol version mismatch (client N, server M)" (client.c:659-667). WezTerm's GUI handoff prints "Please install the same version…", but `wezterm cli` skips that check and fails with generic per-command errors. kitty rejects only a newer client, and its frozen protocol version means that never fires. Zellij keeps one protobuf contract across releases.
- Own binary on PATH: kitty prepends its bundle and kitten dirs when the `kitty`/`kitten` on PATH is not its own file (main.py:478-500). WezTerm exports WEZTERM_EXECUTABLE(_DIR) and prepends to PATH only for AppImage. tmux and Zellij add nothing.
- New windows after an upgrade: tmux, kitty and Zellij run the old, running build. Only WezTerm starts a new GUI when the executable path or codec differs (main.rs:556-570). None tells the user that a newer build is installed.

Decision (proposed, pending contract approval):
- Adopt: the generation's session bin dir also holds `eon` → ../../../bin/eon, so a terminal's PATH resolves `eon` to its own build (kitty's pattern). Commands run by name inside a window then act on that window's generation, and same-EONW-version codec drift between builds cannot misdecode for them.
- Adopt: when an `eon` from another build runs inside an Eon terminal and finds no supervisor of its own generation, caller commands exit 3 (unknown-caller), as EON-C10 already says. The detail names this build's generation and points to the terminal's own `eon`, with no "run `eon` first".
- Rejected: re-exec into the window's binary. The supervisor would have to advertise or persist an executable path, the probe needs the old codec, and AGENTS.md forbids treating store paths as identity. PATH gives the same result with no code.
- Rejected: failing alone with exit 3, which leaves agents and scripts broken until the window restarts.
- Unresolved (Lucca): which build a new window opens (Alt+Shift+N, launcher), and any notice that a newer build is installed.
Checks: a runtime test (no supervisor needed) for exit 3 and the detail; managed-command-path asserts that `eon` on the session PATH is the package's bin/eon; an installed check across one profile refresh covering an old and a new window.

Approved: (1) EON-C10 wording: the Result bullet 'Every Eon terminal's PATH names that terminal's own Eon build as `eon`, ahead of any installed one, so `eon` run by name there acts on that terminal's own window and generation after the installed profile changes. title: Close the selected pane with Alt+W
description:
## Decision
Lucca, 2026-10-18: Eon needs a keyboard command that closes a pane. A direct key, not a pane
mode. Lucca accepted these defaults: Alt+W closes the selected pane with no confirmation, the
same as Alt+Shift+W for tabs; a column whose last pane closes disappears; a tab whose last pane
closes goes with it; the final tab's last pane cannot be closed; `eon pane close PANE` projects
the same action. This lifts EON-C8's boundary "no user-facing per-pane terminal stop/restart
action" for stop only (no restart) and supersedes `eon-pxn.8`'s "no pane-close action" exclusion.

## Contract (EON-C8 change)
- Consumer: one local full-Eon workspace user, or a CLI caller.
- Trigger: Alt+W on a focused pane, or `eon pane close PANE [--json]`.
- Result: the request names a stable `pN` in the active tab. Eon stops that pane's Orbit terminal
  and prunes it through the normal terminal-exit owner, so focus, column and tab removal follow the
  existing natural-exit rules exactly (a column whose last pane ends disappears; a tab left with no
  panes and no popups disappears).
- Failures, each leaving topology unchanged: unknown or stale pane, a pane outside the active tab,
  the last pane of the final tab, a pending tab, a tab with a selected popup or picker, a repeated
  request ID (never repeats a stop). A terminal that ended naturally during the request is
  reconciled as an exit. A failed stop reports failure and keeps the pane represented.
- Venus maps Alt+W directly to the selected pane's identity; plain Ctrl+W stays terminal input.
  Shortcut help and the bottom hints list it.

## Ownership
Eon Runtime workspace owns validation and pruning; the supervisor owns the stop, reusing the tab
close path (`close_workspace_tab`, `stop_owned_session`). EONW owns the wire action. Venus owns the
key and sends only the stable target. Orbit owns terminal shutdown. Eon owns no new default.

## Reference gate (consequential: new EONW action, lifecycle)
- Primary owner evidence: EON-C8 and edge `4910b81` workspace dispatch/pruning, `prepare_close_tab`,
  `close_workspace_tab`, EONW v10 additive `CreateColumn` request (tag 22) as the version pattern.
- Comparable: `eon-pxn.8` tab close (stable target, request dedup, sequential Stop then exit-owner
  pruning). Adopt the same shape for one terminal.
- Key evidence: Alt+W is unbound in pinned Helix `nova-helix` 817dcbc (narHash matches flake.lock;
  `helix-term/src/keymap/default.rs` has 34 Alt chords, no `A-w`), Yazi 26.5.6 preset keymap, and
  Nushell 0.113.1 default files with reedline 0.48.0 (binds Ctrl+W only).
- Decision: EONW v11 adds one `ClosePane { pane }` request encoded as v10 added `CreateColumn`;
  snapshots and every older action stay v10 bytes reframed. v10 joins the historical codecs.
- Rejected: a pane mode (a new input model for one action, and `eon-pxn.8` rejected modes); a
  no-target "close selected" wire action (replay could close a successor); confirmation prompts
  (new UI surface; tab close has none); implicit generation stop on the last pane.

## Scope boundary
In: EONW v11 codec, runtime validation, supervisor stop, CLI `eon pane close`, Venus Alt+W,
shortcut help and hints, EON-C8 text, docs (USAGE, CHANGELOG, venus/CHANGELOG), profile refresh,
isolated installed dogfood.
Out: restart, closing popups, closing panes in other tabs, a pane mode, keybinding configuration,
confirmation, closing the final pane (Eon exit), mouse close buttons on pane headers.

## Acceptance
1. Alt+W in a multi-pane column closes the selected pane's terminal and selects per the exit rule;
   closing a column's last pane removes the column; a non-final tab's last pane removes the tab.
2. Each refusal above leaves topology unchanged and shows the rejected-action notice.
3. EONW v11 round-trips `ClosePane`; v10 decoders reject it; older actions still round-trip.
4. `eon pane close PANE` matches the shortcut; `--json` reports the snapshot.
5. Alt+W reaches no terminal application; Ctrl+W still does.
6. Full Rust (`nix develop -c eon-test`) and Nix builds green; Venus/Orbit fmt and clippy green;
   profile refreshed; one isolated installed dogfood observation of the shortcut and a refusal.

Prerequisites: none.
close_reason: Alt+W and eon pane close stop one pane's terminal over EONW v11 and prune it like a natural exit; refusals for the final pane, other tabs and covered tabs. Full suite on the exact tree, isolated dogfood of the profile's store path, graph at EONW 11. Proof and ledgers in comments.

title: Use the OpenAI Blossom in the Codex quota chip
description:
## Observable contract
Consumer: one full-Eon user with a visible Codex quota observation.

Trigger: Venus projects a fresh, stale, blocked, or unknown EONW v6 Codex quota fact into the Eon Bar.

Result: the chip uses the exact official monochrome OpenAI Blossom instead of the visible Codex word. Fresh and stale facts keep all accepted elapsed/total and remaining labels; blocked, unknown, and old remain explicit. The logo and label form one noninteractive chip and save width before the chip yields under pressure. Hover and AccessKit continue to name Codex and expose the complete human-readable state.

Important failures: absence creates no chip; asset or rasterization failure cannot create guessed branding, block Eon startup, change provider semantics, steal focus, add an action, or disturb tab/control priority.

## Ownership and prerequisites
VEN-C22 Scene owns visible quota content and responsive geometry; the existing Venus renderer owns the exact mark; AccessKit owns the explicit accessible value. EON-C22 and EONW v6 provider facts remain unchanged. Use exact accepted Orbit ea9fd28ce0908f218cf65d4e6df368f0a4e565f5 and Eon workspace protocol 3103a00a904c347472899549ce611da765a71650. After accepted Venus proof, Eon updates only the canonical Venus pin and proof metadata, rebuilds, refreshes the named eon profile, and preserves live Sessions.

Reference gate: inspect the current official OpenAI brand guidance and the exact official OpenAI Blossom asset, record version/hash/provenance and permitted direct-service use, and reread VEN-C22 plus its existing scene/render/accessibility checks before code.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Ordinary and compact chips render the exact monochrome OpenAI Blossom plus the previously accepted quota text without a visible Codex word.
- Blocked, unknown, stale, absent, narrow, hover, hit testing, tab/control priority, and quota-only refresh semantics remain accepted.
- The AccessKit value and hover description still explicitly name Codex, contain human elapsed/total information where applicable, expose no epoch timestamp, and remain non-actionable and unfocusable.
- The asset preserves its official proportions and monochrome color; no altered logo, added color, provider framework, icon system, image dependency, provider change, protocol change, configuration, or other platform claim is added.
- Focused scene/render/accessibility checks go red then green; complete locked Venus checks and one isolated native x86_64 Linux Wayland observation pass on the immutable child source.
- Eon selects that exact child revision through manifest, flake input, and lock; affected Nix checks/build pass; the named eon profile resolves the built artifact without restarting existing supervisors or Sessions.

## Scope boundary
One built-in monochrome OpenAI Blossom only. No generic provider/icon registry, clickable chip, configuration, threshold color, animations, second row, other provider, Orbit work, macOS proof, X11/Xwayland support, or distribution expansion.

title: Keep last Codex quota visible during authenticated refreshes
description:
## Contract and observed defect
The user reports recurring Codex quota-chip disappearance for seconds or minutes at fixed tiling geometry, with no account switching. A deterministic installed full-Eon substitute reproduced a 52-second gap after an authenticated account/updated notification at constant 960px. The original recurring episode remains uncorrelated; a bounded read-only live capture is retained separately.

Consumer: a full-Eon user with an authenticated compatible Codex CLI. Trigger: an authenticated refresh notification or a failed quota refresh. Result: retain the recorded values without an old label through authenticated notifications and failures while the last successful observation is at most one hour old. Publish Stale (old) only after a failure and a strictly greater than 3600-second observation age. Age is measured since the last successful quota read, not window elapsed time. The age transition must occur during ongoing failed retries without requiring a new failure exactly at the threshold. Healthy observations do not become old solely due to age. The user explicitly selected last values and rejected an Unknown placeholder. A response already in flight at any account update is discarded. Each verified read replaces the complete observation atomically. Sign-out, unsupported/malformed authentication, expired stale windows, missing provider and transport/width failures retain their existing behavior. Quota reads remain at least 60s apart.

## Ownership, prerequisites and reference gate
Eon Runtime owns the provider worker, invalidation, normalization, retry and stale expiry; Venus owns existing stale presentation, workspace availability and width rules. Eon owns the exact composition pin and EON-C22; Codex owns auth and quota semantics. Read EON-C22/VEN-C22, worker/supervisor publication and client model/scene/transport before shaping code. Official schema generated by installed Codex 0.160.1 confirms account/updated carries authMode/planType rather than account identity, and ordinaryUsageAllowed is validated by the provider. Original 0.154 source URLs were unavailable and are not claimed inspected. Baseline Eon a4e3d598fe6051a2cc95c4f17b017093e16d7f1b; Runtime/codec b8f18b4374ca0818a64d9cac6a3fcd02d9f2f2aa; accepted Venus bbf4cf41b289f441683eb7a3f225a26a4d3edacc and Orbit b6cecf8f2ee35570b41cfdc578b095889d917fe2. Later child commits are metadata/docs only. Preserve live Sessions and desktop focus.

## Reproduction and acceptance
Focused worker red/green protects authenticated value retention without old, obsolete in-flight rejection, complete replacement and sign-out clearing, alongside failure/retry/reset-expiry cleanup. Deterministic snapshots protect strict 3600/3601-second failure-age boundaries, healthy aged data and failure evidence retained between snapshots.

An installed production-cadence substitute returns 75%, emits authenticated account/updated after 8s and fails the second read. At fitting fixed width, quota remains 75% without old throughout these young-data transitions. Client and generation remain unchanged; provider identity remains unchanged through the notification, with bounded provider cleanup expected after failure. Prove >=60s read spacing, retained tabs/fixed controls and narrow hide/return. Exact affected Rust/Nix packages and checked single-codec preparation pass; profile elements resolve to the built artifacts. Record exact revisions, artifacts and privacy-safe observations; do not restart live user Sessions. The one-hour boundary uses deterministic owner proof rather than a native hour-long wait or host-clock change.

## Scope boundary
Only the confirmed authenticated-refresh gap, user-selected one-hour failed-refresh labeling and their composition/documentation are selected. No Unknown placeholder, extra polling, authentication reader, experimental API, persistent cache, raw telemetry, generic widget/provider framework, dependency, Orbit change or Venus mechanism change. Removing redundant private account identity state does not permit merging windows or republishing invalidated in-flight responses. The original report is not attributed to this mechanism without a correlated recurrence.
close_reason: Refined old label requires a failed refresh and last successful observation age strictly greater than one hour. Boundary red/green, full Rust/Nix, exact profile refresh and installed young-failure/notification proof pass; live user Sessions preserved.

title: Adopt CodexBar for Codex and Claude quota
description:

title: Add an Eon command runner on Alt+Shift+M
description:
## Contract
Alt+Shift+M opens a native, searchable Eon command runner in the current workspace. The user can select and execute an available Eon command with the keyboard, or dismiss it with Escape and return to the previous focus without leaking runner keystrokes into a terminal. Commands act on the intended workspace/tab/pane and retain their existing validation and safety behavior.

## Scope and decision
The shortcut and command runner are chosen by the user. "Maybe all Eon commands" is an open coverage decision: inventory existing user-facing actions and CLI commands, then agree the first useful set before implementation. Record included commands, commands requiring arguments or targets, and exclusions. Do not assume every CLI subcommand belongs in a graphical runner.

Reuse existing command owners and dispatch. This is not an arbitrary shell runner, plugin system, configurable shortcut framework, or a replacement for the read-only Shortcuts viewer. Preserve Alt+M (create pane), existing terminals, and stop confirmations.

## Evidence and ownership
- Eon Desktop `src/application.rs`: `FIXED_SHORTCUTS`, `NativeShortcutAction`, and `shortcut_groups_for` already own native action routing and shortcut presentation; Alt+M creates a pane. Alt+Shift+M creates a column until eon-0ka6 moves that to Ctrl+Alt+M.
- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/managed_environment.rs:583`: `reserved_shortcut` reserves only Alt+/ and Alt+0-9. A configured popup takes any other fixed Venus key (eon-igae.10), so a popup set to Alt+Shift+M would take precedence over the runner. Keep that rule unless Lucca decides otherwise.
- Eon Runtime `crates/eon-runtime/src/cli.rs`: the command surface includes workspace actions, argument-taking commands, inspection commands, and lifecycle commands. Do not derive execution behavior by parsing help text or use machine-output flags to bypass confirmation.
- Eon `docs/CONTRACTS.md`, EON-C20: the existing native Shortcuts viewer is read-only; command execution was outside that earlier slice.

Eon owns product coverage/defaults; Venus owns runner presentation, search, keyboard/focus and accessibility; Runtime retains action validation, workspace state and lifecycle; Orbit retains terminals. Avoid a second command-semantics owner or speculative child APIs.

## Prerequisites and reference gate
No unmet dependency identified. Before implementation, read each affected repository's instructions, current contracts and `docs/REFERENCES.md`; inspect current shortcut/action/CLI owners and one comparable command-palette implementation. Record exact inspected revisions, the coverage decision, reuse choice, and cheapest falsifying check. Implement child behavior first and compose accepted exact revisions through Eon.

## Acceptance
- Installed Eon opens the runner with Alt+Shift+M; search, keyboard selection and execution work for the agreed command set in the correct context.
- Escape restores focus; opening, typing and dismissing do not send input to the terminal. Alt+M and existing shortcuts still work.
- Missing targets, unavailable commands and execution failures are communicated honestly. Included argument-taking/destructive actions preserve validation and explicit safeguards.
- The new chord has one owner and consistent popup-collision handling, shortcut help and accessibility.
- Prove representative execution and cancellation in an isolated installed workspace, including a failure and collision check; use the affected owners' existing harnesses. Refresh the active Nix profile after composition without interrupting live workspaces.

## Stop boundary
If coverage needs new commands, a new protocol/framework, or another platform promise, obtain that scope decision first. Keep the first slice to running existing Eon commands.
notes: 2026-10-15 (prime-beads): paths in Evidence predate consolidation. `Eon Desktop src/application.rs` is now `venus/src/application.rs` (its shortcut policy is slice 1 of `eon-venus-modules-oagt`; coordinate edits). Eon Runtime `crates/eon-runtime/src/*` is now `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/*`.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Design and reference gate (eon-c1, 2026-10-22; awaiting Lucca's approval of the contract text and command list before commit).

User-visible behavior: Alt+Shift+M opens a built-in transient popup, Commands. It shows an fzf list of curated existing eon commands, each line naming the command it runs. Enter runs the command in the popup's terminal, which is the command's caller. Esc, Ctrl+C or no match runs nothing. A successful action ends the popup; a listing or a failure waits for Enter.

Owners: the CLI (runtime cli.rs execute) stays the one owner of command semantics, validation, targets and Stop confirmations. The runner calls execute() in-process, with EON_TERMINAL and EON_TAB from the popup's environment. The popup catalog owns the key, label, enabled state and collisions through the existing [popups.<id>] rules: user popups can rebind, disable or take keys as for any built-in. Eon (product.rs) owns the default entry. Venus needs no change: catalog popups already reach the shortcut viewer and hints. There is no EONW change and no new dependency (fzf is already pinned and on the popup PATH).

References read: Nova yzx menu, /home/lucca/pjs/nova/nova-upstream-theme at 5deea385f8b26b8310aa3749af8d451d641ff146 (runtime/yzx-menu.rs last changed in 72e37087). Kept: a curated allowlist of zero-argument commands, fzf in a popup on Alt Shift M, running the chosen command as a child and waiting for Enter so output stays readable. Eon's own pattern is the Project picker (cli.rs directory_picker: private mode, packaged fzf, exits 130 on cancel). Changed: Eon runs the command in-process rather than spawning the CLI, and keeps the popup only for listings and failures.

Rejected:
(a) A native Venus palette widget. It needs a new search input, IME, rendering and an AccessKit dialog, which is a new Venus module (product scope per venus/AGENTS.md). Its execution would need Venus-side command semantics or a new EONW action, which would make a second owner. The terminal popup gets accessibility from terminal text, as the Project picker does.
(b) Showing each entry's keyboard shortcut. Venus FIXED_SHORTCUTS owns those, and copying them into the runtime would make a second owner. Lines show the eon command instead, which teaches the CLI.

Proposed first command list (Lucca to confirm): new tab, new pane, new window, close this tab (tab close $EON_TAB), move pane left/right/up/down, move tab left/right, show workspace, list windows, list generations, stop older generations (stop previous, with the CLI's y/N), show versions, show config path, show command help.
Excluded: stop all and window stop (they can stop the popup's own terminal mid-command); attach and run (presentation); edit, tab directory and pane close (they need arguments or a pane ID); focus (navigation already has keys); popups and create column (no CLI form; adding one is new scope per this bead's stop boundary).

Contract: EON-C10's popup clause gains a Commands sentence. EON-C20 (read-only shortcut viewer) is unchanged, because the runner is a popup, not part of the viewer.
Check: a cli.rs unit test that every workspace-control entry still parses as an eon command, plus isolated installed dogfood: open, search, run an action, run a listing, Esc, and Stop's confirmation.

title: Add Quit this window to the Commands popup
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-10-22 (eon-pg67): users need one in-window way to end every terminal in this window at once, not only by closing the last tab. He chose a Commands popup entry over a key (an Alt+Shift+Q next to Alt+Shift+W would kill every tab on a slip). Approved on eon-pg67.

## Contract (approved; apply this text in this bead's commit)

- EON-C8 Commands popup text (docs/CONTRACTS.md around :807-820): Commands gains "Quit this window", which runs `eon stop <this window's generation>` and keeps Stop's confirmation listing of live terminals. It adds no EONW action. Runtime writes the exact generation into the line, so the entry works in an independent window (EON-C23) and stops only that window.
- docs/USAGE.md "Stop terminals" (:62-93) mentions Commands > Quit this window.

## Evidence

Commands runs existing `eon` CLI lines in the popup terminal with that terminal's EON_TERMINAL and EON_TAB and keeps the CLI's own validation and Stop confirmation (EON-C8 :807-820). Check how an independent window's namespace reaches `eon stop` from a popup terminal before choosing the exact line.

## Scope

In scope: the Commands list entry in Runtime, its contract and USAGE text, CHANGELOG.
Out of scope: new EONW actions, any key binding, `eon stop` semantics.

## Acceptance

From Commands in a window, "Quit this window" asks with the live-terminal list and, on yes, ends only that window's generation; declining changes nothing. In an independent window it stops only that window.

## Verification

Owned-logic route: focused check of the generated Commands line plus the affected crate build; dogfood observation in the batch proof (child E). Codex on every code change.
close_reason: done

title: Use pN identities with compact CWD pane labels
description:
Consumer: a local Eon user and EONW workspace consumers such as Venus.

Trigger: Eon creates or recovers a pane, or Orbit reports that pane working directory.

Result: new generations assign one stable opaque p<number> identity. Venus renders that exact identity, two ASCII spaces, then a lexical working-directory label: U+F015 at exact HOME, ~/ plus the HOME-relative path below HOME, and the absolute path outside HOME. Overlong labels preserve the rightmost path components and the ~/ anchor. Missing CWD falls back to the identity, root remains /, and terminal title remains only a selected-window compositor semantic.

Important failures: overflow, collision, malformed EONW state, or evidence that an accepted consumer parses the old spelling blocks publication. Existing live generations may retain pane-N and are never migrated or restarted.
design: Eon owns pane identity allocation. EONW transports the opaque string unchanged. Venus owns the one shared visible and AccessKit label projection. Change the two existing Eon constructors and the existing Venus formatter; add no alias, parser, schema, dependency, settings surface, or second accessibility model.
acceptance_criteria: New and recovered panes use stable p1, p2, and later identities without changing tab or Session IDs. EONW, focus actions, CLI projection, and Venus carry the same exact string. Available headers use exactly two ASCII spaces between identity and location: U+F015 at exact HOME, a ~/ path below HOME, and an absolute path elsewhere; overlong labels preserve the leaf. They show no middle dot, terminal title, file URI decoration, or /home/USER prefix for HOME descendants. Focused regressions, affected locked suites, exact composition build/check, profile identity, docs, LOC, and diff pass. Existing live Sessions are not restarted. User-visible installed header dogfood is accepted before closure.
close_reason: Accepted on 2026-08-24 after the user tested the installed pN pane identities, home icon, and compact relative and absolute path labels. Eon source cfcb38e6e711e971ed6004528987761ddd7c87e4 and Venus source ee3defea55c77f7acc4559606965d93d39bba8b5 satisfy the recorded checks; no acceptance gate remains.

title: Compose selectable Venus cursor colors
description:
## Outcome and contract

Expose Venus's accepted cursor-tail color choice through Eon and EonTerm without copying cursor policy into the orchestrator.

- Consumer: a person launching or reopening Eon or EonTerm.
- Trigger: `$EON_CONFIG_HOME/config.toml` omits or supplies optional `[terminal] cursor_trail_color`.
- Result: omission emits no cursor flag and preserves Venus's launch-stable random default. A supplied string is forwarded unchanged as `--cursor-trail-color VALUE` to each new or reopened Venus process in both products. Accepted values are owned and validated by Venus: `random`, `preset:<name>`, or `custom:#RRGGBB`.
- Important failures: malformed TOML fails before a generation or child starts. A syntactically valid string that Venus rejects fails the existing readiness boundary before a new Orbit Session or user command starts; a rejected reopen preserves the live Orbit Session and command.

This advances EON-C1 through EON-C4 only for exact composition and product configuration. It consumes accepted Venus VEN-C1 source `73195f5812cdc8f32841eab644c1bf4b3af9f756`, published on Eon Desktop `edge` with proof metadata `98630154d8f99143936a950027f96ddbb36db7b5`.

## Ownership and minimum shape

Eon owns one optional product-configuration string and exact launch serialization. Venus owns the selector grammar, eight preset names and RGB values, custom-color validation, random selection, automatic outline, tail rendering, and failure diagnostic. Orbit keeps authoritative cursor body state.

Reuse the existing `TerminalConfig`, `venus_command`, startup-readiness boundary, component manifest, and Nix composition. Add no Yazelix Cursors dependency, registry, palette copy, enum mirror, schema, config file, random logic, validation adapter, runtime reload, or live-window reconfiguration. Do not expose the legacy low-level duration/profile flags through Eon.

## Prerequisites and reference gate

Before code, inspect current EON-C1 through EON-C4, EON-C19's accepted terminal-config/argv mechanism, `managed_environment::TerminalConfig`, `supervisor::venus_command`, both product launch/reopen checks, the canonical component manifest and Nix pins, and accepted Venus VEN-C1 launch/help/tests at source `73195f5812cdc8f32841eab644c1bf4b3af9f756`. Treat the existing typography pass-through as the comparable implementation. Reject the superseded Cursors palette producer and split-color contract.

The current Eon Venus pin `2f05a408e499117c1ddb57f99255dcdb4a236bdf` is stale and must advance only to the exact accepted proof-bearing Venus source. Orbit remains at accepted `ea9fd28ce0908f218cf65d4e6df368f0a4e565f5`.

## Acceptance

- Missing `cursor_trail_color` emits no cursor selector in Eon or EonTerm and therefore keeps Venus's random default.
- `random`, one named preset, and one custom RGB value reach both products byte-for-byte as one `--cursor-trail-color` pair.
- Eon does not recognize preset names or RGB syntax. A Venus-rejected value fails admission before a new Orbit Session or command starts; rejected reopen leaves the existing Session and command alive.
- The canonical manifest, flake input/lock, version reporting, package graph, and docs select exact Venus `73195f5812cdc8f32841eab644c1bf4b3af9f756` and its updated VEN-C1 proof while leaving Orbit and wire versions unchanged.
- Focused red/green checks cover absent and forwarded launch values plus rejection at the outer startup boundary. Run the required locked Rust, manifest, Nix, and installed profile route once on the unchanged candidate.
- Refresh both active product profiles from the accepted working tree without restarting live supervisors. Observe one installed Eon and one EonTerm launch with explicit choices and preserve all pre-existing live process identities.
- Update current configuration help, EON-C1 through EON-C4 proof metadata, changelog, and README LOC from accepted evidence.

## Scope boundary

No cursor registry, split colors, gradients, glow, shader effects, cursor-body override, per-pane policy, duration setting, live reload, settings UI, Cursors compatibility, Orbit change, new dependency, schema, distribution channel, platform claim, or restart of existing Sessions.

## Decision

The user superseded the 2026-09-09 Cursors plan on 2026-09-17: Venus owns eight built-in solid presets, custom RGB, random-by-default behavior, and automatic contrast-aware outlines. Eon performs only optional product-configuration pass-through.
notes: Superseded plan removed on 2026-09-17. The accepted implementation is one optional Eon terminal-config string forwarded unchanged to Venus; Venus owns every cursor value and effect. No Yazelix Cursors dependency or split-palette contract remains.

title: Audit hardcoded user-facing settings, design built-in popup overrides, and draft a configurability gate
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-10-23: "we need a configurability gate / a bead to check hardcoded settings that could be a config setting / and thinking if we let the builtin popup be configurations or overwritten, like the agent pane binding etc". Eon's configuration (docs/CONFIGURATION.md) covers the bar widgets, terminal look, shell, Anima, workspace, sidebar and popups. Some popups are partly fixed: Anima's command and lifetime, Project on Alt+Z. Many user-visible values live as constants in code, for example Venus shortcuts, the sidebar's 28-cell width and 80-cell hide threshold, the spinner rate, and notice behavior. Users who differ from those defaults have no recourse.

## Deliverable (audit plus rule draft; no product code)

1. **Inventory.** List every user-visible behavior value that is hardcoded today, with its file:line:
   - keys and shortcuts (Venus shortcuts, Alt+G, Alt+Shift+H, F6 order, popup keys);
   - built-in popups (Project, Git, Agent, Files, Commands, Anima): which of command, keybinding, label, keep_alive, enabled and geometry can be set today, and which are fixed;
   - sizes and thresholds (sidebar width, hide threshold, column minimums, popup margins);
   - timings (spinner Hz, Anima, notices, attention polling as users see it);
   - colors and glyphs outside the theme;
   - text the user might localize or tune;
   - CLI defaults such as focus-by-default.
   Read the code and contracts, not just the docs. Delegate the reading to subagents.
2. **Classification.** For each: make it configurable, keep it fixed, or "configurable later". Give the reason: users plausibly differ, accessibility, conflicts with other tools (for example a key a user's compositor or editor already uses), versus contract, safety or support cost. Flag duplicates where one setting should govern several places.
3. **Built-in popups.** Make a specific proposal for overriding or replacing built-ins: rebinding the Agent popup and every built-in key, replacing a built-in's command, disabling one, and which built-ins must stay fixed and why (for example Project on Alt+Z if the picker depends on it). Include the conflict rules, building on today's "a popup shortcut on a built-in key takes that key" rule, and how Ratconfig edits these.
4. **General key remapping.** Say whether Eon should offer a keybinding table for non-popup shortcuts (Alt+G, Alt+Shift+H, tab and pane keys), compared with how Zellij, WezTerm, kitty and Ghostty do it (`~/pjs/refs`), and the reserved keys (Alt+/, Alt+0–9).
5. **The configurability gate.** Draft a short rule for Lucca's approval, like the Humans and Agents rule: when a change adds or changes a user-visible value, it either exposes it in configuration with a documented default, or records why it stays fixed. Name its home (the .agent-protocols.local.md overlay rendered into AGENTS.md, plus docs/CONFIGURATION.md and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md), and say whether a compile-time or test check can enforce part of it.
6. **Beads.** Propose an epic and fresh-session-sized child beads for the approved items, each naming its contract owner (EON-C for configuration and popups, VEN-C for Venus keys and layout). File them only after Lucca approves the list.

## Scope

In scope: the inventory, classification, popup and keymap proposals, the gate draft and the proposed beads, recorded on this bead.

Out of scope: implementing any setting, and editing AGENTS.md or docs before approval.

## Acceptance

- Lucca approves, or revises, the classification, the popup override proposal, the gate wording and the bead list.

## Verification

Planning route: bead state and the recorded audit.
close_reason: Lucca approved the audit, the popup proposal, the [keys] design, the gate and the beads (2026-10-23). The Configurability rule is landed in AGENTS.md and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, and epic eon-configurability-qkq8 with 12 children and 12 deferred beads is filed. Proof and review ledger are in the comments.

comments.author: eon-19
comments.text:
# eon-configurability-audit-twdr: audit and proposal (draft for Lucca)

Read at edge `e3682d5`. Detailed inventories with file:line are in the same directory:
`keys.md`, `popups.md`, `values.md`, `refs-keymaps.md`. Refs inspected: zellij `efd8fd5a`
(v0.45.1), wezterm `e2a98e1b`, kitty `b2cb8712` (v0.49.2), ghostty `8c425a7b` (v1.3.1-3142),
tmux `7f2a35ad` (3.8), herdr `143bf5fd`, tuios `0047c409`.

## 1. What is fixed today (summary)

- **Keys.** Venus's `FIXED_SHORTCUTS` (`venus/src/application/shortcuts.rs:106-336`, 33 rows)
  drives matching, the Alt+/ viewer, the hints bar and the link hint. No user can rebind a fixed
  key. The only levers are a popup on that key, which takes it (not Alt+/ or Alt+0–9), and
  `[sidebar] enabled = false` (frees Alt+Shift+H). F6, Escape, Tab, Enter/Space in the chrome,
  close-prompt keys and mouse bindings are untouchable. The grammar is physical keys with at least
  one modifier (`managed_environment.rs:534`, `v19.rs:267-314`).
- **Popups.** Defaults are at `eon/crates/eon/src/product.rs:53-131` and merging at
  `managed_environment.rs:390-478`. Read once per supervisor start; every error stops launch.

  | popup | command | key | label | keep_alive | enabled |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | Project | rejected | settable (docs say fixed) | settable | only false | can't disable |
  | Git, Agent, Files | settable | settable | settable | settable | settable |
  | Commands | settable (undocumented) | settable | settable | settable (undocumented) | settable |
  | Anima | rejected | settable (undocumented) | settable | only false | settable |

  Behavior follows the ID, not the command. Files survives folder changes, Agent is parked on
  retarget and gets attention, and Git and Agent get hint priority. Replacing a built-in's
  command keeps all of this. cwd is always the tab folder, and env is only
  `EON_TERMINAL`/`EON_TAB`. Geometry is the global `[popup]` margins only.
- **Values.** There is no theme. The ANSI 0–15 palette is one string in `product.rs:121` that
  Orbit already accepts as input. About 24 chrome colors sit inline in `venus/src/render/`. The
  cursor trail can't be turned off: Venus accepts `--cursor-effect-v1 none`, but the supervisor
  never sends it. Copy on select is always on (VEN-C7), and wheel scroll is 3 rows per notch in
  3 places. The sidebar always starts open at 28 cells and hides below 80 (`scene.rs:1095-1097`).
  The hints bar appears on every fresh window, the clock is always 24h (VEN-C27), the padding is
  12 px, and scrollback is 16 MiB (ORB-C8).
- **Ratconfig** is pinned (`eon-v4.json:332-347`), but no crate uses it, and there is no config
  schema.

## 2. Contract tension found

EON-C28 (planned, binds from 1.0) promises that "a later default never makes a 1.0 configuration
fail". Today two popups on one key is a load error, built-ins included
(`managed_environment.rs:603-608`), so Commands on Alt+Shift+M already collides with a custom
popup there. A built-in popup added in 1.x would break such a configuration, so this must change
before 1.0. EON-C20's boundary also excludes "rebinding UI" and a "second shortcut catalog",
and VEN-C20 excludes rebinding in Venus. A keymap needs both contracts amended.

## 3. Classification

**Configurable now** (users plausibly differ, accessibility, or key conflicts):
- Fixed shortcuts, through a `[keys]` table (section 5).
- A popup's key: a user key beats a built-in popup's default key, and `keybinding = ""` unbinds
  any popup's key, Project's included.
- `[terminal] palette`, 16 colors (Orbit input exists).
- Cursor trail off (accessibility; the Venus input exists).
- Copy on select on/off, and scroll rows per notch (VEN-C7).
- Sidebar width and whether it starts open (VEN-C30). The hide threshold stays derived.
- Hints bar on start, and a 12h/24h clock (VEN-C24, VEN-C27).

**Configurable later:**
- A chrome theme (a palette struct must replace the inline colors first).
- Padding.
- Scrollback (needs a new Orbit input).
- Per-popup geometry, cwd and env.
- Link opener.
- Bell and attention notifications.
- Click interval and word separators (ORB-C9 excludes them today).
- Reduce motion.
- UI font and label size.
- Localization.
- A Ratconfig editor plus a config schema.
- Tab-select modifier (Alt+0–9).

**Fixed, with reason:**
- Alt+/ (keeps the viewer reachable) and Alt+0–9: EON-C20/C28 reserved set.
- F6, Escape, Tab, Enter/Space, and close-prompt keys: accessibility and safety of the
  confirmation.
- Project's command and its required presence (a runtime mechanism that EONW pending tabs
  depend on).
- Anima's command: a replacement would just be a custom popup.
- EONW bounds of 4 columns, 64 tabs and 256 terminals: a protocol bump.
- Spinner at most 5 Hz and attention polling: AP-PERF budget (VEN-C21, EON-C31, ORB-C15).
- Quota old after 1h and gone after 24h: trust in the figures (EON-C27). Intervals may only
  lengthen, later.
- Orbit stop grace: lifecycle safety (ORB-C12).
- Session and admission timeouts, header heights (derived), log retention, and `--json`
  confirmation semantics.

**Duplicates (one value, several owners):**
- Tooltips hardcode Alt+Shift+T, Alt+/ and Alt+Shift+W (`scene.rs:390-406`).
- The reserved set is in Runtime and implicitly in three places in Venus.
- Three chord formatters, one of which prints "Alt+Slash".
- Key text in dialogs and accessibility labels.
- Five hand-kept doc key tables.
- 3 rows per notch in 3 places.
- Minimum tab width `font_size·4` in 4 places.
- Sidebar 28/80/40 in code, VEN-C30 and the docs.
- Quota 60/300 s and 1h/24h in code, EON-C27 and the docs.
- CPU/RAM 2 s as a constant and as a separate string.
- Cursor-trail default: 1.5 in Eon versus 1.0 in standalone Venus.
- fzf options repeated in `cli.rs:289` and `cli.rs:438`.

**Doc and code mismatches:**
- CONFIGURATION.md and EON-C10:877 say Project is "required on Alt+Z", but its key is settable.
- Anima's key and label are settable but undocumented.
- Commands' `command` and `keep_alive` are undocumented.
- Agent defaults include `resume`/`--resume`.
- The parity epic says `xdg-open`, but the code runs `gio open`.
- The CONFIGURATION.md example block reads like the shipped defaults, but they are unset or
  random.
- `venus/docs/INTERACTION.md` lists Alt+Z as a Venus key.

## 4. Built-in popups proposal

- **Rebind.** `[popups.<id>].keybinding` works for every built-in (today's behavior, now
  documented). `keybinding = ""` leaves the popup with no key; it stays reachable from Commands
  and the CLI (`eon-agent-parity-a9g0.1`).
- **Replace.** `command` works for Git, Agent, Files and Commands, and keeps the ID-tied
  behavior (attention, parking, folder survival). It stays fixed for Project (a runtime
  mechanism) and Anima.
- **Disable.** `enabled = false` works for every built-in except Project (pending tabs need it).
- **Conflicts.** Resolve user-configured keys first (`[keys]` and `[popups.*]`): two
  user-configured keys on one chord fail at load, as today. Then each default, whether a
  built-in popup's or a fixed shortcut's, takes its key only if that key is still free; a
  default that loses its key shows as "overridden by X" in Alt+/. Reserved keys always fail.
  This turns Commands' collision into an override and satisfies EON-C28.
- **Project and Alt+Z.** Document that Project's key is settable now. Removing Alt+Z stays with
  `eon-ecne.3`.
- **Ratconfig.** It edits these only once Runtime publishes one config schema
  (`eon config schema --json`) generated from its own config table. That is "later"; until then
  there is nothing for Ratconfig to read without a second owner.

## 5. General keymap proposal

Every reference keeps one defaults table, lets user binds win, and supports per-key unbinding.
herdr (Rust, TOML, popups as bindings) is the closest to Eon.

```toml
[keys]
toggle_sidebar = "Alt+Shift+H"
next_attention = ["Alt+G", "Ctrl+Alt+G"]
new_window = ""            # unbind
```

- Action names are fixed IDs, and a value is a chord or a list of chords. A user value replaces
  that action's defaults, `""` or `[]` unbinds it, and an omitted action keeps its default.
- Errors before any workspace change: unknown action, invalid chord, duplicate user chord,
  reserved chord.
- Keep today's physical-key grammar, which requires a modifier.
- Popups keep their own `keybinding` field and go through the same resolver; there is no
  `launch` action.
- One table: action IDs and default chords live in `eon-workspace-protocol`. Runtime parses and
  resolves, EONW carries the resolved table (a version bump), and Venus dispatches from it.
  The viewer, hints, tooltips, accessibility labels and `eon keys --json` all read that table.
- Rejected: clear-all, modes, leader keys and sequences, a Lua or conditional keymap, silent
  last-wins, writing defaults into the user's file, live reload (later, with
  `eon-agent-parity-a9g0.7`).

## 6. Draft gate rule (for `.agent-protocols.local.md`, rendered into AGENTS.md)

> ## Configurability
>
> When a change adds or changes a value a person sees or feels in Eon (a key, size,
> threshold, timing, color, glyph, text, toggle or CLI default), it either exposes it
> in configuration with its default documented in `docs/CONFIGURATION.md`, or the
> owning bead records why it stays fixed: a contract or protocol bound, safety, a
> performance budget, or a support cost that outweighs users differing. Accessibility,
> a key other tools commonly use, and a reasonable user who differs are reasons to
> expose it. One setting governs each value; tooltips, labels and documentation
> derive from it rather than repeating it. Eon Runtime parses configuration and sends
> resolved values; Venus parses none. Open gaps: `<epic id>`.

A summary line goes in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` next to Humans and Agents.

**Enforcement.** Part can be checked:
- Key display text derives from the single key table by construction.
- A Runtime test serializes a fully populated config and fails when a key path is missing from
  `docs/CONFIGURATION.md`.
- A test checks that every action in the key table has a default and a viewer row.

New hardcoded constants can't be detected mechanically; the review brief checks for them.

## 7. Proposed beads (file after approval)

Epic: **Make Eon's user-visible values configurable** (P2; children carry their own priority).

1. **Popup key precedence and docs** (P1, release-1): a user key beats a built-in popup default,
   `keybinding = ""` unbinds a popup's key, and the popup doc mismatches are fixed.
   EON-C10, EON-C20, EON-C28.
2. **One key table** (P2): action IDs and defaults move into `eon-workspace-protocol`; the Venus
   viewer, tooltips, accessibility and the reserved set derive from it. No behavior change.
   VEN-C20, EON-C20.
3. **`[keys]` table** (P2, after 2): Runtime parses and resolves, EONW is bumped, Venus
   dispatches, Alt+/ shows overrides. EON-C20 and VEN-C20 are amended.
4. **`eon keys --json`** (P2, after 3): the resolved keymap as data (Humans and Agents).
5. **`[terminal] palette`** (P2): 16 ANSI colors. EON-C terminal configuration.
6. **Cursor trail off** (P2, accessibility): EON-C terminal configuration, VEN cursor contract.
7. **Copy on select and scroll rows per notch** (P3): VEN-C7, also unifying the 3 scroll
   literals.
8. **Sidebar width and start state** (P3): VEN-C30, EON-C31.
9. **Hints on start and 12h/24h clock** (P3): VEN-C24, VEN-C27.
10. **Config docs coverage test** (P3): the gate's enforcement test.
11. **Docs mismatches** (P3, docs-only): the remaining non-popup items from section 3.

Deferred (one bead each, deferred): chrome theme, Ratconfig and config schema, scrollback,
padding, per-popup geometry/cwd/env, link opener, bell and attention notifications, reduce
motion, localization, tab-select modifier.

The CLI focus defaults (`eon pane create` focuses, `eon tab create` activates) stay with
`eon-agent-parity-a9g0` and `eon-tab-create-launch-8tl4`.

title: Make Eon's user-visible values configurable
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-10-23: "we need a configurability gate / a bead to check hardcoded settings that could
be a config setting / and thinking if we let the builtin popup be configurations or overwritten,
like the agent pane binding etc". The audit `eon-configurability-audit-twdr` (comment of
2026-10-23, read at edge `e3682d5`) inventoried every hardcoded user-visible value and classified
it. Lucca approved the classification, the built-in popup proposal, the `[keys]` keymap design,
the Configurability rule and this bead list ("agree to everything", 2026-10-23). The rule names
this epic as the home of its open gaps, so the epic stays open while any child does.

## Approved decisions

- **Built-in popups.** Every built-in's key is settable, Project's included. `keybinding = ""`
  leaves a popup without a key. `command` can be replaced for Git, Agent, Files and Commands, and
  the ID-tied behavior (attention, parking, folder survival) is kept. Project's and Anima's
  commands stay fixed. Every built-in except Project can be disabled.
- **Conflicts.** User-configured keys (`[keys]` and `[popups.*]`) resolve first. Two
  user-configured keys on one chord, or a reserved chord, fail at load. A default, whether a
  built-in popup's or a fixed shortcut's, keeps its key only while that key is free; otherwise
  Alt+/ shows it as "overridden by X". This is required for EON-C28 before 1.0.
- **Keymap.** A flat `[keys]` table maps each action to a chord or a list of chords; `""` or
  `[]` unbinds it, an omitted action keeps its default, and errors stop the load.
  - Action IDs and default chords live in `eon-workspace-protocol`. Eon Runtime parses and
    resolves the table, EONW carries the resolved bindings (a version bump), and Venus
    dispatches from them.
  - The Alt+/ viewer, hints, tooltips, accessibility labels and `eon keys --json` all derive
    from that one table.
  - Rejected: clear-all, modes, leader keys and sequences, silent last-wins, writing defaults into
    the user's file, live reload (later), and Venus keeping the defaults while receiving only
    overrides (Runtime could then not list the keymap for agents).
- **Fixed, with reason.**
  - Alt+/ and Alt+0–9: the reserved set, which 1.x never enlarges (it may shrink; `eon-zyef` defers a tab-select modifier).
  - F6, Escape, Tab, Enter/Space in the chrome, and close-prompt keys: accessibility, and the
    confirmation's safety.
  - Project's command and presence, because EONW pending tabs require it. Anima's command,
    because a replacement is just a custom popup.
  - EONW bounds, spinner and attention polling (performance budget), quota aging (trust), and
    Orbit stop grace (lifecycle safety).

## Acceptance

- Every non-deferred child is closed.
- Each deferred "later" bead is either still deferred with its reason, or closed.

## Children (planned)

1. Popup key precedence, an EONW version with an optional popup shortcut, and popup docs (P1, release-1; blocks eon-igae.7, .8, .11)
2. One key table in `eon-workspace-protocol` (no behavior change)
3. EONW carries resolved bindings and Venus dispatches from them, defaults only (after 1 and 2)
4. `eon keys --json` (after 12)
5. `[terminal] palette`
6. Cursor trail off
7. Copy on select and scroll rows per notch
8. Sidebar width and start state
9. Hints bar on start and 12h/24h clock
10. Config docs coverage test
11. Docs mismatches
12. `[keys]` configuration (after 1 and 3; split from 3 by review, 2026-10-23)

## Deferred beads (accepted gap)

The twelve deferred "later" beads carry Why, Shape and Why deferred only. Each gets its contract, acceptance checks and scope boundary when it is un-deferred, before any work starts.

## Known duplicates not scheduled here

The audit also found these duplicates:
- The minimum tab width `font_size·4` at 4 sites (`venus/src/scene.rs:1402,1409,1918,2007`).
- The CPU/RAM 2 s interval, held both as a constant and in a separate string
  (`venus/src/system.rs:62`).
- The cursor trail default: 1.5 in Eon versus 1.0 in standalone Venus (`venus/src/launch.rs:231`).
- The fzf options repeated at `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/cli.rs:289` and `:438`.
- Font fallback names held as product defaults and as Venus constants
  (`venus/src/render/cells.rs:13-14`).

Fix each when a change touches it, under the Configurability rule.
