title: Let a configured popup key beat a built-in popup's default key, and document each built-in's settable fields
description:
## Why

EON-C28 (planned, binds from 1.0) promises that "a later default never makes a 1.0 configuration
fail". Today two popups on one key are a load error, built-ins included, so a built-in popup that
1.x adds on a key a user's custom popup already uses would break that configuration. Commands on
Alt+Shift+M already collides this way. Lucca approved, 2026-10-23 (parent epic): a user-configured
popup key beats a built-in popup's default key, and `keybinding = ""` leaves a popup without a key.

## Evidence

- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/managed_environment.rs:603-608`: popup-versus-popup collision
  is an error, built-ins included. Catalog order is built-ins first, then customs alphabetically.
- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/managed_environment.rs:413-478`: `popup_catalog()` merges the
  built-ins from `eon/crates/eon/src/product.rs:53-131`.
- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/managed_environment.rs:417-432`: Project and Anima guards. Their
  `keybinding` and `label` are accepted.
- `venus/src/application/shortcuts.rs:400-418`, `:518-524`: Venus marks a fixed shortcut
  "(overridden by X)". Built-in popup defaults have no such marking.
- Docs that disagree with the code:
  - `docs/CONFIGURATION.md:168` and EON-C10 "Runtime policy" (`docs/CONTRACTS.md:877`) say
    "Project is required on Alt+Z", but its key is settable.
  - Anima's key and label are settable but undocumented.
  - Commands' `command` and `keep_alive` are undocumented.
  - The Agent defaults' arguments (`codex resume`, `claude --resume`) are undocumented.

## Wire constraint

EONW v19 cannot carry a popup without a key:
- `PopupEntry.shortcut` is a required `Shortcut`
  (`runtime/crates/eon-workspace-protocol/src/v19.rs:318-322`).
- A snapshot rejects two entries on one shortcut (`:1189`).
- `Shortcut::validate` rejects a chord with no modifier (`:306-311`).

A displaced or keyless popup cannot simply be left out of `Snapshot.entries`:
- Every live popup's entry must be listed (`validate_workspace`, `v19.rs:1236`; it runs on
  encode, `:905`).
- `InvokePopup` is refused for an unlisted entry (`check_popup_action`, `:524`).
- Runtime opens Project by ID for pending tabs (`runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/workspace.rs:167`,
  `:520`), and Agent can be live from the sidebar or the CLI.

This child therefore makes the one small EONW change that precedence needs: a new EONW version
in which `PopupEntry.shortcut` is optional. Follow the EONW codec rules: never amend a version in
place.
- A built-in that lost its key, and any popup with `keybinding = ""`, stays listed with no
  shortcut, so it can be live and opened.
- Venus never sees the built-in popup defaults (`eon/crates/eon/src/product.rs:53-131`), and
  derives "(overridden by X)" only for its own `FIXED_SHORTCUTS`
  (`venus/src/application/shortcuts.rs:401-417`, `:518-524`). So the entry must also say why it
  has no key: a user unbound it, or the overriding entry's ID took it (with the default chord, if
  Alt+/ is to show it).
- The entries-uniqueness check (`v19.rs:1189`) must skip entries without a shortcut.

Opening a popup by ID from the CLI is `eon-agent-parity-a9g0.1`. Until it lands, a popup with
`keybinding = ""` cannot be opened from the window. The docs say so. The later bindings bump in
sibling child .3 builds on this version.

This was decided by eon-19 after review on 2026-10-23, to keep the 1.0 path at one bead. The
rejected alternative made .1 wait on .2 and .3.

## Scope

In scope:
- EON-C10, EON-C20 and EON-C28 text (stop for Lucca's approval of the exact wording first).
- Runtime popup catalog resolution.
- The EONW version above.
- Every consumer of `PopupEntry.shortcut`:
  - Venus matching (`shortcuts.rs:826-838`);
  - the Alt+/ rows and popup group (`:533-543`);
  - the hints bar (`:630-646`);
  - header tooltips (`venus/src/scene.rs:395-398`);
  - `eon workspace` text (`key=`, `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/workspace.rs:1622`) and JSON
    (`"keybinding"`, `:1648`).
- The JSON form of a keyless entry (for example `null`, or the field omitted) is a user-visible
  CLI choice that `eon-igae.11` will freeze as a 1.0 fixture. Propose it with the contract text
  for Lucca's choice.
- `docs/CONFIGURATION.md` "Popups".

Out of scope:
- Carrying fixed-shortcut bindings over EONW (sibling child .3).
- The `[keys]` table for fixed shortcuts (sibling child .12).
- Removing Alt+Z (`eon-ecne.3`).
- Popup CLI paths (`eon-agent-parity-a9g0.1`).

## Acceptance

- A custom popup on a built-in popup's default key loads. The custom popup gets the key, the
  built-in stays listed without one, and Alt+/ shows it as overridden.
- Two user-configured popup keys on one chord still fail, as does a reserved chord.
- `[popups.<id>] keybinding = ""` loads for any popup, Project included, and binds no key.
  Project still opens for a pending tab, and the snapshot stays valid while it is live.
- `docs/CONFIGURATION.md` documents each built-in's settable fields exactly as the code
  enforces them.

## Reference gate (consequential: wire format and contract)

Before code, record on this bead:
- the one owner of each behavior: Runtime resolves popup keys, and Venus matches and renders;
- the `docs/REFERENCES.md` route "How should shared popups extend the workspace wire contract
  without breaking the installed client?";
- the comparable keymaps in the `eon-configurability-audit-twdr` audit (herdr `143bf5fd`,
  Ghostty `8c425a7b`), the decision and its check.

## Portability

Neutral: no platform mechanics change.

## Verification

- Full affected Rust and Nix surfaces (shared wire protocol, per the AGENTS.md Verification
  table), including a focused red/green test for built-in-default versus custom precedence and
  for the empty key.
- One isolated installed dogfood check of the precedence and the Alt+/ row.
- Codex review per AGENTS.md "Codex on every code change".

## Stop Conditions

- Stop and coordinate if the sidebar child (.8) is bumping EONW at the same time, so that
  versions land in order.

comments.text:
Reference gate and design (eon-e9, 2026-10-27, read at edge `adc4af7`)

## Approval (relayed by the coordinator)

Relayed by eon-overseer on 2026-10-27, quoting Lucca to eon-overseer on 2026-10-26: "focus on finishing the worspace-switching beads, but try to advance on kitty-graphics too / everything is pre-approved. autonomous. / and sprinkle the ones the subagent listed that are important." and "also pre-aprove changes of plan if a clearly better alternative appears". The coordinator named this bead as covered. It is applied here to: the EON-C10, EON-C20, EON-C28 and VEN-C20 wording below, the keyless-entry JSON form below, and EONW v21 (eon-overseer confirmed v21 is this bead's number; shn4.8 takes v22).

## Owners

- Eon Runtime resolves popup keys (`managed_environment.rs` `popup_catalog`): it alone knows which keys the user configured and which are built-in defaults.
- EONW (`eon-workspace-protocol` v21) carries the result per entry.
- Venus matches and renders from that result; it keeps no copy of the built-in defaults.
- Eon (`product.rs`) keeps owning the default table.

## Why the wire, not Venus derivation

Venus receives only the resolved catalog. It never sees `product.rs` defaults or which keys were configured, so it cannot tell that Commands lost Alt+Shift+M to `[popups.editor]`, nor show the default chord. A keyless entry also cannot be left out of `Snapshot.entries`: `validate_workspace` requires every live popup's entry, `check_popup_action` refuses an unlisted one, and Runtime opens Project by ID for pending tabs. So the snapshot must list keyless entries, and only the wire can say why one has no key.

## Mechanism adopted

- v21 `PopupEntry.shortcut` becomes `PopupKey`: `Bound(Shortcut)`, `Unbound` (the user set `keybinding = ""`), or `Overridden { default: Shortcut, by: entry ID }`. Wire: one tag byte, then the shortcut and/or ID.
- Snapshot validation: chords of `Bound` entries stay unique; `Overridden.by` must name another listed entry whose `Bound` shortcut equals `default`. Other v20 rules are unchanged.
- Resolution: user-configured keys (every custom popup's `keybinding`, and a built-in's when set) are checked first: reserved chords and two configured popups on one chord fail at load, as today. A built-in default then keeps its key only while no configured popup holds it; otherwise it is `Overridden` by that popup. `keybinding = ""` gives `Unbound` for any popup, Project included. Two built-in defaults on one chord stay an error (a product bug).
- Venus: dispatch, hints and header tooltips use only `Bound` entries. Alt+/ lists an `Overridden` entry with its default chord as "<label> (overridden by <popup label>)", the same form as fixed rows, and omits an `Unbound` entry (it has no shortcut to list; the user chose that).
- `eon workspace` text: `key=none` for a keyless entry. JSON entries: `"keybinding": "<chord>" | null`, plus `"overridden_by": "<entry id>" | null` and `"default_keybinding": "<chord>" | null` (both non-null only when overridden), so an agent reads what Alt+/ shows.
- Eon's version moves 0.1.3 to 0.1.4, as every EONW change bumps it.

## References read

- `docs/REFERENCES.md` "How should shared popups extend the workspace wire contract without breaking the installed client?": kept bounded framing, exact entry identities, no runtime negotiation or adapter, no popup policy in Venus, and a new version rather than amending v20 bytes. Rejected: Venus duplicating the defaults table.
- herdr `143bf5fd` (`src/config/keybinds.rs:652`, `:1099-1102`; `src/input/keybind_help.rs:41-47`): user binds are registered before defaults; a default on a taken key is dropped silently; `""` or `[]` unbinds; the help overlay keeps the action with "unset". Kept: user-first resolution and `""` to unbind. Rejected: silent drop with no reason (we show "overridden by X"), and herdr's "first wins, later disabled" for two user binds (Eon keeps failing the load, per the approved epic).
- Ghostty `8c425a7b` (`src/input/Binding.zig:2567-2592`, `:313-315`; `src/cli/list_keybinds.zig`): defaults load first and a later user `keybind` overwrites the trigger; `trigger=unbind` removes it; the list shows only the effective set. Rejected: last-wins and listing nothing for a displaced default.
- Decision: user-configured keys first, defaults yield with a recorded reason. Check: focused red/green tests in `managed_environment.rs` (custom on Commands' default loads, Commands overridden; `keybinding = ""` on Project loads, unbound) and the v21 snapshot validation tests, then one isolated installed Alt+/ observation.

## Contract text adopted (exact)

EON-C10 Runtime policy, first sentence: "Project is required, defaults to Alt+Z, and uses Eon's existing transient chooser command."

EON-C10 Commands sentence: "The Commands popup follows the popup catalog's key precedence below." (replaces "...so a configured popup on the same key is a collision.")

EON-C10 Configuration, added after the `[popups.<id>]` sentence: "A configured `keybinding`, every custom popup's and a built-in's that the user set, takes its key first. A built-in popup's default key applies only while no configured popup holds it; otherwise the built-in stays in the catalog without a key, overridden by that popup. `keybinding = \"\"` leaves any popup, Project included, in the catalog without a key." And "It rejects malformed or colliding shortcuts" becomes "It rejects malformed shortcuts, reserved shortcuts, two configured popups on one shortcut".

EON-C10 Popup snapshot: "The catalog carries enabled entries, each with its normalized physical shortcut or, without one, whether the configuration unbound it or another entry holds its default shortcut, and logical-pixel margins;"

EON-C20 Result, added after "...lists it as overridden by the popup.": "A built-in popup whose default key a configured popup holds is listed with that key as overridden by the configured popup; a popup configured without a key has no row."
EON-C20 Owner: "Eon Runtime resolves popup keys and enforces configured popup collisions."
EON-C20 Boundary: "One exception: the viewer reads `sidebar` from EONW v20." becomes "Exceptions: the viewer reads `sidebar` and each popup entry's override from EONW v21."

EON-C28 Shortcuts: "(`eon-igae.10`, required before 1.0)" becomes "(`eon-igae.10` for fixed shortcuts and `eon-configurability-qkq8.1` for built-in popups, required before 1.0)".

VEN-C20 Result: after "...normalized physical shortcut from the current Eon snapshot" add "; an entry the snapshot marks overridden is listed with its default shortcut as \"<label> (overridden by <popup label>)\", and an entry without a shortcut otherwise has no row". VEN-C20 Owner: "Eon owns the enabled popup catalog and its key resolution and must reserve ...".

## Mixed versions

After a profile refresh, the profile `eon` CLI in terminals of a running v20 supervisor cannot control it until a normal restart. The CHANGELOG entry and the proof record say so.

## Portability

Neutral.

title: Fail a test when a configuration key is missing from docs/CONFIGURATION.md
description:
## Why

The Configurability rule in AGENTS.md, approved by Lucca on 2026-10-23, requires every
configurable value's default to be documented in `docs/CONFIGURATION.md`. Part of that can be
checked mechanically. This child adds that check.

## Evidence

- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/managed_environment.rs:23-135` and `:169-202`: the serde config structs
  (`deny_unknown_fields`) are the only schema. There is no Serialize implementation and no
  schema file.
- `docs/CONFIGURATION.md`: hand-written.

## Scope

In scope:
- A Runtime test that enumerates every accepted config key path and fails when one is missing
  from `docs/CONFIGURATION.md`. A key path looks like `terminal.font_size` or `popups.<id>.command`.
- How to enumerate the paths: prefer deriving them from the structs, for example a Serialize of
  a fully populated value or a small derive, over a hand-kept list. A hand list would be a
  second owner.

Out of scope:
- Detecting new hardcoded constants. Review covers that.
- A published schema or Ratconfig (deferred bead).

## Acceptance

- Adding a config field without documenting it makes `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime`
  fail with the missing key named.
- Today's tree passes (fix any key the test finds undocumented).

## Verification

- Red/green: remove one documented key from a scratch copy of the doc and see the test fail.
- Codex review.

[terminal], [shell] and [anima] serialize from the resolver structs, but [bar], [workspace], [sidebar] and the popups are hand-listed in print_defaults (runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/managed_environment.rs:276-345), so a new key there (e.g. 4ae8a21's animate_working_badge) is caught only if someone also adds it by hand. Remaining scope: derive those sections. Stale: unknown keys now warn (2a2e31e) rather than fail; Serialize exists.

title: Let users rebind and unbind Eon's fixed shortcuts with a [keys] table
description:
## Why

Nobody can rebind Eon's fixed shortcuts, though they collide with keys other tools commonly use:
- Alt+H/J/K/L are Zellij's focus keys.
- Alt+L is Nushell (reedline) lowercase-word, and Alt+M is backspace-word in the shell Eon ships.
- Alt+Shift+J is Helix's join-selections.
- Ctrl+Alt+L locks the screen on KDE and some GNOME setups.

Lucca approved a flat `[keys]` table on 2026-10-23 (parent epic). The sibling "EONW carries
resolved bindings" child already delivers bindings to Venus, so this child adds parsing,
resolution and the contract text.

## Design (approved)

```toml
[keys]
toggle_sidebar = "Alt+Shift+H"
next_attention = ["Alt+G", "Ctrl+Alt+G"]
new_window = ""            # unbind
```

- A user value replaces that action's defaults, `""` or `[]` unbinds it, and an omitted action
  keeps its default.
- Resolution order: user-configured chords from `[keys]` and `[popups.*]` first. Then each
  default takes its chord while it is still free; one that loses its chord shows as
  "overridden by X" in Alt+/.
- Load errors, before any workspace change: unknown action, invalid chord, duplicate
  user-configured chord, reserved chord (Alt+Slash, Alt+0–9).
- Keep today's physical-key grammar (`runtime/crates/eon-workspace-protocol/src/v19.rs:267-314`).
- Not rebindable: F6, Escape, Tab, Enter/Space in the chrome, close-prompt keys, mouse.
- Rejected: clear-all, modes, leader keys, sequences, live reload, silent last-wins.
- Reference shapes: herdr `143bf5fd`, Ghostty `8c425a7b`, kitty `b2cb8712`, WezTerm `e2a98e1b`,
  Zellij `efd8fd5a`. The comparison is in the `eon-configurability-audit-twdr` audit comment.

## Evidence

- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/managed_environment.rs:113-135`: config structs with
  `deny_unknown_fields`.
- `:534`: `parse_shortcut`.
- `:603-608`: today's popup collision check, which the resolver absorbs.
- EON-C28's shortcut item (`docs/CONTRACTS.md:2143-2148`).

## Scope

In scope:
- Runtime `[keys]` parsing and the one resolver for `[keys]` and popup keys.
- Alt+/ marks overridden defaults.
- EON-C20, VEN-C20 and EON-C28 text, after Lucca approves the wording.
- `docs/CONFIGURATION.md` and `docs/USAGE.md`.

Out of scope:
- `eon keys --json` (sibling child).
- Live reload.
- Keys inside child programs (Yazi, fzf, Anima).

## Acceptance

- A `[keys]` entry rebinds or unbinds a fixed action in a fresh window.
- Alt+/ shows the effective keymap and each overridden default.
- Each listed error stops the load with a message naming the key.

## Reference gate (consequential: configuration contract)

Before code, record on this bead the one owner (Runtime resolves `[keys]` and popup keys together), the reference keymaps above and their constraints kept (user wins, per-key unbind, load errors), the rejected shapes, and the decision check. `docs/REFERENCES.md` has no keymap route yet; add one with the review record template.

## Portability

Neutral: chords stay physical-key names that the native host boundary already maps.

## Verification

- A focused red/green Runtime test for each error and for precedence (`nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime`).
- One isolated installed dogfood check of a rebind and an unbind.
- Codex review.

## Stop Conditions

- This child makes no EONW change; .3 carries everything it needs. Stop and ask if one turns out to be required.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Contract conflict, 2026-10-27 (prime-beads pass 2): this design makes an unknown [keys] action a load error, but EON-C28 now says unknown configuration keys are ignored with a warning and that a newer 1.x config may fail on an older release only for an unaccepted value of a known key (2a2e31e, eon-3onw). Whether an unknown action name inside [keys] warns or fails is Lucca's call before code. Stale refs: v19.rs is gone; Shortcut is at runtime/crates/eon-workspace-protocol/src/v22.rs:286, parse_shortcut :778; deny_unknown_fields is gone.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Lucca, 2026-10-27, relayed by eon-overseer: 'agree with everything' (question 16 of the prime-beads passes, recommendation: an unknown action name in [keys] warns, like EON-C28's unknown keys, rather than failing the load). Design: an unknown [keys] action is ignored with a warning naming it; invalid key syntax for a known action follows EON-C28's 'unaccepted value of a known key' rule.

title: Move Eon's shortcut actions and default keys into one table in eon-workspace-protocol
description:
## Why

The approved keymap design (parent epic) needs one table of actions and default chords that
Runtime, Venus and the CLI all read. Today Venus owns the defaults alone, and their display text
is repeated by hand in several places. This child moves the table and derives every display from
it, with no change to which key does what.

## Evidence

- `venus/src/application/shortcuts.rs:108-336`: `FIXED_SHORTCUTS`, 33 rows. It drives matching,
  the Alt+/ viewer, the hints bar and the link hint.
- `venus/src/scene.rs:390-406`: header tooltips hardcode "Alt+Shift+T", "Alt+/" and "Alt+Shift+W"
  and re-implement the override check.
- `venus/src/scene.rs:812-813` and `venus/src/accessibility.rs:213,223,225`: key text written
  into dialogs and screen-reader labels.
- The reserved set has two sources:
  - Runtime's `reserved_shortcut` (`runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/managed_environment.rs:613-631`).
  - Three implicit exclusions in Venus (`venus/src/application/shortcuts.rs:407-416`, `:783`,
    `venus/src/application.rs:4657`).
  - `eon-igae.10` asked for one source and closed without one.
- Three chord formatters: Venus labels, Runtime `shortcut_text`
  (`runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/workspace.rs:1799-1820`, which prints "Alt+Slash"), and the
  hardcoded strings above.

## Scope

In scope:
- An action ID enum with default chords and the reserved set in
  `runtime/crates/eon-workspace-protocol`. It stays standalone, with no workspace-inherited
  settings.
- Venus matching, viewer, hints, tooltips and accessibility labels derive from it.
- Runtime's reserved check uses it.
- One chord formatter per audience (config syntax and display).

Out of scope:
- Any user-visible key change.
- Config parsing of `[keys]`.
- An EONW wire change. The table is shared Rust code, not wire data.

## Acceptance

- Every key text a person sees comes from the table, so changing one default chord in the table
  changes matching, the viewer, hints, tooltips and accessibility labels together.
- Runtime and Venus read one reserved set.
- Key behavior is unchanged.

## Portability

Neutral: a shared table in the protocol crate; no platform mechanics change.

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test` for `eon-workspace-protocol`, `eon-runtime` and `yazelix-venus`.
- `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings` for Venus.
- A test that each action has a default and a viewer row.
- Codex review.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if moving the table forces an EONW change or a protocol-crate dependency on Venus types.

title: Carry resolved shortcut bindings over EONW and dispatch Venus's fixed shortcuts from them
description:
## Why

The approved `[keys]` design (parent epic, Lucca 2026-10-23) has Eon Runtime resolve the keymap
and Venus dispatch from the result. Today Venus matches against its own `FIXED_SHORTCUTS` and only
popup keys come over EONW. This child moves the resolved bindings onto EONW and makes Venus
dispatch from them, still with default chords only, so that the sibling `[keys]` child adds only
parsing and resolution. It is split from that child so each fits one session.

## Evidence

- `venus/src/application.rs:3486-3530` (dispatch chain) and `:2087-2275` (workspace keys:
  Alt+digits, popup keys, fixed actions, focus-only keys).
- `venus/src/application/shortcuts.rs:826-838`: popup keys matched from `Snapshot.entries`.
- `runtime/crates/eon-workspace-protocol/src/v19.rs:264-322`: the `Shortcut` wire type.
- EON-C20 (`docs/CONTRACTS.md:1689`): its boundary excludes "a second shortcut catalog" and an
  EONW change (`:1720`). VEN-C20 (`venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md:1125`).

## Scope

In scope:
- A new EONW version whose snapshot carries, per action, zero or more resolved chords and, for a default that lost its chord, the action or popup that took it (everything the `[keys]` child .12 needs, so .12 makes no EONW change), built from the
  shared key table of the sibling child. Follow the EONW codec rules: never amend a version in
  place.
- Runtime fills it from the defaults.
- Venus dispatches fixed actions from it.
- Build on the EONW version from sibling child .1, which makes `PopupEntry.shortcut` optional.
- EON-C20 and VEN-C20 boundary text, after Lucca approves the wording.

Out of scope:
- Parsing `[keys]`.
- Any user-visible key change.
- Non-rebindable keys (F6, Escape, Tab, Enter/Space, close-prompt keys, mouse), which stay in
  Venus.

## Acceptance

- Every fixed shortcut behaves as before.
- Venus matches fixed actions only from the bindings that EONW delivers.
- Standalone Venus (one Orbit session) still uses the shared table's defaults.

## Reference gate (consequential: wire format and contract)

Before code, record on this bead: the one owner of each behavior (Runtime resolves bindings, Venus dispatches), the `docs/REFERENCES.md` route "How should shared popups extend the workspace wire contract without breaking the installed client?", the comparable keymaps in the `eon-configurability-audit-twdr` audit (herdr `143bf5fd`, WezTerm `e2a98e1b`, whose one defaults table also drives its command palette), and the decision and its check.

## Portability

Neutral: key matching stays in the shared Venus path; native key capture at the host boundary is unchanged.

## Verification

- The full affected Rust and Nix surfaces (a shared wire-protocol change, per the AGENTS.md
  Verification table).
- One isolated installed dogfood check that the shortcuts are unchanged.
- Codex review.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop and coordinate if another child (for example the sidebar child) is also bumping EONW, so
  that EONW bumps once.

No order between them is decided, so no ordering dependency is added. Before writing a version number, check runtime/crates/eon-workspace-protocol/src/ for the latest vNN.rs.

title: List the effective keymap with eon keys --json
description:
## Why

The Humans and Agents rule (AGENTS.md) says that everything a person can see about the workspace,
an agent can read from the CLI as data. Today `eon workspace --json` lists only popup keybindings,
so an agent can't learn which key does what or tell a person which key to press. Approved
2026-10-23 (parent epic).

## Scope

In scope:
- `eon keys [--json]`, printing the resolved keymap that the `[keys]` child produces: action ID,
  label, chords, whether it is a default, user-set, or overridden by another action, plus
  reserved chords and popup entries.
- `docs/USAGE.md`.

Out of scope:
- Changing bindings from the CLI.
- Live reload.

## Acceptance

- `eon keys --json` inside an Eon terminal matches what Alt+/ shows for that window, field for
  field.

## Verification

- A focused CLI test.
- One installed check that compares the output with Alt+/.
- Codex review.

## Maintenance Notes

- Under EON-C28, the JSON fields become stable at 1.0. Add them to the 1.0 JSON fixture
  (`eon-igae.11`) if it is still open.

title: Let users set the 16 terminal colors with [terminal] palette
description:
## Why

Eon has no theme. The 16 ANSI colors are one hardcoded string, and users can't change them,
although Orbit already accepts any 16 colors. Approved as "configurable now" on 2026-10-23
(parent epic).

## Evidence

- `eon/crates/eon/src/product.rs:123`: `ansi_palette` default string.
- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/sessions.rs:1191`: the palette is passed to every Orbit as
  `--ansi-palette-v1`.
- ORB-C2 (`orbit/docs/CONTRACTS.md`): Orbit accepts any 16 colors.
- EON-C19 (`docs/CONTRACTS.md:1628`): terminal configuration.

## Scope

In scope:
- `[terminal] palette`, an array of exactly 16 `"#RRGGBB"` strings. Omitting it keeps today's
  default.
- Runtime parsing and validation.
- `docs/CONFIGURATION.md`.
- EON-C19 text: stop for Lucca's approval of the wording.

Out of scope:
- Default foreground, background and cursor colors, which need a new Orbit input (deferred
  chrome-theme bead).
- Venus chrome colors.
- Named themes.

## Acceptance

- A fresh terminal shows the configured colors.
- A malformed palette (wrong count or bad hex) fails the launch with a message naming the key.

## Verification

- A focused Runtime parse test.
- One isolated installed observation (for example, `printf` the 16 colors).
- Codex review.

title: Let users turn the cursor trail off
description:
## Why

The cursor trail can't be turned off. Venus supports no trail, but Eon never asks for it. Motion
that can't be disabled is an accessibility gap. Approved on 2026-10-23 (parent epic).

## Evidence

- `venus/src/launch.rs:148-155`, `:234`: `--cursor-effect-v1 none|tail` is accepted.
- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/supervisor.rs:413-426`: the supervisor never passes it.
- `docs/CONFIGURATION.md` `[terminal]`: `cursor_trail_color` and `cursor_trail_duration` exist,
  but there is no off switch.
- EON-C19 and VEN-C1.

## Scope

In scope:
- A `[terminal] cursor_trail = true|false` key, default `true`. Prefer a boolean over a magic
  color value, so the color and duration keys keep their meaning.
- When it is false, pass `--cursor-effect-v1 none` and leave out `--cursor-trail-color` and `--cursor-trail-duration-v1` (`supervisor.rs:414`, `:422-426`): Venus accepts `none` only without them (`venus/src/launch.rs:222-237`), and the supervisor passes the duration today because the product default is `Some(1.5)` (`eon/crates/eon/src/product.rs:35`, `supervisor.rs:422-426`).
- `docs/CONFIGURATION.md`.
- EON-C19 text, after Lucca approves its wording.

Out of scope:
- A wider reduce-motion setting (deferred bead).

## Acceptance

- With `cursor_trail = false`, a fresh window draws the cursor with no trail.
- The default is unchanged.

## Verification

- A focused Runtime test that the argument is passed.
- One isolated installed observation.
- Codex review.

title: Make copy on select and wheel scroll rows configurable
description:
## Why

Two selection and scroll behaviors are fixed, though users of other terminals differ on both.
Approved on 2026-10-23 (parent epic).

- **Copy on select.** Releasing a selection always writes both the clipboard and the primary
  selection.
- **Wheel scroll.** It is 3 rows per notch, written as a literal in three places.

## Evidence

- Copy on select:
  - `orbit/src/host.rs:1111`: the Orbit effect.
  - `venus/src/application.rs:4880-4896`: the Venus mapping.
  - VEN-C7 (`venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md:477-479`) and ORB-C9 pin it.
- Wheel scroll, 3 rows in three places:
  - `venus/src/application/scroll.rs:45`: terminal scroll.
  - `venus/src/application.rs:2279-2280`: header and tab scroll.
  - `venus/src/application.rs:3853`: dialog scroll.
  - VEN-C7 (`:456`).

## Scope

title: Consume Orbit same-boot management in Eon
description:
## Outcome and contract routing

Implement Eon's consumer half of Orbit ORB-C13 as candidate EON-C15. This is the exact same-boot phase selected by eon-decide-eon-session-durability-qhf; it adds no reboot, logout, machine-loss, remote, or durable-topology promise.

Consumer: one local Eon or EonTerm user on the same boot and login.

Trigger: Eon starts a managed Orbit run, or a prior Eon supervisor disappears after Orbit published Ready and a later Eon targets that exact generation.

Result: Eon supplies one strict logical Session ID and fresh run ID, validates Orbit's complete Ready identity, acquires the sole management lease, and only then publishes the Session or launches Venus. Replacement Eon recovers each exact surviving Orbit without changing its PTY child or terminal state. EonTerm recovers one run. Full Eon projects recovered runs into one deterministic tab in numeric Session order; prior tab membership and focus are not reconstructed. Stop uses only validated leases and sends EONW Stopped only after every run has an ORB-C12-complete tombstone.

Important failures: partial startup, missing or malformed records, stale or replaced objects, wrong UID/mode/type, identity or generation mismatch, Busy, Orbit exit, and transport loss fail within one shared five-second operation. They never authorize PID, signal, pathname, process-name, cgroup, pidfd, or Child fallback after Ready; never launch a duplicate over unresolved live state; and never report clean stop from uncertain state.

Ownership: Eon owns exact generation selection, Session/run creation, a per-generation scan bounded by its existing MAX_PANES product limit, recovered-workspace projection, lease collection, deadline, EONW response ordering, the Eon-to-Venus control stream, and Eon-owned cleanup. Orbit owns ORBM/ORBR values, live identity, lease, PTY and terminal state, wait outcome, ORB-C12 cleanup, tombstone, and exact endpoint cleanup. Venus remains a transient ORBS client and owns managed presentation loss/retry behavior.

## Exact prerequisites

- User-approved same-boot decisions: eon-decide-eon-session-durability-qhf comment 511 and Orbit orb-define-orbit-session-management-contract-5p1 comments 611-613.
- Accepted and pushed Orbit source 86aa130629c09dce61d0f232150298656fa5cef4, metadata 68377ed9429e974b96757e48bea702150042689a, ORB-C13, ORB-C12, ORBF v1, and ORBS v4.
- Accepted and pushed Venus source a768e9a1bcb61eac5a21d25b7463c9dc44aa2df8, metadata 602e21ee224ad69e1bcd2959a02f3f66857ed55a, and VEN-C3/VEN-C4/VEN-C14; native owner-loss evidence remains scoped to predecessor 754eb057ea71ddee57b2f543d85d08d66edc953e because the accepted successor changes only the ordered control regression.
- Eon currently pins stale Orbit 6de95296d252c119d4fdba2d9b03cec1a09355ae, stale Venus 5d22b09e323212693a8e54c4c63089784b660cad, and ORBS v3. Refresh the one canonical graph only to the exact accepted compatible pair; changing only Orbit is invalid.
- Reconfirm exact remote accepted revisions and the sole active frontier before claim. Replace the provisional Venus starting identity in this Bead with the prerequisite's accepted identity before implementation.

## Scope boundary

In scope: EON-C15; exact manifest/Nix/lock/protocol substitution; canonical orbit-protocol consumption; Eon launch, strict ID handling, bounded discovery, lease acquisition, recovery projection, status/tombstone reconciliation, owner-routed Stop, stream-based Venus supervision, strong focused tests, current docs/LOC/changelog, package/profile refresh, and isolated installed dogfood.

Out of scope: Orbit or Venus source changes inside this issue; ORBM/ORBR/ORBS/ORBF/EONW vocabulary changes; prior topology restoration; persistent launch intent; logout/reboot recovery; cloud/sync/remote; service manager, broker, helper, async runtime, process scan, raw-signal fallback, compatibility adapter, or old-generation backport.

## Acceptance Criteria

The canonical completion criteria are stored in this Bead's acceptance_criteria field.

## Reference and dependency gates

Before code, reread complete EON-C10/EON-C11/EON-C15 and ORB-C12/ORB-C13 boundaries; current launch, startup lock, generation, workspace, control-response, Venus, and Stop owners; Orbit's management codec/artifact rules; the accepted Venus prerequisite; and the recovery route in docs/REFERENCES.md. Reuse the exact Orbit owner reference record where its question and revisions still match.

Consume orbit-protocol from exact Orbit source 86aa1306, with Nix substituting that same pinned source path. Reuse existing eon-workspace-protocol MAX_PANES and the existing request_id entropy source. Add no copied codec, serializer, UUID/random crate, helper, async runtime, or second composition graph.

## Minimum vertical slice

1. Index EON-C15 before production code. Refresh the canonical graph to Orbit 86aa1306, ORBS v4, and the exact accepted Venus successor from ven-release-supervised-venus-on-owner-loss-np8; keep source, metadata, consumer, and runtime-generation identities distinct.
2. Accept only strict Eon-owned session-N identities. Require canonical positive decimal N without leading zeroes; parse numerically and reject zero, overflow, and duplicate live identities. MAX_PANES bounds live count, not the monotonic numeric ID. Reuse the existing bounded process/time/atomic request_id generator for fresh opaque run IDs. Pass the exact Orbit source revision from the manifest as component generation, never Eon's runtime generation.
3. Launch Orbit with --management-v1 SESSION_ID RUN_ID COMPONENT_GENERATION and no parent-death coupling. Derive .management and .record only from the existing presentation endpoint. Wait for owner-authored Ready and complete Acquire within the existing five-second startup budget before workspace publication or Venus launch.
4. Replace direct-child authority with one managed-session owner containing validated live identity, lease, endpoint, and optional local Child only for pre-Ready rollback and reaping. Child never authorizes attach or stop after Ready.
5. Recover only the selected exact generation. Count record candidates and fail closed if more than MAX_PANES exist; decode at most MAX_PANES. This newly reuses Eon's 256-live-pane workspace ceiling as the per-generation record count bound and is unrelated to MAX_GENERATIONS. Preserve the bound by validating and removing an ended run's tombstone before releasing its workspace slot or admitting a replacement Session; cleanup failure retains unavailable diagnostic state. Reject unsafe objects before decoding, sort valid session-N identities numerically, acquire every live lease under one shared deadline, and release all leases on partial failure. Tombstones reconcile ended runs and grant no authority.
6. EonTerm accepts exactly one live recovered run. Full Eon maps session-N to pane-N in one tab-1, selects the lowest surviving N, sets next_tab to 2 and next_pane with checked max(N)+1. If all MAX_PANES slots are live, the existing capacity owner rejects creation; numeric overflow fails recovery. A post-recovery create must never reuse a tab, pane, or Session identity. No prior grouping, focus, argv, request history, or configuration snapshot is claimed.
7. Concurrent replacements retain the startup-convergence owner: one supervisor acquires all leases; a Busy loser converges on that EONW owner or fails visibly without split ownership, partial publication, or duplicate launch.
8. Replace Eon's UnixDatagram presentation pair with UnixStream. The accepted managed Venus exits on stream EOF; its managed-only Busy retry absorbs the departing-client race. Launch presentation only after all leases are acquired. Venus never becomes a Session lifecycle owner.
9. Stop retains the accepted control stream and request until completion. Send canonical Stop to every validated lease before waiting, then reconcile Stopped or exact tombstones under one deadline. Write EONW Stopped only after all explicit-stop tombstones succeed; otherwise write bounded Failure and preserve diagnostic state. The existing six-second control transport bound contains the shared five-second operation.
10. Before Ready, the exact local Child remains rollback owner. After Ready, Orbit management is the sole Orbit stop path. After Orbit reconciliation, close the Venus control stream and reap the transient local client. Immutable old generations are not relabeled, adopted, signaled, deleted, or backported.

3. Eon consumes canonical orbit-protocol management values and existing request_id/MAX_PANES owners; no copied codec, serializer/identity dependency, helper, async runtime, signal fallback, or public management surface is added.
4. Strict session-N parsing rejects noncanonical, zero, overflow, duplicate, malformed, and unsafe records; more than MAX_PANES live candidates fails closed. Numeric ordering yields tab-1/pane-N, lowest-N selection, next_tab=2, and checked next_pane=max(N)+1 without later identity reuse.
5. New launch publishes no Session or Venus until exact Ready validation and Acquire succeed. Partial startup rolls back only its pre-Ready Child and leaves no Eon-owned residue.
6. Killing Eon after Ready leaves the same Orbit, PTY child, work, and terminal state live. Managed Venus releases its old ORBS attachment; replacement Eon preserves exact Session/run/process/start/endpoint/component identity, acquires every lease, and presents through the accepted replacement Venus within five seconds.
7. Two replacements converge on one complete owner. Busy, wrong identity/generation/UID/mode/type, symlink, replaced endpoint, malformed/oversized/partial record, Orbit exit, and transport pressure fail closed without duplicate launch, split lease, partial workspace, signal, or deletion.
8. EonTerm recovers one run. Full Eon recovers every valid run up to MAX_PANES into the deterministic projection while making no prior-topology/focus/argv/history promise.
9. Natural exit and lost Stop response reconcile through exact tombstones. Tombstones never authorize attach or stop, are removed only by validated Eon cleanup, and must be cleaned before Eon releases that workspace slot; cleanup failure retains unavailable diagnostic state and cannot let record count outrun MAX_PANES.
10. Multi-Session Stop sends all requests before waiting, retains the EONW client until reconciliation, and writes Stopped only after every ORB-C12 result is complete. Any uncertain or failed run yields Failure and no clean-generation deletion.
11. Existing attach/present, workspace mutation, ordinary Session exit, Venus crash/reopen, EonTerm separation, startup convergence, confirmation, generations, old-version, and EONW behavior remain correct except for the intentional stream-supervision change.
12. Focused red/green checks, full locked Rust/Nix surfaces, exact manifest validation, package builds, profile refresh without restarting live supervisors, and one isolated installed dogfood observation pass on x86_64 Linux. Source proof precedes metadata; final records name exact commits, artifacts, deadlines, LOC, and unproved macOS/logout/reboot surfaces.

title: Consume Venus background blur in Eon
description:
## Contract

Consumer: one local Eon or EonTerm user and an approved composition using canonical Eon configuration.

Trigger: Eon creates or reopens a Venus surface while `$EON_CONFIG_HOME/config.toml` contains `[terminal] background_blur = true|false`, or contains no such field.

Result: new EON-C14 accepts one strict boolean, defaults absence to `true`, and when true passes exactly one `--background-blur` before Venus socket endpoints. Explicit false omits the flag. `terminal.background_opacity` remains independent; Eon never changes either value because of the other.

Important failures: invalid configuration names `terminal.background_blur` and creates no initial supervisor, Orbit, or Venus process. Invalid replacement configuration returns the existing bounded presentation failure while preserving Orbit and its child. Unsupported or policy-disabled native blur remains Venus VEN-C15 best effort and does not become an Eon failure.

Ownership: Eon owns the configuration schema, true default, apply timing, launch argument, exact Venus selection, and generation policy. Venus VEN-C15 owns the boolean native request through winit; the compositor owns availability, algorithm, strength, and policy. Orbit remains unaware.

## Prerequisites and exact inputs

- User approval: 2026-08-14 direction to create the Eon contract, advance Venus from `74ab5a0b661210f0afec94086f5358fe50b01f05` to exact accepted source `7fc7e4ba97aaf48b586002934a580ef2d1c31694`, and keep opacity independent; the user then superseded the initial false default with “blur on by default.”
- Consume proved Venus VEN-C15 at source `7fc7e4ba97aaf48b586002934a580ef2d1c31694`.
- Preserve Orbit `6de95296d252c119d4fdba2d9b03cec1a09355ae`, ORBF v1, ORBS v3, EONW v1, and all unrelated component identities and contracts.

## Reference gate

Required before code: current Eon instructions; this complete Bead; EON-C13 configuration, validation, launch/reopen, tests, docs, manifest, and Nix owners; Venus VEN-C15 contract, exact source implementation, CLI validation, tests, dependency identity, license, and COSMIC proof.

Comparison only: EON-C13 as the existing direct terminal-presentation configuration pattern.

Rejected scope: compositor detection, capability negotiation, automatic opacity coupling, blur strength, live reload, watcher, CLI/environment override, profile framework, fallback implementation, Eonova repository changes, Orbit changes, X11/macOS guarantees, new dependency, or another graph.

## Smallest implementation

Extend the existing terminal configuration owner and Venus command builder. Advance the canonical component graph and Nix input/lock to the exact accepted Venus source and record VEN-C15. Update only consuming tests and current-state docs/proof metadata. Add no module, abstraction, adapter, dependency, or compatibility window.

Portability disposition: neutral Eon boolean policy consuming an isolated Venus native-platform dependency. Eon makes no new platform guarantee beyond VEN-C15.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Missing config, absent field, and explicit true include `--background-blur` exactly once; explicit false omits it. The option precedes socket endpoints for decorated, undecorated, workspace, EonTerm, replacement, and legacy launch paths.
2. Wrong-type, duplicate, and unknown terminal fields fail through strict configuration parsing with no initial process effects; replacement failure preserves Orbit and its command.
3. `background_opacity` remains independently serialized at its exact accepted value, including `0.0` with blur true.
4. The canonical graph and Nix lock select exact Venus `7fc7e4ba97aaf48b586002934a580ef2d1c31694`, record VEN-C15, and preserve exact Orbit and unrelated identities.
5. Focused behavior, locked Rust checks, canonical manifest validation, Nix checks/builds, installed profile refresh, isolated COSMIC Wayland observation, README LOC, and diff checks pass.
6. Source proof is committed first; EON-C14 proof metadata and Bead closure cite that exact source revision in a follow-up commit.

## Stop conditions

Stop before adding a dependency, capability protocol, compositor-specific Eon branch, automatic opacity policy, Eonova change, or broader platform promise. Stop if exact Venus VEN-C15 cannot build against the preserved Orbit identity or changes another ownership boundary.

title: Make concurrent supervisor startup converge
description:
## Contract routing

Harden EON-C11 and preserve EON-C12. The consumer is a local launcher; the trigger is two Eon processes starting the same current generation when no live control owner is reachable or an owned stale socket exists; the result is exactly one supervisor and Orbit Session owner while every competing attach-capable launcher converges on that owner. Unsafe or genuinely live endpoints still fail explicitly.

This correction adds no manager daemon, public lock, persisted topology, compatibility window, EONW value, child behavior, or distribution promise.

## Why

`create_control_listener` checks connectability, separately removes an owned socket path, and then binds. Two launchers can both observe absence or refusal before either owns the path; one can then unlink a newly bound peer. The existing concurrent-launch test passed seven stress iterations and failed on iteration eight because one launcher exited unsuccessfully instead of attaching.

Impact: MEDIUM. Effort: M. Implementation risk: MEDIUM. Confidence: HIGH.

## Evidence

- `crates/eon/src/main.rs:1830-1878`: connect, stale-path inspection/removal, bind, and listener identity capture are separate operations with no serialized or owner-bound acquisition.
- `crates/eon/src/main.rs:1811-1827`: `ControlListener::drop` protects a replacement after acquisition but does not protect acquisition itself.
- `crates/eon/tests/workspace_control.rs:570-629`: the accepted real-process test expects two launches to produce one supervisor, one successful attached launcher, and one Orbit start.
- Audit reproduction on exact HEAD `1b8836e616222f29c57ac697916872010db14685`: `for audit_run in $(seq 1 100); do cargo test --locked -p eon --test workspace_control concurrent_launches_converge_and_generation_stop_is_owner_routed --quiet || exit 1; done`; runs 1-7 passed and run 8 failed at line 615. The failed fixture recorded one Orbit launch and a dead mode-0600 `eon.sock` after process cleanup.
- `eon-audit-eon-runtime-lifecycle-wqz` comment 271 preserves the complete evidence and proof limits.

## Prerequisite and reference gate

- No implementation prerequisite. Correct this runtime invariant before `eon-5rp`; the later extraction must preserve it.
- Rebaseline the cited symbols after any intervening revision.
- Reuse the audit reference gate: exact Eon code and EON-C11/EON-C12 own the behavior; Ghosthub `072cc83559bd590ed5d759af05ec0a1868dbf359` is comparison-only for process-owned socket namespaces and dead-owner cleanup.
- Compare the standard-library bind/connect path, the already accepted `libc` dependency, and no new dependency. If advisory locking is considered, inspect the exact Linux and macOS primary semantics, crash release, path safety, and portability before choosing it.
- No new crate is expected. Stop for the dependency gate and user approval before a manifest change.

## Scope

In scope:
- `ControlListener`, `create_control_listener`, stale owned control-socket cleanup, and the minimum runtime helper needed to serialize or identity-bind acquisition.
- The focused concurrent-launch integration check and only the smallest deterministic lower-level check needed to prove the old interleaving.
- EON-C11/EON-C12 current-state proof metadata, `CHANGELOG.md`, and README LOC only as required after acceptance.

Out of scope:
- A long-running manager or lock service, persisted registry, PID file, public lock path, second socket namespace, compatibility window, EONW change, Orbit/Venus change, or broad supervisor abstraction.
- Weakening owned-mode-0600 validation, replacing unsafe non-socket paths, killing inferred processes, retry loops without a bound, or treating a stress test as the sole proof.
- Refactoring managed-environment, workspace, manifest, or Nix composition ownership.

## Implementation notes

1. Make the old stale-observation/removal/bind interleaving reproducible before the fix using the smallest deterministic seam that does not create a production framework.
2. Choose the first sufficient Unix-portable acquisition mechanism that ensures a newly bound live listener cannot be removed by a peer that observed earlier absence or refusal.
3. Validate that the path still names the acquired listener after bind and preserve replacement-safe Drop cleanup.
4. Keep one bounded competing-launch recovery path in `launch_current`; do not add another launcher coordinator.
5. Preserve stale owned-socket recovery and explicit refusal of symlinks, non-sockets, wrong owners, unsafe modes, incompatible supervisors, and wrong launch modes.

## Acceptance

- A deterministic regression exercises the former check/remove/bind interleaving and passes without timing luck.
- Two same-mode current-generation launches yield exactly one reachable mode-0600 control listener, one Orbit Session owner, and one launcher that attaches successfully; neither launcher reports a spurious failure.
- A competing wrong-mode launch still fails explicitly and starts no second Session.
- A dead owned socket is recoverable; a live listener, symlink, non-socket, wrong-owner path, or replacement socket is never removed.
- Listener shutdown removes only its own unchanged path and leaves a replacement intact.
- Crash or failed-start cleanup leaves no permanent acquisition blocker.
- The accepted mechanism works within the Linux alpha and has an explicit macOS proof plan; it depends on no mutable Nix/store identity.
- No new product contract, EONW field, dependency, public configuration, or child change is introduced.

## Verification

- `cargo test --locked -p eon --test workspace_control concurrent_launches_converge_and_generation_stop_is_owner_routed` should exit 0 and prove one reachable owner.
- The new deterministic acquisition regression should exit 0 and prove the exact former interleaving without repeated timing attempts.
- A supplementary bounded stress run should complete at least 100 iterations without one nonzero launcher, second Orbit start, unreachable control path, or leaked fixture.
- `cargo fmt --all --check`
- `cargo check --locked --workspace`
- `cargo test --locked --workspace`
- `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo run --locked -p eon-manifest -- components/eon-alpha-v1.json`
- `nix build --no-link --print-out-paths --no-update-lock-file path:.#default`
- `nix flake check --no-build --no-update-lock-file path:.`
- `git diff --check`
- After the proof-bearing commit, refresh the active `eon` profile without stopping running supervisors; verify the selected artifact and report restart required for existing generations.

## Stop conditions

- Stop if listener ownership or EON-C11/EON-C12 has drifted materially.
- Stop if a correct mechanism requires a new dependency, Linux-only foundation, persistent manager, public lock path, protocol change, or process inference.
- Stop if the proposed deterministic check needs broad production-only hooks or cannot distinguish a live replacement from a stale socket.
- Stop if the same verification failure repeats twice after a reasonable correction.

## Maintenance notes

Prefer one local acquisition invariant over retries and cleanup patches at every caller. The stress reproduction is retained as negative evidence, but the regression must prove the race deterministically. The final `eon-audit-eon-runtime-lifecycle-wqz` pass must rerun it after `eon-5rp`.

Second startup interleaving and corrected owner boundary

title: Show a CPU widget in the Eon Bar
description:
## Decision
Lucca, 2026-10-17: add CPU, GPU and IO widgets to Eon. Lucca, 2026-10-20: CPU, RAM and clock are in
1.0 (`eon-igae`); GPU and IO are 1.x. This bead establishes the shared sampling and chip path that
RAM (`eon-igae.3`) reuses.

Lucca, 2026-10-21: accepted the design below. Venus samples locally, following the clock's
precedent (`b18f2cd`, VEN-C27/EON-C29), instead of Runtime sampling and sending facts over EONW.
Reasons: no EONW revision frozen for all of 1.x under EON-C28, and no complete EONW snapshot every
few seconds. Eon is local-only, so Venus runs on the machine it measures.

## Contract (direction approved 2026-10-21; exact wording needs Lucca's approval before commit)
- IDs: new `EON-C30` (product policy: always on, no configuration) and `VEN-C28` (the chip), the
  same pairing as the clock's EON-C29/VEN-C27.
- Consumer: a full-Eon user on native x86_64 Linux Wayland.
- Result: the Eon Bar shows a read-only `CPU 12%` chip with whole-machine CPU utilization, sampled
  every 2 s while the window is open and redrawn only when the shown whole percentage changes.
  Hover and a static accessible label name CPU, the value and its age.
- Failures: an unreadable or invalid sample shows no chip (never 0%); no chip, gap, hit target or
  accessible node while absent; refreshes do not replace attachments, scroll positions or
  navigation or send an Orbit resize; under width pressure the clock hides first, then CPU/RAM, then
  the quota chips, all before required tabs, controls or drag space (VEN-C21 priority).

## Decisions (Lucca, 2026-10-21)
1. Scope: whole machine, as htop and btop show. No per-Eon attribution (process-tree walks or
   cgroups, which Eon's Linux contracts avoid).
2. EONW: no revision. Venus owns sampling.
3. Cadence: 2 s (btop's default) while a window is open; redraw only on a change of the shown
   value. Measure idle wakeups in the installed check.
4. Source: owned `/proc/stat` delta parsing in one Linux-only Venus module (the platform seam;
   compiled out elsewhere). No `sysinfo`.
5. Visibility: shown by default, no toggle. A later toggle is additive under EON-C28; add one only
   if dogfood shows clutter. If added, Eon owns it and passes it to Venus as a startup input.

## Ownership
Venus owns sampling, chip text, geometry, hover and AccessKit. Runtime and EONW are unchanged. Eon
owns the product policy (always on) in EON-C30. This adds a Venus module, which is product scope
approved by Lucca on 2026-10-21.

## Reference gate (consequential: new Venus platform seam)
Before code record: btop and Waybar's cpu module at exact revisions (sampling, delta math, first
sample, counter wrap); constraints kept and approaches rejected; the chosen source and its check.
Read VEN-C21/C22/C26/C27 and EON-C27/C29 and reuse the existing optional-chip and clock paths rather
than adding a second chip owner or timer.

## Prerequisites
None. RAM (`eon-igae.3`), GPU and IO depend on this one.

## Acceptance
Focused sampler red/green (delta math, first sample, wrap and invalid input never becoming 0%);
Venus chip layout/absence/hiding-order/accessibility test; `nix develop -c eon-test -p
yazelix-venus`; fmt and clippy for Venus; nix build; isolated capture showing the chip, its hover
and narrow-width hiding; measured idle wakeups; review loop; profile refresh.

## Scope boundary
CPU utilization only: no per-core bars, graphs, history, temperatures, frequency, memory, process
list, alerts or click actions. Linux Wayland only; no macOS claim.
close_reason: CPU label shipped (VEN-C28/EON-C30 proven); RAM (eon-igae.3) can build on it

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Lucca, 2026-10-21: approved the exact contract wording for VEN-C28 and EON-C30 as proposed in session eon-62. VEN-C28: read-only 'CPU 12%' monospace label, whole-machine use over the last 2 s from /proc/stat; placed after quota chips and version label, before the clock; appears one interval after the surface opens; hover/AccessKit 'CPU use 12%, all cores, over the last 2 seconds'; spare drag space only, only while every quota chip is at full width. Hiding order: clock, then CPU, then version label, then quota compaction, tabs, controls. Failures: unreadable/malformed/non-advancing sample shows no label (never 0%) and it returns on the next valid sample; CPU-only changes keep attachments, navigation, scrolling and send no resize; no action/focus/drag; no label off Linux. Owner: Scene text and geometry, application 2 s wake, Linux-only Venus /proc/stat module. Boundary: no EONW/runtime change, configuration, per-core, history, graph, dependency or platform expansion. EON-C30: always on, no Eon configuration; on/off needs its own decision. Hover drops the sample age (a sample is never older than 2 s). VEN-C27 wording: the clock follows 'the quota chips, version label and CPU label'.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Portability disposition (eon-62): isolated Linux dependency. Only CpuTimes::read touches /proc/stat, behind cfg(target_os = "linux"); elsewhere it returns None and the label never shows. The parser, scene and accessibility code are platform-neutral, and the 2 s wake still runs off Linux, reading nothing (cheaper than a cfg seam in the application loop). This replaces decision 4's 'compiled out elsewhere': only the read is.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Reference gate (eon-62, 2026-10-21). Read at exact revisions: btop v1.4.7 6e39144aaf5a6bc01b9f795010b0914431067183 (Apache-2.0, src/linux/btop_collect.cpp:1094-1158); Waybar 0.15.0 90b209add8937514d0a987aa842e701bd8f1232e (MIT, src/modules/cpu_usage/linux.cpp, common.cpp); Linux v7.3 c03c1a14507dfaf8b856c2608f9ac216021fc222 (Documentation/filesystems/proc.rst:1574-1620, kernel/sched/cputime.c:147-162, fs/proc/stat.c:64). Kept: btop's formula (idle = idle + iowait; total = first eight fields, so steal is busy and guest, already in user/nice, is not counted twice); aggregate line only (covers every possible CPU, so hotplug-stable); 2 s cadence (btop default); integer rounding. Rejected: Waybar's sum of all ten fields (double-counts guest), its 32-bit accumulator and unclamped casts; btop's clamping of a backwards counter into a false 0%/100%; both projects' since-boot or 100 ms first value (Venus shows nothing until a second reading). Decision: owned parser in venus/src/cpu.rs, no dependency. Check: cpu_use_counts_iowait_idle_and_guest_once and cpu_use_rejects_bad_readings_instead_of_showing_zero (red against a ten-field total). Recorded in venus/docs/REFERENCES.md.

title: Make the Nix alpha installable without repository credentials
description:
## Why

The proved Nix alpha cannot be tried by the public because its locked Orbit and Venus inputs require GitHub credentials. Public alpha needs one credential-free path to the same exact component graph; it does not need a second installer or bundle.

Contract: an unauthenticated user clones Eon, resolves the locked flake, builds or installs `.#default`, and obtains the exact reviewed Eon, Orbit, and Venus revisions. Missing or private inputs fail before release, and making source public never exposes secrets or content the user has not approved.

## Evidence

- Baseline `18f1874`: `README.md:93-103` says the alpha uses private Eon child inputs and requires GitHub credentials.
- `README.md:40-44` identifies the canonical Eon, Eon Desktop, and Eon Sessions repositories.
- `docs/DISTRIBUTION.md:35-45` requires one versioned component manifest, opaque Nix launch inputs, and no direct installer or package matrix during alpha.
- `docs/DISTRIBUTION.md:203-215` defines the Nix alpha candidate around exact manifest identity, isolated install, clean native Wayland behavior, lifecycle checks, and closure inspection.
- `flake.lock`, `flake.nix`, and `components/eon-alpha-v3.json` own the exact source and compatibility graph.

Impact: CRITICAL public-alpha access blocker. Effort: M. Risk: HIGH because repository visibility and full history are external user-owned state. Confidence: HIGH.

## Scope

In scope:
- Make the exact Eon, Eon Sessions, and Eon Desktop source revisions needed by the locked Nix graph readable without credentials.
- Audit each repository full reachable history, current issues/releases as relevant, licenses, submodules, LFS objects, CI references, and dependency URLs for secrets or private material before visibility changes.
- Refresh only exact source identities and public installation wording needed to prove the credential-free graph.
- Record the user approval and exact repositories/revisions immediately before any visibility change.

Out of scope:
- Direct bundles, Home Manager, signing, notarization, release automation, mirrors, vendored child source, a second component graph, macOS distribution, or publishing unrelated Yazelix repositories.
- Rewriting published history, removing security checks, or making any repository public by implication.
- Product behavior changes.

## Implementation Notes

1. Reconcile `flake.lock`, `flake.nix`, the component manifest, and each accepted child proof revision.
2. Perform and record a full-history secret/private-content/license review without reproducing secret values in Beads or logs.
3. Present the exact visibility changes and residual findings to the user. Stop until the user explicitly approves changing each repository visibility.
4. Prefer public read access to the canonical repositories. If a repository cannot be public, stop and create a separately approved distribution decision; do not add source mirrors or archives here.
5. After approval, change only the named visibility surfaces, then test from an unauthenticated clean environment and update the installation claim.

## Verification

- In an environment with no GitHub credentials, `git clone https://github.com/Yazelix/eon.git` succeeds and the checked-out release candidate resolves every locked input.
- From that clean clone, `nix build .#default` exits 0 and `./result/bin/eon versions` reports the exact manifest identities without a Nix store path.
- `cargo run --locked -p eon-manifest -- components/eon-alpha-v3.json` exits 0 for the published graph.
- The recorded full-history review finds no unremediated credential, private material, inaccessible submodule/LFS object, or license blocker in any repository made public.
- `git diff --check` exits 0 and README installation/support text plus the LOC scorecard match the public state.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop before changing repository visibility without fresh explicit user approval naming every target.
- Stop and report only credential type and location if a secret or private artifact is found; rotate or remediate under separately authorized scope before publication.
- Stop if credential-free access would require a mirror, copied child implementation, second manifest, history rewrite, or new distribution channel.
- Stop if any exact accepted revision differs from the locked graph; reconcile proof identity before publication.

## Maintenance Notes

The simplest accepted shape is public read access to the canonical three repositories. Alpha remains Nix-only. This issue owns source availability, not the public-alpha acceptance decision or later direct distribution.
close_reason: Public canonical sources and credential-free locked Nix install proved

title: Select the next and previous tab with Ctrl+Tab and Ctrl+Shift+Tab
description:
## Why

Eon has no single key that moves one tab over. Alt+H/L walk columns first and only then spill into the next tab, which is slow in a tab with four columns. Alt+1…0 needs the tab's position. Browsers, VS Code, kitty, WezTerm and Windows Terminal all use Ctrl+Tab for this. Today Ctrl+Tab is unbound and reaches the terminal; in legacy encoding it arrives as a plain Tab, so few programs rely on it.

## Decision (Lucca, 2026-10-23, to the overseer eon-a8)

The overseer proposed: (1) Ctrl+Tab and Ctrl+Shift+Tab select the next and previous tab, wrapping around; (2) in tab order, not most-recently-used. Lucca: "ok, i accept you idea for tabs / indeed. if the tab has 4 columns, it can be expensive to go through each of them". F6 is unchanged: it cycles focus regions, which is a different job.

## Contract

Amend the Venus contract that owns fixed workspace shortcuts and tab selection (find it: likely VEN-C8 Eon workspace presentation, with the shortcut viewer VEN-C20 and hints VEN-C24), plus any EON-C text that lists the fixed shortcuts. Consumer: a user with several tabs. Trigger: Ctrl+Tab / Ctrl+Shift+Tab with terminal or chrome focus. Result: the next or previous tab is selected, wrapping from last to first; selection works as Alt+1…0 does (pane, popup and focus behavior unchanged). With one tab, nothing happens and nothing reaches the terminal. Behavior while the shortcut viewer, a picker or a popup is shown follows the existing Alt+1…0 rule.

## Scope

In scope: a `FIXED_SHORTCUTS` entry in `venus/src/application/shortcuts.rs` reusing the existing tab-selection action (no new EONW request unless the reference gate shows one is needed); shortcut viewer and hints listing; docs/USAGE.md shortcut table, venus/docs/INTERACTION.md, CHANGELOG. Check that a configured popup key cannot take Ctrl+Tab silently.

Out of scope: MRU order, workspace switching (EON-C33 owns Alt+Shift+S), F6, macOS bindings.

## Prerequisites

Lands after the agent sidebar chain (eon-agent-sidebar-yx8.13, yx8.8), which edits the same shortcuts file. Contract text is approved under Lucca's 2026-10-23 approvals while the overseer runs. Record the exact text as relayed.

## Acceptance

- A Venus test: Ctrl+Tab and Ctrl+Shift+Tab select next and previous with wrap, and a single tab is a no-op with no terminal input.
- One installed dogfood observation in isolated Sway with three tabs.

## Verification

`nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-venus`, Venus fmt and clippy, converge plus Codex, and one isolated installed observation.

Portability disposition: neutral (Linux binding; macOS out of scope).

title: Keep the cursor color across eon attach
description:
## Defect
After `eon attach`, every terminal's cursor draws red instead of its color before detach (blue in the default theme), in single- and multi-column tabs alike. Typing still works and the window is focused. Seen in the `eon-splits-opwv` slice 4 isolated dogfood (2026-10-17) on installed /nix/store/86755wd8yc9b63j6lwvic6grpslyg6kk-eon-0.1.1 and on 4wm3a2j2…-eon-0.1.1, private headless Sway 1.12 (pixman), Nushell prompt. Not caused by the splits work: no splits commit touches cursor color.

## Contract
A reattached presentation shows each terminal's cursor in the same color it had before detach (ORB-C6 rich presentation fidelity; VEN-C1 authoritative presentation). Venus draws `frame.colors.cursor`, falling back to the foreground (venus/src/scene.rs, `Color::from(frame.colors.cursor.unwrap_or(frame.colors.foreground))`), so the first suspect is the cursor color Orbit authors in the fresh attachment frame. The owner is decided by the first finding: Orbit if its attach frame carries the wrong color, Venus if it maps a correct color wrongly.

## Prerequisites
None. Reproduce first: launch Eon in an isolated session, note the cursor color, close the window, run `eon attach`, compare. Check whether a build from before `eon-splits-opwv` (for example 0f8462b) reproduces it, and whether the shell or Starship sets OSC 12.

## Acceptance
- A recorded red/green reproduction naming the owning component and mechanism.
- After the fix, the cursor color before detach equals the color after `eon attach` in installed isolated dogfood, and the owner's existing harness covers the regression where one exists.

## Scope boundary
Cursor color across reattach only. No cursor shape, blink, trail, or theme changes. An `orbit-protocol` change needs its own compatibility classification and user decision.
close_reason: Venus seeds an omitted or random cursor preset from the attached endpoint's identity, so reattaching to one live supervisor keeps the color; a new supervisor picks afresh. Not an Orbit defect. Proof, dogfood and 2-pass ledger in comments. Residual: EonTerm's first window predates its Orbit socket and uses the fallback pick (documented in EON-C1/CONFIGURATION).

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Root cause found; stopped before a contract change (worktree agent, 2026-10-17). Not Orbit and not ORB-C6: the attach frame carries no explicit cursor color, so Venus draws the cursor body in its cursor-trail color (render/cursor_trail.rs: explicit_color false -> trail_color). With [terminal] cursor_trail_color omitted, Eon passes no --cursor-trail-color (runtime supervisor.rs venus_command), and each Venus process picks a fresh random preset (venus/src/launch.rs random_cursor_color, RandomState per process). eon attach only asks the supervisor to Present, which launches a new Venus, so every reattach rerolls the color for all terminals in the window. This is today's contracted behavior: VEN-C1 says an omitted choice 'selects one of eight Venus presets once per launch and uses it for that process'; EON-C1 says 'Omission emits no override; Venus chooses one random preset per surface' on new or reopened surfaces; docs/CONFIGURATION.md matches. Red, reproduced on edge c6e1f7d, installed /nix/store/scq38y49ba6i1in59mf48k46h17cff2y-eon-0.1.1, private headless Sway 1.12 (pixman, 1280x720), isolated HOME and XDG_RUNTIME_DIR under one mktemp root (cleaned), grim captures, Venus argv read from /proc, no config: cursor pixels launch (61,85,196) = ocean, attach1 (129,84,196) = nebula, attach2 nebula, attach3 ocean (presets at the surface's ~0.77 alpha); all four Venus argv identical, without --cursor-trail-color. Control, same build, cursor_trail_color = 'preset:ice': launch, attach1 and attach2 each show one 128-px cursor block of (94,168,196) = ice. The two red observations in eon-splits-opwv were magma (#ff3b30) rolled by chance. Keeping the color across attach therefore needs a VEN-C1 and EON-C1 change (user decision). No code changed, no commit.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Decision, Lucca 2026-10-17 (delegated: 'i will trust your judgement'): option (a). Venus seeds its omitted or 'random' cursor preset from the identity of the endpoint it attaches to (device, inode and ctime of the supervisor's eon.sock, or the Orbit socket for EonTerm), so every Venus launch against one live supervisor keeps one preset and a new supervisor picks afresh. VEN-C1 'once per launch' becomes 'once per live endpoint'; EON-C1 and docs/CONFIGURATION.md follow. Rejected: (b) Eon picks per generation (second owner of Venus's preset list); (c) close as not a defect (a color change on reattach reads as a defect). Accepted consequence: all windows of one generation share the preset.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Reference gate (contract change VEN-C1, EON-C1; approved above). Behavior: an omitted or random cursor-tail color stays the same for every Venus launch against one live endpoint, so eon attach keeps it; a recreated endpoint picks afresh. Owner: Venus launch parsing (venus/src/launch.rs) alone owns the preset list and the pick; Eon still forwards only explicit config; Orbit keeps cursor authority. Routes read: venus/docs/REFERENCES.md 'Required for native cursor-tail materialization' (Rio e019a93 is evidence for motion only; no comparable random-per-session color found to adopt); runtime supervisor.rs launch order. Kept: standard-library cosmetic entropy, no new flag, dependency, protocol or Eon code. Mechanism: std DefaultHasher over (dev, ino, ctime, ctime_nsec) of the endpoint socket; a missing socket falls back to RandomState per process. Rejected: seeding from the socket path (generation ids repeat per build, so the color would be fixed per install); from the generation directory (it outlives supervisors); Eon resolving a preset (second owner of the preset list); a renderer colour update after attach (render.rs, out of scope). Constraint found: EonTerm's supervisor admits Venus before start_orbit binds orbit.sock, so EonTerm's first window uses the per-process fallback and later reopens share one preset; full Eon binds eon.sock before Venus, so it is fully covered. Portability: neutral (std::os::unix MetadataExt on Linux and Darwin). Check: random_cursor_preset_is_stable_per_live_endpoint (red on c6e1f7d: solar then forest against one socket) plus isolated installed dogfood of launch and two attaches.
