title: Investigate showing the cursor tail in the pane being left on a focus change
description:
## Question (Lucca, 2026-10-20)
When focus moves to another pane, the cursor tail is visible only inside the incoming pane. Lucca
wants it to show in the pane being left too, so the trail visibly starts at the old cursor and
travels into the new pane. This bead decides whether that is reasonably doable; it does not ship it.

## Today
Venus draws the tail in `Renderer` cursor drawing (venus/src/render.rs, the block that calls
`build_tail_cursor`): `rectangles.clip` is `workspace.visible_terminal()`, the selected pane's
terminal intersected with the pane viewport (venus/src/scene.rs). The trail's corners start at the
previous cursor rectangle (venus/src/render/cursor_trail.rs `start_jump`), so every part outside
the incoming pane is clipped away, including all of the old pane.

## What to find out
- Which switches leave the old pane on screen: column to column (yes), up/down in a stack (the old
pane collapses to a header), tab switches and tab-crossing traversal (old pane gone). The change
only means anything for the first case, and possibly the header case.
- Clip candidates: the union of the old and new pane terminals, the bounding box of both, or the
whole pane viewport. Check what each lets the trail cross: card gaps, headers, a third column
between them, the scrollback pill, popups (a popup-covered tab has no trail target today).
- Whether `RectangleBatch` supports more than one clip rectangle or a non-rectangular clip, or
whether the trail must be drawn in two passes.
- Where the old pane's rectangle comes from at the frame of the switch (the previous scene's
selected terminal) and what happens when the layout also changes in that frame (sideways move,
column created or removed, resize).
- Whether the old pane's last frame still shows its cursor, so the trail does not appear to leave
from a place without one.

## Contract
VEN-C1 ("A bounded four-corner trail approaches Orbit's exact cursor destination"; healthy pane
switches keep window-local cosmetic motion). Shipping the change would need a VEN-C1 text change
and Lucca's approval; this investigation does not.

## Acceptance
A comment on this bead with: the cases where it applies, the chosen clip shape with its trade-offs,
rough size (files, new state), the risks, and a recommendation (do it, do a narrower version, or
drop it). If doable, a follow-up implementation bead with its contract change for approval. A
throwaway prototype is allowed in a scratch branch or worktree, not on edge.

## Scope boundary
Investigation only. No change to the trail's shape, colours, duration, reset rules, or Orbit.
Portability: neutral (Venus rendering).

title: Roll synchronized welcome rendering into Eonova
description:
## Contract routing

Preserve the synchronized welcome rollout for EON-C1, EON-C3, EON-C4, and EON-C12, and harden EON-C11 presentation semantics with a Venus-owned native activation contract.

Consumer: a newly installed Eonova generation launched through the packaged desktop entry, including when that exact generation already owns a live Venus surface.

Trigger: initial desktop launch renders the enabled Anima welcome through Orbit; a repeated launch sends EONW Present to the live supervisor.

Result: synchronized Anima frames present atomically and enter Zellij normally. If the Venus surface already exists, Eon preserves that exact process and sends one bounded private presentation signal; Venus requests native presentation of the window.

Important failures: child mismatch, startup failure, terminal disappearance, missing or saturated presentation control, and unsupported native activation remain explicit or platform-bounded. Profile refresh must not restart existing generations.

## Accepted identities and evidence

Orbit 26b4b9465b3f0e74f091a0aae93fddc61412b893; Nova 9ef7f6530bac3b4296adbaa7b50eaef3c1716cf1; Anima 7ef0ec33378874bdf95b2f8fa156d5fb641017ac; Eon presentation 9942aa87e56da022bbcf9ae0e32b0ce5b640505d; Eonova presentation d014332c069d494a0c6d99a2709ac88640b71f4b. Native COSMIC Wayland acceptance confirmed no bottom flicker, no cell gaps, and correct vivid palette. The repeated desktop launch preserved exact processes; the accepted Venus revision uses the locked xdg activation path.

## Steps to Reproduce

Launch Eonova from its packaged desktop entry. While that exact generation remains live, focus another application and launch Eonova again; inspect the retained process, native presentation request, and synchronized welcome rendering.

## Completed scope

1. Defined the narrow repeated-launch activation contract in Eon and Eon Desktop.
2. Reused EONW Present and the existing Venus child; added only a bounded private process signal and winit native activation.
3. Proved the same Venus process survives a repeated launch and receives one presentation request.
4. Built and pinned the accepted Venus revision in Eon, advanced Eon in Eonova, refreshed profiles without restarting live supervisors, and dogfooded the installed desktop entry on COSMIC Wayland.
5. Updated proof metadata, changelogs, and README LOC scorecards.

Out of scope: new EONW wire values, additional windows, replacing the live Venus process, D-Bus application infrastructure, compositor-specific commands, dependencies, other platform promises, renderer changes, animation redesign, and unrelated input upgrades.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Existing synchronized-welcome checks and accepted native observations remain valid.
- Repeated Eon or EonTerm launch with a live surface keeps its PID and Session, sends exactly one bounded presentation signal, and requests native presentation through winit.
- A closed or saturated signal channel fails without blocking the supervisor or replacing the surface.
- Installed Eonova desktop launch preserves its existing surface process and requests native presentation on COSMIC Wayland; compositor acceptance is not guaranteed.
- Full locked Rust and Nix checks pass for changed repositories; exact component pins, packages, profiles, contracts, changelogs, and LOC remain aligned.

## Stop conditions

Stop if native winit activation fails on COSMIC Wayland, if the change requires an EONW schema revision or a new dependency, if another agent owns an overlapping surface, or if profile refresh would disturb a live generation.
close_reason: Fresh-eyes wording now distinguishes the native presentation request from compositor outcome and uses one concise presentation concept throughout.

title: Keep glyph ink that falls inside a partly scrolled pane fill
description:
## Why

Found by the overseer's narrow Codex re-check of eon-54jv (632052c7 -> 0f776f0b, 2026-10-24): during
header scrolling, Glyphon admits or rejects a whole text run by its line box, not by its ink, so a
glyph whose ink extends below its line box (a combining mark below, such as `g\u0323` in DejaVu Sans
Mono) can vanish while its ink would fall inside the visible fill. Case: the 80-pane, hints-visible
fixture at scale 1.25 and header scroll 1050 puts the cell at y=40 and text at y=38 with the fill top
at y=62; Glyphon computes the run's end as 38 + 23 = 61 and rejects it, although the dot's ink lands
on row 62 (venus/src/render.rs:1147 at that candidate).

The overseer judged this a pre-existing class, not an eon-54jv regression: any clip top that cuts
through a line's box has it, and 54jv only moved the clip top to the column's top edge. eon-54jv
landed without it.

## Goal

Text that is partly inside the visible fill keeps every pixel of ink inside the fill, at any scale and
header scroll, including marks outside the line box; ink outside the fill still never paints.

## Acceptance

- Confirm first whether the base before eon-54jv (4b3be05) shows the same loss at an equivalent clip
  offset (expected yes); record the result.
- A populated regression through Glyphon preparation for the case above, failing first.
- No change to the single rectangular text clip design (eon-54jv's decision: no text bands).

Portability: neutral.

title: Decide Eon durability across supervisor, reboot, and machine loss
description:
## Problem

Eon currently has three different durability stories that must not be collapsed into one promise:

- Venus loss is covered: while Orbit remains running, the exact PTY process and authoritative terminal state survive and Venus can reattach.
- Eon supervisor loss is not covered: at Eon f036f798855668b53fa7e099fcb938ba6f0ffe2f, crates/eon/src/main.rs keeps every Orbit process as a std::process::Child and keeps Workspace only in memory. Normal generation stop terminates those children. An abrupt supervisor loss may leave a process and socket behind, but a replacement Eon has no accepted identity, liveness, exit-status, or stop/adoption contract for it.
- Machine restart is explicitly outside EON-C8, EON-C10, EON-C11, and ORB-C1. Arbitrary Unix process state is gone after reboot; a durable record can only reconstruct a replacement unless a separately selected checkpoint or remote-compute substrate owns stronger behavior.

The user-facing term durable therefore needs an explicit failure-domain matrix before choosing a local database, cloud sync, daemon, protocol, or provider.

## Evidence

Repository evidence:

- docs/CONTRACTS.md and README.md state that Eon topology is live-only and machine restart preserves no undeclared process or layout state.
- Eon f036f798855668b53fa7e099fcb938ba6f0ffe2f owns runtime generations, child observation, stop, and in-memory topology.
- Orbit e60554623d2ad1e238fac84d0f8f49be0e81e522 owns the real PTY and sole libghostty state, installs shutdown handlers, and kills/reaps the PTY process group when Orbit exits.
- Venus VEN-C3 already solves transient presentation loss and same-endpoint reconnect. No Venus persistence work is needed for this decision.
- eon-pxn.4 intentionally excluded manager daemons, durable topology storage, PTY handoff, and machine-restart recovery. eon-pxn leaves durable restoration and remote machines separately decidable.

Primary and pinned comparison evidence:

- tmux master 851c5a933d4838c32ad06c248b2ba975d106149c and its official wiki: a background server owns programs; disconnect survival ends if the server is killed or crashes. https://github.com/tmux/tmux/wiki/Getting-Started and https://github.com/tmux/tmux/wiki/FAQ
- zmx 0.7 checkout 4f3739ef98f44d0b639afa57fd76bffcad5d0ef4, shpool 901e18c3ced010073178b78c0ca2a8cdd43e8581, and abduco 8c32909a159aaa9484c82b71f05b7a73321eb491: long-lived session servers own PTYs; per-session servers isolate failure, while shpool delegates daemon lifetime to systemd or launchd.
- Power Failure Resumer 318d24fbab1b5c0ab1242ee19892419b034faa0e: reboot recovery uses durable provider transcripts and resume IDs to discover, preview, explicitly reopen, and verify new processes; it does not resurrect the dead process. https://github.com/Dicklesworthstone/power_failure_resumer
- FrankenTerm a19d072439b9ee26f934dd49733c6879abfc8610 reconstructs mux topology and optionally replays best-effort scrollback into new panes. This is recipe restoration, not process survival.
- Atuin 18.17 sync and the current record-store docs: local history is a derived SQLite view over encrypted append-only records; optional end-to-end encrypted sync exchanges records and requires the key on another machine. This is a credible metadata-sync pattern, not a terminal or process checkpoint. https://docs.atuin.sh/18.17/reference/sync/ and https://docs.atuin.sh/main/reference/store/
- Amp Orbs documentation observed 2026-08-12: execution continues on a remote machine, clients reconnect from web or terminal, and setup/resume hooks reconstruct services around an orb. Its continuity comes from moving compute off the laptop, not synchronizing local process memory. https://ampcode.com/manual and https://ampcode.com/manual/orbs
- systemd 40315add9176d2a7c28d8d90490f74e9e982e87b and official loginctl documentation: a user manager can own long-running services and cgroups; lingering can keep it alive after logout and start it at boot. This is a Linux platform mechanism, not a portable Eon product contract. https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/40315add9176d2a7c28d8d90490f74e9e982e87b/man/systemd.service.xml and https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/252/loginctl.html
- CRIU criu-dev f4142635867ebc10b6f72d3ec4911e0dd67cb12c supports Linux PTY checkpointing, but external resources, files, devices, sockets, namespaces, privileges, and version/kernel compatibility can prevent dump or restore. It is not a credible default for arbitrary developer sessions. https://criu.org/What_cannot_be_checkpointed and https://criu.org/Advanced_usage

## Smallest observable decision

Consumer: one local Eon user.

Triggers to classify independently:

1. Venus closes or crashes.
2. the Eon supervisor exits or crashes while the host and Orbit process remain alive.
3. the user logs out or the machine reboots.
4. the machine is unavailable, lost, or destroyed.

For each trigger, decide whether Eon promises exact continued process, explicit reconstruction of a replacement, metadata availability only, or no recovery. Name important failures, one source-of-truth owner, retention and deletion behavior, and whether secrets or terminal content ever enter durable storage.

## Proposed scope

Decision and research only. Compare the options below, select the smallest justified durability tier and sequence, and route any chosen implementation to repository-owned child Beads only after the required EON, ORB, or remote-target contracts are approved.

Out of scope: runtime or contract-index edits; an implementation dependency; a cloud account; an encryption format; protocol compatibility; automatic unknown-process adoption; remote transport; CRIU integration; and claims that replayed text or a restarted command is the original process.
design:
## Options to decide

### Option 0 — keep the current contract

Promise exact continuity only across Venus loss while Orbit and the Eon supervisor remain alive. Improve wording, but persist nothing. This is cheapest and honest, but leaves supervisor crash and reboot as manual recovery.

### Option 1 — phased local durability (recommended product sequence)

1. Same boot: make the session owner independent of transient Eon presentation/control loss, so a replacement Eon can validate and reconnect to the exact still-running Orbit process.
2. Reboot: persist only minimum Eon-owned launch intent and topology needed to preview and explicitly reconstruct replacement Sessions. New Session and process identities must link to, but never impersonate, the prior run.
3. Sync: only after the local schema and deletion model prove useful, optionally encode non-secret records as an Atuin-like encrypted append-only store. Treat terminal frames, raw scrollback, arbitrary environment, credentials, socket paths, PIDs, and process memory as excluded by default.
4. Remote: keep remote execution independent. It earns exact laptop-loss continuity only because the process runs on another machine.

This sequence produces value before a cloud service and keeps stronger claims falsifiable.

### Option 2 — Linux service-manager-first exact same-boot ownership

Run each durable session, or one session host, under the systemd user manager and use stable service identity plus owner-authored status/stop. It reuses a mature native supervisor and can survive logout with explicit linger policy. Costs: Linux/systemd coupling, user-manager and runtime-directory semantics, packaging/policy work, and a required macOS replacement seam. It is a mechanism candidate for the Orbit decision, not the Eon durability contract itself.

### Option 3 — Eon-owned portable session broker

Introduce one long-lived broker that remains the parent and lifecycle authority for Orbit processes while Eon CLI/supervisor and Venus are clients. It gives clean child exit and stop ownership and a portable conceptual seam. Costs: a new daemon/binary, shared failure domain, upgrade and recovery semantics, a second Eon process protocol, and more code than current evidence may justify.

### Option 4 — self-owned per-session Orbit service

Let each Orbit server detach safely from its launcher and expose a narrow authenticated local management identity/status/stop boundary in addition to the one presentation attachment. This isolates session failures and resembles zmx or abduco. Costs: Orbit contract expansion, launch/stdio/signal cleanup, safe identity and stale-socket handling, non-parent exit observation, and Eon reconciliation. Orbit must remain PTY and terminal authority; Eon remains product identity and topology owner.

### Option 5 — checkpoint arbitrary processes with CRIU

Reject for the initial product. It is Linux-specific, privilege and environment sensitive, and cannot guarantee arbitrary external resources. Reconsider only for one controlled workload after reconstruction or remote compute is measurably insufficient.

### Option 6 — Amp-Orbs-like remote execution target

Run the workspace on an existing SSH host or later managed provider, then reconnect clients. This is the only straightforward way to preserve the exact process when the laptop disappears. Route target identity, provisioning, repository sync, secrets, billing, sleep/wake, and deletion through eon-az9; route ordinary terminal fallback through orb-permanent-ssh-terminal-access-hd6. Do not call encrypted metadata sync remote process continuity.

## Expected recommendation record

Record a table with rows for the four failure triggers and columns for exactness, owner, durable data, security boundary, cleanup, Linux/macOS disposition, user action, proof, dependency footprint, and reversal cost. Name the evidence that would justify moving from local reconstruction to encrypted sync or remote compute.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The decision states four separate guarantees for Venus loss, Eon supervisor loss, reboot/logout, and machine loss; no guarantee uses durable without naming its failure domain.
2. Exact process continuation, terminal-state reconstruction, command/topology reconstruction, provider-thread resume, metadata backup, and remote execution are distinct outcomes.
3. The comparison covers no change, phased local durability, systemd user services, a portable broker, self-owned per-session Orbit services, CRIU, encrypted record sync, and remote compute without treating all as equally viable.
4. A proposed local durable record names the minimum fields, stable logical identity and run identity, atomicity and corruption behavior, versioning, bounds, retention, deletion, permissions, and explicit exclusions. Socket paths, PIDs, resolved package paths, raw environment, credentials, terminal frames, scrollback, and process memory are not persisted by default.
5. The threat model covers local account compromise, synced-server compromise, key loss, accidental secret capture, rollback/replay, stale records, and deletion across devices before any sync contract is proposed.
6. The selected owner order preserves Orbit PTY/terminal authority, Eon product identity/topology/recovery policy, and Venus transience. Separate implementation Beads use one code-owning repository and owner implementation before consumer and acceptance.
7. Any same-boot implementation is gated by the Orbit mechanism decision referenced from this Bead. Any remote-compute implementation is gated by eon-az9. Ordinary SSH access remains related but not a substitute for host-loss continuity.
8. The final decision names the first cheapest proof and a stop/reversal condition. At minimum, process-continuity proof kills the controlling Eon process while useful terminal work continues; reconstruction proof reboots or uses an isolated fresh runtime and proves new identities plus partial-failure reporting.
9. The user explicitly selects keep current behavior, phased local durability, remote-first durability, or defer. Closure creates no implementation or product contract by itself.
notes:
Planning-only batch authorized by the user on 2026-08-12. This Bead changes no EON-C, ORB-C, or VEN-C contract and claims no implementation.

Priority P1 because the word durable is central to product trust, but status remains deferred behind the current eon-pxn frontier unless the user explicitly reprioritizes it. Recommended starting point is Option 1: exact same-boot continuity first, explicit reboot reconstruction second, optional encrypted sync third, and remote compute as an independent product tier.

Affected areas if later selected: Eon runtime/lifecycle and workspace state; EONW only if a proven control gap exists; Orbit lifecycle/management boundary; Nix and platform service integration; security and data policy; cross-repository acceptance. Venus should require no persistence owner.

Blocked by: eon-pxn completion or explicit user reprioritization. Blocking after selection: any local durability implementation batch. Related: eon-pxn.4, eon-az9, orb-permanent-ssh-terminal-access-hd6, and the Orbit same-boot mechanism decision created in the same planning batch.

Unpeel comparison — 2026-08-15:
- Exact primary source: Unpeel 0.2.0 revision 9580a83f009fe19775116cacb46e74570958ca56 (MIT), including docs/plans/host-controller-transports.md, crates/unpeel-core/src/session_host.rs, crates/unpeel-core/src/terminal_viewport.rs, and apps/native/unpeel-attach/src/main.rs.
- Mechanism evidence: one per-session host owns the PTY; clients replay an append-only output journal and attach to the live socket. A surviving host supports controller replacement. Host loss is handled by starting a replacement provider process with its resume identifier, not by resurrecting the original process. Direct, SSH, and relay transports carry one capability-advertising Host contract; committed output cursors, connection generations, and refusal to replay ambiguous mutations constrain recovery.
- Decision effect: explicitly compare this per-session-host plus restart-with-resume shape in Options 1 and 4. Preserve the separation among exact process survival, presentation reconstruction, provider-thread resume, and remote control. Treat remote control of a live host as distinct from remote-compute continuity after laptop loss.
- Rejected inheritance: raw-byte output journals as Eon terminal truth, client-side duplicate terminal emulation, terminal-query interception or muting, automatic provider restart, and Unpeel relay/mobile/provider scope. Orbit remains sole PTY and terminal-state authority.
- Planning disposition: evidence only; no dependency, contract, implementation, status, priority, prerequisite, or additional bead. First activation check is to revalidate the exact revision and routed files, then record whether the selected durability tier adopts or rejects each mechanism.

Planning-only batch authorized by the user on 2026-08-15; no issue was claimed.

Ghostty terminal-snapshot comparison — 2026-08-15:
- Exact source: Ghostty d760ee96e54657416eb427b793c7e839f003df7d include/ghostty/vt/snapshot.h and src/terminal/snapshot. The API can reconstruct a renderable terminal model, unfinished VT parser continuation, active and alternate screens, and incrementally delivered history from a checksummed binary stream.
- Durability meaning: this is a possible mechanism for presentation-state reconstruction after an Orbit replacement. It does not preserve or resurrect the PTY, shell, foreground job, process tree, file descriptors, sockets, credentials, working resources, or provider execution. A replacement Orbit and process retain new run identities even if a terminal model is restored.
- Constraints: snapshot v1 explicitly lacks binary compatibility; Kitty image and placement state are excluded; continuation admission can be large and needs an explicit bound; an interrupted encode may leave only a partial prefix; and caller-owned durable storage, atomicity, permissions, retention, deletion, migration, corruption recovery, and secret policy remain unsolved.
- Decision effect: add terminal-model reconstruction as a distinct optional row in the failure-domain matrix, between metadata-only recovery and exact process continuation. Do not make it part of the minimum local durability tier unless real dogfood shows that explicit command/provider restart without old pixels is insufficient.
- Rejected inference: the older formatter-specific negative result remains valid, but it no longer proves that current libghostty HEAD lacks a dedicated terminal snapshot. Neither the new API nor its upstream benchmark justifies dependency refresh, persistence, Eon Web, remote transport, or a process-survival claim.

comments.author: Codex /root
comments.text:
Accepted decision — 2026-08-19 America/Sao_Paulo

The user explicitly approved the recommended selection on 2026-08-19: phased local durability, exact same-boot Eon-supervisor-loss continuity first, and the reduced independently managed per-Session Orbit mechanism selected in `orb-decide-orbit-session-adoption-4hu`. This explicitly reprioritizes the decision ahead of `eon-pxn`; the former planning dependency is no longer a prerequisite to recording the product decision. Closure creates no EON-C, ORB-C, or VEN-C contract and authorizes no implementation.

Accepted failure-domain matrix

1. Venus closes or crashes: exact PTY process and authoritative terminal state continue while Orbit remains alive. Orbit owns the process and terminal state; canonical ORBS owns reattachment; Eon owns product selection. No durable data or new work is needed.
2. Eon supervisor is abruptly lost on the same boot and login: selected first phase. Exact continuation is promised only while the same Orbit remains alive. A replacement Eon must validate the exact live logical Session ID, run ID, component/protocol generation, process-start identity, endpoint identity, and user ownership through the Orbit-authored management handshake before acquiring the sole management lease. Runtime locator data is ephemeral and non-authoritative. The owner-first mechanism is Option D from `orb-decide-orbit-session-adoption-4hu`, without double-fork, a shared broker, systemd requirement, new binary, or new crate unless proof later falsifies that reduced shape.
3. Logout or reboot: the old process does not survive and exact continuation is not promised. The selected second phase is explicit reconstruction of a replacement from a bounded Eon-owned local record. Every replacement receives a fresh run and process identity linked to, but never impersonating, the prior run. Preview and explicit user confirmation precede reconstruction; unsupported launch intent and partial failures remain visible.
4. Machine unavailable, lost, or destroyed: no exact process or local-record availability is promised. Encrypted metadata sync is not selected now. It may be considered only after the local record and deletion model prove useful. Remote execution remains a separate product tier because continuity comes from the process running elsewhere; route it through `eon-az9` rather than presenting sync as process survival.

Distinct outcomes

Exact process continuation, terminal-model reconstruction, topology/launch reconstruction, provider-thread resume, metadata backup, and remote execution remain separate. Ghostty snapshots can recreate terminal-model state but not the PTY process. Provider resume creates new provider/process identities. CRIU remains rejected for arbitrary developer Sessions. Ordinary SSH reaches a live host but does not preserve a process when that host is gone.

Minimum phase-two local record, before any future implementation

- Eon owns one versioned record for the current local workspace: schema version, stable workspace ID, monotonic record revision, clean/unclean marker, bounded topology nodes and selected IDs, and for each Session a stable logical Session ID, prior run linkage, and a typed launch disposition.
- The initial reconstructable launch disposition is the managed default shell/profile only. Arbitrary argv, resolved executable paths, cwd, environment, credentials, provider prompts, socket paths, PIDs, terminal frames, scrollback, graphics, process memory, and raw user content are excluded. Unsupported custom commands are reported as not reconstructable rather than silently persisted or executed.
- Bound the record to 256 Sessions and 1 MiB, with at most one current and one previous valid revision. Write a 0600 temporary file beneath one 0700 UID-owned directory, flush it, atomically rename it, and flush the directory. Reject symlinks, wrong ownership or mode, checksum failure, structural overflow, and newer incompatible schemas. Quarantine corrupt/newer state for diagnosis; never partially apply it.
- The record is retained only for the local workspace and deleted with explicit workspace deletion. A stale revision may be previewed but never automatically replayed. Reconstruction creates fresh run IDs and reports every omitted or failed Session.
- This record is a corruption boundary, not protection against compromise of the local account. A same-user attacker may read or replace it; excluding secrets and arbitrary executable content limits consequence. No cloud/server threat exists while sync is absent.
- Before any sync tier, separately decide end-to-end encryption, key creation/export/loss, authenticated record ordering, rollback/replay detection, accidental-secret review, server compromise, retention, per-device deletion acknowledgement, and deletion tombstones. Key loss means no recovery; server compromise must not reveal plaintext; cross-device deletion must be observable and bounded. No sync contract is implied by this decision.

Ownership and sequencing

Orbit remains the only PTY process, libghostty state, query, presentation, child-exit, and contained-stop owner. Eon remains logical Session/run creation, topology, reconstruction, selection, retention, and recovery-policy owner. Venus remains transient. Any implementation is split owner-first: approve/index the Orbit lifecycle-management contract; implement and prove Orbit; implement Eon consumption against the exact Orbit proof; then run cross-repository acceptance. Phase-two durable-record work is a later Eon-owned contract and Bead, not part of same-boot adoption.

Proof and reversal

The first proof kills Eon with SIGKILL while deterministic useful PTY work continues, starts competing replacements, proves exactly one validates and acquires the same Orbit run, attaches through canonical ORBS to the same PTY child and terminal state, then performs owner-routed ORB-C12 cleanup. It rejects stale/replaced endpoints, wrong IDs/UID/modes, incompatible generations, partial startup, Orbit exit during recovery, and reboot. The phase-two proof later uses a fresh runtime or reboot, previews one valid bounded record, creates fresh identities, reconstructs only supported topology/default shells, and fails closed on corrupt/newer/oversized records and partial launch.

Reverse same-boot work to current behavior if the owner proof cannot preserve exact identity without unsafe PID/path authority. Reconsider systemd/launchd only if logout, start-at-login, or administrator supervision becomes selected. Reconsider a broker only if per-Session Orbit cannot own status and a sole management lease without greater total complexity. Do not proceed to phase two until same-boot dogfood is accepted; do not proceed to sync until the local record demonstrates value without secret capture.

Acceptance disposition: AC1–AC8 are recorded above and in the cited research; AC9 is satisfied by the user approval. No implementation, manifest, package, storage, cloud, protocol, or contract-index change occurred.

title: Set Eon opacity default to 0.80 and roll into Eonova
description:
## Contract

Consumer: local Eon, EonTerm, and override-free Eonova users.

Trigger: a Venus surface is created or reopened without `terminal.background_opacity` in the canonical Eon config.

Result: corrected EON-C13 defaults the existing setting to `0.80`; explicit valid values and all validation remain unchanged. Eonova adds no opacity policy and advances only its exact Eon pin to the immutable proof, so a config-free launch consumes `0.80`.

Important failures: invalid config behavior, changed Nova identity, an Eonova override, failed package/profile verification, or interruption of a live Session leaves the work incomplete.

## Evidence and decision

The user tested `0.8` through `~/.config/eon/config.toml` and explicitly selected it as the product default on 2026-08-14. Existing EON-C13 and Venus VEN-C11 already own the field, validation, launch argv, and default-background-only materialization. Decision: change the one Eon `TerminalConfig::default` value and aligned expectations/current-state text, publish one new immutable Eon proof, then advance only Eonova Eon input/assertion and affected lock nodes. Preserve Venus, Orbit, Nova, configuration schema, wrapper, namespaces, and live generations. Add no dependency, setting layer, CLI flag, environment bridge, watcher, or Eonova override.

## Scope

In scope: EON-C13 default/current proof, existing default-consuming checks, README/CHANGELOG/LOC, exact Eon build/profile and installed proof; then trackerless Eonova exact Eon pin/lock, package/profile/boundary proof. This issue is the selected planning owner for both the correction and downstream Eonova rollout.

Out of scope: opacity semantics, explicit-cell transparency, blur, live mutation, child changes, Nova changes, config migration, another platform, or stopping existing supervisors.

## Acceptance Criteria\n
- Missing config and absent field yield `0.80`; explicit values and strict finite `0.0..=1.0` validation remain exact.
- Default Eon and EonTerm Venus argv carries `--background-opacity 0.8`.
- Locked Rust and exact Nix checks pass; Eon source, artifacts, contract proof, profile, and LOC are recorded.
- Eonova pins that exact Eon proof, retains Nova `9ef7f6530bac3b4296adbaa7b50eaef3c1716cf1`, remains override-free and Mars/Rio-free, and passes package, wrapper, desktop, license, closure, and profile checks.

title: Deliver trustworthy Codex quota in full Eon
description:
## Outcome and routed contract

Complete and prove `EON-C22 — Trustworthy Codex quota in the Eon Bar` by composing Eon's accepted Codex quota source with the exact accepted Venus `VEN-C22` revision from `eon-desktop:ven-render-codex-quota-eon-bar-wfe`.

Consumer: one installed full-Eon user on supported native x86_64 Linux Wayland who already uses an authenticated compatible Codex CLI.

Trigger: an isolated full-Eon workspace starts, the Eon-owned provider source publishes fresh/stale/blocked/unknown/absent quota facts, and Venus receives normal complete EONW snapshots while the window is ordinary, narrow, or tiny.

Result: the existing one-row Eon Bar conditionally shows one truthful Codex quota chip by default when a compatible authenticated provider is available. Fresh ordinary width shows provider, elapsed/total window positions, and remaining percentages; compact width keeps `Codex` plus the most constrained window’s elapsed/total position and remaining percentage; stale is visibly `old` or hidden; blocked and unknown are explicit; absent data leaves the core bar unchanged. Tabs, required controls, attention's future higher priority, terminal area, and live Sessions remain intact.

Important failures: stale child proof, component pin mismatch, missing/incompatible/unauthenticated Codex, provider/network loss, account change, malformed response, profile-refresh failure, or narrow layout never substitutes components, exposes credentials/account identity, blocks Eon startup, restarts live supervisors, or presents guessed/fresh-looking quota.

Impact: HIGH from direct user dogfood. Effort: S after both child/source proofs. Integration risk: LOW; installed provider and responsive-UI risk: MEDIUM. Confidence: HIGH after prerequisites close.

## Evidence

- `eon-source-codex-quota-eon-bar-mny` owns EON-C22 Candidate source semantics, EONW v6, Codex app-server lifecycle, account invalidation, freshness/backoff, security, and source-level proof.
- `eon-desktop:ven-render-codex-quota-eon-bar-wfe` owns VEN-C22 scene/layout/text/tooltip/accessibility behavior and native child proof.
- `eon-deliver-native-eon-bar-w4d` owns EON-C21, exact VEN-C21 composition, the one-row bar, fixed controls, tab-first priority, profile refresh, and installed acceptance; the source bead already depends on it.
- `components/eon-alpha-v3.json`, `flake.nix`, and `flake.lock` are the sole exact Eon/Venus composition graph. Eon must pin the accepted child rather than copy presentation.
- Installed Codex `0.154.0` stable generated schema proves a current machine-readable `account/rateLimits/read` boundary. The exact implementation source bead must refresh that evidence before code.
- Nova Bar exact source `bfbf8a7be28b69f9d822c0843bf2dd5066dd49e3` is comparison-only; its `tokenusage`, caches, command widgets, Zellij/zjstatus, tray configuration, and compatibility surface remain rejected.

## Prerequisites and reference gate

Hard prerequisites:
- `eon-source-codex-quota-eon-bar-mny` is closed with exact Eon source, EON-C22 Candidate, EONW v6 proof, and no unresolved provider/security/tool gate.
- `eon-desktop:ven-render-codex-quota-eon-bar-wfe` is closed with immutable accepted Venus source and VEN-C22 proof against that exact EONW v6 revision.
- The native bar EON-C21/VEN-C21 prerequisites remain accepted and no other Eon/Orbit/Venus implementation frontier is active unless the user explicitly changes it.

Before implementation:
- Compare manifest/flake pins with exact accepted Eon Sessions and Eon Desktop revisions. Stop on stale or speculative children.
- Read both complete source/child outcomes, reference gates, proof records, limits, and exact EONW/Codex identities plus current component validation, profile refresh, and installed dogfood owners.
- Reuse those accepted mechanisms. This delivery adds no provider parser, auth path, UI formatter, layout policy, configuration schema, dependency, process owner, or compatibility adapter.
- Reconcile EON-C22 Candidate text and advance it only from one installed unchanged-candidate observation.

## Scope

In scope:
- Pin exact accepted VEN-C22 Venus source/proof through the canonical component manifest, flake input, and lock while preserving exact Orbit and EONW identities.
- Align EON-C22, README, CHANGELOG, and LOC scorecard with only proved current behavior.
- Complete affected Rust/manifest/Nix checks, refresh the named `eon` profile from the working tree without restarting live supervisors, and run isolated installed native Wayland acceptance with real fresh Codex quota plus bounded absent/stale/blocked/unknown substitutes.

Out of scope:
- Provider or Venus implementation; auth/account management; Codex packaging; other providers; token/cost history; quota mutation; reset credits; charts; notifications; attention/sidebar implementation; or Orbit changes.
- Widget lists/order/style, arbitrary commands, plugins, Nova compatibility, persistent cache, a second row, per-tab quota, clickable quota, or a generic provider/status framework.
- EonTerm, macOS proof/support, X11/Xwayland, direct bundles, signing, or distribution expansion.

## Implementation notes

1. Pin only the exact accepted VEN-C22 revision through the existing graph. Keep the source bead's accepted EONW v6 revision exact; stop rather than adapting mismatched child APIs.
2. Update current-state contract/docs once. Keep the default conditional and configuration-free: compatible authenticated Codex produces the chip; absence produces the unchanged core bar.
3. Run the complete affected route once on the unchanged candidate, then refresh `nix profile upgrade eon` without stopping existing supervisors.
4. Start a fresh isolated workspace from the new profile. Observe one real fresh read without recording account identity or credentials; exercise absent/stale/blocked/unknown through the accepted bounded substitute rather than mutating the user's account.
5. Record exact Eon/Venus/Orbit/EONW/Codex/package/profile/compositor/scale identities and the live supervisor/Session identities preserved before and after refresh.

## Acceptance criteria

- The canonical manifest, flake input/lock, package, `eon versions`, and child proof all resolve to the exact accepted EON-C22/EONW v6/VEN-C22 revisions; Orbit remains exact and unchanged unless separately accepted.
- With a compatible authenticated Codex, installed full Eon shows one fresh quota chip in the single-row bar whose elapsed/total window positions, remaining percentages, and accessible description agree with the same accepted app-server snapshot without exposing account identity.
- Ordinary width shows all available bounded windows with elapsed/total positions and remaining percentages; compact width retains `Codex` plus the most constrained window’s elapsed/total position and remaining percentage; stale is visibly `old` or hidden; blocked is explicit; absent data leaves EON-C21 behavior and geometry unchanged.
- The quota chip disappears before active tab identity, New tab, Shortcuts, active Close, or future accepted agent attention; no second row or terminal-grid loss appears.
- Missing/incompatible/unauthenticated Codex, provider crash/network loss, account change, malformed response, and expired stale facts degrade exactly as the source/child contracts specify without blocking startup, workspace actions, terminal attachment, or shutdown.
- No credential, auth file, account id, plan, credits, upsell, transcript, token history, raw JSON, or provider command output appears in logs, EONW captures, UI, docs, or product state.
- Pointer hover, AT-SPI text/order, narrow/overflow layout, terminal keyboard focus, tab scrolling/dragging, bar controls, popup/picker behavior, notices, and cleanup remain accepted.
- Complete locked Rust checks, manifest validation, affected flake checks/package builds, README LOC, and `git diff --check` pass on one unchanged candidate.
- The named `eon` profile resolves to the just-built artifact. Existing supervisors, Venus clients, and Orbit Sessions keep recorded process identities; no automatic restart occurs.
- One isolated native x86_64 Linux Wayland report records exact identities, real fresh facts, substitute failure states, wide/compact/hidden behavior, accessibility, focus, and cleanup. EON-C22 advances to Proven only after one immutable Eon revision records that installed observation.

## Stop conditions

- Stop if either exact prerequisite is incomplete, stale, mismatched, unpublished, or requires an unaccepted Orbit/provider/tool/dependency decision.
- Stop if composition requires Eon-rendered UI, Venus provider logic, copied schemas, credentials, direct HTTP, `tokenusage`, a new component graph, compatibility window, configuration/widget framework, or another row.
- Stop rather than restarting a live supervisor, mutating the user's Codex account/quota, or recording sensitive provider/account data.
- Stop before claiming macOS, another provider/compositor, EonTerm, or another distribution channel.

## Maintenance notes

Quota and agent attention are sibling typed first-party facts, not generic widgets. When both are eventually proved, required bar interactions and active-tab identity stay first, agent attention outranks quota, and quota disappears first. Only then should dogfood decide whether a strict built-in visibility/order setting is worth owning.

title: Deliver the native Eon Bar in full Eon
description:
## Outcome and routed contract

Create and prove `EON-C21 — Native workspace header` by composing the exact accepted Venus `VEN-C21` revision from `eon-desktop:ven-native-eon-bar-header-iqj` into installed full Eon.

Consumer: one installed full-Eon user on the supported native x86_64 Linux Wayland surface.

Trigger: the user operates the existing top workspace row through tabs, New tab, Shortcuts, the active tab's Close control, wheel scrolling, accessibility activation, or empty-background window dragging.

Result: full Eon presents one native Eon Bar at the existing tab-strip height. It keeps Eon-authored tab identity and action policy while exact Venus materializes tab-first responsive layout, fixed New tab and Shortcuts controls, active-tab Close, accessible tooltips/focus, and compositor-owned window dragging from blank header background. No second status row, widget runtime, or protocol field is introduced.

Important failures: an incomplete or stale child proof, manifest/lock mismatch, rejected Eon action, unavailable drag request, narrow surface, or profile refresh failure does not substitute components, mutate the wrong tab, restart live Sessions, or widen support.

Impact: HIGH for native discoverability and window usability. Effort: S after the child proof. Integration risk: LOW; installed interaction risk: MEDIUM. Confidence: HIGH.

## Evidence

- `docs/CONTRACTS.md:558-650` defines EON-C8 tab identity, labels, scrolling, focus, stable-target close policy, and omission of the redundant title bar.
- `docs/CONTRACTS.md:1475-1515` defines EON-C20 and the exact native shortcut viewer.

- Existing EONW v5 already carries CreateTab and CloseTab actions. Shortcuts is Venus-local. The chosen core bar requires no EONW or Orbit change.
- `eon-desktop:ven-native-eon-bar-header-iqj` owns VEN-C21 scene, rendering, input, native drag, tooltip, and AccessKit behavior.
- Nova Bar exact source `bfbf8a7be28b69f9d822c0843bf2dd5066dd49e3` informed only tab-first priority. Its Zellij/WASM widgets, polling, theme, and compatibility surface are explicitly rejected.

## Prerequisites and reference gate

Hard prerequisite: `eon-desktop:ven-native-eon-bar-header-iqj` is closed with an immutable accepted Venus revision, VEN-C21 proof, and no unaccepted EONW or Orbit change.

Before implementation:
- Compare the Orbit and Venus manifest pins with each child repository's latest accepted source. Record exact pinned and accepted revisions; stop on speculative child work.
- Read the complete VEN-C21 outcome, reference decision, checks, limitations, and proof plus current EON-C8, EON-C20, EONW v5, manifest validation, flake identity, profile-refresh, and installed-runtime owners.
- Reuse the child reference gate and presentation mechanism. Eon adds no UI code, native dependency, copied label registry, or separate layout policy.
- Record EON-C21 as Candidate before composition edits.

## Scope

In scope:
- Pin the exact accepted VEN-C21 Venus source and proof through the canonical component manifest, flake input, and lock.
- Add EON-C21 and align the current README, CHANGELOG, and LOC scorecard with proved product behavior.
- Run complete affected Rust/Nix composition checks, refresh the named `eon` profile from the working tree, and perform one isolated installed native Wayland acceptance while preserving live Sessions.

Out of scope:
- Venus rendering/input/accessibility code; EONW or Orbit changes; runtime action-policy changes; a new bar repository.
- A second row, Nova compatibility, widgets, command polling, configuration, plugins, transient-notice relocation, agent attention, per-tab status, cursor-color chrome, tab drag reorder, overview, inactive-tab close, or native window controls.
- EonTerm changes, macOS proof/support, X11/Xwayland, direct bundles, signing, or distribution expansion.

## Implementation notes

1. Wait for the exact accepted Venus child proof, then update the single component graph, flake input, and lock together. Keep Orbit and EONW identities unchanged unless the child explicitly proves and the user approves a narrower prerequisite.
2. Add EON-C21 as Candidate and make EON-C8/EON-C20 references only where necessary; do not duplicate Venus geometry or action descriptors.
3. Update current-state user documentation and changelog only for the behavior actually delivered.
4. Run the full affected Rust, manifest, Nix, package, and installed-profile route once on the unchanged candidate.
5. Refresh `nix profile upgrade eon` without stopping or restarting existing supervisors. Dogfood a fresh isolated workspace and record exact process identities before/after.

## Acceptance criteria

- The canonical manifest, flake input/lock, package, and `eon versions` resolve to the exact accepted VEN-C21 revision and proof; required EONW and Orbit identities remain exact and justified.
- Installed full Eon shows one Eon Bar at the former tab-strip height with no second row or terminal-grid loss.
- Existing tab labels, paths, scrolling, active reveal, pointer/keyboard focus, reorder, picker/popup behavior, and stable identities remain accepted.
- New tab activates the existing picker-first CreateTab policy exactly once; Shortcuts toggles the exact current EON-C20 viewer without EONW traffic; Close names and submits only the accepted active `tN`.
- Empty header background moves the undecorated native window on the proved Wayland environment. Tabs, controls, tab-scroll gaps, pane chrome, terminal content, pickers/popups, and the viewer do not initiate dragging.
- Pointer, keyboard, and AT-SPI activation expose the shortcut-bearing names and visible focus without stealing terminal input or desktop focus.
- Ordinary, overflow, narrow, and tiny surfaces preserve the active tab identity and required controls without overlap.
- Complete locked Rust checks, manifest validation, affected flake checks and package builds, README LOC, and `git diff --check` pass on one unchanged candidate.
- The named `eon` profile resolves to the just-built artifact. Existing supervisors, Venus clients, and Orbit Sessions keep their recorded process identities; no automatic restart occurs.

## Stop conditions

- Stop if the Venus prerequisite is incomplete, unpublished, stale, or requires an unaccepted EONW/Orbit revision.
- Stop if composition requires Eon-rendered chrome, a second layout/action owner, new runtime dependency, compatibility path, widget framework, or protocol field.
- Stop rather than rewriting or discarding the existing user-owned Beads change.
- Stop before restarting a live supervisor or claiming macOS, another compositor, or another distribution channel.

## Maintenance notes

Public documentation may call this surface “Eon Bar.” Its implementation owner remains Venus's existing workspace header, while Eon owns only composition and product policy. Agent attention is deliberately excluded and has its own provider-gated bead.

title: Remove a pane view without stopping its terminal
description:
## Origin
Split from closed `eon-pxn` on 2026-10-16 (its acceptance item 9).

## Contract (provisional)
A user can remove a pane's view from the workspace without stopping its Orbit terminal, and can get
that terminal back. This is distinct from the accepted tab close, which stops terminals, and must
not change it.

## Open design decision
Where a detached terminal lives and how the user reattaches it (a list, a picker, or the CLI), and
when an unreachable detached terminal is cleaned up.

## Owners
Eon Runtime owns topology and the detached-terminal set; Orbit keeps the terminal; Venus presents.

## Prerequisites and reference gate
Consequential (lifecycle and possibly EONW). Read EON-C8 and EON-C15. Stop for Lucca's design and
contract approval before code.

## Acceptance
An isolated installed check detaches a pane running a long process, confirms it keeps running, and
reattaches it; tab close still stops terminals.

## Stop boundary
No background thumbnails, durable restore or change to Stop semantics.

title: Make the program-status check's detached-turns step reliable under load
description:
## Why

The real-PTY program-status check's `detached_turns_end_at_a_return` step failed twice on 2026-10-23, both times in code it doesn't touch:
- eon-agent-sidebar-yx8.11's review ledger: "detached_turns_end_at_a_return fails on its streamed1 marker in the cargo sandbox, unchanged by this diff".
- eon-title-utf8-ends-terminal-atq2 (eon-3f): a debug-build program_status run failed with `wait_for streamed1` timing out at 10 s, at load average 11.8. The step before it passed.

A check that fails under load gets explained away, and then it stops catching real regressions. Agents run this check on a shared 16-core machine, often during other builds.

## Scope

In scope:
- Reproduce under load, for example while a parallel `eon-test` runs, and find whether the 10 s wait is too tight for a debug build under load, or whether the step races (for example, the marker printed before the observer attaches, or output lost between turns).
- Fix the cause. If it's purely timing, scale or lengthen the wait in the check's own harness, not with a retry loop. If it's a race, fix the race in the check, or in Orbit if Orbit is at fault, and say which.

Out of scope: other steps of the check, and the ORB-C15 behavior it proves.

## Acceptance

- The step passes 20 runs in a row under a parallel load of at least the machine's core count, in the debug build, and records the run count and load.
- If the cause is an Orbit race, a red/green check shows it.

## Verification

`nix develop -c eon-test` for the affected crate, and the nix orbit-program-status check once on the final tree.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: eon-3f's reviewer (2026-10-23) reproduced the same failure on base 2112ff3 under nix develop -c eon-test (debug build), so it predates atq2. The nix check (release build) may pass. A third acceptable outcome: if the step can't be made reliable in the debug eon-test route, document that only the nix check proves it, and gate the step accordingly.

title: Make the diagnostics log pruning test independent of its PID
description:
## Report (eon-63 during yx8.11, 2026-10-23)

runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/diagnostics.rs `pruning_keeps_the_newest_and_live_logs_only` builds `own = "-{pid}.log"`. Its foreign fixtures (`g1-abc-2-7.log`, `grocery-1-7.log`, `{GENERATION}-x-7.log`) end in `-7.log`. Under eon-test's PID namespace, the test binary can be PID 7. The foreign files then match `own`, and the assertion around line 311 fails. It failed once in eon-63's sandboxed run and passed on three reruns. It can fail any final proof at random.

## Fix

Give the fixtures a suffix that no PID can produce, such as `-x.log`, or derive them from a PID guaranteed to differ from the test's own. Keep what the test asserts unchanged.

## Acceptance

The test passes when forced to PID 7. Check by making `own` collide in a temporary local run, or by computing the fixture suffix away from the real PID; no new harness. Run eon-test -p eon-runtime and the converge plus Codex review.

Portability disposition: neutral.
close_reason: Fixtures carry a PID other than the test's own

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Fix (eon-9e, 2026-10-23): the pruning test's fixtures carry the PID std::process::id() + 1 instead of a fixed 7. No fixture can then end in the test's own -{pid}.log at any PID. Each fixture keeps its parse path, and the assertions are unchanged.

Proof (on the committed tree, x86_64 Linux, eon-test bubblewrap sandbox):
- Red: with the fixture PID forced to equal the test's own (the PID-7 collision), the test failed at diagnostics.rs:306, created.len() 5 vs 1. Base 0e3912b run at real PID 7 in a fresh PID namespace also failed (5 vs 1).
- Green: the candidate run at real PID 7 in the same namespace passed. CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4 nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime passed (lib 84 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored). cargo fmt --check -p eon-runtime is clean.

Ledger: one round on candidate tree f51de57. Codex (gpt-6.1-sol xhigh) found nothing blocking, and so did the fresh Claude reviewer, who also ran the checks. One style nit (bind process::id() once) was skipped as style-only.

title: Type double quotes and other dead keys under us+intl
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-10-21: typing double quotes in Eon is a struggle. A programmer
types quotes constantly, so this blocks daily use.

## Evidence

- Lucca's layouts (COSMIC `xkb_config`): `us,jp` with variants `intl,kana`.
  Under `us+intl`, the quote key is a dead key: Shift+' is dead_diaeresis and '
  is dead_acute. A quote is typed as the dead key followed by Space, and the
  dead key followed by a letter composes (" then a gives ä).
- VEN-C2 (Native semantic interaction): punctuation keys "stay physical", and
  its Boundary accepts no dead keys on macOS; it says nothing about dead keys
  or compose on Linux. Its proof covers only the plain US layout and
  `caps:swapescape`.
- The exact symptom is not recorded yet: nothing appears, the wrong character
  appears, or Space is needed twice. Reproduce it first.

Owner: Venus native input (VEN-C2) resolves native keys and text; Orbit
encodes terminal input (ORB-C5).

## Scope

In scope: reproduce under `us+intl` in an isolated Eon (wdotool with that
keymap); record the symptom and how Venus handles the compositor's dead-key
and compose state; make dead keys compose as they do in other Wayland apps:
dead key then Space gives the plain character, dead key then a letter gives the
composed letter, and a dead key twice gives the character. Keep shortcuts
layout-independent as VEN-C2 requires.

Out of scope: Japanese kana input and other IMEs; macOS dead keys (VEN-C16).

## Acceptance

- Lucca approved the VEN-C2 text change for Linux dead keys and compose.
- Under `us+intl`, ", ', ` and ~ can be typed in an Eon terminal, as can ä, é
  and ã, as in another Wayland terminal; Alt and Ctrl shortcuts still work.

## Verification

- A Venus test for dead-key composition at the input owner.
- One isolated installed observation under `us+intl`.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop for Lucca's approval before changing VEN-C2 text.
- Stop if composition requires a new Wayland protocol or a dependency.
close_reason: Shift held through a dead key and Space now types the composed character in kitty-protocol programs (Claude Code); VEN-C2 updated with Lucca's approval; proved by test and isolated installed observation; profile refreshed.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Reproduced 2026-10-21 on installed eon-0.1.1 (/nix/store/spcr8z0m452r8v727895yniflra1dsq9) in isolated headless Sway 1.12, wdotool 0.5.3 keymap us+intl. Symptom (Lucca narrowed it): only with Shift still held at the Space press, and only where the app enables the kitty keyboard protocol (Claude Code; not legacy nushell). A raw reader with CSI >1u got a, ESC[32;2u, b ' c ¨ d for: Shift+dead then Shift+Space, dead then Space, Shift+dead twice. Dead then Space, dead then letter and dead twice already compose (winit's xkb compose); foot agrees. Cause: venus/src/input.rs layout_metadata infers consumed Shift only for Key::Character, so Space carrying composed text kept Shift as a binding mod and Ghostty's kitty encoder sent Shift+Space instead of the text. Fix: Space counts " " as its unshifted text, so Shift is consumed when the text differs. Red/green: derives_layout_metadata_without_a_keyboard_map fails without the arm (left (None, 0), right (Some(' '), SHIFT)) and passes with it. Note for later proof: wdotool runs each call on its own virtual keyboard, so a held modifier must be inside each chord (shift+dead_acute, shift+space); physical keysym names (apostrophe, grave) don't reach dead keys, keysym names (dead_acute) do.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Lucca approved 2026-10-21 the VEN-C2 change: Result gains the Shift-consumed rule with Space's unshifted text a space (dead-key text on Space arrives as text with Shift held); Boundary gains acceptance of Linux dead keys and compose sequences from the keymap's compose table.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Lucca approved 2026-10-21 corrected VEN-C2 wording after review: Result says Venus reports Shift consumed by the text, and a program using the kitty keyboard protocol without report-all receives the text (report-all still sends Shift+Space by spec); Boundary names the locale's compose table (winit loads it from LC_ALL/LC_CTYPE/LANG), not the keymap's. Claude Code 2.1.303 pushes only CSI >1u or >5u.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Portability disposition: neutral. The change is in Venus's shared layout_metadata (no Linux, Wayland or Darwin API); the dead-key composition it relies on stays in winit's Linux xkb host path.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Reference gate (consequential: VEN-C2 contract change). Behavior: a character a dead key composes on Space with Shift still held reaches kitty-protocol programs as text. Owners: winit's xkb host path composes; Venus input (layout_metadata) owns the consumed-modifier report; Orbit/Ghostty's encoder owns the bytes (ORB-C5). Routes read: venus/docs/REFERENCES.md (winit 0.30.13 native-event boundary; Ghostling/libghostty-rs ownership), the eon-venus-keysym-named-keys-chnh Ghostty precedent. Comparable: Ghostty 8c425a7bd57de848aa83cb9b003b1ecd6037c56a (~/pjs/refs/ghostty-7501/repo), src/apprt/gtk/class/surface.zig:1396-1404 takes consumed_mods from GDK's per-key xkb consumed modifiers; its kitty encoder (src/input/key_encode.zig:126-214) sends text only when binding mods (mods minus consumed) are empty and report-all is off. Rejected: deriving consumed mods from xkb's per-key consumed modifiers (Ghostty GTK's approach): xkeyboard-config 2.47 pc symbols give <SPCE> one level ({[ space ]}), also under us(intl), so xkb consumes nothing on Space and Shift would stay a binding mod, the same CSI 32;2u; winit 0.30.13 also exposes no consumed-mods API. Rejected: changing Orbit's encoder input (Orbit already passes Venus's consumed mods through). Decision: extend Venus's existing text-vs-unshifted-text inference to Space (unshifted text " "). Check: derives_layout_metadata_without_a_keyboard_map red/green plus an isolated installed raw-byte observation under CSI >1u. Symptom as Lucca reported it, 2026-10-21: 'if i hold shift and the double quote key, and then space, while still holding shift, nothing happens. i have to release shift first' and 'this does not happen in nushell, only in claude'. Proof scope: us+intl dead keys only; Multi_key (Compose-key) sequences are not exercised. The Venus test covers the Shift-consumed rule; composition itself is winit's and is covered by the installed observation.

title: Outline the whole selected pane in a configurable focus colour
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-10-24, on mur2's installed title rules: "shouldnt the the entire focused pane outine
change color?", then "lets just make the entire pane outline get the focus color like we discussed
and change color. then we can test a few colors". Today only the selected pane's title rule turns
the accent (mint); the terminal that receives keys has no outline of its own.

## Contract

VEN-C8 (states sentence) and EON-C8 (states and frameless sentence) change; wording goes to Lucca
before code. New configuration value `[terminal] focus_color` documented in docs/CONFIGURATION.md.

## Behaviour

- With pane frames on, the selected pane in the selected column gets one outline in the focus
  colour around the whole pane: its title rule (still broken around the label), the card's side
  edges beside it, and the next pane's title rule or the card's bottom edge. The outline is twice
  the card border's width (Lucca asked whether a thicker line allows a more purple colour).
- Other panes and other columns keep the neutral 1 px outline. Keyboard focus in the chrome (F6)
  keeps its mint pill outline (Lucca, 2026-10-24: "ok" to keeping mint for F6 and the focus colour
  only for the pane that receives keys).
- Frameless mode: no outline; the selected label keeps its brighter colour.
- `[terminal] focus_color` uses the cursor-trail colour syntax without `random`
  (`preset:<name>` or `custom:#RRGGBB`); Lucca: "ok" to making it configurable. Default from the Eon
  icon (assets/eon.png): Lucca asked for "pink but as close to purple as possible". Sampled: rim pink
  #eb36fb, violet #b207fb, purple #8a02ec, deep #4f03c6. Eon Runtime parses it and passes the
  resolved colour to Venus (Venus parses no configuration).

## Scope

In: Venus pane-outline drawing, the Runtime setting and its hand-off to Venus, contracts,
CONFIGURATION.md, changelogs, tests. Out: per-pane rounded cards (eon-pane-rounded-frames, adjourned),
popup and sidebar restyling, the split-label and strikethrough issues Lucca saw (handled with the
adjourned idea or a later bead).

## Acceptance

- Focused red/green Venus test: the selected pane's outline (rule, both side segments, bottom) is
  drawn in the focus colour at the doubled width, at scales 1 and 1.3, one and several columns;
  unselected columns stay neutral.
- Runtime test: a configured colour reaches Venus; invalid values are refused like other colour
  settings.
- Isolated installed capture with Lucca's opacity and a non-black wallpaper; Lucca then tries a few
  colours in his own window.

Portability: neutral.
close_reason: Selected pane outlined in configurable focus_color (default #b207fb, 2 px); proof in comments

(2) EON-C8 docs/CONTRACTS.md:399-400, replace 'Pane selection, hover and keyboard focus use VEN-C8's title-label and pill feedback.' with 'The selected pane's outline uses `[terminal] focus_color`, `preset:<name>` or `custom:#RRGGBB`, default `custom:#b207fb`. title: Adopt Nova's Yazi popup and retire Alt+Z
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-10-21: Alt+Z's Project chooser is not a place. Pressing Alt+Z again
cancels it and discards the location, browsing means Tab into a restricted Yazi
(`d`, `D`, `r`, `;`, `:`, Ctrl+Z are no-ops, `flake.nix:445-447`, EON-C18
"Creation is the only enabled file-management mutation") and Esc back. A popup
you toggle on and off is the better model, and Yazelix Nova already has it
(Alt Shift Y, `yazelix-5vl-ba6`; Alt Enter sets the tab folder,
NOVA-TAB-WORKSPACE-001; managed-Yazi F+ keys, `yazelix-5vl-managed-yazi-tab-search-49n0`).
Eon adopts Nova's model so both products behave the same, with one way to
change a tab folder.

## Decisions (Lucca, 2026-10-21)

- Add a kept-alive, per-tab, full Yazi popup on Alt+Shift+Y with Nova's keys.
  Alt+Enter sets the tab folder. It survives tab-folder changes.
- The directory chooser stays only where a decision is unavoidable: the
  automatic picker of a fresh workspace and of every new (pending) tab.
- Alt+Z is removed: every tab already has a folder once its picker closes, so
  its only job (changing an established tab's folder) moves to Alt+Enter.
- Opening a file from the popup opens it in Helix in a new pane at the tab
  folder (needs a command on `eon pane create`). Differs from Nova, which reuses
  one managed editor pane; Eon has no managed editor.
- Folder-change effects on Agent and Git follow `eon-tbn1` (park the Agent).

## Acceptance

All children closed; installed Eon shows the Yazi popup with Nova's keys,
Alt+Enter sets the folder, files open in a Helix pane, and Alt+Z does nothing.
Each child changes a contract: stop for Lucca's approval of its text first.

## Children

1. Yazi popup with Nova keys (blocked by `eon-tbn1`).
2. Open popup files in a new Helix pane (after 1).
3. Remove Alt+Z; keep the chooser for pending tabs only (after 4).
4. Alt+Enter sets the tab folder from the popup (after 1).
close_reason: Outcomes delivered or superseded (prime-beads pass 2, 2026-10-27): the Files Yazi popup on Alt+Shift+Y (bf13705), Alt+Enter sets the folder (cbe397c) and files open in a Helix pane via eon edit (08151c3) shipped and are in EON-C10. The remaining outcome, retiring Alt+Z, was superseded: eon-ecne.3 closed as superseded by eon-quick-search-parity-23y9 (Lucca, 2026-10-23, '4. ok'), under which Alt+Z stays and 23y9.2 retires the chooser. All four children closed.

title: Add a kept-alive Yazi popup with Nova's keys
description:
## Why

See the parent epic. This child delivers the place: a toggleable full Yazi
popup per tab, aligned with Yazelix Nova. Changing the tab folder from it is
child 4.

## Evidence

- `eon/crates/eon/src/product.rs:43-90`: default popup catalog (project, git,
  agent, anima); `keep_alive` per entry. Alt+Shift+Y is unused.
- `flake.nix:434-460`: the chooser's Yazi keymap and footer (restricted); the
  popup must use a separate, unrestricted configuration.
- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/workspace.rs:420`: keep-alive popups are
  replaced after a folder change; Yazi must instead be kept.
- Nova reference (nova repo `0c3fa126`): `docs/ideation/yazi-keymap.md`
  (accepted F+), `docs/configuration.md:197`, `defaults/yazi/`.

## Scope

In scope: default `files`/Yazi popup entry on Alt+Shift+Y (keep-alive, opens at
the tab folder); Nova's F+ managed-Yazi keys (Tab/Z one move-only quick search,
Enter moves Yazi, Shift+Z jump, Shift Tab Spot); clean footer with those
hints; keeping the Yazi popup across folder changes.

Out of scope: Alt+Enter tab folder (child 4); file opening (child 2); Alt+Z and the chooser (child 3); Agent/Git
folder-change effects (`eon-tbn1`).

## Acceptance

- Lucca approved the contract text (EON-C18/config and the popup entry).
- Alt+Shift+Y toggles one Yazi per tab that keeps location and cursor while
  hidden; `d` and other file operations work.
- After a folder change the Yazi popup is the same process.

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime` (and Venus if touched, with fmt and
  clippy).
- `nix build --no-link .#default .#eonbase`.
- Profile refresh plus one isolated installed observation; never restart the
  live supervisor.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop before code until the contract text is approved.
close_reason: Files popup on Alt+Shift+Y with Nova F+ keys, kept across retarget; EON-C10 amended and proven (automated + installed), see proof comment

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Decision (Lucca, 2026-10-21): contract approved, with these choices.

1. Entry: a built-in `files` entry, labelled "Files", on Alt+Shift+Y, keep-alive, opening at the tab directory. A user's `[popups.files]` customizes it like any built-in. The CONFIGURATION.md example that used `[popups.files]` moves to another id.
2. Mechanism: an internal `eon-files` launcher in libexec/eon/bin only, beside eon-directory-picker. It is not a public managed command. It runs the pinned Yazi with a packaged popup config (YAZI_CONFIG_HOME); the user's own Yazi config is not read. Rejected: layering the user config (a generated merged dir; possible follow-up).
3. Keys: Nova F+ minus Alt+Enter (ecne.4) and file opening (ecne.2).
   - Tab and Z open one move-only Zoxide-history search (fzf). Enter moves Yazi there; Tab or Esc returns to browsing.
   - Shift+Tab is Spot.
   - Everything else is native, including file operations.
   - Footer: " Tab/Z Search · Shift+Tab Spot".
4. Zoxide: the popup updates Zoxide history like Nova (zoxide plugin update_db = true). Rejected: chooser-style no-update.
5. Retarget: Files is kept as is, with the same process, location and cursor; it is neither parked nor restarted. After its process exits (q), the next invocation starts fresh at the tab directory.
6. Approved EON-C10 text: "Files defaults to Alt+Shift+Y and runs the pinned Yazi at the tab directory with Eon's packaged popup configuration. Tab and Z open one move-only search of Zoxide history: Enter moves Yazi to the selected folder, and Tab or Esc returns to browsing. Shift+Tab spots the hovered file. Every other key keeps Yazi's native behavior, including file operations, and the footer names the search and Spot keys. Files remains live when hidden and keeps its process, location and cursor across tab-directory changes; only after its process exits does the next invocation start a fresh instance at the tab directory." The Git sentence gains "except Files".

Reference: Nova 3325ef5d (defaults/yazi at cd95fee1): keymap.toml, init.lua, plugins/quick-search.yazi, and docs/ideation/yazi-keymap.md. Kept: one quick-search implementation for Tab and Z, `zoxide query --list --exclude CWD` piped to packaged fzf. Rejected: Nova's role switch (YZX_YAZI_ROLE), because Eon's popup config is its own dir; Nova's auto-layout, git and starship plugins.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Accepted gaps (eon-2e, 2026-10-21, from review rounds 1 and 2):

- The retarget exemption is keyed on the `files` entry id (workspace.rs), the same way Project and Agent are. A `[popups.files].command` override is also kept across folder changes rather than restarted. EON-C10 states the policy for "Files", not for its command.
- Until ecne.2, Enter, `o` and `O` on a file run Yazi's default openers inside the popup.
- No unit test covers Tool::Files's environment (YAZI_CONFIG_HOME from EON_FILES_CONFIG, removed PWD, no XDG_CONFIG_HOME); the code reads the process env. The installed observation covers it.
- The Venus footer hint gives built-in popups other than Git and Agent priority 4 (shortcuts.rs), so "Y Files" drops first when the hint bar is short. Alt+/ lists it. Raising it is a Venus change outside this bead.
- Existing configs (0.x): a custom popup on Alt+Shift+Y now conflicts with Files (noted in CHANGELOG), and an existing `[popups.files]` now customizes the built-in.

Fixed in review:
- R1: a foreign EON-C23 hunk from igae.13 in the candidate (shared working tree).
- R2: Files no longer sets XDG_CONFIG_HOME to Eon's config root, so programs opened from Yazi keep the user's config. Also a Lua wait_err fix and doc wording.
