title: Open Yazi popup files in a new Helix pane
description:
## Why

See the parent epic. Enter on a file in the Yazi popup must open it in an editor
beside your work. Lucca chose a new Helix pane (2026-10-21).

## Evidence

- `docs/USAGE.md`: `eon pane create` takes no command; panes run the shell.
- `docs/CONTRACTS.md` EON-C10: typed workspace control; adding a command is a
  contract change, and Eon does "not ... expose commands over EONW".
- EONW v13 `CreatePane` carries no payload, so opening a file in a pane needs a
  wire change (v14).
- At the pinned Yazi (aa526434), native Enter runs `open`, whose folder rule
  starts with the `edit` opener: Enter on a folder would edit it.
- Nova reference: Yazi opens go through `yzx-open` into one reused managed Helix
  pane. Eon has no managed editor or Helix bridge; reusing one pane is a later
  bead if wanted.

## Scope

Shape decided 2026-10-21 (see the decision comments): `eon edit [--json] --
FILE` over a new EONW v14 `Edit { file }` request carrying absolute raw path
bytes. The runtime owns the editor argv (packaged `hx`), and the new pane is
placed as `pane create` places it for the same caller, at the tab folder. In
Files, Yazi's `edit` opener runs `eon edit`; Enter on a hovered folder enters
it, otherwise Enter keeps Yazi's native `open`.

In scope: EONW v14 (protocol crate, Runtime, Venus decoder rename), the CLI
command, the Files opener and Enter binding, EON-C10/EON-C8 text and the v14
doc references. The component graph moves to EONW 14 in a second commit that
cites this one as producer and consumer proof, as b764c63 followed 9a3731b.

Out of scope: editor pane reuse, a Helix bridge, line/column targets,
configurable editors.

## Acceptance

- Lucca approved the EON-C10 text (decision comments).
- Enter on a text file in Files opens a new pane running Helix on that file at
  the tab folder, selected, and the popup hides; Files keeps its location.
  Enter on a folder enters it.
- An unavailable editor or an invalid command fails clearly and changes nothing.

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-workspace-protocol -p eon-runtime -p eon`
  covering the codec, dispatch and the CLI end to end.
- Profile refresh plus one isolated installed observation.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop before code until the contract text is approved.
close_reason: Files Enter opens text files in a new Helix pane via eon edit over EONW v14; EON-C10 amended and proven (automated + installed); graph on EONW 14; profile refreshed, restart pending with Lucca

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Decision (Lucca, 2026-10-21): contract approved.

1. Shape: `eon edit [--json] -- FILE`, not `pane create -- COMMAND`. The wire carries FILE's raw bytes; the runtime owns the editor argv (packaged hx), so EON-C10's 'does not expose commands over EONW' stays true and a later editor-reuse bead can keep the CLI. Rejected: argv over EONW (any socket client could run any argv; amends the boundary).
2. Wire: this takes EONW v14 (yx8.7 had it reserved, unclaimed; it moves to v15). Full Rust and Nix route, Venus decoder included.
3. Files: replace only Yazi's edit opener, as Nova 3325ef5d defaults/yazi/yazi.toml:11-14. The popup hides because a popup caller's pane create already dismisses it.
4. Approved EON-C10 text: "`eon edit [--json] -- FILE` opens FILE in the packaged Helix in a new pane, as `pane create` would for the same caller, with the tab directory as its working directory. A relative FILE resolves against the caller's working directory. The editor's argv is runtime policy and does not cross EONW. An unavailable editor changes nothing and exits 1. In Files, Yazi's edit opener runs `eon edit`, so Enter on a text file opens it in a new Helix pane and hides the popup. Enter on a folder still enters it, and other file types keep Yazi's default openers." Consumes moves to EONW v14.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Decision (Lucca, 2026-10-21, 'pick what is best for the user', from review round 1): at the pinned Yazi, native Enter on a folder runs the edit opener, so 'Enter on a folder still enters it' needs a rebound Enter. Enter on a hovered folder enters it; otherwise Enter runs Yazi's native open (selection respected, one Helix pane per selected file). Amended EON-C10 text: ecne.1's 'Every other key keeps Yazi's native behavior, including file operations, and the footer names the search and Spot keys.' becomes 'Enter on a hovered folder enters it; every other key, including Enter on files, keeps Yazi's native behavior, including file operations, and the footer names the search and Spot keys.' and the approved 'Enter on a folder still enters it' drops 'still'. Rejected: native Enter (a folder would open in a Helix pane).

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Reference gate (eon-ecne.2, 2026-10-21; consequential: EONW wire change).

- Behavior and owners: `eon edit` parsing and relative-path resolution: Eon Runtime CLI (cli.rs). Wire value `Edit { file }` (tag 26, absolute, no NUL, <=4096 bytes): eon-workspace-protocol v14. Pane placement, caller targeting, editor argv (`hx`) and preflight: Runtime workspace (workspace.rs) through the existing popup preflight (managed_environment::prepare_popup_command). Files opener and Enter binding: Eon's packaged Files config (flake.nix). Helix owns editing.
- Routes read: docs/REFERENCES.md Yazi/Nova route; Nova 3325ef5d defaults/yazi/yazi.toml:11-14 (replaces only the edit opener, block = true); pinned Yazi aa526434 source: yazi-config/preset/yazi-default.toml (opener and open rules: folders and text use edit first), keymap-default.toml (Enter = open, l = enter), yazi-actor/src/mgr/open.rs and open_do.rs (open targets selected-or-hovered, grouped per opener), yazi-fs/src/splatter.rs (%s1 = first target, shell-quoted; per-target runs when the command does not spread). Comparable: yazi-rs/plugins smart-enter (hovered folder enters, else open).
- Kept: EON-C10 'does not expose commands over EONW'; caller targeting and popup dismissal of pane create; exact-version EONW with no negotiation.
- Rejected: argv over EONW (decision 1); Nova's one reused managed editor pane (no managed editor in Eon); native Enter (folders would open in Helix); smart-enter with hovered = true (ignores the selection).
- Checks: codec wire bytes and invalid-file cases (v14 tests); runtime `files_edits_a_file_in_a_new_helix_pane_of_its_tab` (preflight failure changes nothing; argv, cwd, selection, Files hidden); CLI `edit_parser_sends_one_absolute_opaque_file` and the end-to-end `commands_from_a_terminal_target_its_column_and_stale_callers_change_nothing` (real binary, relative FILE, EON_TERMINAL, Orbit child argv); installed observation.
- Accepted gaps: the component graph moves to EONW 14 in a second commit (needs this commit as its proof); `o` on a folder now opens a Helix pane on it (folder rule's edit opener), and JSON/JS/ini/empty files also open in Helix (Yazi's edit rules); a missing editor's message is generic.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Consistency fix (eon-2e, from review round 4): EON-C10's EON_TERMINAL bullet now lists `edit` with `pane create`, `pane close`, `pane move` and `tab move`, because its 'Other commands ... ignore it' sentence contradicted the approved 'as `pane create` would for the same caller'. No behavior beyond the approved text.

comments.text:
Proof (eon-2e, 2026-10-21). The revision is this bead's closing commit. The proved code tree is 663d69dc9b460a0e4e3218727239462f5d7372f8 on base fb7a211; the commit adds only the EON-C10 proof record and bead text to it.

  - `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-workspace-protocol -p eon-runtime -p eon` passed: workspace_control 38/38 (including the end-to-end `commands_from_a_terminal_target_its_column_and_stale_callers_change_nothing`: real binary, relative FILE, EON_TERMINAL, Orbit child argv `hx <abs>`), eon-runtime 57/57 (`edit_parser_sends_one_absolute_opaque_file`, `files_edits_a_file_in_a_new_helix_pane_of_its_tab`), protocol 7/7 (v14 wire bytes, invalid files).

In Files at work/, Enter on sub/ entered it; Enter on inner.txt opened pane p2, selected, running `/nix/store/lyq0m2rq…-helix-term/bin/hx <root>/home/work/sub/inner.txt` with cwd work/ (the tab directory); Files was hidden but kept (popup=none, u2 listed); Alt+Shift+Y showed it at work/sub with the same cursor. title: Remove Alt+Z and keep the chooser for new tabs only
description:
## Why

See the parent epic. Once Alt+Enter in the Yazi popup changes a tab folder (child 4),
Alt+Z is a second way to do the same thing. The automatic chooser of a fresh
workspace and of each new tab stays: a pending tab must get a folder before its
first pane exists. If you dismiss it and land in the wrong folder, Alt+Shift+Y
then Alt+Enter fixes it.

## Evidence

- `eon/crates/eon/src/product.rs:49-57`: `project` entry on Alt+Z.
- `docs/CONFIGURATION.md:121`: "Project is required on Alt+Z."
- `docs/CONTRACTS.md` EON-C18 (~1128-1200): Alt+Z trigger and retarget rules;
  EON-C10 runtime policy (~688).
- `runtime/crates/eon-workspace-protocol/src/v12.rs:1635`: the popup catalog
  carries each entry's shortcut; check whether an entry may have none.
- `docs/USAGE.md:119`, shortcut viewer and hints: Alt+Z rows.

## Scope

In scope: remove the Alt+Z shortcut; keep the chooser as the internal pending-tab
picker; update EON-C18, EON-C10, CONFIGURATION, USAGE, shortcut help and
CHANGELOG.

Out of scope: the chooser's own keys (EON-C18 picker behavior); the Yazi popup.

## Acceptance

- Lucca approved the contract text.
- Alt+Z does nothing in Eon and appears in no help or hints; startup and
  Alt+Shift+T still open the chooser; Esc still starts the first pane at the
  starting folder.
- Configuration that binds Alt+Z to a custom popup is accepted.

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test` for affected crates.
- Profile refresh plus one isolated installed observation.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop before code until the contract text is approved.
- Stop if a shortcut-less entry needs an unapproved EONW change.
close_reason: Superseded by eon-quick-search-parity-23y9; 23y9.2 retires the chooser. Lucca approved, 2026-10-23 ('4. ok').

comments.text:
Deferred (Lucca, 2026-10-21). Keep Alt+Z for now and decide by dogfooding Files plus Alt+Enter (ecne.1/ecne.4, landed bf13705 and cbe397c).

Why:
- Removal saves little: the chooser stays for pending tabs either way, so only the catalog entry and its help rows go.
- Alt+Z is the fastest route for the common case of jumping the tab to a known project: Alt+Z, letters, Enter. Through Files the same jump takes Alt+Shift+Y, Tab, letters, Alt+Enter, then closing the popup.
- Files is better for browsing, so the two overlap less than the epic assumed.

Resume rule:
- If Alt+Z stops being used, do this bead as written.
- If it keeps being used, close this bead as won't-do, amend the epic's "Alt+Z is removed" decision, and file a Nova twin to add an equivalent workspace shortcut. That twin should note how it differs from the in-Yazi Alt Z search that Nova rejected in docs/ideation/yazi-keymap.md, and pick a key that fits Zellij.

title: Set the tab folder with Alt+Enter in the Yazi popup
description:
## Why

See the parent epic. Alt+Enter in the Yazi popup becomes Eon's one way to change
an established tab's folder, as in Yazelix Nova (NOVA-TAB-WORKSPACE-001).

## Evidence

- `docs/USAGE.md:216`: `eon tab directory TAB [--json] -- DIRECTORY` already
  sets a tab folder through the supervisor.
- Popup terminals receive no tab identity today, so a popup cannot name its tab.
  Using the active tab instead would race with tab switches; the popup must
  target the exact tab it belongs to.
- Nova reference (nova repo `0c3fa126`): `docs/ideation/yazi-keymap.md` (F+),
  `defaults/yazi/` Alt Enter plugin: hovered directory, else Yazi's current one;
  in quick search, the selected result.

## Scope

In scope: pass the owning tab's identity to popup terminals; a Yazi Alt+Enter
action in the popup config that calls `eon tab directory`; footer hint;
success/error feedback.

Out of scope: the popup itself (child 1); Agent/Git effects (`eon-tbn1`);
Alt+Z (child 3).

## Acceptance

- Lucca approved the contract text.
- Alt+Enter sets the exact owning tab's folder to the hovered directory (else
  the current one), or in search to the selected result; the tab label updates;
  Yazi does not move; other processes stay in place.
- Switching tabs never redirects the change; a vanished folder or a closed tab
  fails clearly and changes nothing.

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime` for the tab identity.
- Profile refresh plus one isolated installed observation.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop before code until the contract text is approved.
- Stop if the tab identity needs an EONW change the user has not approved.
close_reason: Alt+Enter in Files sets the owning tab's folder via EON_TAB with an ownership check; EON-C10 amended and proven (automated + installed), see proof comment

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Decision (Lucca, 2026-10-21): contract approved.

1. Tab identity: every popup terminal's environment carries EON_TAB, its owning tab's tN id. Tab ids are stable and never reused, and a popup never changes tab, so there is no race with tab switches and no EONW change. Rejected: active-tab targeting (racy); extending EON_TERMINAL caller resolution to SetTabDirectory (needs an EONW change, and v14 is reserved by yx8.7).
2. The Files launcher (Tool::Files) exports the running eon executable (current_exe, as windows.rs does) for the plugin, so the plugin calls the same build as the supervisor even when `eon` is not on PATH.
3. Alt+Enter runs `eon tab directory "$EON_TAB" -- DIR`. DIR is the hovered folder if one is hovered, else Yazi's cwd; in search (fzf --expect=alt-enter), the selected result. Yazi does not move. A Yazi notification reports success or the CLI's error, and a failure changes nothing. It follows Nova's tab-workspace plugin (3325ef5d).
4. Footers: browse " Alt+Enter Set tab folder · Tab/Z Search · Shift+Tab Spot"; search "Enter Go here · Alt+Enter Set tab folder · Tab/Esc Browse Yazi".
5. Approved EON-C10 text:
   - "Every popup terminal's environment also carries `EON_TAB`, the `tN` identity of the tab that owns it."
   - "In Files, Alt+Enter sets the owning tab's directory, as `eon tab directory` with its `EON_TAB` would, to the hovered folder, else Yazi's current folder, or in search to the selected result; Yazi does not move. A notification reports the result, and a failure changes nothing. The footers name Alt+Enter."

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Correction (eon-2e, 2026-10-21, from Claude review R1): decision 1's premise was wrong. Tab ids ARE reused after a supervisor recovery: with_recovered_sessions puts every recovered terminal in one t1 with next_tab 2, so a recovered Files Yazi becomes a pane and keeps a stale EON_TAB. Fix within the approved text: the tab-folder plugin first checks, through `eon workspace --json`, that tab EON_TAB still lists a popup whose session is this terminal's (the EON_TERMINAL prefix). Otherwise it refuses with a notification and changes nothing. Session ids are unique while the terminal lives, so a recovered terminal never passes. A small check-then-act window remains (the tab must be closed and an id reused within it); accepted. Wording: EON_TAB names the tab that owned the terminal 'when it started', and EON-C10 states the refusal. Also: EON_TAB is stripped from Venus and CodexBar like EON_TERMINAL. Accepted gaps: Alt+Enter in Yazi virtual views (search://, archives) fails with the CLI's error, as in Nova; the Project picker also gets EON_TAB (consistent with 'every popup terminal'); no unit test for EON_FILES_CLI (same gap as ecne.1's env).

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Proof (eon-2e, 2026-10-21). The revision is this bead's closing commit. The code tree is a63f265690954e25c8e4ef00ab98bc6f94b0d6fa on base 2ef871f; the commit adds only this proof text.

- Automated: run in a clean `git archive` export of a63f265.
  - `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime -p eon` passed: eon-runtime 55/55, including `files_keeps_its_terminal_across_retargets` (popup Start carries tab t1) and `orbit_uses_configured_argv_only_for_default_sessions` (EON_TAB is removed by default and set when given); workspace_control 38/38.
  - clippy `-D warnings` and `fmt --check` passed.
  - `nix build .#default .#eonbase` passed.
- Installed: the package built from that export, /nix/store/l5ss1z32rbzzk13qgl4aqqaiv6m2jn35-eon-0.1.1, ran on an isolated private headless Sway (x86_64 Linux, pixman).
  1. In Files at work/, Alt+Enter on the hovered aproj set t1 to work/aproj. Yazi stayed at work/, and a "Set to …" notification appeared.
  2. In the Tab search, "zzz" plus Alt+Enter (no match) returned quietly; t1 was unchanged.
  3. In the Tab search, "other" plus Alt+Enter set t1 to ~/other. This is the require("tab-folder") path.
  4. After a SIGKILL of the supervisor and an `eon` relaunch, the Files Yazi was recovered as pane p2 in t1. Alt+Enter in it showed "This Yazi is no longer a popup of tab t1", and t1 was unchanged.
  The isolated session was cleaned up with no leftover processes.
  An earlier candidate run (4b3e968) also showed EON_TAB=t1 and EON_FILES_CLI in the Yazi env. The CLI errors went to stderr: invalid-directory exited 1, unknown-tab exited 3.
- Ledger: Claude review rounds: 3.
  - R1: 1 blocking (tab ids are reused after supervisor recovery, so a stale EON_TAB could retarget an unrelated tab). Fixed by the ownership check, the contract wording, and stripping EON_TAB from Venus/CodexBar.
  - R2: 1 blocking (Alt+Enter on a search with no match made fzf exit 1 and showed an empty error). Fixed, along with reporting `eon workspace` failures accurately.

title: Help agents use Eon: skill, onboarding guide, more agents
description:
## Why
Rex ships an agent skill plus a session-start hook for Claude, Codex, OpenCode and Pi; herdr
documents how to add support for an agent and recognizes about 23; T3 Code offers Cursor and
Antigravity. Eon's Agent popup knows five (`codex resume`, `grok`, `opencode`, `pi`, `claude
--resume`: eon/crates/eon/src/product.rs:138-144, docs/CONFIGURATION.md:334) and its attention
works only for agents that speak OSC 7501 (ORB-C15: "OSC 7501 is the sole source of program
status"). There is no public onboarding doc or skill. Cheap, and it makes agents use Eon well.
Source: competitor audit eon-r6yt (2026-10-29), reports in ~/pjs/refs/competitor-audit-2026-10/.
Lucca, 2026-10-29: "file the beads". Filing only; no work is approved yet beyond planning.

## Children (each self-contained)
1. eon-ed9d.1: an Eon skill and opt-in session-start hook that teach agents the eon CLI.
2. eon-ed9d.2: a public "add Eon support to your agent" guide.
3. eon-ed9d.3: more agents in the Agent popup's auto command.
4. eon-ed9d.4: decide how Eon shows attention for agents that do not speak OSC 7501.
"Recognize more agents" in the original bead meant both .3 (launch) and .4 (attention); they have
different owners and contracts, so they are separate.

## Contracts
EON-C8 (Agent popup runtime policy), EON-C31 and ORB-C15 (attention, OSC 7501), EON-C10 (CLI);
docs otherwise.

## Acceptance (epic)
Children closed. Site text follows the release per AGENTS.md "Website".

title: Ship an Eon skill and opt-in session-start hook that teach agents the eon CLI
description:
## Why
Agents running in Eon do not know they can open panes, read the workspace or jump attention through
`eon`, so people have to tell them each session. Rex's `rex skill setup` installs a skill for Claude
Code, Codex, OpenCode and Pi and a session-start hook that tells the agent its session and has it
label it (~/pjs/refs/competitor-audit-2026-10/rex.md:34). Parent: eon-ed9d.

## Scope
In scope: one SKILL.md (provider-neutral text: `EON_TERMINAL`, IDs, `--no-focus`, `--json`, exit
codes, `eon workspace`, `eon pane create`, attention jumps, the Humans and Agents rule's "leave the
person's focus alone"), and an optional session-start hook for Claude Code and Codex that says the
agent runs in Eon and which pane it is. Decide at the contract step how it is delivered: a file in
the repository and package plus documented manual install (docs only), or an `eon` command that
installs it (EON-C10 amendment, consequential: it writes agents' settings, so opt-in only, never
automatic, and reversible).
Out of scope: attention reporting (agents report status themselves through OSC 7501; see
eon-ed9d.4), MCP (eon-ciwn.3), changes to Starcompass skills.

## Reference gate
docs/REFERENCES.md "How should Eon package provider-neutral operating guidance and liaison policy
around existing coding agents?" (firstmate: distribution evidence, not a template), Rex's skill and
hook at a recorded revision. eon-0hvl (pstack evaluation) is related; reuse its findings if done.

## Acceptance
- AP-TEST-001 behaviour check: a fresh Claude Code and a fresh Codex session in an isolated Eon,
  with the skill installed and given a representative task ("start a shell running X beside you
  without disturbing me") and no hint about `eon`, use the eon CLI correctly (pane created, focus
  unchanged). Transcript summary recorded here.
- The skill text matches current commands (AP-CONTRACT-001: docs aligned with commands and flags).

## Verification
- Docs-only delivery: changed paths and diff plus the behaviour check above.
- If an installer command ships: focused process test on the real binary and one isolated installed
  dogfood observation.

title: Publish an 'add Eon support to your agent' guide
description:
## Why
herdr publishes "add herdr support to your agent" and invites agent authors in. Eon's attention
works for any agent that speaks OSC 7501 (Program Status Protocol rev 0.4, ORB-C15), but nothing
public tells agent authors that or how to use the CLI. Parent: eon-ed9d.

## Scope
In scope: one guide in the repository (path decided with eon-readme-agent-workspace-06m3, which
moves user docs to eonterm.com) covering: OSC 7501 reports Eon reads and how they map to EON-C31
states (needs input, error, finished, working, background, idle), the bounds (`app` 32, `title` 96,
`msg` 256 bytes), `EON_TERMINAL`, the eon CLI for agents, and how to test support in Eon. Linked
from the README.
Out of scope: new protocol features; site text (eon-site, after the release).

## Acceptance
- The guide exists, every claim matches ORB-C15, EON-C31 and docs/USAGE.md at the current revision,
  every link resolves, and the README links it.

## Verification
Docs-only route: changed Markdown paths and diff, links checked, claims checked against the
contracts; no runtime profile refresh.

title: Offer more terminal agents in the Agent popup's auto command
description:
## Why
Eon's Agent popup `auto` command tries `codex resume`, `grok`, `opencode`, `pi` and `claude
--resume` in that order (eon/crates/eon/src/product.rs:138-144, docs/CONFIGURATION.md:334).
Users of other terminal agents get nothing unless they set `[popups.agent] command` by hand.
herdr knows about 23 agents; T3 Code offers Cursor and Antigravity. Parent: eon-ed9d.

## Scope
In scope: add terminal agents with a CLI and a resume form to the `auto` list. Candidates from the
audit: Cursor's CLI agent, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot CLI, Amp, Droid, Kimi, Kiro; Antigravity only
if it has a terminal agent. Pick by evidence (installed base, a stable executable name and resume
flag); record the order rule. Update EON-C8's "accepted Nova order" text if the order changes
(contract text: Lucca approves). Configurability: decide whether the `auto` list itself becomes
configurable or record why `[popups.agent] command` suffices.
Out of scope: attention for agents without OSC 7501 (eon-ed9d.4); Eon Bar quota for new providers.

## Acceptance
- Each added agent, when it is the first one found on PATH, starts from the Agent popup in an
  isolated installed run; docs/CONFIGURATION.md lists the new order.

## Verification
One-owned-default route: the cheapest consuming check (the auto-selection test in the eon crate via
`nix develop -c eon-test -p eon`) plus the affected build, and one isolated installed observation.

title: Decide how Eon shows attention for agents that do not speak OSC 7501
description:
## Why
Eon's attention sidebar and Alt+G work only for programs that emit OSC 7501 (ORB-C15: "OSC 7501 is
the sole source of program status"); Claude Code 2.1.295+ and Codex 0.163+ do. herdr covers about
23 agents by screen inference from remote TOML manifests plus a `pane report-agent` CLI for agents
that report lifecycle (~/pjs/refs/competitor-audit-2026-10/herdr.md:25). Parent: eon-ed9d.

## Decision question
How should agents that do not speak OSC 7501 get attention in Eon? Options:
1. Nothing new: agents adopt OSC 7501; eon-ed9d.2 invites them.
2. Per-agent hook shims (agents with hook systems emit OSC 7501 from their hooks), shipped with the
   eon-ed9d.1 skill/hook.
3. An `eon` CLI report path (like herdr's `pane report-agent`) that writes a status record for the
   caller's terminal: a new attention source, so an EON-C31 and possibly ORB-C15 change.
4. Screen inference: rejected by default. docs/REFERENCES.md routes reject screen and stall
   classification as semantic truth, and ORB-C15 makes OSC 7501 the sole source.

## Acceptance
Decision recorded with reasons; any contract change drafted for Lucca and any implementation bead
proposed, not filed before approval.

## Verification
Planning route: bead state only.

title: Start an agent's tab in its own git worktree
description:
## Why
T3 Code, herdr and Amp give each agent task its own git worktree or branch, with per-turn diff
review and restore. In Eon, agents share the checkout unless the person sets worktrees up by hand.
Source: competitor audit eon-r6yt (2026-10-29), reports in ~/pjs/refs/competitor-audit-2026-10/.
Lucca, 2026-10-29: "file the beads". Filing only; no work is approved yet beyond planning.

## Contracts
- EON-C8 (Durable tab and pane workspace): tab identity and the tab header, which already shows
  the launch directory's leaf, so a worktree tab shows its worktree folder name.
- EON-C17 (Tab launch directory) and EON-C18 (Picker-first tab directories): a worktree tab sets
  its launch directory without the picker, like eon-tab-create-launch-8tl4.
- EON-C10 (Typed workspace control): the CLI path. A new EON-C, or amendments to these, needs
  Lucca's approval. Consequential if Eon persists a tab-to-worktree binding or deletes files.

## Ownership
Git owns worktrees and branches; Eon only orchestrates (create, bind to a tab, clean up). The
Humans and Agents rule applies: the window action ships with or after its CLI path.

## Children (each self-contained)
1. eon-el45.1: research and draft the worktree-tab contract (planning only).
2. eon-el45.2: create a tab in a new worktree from the eon CLI.
3. eon-el45.3: the window action for it, and the tab's worktree shown if the header leaf is not
   enough.
4. eon-el45.4: remove a clean worktree when its tab closes; keep and report a dirty one.
5. eon-el45.5: decide whether Eon owns per-turn diff review and restore or hosts a tool for it.
Children .2 to .5 are provisional: el45.1's approved contract may reshape them.

## Related
eon-az9 (deferred P4) decides isolated execution targets (containers, microVMs) for security; a
worktree is not a security boundary, so it neither supersedes nor needs az9. eon-0hvl evaluates an
agent-workflow kit only.

## Acceptance (epic)
An agent or person creates a tab in a new worktree in one action; the tab shows which worktree it
is on; closing a clean one removes it; a dirty one is kept and reported. Children closed.

## Scope
Reference route: docs/REFERENCES.md "How should Eon present an isolated agent attempt from launch
through review without equating it with the durable work item?" (Superset: study
work-to-worktree, diff, handoff; reject an Eon-owned Git, PR service or merge policy).

title: Research agent worktrees and draft the worktree-tab contract
description:
## Why
Before any code, settle who creates and removes worktrees, where they live, how a tab binds to one,
and what happens on close, recovery and reboot. Parent: eon-el45 (competitor audit eon-r6yt).

## Deliverable (research and contract draft only; no product code)
Recorded on this bead:
1. References at recorded revisions: T3 Code, herdr and Amp worktree flows
   (~/pjs/refs/competitor-audit-2026-10/), the docs/REFERENCES.md Superset route, and `git
   worktree` itself (add, remove, prune, lock; behaviour with submodules and a dirty tree).
2. Shape: CLI sketch (for example `eon tab create --worktree [BRANCH] [-- COMMAND]`, building on
   eon-tab-create-launch-8tl4's `--directory`), where worktrees live and how they are named, branch
   creation rules, and whether Eon persists a tab-to-worktree binding (lifecycle and recovery under
   EON-C15 and eon-reboot-restore-im8y) or derives it from the launch directory.
3. Cleanup: "clean" defined exactly (no uncommitted, untracked or unpushed work?), what is reported
   for a dirty one, and that Eon never deletes work without the person's or agent's request.
4. Configurability (AGENTS.md): worktree location and naming defaults in docs/CONFIGURATION.md or
   a recorded reason to keep them fixed.
5. Contract draft (new EON-C or amendments to EON-C8/EON-C10/EON-C17/EON-C18) and confirmation or
   revision of children el45.2 to .5.

## Acceptance
- Findings, owners and decisions recorded with reasons; Lucca approves or revises the contract
  draft and the child split.

## Verification
Planning route: bead state and recorded research; no runtime profile refresh.

## Stop conditions
Stop for Lucca before any contract or code change.

title: Create a tab in a new git worktree from the eon CLI
description:
## Why
An agent (or a script) should start work in its own worktree with one command instead of sharing
the checkout. Parent: eon-el45.

## Scope
In scope: the CLI path approved in eon-el45.1, for example `eon tab create --worktree [BRANCH]
[--no-focus] [--json] [-- COMMAND]`: run `git worktree add` for the caller's repository (Git stays
the owner), create a tab with that launch directory and no picker, optionally run COMMAND as its
first pane, never move the person's active tab or desktop focus unless asked; JSON names the tab and
the worktree path. Failures (not a git repo, branch exists, git fails) are reported with EON-C10
exit codes and leave no half-created tab.
Out of scope: the window action (el45.3), cleanup (el45.4), diff review (el45.5).

## Prerequisites
Blocked by eon-el45.1 (approved contract) and eon-tab-create-launch-8tl4 (tab with a directory and
command, no picker).

## Acceptance
- From an Eon terminal in a repo, one command creates a worktree and a tab on it running the given
  command; `git worktree list` shows it; focus is unchanged; the failure cases above behave as the
  contract says.

## Verification
- Focused process tests on the real binary via `nix develop -c eon-test -p <crate>`.
- Installed runtime route: profile refresh plus one isolated installed dogfood observation.

title: Add a window action for a worktree tab and show its worktree
description:
## Why
The Humans and Agents rule pairs window actions with CLI paths; a person should get a worktree tab
as easily as an agent. Parent: eon-el45.

## Scope
In scope: a window action (key or entry in an existing popup or picker, as eon-el45.1 decides) that
calls the same Runtime action as eon-el45.2; its key configurable with the default documented in
docs/CONFIGURATION.md (Configurability rule) and listed in the Shortcuts viewer (EON-C20/VEN-C20);
showing the worktree or branch on the tab only if el45.1 decides the EON-C8 header leaf is not
enough (VEN-C8 presentation).
Out of scope: CLI (el45.2), cleanup (el45.4).

## Prerequisites
Blocked by eon-el45.2.

## Acceptance
- In installed Eon, the action creates a worktree tab without moving desktop focus; the tab shows
  which worktree it is on; the key is rebindable.

## Verification
Installed UI route: affected profile refresh plus one isolated installed dogfood observation.

title: Remove a clean worktree when its tab closes; keep and report a dirty one
description:
## Why
Worktrees left behind pile up; deleting a dirty one loses work. Parent: eon-el45.

## Scope
In scope: when a tab created on an Eon worktree closes (by key or `eon tab close`), remove the
worktree with `git worktree remove` only if it is clean by eon-el45.1's definition; otherwise keep
it and report it (CLI result and a VEN-C8 notice), never deleting work. The same rule from the CLI.
Out of scope: branches (deleting a branch needs its own decision), worktrees Eon did not create.

## Prerequisites
Blocked by eon-el45.2. Consequential (deletes files): the reference gate in el45.1 covers it.

## Acceptance
- Closing a clean worktree tab removes the worktree (`git worktree list` no longer shows it);
  closing a dirty one keeps it and reports why; both from the window and from the CLI.

## Verification
- Focused tests of the clean/dirty rule against real git repos in the owning crate via
  `nix develop -c eon-test -p <crate>`.
- One isolated installed dogfood observation.

title: Decide whether Eon owns per-turn diff review and restore
description:
## Why
T3 Code and Amp review each agent turn's diff and restore earlier states. With worktrees, Eon could
own this, host an existing tool (lazygit is already the Git popup), or leave it to agents.
Parent: eon-el45 (its "later slice").

## Decision question
Does Eon own per-turn diff review and restore, host an existing tool for it, or leave it out? What
is a "turn" without parsing agent output (docs/REFERENCES.md agent-integration routes reject
screen inference)?

## Constraints
The Superset route rejects an Eon-owned Git, PR service or merge policy; eon-gllr decides git
actions beyond lazygit, so keep the two consistent.

## Prerequisites
Blocked by eon-el45.1.

## Acceptance
Decision recorded with reasons; any follow-up proposed to Lucca, not filed before approval.

## Verification
Planning route: bead state only.

title: Say so when Alt+G or Alt+Shift+G finds no agent needing attention
description:
## Why

Lucca pressed Alt+G and Alt+Shift+G in his window on 2026-10-23 and reported "alt g and alt shift g are doing nothing in this window". Every agent there was working, so the attention queue was empty. EON-C31 says "An empty queue is EON-C10's unchanged-snapshot no-op" (docs/CONTRACTS.md:2353), and the yx8.9 proof recorded "On an empty queue, Alt+G and Alt+Shift+G changed nothing." That is correct to the contract, but a key that silently does nothing looks broken. Lucca approved the fix the same day ("1 do it", answering the overseer's item: "on an empty queue, Alt+G and Alt+Shift+G show a short notice, 'No agent needs attention', in the existing Venus notice style, without stealing focus"). He did not take the alternative of falling back to working agents.

## Contract (bring exact text to the overseer before code)

- EON-C31 NextAttention and PreviousAttention: replace the empty-queue no-op with a result the person can see, for example "On an empty queue, the window shows the notice 'No agent needs attention'; focus, selection and the cursor are unchanged."
- Pick the owner at the reference gate. Either the Runtime answers an empty-queue NextAttention or PreviousAttention with a typed, non-error outcome (which may be an EONW change and a version bump) and Venus renders it as a VEN-C8 notice, or Venus decides locally from the snapshot. Venus deciding locally is only acceptable if the snapshot carries enough to reproduce the queue exactly, including seen raises; otherwise it creates a second owner of the queue (AP-OWNERSHIP-001). Prefer the Runtime owning the answer.
- The notice never takes desktop or keyboard focus and never changes Orbit state.

## Scope

In scope: the contract text, the mechanism, the Venus notice, tests, and VEN-C30 and USAGE lines if they describe Alt+G.

Out of scope: changing what the queue holds, and falling back to working agents.

## Acceptance

- A test shows that an empty queue yields the notice and leaves focus, selection and the cursor unchanged.
- One installed observation: with only working agents, Alt+G shows the notice.

## Verification

The affected Rust surfaces (and Nix, if EONW changes), converge plus Codex, the profile refresh, and one isolated installed observation.

title: Remove an ended window's runtime directory without racing window new
description:
## Why

eon-reattach-after-upgrade-n5qv lists ended windows as ended (Lucca approved choice 4(a) on 2026-10-23, "agree to everything") and leaves their runtime directories in place. Over time, ended window directories pile up in the runtime dir and in `eon windows` output. eon-90 found that removing a window root races `eon window new`'s reservation of a window ID, so removal needs its own lock design.

## Scope

In scope: when a window's last supervisor exits, or on an explicit cleanup, remove that window's runtime directory safely against a concurrent `window new` reservation and a concurrent attach. Contract text (EON-C23 or EON-C11) goes to the overseer or Lucca before code.

Out of scope: n5qv's attach delegation and listing.

## Acceptance

- A test shows an ended window's directory is removed, and a concurrent `window new` never gets a half-removed or reused root.

## Verification

`nix develop -c eon-test -p eon -p eon-runtime`, converge plus Codex.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Constraint from eon-90 (n5qv, 2026-10-23): `eon windows` briefly lists a window as ended while its supervisor is still starting, because the window dir exists before the socket. Removal must never treat a starting window as ended: guard it with launch.log plus the lifecycle lock, or a start grace period.

title: Keep a slow-starting Eon window from being killed at startup admission under load
description:
## Why

An Eon window can fail to open when the machine is busy. Lucca approved filing this on 2026-10-22.

## Evidence

- eon-c1, during eon-0ka6's isolated installed proof on 2026-10-22, on private headless Sway 1.12 with pixman: the first
  launch at load 16 failed with `cannot admit Eon Desktop presentation: EAGAIN`, and Venus was
  SIGKILLed after 5 s. A relaunch at load 5 worked. The record is on eon-0ka6.
- Cause, from reading the code at 3afd58a:
  - `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/supervisor.rs` `PresentationProcess::start` waits for Venus's
    `ready-v1` reply with a read timeout bounded by a deadline of `SESSION_START_TIMEOUT` (5 s,
    supervisor.rs:43).
  - When that read times out, the `WouldBlock` error prints as EAGAIN, and the supervisor stops
    Venus (`stop(&mut process.child)`).
  - So under load, native startup (Wayland connection, Vulkan device, fonts, first frame) can take
    longer than 5 s, and Eon kills a healthy but slow window.
- Not yet established: whether the 5 s also bounds a user's real launch on COSMIC, and how long
  Venus startup takes at idle and under load.

## Owner and contracts

- Runtime owns the presentation admission deadline and its error. Venus owns how fast it reaches
  readiness.
- Read the contracts that own startup admission before choosing a fix:
  - EON-C19 in docs/CONTRACTS.md, which consumes Venus startup admission. Its proof includes
    `startup_snapshot_transfer_uses_the_admission_deadline`.
  - VEN-C19 in venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md.
  - venus/docs/LAUNCH.md.
- A changed deadline or new startup behavior is a contract change that needs Lucca's approval
  first.

## Scope

- Measure Venus startup-to-ready at idle and under a reproducible load (e.g. `stress-ng` or a
  parallel cargo build) in an isolated headless Sway.
- Choose the fix at its owner:
  - a deadline that tolerates a slow but progressing Venus;
  - faster readiness;
  - or a clearer error that names the timeout.

Out of scope: other workspace-exchange timeouts (eon-workspace-action-timeout-287o is closed).

## Acceptance

- A red/green reproduction at the cheapest harness, the existing presentation admission tests in
  `eon/crates/eon/tests/workspace_control.rs` if a slow fake Venus can express it.
- One isolated installed observation under load where the window opens.
- Review loop per AGENTS.md; profile refresh.

A Venus crash or rejection closes stdout and fails at once on EOF, so the deadline only bounds a hung or very slow Venus.
Decision (Lucca, 2026-10-22): change EON-C19 so Venus startup admission has its own 30 s deadline, separate from the 5 s session-start timeout; reopen clients wait just past it; a timeout reports that Venus was not ready within 30 s instead of EAGAIN. EON-C15's Stop read timeout text becomes one preceding thirty-second operation plus five-second cleanup and a one-second margin (36 s). title: Show a busy agent as working when an older unseen finish sits on the same terminal
description:
## Problem

Lucca, 2026-10-27, in his live Eon (build 11905dd, EONW v20): "in the sidebar, both other agents
were showing green [checkmark]. only for them to update their state in the sidebar after i clicked
them." Both agents (Claude Code in panes p54 and p55) were busy at the time. Edge b8533b6 behaves the
same; delivery is not the cause (the supervisor polls every terminal at 2 Hz and Venus inspects every
250 ms, with no focus filter).

Cause, from a coordinator investigation (paths relative to the repo):
- A terminal can hold several OSC 7501 program-status records (Orbit keeps one per id,
  orbit/src/status.rs). The sidebar's "+N" counts the others; p55 showed "+1".
- EON-C31's normalization (docs/CONTRACTS.md, "Agent attention", around lines 2446-2494;
  runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/attention.rs:108-146) ranks Finished above Working, and
  `most_urgent` takes `min_by_key((state, Reverse(changed)))`.
- A finished raise becomes seen only by focus while a Venus is attached (attention.rs:336-399).
- So an older unseen `done` record (Finished, green check) hides a newer `working` record (blue
  spinner) on the same terminal until the user focuses or clicks it. For a single record, done then
  working already gives Working with no raise (attention.rs:298-306).
- Unknown: what Claude Code's second record on p55 is (a subagent or background task under its own
  id, or an earlier program). The CLI JSON omits record ids and count (eon-agent-parity-a9g0.2).

## Expected

A busy agent always shows as working. When a terminal has a Working record that changed more
recently than its unseen Finished raise, the terminal shows Working, and that older raise counts as
seen (so it does not reappear when the work stops). A real finish after the work still raises the
green check as today. Needs input and Error keep their current priority and are not cleared this way.

## Approval

Approved by Lucca 2026-10-27, relayed by eon-overseer. Asked: "1. When a terminal reports
'working' more recently than its unseen 'finished', show working and treat the older finish as
seen. 2. Find out what Claude's second record is (dump the raw records from Orbit) as part of the
same bead. 3. One small bead, started after the two image beads land." Lucca: "yes". This covers the
EON-C31 normalization and seen wording that rule 1 needs. Record the exact adopted contract text on
this bead; any further contract change beyond rule 1 needs Lucca's approval.

## Contract

EON-C31 (Agent attention): Normalization and Seen paragraphs. No wire change expected (the rule
lives in eon-runtime's attention presenter); if one turns out to be needed, stop and ask.

## Prerequisites

- Start after orb-j2i.8 and orb-j2i.11 land (proof-slot scheduling, not a code dependency).
- Read EON-C31 in full and runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/attention.rs.

## Steps

1. Diagnose: in an isolated Eon (headless Sway recipe, never Lucca's running Eon), run Claude Code
   with a subagent or background task and dump the raw ORB-C15 ProgramStatus records of its
   terminal, to name the second record. Record the finding on this bead.
2. Implement rule 1 in eon-runtime's attention (the supervisor-side normalization/seen bookkeeping),
   one owner, no Venus logic.
3. Adopt the EON-C31 wording; update docs/CONTRACTS.md and CHANGELOG.md (user-visible).

## Acceptance

- A unit test in eon-runtime's attention module: terminal with an unseen done record and a newer
  working record presents Working; after the working record goes idle/done again, a new raise shows
  Finished; an older working record does not hide a newer unseen finish.
- The existing attention tests stay green (`nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime`).
- One isolated installed observation: two status records on one terminal (e.g. printf OSC 7501 from
  two ids, or the Claude case from step 1) show the spinner without a click.
- Review per AGENTS.md (converge plus Codex).

## Scope boundary

Only the Finished-versus-Working rule across records of one terminal. Not: sounds or notifications
(eon-iwmz, eon-2kvr), exposing record ids in the CLI (eon-agent-parity-a9g0.2), staleness timing.
close_reason: Rule 1 implemented in eon-runtime attention with EON-C31/C33 wording approved by Lucca (relayed); tests, isolated installed before/after proof and review recorded in comments.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Reference gate (AP-REFERENCE-001; consequential because it changes the EON-C31 contract). Recorded by eon-54, 2026-10-27, before landing.

- User-visible behavior: when a `working` record of a terminal changed later, by ORB-C15 change sequence, than the raise of a finished record (`done` or raised `idle`) of the same terminal, the terminal shows working and that raise is seen, so it does not return when the work stops. A finish raised after the work's last change still shows. Error and needs input are untouched.
- One owner: Eon Runtime's attention presenter (`runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/attention.rs`, `Terminal::see_finishes_before_work`, run on every applied reply). Each `Raise` now records the change sequence it raised at, so an `idle` that inherits its `done`'s raise compares at the `done`'s sequence. Orbit's records and Venus are unchanged. No wire change: EONW still carries the normalized state.
- Routes read: docs/REFERENCES.md "How should Venus direct human attention across many agent-bearing workspaces..." (owner: Eon attention semantics; prefer structured events and exact identities). Comparable implementation: herdr at `143bf5fd4781`, `src/client/shell/endpoint_agent_state.rs:81-84`: a pane reporting Working removes its pending completion, and only a later Idle/Done raises again. That is the same rule (new work supersedes an unseen completion). herdr has one status per pane; Eon applies it across a terminal's records by change sequence.
- Constraints kept: seen stays keyed by (run, id, raise); errors and needs input are never cleared by work; ORB-C15 change sequences are terminal-wide (`orbit/src/status.rs:153-160`), so they order records exactly; fixed `Instant`s are not used for the ordering, because they come from ms ages taken at different receipts.
- Rejected: (a) a Venus-side rule (it would add a second owner; Venus never normalizes); (b) only reordering Working above Finished in normalization (a raise would come back unseen when the work stops, which the approval excludes); (c) comparing the finished record's current change rather than its raise (an `idle` that inherits a `done` raise would compare too late).

title: Accept native terminal text selection in Eon
description:
## Outcome and contract

Accept one exact Orbit and Venus pair that makes terminal text selection usable in installed Eon:

- Drag selects cells.
- Double-click and double-drag select words.
- Triple-click and triple-drag select logical lines.
- Terminal-owned mouse input remains unchanged; Shift forces host selection.
- Release copies to the Wayland primary selection.
- `Ctrl+Shift+C` copies to the ordinary clipboard.

Eon owns only exact component selection, launch integration, update policy, installed proof, and product defaults. Orbit Bead `orb-orbit-native-selection-gestures-qf3` owns terminal semantics. Venus Bead `ven-venus-native-selection-gestures-d3x` owns native input and clipboard effects.

This behavior refreshes the exact installed proofs for the existing EON-C1 through EON-C4 product contracts; it does not create an Eon-owned selection contract.

## Prerequisites and references

Required accepted children:

1. Eon Sessions `orb-orbit-native-selection-gestures-qf3`: exact ORBS and ORB-C9 selection proof.
2. Eon Desktop `ven-venus-native-selection-gestures-d3x`: exact VEN-C7 native input and Wayland clipboard proof.

Before implementation, compare the component manifest pins with both latest accepted child revisions and record the exact identities. Reuse the references and decisions recorded by the child owners. Inspect Eon's manifest, lock, Nix composition, launcher surfaces, profile update path, current EON-C1 through EON-C4 proof, and every packaged Eon, EonTerm, and Eonova entry point.

Impact: HIGH for daily terminal use. Effort: S after both children are accepted. Risk: LOW because Eon adds no selection mechanism. Confidence: HIGH.

## Implementation

1. Wait for both child Beads to close with immutable accepted revisions.
2. Update the canonical component graph and exact lock identities together; add no patch, adapter, fallback, feature flag, or duplicated schema.
3. Build and refresh the active Eon profile from the working tree without stopping live Sessions.
4. Verify each installed launcher consumes the just-built profile artifact.
5. Refresh EON-C1 through EON-C4 proof records, changelog, and LOC only for the accepted exact composition.

## Acceptance

- Manifest, lock, Cargo, and Nix identities resolve to the accepted Orbit and Venus revisions.
- Installed Eon and EonTerm demonstrate cell, word, and logical-line press-drag selection.
- A mouse-reporting application receives ordinary pointer input; Shift performs host selection.
- Release provides the exact frozen text through Wayland primary paste in another application.
- `Ctrl+Shift+C` updates the ordinary clipboard without conflating it with primary selection.
- Eonova launches against the same accepted Eon profile and demonstrates the same boundary.
- Closing and reopening launch surfaces preserves normal lifecycle behavior and does not disturb existing Sessions.
- The full affected Rust and Nix route, profile identity check, installed Wayland dogfood, governance checks, and `git diff --check` pass on one immutable candidate.
- Closure records exact Eon, Orbit, Venus, ORBS, package, profile, compositor, and platform identities plus user acceptance and remaining limits.

## Scope and stop conditions

In scope: exact child pins, canonical component graph and lock, Nix composition, installed launch surfaces, EON-C1 through EON-C4 proof refresh, changelog, LOC, and one accepted Wayland dogfood pass.

Out of scope: Eon-owned selection code, protocol translation, compatibility support, configuration, custom boundaries or timing, middle-click paste, right-click extension, block selection, drag autoscroll, OSC 133 command-output selection, other display systems, and other operating systems.

Stop if either child proof is incomplete or stale; if composition needs an Eon-side behavior patch, adapter, or second schema; if the profile cannot resolve exactly to the candidate; or if another active frontier owns the component graph.

title: Show the last quota reading in a new Eon session until a fresh read succeeds
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-10-22: after starting a new Eon session the Claude chips were missing (screenshot: only
Codex, CPU, RAM and clock). Decision, Lucca 2026-10-22: "just show the old value while it doesn't
[get] the new value".

## Evidence (eon-78, 2026-10-22)

- The new supervisor g1-a8951bc5... started 12:09:43 -03 with the default `[bar] widgets`.
- At 12:12 the same CodexBar call Eon makes (`CodexBarCLI usage --provider claude --source oauth
  --format json --json-only --web-timeout 8`, codexbar 0.74.1) answered once with both windows, then
  twice with `{"error":{"message":"Claude OAuth usage endpoint is rate limited by Anthropic right
  now...","code":3}}` (exit 3).
- The Claude reading is held only in the supervisor's memory (`runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/quota.rs`,
  `Provider.quota`), so a new supervisor starts with none. A failed first read leaves the bar
  without Claude chips until a read succeeds, at least 300 s later (EON-C27 cadence).
- Several live generations and isolated test sessions read with the same login, which makes the
  rate limit more likely.

## Contract (change needs Lucca's approval of the exact text before code)

EON-C27 failure policy: "A failed read keeps retained data unchanged" extends across a supervisor
restart. A new supervisor shows the last good reading for each listed provider until a read
succeeds, under the same rules as today: `old` after one hour, gone after 24 hours, a window gone at
its reset. Recommendation: both providers (one mechanism; Codex has the same gap), and the readings
are shared by all generations of one user, so a new window never shows less than an older one.
Recommended owner: Runtime, a small file per provider under `$XDG_STATE_HOME/eon/` holding only the
typed facts EONW already carries (windows, remaining percentage, resets, observation time). No
credential, identity, raw CodexBar output or billing data is stored (EON-C27 boundary).

## Reference gate (consequential: new persisted state)

Before code record in this bead: the one owner of the stored reading; the EON-C27 and EON-C32
routes read; how an unreadable, malformed, future-dated or other-version file is treated (ignored,
never zero usage); concurrent writers from two supervisors (atomic replace); and that a provider
left out of `[bar] widgets` is still neither read nor shown.

## Acceptance

- A Runtime test: a stored reading is shown by a new quota owner before any read, ages and expires
  as today, and a malformed or future file is ignored. `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime`.
- Isolated installed observation: a reading recorded by one supervisor appears in a newly started
  one whose first Claude read fails (e.g. a fake CodexBar returning the rate-limit error).
- Review loop per AGENTS.md; profile refresh.

## Scope boundary

No new chip state or wording, no change to read cadence, CodexBar, EONW or Venus.

- A provider left out of `[bar] widgets` stays neither read nor shown.
- No Venus, EONW or cadence change.
Do not retry: real CodexBar Claude reads for testing. They count against Anthropic's OAuth usage rate limit, which caused the missing chips in the first place (code 3, "rate limited by Anthropic right now", 2026-10-22 12:12 -03). Use a fake CodexBar script, as quota.rs tests do. Write it to a fresh path and never rewrite it in place: see eon-1fxc for the ETXTBSY race.

Runtime's quota worker (runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/quota.rs, Provider) is the one owner of the stored reading: it loads it when it starts and replaces it after each successful read. title: Eon themes, including light mode
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-10-23: "create a eon-themes epic bead including light-mode". Eon has one look: about 24 chrome colors written inline in venus/src/render/chrome.rs and venus/src/render.rs with no palette struct, terminal default foreground, background, cursor and selection left at libghostty's built-ins, and no light mode. Users in bright rooms, users with light desktops, and users who need higher contrast have no option. The configurability audit (eon-configurability-audit-twdr) recorded a chrome theme as "configurable later" in eon-bepr; this epic owns that work now.

## Goal

Built-in dark and light themes, a user [theme] section, and Eon following the desktop's light or dark preference, with every state glyph (needs input, error, finished, working arc, idle) and every chrome surface legible in both.

## Children (file each when started; one fresh session each)

1. Centralize chrome colors into one Venus palette with one meaning per color, splitting the shared green (focused vs Finished) and red (Error vs hint modifiers). No visible change. Contracts VEN-C1, VEN-C21. This is eon-bepr's step 1.
2. Carry the terminal default foreground, background, cursor and selection colors as an Orbit input (ORB-C2), so a theme sets the terminal too, not just the chrome.
3. A [theme] config section with built-in "dark" (today) and "light", plus overrides; Eon Runtime parses it and sends resolved values (Configurability rule). Contracts EON-C19 and VEN-C21. Integrates eon-configurability-qkq8.5 ([terminal] palette).
4. Follow the system preference: theme = "auto" reads the freedesktop color-scheme setting (xdg-desktop-portal) and switches live, with no restart. Reference gate: how Ghostty, kitty, WezTerm and GTK apps do it.
5. A contrast check: a scene test that renders every state glyph and chrome surface in both themes and fails below a contrast threshold (WCAG-style), so a later color change can't make light mode unreadable.

Reference: docs/VISUAL-REFERENCES.md names Ramps (perceptual OKLCH ramps, semantic light and dark tokens, enforced contrast) as the starting point for an Eon palette.

## Related

eon-bepr (deferred, superseded by this epic's children 1-3), eon-configurability-qkq8.5 (palette), eon-jrz0 (chrome font size), eon-arc-spinner-t6li (arc colors must hold in light mode).

## Acceptance

- Installed observation in both themes and in auto mode switching live, with the contrast test green.

title: Show the running Eon version in the Eon Bar
description:
## Contract

A full-Eon user sees a compact read-only version badge in the existing Eon Bar, like Nova's version badge. Show the version of the Eon runtime serving that window, for example `EON 0.1.0`, with the complete version available to accessibility and hover if visually shortened. Updating a profile or bundle must not make an already-running window report the newer installation's version. Missing, invalid or disconnected identity must never become an invented version or the Venus version.

## Evidence and reference gate

Inspected on 2026-10-11:
- Nova `38a5e29eb078e939d9729dfdbbdf3362292c20b9`, `flake.nix:779` and `packaging/bar-render-request.nix`: packaging supplies runtime_identity.json and passes its runtime directory to the bar. Nova Bar `7295e9976803de8d912f766f1b00ad12652e3e9b`, `src/bin/nova_bar_widget.rs:74-147`: the version command reads that identity and formats a compact NOVA version/channel badge. Adopt the visible runtime-owned identity principle; do not copy its command polling, Zellij machinery, beta formatting or channel assumptions.
- Eon edge HEAD `d3b280870e046246f91c3c82f235c3ef9c6e90e5`, with existing working-tree changes: `crates/eon/src/product.rs:23` supplies Inputs.version from Cargo. There is already a version owner; no second version literal or generated identity file is needed merely for this widget.
- Eon Runtime `e30cf43b7ccc752d33edd4626aabbc4fd1cec579`, `crates/eon-runtime/src/supervisor.rs:1479-1483`: live Runtime facts already contain eon_version and generation. `cli.rs:400` reports the invoked executable's version, which is not sufficient evidence for another running window. Canonical EONW `v7.rs` reexports Runtime/LifecycleResponse; its Snapshot inherited from `v6.rs:42` does not contain the version.
- Venus inspected HEAD `14f6e7e32ff5dccf1f5f9b0b9c79faa2e11be18b` (Eon currently pins accepted runtime source `58f2eaa8057627bdbf73262fdb10a1dc8b681ffc`): `src/scene.rs:234,690` owns the existing read-only quota projection and responsive header, `src/render.rs` draws it and its tooltip, and `src/accessibility.rs:321` exposes static facts. EON-C21/EON-C22 and `docs/REFERENCES.md`'s canonical workspace-protocol route provide the established boundary.

Before implementation, reread these owners and compare accepted Orbit/Venus revisions with Eon's manifest pins. First evaluate reusing the existing live presentation/lifecycle identity boundary; extend the canonical typed snapshot only if that is the smallest correct route. Record that choice and any required exact protocol revision before consumer work. Never parse CLI stdout, inspect Nix store paths, query Git, or guess from the current installation to identify a live window.

## Ownership, prerequisites and scope

Eon owns the requested display policy, product version input, exact composition and delivery. Eon Runtime owns authoritative live identity; canonical EONW owns cross-process facts; Venus owns native layout, rendering, hover and AccessKit. Orbit remains unchanged terminal authority.

The native bar prerequisite is already accepted (`eon-deliver-native-eon-bar-w4d`, EON-C21); the accepted Codex chip is a presentation reference. No Claude/Grok quota bead blocks this work. Keep one active frontier: prove any necessary Runtime/EONW change, then Venus, then consume exact accepted child revisions in Eon.

Deliver one version badge in the current single row, visible at ordinary widths. When shortcut help is visible, place the version badge immediately before `?`, with close remaining last. The user approved restoring this order on 2026-10-13. On constrained widths preserve active-tab identity and required controls ahead of informational chips, without overlap or terminal-grid loss. Keep the badge read-only and preserve keyboard/terminal focus. Index the chosen product contract before implementation and update only affected documentation, changelog and LOC on delivery.

The user approved one startup preference: `[bar] show_version = false` hides the complete label; omission inherits true. No generic widget framework, polling service, new dependency, settings UI, update button, release/channel inference, generation hash display, component inventory panel, second row or platform expansion. The current semver may be identical across development builds; this bead does not promise distinct build identification or change versioning policy.

## Acceptance and cheapest falsifiers

1. An isolated installed native Linux Wayland window shows its supervising Eon's version, with a clear accessible name such as `Eon version 0.1.0`. A controlled old-runtime/new-installation mismatch proves the badge stays bound to the live owner, not PATH, profile, bundle selector or Venus's Cargo version.
2. The same observation covers ordinary/narrow layout, hover, accessibility and preserved tab/control/terminal input behavior. Missing or rejected identity cannot display a fabricated valid version or block workspace use. Reuse existing native scene/accessibility checks; add only focused regression/boundary checks needed for the selected transport, not literal mirror tests.
3. Exact manifest/lock identities and affected builds pass. A shared EONW/runtime boundary change requires the full affected Rust/Nix route; a consumer-only implementation uses the narrower applicable route. Refresh the active eon profile and verify the installed artifact, preserving live supervisors and desktop focus. Check the changed artifact in the approved Nix-free alpha delivery too if its packaging is affected.
4. Record exact revisions, environment, commands/observations and proof phase. Stop and resolve the owner/transport choice if delivery requires a second version source, speculative child API or wider feature scope; do not close on a static mock or source-tree screenshot.
notes: User selected implementation on 2026-10-12: native built-in read-only Eon <version>, visible by default, [bar] show_version = false hides both identity and version. This explicitly supersedes the original no-settings boundary only for this one boolean. Apply at window open/reopen; no widget framework, extra shortcut, polling, live configuration reload, channel inference or build-ID promise.
close_reason: Restored EON version before shortcut help, close last; native and exact installed accessibility/pointer/visibility checks pass. Current combined profile refreshed without restarting live terminals. Concurrent quota work preserved.

title: Decide EonJS renderer-owned capture boundary
description:
## Contract Routing

- This is a planning and architecture decision. It changes no current `EON-C*`, `ORB-C*`, or `VEN-C*` contract and creates no runtime behavior, repository, module, dependency, protocol, language, or compatibility promise.
- `EonJS` is a working label for a possible future **Eon for the web** renderer. The accepted public/repository naming remains `Eon for the web` / `eon-web`; closure must decide the durable technical name and owner before implementation.
- Orbit remains the sole process, PTY, terminal-emulation, terminal-state, attachment, terminal-query, and semantic-input-encoding owner.
- Eon remains the workspace, lifecycle, composition, compatibility, and product-policy owner. Venus remains the native rendering owner. A future web client may own its own pixels but must not become another terminal authority.
- Implementation requires a separately activated owner-specific Bead after exact contract, language/toolchain, reference, dependency, portability, and active-frontier approval.

## Why

A future Eon web renderer could make deterministic screenshots and recordings a nearly free output target of the actual product renderer. If capture is added later as a separate renderer, it would duplicate font/layout/compositing policy and could disagree with the displayed Eon surface. If it is treated as a terminal emulator, it would also violate Orbit authority. The decision is cheap before a web renderer exists and expensive after its rendering boundary hardens.

Effort: S for the decision. Implementation effort is intentionally unestimated until the renderer and protocol boundary exist. Risk: MED because this crosses a future repository, language/toolchain, rendering, and Orbit-client boundary. Confidence: HIGH in the ownership constraint; MED in the future implementation shape.

## Evidence

- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:11-20,65-93` assigns PTY and terminal state to Orbit, native rendering to Venus, workspace policy to Eon, and forbids Eon from implementing terminal parsing or rendering.
- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:38-41` reserves `Eon for the web` / `eon-web` for a separately implemented future client.
- `docs/CONTRACTS.md:18` proves `EON-C4`: Eon adds no duplicate terminal or rendering state.
- `AGENTS.md:252-259` requires explicit user approval before durable TypeScript or another implementation language is added.
- `AGENTS.md:286-302` permits research and Beads to prepare a later frontier but forbids implementation against speculative child APIs.
- Joshka Betamax at exact main revision `7fbaa1598e3601ccb60f244a8c669d60a6d780db` demonstrates an efficient PTY → `libghostty-vt` → persistent renderer → in-process PNG/GIF/state pipeline without tmux, a browser, or termshot. It is a comparison, not a dependency or source-reuse choice.
- Ghostty discussion `#12610`, answered 2026-05-12, records the material limitation: `libghostty-vt` exposes render state but no single canonical Ghostty pixel output; consumers own rendering.
- Related decision `eon-pxn.7` asks whether Eon owns agent-driven terminal-testing behavior. It may later consume a capture surface, but neither decision blocks or implies the other.

## Decision Question

If the user activates Eon for the web, should its actual product renderer be the sole terminal-to-pixel owner for both interactive presentation and deterministic capture, exposing an offscreen RGBA/PNG target from the same render path, or should Eon rely on external capture tooling?

## Smallest Candidate Contract

- Consumer: a future Eon for the web client and an explicitly authorized local capture caller.
- Trigger: the renderer has accepted one exact source-labeled Orbit presentation revision plus fixed render configuration, and the caller requests a bounded capture.
- Result: the same renderer path used for interactive presentation renders an offscreen surface and returns bounded RGBA or PNG with renderer, frame, font, theme, scale, dimensions, and clock identity sufficient to reproduce or reject the artifact.
- Important failures: incompatible or stale presentation revision, incomplete state, missing or mismatched font/resource, unsupported graphic, invalid dimensions, surface/readback failure, cancellation, timeout, and encoder failure are explicit and produce no falsely authoritative artifact.
- Authority: the artifact proves the selected web renderer's pixels only. It does not prove native Venus pixels or a universal Ghostty/Eon appearance.

## Scope

In scope:
- Decide whether built-in renderer-owned capture is part of a future Eon for the web boundary.
- Compare no built-in capture, external Betamax-like tooling, actual-renderer offscreen capture, native Venus offscreen capture, and compositor/window capture.
- Decide the owner and minimum boundary for presentation-state consumption, deterministic rendering inputs, offscreen pixels, artifact metadata, encoding, cancellation, cleanup, and failure reporting.
- Decide whether TypeScript/JavaScript and a browser, Node, Deno, WASM, Canvas, WebGPU, or another runtime removes enough complete responsibility to justify its toolchain and portability cost.
- Select at most one disposable proof, or record that external tooling is sufficient.

Out of scope:
- Implementing EonJS, `eon-web`, a renderer, capture API, tape language, recorder CLI, GIF/video encoder, browser server, agent harness, MCP/plugin surface, CI job, or remote service.
- Creating another PTY owner, VT parser, terminal emulator, Orbit schema mirror, raw-PTY consumer, OCR authority, or concurrent input-capable Orbit client.
- Claiming pixel identity with Venus, Ghostty, arbitrary terminals, operating-system compositors, or different font/platform stacks.
- Choosing arbitrary split trees, broader web access, authentication, collaboration, persistence, streaming, or distribution.

## Reference And Tool Gates

At activation, inspect exact accepted Orbit and Eon protocol revisions, the selected web-renderer candidates, Joshka Betamax `7fbaa1598e3601ccb60f244a8c669d60a6d780db`, and Ghostty discussion `#12610`. Resolve any named `RioTermJS` reference to an exact repository and revision before using it; an unresolved project name is not evidence. Record adopted mechanisms, rejected surrounding scope, licenses, owned LOC, transitive/build/native cost, platform support, headless behavior, font determinism, accessibility implications, upgrade burden, and replacement cost.

## Sequencing

- Status remains deferred until the user activates the Eon for the web product decision.
- This has no hard dependency on `eon-pxn.7`; that agent-testing decision may later consume an accepted capture contract.
- Stop before adding or changing any contract, repository, module, implementation language, dependency, or active frontier without explicit user approval.

## Verification

- `br show <id> --json` should show one deferred, unclaimed decision with the complete boundary and no blocking dependency.
- `br sync --flush-only` should exit 0.
- `git diff --check` should exit 0; only Beads planning state may change.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Closure explicitly decides whether Eon for the web and its renderer are accepted product scope, records the durable technical/repository owner, and does not treat the working label `EonJS` as prior approval.
2. The record chooses renderer-owned offscreen capture or explicit external-tool sufficiency after comparing: no built-in capture, Joshka Betamax-like external capture, future web-renderer capture, native Venus offscreen capture, and compositor/window capture.
3. If renderer-owned capture is selected, one observable contract names the consumer, accepted presentation revision and render configuration trigger, RGBA/PNG result, artifact identity, bounds, cancellation, cleanup, and explicit failures.
4. Interactive and offscreen output use one renderer owner and one terminal-to-pixel path. No screenshot-specific renderer reconstructs font, layout, cursor, graphics, palette, or compositing policy.
5. Orbit remains the sole process, PTY, terminal-emulation, terminal-state, attachment, query, and semantic-input-encoding owner. The selected shape consumes one exact accepted Orbit presentation contract and maintains no raw-PTY path, VT parser, second emulator, or handwritten schema mirror.
6. Eon remains the workspace, lifecycle, composition, authorization, and compatibility owner. Venus retains native rendering. Capture artifacts are explicitly authoritative only for the selected web renderer, not Venus, Ghostty, arbitrary terminals, or every platform/font stack.
7. Deterministic capture inputs cover renderer revision, source frame revision, font/resource identity, theme, dimensions, scale, and controlled presentation time. Unsupported or missing inputs fail rather than silently substituting a falsely reproducible artifact.
8. Encoding stays downstream of terminal rendering. PNG is the first proof surface; an existing bounded encoder such as ffmpeg is preferred for GIF/video unless measurement proves an in-process encoder removes enough lifecycle cost to own.
9. The language/tool gate compares Rust/no new language with any proposed TypeScript/JavaScript, browser, Node, Deno, WASM, Canvas, or WebGPU shape. Closure records platform/headless support, owned LOC, direct/transitive/build/native cost, license, security posture, upgrade burden, replacement cost, and explicit user approval before any durable second language or toolchain.
10. Reference closure records exact inspected Orbit/Eon contracts, Joshka Betamax `7fbaa1598e3601ccb60f244a8c669d60a6d780db`, Ghostty discussion `#12610`, and exact revisions for every adopted renderer candidate. An unresolved `RioTermJS` name is not accepted evidence.
11. The decision selects at most one disposable end-to-end proof and names its cheapest falsifying check, expected failure behavior, portability disposition, and evidence that would reverse the choice. It creates no production code, contract, module, repository, dependency, tape DSL, encoder, browser service, agent harness, plugin/MCP surface, CI job, remote service, or compatibility promise.
12. Any accepted implementation is deferred to separately user-activated owner-specific Beads after exact contracts and one-active-frontier sequencing exist. `eon-pxn.7` remains related but non-blocking; neither issue silently expands the other.
notes:
Ghostty WebAssembly and snapshot comparison — 2026-08-15:
- Exact primary source: Ghostty revision d760ee96e54657416eb427b793c7e839f003df7d, including README.md, example/wasm-vt, include/ghostty/vt/snapshot.h, src/terminal/snapshot, and .github/workflows/release-tip.yml. Mitchell Hashimoto's benchmark post is https://x.com/mitchellh/status/2088378990998524206.
- Evidence: libghostty-vt builds for wasm32-freestanding and exposes terminal, render-state, key, selection, snapshot, and allocator functions through a low-level C ABI. The snapshot is an ordered CRC32C-protected record stream with a renderable READY prefix, unfinished VT/UTF-8 continuation, later history pages, and FINISH. Snapshot v1 has no binary-compatibility guarantee and omits Kitty image and placement state. The module supplies no renderer, PTY, transport, authentication, font, accessibility, or browser product shell.
- Performance disposition: the published Apple M4 Max comparison measures VT writes, resize/reflow, and render-state preparation against current xterm.js. Full and incremental render comparisons reuse xterm.js's WebGL model and exclude drawing and GPU work. Treat the result as candidate-selection evidence, not Eon browser latency, memory, accessibility, or compatibility proof.
- Decision effect: keep a thin exact-version ORBF consumer as the default candidate. Compare checkpoint-plus-ordered-tail replication only if a measured transport, bootstrap, or render-state cost makes structured frames insufficient. A browser replica must remain non-authoritative; Orbit alone answers terminal queries and owns process, PTY, parser, modes, history, selection, and effects. Any relaxation requires a separate Orbit replication contract rather than this capture decision.
- Artifact gate: upstream publishes signed optimized files through a moving nightly release and states that libghostty API signatures remain in flux. Do not select a nightly URL, snapshot v1, WebAssembly SIMD requirement, JavaScript wrapper, or artifact-distribution policy as an Eon contract.
- Rejected scope: xterm.js replacement work, Eon for the web activation, a second terminal emulator or schema owner, raw PTY delivery, browser transport/authentication, and performance claims derived from the upstream chart.
- Cheapest later comparison: feed one bounded recorded corpus through the accepted native Orbit owner and a disposable exact-revision WASM candidate; compare canonical cells, modes, continuation, reflow, alternate screen, effects and declared unsupported graphics, then measure total bootstrap/update cost. Delete the proof if thin ORBF remains sufficient.

Planning-only batch authorized by the user on 2026-08-15. Status, priority, dependencies, acceptance, and implementation scope remain unchanged; the issue is unclaimed.
