title: Read Claude quota every five minutes, aligned with Nova
description:
## Outcome

Eon reads Claude quota at most every five minutes, aligned with Yazelix Nova. Codex stays at one minute.

Decision (Lucca, 2026-10-16): keep Eon and Nova aligned on the CodexBar quota cadence, with Claude every five minutes in both.

## Evidence

- On 2026-10-16, Anthropic's Claude OAuth usage endpoint returned CodexBar's provider error "Claude OAuth usage endpoint is rate limited by Anthropic right now" for this account. Eon (`runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/quota.rs`, `Quotas::start`: one 60s interval and 10s deadline for both providers) and Nova were each reading Claude about once a minute.
- Claude's 5-hour and 7-day windows change slowly, so a five-minute reading costs little freshness. Codex reads go through the local `codex` CLI and are not implicated.
- Nova counterpart: Yazelix Nova bead `yazelix-5vl-yzy2` (Nova Bar reads Claude at most every 300s and waits 300s after a failed read; Codex stays at 60s, with a 120s wait after failure).

## Contract

- Consumer: full-Eon workspace users with Claude quota.
- Trigger: the supervisor's CodexBar Claude worker.
- Result: Claude `codexbar usage --provider claude --source oauth` reads start at least 300 seconds apart, including after a failed read. Codex keeps its 60-second interval. The 10-second deadline, validation, the one-hour `old` marking and 24-hour expiry are unchanged.
- Failure: a failed or rate-limited read keeps the retained reading unchanged until the next 300-second read; nothing new is invented.

## Prerequisites

None. EON-C27 (CodexBar collection) is in place.

## Reference gate

Read EON-C27 in `docs/CONTRACTS.md` and `quota.rs` (`Provider::start`, the worker loop, and their tests) before the code shape. Update EON-C27's "Reads are at least 60 seconds apart per provider" text first, since this is an intentional behavior change.

## Scope boundary

title: Draw columns and popups as one flush workspace sheet
description:
## Decision
Lucca, 2026-10-17: replace the per-column rounded frames, which have side margins and a gap of about
12 logical pixels between columns, with one flush workspace sheet:
- The sheet spans the window's full width; its side edges sit on the window edges (no side margin).
- Adjacent columns share one 1-pixel seam instead of two parallel edges.
- Seams meet the sheet's top line and the footer (or the sheet's bottom line when hints are hidden)
  in straight T-junctions, not rounded notches.
- The sheet's outer corners stay rounded. Rule: objects are round (tabs, chips, the sheet's outer
  corners); dividing lines inside the sheet are straight.
- Popups use the same sheet. VEN-C18 already makes a popup reuse the pane stack's outer frame (one
  full-width frame over several columns), so popups follow the sheet. `popup.side_margin` and
  `popup.vertical_margin` inset popup terminal content inside that frame and stay unchanged.
- Zoom (`eon-zoom-selected-pane-e2pv`) shows the zoomed pane in the same sheet with no seam.

Why: two 1-pixel edges about 12 px apart, each 6-8 px from its own text, read as one double rule;
the gap shows the terminal background (#040507 in the 2026-10-17 dogfood capture) and carries no
information. A clearly wider gap (about 36 px) reads as separate cards but costs about four
terminal cells per seam against Venus's 40-cell column floor. Rounded seam ends pinch into a wedge
at 1 px and an 8 px radius and dent the header fills.

## Contract (to approve before code)
- Consumer: a full-Eon user with `[terminal] pane_frames = true` (the default).
- Result: as in Decision, for one to four columns, with hints shown or hidden, and with a popup
  open. Selection and hover keep their current header fills; the pane-focus outline draws over the
  shared seam where it touches it. `pane_frames = false` keeps removing lines and separators while
  keeping headers.
- Contract edits: EON-C8's frame bullet ("one rounded border around each column's visible pane
  stack", side margins), VEN-C8 frame geometry, VEN-C18 geometry wording if needed, and
  `docs/USAGE.md`'s frame paragraph. No configuration default, EONW or Orbit change.
- Important failures: a double edge left at a seam or window edge; a seam that misses its
  T-junction; a terminal grid that changes size other than by the reclaimed margins; a popup toggle
  that moves any outer edge.

## References (read 2026-10-17)
- Zed `crates/workspace/src/pane_group.rs` @ 62507a19: one 1 px divider (`DIVIDER_SIZE`) with a 4 px
  drag hitbox (`HANDLE_HITBOX_SIZE`).
- Ghostty `src/config/Config.zig` @ 45db2c255: one divider (`split-divider-color`); focus shown by
  dimming unfocused splits (`unfocused-split-opacity` 0.7), not by frames.
- tmux shared pane borders with T junctions; macOS split views (thin divider); Hyprland and niri
  use wide gaps because their windows are separate objects.
- Grouping by shared boundary (NN/g common region), Refactoring UI "use fewer borders", and the
  concentric-radius rule (inner = outer minus the gap; it applies only to nested shapes, never to
  sibling seams).
- Rejected: wider gap (width cost, busy at four columns); rounded seam ends (wedge, mixed signal);
  square outer corners (loses Eon's soft language where the sheet really has a corner).
- Cheapest falsifier: one isolated installed capture at two and four columns, hints shown and
  hidden, with a popup toggled, enlarged at a seam end and at a window edge.

## Owners
Venus owns scene geometry, rendering, hit testing and accessibility. Eon owns EON-C8's product
text. Eon Runtime, EONW and Orbit are unchanged. Portability: neutral.

## Prerequisites
After `eon-7rk3` (closed 2026-10-17; it moved this drawing into `venus/src/render/chrome.rs`).
`eon-zoom-selected-pane-e2pv` follows this bead so zoom is designed on the sheet.

## Acceptance
- Lucca approves the contract edits.
- Installed Eon shows the sheet as decided at one, two and four columns, hints shown and hidden,
  popup open and closed, and `pane_frames = false`; terminal grids gain only the reclaimed width.
- Venus suites pass through `nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-venus`, with any changed geometry
  goldens updated deliberately; Venus fmt and clippy green; `nix build --no-link .#default`; one
  isolated installed dogfood observation; refresh the active Nix profile without interrupting live
  workspaces. Changelog entry for the visible change.

## Scope boundary
No column resizing, focus dimming, theme or color change, popup margin change or new configuration.
Standalone EonTerm keeps receiving no workspace frame.
close_reason: Flush workspace sheet shipped: window-edge sides, shared 1-px seams with straight T-junctions, rounded outer corners only, popups and footer on the same frame; frameless mode unchanged. Proof and 3-pass ledger in comments.

title: Adopt Starcompass 2720d5e (AP-MINIMAL-001 v7, AP-SCOPE-001 v5, AP-CONTRACT-001 v5)
description:
## Why

Eon pins Starcompass 2af5afb, whose AP-SESSION-001 v2 has agents delegate from 100k, add no steps from 180k, and start each issue fresh unless under 100k. On a 1M window, agents suggest a new session at about 15%. Since 2026-10-19 a user-level Claude Code hook (~/.claude/hooks/context-usage.py) reports context usage to the model at each 100k step, so the v2 marks now trigger every time.

Starcompass a37e2b1 (on origin/edge) carries:
- AP-SESSION-001 v3: from 400k add no scope or new steps, close the issue if it can close by 600k, else bring work to a verified state and hand off. Hand off before the host would compact or after any compaction. The 100k, 180k and 250k marks and the fresh-start rule are gone. Evidence and trials are on Starcompass ap-56s.
- AP-MINIMAL-001 v5: the Ponytail paragraph is gone. Starcompass README gives overlay text for repositories that use Ponytail.
- AP-PROOF-001 v10, with performance claims moved to AP-PERF-001, which Eon gets through terminal-engine. AP-REFERENCE-001 v4, with license interpretation moved to AP-LICENSE-001 (fork profile only).

## Scope

1. Re-render from a clean Starcompass checkout at a37e2b1 with Eon's existing inputs: the three nested directories and `--protocol-file docs/AGENT-PROTOCOLS.md`, following Eon's documented import steps.
2. Ponytail: Eon's code carries `// ponytail:` comments, but its overlay doesn't mention Ponytail. Ask the owner whether to paste the Starcompass README's Ponytail overlay snippet into `.agent-protocols.local.md`, and add it if yes.
3. Run `starcompass check` from the checkout at a37e2b1 and `check-consumer`, plus Eon's checks for the changed files.

Out of scope: other overlay changes. A second bump follows Starcompass ap-jo9.7, which lowers the byte caps and reruns the full behavior-trial suite.

## Acceptance

- `.agent-protocols.json` pins a37e2b1, and `AGENTS.md`, `docs/AGENT-PROTOCOLS.md` and the nested files match it. `starcompass check` and `check-consumer` pass.
- The owner's Ponytail decision is recorded on this bead.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop and ask if `check` fails for a reason other than the pin change.

title: Decide whether Orbit survives a Bend worker fault
description:
## Why

Every Orbit decision comes from the Bend worker, so a worker fault ends the user's terminal. When the
worker dies (a Bend `runtime fail-stop`, a crash, the OOM killer) or stalls past the host's 2 s
answer deadline, the host contains the session: it hangs up and reaps the PTY child, removes the
socket and exits (`orbit/docs/BEHAVIOR.md`, "Fatal-exit boundary"). The single-process Rust Orbit
(tag `orbit-rust-final`) had no such failure mode. Orbit's core promise is that the terminal
outlives everything else, so a defect in the policy layer, the part that is meant to be the
safest, now costs the user their live processes.

Decide whether Orbit should survive a worker fault and, if it should, how, without giving Rust a
second copy of the session policy.

## Evidence

- `orbit/docs/BEHAVIOR.md:946`: Fatal-exit boundary. A dead or stalled worker is contained like a
  termination: SIGHUP, 500 ms, SIGKILL, reap, socket unlink, exit 1 for a stall
  (`orbit: worker stalled: no answer within 2 s`).
- `orbit/docs/HOST.md`, "What Rust holds": the host keeps no session state that Bend decides from,
  so today nothing can rebuild Bend's state after a fault.
- `orbit/src/host.rs:305` `decisions()` collects a whole answer before `carry_out`
  (`host.rs:1303`) runs, so a worker that dies mid-answer leaves none of that fact's decisions
  applied.
- `orbit/src/session.bend:36-50`: Bend's whole state, `State{Session, Shown}`, is small:
  lifecycle, four bools, the waiting vertical request, pointer state, the management slot, and the
  revision with the held bit.
- Some facts are applied by the host before Bend answers, such as PTY output fed to libghostty or a
  resize (`HOST.md`, Decisions). Any retry must not apply them twice.
- How often it happens: answers took at most 7 ms in vtebench and at a load average near 10
  (lj8.80, quoted in BEHAVIOR.md). No dogfood signal beads were open at promotion (`eon-awmq.5`
  comment, 2026-10-20). The risk is untested, not observed.

## Options

A. **Keep containment (today).** Fail closed. No new code paths, and a Bend defect is loud.
   Cost: any worker fault ends the terminal.

B. **Restart the worker from a checkpoint Bend owns.** After each answer the worker also writes its
   encoded `State`. The host stores those bytes opaque and never decodes them. On death or stall the
   host starts a new worker, checks the schema handshake, hands it the last checkpoint and resends
   the fact in flight, which is safe because no decision of it was applied. Restarts are bounded,
   for example one per fact. A second fault on the same fact falls back to A.
   - Variant B2: on the repeated fault, instead of A, restore the checkpoint and send a recovery
     fact, such as dropping the client, for Bend to decide. The terminal survives a deterministic
     policy bug, and the client reattaches.
   - Cost: a boundary schema change, a `State` codec on both sides, a round-trip law
     (`decode(encode(s)) == s`) for you to approve, and more bytes per answer, which throughput
     would need to re-measure. B without B2 only helps faults that don't repeat (OOM kill,
     SIGSTOP, a runtime fault that depends on timing). A deterministic `step` bug would crash the
     restarted worker again.

C. **Rejected: a Rust fallback policy.** Rust keeps the child alive and runs its own minimal
   attach and stop rules while Bend is gone. That creates a second owner of session policy
   (AP-OWNERSHIP-001, `orbit/AGENTS.md` "Host and worker"), and a session nobody can attach to just
   leaves processes running unseen.

Recommendation: B with B2, if the reference read and a test of the recovery fact show it fits.
Policy stays in Bend. The checkpoint round trip can be proved. And B2 covers the failure that is
actually plausible: a deterministic bug in `step`. Otherwise keep A and record why.

## Scope

In scope (planning only):
- The reference gate below, recorded here.
- The chosen option, with a proposed contract delta. Survival changes the Fatal-exit boundary and
  probably needs ORB-C12 wording or a new ORB-C ID. Show that proposal and any new law to Lucca
  and stop for approval.
- If B is chosen, the implementation beads (schema and codec, the round-trip law and proof, host
  restart, B2 recovery fact, throughput re-measure), filed after approval.

Out of scope:
- Code, schema, `LAWS.bend` or contract edits in this bead.
- Moving Bend in-process, or a different host/worker split.
- Changing the 2 s stall deadline or the SIGHUP/SIGKILL timings.

## Reference gate

Consequential: lifecycle and failure boundary, host/worker wire format, Orbit contract.
- Required by `orbit/docs/REFERENCES.md` "PTY and session lifetime": FrankenTerm (lifecycle
  states, protocol recovery, crash and reconnect checks) before changing failure semantics. zmx,
  shpool and abduco for how session survival is owned.
- `orbit/docs/REFERENCES.md` "Session policy in Bend": Bend at `234cb9b9` and bend-orbit at
  `e03926274203`, for whether `State` can be encoded and the round-trip law proved within
  BEND.md's proof costs.
- Record sources and inspected revisions, constraints kept, rejected approaches, and the decision
  and its check.

## Acceptance

- One option is chosen, with the reasons for it and for each rejected option recorded here, plus
  Lucca's approval of any contract or law change.
- If B: the implementation beads exist with dependencies. The first one has a check that fails
  first: a fixture worker killed mid-session, after which the terminal survives and a client
  reattaches. Orbit already has the `Fault` containment fixture.

## Verification

- Planning only: `br show` on this bead and on any children, and the diff of `.beads/` after
  `br sync --flush-only`. No runtime proof or profile refresh.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop for Lucca before any contract text, ORB-C status or `LAWS.bend` change.
- Stop if the host has moved enough since `e1d7a7c` that the evidence above is wrong. Note that
  `eon-awmq.8` may move host platform calls.

## Maintenance Notes

- Order the implementation after `eon-awmq.8` (host platform seam) so the two don't edit
  `host.rs` at once.
- Rejected alternatives and their reasons stay in Options above.
- Weigh Bend's native library target (bendlang/bend #813, "planned, not scheduled" at `234cb9b9`).
  It would let Orbit link the worker in process with no C of its own (`orbit/build.rs` already
  compiles Bend's generated C). That removes the pipe round trip and the worker failure mode, so
  B's checkpoint and restart work would be partly wasted if #813 lands soon.
- The architecture stays as it is (Lucca, 2026-10-21): Rust host plus Bend worker, kept for its
  proofs over the shipped policy, its marketing value, and Bend's trajectory. Fallbacks, should a
  trigger fire; neither is a revert to `orbit-rust-final`:
  - **Bend itself becomes the cost** (an upgrade breaks code or proofs, or Bend work makes

    bounded proofs and property tests over fact traces (`orb-reconsider-verus-eon-state-machine-kpw`
    covers the Verus alternative).
  - **Only Bend at runtime becomes the cost** (a measured throughput regression on the shipped
    Orbit, or worker faults this bead cannot contain). Keep Bend's `step` and laws as the proved
    specification, ship a Rust `step` in process, and gate them in CI with a differential check over
    the same fact lines. Cost: every policy change is written twice.

title: Keep a terminal alive when its hyperlinks overflow the frame budget
description:
## Why

Found by eon-69 while fixing eon-osc8-invalid-utf8-ymts (2026-10-23); an inference from the code, not yet reproduced. An Orbit frame has a 4 MiB budget (`MAX_FRAME_BYTES`), and `FrameSize::add_cell` returns EOVERFLOW past it. The pinned Ghostty (8c425a7) stores an OSC 8 URI of up to about 2046 bytes per link. A 100x24 screen whose 2400 cells each carry a different ~2 KB URI makes about 4.9 MB, over the budget. Every frame error propagates to `host.rs` `run` → `contain()`, which HUPs the child, so the terminal ends. Valid output, from a program or a `cat`ed file, could therefore end a terminal. Larger screens need shorter URIs to get there.

## Scope

In scope:
- First, a unit test that builds a frame over the budget from valid hyperlinks, red, to confirm the inference. If it's not reachable (for example Ghostty dedups or caps links per page), record why and close the bead.
- If confirmed: bring the behavior choice to the overseer or Lucca before code. Candidates: (a) send each distinct URI once per frame and have cells reference it, which is an ORBF wire change consumed by Venus and bend-orbit; (b) past the budget, drop links (cells keep text) for the rest of the frame; (c) cap per-frame link bytes. The recommendation goes with the choice. In every case the terminal never ends because of its own output.
- The ORB-C6 (and ORBF, if (a)) wording, the fix, a real-PTY or unit check, and the changelogs.

Out of scope: invalid-UTF-8 URIs (ymts), and link opening in Venus.

## Acceptance

- The red unit test, then green: a frame whose links exceed the budget does not end the terminal, and its cells keep their text.

## Verification

`nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-orbit`, Orbit fmt and clippy, the relevant nix orbit-* check, and converge plus Codex. If ORBF changes, add the full affected Rust and Nix surfaces.

Portability disposition: neutral.
close_reason: A frame whose links exceed the budget keeps every cell's text and a reading-order prefix of the links; the terminal no longer ends. ORB-C6 updated as approved. Proof on the landing commit.

Any viewport spanning >=2 pages can overflow; small screens straddling a page boundary inferred, not reproduced. Option (a) dedup does not fix distinct URIs. Plain greedy (b) can still overflow on later text. Proposed (b'): text first, links in reading order while they fit, plus compatible FrameSize::add_hyperlink. title: Keep a terminal alive when its cell text alone overflows the frame budget
description:
## Why

Today's beads found three ways a program's own output ended its terminal: an invalid UTF-8 title or directory (atq2, landed 4900b7f), an invalid OSC 8 URI (ymts, landed ad64d81), and links overflowing the 4 MiB frame budget (m62b). eon-9b found a fourth while on m62b (2026-10-23), by reading the code, not yet reproduced. Cell text alone can pass the budget. Pinned Ghostty 8c425a7 `page.zig` keeps up to `grapheme_max_len = 64` extra codepoints per cell, and a page's `grapheme_bytes` grows without a practical cap. One cell then encodes to about 284 bytes, so about 14.8k such cells (about 19k with 3-byte marks such as U+20D0, e.g. 200x97) exceed 4 MiB. `frame()` gets EOVERFLOW from `size.add_cell(&text, "")`, and `host.rs` `run` → `contain()` HUPs the child. Zalgo text `cat`ed on a large screen would end the terminal.

The shared cause: any frame error ends the terminal. Fixing each overflow source one at a time leaves the next one live.

## Scope

In scope:
- Reproduce first, with a release-mode unit test or real-PTY zalgo output on a large screen. Red.
- Bring the behavior choice, with a recommendation, to the overseer or Lucca before code:
  (a) cap combining marks per cell in the frame so a full screen fits the budget by construction (cell text truncated past the cap);
  (b) when text alone exceeds the budget, send a degraded frame (for example the cell base codepoints only) instead of failing;
  (c) the general rule: a frame-size error fails or degrades that frame and never ends the terminal, which would also cover any future overflow source. This may combine with (a) or (b).
- The ORB-C6 wording, the fix, the check, and the changelogs.

Out of scope: hyperlink budgeting (m62b) and invalid UTF-8 (atq2, ymts).

## Acceptance

- The red test, then green: a frame whose cell text alone exceeds the budget does not end the terminal, and the client gets a frame whose degraded content is defined by the approved wording.

## Verification

`nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-orbit`, Orbit fmt and clippy, the relevant nix orbit-* check, and converge plus Codex.

Portability disposition: neutral.
close_reason: A frame whose cell text exceeds the budget keeps every cell's first codepoint, then full text and links in reading order while they fit; the terminal no longer ends. ORB-C6 updated as approved. Proof on the landing commit.

Approved: (2) behavior (b'): every cell's first codepoint is budgeted first (at most 28 bytes a cell, 2.8 MB at MAX_CELLS), then full cell text and then links are kept in reading order while they fit; the rest degrade to their first codepoint and no link. Previews unchanged; no host-level change (option c not taken: the remaining frame errors are libghostty EIO/EPROTO internals). Option (a), a fixed per-cell cap, rejected: it would cut real emoji ZWJ and flag sequences. title: Stop spawned Sessions whose Ready identity is rejected
description:
## Contract routing

Hardens EON-C1 launch failure and EON-C15 pre-lease rollback by consuming accepted ORB-C13 owner proof `2518512758c7848bbd87f907b105c8bcf0fc4e1b`. Before Ready, only a launcher-held exact empty record claim authorizes local Child rollback. After Orbit marks that retained inode, Eon uses only canonical management Stop on a matching spawned-child Live identity and never Child/PID fallback. Changes no Orbit, Venus, EONW, or workspace topology contract.

## Why

The original `eon-g3k` work fixed rejected Live identity cleanup but inferred the Ready boundary from record observations. Orbit can publish between the final absent-record observation and local Child stop. Accepted `orb-h1f` supplies the exact-inode lock-and-marker owner boundary needed to remove that race.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start Orbit while Eon retains local-child rollback authority.
2. Let Orbit mark or publish Ready after Eon observes no canonical record but before Eon acts on a startup failure.
3. Observe that an inferred `published` flag can authorize Child SIGKILL after Orbit owns the run, bypassing management cleanup.

## Scope

In scope:
- exact Orbit pin `2518512758c7848bbd87f907b105c8bcf0fc4e1b` in the canonical component graph and derived Cargo/Nix locks
- `crates/eon/src/main.rs` retained Ready claim and `start_orbit` rollback
- `crates/eon/tests/workspace_control.rs` managed helper and regression coverage
- CHANGELOG, EON-C1/EON-C15 proof state, README LOC, Nix profiles

Out of scope:
- Child/PID/signal fallback after Ready
- recovering or killing foreign Live records
- Orbit or Venus source changes, Venus pin changes, EONW, workspace topology
- module-splitting Beads or implementation

## Acceptance Criteria

- Eon creates and retains the exact empty owned 0600 record claim before spawning Orbit.
- A launcher-held empty claim is the sole pre-Ready Child rollback authority and is held through local stop.
- A marked claim permanently forbids Child/PID fallback even if Live later disappears; a matching spawned-child Live record may be stopped only through management.
- Rejected Ready identity leaves no live helper or record, and retry reaches the existing Venus-launch failure path.
- Exact Orbit pin/locks, full Rust/Nix surfaces, refreshed `eon` and `eonterm` profiles, and the cheapest installed behavior check pass without interrupting live Sessions.

## Reference Gate

Consume the accepted ORB-C13 exact-inode claim contract and proof. Preserve EON-C15 one-owner rollback, Orbit ORB-C12 shutdown, FrankenTerm lifecycle-boundary evidence, and Process Triage observe/act serialization. Reject a directory lock, inferred boolean Ready state, Child kill after a marker, record deletion without an Orbit tombstone, a second lifecycle owner, or a new dependency.

## Stop Conditions

Stop if exact claim arbitration cannot remain inside the existing local filesystem/process seam, if Orbit/Venus source must change, or if completion would interrupt live Sessions.
close_reason: Accepted source 871c9f639e519c7e3201fa5d9755d0a77a4cb0df proves rejected-Ready cleanup without post-Ready signal fallback.

title: Draw panes as gapped rounded cards
description:
## Decision
Lucca, 2026-10-18: the flush, fully square workspace sheet (eon-sheet-square-top-corners-e8pp) works
but is not the look he wants. Of two options (two frame styles like Zellij, or only a gaps-and-rounded
style like Superlogical's Rex), he chose to plan the single gapped, rounded style. Recommendation
accepted for planning: one framed look, no style setting; the existing `false` pane-frames setting
stays the frameless option.

## Contract (provisional; wording needs Lucca's approval before code)
- Consumer: a full-Eon user with pane frames enabled (the default).
- Result: each column's pane stack draws as its own rounded card inset from the window by one even
  gap, with the same gap between side-by-side columns. Cards have a 1 px border, rounded corners
  and the terminal background fill; the expanded pane's header sits inside its card. No card corner
  touches a window edge, tab pill or the footer.
- Frameless (`false`) keeps today's meaning: no borders, seams or separators.
- Popups use the same card treatment.
- Terminal grid sizing still follows from the space inside the card; gaps never change terminal
  geometry rules beyond the space they take.
- Edits: EON-C8, VEN-C8, VEN-C24 (footer placement against cards), PRESENTATION.md, LAUNCH.md if it
  mentions the sheet, changelogs. The flush-sheet and square-corner clauses are replaced.

## Open decisions (recommendations)
1. Gap and radius: one gap value (about 8-10 logical px at default typography) and a radius that
   fits inside the smallest card; record exact values from captures, not as configuration.
2. Stacked panes in one column: one card per column with the collapsed headers inside it
   (recommended, keeps the accordion compact), versus one card per pane.
3. Footer hints: sit in the bottom margin below the cards, or inside the window's bottom gap.
4. Tab strip: unchanged in this slice; Rex-style pill tabs are a separate question.

## References (discovery only; no source reuse)
- Superlogical Rex macOS screenshot (Bitdoze article, https://www.bitdoze.com/superlogical-rex/,
  checked 2026-10-18): per-pane rounded cards, even gaps to window edges and between panes, title
  and pane controls inside each card, pill tabs in the title bar.
- Zellij `pane_frames` and `ui.pane_frames.rounded_corners`: record the exact release inspected.
- History to avoid repeating: eon-sheet rounded corners (86ccad7, ba92d0d) failed because curves on
  one flush sheet collided with window corners, the first tab pill, footer and label clearance.

## Prerequisites
None. Presentation only; no EONW, Orbit or runtime change expected.

## Acceptance
Venus suites, fmt, clippy for yazelix-venus; nix build; isolated captures at one, two and four
columns, a stacked column, hints shown and hidden, a popup, and frameless; review loop; profile
refresh. Lucca's installed look is the final acceptance.

## Scope boundary
Pane, column, popup and footer framing only. No new configuration key, second frame style, tab-strip
redesign, color or typography change, animation, or terminal-geometry policy change.
close_reason: Each column draws as its own rounded card with an even 8 px gap; popups as one card; hints bare below. Proof and ledger in comments.

Final values come from captures. Implemented by a delegated worker in its own worktree; the main session commits serially on edge with the eonbase rename and refreshes the profile once.

title: Include generated managed behavior in Eon runtime generation identity
description:
## Contract routing

Harden the accepted EON-C11 runtime-generation contract and preserve EON-C9. The local launcher is the consumer; a build changes generated managed-shell adapters or the private Session command projection; the resulting Eon build must have a different stable generation identity so a bare launch cannot attach a supervisor with older managed behavior. This is a defect correction, not a new command, configuration field, protocol value, compatibility window, or distribution promise.

## Why

The generation digest covers Rust, Cargo, EONW, and component-manifest inputs but omits the Nix-owned generated shell adapters and private command projection. A flake-only runtime behavior fix can therefore retain the previous identity, attach the old supervisor, and give new panes its captured old Session environment.

Impact: HIGH. Effort: M. Implementation risk: MEDIUM. Confidence: HIGH.

## Evidence

- `crates/eon/src/main.rs:35-47`: `current_generation()` does not cover `flake.nix` or an equivalent managed-runtime projection identity.
- `flake.nix:228-479`: Nix generates runtime-visible native shell adapters.
- `flake.nix:537-585`: Nix constructs the private Session command projection and injects it into Session PATH.
- `crates/eon/src/main.rs:1220-1245`: a same-generation launch attaches the existing supervisor.
- `crates/eon/src/main.rs:2019-2025`: new panes use the existing supervisor's captured managed-program inputs.
- `eon-audit-eon-managed-environment-hay` records the exact 1b8836e audit and reproduction analysis.

## Prerequisite and reference gate

- No implementation prerequisite. This Bead is the prerequisite for the two EON-C9 managed-environment corrections found by the audit.
- Before code, record the repository execution baseline and classify the EON-C11 and EON-C9 proof records plus the managed-environment and runtime-generation entries in `docs/REFERENCES.md`.
- Required evidence is current EON-C11 generation selection, the exact Nix-generated adapters/private-bin owner, `eon-pxn.4` acceptance evidence, and the closed managed-environment audit.
- Existing Eon sources define the mechanism. External terminal or shell references are comparison-only unless an observed failure requires them.
- No dependency or crate feature is expected. Stop for the crate gate and user approval before any manifest change.

## Scope

In scope:
- The stable input set owned by `current_generation()` and the minimum Nix/build wiring needed to cover generated managed-runtime behavior.
- Focused unit/build/process proof that a managed-projection-only change selects a new generation while the old one remains live.
- Current-state EON-C11 proof metadata, CHANGELOG, architecture wording, and README LOC only where required by the accepted fix.

Out of scope:
- Hashing profile paths, store paths, PIDs, socket names, package channels, mutable user configuration, or runtime state.
- A Nix evaluator at runtime, a second runtime manifest, a manager daemon, live handoff, automatic old-generation eviction, or wider compatibility.
- Changing EONW, Orbit, Venus, shell behavior, managed command names, defaults, or user configuration.
- Adding a new dependency or speculative distribution framework.

Platform classification: neutral contract with an isolated current Nix build input; no new macOS blocker. A future distributor must be able to provide an equivalent stable behavior identity without Nix-specific runtime state.

## Implementation notes

1. Add the smallest existing build/source input that completely covers the generated adapter and private-bin behavior. Prefer conservative source hashing over a second schema or runtime mechanism.
2. Keep one generation owner in `current_generation()`; build tooling may supply immutable inputs but must not reinterpret launch policy.
3. Preserve old live generations and exact attach/stop behavior. Only the identity of builds with materially different managed projections should need to change.
4. Add one A/B regression whose only observable input difference is generated managed behavior.
5. Advance the EON-C11 proof revision after the proof-bearing commit and refresh the installed runtime without stopping old supervisors or Sessions.

## Acceptance

- Two builds with unchanged Rust, protocol, and component manifest but different observable generated managed behavior report different generation identities.
- A live build A remains discoverable and usable; bare launch of build B selects a fresh B supervisor; a pane created under B observes the B marker rather than A's projection.
- Rebuilding the same accepted inputs yields the same generation identity.
- Identity and persistent records expose no Nix store/profile path or mutable user state.
- Existing exact attach, listing, stop, cleanup, workspace, and managed-environment tests retain their observable results.
- No new contract, dependency, protocol, component identity, or compatibility window is introduced.

## Verification

- One focused A/B build/process check should exit 0 and prove distinct generations plus old-work preservation and B-pane behavior.
- `cargo fmt --check`
- `cargo check --locked`
- `cargo test --locked`
- `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo run --locked -p eon-manifest -- components/eon-alpha-v1.json`
- `nix build --no-link --print-out-paths --no-update-lock-file path:.#default`
- `nix flake check --no-update-lock-file path:.`
- `git diff --check`
- Installed `eon versions` and active profile/store-path checks after the accepted proof commit.

## Stop conditions

- Stop if the cited code or EON-C11 ownership has drifted materially.
- Stop if complete coverage requires a new public manifest, protocol field, dependency, distribution promise, or duplicate generation owner.
- Stop if the candidate identity depends on a mutable path/state value or requires evaluating Nix at runtime.
- Stop if the A/B proof cannot distinguish the corrected build from an ambient PATH or already-running supervisor.
- Stop if the same verification failure repeats twice after a reasonable correction.

## Maintenance notes

The first sufficient shape is one additional immutable generation input consumed by the existing owner. Do not create a general build-fingerprint framework. `eon-5rp` remains responsible only for keeping extracted Rust production sources in the digest.

title: Close a stack with one line: the last collapsed row's label sits in the column's bottom edge
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-10-24, on the installed m5bv build (screenshot of a stack whose last pane, p3, is
collapsed): "shouldnt the bottomost pane of a stack share the same bottom border of the 'project
area'? insteaed of double bordering". Today the column's last collapsed row draws its own label
line (corners curling up, eon-m5bv), and the column's rounded bottom edge closes the stack about
one title row below it, so the stack ends in two parallel lines. At the top the first pane's label
already sits in the column's top line, which shares one snapped line with the agent sidebar card's
top.

## Behaviour

- When a column's last pane is collapsed, its label sits in the column's bottom edge: one line,
  through the middle of that row's title row, with the column's rounded bottom corners curling up
  and the stack's sides continuing up to the expanded pane's frame (eon-m5bv joints). No second
  line below it.
- At the unscrolled bottom that line and the agent sidebar card's bottom line are one snapped line
  (mirror of the top-line rule). The space that frees goes to the column above it (expanded
  terminal), as whole cells where Scene's existing sizing allows; nothing else moves.
- When the last pane is the expanded one, nothing changes (its full frame is the bottom).
- Neutral lines at border_width; the selected pane's focus frame stays its own rounded frame,
  painted once, no neutral paint under it (eon-e8hh/eon-f5pg rule). A selected last collapsed row
  keeps the focus colour on its edge as today.
- Labels, fill (eon-54jv: nothing outside the column's outer edge), hit targets (the last row stays
  clickable over its label) and AccessKit unchanged. Frameless mode unchanged.

## Contract

VEN-C8 collapsed-row sentence (venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md:590-595). Approved addition (see the
Approval comment): after "...its sides continue to the next card in that direction;" add "when the
column's last pane is collapsed, its label sits in the column's bottom edge instead, so the stack
closes with one line; at the unscrolled bottom that line shares one snapped line with the agent
sidebar card's bottom."

## Acceptance

- Venus paint/scene test (fails first): a stack whose last pane is collapsed draws exactly one
  horizontal line at the column's bottom, carrying the last row's label, on the same snapped y as
  the agent sidebar card's bottom; sides continuous from that line to the expanded frame; no paint
  outside the column's outer edge; no neutral paint under focus; scales 1 and 1.3; widths 1/1, 1/2,
  2/2; last row selected and not selected; last pane expanded unchanged.
- Isolated capture with Lucca's opacity: a 4-pane stack with the first pane expanded (before and
  after).

Portability: neutral.
close_reason: Stack closes with one bottom line shared with the sidebar; proof in comments

title: Show a GPU widget in the Eon Bar
description:
## Decision
Lucca, 2026-10-17: add a GPU widget to Eon, alongside CPU and IO.

## Contract (provisional; needs Lucca's approval before code)
- Consumer: a full-Eon user on native x86_64 Linux Wayland.
- Result: the Eon Bar shows a read-only GPU chip with GPU utilization as a percentage for each
  supported GPU, through the chip path the CPU widget bead establishes.
- Failures: an unsupported, sleeping, permission-denied or failed GPU shows no chip (never 0%) and
  never wakes a powered-down discrete GPU just to sample it; failures are per GPU and independent.

## Ownership
As in the CPU widget bead: Runtime samples behind the Linux platform seam, EONW carries typed facts,
Venus presents. No GPU vendor logic in Venus.

## Platform evidence
There is no single Linux source. AMD exposes `gpu_busy_percent` in sysfs. Intel i915/xe whole-GPU
busy needs the perf PMU (CAP_PERFMON or perf_event_paranoid <= 0, which Eon must not require); DRM
fdinfo only gives per-client engine time for processes the user owns. NVIDIA proprietary needs NVML
(`libnvidia-ml`) or `nvidia-smi`. Lucca's machine is hybrid Intel i915 + NVIDIA proprietary, and
neither has `gpu_busy_percent` (checked 2026-10-17); README lists proprietary NVIDIA as unproved.

## Open decisions (recommendations)
1. Which GPUs in the first slice: recommend those Lucca can dogfood (NVIDIA via NVML, plus AMD sysfs
   since it is free), with Intel shown as unsupported until an unprivileged whole-GPU source exists.
2. NVML access: dlopen `libnvidia-ml` from the host driver (it must match the kernel module, so Nix
   cannot pin it) versus a bounded `nvidia-smi` subprocess like the CodexBar reads. Recommend the
   subprocess or a thin dlopen with no new crate; any crate passes AP-DEPENDENCY-001.
3. Hybrid laptops: sample only an already-awake discrete GPU (runtime PM `runtime_status`), or show
   it as asleep; recommend never waking it.
4. One chip per GPU or one chip showing the busiest: recommend the busiest with every GPU in hover.

## Reference gate (consequential: platform seam, host library or subprocess boundary)
Record nvtop, btop's GPU support and Mission Center at exact revisions; how each reads AMD, Intel
and NVIDIA without privilege; rejected approaches; the chosen source and its check.

## Prerequisites
`eon-cpu-widget-eon-bar-acxs` (collection, EONW field and chip path).

## Acceptance
Focused sampler red/green per supported source (invalid, missing and asleep never become 0%);
installed capture on Lucca's hybrid machine with the NVIDIA GPU awake and asleep; `eon-test`, fmt,
clippy, nix build; review loop; profile refresh. Record each unsupported GPU kind honestly.

## Scope boundary

title: Deliver trustworthy Grok quota in the Eon Bar
description:
## Contract

A full-Eon user who uses authenticated Grok Build can see a compact Grok quota chip beside the existing provider chips when a verified read-only source supplies authoritative subscription usage. Show the provider-reported remaining percentage and the actual supplied quota period, with reset details on hover and in the accessible description. Do not relabel a shared subscription pool as a Build-only allowance. Missing or unsupported usage stays absent or explicitly unavailable; local tokens, context usage and dollar balances cannot substitute for quota.

Important failures include missing or incompatible CLI, unsupported billing method/account type, auth change or expiry, malformed/oversized response, absent percentage/period, timeout or network/provider loss. They never block Eon or produce fresh-looking guessed quota.

## Ownership and prerequisites

Eon owns the product outcome and exact composition; Eon Runtime owns the provider source, lifecycle, normalization and freshness; canonical EONW owns the typed facts; Venus owns native layout, icon, hover and accessibility. Grok owns auth and billing semantics; Orbit remains terminal authority.

The accepted Codex delivery and EON-C21/EON-C22 supply the baseline. EONW v7 is Codex-specific, not a general quota schema. Before implementation, index the selected Grok contract and choose the smallest canonical typed extension, reusing an accepted Claude change only if it already exists and fits. Claude-first is scheduling preference, not a hard semantic dependency. Follow one active frontier and consume accepted Runtime/EONW and Venus revisions before Eon delivery.

## Evidence and reference gate

Reviewed on 2026-10-11:
- Official usage semantics: https://docs.x.ai/grok/faq. The documented paid weekly pool can span several Grok products; the percentage shown in Grok settings is subscription usage, not a fixed Build token budget.
- Official CLI and status-line docs: https://docs.x.ai/build/cli/reference and https://docs.x.ai/build/features/status-line. The documented status-line fields include session/model/context facts; this is not proof of an externally available subscription quota query.
- PATH discovery found grok-1.0.41-linux-x86_64. No live authenticated quota read was performed.
- Comparable implementation: CodexBar 444821be54e2571dd115ca07b2ce3d1e0a71a45c, https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar/blob/444821be54e2571dd115ca07b2ce3d1e0a71a45c/docs/grok.md. It describes a candidate ACP x.ai/billing method, historical method-not-found failures and read-only billing fallbacks using existing login credentials. This demonstrates a possible source, not compatibility of our installed Grok.
- Grok Build source discovery: xai-org/grok-build 2bdd1d6a6369de0e8c68132ea4539e9abd9e14a8. Reinspect exact CLI/billing ownership and license before adopting a mechanism.
- Nova e7d8d6ffe9994413944bac388620b9f9f61669d7 consumes Nova Bar 7295e9976803de8d912f766f1b00ad12652e3e9b and tokenusage. Compare quota labels/failure behavior; do not copy its widget, cache or multiplexer architecture.

First falsifier: establish whether the exact installed Grok can return quota through a supported read-only machine boundary without starting an agent turn. Prefer provider-owned auth and a documented CLI route when sufficient. If unavailable, compare a bounded authenticated billing read with leaving the chip unavailable; record endpoint stability, credential ownership, permissions, cost, license and maintenance. Direct HTTP or credential access is unresolved and must be explicitly selected before implementation, not silently inherited from CodexBar. Do not adopt its fallback chain or browser-cookie import wholesale.

## Scope and stop boundary

One read-only native quota chip for one verified Grok auth/account class on the accepted Linux Wayland alpha. Define period, remaining percentage, reset, source/account binding, age/expiry and honest stale/unavailable behavior. Bound retries and I/O, keep authentication out of Venus, and preserve existing provider chips and the bar's tab/control priority.

No billing/credit purchase, reset redemption, login UI, token refresh owner, browser-cookie scraping, transcript/history scanner, token/cost-to-quota inference, generic provider/widget framework, new row, provider bundling or platform/distribution expansion. Do not expose raw billing payloads, credentials or account identity through EONW or logs.

If no acceptable authoritative source exists, record the exact blocker and leave delivery incomplete rather than substitute local usage or close on an unavailable-only chip. Source selection must precede UI implementation.

## Validation

Record exact provider, Eon Runtime/EONW, Venus, Orbit, manifest, package and environment identities. Use focused parser/source red-green checks for meaningful malformed/missing/stale cases, then the full affected Rust/Nix route for shared protocol or dependency changes. Refresh the installed eon profile and observe one isolated native x86_64 Linux Wayland workflow with real provider facts plus bounded failure substitutes, preserving live terminals and desktop focus. Inspect responsive width, hover and AccessKit labels together; do not treat accessibility structure alone as screen-reader qualification.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The exact supported Grok version/auth class supplies a real authoritative quota observation through an explicitly selected read-only source. Source/API stability and any credential-access decision are recorded; no inference turn or provider mutation is needed.
2. Remaining percentage, actual supplied period and reset agree with that observation. Shared subscription usage is labelled honestly, absent facts remain unavailable, and local tokens/context/cost are never used as quota.
3. Bounded parsing/I/O/retry/cleanup, source/account invalidation and explicit freshness/expiry handle missing methods, auth failures, missing fields, malformed responses and provider/network loss without blocking product use or republishing obsolete facts.
4. Canonical EONW carries only bounded normalized facts. The native Grok icon/name, quota, hover/reset details and accessible stale/unavailable labels fit the existing single-row bar beside accepted chips; optional chips yield before tabs and required controls.
5. Exact accepted owner revisions, meaningful focused source/failure checks, affected Rust/Nix proof, profile refresh and one isolated installed real-source observation pass. Current docs/changelog/LOC state the supported scope and limitations; live terminals, desktop focus and user provider configuration are preserved.
notes: User authorized creation of this Claude/Grok planning-only batch on 2026-10-11. Open and unclaimed; no implementation, auth read or provider-configuration write in this run. Recommended after Claude, with no false blocking edge. The first implementation step is the unresolved authoritative-source gate.

Read-only probes with Lucca's existing Grok 1.0.41 (4220f3b224a6) login, same flags as runtime quota.rs: `usage --provider grok --source cli --format json --json-only --web-timeout 8` -> error 'Grok request failed: Method not found' (the installed Grok does not answer CodexBar's billing request; matches CodexBar's documented historical failure); `--source oauth` -> 'No available fetch strategy for grok.' description:

  and left edges and above the cards; pill size and the 4 px gap between pills stay unchanged, so

  On a window too short for it, the inset yields (at most a quarter of the header height).

  changelogs' unreleased card entries.

and clippy; Venus suites via `nix develop -c eon-test`; nix build; isolated captures framed and
frameless; review loop; profile refresh.

Tab-pill inset and header height only. No pill size, inter-pill gap, button width, color or
configuration change. Portability: neutral.

title: Stop evaluation-time GitLab grammar fetches from failing the cache CI
description:
## Problem
Cache workflow run 38929342825 (edge 32bb4ad, 2026-10-16) failed at evaluation: Nix could not fetch git+https://gitlab.com/gabmus/tree-sitter-blueprint (rev 355ef84ef8a958ac822117b652cf4d49bac16c79). Pinned github:Yazelix/nova-helix/817dcbca8b99c3db35ea66ded7492673d1a397ad grammars.nix:36 calls builtins.fetchTree (type git) for grammar sources, so a transient GitLab error fails the whole run before any cached build is used. The same pins passed on a14a90c two hours earlier; GitLab answered again minutes later, and nothing in Eon's Nix inputs changed.

## Contract
Evaluating and building Eon's packages never depends on a git host at evaluation time. Grammar sources resolve through fixed-output fetchers (hash-pinned), so a cached build needs no git host, and an uncached build fails only at build time for that grammar.

## Owner
nova-helix's grammars.nix owns the fetch; Eon consumes it via flake.lock. Fix it in nova-helix (fixed-output fetchers, as already done for Codeberg and SourceHut), then bump Eon's lock. The Eon helix-grammars check already rejects evaluation-time Codeberg and SourceHut fetches; extend it to every evaluation-time git fetch.

## Acceptance
nix eval of Eon's packages succeeds with gitlab.com unreachable (e.g. blocked in a sandbox); the extended helix-grammars check fails on any evaluation-time git fetch; cache CI passes. Full affected Nix surfaces.

## Note
Run 38929342825 was rerun with --failed on 2026-10-16 to restore this edge build's cache; that does not fix this bead.
close_reason: Transient GitLab 503 (run 38929342825 attempt 1); the rerun passed and nothing in Eon changed. Not worth fixing now: nova-helix grammars.nix still fetches ~283 GitHub and GitLab grammar sources during evaluation without hashes, so a host outage can fail evaluation. Reopen if that recurs or slows installs.

title: Design and prove native macOS Eon distribution
description:
## Outcome

Design and prove a native macOS delivery channel for an already accepted full-Eon Apple Silicon runtime. This issue owns delivery only; it does not implement Orbit, Venus, EonTerm, or Eon platform behavior.

## Current activation boundary

Deferred. On 2026-09-11 the user approved Nix-only `aarch64-darwin` runtime work and explicitly left signing, notarization, installers, Homebrew, and public distribution outside that slice. Reopen only after native `EON-C7` dogfood and a fresh distribution-graduation decision.

## Prerequisites and order

1. `eon-p93` approves graduation from Nix-only dogfood and selects the delivery target and maintenance envelope.
2. `eon-ohh` proves the shared direct-release verification, upgrade, rollback, and removal foundation.
3. `eon-prove-full-eon-apple-silicon-macos-t8o` proves the canonical full-Eon composition on Apple Silicon macOS.
4. This issue packages the exact accepted manifest and child proofs without another component graph.

## Reference and tool gate

Required before code: current Apple signing, hardened runtime, entitlements, notarization, stapling, Gatekeeper, quarantine, application bundle and disk-image behavior; Homebrew Cask requirements if selected; architecture-specific versus universal artifacts; exact runtime child proofs; canonical component manifest; active-work-safe upgrade policy; and credible release tooling. Record credentials, secrets boundary, hosted/local cost, dependency footprint, owned LOC, replacement cost, and recovery. Stop for user approval before selecting or adding a release tool.

Keep signing and notarization credentials outside repository state. Direct download and any package-manager entry consume the same immutable artifact, checksums, signatures, manifest, and version diagnostics. A website or package manager is not artifact authority.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The selected architecture set has one immutable Eon application artifact or disk image, checksum, signature, notarization ticket, and exact component manifest.
2. Gatekeeper, quarantine, first/repeat launch, diagnostics, active-work-safe upgrade, rollback where supported, and removal pass on a clean macOS user account.
3. Any selected package-manager entry installs and removes the exact immutable artifact without rebuilding or changing the component graph.
4. Bundle identity, entitlements, privacy prompts, filesystem locations, logs, user data, and cleanup ownership are explicit. Uninstall preserves user data unless the user separately requests exact removal.
5. Exact credentials/tool boundaries, artifact sizes, closure contents, commands, environments, costs, limitations, and recovery results are recorded at an immutable candidate.

No runtime feature, child fix, second manifest, Nova package change, hidden Nix dependency, Intel/universal promise, App Store distribution, or auto-updater is implicit.
notes: Planning refinement — 2026-09-11: native macOS distribution is a deferred epic, not a claimable task. It stays inactive during the Nix-only EON-C7 frontier. If the user later activates distribution graduation, split notarized bundle/signing, delivery/update metadata, and install/upgrade/removal dogfood into owner-sized children after the runtime contract is Proven.

title: Keep older running windows working when config.toml gains a newer setting
description:
## Why

Found 2026-10-24 by the overseer. After eon-f5pg landed, the overseer added `focus_border_width = 1`
to Lucca's `~/.config/eon/config.toml` at his request. An `eon` from an older build that was still on
PATH (the build Lucca's running window started from, cdnmbxk3, before eon-e8hh) then failed on every
read of that file:

    eon: invalid Eon configuration /home/lucca/.config/eon/config.toml: TOML parse error at line 4
    unknown field `focus_border_width`, expected one of `background_opacity`, ... `rows`

The failure aborted an unrelated command in the overseer's shell. The overseer removed the line again
at once. Lucca's live windows run their own build's `eon` (EON_SESSION_BIN), so any old window that
reads the shared config after a newer build's key appears in it rejects the whole file, until the user
restarts that window. Every new setting therefore breaks every running older window the moment the
user adopts it.

## Goal

A newer key in config.toml never breaks an older running build; an older build still refuses real
mistakes (typos, wrong types) for keys it knows. Options for the contract (wording to Lucca): keep
strict parsing but tolerate unknown keys when the file declares a newer config schema; or warn and
ignore unknown keys in running windows while `eon config check` stays strict; or version the
configuration. Name the owner (Eon Runtime parses configuration).

## Acceptance

- A Runtime test: a config with a key the build does not know loads in a running supervisor and its
  CLI without failing (behaviour per the approved contract), while a misspelled known key still fails
  where the contract says it must.
- Reproduce first with an older build and a newer key, as above.

Related: eon-1bq8 (in-place update), eon-newer-build-notice-byd2.
close_reason: Unknown config keys are ignored with a warning; proof in comments

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Approval (Lucca, 2026-10-24, direct to the overseer, "do it"): the contract is "An Eon build ignores a configuration key it does not know, with one warning naming the key and file, so a newer setting never breaks an older running window. A known key with a wrong type or value still fails." The popup clause "Eon rejects unknown fields" changes to match. Rejected: tolerating unknown keys only under a declared newer config version.

title: Name the core count in the CPU tooltip
description:
Contract: the Eon Bar CPU widget's tooltip (find the owning clause, likely VEN-C8 bar widgets / EON-C bar widget text; check whether the tooltip wording is contract text before changing it).

Decision (Lucca, 2026-10-26): show the number of cores in the CPU tooltip. Today it reads "CPU use 6%, all cores, over the last 2 seconds"; for example "CPU use 6% across 16 cores, over the last 2 seconds". The chip itself stays "CPU 6%" (the bar is short on space).

Find first: who measures CPU and who writes the tooltip text (Runtime sends resolved values, Venus parses no configuration; the core count should come from the same owner that computes the percentage, not be recomputed in Venus), and whether the count is logical CPUs (what the percentage averages over) — say "cores" only if that is what it counts, else pick the accurate word.

Configurability: the count is a measured fact, not a user value; no setting.

title: Release Eon 1.0
description:
## Why

Under `eon-versioning-beta-bfyf`, every 0.x release is beta and 1.0.0 leaves beta. Lucca set
1.0 scope on 2026-10-20 with this rule: before 1.0 comes (a) anything that would break users if
it landed later, (b) proof of every claim the README and contracts make, (c) the install path
most users take, and (d) a few high-visibility features for the release. Purely additive work can
land in 1.x.

## Decisions (Lucca, 2026-10-20)

- The Orbit swap is finished (`eon-awmq.5` closed, window waived). `eon-awmq.6` and `.8` stay
  ordinary beads and do not block 1.0.
- 1.0 makes a written 1.x stability promise for commands, config, upgrades and default
  shortcuts (child: stability contract).
- Before 1.0, land the changes that would break that promise later: `eon-8mnr.1` exit codes,
  `eon-8mnr.2` calling-pane targeting, `eon-venus-keysym-named-keys-chnh` key encoding, and
  renaming the manifest's `eon-alpha` graph ID.
- Re-prove what is claimed (or drop the claim) and name the supported compositors.
- Ship the Nix-free install: `eon-qualify-nix-free-linux-public-beta-lm9p`.
- Features in 1.0: plain-text URLs (`eon-nlcy`), the Eon icon (`eon-369s`), pane zoom
  (`eon-zoom-selected-pane-e2pv`), CPU/RAM/clock widgets (`eon-cpu-widget-eon-bar-acxs` plus
  children), the agent attention pipeline and sidebar (`eon-agent-sidebar-yx8`), and restoring
  workspaces after a reboot (`eon-reboot-restore-im8y`). The last two were accepted as
  recommended when Lucca said to create this epic.
- macOS ships in 1.0 as a labelled preview (Nix, Apple Silicon, outside the stability promise,
  gaps listed), not as "unsupported". Full macOS support is 1.x. Accepted as recommended; the
  tier itself is a rule change that needs Lucca's approval of the wording (child decision).

## Not in 1.0 (additive, 1.x)

Full macOS support (`eon-prove-full-eon-apple-silicon-macos-t8o`, `eon-hzq`), GPU and IO widgets
(`eon-gpu-widget-eon-bar-ri16`, `eon-io-widget-eon-bar-baie`), OpenCode Go quota, the Claude chip
split, remote SSH (`eon-remote-ssh-x7dr`), the command runner, mise, MicroVM, and everything
deferred.

## Order

1. Stability contract and the breaking changes.
2. Features: URLs, icon, zoom, widgets, agent state pipeline, then sidebar; reboot restore.
3. macOS preview.
4. Nix-free on Fedora (`lm9p.3`).
5. Re-proofs last, on the final candidate (AGENTS.md "Batch proof").
6. Cut v1.0.0.

## Acceptance

- Every child and every blocking bead is closed, or Lucca accepts it as not blocking.
- The stability contract is approved and indexed; README and docs describe 1.0 truthfully.
- v1.0.0 is tagged only on Lucca's direction (AGENTS.md "Git Workflow").

title: Write the 1.x stability contract
description:
## Why

1.0 leaves beta (`eon-versioning-beta-bfyf`). README "Status and limits" says commands,
configuration and behavior may still change between 0.x releases; 1.0 must say what no longer
changes. Without a written promise, "1.0" means nothing to users or to later agents deciding
whether a change is breaking.

## Draft discussed with Lucca (2026-10-20)

- Commands: every documented `eon` command, flag and exit code keeps working through 1.x.
  Machine-readable output is stable only where the docs say so.
- Config: a config file that loads in 1.0 loads in every 1.x. Old keys produce a warning, never
  a failure; nothing is removed before 2.0.
- Upgrades: installing a newer 1.x never ends live terminals; older generations stay listable and
  stoppable (builds on EON-C11 and the preserved EONW revisions).
- Default shortcuts: existing ones keep their meaning; new ones may be added.
- Not covered: appearance, the ORBS/ORBF and EONW wire protocols (own versions), macOS preview,
  anything outside x86_64 Linux on native Wayland.
Lucca said "ok, let's talk" to the promise; refine the draft with him before writing it.

## Evidence

- `README.md:74`: beta wording to replace at release.
- `docs/CONTRACTS.md`: EON-C1..C27; the next free ID is assigned when written (the CPU widget
  bead also proposes one, so check the index first).
- `docs/DISTRIBUTION.md:38`: 1.0.0 meaning.

## Scope

In: the contract text in `docs/CONTRACTS.md`, its check(s), and the user-facing summary in
`docs/USAGE.md` or `README.md`. Out: implementing exit codes (`eon-8mnr.1`) or other behavior.

## Acceptance

- Lucca approves the final contract text (stop for approval before editing the index).
- The contract names its consumer, trigger, result, failures and the cheapest falsifying check
  for each guarantee (e.g. a config-compatibility fixture, an upgrade-with-live-terminals proof).
- Docs link to it.

## Verification

Planning/docs route: changed Markdown paths, contract ID and diff reviewed; no runtime claim.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if a guarantee needs behavior that does not exist yet; file or link the bead instead.

title: Let configured shortcuts take precedence over default shortcuts
description:
## Why

EON-C28 (1.x stability, `eon-igae.1`) promises that a later default shortcut never makes a 1.0
configuration fail. Today Eon rejects a configured popup shortcut that collides with a workspace
shortcut, and a configuration can bind almost any modified key. So any default shortcut added
during 1.x would break some 1.0 configuration, which would freeze default shortcuts until 2.0.
One gap already exists: Venus binds Alt+Shift+N (new window), but Eon's reserved list does not
include it, so a configuration can bind it today. This must change before 1.0, while breaking
changes are still allowed.

## Evidence

- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/managed_environment.rs:538-542`: a popup shortcut that
  `workspace_shortcut` matches is rejected with "conflicts with an Eon workspace shortcut".
- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/managed_environment.rs:554-581`: `workspace_shortcut`, the
  reserved list; Alt+Shift+N is absent.
- `venus/src/application/shortcuts.rs:96-280`: Venus's fixed bindings, including Alt+Shift+N
  near line 261.
- `docs/CONTRACTS.md` EON-C20: rejects popup shortcuts colliding with Alt+Slash or Alt+0..9.

## Decision to propose (recommendation)

A shortcut the user configures takes precedence over a default on the same key: the default
becomes unbound (and the Alt+/ viewer shows that), instead of the configuration failing.
Keep a small fixed set that can never be overridden (Alt+Slash, so the viewer stays reachable,
and perhaps Alt+0..9), stated in EON-C20. Rejected: freezing default shortcuts for all of 1.x
(blocks features such as the command runner); reserving whole modifier families for Eon
(restricts users and still needs a list).

## Scope

In: the EON-C20 change (approve with Lucca first), Runtime validation, the EONW popup catalog
or a new field telling Venus which fixed bindings are overridden, Venus dispatch and the
shortcut viewer, and one source for the reserved list so Runtime and Venus agree.
Out: user-configurable workspace shortcuts beyond popups; key remapping.

## Acceptance

- A configuration binding a popup to any non-reserved default key loads; the popup wins and the
  viewer shows the default as overridden.
- Alt+Shift+N and every other Venus fixed binding follow the same rule.
- EON-C20 and EON-C28 text agree; the EON-C28 shortcut fixture covers one override.

## Verification

Focused tests for validation and override (red/green), the affected Runtime and Venus builds,
`cargo fmt --check` and clippy for Venus, and one isolated installed dogfood observation.
close_reason: Landed in 4781d01: configured popups take non-reserved default keys; Runtime reserves only Alt+Slash and Alt+0..9. Proof and review ledger in comments. The EON-C28 shortcut-fixture acceptance item moved to eon-igae.11 (Lucca, 2026-10-21).

comments.text: Lucca, 2026-10-21, decision for EON-C20 (contract text still to be shown to him before committing): (1) a configured popup shortcut on the same key as a default Eon shortcut wins; the default becomes unbound and the Alt+/ viewer shows it as overridden, instead of the configuration failing. (2) The never-overridable set is exactly Alt+/ (keeps the viewer reachable) and Alt+0..9 (tab navigation), fixed for all of 1.x. Every other default, including Alt+Shift+N, Alt+W, Alt+Shift+B/M and Ctrl+Alt+Shift+H/L, becomes overridable. Sequencing: touches Runtime (managed_environment.rs validation), EONW (overridden-binding facts for Venus) and Venus dispatch and viewer, which overlap eon-8mnr.1 (Runtime exit paths) and eon-igae.4 (Venus Eon Bar clock), both in flight in other sessions on 2026-10-21. title: Add the EON-C28 stability fixtures on the 1.0 candidate
description:
## Why

EON-C28 (1.x stability, `docs/CONTRACTS.md`) promises that commands, exit statuses, JSON fields,
configuration, default shortcuts, managed command names and older-generation Stop keep working
through 1.x. Each guarantee needs a check that every 1.x build runs, so a breaking change fails
the suite instead of reaching users. These fixtures record the 1.0 surface and must land on the
final 1.0 candidate, after the other 1.0 changes.

## Scope

In, as tests in the workspace suite (`nix develop -c eon-test`) unless noted:
- a configuration setting every documented 1.0 key, loaded with `EON_CONFIG_HOME` and
  `EON_RUNTIME_DIR` set;
- a parse corpus of every `eon` command and flag listed at 1.0;
- the 1.0 JSON fixture: the fields of each listed command's `--json` output (EON-C28 names this
  fixture as the documented JSON schema);
- the documented exit status of each failure class (after `eon-8mnr.1`);
- the 1.0 default shortcut actions, with one configured override (after `eon-igae.10`);
- the `managed-command-path` flake check extended to every documented `eon-` managed command
  name (today it checks only `eon-nu` and `eon-bash`, `flake.nix:642-651`).
Out: the per-release upgrade observation and defaults review (release proof, `eon-igae.9`).
Lifecycle codecs need no new fixture now: each later EONW revision adds its predecessor to the
previous-generation stop test, as v2 through v11 are today.

## Acceptance

Each fixture fails when its guarantee is broken (show one red/green per fixture class) and passes
on the 1.0 candidate.

## Verification

`nix develop -c eon-test` and `nix build --no-link .#checks.x86_64-linux.managed-command-path`
on the candidate revision.

Behavior landed in 4781d01 (EON-C20).

EON-C28 (Upgrades) already promises this; these fixtures and the per-revision previous-generation Stop test are its enforcement, so they must land before v1.0.0.

title: Remove legacy compatibility before 1.0
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-10-20: "we should remove every legacy stuff from the repo. this is very important.
no one is using eon yet." Compatibility with earlier Eon builds, earlier EONW revisions, earlier
names and the pre-consolidation repositories costs code, tests, docs and agent context and
protects no user. It must go before EON-C28 (1.x stability) starts binding at v1.0.0.

## Inventory (edge bca350f, read-only survey)

1. EONW v2-v11 (`runtime/crates/eon-workspace-protocol/src/v2.rs`..`v11.rs`, ~4,800 lines) and
   their callers in Runtime `control.rs`/`generation.rs` and `eon/crates/eon/tests/workspace_control.rs`
   (~6,000 lines total). v12 re-exports v11 down to v2, so v12 must first become standalone.
2. Fixed-namespace "legacy" generation (`generation.rs` `inspect_legacy`, `control.rs`
   `send_legacy_inspect`, the `legacy` CLI target), which keeps `v4.rs` alive.
3. Old-Orbit differential check from the Bend swap (`flake.nix` input `old-orbit`,
   `nix/orbit-checks.nix`, `orbit/tests/real_pty/differential.rs`, `frame_after_vt`).
4. `eon claude-statusline` (remnant of retired EON-C26) and the retired `eonterm` name refusal.
5. Older-supervisor presentation fallback in `probe_presentable_runtime` (`control.rs:426-443`).
6. Pre-consolidation residue: Runtime source self-hash and provenance (`eon-runtime-residue-9475`),
   packaged notices (`eon-packaged-notices-wording-f6go`), "private pre-consolidation archive"
   preambles, ORBS version history table, ARCHITECTURE cutover acceptance.
7. `eon-alpha` naming: already `eon-igae.2`.

## Kept on purpose (recommended to Lucca; revisit only on his word)

- Retired contract stubs (EON-C22, EON-C26): the index rule keeps them so IDs are never reused.
- CHANGELOG.md and the component changelogs `orbit/CHANGELOG.md`, `venus/CHANGELOG.md`, which
  AGENTS.md assigns to wire/protocol changes.
- Dated benchmark records (`docs/benchmarks/`, `venus/docs/benchmarks/`): measurement evidence
  under AP-PERF-001, not compatibility code.
- "Pending re-proof" markers: they close through `eon-igae.7`/`.8`, not by deletion.
- "Eonova" as an example application ID in tests: a reference, not compatibility.

## Live-state constraint

Removing EONW v2-v11 means the new `eon` cannot list or stop generations started by older builds,
including Lucca's own (12 generation directories under `/run/user/1000/eon/generations`, Oct
17-20). Before refreshing the profile with that change, ask Lucca to stop or finish those
generations with the current `eon stop previous`; never stop them without his word.

## Acceptance

Every child closed; no code path, test, doc or Nix check exists only for compatibility with an
earlier Eon build, protocol revision, name or repository layout, except the kept items above.
close_reason: done

title: Make EONW v12 a standalone module with unchanged wire bytes
description:
## Why

Part of the legacy removal epic (Lucca, 2026-10-20). EONW v12 is built by re-export:
`runtime/crates/eon-workspace-protocol/src/v12.rs:7` does `pub use super::v11::*`, v11 re-exports
v10, and so on to v2; the shared Encoder, Decoder, `frame_version` and `identity` live in `v2.rs`,
and `v6::set_version`/`reframe` are reused. v2-v11 cannot be deleted until v12 stands alone.

## Scope

In: make v12 one standalone module (or v12 plus a small shared codec module) with byte-identical
wire output and decoding; move the shared codec pieces out of `v2.rs`; keep v2-v11 compiling
against the moved pieces for now. Out: deleting v2-v11 or their callers (next bead).
EONW is a wire format: this is a consequential shape (AGENTS.md); record in this bead the owner,
the decision and its check before code.

## Acceptance

Every v12 message encodes and decodes byte-identically before and after (golden bytes or a
round-trip corpus over every v12 message kind); Venus, Runtime and Eon build unchanged.

## Verification

`nix develop -c eon-test` (workspace suites), `cargo fmt --check` and clippy for touched crates;
converge review.
close_reason: done

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Reference gate (edge a80a6c6, before code).

Behavior and owner: EONW v12 wire bytes, decode results and errors stay unchanged; Eon Runtime's
`eon-workspace-protocol` crate stays the one owner. No consumer-visible v12 name changes.

Read: v2-v12 sources in full; consumers in Runtime (`control.rs` older-revision dispatch,
`workspace.rs`, `generation.rs`), Venus and Eon via v12 imports. No external comparable: this is an
internal flattening of an owned format.

Constraint found: Runtime `control.rs:294-379` passes a v12 `WorkspaceAction` into v3-v11 requests
and returns v2-v11 `LifecycleResponse`s as v12 values, and `eon/tests/workspace_control.rs` builds
v3-v11 failures from `v2::Failure`. Type identity across revisions is relied on.

Decision: v12.rs defines every v12 type, the framing and primitive codec (Encoder, Decoder, Error,
frame/unframe, identity checks) and flattened message codecs with no reference to v2-v11. The
dependency inverts for the interim: v2-v11 re-export the shared types and primitives from v12 and keep
their own message codecs, so `v2::Failure`, `v3::Action` etc. stay the same types as v12's. No
separate codec module: once v2-v11 go (eon-igae.12.4), v12.rs alone remains. Rejected: a v12 with

## Why

Part of the legacy removal epic (Lucca, 2026-10-20). EONW v2-v11 exist only so a newer `eon` can

sessions, which he stops first.

title: Accept --json on eon window stop all
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-10-20, after `eon window stop all --json` failed with `invalid Eon window ID "all"`.
`eon stop all --json`, `eon stop previous --json` and `eon window stop ID --json` all exist, so the
`--json` form of `eon window stop all` is a reasonable expectation; today the parser
(`runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/cli.rs:358-368`) only matches the three-word form and reads `all`
as a window ID. EON-C28 freezes the 1.0 command surface, so the gap should close before 1.0.

## Contract

EON-C23 (Independent Eon windows): add that `eon window stop all --json` returns one result array
per window without confirmation, matching `eon stop all --json` under EON-C11, with the caller's own
window still last. Changing EON-C23 needs Lucca's approval before code.

## Scope

In: the `window stop all --json` form in the CLI parser and `windows::stop_all_windows`
(`runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/windows.rs:188`), its JSON output shape (follow `eon stop all
--json`), help text (`cli.rs:436`), `docs/USAGE.md` command table, EON-C23. Out: other window
commands; whether stopped windows should drop out of `eon windows` (observed 2026-10-20: a stopped
window still lists with only its unstarted current generation; report separately if it matters).

## Acceptance

`eon window stop all --json` stops every independent window's generations without prompting,
caller's window last, prints machine-readable results, and exits nonzero if any Stop fails; the
human form is unchanged; help, USAGE and EON-C23 list the form.

## Verification

A test next to `new_windows_keep_independent_supervisors_and_stop_by_window_id` through
`nix develop -c eon-test`; installed observation of the command after profile refresh; converge
review.

title: Configure the Eon Bar widgets' order and visibility
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-10-21: for 1.0 the Eon Bar widgets need configuration, both their order and turning
each one on or off. Today the CPU, RAM and clock labels are always on with no configuration
(EON-C29, EON-C30), the version label has a single boolean (`[bar] show_version`, EON-C25), and
quota chips have no switch. Under EON-C28 (the 1.x stability promise) the configuration keys
and their names are frozen at 1.0, so the shape must land before 1.0 (rule (a) of `eon-igae`:
anything that would break users if it landed later).

## Design (proposed by eon-52 and accepted as recommended when Lucca said "create the beads",
2026-10-21; exact contract wording still needs Lucca's approval in each child)

```toml
[bar]
widgets = ["codex_quota", "claude_quota", "cpu", "ram", "clock", "version"]
```

- One ordered string list, the shape Nova uses for `bar.widgets`
  (`~/pjs/nova/nova-upstream-theme/crates/yzx-config/src/catalog.rs:54`, ordered string array,
  `ARCHITECTURE.md:158`), so Ratconfig's ordered string-list picker fits it.
- List order is the left-to-right order between the drag region and Shortcuts/Close.
- A name left out is off; `widgets = []` shows only tabs and controls.
- Omitting the key gives the default above, which is today's bar (`0d27a46`, `eon-igae.3`).
- An unknown or duplicate name is a startup configuration error through the existing
  invalid-configuration handling, which keeps live terminals.
- Applies when a window opens or reopens, like `show_version` today.
- Width pressure keeps a fixed hiding priority by kind (clock, RAM, CPU, version, then quota
  compaction) whatever the order: the list sets placement only, so narrow bars stay predictable.
- `show_version` is removed before 1.0, and a config that still sets it fails with an error
  that names `widgets`. Rejected: keeping both, because two settings for one fact would become a
  permanent 1.x promise.
- A quota chip turned off also stops Runtime polling that provider. Rejected: hiding the chip
  only, because Eon would keep calling CodexBar for data nobody sees.

Ownership: Eon owns the setting, its names and the default; Runtime parses and validates it
(`runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/managed_environment.rs`) and passes it to Venus as a launch
input, the way `--eon-version` goes today (`runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/supervisor.rs:407`);
Venus owns placement, fitting, hover and AccessKit.

## Children (in order)

1. Venus: an ordered bar-item launch input that sets placement and on/off.
2. Eon and Runtime: `[bar] widgets`, replacing `show_version`.
3. Runtime: stop polling a provider whose quota chip is off.

## Acceptance

- Every child is closed, and the contracts they change (a new EON-C ID for the setting,
  EON-C25, EON-C29, EON-C30, and the Venus launch-input contracts) are approved and proven.
- `docs/CONFIGURATION.md` describes `[bar] widgets` and no longer mentions `show_version`.

## Out of scope

New widgets (GPU `eon-gpu-widget-eon-bar-ri16`, IO `eon-io-widget-eon-bar-baie`, cursor color
`eon-rf4c`): they join the list later as new names, which is additive under EON-C28. Per-widget
options (formats, intervals), configurable hiding priority, a settings UI, and live reload
without reopening the window.
