title: Let eon pane close close a named pane from a popup
description:
## Why

On 2026-10-22 the overseer, running in Lucca's Agent popup on t1, tried to close two finished agent
panes with `eon pane close p5 --json`. The Runtime refused: `{"error":{"code":"unavailable",
"detail":"close the popup before closing a pane"}}`. So an orchestrating agent can open panes from
its popup (`pane create --no-focus`, eon-zhjj) but cannot close them, and every finished agent
costs Lucca a manual close. Lucca: "i dont think this rule is good ... the oveerseer should have
powers to do stuff", then "create a p1 bead".

## Decision (Lucca, 2026-10-22, approving the overseer's proposal)

- An explicit `eon pane close PANE` from a popup terminal closes that pane in the calling tab, and
  the popup stays shown.
- Alt+W under a popup stays refused: the selected pane is hidden, so the user can't see what it
  would close. That is the rule's sound purpose.
- Still refused from a popup: a close that would end the calling tab (its last pane), because that
  also stops the calling popup and ends the caller's own session.

**Contract:** amend EON-C10 ("Closing is unavailable while a popup or picker covers the tab", and
"pane close under a popup or picker" in its Important failures). This is a contract change: bring
Lucca the exact EON-C10 wording, in your own session, before code. Decide and record whether the
EONW request shape changes (it should not need to; the same v11 close action is accepted from a
new caller state). Keep the picker case as it is unless the wording says otherwise.

## Evidence (edge 4b150d5)

- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/workspace.rs`: the close validation returns `unavailable`
  "close the popup before closing a pane" whenever `tab.selected_popup.is_some()`, for every
  caller (around line 917; also around line 2533).
- The rule came in with Alt+W, cfeb8b8 "Close the selected pane with Alt+W over EONW v11".
- `docs/CONTRACTS.md` EON-C10, around lines 505 and 524.
- Precedent: eon-zhjj made `pane create --no-focus` keep the caller's popup shown.

## Reference gate

This is a consequential shape (contract and lifecycle boundary). Record on this bead before code:
how comparable tools close a pane by id while another surface has focus, at pinned revisions from
docs/REFERENCES.md routes. tmux `kill-pane -t` (with a `display-popup` open), Zellij
`close-pane`/`--pane-id`, kitty `close-window --match`, and WezTerm `cli kill-pane --pane-id` are
the obvious candidates. eon-n6ga already pins four of them.

## Scope

In scope: the Runtime acceptance rule, the EON-C10 text, CLI help/USAGE if they mention the
refusal, CHANGELOG, and tests: a popup caller closes a named non-final pane and its popup stays
shown and selected; a popup caller naming its tab's last pane is refused with topology unchanged;
Alt+W under a popup is still refused.

Out of scope: closing panes in other tabs (the calling-tab rule stays), pane move under a popup
(the same refusal exists there; report whether it should follow, as a separate decision), and
reading pane text.

## Acceptance

- The three test cases above, red first where the behavior is new.
- An isolated installed observation: from an Agent popup, `eon pane close pN` closes pN and the
  popup stays shown with its conversation.

## Verification

Workspace/runtime route: focused `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime -p eon`, fmt and clippy,
the converge loop with Codex, and the installed observation after the profile refresh.
close_reason: Popup and pane callers close a named non-last pane under a popup; Alt+W and the last pane stay refused (EON-C8/EON-C10). Proof on the bead.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Reference gate (2026-10-22, eon-ad; source read by a research subagent at the pinned revisions in ~/pjs/refs, HEADs verified: tmux 3.8 7f2a35ad3321, Zellij v0.45.1 efd8fd5a89a2, WezTerm e2a98e1b8af1, kitty v0.49.2 b2cb871254fb).

Evidence:
- None of the four refuses a by-id close while a popup/overlay is open, and none confirms it: tmux kill-pane (cmd-kill-pane.c:64-69; modal guards cover only break/join/swap/select), Zellij CloseFocusByPaneId (screen.rs:12627-12641), kitty close-window --match (rc/close_window.py:45-55), WezTerm kill-pane (sessionhandler.rs:481-495).
- The covering surface survives: tmux display-popup is cleared only by client loss/Escape/job exit (server-client.c:1792-1802, popup.c:500); Zellij leaves the floating layer (tab/mod.rs:5718-5733); kitty keeps the overlay in its group (window_list.py:476-495); WezTerm ignores PaneRemoved for overlays (termwindow/mod.rs:1318).
- Closing the last pane takes the container with no guard in all four (tmux server-fn.c:224; Zellij screen.rs:4201-4206; kitty boss.py:1123-1131; WezTerm mux/lib.rs:905-946), killing a popup in it.
- Keybinding closes differ only by confirmation (tmux prefix-x confirm-before, key-bindings.c:444); under a tmux/kitty popup the key goes to the popup.

Decision: adopt "an explicit named close is accepted under a covering popup and the popup stays shown". Keep Eon's refusals that the references lack: Alt+W under a popup (in Eon Alt+W is an Eon chord that would close a hidden pane, unlike tmux/kitty where the key reaches the popup), and a popup caller closing its tab's last pane (it would stop the caller itself; Lucca's decision). Rejected: Zellij-style focus targeting for a bare close (Eon's close always names PANE).
Contract owner: the rule text is EON-C8 (CONTRACTS.md "Closing is unavailable while a popup or picker covers the tab" and its Important failures), plus EON-C10's caller bullet and failures; the bead names only EON-C10.
EONW: unchanged. v18 Request already carries `caller`; Venus Alt+W sends none, so the Runtime distinguishes a popup caller (target_tab returns its tab with no pane) without a new field or version.
Check: the three bead tests in workspace.rs (popup caller closes a non-last pane and its popup stays shown and selected; popup caller naming the last pane refused, topology unchanged; no-caller close under a popup still refused), then the installed observation.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Decision (Lucca, 2026-10-23, relayed by coordinator eon-a8): asked "Should a pane terminal of a tab covered by a popup also be able to close a named pane, not only the popup terminal?", Lucca replied "1 yes". So an explicit eon pane close PANE from a pane terminal of the covered tab is accepted under the same limits as a popup caller: the pane must be in the calling tab, the tab's last pane stays refused, Alt+W (and any close without a caller) under a popup stays refused. The EON-C8/EON-C10 wording still needs Lucca's explicit OK before code.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Contract approval (Lucca, 2026-10-23, relayed by coordinator eon-a8, quoting "1 yes" to "kr1z's EON-C8/EON-C10 wording in p6 ... I recommend approving it if it matches the recorded decision plus your '1 yes'"). Approved text:
1. EON-C8 "Closing a pane" bullet: replace "Closing is unavailable while a popup or picker covers the tab." with "Closing is unavailable while a popup or picker covers the tab, except that a calling terminal of that tab, pane or popup (EON-C10), may close a named pane other than the tab's last; the popup stays shown and selected, and the tab's pane selection follows the ended-terminal rules below."
2. EON-C8 Important failures: replace "pane close under a popup or picker," with "pane close under a popup or picker other than a calling terminal's close of a non-last pane in its tab,".
3. EON-C10 EON_TERMINAL bullet: after "...so `pane create` selects the new pane and dismisses the tab's popup;" insert "`pane close PANE` also works while a popup covers the caller's tab and leaves that popup shown (EON-C8);".
4. EON-C10 Important failures: after "both change nothing and exit 1." add "While a popup covers the caller's tab, `pane close` naming that tab's last pane changes nothing and exits 1, and so does a close sent without a calling terminal, including Alt+W."
Pane move under a popup: not decided; separate bead only if needed.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Proof (eon-ad, 2026-10-23). The commit carrying this record is the proof revision: edge ec13ba6 plus this change (tree 40404a0 before this bead line). x86_64 Linux.

- Red/green: with the old rule, `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime --lib pane_close_targets` failed (the popup caller was refused with "close the popup before closing a pane"); with the change, `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime` passed (84 passed, 1 ignored: the release-Orbit measurement). `-p eon` passed (39 passed). `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --locked -p eon-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings` were clean. These ran on bases 22915af/d6fa09c. The eon-runtime and eon sources are byte-identical in the final tree, since d6fa09c, 3a4955f and ec13ba6 change only docs, .beads and Venus.
- Installed observation: `nix build path:<worktree at ec13ba6 + change>` gave /nix/store/rkvx427rn0jrp8b6f4jpzvb1l6j5j303-eon-0.1.1. It ran in a private headless Sway 1.12 with an isolated HOME and runtime dir, and the Agent popup ran a stand-in agent script. Steps: t1 with p1 and p2 (selected_popup=None); Alt+Shift+L showed the Agent popup u2; Alt+W then left panes [p1, p2] with u2 selected. From inside the popup, `eon pane close p2 --json` exited 0. `eon pane close p1 --json` exited 1 with `{"error":{"code":"unavailable","detail":"close the popup before closing the tab's last pane"}}`. Afterwards: panes [p1], selected_pane p1, selected_popup u2, and the screenshot shows the popup still open with its text. Artifacts: ~/.cache/eon-agents/eon-ad/obs-final. Lucca's live Eon was untouched.
- EONW: unchanged (v18 `caller` already present; Venus Alt+W sends none).
- Profile refresh: batched by coordinator eon-a8 with the other landings; not done in this slice.
- Pane move under a popup keeps its refusal. Whether it should follow is a separate decision, left unfiled until the overseer needs it.

Ledger: converge with Codex. Round 1: Claude found 1 blocking issue (no test for a caller-less close of a non-last pane under a popup; fixed in the test); Codex 0. Round 2: Claude clean. Narrow Codex re-check of the fix and the rebase onto d6fa09c: clean. Rebase onto ec13ba6 (CHANGELOG conflict kept both entries): narrow Codex merge check clean. 2 Claude passes, 3 Codex passes, 1 finding.

title: Initialize Orbit with the Eon vivid ANSI palette
description:
## Outcome and contract

Consumer: a local user opening a new full Eon or EonTerm Session.

Trigger: Eon starts a new Orbit process for that Session.

Result: Eon supplies one exact approved 16-color sRGB ANSI table through a bounded versioned component launch input. Orbit validates it, applies it as the authoritative default palette before processing PTY output, and emits the resulting exact values through existing ORBS frames. Full Eon and EonTerm use the same table. Terminal programs may still override colors through normal OSC semantics.

Important failures: malformed or missing required Eon input fails before the PTY child starts; partial tables are rejected; an Orbit process started outside Eon keeps its existing libghostty defaults; current live Sessions are not recolored or restarted. Direct RGB and palette indices 16 through 255 remain unchanged. OSC 4 overrides remain program-owned, and OSC 104 resets to the Eon-supplied defaults rather than bare libghostty values.

Ownership: Eon is the sole owner of the product default table and component launch policy. Orbit remains the sole terminal-state owner and applies the accepted default through libghostty. Venus remains an exact ORBS consumer and gains no palette setting, rewrite, saturation transform, or renderer change.

Contract routing: harden EON-C1, EON-C3, EON-C4, and EON-C12; change or add an Eon user-visible default contract only after explicit user approval. The producer work must preserve ORB-C1, harden ORB-C2 and ORB-C6, and define the new Orbit launch input before code. Existing ORBS values already carry the complete palette, so no ORBS version or VEN contract change is proposed.

## Why

The P1 Venus issue ven-render-vivid-terminal-colors-2ap proved that YZX Anima indexed colors are muted before Venus: bright indices 10, 14, 12, and 13 arrive as #b9ca4a, #70c0b1, #7aa6da, and #c397d8, while generic direct RGB #00ff88 remains exact. The Venus renderer is not the owner, but the user-visible product defect remains. Without a correct-owner Eon issue, closing the Venus investigation loses the chosen vivid-color outcome.

Impact: HIGH. Common Zellij and Anima indexed output uses the default palette.
Effort: M across one producer-first Orbit slice and one Eon integration slice.
Risk: MED because startup validation and terminal palette reset semantics cross the component boundary.
Confidence: HIGH in ownership and mechanism; the exact 16-color table still requires explicit user acceptance.

## Evidence

- Eon crates/eon/src/main.rs:1596-1635 has one Orbit process and argv owner. It currently sends only serve, socket, separator, and child argv.
- Eon docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:101 assigns component launch policy to the Eon runtime and excludes terminal state.
- Orbit src/main.rs:180-228 accepts only socket and child command, then constructs libghostty with columns, rows, and scrollback.
- libghostty-vt 0.2.1 terminal.rs:158-224 and :710-725 exposes default_color_palette and set_default_color_palette for embedder-owned defaults. It preserves OSC overrides and makes later resets return to the supplied default.
- libghostty-vt 0.2.1 style.rs:225-330 provides the existing 256-entry Palette, base-index setters, and built-in defaults. No new parser crate or palette type is needed.
- Orbit src/presentation.rs:147-153 already emits the effective complete 256-color palette through ORBS.
- eon-eonterm-presentation-e4f is not a duplicate: it routes fonts, geometry, line height, and opacity to Venus and explicitly excludes terminal palette authority.
- No existing Eon or Orbit Bead mentions palette initialization.

Exact inspected identities: Eon a701d55beaf4127c9ff4d1341214b1ebd82221ba; Orbit e60554623d2ad1e238fac84d0f8f49be0e81e522; Venus investigation at eon-desktop b18d5c34f794fd4e3c34beb64952a767c588db41; Ghostty a887df42c56f6de86c0fe6da9c4eeca37931e083 through libghostty-vt 0.2.1; Nova Bar d659fdf5ae0b4013aacaf31399e2bab064654320; packaged Anima d22d091d427af0be307056c65e475802b602d386.

## Minimum shape

1. Before implementation, capture the clean Ghostty palette and the user-approved vivid candidate beside Nova direct colors and the Anima/Zellij indexed corpus. Obtain explicit approval for all 16 RGB entries and whether foreground/background remain unchanged.
2. Create and prove a separate Orbit producer issue first. Define one bounded versioned launch value for exactly 16 RGB entries; reject partial or trailing input before PTY creation. Add no config framework or compatibility window.
3. In Orbit, start from the existing libghostty 256-color default, replace indices 0 through 15 with the supplied table, and call set_default_color_palette before the owner loop processes PTY bytes. Do not synthesize OSC, inject shell output, or change ORBS.
4. Prove initial frames, detach and reattach, OSC 4 override, per-index and full OSC 104 reset, direct RGB, and default standalone Orbit behavior.
5. After the exact Orbit proof is accepted, add the fixed approved table to the existing Eon Orbit-command owner and pass the exact child input for workspace and EonTerm launches. Add no user setting in this first slice.
6. Prove the composed installed artifact, update accepted contract metadata after proof-bearing commits, and refresh the Eon profile without stopping live supervisors or Sessions.

## Scope

In scope:
- One fixed Eon product-default ANSI 16-color table.
- Existing Eon Orbit launch composition and focused argv/process tests.
- A producer-first Orbit launch-input parser and direct existing libghostty palette setter.
- Contract, component-identity, current-state documentation, changelog, and LOC updates required by accepted runtime behavior.
- Native Linux dogfood in full Eon and EonTerm/Eonova with Zellij and YZX Anima Game of Life.

Out of scope:
- Venus source, renderer color transforms, saturation boosting, shaders, color management, or a Venus palette setting.
- A user-editable palette, theme registry, dark/light switching, live reload, per-pane colors, foreground/background changes without explicit approval, or Nova theme ownership.
- Replacing or forking libghostty, adding a dependency, changing ORBS, changing terminal direct RGB, or regenerating indices 16 through 255.
- Recoloring an existing Orbit process or restarting live Sessions.

## Reference classification

Required before code: this complete Bead; closed Venus issue ven-render-vivid-terminal-colors-2ap and its exact capture comments; current Eon launch owner and EON-C1/C3/C4/C12; current Orbit CLI, ORB-C1/C2/C6, palette extraction, lifecycle tests, and libghostty-vt 0.2.1 palette API; Ghostty a887df42c56f6de86c0fe6da9c4eeca37931e083; Nova Bar d659fdf5ae0b4013aacaf31399e2bab064654320; packaged Anima d22d091d427af0be307056c65e475802b602d386.

Comparison only: a clean standalone Ghostty native capture and the users configured Ghostty capture. They inform exact palette choice but do not transfer Ghostty configuration or renderer ownership.

Rejected: Venus palette replacement, global saturation curves, synthetic OSC prelude, shell startup escapes, environment-variable-per-color, a general theme schema, Mars configuration import, source copying, and a new dependency.

## Acceptance

1. The user approves one exact complete 16-color sRGB table before contract or source edits. The proof records the compared clean Ghostty, configured Ghostty, Nova, and current libghostty values without claiming they are identical.
2. Eon owns one fixed table and passes one bounded versioned value to every newly started full Eon and EonTerm Orbit process. No second table or consumer reconstruction exists.
3. Orbit rejects malformed, incomplete, duplicate, or trailing palette input before PTY spawn and reports one bounded launch failure. Omitting the option outside Eon preserves the built-in default.
4. The first ORBS frame contains the exact approved table. Detach and reattach preserve it without changing terminal or process identity.

title: Color the Eon Bar's quota windows by how sustainable the current pace is
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-10-21: "color code the AI quotas according to how sustainable the pace you are going
is. if it should last with confort or barely, or if it will lack, or if it will lack so hard you'd
spend days without usage ... we can tune this positively a bit, optimistic, green, but then it
starts yellowing, then oranging, then red-ing".

Today Codex's chip shows each window's position and remaining percentage (`3h/5h 74% · 6d4h/7d 42%`), and each Claude window has its own chip (`3h/5h 74%`), and the
reader has to work out whether that pace lasts until the reset. A color per window answers that
at a glance.

## Evidence

- `runtime/crates/eon-workspace-protocol/src/v14.rs:267-280`: each quota window carries
  `duration_minutes`, `remaining_percent` and `resets_at: Option<u64>`, and the quota carries
  `observed_at` and a state (fresh, stale, blocked, unknown). That is enough to compute pace in
  Venus with no EONW or Runtime change.
- `venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md` VEN-C22 (Codex chip) Boundary lists "threshold color" as excluded.
  VEN-C26 (Claude beside Codex) follows VEN-C22. Both need contract edits, and Lucca must approve
  them before the code.
- `docs/CONTRACTS.md` EON-C22 and EON-C26 describe the product-side quota chips. Check whether
  they also need a line.
- Related: `eon-claude-chip-split-u3ik` landed (3aa682b): Claude shows one chip per window, Codex
  keeps one chip with both windows. Pace is per window, so color each window's text inside Codex's
  chip and each Claude chip as a whole.

## Scope

In scope:
- One pure Venus function per quota window: from elapsed share and used share, project whether
  usage at the current pace runs out before `resets_at`, and by how long. Return one of four
  levels: green (lasts comfortably), yellow (barely lasts), orange (runs out before the reset),
  red (runs out so early you'd go a long stretch, e.g. days on the 7-day window, without usage).
- Color each window's text (or segment) in the chip by its level. Hover text and the AccessKit
  label say the same thing in words (e.g. "at this pace, runs out about 2 days before reset"),
  so color is never the only signal.
- Edits to VEN-C22 and VEN-C26 (and EON-C22/C26 if they need it), proposed for Lucca's approval
  first.

Out of scope:
- EONW, Runtime polling or CodexBar changes; a configurable threshold setting; alerts,
  notifications, charts or history; other providers.

## Acceptance

- Optimistic tuning, as Lucca asked: green covers "on pace or a little over", and the
  thresholds lean toward green. The exact cut points are proposed with the contract text and
  approved by Lucca. A starting proposal is to compare the projected run-out time with the
  reset: at or after the reset, or less than ~10% of the window early, is green; up to ~25% early
  is yellow; up to ~50% early is orange; more than that is red.
- No color without a basis: a window with no `resets_at`, a stale, blocked or unknown quota, or
  a window too young to judge (proposal: under ~10% elapsed) keeps today's neutral color.
- Hover and AccessKit name the level in words for every colored window.
- Narrow-width hiding, layout and the chip text are unchanged; only color changes.

## Implementation Notes

1. Read VEN-C22, VEN-C26 and the Venus quota chip code (`venus/src/scene.rs` and the chrome
   renderer) for where window text and color are produced.
2. Draft the contract edits and the cut points, then stop for Lucca's approval.
3. Add the pure pace function with unit tests at each boundary (exact pace, each cut point,
   missing reset, young window, the 100%-used window).
4. Wire the color into the chip, then hover and AccessKit text.

## Verification

- `nix develop -c bash -c 'cargo fmt --check -p yazelix-venus && eon-test -p yazelix-venus &&
  cargo clippy --locked -p yazelix-venus --all-targets -- -D warnings'` exits 0.
- Installed: one isolated headless-Sway observation with fixture quota data (check whether a
  fixture route exists; otherwise record the gap) showing at least green and red windows, plus the
  hover text.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop for Lucca's approval of the contract edits and cut points before code.
- Stop if pace needs data the snapshot does not carry (that would make it an EONW change).
- Stop if the theme has no accessible yellow/orange/red on the chip's fill in both themes.

## Maintenance Notes

- Owner: Venus Scene, as a projection of snapshot facts. If Lucca later wants the cut points
  configurable, the policy moves to Eon and travels as a launch input; not in this bead.
- Linear projection (used share over elapsed share) is the simplest model. A smarter model
  (recent rate, time of day) is a later idea, not this bead.

Decision: the window's color is a continuous blend along green -> yellow -> orange -> red, driven by the projected shortfall (how early, as a share of the window, the current linear pace runs out before resets_at), not four discrete levels. Kept from the body: optimistic tuning (pure green through on-pace and a small overshoot, then the blend starts), neutral color when there is no basis (no reset, stale/blocked/unknown, window too young), and hover/AccessKit wording so color is never the only signal (words may stay coarse, e.g. 'lasts until reset' / 'runs out about 2 days early'). The gradient's anchor points (where it turns yellow, orange and full red) are part of the contract proposal Lucca approves. Exactly on pace (projected to run out right at the reset) is a light green just starting toward yellow; full green is reserved for usage comfortably under pace, and any overshoot moves further along the gradient. Lucca floated today's neutral chip color for on-pace; recommendation (eon-c5): don't, since neutral already means 'no basis to judge' and on-pace should read as a judgement. comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
PROPOSAL for Lucca's approval (pace agent, 2026-10-27). No product code is written until approval is relayed.

## Reference gate (consequential: contract change)

- User-visible behavior: each fresh quota window's text in the Eon Bar (Codex's per-window segment, each Claude chip's label) takes a color on a continuous green -> yellow -> orange -> red gradient by how sustainable its current pace is; hover and AccessKit say the same in words. One owner: Venus Scene computes the pace from the current EONW snapshot facts (duration_minutes, remaining_percent, resets_at, observed_at, state); the chrome renderer colors the glyphs; hover/AccessKit reuse the chip description. No EONW, Runtime, CodexBar, config or dependency change.
- Routes read: venus/docs/REFERENCES.md "Codex quota fact chip" (Venus derives labels only from normalized duration, reset and observation facts; Nova Bar styled strings rejected as source).
- Comparable implementation: CodexBar `7c08c0ae783b72040b728757eb85a6cfe4fc2443` (MIT, the pinned quota backend), Sources/CodexBarCore/UsagePace.swift, UsagePaceText.swift, MenuBarLayoutRenderer.swift:687-701. Kept: linear pace (used share against elapsed share), run-out ETA = remaining / rate, "Lasts until reset" / "Runs out in X" wording, no pace without a reset, no pace when the window is not yet measurable. Rejected: its seven stages by percentage-point delta (Lucca asked for a shortfall-driven gradient), its binary green/red tint and half-alpha stale tint (stale stays neutral here), its optional setting `menuBarColorPace`, workday and historical models, and any copied source.
- Decision and check: pure Scene function with boundary and monotonicity unit tests; rich-text glyph color check in the renderer; contrast >= 4.5:1 for every gradient point on BAR_BACKGROUND; one isolated headless-Sway observation with a fake CodexBar (EON_CODEXBAR in a copied wrapper) showing green and red windows and the hover text.

## Model

For one window with a reset, at the snapshot's observed_at (the same instant the position label uses; Venus adds no timer):
- elapsed share e = elapsed / duration; used share u = (100 - remaining) / 100.
- Shortfall s = 1 - e/u: how early, as a share of the window, the current linear pace runs out before the reset (negative = lasts with that much to spare). u = 0 never runs out (full green). u = 1 gives s = 1 - e, the share of the window left without quota.

## Cut points (gradient anchors) -- Q1

Colors blend linearly between these anchors (s, color):

| s (shortfall) | pace (u/e) | 5h window | 7d window | color |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <= -0.25 | <= 0.80 | lasts with 1h15m+ spare | lasts with 1d18h+ spare | full green |
| 0 | 1.00 (on pace) | runs out at reset | runs out at reset | light green, 30% toward yellow |
| +0.10 | 1.11 | 30m early | ~17h early | yellow |
| +0.25 | 1.33 | 1h15m early | ~1d18h early | orange |
| >= +0.50 | >= 2.00 | 2h30m+ early | 3d12h+ early | full red |

Colors (dark bar only; Venus has one theme): green rgb(96,196,96), yellow rgb(255,196,87), orange rgb(255,150,70), red rgb(255,107,107); each, and every blend between them, is >= 4.5:1 on BAR_BACKGROUND rgb(10,13,20) (computed minimum over the whole gradient 7.0:1, endpoints 7.0:1 to 12.3:1; today's neutral text is 8.6:1). New palette constants named for this role.

## No basis -> today's neutral text color

Stale, blocked or unknown quota; a window without resets_at; a window younger than 10% of its duration (first 30m of 5h, first ~17h of 7d) -- except a used-up window (0% remaining), which is always judged.

## Proposed contract text

New subsection after "VEN-C22/VEN-C26 -- Optional-reset consumer refinement":

### VEN-C22/VEN-C26 -- Pace color

- **Status:** Proposed.
- **Contract:** Each fresh quota window with a reset, past its first tenth, colors
  its text (one segment of Codex's chip, the label of a Claude chip) on a
  continuous green, yellow, orange, red gradient by how early its current pace
  runs out before the reset, projected linearly from the snapshot's used and
  elapsed shares at the observation time. Full green is comfortably under pace;
  exactly on pace is a light green turning toward yellow; full red runs out at
  least half a window early. A used-up window is always colored. Stale, blocked,
  unknown, reset-less and younger windows keep the neutral text color. Hover and
  the static accessible label say, for each colored window, that at this pace it
  lasts until reset, runs out about a stated time before reset, or is used up, so
  color is never the only signal. Separators, `old`, the marks, text, compact
  choice, widths and hiding order are unchanged; every gradient color keeps at
  least 4.5:1 contrast on the Eon Bar.
- **Owner:** Venus Scene projects the color and wording from snapshot facts;
  the existing glyphon renderer, hover and AccessKit owners present them. No
  EONW, Runtime, provider, configuration, timer, dependency or module change.
- **Proof:** pending (`eon-l8lt`).

Edit in VEN-C22 **Boundary**: "alert, threshold color, chart" -> "alert, threshold
color other than the pace gradient (VEN-C22/VEN-C26 -- Pace color), chart".

EON-C22 and EON-C26 are retired; EON-C27 describes collection, not color. No EON contract edit.

## Numbered questions (recommendation first)

1. Cut points: approve the table above? Recommended as is. Alternative: full red at +0.40 (about 2d19h early on 7d) if "days without usage" should go red sooner.
2. Young-window guard at 10% of the window, with the used-up exception? Recommended as is.
3. Configurability: keep the anchors and colors fixed in this bead and record why (bead scope excludes a setting; a setting needs Runtime to parse and send it over EONW, which this bead excludes; the words carry the meaning for anyone who cannot use the colors), with a follow-up bead for a `[bar]` toggle only if you want one? Recommended: fixed, no follow-up bead unless you ask.
4. Contract text above: approve as written?

## Contract routing

This repository-governance, distribution-metadata, and local-delivery task changes no EON product contract. The user selected Apache-2.0 for the whole Eon repository and directed agents to update the user runtime whenever Eon changes.

## Scope

- Add the exact Apache License 2.0 text used by Yazelix Nova; align all Cargo and Nix package metadata and Nix license retention.

- Refresh the active eon profile element now.
- Preserve all unrelated dirty work. Do not activate direct distribution, change dependencies, repin components, or interrupt live Sessions.

## Safety boundary

Updating the installed Nix profile is authorized. Stopping or restarting a live Eon supervisor is not automatic because it terminates active Sessions; report the remaining restart requirement unless the user explicitly authorizes interruption.

title: Deliver a terminal key's release when another key on the same resolved key starts a capture
description:
## Why

eon-venus-keysym-named-keys-chnh (VEN-C2 named-key resolution) records an accepted gap. Venus pins each native key's resolved key and coalesces two physical keys that resolve to one key. When a terminal press is held and a second physical key on the same resolved key starts a shortcut capture that does not retire the attachment, the terminal press's release is never delivered.

## Repro (reasoned, from Codex review of tree 1acfa397)

caps:backspace plus a configured Alt+Backspace popup. Hold physical Backspace (reaches Orbit), hold Alt, press CapsLock (resolves to Backspace, captured by the popup shortcut). If the popup request fails (for example at workspace capacity) the attachment stays. The first native release is consumed as shared by pin_key; the last is consumed by consumes_shortcut. Orbit never sees Backspace's release and pressed_keys keeps it until the next retirement or native focus loss.

## Scope

venus/src/input.rs InputState pin_key / consumes_shortcut only. Preserve release delivery for an admitted terminal sequence when another native key starts a capture. Out of scope: VEN-C2 text (unchanged), Orbit.

## Acceptance

A focused InputState test covering both release orders through capture and terminal bookkeeping (red before, green after); existing Venus suite, fmt and clippy green.
close_reason: Capture release hands the resolved key's one release to the terminal when it holds that key; red/green test, Venus suite, fmt, clippy green; Claude+Codex clean

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Implemented. Not consequential (no dependency, protocol, contract or boundary change; VEN-C2 text unchanged), so no reference gate.

Fix: InputState::consumes_shortcut (venus/src/input.rs). When a captured key's release arrives while the terminal still holds the same resolved key in pressed_keys, the capture ends and the release passes on to the terminal. This happens only when two native keys coalesce on one resolved key (VEN-C2). Each handler in the KeyboardInput chain acts only on Pressed, so the release reaches InputState::key and commit_key. Retiring paths are unchanged: retirement empties pressed_keys. The pin_key doc now names the hand-off.

He approved the shape the same day ("file", answering the overseer's item: auto-dismiss the success notice after about 2 seconds, keep failure notices until acknowledged, and never let any notice block links).

## Why it matters

After a link opens, the browser takes focus, so the VEN-C8 notice waits for the next input in Eon and lingers. eon-empty-attention-notice-opy3 (landed 8f375fb) found that every VEN-C8 workspace notice outranks the link status and disables link highlight and open while it shows (venus/src/application.rs around 2564 and 3125 at that time). So a lingering link notice silently blocks the next link click.

## Change (VEN-C8 wording to Lucca before code)

- The link-opened success notice dismisses itself after about 2 s, and on the next input as today. It schedules one timed redraw and no repeating ticks.
- Link open failures keep today's lifetime: they persist until the user acts.
- No notice disables link highlight or open. Link hover and click work while any notice shows.
- Configurability rule: record whether the 2 s value is configurable or fixed, and why. The overseer leans toward fixed, a UX timing with no reason for users to differ, unless the audit epic (eon-configurability-qkq8) already plans a notice-duration setting.

## Acceptance

- A Venus model or scene test: the success notice is gone after its timeout with no input, a failure notice persists, and a link is clickable while a notice shows. The test fails on today's code.
- One installed observation: open a link, return to Eon after a few seconds, and the notice is gone.

## Verification

`nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-venus`, Venus fmt and clippy, converge plus Codex, and the profile refresh plus the observation.

title: Define Eon as a Linux Wayland product
description:
Contract: revise EON-C7. Consumer: Eon users, release work, and child repositories. Trigger: platform, desktop-backend, or distribution decisions. Result: Eon supports Linux on native Wayland; each channel names the Linux architectures it actually proves. X11, Xwayland, and macOS are outside the product contract. Preserve platform-neutral wire formats and state where they remain the natural owner, without preserving a portability promise or parallel backend. Important failures: public docs, policy, and release design must not claim macOS or X11 support; child implementations must not be changed from this owner-only slice. Prerequisite: user selected Linux/Wayland-only on 2026-08-21. Scope boundary: Eon policy, contracts, distribution design, references, generated agent instructions, and LOC only. Venus backend removal and child policy cleanup require ordered follow-up beads.

## Acceptance Criteria

EON-C7 states the Linux/Wayland-only product contract, distinguishes platform support from each channel exact architecture proof, and claims no runtime proof beyond the accepted x86_64 alpha. README and distribution docs describe macOS, X11, and Xwayland as unsupported rather than deferred targets. Repository-local policy names Linux/Wayland as the sole platform and generated AGENTS.md matches it. The reference route records the adopted foot/Monstar mechanism and rejected cross-platform scope. README LOC is exact. No runtime, component manifest, child repository, or live Session changes occur.
design: Owner: Eon product platform and distribution policy. Reference gate: foot 85655c74a4ded119392ea8b632626c3920042807 demonstrates a maintained Wayland-only terminal and headless Wayland proof; Monstar 71e4babde8e47e0739abd610f2afe202c8e99c00 demonstrates a compact direct-Wayland Zig terminal; Ghostty remains the comparison showing that cross-platform GUI support entails distinct native application and renderer ownership. Adopt: Linux native Wayland as the one supported platform, keep existing winit/Wayland ownership in Venus until its follow-up, and retain neutral protocols. Reject: macOS signing/notarization work, X11/Xwayland compatibility, raw-Wayland rewrites in Eon, and speculative portability seams. Cheapest check: rendered Starcompass import, exact contract/reference/doc assertions, LOC, Beads state, and git diff checks.

title: List every Eon window, including the default workspace, as open or detached (optional)
description:
## Why

eon-n77e (Lucca pre-approved its pick on 2026-10-22) puts window switching in 1.0 as shape A: an in-Eon picker over every Eon window. Today `eon windows` cannot back such a picker:

- It does not say whether a window is open or detached. The Runtime reply has no presentation field (runtime v17.rs:348-356), and attach always reads as available (supervisor.rs:1781-1788).
- It omits the default workspace, because that lives outside `w/` (windows.rs:255-301).
- It gives no summary a user could recognize a window by.
- After a profile upgrade, a window still on the previous generation cannot be reattached (`window attach` uses the exact current generation only: windows.rs:176-191, generation.rs:430-450). The listing still shows attach as available for it.

## Contract (proposed; bring the exact EON-C23 amendment to Lucca before code)

`eon windows` and `eon windows --json` list every Eon window of this user, including the default workspace. Each entry has:

- its ID (the default workspace gets a fixed, documented ID);
- whether it is open (a Venus is presenting it) or detached;
- a short summary of its tabs taken from data the runtime already owns, such as tab directory names;
- whether this Eon can attach it, and if not, why (for example, it runs another generation).

`eon window attach ID` also accepts `--json`. The listing never starts, attaches or focuses anything.

## Reference gate

Consequential only if presentation state has to cross EONW: then it changes EON-C11/EONW and needs the full gate.

- The gate is recorded on eon-n77e: tmux 3.8, Zellij v0.45.1, WezTerm e2a98e1b, kitty v0.49.2, Rex, herdr and tuios. Every one lists detached work with an attached/detached marker and lists it on the CLI as JSON.
- In this bead's commit, add a docs/REFERENCES.md route for session and window switching, citing those pins. Its rejections:
  - B, in-window swap;
  - name-as-identity;
  - a merged inventory that guesses state (Ghosthub route :107).
- Prefer deriving "open" from state the runtime already has (`state.venus`), without adding a second owner.

## Scope

In scope: listing data and its JSON, the default workspace entry, attachability, `--json` on attach, EON-C23/USAGE text, CHANGELOG.

Out of scope:

- names (the next bead);
- the picker;
- making attach work across generations: this bead only reports it honestly, and fixing it is a separate decision.

## Acceptance

With a default workspace, one open window and one detached window, `eon windows --json` lists all three, with the correct open or detached state and a non-empty summary. A detached window from another generation shows as not attachable, with its reason.

## Verification

Run through `nix develop -c eon-test` with focused tests. If EONW changes, the full affected Rust and Nix surfaces. One installed observation in the switching batch. Codex on every code change.

title: Turn stacked rows' corners toward the expanded pane and join their sides
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-10-24, on eon-2x6h's stacked collapsed rows (installed, after eon-54jv): "can we extend the
borders from the rounded edges into the edges of the visible pane of the stack? tiny nit", then, on the
rows below the expanded pane: "lol. these guys are pointing down instead of up". Today every collapsed
row draws its card's rounded top edge with short corner hooks that curl down, also below the expanded
pane, and the hooks stop after one corner radius, so the stack's sides are broken curls.

## Behaviour

- A collapsed row's corner hooks turn toward the column's expanded pane: rows above it curl down, rows
  below it curl up.
- Its sides continue in that direction to the next card, so each side of the stack is one continuous
  line with rounded joints that meets the expanded pane's frame.
- Neutral rows use the border width; the selected pane's focus frame stays its own rounded frame, and
  no neutral paint lies under it (eon-e8hh/eon-f5pg rule).
- Labels, fill (eon-54jv), rows (33/31/30), hit targets and AccessKit unchanged.

## Contract

VEN-C8 collapsed-row sentence; wording to Lucca before code.

## Acceptance

- Venus paint test (fails first): hooks above the expanded pane point down and below it point up;
  continuous sides from the top row to the expanded frame and from it to the bottom row; no neutral
  paint under the focus frame; scales 1 and 1.3; widths 1/1, 1/2, 2/2; first/middle/last selected.
- Isolated capture with Lucca's opacity: a stack with rows above and below the expanded pane.

Portability: neutral.
close_reason: Stack corners turn toward the expanded pane and sides join; proof in comments

Read as approval of the behaviour above and of the proposed VEN-C8 replacement: 'A collapsed pane is one title row showing its card's rounded top edge with its label in it' becomes 'A collapsed pane is one title row showing a rounded edge with its label in it; its corners turn toward the column's expanded pane and its sides continue to the next card in that direction' (the rest of the sentence unchanged). title: Launch Eon on Apple Silicon macOS: agents port and prove it, Yu checks last
description:
## Why

Lucca wants Eon to launch with Apple Silicon macOS support, with agents doing nearly all of the
port and proof on Linux plus automated Mac runs, and Yu doing only a short final check. Today
Eon cannot even build for `aarch64-darwin`: `flake.nix:62` hardcodes `x86_64-linux`, every
component in `components/eon-v4.json` targets `x86_64-linux`, and Eon Runtime reads Linux
peer credentials and `/proc` unguarded (`runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/sessions.rs:424-458`,
`:572-593`), so on macOS it would fail to compile, and if it compiled it would treat every live
terminal as dead (`:767`, `:1386`).

Native history: ORB-C14 passed on the old Rust Orbit at `4910b81` (`eon-orb-c14-mac-reproof-l8rz`)
and is "Not proved for this tree" after the Bend swap (`orbit/docs/CONTRACTS.md:809-841`). VEN-C16
has a partial native proof at `e0aa47e` on one scale-1 VNC display (`eon-z4n6`;
`venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md:1053-1090`: Retina, Kotoeri IME, renderer recovery not observed; Han
blank and some emoji uncomposed with stock fonts). Full Eon (EON-C7,
`eon-prove-full-eon-apple-silicon-macos-t8o`) never ran on a Mac. The Scaleway Mac was deleted
on 2026-10-20.

## Lucca's direction (relayed by eon-overseer, 2026-10-27; his words)

> "Yu is time constrained and already has ssh on his plate. i'd rather test everything possible
> and fix myself, letting to Yu only final testing and final fixes that i missed. we can even give
> him a list of tests to run (without overwhelmiing him). so the more automated, the better."

On launching: "it would be nice to launch with mac support, and we already have yu and his
friends". He also approved: "Yu's friends start only after full Eon builds and launches on Yu's
Mac with the Orbit and Venus suites passing; the README lists the macOS gaps; their patches
count as outside contributions."

Standing constraints: no slow manual VNC proof; everything on a remote Mac is driven over SSH,
GUI captures included (memory `no-slow-manual-vnc-proof`, decision on
`ven-prove-venus-apple-silicon-macos-nm7` 2026-10-18). Hosted macOS stays within R$100/month
(`eon-prove-full-eon-apple-silicon-macos-t8o`, 2026-09-11). Nix-only, Apple Silicon only; no
signing, notarization, DMG, Homebrew or Intel macOS (`eon-hzq` owns distribution).

## Children, in order

1. Map compile errors and Linux-only assumptions from Linux (gate + sweep).
2. Port Runtime peer identity and liveness to macOS.
3. Venus CPU/RAM chips on macOS.
4. Remaining Linux-only runtime assumptions (runtime dir, socket path bound, notification).
5. Runtime and Eon test suites runnable on macOS (Darwin `eon-test`).
6. Admit `aarch64-darwin` in the one component manifest.
7. `aarch64-darwin` flake outputs, evaluated from Linux.
8. macOS proof harness, part 1: build and suites.
9. macOS proof harness, part 2: GUI scenario, Retina probe, Yu's evidence command.
10. Decision: GitHub Actions macOS job (not scope until Lucca decides; blocks nothing).
11. Yu's guided final check: one command, at most ten items, one evidence bundle.
12. Remote batch: one rented Mac for 24 h (needs Lucca's go), fix loop, record proofs, dry-run
    Yu's check.
13. Yu runs the check; his findings are fixed or accepted as gaps.
14. Friends' gate: README gaps, preview wording (`eon-igae.5`), AGENTS.md Status.

Children 2-4 and 6 can run in parallel after 1 (2 and 4 both touch Runtime: land 2 first).
Each child is one session; 12 and 13 wait on a Mac and on Yu.

Existing beads this epic feeds, not duplicates: `eon-prove-full-eon-apple-silicon-macos-t8o`
(EON-C7; blocked by the batch), `ven-prove-venus-apple-silicon-macos-nm7` and its children
`c3b`, `yzw`, `piy` (VEN-C16; the harness gathers their automatable evidence),
`eon-igae.6` (Retina for the 1.0 preview; blocked by Yu's run), `eon-igae.5` (tier wording;
blocks the friends' gate), `eon-agent-background-work-yte0.1` (its Darwin path is compiled by
the gate and run natively by the harness), and the recipes in closed `eon-orb-c14-mac-reproof-l8rz`
and `eon-z4n6`.

## Acceptance

- Full Eon builds from this repository's flake on `aarch64-darwin` and launches natively from the
  harness, with ORB-C14's Orbit suite, Venus's suite and Runtime's suite passing natively;
  ORB-C14, VEN-C16 and EON-C7 proof records name the exact revision, Mac, macOS and artifacts.
- Yu has run a checklist of at most ten items on his Mac and reported through one evidence
  command; what he found is fixed or listed as a README gap.
- README lists the macOS gaps and the preview tier text approved on `eon-igae.5`; only then do
  Yu's friends start.
- Linux proofs stay green: `x86_64-linux` derivations unchanged unless a child says why.

## Stop conditions (all children)

- Any contract add/change (EON-C, ORB-C, VEN-C wording or status beyond a proof record) stops for
  Lucca's approval.
- Renting a Mac stops for Lucca's explicit go on the cost.
- A new dependency, toolchain input, language or CI workflow stops for Lucca's decision.
- A platform blocker (AGENTS.md "Platform Discipline") stops for Lucca's choice.

title: Map Eon's macOS compile errors and Linux-only assumptions from Linux
description:
## Why

Agents on Linux cannot build or run `aarch64-darwin`, so the cheapest early signal is a Rust
compile check for the Apple target plus a sweep for Linux-only assumptions. This bead produces
the exact list the port beads fix, so no Mac time is spent finding compile errors.

Lucca (2026-10-27, relayed by eon-overseer): "i'd rather test everything possible and fix myself,
letting to Yu only final testing and final fixes that i missed ... so the more automated, the
better."

## Evidence

- `rustup target list --installed` on this machine includes `aarch64-apple-darwin` (outside the
  Nix dev shell; nixpkgs `rustc` ships only the host std).
- Preliminary sweep at `4ae8a21` (verify and extend):
  - `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/sessions.rs:424-458` `validate_management_peer`:
    `libc::ucred`/`SO_PEERCRED` (absent on Apple targets, so a compile error) and
    `/proc/<pid>/stat` start time. Owner: Runtime port bead.
  - `sessions.rs:572-593` `recorded_process_is_dead`: `/proc` NotFound means dead; callers `:767`,
    `:1386` would retire every live terminal on macOS. Owner: Runtime port bead.
  - `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/supervisor.rs:681-692` `base_runtime_directory`: macOS has no
    `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, so every launch warns and falls back to `$TMPDIR/eon-<uid>`
    (`/var/folders/...`, long). macOS `sun_path` is 104 bytes. Owner: remaining-assumptions bead.
  - `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/notification.rs:10,44-51`: first-detach notification is
    Linux-only (zbus); macOS is a silent no-op. Owner: remaining-assumptions bead.
  - `venus/src/system.rs:13-19,93-99`: CPU/RAM from `/proc`; `None` elsewhere. Owner: Venus chips bead.
  - Tests: `sessions.rs:1676,1819,1938`, `supervisor.rs:2156-2161,2290`, and about 25 `/proc`
    reads in `eon/crates/eon/tests/workspace_control.rs`; `nix/test-sandbox.nix` needs bubblewrap.
    Owner: tests bead.
  - Already split: `orbit/src/platform.rs` (Linux/macOS seams), `orbit/build.rs:46-48`,
    `orbit/tests/lifecycle.rs` (3 Linux-only tests), `venus/src/launch.rs:424-427`,
    `venus/src/application.rs`, Venus render tests (`#[cfg(target_os = "linux")]`, ignored).
  - Nix: `flake.nix:62`, `:202` (CodexBar linux-musl asset), `:320-348` (X11/Wayland libs, Mesa,
    fontconfig), `:875` (kinestra recorder, `x86_64-linux` only), `:888-919` bundle relink
    (`relink/src/main.rs:20` ld-linux), `:919-934` br/bv Linux assets, `:652` manifest target
    assert; `components/eon-v4.json` targets. Owners: manifest and flake beads.

## Scope

In scope: run the check; extend the sweep (also `std::os::linux`, `/sys`, `/dev/shm`, `pidfd`,
`epoll`, `inotify`, `prctl`, `MSG_NOSIGNAL`, `SOCK_CLOEXEC`, `accept4`, `pipe2`, `O_PATH`,
`getrandom`, Wayland-only env, shell scripts under `nix/` and `eon/`); record results as a comment
on this bead and on each owning sibling bead; fix nothing except trivially mis-scoped `cfg`s that
block the check for other crates (if any, one commit, Codex per AGENTS.md).

Out of scope: the fixes owned by sibling beads; Nix changes; a permanent Nix route for the check.

## Acceptance

- One exact command per crate (`cargo check --locked --target aarch64-apple-darwin -p <crate>
  --all-targets` where possible) with its result for: `orbit-protocol`, `eon-workspace-protocol`,
  `eon-manifest`, `eon-runtime`, `eon`, `yazelix-venus`, `yazelix-orbit`. Crates whose build
  scripts cannot run for the Apple target on Linux (likely `libghostty-vt-sys` via Zig and the
  Apple SDK, and Orbit's Bun/clang worker) are named with the failing step.
- The sweep list above, confirmed or corrected with `file:line`, each item assigned to a sibling
  bead or recorded as already handled.
- `yte0.1`'s Darwin `proc_listchildpids` path is included if it has landed.

## Verification

- The commands and outputs summarized on the bead (first error per crate). No proof claim: a
  compile check is not native proof (EON-C7 rejects compile-only claims).

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if making the check permanent needs a new flake input (rust-overlay, fenix) or a CI job:
  that is a dependency/CI decision for Lucca.
- Stop if a finding needs a contract change or a platform blocker.

## Maintenance Notes

- Rejected: adding the Apple std to the Nix dev shell in this bead (dependency gate).
- This list is the input to beads 2-7 of the epic; keep it on this bead so they can cite it.

comments.text:
Review pass 3 (fresh context): 3 blocking, 10 nits. Final amendment; with this the deliverable is the map plus its three amendments, read together.

Missed, no owner: macOS system ncurses likely cannot read `TERM=eon`. Orbit sets TERM=eon (orbit/src/pty.rs:750; ORB-C10). orbit/terminfo/eon.terminfo is `use=xterm-256color`, compiled with nixpkgs ncurses `tic -x` (flake.nix:301); xterm-256color's pairs#0x10000 makes tic write the 32-bit extended format: the built entry /nix/store/0dnmgm3iy2qzil53m30dpyfrh5gjlyz6-yazelix-orbit-0.1.0/share/terminfo/e/eon starts with bytes 1e 02 (magic 01036, checked). macOS's system ncurses (5.7) reads only the legacy 0432 format and its terminfo tree uses hex directory names (65/, not e/). Terminals get TERMINFO_DIRS pointing at Orbit's tree (flake.nix:646, :766), so system-ncurses programs (/bin/zsh, less, vim, top, man) most likely report an unknown terminal inside Eon (inference; not run). The `orbit-terminfo` check (nix/orbit-checks.nix:244-255) uses Nix ncurses and would not catch it.

Wrong owner, corrected: the socket-path roots of the Darwin test runs are not kz4p.5's (its Scope is the process-read helper). workspace_control.rs:66 roots at env::temp_dir() and :3788 already notes the length; on Darwin the eonPackage check runs under the nix-build TMPDIR (flake.nix:679-686 is Linux-only), so `<nix-build root>/ec-<pid>-<n>/r/w/<8hex>/generations/g1-<32hex>/session-9999.sock.management` exceeds 104 bytes; eon-test's macOS branch has the same exposure. Owner pending: question 4.

Nits taken:
- application.rs:5697 is a cfg(linux) helper (`native_startup`), not an ignored render test.
- fontdb on macOS also scans /System/Library/AssetsV2 and /Network/Library/Fonts; conclusion unchanged. Question 2's fonts.conf option must handle `<dir prefix="relative">`, which flake.nix:328-331 writes on purpose.
- The poll() risk: the tree has 50 real-PTY checks and bend-orbit ran 36 natively, so 14 have never run on a Mac.
- Logs check-orbit-governance.log and check-yazelix-orbit-narrow.log hold cached output only; their commands are `check-env.sh orbit-governance` and `check-env.sh yazelix-orbit --lib --bins --test lifecycle`, which run the cargo check command above.
- Native-only risk for kz4p.7/kz4p.8: nix/shell-environment.nix's `substituteInPlace --replace-fail` and `sed '1c'` rewrites depend on starship, atuin and carapace init text on Darwin; Linux evaluation cannot catch a mismatch.
- ORB-C14's Boundary (orbit/docs/CONTRACTS.md:805-808) lists Nix packaging as unsupported; a Darwin Orbit proof built through Nix may need that wording reviewed under the epic's contract stop (kz4p.7, kz4p.12).
- Sibling comments now carry the corrected lines (kz4p.2, kz4p.8), the fontconfig refusal (kz4p.16) and question 2's pointer (kz4p.9).

Open questions for Lucca (via eon-overseer), adding to 1 (as amended) and 2:

3. `TERM=eon` on macOS has no owner and its fix touches ORB-C10. Recommendation: a new small child of kz4p, "Make Eon's terminfo readable by macOS system ncurses", blocking kz4p.9 and kz4p.11: compile a legacy-format entry for Darwin (for example cap pairs at 0x7fff, as kitty's entry does, and install both the e/ and 65/ directory names), plus a check that runs /usr/bin/infocmp on the Mac in kz4p.8's harness. Reason: the default macOS shell and pagers inside Eon are the first thing Yu sees; ORB-C10 wording needs Lucca's approval, so that bead stops there.
4. The Darwin test runs' socket roots have no owner. title: Decide whether a GitHub Actions macOS job builds and tests Eon for aarch64-darwin
description:
## Decision needed (Lucca)

Should a GitHub Actions job on GitHub's Apple Silicon macOS runners build Eon for
`aarch64-darwin` and run the harness's headless parts (and optionally its GUI scenario)?
This is a decision, not scope: it adds a workflow (AP-CI-001), needs pushes to `edge` to run,
and costs runner minutes. Nothing is implemented until Lucca answers.

Lucca (2026-10-27, relayed by eon-overseer): "i'd rather test everything possible and fix myself,
letting to Yu only final testing and final fixes that i missed ... so the more automated, the
better."

## Evidence

- `gh repo view` on 2026-10-27: `Yazelix/eon` is PUBLIC. GitHub's standard hosted runners,
  including the Apple Silicon macOS ones, are free for public repositories (verify current
  terms when deciding).
- `.github/workflows/cachix.yml` already builds `x86_64-linux` on push to `edge` and publishes the
  runtime closure to the `eon-yazelix` Cachix cache; a Darwin job could push the Darwin closure
  too, so Yu and his friends install without compiling Rust, Ghostty and Helix on their Macs.
- `ven-qualify-venus-stack-apple-silicon-macos-ili` closed Conditional-Go from GitHub Actions run
  34809546212 on a standard M1: wgpu Metal, glyphon, AccessKit, AppKit window creation and
  visible presentation initialized there (per `ven-prove-venus-apple-silicon-macos-nm7`). So a
  runner can likely run Venus and the GUI scenario, at a virtual display without Retina.
- `eon-prove-full-eon-apple-silicon-macos-t8o` already planned "bounded standard Apple Silicon
  GitHub-hosted jobs first" for automated child and composition checks.

## Options

1. Workflow-dispatch and push-to-`edge` job on `macos-15` (arm64): `nix build` of the Darwin
   package, Darwin checks, `eon-test`, harness `run` (and `scenario` if the runner's GUI session
   allows), evidence uploaded as an artifact with short retention, Darwin closure pushed to
   Cachix. Bounded: one job, timeout, concurrency cancel, no fork secrets, repository guard as in
   `cachix.yml`.
2. Workflow-dispatch only (agents trigger it for a candidate), no push trigger.
3. No CI; rely on the rental and Yu.

## Recommendation

Option 2 first, then option 1 once green. Reason: on a public repository it gives agents a free
native Darwin build-and-test loop from Linux sessions, so the fix loop happens before any paid
rental; it can shrink or remove the rental, and the Cachix push makes Yu's install fast. Retina,
IME, VoiceOver and real-GPU behavior still need a physical Mac (Yu).

## Open sub-questions for Lucca

- Is a GitHub VM run (Apple Virtualization on Apple Silicon) acceptable as native proof for
  ORB-C14 and the suite parts of VEN-C16/EON-C7, or only as candidate evidence before the
  bare-metal batch? Recommendation: candidate evidence only, plus suite proof for ORB-C14 if he
  agrees; GUI proof stays on bare metal or Yu's Mac.

## Acceptance (if approved)

Lucca's answer is quoted on this bead with date; if he approves, a separate implementation bead
(or this bead retyped to a task) names the workflow file, triggers, permissions, timeout,
artifacts, cache behavior and its removal condition per AP-CI-001, and is proved by one green
workflow run on the candidate revision.
close_reason: Decided 2026-10-27 (Lucca, relayed by eon-overseer, comments on this bead): '1 ok' = a GitHub Actions macOS job, run by hand at first (option 2, then option 1 once green); '2 ok' = a runner VM is candidate evidence plus ORB-C14 suite proof, never GUI proof. Implementation: eon-mac-launch-kz4p.15, which now blocks the rental kz4p.12 ('only after the harness passes on CI', kz4p.12's '3 ok').

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Lucca approved (relayed by eon-overseer, 2026-10-27), answering "GitHub Actions macOS job: yes, run by hand at first ...": "1 ok". The workflow needs a push, which stays on his explicit request.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Lucca (relayed by eon-overseer, 2026-10-27), after the explanation that the GitHub runner gives free repeated build/test rounds so the paid rental day goes to GUI and hardware proof, and that a runner VM counts only as candidate evidence (plus ORB-C14 suite proof), never GUI proof: "2 ok".

title: Build Yu's guided macOS final check: one command, ten items, one bundle
description:
## Why

Yu has little time ("Yu is time constrained and already has ssh on his plate"). His check must
be short, guided and self-reporting: one command that walks him through at most ten items,
captures evidence for each, and produces one bundle he sends back. This bead builds that guided
mode and the list; the next sibling is Yu actually running it.

Lucca (2026-10-27, relayed by eon-overseer): "i'd rather test everything possible and fix myself,
letting to Yu only final testing and final fixes that i missed. we can even give him a list of
tests to run (without overwhelmiing him). so the more automated, the better."

## Evidence

- Yu has a Mac mini; Retina needs a HiDPI monitor (scale 2), which no remote Mac we used had
  (`venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md:1053`, 1920x1080 scale 1).
- Items no remote run has observed: Retina redraw, Kotoeri IME (`venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md:1081`),
  Han/emoji with stock fonts (`:1085-1086`), a real Claude agent in the sidebar (EON-C31), Yazi
  images on the installed Eon on macOS, detach/attach by hand.
- Harness tool and evidence layout: the two harness siblings.

## Scope

In scope: a `final` subcommand of the harness tool, run by Yu as one command (e.g.
`nix run github:Yazelix/eon/<tag-or-rev>#mac-proof -- final`), which installs or runs the exact
build, then for each item prints one or two lines of what to do, waits for Enter, takes a
`screencapture` (asks for Screen Recording permission once, explaining why), asks pass/fail plus
an optional note, and finally writes `eon-mac-final-<rev>-<date>.tar.gz` with versions, hardware
and display info, logs, captures and answers. A short `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md` (or README "Mac
preview" link) section with the same list for reading ahead.

Proposed list (at most ten; final wording on this bead before code):
1. Install and launch: the command above opens Eon; `eon versions` shows `aarch64-darwin`.
2. Retina: on the HiDPI monitor, text is crisp; the tool records backing scale 2.
3. Resize and move the window between the HiDPI and another display, if he has one (skip
   otherwise).
4. Typing and IME: type in a shell; switch to a Japanese or Chinese input source and compose one
   word.
5. Fonts: `cat` a prepared file with Han, emoji (modifier and flag), combining marks.
6. Tabs, panes and popups by keyboard: new tab, split, Alt+Z zoom, Helix and Yazi popups.
7. Yazi image preview of a prepared PNG.
8. Agent sidebar: start `claude` in a pane, ask one short question, see working then done.
9. Copy and paste with Command+C/Command+V to and from another app.
10. Detach and attach: quit the window, run `eon attach`, the shell history is still there.
Plus automatic, no action: the harness suites summary from his Mac (`run`), since the friends'
gate requires "the Orbit and Venus suites passing" on Yu's Mac.

How to report: send the tarball to Lucca (channel Lucca names); failures become beads.

Out of scope: VoiceOver and blur (unless Lucca adds them), fixes (next sibling), anything that
needs ssh access to Yu's Mac.

## Acceptance

- `final --dry-run` walks the list without capturing; the full `final` was run once on the rented
  Mac in the batch bead (sibling) and its bundle reviewed.
- The list has at most ten manual items, each with expected result in one sentence.
- Deterministic parts (bundle manifest, answer recording) have a few tests; fmt, clippy, Codex.

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test -p <harness crate>` exits 0.
- One dry-run bundle attached to this bead's notes (path outside the repository).

## Stop Conditions

- Stop for Lucca's approval of the final list wording before building (one comment, numbered).
- Stop if any item needs Yu to install extra software beyond Nix and `claude`.
close_reason: final built and dry-run proved on Linux (fmt, clippy Linux and darwin, eon-test -p mac-proof, nix run .#mac-proof -- final --help, dry-run bundle); Opus gates plus Codex review clean. The one native final run and its bundle review are kz4p.12's acceptance.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Lucca approved Yu's ten-item list as drafted (relayed by eon-overseer, 2026-10-27): "9 okay". This satisfies the stop condition on the list wording.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Plan (yufinal, Opus planner; Codex implements, Opus gates), 2026-10-28, on edge a36f243.

Approval relayed by eon-overseer (AP-COORDINATOR-001): Lucca, 2026-10-27, "do these two too, then ... i want to move closer to the 'yu testing' gate", standing for the macOS launch path. It covers this bead's build; it does not cover push, promotion, GitHub posts, workflow dispatch or a rented Mac.

## Q1 for Lucca: the revised list (stop condition; code waits for his answer)

The 2026-10-27 approval ("9 okay") was for the drafted ten. kz4p.9 and kz4p.17 now automate four of them, so the list shrinks to eight. Each item below is what `final` prints, then the expected result.

Done automatically first, with no action from Yu: the whole `run` on his Mac. That covers the package build, terminfo, the flake checks, the Orbit, Venus and Runtime suites, and the GUI scenario. The scenario covers launch, `eon versions` naming aarch64-darwin, Retina scale 2, panes, tabs, Files, zoom, Shortcuts, Kitty images, Command+V paste, detach/attach, crash, adoption and leftovers. That retires drafted items 1 (install and launch) and 10 (detach and attach). It also halves item 9: only Command+C on a pointer selection is still manual, as the scenario's help says.

1. Look. On a Retina screen (HiDPI monitor or a MacBook's display), look at Eon's window.
   Expected: text and the Eon Bar are sharp, not blurry, and the bar's CPU and RAM chips show numbers that change.
2. Second display (answer s to skip if you have only one). Drag the window to the other display and back, then resize it.
   Expected: text stays sharp on each display and the panes refit with no gaps or garbage.
3. Typing and input methods. Type `echo hello` and press Return. Then switch to a Japanese or Chinese input source, compose one word and commit it.
   Expected: the composition shows at the cursor and the committed word lands in the shell.
4. Fonts. Run `cat glyphs.txt`.
   Expected: Han characters, emoji (one with a skin tone, one flag) and accented letters each show as one glyph, with no empty boxes or overlaps.
5. Keyboard. Open Shortcuts with Option+/. Then use the keys it lists to open a tab, split a pane, move between panes and open the Helix popup.
   Expected: each key does what Shortcuts says.
6. Yazi images. Open Files with Option+Shift+Y and select `eon.png`.
   Expected: the picture shows in Yazi's preview.
7. Agent. In a pane, run `claude` (Claude Code 2.1.295 or later) and ask one short question.
   Expected: the sidebar marks the agent working, then done when it answers.
8. Copy out. Select text in Eon with the pointer, press Command+C and paste into another app (for example Notes).
   Expected: the same text arrives.

Out of scope, as drafted: VoiceOver and blur. Recommendation: approve these eight. Each is something no automated step observes, and each costs Yu about a minute.

## Implementation plan

All of it lives in `eon/tools/mac-proof`, plus the flake app and docs. No new crate dependency, protocol, contract or trust boundary is added, so this is not a consequential shape and needs no reference gate. Yu's Mac is driven only by the tool he runs himself, with no ssh.

What Yu types is one command: `nix run github:Yazelix/eon/<rev>#mac-proof -- final`. The flow:

1. **Preflight.** Require Apple Silicon macOS (dry runs excepted). Check both grants with `mac::grants()`. If either is missing, explain why it is needed: Screen Recording for the captures, Accessibility for the scenario's keys. Then open the matching System Settings pane and exit 2 before any long work, telling Yu to grant his terminal app, reopen it and rerun.
2. **Source.** The flake app's wrapper sets `MAC_PROOF_SOURCE=${self}` and `MAC_PROOF_REV=${self.rev or "dirty"}`. This goes in a small app wrapper, not in the cargo derivation, so the crate does not rebuild per commit. `final` copies that tree into a fresh temp directory and makes it writable. `run`'s source step already commits an archive extraction, so the copy can feed it. Without `MAC_PROOF_SOURCE`, `final` uses the current directory, as `run` does.
3. **Automatic part.** `final` calls the same steps `run` does, with evidence in `<out>/run`, under `caffeinate -d -i -s -w <own pid>` so the Mac stays awake. It first prints that the run takes hours, that Yu must leave the Mac awake and untouched until it rings, and that the GUI scenario types into Eon. It rings (BEL plus `osascript display notification`) when the manual part starts.
4. **Manual part.** If the package step passed, `final` launches Eon from the built package. Yu's real HOME and environment stay, so his shell setup and logged-in `claude` work. Eon's own state is private: `EON_CONFIG_HOME`, `XDG_STATE_HOME` and `EON_RUNTIME_DIR` go under a private root. The launch directory holds `glyphs.txt` and `eon.png`, copied from `assets/eon.png`. For each item, `final`:
   - prints the item and waits for Enter;
   - re-attaches Eon if Venus is gone;
   - captures only Eon's window, with `screencapture -x -R` on its bounds from `mac::windows`;
   - asks `p`, `f` or `s` and an optional note.

   After the last item it runs `eon stop all` and copies Eon's logs.
5. **Bundle.** `final` writes the evidence folder and the archive in HOME:
   - folder `<out>` (default `~/eon-mac-final-<rev12>-<YYYY-MM-DD>`, then `-2` and up if it exists), holding `summary.txt`, `final.json` (schema 1: rev, tree, date, run result, items with answer, note, capture and seconds), `run/`, `manual/`, `versions.txt` and `displays.json`;
   - archive `<out>.tar.gz`, beside the folder.

   It prints the archive's path and that Yu can look inside before sending it to Lucca.

Reuse, not parallel code:
- **Scenario.** Its environment becomes a parameter: private HOME, or Yu's own with private Eon roots. `final` reuses `start`, `wait_for_workspace`, `wait_for_venus`, `reattach`, `act`, `stop` and `clean` through a narrow pub surface.
- **retina.rs.** `report` writes `displays.json`, and `mac::displays` supplies the display list.
- **run.rs.** `run`'s step list is shared between `run` and `final`.
- **Privacy fix in a shared owner.** A new pure function strips serial numbers and hardware UUIDs from `system_profiler` JSON. Both run's host step and the scenario's retina report use it. `uname -a` becomes `uname -srm` (no hostname). Only Yu's bundle goes to a person, but one owner fixes both.

Pure and tested on Linux, run with `nix develop -c eon-test -p mac-proof`:
- the item table: eight or fewer items, each with a one-sentence expected result;
- answer parsing: p/f/s, a re-ask on anything else, and EOF making the rest "unanswered";
- `final.json` and `summary.txt`;
- the bundle name and the civil date computed from Unix time (no new dependency);
- the redaction;
- an integration test: `final --dry-run` with scripted stdin writes a `.tar.gz` whose listing and `final.json` match. The dry run walks the list without launching or capturing.

Mac-only, proved only in kz4p.12's rented-Mac batch: grants, caffeinate, the manual launch, the window capture and the full flow.

Scope boundary: the `final` subcommand, the shared refactors above, the redaction, the flake app wrapper, and a short "Yu's final check" subsection in `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md` (command, item titles, where the bundle goes). The README is left alone. Out of scope: running the list on a Mac (kz4p.12, kz4p.13), fixes to what it finds, VoiceOver and blur, and any change to the scenario's steps or run's step order.

Checks:
- `nix develop -c eon-test -p mac-proof`;
- `cargo fmt --check`;
- clippy `-D warnings` for mac-proof on Linux and `--target aarch64-apple-darwin`;
- `nix build .#mac-proof` on Linux and an eval of the aarch64-darwin app;
- one dry-run bundle, kept outside the repository and named on this bead;
- the Codex review AGENTS.md requires.

Lucca approved Q1 and Q2 (relayed by eon-overseer, 2026-10-28). His words: "approve".
- Q1: Yu's list is the eight items exactly as worded in the plan comment. This satisfies the stop condition on the list wording; it replaces the 2026-10-27 ten-item approval.

Proof and review (yufinal, 2026-10-28). The candidate is rebased onto edge c9c01d1 and committed as one commit, whose revision is this proof's. Tree: c6acbe350572f8ef4a2f5b1da3987e1f1ca8d2ec, with untracked files and this worktree's .beads included.

title: Run the macOS harness on one rented Mac and record ORB-C14, VEN-C16 and EON-C7 proof
description:
## Why

The ported code, Darwin flake outputs and harness are proved only by running them on a Mac. One
bounded rental, driven entirely over SSH by the harness, should turn the candidate into recorded
native proofs for ORB-C14, the suite and launch parts of VEN-C16, and EON-C7, and fix what
breaks while the Mac is still rented. Yu then only checks what a remote Mac cannot show.

Lucca (2026-10-27, relayed by eon-overseer): "i'd rather test everything possible and fix myself,
letting to Yu only final testing and final fixes that i missed. we can even give him a list of
tests to run (without overwhelmiing him). so the more automated, the better."

## Evidence

- Previous rental: Scaleway M2-M, fr-par-1, macOS 26.7.1, 24 h minimum; ORB-C14 (old Rust Orbit)
  and the VEN-C16 baseline were run from it (`eon-orb-c14-mac-reproof-l8rz`, `eon-z4n6`).
  Deleted 2026-10-20 (`ven-prove-venus-apple-silicon-macos-nm7` comment). Hosted macOS ceiling
  R$100/month (`eon-prove-full-eon-apple-silicon-macos-t8o`, 2026-09-11).
- Proof records to write: ORB-C14 "Open proof" (`orbit/docs/CONTRACTS.md:835-841`); VEN-C16
  native environment and gaps (`venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md:1053-1090`); EON-C7 "Open proof"
  (`docs/CONTRACTS.md:345-355`). AGENTS.md: "Do not mark a contract `Proven` from a document or
  mock"; proof records cite check, exact revisions, platform and artifact.

## Scope

In scope:
1. Ask Lucca for the go on one 24 h rental (Scaleway M2 or a cheaper equivalent he names), with
   the expected cost against the R$100/month ceiling. If the CI decision bead approved a runner
   route, first run the harness there and rent only for what remains.
2. Prepare the Mac over SSH only: Nix install, GUI auto-login if needed, the TCC items the
   harness probe reports (any click goes to Lucca as one short request, with "defer to Yu" as the
   alternative).
3. `mac-proof remote` on the frozen candidate (coordinate a branch freeze with eon-overseer per
   AP-COORDINATOR-001); fix failures on Linux in their owning code with focused commits (each
   through its normal review), re-run the harness on the new candidate; stop new fixes with
   enough rental left for one final full run on the final revision (AGENTS.md "Batch proof").
4. Dry-run Yu's guided check (sibling) on the Mac so Yu's first run is not its first run.
5. Record proofs from the final run only: ORB-C14 (Orbit suite natively), VEN-C16 native
   environment and observations updated (still partial unless piy's acceptance is met), EON-C7
   evidence (full Eon on `aarch64-darwin`); status changes beyond proof records need Lucca's
   approval. Record the evidence folder location and keep it outside the repository.
6. Cleanup: Lucca deletes the server; record the deletion.

Out of scope: VoiceOver, Kotoeri IME and blur acceptance (`c3b`, `yzw`), Retina proof unless the
remote display offers scale 2 (harness reports it), distribution (`eon-hzq`).

## Acceptance

- The harness's final `summary.txt` on the final revision shows every suite and scenario step
  passing or `skipped` with a reason that is on Yu's list.
- ORB-C14, VEN-C16 and EON-C7 proof text updated from that run (exact revision, Mac model,
  macOS build, Nix and toolchain versions, display scale, commands, artifacts, limits), through
  the Codex re-check AGENTS.md requires for contract proof records.
- A gaps list (what failed or could not be shown) is posted on the friends'-gate bead for README.
- The Mac is deleted and the cost recorded.

## Verification

- Harness `summary.json` exit status 0 on the final revision; Linux suites still green on the
  same revision (`nix develop -c eon-test`, Linux package build).
