title: Add a hand-dispatched GitHub Actions job that runs the macOS harness on Apple Silicon
description:
## Why

Lucca decided on 2026-10-27 (relayed by eon-overseer, recorded on the closed decision bead
`eon-mac-launch-kz4p.10`) that a GitHub Actions job on GitHub's Apple Silicon macOS runners
builds and tests Eon for `aarch64-darwin`, "run by hand at first" ("1 ok"), and that a runner
VM counts only as candidate evidence plus ORB-C14 suite proof, never GUI proof ("2 ok"). The
rental decision on `eon-mac-launch-kz4p.12` says: "one 24 h Scaleway M2, only after the harness
passes on CI" ("3 ok"). So this job is the free native fix loop that runs before any paid Mac
time, and its green run gates the rental.

## Evidence

- `Yazelix/eon` is public (`gh repo view`, 2026-10-27); standard hosted runners, Apple Silicon
  macOS included, are free for public repositories (re-check current terms before landing).
- `.github/workflows/cachix.yml`: the existing `x86_64-linux` push-to-`edge` workflow and its
  repository guard; reuse its shape (permissions, concurrency, guard).
- `ven-qualify-venus-stack-apple-silicon-macos-ili` (closed Conditional-Go, run 34809546212 on a
  standard M1): wgpu Metal, AppKit window creation and presentation initialized on a runner.
- Harness: `eon-mac-launch-kz4p.8` (`mac-proof run`: build, Darwin checks, Darwin `eon-test`,
  `summary.json`).

## Scope

In scope:
- One workflow file (name it in the bead before code) with `workflow_dispatch` only (option 2 of
  `kz4p.10`): input `rev`; one job on an arm64 macOS runner (`macos-15` or the current arm64
  label); installs Nix; runs `nix run .#mac-proof -- run` on the checked-out revision; uploads
  the evidence folder as an artifact with short retention; job timeout, concurrency cancel, no
  secrets for forks, repository guard as in `cachix.yml`; least permissions (`contents: read`).
- `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md` harness section: how an agent dispatches the job for a candidate
  (`gh workflow run ... -f rev=...`) and fetches the artifact. Dispatching needs the revision on
  GitHub, which needs a push; pushes stay on Lucca's explicit request.
- The AP-CI-001 record on this bead: trigger, permissions, timeout, artifacts, cache behaviour,
  cost, and the removal condition (for example: replaced by option 1 or removed when a
  maintained Mac exists).

Out of scope:
- A push trigger and a Cachix push of the Darwin closure (option 1): only after this job is
  green and Lucca says go.
- The GUI scenario on the runner (`kz4p.9`); add it later only if the runner's session allows,
  as candidate evidence.
- Renting a Mac (`kz4p.12`).

## Acceptance

- One green dispatched run on the candidate revision whose artifact holds the harness
  `summary.json` with every build and suite step passing (or a recorded, owned failure filed as
  a bead).
- If the Orbit suite passes natively there, ORB-C14's proof record may cite the run as suite
  proof (Lucca, "2 ok"); VEN-C16 and EON-C7 get candidate evidence only.

## Verification

- `actionlint` (or the repository's workflow check) is clean; the dispatched run's URL and
  artifact are recorded here.
- Codex review per AGENTS.md (a CI file is code).

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if the job needs a secret, a paid runner or a third-party action beyond the official
  checkout/upload actions and the Nix installer already trusted by `cachix.yml`: ask Lucca.
- Stop if pushing a candidate revision is needed and Lucca has not asked for the push.

Evidence: /home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-overseer/ci-40842410369/. Acceptance met: a green dispatched run whose summary.json has every build and suite step passing. Follow-ups: ORB-C14's proof record may cite this run as suite proof (Lucca, '2 ok'; contract record change, needs its Codex re-check); docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:107-108 'No Mac has run the scenario yet' is stale.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
AP-CI-001 record, additions after the first review round (a Claude reviewer and Codex, both nothing blocking):
- `extra_nix_config: sandbox = false` restates Nix's macOS default explicitly, because Venus's build tests run /bin/ps (eon-zuou) and the harness only logs the setting; it adds no surface beyond the docs' existing requirement.
- Concurrency differs from cachix.yml on purpose: a fixed group `eon-mac-proof`, not per ref, so only one proof runs at a time whatever branch it was dispatched from.
- actions/upload-artifact is not in cachix.yml; it is allowed by this bead's stop condition, which names the official checkout and upload actions. Pinned to v4.6.2 (ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02), the same major as the checkout pin.
- Reduce: dispatch only for candidates that change Orbit, Venus, Eon Runtime, Nix composition or the harness; a docs-only or Linux-only change needs no run.
- Maintenance: SHA-pin bumps with cachix.yml's, and moving off `macos-15` before GitHub retires that image.
- Latency risk: a cold Darwin build on 3 M1 cores may spend most of the 320-minute limit in the `package` step, leaving later steps `skipped` by the run limit. Such a run is recorded and filed as a bead, not counted as acceptance.
- Docs: `rev` must be a full commit SHA (or a branch or tag name); actions/checkout treats a short SHA as a ref name and fails.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Approval (relayed by eon-overseer, the coordinating session): Lucca, 2026-10-27, to eon-overseer: "do these two too, then ... i want to move closer to the 'yu testing' gate", standing for the macOS launch path. Covers this bead's adopted scope only; push, workflow dispatch and GitHub posts stay on Lucca's explicit request.

Workflow file: `.github/workflows/mac-proof.yml` (workflow "macOS proof harness", job `prove`).

Reference gate (hosted automation is a trust boundary):
- Behaviour: a maintainer dispatches the workflow with `rev`; a GitHub-hosted arm64 macOS runner runs `mac-proof run` on that checkout and uploads the evidence folder. Owners: the harness (`eon/tools/mac-proof`, kz4p.8) owns the steps, deadlines and summaries; the workflow owns only trigger, runner, Nix install and artifact upload. No second step list.
- Routes read: `.github/workflows/cachix.yml` (guard, permissions, concurrency, action pins: reused unchanged); GitHub hosted-runner reference (docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/runners/github-hosted-runners, read 2026-10-28): arm64 labels `macos-latest`, `macos-14`, `macos-15`, `macos-26`, 3 M1 CPUs, 7 GB RAM, 14 GB SSD, "free and unlimited on public repositories"; `actions/upload-artifact` tags (v4.6.2 = ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02, `git ls-remote`); the Venus qualification run 34809546212 (`ven-qualify-venus-stack-apple-silicon-macos-ili`) showed wgpu Metal and AppKit start on a standard M1 runner.
- Kept: SHA-pinned actions; only actions/checkout, actions/upload-artifact and cachix/install-nix-action (already trusted by cachix.yml), so no stop condition is hit; `contents: read`; no secrets; repository and public-repo guard.
- Rejected: a push trigger and a Darwin Cachix push (option 1, out of scope until this job is green and Lucca says go); `macos-latest` (moves under us; `macos-15` is a fixed arm64 image, macOS 15 ≥ the harness's 14); a Nix store cache action (another third-party action and cache owner); `mac-proof remote --local` (adds a git archive round trip the checkout does not need: `run` accepts a clean Git checkout directly).
- Decision and check: actionlint 1.7.12 with shellcheck (nixpkgs) clean; the acceptance run is one green dispatched run after Lucca pushes.

AP-CI-001 record:
- Contract: ORB-C14 suite proof (Lucca "2 ok"), candidate evidence for VEN-C16 and EON-C7; never GUI proof. Local proof is insufficient because no maintainer has a Mac (eon-next-expansion-0wfb), and this free loop gates the paid rental (kz4p.12, "3 ok").
- Trigger: `workflow_dispatch` only, input `rev` (empty = the dispatched branch head). No push, schedule or pull-request trigger, so forks and pull requests never start it.
- Jobs: one, `prove`, on `macos-15`.
- Timeout: job 360 minutes (the hosted maximum); harness `--timeout 320m`, so a hung step ends inside the job and the evidence still uploads.
- Permissions: `contents: read`; checkout with `persist-credentials: false`. install-nix-action passes the read-only job token to Nix for GitHub fetches.
- Secrets and forks: none used; the job runs only in `Yazelix/eon` while it is public.
- Concurrency: group `eon-mac-proof`, cancel in progress: one proof at a time, a newer dispatch replaces the running one.
- Artifacts: the evidence folder (`summary.txt`, `summary.json`, `steps/*.log`) as artifact `mac-proof`, uploaded even on failure, kept 14 days.
- Cache: none between runs. Nix substitutes from cache.nixos.org (the flake's Cachix holds Linux paths only); each run builds Eon's Darwin closure and fills ~/.cargo afresh. Risk: the 14 GB nominal SSD may be tight; a disk failure shows in the failing step's log and becomes a bead.
- Cost: free on the public repository (standard runner); none if the repository turns private (guard skips). Latency: hours per run.
- Expand: a push trigger plus Darwin Cachix push (option 1) only after a green run and Lucca's go; the GUI scenario (kz4p.9) only as candidate evidence if the runner session allows.
- Remove: when option 1 replaces it, or when a maintained Mac runs the harness routinely.

## Why

`eon-test` is the only supported route for the Rust suites (AGENTS.md "Testing Discipline"), and
it refuses to run without bubblewrap, which macOS lacks. The macOS harness (`kz4p.8`) and the CI
job (`kz4p.15`) call `nix develop -c eon-test` on the Mac, so `eon-test` needs a macOS branch
with honest isolation. Split on 2026-10-27 from `eon-mac-launch-kz4p.5` (which keeps the tests'
process-read port) so each fits one session.

Lucca (2026-10-27, relayed by eon-overseer): "i'd rather test everything possible and fix myself,
letting to Yu only final testing and final fixes that i missed ... so the more automated, the
better."

## Evidence

- `nix/test-sandbox.nix:1-50`: `eon-test` refuses to run without `bwrap --unshare-all`; it hides
  live Wayland, D-Bus and Eon sockets and gives private PID/network.
- Yu's Mac may run Eon (memory `isolate-eon-test-suites`: never run Eon tests against a live Eon
  without isolation).

## Scope

In scope:
- A macOS branch of `eon-test` in `nix/test-sandbox.nix`: private `HOME`, `TMPDIR`,
  `EON_RUNTIME_DIR` and config roots under a fresh temp directory; a refusal when an Eon
  supervisor of the same user is running; the help text names what it does not isolate (no PID
  or network namespace). Arguments pass to `cargo test` as on Linux.
- The Linux branch unchanged.

Out of scope: the tests' own `/proc` reads (`kz4p.5`), the flake's Darwin outputs (`kz4p.7`),
CI, Orbit's and Venus's tests.

## Acceptance

- `nix develop -c eon-test` on Linux behaves exactly as before (same tests, same isolation).
- `nix eval .#devShells.aarch64-darwin.default.drvPath` evaluates with the macOS branch in it.
- The script's macOS branch is shellcheck-clean and refuses clearly when a same-user supervisor
  runs or the toolchain is missing.
- Native pass/fail is the harness's job; this bead claims none.

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test` exits 0 on Linux.
- The `nix eval` above exits 0 on Linux.
- Codex review per AGENTS.md (Nix and script change).

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if honest macOS isolation needs a new tool (sandbox-exec profiles, a VM): ask Lucca.
- Stop if the Darwin dev shell from `kz4p.7` is not in place.

title: Add the Retina probe to the macOS harness
description:
## Why

The macOS preview's minimum bar includes Retina-scale rendering (`eon-igae.5`, `eon-igae.6`), and
no Mac run has ever observed it. The harness must record each display's backing scale and the
scale Venus actually uses, so a remote run claims Retina only when it really ran at scale 2, and
Yu's item 2 ("Retina: ... the tool records backing scale 2", `kz4p.11`) has a recorded value.
Split on 2026-10-27 from `eon-mac-launch-kz4p.9` (which keeps the GUI scenario) so each fits one
session and the one Venus change is reviewed on its own.

Lucca (2026-10-27, relayed by eon-overseer), on Retina: the harness records the display scale and
claims Retina only at scale 2 or more; no private-API virtual display; Yu's HiDPI monitor is the
proof: "7 ok, we can check with him" (comment on `kz4p.9`).

## Evidence

- The only native Venus run used one 1920x1080 scale-1 VNC display
  (`venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md:1053`), and Retina-scale redraw was never observed (`:1081-1082`).
- Venus reads `window.scale_factor()` (`venus/src/application.rs:849-854`, edge 01f5e3c) and
  logs no scale line today (check before adding one).

## Scope

In scope:
- A `retina` step of the harness tool (after `kz4p.9`'s scenario launch, or standalone): records
  each display's backing scale factor and available modes (`osascript -l JavaScript` with AppKit,
  `system_profiler SPDisplaysDataType -json`) into the evidence folder, and the scale Venus
  reports in its log; if a display offers a HiDPI mode, records it; switches modes only if that
  is possible without a new dependency. Reports "Retina proved remotely" only for scale >= 2 with
  a capture; otherwise `skipped: no HiDPI display`, which lands on Yu's list.
- One Venus `venus:` log line at window creation and on scale change naming the scale factor, if
  none exists (presentation diagnostics only; no behaviour change).

Out of scope: a CGVirtualDisplay or any private-API virtual display (rejected by Lucca), the
scenario steps (`kz4p.9`), Yu's guided mode (`kz4p.11`).

## Acceptance

- `retina --help` states what it records and when it claims Retina.
- The parse of the display report into scale and modes is a pure function with a test on Linux
  from a recorded `system_profiler` JSON sample.
- Venus logs its scale at window creation (seen in a Linux isolated run's log at scale 1).

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test -p <harness crate> -p yazelix-venus` exits 0; `cargo fmt --check` and
  `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings` for both crates.
- Codex review per AGENTS.md. Read `venus/AGENTS.md` before the Venus change.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop for Lucca if switching to a HiDPI mode needs a new tool (displayplacer, a CoreGraphics
  crate).
- Stop if the Venus change needs more than a diagnostic log line.
close_reason: Retina step landed in mac-proof's scenario (CoreGraphics display scale and modes, reversible HiDPI switch, passes only at Venus scale >= 2 with a capture) plus Venus's scale log line. Linux acceptance proved (tests, fmt, clippy on Linux and darwin, headless Sway live run logging scale 1); converge plus Codex clean. Mac observation belongs to kz4p.11 or the rented-Mac run (kz4p.12).

The overseer's 2026-10-28 scope update (mac.rs instead of osascript; mode switching through the pinned objc2-core-graphics allowed if reversible) governs.

Reference gate (consequential: dependency features and a temporary change to the Mac's display configuration).
- Behavior and owners: the harness tool (eon/tools/mac-proof) owns probing and recording display scale and modes, and the one temporary HiDPI mode switch; Venus owns its window's scale factor and only reports it (one `venus: window scale factor N` stderr line at window creation and on each scale change; no behaviour change). The scenario reads that line from scenario/eon.log, where the supervisor relays Venus's stderr.
- Dependency: no new crate. objc2-core-graphics =0.3.2 gains features CGError and CGDisplayConfiguration (CGGetActiveDisplayList, CGDisplayCopyAllDisplayModes, CGDisplayCopyDisplayMode, CGDisplayMode getters, CGBegin/Configure/CompleteDisplayConfiguration, CGDisplayIsMain/IsBuiltin); objc2-core-foundation =0.3.2 keeps its features (CFDictionary::from_slices, CFBoolean from CFNumber). macOS-only target dependencies, as kz4p.9 set them.
- References read: objc2-core-graphics 0.3.2 generated bindings (CGDirectDisplay.rs, CGDisplayConfiguration.rs: kCGDisplayShowDuplicateLowResolutionModes, CGConfigureOption::ForAppOnly) and objc2-core-foundation 0.3.2 (dictionary.rs, number.rs); winit 0.30.13 (Yazelix fork rev 7c209ec, the one Venus uses) src/platform_impl/macos/monitor.rs: Venus's scale_factor is NSScreen backingScaleFactor, and winit lists modes with null options, so it never sees HiDPI duplicates. Kept: a mode's backing scale is pixel width over point width, which is what backingScaleFactor reports for the display's current mode; HiDPI duplicates are listed only with kCGDisplayShowDuplicateLowResolutionModes. Rejected: NSScreen in the harness (needs the main-thread marker and gives no mode list); CGDisplaySetDisplayMode (session-wide, survives a crashed harness); displayplacer and CGVirtualDisplay (new tool / private API, rejected by Lucca).
- Decision: switch only the main display, only when it runs below scale 2 and offers a usable HiDPI mode, through a display configuration completed ForAppOnly, so macOS reverts it when the harness exits however it exits; the step also restores the original mode itself before it ends, pass or fail. title: Make Orbit's and Venus's tests compile and run on macOS
description:
## Why

eon-mac-launch-kz4p.1 (map at 66b32d5, open question 1 as amended) found that Orbit's and Venus's own test targets have no macOS owner. `cargo check --target aarch64-apple-darwin -p yazelix-orbit --all-targets` fails only in the real_pty test target: orbit/tests/real_pty/unreaped_stop.rs uses ptrace. eon-agent-background-work-yte0.1 adds another Linux-only site there: the `age()` helper in real_pty/program_status.rs uses CLOCK_BOOTTIME and /proc. The flake's package builds run these suites (`orbitPackage` tests `--lib --test real_pty` at flake.nix:276-282, and postInstall requires exactly one real_pty binary at :295-299; `venusPackage` runs Venus's tests at :361-364), so the Darwin `packages.default` cannot build until they compile and pass. The Nix checks `unreaped-stop` (nix/orbit-checks.nix:188) and `program-status` (:219) are Linux-only as written, and real_pty/detached_exit.rs:8 needs `lsof` on macOS while the checks supply only procps (:77).

## Decision

Lucca, 2026-10-27, to eon-overseer: "agree to all that". That answered question 1 with its recommendation: create this bead, blocking kz4p.7 and kz4p.8, and gate unreaped_stop (ptrace) to Linux. This narrows ORB-C14's macOS check set from "every real-PTY check" (orbit/docs/CONTRACTS.md:837-839) to every real-PTY check except the Linux-only ones. Record the exact ORB-C14 wording change on this bead and in orbit/CHANGELOG.md.

## Scope

In:
- Make Orbit's lib and real_pty targets, and Venus's tests, compile for aarch64-apple-darwin.
- Gate unreaped_stop.rs and the Linux-only parts of program_status.rs with `#[cfg(target_os = "linux")]`, or give them Darwin equivalents where cheap.
- Keep exactly one real_pty binary.
- Amend ORB-C14's macOS check-set sentence.

Out:
- Flake changes (kz4p.7, which wires `lsof` and the Darwin check policy).
- Venus fonts (sibling bead "Give Venus Eon's fonts on macOS").
- Native runs (kz4p.8).

## Acceptance

- `cargo check --locked --target aarch64-apple-darwin -p yazelix-orbit -p yazelix-venus --all-targets` passes on Linux.
- Linux behaviour unchanged: `nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-orbit -p yazelix-venus`, fmt and clippy -D warnings for both crates.
- Codex review per AGENTS.md.

## Portability disposition

Isolated Linux test mechanisms behind cfg gates.

Linux suites unchanged and passing. macOS runs are kz4p.8's.

title: Give Venus Eon's fonts on macOS
description:
## Why

eon-mac-launch-kz4p.1 (map at 66b32d5, open question 2) found that Eon gives Venus its fonts only through fontconfig, which Venus ignores on macOS.
- Venus builds its font database with cosmic-text `FontSystem::new()` (venus/src/render/fonts.rs:90).
- On macOS, fontdb 0.23 reads only the system font directories. It also scans /System/Library/AssetsV2 and /Network/Library/Fonts. FONTCONFIG_FILE is read only off macOS (fontdb-0.23.0/src/lib.rs:424-428, :461, :509).
- Eon supplies its fonts only as `venusFontsConf`, set as FONTCONFIG_FILE (flake.nix:329-345, :370, :987). That file writes `<dir prefix="relative">` on purpose.
- The default fallbacks "Symbols Nerd Font Mono" and "Accelerando Terminal" (eon/crates/eon/src/product.rs:41-44) are always passed as `--font-fallback` (runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/supervisor.rs:424-426).
- `FontSetup::resolve` errors when a family is unavailable (fonts.rs:104-111).

So on a stock Mac the default configuration most likely cannot open a window. That is inferred from code, not run. VEN-C16's record (venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md:1063-1066) already shows six Venus library tests failing on stock macOS without those fonts.

## Decision

Lucca, 2026-10-27, to eon-overseer: "agree to all that". That answered question 2 with its recommendation: create this bead, blocking kz4p.7, kz4p.8 and kz4p.9.

## Shape (decide under the reference gate)

Venus loads Eon's packaged font directories explicitly on macOS. Two candidate mechanisms:
- a font-directory startup input that Runtime passes from launch inputs Eon already owns (recommended starting point: it keeps Venus parsing no configuration);
- Venus reading the same fonts.conf's `<dir>` entries, including the relative prefix.

kz4p.7 wires the Darwin font package. A new Runtime-to-Venus startup input is an interface change, so record the reference gate on this bead before code. Stop for Lucca if it changes VEN-C16's text.

## Acceptance

- With the default configuration and Eon's fonts but no system copies, `FontSetup::resolve` succeeds for a macOS-shaped font environment.
- A Venus unit or integration check that runs on Linux exercises the explicit-directory path.
- Linux behaviour unchanged: `nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-venus -p eon-runtime`, fmt and clippy.
- Codex review per AGENTS.md.
- Native proof comes in kz4p.8 and kz4p.9.

## Portability disposition

Isolated Darwin font loading behind Venus's platform code.
close_reason: Venus loads EON_VENUS_FONT_DIRS before resolving fonts; Linux unchanged; Darwin wiring in kz4p.7, native proof in kz4p.8/9

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
## Approval (relayed)

Relayed by eon-overseer (coordinator), 2026-10-27. Lucca, 2026-10-27, to eon-overseer: "do these two too, then ... i want to move closer to the 'yu testing' gate". It names this bead (Venus fonts on macOS) for implementation now. Contract text already adopted on this bead or its parent stands.

## Reference gate

**Behavior.** On macOS, Venus resolves the default fallbacks ("Symbols Nerd Font Mono", "Accelerando Terminal") and DejaVu from Eon's packaged font directories, not from system copies. Linux is unchanged. Owners: Eon's Nix composition chooses the font set, which is today's `venusFontsConf` list (flake.nix:328-343). Venus's package wrapper delivers it, as it already sets `FONTCONFIG_FILE` (flake.nix:345). Venus's `FontSetup` owns loading it into the font database.

**Evidence read.**
- fontdb 0.23.0 `Database::load_system_fonts` (src/lib.rs:400-475). On macOS it scans only /Library/Fonts, /System/Library/Fonts, AssetsV2, /Network/Library/Fonts and ~/Library/Fonts. It reads `FONTCONFIG_FILE` only on non-macOS unix (:461, :509). `fontconfig-parser` is a dependency only for that cfg (Cargo.toml:80), so the macOS build does not compile it. `Database::load_fonts_dir` is public and recursive.
- cosmic-text 0.19.0 `FontSystem` (src/font/system.rs:191-299). `new()` loads system fonts and sets the generic families. The constructor computes the monospace ID lists once, so faces added later through `db_mut()` are missing from them. `into_locale_and_db` plus `new_with_locale_and_db` rebuilds the font system with those lists computed.
- Venus: `FontSetup::new`/`resolve` (venus/src/render/fonts.rs:89-111), the single app caller `create_window` (venus/src/application.rs:832), existing env inputs `EON_VENUS_PRESENTATION_CONTROL` (main.rs:16) and `EON_NEW_WINDOW_EXECUTABLE` (application.rs:768); VEN-C16 text (venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md:1018-1090), VEN-C19 fallback decision (venus/docs/CRATES.md:122-141).
- Runtime: `venus_command` (runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/supervisor.rs:388-460) and `Inputs` (runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/cli.rs:42-52). Eon launches the wrapped `${venusPackage}/bin/yazelix-venus` (flake.nix:631, :764), so the Venus wrapper's environment reaches every Eon-launched Venus.
- Comparable implementation: WezTerm `e2a98e1b8af156988ad0ac778658ac27b60a55fb`, `wezterm-font/src/db.rs:36-60` (`font_dirs`). It walks the listed directories on every platform and adds them beside system fonts. Kept: extra directories are additive and platform-neutral. Rejected: making it user configuration. Here it is a packaging input, not a value a person sees.

**Adopted.** Venus reads `EON_VENUS_FONT_DIRS`, an OS path list (`std::env::split_paths`, colon-separated). It loads each directory into the platform font database before resolving typography. Empty entries are skipped. A relative or missing directory fails startup with a bounded "font directory is unavailable" error before the window opens. When the variable is unset, Venus follows today's path exactly. The Darwin Venus wrapper (kz4p.7) sets it from the same list as `venusFontsConf`. Linux sets nothing, so Linux behavior and derivations do not change.

**Rejected.**
1. Runtime passes `--font-dir` (the bead's suggested starting point). That needs a new Eon launch input, a new field in Runtime's public `Inputs`, Eon product code and a supervisor.rs change, which collides with kz4p.4. Runtime would become a second carrier of a font set the Venus package already owns. Standalone `yazelix-venus` and Venus's own test environment would still lack the fonts.
2. Venus reads `FONTCONFIG_FILE`'s `<dir>` entries on macOS. Doing it properly means adding `fontconfig-parser` to the macOS build, a new dependency that fontdb deliberately leaves out there. A hand-rolled `<dir>`/`prefix="relative"` reader would reinterpret fontconfig's format partially.
3. A `--font-dir` flag added by the wrapper (`--add-flags`). It works, but it is a second argv surface for a packaging input, and it is prepended to every invocation. The env var follows the existing `FONTCONFIG_FILE` channel.

**Contracts.** No contract text changes: VEN-C16's Result already confines variation to native host mechanics, and VEN-C19's typography is unchanged. No new dependency. Interface: one new Venus environment input, documented in the code. Its producer is the Darwin wrapper (kz4p.7).

**Portability disposition.** `neutral`: the mechanism is platform-neutral and runs on Linux in tests. Only the Darwin package sets the variable. This replaces the bead's "isolated Darwin font loading", because no cfg-gated code is needed.

**Check.** A Venus unit test on Linux builds a "macOS-shaped" font system. Its platform fonts are DejaVu only, with no Eon fallback families. Default Eon fallbacks fail to resolve without the directory list and resolve with it. A missing directory is rejected. Linux: `nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-venus`, fmt, clippy (host and `--target aarch64-apple-darwin`).

**Handoff.** kz4p.7: set `EON_VENUS_FONT_DIRS` on the Darwin Venus wrapper from the font package list used for `venusFontsConf`. Rejected option 1's test advantage does not apply to this design either. Venus's library tests build font systems directly (`FontSystem::new()`), so the variable does not reach them. kz4p.8's harness still has to make the fixture fonts visible to those six tests, as `eon-z4n6` did by installing them for the user.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Correction to the reference-gate comment. Rejected option 1 says that with a Runtime-passed flag "Venus's own test environment would still lack the fonts". That is true, but it is equally true of the adopted design. Venus's library tests build font systems directly, so neither mechanism reaches them; the Handoff paragraph says so. Option 1 is rejected only for its extra Eon/Runtime plumbing, its second carrier of the font set, and its supervisor.rs collision.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
## Proof

The revision is the commit that carries this comment. The checks ran on its code tree. That tree is 5e2fd658e6088d19f338c3fbf99960c4a421fb17, which differs from the commit only by this record. Platform: x86_64 Linux, `nix develop` shell from that tree, Cargo `-j 4`.
- `nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-venus`: pass. Lib 153 passed, 2 ignored, including `render::fonts::tests::packaged_font_directories_supply_fallbacks_missing_from_platform_fonts`. main.rs 65 passed, 4 ignored; canonical_scene 21 passed.
- `cargo fmt --check -p yazelix-venus`: pass.
- `cargo clippy --locked -p yazelix-venus --all-targets -- -D warnings`: pass, on host. Also `--target aarch64-apple-darwin`, with rustup stable outside nix: pass. Cross `cargo check` for the same target: pass.
- The checks left the tree unchanged, verified by write-tree before and after.
- The new test models stock macOS: platform fonts DejaVu only. Default Eon fallbacks fail without the directory list and resolve with it. Missing and relative entries are rejected.
- Not proved: native macOS behavior and the Darwin wrapper that sets `EON_VENUS_FONT_DIRS`. Those belong to kz4p.7 (wiring), kz4p.8 and kz4p.9 (native runs). Linux sets nothing, so Linux behavior is unchanged.

Text note: the gate comment quotes the startup error's earlier wording. The shipped message is "font directory is relative or unavailable: <path>".

## Ledger

Converge plus Codex took 2 Claude rounds and 2 Codex passes.
- Round 1:
  - Codex: clean, 1 nit (document the variable beside its consumer), applied.
  - Claude: 2 findings.
    - The recorded tree predated a bead comment; re-recorded.
    - The gate overstated that DejaVu becomes macOS's primary face; corrected, and question 1 opened (non-blocking).
  - Claude nits: 2 applied, 2 declined with reasons.
- Round 2, Claude: nothing blocking.
- Narrow Codex re-check of 7036c37..5e2fd65: nothing blocking.

Open: question 1 (macOS default face) for Lucca, relayed to eon-overseer. It does not block this bead.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
## Review round 1 and a corrected gate claim

**Correction.** The gate's Behavior line says macOS resolves "DejaVu from Eon's packaged font directories, not from system copies". That overstates the change. What holds is narrower:
- The default fallbacks, "Symbols Nerd Font Mono" and "Accelerando Terminal", resolve from the packaged directories. That is the bead's acceptance.
- The primary terminal face, with Eon's default `font-family` unset, is chosen as today. `resolve` shapes a space through `Family::Monospace`. cosmic-text 0.19.0 does not have its default "Noto Sans Mono", so it falls back to the monospaced face that ranks first, and IDs (load order) break ties (fallback/mod.rs:177-182, 378-421).
- The packaged directories load after the system fonts. On stock macOS the primary is therefore most likely a system monospace face (Menlo, SF Mono, Courier and similar), not DejaVu Sans Mono. The UI sans-serif face is picked the same way.

This is inferred from source and not run on a Mac. VEN-C19's typography contract is unchanged; only which face macOS's platform default yields is in question.

## Question for Lucca

1. Which default terminal face should Eon use on macOS when `font-family` is unset?
   - (a) The platform's own monospace face, as the code now does.
   - (b) DejaVu Sans Mono, matching Linux.

   **Recommendation: (a) for now**, and kz4p.9's GUI scenario records which face it gets.
   - Mac users expect their native monospace face.
   - (b) would rest either on fontdb load order, which is a fragile tie-break inside cosmic-text, or on a macOS-specific product default in Eon's configuration.
   - If you pick (b), the cleaner route is an explicit product default family on macOS in `eon` (product.rs), a small follow-up bead, not load-order tricks in Venus.

   This does not block this bead's acceptance.

## Round-1 ledger (in progress)

- **Codex:** clean. Nit: document the variable's name and path-list rules beside the consumer. Applied as code comments.
- **Fresh Claude reviewer.** Checks green: `eon-test -p yazelix-venus` gave 153 passed, 2 ignored in the lib; 65/4, 21 and 0 in the other binaries. fmt passed; clippy `-D warnings` passed on host and on aarch64-apple-darwin. Findings:
  - B1: the recorded tree predated a bead comment. Re-recorded.
  - B2: the claim corrected above.
  - Nits applied: the error for a relative entry now reads "font directory is relative or unavailable"; the env read site is commented.
  - Nit declined: making `with_directories` `pub(crate)`. Its caller is the `yazelix-venus` binary crate, which uses the library's public API.
  - Nit declined: testing the env read in application.rs. It would need process-env mutation in tests, and kz4p.9's native run exercises it.
  - Nit noted for kz4p.7: the variable takes absolute paths, so a future relocatable launcher must compute them at launch.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Configuration boundary: `EON_VENUS_FONT_DIRS` is a packaging input that the Darwin Venus wrapper sets. It is not user configuration, so Venus still parses no configuration (AGENTS.md "Configurability": "Eon Runtime parses configuration and sends resolved values; Venus parses none"). It also needs no `docs/CONFIGURATION.md` entry, because no value a person sees or feels changes. eon-overseer agreed on 2026-10-27: "it's a packaging input set by the wrapper, not user configuration, so Venus still parses no configuration."

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Answer to Question 1 (default macOS terminal face when font-family is unset), Lucca 2026-10-27 to eon-overseer, his words: "ok to all". It accepted the recommendation, option (a): the platform's own monospace face (Menlo, SF Mono and similar), as the landed change already behaves. No follow-up bead. Relayed by eon-overseer.

title: Port Eon Runtime's terminal peer and liveness checks to macOS
description:
## Why

Eon Runtime validates each Orbit run's management peer and process identity with Linux-only
calls. On macOS it does not compile, and the liveness check would read a missing `/proc` as "the
run is dead" and retire every live terminal. This is the one Runtime change full Eon needs on
macOS before anything launches.

Lucca (2026-10-27, relayed by eon-overseer): "i'd rather test everything possible and fix myself,
letting to Yu only final testing and final fixes that i missed ... so the more automated, the
better."

## Evidence

- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/sessions.rs:424-458` `validate_management_peer`: `SO_PEERCRED`
  pid/uid, then `/proc/<pid>/stat` field 22 compared with the Ready `process_start`.
- `sessions.rs:572-593` `recorded_process_is_dead`: NotFound means dead; state `Z`/`X` means dead;
  start mismatch is an error. Callers `:767` (adoption) and `:1386` (owner loss).
- Orbit already publishes the macOS identity: `orbit/src/platform.rs:333-341` `getpeereid`,
  `:353-376` `process_start_identity` = `pbi_start_tvsec * 1_000_000 + pbi_start_tvusec` from
  `proc_pidinfo(PROC_PIDTBSDINFO)`. `orbit/tests/lifecycle.rs:658-678` reads it independently.
- `orbit/crates/protocol/src/management.rs:48,433` carries `process_start` as an opaque nonzero
  `u64`; its unit is the platform's.
- Contract: EON-C15 (`docs/CONTRACTS.md:1436`): "stale or mismatched process identity ... fails
  closed without PID/process-name fallback". ORB-C13/ORB-C14 own Orbit's side.

## Scope

In scope: a narrow Runtime-local platform seam (one module, Linux and macOS functions) for: peer
pid and uid of a Unix stream (macOS: `getsockopt(SOL_LOCAL, LOCAL_PEERPID)` plus `getpeereid`),
process start identity of a pid in Orbit's unit (macOS: `proc_pidinfo` as Orbit does), and
process state (macOS: `ESRCH` from `proc_pidinfo` is dead, `pbi_status == SZOMB` is dead).
`validate_management_peer` and `recorded_process_is_dead` call it; Linux behavior unchanged.

Out of scope: Orbit, `orbit-protocol`, EONW, Venus; the Runtime test files' own `/proc` reads
(tests bead); runtime directory and notification (remaining-assumptions bead).

## Acceptance

- `cargo check --target aarch64-apple-darwin -p eon-runtime` (gate command from the mapping bead)
  passes this item: no `ucred`/`SO_PEERCRED`/`/proc` on the macOS path.
- On Linux, existing Runtime identity tests pass unchanged through `nix develop -c eon-test -p
  eon-runtime`; one focused test covers the seam's "missing process is dead, mismatched start is
  an error" rule if no existing test does (name the failure it catches).
- Native macOS proof is deferred to the harness (Runtime suite plus full-Eon launch, where an
  identity mismatch fails closed and is visible).
- Portability disposition recorded: isolated Linux and Darwin mechanisms behind one seam.

## Implementation Notes

1. Read EON-C15, ORB-C13/C14, `orbit/src/platform.rs` seam and the mapping bead's list.
2. Add the seam; keep Linux code byte-for-byte equivalent in behavior.
3. Run the gate check, `cargo fmt --check`, clippy, `eon-test -p eon-runtime`; Codex per AGENTS.md.

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime` exits 0.
- `cargo check --locked --target aarch64-apple-darwin -p eon-runtime` (outside the dev shell as
  the mapping bead records) shows no error from `sessions.rs`.

## Stop Conditions

Reference gate (consequential: it ports the management-peer trust check and the liveness rule that decides whether a terminal's run is retired). Recorded at 2e7f6e6 before code.

title: Make Eon's terminfo readable by macOS system ncurses
description:
## Why

eon-mac-launch-kz4p.1 (map at 66b32d5, open question 3) found that macOS's system ncurses most likely cannot read `TERM=eon`.
- Orbit sets TERM=eon (orbit/src/pty.rs:750; ORB-C10).
- orbit/terminfo/eon.terminfo is `use=xterm-256color`, compiled with nixpkgs ncurses `tic -x` (flake.nix:301). xterm-256color's pairs#0x10000 makes tic write the 32-bit extended format: the built entry starts with bytes 1e 02, magic 01036.
- macOS's system ncurses (5.7) reads only the legacy 0432 format, and its terminfo tree uses hex directory names (65/, not e/).
- Terminals get TERMINFO_DIRS pointing at Orbit's tree (flake.nix:646, :766). System-ncurses programs (/bin/zsh, less, vim, top, man) would therefore most likely report an unknown terminal inside Eon. That is inferred, not run.
- The `orbit-terminfo` check (nix/orbit-checks.nix:244-255) uses Nix ncurses and would not catch it.

## Decision

Lucca, 2026-10-27, to eon-overseer: "agree to all that". That answered question 3 with its recommendation: create this bead, blocking kz4p.9 and kz4p.11. Show the exact ORB-C10 text change to Lucca before landing.

## Shape

Compile a legacy-format entry for Darwin and install it under both the e/ and 65/ directory names. Example: cap pairs at 0x7fff, as kitty's entry does. Add a check that runs /usr/bin/infocmp eon on the Mac in kz4p.8's harness.

## Acceptance

- The Darwin terminfo output, inspected from Linux, starts with legacy magic 0432 and exists under both directory names.
- Linux's entry is unchanged, or any change is justified on the bead.
- The native /usr/bin/infocmp check is added to kz4p.8's harness list.
- Codex review per AGENTS.md (Nix change).

## Portability disposition

Isolated Darwin packaging of the terminfo entry.
close_reason: macOS Orbit installs a legacy-format eon terminfo entry (pairs#0x7fff, e/ and 65/) checked from Linux by orbit-terminfo-darwin; Linux entry unchanged; ORB-C10 Partially proved with the approved macOS clause; native run is ORB-C10's open proof (kz4p.8/.12).

Reference gate (consequential, because it changes the ORB-C10 contract):
- Behavior: Programs that link the system ncurses on macOS (/usr/bin/infocmp, /bin/zsh, less) resolve TERM=eon from the package's share/terminfo on TERMINFO_DIRS. Linux behavior is unchanged.
- Owners: orbit/terminfo/eon.terminfo stays the one source (name, description, use=xterm-256color). The flake's Orbit package owns the compiled tree, and on Darwin installs the entry built by the new `darwinTerminfo` derivation. ORB-C10 owns the contract.
- Evidence (Linux, nixpkgs ncurses 6.6 at the flake pin):
  - `tic -x` on today's source writes magic 1e 02 (01036, extended numbers), 4054 bytes, because xterm-256color has pairs#0x10000.
  - Adding `pairs#0x7fff,` before `use=` writes 1a 01 (0432, legacy), 4024 bytes. `infocmp -x` differs only in pairs. pairs is the only number above 0x7fff (colors#0x100, cols#80, it#8, lines#24).
- Comparable implementations:
  - kitty b2cb871 (~/pjs/refs/kitty): terminfo/kitty.terminfo has pairs#32767. The compiled x/xterm-kitty is legacy (1a 01, 3721 bytes), with a `78 -> x` symlink for hex-directory readers.
  - Ghostty at the flake's pinned input (src/terminfo/ghostty.zig:99): pairs 32767 on every platform.
  - WezTerm e2a98e1 (termwiz/data/wezterm.terminfo:37): pairs#0x7fff.
- Constraints kept: one source file. Linux's compiled entry and the Linux orbit derivation stay unchanged. No new dependency.
- Rejected:
  - (a) Capping pairs in eon.terminfo for all platforms. This is simpler and matches kitty and Ghostty, but it changes Linux's entry, and the bead says to keep Linux unchanged without a reason to change it.
  - (b) A second checked-in Darwin source, which would put the name in two owners.
  - (c) Rewriting `infocmp` output with sed after compiling.
  - (d) Copying the file into 65/ instead of symlinking. Kitty's symlink keeps one file.
- Inference, not run: macOS ncurses 5.7 reads only the legacy format, looks up hex directory names, and reads at most 4096 bytes per entry (MAX_ENTRY_SIZE in 5.x). These come from kz4p.1's map and ncurses history. The native /usr/bin/infocmp check in kz4p.8's harness is the proof.
- Decision check:
  - New Linux flake check `orbit-terminfo-darwin`: the Darwin tree's entry starts with 0432, is at most 4096 bytes, is reachable as e/eon and 65/eon, and differs from a fresh Linux compile only in pairs.
  - `nix eval` of the Linux orbit drvPath must be unchanged.

Portability disposition: isolated Darwin packaging of the terminfo entry. The Darwin branch in orbitPackage is evaluated only once kz4p.7 adds aarch64-darwin outputs. Until then, the Linux check builds `darwinTerminfo` itself.

title: Check on macOS that a zombie grandchild neither counts nor hides a live sibling
description:
## Why

On macOS, `proc_pidinfo(PROC_PIDTBSDINFO)` with arg 0 cannot see zombies. Orbit's macOS `bsd_info` (orbit/src/platform.rs:374-379) passes arg 0, so the background-process walk's `process()` returns None for a zombie (found in XNU source, xnu-12377.1.9, by kz4p.2 on 2026-10-27; note on kz4p.8; not observed natively). Likely harmless: the walk counts zombies as not running, and a zombie keeps no children. But no Darwin check exercises it. program_status.rs has no zombie case, and unreaped_stop.rs is Linux-only (eon-32, kz4p.8 question 1, 2026-10-28).

## Goal

A real-PTY check, run natively on macOS by the harness, shows that a zombie grandchild neither counts as background work nor hides a live sibling from the count.

## Shape

- Add a case to orbit/tests/real_pty/program_status.rs on both Linux and macOS. A foreground child forks two grandchildren into their own process group: one exits and stays unreaped (a zombie), the other sleeps. The count is exactly 1 while the sleeper lives, and 0 after it exits.
- Add the check entry in nix/orbit-checks.nix if program_status needs one. The harness (kz4p.8) builds every Darwin check the flake lists, so it needs no change.
- If the native run shows the zombie hides its sibling, fix it at Orbit's platform seam, the way kz4p.2 fixed Runtime.

## Acceptance

- Green on Linux through the orbit-program-status Nix check.
- Compile- and clippy-clean for aarch64-apple-darwin.
- Native result: recorded by kz4p.12, which this bead blocks, from its native run of orbit-program-status; it is not a condition for closing this bead (eon-overseer, 2026-10-28: "The native run belongs to kz4p.12").
- Codex review per AGENTS.md.

## Scope boundary

Orbit tests and, only if the native run demands it, orbit/src/platform.rs. No contract change.

- New case `zombies_neither_count_nor_hide` in orbit/tests/real_pty/program_status.rs. A job-control foreground job starts two grandchildren in their own groups, reports `done`, then runs `exec cat "$GATE" "$GATE" > "$EXIT"`. `cat` opens the gate only after the exec, so when the check's gate write returns, the zombie's parent is a process that never waits. The line `cat` relays ends the first grandchild, which stays a zombie. The second `"$GATE"` operand keeps `cat` blocked. The check waits until the first is a zombie and the second is 1.1 s old, asserts background == 1 and that the zombie is still unreaped, then releases the second and waits for 0.

comments.text:
Review round 1 on candidate tree d890c2122bdea475b90f05017890e6727a7e7e64 (base 1d731f5). Codex (gpt-6.1-sol, xhigh, read-only) and a fresh Claude reviewer ran in parallel on one review-only brief. Both reported the same two blocking findings:

1. The "hides a live sibling" half could not fail on macOS. In XNU (xnu-12377.1.9, bsd/kern/proc_info.c `proc_listpids`, which `proc_listchildpids` wraps), live processes are walked on `allproc` before zombies on `zombproc`. The Linux run cannot catch it either, because a Linux zombie's record is readable. Fixed: the sibling now has a child in its own group, so the walk meets the zombie while that child is still pending. The count is 2 while both live. (Ending only the loop over a parent's children at a zombie, `break`, is harmless on macOS, since zombies come last.)
2. BEHAVIOR.md said kz4p.2 observed the arg-0 zombie behavior natively. kz4p.2 confirmed it against XNU source (xnu-12377.1.9); nothing ran natively. Fixed: the bullet cites the source. The same wording in this bead's Why and in my start comment is corrected here: it is source evidence, not a native observation.

Both reviewers found the zombie deterministic on both platforms: bash is gone before the line that ends the first grandchild exists, and the second gate open keeps `cat` alive. Both found the test's `bsd_info` argument change (0 to 1) leaves live-process reads unchanged, because XNU tries `proc_find` first. Claude nit, not taken: the message on `assert!(is_zombie(zombie), ...)` is effectively unreachable, since a reaped pid panics in `stat_fields`/`bsd_info` first; the check still fails.

Process slip: I edited the tree before the Claude report was in, against AGENTS.md's "nothing edits the tree until both reports are in". The reviewer reran fmt, Linux clippy and Darwin clippy on a `git archive` export of d890c21 (all exit 0), plus orbit-program-status on that candidate (once, then three `--rebuild`s, all ok). Its checks left no drift.

Sensitivity on the fixed case, x86_64 Linux. Each variant mutates orbit/src/platform.rs in a scratch copy (/home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/zombie-work/sens, its own git repo). It runs `nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-orbit --test real_pty -- --ignored --exact program_status` against a release Orbit (`ORBIT_BIN`), because the debug Orbit is too slow for the existing flood case `detached_turns_end_at_a_return`:
- A: Linux counts state `Z` as running. FAIL, background 3 (expected 2).
- B: Linux `process()` returns None for `Z`, as the macOS walk's arg-0 read does. PASS.
- C: B, plus `break` instead of `continue` at the unreadable entry. FAIL, 0 (Linux lists the zombie first).
- D: B, plus each Linux children list reversed so the zombie comes last as on macOS, plus `return count` at the unreadable entry. FAIL, 1.
(The first shape, before the fix, failed A with 2, passed B and failed C with 0.)

title: List detached Eon processes in mac-proof's leftovers check
description:
## Why

The harness's leftovers step (kz4p.8) checks that no Eon process survives the run. On macOS it
lists processes with `ps -U <uid> -o pid=,comm=` in `eon_processes`
(eon/tools/mac-proof/src/run.rs:528). BSD `ps` without `-x` leaves out processes that have no
controlling terminal, which is exactly what a detached Eon supervisor, Orbit host or Venus launched
from the GUI is. So a leaked background Eon process passes the leftovers check unseen. Reported by
the kz4p.9 agent; kz4p.9's scenario already lists with `ps -A -ww` filtered by uid.

## Contract

kz4p.8's acceptance: the harness reports Eon processes left after the run. No product contract
changes.

## Change

List every process of the user, with or without a terminal (`-x`, or the scenario's `-A` plus a
uid filter; prefer one shared helper if kz4p.9 has landed one).

## Acceptance

- On Linux: `nix develop -c eon-test -p mac-proof` passes, plus fmt and clippy for mac-proof on the
  host and `--target aarch64-apple-darwin`.
- The first native run (kz4p.12 or the macOS CI workflow) would show a detached Eon process in the
  leftovers; claim it only once a Mac run has exercised it.

## Scope

mac-proof's process listing only. Prerequisite: kz4p.9 lands first (both edit run.rs and the
scenario's listing). Converge plus Codex review as for any code change.
close_reason: Leftovers listing shares scenario.rs's ps -A -ww uid-filtered helper; Linux checks pass; the native detached-process claim waits on the first Mac run (kz4p.12)

title: Give Orbit's Nix build Apple libtool on macOS
description:
## Why

macOS CI run 40721211773 attempt 2 (macos-15, e04553c; evidence in
/home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-overseer/ci-40721211773-a2/) failed about 50 Nix checks, plus
`check:eonbase-closure` and `check:managed-command-path`, in the same place: building
`libghostty-vt-sys` inside `yazelix-orbit`. `steps/10-check-orbit-clipboard.log:81-83,108-109`:
`libtool ghostty-vt (libghostty-vt-fat.a) failure` / `failed to spawn and capture stdio from
libtool: FileNotFound` / `build.rs:473:5: zig build failed`. Ghostty's Zig build calls Apple's
`libtool -static` by bare name, and `orbitPackage` (flake.nix:300-335) gives the builder only bun,
ncurses and zig.hook. Cargo's `test:yazelix-orbit` passed on the same Mac because the dev shell
keeps /usr/bin on PATH (inference).

## Contract

ORB-C14 / EON-C7 need the Nix-built Orbit on aarch64-darwin. No contract text changes.

## Change

Add Apple's libtool to Orbit's darwin build: `lib.optionals stdenv.isDarwin [ pkgs.cctools ]` (or
the cctools output that carries `libtool`) in `orbitPackage.nativeBuildInputs`. GNU `pkgs.libtool`
is the wrong tool. The next step in the chain (linking with Apple ld) may surface another missing
host tool; fix it in the same slice if it is the same kind of gap.

## Acceptance

- Linux: `nix build .#default --no-link` and the Orbit Nix checks are unchanged (the edit is
  darwin-only; show the Linux derivation is identical or rebuilt green).
- `nix eval` of the darwin orbitPackage shows cctools in its inputs.
- The next macOS CI run gets past libghostty-vt-sys (the native claim waits for that run).

## Scope

flake.nix / nix only. Orbit's AGENTS.md applies (Orbit owns the pinned build inputs). Codex
review per AGENTS.md.

Plan (Opus planner, 2026-10-28)

Approval, relayed by eon-overseer: Lucca, 2026-10-27: "do these two too, then ... i want to move closer to the 'yu testing' gate", standing for the macOS launch path; and 2026-10-28: "lets get to working", on the plan to fix the macOS CI failures (kz4p.23-.28) with Opus planning and gating and Codex implementing. It does not cover push, promotion, workflow dispatch, GitHub or site posts.

Evidence (read at a409e4a):
- Ghostty 521cf2c `src/build/LibtoolStep.zig:34` runs bare `libtool -static -o`; the same build runs `/usr/bin/ranlib` (`LibtoolStep.zig:66-74`) and `/usr/bin/xcrun --sdk macosx clang -fuse-ld=ld` (`pkg/apple-sdk/native_link.zig:33-41`) by absolute path. The CI runner has `sandbox = false` (steps/01-host.log:39-40), so the ranlib steps passed and only `libtool` (not on the builder's PATH) failed.
- nixpkgs (flake input) splits Apple's libtool into `cctools.libtool` (`pkgs/by-name/cc/cctools/package.nix:34-39,148-150`, cctools 1010.6) so packages can add it alone. Its aarch64-darwin output `/nix/store/albld8nis2gsip1yf4girprwssc3r7aj-cctools-1010.6-libtool` is on cache.nixos.org with `bin/libtool`.
- The next step, `/usr/bin/xcrun ... clang`, runs with nixpkgs' apple-sdk `DEVELOPER_DIR` (`apple-sdk/setup-hooks/sdk-hook.sh`). The dev shell sets the same DEVELOPER_DIR and its `eon-test -p yazelix-orbit` compiled libghostty-vt-sys and passed on the same Mac (steps/63-test-yazelix-orbit.log:361,431), so I expect the link step to work in the builder too (inference; the next macOS CI run decides).

title: Check Venus's stalled-link reaping without /bin/ps on macOS
description:
## Why

macOS CI run 40721211773 attempt 2 (e04553c; evidence in
/home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-overseer/ci-40721211773-a2/) failed `package` because the Venus
test `application::tests::stalled_link_dispatcher_is_bounded_and_reaped` panicked inside the Nix
build: `steps/03-package.log:8714-8715`, `venus/src/application.rs:7301:14 ... Os { code: 1,
kind: PermissionDenied, message: "Operation not permitted" }`. That line (at e04553c) unwraps
`Command::new("/bin/ps").args(["-p", pid]).status()` in the `#[cfg(not(target_os = "linux"))]`
branch (7297-7302). The same test passed under cargo (`66-test-yazelix-venus.log:342`), so the
Nix build user cannot exec macOS's setuid `/bin/ps` (inference). Not timing and not a product bug.
A failed `package` also skips the GUI scenario and the Retina step.

## Change

Venus test only: drop `ps`. After `drop(opener)`, tell a reaped child from a live or zombie one
with `waitpid(pid, WNOHANG)` (ECHILD once reaped) or `kill(pid, 0)` (ESRCH once reaped; a zombie
still answers), whichever matches what the test proves. Also drop the workflow's and harness's
comments that say sandbox=false exists for this ps call if nothing else needs it, or leave them
and say why.

## Acceptance

- `nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-venus` passes on Linux; fmt and clippy for Venus on Linux
  and `--target aarch64-apple-darwin`.
- The test still fails if the dispatcher leaves the child unreaped (state the red check).
- The next macOS CI run's `package` step gets past this test.

## Scope

venus/src/application.rs tests only. Read venus/AGENTS.md. Codex review per AGENTS.md.

The GUI scenario failure there is kz4p.34 (Venus Metal alpha mode), unrelated to this bead.

comments.text:
Plan (Opus planner, 2026-10-28)

Approval, as relayed by eon-overseer: Lucca, 2026-10-27: "do these two too, then ... i want to move closer to the 'yu testing' gate", standing for the macOS launch path; Lucca, 2026-10-28: "lets get to working", on the plan to fix the macOS CI failures (kz4p.23-.28) with Opus planning and gating and Codex implementing. Does not cover push, promotion, GitHub posts, workflow dispatch or a rented Mac.

Evidence: CI host step ran with `nix config show sandbox` = false (steps/01-host.log:39-40), and the build still got EPERM from exec of /bin/ps (03-package.log:8714-8715). So sandbox=false never made /bin/ps usable for the build user; the test, not the sandbox, is the cause.

Approach: in `application::tests::stalled_link_dispatcher_is_bounded_and_reaped` (venus/src/application.rs:7278), replace the `#[cfg(not(target_os = "linux"))]` /bin/ps branch with a `#[cfg(target_os = "macos")]` branch that asks `libc::waitpid(pid, &mut status, WNOHANG)`: reaped iff it returns -1 with ECHILD. A live child returns 0 and an unreaped zombie returns the pid (and gets reaped by the check), so both fail the assert. libc is already a macOS dependency of Venus (venus/Cargo.toml:27): no new dependency, no manifest change. Linux keeps its /proc branch (libc is not a Linux dependency of Venus; adding one is out of scope). Update the test's comment to match.

Comments: the workflow (.github/workflows/mac-proof.yml:32), the harness (eon/tools/mac-proof/src/run.rs:273-274) and docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:60-61 justify sandbox=false by this ps call. Keep sandbox=false (Nix's macOS default and the only setting the Darwin build has run under; whether a sandboxed Darwin build passes is eon-zuou's, which needs a Mac) and reword those three to stop citing /bin/ps and point at eon-zuou. No behavior change.

Red check: with `let _ = self.child.wait();` removed from `impl Drop for LinkOpener` (application.rs:387), the Linux test fails (zombie keeps /proc/<pid>). The macOS branch's red check is the same edit on a Mac; Linux proves only that the darwin branch compiles (clippy --target aarch64-apple-darwin).

Checks: `nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-venus`; `cargo fmt --check` for Venus; `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -p yazelix-venus -- -D warnings` on Linux and with `--target aarch64-apple-darwin` (Darwin clippy recipe on kz4p.1); `cargo check -p mac-proof` (or its clippy) for the comment edit. Native proof: the next macOS CI run's `package` step gets past this test.

comments.text:
Plan amendment (Opus, 2026-10-28), after Codex's first round stopped without edits: venus/src/main.rs:1 forbids unsafe code, and the binary includes `mod application`; docs/CRATES.md ("macOS CPU and memory readings") keeps the binary root forbidding unsafe, and system.rs's host module is "the only unsafe code in Venus" (eon-b4vh tracks removing it). So `libc::waitpid` is rejected: it would need a policy change.

Adopted: the test runs `kill -0 <pid>` (PATH lookup, like its `sleep`) and treats a non-zero exit as reaped, on both Linux and macOS, dropping the cfg split and the /proc branch. kill(2) with signal 0 succeeds for a live process and for an unreaped zombie and fails with ESRCH once it is reaped: on Linux observed here (coreutils 9.11 kill: zombie 0, reaped 1); on macOS XNU's kill() returns success for a zombie found by pzfind, per POSIX's rationale (inference from the XNU source as remembered, not run on a Mac). kill is not setuid: coreutils in the Nix build's stdenv, /bin/kill under cargo. One mechanism means the Linux red check exercises the same code macOS runs. Rejected: Nix-provided ps in Venus's Darwin check inputs (a Nix and dependency change for the same answer); a test-only unsafe exception in main.rs (a recorded crate policy change).

title: Keep the eon CLI's socket reads working after the supervisor closes on macOS
description:
## Why

On macOS the `eon` CLI fails against a live supervisor. macOS CI run 40721211773 attempt 2
(e04553c; evidence in /home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-overseer/ci-40721211773-a2/): 32 of 49
`workspace_control` tests in `test:eon` failed, almost all with `cannot bound Eon action result:
Invalid argument (os error 22)` (`steps/69-test-eon.log` lines 85, 96, 126, 165, 227 and others).
`runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/control.rs:232-235` calls `set_read_timeout` before each read
(header, then body). Inference (XNU): Darwin's setsockopt returns EINVAL once a Unix socket is
shut down both ways, which happens when the supervisor writes its reply and closes; the reply is
already buffered. `supervisor.rs:578` uses the same per-read pattern. This is a product bug on
macOS, not only a test failure.

## Contract

The eon CLI's workspace actions (EON-C7 on macOS; the CLI contracts in docs/CONTRACTS.md). No
contract text changes: the CLI must behave on macOS as it does on Linux.

## Change

In Eon Runtime, set each socket's timeouts once per connection before the first read or write, or
treat EINVAL from `set_read_timeout` / `set_write_timeout` after a peer close as "read what is
buffered". Apply it at every per-read timeout site (control.rs, supervisor.rs, and any other
found by search). Prefer one helper as the single owner.

Also check `workspace_control.rs:1591`: on macOS a directory came back as `/private/tmp/...` where
the test (`...preserves_raw_directory`) expected the raw `/tmp/...`. Decide whether Eon
canonicalizes a path it should keep raw (product bug) or the test's expectation is wrong; fix
the owner. Low confidence; keep it in this bead only if the fix is small, else file a bead.

## Acceptance

- Linux: `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime -p eon` passes; fmt and clippy on Linux and
  `--target aarch64-apple-darwin`.
- A test that fails without the fix where possible on Linux (for example a peer that closes
  right after writing), else the macOS CI run is the red/green and the bead says so.
- The next macOS CI run's `test:eon` no longer shows os error 22.

## Scope

runtime/ (and eon/ tests if needed). Codex review per AGENTS.md. Consequential? It changes no
wire format; it is a lifecycle detail of one read path, so no reference gate unless the fix
grows.

comments.text:

Approval, relayed by eon-overseer (AP-COORDINATOR-001), recorded 2026-10-28: Lucca, 2026-10-27: "do these two too, then ... i want to move closer to the 'yu testing' gate", standing for the macOS launch path; Lucca, 2026-10-28: "lets get to working", on the plan to fix the macOS CI failures (kz4p.23-.28) with Opus planning and gating and Codex implementing. Evidence read: steps/69-test-eon.log of run 40721211773 attempt 2. Every `os error 22` failure is "cannot bound Eon action result", i.e. control.rs `send_prepared_action`'s per-read `set_read_timeout`. The other failures (corrupt instead of incompatible, stop prompt EOF, window not ready, picker did not close) are downstream of the same inspection/action failure, except workspace_control.rs:1591. Inference (XNU `sosetoptlock`): setsockopt fails with EINVAL once a socket has both SS_CANTRCVMORE and SS_CANTSENDMORE, which a Unix stream socket gets when its peer closes. The reply is already buffered, and I/O on such a socket cannot block. Linux allows setsockopt after shutdown, so it cannot reproduce this.

Approach: keep the per-read deadline (it bounds the whole exchange), and give Eon Runtime one helper that applies a socket timeout and treats EINVAL as success, with a comment naming the Darwin rule. Rejected: setting the timeout once per connection, because each blocking read could then wait the full timeout again and the shared `deadline` (supervisor inspection) would stop bounding the exchange; poll(2) with nonblocking I/O, more code for the same result.

Left as they are: connect/accept-time setup (control.rs connect and handle_client, pane_labels observe setup) and pane_labels' `set_read_timeout(None)`, where the peer cannot have closed yet or a closed peer ends the connection with the same result.

workspace_control.rs:1591 (`directory_picker_retargets_cancels_and_stops_with_venus`): Eon takes the launch directory from `env::current_dir()` (supervisor.rs:757), i.e. getcwd, which on macOS returns the physical `/private/tmp/...` for a `/tmp/...` cwd. Eon canonicalizes nothing; the test's expectation is wrong. Fix the test to expect the physical path (`fs::canonicalize` of the launch directory at that assertion and any sibling assertion with the same cause), not the temp root, since a longer root lengthens socket paths toward macOS's 104-byte limit. Whether Eon should prefer a validated logical $PWD is a product question outside this bead; reported to eon-overseer, not filed.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Plan amendment (after eon-overseer's review of the plan): the helper treats EINVAL as success only when the socket also shows the peer's hangup, so a timeout is never silently dropped on a live connection. On EINVAL it polls the stream with zero timeout (events POLLIN, retrying EINTR) and returns Ok only if revents has POLLHUP; otherwise it returns the original EINVAL. Linux (unix_poll, sk_shutdown == SHUTDOWN_MASK after the peer's release) and XNU (EV_EOF on the read filter) both report POLLHUP once the peer has closed, and I/O on such a socket then returns buffered data, EOF or EPIPE without blocking. Taking the setter's result as an argument makes this testable on Linux: one unit test feeds a synthetic EINVAL with (a) a peer that wrote and closed, expecting Ok and then the buffered bytes followed by EOF, and (b) a live peer, expecting the EINVAL back. It fails if the helper swallows EINVAL unconditionally or rejects the closed case. The macOS red/green stays run 40721211773 attempt 2 against the next macOS CI run.

Out of scope, recorded, not filed (eon-overseer will raise it with Lucca): on macOS a launch from a `/tmp/x` directory shows the tab directory as `/private/tmp/x`, because Eon takes getcwd's physical path (supervisor.rs `env::current_dir()`). Preferring a validated logical `$PWD` would be a product choice.

comments.text:

Raw expectations (HOME, picker selections, explicit snapshot directories, the temporary root) are unchanged.

- `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime -p eon`: pass (eon-runtime lib 131 passed, 1 ignored; workspace_control 49 passed; other targets 0 tests).
- `cargo fmt -p eon-runtime -p eon --check`: pass. `cargo clippy --locked -p eon-runtime -p eon --all-targets -- -D warnings` (dev shell): pass.

title: Make the Unix connect-timeout test fill the backlog on macOS
description:
## Why

macOS CI run 40721211773 attempt 2 (e04553c; evidence in
/home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-overseer/ci-40721211773-a2/): `test:eon-runtime` failed
`sessions::tests::unix_connection_attempt_obeys_timeout` at
`runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/sessions.rs:2546:9` (`assertion failed: result...is_err()`,
`steps/68-test-eon-runtime.log:190-191`). The test (2523-2550) uses `listen(0)`, queues one
connect, and expects `unix_connect_with_timeout` (sessions.rs:380) to time out. On Linux backlog 0
holds exactly one connection; Darwin evidently admits more (inference).

## Change

Eon Runtime test only: fill the listener's backlog in a loop (non-blocking connects until one
would block, with a bound) before the timed attempt, so the test holds on both kernels. Do not
make it Linux-only unless filling cannot be made deterministic on Darwin; then say why.

## Acceptance

- `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime` passes on Linux; fmt and clippy on Linux and
  `--target aarch64-apple-darwin`.
- The next macOS CI run passes the test.

## Scope

sessions.rs tests only. Codex review per AGENTS.md.

comments.text:
Plan (Opus, 2026-10-28). Not covered: push, promotion, main/stable, GitHub or site posts, workflow dispatch, renting a Mac, Lucca's running Eon.

Approach: in `sessions::tests::unix_connection_attempt_obeys_timeout` (runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/sessions.rs, ~2581 at 32e0617), replace the single `queued` UnixStream with a loop of non-blocking socket2 connects to the listener that stops at the first WouldBlock (Linux, EAGAIN on a full AF_UNIX backlog) or ConnectionRefused (BSD/XNU refuse a full AF_UNIX queue at once instead of blocking), keeping the connected ones alive until after the timed attempt. A hard bound (512 connects) fails the test with the count instead of running out of descriptors; any other error panics with the error. The timed `unix_connect_with_timeout` attempt and the 1 s recv bound and `is_err` assertion stay as they are, so on Linux the attempt still exercises the poll timeout, and on Darwin it must return promptly with an error.

Not Linux-only: the fill is deterministic on both kernels because it stops on the kernel's own full-queue signal rather than on a guessed backlog size.

Red check: none on Linux (the test passes there today; the failure is Darwin-only). The native red is CI run 40721211773 attempt 2, steps/68-test-eon-runtime.log:190-191; the native green is the next macOS CI run.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Change: `sessions::tests::unix_connection_attempt_obeys_timeout` now listens with backlog 1 instead of 0 and, before the timed attempt, fills the queue with non-blocking socket2 connects until the kernel reports it full (WouldBlock on Linux, ConnectionRefused on XNU), holding the connected sockets until the attempt finishes. More than 16 connects without a full-queue signal fails the test with the count; any other connect error panics with it. The timed `unix_connect_with_timeout` attempt, its 1 s watchdog and the `is_err()` assertion are unchanged. Root cause, from XNU source (bsd/kern/uipc_socket.c solisten): Darwin maps backlog 0 to somaxconn (128), so one queued connection never filled the queue and the timed connect succeeded. With backlog 1, Linux and XNU each admit 2. Plan amendment: listen(1) and bound 16 replace "listen(0), bound 512" after the Codex review (below), because listen(0) on XNU would hold about 193 descriptors before filling.

title: Kill every supervisor a failing eon test spawned, on macOS too
description:
## Why

macOS CI run 40721211773 attempt 2 (e04553c; evidence in
/home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-overseer/ci-40721211773-a2/): failing `test:eon` tests leaked
supervisors (`steps/72-leftovers.log:258,263,286`: `/tmp/e0/ec-38994-14/eonbase` and
`target/debug/eon`). eon-test's guard (nix/test-sandbox.nix:27-30) then refused the next two
suites (`test:eon-manifest`, `test:mac-proof`: "an Eon supervisor of this user is running").
On Linux the sandbox's PID namespace cleans up; macOS has none.
`eonbase_replaces_exact_residue_after_its_supervisor_and_session_die` (workspace_control.rs
2853-2908) holds `second` as a plain `std::process::Child` and panicked at 2906; the debug `eon`
leak is likely another test holding a plain Child.

## Change

eon test code: hold every spawned supervisor or eon process in a kill-on-drop guard (reuse the
existing `ManagedChild` / `TestProcess`), so a panicking test cannot leak it. Search all of
eon/tests and runtime tests for plain `Child` holds of supervisors.

## Acceptance

- `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon` passes on Linux; fmt and clippy on Linux and
  `--target aarch64-apple-darwin`.
- A forced panic in one such test (local red check, not committed) leaves no process behind.
- The next macOS CI run shows no leftovers from test:eon and runs eon-manifest and mac-proof.

## Scope

Test code only. Codex review per AGENTS.md.

title: Build the macOS harness's shared Nix inputs once, not per check
description:
## Why

macOS CI run 40721211773 attempt 2 (e04553c; evidence in
/home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-overseer/ci-40721211773-a2/) used 263 of the harness's 320
minutes, about 230 of them on 50 `check:` steps that each rebuilt Orbit from scratch (2.5-5 min)
before failing the same way: Nix does not cache build failures. Once Orbit builds, those checks
will do real work, so the budget will be tight, and Mac minutes (CI queue, the rental, Yu's time)
are scarce.

## Change

In eon/tools/mac-proof: build what the checks share once, and stop repeating a known failure.
Either build all check attributes in one `nix build --keep-going` and report each check from it,
or add one Orbit build step that the `check:orbit-*` steps need, so they are skipped (listed,
never passed) when it fails. Keep per-check status in summary.txt/json. Re-check the 320m
`--timeout` and the job's 360m against the new shape and say what a full green run should take.

## Acceptance

- `nix develop -c eon-test -p mac-proof` passes; fmt and clippy on Linux and darwin.
- `run --dry-run` shows the new plan; a Linux test covers "shared build failed, checks skipped".
- Report the expected macOS run time.

## Scope

mac-proof only (and the workflow's timeout if the estimate needs it). Codex review per AGENTS.md.
close_reason: mac-proof builds the checks' shared inputs once in check-inputs and skips checks whose input failed; Linux tests, fmt, clippy (Linux and darwin) pass; expected green macOS run ~165m, timeouts unchanged; native proof is the next macOS CI run

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Plan (Opus, 2026-10-28). Codex implements; Opus gates.

Approvals, relayed by eon-overseer with the user's words: Lucca, 2026-10-27, "do these two too,
then ... i want to move closer to the 'yu testing' gate" (standing for the macOS launch path);
2026-10-28, "lets get to working" (the plan to fix the macOS CI failures kz4p.23-.28, Opus plans
and gates, Codex implements). Not covered: push, promotion, workflow dispatch, GitHub posts,
renting a Mac.

Evidence (ci-40721211773-a2/summary.txt): 47 check:orbit-*, eonbase-closure and
managed-command-path each rebuilt the same `orbitPackage` (flake.nix:286, shared by every
nix/orbit-checks.nix real-PTY check) and failed in libghostty-vt-sys, 2.5-13 min each.

Approach: shared direct inputs, built once, per-check skip. Nix dedupes a derivation inside one
invocation, and a check's real work stays its own step (own log, time, HOUR timeout, checks still
serial, which keeps the real-PTY checks off each other's CPU).

- `check_list` (eon/tools/mac-proof/src/run.rs:525): also record each check's .drv path
  (`nix eval --json .#checks.<sys> --apply` mapping names to `drvPath`).
- New step `check-inputs` (requires `check-list`, after it, before the `check:` loop at
  run.rs:214): the union of the checks' direct input derivations (`nix-store --query
  --references <check.drv>`, lines ending `.drv`; plain-line legacy output, stable across Nix
  versions, unlike `nix derivation show` JSON), built in one `nix build --keep-going --no-link
  --print-build-logs <drv>^*...`. Afterwards it records which inputs have an invalid output
  (`nix-store --query --outputs` then `nix-store --check-validity --print-invalid`), whether
  the build passed or not.
- Each `check:<name>` requires `check-list` when all its inputs are valid, else
  `check-inputs`, so the Runner's existing skip names it: "needs check-inputs, which did not
  pass". Checks whose inputs built run as now even when `check-inputs` failed.
- If `check-inputs` cannot tell which inputs failed (timeout, query failure), every check
  requires it (all skipped), never a re-run of a known failure.
- Help (main.rs:55-70) and docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:41 name the step.

Red check: a Linux test of the real check loop with a stub nix (no PATH mutation; a Context
field for the program is acceptable), where one shared input fails: checks on it are skipped
with the message and never run; a check off it runs and passes; summary.json keeps each
check's status. Red before the change (the stub sees every check build).

Scope: eon/tools/mac-proof, docs/DEVELOPMENT.md, and .github/workflows/mac-proof.yml only if
the run-time estimate needs a different timeout. No flake change, no new dependency, no contract
change.

Checks: `nix develop -c eon-test -p mac-proof`; `cargo fmt --check`; clippy `--locked
--all-targets -D warnings` on Linux and for aarch64-apple-darwin (recipe on kz4p.1);
`mac-proof run --dry-run` shows check-inputs. Report the expected full green macOS run time
from the a2 step durations against the 320m limit and 360m job.

comments.text:
Proof (Opus final gate, 2026-10-28), on the tree of this commit (candidate tree deeeb1d335feec60bc5e5e8508059fc53888801b
before this comment), x86_64 Linux, worktree at base a211379:

- `nix develop -c eon-test -p mac-proof`: pass, 19 unit + 3 integration tests, including
  `failed_shared_inputs_skip_only_the_checks_that_need_them` (two checks share a failing input:
  both skipped with "needs check-inputs, which did not pass" and never built; a check on a good
  input passes; the shared input is built once) and `failed_combined_evaluation_keeps_the_shared_build`
  (combined drvPath eval fails: per-check evals, one check that does not evaluate runs its own
  build, the rest still share one `build --keep-going`). Red against the old loop and against
  round 2, as Codex reported.
- `cargo fmt --check -p mac-proof`: pass. `cargo clippy --locked -p mac-proof --all-targets -- -D
  warnings`: pass on Linux and with rustup stable for `--target aarch64-apple-darwin`
  (cross-target lint only).
- Dry run: tests/local.rs's round trip now expects `check-inputs=planned`; it passes.
- Not proved: native macOS execution, a real Nix shared-input build. The next macOS CI run is the
  native check.

Shape as landed: `check-list` discovers names only (attrNames, as before). New step
`check-inputs` (2h, requires check-list) evaluates drvPaths (tryEval; on a failed combined eval,
one `nix eval --raw` per check), takes each check's direct input derivations from
`nix-store --query --references`, builds their union once with `nix build --keep-going
<drv>^*`, then marks inputs with an invalid output as failed. A check runs when check-inputs
passed, none of its inputs failed, or its drvPath did not evaluate; otherwise it is skipped.
If check-inputs times out or a query fails, checks with known inputs are skipped, never rebuilt.

Known cost, accepted: when the `package` step fails, check-inputs rebuilds the failing package
once (eon-managed-command-path and eonbase-closure take eonPackage and venusPackage as inputs),
not once per check.

setup and upload, so the workflow is unchanged. It is an estimate: a2 never reached a successful

input per check; per-check eval fallback added). Opus round on deeeb1d: clean. Narrow Codex
