title: Keep the supervisor's side of a control connection working after the client closes on macOS
description:
## Why

macOS CI run 40779777680 (head 32c3dff; evidence in
/home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-overseer/ci-40779777680/) still fails `package` (so all 16 GUI
scenario steps were skipped), check:eonbase-closure, check:managed-command-path and test:eon on two
eon tests:

1. `lost_stop_response_still_finishes_the_supervisor`: `69-test-eon.log:71-72`, panicked at
   workspace_control.rs:1071 "Eon process did not exit" (from :5714). The test writes Stop, then
   shuts down and drops before the supervisor accepts. Inferred cause: the server side kz4p.25
   missed. `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/control.rs:511` (`handle_client`) does
   `if stream.set_read_timeout(timeout).is_err() || stream.set_write_timeout(timeout).is_err() {
   return false; }` without `bound_io` (sessions.rs:390), so on Darwin, after the peer has gone,
   EINVAL drops the buffered Stop and the supervisor never exits. A product bug on macOS.
2. `tab_directory_retargets_future_sessions_without_crossing_tabs`: fails in every macOS run.
   `wait_for_picker_close` times out at :1175, and in the package build the request `write_all`
   at :1111 gets BrokenPipe (`03-package.log:10287-10288`): the supervisor closed early. Cause not
   found because the test sends the supervisor's stderr to null. Candidates: the same
   handle_client EINVAL path, or the macOS /tmp -> /private/tmp mismatch.

## Change

- Wrap both timeout calls in control.rs `handle_client` with `bound_io`. Audit every other
  `set_read_timeout` / `set_write_timeout` in Eon Runtime (diagnosis named pane_labels.rs:144-145
  and 178, sessions.rs:523 and 1632) and use `bound_io` wherever a peer may already have closed.
- For test 2: first send that test's supervisor stderr to a file kept on failure (test-only), so
  the next macOS run shows the cause even if this guess is wrong. If the evidence on Linux points
  at a fix (same EINVAL path or a path mismatch), make it; otherwise leave the diagnostic and say
  so on the bead.

## Acceptance

- `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime -p eon`; fmt and clippy on Linux and
  aarch64-apple-darwin.
- A Linux test that exercises a client closing right after writing a request where possible.
- The next macOS CI run passes `package` and test:eon, or test 2's log names its cause.

## Scope

runtime/ plus eon/crates/eon/tests/workspace_control.rs diagnostics. Codex review per AGENTS.md.
Approval: Lucca, 2026-10-28, "diagnose, fix, commit, push".
close_reason: Native macOS proof: mac-proof.yml run 40808735721 (head 6f7eb99, tree d142235, aarch64-macos, macos-15 runner) passes package, check-inputs, every check:* and test:* step, and leftovers (summary.txt in /home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-overseer/ci-40808735721/). The GUI scenario failure there is kz4p.34 (Venus Metal alpha mode), unrelated to this bead.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Correction to the proof comment above: Rust std uses plain accept(2) on macOS, which keeps the listener's O_NONBLOCK; on DragonFly, FreeBSD, NetBSD and OpenBSD it uses accept4(SOCK_CLOEXEC) (Rust 1.96 library/std/src/sys/net/connection/socket/unix.rs:247). The inherited-nonblocking claim covers macOS only; "and the BSDs" does not hold.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Plan (Opus planner, 2026-10-28; Codex implements, Opus gates).

Approval relayed by eon-overseer, recorded 2026-10-28: Lucca, 2026-10-27, "do these two too, then ... i want to move closer to the 'yu testing' gate" (macOS launch path); 2026-10-28, "lets get to working" (fix the macOS CI failures kz4p.23-.28 with Opus planning and gating, Codex implementing); 2026-10-28 after the second macOS run, "diagnose, fix, commit, push". The coordinator lands and pushes. This slice does no push, promotion, GitHub post or workflow dispatch.

Not consequential (AP-REFERENCE-001): no dependency, protocol, contract or trust boundary change. It applies the existing `bound_io` (sessions.rs:390, the one owner of the Darwin peer-closed EINVAL rule) at the remaining sites. Portability: neutral (bound_io is a no-op off EINVAL, so Linux behavior is unchanged).

Approach:
1. control.rs `handle_client` (:511): wrap both timeout calls in `bound_io`, so the supervisor still reads a request whose client already closed (lost Stop -> supervisor exits).
2. Audit of the other timeout sites; wrap each in `bound_io`, since a peer may have closed at each:
   - control.rs:157-158 (CLI connect): a supervisor that closed right after accept is now reported by the next read or write, not as a corrupt endpoint.
   - pane_labels.rs:144-145 and :178 (metadata observer): metadata Orbit sent before closing is still read.
   - sessions.rs:523-524 (lease after acquisition) and :1632-1633 (lease restore after a failed stop): a lease whose Orbit has already closed goes through the normal lost-terminal path instead of failing setup.
   - supervisor.rs and the rest of control.rs already wrap. pane_labels.rs:363 is test code with a live peer; no change.
3. `tab_directory_retargets_future_sessions_without_crossing_tabs` diagnostic (test-only, workspace_control.rs): send that supervisor's stderr to a file under the test root and print it when the test panics, through a drop guard that checks `thread::panicking()`, so cargo shows it in the failure output. `wait_for_picker_close`'s timeout message names the last response (the active tab's directory against the expected one), which tests the /tmp -> /private path guess. Fix test 2 only if Linux evidence points at a cause; otherwise leave the diagnostic and say so here.

Red check: Linux cannot produce the Darwin EINVAL, so no Linux red exists. Native red: the macOS run's `lost_stop_response_still_finishes_the_supervisor` (69-test-eon.log:71-72). Add one eon-runtime unit test in control.rs: `handle_client` on a `UnixStream::pair` whose peer wrote a Stop-shaped request and closed must dispatch it and return the dispatcher's shutdown flag. It runs in test:eon-runtime on macOS and points at handle_client if it fails there. Green on Linux; native red/green comes from the next macOS CI run.

Scope: runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/{control,pane_labels,sessions}.rs plus the test-only diagnostic in eon/crates/eon/tests/workspace_control.rs. No contract, CHANGELOG or docs change (test-only and Darwin-only fix of an unproven platform).

Checks: `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime -p eon`; `cargo fmt --check`; `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -p eon-runtime -p eon -- -D warnings` on Linux; Darwin `cargo clippy --locked --target aarch64-apple-darwin -p eon-runtime -p eon --all-targets -- -D warnings` (recipe on kz4p.1). Codex review per AGENTS.md. Next macOS CI run: package and test:eon pass, or test 2's failure output names its cause.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Proof and result (2026-10-28; Codex implemented, Opus gated). The commit that carries this comment is the proof's revision. Its tree differs from the checked candidate tree 602284436b337cddc76339062a65fde9731f20c0 (base 7f605f6) only by this comment.

Change:
- control.rs `handle_client`: clears the accepted stream's nonblocking mode before setting its timeouts, and wraps both timeout calls in `bound_io`.
- `bound_io` also wraps the timeout calls at control.rs:156-157 (CLI connect), pane_labels.rs:145-146 and :179 (metadata observer), and sessions.rs:522-523 and :1629-1630 (lease). Every production timeout site in Eon Runtime is now covered; supervisor.rs and the rest of control.rs were already wrapped.
- workspace_control.rs, test only: `tab_directory_retargets_future_sessions_without_crossing_tabs` writes the supervisor's stderr to a file and prints it when the test panics. When `wait_for_picker_close` times out, it names the last response (the active tab's directory against the expected one).

Likely test 2 cause (inferred from the code and the CI logs; native proof pending), found at the gate and not named in the bead: `ControlListener` is nonblocking (control.rs:475). On macOS and the BSDs, accept(2) gives the new socket the listener's O_NONBLOCK, and Rust std uses plain accept() there, while Linux accepts blocking. So when the supervisor accepted before the client's request arrived, `read_request` hit WouldBlock at once, replied malformed-action and closed. The client then saw BrokenPipe on its write (03-package.log:10287-10288). A dropped picker commit would also leave the popup open (69-test-eon.log, "directory picker did not close"). This is a product bug on macOS for any control request that races the accept. The /tmp -> /private path guess was ruled out: the supervisor keeps the picker's selection as given (no canonicalization), and the test's later cwd checks already canonicalize. Orbit has no such gap: it sets the mode on every accepted stream (orbit/src/host.rs:877, orbit/src/management.rs:180, :199, :395).

Tests (eon-runtime, control.rs):
- `handle_client_waits_for_request_on_a_nonblocking_stream`: models the inherited mode with a nonblocking server stream and a peer that writes after 50 ms. Linux red on the tree without the clear: the peer got BrokenPipe at control.rs:725 and "delayed request was not dispatched" at :736 (line numbers on that tree). Green with it. It depends on scheduling: if the test thread starts after the peer has written, it passes without the fix (Codex nit, not taken).
- `handle_client_dispatches_buffered_request_after_peer_closes`: green on Linux before and after, because Linux never returns that EINVAL. On macOS it narrows a failure to handle_client. Native red evidence for this path is the macOS run's `lost_stop_response_still_finishes_the_supervisor` (69-test-eon.log:71-72).

Checks on tree 6022844, x86_64 Linux (Pop!_OS 24.04 host, nix develop shell, CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4), run by Opus at the final gate:
- `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime -p eon`: pass (eon 49 passed; eon-runtime 133 passed, 1 existing ignored measurement).
- `nix develop -c cargo fmt --check`: pass.
- `nix develop -c cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -p eon-runtime -p eon -- -D warnings`: pass.
- `rustup run stable cargo clippy --locked --target aarch64-apple-darwin -p eon-runtime -p eon --all-targets -- -D warnings` (rustc 1.96.0, dev-shell build inputs exported, recipe on kz4p.1): pass.
- Running the checks left the tree at 6022844 unchanged.
Not proven: native macOS behavior. Acceptance is still open on the next macOS CI run: `package` and test:eon pass, or test 2's failure output names its cause.

Review ledger: Opus gate 1 on Codex's first diff found 1 blocking issue (the inherited nonblocking accept), fixed in one Codex fix round with a Linux red/green. Codex review pass 1 on 6022844 (read-only, gpt-6.1-sol xhigh): 0 blocking, 1 nit (above, not taken). Opus final gate on 6022844: clean. Converged with 2 Codex passes counted (implementation excluded): the review pass, and the narrow re-check of this proof record.

title: Read CPU and RAM for the Eon Bar chips on macOS
description:
## Why

The Eon Bar's CPU and RAM chips are a 1.0 feature (EON-C30, VEN-C28) but read `/proc`, so on
macOS they never appear. A Mac user would see a bar that silently lacks two default items.

Lucca (2026-10-27, relayed by eon-overseer): "i'd rather test everything possible and fix myself,
letting to Yu only final testing and final fixes that i missed ... so the more automated, the
better."

## Evidence

- `venus/src/system.rs:13-19` CPU from `/proc/stat`, `:93-99` RAM from `/proc/meminfo`; both
  return `None` when not Linux, so the chip is hidden (VEN-C28 "an unreadable reading shows no
  label rather than 0%").
- VEN-C28 (`venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md:1826`) names Linux, `/proc/stat` and MemTotal minus
  MemAvailable; EON-C30 (`docs/CONTRACTS.md:2374`) names "users on x86_64 Linux". Both are
  contract text, so macOS readings need Lucca's approval of new wording first.

## Scope

In scope: propose VEN-C28 and EON-C30 wording for macOS (CPU: whole-machine busy ticks over the
interval from `host_processor_info`/`host_statistics(HOST_CPU_LOAD_INFO)`; RAM: a stated
definition, recommended Activity Monitor's "Memory Used" = (active + wired + compressed) pages
over `hw.memsize`), stop for approval, then implement the macOS readers in `venus/src/system.rs`
behind `cfg(target_os = "macos")` with the existing parse/reject structure.

Out of scope: chip layout, settings, EONW, Runtime, other widgets (GPU/IO beads).

## Acceptance

- Lucca approved the contract wording (quoted on this bead with date) before code.
- macOS readers return `None` on a failed call, never 0% (existing rule); Linux readers and their
  four tests unchanged.
- Deterministic parts (tick deltas to percentage, page counts to percentage) are pure functions
  with one test each that runs on Linux; the syscall wrappers compile for the Apple target.
- Native observation is deferred to the harness's GUI scenario (chip visible with a plausible
  value in the capture, and the Venus log).

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-venus` exits 0; `cargo fmt --check`; `cargo clippy --locked
  --all-targets -- -D warnings` for Venus (AGENTS.md Verification).
- Gate check: `cargo check --locked --target aarch64-apple-darwin -p yazelix-venus` shows no
  error from `system.rs`.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop for Lucca's approval of the VEN-C28/EON-C30 wording before implementation.
- Stop if `libc` lacks the Mach host calls and a new crate (`mach2`) seems needed (dependency
  gate); report the gap instead.
- Read `venus/AGENTS.md` first; follow its rules.

## Maintenance Notes

- Alternative if Lucca prefers no contract change before launch: leave the chips hidden on macOS
  and list "no CPU/RAM chips" as a README macOS gap (friends'-gate bead).
close_reason: macOS CPU and RAM readers implemented under the approved VEN-C28/EON-C30 wording; Linux checks and darwin clippy green; native observation deferred to eon-mac-launch-kz4p.12

comments.text:
Started 2026-10-27 by agent in worktree ~/.cache/eon-agents/chips at 0833b3c. Approval (relayed by eon-overseer): Lucca, 2026-10-27: "do these two too, then ... i want to move closer to the 'yu testing' gate". - Behavior and owners: on Apple Silicon macOS the Eon Bar shows the VEN-C28 CPU and RAM chips instead of hiding them. Venus's system module (venus/src/system.rs) alone owns sampling and parsing; application.rs's 2-second wake, CpuUse::between and the labels are unchanged and shared with Linux.
- References read (clones under ~/pjs/refs/sysstat-macos/):
  - btop v1.4.7 6e39144aaf5a6bc01b9f795010b0914431067183 src/osx/btop_collect.cpp: host_processor_info per core, busy = user+nice+system, sysconf page size, hw.memsize total; memory meter used = active+wire (does not match Activity Monitor; rejected).
  - htop 3.5.3 20882b8ef8271fb49ea0eb74bbfd484e9b0a11d8 darwin/Platform.c: used = wire + (internal - purgeable) + compressor; ChangeLog 3.5.2 "darwin: fix used memory calculation to match Activity Monitor". htop 3.4.1 348c0a6b had the older active+inactive+speculative+wire+compressor-purgeable-external form (rejected: XNU counts speculative inside free and throttled inside wire, so it drifts).

title: Drain Orbit's PTY while it waits for a stopping shell on macOS
description:
## Why

macOS CI run 40779777680 (head 32c3dff; evidence in
/home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-overseer/ci-40779777680/):

1. check:orbit-program-status: `42-check-orbit-program-status.log:15-16`, panicked at
   orbit/tests/real_pty/program_status.rs:80 `Timeout`: `stop()` got Reply::Timeout after the
   lease's 3 s read timeout (management_lease.rs:53), in `answer_time_under_load` (511-546) where
   the child runs `yes`. Stops with no pending output passed.
2. test:yazelix-orbit: `simultaneous_stale_socket_claim_has_one_reachable_owner`,
   `63-test-yazelix-orbit.log:462-463`, lifecycle.rs:1897 `wait_bounded(winner)?.success()`
   failed: the winner exited with 128+signal (host.rs:1737-1738, child not reaped after the
   termination signal). Intermittent (1 of 25 attempts; passed the run before).

Inferred common cause (medium confidence): on Darwin (4.4BSD heritage) a session leader's exit
blocks in `ttywait` until the PTY output queue drains, and an exiting process no longer takes
signals. Orbit's `contain()` (orbit/src/host.rs:1602-1636) and `reap()` (~1510) only sleep and
`try_reap`; they never read the master, so the shell cannot finish exiting within the SIGHUP 500 ms
+ SIGKILL 2 s window. Linux has no ttywait.

## Contract

ORB-C12 (bounded PTY process-group shutdown). No contract text change: this keeps its bound on
macOS. If the fix would change what ORB-C12 promises, stop and send the wording to eon-overseer.

## Change

While `contain()` and `reap()` wait, keep draining (and discarding, or routing as normal output
if that is the existing owner's job) the PTY master, or close/flush the master before waiting,
whichever fits Orbit's ownership of terminal state without losing output that ORB contracts say
is delivered. First confirm the mechanism with a reproducer the Linux harness can run where
possible (it may not reproduce on Linux; then rely on the macOS CI run and say so).

## Acceptance

- Orbit's AGENTS.md checks for the changed crate: `nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-orbit`, the
  affected orbit real-PTY Nix checks (program-status, lifecycle), `cargo fmt --check`,
  `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and clippy for aarch64-apple-darwin.
- Portability disposition recorded (isolated Darwin behaviour or neutral).
- The next macOS CI run passes check:orbit-program-status and test:yazelix-orbit.

## Scope

orbit/ only. Read orbit/AGENTS.md first. Codex review per AGENTS.md. Approval: Lucca,
2026-10-28, "diagnose, fix, commit, push".

The GUI scenario failure there is kz4p.34 (Venus Metal alpha mode), unrelated to this bead.

Plan (Opus, 2026-10-28; Codex implements, Opus gates).

Approval, relayed by eon-overseer (2026-10-28): Lucca 2026-10-27 "do these two too, then ... i want
to move closer to the 'yu testing' gate" (macOS launch path); 2026-10-28 "lets get to working" (the
plan to fix the macOS CI failures with the Opus-plans/Codex-implements split); 2026-10-28 after the
second macOS run "diagnose, fix, commit, push". Not covered: push, promotion, main/stable, GitHub or
site posts, workflow dispatch, Lucca's running Eon.

Mechanism (inference, from the code at 7f605f6): both failures are a stop that waits for a shell
the host is not reading. answer_time_under_load: `yes` fills the PTY; Stop -> stop_explicitly ->
contain() sends SIGHUP, the shell (session leader) exits and, on Darwin, blocks in ttywait until
the slave's output queue drains; contain() and then reap() only sleep and try_reap, so SIGKILL
cannot help (an exiting process takes no signals), contain returns NotReaped and Bend's Reap loop
waits 2 s at a time past the lease's 3 s read timeout -> Timeout. The lifecycle winner is the
same wait after SIGTERM (run()'s error path calls contain()), with a little pending shell output,
hence intermittent. Linux has no ttywait, so the Linux harness cannot reproduce it.

Approach: while contain() and reap() wait for the child, read the PTY master and discard what it
returns, bounded per wait tick so a writer that survives the signals cannot pin the host. No
terminal feeding: after a stop the client closes without Exited, nothing is published, and the
tombstone holds only reason and status, so no ORB contract delivers that output; discarding also
keeps libghostty replies, clipboard and pointer mechanics out of shutdown. One helper on Orbit in
orbit/src/pty.rs (next to read_into), called from the two wait loops in orbit/src/host.rs
(contain's reaped_by closure, reap()). Mechanism is platform-neutral (also harmless on Linux);
the reason is Darwin's.

Portability disposition: neutral (no cfg); motivated by isolated Darwin behaviour (ttywait).
Contract: ORB-C12 keeps its text; this restores its bound on macOS. orbit/docs/BEHAVIOR.md gets
one present-tense sentence in the ORB-C12 shutdown text naming the drain and the check that
covers it on macOS (orbit-program-status's answer_time_under_load).

Red: macOS CI run 40779777680 (head 32c3dff) steps 42 and 63 (evidence in the bead body). No
Linux red is possible; no new test (an existing check already exercises it natively on macOS).
Green on Linux = no regression; the native green is the next macOS CI run.

orbit-program-status, orbit-lifecycle, orbit-guardian-containment, orbit-unreaped-stop,
orbit-descendant-exit (--keep-going); cargo fmt --check and cargo clippy --locked --all-targets
-- -D warnings for yazelix-orbit; aarch64-apple-darwin cargo check/clippy of yazelix-orbit
(lib, bin, --test lifecycle; real_pty's unreaped_stop is Linux-only) per kz4p.1's recipe.

Scope: orbit/src/host.rs, orbit/src/pty.rs, orbit/docs/BEHAVIOR.md, this bead. No Bend, schema,
protocol, contract or test-harness change.

title: Remove the eon check's temporary directory when its build fails
description:
## Why

macOS CI run 40779777680 (head 32c3dff; evidence in
/home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-overseer/ci-40779777680/) failed `leftovers`: "left behind:
directories [e0, e1, e2, e3]". None existed before the run (`01-host.log:21`). The eon package
check (flake.nix:737-755) makes `/tmp/e$name` in preCheck and removes it only in postCheck, which
does not run when checkPhase fails; four failed eon checkPhases (package, eonbase-closure twice,
managed-command-path) account for exactly four directories. eon-test steps clean up (EXIT trap,
nix/test-sandbox.nix:54). The harness comment at run.rs:315 already expects "a failed build
leaves its own".

## Change

Make the derivation remove its `/tmp/e$name` on failure as well as success (for example an EXIT
trap set in preCheck, or failureHook), so a failed build leaves nothing. Keep the harness's
leftovers check strict. Linux builds use the sandbox's /tmp, so show the Linux derivation output
is unchanged or rebuilt green.

## Acceptance

- Linux: the x86_64-linux preCheck/postCheck strings are byte-identical to the base, and the
  combined `nix build .#default --no-link` follows at landing (overseer), after .29, .30 and .31.
  (Amended 2026-10-28 with eon-overseer: workspaceSource includes flake.nix, so any flake.nix
  edit rebuilds the Linux packages; one combined build replaces a .31-only one.)
- A forced checkPhase failure (local, not committed) leaves no /tmp/e* directory where the
  builder's /tmp is visible, or the reasoning is recorded if that cannot run on Linux.
- The next macOS CI run's leftovers lists no e* directories from failed builds.

## Scope

flake.nix (or nix/) only. Codex review per AGENTS.md. Approval: Lucca, 2026-10-28, "diagnose,
fix, commit, push".

comments.text:

Contract: a Darwin build of the eon package removes the /tmp/e<c> directory it claimed whether its checkPhase passes or fails; a build that dies by SIGKILL may still leave one (nothing in the builder can run then), which is why mac-proof records the directories present before a run.

Approach: in flake.nix's eon package (the Darwin branch of preCheck/postCheck only, flake.nix:729-755), keep the claimed path in its own variable, define a small function that removes it when the variable is set, and register it with `failureHooks+=(...)` once mkdir succeeds. stdenv's setup.sh (pinned nixpkgs, generic/setup.sh:297-331) runs `runHook failureHook` from its own EXIT trap `exitHandler`; an EXIT trap of our own would replace that handler, so it is rejected. postCheck removes the directory and clears the variable, so a later failure (install, fixup) cannot delete a /tmp/e<c> another build claimed after ours. The Linux branch stays byte-identical.

Not changed: eon/tools/mac-proof/src/run.rs:344's comment ("a failed build leaves its own") stays; a killed build still can, and editing workspace source would change the Linux derivation. The leftovers check stays strict.

Red/green (local, uncommitted, outside the repo): a scratch derivation on the Linux stdenv whose preCheck/postCheck are the flake's evaluated aarch64-darwin eon preCheck/postCheck strings, with a checkPhase that fails on demand and an observer failureHook registered after ours that lists /tmp/e* to the log. Red at base (directory listed), green at candidate (none), plus the success path and a post-check failure leaving none. Host /tmp is never touched.

Checks: `nix eval --raw .#packages.x86_64-linux.default.drvPath` equal at base and candidate (Linux output unchanged, so the existing build stands); `nix eval --raw .#packages.aarch64-darwin.default.drvPath` evaluates; the red/green above; nixfmt check if the flake has one. title: Compare the canonical directory when waiting for the picker to close
description:
## Why

macOS CI run 40797703159 (head b8ed850; evidence in
/home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-overseer/ci-40797703159/) fails `package`, `check-inputs` and
test:eon on one test, so the 16 GUI scenario steps are skipped again. kz4p.29's stderr diagnostic
names the cause (`steps/70-test-eon.log:71-75`):

    panicked at eon/crates/eon/tests/workspace_control.rs:1185:9:
    directory picker did not close: active tab directory Some("/private/tmp/e0/ec-64533-44/first"),
    expected "/tmp/e0/ec-64533-44/first"

On macOS `/tmp` is a symlink to `/private/tmp`, and Eon reports the physical cwd. kz4p.25 already
canonicalized eight such expectations in this file (for example :4674-4675); `wait_for_picker_close`
(around :1150-1190) still compares the raw path. The supervisor did not crash: the earlier
BrokenPipe was the test tearing down after this timeout.

## Change

Test-only: make `wait_for_picker_close` (or its callers) compare against the canonical directory,
matching how kz4p.25 handled the others. Check every caller and any other raw-path comparison in
workspace_control.rs that a /tmp root reaches on macOS (it runs under /tmp/e0 in the package build
and under the eon-test sandbox root in test:eon). The product fix that would show the logical path
is eon-2cm5, which will revert these expectations; do not implement it here.

## Acceptance

- `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon --test workspace_control` passes on Linux.
- A Linux red/green where possible: run the test with its root reached through a symlink (local,
  not committed) and show it fails before and passes after; otherwise record why not.
- The next macOS CI run passes `package`, `check-inputs` and test:eon.

## Scope

eon/crates/eon/tests/workspace_control.rs only. Codex review per AGENTS.md. Approval: Lucca,
2026-10-28, "diagnose, fix, commit, push".
close_reason: Native macOS proof: mac-proof.yml run 40808735721 (head 6f7eb99, tree d142235, aarch64-macos, macos-15 runner) passes package, check-inputs, every check:* and test:* step, and leftovers (summary.txt in /home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-overseer/ci-40808735721/). The GUI scenario failure there is kz4p.34 (Venus Metal alpha mode), unrelated to this bead.

Which of the two waits (:4583 after startup, :4590 after `tab create`) reports the launch directory and which a raw commit is settled empirically by the red run, not assumed.

Then the fix; green is the same hacked run passing for this test, plus the unhacked file passing. Tests that fail only under the hack but passed natively on macOS are reported, not changed.

The startup wait_for_picker_close expects fs::canonicalize(&first), because the startup tab keeps the launch directory (getcwd, physical: /private/tmp on macOS). title: Find and fix the macOS orbit-clipboard check failure
description:
## Why

macOS CI run 40797703159 (head b8ed850; evidence in
/home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-overseer/ci-40797703159/) fails check:orbit-clipboard
(`steps/11-check-orbit-clipboard.log:14-15`), after 1.06 s:

    panicked at orbit/tests/real_pty/support.rs:480:26:
    peer closed before a complete ORBS message

The same check passed in run 40779777680 (head 32c3dff). The only Orbit change between the two
heads is kz4p.30 (d8222a5): `reap()` and `contain()` in orbit/src/host.rs now call
`discard_shutdown_output()` (orbit/src/pty.rs) each tick. `reap()` runs on `Decision::Reap`
(host.rs ~1448), which may also follow a natural exit or hangup, where ORB contracts say output
still feeds the terminal. If discarding there drops bytes or closes a peer early, that is a
regression from kz4p.30; otherwise the failure is an intermittent macOS race. Unknown which.

## Change

1. Find which receive closed (observer or client, which phase of orbit/tests/real_pty/clipboard.rs)
   and why. Try to reproduce on Linux: repeat `nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.orbit-clipboard`
   (with --rebuild) at b8ed850 and at 32c3dff, and the eon-test real-PTY path, enough times to
   tell a regression from a flake. Read when Bend decides Reap and whether pending PTY output can
   still be owed to a client or observer at that point.
2. If kz4p.30 is at fault, narrow the drain to the paths where nothing is owed (explicit stop,
   termination containment), keeping kz4p.30's macOS ttywait fix. If it is a pre-existing race,
   fix its owner. If no cause is found on Linux, add the smallest diagnostic that makes the next
   macOS run name it (which peer, last message received) and say so on the bead.

## Contract

ORB-C12 and whatever ORB contract covers clipboard writes / output delivery; no contract text
change. If a fix would change what one promises, stop and send the wording to eon-overseer.

## Acceptance

- Orbit's AGENTS.md checks for the changed crate: `nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-orbit`, the
  orbit real-PTY Nix checks touched (clipboard, program-status, lifecycle, stale-socket),
  `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and clippy for
  aarch64-apple-darwin.
- Portability disposition recorded.
- The next macOS CI run passes check:orbit-clipboard, check:orbit-program-status and
  test:yazelix-orbit.

## Scope

orbit/ only. Read orbit/AGENTS.md first. Codex review per AGENTS.md. Approval: Lucca,
2026-10-28, "diagnose, fix, commit, push".

The GUI scenario failure there is kz4p.34 (Venus Metal alpha mode), unrelated to this bead.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Plan (Opus planner, 2026-10-28). Roles relayed by eon-overseer: Opus plans and gates, Codex implements.

Approvals, relayed by eon-overseer, 2026-10-28: Lucca, 2026-10-27, "do these two too, then ... i want to move closer to the 'yu testing' gate" (standing for the macOS launch path); 2026-10-28, "lets get to working" (fix the macOS CI failures with this role split); 2026-10-28 after the second macOS run, "diagnose, fix, commit, push". Not covered: push, promotion, workflow dispatch, GitHub/site posts, the running Eon.

Evidence read (b8ed850 tree = 8e77c5b for orbit/):
- kz4p.30's drains cannot run on this test's paths. Bend decides Reap only after ChildExited (session.bend:474 via exit_stop; the child is already reaped, so host.rs reap() returns from try_reap before the drain) or after NotReaped (session.bend:1194, which follows ManageStop/contain). contain() runs only for ManageStop (host.rs:1482) and the host-failure/termination stop (host.rs:1713). The clipboard test uses no management and ends naturally (exit 5). So a kz4p.30 regression is unlikely unless the host already failed. Inference, not proof: Codex verifies it.
- History: check:orbit-clipboard passed once on macOS (run 40779777680, 32c3dff) and failed once (40797703159, b8ed850); run 40721211773 never built it. test:yazelix-orbit runs the real-PTY tests ignored, so no other macOS sample exists.
- The panic loses its phase and the host's side: support.rs:480 reports its own line, not the clipboard.rs call, and a test that panics before Server::passed drops the host's captured stderr ("orbit: <error>", main.rs:22/30) and exit status.

Approach:
1. Diagnose. Name each receive in clipboard.rs that can see EOF (observer metadata loop, reattach after overflow, exited(5), ...) and for each the server path that closes that peer with no message (host error, Drop, observer drop, overflow close). Look for macOS-specific behavior on each path (PTY read sizes for the 300-write overflow, ECONNRESET/close on the overflowed client, PTY EOF vs EIO at exit). Try to reproduce on Linux: loop the clipboard real-PTY test (eon-test with ORBIT_BIN set to a release build, ~200 runs, and `nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.orbit-clipboard --rebuild` ~10 times), under load too (e.g. run it alongside a parallel build). Report counts.
2. If a cause is found: fix its owner in orbit/ with a red/green check (a real-PTY or unit check that fails before the fix), keeping kz4p.30's ttywait drain. If kz4p.30 proves at fault, narrow its drain to the stop paths where nothing is owed.
3. If no cause is found on Linux: add the smallest diagnostic so the next macOS run names it, in orbit/tests/real_pty/support.rs (plus clipboard.rs for its helper):
   - #[track_caller] on the Peer receive chain (receive_within, receive, expect, frame, frame_titled, metadata, exited, and clipboard_until_frame), so the panic location is the clipboard.rs call, i.e. the phase and peer;
   - the panic message carries the last message that peer received (brief());
   - when a test panics with a Server alive, print the host's exit status and captured stdout/stderr to the test's stderr (Drop under thread::panicking()), so a host failure shows "orbit: <error>".
   Red/green for the diagnostic: in a scratch copy only, break the clipboard test or host so a receive sees EOF, and show the panic names the clipboard.rs line, the last message and the host's output; not shipped.

Files: orbit/tests/real_pty/support.rs, orbit/tests/real_pty/clipboard.rs; orbit/src/* only if a cause is found. No contract text change (ORB-C3, ORB-C12, clipboard delivery stay as written); if a fix would change what one promises, stop and send the wording to eon-overseer.

Scope boundary: orbit/ only; nix/orbit-checks.nix unchanged (no RUST_BACKTRACE there); no change to Bend policy or the wire. kz4p.32 (workspace_control.rs) runs in parallel and is not touched.

Checks: nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-orbit; the orbit real-PTY Nix checks clipboard, program-status, lifecycle, stale-socket (x86_64-linux); cargo fmt --check and cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings for yazelix-orbit; clippy for aarch64-apple-darwin. Portability disposition: neutral for a test-harness diagnostic; a host fix records its own. Native macOS result: the next macOS CI run (not claimed here).

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Proof and review (Opus gate, 2026-10-28). The commit carrying this comment is the proof's revision; the code is candidate tree 7aebbe2e1ebb2d63f31d2d6dfd510206e5e87fce over 8e77c5b (this comment adds only bead metadata).

Cause (reproduced on Linux): the clipboard test re-attached right after the overflowing read closed the first client, and took that close as proof that Orbit had read the whole 300-write burst. The close proves only that one PTY turn had more than 64 writes. Capture resets each turn (pty.rs start_turn) and is on while a client is attached, so when the burst splits across reads, its unread tail can overflow the new attachment too. Bend then detaches it (session.bend output_writes -> host drop_client) without a message, and the test's wait for AFTER OVERFLOW sees EOF ("peer closed before a complete ORBS message", support.rs:480). Linux counts on the unmodified tree: eon-test loop 200/200 and 10/10 under CPU load passed; Nix --rebuild 9 passed and 1 failed with that EOF; a scratch-only diagnostic build failed 1 of 64 at the wait after reattach, with the new client's last message being its initial HELD frame. This is the same phase and the same timing (~1 s) as macOS run 40797703159. kz4p.30 is not the cause: Reap follows ChildExited, where the child is already reaped and reap() returns before discard_shutdown_output, or NotReaped; contain() runs only for ManageStop and the failure stop. kz4p.30 is unchanged.

Change (test-only, 7 lines): orbit/tests/clipboard-shell.sh sends a second 300-write burst while detached, ending with the title OVERFLOW DRAINED, behind one more gate. orbit/tests/real_pty/clipboard.rs::run releases that gate after dropping the overflowed client and waits for the title through the existing metadata observer before it re-attaches. PTY output is FIFO, so the title proves that both bursts were read while detached. No production, Bend, wire, Nix or contract change. ORB-C11/ORB-C3/ORB-C12 and BEHAVIOR.md "Clipboard writes" stay as written.

Red/green: final shell with the original clipboard.rs: `nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-orbit --test real_pty clipboard -- --ignored --exact` failed with the same EOF (0.85 s). With the observer wait it passes (0.36 s).

Checks on tree 7aebbe2e (x86_64-linux, CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4), all run by the Opus gate:
- nix develop -c cargo fmt --check -p yazelix-orbit: ok
- nix develop -c cargo clippy --locked -p yazelix-orbit --all-targets -- -D warnings: ok
- nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-orbit: 54 unit + 18 lifecycle passed (50 real-PTY ignored by design, run via Nix)
- nix build --keep-going .#checks.x86_64-linux.orbit-{clipboard,program-status,lifecycle,stale-socket}: all built (clipboard /nix/store/76sa8kawjhywz4y35jm8148mj899dwci-orbit-clipboard)
- nix build --rebuild .#checks.x86_64-linux.orbit-clipboard: 15/15 passed (Codex's run: 10/10)
- aarch64-apple-darwin (Codex, rustup stable outside the dev shell with kz4p.1's env): cargo check and cargo clippy --locked -p yazelix-orbit --lib --bins --test lifecycle --test real_pty -- -D warnings: ok
- the working tree was unchanged by the checks
Portability disposition: neutral (an existing Unix real-PTY test and fixture only).

Not proved on macOS. The next macOS CI run (check:orbit-clipboard, check:orbit-program-status, test:yazelix-orbit) is the native check, and this bead stays in_progress until it runs. Residual risk (Codex review): the CI log alone does not show that this race caused the macOS failure. An unanswered peer at the negotiation deadline (host.rs:843) or the host-failure cleanup (host.rs:1710) would give the same phase-less panic. If check:orbit-clipboard fails again, the follow-up is the plan's test-harness diagnostic (track_caller on the receive chain, the last message received, and the host's output on panic). The scratch version of that diagnostic is in claude-clipboard-work.

Ledger: Codex implemented in 1 round (session 01a18571), no fix rounds. Opus first gate: 0 blocking, 1 optional nit (shell comment wording; not taken). AGENTS.md Codex review (fresh read-only, gpt-6.1-sol xhigh, session 01a18586): 0 blocking, 1 optional nit (BEHAVIOR.md:816 "a read with 300 writes" could say "an overflowing read during a 300-write burst"; pre-existing text; not taken), and the residual attribution risk above. Converged on 7aebbe2e in one round.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Correction to the proof record above (narrow Codex re-check, session 01a1858a, 2 blocking wording findings; no code or check changes):
1. Read "This is the same phase and the same timing (~1 s) as macOS run 40797703159" as: the same EOF text and about the same duration as macOS run 40797703159. Only the Linux diagnostic names the phase. The macOS failure's phase is unknown.
2. Read "PTY output is FIFO, so the title proves that both bursts were read while detached" as: PTY output is FIFO, so the title proves that both bursts were fully read before the re-attachment. The first burst is partly read while attached, and that read ends the attachment. Its unread tail and the second burst are read while detached.

title: Let Venus show a translucent background on Metal
description:
## Why

macOS CI run 40808735721 (head 6f7eb99; evidence in
/home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-overseer/ci-40808735721/) passes every build, check and test for
the first time, then the GUI scenario's `launch` fails in 3 s and every later scenario step is
skipped (`stop` fails only because the supervisor is already gone). Supervisor log
(`scenario/logs/g1-6b3eafce...-80952.log`):

    Eon Desktop started: pid 80954
    Error: "the GPU surface does not support premultiplied transparency"
    Eon Desktop exited: exit status: 1
    supervisor failed: cannot admit Eon Desktop presentation: Venus closed before native startup admission

Cause (confirmed from source): `surface_alpha_mode` (venus/src/render.rs:2976-2989, called at :999)
requires `CompositeAlphaMode::PreMultiplied` whenever `background_opacity < 1.0`, but wgpu-hal
30.0.0's Metal backend only ever reports `[Opaque, PostMultiplied]`
(wgpu-hal-30.0.0/src/metal/adapter.rs:468-471). Eon's default is `background_opacity = 0.80`
(docs/CONFIGURATION.md:12), so Eon fails to launch with the default config on every Mac, not
just the CI VM. A blocker for Yu's `final` run.

Lead to verify, not assume: wgpu's Metal `PostMultiplied` only does `render_layer.setOpaque(false)`
(wgpu-hal-30.0.0/src/metal/surface.rs:232-233); CoreAnimation composites a CAMetalLayer's contents as
premultiplied regardless, so on Metal `PostMultiplied` may in fact be premultiplied compositing.

## Contract

The Venus contract that owns window transparency / background opacity (find its VEN-C in
venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md) and EON-C configuration of `background_opacity`. Expected: no contract text
change (this makes the documented setting work on macOS). If the fix would change what a contract
promises (for example falling back to opaque on macOS), stop and send the wording to eon-overseer.

## Change

Plan first, with the reference gate (AGENTS.md consequential shape: platform presentation):
read the owning docs/REFERENCES.md routes and at least one comparable wgpu/Metal implementation
(wgpu upstream issues/examples on Metal alpha modes; another wgpu-on-macOS terminal or app with a
translucent window) and record what they do. Then choose the alpha mode per what the surface offers
so a translucent background works on Metal with Venus's colour math still correct (premultiplied
vs straight; check clear_color and the shaders), keep PreMultiplied where offered (Wayland), and
keep the error only where no correct mode exists. Check the macOS window is created transparent
(winit) so non-opaque layer content shows the desktop behind it. Update the unit test at
render.rs:~5800 to cover the Metal mode list.

## Acceptance

- Unit test for the chooser covering `[Opaque, PostMultiplied]` (Metal) and the Wayland lists.
- Venus's AGENTS.md checks: `nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-venus`, `cargo fmt --check`,
  `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and clippy for aarch64-apple-darwin.
- Linux behaviour unchanged (same mode chosen on Wayland; state why).
- Portability disposition recorded.
- The next macOS CI run passes `launch`, and the scenario's captures show a translucent
  background over the desktop (the colour must not be visibly wrong).

## Scope

venus/ only. Read venus/AGENTS.md first. Codex review per AGENTS.md. Approval: Lucca, 2026-10-28,
"diagnose, fix, commit, push" and "handle it. get it done." (overnight, 2026-10-29).

Evidence: /home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-overseer/ci-40842410369/.

comments.author: lucca

title: Give the macOS scenario a known backdrop behind Venus
description:
## Why

macOS CI run 40817193873 (head 97febc7; evidence in
/home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-overseer/ci-40817193873/) is the first where Eon renders on macOS:
`scenario/captures/02-launch.png` shows the tab bar, status widgets, the project picker (fzf) and
the hints bar. Yet `launch` fails and the other 13 scenario steps are skipped:

    Venus's window is blank or differs from the desktop before launch in only 4.6% of it

The runner's desktop is pure black (`01-desktop.png`, pixel (0,0,0)), and Venus's translucent
background over it captures as (1,1,1), so only text and chrome differ. `shown()`
(eon/tools/mac-proof/src/scenario.rs:~400-433) compares the window region with the pre-launch
desktop at `SHOWN = 0.05` (:24) using `near()` with picture.rs's TOLERANCE; no threshold or
tolerance can separate (1,1,1) from (0,0,0). The check is blind on any dark desktop, so Yu's `final`
run (Environment::User) could fail the same way on a dark wallpaper. A black desktop also cannot
show translucency, which kz4p.34's acceptance needs (translucent, correctly coloured background).

## Change

Give the scenario a known, non-black backdrop behind Venus so the "window shown" check and a
translucency observation are deterministic on any Mac, in both environments. Recommended shape
(overseer): the harness shows its own opaque solid-colour backdrop window (objc2, in mac.rs where
the scenario's other AppKit code lives) covering the main display beneath Venus, before the
pre-launch desktop capture, and closes it when the scenario ends (including on failure). Rejected:
changing the desktop wallpaper (persistently changes the user's settings on Yu's Mac); lowering
SHOWN (would let a blank window pass). If the planner finds a simpler deterministic route, record
why on the bead.

With a known backdrop colour B and Venus's background C at opacity 0.8, also check that the window
body is translucent and roughly correctly blended (≈ 0.8·C + 0.2·B per channel, tolerance chosen
from the capture path, Retina/colour-profile aware), and report it as a scenario observation.
That is kz4p.34's native proof (VEN-C11 on Metal); do not edit VEN-C11's proof record here.
If the observation shows wrong blending (for example straight vs premultiplied), report it to
eon-overseer rather than loosening the check.

## Acceptance

- `nix develop -c eon-test -p mac-proof` (or the crate's existing test path), fmt, clippy on Linux
  and aarch64-apple-darwin.
- Unit tests for any new picture logic (blend check) on synthetic pictures.
- The next macOS CI run passes `launch`, its captures show Venus over the backdrop, and the
  translucency observation passes.
- The backdrop leaves nothing behind (leftovers step stays green).

## Scope

eon/tools/mac-proof only. Read the harness's README/docs first. Codex review per AGENTS.md
(gate/validator code: include the scope line). Approval: Lucca, 2026-10-28, "diagnose, fix,
commit, push"; 2026-10-29 overnight, "handle it. get it done."

comments.text:
Plan (Opus planner, 2026-10-29). Implementer: Codex; gates: Opus first, Codex review, Opus final.

Approvals, relayed by eon-overseer: Lucca, 2026-10-27, "do these two too, then ... i want to move closer to the 'yu testing' gate" (the macOS launch path); 2026-10-28, "lets get to working" (fix the macOS CI failures with the Opus-plans/Codex-implements split) and "diagnose, fix, commit, push"; 2026-10-29 overnight, on the fourth run, "ok, going to sleep. handle it. get it done." Push, dispatch, promotion and GitHub posts are not covered by this session.

Contract (smallest observable): in the Private scenario (`run`, `scenario`, and `final`'s automatic part), when Screen Recording is granted, the harness shows an opaque solid backdrop below every normal window on the main display before its pre-launch captures, so `shown()` compares Venus against a known colour; a new `translucency` step measures the backdrop's share through Venus's default background with two backdrop colours and checks it is 1 - background_opacity within 0.05 per channel. No EON-C/VEN-C text or proof record changes; VEN-C11's record stays for kz4p.34.

Approach:
1. Backdrop process. `mac-proof` re-executes itself (std::env::current_exe) with an internal `backdrop R G B` command that only main.rs dispatches (not in USAGE). On macOS, mac.rs `backdrop(rgb)` on the main thread: NSApplication with the Accessory activation policy (no Dock icon, never activated), a borderless, opaque, shadowless NSWindow covering NSScreen::screens()[0] (the main display), sRGB background colour, level CGWindowLevelForKey(DesktopIconWindowLevel) + 1 (above the wallpaper and desktop icons, below every normal window, so below Venus and never in Venus's layer-0 window list), ignores mouse events, collection behaviour CanJoinAllSpaces | Stationary | IgnoresCycle, orderFrontRegardless (no key, no activation: desktop focus kept), prints `shown` on stdout, then runs the app. A thread reading stdin exits the process at EOF, so the window goes with the harness however it ends. Elsewhere `backdrop` errs "macOS only".
2. scenario.rs: a `Backdrop` holding the child (stdin piped, stdout read for `shown` with a 10 s limit, stderr to the step log), killed and reaped on drop. `Scenario` keeps an `Option<Backdrop>`; `clean()` drops it, and so does Scenario's drop, independent of the supervisor condition. `launch`, when Screen Recording is available: show the dark backdrop (32,32,32) and capture `backdrop`, then the light one (224,224,224) and capture `desktop` (the picture `shown()` compares with). Changing colour stops the old process, starts a new one, waits for `shown` and 1 s.
3. Config: the private config.toml also sets `[terminal] background_opacity = OPACITY` (0.8), so the check's expectation is the scenario's own input, not a mirrored default.
4. `translucency` step (needs GUI login + Screen Recording, requires launch, placed right after it, window: true): capture Venus over the light backdrop, switch to the dark one and capture again, switch back to light (also on error) so later `shown()` checks still hold. In picture.rs, pure helpers: the most common colour of a picture and its share, and the per-channel backdrop share (P_light - P_dark)/(B_light - B_dark), with B taken from the pre-launch captures cropped to Venus's window. Unavailable (left for Yu) when either pre-launch crop is not uniform (something else lies behind Venus). Check fails when a dominant colour covers under 25% of the window, the backdrops differ by under 64 in a channel, or a share is off 1 - OPACITY by more than 0.05; the log records P, B, the shares and the implied background C = (P_dark - s*B_dark)/(1 - s). A failed blend is reported to eon-overseer, not loosened.
5. Docs: `scenario --help` step text and Evidence paragraph; docs/DEVELOPMENT.md's macOS harness paragraph (one or two sentences).

Dependency note (AP-DEPENDENCY-001): no new crate. objc2-app-kit 0.3.2 and objc2-core-graphics 0.3.2 gain features (NSApplication, NSResponder, NSWindow, NSColor, NSScreen, NSGraphics; CGWindowLevel), and objc2-foundation =0.3.2 (already locked under objc2-app-kit) may become a direct dependency for MainThreadMarker/NSArray. Comparable: winit 0.30.13's macOS window setup (cargo registry) for objc2 0.6 NSWindow creation; kept: main-thread AppKit, borderless window; rejected for the harness: an in-process window (the scenario's waits never run the AppKit run loop), changing the wallpaper (changes Yu's settings), lowering SHOWN (passes a blank window), osascript/JXA (a new checked-in language).

Red check: picture.rs unit tests on synthetic pictures: dominant colour and share; backdrop share accepts 0.2 and rejects an opaque window (0) and a linear-light blend (~0.48). The CI failure itself (a (1,1,1) window over a (0,0,0) desktop) is the native red; the next macOS CI run is the native green. Linux proves only compilation and the pure logic.

Scope: eon/tools/mac-proof, Cargo.lock if features change it, docs/DEVELOPMENT.md. Not Venus, not the manual (User) part of `final`, not VEN-C11's proof record, no push or dispatch.

Checks: nix develop -c eon-test -p mac-proof; cargo fmt --check; cargo clippy --locked -p mac-proof --all-targets -- -D warnings on Linux; rustup run stable cargo clippy --locked --target aarch64-apple-darwin -p mac-proof --all-targets -- -D warnings (kz4p.1 recipe). Portability: Darwin-isolated (mac.rs native module); Linux stubs.

Diagnosis (step 1): Eon does not honour a lone OSC 11, on any platform; this is case 2.
- Evidence, code at the pinned revisions: Orbit sets libghostty's default palette only
  (orbit/src/pty.rs:200-206, from `--ansi-palette-v1`) and never `set_default_fg_color` or
  `set_default_bg_color`. libghostty (ghostty 521cf2c5, src/terminal/stream_terminal.zig:2104-2106)
  stores OSC 10/11 as overrides, but its render state (src/terminal/render.zig:1052-1066) copies
  background and foreground only when both `get()` are non-null; otherwise it keeps its initial
  (0,0,0) background and (255,255,255) foreground (render.zig:380-382). With no default foreground,
  an OSC 11 alone never reaches `snapshot.colors()` (orbit/src/frame.rs:302, :457), so Venus's
  default-background fill (venus/src/scene.rs:3560, render.rs:1557) stays black. OSC 111 then has
  nothing to restore. The same gap leaves an OSC 11 query unanswered (Terminal.zig:189-194 returns
  null with nothing set), so programs that ask for the background to choose light or dark get no
  reply.
- Evidence, CI run 40828543315: fd 3 is the driver's PTY (DRIVER's `exec 3>&1`; kitty's image
  went the same way), the OSC 11 command ran (`steps/78-translucency.log:542`), and the implied
  background stayed about 0.6 of 255.
- Inference: an OSC 10 sent with the OSC 11 would make libghostty apply both today. That is an
  accident of libghostty's render state, not Eon behaviour, so the scenario does not use it.
- No cheap Linux observation exists without a new Orbit test; the code path is
  platform-neutral, so Linux behaves the same. Reported to eon-overseer to file the product gap.

Share 0.172 against 0.2 (inference): colour management on the capture path, not wrong blending.
With a black window colour, straight and premultiplied alpha give the same result, and
linear-light compositing would give about 107 over 224, not 39. A transfer-curve mismatch between
the window and capture colour spaces (a power of about 1.09, close to 2.4/2.2) fits both backdrops:
0.2^1.086 * 224 = 39 and 0.2^1.086 * 32 = 5.6 (observed 6). It stays within the 0.05 share
tolerance.

title: Find and fix the macOS orbit-selection check failure
description:
## Why

macOS CI run 40828543315 (head c03ca4b; evidence in
/home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-overseer/ci-40828543315/, `steps/*-check-orbit-selection.log`)
fails check:orbit-selection after 0.08 s:

    panicked at orbit/tests/real_pty/selection.rs:208:5: assertion failed: !selected(&last)

The test's last phase (selection.rs:~186-208) expects the child's exit to clear a presented
selection, so the last Frame before Exited shows none. The check passed in runs 2-5 (heads 32c3dff
through 97febc7); no Orbit source changed since run 5 (only eon/tools/mac-proof). So likely an
intermittent race: either the test reads a frame order Orbit does not promise, or Orbit can send
Exited before the selection-clearing frame (an ordering bug under ORB contracts).

## Change

Find which: read Orbit's exit path (child exit -> selection clear -> final frame -> Exited) and the
contract that promises the clear. Try a Linux repro (`nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.orbit-selection
--rebuild` in a loop, and under CPU load), as kz4p.33 did for clipboard. Fix the owner: Orbit if
the promised order can break, else the test. If no repro and no cause, add a test-only diagnostic
naming the frames received after the gate, and say so on the bead.

## Contract

The ORB contract covering selection and exit (find it in orbit/docs/CONTRACTS.md). No text change;
if one seems needed, stop and send the wording to eon-overseer.

## Acceptance

- Orbit's AGENTS.md checks for the changed crate (`nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-orbit`, the
  orbit-selection Nix check repeated, fmt, clippy Linux and aarch64-apple-darwin).
- Portability disposition recorded.
- The next macOS CI run passes check:orbit-selection.

## Scope

orbit/ only. Read orbit/AGENTS.md first. Codex review per AGENTS.md. Approval: Lucca, 2026-10-28,
"diagnose, fix, commit, push"; 2026-10-29 overnight, "handle it. get it done."
close_reason: Native macOS proof: mac-proof.yml run 40842410369 (head 0b6ef93, tree d679722, aarch64-macos, macos-15 runner): 89 of 90 steps pass, including every build, check and test step and every GUI scenario step (launch, translucency, picker ... stop) and leftovers; only retina is skipped (no HiDPI display on the runner; left for Yu by design). Evidence: /home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-overseer/ci-40842410369/.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Plan (Opus, 2026-10-29, at 08e8873). Approvals relayed by eon-overseer: Lucca 2026-10-27 "do these
two too, then ... i want to move closer to the 'yu testing' gate" (macOS launch path); 2026-10-28
"lets get to working" (fix the macOS CI failures with the Opus-plans/Codex-implements split) and
"diagnose, fix, commit, push"; 2026-10-29 overnight "ok, going to sleep. handle it. get it done."
Not covered: push, promotion, workflow dispatch, posts, Lucca's running Eon.

## Cause (from source; no repro yet)

The child's exit reaches Bend by one of two orders:
- reap first: host.rs `wake` -> `drain_exited` -> `ChildExited{drained}` -> session.bend `exited`
  -> `exit_cleared`, which with a presented selection decides `Unselect{True}` + `output` (a frame
  with no selection) before the stop, then Exited;
- PTY first: the slave closes at exit before the zombie is reapable, `read_into` sees EIO,
  host.rs `pty_closed` finds no reap -> `PtyClosed` -> session.bend `ended`, which decides only
  `Unselect{presented}`. Unselect clears libghostty (host.rs:1377) but publishes nothing; the later
  `ChildExited{drained: False}` sees presented = False, so no frame follows and Exited arrives
  after the last frame that still shows the selection.

The failure at selection.rs:208 is the second order (wider window on macOS; tiny on Linux).
docs/BEHAVIOR.md already limits its claim to "when the host reaps the child while the PTY is
open". ORB-C9 says client loss or exit clears the selection; the PTY-first order leaves the client
presenting a cleared selection. Owner: Orbit's Bend policy, not the test.

## Fix

- orbit/src/session.bend `ended` (PtyClosed): when a selection was presented, publish the clear as
  `exit_cleared` does without drained output: `Unselect{True}` then `output(flags, ...)` with the
  route Idle and presented False; otherwise unchanged (`Unselect{False}`, no frame). `step` passes
  flags. Comment updated.
- Laws unchanged: LAWS.bend's PtyClosed lifecycle law is `quiet` (no lifecycle moves) and the view
  law takes a Framed act in Plain pace. Regenerate proof/ lemmas with tools/step-proof.rs if the
  step shape needs it; orbit-laws must print ALL PROOFS CHECK. If a law would have to change, stop.
- Test (red check): orbit/tests/real_pty/selection.rs keeps its first server (usually reap first,
  now passes either way) and adds a second run of the same selection-shell.sh in a close mode
  (env var): print text, host-select it, gate, close fds 0-2 (as tests/pty-reopen-shell.sh does),
  gate, exit 3. The test releases the first gate, requires a frame with no selection while the
  child still lives (deterministic PTY-first order), then releases the second gate and expects
  Exited 3 with no selected frame between. Red at the base: no frame arrives (receive timeout).
- docs/BEHAVIOR.md: drop the reap-while-open limit; describe both runs. ORB-C9 text unchanged.

Scope: orbit/ only (session.bend, proof/ if regenerated, tests/real_pty/selection.rs,
tests/selection-shell.sh, docs/BEHAVIOR.md). No host.rs, protocol, or nix change expected.
Portability: neutral (Bend policy and test; fd close is POSIX).

Checks: `nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-orbit`; orbit-selection Nix check repeated (--rebuild
loop); orbit-laws; orbit-boundary unchanged; cargo fmt --check; clippy -D warnings on Linux and
aarch64-apple-darwin (kz4p.1 recipe). Red/green: the close-mode run fails with 08e8873's
session.bend and passes after.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Final shape and proof (Opus gate, 2026-10-29). Supersedes the plan comment where they differ.

## Cause (corrected)

`PtyClosed` arises only when a PTY master read returns 0 (end of file) before the child is
reapable. EIO never produces it: orbit/src/pty.rs `read_into` closes on EIO only after a
successful reap, which then takes the `ChildExited` path. On macOS the session's controlling
terminal keeps the slave open while the child lives (so orbit-pty-reopen passes there, CI run
40828543315 step 44); when the session leader exits and releases it, the master reads 0 while the
child is not yet reapable. session.bend `ended` then decided `Unselect` without publishing, and
the later `ChildExited{drained: False}` saw nothing presented, so `Exited` followed a frame that
still showed the selection: the CI failure at selection.rs:208. The macOS kernel mechanism is
inference from the source paths and that CI evidence, not a native observation.

## Change

- orbit/src/session.bend: `ended(flags, session)` (PtyClosed) decides `Unselect{True}` and
  `republished` when a selection is presented (route Idle, presented False, copy kept); otherwise
  exactly the base decisions. `republished`, not `output`: `output` can deliver clipboard writes
  and detach on overflow, which `lifecycle_follows_its_contracts` forbids for PtyClosed (Codex
  stopped on it, round 1). The base helper is kept as `end_sequence` for the anchor-lost tick,
  whose decisions are unchanged.
- orbit/proof/{step,view,lease}.bend: `fits_pty_closed` case splits regenerated with
  tools/step-proof.rs; no lemma statement, law, or other definition changes (checked by diff and by
  the Codex review).
- orbit/tests/real_pty/selection.rs: the last phase's assertion names the frames received after
  the exit gate (revision, selected), so a future macOS failure shows what arrived.
- orbit/docs/BEHAVIOR.md: the clear is published in either order; no real-PTY check forces the
  end-of-file order. The reap-first sensitivity claim is kept.
- Dropped from the plan: the close-mode second run. Closing fds 0-2 reaches `PtyClosed` on
  neither platform (Linux: EIO waits for the reap; macOS: the controlling terminal holds the slave).

Portability: neutral (Bend policy, test diagnostic, docs). Contract: ORB-C9 text unchanged; laws
unchanged. No CHANGELOG entry: no wire, protocol, or contract change, and the visible effect is on
unsupported macOS.

## Accepted gap

No deterministic regression check: the end-of-file-before-reap order cannot be forced by a child
from bash on either platform, and the unchanged laws permit a clear without a frame. Red evidence
is macOS CI run 40828543315 (head c03ca4b, steps/50-check-orbit-selection.log). Green is
probabilistic: the next macOS CI runs of check:orbit-selection. A law requiring a published clear
before `Exited` would make it a policy check; that is a law change, put to Lucca via eon-overseer.

## Proof (tree bb5fed43d24144f6d1c7fcbe17863463fdda58fb on base 08e8873, x86_64 Linux, Opus run)

- `nix build --no-link -L --keep-going` orbit-laws, orbit-boundary, orbit-selection,

  orbit-detached-exit: all pass; orbit-laws log `ALL PROOFS CHECK`.
- orbit-selection `--rebuild` x5: pass.
- `nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-orbit`: 54 unit + 18 lifecycle pass (50 real-PTY ignored,
  run through the Nix checks above).
- `cargo fmt --check -p yazelix-orbit`; `cargo clippy --locked -p yazelix-orbit --all-targets --
  -D warnings`: pass.
- `cargo clippy --locked --target aarch64-apple-darwin -p yazelix-orbit --all-targets -- -D
  warnings` (kz4p.1 recipe, rustup stable 1.96.0): pass. Compilation only; no macOS runtime claim.

Ledger: Codex implementation 1 run + 3 resumes (round 1 law stop: `output` detaches on clipboard
overflow; round 2 scope stop: close-mode run cannot reach PtyClosed; round 3 docs). Opus first
gate: 1 finding (BEHAVIOR.md dropped the reap-first sensitivity claim), fixed. Codex review

title: Fix Eon Runtime's remaining Linux-only session assumptions for macOS
description:
## Why

Beyond peer identity, Eon Runtime assumes a Linux session in a few places that would make the
first macOS launch noisy or broken: no `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` (a warning on every launch and a long
`$TMPDIR` root), macOS's shorter Unix socket path limit, and a first-detach notification that is
a silent no-op. Fixing these on Linux before the Mac run saves rental time.

Lucca (2026-10-27, relayed by eon-overseer): "i'd rather test everything possible and fix myself,
letting to Yu only final testing and final fixes that i missed ... so the more automated, the
better."

## Evidence

- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/supervisor.rs:681-692` `base_runtime_directory`:
  `EON_RUNTIME_DIR`, else `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/<product>`, else a warning and
  `env::temp_dir()/<product>-<uid>`. On macOS `env::temp_dir()` is the per-user
  `/var/folders/xx/<hash>/T/`, about 50 bytes before Eon's own path segments.
- macOS `sockaddr_un.sun_path` is 104 bytes (Linux 108). Runtime paths:
  `root/generations/<generation>/...` (`runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/generation.rs:55-57`)
  plus Orbit endpoint names. Memory `isolated-eon-capture-recipe` already needs a "short root" on
  Linux, so headroom is thin.
- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/notification.rs:10,44-51`: Linux zbus notification; other
  platforms do nothing.
- The mapping bead's sweep list (sibling, first child) may add items; take the ones it assigns here.

## Scope

In scope: choose the macOS runtime root (recommended: `$TMPDIR` is already per-user and private,
so use it without the warning on macOS, keeping `EON_RUNTIME_DIR` first); compute the longest
socket path Eon and Orbit create for a realistic macOS root and either show it fits 104 bytes
with margin or shorten the root (e.g. a short per-user directory) with a bounded, explicit error
when a path would not fit; make the notification gap explicit (recorded as a README macOS gap,
no new mechanism); the sweep's other Runtime items.

Out of scope: a native macOS notification mechanism (needs a decision; propose it as a follow-up
only if Lucca asks), Orbit's socket code unless the length check shows Orbit must change (then
stop), Venus.

## Acceptance

- The worst-case socket path for a macOS-style root is computed in a deterministic test or
  recorded calculation, and fits 104 bytes or fails with a clear message before bind.
- No `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` warning on macOS; Linux behavior and messages unchanged.
- The notification gap text is recorded on the friends'-gate bead for README.
- The changes compile for the Apple target (gate check) and pass Linux suites.

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime` exits 0; `cargo fmt --check`, clippy.
- `cargo check --locked --target aarch64-apple-darwin -p eon-runtime` has no new error.
- Native confirmation in the harness: full Eon launches with default environment (no
  `EON_RUNTIME_DIR`) on the Mac and logs no runtime-root warning.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if the runtime root rule is user-visible enough to need CONFIGURATION.md or contract text
  (ask Lucca with a recommendation).
- Stop if Orbit's endpoint naming must change (ORB contract owner).
- Stop on any platform blocker.
close_reason: macOS runtime root /tmp/<product>-<uid> without warning; platform socket-path bound in windows.rs and start_orbit; bounds for all roots recorded; notification gap on kz4p.14. Compile-checked for aarch64-apple-darwin; native confirmation stays with kz4p.12.

Include both in this bead's worst case. supervisor.rs:652-658 configuration_directory (XDG_CONFIG_HOME or ~/.config/eon) is the same record-or-accept case as diagnostics.rs. The Darwin nix-build of eonPackage runs Runtime tests under the build TMPDIR (flake.nix:679-686 keeps /dev/shm Linux-only), so the root choice also matters there.

Minor: diagnostics.rs:168-175 uses XDG_STATE_HOME/~/.local/state (portable; record or accept). eon/crates/eon/tests/workspace_control.rs:66 roots tests at env::temp_dir(), which hits the same 104-byte bound on macOS (kz4p.5 consumes the result).

comments.text:
Scope addition. Lucca, 2026-10-27, to eon-overseer: "agree to all that". That answered eon-mac-launch-kz4p.1's question 4 with its recommendation: no new bead for the socket roots of the Darwin test runs (macOS sun_path is 104 bytes). Instead:
- kz4p.4 computes the bound for all roots, product and test, including the first window's `<base>/generations/g1-<32hex>/session-N.sock.management` path, which windows.rs:113-119 does not guard.

Evidence: kz4p.1's amendments (workspace_control.rs:66 roots at env::temp_dir(); :3788 notes the length).

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Approval: Lucca, 2026-10-27, to eon-overseer (relayed by eon-overseer): "do these two too, then ... i want to move closer to the 'yu testing' gate". This starts the bead.

Reference gate (AP-REFERENCE-001). The change touches the runtime root's trust boundary on macOS.

Behavior and owners: Runtime owns its runtime root (supervisor.rs base_runtime_directory) and checks each terminal socket path before Orbit binds it. Orbit owns binding, unchanged. The platform module (runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/platform.rs) owns the platform facts: the sun_path length and the fallback root without XDG_RUNTIME_DIR.

References read:
- tmux 3.8 at 7f2a35a (~/pjs/refs/tmux-3.8), tmux.c:217-243 and server.c:114-120. tmux ignores $TMPDIR and uses $TMUX_TMPDIR or /tmp, with base /tmp/tmux-<uid>. It refuses a base it does not own or one that others can access, and it checks sizeof(sun_path) before bind (ENAMETOOLONG).
- Orbit's own standalone default: orbit/src/cli.rs:138-160, /tmp/yazelix-orbit-UID with an owner and mode check.

Kept:
- EON_RUNTIME_DIR first, then XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/<product>.
- prepare_runtime's owned-0700 validation (symlink_metadata, so no symlink is followed).

Measured socket paths (Explore survey of f495068):
- The longest Orbit path is <root>/w/<8hex>/generations/g1-<32hex>/session-N.sock.management, 83+d bytes relative to the base root, where d is the number of digits in N.
- N is a counter that only goes up. It is refused only at usize::MAX, and MAX_SESSIONS=256 caps live terminals, not N.

Rejected:
- (a) $TMPDIR on macOS, the bead's first recommendation. /var/folders/xx/<28>/T/ is about 49 bytes, and 49+1+87 > 103, so a window's sockets cannot fit.
- (b) A fixed bound on the main root that assumes N<=9999. It would refuse Linux roots of 30 bytes or more that work today, for example a /dev/shm/ec-<pid>-<n>/runtime test root, so Linux would change.

Decision:
- macOS fallback root: /tmp/<product>-<uid>, with no warning. Linux keeps its warning and env::temp_dir(), unchanged.
- One platform-derived bound: sun_path length from libc::sockaddr_un, minus its NUL. It is used in the windows.rs check, which until now hardcoded 108, and in start_orbit on each terminal's exact .management path before Orbit runs. A too-long path then fails with a clear message that names EON_RUNTIME_DIR, instead of "terminal exited before publishing Ready". On Linux this changes only the error text of launches that already fail.
- Check: a platform test that binds paths at the bound and one byte past it, so a wrong constant fails on the platform the test runs on.

No dependency, no contract text. CONFIGURATION.md:361-364 already says "private per-user fallbacks".

title: Port the Runtime and Eon tests' process reads to macOS
description:
## Why

Lucca wants every possible check automated before Yu sees the Mac build. Today the Runtime and Eon
suites cannot run on macOS: their tests read `/proc` directly, and `eon-test` (the only supported
route, AGENTS.md "Testing Discipline") needs bubblewrap, which macOS lacks. Without this, the Mac
run proves only Orbit and Venus. This bead ports the tests' process reads; the sibling "Give
eon-test a macOS branch" gives `eon-test` its macOS isolation.

Lucca (2026-10-27, relayed by eon-overseer): "i'd rather test everything possible and fix myself,
letting to Yu only final testing and final fixes that i missed ... so the more automated, the
better."

## Evidence

- `nix/test-sandbox.nix:1-50`: `eon-test` refuses to run without `bwrap --unshare-all`; it hides
  live Wayland, D-Bus and Eon sockets and gives private PID/network.
- Test `/proc` reads: `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/sessions.rs:1676,1819,1938`;
  `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/supervisor.rs:2156-2161` (worker via `/proc/<pid>/task/*/children`
  and `cmdline`), `:2290`; about 25 sites in `eon/crates/eon/tests/workspace_control.rs` (`stat`,
  `environ`, `cmdline`, process existence), e.g. `:657,1013,1758,3026,4160,5491`.
- Precedent: Orbit's real-PTY checks use `lsof` on macOS where Linux reads `/proc`
  (`orbit/docs/CONTRACTS.md:831-832`); `orbit/tests/lifecycle.rs` keeps 3 tests Linux-only.

## Scope

In scope:
- A small test-only process helper (alive, start identity, environ, cmdline, children) with Linux
  `/proc` and macOS implementations (`proc_pidinfo`, `proc_listchildpids`, `sysctl
  KERN_PROCARGS2`), used by the Runtime and Eon tests in place of raw `/proc` reads; tests whose
  property is Linux-only stay `#[cfg(target_os = "linux")]` with the reason in a comment.

Out of scope: product code (Runtime port bead owns `sessions.rs` outside its test module), Orbit's
and Venus's own tests, CI, and the macOS branch of `eon-test` in `nix/test-sandbox.nix` (split out
on 2026-10-27 to its own sibling bead, "Give eon-test a macOS branch", for size).

## Acceptance

- `nix develop -c eon-test` on Linux runs the same tests as before (count unchanged except tests
  this bead deliberately splits; list any).
- The Runtime and Eon test targets compile for `aarch64-apple-darwin` (gate check with
  `--all-targets`).
- Native pass/fail is the harness's job; this bead does not claim it.

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test` exits 0 on Linux.
- `cargo check --locked --target aarch64-apple-darwin --all-targets -p eon-runtime -p eon` has no
  test-code error.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if a macOS reader needs a crate beyond `libc` (dependency gate): ask Lucca.
- Stop if a test can only be ported by weakening what it checks; keep it Linux-only and list it.
- Codex review per AGENTS.md (test code change).
close_reason: Runtime and Eon tests read processes through Linux /proc or macOS libproc/KERN_PROCARGS2 test readers (Runtime via platform::process); window test root shortened; Linux suites unchanged (130+1 ignored, 49); compile- and lint-checked for aarch64-apple-darwin; native run stays with kz4p.8/kz4p.12.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Correction to the proof record (narrow Codex re-check). The code is unchanged.

"h is 1-2 hex digits" holds only while one of ew0 to ewff is free in T. The loop searches 0_u32.., so stale ew<n> directories left by failed runs can push h higher, up to 8 digits. Each failed run leaves at most one, and the test removes its root on success.

So both macOS conditions remain for the harness roots:
- len(T) + h <= 10, the windows.rs reserve for this test;

Example: with T=/tmp/eon (8 bytes) and ew0 to ewff all taken, ew100 gives a 104-byte reserve path, over macOS's 103.

title: Admit aarch64-darwin in Eon's one component manifest
description:
## Why

EON-C7 requires that Linux and `aarch64-darwin` consume the same component graph, with target
artifacts varying explicitly. Today the one manifest names a single target, the validator rejects
any component whose target differs, the flake asserts `manifest.product.target == system`, and
`eon versions` would print `x86_64-linux` on a Mac. A Darwin flake output cannot exist until the
manifest admits a second target.

Lucca (2026-10-27, relayed by eon-overseer): "i'd rather test everything possible and fix myself,
letting to Yu only final testing and final fixes that i missed ... so the more automated, the
better." On launching: "it would be nice to launch with mac support".

## Evidence

- `components/eon-v4.json:5` `"product": {"target": "x86_64-linux"}`; every component repeats
  `"target": "x86_64-linux"` (`:60,76,110,...`).
- `eon/crates/eon-manifest/src/lib.rs:19-22` `Product { id, target }`; `:165` target token;
  `:180-181` "component target differs from product target"; `:121-136` `version_report` prints
  the product and component targets.
- `eon/crates/eon/src/product.rs:8-11` embeds the manifest for `eon versions`.
- `flake.nix:66,652,943` read the manifest; `:652` asserts the single target.
- Contracts: EON-C2 (`docs/CONTRACTS.md:154-180`, "channel-specific graph drift fail
  validation"), EON-C6 (`:285`), EON-C7 (`:314`, "Both consume the same component graph").

## Scope

In scope: the smallest manifest shape where one graph lists its supported targets (for example
`product.targets: ["x86_64-linux", "aarch64-darwin"]` and per-component `targets`, schema 4 -> 5,
file renamed only if the schema rule requires it), validator rules and tests, `eon versions`
reporting the running build's target, flake readers updated so `x86_64-linux` evaluation is
unchanged. A component unavailable on a target (if the flake bead finds one, e.g. CodexBar) is
stated in the graph, not hidden.

Out of scope: building Darwin outputs (flake bead), Runtime behavior, any channel or
distribution change.

## Reference gate (consequential: manifest format)

Before code, record on this bead: user-visible behavior (`eon versions` target line); the one
owner (manifest + validator); `docs/REFERENCES.md` routes read; at least one comparable
multi-target manifest (e.g. Nix flake `systems`, Cargo target tables) with revision, kept
constraints, rejected shapes (a second manifest per platform: rejected by EON-C7; a
platform-keyed copy of the graph: rejected as drift).

## Acceptance

- One manifest validates for both targets; a component listing an unknown or unsupported target,
  or a product target missing from a required component, fails validation with a named error.
- `canonical_manifest_is_valid`, `invalid_graphs_are_rejected` and the version report test cover
  the new rule (extend, do not duplicate).
- `nix eval .#packages.x86_64-linux.default.drvPath` changes only because the manifest file
  changed (record before/after and the reason), and the Linux packages build.

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-manifest -p eon` exits 0.
- `nix build .#packages.x86_64-linux.default .#packages.x86_64-linux.eonbase` succeeds.
- Codex review per AGENTS.md (manifest is a "Shared ... component manifest" route: full affected
  Rust and Nix surfaces).

## Stop Conditions

- Stop for Lucca's approval if EON-C2/EON-C6/EON-C7 text must change (it may not: their wording
  already speaks of one graph for every channel).
- Stop if the shape needs a second graph or platform-specific policy.
close_reason: Schema 5 graph components/eon-v5.json lists x86_64-linux and aarch64-darwin per product and component; validator, tests, eon versions (build target) and flake readers follow; Linux report byte-identical; proof and review ledger on the bead.
