comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Approval (relayed by eon-overseer, 2026-10-27): Lucca to eon-overseer: "do these two too, then ... i want to move closer to the 'yu testing' gate". Covers implementing this bead as scoped; contract text, push, promotion and site/GitHub posts are not covered.

Reference gate (consequential: manifest format), recorded before code at f495068.

Question: what is the smallest shape in which Eon's one component graph lists x86_64-linux and aarch64-darwin, with per-target availability explicit?
Contract: EON-C2 (one graph, "channel-specific graph drift fail validation"), EON-C6, EON-C7 ("Both consume the same component graph"; "a second component graph ... is rejected"). Their text needs no change: the shape keeps one graph.
User-visible behavior: `eon versions` prints `eon <build target>` and one `<id> <version> <revision|workspace> <build target>` line per component available on that target. On x86_64 Linux every component lists x86_64-linux, so the report is byte-identical to today's, and supervisors comparing component reports (supervisor.rs:336) see no graph change.
Owner: `components/eon-v5.json` (graph) and `eon/crates/eon-manifest` (validator, target vocabulary, build-target mapping, version report). The flake only reads: it asserts its `system` is a product target and that each component it composes lists `system`.
Routes read: docs/REFERENCES.md "Runtime package composition" (keep one root Cargo.lock and one component graph; reject a second graph); docs/DISTRIBUTION.md#reference-routing (no route active: distribution graduation is not; dist's `targets` not read); docs/ARCHITECTURE.md "Component graph" owner; docs/CONTRACTS.md EON-C2/C6/C7.
Sources and revisions:
- nixpkgs 567a49d1913ce81ac6e9582e3553dd90a955875f (Eon's pin): `lib/meta.nix` `availableOn` (`meta.platforms` / `meta.badPlatforms`), `doc/stdenv/meta.chapter.md` `meta.platforms`. Per-package list of supported system doubles, checked against the target.
- Nix flakes' per-`system` outputs (flake.nix `packages.${system}`): one product-level system set.
- Cargo 1.95 platform-specific dependencies (`[target.'cfg(..)'.dependencies]`): availability keyed by platform.
Constraints kept: the Nix system-double vocabulary Eon already uses (`x86_64-linux`, `aarch64-darwin`); one product-level target list plus a per-component list (nixpkgs' `meta.platforms` shape); no store paths; exact pins unchanged.
Options compared and rejected:
- A second manifest per platform: rejected by EON-C7 (second graph).
- A platform-keyed copy of the graph (`{"x86_64-linux": {components...}, ...}`) or Cargo-style per-target tables of components: rejected as drift; identities and pins would repeat per target.
- nixpkgs' `badPlatforms` negative list and "absent `platforms` means all": rejected; two lists split one fact, and an implicit default hides a component's unavailability. Each component states `targets` explicitly, so a new product target forces a review of every component.
- Reporting every product target in `eon versions`: rejected; the report identifies the running build, and a Mac build would then claim Linux identity.
Decision: schema 4 -> 5. `product.targets` (non-empty, unique, each one of Eon's approved targets: x86_64-linux, aarch64-darwin) replaces `product.target`; each component's `targets` (non-empty, unique, each a product target) replaces `target`. Services, clients and libraries list every product target; a tool may omit one (stated in the graph). A requirement's component lists every target of the component requiring it. The file is renamed `components/eon-v5.json`: 4a8ead7 named the file for the graph version ("Graph version 4, components/eon-v4.json"), and a v4 name over schema 5 would be a wrong claim; path consumers follow (flake, product.rs, tests, demo/record.rs, docs). The canonical graph lists both targets on every component; the flake bead (kz4p.7) narrows a tool it cannot build for aarch64-darwin.
Named failures: "product has no targets", "duplicate product target", "unsupported product target", "component has no targets", "duplicate component target", "component target is not a product target", "<role> lacks a product target" (service/client/library), "required component lacks a requiring component's target", "unsupported build target" (version report on a build outside the approved set).
Cheapest proof: eon-manifest tests (`canonical_manifest_is_valid`, `invalid_graphs_are_rejected`, the version report test, extended); `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-manifest -p eon`; Linux drvPaths before/after with the reason; `nix build` of default and eonbase.
Linux drvPaths at f495068 (before): default /nix/store/ra81359p7zs6mmlv45kxjvssa2267jr2-eon-0.1.6.drv, eonbase /nix/store/9jb79c1079kxy1f5ig4cyiyda1xwyyns-eonbase-0.1.6.drv. Expected change: Eon's, Orbit's and Venus's derivations take `workspaceSource`/`crateSource`, which include components/, eon/ and flake.nix, so editing any of them changes those derivations; every other derivation must stay identical.
Exit condition: the shape is replaced only if a third target or a per-target artifact difference needs more than a target list; that is new scope.

Review ledger: 1 round on d8add46. The fresh Claude reviewer (who also ran the checks; tree unchanged after them) and Codex gpt-6.1-sol xhigh (1 pass) found nothing blocking, so the loop converged on that tree.

Nits left as they are (nits do not block, and fixing any of them reopens the loop and forces another Orbit/Venus/Eon rebuild):
1. The version report test accepts either target's report for `version_report`, so a wrong ARCH/OS mapping would pass it. The mapping is the two-row `TARGETS` table.
2. The comment "only a tool may be unavailable on one of its targets" means the product's targets.
3. The service/client/library rule compares lengths, which relies on the preceding unique-and-product-target checks.
4. Activation entries do not themselves require every product target. Today they name only orbit, venus and eon-workspace-protocol, which the role rule already forces onto every target.
5. The flake's `component` throw covers both a missing/duplicate component and one that does not list `system`.
6. No test feeds a schema-4 graph (gap predates this change; `deny_unknown_fields` rejects `target`).
Recorded behavior: on a build outside the approved targets (e.g. aarch64-linux), `version_report` returns "unsupported build target" and generation start fails there (generation.rs:32). title: Add aarch64-darwin packages, checks and dev shell to the flake
description:
## Why

The proof harness, Yu and his friends all install through Nix (Nix-only is the approved channel).
The flake has outputs only for `x86_64-linux`. Agents cannot build Darwin on Linux, but they can
write and evaluate the Darwin outputs here, so the first Mac run builds instead of debugging Nix.

Lucca (2026-10-27, relayed by eon-overseer): "i'd rather test everything possible and fix myself,
letting to Yu only final testing and final fixes that i missed ... so the more automated, the
better."

## Evidence

- `flake.nix:62` `system = "x86_64-linux"`; outputs `packages`, `apps`, `checks`, `devShells`
  keyed by it (`:936-988`).
- Linux-only pieces: `:320-327` X11/Wayland/xkb libraries in `venusRuntimeLibraries`, `:348`
  `XDG_DATA_DIRS` with Mesa, `:329-345` fontconfig file (Venus loads fonts with `fontdb`,
  `venus/src/render/fonts.rs:323`), `:202` CodexBar `linux-musl-x86_64` asset, `:875` kinestra
  recorder (kinestra exports only `x86_64-linux`), `:888-919` bundle relink and `:938-945`
  installer/manual bundle (Linux bundle; out of the Nix-only Mac scope), `:919-934` br/bv Linux
  assets, `:652` single-target assert (manifest bead).
- Checked 2026-10-27 by `nix eval` from Linux: `nixpkgs-zig` `zig_0_17` and nixpkgs `bun` are
  available on `aarch64-darwin`; the `helix` and `anima` inputs export `aarch64-darwin`.
- Previous native Mac runs used Zig 0.15.2 with a macOS 15.4 SDK `xcrun` wrapper because Zig 0.15
  could not link against the macOS 26 SDK (`eon-orb-c14-mac-reproof-l8rz`, `eon-z4n6`;
  `orbit/docs/CONTRACTS.md:820-821`). Under Nix, the SDK comes from nixpkgs' Darwin stdenv
  (`apple-sdk`), so the wrapper should not be needed; unproved until a native build.
- `orbit/build.rs:35-49` builds the Bend worker with `bun` and `BEND_CLANG`; `-z noexecstack` is
  already Linux-only.

## Scope

In scope: `flake.nix` (and `nix/*.nix` it calls) gain `aarch64-darwin` `packages.default`,
`packages.eonbase`, `apps.default`, `checks` (the Orbit checks and package build), and
`devShells.default`, from the same manifest and the same package expressions with platform inputs
narrowed: no Mesa, X11, Wayland or fontconfig on Darwin unless a native need is shown; Zig 0.17
and nixpkgs' Apple SDK; Bun and clang for Bend; CodexBar's macOS asset if its release has one,
else the gap is stated in the manifest; br/bv only where a Darwin release asset exists (else
omitted from the Darwin dev shell, noted); recorder, relink, installer and manual bundle stay
Linux-only.

Out of scope: building on a Mac (harness), Cachix publishing (CI decision), Rust changes,
direct macOS bundles (`eon-hzq`).

## Acceptance

- `nix flake show --all-systems` lists the Darwin outputs without evaluation errors.
- `nix eval --raw .#packages.aarch64-darwin.default.drvPath`,
  `.#devShells.aarch64-darwin.default.drvPath` and each Darwin check's `drvPath` evaluate on Linux.
- `x86_64-linux` `drvPath`s for `packages.default`, `packages.eonbase` and `devShells.default` are
  identical before and after (record both), unless the manifest bead already changed them.
- Each omitted Linux-only output and each unavailable Darwin tool is listed on this bead and
  handed to the friends'-gate bead for README.

## Verification

- The three evaluation commands above exit 0; `nix flake check --no-build` for
  `x86_64-linux` exits 0.
- Codex review per AGENTS.md (Nix change). No native build claim.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop before adding a flake input (e.g. a Darwin-capable recorder, rust-overlay) or fetching a
  new binary asset whose license or provenance is unrecorded (dependency gate).
- Stop if Darwin needs a second component graph or a platform branch of the package expressions
  beyond narrowed inputs.
- Stop if `nixpkgs` at the pinned revision cannot evaluate the Darwin stdenv for a needed package;
  record which and ask Lucca whether to bump.
close_reason: Darwin outputs evaluate from Linux; x86_64-linux build of all 63 attributes green; native proof is kz4p.8's

Question: how should the flake give aarch64-darwin the same packages, checks and dev shell from the one manifest without a second graph or a Darwin branch of the package expressions?

comments.text:
Implementation decisions (flake.nix, nix/orbit-checks.nix; no Rust, no manifest change, no new flake input).

1. Shape: the existing per-system `let` becomes `perSystem system`, mapped over `manifest.product.targets` (components/eon-v5.json is the one owner of the system list) and merged with lib.recursiveUpdate. The reindent is mechanical; `git diff -w` shows the real change.
2. Every manifest component stays on aarch64-darwin; no target is narrowed. CodexBar, br and bv take the same release's darwin arm64 asset (gate comment above: hashes equal GitHub's published digests; same archive layout; licenses unchanged).
3. Narrowed on Darwin, unchanged on Linux: Venus's buildInputs (fontconfig, freetype, X11, xkbcommon, Wayland) and its wrapper's LD_LIBRARY_PATH and Mesa XDG_DATA_DIRS are empty; its fonts come through EON_VENUS_FONT_DIRS (kz4p.19) built from the same list as venusFontsConf, on the Venus wrapper, the Venus build and the dev shell (where Linux sets FONTCONFIG_FILE). Venus's build tests on Darwin get HOME=$TMPDIR/home with Library/Fonts symlinks to those font packages, because they build their font database without EON_VENUS_FONT_DIRS and fontdb 0.23 on macOS reads only the system folders and $HOME/Library/Fonts (it follows symlinks). Native: unproved.
4. eonPackage keeps its tests and `--include-ignored` on Darwin (no skip), with preCheck TMPDIR=/tmp (kz4p.4: 103-byte socket paths; /tmp is the 4-byte root its bound needs); postCheck restores TMPDIR on both systems. Its Darwin build therefore passes natively only after kz4p.5 ports the tests' /proc reads; kz4p.8 already depends on kz4p.5.
5. Orbit checks on Darwin: mismatchedWorker drops `-Wl,-z,noexecstack` (Apple ld64 rejects `-z`); real-PTY checks add nixpkgs lsof (real_pty/detached_exit.rs:8); orbit-unreaped-stop is Linux-only (kz4p.18). Every real-PTY session start calls `pgrep -P` (orbit/tests/real_pty/support.rs:716-727, from Session::open via pty_child), and nixpkgs builds no pgrep for macOS (adv_cmds' meson.build skips pkill/pgrep; Darwin procps = ps, sysctl, top, watch). So the Darwin real-PTY checks admit the system's /usr/bin/pgrep through `__impureHostDeps` and a PATH entry linking only that file. Alternative not taken (needs a Rust test change, outside this bead): have `children` list `ps -A -o pid=,ppid=`, which nixpkgs provides on both systems.
6. Kept on Darwin as platform-neutral and harmless: the hicolor icons and eon.desktop (a macOS .app is eon-hzq's), eonbase-closure, managed-command-path, helix-grammars (helix exports it for aarch64-darwin).

Omitted on aarch64-darwin (for kz4p.14's README gaps):
- packages.installer and packages.manual-bundle (Linux bundle; direct macOS bundles are eon-hzq), apps.record-demo (kinestra exports only x86_64-linux), checks.bundle-relink and checks.bundle-launch, checks.orbit-unreaped-stop.
- `eon-test` from the dev shell: it needs bubblewrap, which is Linux-only; kz4p.16 gives it a macOS branch and must add it to the Darwin dev shell.
Unavailable Darwin tools: none. pgrep comes from the host (item 5).

Linux identity: devShells.x86_64-linux.default, packages.x86_64-linux.installer and every Orbit check keep their drvPaths. packages.default, packages.eonbase and packages.manual-bundle and the checks built on them (default, eonbase-closure, managed-command-path, bundle-relink, bundle-launch) change only because eonPackage's source includes flake.nix: `nix derivation show` of the old and new eon and eonbase drvs differs only in `src` (and `out`), with identical input drvs, and the two source trees differ only in flake.nix.

comments.text:
Review round 1 (Codex gpt-6.1-sol xhigh + fresh Claude, on candidate tree 01fc7de3 at base 8c42c73), then rebased onto edge 51e945c (kz4p.5 and yte0.3 landed; neither touches flake.nix or nix/). This supersedes items 4 and 5 of the decisions comment above.

Fixed:
- (Codex 1, kz4p.5's note) eonPackage's Darwin tests no longer use the shared /tmp: the eon tests put HOME and XDG_STATE_HOME at fixed names under the temp dir (eon/crates/eon/tests/workspace_control.rs:1187-1189, :1814, :2739), so builds under different nixbld users would collide on 0700 leftovers. preCheck now takes a fresh private directory, `mkdir -m 700 /tmp/e<c>` for the first free c in 0-9a-z (7 bytes), and postCheck removes it. 7 bytes is the most both bounds allow: workspace_control.rs:3786 needs T + 88 + P + n <= 103 (P = pid digits, at most 5 on macOS; n = test counter digits, up to 3), and the ew<n> window root needs len(T) + h <= 10 (h = 1 on a fresh T). A build that fails mid-test leaves its directory, and the next build takes the next name; 36 names, /tmp clears on reboot.
- (Codex 2, Claude 1) The Darwin real-PTY checks no longer use the host's /usr/bin/pgrep: `__impureHostDeps` must also be in the daemon's allowed-impure-host-deps when the Darwin sandbox is on, and /usr/bin is not by default, so a sandboxed builder would refuse every real-PTY check. They now get a Nix-built `pgrep` that answers only `pgrep -P PID` (the tests' only use, orbit/tests/real_pty/support.rs:716-727) from nixpkgs' Darwin `ps -A -o pid= -o ppid=` and gawk, and fails on any other arguments. Its pipeline matches `pgrep -P` on Linux (checked by hand with procps-ng). The Rust alternative (`children` through ps) stays out of scope.
- (found while fixing) terminal-identity replaced the checks' nativeBuildInputs, which would have dropped lsof and the pgrep shim on Darwin; entries now add inputs through `inputs`, and Linux's list stays [procps ncurses].

Accepted gaps, with reasons:
- (Codex 3) Venus's `stalled_link_dispatcher_is_bounded_and_reaped` runs the absolute /bin/ps (venus/src/application.rs, recorded by kz4p.18), which a sandboxed Darwin build cannot reach, and `__impureHostDeps` has the allowed-impure-host-deps problem above. Fixing it needs a Rust test change (outside this bead). Darwin packages therefore build on an unsandboxed Darwin builder, upstream Nix's default on macOS; a builder with `sandbox = true` fails that test. For kz4p.8 (check the harness Mac's sandbox setting) and kz4p.14 (README).
- The macOS CodexBarCLI binary needs macOS 14.0 or later (LC_BUILD_VERSION minos 14.0, per the Claude reviewer), and codexbarPackage runs `CodexBarCLI --version` at install, so the Darwin package does not build on macOS 13 or older. For kz4p.14 (README: minimum macOS 14). br and bv need macOS 11 and 12.
- Venus's Darwin build tests and Venus at runtime also load the host's system fonts besides Eon's, so font-dependent results can vary with the Mac's fonts. Native: unproved (kz4p.8).
- docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:8 still calls the dev environment "the pinned x86_64-linux development environment", which stays true of the proved one; the Darwin shell lands in docs with kz4p.14.
- LIBGHOSTTY_VT_SYS_CPU=baseline also applies to aarch64-darwin (generic armv8), as on Linux.

Ledger so far: Codex pass 1, 3 blocking findings (2 fixed, 1 accepted above); Claude pass 1, 1 blocking (fixed) and 4 nits (folded into this comment and the proof record).

title: Write the SSH-driven macOS proof harness: build and suites
description:
## Why

Mac time is scarce (a 24 h rental within R$100/month, then Yu's limited time), and Lucca refuses
slow manual VNC proof. One command that turns a Mac reachable over SSH into a complete evidence
folder makes every Mac minute count and makes the same run repeatable on a rental, a CI runner or
Yu's Mac mini. This first part covers the build and the automated suites; the GUI scenario is the
next sibling.

Lucca (2026-10-27, relayed by eon-overseer): "i'd rather test everything possible and fix myself,
letting to Yu only final testing and final fixes that i missed. we can even give him a list of
tests to run (without overwhelmiing him). so the more automated, the better."

## Evidence

- Recorded manual recipe (`eon-orb-c14-mac-reproof-l8rz`, `eon-z4n6`, and the 2026-10-18 handoff
  on `ven-prove-venus-apple-silicon-macos-nm7`): `git archive <rev>` copied over SSH into a fresh
  `~/eon-<bead>`, rustup, a Zig tarball, an SDK 15 `xcrun` wrapper, `GHOSTTY_SOURCE_DIR`,
  `LIBGHOSTTY_VT_SYS_CPU=baseline`, `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` inside the run directory; the Mac has no
  `timeout`; SSH needs `</dev/null`; agent `rm -r` under `~` is blocked by dcg there, so cleanup
  is a named step.
- ORB-C14 open proof (`orbit/docs/CONTRACTS.md:835-841`): native re-proof runs `orbit-laws`, the
  unit tests, every real-PTY check and `tests/lifecycle.rs` on Apple Silicon.
- Precedent for Rust tooling: `orbit/tools/governance` is a workspace tool crate. AGENTS.md
  "Implementation Languages": Rust owns repository tooling; shell only for irreducible glue.

## Scope

In scope: a dev-only Rust tool (proposed `tools/mac-proof`, a workspace member, never in the
product closure, exposed as a flake app on both systems) with two subcommands:
- `remote --host USER@HOST [--rev REV]` (runs on Linux): checks the tree is clean or records the
  candidate tree hash, sends `git archive` of the revision over SSH into a fresh run directory,
  runs `run` there with stdin closed and a wall-clock bound, and copies the evidence folder back.
- `run` (runs on the Mac): records hardware (`sysctl hw.model`, `system_profiler
  SPHardwareDataType SPDisplaysDataType -json`), macOS and Nix versions; builds
  `.#packages.aarch64-darwin.default`; builds the Darwin Orbit checks (Bend laws, boundary,
  real-PTY) and runs `nix develop -c eon-test` (Darwin branch: Orbit unit and lifecycle,
  `orbit-protocol`, Venus, Runtime, Eon); each step has its own timeout (enforced by the tool,
  since macOS lacks `timeout`), log file and status; writes `summary.json` and a short
  `summary.txt` (step, status, duration, first failing line); exits nonzero on any failure.
- A bootstrap note or the shortest shell glue for a Mac without Nix (official or Determinate
  installer; needs sudo once) and the cleanup command Lucca runs.

Out of scope: the GUI scenario and Retina probe (next sibling), Yu's guided mode (checklist
sibling), CI (decision bead), renting a Mac (batch bead).

## Acceptance

- `nix run .#mac-proof -- remote --help` and `run --help` work on Linux; `run` refuses clearly on
  Linux ("macOS only").
- A dry run on Linux against a fake host directory (or `--local` mode) exercises archive, copy,
  timeout and summary logic; the deterministic parts (step table, summary rendering, timeout
  handling) have a few strong tests.
- The evidence folder layout is documented in the tool's `--help` and in
  `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md` (one short section, which the batch and Yu's beads reuse).
- Native execution is the batch bead's job; this bead claims no Mac result.

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test -p mac-proof` (or the chosen crate name) exits 0; fmt and clippy clean.
- `nix flake show --all-systems` lists the app for both systems.
- Codex review per AGENTS.md (new crate, Cargo.lock, flake change).

## Stop Conditions

- Stop for Lucca's decision if the tool needs a new dependency beyond the workspace's existing
  crates (e.g. an SSH library: prefer invoking the system `ssh`/`scp`).
- Stop if adding a workspace member conflicts with the Product Boundary rule on crate
  dependencies.
- Stop if the Darwin `eon-test` branch (tests bead) is not in place; the harness calls it, it
  does not reimplement isolation.
close_reason: Harness for build and suites landed in 09b18e7; Linux-side acceptance proved (help, refusal, local dry run, tests, flake app on both systems, Codex review). Native execution belongs to kz4p.12.

comments.text: Lucca (relayed by eon-overseer, 2026-10-27), after the explanation (a dev-only Rust crate, like orbit/tools/governance, that copies the source over SSH, builds, runs the Orbit/Runtime/Venus suites, launches full Eon with a scripted scenario, and brings back an evidence folder with one pass/fail summary, using the system ssh/scp and no new dependencies): "6 ok".

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Correction to kz4p.1's comment above: program_status.rs's /proc read is :66 (function :65-70). On poll(): bend-orbit passed its 36 real-PTY checks natively at b017e4f0 (orbit/docs/CONTRACTS.md:823-826), so the PTY-master risk is mostly retired, but this tree has 50 real-PTY checks and 14 have never run on a Mac. Also for this harness: run /usr/bin/infocmp eon inside Eon on the Mac (kz4p.1 question 3, TERM=eon format), and expect nix/shell-environment.nix's init-text rewrites (starship, atuin, carapace) to be first checked natively.

comments.text: From kz4p.1's map at 66b32d5: yazelix-orbit lib, bin and lifecycle tests check clean for aarch64-apple-darwin; `--all-targets` fails only in real_pty (unreaped_stop.rs:36,57: PTRACE_SEIZE, __WALL); real_pty/program_status.rs:64-66 reads /proc tpgid unguarded (panics natively). Owner pending (kz4p.1 question 1). Orbit polls PTY masters with poll() (orbit/src/platform.rs), which only a native run can check.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Observation from eon-a5 (kz4p.2, 2026-10-27, relayed by eon-overseer): on macOS, proc_pidinfo(PROC_PIDTBSDINFO) with arg 0 cannot see zombies. Orbit's macOS `bsd_info` (orbit/src/platform.rs:374-379) passes arg 0, so the background-process walk's `process()` returns None for a zombie.

Coordinator assessment: likely harmless. The walk counts zombies as not running anyway, and a zombie keeps no children (they are reparented). The other caller reads Orbit's own pid. No bead filed. The native real-PTY run (kz4p.8/.12) should confirm that a zombie grandchild neither counts nor hides a live sibling. If it does, fix it at the platform seam the way kz4p.2 did for Runtime.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Harness item from eon-mac-launch-kz4p.20 (ORB-C10's open proof for macOS). The `run` subcommand adds one step with its own log and status. It runs after the aarch64-darwin package build and uses the system's ncurses, not Nix's:

    env -u TERMINFO TERMINFO_DIRS=<orbit package>/share/terminfo /usr/bin/infocmp eon
    env -u TERMINFO TERMINFO_DIRS=<orbit package>/share/terminfo TERM=eon /usr/bin/tput clear | od -An -tx1

It passes when infocmp exits 0 and prints `eon|Eon terminal,`, and when tput exits 0 and prints the same bytes as `TERM=xterm-256color /usr/bin/tput clear` without TERMINFO_DIRS. Record `/usr/bin/infocmp -V` (macOS ships ncurses 5.7) in the step log. A pass is the native evidence that moves ORB-C10 back to Proved; the batch bead (kz4p.12) records it in ORB-C10's proof.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Correction to the eon-mac-launch-kz4p.20 harness item above. This comment replaces its commands. ncurses searches ~/.terminfo before TERMINFO_DIRS, so with the user's HOME an `eon` entry installed earlier by hand can hide a missing or unreadable package entry. Run each command with a fresh empty HOME (`mktemp -d`) and TERMINFO unset:

    env -u TERMINFO HOME=<empty> /usr/bin/infocmp eon                    # must fail: no eon without the package
    env -u TERMINFO HOME=<empty> TERMINFO_DIRS=<orbit package>/share/terminfo /usr/bin/infocmp eon
    env -u TERMINFO HOME=<empty> TERMINFO_DIRS=<orbit package>/share/terminfo TERM=eon /usr/bin/tput clear | od -An -tx1

Passes when:
- the first command fails;
- the second exits 0 and prints `eon|Eon terminal,`;
- the third exits 0 and prints the same bytes as `env -u TERMINFO HOME=<empty> TERM=xterm-256color /usr/bin/tput clear`.

Record `/usr/bin/infocmp -V` in the step log. (Found by Codex review of kz4p.20.)

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Second correction to the eon-mac-launch-kz4p.20 harness item. This recipe replaces both earlier ones. ncurses searches TERMINFO, ~/.terminfo and TERMINFO_DIRS before the system directory. Inside an Eon terminal, TERMINFO_DIRS already holds Orbit's entry, so a recipe that only unsets TERMINFO would find `eon` even without the package. Run every command in a cleared environment with a fresh empty HOME (`mktemp -d`):

    env -i PATH=/usr/bin:/bin HOME=<empty> /usr/bin/infocmp eon                    # must fail: no eon without the package
    env -i PATH=/usr/bin:/bin HOME=<empty> TERMINFO_DIRS=<orbit package>/share/terminfo /usr/bin/infocmp eon
    env -i PATH=/usr/bin:/bin HOME=<empty> TERMINFO_DIRS=<orbit package>/share/terminfo TERM=eon /usr/bin/tput clear | od -An -tx1
    env -i PATH=/usr/bin:/bin HOME=<empty> TERM=xterm-256color /usr/bin/tput clear | od -An -tx1   # control

Passes when:
- the first command fails;
- the second exits 0 and prints `eon|Eon terminal,`;
- the third exits 0 and prints the same bytes as the control.

Record `/usr/bin/infocmp -V` in the step log. (Found by Codex review of kz4p.20.)

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
From eon-mac-launch-kz4p.7 (landed flake Darwin outputs): native-only items the harness's first build should watch, none provable from Linux:
- Builder sandbox: Venus's build tests run the absolute /bin/ps, so the Darwin packages need an unsandboxed builder (upstream Nix's macOS default); record the harness Mac's `sandbox` setting.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Expected native failure, from eon-mac-launch-kz4p.16's Codex round 1 (2026-10-27, relayed by eon-overseer). On macOS, eon/crates/eon/tests/workspace_control.rs:2174-2190 (relative_configuration_root_is_resolved_once) likely fails. It compares `config-path` output, which is resolved from current_dir, so getcwd returns /private/tmp/e<c>/..., with root.join("config"), spelled /tmp/e<c>/.... This happens under both eon-test's and eonPackage's Darwin TMPDIR. A canonical /private/tmp root would break the 7-byte socket bound, so fix the test's expectation (canonicalize root before comparing), not the harness. Coordinator routing: fix it in this bead's first native fix loop. It can also be done ahead from Linux if a slot is free.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Approval (relayed by eon-overseer, 2026-10-28): Lucca, 2026-10-27, to eon-overseer: "do these two too, then ... i want to move closer to the 'yu testing' gate", which starts this bead. Earlier scope approval ("6 ok", 2026-10-27) is in the first comment.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Reference gate (2026-10-28, at a47f9b6). Consequential: a new workspace crate (Cargo.lock), a new flake app on both systems.

Behavior and owners:
- `nix run .#mac-proof -- remote --host USER@HOST --out DIR` (Linux) and `run --out DIR` (macOS). The tool owns sequencing, per-step deadlines, logs and the summary. eon-test owns test isolation (called per workspace package, never reimplemented). The flake owns the list of Darwin checks and Cargo owns the list of workspace packages: `run` reads them (`nix eval .#checks.aarch64-darwin --apply builtins.attrNames`, `cargo metadata --no-deps`) instead of keeping a second copy.
- Source identity: `remote` sends `git archive` of HEAD when the tree is clean, else of the candidate tree written through a private index (untracked files included). `run` git-inits the extracted source and fails unless `git write-tree` equals the sent tree, so the evidence names the exact tree.
- The ORB-C10 terminfo step (kz4p.20 recipe, env -i, empty HOME) takes Orbit's terminfo from the built Eon package's closure: exactly one path holding share/terminfo/e/eon, so no new flake output.

Read: orbit/tools/governance (precedent: a workspace tool crate, serde_json =1.0.151), nix/test-sandbox.nix (Darwin eon-test), nix/orbit-checks.nix, flake.nix outputs, the manual recipe in this bead's evidence, the kz4p.20/.7/.16 watch items. No external comparable needed: system ssh/scp/tar carry the transport.

Decisions and rejections:
- Placement eon/tools/mac-proof, not the proposed tools/mac-proof: it mirrors orbit/tools/governance and ./eon is already in the flake's crate fileset, so no Nix source change.
- No new crate: serde_json at the workspace's existing exact pin. Rejected: an SSH library (stop condition), libc for killpg (a `kill` child does it), a shell harness (AGENTS.md: Rust owns tooling), hard-coded check and package lists (second owner).
- Deadlines: macOS has no `timeout`, so each step's child runs in its own process group, which the tool signals TERM then KILL at its deadline.
- Version policy: dev-only, never in the product closure (its own flake package and app). Exit: retire or fold into CI if kz4p.15 supersedes it.

Check: the crate's tests (step table, summary rendering, deadline kill) through eon-test, fmt, clippy (Linux and aarch64-apple-darwin), and a local dry run (`remote --local DIR --dry-run`) that exercises archive, extraction, tree identity, copy-back and summary. This bead claims no Mac result.

Stop conditions checked: no new dependency; the crate depends on no workspace crate (Product Boundary unaffected); the Darwin eon-test branch landed (a47f9b6).

title: Add the full-Eon GUI scenario to the macOS harness
description:
## Why

EON-C7 needs full Eon launched and used natively, not only suites. Lucca refuses slow manual VNC,
so the full-product scenario must run from SSH in the Mac's logged-in GUI session, drive Eon,
capture what it shows and decide pass/fail without a person. Whatever this scenario cannot
observe becomes an item on Yu's short list, so its coverage directly sets how much Yu must do.

Lucca (2026-10-27, relayed by eon-overseer): "i'd rather test everything possible and fix myself,
letting to Yu only final testing and final fixes that i missed. we can even give him a list of
tests to run (without overwhelmiing him). so the more automated, the better."

## Evidence

- Memory `no-slow-manual-vnc-proof`: "a launched-from-SSH GUI app reaches the logged-in Aqua
  session"; `stty -f /dev/ttysN size` resizes; prepared files replace typed Unicode.
- AGENTS.md "Humans and Agents": every workspace action has an `eon` CLI path and everything a
  person sees is readable as data (`docs/USAGE.md:350-391`: `eon workspace --json`, `eon pane
  create`, `eon tab create`, `eon focus`, `eon windows`, `eon window attach|stop`, `eon attach`,
  `eon stop`, `eon versions`, `eon edit`). The scenario drives through these first; keystrokes
  only test key paths.
- macOS privacy (TCC): `screencapture` needs Screen Recording and `osascript` System Events
  keystrokes need Accessibility for the responsible process; over SSH that is `sshd` or the tool.
  Not yet probed on any Mac we use.
- EON-C7 epic acceptance item 3 (`eon-prove-full-eon-apple-silicon-macos-t8o`) lists the product
  surfaces to exercise.

## Scope

In scope: a `scenario` step of the harness tool (after `run`'s suites), which:
1. Probes the session: GUI login present, Screen Recording and Accessibility usable for the
   tool; records each as available or not, and continues with what is available. Documents the
   one-time ways to enable them without VNC where they exist (e.g. auto-login via
   `sysadminctl -autologin`; a TCC grant that needs a click is listed as a Yu/Lucca item, never
   performed silently).
2. Launches full Eon from the built package in the GUI session with an isolated config and
   runtime root, waits for Ready, and runs a scripted scenario mostly through the `eon` CLI:
   version identity (target `aarch64-darwin`), picker and first tab, panes and tabs, focus
   traversal, `eon edit` (Helix), Yazi and Ratconfig popups, a command's output in a pane (read
   back where the CLI allows), CPU/RAM chips, Kitty image display, detach (quit Venus) with Orbit
   survival and `eon attach`, Venus crash and reattach, Runtime adoption, `eon stop` and cleanup
   with no leftover processes.
3. Where Accessibility is available: key paths (Alt+Z zoom, Command+C/V with `pbcopy`/`pbpaste`,
   a shortcut popup). Where Screen Recording is available: `screencapture -x` after each step
   into the evidence folder, plus a cheap automated check (non-blank, window region differs from
   desktop).

Out of scope: the Retina probe (split on 2026-10-27 to its own sibling bead, "Add the Retina
probe to the macOS harness", for size), VoiceOver, Kotoeri IME and blur judgement (Yu's list or `c3b`/`yzw`), Yu's guided
mode (next sibling), renting (batch), a CGVirtualDisplay helper (decision on the epic).

## Acceptance

- `scenario --help` lists every step and what each needs (GUI, Screen Recording, Accessibility).
- Steps that cannot run report `skipped: <reason>` and land in `summary.txt` as items for Yu,
  never as passes.
- Deterministic parts (step table, skip logic, image non-blank check) have few strong tests on
  Linux; the scenario itself is first exercised natively in the batch bead.
- `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md` harness section lists what the scenario proves and what it leaves to Yu.

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test -p <harness crate>` exits 0; fmt, clippy.
- Codex review per AGENTS.md.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop for Lucca if a scenario step needs a new dependency (e.g. cliclick, a CoreGraphics crate)
  or any Venus behavior change.
- Stop if a needed workspace action has no `eon` CLI path: that is an AGENTS.md "Humans and
  Agents" gap; note it on `eon-agent-parity-a9g0` and use a key path or Yu item instead.
close_reason: Scenario landed with the JXA-to-Rust rework (objc2 0.3.2, macOS-only). Linux-side acceptance proved: eon-test -p mac-proof, fmt, clippy on Linux and aarch64-apple-darwin, help and dry-run of all 15 steps; Claude converge plus Codex review clean. Native execution belongs to kz4p.12, as for kz4p.8.

Confirm with Yu that his monitor is HiDPI; if not, a friend's MacBook runs the same check.

Both are inferences from code with owners pending (kz4p.1 questions 2 and 3); this GUI scenario depends on them.

comments.text:

Scratch files, briefs and Codex logs are in /home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/scenario-work/; cargo target is /home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/scenario-target. Run br with BEADS_DIR=/home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/scenario/.beads.

Do not start until eon-overseer relays Lucca's words. The decision pending is question 3 above plus a dependency approval, which eon-overseer puts to him in these terms:
- The four JXA snippets in eon/tools/mac-proof/src/scenario.rs (PROBE_SCRIPT, KEYS_SCRIPT, TREE_SCRIPT, WINDOW_SCRIPT) become a macOS-only Rust module (cfg(target_os = "macos")) using three crates already in Cargo.lock, pinned exactly at 0.3.2 and added to mac-proof only: objc2-core-graphics, objc2-app-kit and objc2-core-foundation. Record the AP-DEPENDENCY-001 gate on this bead before code: capability, alternatives (JXA via osascript; raw extern "C" FFI), replacement cost.

Plan once approved:
1. Replace the JXA with the Rust module, keeping the scenario's step table, needs and checks as they are. Linux keeps compiling: give the macOS calls a non-macOS stub that is never reached, since run and scenario refuse non-dry runs off Apple Silicon. Keep the pure parsers that stay useful (region, the probe answers if any remain) under test.
2. Open question, post_to_pid or activation: posting to Venus's pid leaves desktop focus alone (AGENTS.md "Desktop Focus"), but whether winit in Venus receives Option and Command chords posted to an inactive app is unproven. Recommendation: post to the pid after activating with NSRunningApplication, keeping activation until the first Mac run (kz4p.12) shows that posting alone works. Either way, record the choice and why in the help.
3. Drop the AX chip read: remove the `chips` step and TREE_SCRIPT. Add the chips (Eon Bar CPU/RAM) to the help's and docs/DEVELOPMENT.md's "left for Yu" list. Ask eon-overseer to file, or file with its approval, a CLI data-parity bead for reading the Eon Bar's chips (AGENTS.md "Humans and Agents"), linked to eon-agent-parity-a9g0.
4. Keep the key-driven picker (Escape) until the tab-create beads give the first tab a CLI path.
5. Fold in the leftovers fix: run.rs `eon_processes` lists with `ps -U <uid> -o pid=,comm=`, which on macOS leaves out processes with no controlling terminal. Reuse scenario.rs `listing()` (`ps -A -ww -o uid=,pid=,ppid=,command=`, filtered by uid) and match names on the executable's file name as `Process::name()` does.
6. Update `scenario --help`, RUN_HELP if needed, and the docs/DEVELOPMENT.md paragraph (keep that edit small). Bead comments 1, 4 and 5 describe JXA and the chips step; post a short superseding comment.
7. Finish per AGENTS.md: Claude converge rounds until one is clean, then the narrow Codex re-check of git diff 2a9e45abd7cefb28aa087ad2f51b78208b990811 (the converged code tree) to the new tree, scoped to eon/tools/mac-proof, docs/DEVELOPMENT.md, Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock. Its brief carries the gate-code scope line. Checks: eon-test -p mac-proof; fmt; clippy -D warnings in the dev shell, and with `rustup run stable ... --target aarch64-apple-darwin`, which now actually compiles the macOS module. Ask eon-overseer before the first test run if machine load is in doubt (free -g ≥ 5 GB is the standing rule). Amend 0c7ee8a, record the proof in a bead comment within the amend, and send eon-overseer the new SHA and the bead comment files.

Bead changes this session made, for replay in the main DB (files in scenario-work/): kz4p.9 status → in_progress; kz4p.9 comments comment-1-design.txt, comment-3-question.txt, comment-4-design-update.txt, comment-5-correction.txt, comment-6-proof.txt, and this comment-7-handoff.txt; eon-agent-parity-a9g0 comment comment-2-parity.txt.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Approval, Lucca 2026-10-28 to eon-overseer, his words: "1 ok". It answered the JXA question with the coordinator's researched recommendation:
- Replace the four JXA snippets with a macOS-only Rust module in mac-proof.
- New direct dependencies, mac-proof only, pinned at 0.3.2 and already in Cargo.lock: objc2-core-graphics, objc2-app-kit, objc2-core-foundation. This is the AP-DEPENDENCY-001 decision.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Approval (relayed by eon-overseer, 2026-10-28): Lucca, 2026-10-27, to eon-overseer: "do these two too, then ... i want to move closer to the 'yu testing' gate", standing for the macOS launch path. It covers this bead's implementation within its recorded scope. It does not cover push, promotion, GitHub posts, workflow dispatch, renting a Mac, or Lucca's running Eon.

Base: 1d731f5, moved onto edge 046dd8e (kz4p.15) before commit. Not a consequential shape: no product dependency, protocol, contract, or product lifecycle or trust boundary changes. The harness calls only stock macOS programs: osascript (JXA), screencapture, sips, pbcopy, stat, ps and kill. No crate is added. Portability: the scenario's steps run on Darwin only; on Linux, `scenario --dry-run` and `run --dry-run` plan them.

Mechanism:
- Each step has one entry in a table (scenario.rs `STEPS`): name, needs (GUI login, Screen Recording, Accessibility), required steps, what a pass shows, and whether the window shows afterwards. `scenario --help` is generated from it. A Retina step (kz4p.17) is one more entry after `launch`, and can use `Scenario::capture` and `venus()`.
- A missing need ends the step as `Failure::Unavailable`, so it is skipped with for_yu set. A step that requires only such skipped steps is also skipped for Yu. summary.txt lists them under "for Yu", and summary.json marks them `for_yu`. They never pass, and the run's result is then fail.
- The `session` step decides the needs without prompting. GUI login: the owner of /dev/console is the tool's user. The two grants: JXA `AXIsProcessTrusted()` and `CGPreflightScreenCaptureAccess()`.
- Launch: `eon run -- /bin/sh driver.sh EXCHANGE` under env_clear, with a private HOME, XDG_* under it, `[anima] enabled = false`, and EON_RUNTIME_DIR and TMPDIR at /tmp/es-<pid> (socket paths have 103 bytes on macOS). It waits for `eon workspace --json` to answer and for Venus to run under the supervisor.
- The driver is a /bin/sh loop in the first pane. It runs N.cmd files and writes N.out and N.status, and fd 3 is the pane's terminal. This gives the harness a caller inside an Eon terminal (for `eon pane create -- CMD`) and a readback of command output.
- Keys: JXA activates Venus by pid, then posts CGEvents (US-layout key codes). Activation takes desktop focus, because macOS sends keys to the frontmost application; the proof Mac has no person at it.
- Captures: `screencapture -x`, then `sips -Z 640` to an uncompressed BMP. picture.rs reads it and checks it is not blank, how much differs from the pre-launch desktop (0.5% minimum), and the share of magenta pixels for the Kitty image.
- Kitty image: 2x2 f=24 pixels stretched over c=20,r=10, sent with the pixels inline. Orbit stores only inline RGB/RGBA (ORB-C16; orbit/docs/BEHAVIOR.md "Kitty graphics placements").
- Chips: a JXA walk of Venus's accessibility tree, looking for `CPU n%` and `RAM n%` (venus/src/system.rs:91,165).
- Cleanup: every process seen (by descent from a supervisor, or by a command naming the private root or runtime root) is kept by pid and command. Stop kills the survivors by exact pid and fails naming them. A Drop impl cleans up after a skipped or failed stop.

Departures from the bead text, following the evidence:
1. Zoom is Option+Shift+Z. Alt+Z opens the Project directory picker (docs/USAGE.md shortcut table).
2. There is no Ratconfig popup. Ratconfig is a component library (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:26), so the scenario checks the Files (Yazi) popup and `eon config-path` instead.
3. The first tab's picker has no CLI path: `eon tab directory` refuses `choose-directory-first` (runtime workspace.rs:1970-1974). The scenario uses the key path (Escape, which dismisses the picker into a terminal in the launch directory), so every step after it needs Accessibility. Noted on eon-agent-parity-a9g0, per this bead's stop condition.
4. No CLI reads a terminal's screen (orb-p92). Pane output comes back through the driver's files instead.
5. Command+C needs a pointer selection, and the harness drives no pointer, so it is a Yu item along with VoiceOver, Kotoeri, blur and Retina.

Accepted gaps: the JXA scripts (probe, keys, accessibility tree), the ps-based process tree, `eon attach`'s behaviour from outside, and every screencapture/sips call have never run on a Mac. The batch bead (kz4p.12) exercises them first and fixes what fails there. Linux tests cover the step table and skip logic, the BMP reader and its checks, the driver protocol (real /bin/sh), and the parsers of ps, `eon workspace --json`, `eon versions`, the chip text and the probe answers.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Correction to the design update above (kz4p.9, 2026-10-28):
- The keys step does not save or restore the Mac's clipboard. pbpaste cannot keep non-text items, so a restore would claim more than it does. The step's `pbcopy` replaces the clipboard, as `scenario --help` says, and pbpaste is not called.
- Panes carry no usable `live` flag: the runtime writes `live: true` for every pane, and an ended terminal removes its pane instead. So `edit` checks that exactly one pane was added and still exists after 3 s, and detach, crash and adoption compare terminal sets. Detach and crash require the terminals from before Venus ended to be a subset of those after it ended, since Venus ending cancels the tab that `panes` left pending, which starts a terminal. After `eon attach` they require the set to be unchanged.
- The process markers are the private root and the runtime root, each with a trailing `/`, so another run's paths do not match.
- The `picker` step checks that the driver started in the launch directory.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Design update (kz4p.9, 2026-10-28). It supersedes the design comment above where they differ.
- detach, crash and adoption require `picker`. Without a resolved first tab there is no durable terminal to outlive Venus: killing Venus cancels the pending picker, and that alone starts a terminal. So without Accessibility only `launch`, `identity` and `stop` run, and everything else is listed for Yu.
- Screen checks use Venus's window region. A fourth JXA snippet reads it: CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo, the largest layer-0 window of Venus's pid, as shares of the main display. After each step that shows the window, its region must differ from the same region of the pre-launch desktop in at least 5% of pixels, retried for up to 30 s while the window draws. kitty needs magenta to gain at least 1% of the window. views needs each key to change at least 1% of the window and pressing it again to restore it to within 1%. The thresholds are first guesses, which the first Mac run calibrates.
- The chips step parses Venus's accessibility values, `CPU use n% ...` and `RAM use n% of ...` (venus/src/accessibility.rs sets the description as the value).
- The output step reads the size with `stty size` on the pane's own terminal (fd 3), and `tput longname` must print `Eon terminal`, which shows that macOS's ncurses resolves TERM=eon inside the pane.
- The runtime root is created 0700, as Eon's runtime requires. `--package` is canonicalized. A probe answer other than yes or no fails `session`, rather than becoming Yu items. ps runs as `-A -ww -o uid=,pid=,ppid=,command=`, filtered by uid. Cleanup kills both the processes found now and those seen before, with a fresh deadline, after up to 15 s for them to end. The keys step saves the Mac's clipboard with pbpaste and restores it.
- Programs called: osascript, screencapture, sips, pbcopy, pbpaste, stat, ps, kill, id, cp, /bin/sh, /bin/stty, /usr/bin/tput and /bin/sleep, all stock macOS. Darwin-target clippy runs with the rustup toolchain (rustc 1.96.0), since the dev shell has no aarch64-apple-darwin std.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Question for Lucca (kz4p.9, 2026-10-28), raised by the first review round (finding B6).

AGENTS.md "Implementation Languages" says Rust owns repository tooling, shell is limited to irreducible process glue, and any other language needs an explicit user decision. The scenario holds three short JavaScript-for-Automation (JXA) snippets that it runs with macOS's own `/usr/bin/osascript`. Together they are about 60 lines inside Rust string constants in eon/tools/mac-proof/src/scenario.rs:
- the grant probe: AXIsProcessTrusted and CGPreflightScreenCaptureAccess, which ask nothing;
- keys: activate Venus by pid with NSRunningApplication, then post CGEvent key presses;
- the accessibility-tree walk that reads the Eon Bar's `CPU n%` and `RAM n%` chips.

1. Accept JXA through osascript, confined to these mac-proof snippets, as macOS-only process glue. (Recommended.) It adds no toolchain, since osascript ships with every Mac, and no unsafe Rust. It reads like the Apple APIs it calls and is never part of the product. Cost: a second language in the harness, whose ObjC bridge quirks show up only on a Mac. The batch bead kz4p.12 runs it first.
2. Replace it with Rust FFI through `#[link(kind = "framework")]`, with no new crate. Cost: roughly 200 lines of unsafe CoreFoundation and AX code, plus Objective-C runtime calls (objc_msgSend) for activation, all of it also untestable on Linux.

title: Make Eon's private Session PATH resolve managed commands
description:
## Contract routing

Harden accepted EON-C9 without changing its command surface. A local Eon Session is the consumer; the configured/default argv names `eon-nu`, `eon-bash`, `eon-zsh`, or `eon-fish`; the package-private Session PATH must resolve that stable prefixed command to Eon's pinned managed dispatcher without relying on an ambient profile PATH. Missing packaged artifacts must still fail explicitly. Preserve EON-C11 generation selection.

## Why

The default is `eon-nu`, but the only PATH segment Eon guarantees to Sessions contains unprefixed private aliases. Direct package, Nix app, or composition launches can therefore fail before a shell starts; an installed profile in ambient PATH merely hides the defect.

Impact: HIGH. Effort: S. Implementation risk: LOW. Confidence: HIGH.

## Evidence

- `crates/eon/src/main.rs:951-959`: the default shell argv is `command = ["eon-nu"]`.
- `crates/eon/src/main.rs:1797-1805`: Session startup prepends only the private Session bin before executing the configured argv.
- `flake.nix:544-550`: `$out/bin` exposes `eon-*`, while `$out/libexec/eon/bin` exposes only unprefixed names.
- `flake.nix:584`: only `$out/libexec/eon/bin` is injected as the Session PATH prefix.
- `eon-audit-eon-managed-environment-hay`: exact artifact `/nix/store/h7vvb4lrxnyr23lzglclmf02ajwrk2ar-eon-0.1.0` failed to launch `eon-nu` with only the private PATH, while `nu --version` succeeded.

## Prerequisite and reference gate

- Blocked by `eon-generated-runtime-identity-h4g`; the flake-only correction must select a fresh supervisor after a profile update.
- Before code, record the execution baseline and read the complete closed audit, current EON-C9/EON-C11 proofs, the private-bin construction, and the managed-command dispatch tests.
- `docs/REFERENCES.md` evidence for the four native shells is comparison-only here; this fix changes name resolution, not shell startup semantics.
- No dependency or crate feature is expected. Stop for the crate gate and user approval before any manifest change.

## Scope

In scope:
- `flake.nix` private Session-bin projection for the four existing prefixed managed shell commands.
- The cheapest package-level regression that launches the exact packaged Orbit boundary with a private-only PATH.
- Current-state EON-C9 proof metadata, CHANGELOG, and README LOC where required by the accepted fix.

Out of scope:
- Changing the default shell, command names, public `$out/bin` behavior, unprefixed private aliases, PATH precedence, shell configuration, integration toggles, or argv semantics.
- Adding wrappers when the existing dispatcher/symlink pattern is sufficient.
- Changing Orbit, Venus, EONW, component pins, user PATH, or distribution policy.
- Adding dependencies or a shell framework.

Platform classification: neutral command contract with isolated current Nix packaging proof; no new macOS blocker.

## Implementation notes

1. Reuse the existing package-owned managed dispatcher and symlink projection; add the stable prefixed names to the private bin while preserving unprefixed aliases.
2. Add the failing package-boundary check first. Clear ambient PATH so it cannot mask the result.
3. Prove all four prefixed commands resolve to their pinned packaged shells; one parameterized check is sufficient.
4. Advance EON-C9 proof metadata after the proof-bearing commit and refresh the installed runtime without stopping older generations.

## Acceptance

- With HOME isolated and PATH containing only the exact package's private Session bin, `eon-nu --version`, `eon-bash --version`, `eon-zsh --version`, and `eon-fish --version` resolve and report their pinned package identities.
- The default `command = ["eon-nu"]` launches through exact packaged Orbit without any ambient profile bin.
- Unprefixed private aliases and public prefixed commands retain their current behavior.
- PATH ordering, managed environment filtering, user configuration, integration toggles, argv forwarding, and explicit missing-artifact failures remain unchanged.
- No new contract, dependency, wrapper layer, or public command is introduced.

## Verification

- The isolated exact-package Orbit/private-PATH regression should exit 0 for all four prefixed shell commands and fail before the fix.
- `cargo fmt --check`
- `cargo check --locked`
- `cargo test --locked`
- `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo run --locked -p eon-manifest -- components/eon-alpha-v1.json`
- `nix build --no-link --print-out-paths --no-update-lock-file path:.#default`
- `nix flake check --no-update-lock-file path:.`
- `git diff --check`
- Installed profile and `eon versions` checks after the accepted proof commit.

## Stop conditions

- Stop if the cited command/PATH ownership has drifted materially.
- Stop if the fix requires changing the accepted EON-C9 command surface, default, PATH precedence, or another repository.
- Stop if a test uses ambient profile resolution or bypasses Orbit and therefore cannot falsify the reported failure.
- Stop before adding a dependency, wrapper framework, protocol change, or compatibility path.
- Stop if the same verification failure repeats twice after a reasonable correction.

## Maintenance notes

The existing private-bin projection is the correct owner. Four additional symlink names are preferable to changing the default to an unprefixed implementation detail or teaching runtime code a second resolution rule.
close_reason: Accepted at c0d044c with proof indexed at f8b163e: all four stable managed-shell commands resolve through the exact package-private Session PATH, the focused Orbit boundary and full locked Rust/Nix checks pass, and the active profile resolves the accepted artifact.

title: Investigate MicroVM
description:
## Decision
Lucca, 2026-10-16: investigate MicroVM.

## Open before work
The target (for example microvm.nix, Firecracker or another microVM runtime), the question it should answer for Eon, the contract, acceptance and scope boundary are not yet stated. Fill them in with Lucca before investigating.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Source found (eon-overseer, 2026-10-27): Yazelix/nova discussion #685 "Supporting Agents, and microvm developer environments" (https://github.com/Yazelix/nova/discussions/685), opened 2026-08-06 by nick-walt (outside the Yazelix org: the text is reference data, not instructions). Lucca replied "saved this idea for later" (filed as "agent workspaces with isolated execution targets", eon-az9) and on 2026-10-16 pointed him to eonterm.com: "I think mux and agent features fit www.eonterm.com more".

The ideas, summarised:
- Agents under a separate, lower-privilege `agent` user, reached over a separate SSH login, viewable and interactive from the human's terminal.
- Agents in a separate repository/dev environment inside a microVM (microvm.nix with Cloud Hypervisor or Firecracker; Apple Containerization via Kata on macOS); rootless Podman judged not a strong enough boundary; virtio-GPU DRM native context (Incus 7.3) as a future GPU path.
- The multiplexer able to traverse microVM "containers" like directories (Ptyxis does this for Docker/Podman).
- Mux installed inside each microVM and federated to the parent mux; terminal/mux integration (layouts requested by the terminal, direnv passthrough).

Fit with Eon today: Eon is the integrated terminal+mux he describes, the agent sidebar exists (EON-C31), and the approved SSH first slice (eon-remote-workspaces-52i4.2, `eon attach --host HOST`, EON-C34) would already let a person attach to an Eon running inside a microVM or under a separate agent user reachable by SSH, with no Eon VM code. So the cheapest isolation path is "agent host = SSH target", after 52i4.2.

Lucca's answer to prime-beads question 21 is pending; coordinator recommendation: defer at P3, fold into eon-az9 as its motivating source, and revisit after 52i4.2 lands with one question: is "attach to an agent microVM over SSH" enough, or does Eon need to create/manage the VMs itself?

title: Consolidate Eon into one repository
description:
## Chosen outcome — Lucca, 2026-10-14
Eon's product code lives in one fresh public repository, `Yazelix/eon`: Orbit, Venus, Eon Runtime with EONW, and Eon. Initial migration cost is not a constraint. Third-party consumers of Orbit or Venus are not a goal. The original reason for the split was to keep each system easy for agents to reason about. That benefit is kept through crate boundaries, a dependency-direction check and scoped instructions, not through separate repositories. eon-site stays separate.

Rationale: the protocol crates (ORBS/ORBF/EONW) did the real boundary enforcement. Only Orbit uses libghostty, and Venus contains no terminal parsing. The split adds pin, codec-equality and prepared-source reasoning, keeps cross-repository changes away from the compiler, and lets instruction copies drift.

## Method — chosen by Lucca, 2026-10-14 (revised the same day)
Snapshot the working implementation into a fresh repository, then restructure selectively. No ground-up rewrite. Eon already has the behavior Lucca wants. Its hard-won knowledge is in the contracts, the tests and Orbit's process and FFI handling: process groups, PID reuse, socket replacement, owner-loss retirement, historical lifecycle codecs, and input ordering around frames.

The fresh repository starts from one documented consolidation commit, with no imported history. Its first commit names each source repository and SHA. The original four repositories become private and remain the historical archive for Yazelix organization admins. Lucca chose this over a history-preserving merge for a clean public history; the four repositories have one star, one fork and no open issues, so there is effectively no public audience to disrupt.

The 2026-10-14 discussion with Codex (gpt-6.1-sol xhigh) proposed the selective restructuring below, each run as its own slice with Lucca's convergence loop after consolidation. Claude spot-checked the json_escape import and the size of application.rs's test module.
1. Venus `application.rs`: extract shortcut policy (catalog, matching, platform labels, help and hint projection) into one private module. Application keeps event dispatch, focus and action execution. One catalog, no keymap framework. This is the first slice: its existing tests are the oracle.
2. Venus `render.rs`: extract font resolution and fallback. Keep one `CellMetrics` owner and the existing shaping.
3. Runtime `workspace.rs`: move shared CLI output formatting (`json_escape`, failure formatting) out of the topology owner. `generation.rs` and `windows.rs` currently import it from there.
4. `flake.nix`: extract shell-environment generation during consolidation, and keep the extracted inputs in generation identity.

Leave Runtime `supervisor.rs` and `sessions.rs`, and Orbit `interaction.rs`, as they are unless a concrete structural failure is shown.

If a later owner rewrite is chosen, do it per owner: Runtime against the old Orbit and Venus, then Venus, then Orbit last. Keep the existing behavioral assertions and adapt only their execution.

## Target shape
- One Cargo workspace. Subsystem roots `orbit/`, `venus/`, `runtime/` and `eon/` each hold their crates: Orbit's server, `orbit-protocol` and governance tool; Venus; `eon-runtime` and `eon-workspace-protocol`; Eon and `eon-manifest`. Names may change.
- `orbit-protocol` and `eon-workspace-protocol` stay standalone crates with no workspace-inherited settings, usable from outside the workspace (bend-orbit).
- A governance check enforces dependency direction: Venus may depend only on the protocol crates, Runtime only on the protocol crates, Eon on Runtime, and only Orbit on libghostty.
- Instructions: one root AGENTS.md with a single protocol import, plus a per-subsystem AGENTS.md holding only local rules. Every loaded chain stays within Codex's 32 KiB default.
- One Beads tracker that keeps the existing `orb-`/`ven-`/`eon-` IDs.
- Workspace-root `[patch]` and profiles are chosen deliberately, with per-package overrides where a crate needs different settings.

## Repository identity
- Rename the current `Yazelix/eon` to `Yazelix/eon-legacy`, then make it private along with eon-sessions, eon-desktop and eon-runtime. Do not delete any of them. The fresh repository takes the canonical name `Yazelix/eon`, which the install command, eon-site and every link expect. GitHub's redirect from the old name ends when the new repository takes it.
- **Accepted gap:** from privatization until the fresh repository's first tag there is no public install, and the Cachix workflow stops publishing because it only runs on public repositories. The donated `eon-yazelix` cache and its existing binaries are unaffected; send its owner, bioinformatist, a courtesy note. The single existing fork stays public as a detached copy.
- **Authenticated fetches first:** Eon's current flake, bend-orbit and Eonova fetch the split repositories. Before privatizing, configure Git credentials (`gh auth setup-git`) and a Nix `access-tokens` entry, and prove that a local build still works afterwards.

## Constraints
- **Proofs:** the public contract indexes (EON-C*, plus the moved ORB-C* and VEN-C* indexes) cite only proofs run in the fresh repository. Nothing public links to a private repository. Historical Beads text may still cite archive SHAs; that is history, not proof.
- **Freeze:** eon-sessions, eon-desktop and eon-runtime take no new feature work and no policy rewrites until consolidation. An urgent fix runs under that repository's existing rules.
- **Write subsystem instructions fresh.** Orbit's clean-room rule and terminal authority, Venus's ban on terminal-state reconstruction, and Runtime's ownership limits are written once under the simplified root policy. The old overlays are source material only. Their execution-baseline, reference-gate and metadata-commit ceremony is not carried over beyond rule 4 of the ceremony bead.
- **Other consumers:** bend-orbit repins to the fresh repository when it next needs ORBS (its planned ORBS v13 task); until then it builds with authenticated access. Eonova retires (Lucca, 2026-10-14): add a README note marking it superseded, then archive it. Update the links in cosmix/references.
- **Accepted consequence (Lucca, 2026-10-14):** source builds of pre-consolidation revisions require access to the private archive, which organization admins keep. History is not rewritten.
- Nix stays the sole composition owner with one component graph. Platform scope is unchanged: x86_64 Linux Wayland is proved, and the aarch64-darwin expansion under EON-C7 continues.

## Re-proof policy (Lucca, 2026-10-14)
The fresh repository is canonical only when its contract indexes cite proofs at its own revisions:
1. **Automated contracts:** `cargo test --locked --workspace` and the Nix checks, run once at the consolidated revision.
2. **Installed and native contracts:** one installed dogfood session with a checklist that covers each contract cluster: lifecycle, attach/detach and Stop, generations, workspace tabs and panes, popups and picker, shortcuts and hints, Eon Bar, quota, typography, opacity and blur.
3. **Expensive proofs that the snapshot doesn't change** (macOS ORB-C14, Orca reader qualification, extra compositors): status becomes "Pending re-proof in this repository". Re-prove them when that platform or feature is next touched. No private SHA appears in the public index.

## Sequence (children)
1. `.7` Rename and privatize the existing repositories (first, after authenticated fetches work)
2. `.1` Assemble the consolidated tree in a fresh repository
3. `.2` Compose the consolidated workspace in Nix; `.3` enforce dependency direction; `.4` write root and subsystem agent instructions; `.5` merge the Beads trackers (all after `.1`)
4. `.6` Prove and publish the fresh repository, and cut its first tag (after `.2`–`.5`)

This epic is a planning container. Claim its children, not the epic.

## Scope boundary
No new features, protocol changes, platforms or distribution channels as part of consolidation. The selective restructurings above are separate slices that follow it.
acceptance_criteria:
- The fresh public `Yazelix/eon` builds Eon and EonTerm through Nix, `cargo test --locked --workspace` runs every workspace suite, and `cargo test --locked --manifest-path installer/Cargo.toml` runs the installer's separate static workspace.
- The dependency-direction check passes, and fails on a deliberately forbidden edge.
- The three re-proof tiers are complete. Every "Proven" in the public indexes cites a fresh-repository revision; everything else is labelled "Pending re-proof in this repository".
- Independence: with Git URLs for eon-legacy, eon-sessions, eon-desktop and eon-runtime blocked (temporary `url.<blocked>.insteadOf`), a fresh clone builds Eon and EonTerm, and so does the first tag's install command. No public file in Eon or eon-site links to a private repository.
- eon-legacy, eon-sessions, eon-desktop and eon-runtime are private, and local checkouts point at their new remotes.
- Docs, the contract indexes and README describe one repository.
close_reason: All children closed: one public Yazelix/eon repository, re-proved, tagged and cached; legacy repositories private
