comments.text: Decision, Lucca, 2026-10-14: installer/ and bundle/ stay separate static workspaces with their own locks and Nix builds, as docs/ARCHITECTURE.md records. Joining the root workspace would re-resolve the installer against Venus's graph and apply the root release profile to static artifacts. Acceptance now names the installer's --manifest-path test run; the bundle has no tests.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Decision (Lucca, 2026-10-14): keep the single repository. Lucca asked whether planned mobile and native macOS clients argued for separate repositories. Kept because ORBS/ORBF/EONW and the standalone protocol crates own the boundaries; .3's dependency-direction test enforces crate edges in-repo, and Orbit, Venus, Runtime and Eon ship as one Nix package, so splitting would only restore pins. Deferred: protocol-compatibility checks (golden wire fixtures per protocol version, compatibility check on the protocol crates) start with the first client that ships on its own schedule: a mobile app, a separate SwiftUI client, or Orbit remote transport. Such clients live in their own repositories and consume tagged protocol crates. Venus on Metal (VEN-C16) stays in this repository.

title: Assemble the consolidated tree in a fresh repository
description:
## Outcome
A new local repository, published later by `.6` as `Yazelix/eon`, contains the working Orbit, Venus, Eon Runtime and Eon implementations as one Cargo workspace. It starts from one consolidation commit with no imported history. That commit's message names each source repository and the exact SHA it was taken from, which gives provenance into the private archive. Eon uses path dependencies instead of Git pins.

## Shape
- **Location:** build the fresh repository at `/home/lucca/pjs/eon/eon-next`. The legacy checkout at `/home/lucca/pjs/eon/eon` keeps its path, its tracker and the installed profile's source until `.6` swaps the directories. Until `.5` imports the trackers, run `br` for these beads in `/home/lucca/pjs/eon/eon`.
- Take each source from `git archive <sha>` of its accepted `edge` head, so only tracked content is included. Record the SHAs at execution; the freeze means they won't move.
- Layout: subsystem roots `orbit/`, `venus/`, `runtime/` and `eon/` holding their existing crates. Subsystem docs go under each root's `docs/`. Keep internal file layout within each crate.
- Leave out: per-repository `Cargo.lock`, `.github/`, rendered `AGENTS.md` and `.agent-protocols.*` (`.4` replaces them), and `.beads/` (`.5` imports it).
- Unify the locks deliberately. Compare the merged `Cargo.lock` with each source lock and record every resolved-version change. Venus's `[patch.crates-io]` (accesskit and winit forks) and release profile move to the workspace root; use per-package profile overrides where another crate must keep different settings.

## Prerequisites
`.7`: the originals are private and authenticated fetches work.

## Reference gate (consequential: build and dependency boundary)
Read Cargo's workspace reference (root-only `[patch]` and `[profile]`, `resolver = "3"`, per-package profile overrides). Record the lock-unification diff and the chosen patch and profile placement.

## Scope boundary
No behavior, protocol or contract changes. Nix is `.2`, instructions `.4`, Beads `.5`. Selective restructuring comes after the epic.
acceptance_criteria:
- `cargo test --locked --workspace` passes in the new repository.
- Each subsystem tree matches `git archive` of its recorded source SHA, apart from the documented moves and exclusions. Verify by a recursive diff.
- The bead records the lock-unification diff and the patch and profile decisions.
- No Rust manifest has a Git dependency on eon-legacy, eon-sessions, eon-desktop or eon-runtime.
notes:
Implemented as /home/lucca/pjs/eon/eon-next commit 2586d7cf63af0a4ff5ba8183aa80e153ccc4cb25 (branch edge, one root commit, no imported history).

Sources (git archive of each accepted edge head): eon-legacy f8aba503a5e8bff972836eb4e055c6c0a28820a9 (root and eon/), eon-sessions df38eebc10db801b85eca3530e5d8299b03d359f (orbit/), eon-desktop 7f74eeea9625ffce068efd25621f95f0e728000d (venus/), eon-runtime f9fef805313f6d5a47d1c6695d31bd16beb9b341 (runtime/). Freshness: Eon's pins (Orbit 427cf2d, Venus d0642ed, Runtime 0de24d0/d0a184b) differ from these heads only in docs, policy, beads and one Orbit comment. orbit-protocol and eon-workspace-protocol sources are byte-identical across every pinned revision and the snapshot SHAs.

Layout: Eon's repository-level files stay at the root (flake, components/, nix/, docs/, installer/, bundle/, .github/workflows/cachix.yml); Eon's crates move to eon/crates/{eon,eon-manifest}; orbit/, venus/ and runtime/ keep their repository layouts. Excluded: per-repository Cargo.lock, Runtime's virtual Cargo.toml, orbit/.github (CI), venus/.github (qualification patch) and venus/.gitattributes (configured only that patch), rendered AGENTS.md and .agent-protocols.*, .beads/. Recursive diff against each git archive shows only these plus the edits below.

Edits: root virtual workspace (8 members, resolver 3); Git dependencies on the split repositories become path dependencies (venus, eon-runtime, eon); Orbit's [workspace] table removed; Venus's [patch.crates-io] and [profile.release] moved to the root; Eon's include_str!/include_bytes! root paths gain one level (6 in product.rs, 1 in eon-manifest).

Reference gate: Cargo workspace and profile references read. [patch], [replace] and [profile] are honoured only in the root manifest. A virtual root must set resolver. Per-package profile overrides cannot set lto, panic or rpath.
- Patch: Venus's accesskit (4 crates) and winit forks at the root; no other member depends on them.
- Profile: root [profile.release] lto = "thin", strip = "debuginfo" now applies to every crate. lto cannot be overridden per package and no crate's contract needs different release settings, so no overrides. Consequence: Orbit, Runtime and Eon release builds gain thin LTO (Nix fixup already strips); .2's package builds exercise it.
- Rejected: per-crate custom profiles, which would add a profile surface for no contract.
- Note: resolver 3 resolves new versions for Rust 1.85, orbit-governance's rust-version.

Lock unification: seeded from Venus's lock; Cargo added the remaining packages. Cargo drifted serde_spanned 1.1.1->1.1.2 and toml_writer 1.1.2->1.1.3 unforced; both restored with cargo update --precise. Final lock: 358 packages, each present at the same version in some source lock.
- Orbit and Venus: no resolved-version change.
- Eon and Runtime: serde, serde_core and serde_derive 1.0.228 -> 1.0.229; serde_json 1.0.150 -> 1.0.151 (manifest pins in eon-runtime, eon-manifest and eon dev-deps). Forced because orbit-governance pins =1.0.229/=1.0.151, Venus resolves serde 1.0.229, and Cargo cannot hold two semver-compatible versions. Rejected: downgrading governance and Venus's shipped graph to 1.0.228.
- Git sources orbit-protocol (b6cecf8, 6bc269c) and eon-workspace-protocol (d0a184b, 0de24d0) become path packages.
- installer/ and bundle/ stay separate static workspaces with their own locks (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md). cargo metadata --locked resolves each as its own root. Their tests run by --manifest-path, outside cargo test --workspace.

Proof (mechanically verified, revision eon-next 2586d7c): cargo test --locked --workspace passed, 339 tests, 0 failed, 7 pre-existing ignores (Orbit 2, Venus 5), 44 s. Environment: x86_64 Linux, cargo/rustc 1.96.0, zig 0.15.2, inside bubblewrap 0.12.0:
- no network; private PID, IPC and UTS namespaces; private /dev and /tmp; empty /run/user/1000
- read-only root except the repository and ~/.cargo
- cleared environment, plus FONTCONFIG_FILE=/nix/store/xf3n7fwv2hd2y5nrbwk43z8pl238dqkq-fonts.conf, the installed Venus wrapper's accepted font environment. Without it, three Venus font tests fail: they need DejaVu and Symbols Nerd Font Mono.
No Rust manifest or Cargo.lock references eon-legacy, eon-sessions, eon-desktop or eon-runtime.

Incident 2026-10-14 13:36 local: the first, unsandboxed run of this suite was started from Claude inside Lucca's live Eon terminal. Within a second of Eon's workspace_control tests starting, the live Venus window and that Claude process exited; supervisor g1-98f3 and its Orbit sessions survived. A sandboxed strace replay of the same test binary in the same environment found no signal to any process the tests did not create, no access to /run/user/1000, ttys or $HOME, and 38/39 passing. Cause unidentified. Agents must run these suites sandboxed.

Gaps for later children (not changed here):
- flake.nix still fetches the split repositories and references ./crates (.2).
- orbit-governance's CLI expects .beads and docs at its argument root (.3, .5).
- Docs still name old paths and per-repository commands (.4, .6).
- Orbit's hosted Ubuntu and macOS CI was not carried over; re-homing it is an AP-CI-001 decision.
- Eon's integration tests inherit the caller's EON_* environment (the real CodexBar ran 60 times) and leak at least one directory picker (pid 92003 from a 2026-10-13 run).

Ledger: 1 review pass by the implementing agent in its own context, 1 finding (dead venus/.gitattributes, removed before commit). Not a fresh-context pass.
close_reason: Consolidated tree committed as eon-next 2586d7c; cargo test --locked --workspace passes in the sandbox

title: Compose the consolidated workspace in Nix
description:
## Outcome
Nix builds Eon and EonTerm entirely from the in-repository crates. The flake has no inputs for orbit, venus, eon-runtime or the codec. The component graph represents the in-tree components without separate source revisions, and generation identity covers every in-tree source.

## Shape
- Remove the four split-repository flake inputs and their locks; build Orbit, Venus and Runtime from the workspace.
- Delete `nix/workspace-package-check.nix` and the codec-equality and prepared-source machinery that existed only because of independent pins.
- Change `components/eon-alpha-v3.json` and `eon-manifest` validation so in-tree components carry the repository revision implicitly. External tools (Anima, Helix, Yazi, Ghostty, Ratconfig, Kinestra and others) stay exactly pinned. This changes EON-C2 and EON-C3 under the consolidation decision; update their index entries.
- Extract shell-environment generation out of `flake.nix` into `nix/` (restructuring item 4), and keep its inputs in generation identity.
- Make the generation assembly cover every in-tree crate (Eon's `product.rs` `ASSEMBLY` and runtime-owned bytes) without constructing store paths.

## Reference gate (consequential: component graph and generation identity)
Read the EON-C1–C4 and EON-C11 contracts, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` (component graph, generation lifecycle, Nix composition), the current `flake.nix` assertions and `eon-manifest` validation. Record the new manifest representation and the rejected alternatives.

## Prerequisites
`.1`.

## Scope boundary
No new channels, platforms or runtime behavior. The external tool set is unchanged.
acceptance_criteria:
- `nix build --no-link .#default .#eonterm` and every flake check pass, including helix-grammars, the EonTerm closure and managed command path checks.
- `flake.nix`, `flake.lock`, `Cargo.toml`/`Cargo.lock` and the manifest contain no reference to eon-sessions, eon-desktop or eon-runtime.
- Red/green: editing one byte in Orbit, Venus or Runtime source changes the generation ID; editing mutable configuration doesn't.
- `cargo run --locked -p eon-manifest -- components/eon-alpha-v3.json` validates the new graph. EON-C2 and EON-C3 index entries describe it.
close_reason: Fresh-eyes and simplification round: ComponentFacts and Requirement.revision removed, in-tree package-name assert, build.rs read errors; review converged

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Handoff, 2026-10-14 (session stopped at 67% context, before any .2 edit; the bead stays claimed and in progress).

Read so far:
- EON-C2 and EON-C3 in docs/CONTRACTS.md.
- eon/crates/eon-manifest/src/lib.rs. It validates schema 3. Every component needs a 40-hex revision and an HTTPS Git source. Each `requires` entry must equal the target's revision and interfaces. Activation contracts and interfaces must be listed on their components. Tests include the canonical JSON with include_str!.
- components/eon-alpha-v3.json, in-tree entries:
  - orbit: 427cf2d; ORB-C1..C13 proofs; ORBF 2, ORBS 13
  - venus: d0642ed; requires orbit 427cf2d (ORBF/ORBS) and eon-workspace-protocol
  - eon-runtime: 0de24d0; cargo-package; requires eon-workspace-protocol d0a184b (EONW 9) and orbit (ORBS 13)
  - eon-workspace-protocol: d0a184b; EONW 9
  All source URLs point at the private split repositories.
- eon/crates/eon/src/product.rs:
  - ComponentFacts.report = eon_manifest::version_report(MANIFEST), the `eon versions` lines `id version revision target`.
  - ComponentFacts.orbit_revision = component_revision(MANIFEST, "orbit").
  - ASSEMBLY includes nix/workspace-package.nix, which .2 deletes, so update the list.
- orbit_revision is Orbit's management `component_generation`:
  - supervisor.rs:646 passes it to `yazelix-orbit serve --management-v1 SESSION RUN COMPONENT_GENERATION`.
  - sessions.rs validate_management_identity rejects any acquired or recovered session in the generation runtime directory whose recorded value differs.
  - The value only has to be stable and consistent within one generation, under MAX_ID_BYTES.
  - Not yet checked: whether generation.rs stop_generation(s) compares it across generations.

Not read yet: flake.nix (1,019 lines; it assembles the four inputs, prepares sources and asserts revisions), nix/workspace-package.nix and nix/workspace-package-check.nix (both to be deleted), EON-C1/C4/C11, the ARCHITECTURE graph and generation sections, and the consumers of `eon versions` output.

Proposed shape, to confirm against the remaining references:
- Manifest schema 4. In-tree components (orbit, venus, eon-runtime, eon-workspace-protocol) get `source: {"kind": "workspace", "path": "<dir>"}` and no `revision`. Requirements on in-tree targets carry no revision, since the repository revision is implicit.
- External components keep git and an exact revision.
- Contract and interface `proof` SHAs stay until .6 re-proves them.
- `eon versions` prints `workspace` for in-tree revisions.
- component_generation becomes a stable in-tree identity, preferably derived from the runtime's own generation identity; decide after reading generation.rs.
- Rejected: sentinel revisions (fake identity), and dropping in-tree components from the manifest (it loses the activation contracts and interfaces).

Constraints:
- Run Rust suites only in the sandbox (root AGENTS.md Testing Discipline). Recipe: bubblewrap, --unshare-all --new-session, read-only root with eon-next and ~/.cargo writable, cleared environment with RUSTUP_HOME and FONTCONFIG_FILE set to the installed Venus fonts.conf. Before the change, `cargo test --locked --workspace` passed 339 tests there.
- Never restart the live Eon supervisor.
- Refresh the eon profile only from the swapped canonical checkout in .6, unless Lucca says otherwise.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Reference gate, 2026-10-14 (fresh session after the handoff).

Read: EON-C1–C4 (docs/CONTRACTS.md), ARCHITECTURE "Repository subsystem boundaries", "Runtime library boundary" (including "Independent package selection") and "Composition unit"; all of flake.nix; nix/workspace-package.nix; nix/linux-bundle.nix; nix/installer.nix; eon-manifest lib.rs/main.rs; product.rs; runtime generation.rs (current_generation, generation_id), supervisor.rs:646, sessions.rs validate_management_identity; orbit management MAX_ID_BYTES (128); the `eon versions` consumers (cli.rs, installer: success only, docs).

Evidence:
- flake.nix still reads the pre-.1 layout (`./crates/eon/Cargo.toml`, `./crates`), so it does not evaluate in eon-next today.
- component_generation is compared only within the owning generation (supervisor state and recovery in that generation's runtime directory). The generation stop path routes through the owning supervisor over EONW. Nothing compares it across generations. Orbit bounds it at 128 bytes.
- Present requires equality of the component report with the running supervisor (generation.rs:251). That holds within one build.
- Orbit and Venus bytes reached generation identity only through their manifest revisions (the manifest and flake.lock in ASSEMBLY). Removing in-tree revisions removes that coverage unless Eon's assembly covers the sources directly.

Decision:
1. Manifest schema 4. In-tree components (orbit, venus, eon-runtime, eon-workspace-protocol) carry `source: {"kind": "workspace", "path": "<relative crate dir>"}` and no `revision`. External components keep `git` plus an exact 40-hex revision. A requirement names a revision exactly when its target has one. Interface and proof checks are unchanged. Workspace paths must be relative, with no empty, `.` or `..` segments. The projects are renamed to Orbit and Venus. Contract and interface proof SHAs stay until .6 re-proves them.
2. `eon versions` prints `workspace` in the revision column for in-tree components (four columns are kept; the installer checks only exit status). The generation ID on the first line identifies the in-tree build.
3. Generation identity: a std-only `build.rs` in the eon crate walks the workspace root it was compiled from. It skips dot entries, `target` directories and symlinks, and hashes (relative path, length, bytes) in sorted order with FNV-1a-128 into `EON_WORKSPACE_DIGEST`. `ASSEMBLY` becomes that digest, which replaces the hand-kept include list. Runtime keeps its own runtime/EONW include list. In Nix, the workspace source fileset (one owner, shared by Orbit, Venus and Eon) decides which files are installed identity. A dev checkout also hashes its docs, which is harmless. No store path is constructed or read.
4. component_generation becomes the runtime's own generation ID. `ComponentFacts.orbit_revision` and `eon_manifest::component_revision` are removed. The ID stays stable within a generation and is 35 bytes.
5. Nix builds Orbit, Venus and Eon from one workspace fileset with the root Cargo.lock. It deletes the four split inputs, `nix/workspace-package.nix`, `nix/workspace-package-check.nix`, the orbit-protocol equality and the Git-to-path substitutions. A generic assert checks each workspace component's Cargo name and version against the manifest. Shell-environment generation moves to `nix/shell-environment.nix` inside that fileset, so it stays in identity.

Rejected:
- Sentinel or repository-HEAD revisions in the manifest: fake identity, or unavailable to cargo builds.
- Dropping in-tree components from the graph: loses the activation contracts and interfaces.
- A hand-listed include_bytes! of Orbit/Venus sources: drifts silently when files are added, and embeds megabytes.
- Nix-computed source hashes passed into the build: the cargo route would lack identity, and identity would be derived from Nix.
- A constant component_generation: weakens the recovered-record check.

Checks: the eon-manifest unit tests for schema 4 (workspace/git revision rules) and `cargo run -p eon-manifest`; red/green on `eon versions` generation (one byte in orbit/venus/runtime changes it; a config edit does not); `nix build .#default .#eonterm` plus `nix flake check`; Rust suites in the sandbox.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:

title: Enforce dependency direction across workspace crates
description:
## Outcome
A Rust governance test enforces the ownership boundaries that separate repositories used to imply. The test reads `cargo metadata`:
- `venus` depends only on `orbit-protocol` and `eon-workspace-protocol` among workspace crates;
- `eon-runtime` depends only on the protocol crates;
- `eon` depends on `eon-runtime`, the protocol crates and `eon-manifest`;
- only Orbit depends on `libghostty-vt`;
- the protocol crates have no workspace-internal dependencies and no workspace-inherited settings, so they stay usable from outside (bend-orbit).

## Shape
Extend Orbit's existing Rust `tools/governance` crate, or move it to a root tool, rather than adding a new harness. It runs under `cargo test --workspace`.

## Prerequisites
`.1`. It can run alongside `.2`.

## Reference gate
Not consequential beyond the existing test harness. Read the current `tools/governance` crate and `cargo metadata` output format.

## Scope boundary
It enforces dependency edges, not code semantics. Venus terminal-state reconstruction remains a review and contract-test matter, as the 2026-10-14 discussion established.
acceptance_criteria:
- The governance test passes in `cargo test --locked --workspace`.
- Red/green: temporarily adding a forbidden edge (for example `venus` → `libghostty-vt`, or `venus` → `yazelix-orbit`) makes it fail with a message naming the edge. Revert after the check.
close_reason: Dependency-direction test in orbit-governance runs under cargo test --locked --workspace (340 passed in sandbox); red/green named every injected edge; review converged after 5 passes. Open user decision: workspace-edge rules for yazelix-orbit and orbit-governance.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Implementation shape: a cfg(test) dependency_direction module in orbit/tools/governance/src/main.rs runs `cargo metadata --format-version 1 --no-deps --offline` (cargo from $CARGO, cwd CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR) and checks declared edges of every kind (normal, dev, build, target). Rules: protocol crates allow no workspace edges; yazelix-venus and eon-runtime allow only the protocol crates; eon-manifest allows eon-runtime and the protocol crates (root AGENTS.md: 'Eon's crates depend on Eon Runtime and the protocol crates'); eon also allows eon-manifest; only yazelix-orbit may depend on libghostty-vt, and yazelix-orbit must still depend on it so a rename cannot make the rule vacuous. Protocol manifests must not contain workspace = true inheritance (text scan; quoted values containing that text would false-positive, accepted given the tiny manifests). Rejected: --no-deps-free full resolution (needs registry sources, direct edges suffice because internal edges are allowlisted); a toml dependency for the scan; moving the tool to a root crate (bead allows extending in place).

Open user decision (not encoded): yazelix-orbit and orbit-governance have no workspace-edge rule, because no written rule states Orbit's allowance. Deny-by-default with yazelix-orbit -> [orbit-protocol] and orbit-governance -> [] would also reject e.g. yazelix-orbit -> eon-runtime.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Shape update after review: every workspace member must have a rule entry (unlisted members fail); yazelix-orbit and orbit-governance are listed with no workspace-edge rule pending the open decision above. The terminal-engine rule covers every libghostty* package (libghostty-vt-sys is in the graph), and yazelix-orbit must still depend on libghostty-vt. The table-presence loop was dropped as redundant with deny-by-default.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Accepted gap: the check sees only direct declared dependencies (cargo metadata --no-deps), so a libghostty crate reached through a third-party registry package is not detected. Full resolution would need every target's crates (for example macOS-only arboard) in the local cache, so it is a poor fit; review owns that case.

An earlier red run named yazelix-venus -> libghostty-vt. All manifests and Cargo.lock were restored; green afterwards.

Pass 4: doc omitted protocol-manifest check (fixed). Pass 5: nothing actionable.

title: Write root and subsystem agent instructions
description:
## Outcome
Agents get one shared policy and short subsystem rules. A root `AGENTS.md` renders the Starcompass import once, with Eon's simplified overlay adapted to one repository. `orbit/`, `venus/` and `runtime/` each get an `AGENTS.md` that holds only that subsystem's local rules.

## Shape
- Root: profiles `greenfield`, `orchestrator` and `terminal-engine`, because Orbit is now in the repository. Remove rules made obsolete by consolidation: the cross-repository frontier, child revision freshness, isolated candidates, and the child freeze and its Status note.
- Subsystems: write the rules fresh from the old overlays. Orbit: clean-room rule, terminal authority, one client, fixed boundaries, the platform seam. Venus: no PTY, raw VT parsing or terminal-state reconstruction; the native host boundary. Runtime: its ownership limits. Carry no old execution-baseline, reference-gate or metadata-commit ceremony beyond the root rules.
- If Starcompass can't render an overlay-only subsystem file, hand-write the subsystem files and record that gap for Starcompass. Don't fork Starcompass.

## Prerequisites
`.1`, which leaves the old rendered instructions out.

## Reference gate
Read the four current policies, Starcompass's README (profiles, budgets, consumer layout) and Codex's AGENTS.md discovery rules (ancestor chain from the working directory, 32 KiB combined default).

## Scope boundary
Instructions only. Eon's AP-TEST-001 exception covers validation.
acceptance_criteria:
- The root `AGENTS.md` passes `starcompass check`.
- For each subsystem directory, the root plus subsystem chain an agent loads from there is at most 32 KiB.
- Each moved rule appears exactly once, at the root or in its subsystem, and no surviving text names the split repositories as live.
notes:
Root and directory AGENTS.md render from Starcompass 4a8554661fe8821cd2d9e6540a5fec07c0268b84 (clean detached checkout; the current local Starcompass edge, not yet pushed) with profiles greenfield, orchestrator and terminal-engine: 17 protocols, adding AP-TERMINAL-001 and AP-FAILURE-001. Eon's AP-TEST-001 exception is carried unchanged. orbit/, venus/ and runtime/ keep their rules in .agent-protocols.local.md and render with --nested; the root import record lists them.

Starcompass gap, closed 2026-10-14 on Lucca's direction ("we don't want any gaps"): ap-6hg added `render --nested` with directory checks (Starcompass 517a3d1, self-adopted at 4a85546). The first close of this bead had hand-written subsystem files; it was reopened to adopt the rendered files.

- Read the four source policies: Eon's overlay at eon-legacy 97b0a79, Orbit's at df38eeb, Venus's at 7f74eee, Runtime's AGENTS.md at f9fef80.
- Read Starcompass's README: model, profiles, budgets, consumer layout, render and check.
- Read Codex's AGENTS.md guide. Codex walks from the Git root to the working directory, reads at most one file per directory, joins them with blank lines, and stops adding files once the combined size reaches project_doc_max_bytes (32 KiB by default).

Rule disposition:
- Root kept verbatim: implementation languages, core rule, desktop focus, composition and distribution, platform discipline, testing discipline, local runtime synchronization, Git workflow, Beads, proof and review (index wording only).
- Root adapted:
  - intro: the layout, and a pointer to read the subsystem AGENTS.md
  - status: consolidation freeze removed
  - product boundary: subsystems instead of repositories; dependency direction; standalone protocol crates; fix the owning subsystem; naming without the Eon Sessions repository
  - contract method: three owner indexes; never renumber; stop for user approval before a contract change (moved once from Orbit and Venus); the owning REFERENCES.md; repository revision in proof records
  - documentation: subsystem changelogs (moved once from Orbit and Venus)
  - verification: external pins; workspace and installer test commands; fmt and clippy for Orbit and Venus crates (moved once)
  - portability disposition: moved once from Orbit and Venus, with their vocabularies merged
- Root removed as obsolete, per this bead: child freeze, One Active Frontier, Child Revision Freshness, Isolated Candidates.
- Orbit kept: terminal authority, fixed boundaries, protocol change classification (reduced from cross-repository compatibility; consumers are Venus, Eon Runtime, Eon and bend-orbit), platform seam, clean-room rule, contract granularity, CRATES.md, test doubles and lossy projections, Superlogical naming.
- Orbit dropped:
  - Status, because CONTRACTS.md owns status.
  - The proof lifecycle and the orb-bi4.3, orb-pmp and orb-bi4.4 gate history.
  - The execution-baseline, reference-gate, crate-gate and protocol-exception comment ceremonies; canonical AP-REFERENCE, AP-DEPENDENCY and AP-EXCEPTION plus the root consequential-shape rule cover them.
  - Bead size and method (AP-PLAN, AP-MINIMAL, AP-TEST), the core rule (already at the root), and the LOC scorecard (deleted under eon-simplify-ceremony-2xfw rule 5).

title: Merge the Beads trackers into the fresh repository
description:
## Outcome
The fresh repository's tracker is the one canonical Beads graph. It holds every Orbit (`orb-`), Venus (`ven-`) and Eon issue with its IDs, comments, dependencies and history, and cross-tracker references are native links. The moved subsystem `.beads/` directories are gone.

## Evidence (scratch trial, 2026-10-14, br 0.2.11 from the Nix profile)
- The three trackers hold 234 + 111 + 117 = 462 issues with no duplicate IDs; the prefixes are distinct.
- Importing their concatenated JSONL with `br sync --import-only` into a copy of Eon's `.beads` created all 462 issues, preserved IDs, comments and dependencies (for example, `orb-1sd` kept 54 comments and its dependency), and found no cycles. The `issue_prefix: eon` setting accepts the imported `orb-`/`ven-` IDs, and new issues still get `eon-`.
- The import fails on br's unique `external_ref` rule. Two pairs collide: `eon-desktop:ven-selection-upward-autoscroll-161` (`eon-adopt-upward-selection-autoscroll-dmyk` and `orb-selection-upward-autoscroll-zlt`), and `eon:eon-prove-full-eon-apple-silicon-macos-t8o` (`eon-hzq` and `ven-accept-venus-apple-silicon-orbit-piy`).
- About 60 issues use `external_ref` to point at sibling trackers (`eon:`, `eon-sessions:`, `eon-desktop:`, `orbit`, `venus` forms).

## Method (only through br; never edit `.beads/` directly)
The target tracker is `/home/lucca/pjs/eon/eon-next/.beads`. After the import, run all `br` work there. The legacy tracker at `/home/lucca/pjs/eon/eon` becomes read-only history.
1. In the source trackers, clear the two colliding `external_ref` values with `br update`, recording the replacement link. This is tracker metadata needed for consolidation and is permitted despite the freeze.
2. Build the merged JSONL outside `.beads/` from the three committed exports (eon-legacy, eon-sessions, eon-desktop), then import it with `BEADS_JSONL=<path> br sync --import-only --allow-external-jsonl` and export it with `br sync --flush-only`.
3. Canonicalize: turn each sibling-tracker `external_ref` into a native `br dep add -t related` link, or `blocks` where the text states a prerequisite, then clear the ref. Leave real external references (`https:`, `nova`, `astra-*`, upstream projects) unchanged.
4. Keep `orb-`/`ven-` IDs. Don't use `--rename-prefix`, because commits, docs and comments cite those IDs. Add `orbit`/`venus` area labels where missing.
5. Triage the imported open issues (12 in Orbit, 4 in Venus). Close ones that only existed as cross-repository gates, citing consolidation, and keep real work.
6. Leave historical issue text unchanged. Its repository-qualified paths and SHAs refer to the private archive. That is history, not proof.

Use the br version the repository pins (`nix develop`, documented as 0.7.2). Recheck the trial if it differs from 0.2.11.

## Prerequisites
`.1`. Venus's pending bead was committed as eon-desktop `7f74eee`.

## Scope boundary
Tracker consolidation only. No content rewrites beyond the link canonicalization and gate-closure notes above.
acceptance_criteria:
- The fresh repository's `br list --all` count equals the sum of the three source trackers. Spot-checks of several orb-/ven-/eon- issues show identical comments and dependencies.
- `br dep cycles` reports none, `bv --robot-triage` runs, and `br sync --flush-only` is clean.

title: Prove and publish the fresh repository, and cut its first tag
description:
## Outcome
The fresh repository is public as `Yazelix/eon`, proved under the epic's re-proof policy, with canonical contract indexes, and its first tag is the install path.

## Shape
- After `.7`'s rename frees the name, create the public `Yazelix/eon` and push. Add the `CACHIX_AUTH_TOKEN` secret and confirm one Cachix run publishes.
- Run the three re-proof tiers at fresh-repository revisions: the automated suites once; one installed dogfood session with the contract-cluster checklist; "Pending re-proof in this repository" for unchanged expensive proofs. The public EON, ORB and VEN indexes cite only fresh-repository revisions.
- Remove every public link to a private repository from README, docs, the contract indexes and CHANGELOG. Condense pre-consolidation CHANGELOG history into a short summary without links.
- Swap the local directories: `/home/lucca/pjs/eon/eon` becomes `/home/lucca/pjs/eon/eon-legacy`, and `/home/lucca/pjs/eon/eon-next` becomes `/home/lucca/pjs/eon/eon`, so the canonical checkout keeps the familiar path. Then refresh the active `eon` profile from it. Don't restart a running supervisor.
- Cut the first tag on Lucca's explicit go-ahead at execution, because it is outward-facing. Move the install command in Eon's README and docs and in eon-site (`src/pages/index.astro`, README). Update the cosmix/references links.

## Prerequisites
`.2`, `.3`, `.4` and `.5`.

## Reference gate
The epic's re-proof policy, the current index proof fields, `docs/USAGE.md`, and eon-site's install text.

## Scope boundary
No behavior changes. A defect found during dogfood gets its own bead.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every "Proven" in the public indexes cites a `Yazelix/eon` revision or reads "Pending re-proof in this repository".
- Independence: with the four legacy URLs blocked (temporary `url.<blocked>.insteadOf`), a fresh clone builds Eon and EonTerm, and so does the first tag's `nix profile add` in an isolated profile.
- A search of Eon and eon-site finds no link to eon-legacy, eon-sessions, eon-desktop or eon-runtime.
- The installed profile resolves to the fresh repository's build. The dogfood checklist results are recorded in this bead, and one Cachix run has published.
close_reason: Public, re-proved, tagged linux-alpha-2026-10-14, and the binary cache publishes

title: Rename and privatize the existing repositories
description:
## Outcome
The four existing repositories are private and preserved as the historical archive, the canonical name `Yazelix/eon` is free for the fresh repository, and Lucca's local builds keep working.

## Shape
1. Configure authenticated fetches: `gh auth setup-git` for `git+https` inputs and Cargo Git dependencies, plus a GitHub token in Nix `access-tokens` for `github:` inputs. Prove that a local `nix build --no-link .#default` of current Eon works before changing anything.
2. With Lucca's explicit go-ahead at execution: rename `Yazelix/eon` to `Yazelix/eon-legacy`, then make eon-legacy, eon-sessions, eon-desktop and eon-runtime private (`gh repo edit --visibility private --accept-visibility-change-consequences`). Do not delete anything.
3. Point the local checkouts' `origin` at `Yazelix/eon-legacy` and the renamed repositories.
4. Rerun the local `nix build` against the now-private sources.
5. Retire Eonova: add a README note marking it superseded, then archive it.
6. Draft a short courtesy note for bioinformatist, owner of the `eon-yazelix` Cachix cache, for Lucca to send.

The old tag `linux-alpha-2026-09-24` becomes private with eon-legacy, so no deletion is needed.

## Prerequisites
None. This runs first.

## Reference gate
Not consequential. Check GitHub's rename and visibility-change consequences at execution: redirects, detached forks, and removed stars and watchers.

## Scope boundary
No deletion and no history rewrite. The fresh repository is created in `.6`, not here.
acceptance_criteria:
- `gh repo view` reports PRIVATE for eon-legacy, eon-sessions, eon-desktop and eon-runtime, and `Yazelix/eon` no longer resolves.
- A local `nix build --no-link .#default` of current Eon passes after privatization, with authenticated fetches.
- Local `origin` remotes point at the renamed repositories, and Eonova is archived with its superseded note.

Proof, 2026-10-14, executed with Lucca's explicit go-ahead.
- Before: `gh` is Git's GitHub credential helper (token scopes include repo and admin:org). A cold-cache Nix fetch of the already-private Eonova (`git+https`, rev f4717ef) succeeded, so no Nix access-tokens entry is needed: no `github:` input points at a privatized repository. Baseline `nix build --no-link .#default` at 2f04e78 produced /nix/store/mqqiqj3qfxxf526k2z7zsqkhn9cf7vqy-eon-0.1.0.

title: Investigate moving a live terminal between Eon windows
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-10-27, after opening a second Eon window: "can eon move panes across windows? that would
be insterestingg". Each Eon window is an independent generation with its own supervisor
(docs/USAGE.md "Stop terminals"; `eon window attach`, `eon window stop all`), and each terminal is
its own Orbit host whose socket lives under its generation's directory
(/run/user/<uid>/eon/generations/<G>/session-N.sock). Moving a pane between windows means one
supervisor taking over a live Orbit host from another without stopping it.

## Approval

Lucca, 2026-10-27, relayed by eon-overseer. Asked: "2. Investigate moving across windows as its own
bead. One supervisor would take over a live Orbit host from another, and windows on different Eon
versions are excluded at first. The investigation ends with a proposal and contract text for you.
P2, after 1. ... File 1 and 2?" Lucca: "file". This approves filing and investigating only.

## Investigate (consequential: lifecycle, ownership, trust; record the reference gate)

1. What ties an Orbit host to its generation: socket path, management channel (`--management-v2`),
   supervisor bookkeeping, process parentage and reaping (Orbit owns bounded PTY process-group
   shutdown and direct-child reaping; an adopted host is not the new supervisor's child), and what
   happens to it when the old generation stops.
2. Can a second supervisor adopt a live host: hand-off protocol between two supervisors (both
   same EONW; refuse otherwise), socket relocation or an indirection, management channel transfer,
   attention and pin records, and failure modes (either side crashes mid-move; the terminal must
   never be lost or end up owned twice).
3. Trust: both windows are the same user; confirm the boundary (no cross-user moves) and what
   authorization the CLI path needs.
4. Comparables: tmux `move-window`/`join-pane -s other-session` (one server), Zellij, WezTerm mux
   domains; note which have one server for all windows (the simpler design: is a shared
   supervisor across windows a better answer than a hand-off?).
5. Darwin path per Platform Discipline.
6. Proposal to eon-overseer, numbered with recommendations: the design (hand-off vs shared
   supervisor), contract text (EON-C33 and the window/generation contracts it touches, ORB-C*
   for Orbit's side), wire changes and a bead split. Stop for Lucca.

## Prerequisites

The same-window workspace move bead filed beside this one (its CLI and landing rules are reused).

## Acceptance

The proposal is recorded on the bead with sources, revisions and the rejected approaches, and
relayed to Lucca. No product code in this bead.

## Scope boundary

Investigation and proposal only. Not: drag and drop between windows, windows on different Eon
versions.

title: Move a pane or tab to another workspace in the same window
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-10-27, after opening a second Eon window: "can eon move panes across windows? that would
be insterestingg". Today panes move only within a tab (up/down in a column, Ctrl+Alt+H/L between
columns, `eon pane move`) and tabs only left/right (`eon tab move`). Nothing moves a pane or a tab
to another workspace. Within one window every workspace belongs to one supervisor, so this needs no
ownership handoff and is the first step toward moving across windows
(see the cross-window investigation bead filed beside this one).

## Approval

Lucca, 2026-10-27, relayed by eon-overseer. Asked: "1. Move a pane or tab to another workspace in
the same window first ... It's useful on its own, and it ships with `eon pane move --workspace` and
`eon tab move --workspace` CLI paths. I'd make it a P2 feature bead. 2. Investigate moving across
windows as its own bead ... File 1 and 2?" Lucca: "file". This approves filing. The interaction
design (keys, Commands entries, picker), the EONW change and the contract text need his approval
before product code.

## Scope

- Move the selected (or calling) pane to another workspace of the same window, landing as a new
  tab there or into that workspace's active tab (propose which; recommendation in the proposal).
- Move the active (or calling) tab to another workspace, appended after its tabs.
- The terminal keeps running: same Orbit host, attachment and scrollback; pins and attention
  follow it (EON-C31 records move with the terminal; seen state preserved).
- Moving the last pane or tab out of a workspace follows EON-C33's last-tab rule (propose: the
  emptied workspace closes without a prompt, since no terminal stops).
- Humans and Agents rule: `eon pane move --workspace WS [--tab new|TAB]` and
  `eon tab move --workspace WS`, naming targets by ID, leaving the person's shown workspace,
  active tab and focus as they are unless asked; a Commands entry and, if wanted, a key or a
  picker action (Alt+Shift+S picker) for people.

## Contract

EON-C33 (workspaces), the EON-C10 CLI surface and EONW (a new action: a version bump; never amend
EONW in place). Read docs/ARCHITECTURE.md#naming-boundary for product terms.

## Steps

1. Read EON-C33, EON-C10, the existing `pane move` / `tab move` paths in runtime and Venus, and how
   the supervisor tracks a terminal's workspace and tab.
2. Propose to eon-overseer (numbered, with recommendations): landing spot, last-tab behaviour,
   keys/Commands/picker entries, the EONW action and exact contract text. Stop for Lucca.
3. Implement after approval.

## Acceptance

- Runtime tests: moving a pane and a tab between workspaces keeps the terminal session, its
  attention record and pins; IDs stay stable; the emptied-workspace rule holds.
- The a9g0.8 test (every EONW action has a CLI path) stays green.
- One isolated installed observation: a pane running `top` moved to another workspace keeps
  running and its scrollback; a tab moved likewise; done by CLI with the picker closed.
- CHANGELOG.md and docs/USAGE.md updated; review per AGENTS.md (converge plus Codex).

## Scope boundary

Same window only. Not: moving across windows (the investigation bead), drag and drop.

When Lucca approves the proposal (step 2), split it like eon-agent-background-work-yte0 before code: (a) Runtime move + EONW bump + EON-C33/EON-C10 text + CLI paths + runtime tests; (b) Venus Commands/picker/key entries + the isolated installed observation. eon-move-across-windows-akdu waits on this bead per Lucca's 'P2, after 1'; if the split happens, it can wait on (a) only, since it reuses the CLI and landing rules, not the Venus entries.

title: Choose a slimmer pane chrome: titles in thin borders instead of header bars
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-10-22 ~18:45 -03, comparing a screenshot of another terminal tool: "maybe zellij and rex
borders are better", "why did we pick a thick pane bar?". He asked for this bead ("create the bead")
and for an investigation of the best shape for Eon.

The other tool draws each pane as a thin rounded single-line border with its title embedded in the
top border line ("╭ sidebar ──", "╭ editor ──"). He called it "rex". Identify it in the reference
gate, or record it as unidentified.

## Current shape and how it came about

- VEN-C8 (venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md, Eon workspace presentation): each column is an accordion. Every
  pane in the active tab has a visible ordered header row, and only the selected pane shows its
  terminal body; the others collapse to their header. Headers show `pN  <cwd>`, act as hit
  targets, have hover/selected fills, and are AccessKit buttons. `--pane-frames true|false` toggles
  the rounded card borders and separators.
- The header row came from ven-599 (2026-08-10, accordion navigation), where a collapsed pane is
  only its header. The window title moved into pane chrome with eon-adopt-pane-chrome-undecorated-tz0.
  Later styling (eon-sheet-round-corners-ab92, eon-sheet-bottom-square-top-thick-5iy8) built on it.
  No bead compared the header row with border-embedded titles. The only layout reference then was
  Canario/Rio for accordion geometry.

## Goal

Pick the pane chrome shape that gives the terminal the most rows and reads cleanly, while keeping
the accordion, click targets, focus visibility and accessibility. Candidate recommended so far
(not decided): the expanded pane gets a thin rounded frame with `pN ~/dir` in its top border, and
collapsed panes become one-line border-title rows, like Zellij's stacked panes.

## Reference gate (before code shape)

Record, at inspected versions: Zellij normal frames and stacked panes, the "rex" tool, tmux
`pane-border-status`, and WezTerm/kitty pane and tab titles. For each candidate, note vertical
space spent per pane, selection, hover and focus, hit areas, `--pane-frames false`, cell-grid
alignment and fractional scaling. A coordinator-run investigation (2026-10-22) will add its findings
here as a comment. Start from them.

## Contract

VEN-C8 changes (header and frame presentation). Bring Lucca the exact wording before code, with
the cheapest confirming artifact first: a mockup or one isolated installed screenshot of the
candidate next to the current shape.

## Portability disposition

neutral (Venus rendering; no platform API).

## Prerequisites

Start after m798, eon-1u9e and eon-10qt land. They touch the same Venus render and input code.

## Scope

In scope: pane header and frame geometry and drawing in Venus (render/chrome.rs, scene geometry),
hit targets, AccessKit bounds, `--pane-frames` behavior, VEN-C8 text, `venus/CHANGELOG.md`,
`CHANGELOG.md`, and the Venus suite geometry tests.
Out of scope: the Eon Bar (VEN-C21), popups (VEN-C18), the accordion model itself, and new
configuration options unless Lucca asks.

## Acceptance

- Lucca approves the chosen shape from a screenshot or mockup before implementation.
- A column of N panes spends measurably fewer rows on chrome than today (record before and after).
- Selection, hover and keyboard focus stay distinct. Every pane stays clickable with a hit area of
  at least one cell row. AccessKit names and order are unchanged.
- One isolated installed dogfood screenshot of the final shape.
close_reason: Shape C title rules landed: thin mid-row rules with labels, shared title metric, shared painted card top; proof in comments

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Investigation (coordinator subagent, 2026-10-22, edge 6a3b231). Evidence: headers are round(1.5 x cell) = 27 px at scale 1 (venus/src/scene.rs:747-754), with full-width selected/hover fills (render/chrome.rs:772-797), a 1 px card outline and separators (render.rs:1037-1066), and 8 px gap/radius (scene.rs:795-797). A column spends 27*N + 24 px; in a 1280x720 window the card holds 33/31/30/28 rows for N=1..4. The 1.5-cell height was inherited (ven-pane-stack-chrome-suu kept the existing height; venus/docs/REFERENCES.md:186-188). No thinner shape was compared, and neither VEN-C8 nor EON-C8 fixes the height. Rex = Superlogical Rex (closed-source native macOS app; Eon's column cards already cite it, REFERENCES.md:180-184). The screenshot's box-drawing titles and grip marks are TUI output, most likely Zellij/Nova, not Rex. Zellij (pane_boundaries_frame.rs at c7c4ce42) puts the title in the top border and collapses stacked panes to one title row. Its space cost is about the same as Eon's (N+1 rows vs 1.5N); Eon's 'thickness' is mostly the 27 px filled band. Candidates: A, thin bars (one 18 px row, keep fills; one constant, no contract text change; +1 row at N=2-3, +2 at N=4). B, Zellij-literal per-pane boxes (fights the column cards, largest render change, rewrites the frames clause). C, title rule: an 18 px header row whose 1 px separator runs at mid-height and breaks around the label (first pane's rule = card top edge, like 'p1 ~/x' inside the border). Selected = accent-coloured rule and bright label; hover = pill behind the label; focus = rounded outline. The hit target stays the full row. Frameless mode = label only. Changes the VEN-C8 :579-587 and EON-C8 :385-402 wording. Recommendation: C, falling back to A if label-in-line reads poorly at 16 px. Cheapest check before code: a pixel-exact static mockup (1280x720) of current, A and C with 1/3/4 panes and selected/hover/focus states, for Lucca to pick.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Mockup (2026-10-22, edge d10c0ad, no repo or Venus changes). A canvas page in the session scratchpad, rendered at 1280x720 by headless Chrome, redraws pane chrome from the Venus constants: 40 px bar, 27 px current headers vs 18 px for A and C, 8 px gap/radius, card 8..1272 x 40..687, hints row at 687, cell 10x18, DejaVu Sans Mono 16. Pixel samples match the colours in render.rs/chrome.rs (accent 126,231,185; outline 58,75,91). Text baselines are approximate (+-1 px); the bar and hint contents are simplified. Nine frames: current, A and C at 1/3/4 panes. States: 1 pane = selected plus keyboard focus; 3 panes = p2 selected, hover p3; 4 panes = p3 selected plus focus, hover p1. Each terminal prints its tput lines value: current 33/30/28, A and C 33/31/30. C as drawn: a 1 px mid-row rule breaks 6 px around the label; the first rule is the card's top edge, so the card outline starts at y=49. Selected = accent rule plus bright label. Hover = a pill in 23,34,46. Focus = an accent pill outline. Pills are inset 1 px so they never cover a neighbouring rule or the card edge. Seen at 1:1: A's and current's hover fill (16,22,32) barely shows. C stays legible at 4 panes. Waiting for Lucca's pick.

Fallback A if C's label-in-line reads poorly in the real font on the first installed screenshot. Implementation goes to a fresh agent after eon-final-close-prompt-and-detach-key-m798 lands. The VEN-C8/EON-C8 wording goes to Lucca before code.

title: Let eon pane create start a command in the new pane
description:
## Why

On 2026-10-22 Lucca asked the orchestrating agent to open two new panes in his tab, start
Claude in each and give them instructions. The agent could create the panes (`eon pane create`)
but not start anything in them: a new pane always runs the default shell, and Eon has no way to
run a command there. Lucca had to paste a `claude "..."` line into each pane himself. He called
it a gap ("this seems like a gap maybe? lets create beads").

Users and agents expect "open a pane running X" from a terminal workspace. tmux has
`split-window CMD`, Zellij has `zellij run -- CMD`, WezTerm has `wezterm cli split-pane -- CMD`,
and kitty has `kitten @ launch CMD`. This matters most for Eon's main use case, supervising
coding agents.

## Evidence (edge b1a275a)

- `docs/USAGE.md` command table: `eon pane create [--json]` takes no command;
  `eon run [-- COMMAND...]` and `eon edit [--json] -- FILE` do.
- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/workspace.rs:362-370`: `Action::Edit` already starts a pane
  with an exact argv through `prepare(&PopupCommand::Argv(..), &tab.directory)` and
  `create_pane(.., LaunchCommand::Tool(argv), ..)`. The mechanism exists; only the action and
  CLI surface are missing.
- `runtime/crates/eon-workspace-protocol/src/v14.rs:65,126,509,636`: `WorkspaceAction::CreatePane`
  carries no payload, so passing a command needs a new or extended EONW action.
- `docs/CONTRACTS.md:715-735` (EON-C10): `pane create` placement, caller column and popup
  dismissal rules. The new form must keep them.

## Proposed contract (for Lucca's approval before code)

- `eon pane create [--json] -- COMMAND [ARGS...]` starts a new pane, placed exactly as
  `eon pane create` places it, at the tab's directory, running COMMAND as an exact argv with no
  shell interpretation. This matches `eon run -- COMMAND` and `eon edit`. When COMMAND exits,
  the pane ends like any other terminal (EON-C8 ended-terminal rules); it does not fall back to a
  shell.
- Failures: an empty COMMAND after `--` is a usage error; a command that cannot start reports
  the error and leaves no dead pane. All other `pane create` failures stay as they are.
- `--json` reports the new pane ID (and its terminal ID), so an agent can then `eon focus` it or
  address it.

## Scope

In scope: the EON-C10 text change, the EONW action carrying the argv (Runtime owns validation
and bounds, reusing `Action::Edit`'s path), the `eon` CLI parsing, `docs/USAGE.md`, the
`CHANGELOG.md` entry, and one focused check.

Out of scope:
- typing or sending input into an existing pane (tmux `send-keys`, WezTerm `send-text`);
  that needs its own trust-boundary decision;
- `eon tab create -- COMMAND` (file separately if wanted);
- Venus key bindings.

## Reference gate (consequential: protocol/wire change)

Before code, record in this bead: the comparable CLIs above at inspected revisions (argv versus
shell string, cwd, what happens on exit, focus behavior), the EONW versioning decision (extend
v14 or add a v15 action, and what an old supervisor answers), and the size bounds reused from
`MAX_*` in the protocol crate.

## Acceptance

- `eon pane create -- claude "prime, then continue X"` run from an Eon terminal opens a pane in
  the caller's column running that exact argv at the tab directory, and `--json` names it.
- An unknown command reports an error and adds no pane.

## Verification

- Focused red/green test at the existing workspace-control harness
  (`eon/crates/eon/tests/workspace_control.rs`) through `nix develop -c eon-test`.
- One isolated installed observation (headless Sway) per AGENTS.md, since this is installed
  runtime behavior, plus the full affected Rust and Nix surfaces for the protocol change.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop for Lucca's approval of the contract text and the EONW versioning choice.
- Stop if the change would let a process outside the caller's generation or window start
  commands.

(2) EONW: ship alone as v15 now, accepting one more restart (the new eon cannot manage EONW 14 generations); yx8.7 takes v16 later. Rejected: holding n6ga to share yx8.7's bump (delays it behind yx8.6/yx8.7).

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Reference evidence (2026-10-22, research subagent of the orchestrator session; source read at pinned revisions). Discovery input for the reference gate, not yet the gate record.

Revisions: tmux 3.8 7f2a35ad3321f9ba57a1062ca73b1f3ff26aca53; Zellij v0.45.1 efd8fd5a89a20c07a111d248ad7fce53848d2c18; WezTerm main e2a98e1b8af156988ad0ac778658ac27b60a55fb; kitty v0.49.2 b2cb871254fbdac19a085188813c8dfb258b95cd.

- argv vs shell: Zellij, WezTerm and kitty use argv only. tmux runs one argument through `$default-shell -c` and execs two or more directly (tmux.1 L983-1022, spawn.c L547-575).
- Default cwd: Zellij uses the caller's cwd (src/main.rs L58), WezTerm the split pane's (mux/src/lib.rs L1163-1193), tmux the session start directory (spawn.c L290-305), kitty its process cwd (kitty/child.py L358). All take --cwd (tmux -c).
- On exit: tmux, WezTerm and kitty close the pane by default. Zellij holds it with EXIT CODE, re-run on Enter (zellij-server/src/ui/hint_text.rs).
- Command not found: WezTerm fails the spawn before inserting the pane, so the CLI errors and no pane appears (mux/src/domain.rs L101-108). Zellij holds a "Command not found" pane; kitty shows an error and waits; tmux argv _exit(1)s and the pane closes.
- Focus: all four focus the new pane; tmux -d, Zellij --no-focus and kitty --keep-focus keep focus where it was (WezTerm has no flag).
- Output: Zellij, WezTerm and kitty print the new id; tmux prints it with -P/-F.
- Access: all rely on a per-user socket or server-owner access. kitty additionally gates remote control (allow_remote_control defaults to no; kitty/options/definition.py L2913-2944). tmux $TMUX_PANE, WezTerm WEZTERM_PANE and kitty --self target the caller.
- Bearing on the approved text: argv with no shell matches 3/4; closing on exit matches 3/4 and EON-C8; failing before any pane is created matches WezTerm and the approved "adds no pane"; the tab-directory cwd matches none exactly. Open: EON-C10 L812 "does not ... expose commands over EONW" and the ecne.2 rejection of argv over EONW. Lucca has been asked whether to amend the boundary.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Decision (Lucca, 2026-10-22, chose option 1 'Change the boundary on purpose'): this deliberately reverses eon-ecne.2's rejection of argv over EONW, for pane create only. EON-C10 gains: a command-carrying pane-create request is accepted only with a caller naming a live terminal of the addressed supervisor (from an Eon terminal of that window); without one it is refused and changes nothing. The caller check expresses intent, not security: the socket is 0600 under /run/user, any same-UID process can already run any command, and caller identities are readable by same-UID processes. EON-C10's 'does not ... expose commands over EONW' (docs/CONTRACTS.md:812) is amended to name this one exception. Rejected: a config allow-list of commands (cannot carry a per-call prompt such as claude "prime, then continue X"); dropping the bead.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Reference gate (eon-n6ga, 2026-10-22; consequential: EONW wire change and a trust-boundary amendment).

- Behavior and owners: `pane create [--json] -- COMMAND...` parsing, Eon Runtime CLI (cli.rs `parse_command_pane_arguments`; the argv passes through unchanged as raw bytes). Wire value `CreateCommandPane { argv }` (tag 27; 1-256 arguments, each up to 32 KiB with no NUL, first non-empty, the whole request within the 2 MiB frame): eon-workspace-protocol v15. Caller gate, placement, cwd and program preflight: Runtime workspace (workspace.rs `apply`), through the existing popup preflight (`prepare_popup_command`: a bare name resolves through the terminal PATH, a relative one against the tab directory) and `create_pane`, as `Edit` does. Orbit owns the terminal.
- Routes read: the research comment above (tmux 3.8, Zellij v0.45.1, WezTerm e2a98e1b, kitty v0.49.2), plus Eon's own precedent eon-ecne.2 (08151c3 wire, 22aa25d graph).
- Kept: exact-version EONW with no negotiation; `pane create` placement, caller targeting and popup dismissal (EON-C10); no shell interpretation (as `eon run --` and popup argv); argv as in 3 of the 4 tools.
- Decisions: argv with no shell (Zellij, WezTerm, kitty; tmux with 2+ args). The pane closes when the command exits (tmux, WezTerm, kitty, EON-C8), not Zellij's held pane. A missing or non-executable program fails before any pane exists (WezTerm). Working directory is the tab directory, like every Eon pane (matches none of the four exactly; a `--cwd` option is left for later). The 32 KiB per-argument cap leaves room for long agent prompts and fits the u16 field length; Linux allows 128 KiB, so longer prompts belong in a file.
- Rejected: shell strings (quoting bugs, see tmux's one-argument form); a config allow-list (decision comment); holding the pane on exit; sharing yx8.7's EONW bump.
- Checks: v15 wire bytes plus invalid and bound cases (`messages_keep_their_wire_bytes`, `command_panes_bound_their_argv`, the invalid table); runtime `a_command_pane_runs_its_exact_argv_only_for_a_calling_terminal` (caller-required, preflight failure unchanged, exact argv at the tab directory); CLI `command_pane_parser_passes_the_argv_through`; end to end `commands_from_a_terminal_target_its_column_and_stale_callers_change_nothing` (real binary: refused without EON_TERMINAL with caller-required, exit 1, unchanged snapshot; --json names p5; Orbit child argv ends `hx\0two words\0`); one installed observation.
- Accepted gaps: (1) The component graph moves to EONW 15 in a second commit that cites this one as producer and consumer proof, as 22aa25d followed 08151c3. (2) A program that passes preflight but then fails to exec (e.g. a script with a missing interpreter) can leave a calling popup hidden or stopped. That path already exists for `pane create` and `eon edit` (`create_pane` dismisses the popup before Orbit starts), and this change does not add it; the contract claims "changes nothing" only for a missing or non-executable program. (3) The pane's working directory is not configurable per call.

title: Decide: session switching in Eon 1.0
description:
## Decision

Does Eon 1.0 support switching sessions, and if it does, in what form? Lucca asked for this
bead (2026-10-22: "open a p1 bead to decide about session switching in 1.0").

"Session" here means a whole Eon workspace (a window's tabs, panes and terminals), as in tmux
sessions or Zellij's session manager. It doesn't mean an Orbit Session ID, which is a technical
identity (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md#naming-boundary). Settle the product term as part of the decision.

## What exists today (edge 891e21f)

- EON-C23, independent Eon windows: `eon window new`, the launcher action, or Alt+Shift+N opens a
  second native window with its own supervisor, tabs and durable Orbit terminals.
  `eon windows` lists windows, `eon window attach ID` re-presents a detached window, and
  `eon window stop ID` stops one window.
- Closing a window detaches it. `eon attach [GENERATION]` and `eon generations` handle
  generations. Each workspace is shown in its own OS window, and nothing switches the current window
  to show another workspace.
- No picker lists detached workspaces inside Eon. Users find them only through the CLI.

## Questions to decide

1. Is session switching in 1.0 scope (label release-1), or deferred?
2. Shape:
   - A: no in-window switching. Add a picker (popup or Commands entry) that lists windows,
     including detached ones, and focuses or attaches the chosen one in its own OS window.
     It reuses EON-C23.
   - B: in-window switching. The current window's presentation swaps to another workspace,
     like tmux `switch-client` or Zellij's session-manager. Venus would re-present a different
     supervisor's workspace in the same surface.
   - C: named, persistent sessions, created and resumed by name (`eon session NAME`), with A or B
     for switching.
3. Naming: "window", "workspace" or "session" for users, consistent with the naming boundary.
4. Contracts it touches: EON-C23 and VEN-C8/VEN-C18 (picker), and EONW if B changes the
   presentation handoff.

## Reference gate

Before the proposal, record at inspected versions: tmux sessions (`choose-tree`, `switch-client`),
Zellij session-manager (attach and switch, resurrection), WezTerm workspaces (`SwitchToWorkspace`),
kitty sessions, and Superlogical Rex if documented (~/pjs/refs/agent-sidebar-research). For each,
note how users discover detached sessions, whether switching stays in one OS window, and how
naming works.

## Recommendation (to confirm after the reference gate)

Lean A for 1.0. It closes the real gap, which is that detached workspaces are invisible inside
Eon, using the proven EON-C23 mechanism and no new presentation lifecycle. B needs Venus to tear
down and re-present another supervisor in one surface. That's a new lifecycle and trust boundary,
and better after 1.0 unless the reference gate shows users expect it on day one. Bring Lucca a
numbered proposal with a recommendation for each question.

## Scope

This bead decides only: a written proposal, Lucca's decisions recorded here, and implementation
beads filed for the chosen shape (each bead sized for one session). No code.

## Acceptance

- Lucca's decisions on questions 1-4 are recorded on this bead.
- If anything is in 1.0, implementation beads exist with the release-1 label, their contracts
  named, and their dependencies set.

comments.text:
Reference gate (2026-10-22, edge b5a6b1a). Sources were read at pinned revisions, not from memory. E means evidence, I means inference. Full notes with file:line citations stay outside the repo; the citations below are the load-bearing ones.

## Pinned sources

- tmux tag 3.8 7f2a35ad3321f9ba57a1062ca73b1f3ff26aca53; tmux-resurrect cff343cf9e81983d3da0c8562b01616f12e8d548; tmux-continuum 0698e8f4b17d6454c71bf5212895ec055c578da0
- Zellij v0.45.1 efd8fd5a89a20c07a111d248ad7fce53848d2c18; zellij.dev docs 111f441276770f871419949a6695bbad6b518551
- WezTerm main e2a98e1b8af156988ad0ac778658ac27b60a55fb (2026-10-10); kitty v0.49.2 b2cb871254fbdac19a085188813c8dfb258b95cd
- Rex: closed source. Public docs snapshot llms-full.txt, sha256 fc17b069a3c46efd37a4c9bdc934fbb7928f43c207a00f14f8378d5018e8ffe6 (~/pjs/refs/agent-sidebar-research/web)
- herdr 143bf5fd4781d164260c63fe28e7dc08054ad32f; tuios 0047c409185f37e568933a566e0253b2a6e96a96
- All clones are under ~/pjs/refs.

## Discovery of detached sessions

- **E, every reference:** detached work is listed in the UI as well as on the CLI.
  - tmux: `C-b s` choose-tree and the 3.8 `C-b S-Tab` fuzzy switcher. Rows read "N windows, attached|detached", with an info view of activity and last-attached times (key-bindings.c:439-442; window-switch.c:42-52; window-tree.c:194-217).
  - Zellij: the session-manager lists live sessions, then exited ones, by recency. Rows show "N tabs, M panes, K clients"; the current session is omitted (session-manager single_screen.rs:22-104, components.rs:75-200).
  - WezTerm: launcher and palette (launcher.rs:273-294).
  - kitty: `goto_session` picker (session.py:440-585).
  - Rex: `session.switch` "Change Session…", with an indicator for completed or blocked tasks (llms-full L232, L2366).
  - tuios: sidebar session section plus the `Ctrl+B S` switcher.
  - herdr: sidebar and Goto list workspaces with their agent state. Its named sessions are CLI-only.
  - CLI lists: `tmux ls -F`, `zellij ls`, `wezterm cli list`, `rex ls --json`, `tuios ls --json`, `herdr session list`.
- **E, Eon (gap):**
  - Detached windows are visible only through `eon windows`, which does not say whether a window is presented or detached. The Runtime reply has no presentation field (runtime v17.rs:348-356), and attach always reads as available (supervisor.rs:1781-1788).
  - The listing omits the default workspace, because it lives outside `w/` (windows.rs:255-301).
  - Commands > List windows is read-only output (cli.rs:106-200).
  - Windows have no name; the OS title is the selected terminal's title (venus application.rs:3898-3902).

## Switching: one OS window or several

- **E, in place:** tmux `switch-client` (cmd-switch-client.c:49-167), Zellij (client re-attaches to the other server's socket; zellij-client lib.rs:1448-1635), tuios (client rebuilds its view; os.go:810-860) and herdr workspaces all switch inside one terminal. The session left behind keeps running detached.
- **I:** that is forced. Terminal multiplexers own no OS windows.
- **E, GUI terminals:**
  - kitty switches by focusing the session's window, opening its OS window if needed (session.py:371-434, boss.py:708-733). Its docs call one session per OS window "the natural way"; several sessions can also share one OS window, the others' tabs hidden by a tab filter.
  - WezTerm swaps *every* GUI window of the client to the new workspace. `reconcile_workspace` reuses, closes and opens OS windows (wezterm-gui frontend.rs:359-470). When the last window of a workspace closes, the GUI jumps to another workspace (:364-379). A recent fix covers a render freeze when workspaces close (changelog.md:306).
  - Rex does not document multi-window behaviour.
- **E, Eon cost of in-window switching (shape B):**
  - Venus parses its workspace socket once (venus launch.rs:187-197) and exits when the control stream closes (VEN-C14).
  - The supervisor spawns and owns its one Venus (supervisor.rs:382-454, :986).
  - EONW `Present` has no target (v17.rs:65-67).
  - VEN-C23 excludes a multi-window event loop (:1245-1247).
  - EON-C31 seen-marking and popup cleanup key on "Venus attached" (supervisor.rs:1014, :1399-1413).
  - Today only Eon Runtime chooses and validates a supervisor (`validate_runtime`, supervisor.rs:330-365).
- **I:** B would change EON-C11, EON-C23, EON-C10, EON-C31, EONW, VEN-C3, VEN-C8, VEN-C14, VEN-C18 and VEN-C23, and add a trust boundary where Venus picks a supervisor.
- **E, focus on Wayland:**
  - Presenting an already-presented, unfocused window only requests attention (application.rs:3541-3548). VEN-C14 notes that winit cannot focus directly and that xdg activation is controlled by the compositor.
  - venus/docs/REFERENCES.md:680-693 rejects carrying a platform token in EONW.
  - Attaching a detached window opens a new toplevel.

## Naming

- **E:**
  - tmux defaults to numbers, requires unique names, and resolves `new -A -s NAME` as create-or-attach (cmd-new-session.c:122-140).
  - In Zellij the random adjective-noun name is the only identity. Rename renames the socket and cache directory, non-atomically, with a TODO in the source (screen.rs:11476-11553).
  - kitty takes the name from the session file's basename and has no rename, so two files with the same basename collide.
  - WezTerm's rename has no collision check (mux lib.rs:652-675).
  - Rex keeps a stable, never-reused ID plus an optional label. Targets resolve as ID > label > position, and an ambiguous target exits 3 without acting (L963-1018). tuios likewise separates its `set-session-name` label.
  - herdr auto-labels each workspace from its git repo or cwd (discovery.rs:24-43).
- **I:** name-as-identity is where Zellij and kitty break. Rex's ID plus label avoids that.
- **E, Eon:**
  - ARCHITECTURE.md:34-47 defines workspace, tab, pane, column and terminal. "Session" is technical only (`session-N`, JSON fields), and yx8.11 uses "session name" for an agent's own session.
  - Product text and the CLI say "window" (`eon window new`, `eon windows`). Window, workspace and supervisor namespace are 1:1:1.

## Persistence and resurrection

- **E:**
  - tmux core keeps sessions in memory only. Resurrect saves layout and working directories, and restores programs by typing their commands into new shells, allowlist only; its docs call `:all:` dangerous (process_restore_helpers.sh:38, restoring_programs.md:8-49).
  - Zellij serializes a KDL layout every 60 s. Every saved command waits behind "Press ENTER to run" (session_serialization.rs:488-496). Exited sessions never expire. Its changelog shows a long run of resurrection fixes.
  - kitty persists only session files (`save_as_session`); WezTerm keeps nothing past its mux server.
  - herdr and tuios restore structure with fresh shells and label it (`TUIOS_RESTORED=1`). Agents resume through their own resume commands.
  - Rex keeps sessions live only.
- **I:** no reference keeps live processes across a reboot. Eon's labelled-restore question is already owned by eon-reboot-restore-im8y (release-1) and stays there.

## Keyboard flows

- **E:**
  - tmux binds `s`, `S-Tab`, `(`, `)`, `L` and `$`.
  - Zellij uses `Ctrl o w`. Inside the manager, typing filters or names a new session; Enter attaches, resurrects or creates.
  - tuios binds `Ctrl+B S` and alt+shift+n/p.
  - WezTerm, kitty and Rex bind nothing by default.
  - Eon's free Alt+Shift letters include S. Alt+Shift+D is being taken by m798.
- **I:** in a GUI, the window manager's own window switching already covers next, previous and last.

## Agent and CLI control

- **E:**
  - Rex: `rex ls/new --json` and `rex api call session.*`. Agents open work without taking focus, and showing a session to the user is opt-in (L1082-1089).
  - herdr: `workspace create --no-focus` returns IDs as JSON, with an explicit `workspace focus` (cli-reference.mdx:205).
  - tuios: verbs that need a client return `needs_client`.
  - Zellij: a scripted switch moves the last-active client and cannot name a target (route.rs:2416-2433).
  - WezTerm has no CLI command that switches workspace.
- **E, Eon:**
  - `window new` prints the ID; `windows` and `window stop` take `--json`, but `window attach` does not.
  - There is no `--window` targeting. Commands run inside a window target it through the inherited `EON_WINDOW_RUNTIME_DIR` (sessions.rs:1180-1200).

## Other Eon facts found

- **E:** `eon window attach ID` attaches only the exact current generation (windows.rs:176-191, generation.rs:430-450).
- **I:** after a profile upgrade, a window detached under the old generation cannot be reattached from the new CLI. A picker must show such a window honestly.
- **E:** docs/REFERENCES.md has no route for tmux, Zellij, WezTerm workspaces or kitty sessions. The nearest are the routes at :107 (Ghosthub: detach-only close, fresh attach), :171 (TUIOS), :200 (pickers: Kitty overlays, Zellij in-place commands, Eon-owned fzf popups), :430 (cmux jump-to-work) and :479 (recovering an interrupted session).

comments.text:
Decision (2026-10-22). Lucca pre-approved this bead's pick ("auto-approve its pick", relayed by the overseer and recorded above). The pick follows the reference gate in the previous comment.

1. **Scope:** session switching is in 1.0 (release-1), as Lucca decided.
2. **Shape:** A, plus the ID-and-label half of C.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Shape D against A and B (2026-10-22, edge 3777926). Code read only. E means evidence, I means inference. This comment calls the new layer a "group" until the noun is chosen.

## D: several groups inside one supervisor, one window showing one group at a time

**Today (E):**
- The supervisor holds one `Workspace` (supervisor.rs:980-994). It has tabs, active, and the ID counters `next_tab`, `next_pane`, `next_session` and `next_popup` (workspace.rs:124-135).
- The EONW v17 snapshot is built from it (workspace.rs:218-275, v17.rs:316-323), and Venus polls it every 250 ms.
- Venus attaches Orbit only for what is visible: the active tab's selected pane or popup, plus the expanded panes of the other columns (model.rs:173-215). When the active tab or the tab list changes, it ends zoom, cancels scroll and re-attaches (application.rs:1513-1556).

**I:** swapping the shown group looks to Venus like a tab switch, because background tabs are already detached from view. Rendering and ORB-C3 are unaffected.

**What D needs:**
- **A group layer in the runtime.** One ID allocator shared across groups. Today's per-workspace counters would collide on socket names (`session-N.sock`, `kN.sock`) and on tab IDs. A stale `CloseTab` sent across a switch could hit another group's `t2` (application.rs:1762, :4135).
- **A new EONW version:**
  - `tabs` and `active_tab` stay the shown group's.
  - New fields `groups[{id,name,tab count,attention rollup}]` and `active_group`.
  - Group requests: new, switch, rename, close.
  - Replies scoped to the caller's group.

  A filtered snapshot alone is not enough: the CLI, the m798 final-close prompt (decided from `tabs.len()`) and the shown-group label all need the extra data.
- **Close semantics.** Closing a group's final tab switches to the most recent other group. Only the last group's final close ends the window. Today the window ends when no terminals remain (supervisor.rs:899).
- **CLI targeting.** No new environment variable is needed: `EON_TERMINAL` resolves to a tab and so to its group (supervisor.rs:1230-1252). Callers outside a group get the shown group or `--group`.
- **The picker** is an Eon-owned fzf popup, as Commands is (VEN-C18 holds).

**Contracts under D:**
- **EON-C8:** the group layer. Traversal, tab moves and the final-tab rule work per group. Recovery collapses everything into `t1` (:500-502).
- **EON-C10:** group requests, reply scoping, `CreateTab` targeting, and Commands entries. "Quit this window" stops every group.
- **EON-C11:** wording only.
- **EON-C23:** a window holds N groups.
- **EON-C31:** focus means the shown group's active tab, and the rollup is per group. Decide whether the attention queue spans groups and switches group on a jump.
- **EON-C28:** the `eon workspace --json` fields freeze at 1.0, so D lands before the eon-igae.11 fixture.
- **VEN-C8:** shows the shown group's tabs.
- **VEN-C21:** a group label in the bar.
- **Unchanged:** VEN-C14, VEN-C18, VEN-C23. No trust boundary and no Venus lifecycle change.

## Risks of D

**(a) Blast radius (E):**
- The supervisor is a single-threaded loop. Venus exits when the control stream ends (VEN-C14).
- Orbit runs survive a crash, and a replacement supervisor of the same generation adopts them (EON-C15; its installed proof is still open).
- Recovery projects everything into one tab, `t1` (workspace.rs:176-216), and no topology is persisted.

**I:** one supervisor crash closes the window and flattens all N groups into one tab. `eon stop`, Quit this window, and the last group's final close stop every group. Blast radius is strictly coarser than in A.

**(b) Detach:** closing the window or Alt+Shift+D detaches all groups together. A hidden group is like a background tab, not "detached". Stopping one group means closing its tabs.

**(c) Attention:** hidden groups never hold focus, so their raises stay unseen, which is correct. The poller already covers every terminal.

**(d) Generations:** after a profile upgrade, the old supervisor keeps all of its groups. The new window cannot switch to them, because that would be B. The known stranding bug therefore strands N groups at once.

**(e) Load:** the terminals are the same either way, and D runs one quota poller instead of N.

## B re-checked

**E:** Venus fixes its socket at launch (launch.rs:187-197, transport.rs:216-238). The supervisor owns its Venus (supervisor.rs:382-622), and seen-marking keys on that child (:1009-1017).

**I:** under B,
- supervisor A would mark its own focused terminal seen while Venus shows B, and B would never mark anything seen;
- `window attach B` would spawn a second Venus;
- quitting A would kill the view of B.

The earlier cost of about ten contracts plus a trust boundary holds.

## Fit with A, and migration

- D and A coexist: each window is a supervisor holding N groups, and New window still works.
- "Move a group into its own window" would need an Orbit lease handoff, which the EON-C15 boundary excludes. That is post-1.0.
- Nothing is persisted, so today's workspace becomes group 1 in the next generation.
- eon-reboot-restore-im8y must save group membership and names when it lands.

## Size: about 9 beads, each one session

1. D0 contracts and the user noun (Lucca approves).
2. D1 runtime group layer and shared allocator. Behaviour is unchanged with one group, and the wire is unchanged.
3. D2 the next EONW version with groups and group requests. It folds after eon-agent-sidebar-yx8.7, which also bumps EONW.
4. D3 close and exit semantics.
5. D4 CLI list/new/switch/rename/close and `--group`.
6. D5 the Alt+Shift+S picker.
7. D6 the Venus bar label and the m798 prompt wording.
8. D7 the per-group attention rollup and picker sort.
9. D8 the batch installed proof.

Order: D0 → D1 → D2 → {D3, D4} → D5 → D6 → D7 → D8.

**What survives of A:**
- 1opf → group names (D4).
- i92k → the group picker (D5).
- vgfx → the per-group rollup (D7).
- suox shrinks to window listing state and the default-workspace entry. That is optional under D.
