title: Orbit dies without a tombstone when a stopped child is not reaped
description:
## Report

The trigger of eon-tab-close-kills-supervisor-7iap's 13:22 -03 crash (2026-10-23). Lucca closed tab
t3. Its terminal session-32 had started 6 s earlier, under Orbit
/nix/store/7vv3pwvpyir2r0vgmjczf90gw3ji2fbg-yazelix-orbit-0.1.0 (bend-orbit, PID 675175). Its stderr,
caught by Lucca's private wrapper (~/.local/share/eon/orbit-window/logs/675175.log), ends with:

```
PTY child was not reaped after canonical session exit
```

Approved by Lucca, 2026-10-23 ("create the beads", answering the overseer's item 9: file it, P1).

## Mechanism (as read at edge 0ca4a64)

- The Runtime's Stop reaches `Host::stop_explicitly` (orbit/src/host.rs ~1390). `contain()` (~1507)
  sends SIGHUP to the child and the foreground group, waits 500 ms, sends SIGKILL, waits 2 s. If
  the child is still unreaped, the fact is `NotReaped`.
- The Bend worker answers `Boundary.NotReaped` with `IO.die(Unit, 1, ...)` (orbit/src/main.bend
  ~56). The worker's death takes the host's failure path; `RecordGuard`'s drop deletes the Live
  record and publishes no tombstone (orbit/src/management.rs ~585, host.rs ~1590).
- So the Runtime saw a stop that never confirmed and a record that vanished. eon-d8's 7iap fix
  makes the Runtime survive this, but the terminal still fails to close cleanly, and the
  outcome is indistinguishable from a crash.

## Questions to answer

1. Why did a child survive SIGKILL for 2 s? Candidates: a process in uninterruptible sleep (D
   state, e.g. a new tab's shell or tool doing I/O at startup), SIGKILL sent to the wrong group, or
   the child pid already being a zombie that `try_reap` mishandles. Reproduce: stop a terminal
   whose child is held in D state (e.g. a FUSE or `vfork` fixture), or a child that ignores SIGHUP
   and is slow to die.
2. What should Orbit do on NotReaped? Today it dies without a tombstone. Options: keep
   waiting and report a bounded stop failure through management with the record intact, or
   publish a tombstone that names the unreaped child so the Runtime reconciles it as lost. The
   owning contract is ORB-C12 (bounded PTY process-group shutdown). Any change to its failure
   text goes to Lucca first.

## Acceptance

- A red/green Orbit test, in the existing lifecycle harness, for the chosen NotReaped outcome.
- The Runtime sees a reconcilable terminal (a record or a tombstone) after a NotReaped stop.
- Orbit fmt and clippy, plus the Bend proof check (`orbit/PROOF.bend`) if the session policy changes.

## Scope

Orbit only. Not the Runtime containment (7iap) and not stderr logging (eon-euzm). Portability
disposition: expected `neutral`; record it.

## Related

eon-tab-close-kills-supervisor-7iap, eon-euzm.
close_reason: NotReaped keeps the run until reaped (ORB-C12 as approved); Nix checks, eon-test and isolated installed observation recorded

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Answers and decision (2026-10-23).

Q1, why the child outlived SIGKILL: it was a slow-dying child, not a wrong target and not try_reap mishandling a zombie. The close began at 13:22:03.882. Orbit's NotReaped line was written at 13:22:06.427 (the mtime of 675175.log), 2.545 s later, which is exactly SIGHUP + 500 ms + SIGKILL + 2 s. The worker's death then ran the host failure path's contain() a second time, with the same pid, signals and waitpid. The record was gone before the Runtime's 13:22:08.005 check, earlier than a second full contain could end (~08.93), so the child became reapable 2.5 to 4.1 s after the first SIGHUP. Linux delivers SIGKILL, but a task in uninterruptible sleep (page-fault I/O or reclaim on a loaded machine, FUSE/NFS) or a leader whose last thread is still exiting is reapable only once it leaves that state. A second occurrence has the same signature: orbit-window logs g1-6fa0eda…/session-36…log, 2026-10-21 20:37 -03, on a long-lived terminal. Which process the child was is not recoverable. Reproducer: the test ptrace-seizes Orbit's PTY child, which Yama scope 1 allows for a descendant. A ptraced zombie is visible only to its tracer until the tracer waits.

Q2, decision (Lucca, relayed by eon-overseer 2026-10-23 ~17:50 -03: "yes to everything"): option 1, built the lean way. Bend answers NotReaped with one Reap, and the host keeps the run and its Live record until the child is reaped, then publishes the ExplicitStop tombstone and answers Stopped. Termination signals still exit bounded, and nothing else is served during the wait. LAWS.bend `stopping` gains `case Boundary.NotReaped{}: reaping(moves)`, with its PROOF lemma and a sensitivity check, and NotReaped's answer moves into Session.step. ORB-C12 wording: Result "After escalation, Orbit requires the direct child to be reaped within two seconds." becomes "After escalation, management Stop succeeds once the direct child is reaped; a child not reaped within two seconds keeps the run and its live record until it is reaped, then Stop succeeds with its outcome. After a termination signal, Orbit requires the direct child to be reaped within two seconds." Important failures: "...cannot cause delayed signaling, and only a child the kernel never releases after a management Stop extends server lifetime." Rejected: exiting non-success while keeping the Live record (still crash-like), and a new tombstone outcome or Failure code (breaking orbit-protocol change). Full responsiveness while stopping is a separate P3 bead (eon-overseer files it). Portability: neutral.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Implementation and proof (2026-10-23). Correction to the decision comment: Lucca's "yes to everything" came at about 17:39 -03, not 17:50 (relayed by eon-overseer).

Change: Session.step answers NotReaped with one Reap, in place of the worker's IO.die in main.bend. LAWS.bend `stopping` gains `case Boundary.NotReaped{}: reaping(moves)`, and proof/step.bend's NotReaped lemma is regenerated with `step-proof` (lifecycle, view and management; only step.bend changed). host.rs: `reap()` honors a termination signal. `contain()` returns io::Result<bool>: an unreaped child that the SIGKILL could not reach is an error, so `stop_explicitly` takes the bounded host-failure path in place of an endless wait. The `run` failure path is unchanged. Docs: ORB-C12 text as approved, plus its Proof and Evidence; BEHAVIOR.md and LIFECYCLE.md; orbit/CHANGELOG.md and CHANGELOG.md, which note that Eon Runtime's 5 s Stop still fails a close whose child is reaped later.

Red/green, new real-PTY check `orbit-unreaped-stop` (tests/real_pty/unreaped_stop.rs). It ptrace-seizes Orbit's PTY child, which Yama scope 1 allows for a descendant, so the SIGKILLed zombie stays hidden from Orbit, then sends Stop through the lease. Red at edge efa9565 (eon-test): about 5.5 s after Stop the record was gone (NotFound), the incident's signature. Green: the record stays Live past two rounds of escalation and re-wait; once released, the lease hears Stopped{ExplicitStop, Signal(SIGKILL)}, the tombstone matches, and Orbit exits 0 silently. A second run sends SIGTERM during the wait: exit 143, no record. Sensitivity: the old policy (NotReaped answered with Nil) under the new law fails PROOF.bend at the NotReaped lemma.

Final proof, tree ffed0c12 (a06f10c plus this change; this commit's code tree), x86_64 Linux:
- `nix build --max-jobs 2 --no-link --keep-going` of all 43 `checks.x86_64-linux.orbit-*` checks: exit 0, ALL PROOFS CHECK, every real-PTY check `1 passed`, ptrace works in the Nix build sandbox.
- `nix develop -c eon-test` (workspace and installer): exit 0, 434 passed, 0 failed, 46 ignored in 24 suites.
- Earlier, on the candidate: cargo fmt --check and clippy -D warnings for yazelix-orbit are clean. Under plain eon-test, 5 real-PTY checks fail for lack of the Nix-check environment (schema_mismatch and terminal_identity need MISMATCHED_WORKER and the package terminfo; program_status, refused_flush and stopped_client_exit fail only there). All five pass as Nix checks.
Pending: the batch's isolated installed observation, with eon-hfzr, after the profile refresh (eon-overseer schedules it).

Review ledger: round 1 ran Codex xhigh and one Claude reviewer on candidate tree 5f350337. Codex had 2 blocking findings: a failed SIGKILL turned into an endless wait, and CHANGELOG overstated the tab close. Claude had 1, the same changelog issue; its nits were taken. The author edited the tree before Claude's report was in, a loop slip; Claude's checks had already run on the candidate. Fixes are in tree 1b72f7df. The narrow Codex re-check found nothing, and a fresh Claude round found nothing blocking; two nits (BEHAVIOR's SIGKILL-failure sentence omits "unreaped"; a law comment's placement) are left. Converged in 2 Codex passes and 2 Claude passes.

comments.text:
Installed batch observation (eon-orbit-stop-not-reaped-7vb4 + eon-reap-error-unstopped-hfzr), 2026-10-23 18:27 -03. Profile refreshed by eon-overseer from edge b1143190 (clean tree): /nix/store/ddxhzscqiqfysjas2ha6qrhkgk3h32d3-eon-0.1.1, run by that exact store path. x86_64 Linux, one isolated window: private headless Sway (pixman), env -i, private HOME and runtime dirs. (1) 7vb4: tab t2's shell (PID 1518888) was ptrace-seized, and `eon tab close t2 --json` ran. The close exited 0 after 3.55 s, and the supervisor logged "closed tab t2 in 3501 ms". Afterwards the workspace lists only t1 (session-1), and the supervisor runs on. title: Keep Orbit responsive while a management Stop waits for its child
description:
## Why

eon-orbit-stop-not-reaped-7vb4 (approved by Lucca, 2026-10-23, "yes to everything", item 3) makes a
management Stop wait for a child the kernel holds past Orbit's 2 s grace, instead of dying. It
builds this the lean way: while stopping, the host serves nothing but its reap and termination
signals. Management Status, a second manager, attach, and client input wait in the socket backlog
until the child is reaped, as they already do during today's 2.5 s contain. In the two known
incidents (2026-10-21 20:37 and 2026-10-23 13:22 -03) the wait lasted a few seconds.

Lucca approved filing full responsiveness separately, P3 (same message, item 4).

## Change

A Stopping-phase Bend policy for every fact Orbit can see while stopping: admit or refuse a peer,
answer Busy to a second manager, ignore client input, and ChildExited -> Reap. That needs new laws
in orbit/LAWS.bend (`stopping` today accepts only Reaped, ExitedBeforeStop, ObserverGone, Tick and
Selected; anything else marks the run Outside) and matching lemmas in orbit/PROOF.bend.

## Contract

ORB-C12 and the Orbit management contract. Wording and the new laws go to Lucca before code.

## Acceptance

- A lifecycle test with a held child: Status answers and a second Stop gets Busy during the wait,
  and the stop then succeeds.
- The Bend proof check stays green, with a sensitivity check for each new law.

## Prerequisites

eon-orbit-stop-not-reaped-7vb4 landed.

'stopping' in orbit/LAWS.bend:517-535 now accepts Reaped, ExitedBeforeStop, NotReaped (-> 'reaping', LAWS.bend:375), ObserverGone, Tick, Selected and Resources; the policy here must also cover the reaping wait.

title: Write why Orbit's worker ended to Orbit's stderr
description:
## Why

eon-euzm (landed cc62679) sends each Orbit host's stderr to a per-terminal log, and the supervisor
names that file. Its installed observation (2026-10-24) SIGKILLed a terminal's Orbit worker. The
supervisor named the log, but the log was empty: Orbit's host exits with status 1 without writing
why its worker ended. A user who opens the named log after a crash finds nothing.

Filed on Lucca's approval, 2026-10-24 ("agree", answering the overseer's item 34).

## Change

When Orbit's host takes its failure path because its worker ended or failed, write one line to
stderr before exiting. It should name what happened: the worker's exit status or terminating
signal, or the I/O error on the worker channel, plus the session and run. Keep it to one line per
failure. Orbit owns this, and the Runtime needs no change.

## Contract

Check ORB-C12 and Orbit's failure-reporting text. A new diagnostic line probably needs no contract
change; if it does, bring the wording to Lucca first.

## Acceptance

- An Orbit lifecycle test: kill the worker, and Orbit's stderr holds one line naming the signal.
  It fails on today's code.
- One installed check: SIGKILL a scratch terminal's worker, and the euzm log file holds that line.

## Scope

Orbit host only. Orbit fmt and clippy, and the Bend proof check only if the session policy changes
(it shouldn't). Portability disposition: neutral.

## Related

eon-euzm, eon-orbit-stop-not-reaped-7vb4.
close_reason: Orbit names a dead worker's status, the host's error and the run on stderr; guardian check and installed euzm-log check pass

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Design (2026-10-27, ztcq session).

Gap: in `orbit/src/host.rs` `run()`, when the worker dies the host contains the child, reaps the worker
within 500 ms and returns `Ok(status_code(status))` (137 after SIGKILL, the worker's code after IO.die),
so `main` prints nothing. Only an unreaped worker returns `Err`, which `main` prints.

Change: one stderr line just before the host exits with a dead worker's status, when no termination
signal stopped the host (an orderly stop stays silent):
`orbit: worker ended (<ExitStatus Display>); the host saw: <io error>; session <S>, run <R>`.
An unmanaged run names `socket <path>` instead of session and run. IDs and the path go through
`escape_debug` so the line stays one line. A worker that exits non-zero after the session's natural
finish gets the same line without "the host saw". Host errors with a live worker, and a stalled worker,
keep their existing `orbit: <error>` line from `main`.

Reference gate: not consequential. No dependency, protocol or wire format, contract, or lifecycle,
security or trust boundary changes; the stderr line is a diagnostic, not a format. ORB-C12 and
ORB-C13 say nothing about stderr, so no contract change; orbit/docs/CONTRACTS.md is untouched.
Bend policy unchanged, so no proof check.

Portability disposition: neutral (std `ExitStatus` Display and `eprintln!`).

comments.text:

  ... ok`. It asserts the SIGKILL case's one stderr line (`orbit: worker ended (signal: 9 (SIGKILL)); ...;
  socket <path>`) and the managed IO.die case's one host line (`exit status: 1`, `session session-1, run run-1`).
- Red: the same check with only orbit/src/host.rs reverted to 17b9920 fails at the new SIGKILL assertion with

Installed check (bead acceptance 2): package /nix/store/fcd9grzqv5ka19iqccbnkd0ixldxy1fv-eon-0.1.3 built from
this tree (Orbit /nix/store/xs75m4zh91kb81mlh9lbz9k8vw49nb81-yazelix-orbit-0.1.0), run in a private headless Sway

Everything was torn down (no owned PIDs left, runtime dir removed). Driver:

after a worker SIGKILL, and with its only terminal gone the isolated supervisor exited with status 1.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Scope and configurability (2026-10-27, ztcq session, after review round 1).

Configurability: the new stderr line's text stays fixed. It is an Orbit diagnostic in the per-terminal
log that Eon names after a failure, read by a person or agent debugging a crash, not a value anyone sees
or feels in normal use. Exposing it would add an Orbit configuration surface, which orbit/AGENTS.md
excludes ("no ... configuration framework"), for a support cost with no user who reasonably differs.

Line written: `orbit: worker ended (<ExitStatus Display>); the host saw: <io error>; session <S>, run <R>`
(unmanaged runs: `; socket <path>`), only when the worker died during the session and no termination
signal stopped the host. The write is best-effort (`writeln!` with its result ignored), so a full log
filesystem cannot turn the worker's status into a panic exit.

Dropped from the first draft: a line for a worker that exits non-zero after the session's natural
finish. The worker exits 0 after Finished, no fixture can produce that path, and an unchecked claim is
worse than none.

Out of scope, left as is: a worker that dies at startup (before its bounds, or while Host::open runs)
still yields main's bare `orbit: <error>` line (for example `orbit: Broken pipe (os error 32)`) without
status or run. The euzm gap this bead closes is a running terminal's worker dying, which is the
SIGKILL/IO.die path above. Host errors with a live worker and a stalled worker keep main's existing line.

title: Keep a terminal alive when an OSC 8 hyperlink URI is invalid UTF-8
description:
## Why

Found by eon-3f while fixing eon-title-utf8-ends-terminal-atq2 (2026-10-23), from reading the code; not yet reproduced. `orbit/src/frame.rs:334` (`hyperlink_uri`) turns a hyperlink URI that isn't valid UTF-8 into an EPROTO error, and the pinned libghostty-vt stores OSC 8 URIs without checking them. So a program that prints `ESC]8;;http://x/\377 ESC\` followed by text, while a client is attached, probably ends the terminal through the frame path, the same way atq2's invalid titles did. Any program, or any file a user `cat`s, could do this. Losing a terminal to a stray escape sequence is the worst failure Eon has.

## Contract

ORB-C6 (cell content). atq2's ORB-C3 wording covers only title and directory metadata. Whether a URI that isn't valid UTF-8 shows as no link or as a lossy link is a behavior choice: bring the exact ORB-C6 wording to the overseer, or to Lucca, before code.

## Scope

In scope:
- Reproduce with a real-PTY step: an attached client plus an OSC 8 URI with invalid UTF-8. Red first.
- Fix at the frame boundary: the cell keeps its text and drops the invalid link (recommended), with the same single fallback style atq2 used.
- Check the frame path for any other `?` on libghostty strings that a program controls (cell graphemes, other OSC payloads) and handle them in the same change if they have the same failure.
- The ORB-C6 text, orbit/CHANGELOG.md and the root CHANGELOG.

Out of scope: OSC 8 link behavior for valid URIs, and Venus link opening.

## Acceptance

- The real-PTY step fails before the fix (the terminal ends) and passes after it (the terminal lives, and the text renders without the link).

## Verification

`nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-orbit`, Orbit fmt and clippy, the nix orbit-* check that holds the step, converge plus Codex.

Portability disposition: neutral.
close_reason: Fixed: a hyperlink URI that is not valid UTF-8 becomes no link (ORB-C6), proved by orbit-late-observer, orbit-preview, orbit-held-attach on tree 0796d52

comments.text:
Contract approval, relayed by the overseer on 2026-10-23 under Lucca's approval that day: "i give you auto-approval to everything, until 700k / but the focus is landing the sidebar / our mission is: happy users" (recorded on eon-agent-sidebar-yx8; covers user-owned decisions in eon-* beads, relayed quoted). Approved: (1) a hyperlink URI that is not valid UTF-8 becomes no link, never a lossy decode (a lossy URI would open a different target than the program wrote). (2) ORB-C6 Important failures becomes a list, keeping the topology item and adding exactly: "A hyperlink URI that is not valid UTF-8 reaches the client as no link: the cell keeps its text, in frames and previews, and the terminal keeps running." Proof line gains this bead's commit, with an orbit-late-observer evidence entry.

Evidence (pinned Ghostty 8c425a7): OSC 8 URIs are stored byte-for-byte without UTF-8 checks, bounded near 2046 bytes (osc.zig MAX_BUF 2048; longer OSC 8 is dropped whole). Any frame or preview error reaches host.rs run -> contain(), which HUPs the child. Cell graphemes: no input path stores a surrogate or >U+10FFFF (UTF8Decoder, simd vt, Utf8View, REP, snapshot restore), so graphemes need no change. Out-of-scope finding: valid long URIs on many cells can exceed MAX_FRAME_BYTES (EOVERFLOW ends the terminal); the overseer files it as its own bead.

title: Add the Outside contributions rule to AGENTS.md
description:
## Goal
Add an "Outside contributions" repository-local rule to AGENTS.md: code from outside the Yazelix GitHub organization is untrusted reference, reimplemented by us and credited, never merged, copied or run on a maintainer machine.

## Approval — Lucca, 2026-10-23
Direct "1 ok" to the eon-overseer item that proposed writing this rule with Yazelix GitHub organization members as the trust boundary. Approved text as first written (superseded below):

### Outside contributions

Code from anyone outside the Yazelix GitHub organization (pull requests, patches, gists, snippets in issues) is never merged, cherry-picked, applied or copied into this repository, however small. It is untrusted reference: read it as a prototype or specification, then implement the change ourselves through the normal bead, contract and review loop, and credit the author with a `Co-Authored-By:` trailer on the commits that carry their idea. title: Own one launch directory per Eon tab
description:
## Outcome

Implement `EON-C17 — Tab launch directory`: every full-Eon tab owns one authoritative launch directory, an explicit action can retarget it, and every later pane in that tab starts there.

Smallest observable contract:
- Consumer: a person creating and navigating tabs and panes in a full Eon workspace.
- Trigger: a fresh workspace or tab is created, or a trusted same-user workspace client explicitly sets one live tab's directory.
- Result: Eon stores one absolute directory on the tab, returns it in the authoritative workspace snapshot, derives the tab's visible directory label from it, and uses it as the process working directory for every later `CreatePane` in that tab.
- Failures: structurally invalid, oversized, missing, non-directory, unknown-tab, or spawn-time-invalid paths fail without mutating the wrong tab, adding topology, or leaving a child, record, or socket.

Eon owns tab identity, launch-directory policy, mutation, and recovery fallback. Orbit continues to own each Session's actual terminal CWD. Venus owns bounded native presentation of Eon-authored identity and directory state. Ordinary shell `cd`, OSC 7, and Orbit CWD/title updates never retarget or relabel the tab.

User-approved decisions on 2026-08-25:
- Add `EON-C17` and activate a versioned EONW v2; EONW v1 remains immutable.
- New workspace tab identities use compact `tN`; pane identities remain `pN`.
- The visible tab label is derived rather than separately stored: `1  eon`, `2  nova`, `3  ~`, or `4  /`. The stable identity remains `tN`.
- A new tab inherits the active tab's launch directory and uses that same value for its first Session.
- A recovered synthetic `t1` uses the replacement supervisor's absolute launch directory as new policy state and never infers prior truth from a surviving pane.
- Stage the exact Eon/Venus source update without any running supervisor accepting both EONW versions.

Impact: HIGH for current daily navigation and the planned Yazi picker. Effort: L. Implementation risk: HIGH because workspace state, launch, recovery, wire compatibility, exact consumer pins, native presentation, and installed-runtime proof meet here.

## Evidence

- Current Eon source at `fad3f01d446b33fc04b5381633e9eb4ac1976dc2` stores `Tab { id, panes, selected }` in `crates/eon/src/workspace.rs`; `CreateTab` and `CreatePane` start a Session before committing topology.
- `crates/eon/src/supervisor.rs` sends dynamic workspace starts through `start_orbit` with the configured default child and no directory argument.
- `crates/eon/src/sessions.rs` builds the Orbit command without `Command::current_dir`, so every current child inherits the supervisor process directory.
- EONW v1 snapshots/actions carry topology, endpoint, liveness, and focus only. EON-C8/EON-C10 intentionally do not promise tab launch state, command/CWD history, or workspace persistence.
- Current Venus source retains stable tab identity for hit testing, focus, and accessibility and renders that identity directly. Its pane labels already demonstrate bounded directory compaction, but pane CWD remains Orbit-authored state and is not tab policy.
- Orbit ORBF carries the current terminal working directory. Polling or copying it into the tab would create a second policy owner and make ordinary shell navigation change future process launch.
- Nova's exact `zellij-pane-orchestrator` at `e76ae565f0dc25844293544bf9b58a6dcf127947` owns one canonical root per stable tab, changes it only through explicit retarget behavior, and derives a native tab name from the root basename. Preserve the user outcome, not its Zellij calls, UTF-8-only state, shell injection, editor synchronization, or recovery heuristics.
- Upstream Zellij separates tab identity/name from an optional tab CWD and has had multiple CWD lifecycle and inaccessible-path failures; use it as failure evidence rather than as Eon architecture.

## Scope

In scope:
- One `PathBuf` launch directory on each live full-Eon tab and one raw bounded byte field on each EONW v2 tab snapshot.
- Fresh `t1` starts at the absolute process directory Eon uses for its first Session.
- `CreateTab` copies the active tab's launch directory, uses it for the new tab's first Session, then commits the new `tN` only after Session startup succeeds.
- One semantic `SetTabDirectory { tab, directory }` EONW v2 action. The CLI surface is `eon tab directory TAB -- DIRECTORY`; it carries the exact `tN` identity and one opaque Unix path argument.
- Protocol representation is a nonempty raw byte sequence bounded to 4096 bytes. Eon rejects NUL and non-absolute paths, follows the path only to verify that it currently names a directory, and preserves the accepted spelling. It promises no symlink canonicalization or stable filesystem object identity.
- An accepted set mutates only the addressed tab and returns one complete snapshot containing the authoritative value.
- `CreatePane` passes the tab directory through Rust `Command::current_dir` to Orbit. Existing Sessions, PTY children, and their current directories do not change.
- If an accepted directory later disappears, becomes inaccessible, or changes through a symlink race, the next spawn is the final authority: `CreatePane` fails without adding a pane or leaking launch residue, while the tab retains its accepted directory until another explicit set.
- Same-boot recovery projects surviving Sessions into synthetic `t1` and assigns the replacement supervisor's absolute launch directory as fresh future-pane policy. Documentation must not call that value recovered prior workspace state.
- Venus derives a bounded visual label from the authoritative tab directory: numeric identity prefix plus home marker, root marker, or final path component. Duplicate leaf names remain distinguishable by the number. Hit testing and actions continue to use `tN`; accessibility and diagnostics include stable identity plus the bounded full path.
- EONW v2 source and exact consumer staging: first publish an unactivated v2 codec surface from Eon while the running product remains v1; then update and prove the exact Venus consumer; finally activate v2 in Eon, pin that Venus revision, and remove staging-only v1 source where no accepted consumer requires it. No supervisor accepts both versions.
- Focused TDD for the codec and workspace transition plus one outer integration proof for directory inheritance, retarget, spawn failure, label/accessibility projection, and tab independence.

Out of scope:
- Manual tab names, a separately stored label, label configuration, rename commands, directory history, persistence, global/project roots, or restoration of pre-crash tab roots.
- Tracking ordinary shell `cd`, synchronizing tab and pane CWD, retargeting existing processes, polling OSC 7, or inferring policy from Orbit metadata.
- Yazi/zoxide UI or configuration, automatically opening a pane after retarget, pane-title changes, arbitrary split trees, EonTerm, or a generic settings/profile service.
- Canonicalizing symlinks, retaining directory file descriptors, filesystem watches, TOCTOU elimination, authorization beyond the existing private same-UID EONW boundary, or a new dependency.
- A second composition graph, a runtime compatibility adapter, or simultaneous EONW v1/v2 service.

## Reference gate before code

Required:
- Current EON-C8, EON-C10, EON-C11, and EON-C15 workspace/action/generation/recovery owners and exact accepted checks; EON-C6 remains distribution planning rather than runtime ownership.
- Complete EONW v1 codec, validation, caller inventory, exact Venus dependency/substitution path, generation identity inputs, and incompatibility behavior.
- Rust `std::process::Command::current_dir`, Unix `Path`/`OsStrExt`, `execve`/`chdir` failure behavior, and the impossibility of validating away a later filesystem race without retaining a stronger object handle.
- Exact Nova tab-workspace and retarget implementation at `Yazelix/zellij-pane-orchestrator@e76ae565f0dc25844293544bf9b58a6dcf127947`.
- Exact pinned Zellij source used by Nova for new-tab CWD, naming, and inaccessible/missing directory behavior.
- Current Venus workspace scene, renderer, accessibility projection, protocol transport, and exact source update mechanics.

Record in the bead before implementation:
- The inspected exact source paths/revisions and the preserved or rejected mechanisms.
- The minimal EONW v2 staging shape that avoids duplicate runtime ownership while breaking the Eon/Venus revision cycle.
- The exact protocol seed, Venus consumer, and Eon activation revisions as they become available.

Adopt one tab field, one action, `Command::current_dir`, and a Venus-derived label. Reject a stored display name, shell wrapper, environment-variable shadow state, per-pane root, Orbit-derived policy, polling, persistence scaffolding, or dependency.

## Acceptance Criteria

- EON-C17 is recorded as Candidate before implementation and names Eon as the sole tab launch-directory owner.
- Every fresh workspace uses `t1`; later tabs use checked monotonic `tN`; panes remain `pN`. EONW v1 and older live generations are not rewritten.
- Fresh `t1` owns the absolute directory used for its first Session. `CreateTab` inherits the active tab directory and uses it for its first Session.
- `SetTabDirectory` accepts an exact live `tN`, atomically changes only that tab, and returns a complete snapshot containing the exact raw directory bytes.
- Visual labels derive from the directory without another stored owner: `N  leaf`, `N  ~`, or `N  /`. Retarget updates the label; shell navigation does not. Duplicate leaves remain distinguishable, and accessibility exposes identity plus bounded path context.
- `CreatePane` after retarget starts Orbit and its child with that directory as process CWD. Existing Sessions and terminal CWDs do not change; another tab remains independent.
- Empty, relative, NUL-containing, oversized, missing, and non-directory set requests fail without state change. Unknown/stale `tN` fails without changing another tab.
- If an already accepted path is removed, made inaccessible, or raced before a later spawn, `CreatePane` returns a bounded start failure without adding topology or leaving child/record/socket residue. The accepted tab directory is not silently rolled back.
- Recovery assigns replacement-launch CWD to synthetic `t1`, identifies it as fresh fallback policy, and never projects a surviving pane's current CWD as recovered tab truth.
- EONW v1 stays immutable. Exact clients reject unsupported versions. The staged source order yields no runtime dual-stack and final Eon pins the accepted Venus consumer.
- Focused red/green checks cover v2 raw-path/action/snapshot codec validation, `tN` identity validation, active-tab inheritance, exact-tab/no-mutation transitions, derived label/accessibility parity, and spawn rollback.
- One outer installed integration check retargets one tab, creates a pane whose child reports the expected CWD, proves a second tab remains independent, removes an accepted directory and observes bounded no-topology failure, and preserves all pre-existing live Sessions during profile refresh.
- The unchanged final candidate passes the full affected Rust and Nix surfaces, manifest validation, required docs/contract/help/changelog updates, LOC scorecards, and `git diff --check`.

## Stop conditions

- Stop before implementation until the reference-gate evidence and exact EONW v2 staging mechanism are recorded. The contract identity, path representation, fresh/new/recovered semantics, `tN` identity, derived label, and no-runtime-dual-stack policy are already user-approved.
- Stop if the work requires Orbit to own tab policy, Venus to infer it from pane CWD, a shell `cd` wrapper, manual naming, workspace persistence, a new dependency, or a runtime compatibility window.
- Stop before changing EonTerm, Yazi, zoxide, existing Session CWD, pane labels, or ordinary shell navigation.
- Stop if another active frontier owns EONW, workspace, supervisor, launch, or Venus workspace-presentation surfaces.

## Maintenance notes

This bead remains the sole prerequisite for `eon-start-tabs-with-yazi-picker-1az`. It supplies the stable `tN` target, authoritative directory, and derived label needed by that later adapter, but does not choose the Yazi binding or introduce a sidebar, popup, editor integration, or manual naming.

title: Fix the intermittent generation discovery cleanup test
description:
## Defect
eon-runtime's generation::tests::discovery_bounds_dead_cleanup_and_rejects_unsafe_metadata fails intermittently at runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/generation.rs:738, assert!(!dead.exists()): the second, uncontended discover_generations does not remove the dead generation's control metadata. Seen twice on 2026-10-21 under machine load (1-minute load about 15-30 while several agents built and tested), in eon-test runs on edge cd1f4cf and 9f972e5. It passed 3/3 alone and on rerun. Reported by claude-w3 while working on eon-awmq.8 and eon-popup-covered-pane-reorder-iw2k; neither change touches generation.rs.

## Contract
No contract change. The test protects dead-generation cleanup (EON-C11 lifecycle). Either the cleanup has a timing dependency (for example a liveness probe or lock that is still held, or races the inspection thread joined just before), or the test does.

## Acceptance
- Name the cause from the code and a reproduction under load (for example the test looped while a parallel build runs).
- A fix that makes the test deterministic without weakening what it checks; red/green evidence from the load reproduction.
- nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime.

## Scope boundary
This test and the cleanup path it exercises only.
close_reason: Test-only fix: wait for the dead socket to refuse, unlock the fixture lock explicitly; red 11/40, green 0/80 and 0/30 on the exact tree; cause was fork inheritance of open file descriptions, not a cleanup defect

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Update (claude-w3, 2026-10-21): it also failed at low load (1-minute load about 1-2) in an eon-test run on edge b764c63 plus an unrelated change, then passed on rerun. So it is not only load-driven. Four failures seen today in about eight full runs.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Cause (2026-10-21): fork inheritance of the test's open file descriptions, not a cleanup defect. Instrumented loops of eon-test -p eon-runtime --lib: the dead generation's probe reports 'Connection refused' (dead) as intended, but right after drop(held) the lifecycle flock is still held (try_lock Ok(None)) and frees within about 0.3 ms; no /proc fd still names the lock by the time it is scanned. Failing runs: 11 of 40 full-suite runs at load about 1-2 (10 at the uncontended !dead.exists() assertion, 1 at the contended state == dead assertion, the listener variant), 0 of 25 with --test-threads=1, 0 of 40 running the test alone. Other eon-runtime tests spawn children (sessions.rs, supervisor.rs, quota.rs); a child forked by a concurrent test shares this test's file descriptions until it execs, so a dropped lock briefly stays held and a dropped UnixListener briefly accepts. Product impact: none beyond a cleanup deferred to the next discovery. Fix (test only): wait until the dead socket refuses connections, and retry the uncontended discovery until it removes the metadata (5 s deadline). Rejected: probing the lock with try_lock before the uncontended discovery, which still failed 1 of 60 because the probe's own lock descriptor is inherited the same way. Green: 0 of 80 full-suite runs fail this test. Seen once in those 80 runs, out of scope: quota::tests::workers_isolate_failure_and_bound_output_timeout_and_shutdown at quota.rs:447 (snapshot still None after 2 s), plausibly the same inheritance class on a worker pipe.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Fix and proof (2026-10-21), superseding the fix described in the earlier cause comment. The diagnosis there stands; the retry fix and its 0 of 80 green were for an earlier candidate and are not this fix's proof.

Fix (test only, runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/generation.rs, code tree 6eeaff1d206e93d902f6fa5d582600f28fef7074 on base 9e0bb86):
- After dropping the listener, wait (5 s deadline) until the dead socket refuses connections. A refused socket cannot accept again, so the contended inspection sees a dead generation.
- Call `held.unlock()` before dropping the fixture's lock. flock belongs to the open file description, so an explicit unlock releases it even where a concurrently forked child still holds a copy; dropping alone does not. The single uncontended discovery and `assert!(!dead.exists())` stay as they were.
- Rejected: retrying the uncontended discovery until cleanup (it accepts cleanup that needs several passes, e.g. a swapped socket/directory removal order; both reviewers flagged it) and probing with try_lock first (1 of 60 still failed: the probe's own descriptor is inherited the same way).

Red/green (eon-test -p eon-runtime --lib, full suite, x86_64 Linux, load about 1-13):
- Red, base: 11 of 40 runs failed this test (10 at the uncontended assertion, 1 at the contended state == dead assertion); 0 of 25 with --test-threads=1; 0 of 40 alone.
- Green, this fix: 0 of 80 runs (working tree with generation.rs at 6eeaff1, load 2.5-4.3) and 0 of 30 on the exact tree in a detached worktree (fresh reviewer, load 8.5-13); cargo fmt --check and clippy -D warnings clean.

Out of scope, reported: quota::tests::workers_isolate_failure_and_bound_output_timeout_and_shutdown failed once (quota.rs:447) in one 80-run loop of an earlier candidate; not seen in the 110 runs above.

Ledger: Claude pass 1 (1 blocking: the retry accepted multi-pass cleanup) + Codex pass 1 (same finding; proposed the explicit unlock) -> fixed tree 6eeaff1; Claude pass 2 clean on code (1 blocking on this bead's record, fixed by this comment).

title: Graduate Linux distribution after repaired Nix reliability
description:
User-approved exception — 2026-10-10
The user accepts the demonstrated Orca #757 stale Say All reading-position failure as a known upstream limitation while its correction is reviewed: https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/orca/-/work_items/757#note_2894216. It no longer blocks this distribution-graduation decision or its downstream bundle development. This exception covers the reproduced terminal-to-picker query/path omission and GNOME Terminal/Vim skipped-page text only. Full screen-reader qualification remains open under eon-qualify-repaired-linux-screen-reader-tvkf; retain its negative and do not advertise full screen-reader support. Other accessibility defects, child-source acceptance, active-work protection, trust boundaries and delivery/public-beta proof are not waived. Revisit when upstream accepts a correction or the relevant candidate/behavior changes. No patched Orca is installed or selected as the product reader.

Planning activation and order — user decision 2026-10-07:
The user selected a Nix-free x86_64 Linux native-Wayland bundle and small user-local installer before beta aimed beyond Nix users. This is the named planning gate for that direction, after repair and accepted Nix reliability through eon-accept-repaired-nix-linux-reliability-ws9g. Existing alpha/early dogfood remains Nix-only until the separate bundle, installer and public-beta delivery gates are accepted.

This decision finalizes the accepted product evidence, first direct target, release owner/tool and maintenance envelope. It does not infer acceptance from the closed No-Go eon-qualify-nix-linux-beta-bxoh. After this gate, eon-ohh is delivered by eon-prove-manual-nix-free-linux-bundle-216b first and eon-prove-thin-linux-bundle-installer-8r7n second; eon-qualify-nix-free-linux-public-beta-lm9p qualifies the wider beta. The user approved this planning sequence, not immediate publication or expansion to other targets/formats.

Contract:
EON-C5 and EON-C6, informed by EON-C1 through EON-C4 and every accepted active-work lifecycle contract.

Required evidence:
- The Nix composition launches one accepted Orbit and Venus pair with Helix, Yazi and Ratconfig through their owned contracts.
- Sustained fresh-session dogfood covers launch, detach, reattach, configuration, diagnostics, upgrades, Venus restart, declared Eon relaunch semantics, partial-child failure, and the real coding-agent lifecycle required by eon-ax4.
- An upgrade cannot silently terminate an active Orbit-backed agent or other long-running process.
- Orbit or machine restart persistence remains an explicit limitation unless a separate accepted child contract proves it.
- Exact selected component revisions have no unresolved P0 or P1 integration defect except the narrowly accepted upstream Orca #757 limitation above.
- Product code accepts explicit component paths, invokes no Nix evaluator during normal use, and persists stable component identity instead of store paths.
- The component manifest describes the accepted product without using derivation identity as a runtime contract.
- The team has capacity to maintain artifacts, verification, safe staging, upgrades, rollback and removal.

Decision record:
Compare staying Nix-only longer with one direct Linux bundle. Name the user value, first target, release owner, expected CI and maintenance cost, active-work upgrade policy, tool-gate evidence, and deferred features.

Scope:
This Bead authorizes one direct-distribution decision. It does not implement a bundle, live handoff, restart persistence, provider integration, or another package channel. If safe replacement requires a new Orbit lifecycle contract, route that separately before distribution proceeds.
design:
Treat active agent and terminal work as user data at risk during upgrades.

Before approving direct distribution, exercise the exact update path while an ordinary long-running process and the selected real coding-agent workload are active. Replacing Venus may reconnect through accepted contracts. Replacing Orbit must not be assumed safe: when no accepted live-handoff contract exists, stage or defer the incompatible Orbit update until affected sessions stop, or require explicit informed confirmation naming the processes and state that will be lost. Automatic or background update must never kill active work silently.

Inspect exact current Herdr session-state and live-handoff behavior as comparison evidence for preserving PTYs across runtime replacement, plus official platform update and process-lifecycle sources relevant to the selected bundle. This selects no handoff architecture. A live-handoff, external PTY owner, daemon-restart persistence, or agent-native restore path requires its own Orbit or Eon contract and proof.

The release tool gate still compares staying Nix-only, local owned or Nix-native commands, one direct Linux bundle and credible maintained tooling. Record artifacts, verification, signing or attestation, rollback, removal, CI cost and the user hard spending boundary.

Proof reuse: eon-accept-repaired-nix-linux-reliability-ws9g accepted Eon 84a6e6f with Venus a27aad2 and the recorded exact graph. It is evidence only for unchanged identities/behavior exercised there; it does not blanket-accept a later component candidate. Select the graduation candidate, reuse unaffected evidence, and identify the cheapest remaining outermost checks without repeating complete suites for metadata alone.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The Nix-only Eon composition has sustained fresh-session dogfood for launch, detach, reattach, configuration, diagnostics, upgrades, Venus restart, declared Eon relaunch semantics, partial-child failure, and one real coding-agent lifecycle.
2. The exact upgrade path is exercised while both an ordinary long-running process and a real agent process are active.
3. No upgrade, rollback or automatic update silently terminates an active Orbit-backed process. If Orbit replacement cannot preserve it, the update is staged or deferred until sessions stop, or explicit confirmation names the affected sessions, processes, unpersisted state and exact loss.
4. Orbit and machine restart persistence is either backed by a separately accepted child contract or recorded as an explicit limitation. Distribution code does not simulate or imply it.
5. Any proposed live handoff, external PTY owner, agent-native restoration or new recovery behavior is routed to a separate approved owner contract before distribution consumes it.
6. The accepted component set has no unresolved P0 or P1 integration defect except the user-approved 2026-10-10 Orca #757 limitation described above. New or broader accessibility failures are not covered.
7. The selected Venus revision retains exact scoped structured-accessibility evidence under VEN-C1/VEN-C2/VEN-C4 and the relevant history/workspace contracts. Retain native composed reader observations for bounded scene-derived semantics, keyboard/AT actions and failure UX, plus the demonstrated Orca #757 negative. The user permits distribution graduation/development with this specific upstream limitation; complete Linux reader qualification stays open under eon-qualify-repaired-linux-screen-reader-tvkf and full screen-reader support remains unqualified. Closed ven-q3w or AT-SPI tree inspection alone is insufficient evidence. The separately owned Venus caret repair must be accepted and adopted exactly; closed ven-expose-authoritative-accessible-caret-zki and eon-adopt-venus-authoritative-caret-45yu fulfill that source gate at 58f2eaa. No new reader failure is waived.
8. Product code invokes no Nix evaluator during normal use and persists no store path as stable component identity.
9. The component manifest describes the accepted product without derivation identity as a runtime contract.
10. The tool gate compares staying Nix-only with one direct Linux bundle and records maintenance, CI, active-work staging, artifact verification, rollback and removal costs. Before Go, name the responsible release operator and explicitly accept a bounded maintenance/cost envelope: available local build/verification measurements, provisional artifact/storage/transfer estimates with uncertainty, expected release/support cadence and capacity for failed staging, rollback and removal. Keep $0 additional hosted spend unless the user explicitly changes it; this selects no hosted job or service. The downstream bundle proves actual delivery costs and reopens this decision if they exceed the accepted envelope.
11. Record the user-approved 2026-10-07 direction and first target: x86_64 Linux on native Wayland, one Nix-free direct bundle and small user-local installer before broader public beta. Accepted repaired Nix reliability is required before completing this graduation decision.
12. The decision records the exact component manifest, Orbit and Venus proof revisions, agent-work and accessibility dogfood environments, proof commands, active-work upgrade policy, known limitations, artifact authority and rollback condition.
13. Approval covers one direct-distribution slice and no additional package channel or runtime feature.
14. eon-accept-repaired-nix-linux-reliability-ws9g remains the historical exact Eon 84a6e6f reliability record. The selected repaired candidate needs accepted scoped crash/reliability evidence from eon-isolate-unclean-orbit-exit-1v4a, valid reuse of unchanged earlier boundaries, accepted exact Venus repair adoption and retained composed reader observations. The two notice files that the Nix package installs drop their split-repository wording.

Fold this into the next slice that changes the packaged Eon artifact anyway, so it costs no separate rebuild, profile refresh or generation.

- Both files carry the corrected wording and the root and Venus notices agree.
- That slice's normal package proof covers the changed artifact; the profile is refreshed per Local Runtime Synchronization.

Notice wording only; no license terms change.

title: Extend edge cell backgrounds into pane padding, like Ghostty's window-padding-color
description:
## Report

Lucca, 2026-10-24 (screenshot of opencode in an Eon pane): "this gap is weird". A full-screen TUI
that paints its own background (opencode, also Helix, lazygit and other full-screen apps) leaves a
visible frame between its cells and the pane's outline. Venus pads the terminal grid inside the
pane card, because the grid rarely divides the pane exactly, and paints that padding with the
translucent card, so the window background's warm glow shows through. With a shell using the
default background the padding blends in; with a TUI's darker background it reads as a gap.

Filed on Lucca's request, P1 (2026-10-24, "do it. p1.", answering the overseer's item 35).

## Reference

Ghostty's `window-padding-color` setting:
- `background` (pad with the terminal background);
- `extend` (extend the nearest edge cells' background into the padding, except where that would
  look wrong, e.g. when the edge cells differ along the row or column);
- `extend-always`.

Read Ghostty's implementation (renderer padding extension) and record what it extends and when it
declines, before choosing. Check ~/pjs/refs for a Ghostty clone first.

## Change

Venus paints each pane's padding from the terminal's edge cells, Ghostty-style `extend`: the
padding next to a row or column takes the background of the edge cell beside it, so a full-screen
TUI looks edge to edge. Keep today's look when the edge cells use the default background. The pane
outline, card corners and header are unchanged.

## Configurability

A user may prefer today's frame, so expose a Venus-rendered setting parsed by Eon Runtime (Venus
parses no config), with values modeled on Ghostty's (`background` / `extend` / `extend-always`)
and default `extend`. Document it in docs/CONFIGURATION.md.

## Contract

Find the VEN-C that owns terminal presentation and padding, and bring any wording change to Lucca
first. The setting adds a resolved value on the Runtime-to-Venus path; check whether that touches
EONW, which would need a version bump (memory eonw-codec-change-needs-bump).

## Acceptance

- A Venus scene test: a grid whose edge cells have a non-default background extends it into the
  padding; default-background edges keep today's look. It fails on today's code.
- One installed observation: opencode or Helix in a pane shows no frame.

## Scope

Venus padding rendering plus the one setting. Not pane chrome (eon-mur2) or themes
(eon-eon-themes-or3q).

title: Research sending text to an existing pane or popup, and draft its contract
description:
## Why

Eon can start a command in a new pane (`eon pane create -- COMMAND`), but it can't send input to a pane or popup that's already running. Every comparable multiplexer can: tmux `send-keys`, WezTerm `cli send-text`, kitty `@ send-text`, Zellij `action write-chars`. Agent orchestrators depend on it; ntm drives its agents through tmux `send-keys`. In Eon, the overseer can message Claude sessions but has no way to reach a Codex, Grok, OpenCode or Pi agent running in a pane, and users and scripts can't drive a REPL or re-run a command in a live shell.

Lucca asked for it on 2026-10-23 and chose its shape and order from the overseer's numbered items: "yeah, it need a very deep research. create". That accepted:
1. One CLI command along the lines of `eon pane send TARGET [--enter] -- TEXT`, P2, after the agent sidebar epic (eon-agent-sidebar-yx8).
2. Targets cover panes and popups, by their IDs.

## Deliverable of this bead: deep research, then a contract for approval

This bead is research and contract drafting only, with no product code. Its output, recorded on this bead:

1. **References.** Read the source of each comparable implementation, not just its docs, at a recorded revision, and note what Eon should take from it or reject. That includes the input path (pty write, key encoding or paste), the target addressing, the paste handling, and the safety and focus behavior:
   - tmux `send-keys` (`-l`, `-H`, paste buffers);
   - WezTerm `cli send-text` (`--no-paste`, bracketed paste by default);
   - kitty `@ send-text` and `send-key` (remote-control auth and password, `--match`);
   - Zellij `write-chars` and `write`;
   - ntm's use of `send-keys` to drive agents (what it sends, how it submits a prompt, its failures), and how Claude Code, Codex and the other launchable agents treat bracketed paste and Enter in their prompts.
   Use `~/pjs/refs` clones where present (see the refs-research-folder memory).
2. **Eon owners and path.** Trace how a request would flow (CLI → EONW request → Runtime → Orbit input write) through the current code and contracts (the EON_TERMINAL rule, the CLI and generation contracts, the Orbit attach and input contracts), and name the single owner of each step. Say whether Orbit's existing input path covers it or a new ORB-C or EONW request is needed, and whether this bumps EONW.
3. **Trust boundary.** Who may send (same user via the existing socket permissions; from inside an Eon terminal only, or any process of the user), and whether that's enough, compared with kitty's remote-control model. Size limits, and how control and escape bytes are handled.
4. **Safety defaults.** Paste by default (bracketed when the program enabled it) and submit only with an explicit flag. How Enter is sent to programs that ignore a newline inside a paste. What happens when the target is dead, stale, in another generation, or the wrong kind of terminal.
5. **Focus.** It never moves desktop, tab, pane or popup focus, and never shows a hidden popup. Confirm a hidden keep-alive popup can receive input.
6. **Contract draft.** Exact text for the new or amended EON-C (and ORB-C or EONW if needed): consumer, trigger, result, failures and exit codes, JSON output. Bring it to Lucca for approval.
7. **Implementation split.** Propose small implementation and proof beads, each one fresh-session sized, for Lucca to approve. Don't file them before the contract is approved.

## Scope

In scope: research, the reference gate record, and the contract draft and bead split above.

Out of scope: any product code, wire or contract edit before approval; reading back terminal output (a separate capability: tmux `capture-pane`, WezTerm `get-text`; mention it if the research shows the two belong together); and macros or key-chord sending beyond what a minimal contract needs.

## Acceptance

- The bead records the reference findings with sources and revisions, the owner and path trace, and the trust, safety and focus decisions with their reasons.
- Lucca approves, or revises, a contract draft and an implementation split.

## Verification

Planning route: bead state and the recorded research; no runtime profile refresh.

The contract draft this bead produces amends n8ic's provisional contract rather than starting a second one.

title: Deliver rounded pane frames enabled by default in Eon
description:
## Outcome
The installed full-Eon workspace presents the rounded pane borders proved by ven-pane-stack-chrome-suu. Per the user's decision on 2026-09-09, Eon exposes the persistent pane_frames boolean, defaulting to true so each pane has rounded borders; false disables the decorative frames.

Eon owns component selection, product configuration and startup serialization. Venus retains layout/rendering/accessibility; Orbit retains terminal authority. Any product-setting contract is settled before configuration code.

## Prerequisites and reference gate

Required before code: the complete Venus Bead and proof; current Eon manifest/locks, configuration and venus_command owners; EON-C8/EON-C18/EON-C19; current README appearance documentation and installed-profile rules. Recheck accepted Orbit/Venus revisions at activation. Reuse Eon's existing configuration pattern; no additional config owner.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Pin the exact accepted Venus artifact in the canonical graph and verify manifest/lock identity and affected builds.
- Document and consume pane_frames through the accepted startup boundary. Omitted configuration defaults to true and shows rounded borders around each pane; explicit true has the same behavior. Explicit false removes decorative frames while retaining pane handles, selection and keyboard focus. Invalid values fail before the new launch, preserving running work. - Full Eon owns this workspace policy; EonTerm retains its absence of workspace chrome.

## Scope boundary
Eon composition and the pane_frames product setting only. No child renderer edits, tab redesign, new layout model, arbitrary themes, live reload, unrelated upgrades or additional platform promise.

Added during the user-requested prime-beads pass on 2026-09-09 to close the missing Eon delivery handoff. Activated by the user on 2026-09-09. Implementation, affected profile refresh and isolated installed proof are complete; source remains uncommitted for review.

title: Let users close the final tab, and choose between quitting Eon and keeping it running
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-10-22: "create a p1 bead to remove this 'the final tab cant be closed'. we want happy
users, remember? they need to able to close the final tab. we need a way to 'close everything for
real' and a way to 'close but keep running in the background'. this requires a bit of thinking,
and we need to decide what happens when you close the final tab."

Under AGENTS.md "Happy Users", the contract boundary that refuses final-tab close is a gap to
close, not the answer. Users expect to close the last tab the way they close any other tab. They
also need two clear, discoverable exits: quit (end every terminal) and keep running in the
background (detach).

## Evidence (edge 0c2c70f)

- `docs/CONTRACTS.md:480`, EON-C8: "The final tab's last pane cannot be closed". Final-tab
  close is listed as an important failure at `docs/CONTRACTS.md:498`, and
  `docs/CONTRACTS.md:1374` (EON-C18) says "final-tab close remains unavailable".
- `docs/USAGE.md:117-118` and `:248`: Alt+W refuses the final tab's last pane; Alt+Shift+W and
  `eon tab close` close only "the active non-final tab".
- Ending everything already exists, but only indirectly. EON-C8 (`docs/CONTRACTS.md:486`): "an
  empty workspace closes Venus and the supervisor", so typing `exit` in every shell quits Eon,
  while the close controls refuse to do the same thing.
- Keep running already exists as window close: `docs/USAGE.md:51` "Closing the Eon window
  detaches the desktop without stopping its terminals", and `eon attach` returns to them.
- Quitting for real exists only on the command line: `eon stop GENERATION`,
  `eon window stop ID` (EON-C11, EON-C23), with a confirmation that lists live terminals
  (`docs/USAGE.md:62-76`). Nothing in the window does it.
- Related bug: `eon-jqxr` (closing tab 1 closed the whole window). Keep its fix separate, but
  the new final-tab rule must not make that bug look like intended behavior.

## Decisions to make (recommend an answer to each, Lucca approves)

1. **What closing the final tab does** (Alt+Shift+W, the tab's close control,
   `eon tab close`, and Alt+W on its last pane).
   - Recommendation: quit that window for real. Stop its terminals, close the window and end
     its supervisor, exactly as when the last shell exits today. This matches browsers and
     makes the close controls agree with `exit`.
   - Alternative: replace the final tab with a fresh directory-picker tab, so the window
     never empties.
   - Alternative: detach, which keeps everything running. Rejected as a default: a close
     control that keeps processes alive surprises users and leaks agents and servers.
2. **Confirmation.** Whether closing the final tab, or Quit, asks first when any terminal runs
   something other than an idle shell, such as an agent, a build or a server, and how that
   prompt names what will stop. Recommendation: confirm only when a non-shell foreground
   program is running, and reuse Stop's live-terminal listing.
3. **Explicit Quit and Detach actions in the window.** Quit means end this window's terminals
   now; Detach means close the window and keep running. Pick the shortcuts (check EON-C20 and
   Venus for collisions), their Commands popup (Alt+Shift+M) entries, their Shortcuts dialog
   (Alt+/) lines and any Eon Bar control. Recommendation: both in the Commands popup and the
   Shortcuts dialog, plus one shortcut each.
4. **What the window close button does** (the compositor close or title-bar X). It stays detach
   unless decided otherwise. Say whether the first detach should tell the user once how to
   return (`eon attach`) and how to quit.
5. **Multiple windows (EON-C23).** Quit and final-tab close end only the calling window's
   generation; other windows are untouched. Confirm this.

## Scope

In scope: the decisions above, the reference gate (how comparable tools handle the last tab and
quit versus detach: at least tmux or Zellij detach/kill-session, WezTerm or Ghostty last-tab
close, and a browser), and the contract text changes for Lucca's approval: EON-C8 and EON-C18
(final tab), EON-C10 (`eon tab close`, `eon pane close`), EON-C20 (shortcuts), any Venus VEN-C
contract that maps the keys, plus `docs/USAGE.md` wording. After approval, file the
implementation beads (Runtime lifecycle, Venus keys and controls, docs and installed proof) as
children or follow-ups, each sized for one session.

Out of scope: implementation code in this bead; the `eon-jqxr` window-close bug; durable
restoration across reboot (`eon-reboot-restore-im8y`); `eon stop` CLI semantics beyond the new
actions.

## Acceptance

- This bead records the reference gate and an approved contract proposal answering decisions
  1-5, with the alternatives rejected and why.
- Implementation beads exist for the approved behavior, with dependencies set, and the first
  one is ready.

## Verification

Planning route (AGENTS.md Verification table): beads state, changed Markdown paths and
contract IDs, and the diff. No runtime proof in this bead.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop for Lucca's approval before editing any contract text.
- Stop if the chosen behavior needs an EONW or Orbit wire change; record that and ask before
  filing it.

## Maintenance Notes

- AP-FAILURE-001: quitting must give bounded, idempotent shutdown with no orphaned popup
  terminals. Detach must keep every terminal attachable.
- Keep one owner per behavior: Runtime owns the lifecycle decision, Venus only maps input and
  shows the prompt.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Reference gate (claude, 2026-10-22 ~15:00 -03). Evidence read at these revisions; inference marked.

Comparable tools:
- tmux 1c418f0b: last pane -> window ends -> session ends (server-fn.c:251-252, 428-449); detach-on-destroy on, exit-empty on, destroy-unattached off. prefix d = detach-client (key-bindings.c:429); kill-session unbound. Kill confirms are plain y/n that name nothing (key-bindings.c:397, 445). Detach prints 'detached', no reattach hint (client.c:194-198).
- Zellij main c7c4ce42 (v0.45.1 efd8fd5a): last tab/pane ends the session (zellij-server/src/lib.rs:4493-4515). Main adds a quit prompt 'Close this window?' with Detach (session keeps running) / Quit (ends session, N other clients) / Cancel plus 'Always do this' (screen.rs:1846-1879); on_quit = ask_quit (default) | ask_detach | quit | detach (zellij-utils/src/input/options.rs:53-69). Not in v0.45.1. on_force_close (terminal window closed) defaults to detach (options.rs:104-107). Ctrl q quit, Ctrl o d detach.
- WezTerm e2a98e1b: last tab closes the window (mux/src/lib.rs:905-927); quit_when_all_windows_are_closed true. Confirms tab/window close only for a 'stateful' process tree, i.e. a name outside skip_close_confirmation_for_processes_named (bash, sh, zsh, fish, tmux, nu, ...) (config.rs:1843-1858, mux/src/localpane.rs:561-624); QuitApplication always prompts. Prompts never name programs. DetachDomain has no default key.
- Ghostty 8c425a7b (refs clone): last tab closes the window (src/apprt/gtk/class/window.zig:1848-1855); quit-after-last-window-closed true on Linux. confirm-close-surface=true confirms unless the cursor sits at an OSC 133 prompt, so without shell integration it always confirms (Surface.zig:977-995). Dialogs name nothing. Ctrl+Shift+Q quits; no detach.
- Firefox e33ac8a9: closeWindowWithLastTab true (firefox.js:1112); warnOnClose false, warnOnQuit true for the quit shortcut (BrowserGlue.sys.mjs:1294-1470). Chromium 9c189443: an empty tab strip closes the window (browser.cc:615-628); quit warning Mac-only.
- herdr 143bf5fd (refs clone; closest in shape): closing the last tab removes the workspace, and an attached server recreates a default one (src/server/headless.rs:525, 3266); prefix q detaches; stop is a separate 'herdr server stop'.

Synthesis: graphical terminals and browsers close the window with the last tab; multiplexers end the session. Confirm-only-when-busy is common, but detection is weak (name allowlist or prompt marks) and no tool names what will stop. Zellij's three-way Detach/Quit/Cancel prompt is the clearest discovery path for detach, and closing the terminal window detaches by default. Rejected for Eon: a window close that kills (contradicts persistent terminals); WezTerm's process-name allowlist (misses background jobs; Orbit owns process state); always-confirm Quit with nothing named (users learn to click through).

Eon constraints found (edge bc62728):
- Wire: CloseTab/ClosePane replies decode only as Snapshot or Failure (runtime/crates/eon-workspace-protocol/src/v14.rs:769-777), and a snapshot needs at least one tab (v14.rs:962). A Runtime-owned final close that ends the generation therefore needs an EONW v15 reply such as Ended. Stop condition: ask Lucca before filing.
- Stop { generation } already exists in EONW v14 (v14.rs:72) and is answered as a lifecycle response; Venus has no lifecycle client yet.
- Orbit exposes no 'foreground program running' query (ORB-C15 samples the foreground group internally, orbit/docs/CONTRACTS.md:858-880), and only Orbit holds the PTY master. Busy-aware confirmation needs a new Orbit management request, which is a wire change.
- Window close is already detach (venus/src/application.rs:2924, VEN-C14), and implicit attach reattaches only the exact current generation (EON-C11). After a build change, detached generations linger unseen: g1-e52499df… detached 2026-10-22 00:46 and ran until 14:19.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Handoff (claude, 2026-10-22 ~15:10 -03). The reference gate is the comment above. No contract text edited; nothing committed. Waiting on Lucca's answers to decisions 1-5.

Draft recommendations put to Lucca (not yet approved):
1. Final-tab close (Alt+Shift+W, the bar's Close tab button, Alt+W on the last pane, eon tab close) opens a Venus prompt, after Zellij main: 'Close the last tab?', listing the panes and popups that will stop (from the snapshot Venus already has), with Quit (Enter, preselected) / Keep running in background (D, which closes the window as a detach) / Cancel (Esc). Runtime owns the rule: a close that removes the window's last terminal ends the generation, as exit in the last shell does today. That needs an EONW v15 'Ended' reply (stop condition: Lucca must approve the wire change; it lands after eon-n6ga's v14 work). If a new tab appears while the prompt is open, the close removes only that tab. eon tab close confirms like eon stop; --json does not ask. Alternatives: quit without asking; replace the tab with a fresh picker tab (herdr; no wire change, but the close key never closes).
2. Config key [workspace] close_last_tab = ask|quit|detach, default ask (like Zellij's on_quit). Ask-only-when-busy needs a new Orbit foreground query (wire change): offer it as an optional follow-up.
3. Alt+Shift+Q opens the same prompt with Quit preselected and sends the existing EONW v14 Stop{generation} (Venus needs InspectRuntime for its generation, which is a VEN contract change, not a wire change). Alt+Shift+D detaches at once. Both keys are free. They go in the Shortcuts dialog and the footer. The Commands popup gets 'Quit this window' through Stop. No Detach in Commands (would need another wire action) and no new bar button.
4. The window close button / Alt+F4 stays a silent detach, with no notification after close (desktop-focus rule). Optional follow-up: a new window reports leftover detached windows (needs a snapshot field).
5. Quit and final-tab close end only the calling window's generation; eon window stop all stays the way to end every window (EON-C23).

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Decisions (Lucca, 2026-10-22 ~16:00 -03; recorded by claude). They replace the draft recommendations in the handoff.

1. Closing the final tab quits that window, like closing any other tab: it stops the window's terminals, closes the window and ends its generation, as exit in the last shell does today. Applies to Alt+Shift+W, the bar's Close tab, Alt+W on the last pane and eon tab close. Rejected: picker-tab replacement (the close key never closes) and detach-on-close (leaks processes). Lucca approved the wire consequence: EONW 15 already shipped (eon-n6ga), so the Runtime-owned final close needs an EONW 16 reply (Ended).
2. Config key warning_close_last_tab, default on (Lucca chose it over no config and over close_last_tab = ask|quit|detach). When on, closing the final tab first shows a Quit / Cancel prompt (Enter / Esc) that says the window will quit and names what stops. The prompt has one hint line, 'Alt+Shift+D keeps it running instead' (Lucca asked where the detach hint should go; claude recommended inline over a (?) or an in-Eon popup, as the cheapest discoverable option). Alt+Shift+D works while the prompt is open because it is the global detach key. When off, final-tab close quits at once. Busy-only asking is not in scope (it needs an Orbit foreground query, a wire change).
3. Keys: Super+Q / Super+D rejected. COSMIC binds Super+Q to Close window (/usr/share/cosmic/com.system76.CosmicSettings.Shortcuts/v1/defaults:6, so on COSMIC it would detach), sway uses $mod+d and KDE Meta+D, and Eon's keys are all on Alt. Chosen: Alt+Shift+D detaches the window at once. Quit-all has no key; the Commands popup (Alt+Shift+M) gets 'Quit this window', sent as the existing Stop{generation}. Both go in the Shortcuts dialog (Alt+/). No new bar button. Rejected: Alt+Shift+Q, which sits next to W and would kill every tab on a slip.
4. The window close button and Alt+F4 stay detach. The first detach ever, from any path, shows a one-time, non-activating desktop notification saying Eon is still running, how to return (open Eon again) and how to stop it (close the last tab, or Commands > Quit this window). This needs a freedesktop notification call (dependency gate, Linux platform seam) and a 'shown once' marker in Eon state.
5. Quit and final-tab close end only the calling window's generation. eon window stop all stays the way to end every window (EON-C23). Lucca did not object to this recommendation.

Next: propose exact contract text (EON-C8, C10, C18, C20; VEN key and window-close contracts; docs/USAGE.md; the config doc for warning_close_last_tab) and stop for approval.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Contract proposal for Lucca's approval (claude, 2026-10-22). It implements the recorded decisions. No contract text has been edited yet.

EON-C8 (Durable tab and pane workspace)
- Tab close: replace "Closing names the expected active `tN` and requires another live tab." with "Closing names the expected active `tN`." Add: "Closing the final tab ends the window. Eon stops its pane and popup terminals as above, and once every stop is confirmed it ends the generation, as when the last terminal exits. The reply is EONW 16 `Ended`, and Venus then exits. A failed stop keeps the window and its remaining terminals, as a partial close does."
- Pane close: replace "The final tab's last pane cannot be closed, and closing is unavailable while a popup or picker covers the tab." with "Closing the final tab's last pane ends the window as final-tab close does. Closing is unavailable while a popup or picker covers the tab."
- Important failures: drop "final-tab close" and "the final tab's last pane". Add: "a final close never ends the generation until every terminal stop is confirmed; a repeated request ID never ends it twice."

EON-C10 (Typed workspace control)
- `eon tab close TAB` and `eon pane close PANE` may name the final tab or its last pane. When `warning_close_last_tab` is on and stdin is a terminal, the CLI first lists the terminals that will stop and asks, as `eon stop` does; `--json` never asks. Success on a final close prints that the window ended and exits 0. The caller's own terminal may end with it (same caveat as Stop).
- EONW 16: the CloseTab and ClosePane replies gain `Ended { generation }` beside Snapshot and Failure. Only those two replies change. EONW 16 replaces 15 everywhere, as each earlier bump did.

EON-C18 (Picker-first tab directories)
- "Explicitly closing a non-final pending tab" becomes "closing a pending tab". When it is the final tab, the close stops the picker and ends the window. Delete "final-tab close remains unavailable".

EON-C20 (Discoverable native shortcuts)
- Fixed bindings gain Alt+Shift+D, "Keep running in background (detach)". Its viewer line reads "Detach: close the window, keep terminals running". The Alt+Shift+W and Alt+W lines drop "non-final".
- Boundary: unchanged except that the viewer lists Alt+Shift+D.

EON-C11 (Runtime generations and presentation), Commands entry (EON-C8 popup text near Commands)
- Commands gains "Quit this window", which runs `eon stop <this window's generation>` and keeps Stop's confirmation listing of live terminals. It adds no EONW action. Runtime writes the exact generation into the line.

EON-C24 (Bottom shortcut hints): adds a footer hint for Alt+Shift+D ("detach"), derived like the others.

New, owned by Eon (EON-C8 Configuration or a short EON-C33, your call; recommend inside EON-C8):
- `[workspace] warning_close_last_tab = true` (default). When true, a final close from Alt+Shift+W, the bar's Close tab button or Alt+W first shows a Venus prompt: "Close the last tab? This quits the window and stops N terminals." It lists the panes and popups by title from the current snapshot, then "Enter Quit · Esc Cancel", then the hint "Alt+Shift+D keeps it running instead". Alt+Shift+D works while the prompt is open. If the snapshot gains a tab while the prompt is open, Enter closes only the named tab and the window stays. When false, a final close quits at once. Eon validates the key (boolean) before launch, and Venus receives it as a launch argument.
- First-detach notice: the first time any of this user's windows detaches (window X, Alt+F4, Alt+Shift+D), Eon sends one non-activating desktop notification: "Eon is still running in the background. Open Eon to return; close the last tab or use Commands > Quit this window to stop it." A marker in Eon's state directory makes it once per user. A missing notification service is a silent no-op. It never takes focus.

Venus
- VEN-C8: Alt+Shift+W and Alt+W may target the final tab and its last pane. Alt+Shift+D is a new non-repeating key that detaches (the same path as compositor close). Venus handles an `Ended` reply by exiting through the native event loop, as on control EOF. It shows the warning prompt when `warning_close_last_tab` is on.
- VEN-C14: add "Alt+Shift+D and the compositor close request both detach; an EONW `Ended` reply exits like control loss, leaving no Orbit terminal of that generation."
- VEN-C20: viewer rows from EON-C20.
- VEN-C21: the bar's Close tab is available on the final tab and goes through the same prompt.

docs/USAGE.md: lines 117-118, 130 and 248 drop "non-final". Install and start (line 51) adds "Alt+Shift+D does the same from the keyboard; closing the last tab quits the window." The key table gets Alt+Shift+D, and Stop terminals mentions Commands > Quit this window. docs/CONFIGURATION.md gets `[workspace] warning_close_last_tab`.

Unchanged: EON-C23 (Quit and final close end only the calling window's generation; `eon window stop all` ends every window), eon-jqxr stays a separate bug, and busy-only asking is not in scope.

Implementation beads after approval (each sized for one session; dependencies in this order):
A. EONW 16 Ended reply plus the Runtime final close (protocol crate, Runtime, CLI and its confirmation, component graph bump). Full Rust and Nix surfaces.
B. Venus: final-close prompt and `warning_close_last_tab` launch argument, Ended exit, Alt+Shift+D detach, viewer, footer and bar. Depends on A.
C. Commands "Quit this window". Runtime only; can run beside B, after A only if it shares the Commands list file.
D. First-detach notification. Starts with the dependency gate: freedesktop Notifications through a packaged notify-send versus a Rust D-Bus crate, Linux seam, marker owner. Independent of A.
E. Docs (USAGE, CONFIGURATION, CHANGELOG) plus one installed dogfood proof of the batch. Depends on A-D.
