title: Use consistent Tab switching and cancellation in every directory picker
description:
## Contract
Consumer: every full-Eon directory picker opened at startup, for a new tab, or by Alt+Z in an existing pane. User approved option 1 in this session: Tab switches quick search and Yazi in both directions; Enter accepts; Esc and Ctrl+C cancel at either main screen. Esc dismisses a nested Yazi prompt/help/search first. All entry points use the same EON-C18 policy. Preserve EON-C17: changing a tab directory affects future Sessions only.

## Owner and scope
Eon owns mode selection and packaged picker keys/footer through the existing directory_picker path; fzf owns history selection, Yazi owns browser navigation, Orbit owns the one transient Session. No Venus/Orbit/schema/dependency changes, simultaneous pickers, shell cd injection, or live Session restart. Keep a browser's chosen location when switching away and back. No new public interface or configuration.

## Prerequisites and reference gate
Current Orbit 91999d79546422b49bdbc124166a65859d0bd872 and Venus 541a9cb43c155b8b97069904593dc81c73682613 pins match latest accepted source. Read EON-C17/C18, shared CLI and supervisor/workspace paths, existing picker integration tests, pinned Yazi 26.5.6 quit/keymap/cwd behavior, fzf 0.73.1 expected-key/NUL output, Zoxide 0.9.9 list semantics, and the routed Nova browser-versus-commit comparison before implementation. Prefer the existing child quit status and raw CWD result to a plugin, control channel, or new process owner.

## Acceptance Criteria
One focused red/green integration check covers bidirectional switching, exact raw paths, acceptance/cancellation without unintended tab changes, and prompt history-child cleanup. Build the affected package; exercise actual packaged fzf/Yazi in isolated terminal proof, including startup and Alt+Z retargeting, then refresh the Eon profile and check its exact installed artifact. Preserve desktop focus and every live user Session. Update EON-C18, README keys/LOC, and changelog; keep candidate proof qualified until accepted source identity exists.

Startup, new-tab and Alt+Z share Tab switching, main Esc/Ctrl+C cancellation and nested Esc dismissal; browser CWD survives switching and retargeting affects future Sessions only. User authorized commit and push after the fresh-eyes pass. EON-C18 records acceptance without widening fractional-scale, compositor or accessibility proof. Existing live user Sessions retain their older runtime; no restart or desktop focus change occurred.

title: Tell the user on reattach about a picker that failed to stop while detached
description:
## Why

eon-popup-cancel-failure-ends-supervisor-k9sx (EON-C18 sentence approved by Lucca, 2026-10-23, "go
ahead") keeps a transient picker whose stop failed during presentation detachment in its tab, for a
retry at the next detachment, and "reports the failure once". While detached no window shows, so
the report reaches only the supervisor log. On reattach the user may find that tab still pending,
showing a picker that may be dead, with no explanation.

Filed on the overseer's recommendation (item 7, same message), as a P3 follow-up outside k9sx.

## Change

On reattach, if a picker failed to stop during the last detachment, show one VEN-C8 workspace
notice naming the tab and offering the usual way out (close the tab, or retry). Or, simpler: retry
the stop at reattach as well, and show the notice only if that also fails. Pick the cheaper shape
that leaves no silent dead picker, and bring any EON-C18 or VEN-C8 wording to Lucca first.

## Acceptance

- A Runtime or Venus test: a picker whose detach-time stop failed leads to a visible notice (or a
  successful retry) on reattach.
- One installed observation.

## Prerequisites

eon-popup-cancel-failure-ends-supervisor-k9sx landed.

title: Tell Nova users that Eon loads their own shell configuration
description:
Contract: EON-C9 (managed shells load native user configuration). No contract change.

Why: a Nova user found `make proxy` (aws ssm start-session) failing with 403 in Eon but working in Nova. Cause: `~/.config/nushell/secrets.nu` exported Cloudflare R2 keys as `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`/`AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`. Eon's managed Nushell loads `~/.config/nushell` (EON-C9); Nova layers its packaged config with `~/.config/yazelix/nu` and never loads `~/.config/nushell`, so the leak was hidden there. Nothing in Eon's docs tells a Nova user why the same command behaves differently.

Decision (Lucca, 2026-10-26): keep Eon's model (EON-C9 unchanged); no clean-shell opt-out for now; add one troubleshooting note for people coming from Nova.

Scope: one bullet in `docs/USAGE.md` "Troubleshooting and reporting". No code, contract, or site change (site text follows releases).

Acceptance: the bullet names the files Eon's managed Nushell and Bash load (`~/.config/nushell`, `~/.bashrc`) and the one Nova used (`~/.config/yazelix/nu`), and tells the reader to look there first. Proof route: docs-only (diff, changed path).
close_reason: done

## Report

Found by Codex while reviewing eon-reap-error-unstopped-hfzr (2026-10-23). When Eon Desktop
exits, `reap_presentation` calls `cancel_transient_popups`
(runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/supervisor.rs, around line 1412). That function stops each
transient popup, such as a Project picker, with `stop_owned_session(...)?`. If one popup's stop
fails, or its end cannot be reconciled, the error escapes through `reap_presentation` and ends
the supervisor, taking every healthy tab with it. Before the error, the loop also stops cancelling
the remaining popups.

Reachable cases:
- A picker whose earlier tab close failed and that 7iap kept in its tab (stop_failed).
- A picker that hfzr keeps after its reap failed: an exit on its own whose end does not reconcile.

Before hfzr, the second case ended the supervisor even earlier, in the reap. hfzr moves the
failure from reap time to detach time; it does not make it worse.

## Change

Contain a failed popup cancel at that one popup. Log it once, keep the popup and its terminal for
a retry on the next detach or reap, and keep cancelling the other popups. A
"missing from the supervisor" error should fall through to `session_ended`, as
`stop_transient_popups` already guards against it. Reuse 7iap's and hfzr's containment
(`reap_failure_reported`) rather than adding a second path, so one terminal is not logged twice.

The containment was drafted during hfzr: log, `continue`. The Claude review found no runtime bug
in it. It was taken out of hfzr only for scope, because it needs its own test and possibly
EON-C18 wording.

## Contract

EON-C18 says "presentation detachment cleans the transient picker and attempts the first pane",
and does not cover a failed stop. Any EON-C18 failure wording goes to Lucca through eon-overseer
before code. EON-C8's failed-stop rule ("A failed stop reports failure and keeps the pane") is the
model to follow.

## Acceptance

- A Runtime red/green test with a workspace-picker fixture: a transient picker whose stop fails
  on presentation detach. The supervisor and the other tabs keep running, the failure is logged
  once, and the next detach retries.
- An isolated observation only if eon-overseer asks for one.

## Prerequisites

eon-reap-error-unstopped-hfzr landed.

## Scope boundary

Only the detach-time popup cancel. Not `stop_transient_popups` on generation Stop, which fails
its request rather than the supervisor.

title: Refuse Ctrl+Alt+K/J pane moves under a covering popup
description:
## Decision
Lucca, 2026-10-20: while a popup covers the tab, Ctrl+Alt+K/J (move the selected pane up/down in
its stack) does nothing behind it, as Ctrl+Alt+H/L already does. Reason: the popup covers most of
the screen, so the user cannot see or focus a specific pane, and moving one makes no sense. Alt+M
keeps today's behaviour (dismiss the popup, then add a pane): it can act tab-wise, so it stays.

## Today
The runtime's up/down `move_direction` calls `dismiss_for_pane_action`, which dismisses the covering
popup and then reorders behind it (runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/workspace.rs). Sideways moves
refuse with 'close the popup before moving a pane sideways' (eon-sideways-pane-moves-k9ca).

## Outcome
- Ctrl+Alt+K/J and `eon pane move up|down` under a covering popup fail with `unavailable` before
any change; the popup stays and the topology is unchanged. Wording follows the sideways refusal.
- Venus shows the refusal like the sideways one. Check that Venus's handling of covered tabs does
not dismiss the popup on its own first.
- No EONW change: the request already exists and a refusal is a normal Failure response.

## Contract (needs Lucca's approval before code)
EON-C8: the movement bullet now says sideways movement is unavailable while a popup or picker
covers the tab. Extend that to up/down pane moves. Tab moves (Ctrl+Alt+Shift+H/L) are untouched.

## Open question for Lucca
Alt+K/J up/down *traversal* also dismisses a covering popup before changing the expanded pane. By
the same reasoning (no visible pane to focus) it could refuse too. It is not in scope unless Lucca
adds it; recommendation: decide when this bead starts.

## Scope boundary
In scope: up/down pane moves under a covering popup, runtime and Venus, plus docs (CONTRACTS
EON-C8, USAGE/INTERACTION where they describe popups). Out of scope: Alt+M, Alt+Shift+M, traversal,
tab moves, picker-bound behaviour (already unavailable).

## Acceptance checks
- Runtime test: with a selected popup, Up/Down move fails `unavailable`, popup and order unchanged
(extend sideways_pane_moves_refuse_covering_popups_without_changing_tabs or its neighbour).
- Existing up/down move tests still pass; full suite via `nix develop -c eon-test`; fmt and clippy.
- One isolated installed dogfood observation: Git popup open, Ctrl+Alt+K changes nothing and shows
the refusal. Refresh the profile; do not restart the live supervisor.

## Reference gate
Not consequential: no dependency, wire, or trust-boundary change. Contract text change only.
Portability: neutral.
close_reason: done

title: Always show the popup marker on sidebar rows that come from a popup
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-10-23, after eon-agent-sidebar-yx8.16 shipped the shown-popup marker: "the popup pane in the sidebar should have the popup marker always on". Today (VEN-C30 "Shown popup"), a sidebar row whose source is a popup shows the marker only while that popup is shown. The glyph is better as the popup's identity on its row, so the user always sees at a glance that the agent lives in a popup. The tab header keeps marking a shown popup.

## Contract (VEN-C30; wording approved by the overseer under Lucca's 2026-10-23 approval: "i give you auto-approval to everything, until 700k / but the focus is landing the sidebar / our mission is: happy users")

Replace the "Shown popup" bullet in VEN-C30 Contents with exactly:
"- **Popup marker.** A row whose source terminal is a popup always shows the popup marker glyph after its catalog label. When a listed tab shows a popup (its snapshot `selected_popup` is set), its header ends with the same glyph; a tab whose popups are all hidden gets no header marker. The row's accessible label adds "popup", and the header's adds "popup shown"."

## Scope

In scope: the Venus sidebar row and accessible-label change, the VEN-C30 text, venus/CHANGELOG.md and the root CHANGELOG, USAGE if it describes the marker, and the scene golden or test.

Out of scope: the glyph's shape, the header rule, and Eon Bar tab pills.

## Acceptance

- A Venus scene or unit test: a row sourced from a hidden popup shows the marker, a row sourced from a shown popup shows it too, and a pane-sourced row never does; the header marker still follows `selected_popup`. The test fails on today's code.
- One installed observation after the profile refresh.

## Verification

`nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-venus`, Venus fmt and clippy, converge plus Codex, the nix build, and the installed observation.

Portability disposition: neutral.

description:

"and we should align the borders and font sizes here", then "make the popups name larger, not agents smaller".

title: Preserve Helix keybinding continuity in an Eon editor
description:
## Contract Routing

This is a planning and research decision. It changes no EON product contract and implements no keybinding, editor, or Venus behavior. Helix remains the accepted editor under EON-C4. If `eon-ofb` later selects an Eon-native editor, the exact default-key continuity selected here must be included in that editor's approved product contract before implementation.

## Why

The user requires an eventual Eon editor engine to keep most Helix keybindings whether the engine reuses `helix-core` or not. Physical mappings are not supplied by `helix-core`: Helix's default trie and much of its command dispatch live in `helix-term`. Eon also has workspace shortcuts, so a native editor needs an explicit focus and conflict policy or Venus could steal editor muscle memory.

## Evidence

- Official Helix revision `079a789e8cb08ead67f19e1971a1b7438b37354b`, `helix-term/src/keymap/default.rs`: the default Normal, Select, and Insert tries occupy 412 lines and include prefix maps, aliases, command sequences, and mode-specific behavior.
- The same revision, `helix-term/src/commands.rs`: 7,228 lines contain mappable command dispatch used by the keymap, demonstrating that reuse of `helix-core` alone does not preserve bindings or their behavior.
- The same revision, `docs/architecture.md`: `helix-view` was intended to be frontend-neutral but is currently tied to the terminal UI; commands and keymaps are explicitly routed through `helix-term`.
- README and EON-C8 own current Eon/Venus shortcuts, including Alt+H/L, Alt+K/J, Alt+M, Alt+Shift+T, Alt+Shift+W and Ctrl+Alt reorder chords. Reinventory every accepted chord at activation; the earlier Ctrl+T creation reference is superseded. Check focus and modifier normalization rather than assuming global safety.
- `eon-specify-helix-modal-semantics-3kl` owns the semantic commands and modes to which keys may bind.
- Helix is MPL-2.0 at the inspected revision. Copying or adapting its keymap implementation is a separate license and reuse decision; behavioral compatibility does not authorize source reuse.

## Scope

In scope:
- Inventory every leaf in the pinned Helix default key tries by mode, full key sequence, command identity, aliases, prefix label, and semantic family.
- Map the commands accepted by `eon-specify-helix-modal-semantics-3kl` to their exact Helix default sequences.
- Classify each upstream binding as exact default, accepted alias, deferred with its feature, rejected with reason, or collision requiring explicit user choice.
- Define focus and routing precedence among Venus/Eon workspace actions, editor modes, native IME composition, accessibility actions, and platform-reserved shortcuts.
- Define a generated or mechanically checked coverage report so later upstream keymap drift is visible rather than silently changing Eon behavior.
- Decide whether user keymap configuration is absent, native to the new editor, or separately compatible; default-key continuity does not imply Helix TOML, macro, or Steel compatibility.

Out of scope:
- Implementing key handling, keymap parsing, commands, a configuration framework, Venus focus changes, or an editor.
- Copying the Helix keymap source, forking Helix, adding a runtime dependency, or creating a compatibility adapter.
- Preserving terminal escape encodings, terminal-protocol limitations, Helix widget layout, themes, plugins, Steel scripts, or every application command.
- Rebinding an absent Helix feature to unrelated Eon behavior merely to increase a coverage percentage.

## Decision Work

1. Complete the modal-semantic decision and use its accepted command identities as the mapping target.
2. Mechanically inventory the pinned Helix default tries and record an auditable denominator.
3. Define the core-editing set: mode transitions, navigation and extension, selection manipulation, change/delete/yank/paste, insertion, undo/redo, search/find, registers, repeat, macros, text objects, and accepted language-aware actions.
4. Preserve the exact mode plus key sequence for every accepted core command. Target at least 90% exact sequence continuity among upstream default leaf bindings whose commands exist in the accepted pre-replacement feature set; list every exclusion and never count absent features as preserved.
5. Resolve every collision with Eon/Venus workspace shortcuts using explicit focus ownership. The default recommendation is that a focused editor receives editor bindings, while workspace actions use an explicit non-conflicting chord or workspace-focus mode.
6. Define checks for modifier normalization, prefix timeout or ambiguity, incomplete sequences, IME composition, key repeat, and platform-reserved shortcuts on Linux/native Wayland. macOS feasibility work is outside current EON-C7 scope and requires a separate platform decision.
7. Obtain explicit user approval of the mapping, threshold, collision policy, and configuration non-goals. Do not implement during this Bead.

## Acceptance

- The final matrix covers every pinned default Helix keymap leaf and reports totals by mode and semantic family.
- Every command accepted for the first editor proof and every command required before Helix replacement has an exact default sequence, accepted alias, or explicit rejected/deferred disposition.
- One hundred percent of the accepted core-editing command set preserves its Helix default mode and sequence. Overall exact continuity is at least 90% of applicable upstream default leaves before replacement; the denominator, exclusions, and aliases are inspectable.
- No missing command is rebound to unrelated behavior, and no Eon/Venus shortcut silently shadows a preserved editor binding while the editor owns keyboard focus.
- Prefix maps, aliases, multi-key sequences, modifier distinctions, incomplete sequences, IME, repeat, and focus transitions have deterministic routing and failure behavior.
- The result states whether user remapping is absent or separately scoped and makes no Helix configuration, plugin, terminal-encoding, or source-compatibility promise.
- The result creates no implementation, repository, dependency, EON/VEN contract, or Helix fork.

## Verification

- `git -C /home/lucca/pjs/yazelix-dir/helix rev-parse HEAD` must report the inspected revision, or the Bead must record a newly inspected exact revision and regenerate the matrix.
- The inventory command or focused proof must derive mappings from `helix-term/src/keymap/default.rs` and retain its output or digest with the decision evidence.
- `rg -n 'Alt\\+|Ctrl\\+|F6|shortcut' README.md /home/lucca/pjs/yazelix-dir/eon-desktop/README.md` must identify every accepted Eon/Venus shortcut considered by the collision matrix.
- The final Bead state must contain the complete matrix or durable evidence location, counts, coverage calculation, collision decisions, platform disposition, rejected alternatives, and explicit user decision.
- No source, test, manifest, contract index, dependency, generated artifact, or ambient configuration changes during this decision.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if the semantic command set is unresolved or a key would map to behavior different from Helix under the same mode and sequence.
- Stop for explicit user choice when an Eon workspace shortcut conflicts with a required editor binding and neither context nor an existing focus mode resolves it cleanly.
- Stop if reaching the target would require promising unselected Helix features, configuration compatibility, or copying/adapting MPL source without the required gate.
- Stop if platform input behavior cannot distinguish a required sequence reliably; record the exact blocker and replacement cost.

## Maintenance Notes

Effort M, implementation risk MEDIUM after modal semantics stabilize, confidence HIGH. This Bead depends on `eon-specify-helix-modal-semantics-3kl` and constrains any positive `eon-ofb` decision. It preserves muscle memory while leaving implementation reuse open. Helix remains Eon's default editor until a separately proved replacement is explicitly accepted.

title: Preserve live replacement sockets during dead cleanup
description:
## Contract

Preserve EON-C11: when generation inspection or supervisor cleanup observes an owned dead Unix socket, Eon may remove only that exact dead socket. If the pathname changes to a replacement before removal, Eon leaves the replacement and every Session untouched. Missing, live, unowned, or non-socket paths remain unchanged.

Consumer: local Eon and EonTerm generation inspection, launch, attachment, and stop flows. Trigger: dead-endpoint cleanup concurrent with pathname replacement. Result: cleanup is identity-bound and live replacement supervisors remain reachable. Important failures: metadata or connection races fail closed without killing children or unlinking an unobserved owner.

## Evidence

Audit eon-audit-eon-runtime-lifecycle-wqz at exact edge revision 88a57f066e426cb2882c4969b9036c4e358fc48b records the TOCTOU at crates/eon/src/main.rs remove_dead_socket and the existing sufficient SocketIdentity / ControlListener drop pattern. No existing Bead owns this defect.

## Prerequisites and reference gate

The lifecycle audit is closed. Orbit 26b4b9465b3f0e74f091a0aae93fddc61412b893 and Venus 50b7ef7f6c9d5b531b79ecca67c9c8fdf40f355f remain the latest accepted source revisions; later child changes are proof/docs only. Reuse the unchanged Ghosthub 0.7.0 ownership evidence recorded by the audit: preserve exact destructive-target revalidation and process-owned socket namespaces. Prefer the existing local identity mechanism; reject a daemon, PID inference, protocol field, new dependency, child change, or broad supervisor abstraction.

## Scope

In scope: the shared dead-socket removal invariant in crates/eon/src/main.rs, one deterministic regression check, required EON-C11 proof/current docs, CHANGELOG, README LOC, exact Rust/Nix/profile verification, and a post-change fresh-eyes/simplification pass.

Out of scope: the separately audited workspace action timeout, child behavior, new contracts, new dependencies, compatibility surfaces, distribution expansion, unrelated refactors, and interruption of live supervisors.

## Acceptance

- A deterministic red/green check replaces a socket after dead observation and proves cleanup preserves the reachable replacement.
- The same owner still removes an unchanged owned dead socket and leaves missing, live, unowned, and non-socket paths unchanged.
- Cleanup reuses one existing identity mechanism with the smallest coherent diff and adds no dependency or public surface.
- Locked format, check, tests, Clippy, Nix build/check, LOC, and git diff checks pass.
- The active eon profile resolves to the exact working-tree artifact; installed artifact identity is checked without restarting any supervisor.
- A complete post-change correctness and simplification pass finds no further in-scope correction.
close_reason: Deduplicated and strengthened EON-C11 discovery proof, corrected changelog precision, and reconverged with full Rust/Nix/profile verification.

Proposed behavior intentionally changes only that replacement race; all ordinary behavior stays the same.
- Outputs/errors/status/ordering/logs: same outside the bug window; cleanup remains silent and best-effort.
- Side effects/lifecycle: unchanged dead socket is still removed; live, missing, non-socket, unowned, and changed paths remain untouched; ControlListener still removes its own path and preserves replacements.

Fresh-eyes correction to comment 438 — 2026-08-13

The first green identity-recheck draft narrowed the race but did not eliminate it: pathname replacement can still happen between the final metadata read and unlink. Revised decision:
- Keep the specialized ControlListener Drop unchanged.
- Reuse the existing root startup lock only after a generation probe reports dead, then re-probe through remove_dead_socket before unlinking and removing the empty generation directory.
- Move generation-directory preparation under that same existing launch lock; otherwise cleanup could remove a just-prepared directory before bind.
- Stop mutating legacy fixed-namespace sockets: current Eon does not launch that namespace and cannot serialize an older implementation replacement.

title: Preserve opaque endpoint bytes in workspace JSON
description:
## Contract routing

Harden accepted EON-C10 without changing EONW v1. The consumer is local automation invoking a successful workspace command with `--json`; the trigger is a Snapshot whose opaque Orbit endpoint contains bytes that are not valid UTF-8; the result is valid JSON that preserves every endpoint byte exactly and deterministically. The human view remains a safe diagnostic, and Venus continues to consume the typed EONW byte field directly.

The current JSON projection is expressly not the protocol schema, but it is a machine-readable projection of the same accepted result. This correction changes no command, EONW field, runtime-path policy, Orbit or Venus contract, dependency, or distribution promise.

## Why

Workspace state preserves endpoint paths as Unix bytes, but the JSON view calls `String::from_utf8_lossy`. Different endpoints can therefore collapse to the same replacement-character string, and automation cannot reconstruct the socket path it was given.

Impact: MEDIUM. Effort: S/M. Implementation risk: MEDIUM because the JSON endpoint field representation changes. Confidence: HIGH.

## Evidence

- `crates/eon/src/workspace.rs:54`: Snapshot construction copies exact `Path` bytes.

title: Deliver every scroll preview answer so Venus needs no retry timer
description:
## Problem

Orbit's client OutputQueue (orbit/src/socket.rs, `replaceable_suffix`) lets a newer Frame, WheelOutcome::Viewport or ScrollOutcome::Viewport replace a VerticalPreview answer that it has not started writing. Venus therefore cannot tell from a frame whether the answer to its outstanding PreviewVertical was dropped or is still coming. That includes the case where Orbit is holding the request under DEC 2026 synchronized output.

eon-scroll-preview-per-frame-hhzy works around this in Venus. After the first frame that follows a preview request, Venus waits PREVIEW_ANSWER_GRACE (50 ms) for the answer, then asks again. The retry can overlap a request that Orbit still holds under DEC 2026, if a frame already in flight started the grace and the hold lasts more than 50 ms. Orbit then fails the retry with InvalidInput "vertical interaction is already deferred". Venus shows that as an Orbit notice and resets the gesture, losing its distance and momentum. Base Venus had the same exposure on the very next frame. hhzy reduced it but cannot remove it from the client side.

## Expected

Every PreviewVertical gets exactly one answer, or the attachment ends. A newer frame no longer discards an unsent preview answer. A newer preview may still replace an older unsent one, so the queue stays bounded to one preview. Venus can then hold its single outstanding preview until the answer arrives, and drop PREVIEW_ANSWER_GRACE, frame_arrived, retry_preview and the about_to_wait deadline.

## Contract

ORB-C8 (vertical exchange) and the client output queue rules it relies on. Check whether ORB-C8's text or Orbit's PROTOCOL.md describes preview replacement. If any contract text changes, stop for Lucca's approval.

## Prerequisites

eon-scroll-preview-per-frame-hhzy landed.

## Scope

In scope: Orbit OutputQueue replacement rules for previews (orbit/src/socket.rs and its tests), and Venus dropping the grace retry in venus/src/application/scroll.rs and application.rs. Out of scope: other queue classes and pressure bounds.

## Acceptance

- An Orbit queue test: a frame queued after an unsent preview keeps the preview, and the frame still replaces older frames.
- A Venus test: the hold is released only by an answer or a reset, with no timer.
- One isolated installed observation: wheel scrolling during a burst that uses DEC 2026 synchronized output keeps the gesture, with no "already deferred" notice.

## Portability disposition

neutral.

title: Replace a scroll preview kept in history when scrollback pruning moves the viewport
description:
## Problem

Seen in the eon-stale-preview-row-during-output-h7y0 installed observation (2026-10-27): package /nix/store/hcqibfi1dhi00shvbn8qvimqsb1i4nr3-eon-0.1.3, isolated headless Sway 1.12, pixman, 1600x900, wdotool 0.5.3 wlr-protocols. While `./b` printed 30,000 numbered lines, the pane was scrolled into history and left with a sub-row Down remainder: the viewport covered rows 14602 to 14643, with a partial 14644 drawn from a fresh Down preview. Output kept running, and the viewport later jumped about 400 rows while still in history. At the end it covered 15002 to 15043 (`↓ 14959 rows`), but the bottom edge still drew a partial "burst line 14644". That row came from the Down preview kept from before the jump. The likely cause is that Orbit prunes its 16 MiB scrollback budget (SCROLLBACK_BUDGET_BYTES, orbit/src/frame.rs) past the pinned viewport, which then moves to the oldest retained row. This has not been verified.

Venus keeps a compatible Viewport preview across frames (venus/src/model.rs, Frame arm). After h7y0, TerminalScroll::next_request replaces a kept preview only while the accepted frame is at live, because VEN-C7 says "after history entry, later output leaves the authoritative viewport pinned". At the scrollback budget's oldest edge, that claim does not hold.

Evidence: /home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/h7y0-work/obs1/{live1,done}.png, with bottom-edge crops in obs1/crops/bot.png. Driver: /home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/h7y0-work/run.sh and obs.sh.

## Expected

When pruning moves a viewport that is in history, Venus draws no row from before the move. It either asks for a replacement preview, through h7y0's paced and held path, or Orbit reports the move. First confirm the mechanism in Orbit: whether pruning moves the viewport pin, and whether the frame reports it in a way Venus can see without comparing rows.

## Contract

VEN-C7, and perhaps ORB-C8. The pinned-history sentence may need an exception at the scrollback budget edge. Any change to contract text stops for Lucca's approval.

## Prerequisites

eon-stale-preview-row-during-output-h7y0 (the paced replacement path).

## Scope

In scope: deciding when a preview kept in history is stale, in venus/src/application/scroll.rs and venus/src/model.rs, and confirming Orbit's pruning behavior. Out of scope: Orbit's output queue (eon-preview-answer-survives-frames-u979).

## Acceptance

- A Venus test with a kept preview over a frame whose history viewport moved.
- One isolated installed observation: scrolled to the oldest retained history while a burst prunes it, with no stale edge row.

## Portability disposition

neutral.

(residual 1). The Claude reviewer raised the same point as a nit.

Revised gate: SessionModel::preview_may_be_stale is true when `rows_from_live == 0` (at live) or
`rows_from_live == history_rows` (at the oldest retained row). In libghostty's PageList.grow(), at the

either leaves the viewport's pin intact, so its rows and the rows beside it stay the same, or moves the
viewport to the oldest retained row. So a moved viewport always lands at distance 0, and that one

in-history case that sends anything.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Diagnosis (by source, before code; no Orbit change needed):
- Orbit keeps no viewport position of its own. It sets libghostty's scrollback byte budget
(set_scrollback_max_bytes(Some(SCROLLBACK_BUDGET_BYTES)), orbit/src/frame.rs and orbit/src/pty.rs) and
reports libghostty's native viewport. In libghostty's PageList.grow(), pruning drops the first page.
A viewport pinned inside that page becomes `.top` (the oldest retained row). A viewport pinned below
it keeps its rows, but its offset from the oldest row drops by the page's rows. A viewport already at
`.top` stays there while its rows change on every prune. Orbit's own test
(orbit/src/frame.rs, byte-budget eviction with the viewport held at Top) shows the moved case:
`rows_from_live == history_rows` with different rows. (The PageList reading came from a libghostty
source tree in another worktree's build dir; the Orbit test confirms the behavior at this revision.)
- The frame carries only ScrollPosition { rows_from_live, history_rows }. history_rows -
rows_from_live is the viewport's distance from the oldest retained row. Output below a pinned
viewport keeps it constant. Pruning lowers it, and at the oldest row it stays 0 while the rows change.
- Venus keeps a compatible Viewport preview across frames (model.rs Frame arm). After h7y0,
TerminalScroll::next_request replaces it only when SessionModel::at_live, so a pruned viewport in
history kept the pre-move preview: the observed "burst line 14644" under 15043.

Decision: widen h7y0's replacement gate, keeping its path. SessionModel::at_live becomes
SessionModel::preview_may_be_stale. It is true at live (as before), at the oldest retained row, or
when the viewport's distance from the oldest retained row differs from that distance when Orbit
answered the retained preview. The model records that distance (scroll_preview_top) where it
accepts a Viewport preview (VerticalPreview answer, ScrollOutcome next). next_request is unchanged
except that its `live` parameter is now `stale`, so the replacement keeps h7y0's pacing (at most once
per PREVIEW_ANSWER_GRACE, 50 ms), the revision check, and hhzy's one-outstanding hold. Pinned history
with no prune still sends nothing.

Rejected:
- Retiring the kept preview when the distance changes. It would show the remainder as zero until
the replacement arrives, which VEN-C7 rejects ("instead of presenting the remainder as zero"). It
also cannot see the oldest-row case, where the counts do not move.
- An Orbit position field (an absolute top row or prune epoch). That is a protocol change for Orbit,
it is outside this bead's scope, and eon-preview-answer-survives-frames-u979 and orb-j2i.7 are
changing Orbit now.

Residuals:
1. Until the replacement answer arrives (normally the Orbit message after the frame; up to one grace
if a replacement went out in the last 50 ms), the sub-row band can still show rows from before the
move. This matches h7y0's residual at live.
2. At the oldest retained row, Venus cannot tell a prune from plain output. So with a sub-row
remainder held there while output runs, it sends up to one preview per 50 ms, even when history is
under budget.

Not consequential under AGENTS.md: no dependency, protocol, contract, or lifecycle change. Contract
text is unchanged; the change implements VEN-C7's "Venus keeps only that bounded revision-bound
preview until Orbit supplies its replacement". Configurability: no new value (it reuses
PREVIEW_ANSWER_GRACE). Portability: neutral.

Question for Lucca (does not block this bead):
1. VEN-C7 says "after history entry, later output leaves the authoritative viewport pinned", and
ORB-C8 does not say where a pruned pin goes. Both are inaccurate at the 16 MiB budget edge, where
libghostty moves the viewport to the oldest retained row. Recommendation: one contract-text bead for
ORB-C8 (a viewport pinned in pruned history moves to the oldest retained row) and VEN-C7 (pinned
until the byte budget prunes past it; Venus then replaces a kept preview through the same paced
path). That way the contracts state what the code already does. Not adopted here, because contract
text needs your approval and its own Codex round.

Red/green: kept_previews_go_stale_when_output_moves_the_viewport (venus/tests/canonical_scene.rs).
With base's gate (the at_live body under the new name) it failed at the first pruned case: "assertion
failed: kept_over(at(1, 10, 100), at(2, 12, 60))". With the change it passes. h7y0's
sub_row_remainder_replaces_a_preview_older_than_the_frame still covers the pacing and the hold.

title: Prove EON-C7 on Apple Silicon macOS
description:
## Outcome and contract

Extend and prove `EON-C7` by running full Eon on Apple Silicon macOS through the same canonical component graph, lifecycle policy, workspace contracts, and child ownership used on Linux.

- Consumer: a user launching full `eon` on `aarch64-darwin`.
- Trigger: start the Nix-composed accepted Eon component set on macOS.
- Result: Eon launches exact accepted Orbit and Venus, materializes the accepted workspace and managed environment, reports exact component identity, and preserves orchestration, lifecycle, configuration, and failure ownership without a second platform composition.
- Important failures: an unavailable artifact, incompatible child proof, unsupported managed tool, unsafe lifecycle, or platform-specific graph divergence fails explicitly before a support claim.

## Order and ownership

Prerequisites are exact accepted Orbit `ORB-C14` from `orb-prove-orbit-apple-silicon-macos-w4j` and the Apple Silicon slice of Venus `VEN-C16` from `ven-prove-venus-apple-silicon-macos-nm7`. Nova and the historical EonTerm-for-Nova package matrix are independent and do not block Eon.

Keep one versioned component manifest and one Rust orchestration path. Platform artifact identities, paths, process mechanics, desktop integration, and Nix target expressions remain narrow inputs or adapters. Orbit owns Sessions and PTYs; Venus owns native presentation; Eon owns composition and product policy.

Rejected: separate branches, per-platform component graphs, copied child schemas, Nova/Mars/Eonova fallback, a generic platform framework, and treating Nix evaluation or compilation as native proof.

## References before code

Required: current Eon contracts, architecture, canonical manifest/schema/validator, runtime and workspace owners, Nix composition, exact child proofs, official Apple process/path/application behavior relevant to Eon-owned policy, and each managed component's exact Apple Silicon support and artifact identity. Any new build/runtime tool or dependency passes the normal gate before edits.

## Cost and proof boundary

Automated child and composition checks use bounded standard Apple Silicon GitHub-hosted jobs first. Interactive full-product proof uses a temporary Apple Silicon host only after Orbit and Venus candidates pass. Paid macOS infrastructure stays within R$100 per month; rental instances are deleted after each proof session. The Nix-only phase adds no signing, notarization, installer, package manager, or release automation.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. One canonical manifest describes the same component roles and compatibility on Linux and `aarch64-darwin`; target artifacts vary explicitly without duplicating graph or policy.
2. A native Apple Silicon Nix build/install in an isolated destination launches full Eon, one Orbit Session, one Venus client, the accepted tab/pane workspace, Helix, Yazi, Ratconfig, the managed shell environment, and exact version diagnostics.
3. Native proof covers first launch, repeat launch/present, rendering, input, resize, clipboard, workspace actions, Alt+Z, tool popups, detach/reconnect, child failure, configuration, update staging, Stop, cleanup, and preservation of live Session ownership.
4. Linux canonical Rust/Nix/manifest checks remain green. Native evidence records exact hardware, OS, toolchain, artifacts, component closures, commands, failures, observations, and limitations.
5. Missing managed tools or behavior are explicit blockers, not silent omissions or target-specific policy.
6. No signing, notarization, DMG, Homebrew, public release channel, Intel macOS, universal binary, or Nova integration is claimed; `eon-hzq` owns any later distribution decision.

Stop if macOS requires a second manifest, child-behavior copy, incompatible lifecycle promise, hidden fallback, or unapproved dependency/tool decision.
notes: User pause — 2026-09-17: ORB-C14 is accepted, but the remaining VEN-C16 proof and full-Eon native acceptance require interactive Apple Silicon hardware. Tyce has been asked; keep this epic deferred and unclaimed until Venus is accepted on a real Mac. After that, create only the Eon-owned children revealed by the child proofs: component-graph/Nix admission, local orchestration trust/lifecycle, and installed product dogfood. Keep one owner and failure domain per child.

User platform decision — 2026-08-21 America/Sao_Paulo

Current chosen direction:
- Eon is Linux-only for active product scope.
- Wayland is the primary quality and performance target.
- X11/Xwayland remains a bounded compatibility and isolated-verification backend, not a parity target; retain it while its value exceeds its measured cost.
- macOS implementation, proof, CI, packaging, distribution, and support remain inactive. EON-C16 is not approved.
- Reconsider macOS only when concrete user, adoption, or revenue evidence justifies the permanent platform and proof cost. A later concentrated port is accepted as preferable to paying an unproved dual-platform tax now.

Preserve the future option without carrying speculative implementation:

2. Linux PTY, process, path, graphics, and desktop APIs stay behind explicit platform owners.
3. Shared scene and renderer models do not contain Wayland object types.
4. No macOS backend, dependency feature, CI, artifact, compatibility promise, or proof is retained solely for possible future support.

This is a reversible planning and product-scope decision. It changes no EON-C, ORB-C, or VEN-C contract or proof status, claims no Bead, and authorizes no source, manifest, dependency, documentation, or distribution change. title: Roll accepted Orbit-managed Stop into Eonova
description:
## Contract routing

Roll the already accepted EON-C15/ORB-C13 Stop result into the private Eonova composition. This issue adds no Eon, Orbit, Venus, or Eonova runtime contract and does not rerun the accepted Eon/EonTerm recovery suite.

Consumer: the authorized local user running installed private Eonova on x86_64 Linux.

Trigger: eon-accept-eon-orbit-same-boot-recovery-iwc has accepted and published the exact Eon/EonTerm artifact.

Result: Eonova pins that exact Eon source, preserves its private namespace and Nova composition, and exposes the same EonTerm owner-routed Stop result. Stopped means the one Orbit-owned containment is empty; Failure remains bounded and visible.

Important failures: no live profile update interrupts a supervisor; no old generation is relabeled; no Eonova shutdown code, hidden child pin, Mars/Rio fallback, process scan, compatibility adapter, or duplicated Eon proof.

## Exact prerequisite

- Closed accepted eon-accept-eon-orbit-same-boot-recovery-iwc with exact Eon, Orbit, Venus, manifest, lock, package, and installed proof identities.
- Current complete Eonova instructions and exact input/lock/wrapper/namespace/desktop/package/profile/docs surfaces.
- This issue remains deferred until that prerequisite closes.

## Smallest rollout slice

Advance only Eonova's exact Eon input/assertion and generated lock as required. Preserve the accepted Nova no-Mars pin, yzx enter argv, private XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/eonova namespace, desktop identity, and visibility. Update current-state docs/LOC only where the consumed artifact identity or Stop result requires it. Build/install the private package, refresh its profile without restarting live supervisors, and run one isolated Eonova no-survivor observation.

Reuse the accepted Eon/EonTerm multi-Session, recovery, authority-negative, and failure proofs by exact identity. Add no runtime code, test framework, helper, protocol, updater, branch, or compatibility layer. Old immutable Eonova generations retain historical semantics.

## Acceptance Criteria

The canonical completion criteria are stored in this Bead's acceptance_criteria field.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Eonova pins the exact published EON-C15 source and generated lock; evaluation rejects drift and contains no hidden Eon, Orbit, or Venus pin.
2. The private Eonova package retains exact Nova no-Mars yzx enter argv, XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/eonova, private visibility, desktop identity, and Mars/Rio absence; regular Eon artifacts and namespaces remain unchanged.
3. One fresh isolated Eonova run contains a deterministic HUP/TERM-ignoring descendant. Stop stays pending through Orbit-owned cleanup, returns Stopped only after Orbit containment is empty, and leaves no Eonova-spawned process or runtime residue.
4. Profile refresh restarts or stops no pre-existing Eon, EonTerm, or Eonova supervisor; exact PID/start-time observations prove preservation.
5. Package, closure, lock, license, namespace, desktop, repository, LOC, diff, Beads, and remote-edge checks pass; installed artifacts trace to pushed edge commits.
6. The accepted Eon/EonTerm recovery, multi-Session Stop, failure, and authority-negative proofs are cited by exact identity and not rerun. Eonova contains no shutdown code or duplicated policy; Orbit remains the descendant-cleanup owner.

title: Prove the manual Nix-free Linux bundle
description:
## Contract

First implementation slice of eon-ohh under EON-C5/EON-C6: a user manually extracts one immutable relocatable x86_64 Linux native-Wayland archive and runs the accepted useful Eon composition without host Nix. Children retain their mechanisms; Eon owns assembly and consumes the canonical exact component graph.

## Prerequisites and reference gate

Accepted eon-p93 supplies repaired Nix reliability, active-work and accessibility evidence, release ownership and maintenance/cost decisions. Read docs/DISTRIBUTION.md, EON-C1 through C7, the accepted graph and child artifact/launch contracts. Consume the exact selected release tool; compare closure relocation, loader/system-library/driver prerequisites, fonts, managed tools, license/redistribution obligations, verification and owned LOC. Doodlestein/dist/local Nix evidence remains a tool-gate input, not tool adoption. A materially different assembler/tool or maintenance envelope reopens the decision.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Produce one immutable archive, checksum and signature or attestation binding it, with exact graph/provenance and retained size/closure observations. Immutable release assets remain authority; prepare manual-download website copy without publishing it.
- On a clean non-Nix native-Wayland machine/user environment, extraction launches useful composed Eon and its managed tools/child processes. No host Nix store, daemon/evaluator, development checkout or undeclared machine-local reference is needed. Record actual host prerequisites and portability limits.
- Direct and supported Nix diagnostics report the same accepted exact graph and runtime semantics; no second graph, hidden substitution or store path as component identity.
- Record exact source/artifact/environment, commands, failures and results. Prove the manual delivery boundary and introduced deterministic logic through the narrowest affected Rust/Nix route; reuse valid unchanged runtime evidence. Align bundle usage/contract docs and README LOC at implementation acceptance.
- Hand one accepted artifact/verification contract to the installer slice. This task does not claim installer, active-work upgrade/removal or public-beta acceptance.

## Scope boundary

One manual Linux bundle only. No extra architecture, macOS, X11/Xwayland, Home Manager, extra package format, service-manager requirement, auto-updater, live handoff or restart persistence. Publication/promotion remains a separate explicit user decision. Implemented and mechanically verified as an unpublished manual-development candidate; installer/public-beta gates remain separate.
notes:
Manual development slice implemented and mechanically verified on 2026-10-10. Exact source: Eon base 68bafb63e58fa38ca2f58562865ed70c4315ba43 plus the source SHA-256 receipt in delivery-final/SOURCE.json. Final archive output /nix/store/54fi35mngm4ryzc3pb6h4fi369vg9dg8-eon-0.1.0-x86_64-linux-bundle; SHA-256 ad351bb2c914f7319ba0bd1006a8ab77041a05375687a6aac350cd7a6294f971. It preserves accepted Eon /nix/store/ayb2ilp1rq7c95q4r1b3qn8qzdx5pw02-eon-0.1.0 and the unchanged manifest/lock/child graph. Complete receipts: /home/lucca/.local/state/eon/proofs/eon-manual-bundle-2026-10-10-m7mqh_vg/acceptance.json; manually verifiable archive, signed checksums, SOURCE.json and disposable proof public key are in delivery-final/.

Nix remains the composition owner. A 51-line std-only static Rust entrypoint delegates namespace mechanics to locked Bubblewrap 0.11.2 and maps the unchanged complete closure read-only at private /nix. The user-requested Nova comparison inspected ffc9df53b57c354b2d22b2183f611c010e235850 packaging/runtime and native probes. Adopt normalized archives, executable-root selection and clean relocated interaction proof; reject coordinated ELF/shebang/config/provider rewriting for this slice. Earlier reference comments retain exact decisions and rejected tools. Later evidence confirms non-UTF-8 invalid Eon CLI gets the same graceful Nix/direct diagnostic; the helper imposes no new Unicode restriction.

Native proof: fresh isolated non-Nix user on Pop!_OS 24.04/Linux 7.1.5, private native Sway 1.12/lavapipe with host store/checkout/home hidden. Relocated read-only root/external symlink, same exact diagnostics, twelve managed tools, Unicode argv/cwd, native Nushell keyboard input, unchanged Orbit/workload PIDs across detach/reopen, and exact Stop/cleanup pass. Missing private closure refuses host store fallback. All product and private observer processes ended; original ambient PID/start/executable identities and unrelated profile elements remain. The active Eon profile was refreshed twice and resolves to the proved package; live work remains on its prior generation.

Affected Eon/EonTerm Rust builds each pass the same 79 Eon/Runtime checks; static bootstrap build/fmt/Clippy, full flake checks and source-package gate pass. Static ELF guard red/green rejects inspection errors and dynamic bootstraps. The final rebuilt archive is byte-identical to the native-proved candidate. Signature/checksum verification and tamper rejection pass. 406,102,478 archive bytes; 409 closure paths/1,830,687,400 NAR bytes; extraction allocated 1,877,639,168 bytes and took 14.88s in this environment. No bounds or hosted cost are added. Contracts, manual-download draft, development docs, changelog and LOC are aligned.

Installer handoff: consume this one verified archive and preserve its layout/entrypoint and payloads used by live work. No installer, upgrade/removal, wider public-beta, hardware-GPU, human-reader, publication or promotion acceptance. Namespace support is required; private /nix hides a host Nix store, so Nix users keep the Nix channel. Public release still needs Lucca's real trust anchor and exact closure redistribution notices/source obligations, including static helper dependencies; a disposable proof key is not release authority. A preexisting Orbit non-UTF-8 child-argument panic was reproduced in the accepted Nix binary and retained as an out-of-scope child finding; no child change or extra bead was made. Existing narrow Orca #757 waiver remains unchanged.
close_reason: Manual Nix-free candidate and verification/native proof complete; installer and public release gates remain separate.

title: Prove the thin Linux bundle installer and safe updates
description:
## Contract

Second implementation slice of eon-ohh under EON-C5/EON-C6: an inspectable user-local installer consumes the exact accepted manual bundle and safely installs, selects, upgrades, rolls back and removes only Eon-owned installation/integration. User configuration/data and active work survive. Nix remains supported; manual extraction stays available.

## Prerequisites and reference gate

Wait for the accepted manual Nix-free Linux bundle and its exact artifact, graph, host prerequisites and verification contract; eon-p93 remains the release-owner/tool/cost decision. Read docs/DISTRIBUTION.md, EON-C5/C6, current EON-C11/C15 generation/lifecycle proofs, the accepted active-work policy and installer/tool comparisons. Name the sole owner of download/verification, extraction, version payload retention, atomic selection and removal. Prefer the accepted release tool; any new dependency or durable non-Rust implementation language requires the existing gate and user decision.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Resolve a pinned immutable release over TLS and verify its artifact binding before use. Provide inspection/dry-run, a versioned user prefix, atomic current selection, upgrade, rollback and removal; avoid unrequested shell-profile edits and collisions with unrelated tools or Nix installations.
- Partial download, verification, extraction or activation failure leaves the prior installation usable. Malformed/untrusted archive content cannot escape owned extraction/activation paths or overwrite unrelated files; enforce the trust boundary with the selected tool rather than assuming an artifact is safe.
- Switching current never silently stops live supervisors/terminals. Preserve any prior executable/version payload required by retained live work or stage its removal, under accepted generation contracts. Prove ordinary long-running work and a real agent retain exact identity across upgrade/rollback; introduce no new restart-persistence or live-handoff promise.
- Removal affects only exact owned installation/integration points, preserves configuration/data and unrelated tools, and retains or stages payload still required by live work. Verification failure and interrupted operations have documented recovery.
- At the outermost delivery boundary, prove fresh install, active-work upgrade/rollback and safe removal using the accepted exact graph. Record exact artifacts/environment/failures/results; add the cheapest checks for introduced deterministic logic and use the affected Rust/Nix route. Align install/usage/contract docs and README LOC.
- Prepare inspectable yazelix.com installer copy pointing to immutable release assets. Hand delivery proof to eon-ohh and eon-qualify-nix-free-linux-public-beta-lm9p; this task does not publish, promote or qualify the wider beta.

## Scope boundary

One small installer over the accepted Linux artifact. No second composition graph, new runtime feature, Home Manager, macOS, extra architecture/package format, service-manager requirement, auto-updater, live handoff or restart persistence. Accepted development installer; public publication remains an explicit user decision.
notes:
Implementation contract and reference gate, 2026-10-10:
A separate Linux eon-install bootstrap consumes a caller-selected exact HTTPS archive and same-directory SHA256SUMS/OpenSSH signature. An independently supplied allowed_signers record authorizes eon-release in namespace eon-bundle; no downloaded key becomes trusted. Verify before extraction/execution. Install under an owned private prefix, with content-addressed versions, one atomic current selector and prefix/bin/eon. Rollback selects an explicit installed digest. Remove owned selectors only; retain every version at its original path to protect live work without a second runtime-liveness owner. No automatic pruning, shell edits, desktop integration, Nix calls or publication. Dry-run verifies the download without changing the prefix. Public release trust/licensing remain separate gates.

Nova comparison: Yazelix/nova ffc9df53b57c354b2d22b2183f611c010e235850, docs/portable-runtime.md and planned installer yazelix-nix-free-installer-nx4-a48.5. Adopt one artifact consumer, version directories, atomic selection, failure preservation and no automatic old-version deletion. Its POSIX-shell implementation is planned, not an existing implementation to copy. Eon keeps durable policy in Rust under its language decision.

Tool/dependency gate: retain the accepted local Nix/Rust release owner; reject cargo-dist 0.33.0's broader release/CI framework for this one lifecycle (https://axodotdev.github.io/cargo-dist/). Standard Rust owns filesystem transitions and File::try_lock. Host curl owns TLS/redirects with curlrc disabled and HTTPS-only protocols; host ssh-keygen owns the already selected OpenSSH signature format. A Rust HTTP/TLS/signature stack would duplicate those platform responsibilities in this slice. New exact crates: tar=0.4.46 (MIT/Apache-2.0, safe streaming entry unpack), zstd=0.14.2 (BSD-3-Clause, vendored/static decoder; optional features off), sha2=0.11.0 (MIT/Apache-2.0, streaming SHA-256), tempfile=3.27.0 (MIT/Apache-2.0, private staging/cleanup). They own complete parser/decoder/hash/temp responsibilities; native tar/zstd/hash pipelines add host prerequisites and status/metadata parsing. No new framework or runtime composition graph. Cargo.lock pins transitives; replace crates only with an equally safe smaller complete owner. tar's concurrent hostile destination mutation exclusion is addressed by private 0700 staging; same-user hostile concurrent mutation remains outside the existing contract.

Primary evidence: exact downloaded crate Cargo.toml/licenses/source; tar::Entry::unpack_in and crate Security section; Rust File::try_lock; curl --disable/--proto/--proto-redir; OpenBSD ssh-keygen -Y verify. Cheapest falsifiers: real archive escape and selector ownership fixtures first (TDD), then exact static installed bootstrap over a local TLS proof release, failed signature/hash/extraction/activation and interrupted staging, and native non-Nix active ordinary/agent work across upgrade/rollback/removal. No official release key or publication is inferred.

Baseline edge d3b280870e046246f91c3c82f235c3ef9c6e90e5; existing agent-protocol files, AGENTS.md, README LOC and unrelated Beads edits are user-owned and preserved. Orbit6bc269c and Venus58f2eaa remain latest accepted source changes; later child HEAD changes are metadata/docs only. Accepted development slice, 2026-10-11 — EON-C5/C6

Implemented the separate static Rust eon-install workspace and Nix installer package. TLS/signature/hash verification precedes private extraction and executable smoke checks; a prefix ownership marker and exclusive lock guard content-addressed payloads and atomic selection. Explicit installed-digest rollback and owned-selector removal retain every payload, user configuration and live processes. No shell/profile rewrite, runtime liveness mechanism, pruning, Nix target dependency, public signer or publication.

Limits/negatives: first observer killed only Bubblewrap's wrapper, so its installer child continued; attempt-1-observer-interruption retains that rejected harness result. Corrected process-group interruption passes. The Codex TUI is real/authenticated but idle: no model turn, delegated coding task, semantic resume or new active-agent policy is claimed. Its temporary CODEX_HOME produces a helper-alias warning; the TUI still reaches its input prompt. This scripted same-host proof is not independent-machine, hardware-GPU, human-reader or wider beta acceptance. Delivery/handoff: active eon profile refreshed to exact f9j917vzqqnn64ni2vc67cz6g4jsx19r artifact; installed versions and artifact equality pass, every other profile element remains unchanged, no live supervisor restarted. Release trust anchor, exact redistribution obligations, public-beta qualification, publication, promotion and commit/push remain outside this completed development slice.

Fresh-eyes correction baseline, 2026-10-11:
The user authorized fixes/simplification over the unchanged accepted installer candidate. Bound to this same bead; no other planning writes. Confirmed empty XDG_DATA_HOME makes dry-run fail instead of falling back; the freedesktop Base Directory spec0.8 requires empty/unset fallback and ignores relative values. The preflight child.kill only terminates the bundle/Bubblewrap wrapper, leaving descendants on timeout, the same wrapper mechanism observed in the original interrupted-probe failure. Keep prior selection/live user work protected.
Choose existing host GNU coreutils timeout to own the bounded preflight process group, rather than extending Rust with libc group-kill and signal/timer/cancellation policy. This adds one explicit host tool for install/rollback, no bundled dependency or license incorporation; inspect GNU source GPLv3 as invocation-only. Missing tool or failed check leaves current unchanged. Primary: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/coreutils/coreutils/v9.4/src/timeout.c; https://specifications.freedesktop.org/basedir/latest/. Remove local polling/sleep/deadline ownership; error text reports failed/timed-out check. This is a regression correction with an explicit host-prerequisite change, not claimed fully isomorphic.
No hash formatter simplification: sha2.11's hybrid-array output lacks LowerHex; adding a crate for32 bytes would increase net complexity. Retain private extraction/checksum/ownership validation and intentional payload retention. title: Make the diagnostic-log pruning test deterministic
description:
## Report

`diagnostics::tests::pruning_keeps_the_newest_and_live_logs_only`
(runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/diagnostics.rs, assertion ~392 at the time) fails intermittently
on code that doesn't touch it. It was seen 2026-10-23 in eon-63 (`notes/rebase-checks.log`), mno4
(`review-logs/claude-r1-test.log`) and eon-9e (`codex2.log`, a different assertion), and on
2026-10-24 in the eon-euzm Opus gate's first run (it passed on rerun). It wastes a rerun for every
agent that hits it.

Filed on Lucca's approval, 2026-10-24 ("yes", answering the overseer's item 31).

## Suspected cause (from the euzm Opus gate; not confirmed)

The test decides "live" by whether a log's flock is held. When another test in the same process
spawns a child, the child holds copies of the parent's file descriptors between fork and exec
(O_CLOEXEC closes them only at exec). An flock belongs to the open file description, so for that
moment the log looks locked, and prune skips it as live.

The same window exists in production when the supervisor spawns Venus or Orbit. There it only
makes one prune pass keep a finished log, which is harmless, but confirm that.

## Change

Confirm the cause with a reproduction (for example, many spawns in parallel with the test). Then
make the test deterministic: have prune's liveness check tolerate a transient lock, or isolate the
test from concurrent spawns, whichever fixes the cause rather than hiding it. Production behavior
changes only if the cause shows a real production defect.

## Acceptance

- The test passes 50 consecutive runs under `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime
  pruning_keeps_the_newest_and_live_logs_only` while the rest of the suite runs in parallel.
- The reproduction and the cause are recorded in the bead.

## Scope

Runtime diagnostics tests only, unless the cause shows a production defect; in that case, report
it before changing production code.
close_reason: The pruning test unlocks its created log before dropping it, so a parallel test's fork cannot keep it locked; 50 consecutive eon-runtime suites passed

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Seen again 2026-10-25 ~02:30 -03 (overseer): the eon-pane-padding-extend-d9t8 implementer's parallel runtime suite failed this test at diagnostics.rs:392 on code that does not touch it; it passed in isolation and serially (~/.cache/eon-agents/d9t8/runtime-suite-fixed.log).

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Cause confirmed (sj0c, 2026-10-27, base 1869c19, x86_64 Linux, eon-test bubblewrap sandbox).

Failing assertion: in the recorded failures (d9t8, shn4.3) it is `!left().iter().any(|name| name.ends_with(&own))` after `prune(&logs, 0)`: the log that `create()` made, and the test dropped, survives as if live. The `others == expected` assertion cannot fail this way: the only fixtures ever locked are `live` (expected to stay) and the created log (kept as newest by `prune(&logs, 2)` either way).

Mechanism: `create()` takes an flock on its O_CLOEXEC descriptor. A child forked by a parallel test while that descriptor is open shares its open file description until it execs. The flock belongs to the description, so dropping the test's descriptor leaves the log locked for that window, and prune skips it.

Reproduction (temporary test, not committed; patch kept at ~/.cache/eon-agents/sj0c-work/repro.patch): four threads loop `Command::new("true").status()` while 4000 rounds alternate create → (unlock) → drop → `prune(dir, 0)`, counting logs that survive. `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime --lib sj0c_repro -- --nocapture`: drop only, 42/2000 survived; unlock through the descriptor before the drop, 0/2000.

Fix (test only): the test unlocks the created log through its own descriptor before dropping it. An unlock releases the lock on the open file description, so copies held by forked children no longer keep it. Assertions unchanged. Not a consequential code shape (no dependency, protocol, contract, lifecycle or trust-boundary change), so no reference gate.

Production disposition (overseer's question): no defect; no separate bead. Std opens every log with O_CLOEXEC and nothing dup2s a log onto a standard descriptor, so the only lock that outlives exec is the Orbit log, which sessions.rs hands to Orbit as stderr on purpose (and drops its own copy after spawn). A supervisor child forked during prune can hold at most: the supervisor's own log (live anyway), an Orbit log being opened for its Orbit (live anyway), or prune's own probe descriptor on a log prune is deleting. Each lasts only until that child execs, so at worst one prune pass, possibly in another supervisor, keeps a finished log that the next pass removes.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Corrections to the cause comment above (sj0c review, 2026-10-27):
- "The only fixtures ever locked" should read "the only logs locked before pruning": prune's own probe also locks fixtures 2 and 3, but only as it deletes them, so a leftover probe lock sits on a deleted file.
- Production worst case: a finished log is kept until every inherited copy of its descriptor closes, at each child's exec. That can span more than one prune pass, not just one. It is still bounded by exec, so the conclusion stands: no product defect.
- The shn4.3 log has since been overwritten by a passing rerun. Its `diagnostics.rs:392` is the same `!left()...ends_with(&own)` assertion as at e572c519, which is that tree's line 392. The earlier eon-63, mno4 and eon-9e failures (lines 306-313) were the PID-collision flake that eon-diagnostics-test-pid-flake-ydam fixed, not this race.

Proof (the commit that carries this comment; x86_64 Linux; eon-test bubblewrap sandbox; CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4):
- Red/green reproduction on base 1869c19 (comment above): drop only, 42/2000 logs survived `prune(dir, 0)`; with unlock first, 0/2000.
- Acceptance: 50 consecutive full `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime` runs on the candidate. Each runs the test in the same process as the rest of the suite, and each passed (117 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored; `pruning_keeps_the_newest_and_live_logs_only ... ok` in every run).
- The fresh reviewer's checks on the same tree passed: `cargo fmt -p eon-runtime --check`, `cargo clippy --locked -p eon-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and one more `eon-test -p eon-runtime` (117 passed). The tree was unchanged afterwards.

comments.text:
Corrections to the comment above (sj0c review, 2026-10-27):
- Earlier failures: eon-63 (`notes/rebase-checks.log`, diagnostics.rs:311) and mno4 (`review-logs/claude-r1-test.log`, :313) both failed on `!left()...ends_with(&own)`, so they are this race at older line numbers, as the original report said. A PID-7 collision fails earlier, at `created.len()` (5 vs 1). Only eon-9e's `codex2.log` failures are that collision, and those are ydam's deliberate red controls. ydam's report attributed eon-63's :311 failure to PID 7, which was wrong.
- Acceptance: all 50 runs reported 117 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored. The script found the test's own `... ok` line in 49 of them. For run 19 it counted 0, probably because other output interleaved with that line. That run's full log was not kept, so I cannot confirm it.
- The production bound "until each child's exec" assumes the forked child execs promptly, which holds for the std `Command` spawns in the runtime.

comments.text:
Final correction (sj0c, 2026-10-27). This replaces the acceptance bullet of the comment two above and the acceptance bullet of the comment just above:

The script found the test's own `... ok` line in 47 of the 50 runs; it counted 0 in runs 19, 33 and 37. The script keeps only the last run's full log, so I can't say why. It still passed in all 50: each run was the full, unfiltered eon-runtime suite (0 filtered out), and each reported 117 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored. The ignored test is not this one, and the script would have stopped at the first failure. The ok-line count was only a cross-check.

The comment just above also replaces the earlier-failures bullet of the comment two above: eon-63 and mno4 hit this race; only eon-9e's red controls were the PID collision.

title: Publish optional Eon Linux binaries to the donated Cachix cache
description:
Contract: one bounded Eon-owned Linux publisher builds the canonical packages.x86_64-linux.default and eonterm with their required checks, then publishes both runtime closures to the optional public eon-yazelix Cachix cache. Consumers opt into the donor's signing key; source builds remain available. Eon owns composition at exact accepted child pins; this is no child-HEAD CI or new release/platform contract.

User approval 2026-10-08: improve PR #2, verify locally, land with linear history, run manual hosted publishing and prove fresh-store substitution; enable automatic edge publishing only after that proof. Start workflow_dispatch-only. Existing lifecycle investigation metadata and live terminals must be preserved.

Prerequisites/reference gate: canonical graph and accepted Runtime/Orbit/Venus revisions; public cache/key and maintainer-installed CACHIX_AUTH_TOKEN. Inspected pinned cachix-action v17 and install-nix-action v31, official Cachix runtime-closure and GitHub workflow_dispatch docs, root distribution/development rules and exact source preparation. Adopt existing explicit uploader and one product-owned graph; reject duplicate child publishers, new flakes/uploader, skipped checks, blanket timeouts and reliability acceptance by cache success.

Acceptance: both exact product builds pass with required checks; bounded workflow passes hosted build and upload; both exact published outputs and complete runtime closures substitute into an initially empty isolated Nix store using the declared signing key, with no local builds. Retain revision, outputs, environment and logs. Only then enable edge pushes and align docs/LOC. Refresh installed Eon if the accepted package change requires the repository synchronization rule; preserve other profile elements and live processes. Any product lifecycle failure remains with its existing owner and issue.

CI bounds: one public-upstream ubuntu-24.04 job, 90 minute timeout, same-ref cancellation, contents read only, no PR/fork secret access, no Actions artifacts/cache or paid runner. Initially explicit dispatch only; at most one run per edge push after proof. Cachix storage/retention belongs to bioinformatist. Revisit or remove if builds repeatedly time out, donation ends, or public-runner eligibility changes. Local commands stay canonical; publication proof requires the hosted secret/upload path.

Scope: this cache rollout and its delivery proof only; no child source/manifest pins, runtime mechanism, new platform/release tag, channel promotion or beta acceptance.
