title: Compose agent work and durable Orbit sessions into an Eon workspace
description:
Current disposition (2026-09-08): deferred, unclaimed product horizon. The accepted workspace, directory picker, close/reorder shortcuts, managed shells, presentation and typography already ship. Remaining AgentRun/provider-attention, contextual action discovery, detach-only view removal, focused-terminal chrome and declarative-profile work require a separately selected child. The outcome below is future scope, not a claim that those features exist. No pending implementation is created by this reconciliation.

Contract routing:
- Consumes user-approved EON-C8 and EON-C10. The current contract index marks EON-C8 Partially proved and EON-C10 Proven; completed children established the topology owner, EONW producer and Venus consumption, Session-exit pruning, managed-environment corrections, and generation lifecycle. The circular-traversal and picker-open tab-traversal slices are accepted. Non-wrapping reorder mechanics and direct tab-close/reorder shortcuts are accepted in closed `eon-pxn.8.1` and `eon-pxn.8`. Current creation/close chords are Alt+Shift+T and Alt+Shift+W; EON-C8 and README own the complete current action contract. AgentRun and provider-attention work remain separately gated.
- Preserves EON-C1 through EON-C4 and consumes exact accepted Orbit and Venus contracts.
- Requires separate owner contracts for any new Orbit session discovery or observation and Venus multi-surface or agent-attention behavior. This epic record changes no runtime behavior; later slices require their own approved contract routing.

## Success Criteria

The accepted workspace and action ownership remains singular across Eon, Orbit, and Venus. This epic closes only after every required activated child is accepted or explicitly detached; deferred horizons do not silently become prerequisites. The detailed Acceptance Criteria remain governing.

Why:
Eon should be agent-first rather than merely agent-compatible. Its defining product opportunity is to organize durable human and agent work without moving terminal state or UI layout into Orbit. The accepted alpha now has Eon-owned tab and pane topology, independent Orbit Sessions, canonical EONW v7 owned by Eon Runtime, Venus consumption, Session-exit pruning, and a proved managed environment. It still has no explicit repository or worktree, AgentRun, provider-semantic, source-aware attention, service, artifact, or background-task model.

Irreducible model:
- Eon Workspace groups repositories or worktrees, AgentRuns, services, artifacts, execution-target references, and mappings to independent Orbit sessions.
- AgentRun is an explicit Eon product identity. It is not a pane, PTY, process, Orbit session, provider thread, or Venus view, although it may link to those values.
- Orbit owns authoritative process and terminal-session lifetime and terminal content.
- Provider integrations, when separately approved, own provider-native semantic evidence.
- Eon owns normalized AgentRun identity, relationships, lifecycle policy, source-aware status, attention policy, and the ordered horizontal-tab and per-tab vertical-pane topology.
- Venus owns native horizontal-tab and visual accordion-pane materialization, attention presentation, focus, geometry, hit testing, and ephemeral view state.

Scope:
In scope are Eon-owned workspace and AgentRun identities; repository/worktree and session mappings; launch, resume, stop and cleanup policy; one real coding-agent workflow; a bounded native two-axis workspace with horizontal tabs and per-tab visual vertical accordion stacks; explicit tab and pane creation; direct directional traversal; source-aware attention in persistent headers; the smallest deterministic machine-readable Eon actions; one bounded declarative workspace or profile schema over those same identities and actions; and a separately proved Eon-managed interactive environment whose tool selection, private configuration, command projection, and component identities remain Eon product policy.

Out of scope are terminal-text or process-name heuristics as authoritative agent state, provider compatibility promises, arbitrary raw terminal control, Orbit-owned agent policy or layouts, a virtual or fuzzy picker for ordinary vertical pane traversal, arbitrary split trees, nested or floating terminal panes, generic popup infrastructure, a generalized widget or plugin framework, remote machines, web or mobile, machine-restart recovery, durable layout restoration, and Nova or Zellij compatibility. The managed tools remain independently owned components rather than Eon forks or compatibility surfaces.

Canonical CLI and action boundary:
- Eon owns one semantic action registry for workspace and AgentRun product state.
- The `eon` CLI is the canonical external projection for both humans and agents. Human-readable output and deterministic `--json` output consume the same actions and identities rather than forming separate APIs.
- The running Eon supervisor remains the only live workspace and action-state owner. A second CLI invocation reaches it through one private Eon-owned local control endpoint and never addresses Orbit, ORBS, ORBF, or Venus directly or reconstructs live state from files.
- Configuration, external programs, and a later MCP adapter may consume the same accepted actions. None of them becomes an authorization owner, plugin ABI, or second state owner.
design:
Implementation sequence:
1. The initial workspace slice began after eon-ax4 proved the one-session composition with real agent dogfood, Orbit and Venus graduated, and orb-bi4.7 accepted the frontier; that slice is complete.
2. EON-C8 and EON-C10 were approved and indexed before their runtime work. Completed children proved the minimal Eon topology and actions, managed-environment baseline and corrections, EONW producer and Venus consumption, Session-exit pruning, and generation lifecycle. Circular traversal, picker-open tab traversal, and non-wrapping reorder mechanics are accepted. `eon-pxn.8` is closed; tab-close/reorder actions and direct Venus shortcuts are complete. The later tab labels, picker behavior, presentation and typography slices are also accepted at the exact phases recorded in docs/CONTRACTS.md. No implementation child is active. Create any AgentRun, provider-attention, durable-workspace, appearance, declarative-profile, or required child-repository issue only immediately before its turn and after its exact contract routing is approved.
3. Complete the Eon reference gate. Required before code: exact accepted Orbit and Venus revisions; exact current Herdr runtime, agent-state and socket/action surfaces; Amp Orbs workspace model; VS Code Agent Host client-independent execution; Canario workspace interaction; and exact Nova and Zellij workflow comparisons, including Zellij visual stacking and its alternative virtual picker behavior. Accept mechanisms only for the question they answer; neither Zellij surface is a compatibility target.
4. Keep an AgentRun independent from its representations. A workspace may contain ordinary non-agent sessions. An AgentRun may link to a provider thread, one or more Orbit sessions, services and artifacts. A Venus tab or pane only materializes a session and never becomes the session or AgentRun identity.
5. Separate three kinds of state:
   - execution state from the authoritative process or Orbit lifecycle;
   - semantic agent state from an explicit provider integration, or unknown;
   - attention state computed by Eon from explicit fresh evidence.
   Every semantic value carries its source and freshness. Never silently promote scraped output, process names, elapsed time, or titles into provider truth.
6. Prefer one Orbit process and socket per session until measurements justify a separately approved multi-session Orbit process.
7. Prove the registry together with one fixed two-axis materialization. Eon orders horizontal tabs and the vertical pane stack inside each tab. Venus shows that stack as a visual accordion: one focused pane expands, collapsed pane headers remain visible within a bounded scrollable header region, and only the focused terminal presentation is actively materialized. Directional workspace commands traverse tabs left or right and pane headers up or down; the stack itself scrolls to keep focus visible. Ordinary traversal requires no picker, palette, modal list, or fuzzy search. Every independent Orbit session continues while unfocused, collapsed, on another tab, or while Venus is absent.
8. Prove one Eon-owned semantic action registry and its canonical `eon` CLI projection. The running Eon supervisor is the only live workspace and action-state owner. A second CLI invocation uses one private Eon-owned local control endpoint; it never addresses Orbit, ORBS, ORBF, or Venus directly or reconstructs live state from files. The first actions cover status and list, create tab, create pane, focus by stable identity or direction, attach, start, wait, explicit stop, and removal of a view separately from stopping its session. Contextual action discovery reports stable action identities, typed arguments, current targets, structured results, cancellation, bounded errors, and owner-authored reasons an action is unavailable. Human-readable output and deterministic `--json` output are projections of the same registry. Structured mode emits data on stdout, diagnostics on stderr, stable symbolic error codes, and no prompts when stdout is not a terminal. Preserve the accepted meaning of the existing `eon run` command rather than overloading it with AgentRun semantics. Bounded terminal observation remains absent until orb-p92 is accepted. A general event stream remains deferred until one workflow needs more than bounded `wait`. Configuration, external programs, and a later MCP adapter may consume accepted actions but do not become a plugin ABI or authorization owner.
9. Define explicit capabilities and user consent. Read-only observation and mutating actions remain separate. Raw keystroke injection, provider-specific approval, arbitrary shell execution, remote access, and secret access require separate decisions.
10. Venus consumes Eon-authored tab, pane, AgentRun and attention state through a separately approved contract. Its first native workspace surface is the horizontal tab strip and visual vertical accordion stack. Persistent tab and pane headers identify ordinary sessions and linked AgentRuns, expose only bounded source-aware attention, and provide deterministic pointer and accessible focus. This is not a sidebar, picker, popup, arbitrary layout framework, or third-party widget API. A focused-terminal mode may hide and restore workspace chrome without stopping, detaching, or changing an AgentRun or Orbit session.
11. Define tab and pane creation, focus, collapse, expansion, removal, attach, detach, workspace-chrome hide and restore, agent or process exit, Venus crash, Orbit crash, stale endpoint, explicit shutdown, cancellation, and abandoned-resource cleanup with strict bounds. Removing a view and stopping its Orbit session or AgentRun remain distinct explicit transitions.
12. Keep collapsed headers to bounded owner-authored metadata and do not continuously render inactive sessions. Add previews only after dogfood proves that headers are insufficient.

Chosen workspace shape:
- Tabs are the visible horizontal axis; each tab contains one ordered visual vertical accordion pane stack.
- Each pane maps to one independent Orbit session. Exactly one pane in the active tab is expanded; collapsed headers remain visible within bounded scrolling and do not render terminal previews.
- Directional workspace commands move left or right between tabs and up or down through the visible stack. Pointer and accessibility actions target the same ordered identities. No picker is required for vertical pane traversal.
- Tab and pane headers may display only bounded owner-authored identity, lifecycle and source-aware attention metadata. They never scrape terminal text or guess provider state.
- A hidden or unfocused pane preserves its Eon-managed lifecycle while Venus owns geometry, z-order and ephemeral focus.
- A declarative Eon workspace or profile may request this topology and its launch inputs; Eon remains topology owner, Orbit remains session owner, and Venus only materializes accepted views.
- Working-directory and environment discovery remain with the launched shell or tool, including Direnv when selected. Eon passes explicit launch inputs and does not snapshot, reinterpret, or become a second owner of the resolved environment.

Configuration boundary:
- Eon owns one versioned declarative workspace or profile schema over the same stable identities and semantic actions exposed by the CLI. Ratconfig may edit that Eon-owned schema but does not own its meaning or apply policy.
- The first schema may describe the accepted tab and pane topology, launch inputs, keybindings, and named action sequences. Applying it routes through the same action owner and cannot address Orbit or Venus protocols directly.
- Validation and apply failures are deterministic and leave prior accepted state intact. The schema has no loops, mutable variables, asynchronous callbacks, arbitrary code, custom widget trees, raw terminal control, ambient environment capture, or second workspace state owner.
- The configuration proof is a separately activated Eon child when this epic starts; planning it here creates no schema or compatibility promise.

Deferred pressure test:
- Simultaneously expanded panes, arbitrary horizontal or vertical splits, nested layout trees, floating terminal popups, drag-and-drop reordering, virtual pane pickers and durable layout restoration remain outside the first workspace slice.
- Fixed status items consume bounded owner-authored metadata and never scrape terminal text.
- Graphics remain an independent Orbit-to-Venus resource plane.
- A local execution target can later become remote or isolated without treating a host path, pane or Nix store path as global AgentRun identity.

Stop if the slice duplicates terminal, provider, protocol, layout or agent-state ownership; if child contracts are speculative; if authorization has no owner; if background cleanup cannot be bounded; if ordinary vertical traversal requires a picker, popup or generic layout framework; or if a published compatibility surface is required before this single workflow proves value.

Accepted managed interactive environment:
- EON-C9 and README own the shipped shell/tool inventory, current defaults and exact proof. Nushell, Bash, Zsh and Fish load native user configuration before guarded Eon integration; Starship, Zoxide, Atuin and Carapace are shipped and independently configurable. Helix, Yazi and LazyGit remain child-owned.
- One private Session PATH supplies the accepted unprefixed commands; stable eon-* commands are available outside Sessions. Preserve native prompt/completion configuration, normal Starship discovery, and explicit eon run -- COMMAND... inputs. Do not restore the earlier custom Starship marker or deferred-Carapace plan.
- Direnv/Mise activation and an unprefixed-command toggle remain separately selected horizons; no ornamental wrappers or generic alias system.
- The canonical component manifest and eon versions remain the identity owner. Later distribution and Home Manager consumers use the same graph and accepted behavior.
- Exact Nova revision 37f36efcabf16c41d03e182917926e7b8e56139c remains historical comparison evidence for native configuration, managed commands and tool composition, not compatibility authority.
- Any later dependency change names its exact version, license, closure cost, Linux/native-Wayland behavior, upgrade burden and replacement cost. It creates no macOS work or speculative platform seam.

Accepted presentation and remaining appearance scope:
- EON-C13, EON-C14 and EON-C19 and README own current settings: opacity 0.80, blur requested by default, omitted typography delegated to Venus with nominal 16 px text and 1.125 line height. Font family/fallbacks, size, line height and initial geometry are configurable; compositor sizing remains authoritative.
- Venus owns its shipped blue cursor tail. Eon passes no cursor-effect profile; optional Yazelix Cursors consumption remains deferred in eon-compose-yazelix-cursors-bcc. Do not restore the superseded JetBrains Mono 15, 0.92 opacity or no-cursor-effects defaults.
- Preserve explicit cell backgrounds, selection, cursor, graphics and other semantic surfaces when changing default-background opacity; opacity 1.0 remains supported.
- Earlier violet-accent/visual-bell/audio-bell requests are retained as unactivated appearance goals where not covered by current contracts. They require a selected owner contract and are not accepted runtime claims.
- Native proof remains scoped to its exact Linux environment. Fractional-scale, broader compositor, accessibility and non-systemd qualifications cannot be widened by this epic.
acceptance_criteria:
1. eon-ax4, Orbit and Venus graduation, and orb-bi4.7 acceptance precede implementation; EON-C8 is explicitly approved and indexed first.
2. Eon alone owns ordered horizontal-tab and per-tab vertical-pane topology, AgentRun identity and relationships, session registry, launch/resume/stop policy, attention policy, and workspace-to-Orbit mapping. Orbit retains each independent process, PTY, terminal and history authority; Venus retains native accordion materialization, geometry, focus, accessibility and interaction.
3. AgentRun is never equated with a pane, process, PTY, Orbit session, provider thread or Venus view. Stable explicit links connect those independently owned identities.
4. The smallest proof creates a workspace over an explicit repository or disposable worktree with at least two horizontal tabs and three independent Orbit sessions; at least one tab contains two visually stacked panes and at least one pane links to a real coding-agent run. Direct left or right tab traversal and up or down pane traversal select the intended stable identity, only the focused pane expands, and useful background work survives focus changes, tab changes and Venus exit.
5. Process execution, provider semantic state and Eon attention state remain distinct. Provider semantic state is unknown when no explicit integration supplies it; heuristics cannot silently label an agent working, blocked, completed or failed.
6. A bounded native horizontal tab strip and visual vertical accordion stack persistently identify ordinary sessions and linked AgentRuns. Collapsed headers expose only bounded source-aware accepted state, retain stable visible ordering, and support pointer, directional keyboard and accessible focus without a picker. Focused-terminal mode may hide and restore the chrome without stopping, detaching or changing any AgentRun or Orbit session; restored headers report current state and keep stale or unknown evidence explicit.
7. One Eon-owned semantic action registry and the canonical `eon` CLI prove bounded status and list, tab and pane creation, stable-ID or directional focus, attach, start, wait, explicit stop, and view removal distinct from session termination. The running supervisor is the only live action-state owner; CLI invocations use a private Eon-owned local control endpoint and never control Orbit or Venus directly or reconstruct live state from files. The current workspace or selection exposes valid action identities, typed arguments, current targets, structured results, cancellation, stable symbolic errors, and bounded unavailable-action reasons from owner-authored capability state. Human output and deterministic `--json` output consume the same registry; structured non-interactive use keeps data on stdout, diagnostics on stderr, and never prompts. Existing `eon run` semantics remain unambiguous. The slice adds no general event stream, MCP server, plugin system, raw terminal-control API, or provider compatibility promise. Terminal observation is absent until orb-p92 is accepted.
8. Read-only observation and mutating action capabilities are separately authorized, bounded and revocable. Neither bypasses Orbit ownership or the one-interactive-client contract.
9. Tab and pane creation, directional focus, collapse, expansion, view removal, attach, detach, chrome hide and restore, agent and child exit, component crash, stale endpoint, cancellation, explicit shutdown and abandoned-resource cleanup have deterministic user-visible behavior. A future detach-only view-removal action does not stop its Session or AgentRun and remains distinct from the accepted explicit tab-close/Stop action; it must not reinterpret current close semantics.
10. One-session-per-Orbit remains the default unless measurements and a separate owner decision justify consolidation.
11. The native proof covers stable tab and pane order, direct left or right and up or down traversal, pointer and accessibility order, one expanded pane, collapsed source-aware headers, focus restoration, and bounded header overflow that scrolls within the visual stack rather than opening a picker. A recorded pressure review keeps simultaneous expanded panes, arbitrary splits or nesting, floating terminal popups, drag-and-drop reordering, durable layout restoration, graphics, and later isolated or remote targets outside the first slice.
12. Background metadata and previews are bounded and do not scrape terminal text, retain secrets as product state, or continuously render every inactive session.
13. Exact component revisions, compatibility order, Nix composition checks, focused integration checks and fresh Linux dogfood pass without modifying Nova.
14. Closure records ownership, contract and authorization decisions, the chosen horizontal-tab and visual vertical accordion shape, the rejected picker traversal, reference identities, dependency footprint, portability, LOC, performance and resource observations, agent workflow evidence, pressure-test results, and deferred provider, observer, durability, graphics, extension, remote, popup and arbitrary-layout scope.
15. A separately activated Eon child proves one bounded declarative workspace or profile schema over the same stable identities and semantic actions as the CLI. Eon owns schema meaning, validation, and apply policy; Ratconfig edits the Eon-owned model. The profile may describe only accepted topology, launch inputs, keybindings, and named action sequences. Applying it routes through the action owner, reports deterministic failures without corrupting prior accepted state, and adds no loops, mutable callbacks, arbitrary code, custom widget trees, raw child-protocol access, ambient environment snapshot, or second workspace state owner.
16. Child sequencing delivers the first visible vertical slice before the broader epic surface: an Eon owner child defines stable tab and pane identities, ordered topology, independent Orbit-session mappings, and only the semantic actions required by that slice; a separate Eon child proves the managed interactive environment; a Venus consumer child materializes opaque horizontal tabs and the one-expanded vertical accordion; then cross-repository acceptance proves the real composition. Complete provider semantics and attention, declarative profiles, terminal observation, MCP, plugins, isolation, generalized APIs, and appearance effects do not block this workspace proof unless an owner-contract gap is discovered.
17. Preserve the accepted EON-C9 managed environment and current README command inventory: four native-config-aware managed shells, guarded Starship/Zoxide/Atuin/Carapace integrations, managed Helix/Yazi/LazyGit, exact manifest identities, eon versions, stable external eon-* commands, private Session PATH and explicit eon run -- COMMAND... inputs without globally shadowing user commands. These shipped outcomes are not new prerequisites to implement again.
18. A later dependency gate records exact versions, licenses, closure cost, Linux/native-Wayland behavior, upgrade burden and replacement cost. Carapace is shipped. Automatic Direnv/Mise activation and an unprefixed-command toggle remain deferred until selected; ornamental wrappers and speculative macOS work are excluded.
19. Preserve EON-C13/EON-C14/EON-C19 current presentation, Venus-owned cursor behavior and exact proof qualifications. The earlier JetBrains Mono 15, 0.92 opacity and no-cursor-effects defaults are superseded; visual-bell/audio-bell/accent requests outside current contracts remain unactivated owner-scoped goals. A later appearance slice must preserve explicit semantic surfaces, the opaque override, accessibility and the Linux/native-Wayland boundary.
20. Later packaging channels consume the same canonical component manifest, managed commands, private configuration, and defaults; they do not become second owners. A future unprefixed-command toggle, if collision evidence requires it, is one declarative-profile policy over the same managed executables rather than a second alias system.
notes:
Priority P1: the user selected this product horizon because agents are strategically central to Eon. orb-bi4.7 records the completed ownership and sequencing decision. EON-C8 is Partially proved and EON-C10 is Proven, as the current contract index records; accepted slices do not widen the aggregate proof. Completed children established the workspace topology, EONW and Venus composition, Session-exit pruning, managed-environment corrections, and generation lifecycle. No implementation child is active; AgentRun and provider-attention work remain unactivated. This epic is a deferred planning container and must not be claimed.

Local dependency: eon-ax4. External dependencies: Orbit orb-bi4.7 and every exact child contract activated by the chosen slice. The minimal agent dogfood in eon-ax4 does not itself prove EON-C8.

Canario remains comparison-only evidence for compact workspace interaction. Herdr, Amp Orbs and VS Code Agent Host are required agent-workspace comparisons at exact current identities when this Bead activates. Eon accepts durable-work and action-surface lessons only after source review and rejects inherited terminal ownership, plugin, hosted, remote, marketplace and provider-support scope.

Feature routing:
- Orbit orb-p92 owns bounded read-only terminal observation; Eon owns capability issuance, agent/session selection and product actions.
- Native horizontal tabs, visual accordion panes, bounded header attention and focused-terminal chrome are Venus materializations of Eon-managed topology. Generic windows, floating terminals and overlays remain deferred.
- Current ORB-C5 and VEN-C2 continue to own interactive terminal input.
- Orbit orb-j2i owns graphics resources; Eon owns no graphics identity, bytes, cache or placement.
- General third-party contributions remain under eon-ix6 only after concrete extension cases.
- Isolated execution remains eon-az9 after local agent work proves a real threat-model need.

Rejected alternatives include agent equals pane, terminal-text status scraping, process-name detection as truth, raw-keystroke control as the only agent API, tabs or splits inside Orbit, a multi-session Orbit daemon by default, a virtual or fuzzy picker for ordinary vertical pane traversal, arbitrary split trees, floating terminal popups, continuous thumbnails, a generic action or provider framework before one proof, and treating MCP or plugins as prerequisites.

User activation on 2026-08-08 created only eon-pxn.1 for the minimal topology/action owner. Create later implementation children only when their turn arrives and the user approves their exact owner or consumer contracts.

Discussion #685 (https://github.com/luccahuguet/yazelix/discussions/685) is source evidence for dismissible agent surfaces, contextual action discovery, declarative profile/topology pressure, environment integration, and the separately routed isolated-target decision. User decision on 2026-08-07: the first native workspace uses horizontal tabs and visually stacked vertical accordion panes with direct directional traversal; it does not use a virtual picker for ordinary vertical pane navigation. This selects no general panel framework, arbitrary layout format, environment tool, terminal traversal compatibility target, or isolation provider.

User-approved CLI disposition on 2026-08-08:
- The `eon` CLI is the primary human and agent control surface over the same Eon-owned semantic actions.
- Human-readable and deterministic structured output are projections of one registry, not separate APIs.
- The running supervisor owns live workspace and action state behind one private Eon control endpoint; the CLI never bypasses Eon ownership by speaking child protocols directly.
- Configuration and external automation follow the CLI/action proof. A plugin host, language runtime, general event stream, MCP server, and stable 1.0 compatibility promise remain deferred.

First-slice sequencing clarification (2026-08-08): when eon-pxn activates, prioritize the smallest visible workspace proof: minimal Eon-owned tab and pane topology plus the actions that proof needs; the separately scoped managed interactive environment; Venus opaque horizontal tabs and stacked accordion panes; then cross-repository acceptance and dogfood. Do not make the complete AgentRun/provider-attention model, declarative profiles, terminal observation, MCP, plugins, isolation, or a generalized action surface prerequisites beyond that accepted environment and workspace slice. If a required child contract is absent, pause at that boundary and return to its owning repository; Venus never invents or reconstructs Eon topology.

Historical defaults disposition (reconciled 2026-09-08): the 2026-08-08 sequence delivered the workspace and managed environment. EON-C9 and EON-C13/EON-C14/EON-C19 supersede its custom prompt, JetBrains Mono 15, 0.92 opacity and no-cursor-effects choices. Current inventory and configuration remain with README and the contract index. The design and acceptance fields retain unactivated bell/accent, declarative-profile and agent goals without claiming them as shipped.

Current cmux architecture comparison — 2026-08-10:
- Exact source inspected: manaflow-ai/cmux a35880b1031e673e5e006f0ccb78c3ffa12c4bcb. The older be29dfa7c586 reference remains valid for its recorded question but predates the current reconnectable event stream and Feed architecture.
- Preserved Eon decision: keep Orbit as the sole process, PTY, terminal-state, attachment, and Session-lifetime owner; keep Venus transient; keep Eon as the semantic workspace, AgentRun, attention, and action owner. cmux ordinary local PTYs do not survive app restart, so its app-owned runtime is comparison evidence rather than an ownership model for Eon.
- Adopt for a separately activated provider-attention slice: bootstrap from one complete authoritative Eon snapshot; carry sequenced, bounded events with explicit source and freshness; make replay gaps require snapshot refresh; define heartbeat, reconnect, backpressure, and slow-consumer failure; and treat events as invalidations or evidence, never as a second state owner.
- Adopt at the provider edge: prefer native hooks, provider session identifiers, and explicit reply channels; retain provider-specific limitations; bound any blocking decision bridge and fall back to the provider native interaction path rather than freezing work. Unsupported semantics remain unknown.
- Keep live Session continuity distinct from restart recovery. A later durable-workspace decision may persist Eon-owned topology and provider resume references, but must not claim arbitrary process checkpointing or replace Orbit attachment.
- Rejected inherited scope: GUI-owned PTYs, generic keystroke injection as an agent contract, screen or process inference as authority, browser automation, provider compatibility promises, remote or mobile control, cloud execution, and cmux CLI or socket compatibility.
- Planning consequence at that 2026-08-10 baseline: EONW v5 polling served the workspace slice. Current codec/version ownership is indexed in EON-C8 and Eon Runtime; the event-stream gate below remains unchanged. Do not create a general event-stream child until the user activates one provider-backed attention workflow and its latency or blocking contract demonstrates that bounded wait or polling is insufficient.

Unpeel provider/action comparison — 2026-08-15:
- Exact primary source: Unpeel 0.2.0 revision 9580a83f009fe19775116cacb46e74570958ca56, especially docs/agents/session-activity.md, docs/agents/sessions-mcp.md, crates/unpeel-core/src/mcp_host.rs, and docs/plans/shared-core.md.
- Useful evidence for a separately activated provider-attention slice: persist evidence source and freshness; let explicit provider hooks own known-provider activity after their first event; keep provider-specific semantics in adapters; and expect provider event meanings to drift. Unpeel's Codex stop workaround demonstrates why a generic provider state cannot be inferred safely.
- Useful action evidence: one compact domain/action surface with lazy help limits agent context and can project an existing semantic action owner. This supports Eon's current canonical registry and CLI direction; it does not justify an MCP server or second action schema.
- Rejected inheritance: output-growth and rendered-menu scans as authoritative working, blocked, done, or failed state; same-user cooperative restrictions described as security isolation; duplicated Rust/Swift policy; broad provider compatibility; and browser, relay, mobile, or artifact-gallery scope.
- Planning disposition: keep unsupported semantics unknown and source-labeled. Create no AgentRun, provider-attention, MCP, browser, or event-stream child until the user activates its exact owner/consumer contract. No status, priority, prerequisite, or epic acceptance change is required.

Planning-only batch authorized by the user on 2026-08-15; the epic remains unclaimed.

Readiness reconciliation (2026-08-21): the Venus lifecycle remediation frontier is complete. This epic remains a deferred planning container, not a claimable implementation unit; reactivate only through one user-approved non-epic child after checking current contracts and exact accepted child revisions. The integration-audit chain and close/reorder slice are complete; remaining contract qualifications stay explicit.

TUIOS comparison - 2026-08-15

- Exact source: Gaurav-Gosain/tuios revision 0047c409185f37e568933a566e0253b2a6e96a96, including docs/protocol.md, docs/AGENT_STATE.md, docs/SESSIONS.md, integrations/claude-code, and the shared verb registry in internal/session.

Bounded wait-for operations consume the same event owner used by subscriptions. This corroborates the accepted Eon semantic action registry and one human/structured CLI projection; it does not justify EONW v2, a general event stream, or another schema.

Zeron comparison — 2026-08-16

- Exact comparison source: zeronsh/comet `v0.2.3` revision `9ab250ceb6317d080a8429435cb15a9eaef5663e` (MIT), cloned under `yazelix-related/comet`. title: Own the minimal Eon workspace topology and semantic actions
description:
Contract routing:
- Changes and may partially prove EON-C8 only. EON-C8 is user-approved and indexed as Planned before implementation.
- Preserves EON-C1 through EON-C4 and the existing meanings of eon run, eon attach, versions, and config-path.
- Consumes independent Orbit session identities and accepted lifecycle behavior without changing ORBS, ORBF, Orbit, or Venus. Any missing child contract stops this Bead and returns to the owning repository.

Consumer, trigger, result, failures:
The consumer is one local Eon user through the canonical eon action projection and, later, a separately approved Venus adapter. Creating or focusing a tab or pane, or traversing left, right, up, or down, changes one Eon-owned live topology of stable tab and pane identities. Tabs are horizontally ordered; every tab has an ordered vertical pane stack; each pane maps explicitly to one independent Orbit session identity; Eon retains one selected pane per non-empty tab and one active tab. Venus will later render the selected pane in the active tab as the only expanded accordion pane. Unknown or stale identities, missing sessions, invalid transitions, unavailable directions, supervisor loss, and malformed actions return bounded explicit failures and leave the last accepted topology unchanged.

Current gap:
The accepted alpha supervises one Orbit socket and one Venus client. It has no Eon-owned workspace topology, stable tab or pane identity, multi-session mapping, semantic workspace action owner, or live control endpoint. Venus must not invent those values.

Prerequisites:
- eon-ax4 is closed with the accepted Nix-only Linux alpha.
- orb-bi4.7 is closed and selects eon-pxn as the sole post-graduation frontier.
- EON-C8 is approved and indexed.
- At the execution baseline, record the exact accepted Eon HEAD, affected EON-C8 state, Orbit ORB-C1 and ORB-C3 proof revision, current pinned Orbit artifact, intended surfaces, dirty paths, and active session identity. Stop if the accepted Orbit artifact cannot supply independent endpoints without a new Orbit contract.

Ownership:
- Eon owns stable opaque workspace, tab, and pane identities; ordering; active and selected identities; explicit pane-to-Orbit-session mappings; semantic workspace actions; and the private local control boundary.
- The running Eon supervisor is the sole live topology and action-state owner. CLI invocations and the later Venus adapter consume that owner rather than rebuilding state from files.
- Orbit remains the sole owner of every process, PTY, terminal state, retained history, attachment, and session lifetime.
- Venus remains the future owner of native geometry, focus, rendering, accessibility, hit testing, and accordion materialization.

First slice:
Implement only the state and actions needed to inspect the topology, create tabs and panes, focus a stable identity, and traverse tabs left or right and pane selections up or down. Human-readable CLI output and deterministic --json output must project the same action results. A direction with no target is explicitly unavailable and does not wrap or mutate state. Keep one Orbit process and endpoint per pane unless measured evidence and a separately approved Orbit decision justify consolidation.

Scope boundary:
No Venus UI, managed Nushell or tool defaults, AgentRun or provider model, attention inference, terminal observation, arbitrary split tree, picker, simultaneous expanded panes, drag-and-drop, durable layout restoration, declarative profile, event stream, MCP, plugins, remote access, isolated execution, appearance effects, new public protocol, or compatibility promise. View removal and session stop remain separate later actions; this child must not conflate them.
design:
Reference classification before code:
- Required: this Bead and comments; AGENTS.md; docs/CONTRACTS.md EON-C8; current Eon launcher and tests; exact accepted Orbit ORB-C1 and ORB-C3 contracts and proof; exact current Herdr workspace, supervisor, and socket/action surfaces; Amp Orbs workspace identity model; VS Code Agent Host client-independent execution; Canario frontend and SessionStore at Rio 3e41b8b19a1c; exact current Zellij tab and stacked-pane action mechanisms; and exact Nova 37f36efcabf16c41d03e182917926e7b8e56139c only for workflow comparison.
- Comparison only: Helheim live-modifiable Emacs architecture and broader extension model. It does not change Eon ownership or justify an embedded language.
- Conditional on a named failure: current Venus source and protocol only if the opaque consumer handoff cannot be specified from accepted contracts; other Orbit source only if independent session endpoints are insufficient.
- Rejected scope: copying reference code, adopting a reference protocol or compatibility target, provider semantics, general plugins, arbitrary layouts, or moving PTY or rendering ownership into Eon.

Minimum code shape:
1. Reuse the existing Rust product binary and supervisor boundary. Prefer a small Eon-owned topology model and direct action dispatcher; add no framework or runtime dependency unless the crate gate proves a complete responsibility.
2. Give the topology model stable opaque identities, explicit order, active-tab selection, per-tab pane selection, and opaque Orbit endpoint mappings. Store no terminal frame, text, PTY state, provider state, or Venus geometry.
3. Route the canonical CLI and future adapters through the same action owner. The private local control transport is an implementation seam, not a public plugin ABI.
4. Prove deterministic state transitions first, then prove one live supervisor with two tabs, three substitute Orbit endpoints, and a second CLI invocation. Do not require Venus for this owner proof.
5. Keep process, path, and socket code behind the existing Unix boundary and record neutral or isolated-platform-dependency disposition. Stop for a macOS blocker instead of creating a speculative platform framework.

First meaningful check:
A deterministic transition test starts from an empty owner state, creates two tabs and three panes mapped to three distinct opaque session identities, focuses by identity and left/right/up/down direction, and proves stable order, one selected pane per non-empty tab, explicit boundary failures, and no mutation after rejected actions.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The execution baseline and Reference gate are recorded before production, test, manifest, or generated-fixture edits, including exact source identities, licenses, adopted mechanisms, rejected scope, ownership consequences, platform disposition, and the first check.
2. One Eon-owned model holds stable opaque tab and pane identities, horizontal tab order, vertical per-tab pane order, active tab, one selected pane per non-empty tab, and explicit mappings to distinct Orbit session identities. It stores no terminal, PTY, presentation, provider, or Venus state.
3. One semantic action owner supports bounded topology inspection, tab creation, pane creation, stable-identity focus, left/right tab traversal, and up/down pane traversal. The CLI human view and deterministic --json view consume the same results.
4. Left/right and up/down select the intended stable identity. A missing target, unknown or stale identity, duplicate request, invalid transition, malformed action, unavailable supervisor, or missing session yields a bounded explicit error and leaves the last accepted topology unchanged.
5. The running supervisor is the sole live topology and action-state owner. A second eon invocation reaches it through one private Eon control boundary; it does not read live topology from files or speak ORBS, ORBF, or Venus protocols directly.
6. The proof uses at least two tabs and three independent substitute or accepted Orbit session endpoints. Useful child work survives focus and tab changes and control-client loss. The child introduces no multi-session Orbit daemon assumption.
7. Existing eon run, eon attach, versions, config-path, EON-C1 through EON-C4 behavior, manifest identity, private runtime-directory validation, and accepted partial-failure semantics remain green.
8. Focus changes never stop, detach, replace, or reinterpret an Orbit session. View removal and session termination are not added or conflated.
9. Strong tests cover the deterministic transition boundary and one process-level action path. Run cargo fmt --check, cargo check --locked, cargo test --locked, cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings, the cheapest relevant Nix composition check, and git diff --check.
10. No new dependency, public protocol, schema, Venus surface, managed tool default, AgentRun/provider state, observation capability, arbitrary layout, picker, persistence promise, plugin/MCP surface, isolation target, remote behavior, or appearance effect is introduced.
11. Closure updates EON-C8 with the exact proof revision and honest status, records limitations and cross-repository handoff requirements, reconciles the parent Bead and dependency graph, updates current documentation and README LOC accounting, and does not claim full native workspace proof before the separate Venus and dogfood children pass.
notes: Implemented and mechanically proved the minimal Eon-owned live topology/action slice at 1a00a9f6de171e944c3c31a9f72ee2cc92d8fa15; documentation proof is 0d25711ef5fb12cbc1576cf9800c7931a67ba432. Five fresh-eyes passes removed 22 net Rust lines and corrected bounded control scheduling, timeout failure handling, socket ownership and cleanup, test cleanup and readiness ordering, active-tab missing-session validation, impossible-status handling, and initial-session documentation. Proof asserts mode 0600 only after a completed control round trip, ordinary cleanup at supervisor exit, and preservation of a replacement socket. EON-C8 is Partially proved pending the separately approved Venus consumer and composed native dogfood. No dependency, manifest, child protocol, defaults, provider, plugin, persistence, remote, or appearance scope was added.
close_reason: Minimal live topology/action owner corrected, simplified, and mechanically proved; EON-C8 remains partially proved pending its separate Venus consumer.

Adopted owner and minimum code shape
- The running eon supervisor is the only live topology/action owner. One small Eon module owns opaque sequential tab-N, pane-N, and session-N identities, horizontal tab order, vertical pane order, active/selected identities, endpoint mapping, deterministic projection, and action validation.

Third-pass failing proof — root cause

Command: cargo test --locked -p eon --test workspace_control
Result: failed at the new post-supervisor assertion because runtime/eon.sock still existed after a successful supervisor exit.

- create_control_listener records the full SocketIdentity before fs::set_permissions.
- SocketIdentity includes ctime and ctime_nsec so Orbit startup can distinguish a replaced endpoint.

- Keep the guard before chmod so permission or nonblocking setup failure still cleans its own socket.
- Production behavior changes only from stale control-path leakage to correct identity-checked removal. Permissions, public outputs, wire, process lifecycle, Orbit checks, and all other behavior remain unchanged.

title: Prove the Eon-managed interactive environment
description:
Contract routing:
- Follows the completed eon-pxn.1 topology and action owner. This child changes no runtime behavior until its managed-environment contract is approved and indexed.
- Preserves EON-C1 through EON-C4 and the partial EON-C8 topology proof. It may extend the canonical component graph and composed launch policy only through an explicitly approved Eon contract and exact child identities.

Consumer, trigger, result, failures:
A local Eon user starts the default interactive Session, invokes an Eon-managed command outside Eon, or launches a subprocess inside an Eon Session. Eon selects one exact managed interactive environment: Nushell, sparse Starship, Zoxide, Helix, Yazi, and LazyGit. Outside Eon, stable eon-prefixed commands expose managed executables without shadowing the user toolchain. Inside Eon, one Eon-private PATH projects the accepted unprefixed executable names to the same artifacts, and managed Nushell supplies lg. Missing artifacts, invalid private configuration, manifest mismatch, or launch failure returns an explicit bounded error and never mutates global user configuration or PATH.

Ownership:
- Eon owns component selection and exact versions, launch policy, the existing private configuration root, stable managed command names, the Eon-session PATH projection, and component identity reporting.
- Nushell, Starship, Zoxide, Helix, Yazi, and LazyGit retain their native behavior and configuration schemas.
- Orbit launches exact argv and retains process, PTY, terminal state, and Session authority. Venus owns no shell or tool policy.

Accepted first slice:
- Nushell is the default Eon shell through eon-nu.
- Starship uses native modules plus one sparse Eon override, a violet ∴ prompt marker, and no extra blank line.
- Zoxide initialization is enabled in managed Nushell.
- Stable external commands are eon-nu, eon-hx, eon-yazi, eon-ya, eon-lazygit, and eon-lg.
- Inside an Eon Session, an Eon-private PATH exposes nu, hx, yazi, ya, and lazygit as process-visible names backed by the same managed artifacts. Managed Nushell supplies lg.
- eon run -- COMMAND... remains the explicit escape hatch and retains its accepted semantics.

Scope boundary:
No global aliases or PATH mutation, first-slice alias-mode setting, ornamental eon-git/eon-starship/eon-zoxide commands, copied child schemas, child forks, Carapace, automatic Direnv or Mise activation, arbitrary shell framework, plugin/MCP surface, declarative profile, direct bundle, Home Manager module, remote behavior, or editor replacement. The eon-ofb decision continues to own any later Eon-native editor.
design:
Reference classification before code:
- Required: AGENTS.md; this Bead and parent decisions; current Eon manifest, flake, wrappers, launcher, configuration path, eon versions, and runtime tests; exact Nova revision 37f36efcabf16c41d03e182917926e7b8e56139c for isolated native configuration, managed wrappers, and prompt/tool composition only; primary documentation and exact selected releases for Nushell, Starship, Zoxide, Helix, Yazi, and LazyGit; their licenses; and current Nixpkgs package composition.
- Conditional: current Orbit launch contract if exact default argv cannot be supplied by its accepted interface; macOS package evidence if a selected tool or path projection reveals a concrete blocker.
- Comparison only: user shell frameworks, Direnv, Mise, and Carapace. They do not enter the first slice.
- Rejected: copying Nova configuration or schemas, compatibility with Nova, global command shadowing, shell aliases as the process-visible projection, a second component graph, or moving tool behavior into Eon.

Minimum code shape:
1. Approve and index the smallest managed-environment Eon contract before production or manifest edits.
2. Run one dependency gate covering exact versions, licenses, direct/transitive/native/Nix closure cost, overlap with the existing closure, upgrade burden, Linux behavior, macOS feasibility, and replacement cost. Stop for approval before manifest changes.
3. Extend the canonical component manifest once; Nix and eon versions consume that same graph. Add no second version table.
4. Reuse the existing Eon configuration root and propagate that exact root into Sessions as EON_CONFIG_HOME while retaining XDG_CONFIG_HOME for child configuration. This prevents nested managed dispatch from resolving an eon/eon path. Store only sparse Eon-owned overrides and native child configuration; do not translate or mirror whole child schemas.
5. Install stable eon-prefixed wrapper or symlink names outside Eon. Build one private bin directory for Eon Sessions whose unprefixed names target those same artifacts. Do not mutate the ambient user PATH.
6. Route the default no-command Session to the accepted eon-nu executable through the existing Eon-to-Orbit launch boundary. Preserve eon run -- COMMAND... byte-for-byte and semantically.
7. Prove artifacts and behavior, not configuration literals: executable resolution outside and inside Eon, exact identity reporting, isolated config paths, shell startup, prompt behavior, zoxide initialization, managed lg, subprocess lookup, explicit-command escape, and absence of global shadowing.

Platform disposition:
The selection policy and command semantics are neutral. The current canonical manifest target, Nix composition, and Unix PATH/symlink/exec projection are x86_64-linux isolated platform dependencies. A macOS channel will require one accepted target-capable manifest representation plus bundle-relative artifact injection and link creation; this must preserve the same component graph rather than introduce a second version owner. Any newly discovered tool or wrapper assumption that blocks a native signed macOS bundle must name the exact replacement shape and removal cost before acceptance.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Before implementation, the user-visible managed-environment contract is approved and indexed; the execution baseline records HEAD, AGENTS hash, affected EON contracts, exact component proofs, intended surfaces, dirty paths, and active identity.
2. The reference gate records exact source identities, licenses, adopted mechanisms, rejected surrounding scope, ownership consequences, platform disposition, and the first meaningful check.
3. The dependency gate records exact versions, maintenance and API status, direct/transitive/native/Nix cost, closure overlap and marginal size, Linux behavior, macOS feasibility, upgrade burden, and replacement cost; manifest edits wait for explicit approval.

title: Layer native user Nushell configuration into Eon
description:
Contract: extend EON-C9 for one local Eon user. When managed Nushell starts, Eon loads its packaged env.nu and config.nu first, then loads existing optional user sources at <EON_CONFIG_HOME>/nu/env.nu and <EON_CONFIG_HOME>/nu/config.nu. The default root is ~/.config/eon. Missing user files are ignored. Invalid executable user configuration fails through Nushell with a bounded startup error. Eon never creates, rewrites, parses, or owns the user files or Nushell schema. Packaged Nushell disables its startup banner.

Ownership and shape: Eon owns layering order, selected paths, packaged defaults, and launch materialization. Nushell owns source evaluation and configuration semantics. Reuse the existing Eon configuration-root selector and managed dispatcher. Compose launch-only files outside the user configuration root, using standard-library file handling and atomic replacement if materialization is required. Add no dependency, configuration UI, starter-file generator, schema mirror, Nova compatibility, Mise, Atuin, or Carapace.

Required reference gate: AGENTS.md; this Bead; EON-C9 and its proof; current managed dispatcher, Nix defaults, tests, README, CHANGELOG, and exact package artifact; Nushell 0.113.1 source/help for config arguments, source semantics, and banner setting; Nova exact revision db2e5695a25229df108d9b4d4aef3b96f5db20d9 runtime/yzx-nu.rs only as comparison for packaged-before-user layering and runtime materialization. Nova remains an independent product and no source is copied.

Acceptance: update EON-C9 current-state contract before implementation; record execution baseline and reference gate; TDD proves packaged-before-user order, optional-file absence, exact EON_CONFIG_HOME resolution, nested managed nu, invalid user config failure, and disabled startup banner through the built artifact. Preserve external prefixed and Session-private command boundaries, explicit eon run child behavior, exact component pins, and all other EON contracts. Update README, CHANGELOG, and LOC. Run locked Rust checks, Nix flake check/build, real managed Nushell dogfood, git diff --check, refresh the active Nix profile without stopping live Sessions, then close with exact proof evidence.

What is the minimum Eon-owned mechanism that preserves packaged managed Nushell defaults, layers optional native user configuration from the existing Eon root, and disables the default banner without copying Nushell semantics?

- Nushell 0.113.1 source 7b7df4aa68e957cf38b9d8157c35fa7523f44a6d from the locked Nixpkgs source /nix/store/3k3wi82n4jcwidzzywgfrvzqsxxaq6r7-source, MIT. Inspected CLI configuration arguments, parser parse_source, source-env tests, default config documentation, and REPL banner dispatch. --config and --env-config each accept one alternate file; source and source-env require a parse-time constant path; source-env null is a no-op; $env.config.show_banner = false selects no banner.
- Yazelix Nova db2e5695a25229df108d9b4d4aef3b96f5db20d9, Apache-2.0: inspected complete runtime/yzx-nu.rs and license. It atomically materializes runtime files which source packaged configuration before optional user files. Inspection is independently permitted; the Eon implementation will reuse the mechanism, not copy Nova product configuration, source, or surrounding Mise/Atuin/Starship/config-editor behavior.
- Live negative check against the exact installed managed Nushell: both const file = $env.FOO; source-env $file and source-env $env.FOO fail at parse time as not constant. A packaged file cannot therefore discover EON_CONFIG_HOME dynamically.

Constraints preserved:
- Eon remains the sole owner of root selection, packaged defaults, layering order, launch paths, and generated runtime files.
- Nushell remains the sole owner of parsing, evaluation, schema, and error presentation.
- User files are exact native sources at <root>/nu/env.nu and <root>/nu/config.nu; missing files are ignored and existing files are never created or rewritten.
- Packaged sources run first and user sources second. A user may intentionally override the packaged banner default.
- Generated files live beneath the existing private Eon runtime owner, not beside user configuration. Component pins, the manifest, dependencies, global PATH, explicit child argv, and other managed tools remain unchanged.

Options compared:
1. Pass the user file directly with --config: rejected because it discards packaged defaults.
2. Source an environment-selected path from the packaged file: rejected by exact Nushell parse-time constant behavior.
3. Generate files inside the user configuration root: rejected because it mixes Eon runtime artifacts with user-owned native sources.
4. Materialize two small runtime files atomically beneath the existing private runtime root: selected. It is the first complete option and uses only the Rust standard library.

Code-shape and platform consequences:
Add one focused materializer called only before managed Nushell exec; keep managed_command as the launch-policy owner and replace only its Nu file inputs with the materialized paths. Use the existing owned 0700 runtime-directory validation and atomic same-directory rename. This adds no dependency or schema. It stays within the existing Unix process/runtime seam; a native macOS distribution can use the same filesystem shape behind its already-required runtime-directory owner.

Cheapest proof:
A deterministic Rust test first proves exact packaged-before-user content and optional absence. Existing command tests prove argv and root propagation. The exact built package then proves env/config ordering, nested managed nu, missing files, invalid source diagnostics, and a banner-free interactive startup.

Exit condition:
Revisit only if Nushell gains a supported native multi-file configuration argument or parse-time optional dynamic source that removes runtime materialization without weakening ordering or user ownership.

title: Use native Nushell configuration with guarded Starship fallback
description:
Replace the EON-C9 managed Nushell configuration layer with native Nushell and Starship configuration discovery.

Accepted behavior:
1. Pinned Nushell loads the user's normal XDG/Nushell configuration.
2. Eon supplies one Nushell vendor-autoload script.
3. If the user has replaced Nushell's built-in PROMPT_COMMAND, Eon does not initialize Starship; otherwise it initializes Eon's pinned Starship.
4. The vendor script initializes Eon's pinned Zoxide.
5. Starship reads the normal user configuration; Eon never sets STARSHIP_CONFIG.
6. Native user autoload runs after Eon's vendor script and may override either integration.

Ownership and boundary:
- Eon owns only pinned default artifacts and bounded vendor activation.
- Nushell owns native config and autoload order.
- Starship owns prompt behavior and config discovery.
- Zoxide owns directory ranking, hooks, and commands.
- Session child processes inherit ambient XDG_CONFIG_HOME; Eon private component config remains EON_CONFIG_HOME.

Consequences accepted by the user: remove Eon-owned Nu config materialization, custom Starship preset, lg alias, and banner suppression. Keep pinned Nu, Starship, Zoxide, LazyGit, Helix, and Yazi artifacts, including native Zoxide activation.

Acceptance:
- Native ~/.config/nushell/config.nu and env.nu are loaded.
- A user-replaced PROMPT_COMMAND is preserved.
- With Nushell's built-in default prompt, pinned Starship initializes through vendor autoload.
- Pinned Zoxide initializes through vendor autoload.
- Native ~/.config/starship.toml is honored and STARSHIP_CONFIG remains unset.
- User Nushell autoload may override either integration.
- Tests, contracts, README, changelog, architecture, LOC scorecard, Nix build, and active Nix profile are current.
- No new dependency or product contract.
close_reason: Proved native Nushell and Starship configuration ownership with guarded pinned Starship, pinned Zoxide vendor activation, user-autoload precedence, exact artifact checks, current docs, and runtime-ready package.

title: Extend EON-C9 across four managed shells
description:
Change EON-C9 from a Nu-only managed default to one configurable four-shell environment.

Accepted contract:
- $EON_CONFIG_HOME/config.toml owns [shell] command = ["eon-nu"] plus starship, zoxide, atuin, and carapace booleans, all true by default. command is one non-empty argv vector executed without shell parsing.
- Eon installs pinned Nushell, Bash, Zsh, and Fish and exposes managed eon-nu, eon-bash, eon-zsh, and eon-fish launchers. Arbitrary commands remain valid and unmanaged.
- Native user shell configuration loads first. Each enabled integration is a guarded Eon fallback: it does not replace an existing user prompt, completer, or same-tool hook. false disables only Eon activation.
- Managed activation invokes pinned tools while retaining native Starship, Zoxide, Atuin, and Carapace configuration and state paths. It never edits user files or global PATH. Optional init failure warns and the shell still opens. Settings affect new Sessions only.
- Atuin honors ATUIN_NOBIND and leaves accounts, sync, import, AI, daemon, and pty-proxy policy to Atuin and the user. Mise remains entirely user-owned. Managed Nushell suppresses its stock startup banner; native user autoload remains last.

Prerequisites and references:
- Preserve accepted Orbit source 64db581445bafca1a08a6530f8e44f9c1edbc169 and Venus source/proof 33a3d9af9f4c6015301ad6829fe733413c5b683d.
- Required reference gate: exact current Eon EON-C9 implementation; Nova shell integration at exact commits a705382a, db2e5695, and f1beb34f; exact upstream shell startup and Starship, Zoxide, Atuin, and Carapace generated-init behavior and licenses.
- Apply the Eon crate/tool gate before adding Bash, Zsh, Fish, Atuin, Carapace, or a TOML parser to the runtime graph.

Acceptance checks:
- One built-artifact matrix proves normal native configuration, user-owned guards, enabled and disabled Eon activation, ATUIN_NOBIND, direct argv handling, all four managed shells, arbitrary unmanaged commands, nonfatal optional-init failure, and normal tool config/state discovery.
- Canonical manifest validation and identity reporting include every installed shell/tool and exact revision. Licenses are installed. Locked Rust checks, Nix flake check/build, LOC scorecard, current-state contract/README/changelog, and active-profile refresh pass.

Scope boundary:
- Eon owns selection, pinned artifacts, bounded launch adapters, and defaults only. No shell framework, global aliases or dotfile mutation, custom prompt or completion schema, Mise/Direnv activation, history import/sync policy, remote behavior, distribution expansion, child contract change, or new Venus/Orbit behavior.

comments.text:
Reference and tool gate

Question and contract
- Question: how can EON-C9 offer one reproducible Nu/Bash/Zsh/Fish default with Starship, Zoxide, Atuin, and Carapace while native shell/tool configuration remains user-owned?
- Changes EON-C9 only. Orbit 64db581445bafca1a08a6530f8e44f9c1edbc169 and Venus 33a3d9af9f4c6015301ad6829fe733413c5b683d remain exact, current, and unchanged. Platform classification: neutral shell/config policy with isolated Nix packaging; every selected upstream package declares x86_64-darwin and aarch64-darwin support, but this Bead proves x86_64 Linux only.

Current owner and comparable implementation
- Eon 2bb95a166c0351349a17be6647de5bab0051822d: crates/eon/src/main.rs already owns one multicall managed-command dispatcher, exact argv construction, config-root resolution, Session-private PATH, and the eon-nu vendor-autoload handoff. flake.nix already owns build-time generated Starship/Zoxide init and exact package injection. Extend those owners; add no launcher framework or second config service.
- Yazelix Nova (Apache-2.0) at a705382a, db2e5695, and final startup correction f1beb34fe6060cfa2c0201d7f8095f6ef707f467: adopt only the independently useful mechanisms of build-generated upstream init, Bash --rcfile sourcing ~/.bashrc, Zsh ZDOTDIR shims that source native files, Fish -C after native config, Atuin bind/no-bind variants, existing-hook guards, and nonfatal diagnostics. Reject Nova runtime config materialization, managed Starship schema/preset, Mise activation, compatibility surface, and product config implementation. No Nova source is copied or adapted.

Exact primary shell evidence
- Nushell 0.113.1 at 7b7df4aa68e957cf38b9d8157c35fa7523f44a6d (MIT): src/config_files.rs and crates/nu-protocol/src/eval_const.rs prove native env.nu/config.nu, then vendor autoload, then native user autoload; NU_VENDOR_AUTOLOAD_DIR is a supported prelaunch input. Generated files can set show_banner before the REPL.
- GNU Bash 5.3p9, upstream 5.3 tag b8c60bc9ca365f8261fa97900b6fa939f6ebc303 plus Nixpkgs 567a49d1913ce81ac6e9582e3553dd90a955875f patch set (GPL-3.0-or-later): the exact bash.1 states --rcfile replaces ~/.bashrc for an interactive non-login shell, so the managed rc must source ~/.bashrc first.
- Zsh 5.9.1 at 0e0d4ea11731c47f57bad042fbe75e3979d8a1d2 (MIT-Modern-Variant): exact files.yo specifies ZDOTDIR/.zshenv, .zprofile, .zshrc, .zlogin, and .zlogout ordering. A small ZDOTDIR shim is the supported way to append integration without changing user files.
- Fish 4.7.1 at efb0223da10367031b7c887a3e40eccdf9bf7b06 (GPL-2.0-only): exact fish --help states -C runs after normal configuration and before interactive input, which gives Eon one post-config integration hook.

Exact integration evidence
- Starship 1.25.1 at 8758daa7767d4e73874330b1e262fca66a7ffd30 (ISC): exact init output for all four shells installs named prompt hooks/functions and invokes the pinned store binary; Eon guards it behind the shell default prompt and leaves STARSHIP_CONFIG unset.
- Zoxide 0.9.9 at 9cdc6aa3740b4d8a9d62406c99e84c5de49645e9 (MIT): exact init output for all four shells owns the z/zi commands and an internally duplicate-guarded directory-change hook. Eon invokes the pinned binary and native user autoload remains the final Nu override.
- Atuin 18.16.1 at 671f96b60dac49d1d2de73cc0812986a5e22ce7b (MIT): exact init output for all four shells owns capture hooks and Ctrl-R search; generation with --disable-up-arrow --disable-ai and ATUIN_NOBIND yields the accepted bounded variants. Existing Atuin hook/function markers suppress Eon activation. Accounts, sync, import, daemon, pty proxy, and data/config paths remain upstream/user-owned.
- Carapace 1.6.3 at e4ed2a5ae661848b228224ad7edb20ea678d33d4 (MIT): exact _carapace output supports nushell, bash, zsh, and fish; Nushell preserves a pre-existing external completer and the other shells expose _carapace_completer as the idempotence marker. Generation must replace only the build-user config-bin literal with the native runtime XDG/HOME location.
- License fit: these are separate packaged programs and generated init outputs, not relicensed Eon code. Preserve each upstream license verbatim in share/licenses/eon; GPL Bash/Fish source obligations remain attached to those exact programs and do not relicense the aggregate. Eon remains Apache-2.0.

Dependency decision
- Package the five user-approved missing runtime tools instead of probing ambient installs: ambient shells/tools would make defaults non-reproducible and break exact identity. Individual current closures are Bash 47.2 MiB, Zsh 48.9 MiB, Fish 301.6 MiB, Atuin 100.7 MiB, and Carapace 105.9 MiB; unioning all five with the accepted Eon artifact adds 248,669,008 NAR bytes because of overlap. Remove a component if dogfood shows its default value does not justify that measured cost.
- Parse config.toml with exact toml 1.1.4+spec-1.1.0 at beee9fe5a93347722335e1b99a693f3216986132 and existing Serde 1.0.228 at a866b336f14aa57a07f0d0be9f8762746e64ecb4 (both MIT OR Apache-2.0). Hand parsing is rejected as a second, incomplete TOML implementation; Ratconfig is an editor/model owner, not the supervisor parser and would import a larger UI-oriented boundary. The parser adds no runtime process or native dependency and replaces roughly a hundred lines of unsafe ad-hoc parsing with a strict derived model. Replacement is one decode call if Eon changes format later.

Decision and first proof
- Keep the existing Rust multicall binary as sole runtime policy owner. It reads one strict $EON_CONFIG_HOME/config.toml model for new Sessions and managed-shell launches, passes argv directly, and selects existing Nix-generated native startup assets. Nix supplies exact shells/tools and init; user files are never written.
- First meaningful check: TDD the absent/default, exact override, malformed/unknown, and empty-command config behavior plus argv construction. Then build one exact artifact and execute an isolated four-shell matrix covering native config order, prompt/completer/hook guards, booleans, ATUIN_NOBIND, arbitrary commands, warnings, normal tool paths, identities, and licenses.
- Rejected: ambient dependency discovery, four standalone launcher implementations, runtime init generation, dotfile edits, an Eon shell framework, a second config daemon, or copying Nova code. Exit condition: remove any adapter or dependency whose exact built-artifact proof fails or whose ownership requires replacing native user configuration.

title: Expose a versioned Eon workspace snapshot/action boundary to Venus
description:
Contract routing:
- Implements the missing Eon producer prerequisite for the approved Venus materialization bead ven-c87.
- Extends the approved EON-C8 workspace owner with one versioned consumer boundary. Preserves EON-C1 through EON-C4 and EON-C9.
- Adds EON-C10 under the user's explicit direction to fix the named versioned Eon workspace snapshot/action prerequisite.

Consumer, trigger, result, failures:
Venus or the canonical Eon CLI connects to the explicit local Eon workspace endpoint and submits a versioned inspect or existing semantic workspace action. The running Eon supervisor validates the request, remains the sole live owner, and returns one complete accepted workspace snapshot containing stable ordered tab, pane, and session identities, active and selected identities, liveness, and exact Orbit endpoint mappings. Version mismatch, malformed or oversized input, unavailable action, unknown identity, unrepresentable state, or supervisor absence returns a bounded structured failure without partial state mutation.

Ownership:
- Eon owns EONW v1, its codec, action vocabulary, workspace topology and mappings, acceptance, and complete snapshot.
- The running Eon supervisor remains the sole live state and action owner.
- The CLI and Venus are consumers; neither mirrors the schema or reconstructs state.
- Orbit remains the sole PTY, process, terminal-state, and session authority.
- Venus later owns native materialization, geometry, focus, accessibility, and semantic event emission.

Scope and update order:
This issue publishes the Eon producer boundary by reusing the existing private local control endpoint and Workspace::dispatch owner. The exact current Venus revision accepts only one Orbit socket and cannot truthfully declare or receive EONW. Therefore the canonical consumer requirement and second launch input belong after an exact Venus consumer revision exists: Eon producer proof, then ven-c87 consumption, then Eon composition integration. No event stream, general plugin or MCP API, remote access, authorization framework, durable layout storage, AgentRun model, raw terminal data, Venus implementation, or compatibility window.
design:
Reference classification before code:
- Required: AGENTS.md; this Bead and ven-c87 blocker evidence; EON-C8 owner and tests at 1a00a9f6de171e944c3c31a9f72ee2cc92d8fa15; current control/supervisor flow; canonical manifest and validator; exact accepted Orbit ORBS v2 codec proof 9d6d2bb37f20ab4ad9e186c7bc715eabef43e757 and manifest source 00b136318bea13e3f08d490468f069de6f6b9bd2; exact Venus launch boundary 2d36c72dc87ca5416e22d6afdc35c6ab4e2fb832.
- Comparison only: exact Canario/Rio reference 3e41b8b19a1cad9cd9bdfc8f7900cf61ce5a9098 and the locally inspected Helheim project. They inform workspace UX, not protocol code shape.
- Rejected: exposing handwritten CLI JSON as the cross-repository schema, making Venus speak the private tab-delimited format, duplicating protocol types in Venus, changing the declared requirements or argv of an exact Venus revision that does not consume EONW, or moving topology/session authority.

Minimum code shape:
1. Index EON-C10 before implementation.
2. Add one dependency-free Eon-owned EONW v1 crate with bounded binary request/response framing, semantic actions, complete snapshots, and structured failures. Use the accepted ORBS fixed-header mechanism independently; copy no Orbit implementation.
3. Route the CLI and later Venus through the same EONW codec and existing Workspace::dispatch owner. Keep human and JSON CLI output as projections outside the protocol.
4. Reuse eon.sock and one request per connection. Every success returns a complete snapshot; a client may inspect again when it needs current state. No subscription or event stream.
5. Prove codec boundaries, action/snapshot round trips, CLI preservation, and real supervisor behavior with the fewest strong checks.
6. After an exact producer proof exists, register the Eon provider revision. After ven-c87 produces an exact consumer revision, separately wire the canonical requirement and explicit launch input; never predict those revisions.

Platform classification: isolated Unix local-socket dependency. EONW values are platform-neutral bytes and identities; Eon and Venus own their narrow Unix path conversion. A macOS client can consume the same bounded byte protocol over a local Unix-domain socket.
acceptance_criteria:
1. EON-C10 is approved and indexed with consumer, trigger, complete result, bounded failures, one owner, and honest candidate/proof status.
2. One dependency-free Eon-owned EONW v1 crate represents complete workspace snapshots and the existing bounded actions without copying Orbit schemas or exposing raw terminal state.
3. The supervisor accepts only EONW v1, bounds all input, rejects malformed requests deterministically, and applies mutations only through Workspace::dispatch.
4. Every successful inspect or accepted action returns a complete snapshot with ordered stable tab/pane/session IDs, active/selected identities, liveness, and exact Orbit endpoint bytes. Failed actions preserve prior state.
5. The canonical CLI uses the same EONW request/response codec while preserving current human and JSON behavior.
6. Focused tests prove fixed framing, version mismatch, malformed/oversized input, every action round trip, complete snapshot round trip and invariants, structured owner failures, and existing real workspace control.
7. The current canonical Venus identity, requirements, and one-socket launch plan remain unchanged because revision 2d36c72dc87ca5416e22d6afdc35c6ab4e2fb832 does not consume EONW. The Bead records the exact producer-to-consumer-to-composition update order.
8. No event stream, general plugin surface, remote transport, authorization framework, AgentRun state, durable restoration, raw terminal content, or Venus rendering is added.
9. README, architecture/contracts documentation, CHANGELOG for the consumer-visible protocol, and the handwritten LOC scorecard describe the exact implemented boundary while preserving concurrent icon work.
10. Required Rust checks, existing canonical manifest validation, and git diff --check pass. Proof and graph registration wait for an exact committed producer revision; consumer requirement and launch wiring wait for an exact committed Venus revision.
close_reason: Proved EON-C10 at exact revision 4af395aea06c230ee6b18cf0755ae25915c0b88d; the versioned Eon workspace producer boundary is complete and ready for ven-c87 consumption.

- Current tab-delimited control bytes are unversioned and mix presentation mode with actions; Venus must not learn them.

- New source-of-truth owner: one eon-workspace-protocol crate for EONW v1 values and codec.

Cheapest first meaningful check:
A dependency-free protocol unit test that round-trips every action and one complete snapshot and rejects a changed version, malformed shape, and trailing bytes. It must fail before the codec exists.

Exit condition:
Stop if the shared crate cannot remain the only protocol-schema owner, if exact endpoint mapping cannot be represented within the bounded frame, if mutation bypasses Workspace::dispatch, if a new dependency becomes necessary, or if the current Venus revision would need to be misrepresented.
