comments.text:
Candidate spike and No-Go for the current bundle shape (2026-10-18, Lucca asked to do what's best; reads plus one scoped evidence run, no code change).
Candidate: nix build .#manual-bundle at edge ef238be -> /nix/store/qb3svi8fgz3a7d9vq324kvnvgi4s33mv-eon-0.1.1-x86_64-linux-bundle, eon-0.1.1-x86_64-linux.tar.zst sha256 5f08ec4d23171e66d82e6e5a0d82f2725f18b9e34e61cb4805a1e1aafd8a2f4b (488,258,452 bytes), bundled bubblewrap 0.11.2.

Blocker A (installation, Ubuntu): on a stock Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS cloud image (official image sha256 8800651811af9a85465ad1d552add729947bb16488dddb4a9b5305a3d97332b2, kernel 7.0.0-34-generic, QEMU 11.1.1/KVM, headless, cloud-init user with no Nix and no /nix), kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=1 and apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_unconfined=1. After sha256sum -c and tar --zstd extraction, both 'eon versions' and 'eon --help' exit 1 with 'bwrap: setting up uid map: Permission denied'. dmesg shows apparmor=DENIED profile=unprivileged_userns comm=bwrap capname=setpcap plus a denied write to /proc/PID/uid_map. eon-install's preselection check runs the packaged 'eon versions', so install fails the same way. Ubuntu's shipped bwrap-userns-restrict profile attaches only to the system /usr/bin/bwrap. A root-installed per-path profile (flags=(unconfined) { userns, } on the extracted libexec/bwrap) makes 'eon versions' pass. That remedy needs root and grants userns to a binary the user can overwrite, so it is not a user-owned install and it weakens Ubuntu's hardening. This Pop!_OS 24.04 host has no apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns sysctl at all, so the 2026-10-10 Pop!_OS proof could not see this. Ubuntu 24.04 is not observed here; public reports put the same default on 24.04 and later.

Blocker B (core use, every host): the entrypoint (bundle/src/main.rs) runs eon, and so Orbit and every terminal child, inside bwrap --unshare-user. bwrap sets PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS, which is inherited and cannot be cleared. Reproduced on this host with the bundle's own bwrap 0.11.2 and the entrypoint's exact argument shape: NoNewPrivs 1; /usr/bin/sudo and /etc/shadow show nobody:nogroup; sudo -n true fails ('The "no new privileges" flag is set'); su fails; id shows groups 1000,65534 instead of 1000,4,27,108,987,995. So sudo, su, pkexec, passwd and setuid helpers such as rootless Podman's newuidmap fail in every Eon terminal of a Nix-free install. orb-prove-no-survivor-session-shutdown-btg already rejected this shape for Orbit ('Unmapped root also makes setuid-root behavior unavailable ... not an acceptable Orbit terminal contract'). The 2026-10-10 bundle proof did not check sudo.

Unverified risk: the payload carries Mesa's software Vulkan driver. Whether Venus uses the host GPU from the bundle is not observed.

Recommendation: No-Go for any bwrap/user-namespace candidate. Qualification resumes only on a candidate whose terminals run outside any user namespace. The reference route that fits: a namespace-free relocation, i.e. a small static launcher that runs the bundled ld.so with --library-path for the dynamically linked GUI (Venus), with static Orbit, eon and managed tools (the Exodus pattern; fzakaria 2026 'Nix needs relocatable binaries' proposes the same launcher; Guix relocatable packs and nix-portable rely on userns or PRoot and share these limits). That supersedes docs/MANUAL-BUNDLE.md's bwrap /nix projection and its 'no ELF/config path rewriting' decision, so it needs Lucca's approval and its own bead, with a reference gate, before code. lm9p's scope forbids runtime changes.
Harness for the rerun: official cloud images plus a cloud-init NoCloud seed (Ubuntu 26.04 LTS required; Ubuntu 24.04 LTS and Fedora Workstation; Debian 13 optional), disposable qcow2 overlays, QEMU -display none with QMP screendump and input-send-event for the outermost GUI observation, SSH for commands, and a desktop plus GDM autologin for the interactive steps. Add sudo -n true, id and a GPU-selection check to the terminal checks.
Next step: Lucca chooses whether to open the relocation redesign bead. lm9p returns to open.

title: Prove Nix-free install failure and recovery paths on Ubuntu 26.04
description:
## Why

lm9p's acceptance requires that "artifact verification, partial-install/upgrade failure and recovery
behave as documented" for the Nix-free install. eon-zti4.9 proved only the happy path of the relinked
candidate on stock Ubuntu VMs; its record lists the failure paths as not repeated. The earlier
failure proof (eon-prove-thin-linux-bundle-installer-8r7n, eon-prove-manual-nix-free-linux-bundle-216b)
used the bwrap-era archives the installer no longer accepts.

## Evidence

- docs/INSTALLER.md "Failure and recovery": signature/hash, download, archive-boundary and
  preselection failures leave `current` unchanged; extraction rejects absolute symlinks, duplicate
  entries and special files; one prefix lock; interrupted installs leave `.eon-stage-*` or
  `.eon-select-*` residue and a rerun selects only a complete checked version; an unmarked prefix
  is refused; conflicting commands are preserved; no HTTP fallback, TLS verification stays on.
- docs/MANUAL-BUNDLE.md "Verification before extraction": `ssh-keygen -Y verify` and
  `sha256sum -c` before extraction.
- installer/src/tests.rs: unit tests already cover extraction rejection (absolute link, escapes,
  special files) and failed selection/locking (eon-zti4.6 proof).
- eon-zti4.9 proof comment: candidate A b396b4a2c538bbaed310a9c8755bc3ee602da3a1e9a2f7caf4660426dc2c3859
  (edge b5af62f), installer f9igv6rj7qhw5ch1l6vw7hg2izxf22ll, VM recipe and guest script shape.

## Scope

In scope:
- One stock Ubuntu 26.04 LTS cloud-image VM with no Nix (eon-zti4.9 recipe), the exact lm9p
  candidate, and disposable fixtures in session scratch: a throwaway signer, a local HTTPS server,
  tampered SHA256SUMS/signature/archive copies, a signed archive whose packaged `eon versions`
  preflight fails, and an untrusted TLS certificate.
- Outermost observations: manual verify rejects a tampered SHA256SUMS and a wrong archive digest;
  eon-install rejects a bad signature, a digest mismatch, an untrusted certificate and an http://
  URL, each leaving `current` unchanged; a failing preflight is not selected; an install killed
  mid-extraction leaves residue, a rerun installs and selects cleanly; a concurrent second
  mutation is refused by the lock; an unmarked existing prefix is refused; a pre-existing
  PREFIX/bin/eon not owned by the installer is preserved.

Out of scope:
- Installer or bundle code changes. A failing check is a finding: record it and stop.
- Re-running extraction-rejection cases already proved by installer/src/tests.rs; cite them.
- Fedora (sibling bead), the interactive workflow (sibling bead), publication, signing anchors.

## Acceptance

- Every listed failure behaves as docs/INSTALLER.md and docs/MANUAL-BUNDLE.md describe on the VM,
  with `current` and live work unchanged where the docs promise it, and a clean rerun after
  interruption.
- The bead records the candidate identity, VM image sha256, kernel, glibc and each observation.

## Implementation Notes

1. Rebuild or reuse the candidate at the current edge; if `nix build .#manual-bundle` no longer
   yields b396b4a2..., record the new identity and say which earlier proof it invalidates.
2. Boot the VM with the eon-zti4.9 recipe (boot.sh, prep.sh shape; dcg blocks redirects to variable
   paths, so write scripts with the Write tool and scp them).
3. Script each case with exit codes and the `current` link before and after.

## Verification

- The guest transcript summary is recorded in this bead; each case shows the expected non-zero exit
  or refusal plus unchanged `current`, and the recovery rerun exits 0.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if any case diverges from the documented behavior; record it and ask Lucca before changing
  code or docs.
- Stop if the candidate changes materially mid-run.

## Maintenance Notes

- Part of lm9p's split (Lucca, 2026-10-19): this child, the Ubuntu workflow child and the Fedora
  child; lm9p keeps the Go/No-Go.
close_reason: Every documented failure and recovery path behaves as described on stock Ubuntu 26.04.1 with live work preserved (proof comment). One message finding (unmarked 0700 prefix reports os error 2) reported, not fixed.

title: Prove the Eon workflow from the Nix-free install on Ubuntu 26.04
description:
## Why

lm9p's acceptance requires current candidate proof of the documented Eon workflow from the Nix-free
install: first launch, help, managed tools, tabs/panes and independent windows, representative
configuration/child errors, detach/reopen and exact Stop, plus upgrade/rollback that keep retained
generations usable and removal that preserves user configuration and data. eon-zti4.9 proved
install, a Venus window and one terminal's identity checks only.

## Evidence

- docs/USAGE.md: "Install and start", "Stop terminals", "Workspace and picker", "Eon Bar and tabs",
  "CLI commands", "eonbase", "Troubleshooting and reporting".
- `eon --help`: run, window new/attach/stop, attach, generations, stop, tab create/close/directory,
  pane create/close, focus, workspace --json, versions.
- eon-zti4.9 proof comment: candidate A b396b4a2... and upgrade target B eb4639bd... (the B recipe:
  one comment line in flake.nix of a `git archive` export), installed-window recipe (headless sway,
  `wtype -s 6000 -k Return` for the picker, evidence written to files because Eon does not forward
  arbitrary env to terminals).
- eonbase (the renamed EonTerm, docs/USAGE.md "eonbase") is a separate Nix package and is not in the
  manual bundle's closure-paths.txt.

## Scope

In scope:
- One stock Ubuntu 26.04 LTS VM with no Nix, the exact lm9p candidate installed by eon-install, and
  scripted observations through the typed CLI (`eon workspace --json`, tab/pane/window commands),
  wtype key input and grim screenshots:
  - first launch through the picker; `eon --help`; managed tools run in a terminal (nu, hx, yazi,
    lazygit, zoxide/zi, starship, atuin, carapace, fzf) and the Git popup;
  - a second tab and pane, an independent window (`eon window new`);
  - one invalid configuration value and one failing child command, each showing its documented
    notice or error;
  - detach by closing the window, `eon attach`, the same terminals present;
  - upgrade to B with that work live: a new launch runs B's generation, A's generation stays
    attachable through its retained payload; rollback; removal leaves config and state directories
    byte-identical; exact `eon stop GENERATION` ends only the named generation.
- Record the declared host prerequisites as observed.
- Record that eonbase is Nix-only today, for lm9p's Go/No-Go; do not add it to the bundle.

Out of scope:
- Code, docs or contract changes; failure-path cases (sibling bead); Fedora (sibling bead);
  agent providers' sign-in and quota (no credentials in the VM; note the observed unsigned state).

## Acceptance

- Each listed workflow step is observed on the VM from the installed candidate with its evidence
  (command output, workspace JSON or screenshot) recorded in this bead, or recorded as a finding.
- Retained-generation behavior across upgrade, rollback and removal matches docs/INSTALLER.md and
  the generation rules in docs/USAGE.md.

## Implementation Notes

1. Reuse or rebuild candidate A and target B at the current edge; record identities.
2. Boot the VM with the eon-zti4.9 recipe; drive Eon headlessly (never on Lucca's desktop).
3. Prefer typed CLI control and file evidence over screenshots; take one screenshot per window state.

## Verification

- The guest transcript summary and screenshot descriptions are recorded in this bead.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if a workflow step fails in a way that looks like a bundle defect (for example a missing data
  root or a /nix path lookup); record it and ask Lucca before fixing, since a fix changes the
  candidate and invalidates earlier proof.
- Stop if the session nears its context budget before the upgrade/rollback part; hand off with the
  steps done.

## Maintenance Notes

- Part of lm9p's split (Lucca, 2026-10-19). Desktop focus: headless VM only.
close_reason: Every workflow step observed on Ubuntu 26.04 from installed candidate A, or recorded as a finding; retained generations behave per docs/INSTALLER.md and USAGE.md across upgrade, rollback, removal and exact Stop. Finding 1 (failed child blocks later terminals) is a core-use input to lm9p's Go/No-Go.

title: Prove the Nix-free install on Fedora 44
description:
## Why

lm9p's qualification matrix names Fedora Workstation beside Ubuntu 26.04 and 24.04. The relinked
bundle has been proved only on Ubuntu (eon-zti4.9). Fedora differs in ways that can break it:
SELinux enforcing by default, a different glibc build (Fedora 44 ships 2.43), different Mesa and
Vulkan packaging, and different library paths.

## Evidence

- eon-zti4.1 reference record: Fedora 43 glibc 2.42-17.fc43, Fedora 44 2.43-2.fc44; the bundle's
  glibc floor is 2.39 (docs/MANUAL-BUNDLE.md "Execution and host boundary").
- eon-zti4.9 proof comment: the candidate (b396b4a2..., edge b5af62f), signer and HTTPS fixtures,
  and the Ubuntu guest script shape (manual verify/extract, eon-install install/upgrade/rollback/
  remove, a Venus window, terminal NoNewPrivs/id/sudo checks).
- docs/MANUAL-BUNDLE.md: the host supplies glibc, libgcc_s, libwayland-client and a Vulkan driver.

## Scope

In scope:
- One Fedora 44 Cloud Base Generic qcow2 VM (official image, sha256 checked against Fedora's
  CHECKSUM file), SELinux enforcing, no Nix; stand-in packages installed with dnf (sway, grim, wtype,
  mesa-vulkan-drivers, vulkan-loader, zstd) as the only root step.
- The eon-zti4.9 checks on the exact lm9p candidate: manual verify and extract, `eon versions`
  (byte-identical to the Nix product), `eon --help`, eon-install dry run, install, upgrade to a
  second archive, rollback and remove with live work kept, a Venus window, and inside a terminal
  NoNewPrivs 0, `id` as on the host, `stat -c %U /usr/bin/sudo` root and `sudo -n true` as on the
  host; also `getenforce` and any AVC denials (`journalctl -t audit` or `ausearch -m avc` via sudo,
  read-only) during the run.

Out of scope:
- A full GNOME Workstation session (record that the stand-in is sway on Cloud Base); Fedora 43;
  code, docs or contract changes; failure paths and the interactive workflow (sibling beads).

## Acceptance

- Every listed step passes on the Fedora 44 VM with SELinux enforcing and no AVC denial attributable
  to Eon, or each divergence is recorded as a finding.
- The bead records image sha256, kernel, glibc, Mesa/Vulkan versions and the candidate identity.

## Implementation Notes

1. Reuse the eon-zti4.9 scripts' shape; Fedora's cloud-init NoCloud seed works the same way, the
   default user differs and package names differ.
2. Fetch the image from https://fedoraproject.org/cloud/download and verify its CHECKSUM signature
   or digest.

## Verification

- The guest transcript summary is recorded in this bead, plus the SELinux mode and AVC result.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if any step needs root beyond the stand-in packages, an SELinux policy change or a
  namespace; record it and ask Lucca.
- Stop if the candidate changes materially mid-run.

## Maintenance Notes

- Part of lm9p's split (Lucca, 2026-10-19). Cloud Base plus sway is a stand-in for Workstation;
  lm9p's Go/No-Go states that limit honestly.
close_reason: Fedora 44 Nix-free install proved on candidate 6379a43c with SELinux enforcing and no AVC denials

title: Qualify the current Nix-only Linux build for beta
description:
## Contract

Qualify one exact current Eon build for a Nix-only x86_64 Linux native-Wayland beta. A clean user can install it, perform the documented everyday workspace flow, detach and reconnect to the same terminals, stage an upgrade without terminating active work, diagnose failures, and explicitly stop only the intended work. The result is revision-stamped evidence, concrete blockers and known limitations, and a beta go/no-go recommendation.

## Prerequisites and reference gate

The Linux public-alpha qualification, eon-qualify-linux-public-alpha-8ue, is accepted. Planning baseline: Eon edge 92e0d7b379a14d003f37e5c2df9c468cb43e74b7. Before execution, select one immutable candidate, record its manifest/lock and exact runtime, codec, Orbit and Venus revisions, and compare child pins with their latest accepted source revisions. Prior proof applies only to the identities and surfaces it actually exercised.

Read docs/CONTRACTS.md (EON-C1 through C4, C7, C8, C10, C11, C15, C17, C18 and C23), docs/USAGE.md, docs/CONFIGURATION.md, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md and docs/DISTRIBUTION.md, plus the earlier alpha evidence and selected child acceptance records. Use docs/REFERENCES.md for any unresolved mechanism question; this task selects no new mechanism, dependency or release tool.

## Acceptance

1. An isolated clean user/profile installs the immutable Nix candidate from its public source without relying on checkout state or development credentials. Installed version diagnostics and artifacts match the recorded component graph.
2. Installed dogfood covers first launch and directory selection, help, managed tools and popups, tab/pane creation, movement, directory behavior and close, configuration including cursor-tail settings, and independent windows. EonTerm receives its own small exact-command check.
3. Closing/reopening a window and same-boot supervisor recovery preserve the intended terminal identity, command and endpoint without duplicate terminals. Independent workspaces remain independent.
4. The actual Nix profile upgrade is exercised while long-running terminal work is active. That work survives at its original identity; new launches select the candidate. Retained generations remain inspectable and stoppable under their existing contracts. No automatic supervisor restart or Orbit live-handoff claim is introduced.
5. Representative invalid configuration and child startup/reopen failures report useful errors and preserve existing work. Stop ends only the selected disposable generation/window; cleanup leaves no test-owned processes or endpoints.
6. Applicable Rust/Nix/package delivery checks and the clean installed observation pass for the recorded candidate. Reuse valid unchanged proof rather than repeating unrelated suites; retain failures and do not widen proof to another revision or environment.
7. A compact record names the exact sources/artifacts, environment, observations, pass/fail result, unresolved blockers and known limitations. A Go requires the scoped workflows to pass with no unresolved defect that loses active work or prevents installation or core documented use. Otherwise report No-Go with the concrete violated owner/contract.

## Ownership and scope boundary

Eon owns this qualification and the final recommendation; Runtime, Orbit and Venus retain their mechanism and state ownership. Use disposable workspaces and isolated or non-activating native-Wayland surfaces. Preserve the user's desktop focus, live supervisors, terminals, configuration and unrelated profile elements.

This bead authorizes qualification only. Public tags/releases/announcements, channel promotion, version changes and implementation fixes require separately chosen work. Report concrete blockers for user disposition rather than creating a speculative fix backlog. Keep the current explicit accessibility, compositor, hardware and recovery limitations honest. Apple Silicon proof and direct distribution remain separate; no additional platform, installer, package channel, feature or lifecycle guarantee is included.

title: Verify Nova's quick search (no side effects, Ctrl+O opens and sets the first pane's cwd) and align Eon or Nova
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-10-23: "another p1 bead: verify nova's quick search with no side-effects and ctrl+o to open and set cwd on the first pane / it's different from eon, so we likely have to update eon or nova".

The two products' directory quick search (Zoxide history through fzf) differs.
- **Nova** (~/pjs/nova/nova): startup search binds Ctrl+O, which passes the selected directory to the editor-open boundary, so the result opens in the editor and becomes the tab's folder. The popup search binds Alt+Enter to set the tab folder. Sources: `docs/ideation/yazi-keymap.md` (implementation constraints; `--expect=ctrl-o` at startup, `--expect=alt-enter` in the popup), `crates/yzx-config/src/catalog.rs:225-229`, and `checks/startup-picker-cancel.rs:261-316` ("Ctrl+O Open in editor").
- **Eon** (EON-C18 Picker-first tab directories, docs/CONTRACTS.md:1443ff): Enter accepts one result and starts the tab's first pane, a shell, there; Tab opens Yazi; Esc and Ctrl+C cancel. There is no Ctrl+O. Browsing adds no Zoxide history, and each exit stops and reaps the history query.

Users moving between the two get different keys and different results, and a quick search that leaves side effects (Zoxide history, a stray process, a changed directory before acceptance) would surprise them.

## Deliverable

1. **Verify Nova on its installed build**, in isolation and with no desktop focus taken. Check that quick search has no side effects until acceptance: no Zoxide history added by browsing or cancelling, no leftover query process, no directory change on cancel, and no tab or pane change before acceptance. Check that Ctrl+O opens the selected directory in the editor and sets the cwd of the first pane, the tab folder included. Record exactly what happens, including anything that differs from Nova's own docs. Coordinate with the Nova session (`last`, ~/pjs/nova) through eon-overseer before touching Nova's tree or its running sessions.
2. **Verify Eon's equivalent** (the startup, new-tab and Alt+Z pickers) for the same side effects.
3. **Diff the two behaviors**, then propose which product changes, with a recommendation:
   - Eon gains Ctrl+O: accept, and the first pane opens the directory in Helix (`eon edit`-style) instead of a shell;
   - or Nova aligns with Eon;
   - or both converge on a shared key table.
   Name the contract owners (Eon EON-C18, Nova's own contracts) and give the exact contract wording change for Lucca.
4. File any Nova change in Nova's tracker, not Eon's, after Lucca approves, and the Eon implementation as a child bead here.

## Scope

In scope: the verification of both, the diff, the proposal, and the contract wording draft.

Out of scope: implementation before Lucca chooses, and unrelated picker features.

## Acceptance

- Recorded observations for both products (keys, side effects, first-pane cwd), and Lucca's choice with approved wording.

## Verification

Installed isolated observations of both products, following the isolated capture recipe; no live supervisor stopped.

comments.text:
# eon-quick-search-parity-23y9: source findings (not yet installed observations)

Eon edge e3682d5; Nova ~/pjs/nova/nova f486212a (ZPO 7b3f495, Yazi 26.9.1). Nothing run.

## Nova startup picker (Yazi role startup-picker, quick-search.yazi)
- Quick search opens automatically (defaults/yazi/init.lua:11). fzf over `zoxide query --list --exclude <cwd>`.
- Enter: Yazi `cd` to the result only (quick-search main.lua:58). Not acceptance.
- Ctrl+O (startup only, `--expect=ctrl-o`): runs `$YZX_OPEN <dir>`; at startup yzx-open retargets the tab
  folder to the exact dir (orchestrator root + tab label, `cd_focused_pane:false`), then opens
  `yzx-hx <dir>` in a new pane with cwd=<dir>; on editor failure it restores the old root; the picker
  pane closes once the tab has an editor. The sidebar pane keeps its own cwd.
- Alt+Enter ignored at startup; in the popup it sets the tab folder.
- Tab/Esc/Ctrl+C in fzf: back to Yazi browsing. q/Q/Esc/Ctrl+C in Yazi: cancel (exit 130); tab closes if it has no editor.
- SIDE EFFECT: init.lua:6-8 `require("zoxide"):setup({ update_db = true })` for every role, so every
  Yazi `cd` (quick-search Enter, each browse step) runs `zoxide add`. Cancel does not undo it. Yazi's
  process cwd also follows browsing. Ctrl+O itself adds nothing.
- No leftover processes: zoxide query awaited via :output(); Command kill_on_drop.
- Contracts: no CONTRACTS.md; ARCHITECTURE.md:289 C6 (gap "Picker/Yazi UI"); docs/ideation/yazi-keymap.md.
- Docs never mention the zoxide writes; checks/startup-picker-cancel.rs does not check zoxide history.

## Eon picker (EON-C18; runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/cli.rs:306-409, flake.nix directoryPickerConfig)
- fzf `--expect=tab`; Enter = CommitDirectory -> first pN shell at dir (workspace.rs:760-781). No Ctrl+O.
- history.kill()+wait() after every fzf exit (cli.rs:350-353). Esc/Ctrl+C exit 130 -> pending tab keeps
  its starting dir.
- Picker Yazi config has no zoxide setup (update_db defaults false): browsing and Shift+Z add no history.
- Eon's Files popup (ported Nova keys) DOES set update_db = true (flake.nix:501): browsing there adds
  history, as Nova's popup does. Not a picker; outside this bead unless Lucca says otherwise.
- Ctrl+O would need CommitDirectory to carry "start Helix" (EONW wire change -> version bump, reference gate).

Both runs were isolated, with no display focus taken and no live supervisor or session touched. Evidence is in ~/.cache/eon-agents/eon-73/out-eon1 and out-nova1; scripts are in ~/.cache/eon-agents/eon-73/iso/{eon,nova}-probe.sh.

## Eon: installed profile /nix/store/l2nvws89r5w9zaq0fqanaaby18j1i69h-eon-0.1.1
Setup: private headless Sway and wdotool, with a private HOME, runtime dirs and _ZO_DATA_DIR. Each pane runs `sh -c 'exec sleep 900'`, so the picker is the only Zoxide writer. Zoxide was seeded with work, alpha and beta.
- **Startup picker** (s1-s5). I moved through the list, pressed Ctrl+O, Tab into Yazi, went Down/Right twice into work/sub/deeper, used Shift+Z jump then Esc, Tab back, and Esc to cancel.
  - The Zoxide db was byte-identical to the seed at every step.
  - No zoxide process existed at any observation.
  - Ctrl+O did nothing: the tab stayed pending with only the project popup and no pane.
  - Until cancel, t1 stayed pending with no pane. On cancel it got p1 at its starting dir (work); the pane's cwd was work.
- **New-tab picker** (Alt+Shift+T, s6-s7). t2 was pending at HOME with no pane. Down then Enter accepted alpha. t2's directory became alpha, and p2 started at cwd alpha. The db was unchanged.
- **Alt+Z** (s8-s10). The picker opened as t2's project popup. Browsing then Esc left t2's directory (alpha), p2's cwd and the db unchanged.
  - Accepting again chose alpha, the same entry, so this run does not show the retarget. EON-C18 already proves that retarget.
- Cleanup: stop by exact generation, exit 0; private dirs removed.

## Nova: Edge 2.0 /nix/store/2a0z0m72fakmrb1671ch5cqgi856pv9r-yzx (2.0.0, 56c97c82), measured; 1.5.0 not measured
Setup: `yzx enter --session nvq` in a private tmux pty with a private HOME, XDG and Yazelix dirs, _ZO_DATA_DIR, TMPDIR and ZELLIJ_SOCKET_DIR (/run/user/1000/nvrXXX/z). Zoxide was seeded with work, alpha and beta at 4.0. The launch cwd was work.

| Step | Zoxide db | Other state |
| --- | --- | --- |
| n1: startup picker opened | work 4→8 | Yazi starts in work. Opening the picker alone adds history. |
| n2: typed beta, Enter | beta 4→8 | fzf closed; Yazi cwd is beta; the tab is still named "work". |
| n3: Right into beta/child | beta/child added (4) | |
| n4: typed alpha, Ctrl+O | unchanged | See below. |
| n5-n7: Alt+Shift+T new tab | beta 8→12, beta/child 4→8 | The tab opened as "home". Typed beta, Enter, Right, then Esc. Cancel closed tab 2, and history kept every write. |

At n4, Ctrl+O renamed the tab to "alpha". The yazi_picker pane was replaced by an "editor" pane running Nova's hx with cwd alpha; Helix shows its file picker and Explorer on alpha. The sidebar plugin pane remained.

- No zoxide or fzf process outlived its step.
- Cleanup: the private Zellij server needed SIGKILL after kill-session and TERM. It was matched by HOME/ZELLIJ_SOCKET_DIR environ only. Private dirs removed.
- The Zellij pane/tab JSON query in the script did not find the server binary, so the tab and pane state above comes from tmux screen captures and /proc.

## Diff
- **Acceptance key.** Eon's Enter accepts and starts a shell first pane at the directory. In Nova, Enter only moves Yazi, and Ctrl+O accepts: it sets the tab folder and opens Helix at that directory in a new pane that replaces the picker.
- **Ctrl+O in Eon:** none.
- **Side effects before acceptance.**
  - Eon has none: no Zoxide writes from opening, browsing, jumping or cancelling, and no leftover processes.
  - Nova writes Zoxide history when the picker opens (the launch dir), on Enter and on every browse step, and cancelling does not undo it. The cause is Yazi's zoxide plugin `update_db = true` for every role, in defaults/yazi/init.lua:6-8.
  - Neither product changes the tab folder before acceptance or cancellation.

# Final form agreed with Lucca, 2026-10-23

This supersedes the earlier "Eon unchanged" decision. Lucca reasoned it through from first principles and called this "the final form". The EON-C18 text and the Nova bead text are not written yet; each needs Lucca's approval.

## Principles
- Exploring is free. Nothing persists until you pick: no Zoxide history, no tab folder, and no folder that something reads later.
- A pick records history once: the picked directory gets one visit (pending Lucca's explicit yes).
- The common path takes one key, and every action has exactly one key.
- One quick search, one Yazi. Tab switches between them.

## One pair, two screens
Startup, new tab and Alt+Z open the pair on quick search. Alt+Shift+Y opens it on Yazi.

| Screen | Enter | Alt+Enter | Tab | Esc / Ctrl+C |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Quick search | pick the highlighted result | none | Yazi opens at the highlighted result: move only, nothing written | close |
| Yazi | open: step into a folder, or edit a file | pick the hovered folder, else the current one | quick search; Yazi does not move | close |

- **Pick.** A pending tab starts its first pane in the folder: a shell in Eon, Helix in Nova. An existing tab changes its folder and leaves running panes alone.
- **Moving with Zoxide.** Type, then press Tab. Lucca: "typing and tab serving quick search movement only is pretty smart".
- **Removed keys.** Z as a Tab alias, Yazi's separate Shift+Z jump, q as cancel, and Nova's Ctrl+O.
- **Known cost.** Tab with an empty query opens Yazi at the top result instead of where it was.
- **Enter means pick in quick search in every entry**, the Files popup included. That was option 1, chosen over making Enter's meaning depend on the entry.

## Changes
- **Eon.** The Project and Files popups merge into one pair. The directory-only chooser goes away, so startup and new-tab pickers become the full file manager. This reverses EON-C18's file-operation exclusion. Picking from Yazi moves to Alt+Enter, and quick-search Tab follows the highlighted result. This is an EONW and contract change; it gets a reference gate and child beads.
- **Nova** (startup picker and popup). Enter in quick search picks and Tab moves. Esc closes. Ctrl+O is removed. No history writes before a pick. The rejoin-cwd read of an unaccepted picker is fixed (orchestrator commands.rs:719-740, from source). Filed in Nova's tracker through eon-overseer and `last`.

## Still to confirm with Lucca
1. Use the pair at startup and on new tabs as well, not only for Alt+Z and Alt+Shift+Y.
2. In a pending tab, opening a file picks its folder and opens the file in Helix as the first pane.
3. On an existing tab, Esc hides the pair and keeps its state. On a pending tab, Esc keeps EON-C18's dismissal: the first pane starts at the starting folder.
4. A pick writes one Zoxide visit for the chosen directory.
5. Cancel stays a product difference: Eon starts the pending tab, Nova closes it.

title: Spike: host a pending tab's picker in the Files Yazi and commit it from a pick
description:
## Why

Lucca approved the directory pair on 2026-10-23; see the parent eon-quick-search-parity-23y9 and its comments "Final form" and "Lucca approved the whole draft".

- **The pair:** each tab gets quick search (Zoxide through fzf) plus the tab's Files Yazi.
- **How it opens:** startup, new-tab and Alt+Z open it on quick search. Alt+Shift+Y opens it on Files.
- **What it retires:** the separate Project chooser.

The mechanism is not proven yet. Today, a pending tab's only popup is the transient Project chooser. That chooser runs `eon-directory-picker` (runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/cli.rs:306-409) and commits through `Action::CommitDirectory` (runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/workspace.rs:358, 760-781). Files is a keep-alive popup, and only established tabs have it. Per the small-beads rule, spike the mechanism first.

## Evidence

- `eon/crates/eon/src/product.rs:60,84-88`: the `project` and `files` popup entries.
- `flake.nix:446-476`: directoryPickerConfig.
- `flake.nix:479-600`: filesPopupConfig, quick-search.yazi and tab-folder.yazi.
- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/workspace.rs:450`: `SetTabDirectory` calls `set_tab_directory`. Today it cannot resolve a pending tab. The memory file isolated-eon-capture-recipe notes that `eon tab directory` cannot resolve the startup picker.
- EONW is at v19 (`runtime/crates/eon-workspace-protocol/src/v19.rs`). yx8.11 is taking EONW 19 and later, so coordinate the number.
- `EON_YA` is packaged (`flake.nix:639`). `ya emit-to <id> plugin quick-search` is one candidate for switching a live Files Yazi to quick search.

## Scope

In scope: a throwaway spike plus the reference gate. Answer these four questions and record the answers here:

1. Can a pending tab host the Files Yazi popup with quick search shown first?
2. How does a pick from the pair (Enter in quick search, or Alt+Enter in Yazi) commit the pending tab atomically, starting exactly one first pN? The candidates are making `SetTabDirectory` commit pending tabs, or a Files-side `CommitDirectory`.
3. How do Alt+Z and Alt+Shift+Y switch the shown screen, or hide the pair? The owner is either Venus or the Runtime, the latter through `ya emit-to`.
4. What exact EONW change and version number does this need?

Out of scope:
- product code on edge;
- contract text edits;
- Nova.

## Acceptance

- The four answers are recorded, with a red/green reproducer kept under ~/.cache/eon-agents/<session>/.
- The reference gate is recorded:
  - the owner of each step: Venus key, Runtime popup, Files Yazi, the pick, the Orbit terminal;
  - the docs/REFERENCES.md routes read;
  - Nova's quick-search.yazi and yzx-open retarget, at an inspected revision;
  - Yazi's DDS/`emit-to` and `--chooser-file` semantics;
  - what was kept and what was rejected;
  - the EONW decision.
- If the chosen mechanism differs from the approved draft, Lucca has approved it.

## Implementation Notes

1. Ask eon-overseer before any nix build or isolated session.
2. Prototype in a worktree under ~/.cache/eon-agents/<session>/wt. Build with `--out-link`.
3. Use the parent's isolated probe: ~/.cache/eon-agents/eon-73/iso/eon-probe.sh.

## Verification

- An isolated installed run of the prototype shows a pending tab committed from Files with exactly one first pane.
- The Zoxide db is unchanged before the pick.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop for Lucca if a pending tab cannot host Files without a contract change beyond the approved draft.
- Stop if the EONW number collides with in-flight work.

title: Merge the Project chooser and Files popup into one directory pair
description:
## Why

This is slice 2 of the parent's approved design. It merges the Project chooser and the Files popup into one directory pair. It uses the mechanism proved by the spike child, which blocks it. Lucca approved the EON-C18 and EON-C10 wording on 2026-10-23. The approved text is in the parent's comments and in ~/.cache/eon-agents/eon-73/draft-contract-and-beads.md, sections A1 and A2.

## Evidence

- `eon/crates/eon/src/product.rs:60`: the `project` entry on Alt+Z.
- `flake.nix:446-476`: the directory-only chooser's Yazi config, which this slice retires.
- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/cli.rs:306-409`: `eon-directory-picker`.
- Contract and docs text to change:
  - `docs/CONTRACTS.md` EON-C18 (~1479) and the EON-C10 runtime policy (~878-910);
  - `docs/CONFIGURATION.md`;
  - `docs/USAGE.md:137`, the Alt+Z row;
  - the shortcut viewer and hints.
- `eon-ecne.3` (deferred) planned to remove Alt+Z. That plan is superseded: Alt+Z stays and opens the pair on quick search.

## Scope

In scope:
- **Entry points:**
  - Startup, new-tab and Alt+Z open the tab's Files Yazi on quick search.
  - Alt+Shift+Y opens it on Files.
- **Retirement:** remove the Project chooser entry and its Yazi config.
- **Pending tab:** a pick commits the tab and starts one first pN shell. Closing the pair is EON-C18 dismissal: the first pane starts at the starting directory.
- **Established tab:** closing hides the pair and keeps its state.
- **Hotkeys:** Alt+Z and Alt+Shift+Y each switch to their own screen, or hide the pair if their screen is already shown.
- **Protocol:** the EONW bump.
- **Docs:** EON-C18 and EON-C10 text exactly as approved; CONFIGURATION, USAGE, shortcut help, hints and CHANGELOG.

Out of scope:
- the in-pair key changes (child 3);
- pending-tab file open (child 4);
- Nova.

## Acceptance

In installed Eon:
- A fresh workspace, Alt+Shift+T and Alt+Z each show quick search over the tab's Files Yazi.
- Alt+Shift+Y shows Files.
- A pick on a pending tab starts exactly one pane in the picked directory.
- Esc on a pending tab starts its pane at the starting directory.
- Esc on an established tab hides the pair, and the next Alt+Shift+Y returns to the same place.
- No `project` popup entry and no directory-picker config remain.

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test` passes the workspace suites.
- Profile refresh, then one isolated installed observation with the parent's probe script, covering `eon workspace --json`, procs and the Zoxide db.
- Codex and Claude review per AGENTS.md.

## Stop Conditions

- If the spike's mechanism differs from the approved draft, stop before code until Lucca approves it.
- Stop for Lucca if the work needs any contract wording beyond the approved text.

title: Pair keys: Enter picks, Tab moves, nothing persists before a pick
description:
## Why

This is slice 3 of the parent's approved design: the pair's keys and its rule that nothing persists before a pick. Lucca, 2026-10-23: "typing and tab serving quick search movement only is pretty smart".

| Screen | Enter | Alt+Enter | Tab | Esc / Ctrl+C |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Quick search | pick the highlighted result | none | Files at the highlighted result (move only) | close |
| Files | open: enter a folder, or edit a file | pick the hovered folder, else the current one | quick search; Files does not move | close |

Removed: Z as a search key, the Shift+Z jump, and q/Q as cancel.

## Evidence

- `flake.nix:501`: Files has `require("zoxide"):setup({ update_db = true })`, so browsing writes history today. Lucca approved removing it.
- `flake.nix:529-560`: quick-search.yazi. Today Enter moves Yazi and Alt+Enter sets the tab folder.
- `flake.nix:492-495`: in the Files keymap, Tab and Z both open search.
- Installed observations on the parent: Eon's picker writes nothing to Zoxide, even when you pick.

## Scope

In scope:
- the quick-search plugin and the Files keymap and init in `flake.nix`;
- the footers: "Enter Use · Tab Browse from here · Esc Close" and "Enter Open · Alt+Enter Use folder · Tab Search · Esc Close";
- `update_db = false`;
- exactly one `zoxide add <picked dir>` per pick;
- stopping and reaping a still-running history query on every exit;
- Tab with an empty query: Files opens at the top result;
- Tab with empty history: Files opens where it already is.

Out of scope:
- Nova, which has its own bead;
- the pair mechanism (child 2).

## Acceptance

In an isolated installed run:
- The Zoxide db stays byte-identical through open, search, Tab moves, browsing, screen switches and close.
- After a pick, the db has exactly one added visit, for the picked dir.
- In quick search, Enter picks, Tab moves and Esc closes.
- In Files, Alt+Enter picks and Enter opens.
- Z and q do nothing in the pair.

## Configurability (AGENTS.md)

The in-pair keys stay fixed. They are the contract-bound key table that Eon and Nova share (EON-C18 as approved). The Alt+Z and Alt+Shift+Y hotkeys stay configurable as popup shortcuts. Record this reason in the bead comment that lands with the commit.

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test` passes for the affected crates.
- Profile refresh, then an isolated installed observation with ~/.cache/eon-agents/eon-73/iso/eon-probe.sh, extended with a Zoxide diff after each key.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if fzf or Yazi cannot express "Tab opens at the highlighted result" without a custom walker, which EON-C18 forbids.

title: Opening a file in a pending tab picks its folder and starts Helix as the first pane
description:
## Why

This is slice 4 of the parent's approved design. Lucca approved on 2026-10-23 that opening a file in a pending tab picks the file's folder and starts the first pane as Helix on that file. Nova does the same at startup: yzx-open retargets to the file's parent and opens the editor.

## Evidence

- The Files edit opener runs `eon edit` (`flake.nix:482-486`).
- `eon edit` (`runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/cli.rs:1024-1047`) needs an established tab today.
- `eon-tab-create-launch-8tl4` needs the same Runtime step: start a tab's first pane at a directory with an argv. Share that step rather than add a second one.

## Scope

In scope:
- In a pending tab, Enter on a file in Files commits the tab directory to the file's folder.
- It then starts exactly one first pN running packaged Helix on that file.
- When Helix exits, that pane ends like any `eon edit` pane.

Out of scope: `eon edit` on established tabs, which stays as it is.

## Acceptance

- In installed Eon, open a new tab, press Tab into Files, then Enter on a text file. The result is a tab whose directory is the file's folder and whose only pane is Helix on that file.
- No shell pane starts.
- The Zoxide db gets one visit, for the folder.

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test` passes for the affected crates.
- Profile refresh, then one isolated installed observation.

## Stop Conditions

- If 8tl4 has landed a different shape for starting a first pane with an argv, stop and coordinate.

title: eon tab directory picks for a pending tab
description:
## Why

AGENTS.md (Humans and Agents) requires a CLI path for every window action. Lucca approved on 2026-10-23 that `eon tab directory TAB -- DIR` also picks for a pending tab: it commits the directory and starts the first pane, as a pick in the pair does. Today it cannot resolve a pending tab's picker.

Two related actions need no new command:
- Which screen of the pair is shown is Venus-local view state, so it gets no CLI path.
- Opening a file is already `eon edit`.

## Evidence

- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/workspace.rs:450`: `SetTabDirectory` calls `set_tab_directory`.
- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/cli.rs` (~1000-1021): the `tab directory` parser.
- Parity epic: eon-agent-parity-a9g0.

## Scope

In scope:
- `eon tab directory` on a pending tab commits it the way a pick does: one first pN shell and one Zoxide visit.
- The command leaves the person's active tab, selection, shown popup and focus as they are.
- USAGE and the EON-C10 CLI text.

Out of scope: the rest of the pair. If the spike child already made `SetTabDirectory` the pick path, this bead only adds proof and docs, or closes as done by child 2.

## Acceptance

- From an Eon terminal, `eon tab directory <pending tab> -- DIR` starts that tab's first pane in DIR.
- The caller's active tab stays active.

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test` passes for the affected crates.
- One isolated installed observation, comparing `eon workspace --json` before and after.

title: Keep routine workspace navigation quiet
description:
## Outcome
Routine tab and pane navigation stays quiet. Selecting an already-selected live target, traversing an axis with one target, or trying to reorder past an ordered edge succeeds with the unchanged workspace snapshot. Ordinary workspace attachment progress shows no connecting/waiting banner. Actual unknown/stale targets, picker restrictions, offline endpoints, transport/protocol failures and lifecycle failures remain visible.

## Ownership and contract
Eon owns navigation policy and accepted no-op results in EON-C8/EON-C10. Venus owns transient connection presentation in VEN-C4/VEN-C8; preserve terminal authority, attachment identity, accessibility and input admission. No copied error filtering in Venus and no new protocol variant/schema. Linux native Wayland only. This one Eon issue owns the user-selected product fix across sequential Venus source acceptance and Eon delivery; no second issue is claimed.

## Prerequisites and references
Accepted Orbit ea9fd28ce0908f218cf65d4e6df368f0a4e565f5 (ORB-C4/C6/C8; ORBF v2 / ORBS v11) and Venus 74d22276e9039dc3ee6151d69b9283114ab02ea1. Eon currently pins older Orbit 91999d7 and Venus bc5a2bd; deliver the corrected accepted Venus and its exact compatible Orbit pair. Keep EONW v4 c305453bba4fe50c29f65e829b9cd65af31ced8a.
Required before code: existing workspace action/result, client status/accessibility and attachment owners; complete affected contracts/tests; Canario/Rio 3e41b8b19a1cad9cd9bdfc8f7900cf61ce5a9098 navigation comparison routed by docs/REFERENCES.md. Nova Zellij navigation is comparison only. No dependency capability or copied source.

## Acceptance
- Existing action-boundary tests go red for successful unchanged snapshots at singleton/same-target/ordered-edge navigation, then pass with unknown identity, duplicate request and picker/lifecycle failures preserved.
- The actual Venus Application status path is silent while a valid workspace attachment connects or awaits its first frame, and still reports genuine failure; standalone diagnostic behavior remains intact.
- Exact manifest/Cargo/Nix identities agree; affected Rust/build checks pass and installed Eon/EonTerm profiles resolve to the just-built artifacts.
- One private headless Wayland observation exercises real pane/tab switches, navigation no-ops, useful failure, retained Session identities and quiet connection phases. Preserve ambient desktop focus and all live user Sessions.

## Boundary
No popup/sidebar, navigation wrap redesign, generic notification framework, new settings, timeout/debounce layer, cached terminal history, live supervisor restart, unrelated tool update or expanded platform proof. Existing scrollback is included only through the required accepted paired component refresh; its separate planning issue is not modified here.
close_reason: Quiet routine navigation accepted through native status regressions and installed paired Eon/EonTerm proof; real failures and live Sessions preserved.

title: Mark quota chips old only after an hour without a good reading
description:
## Decision
Lucca, 2026-10-16: the chip shows `old` too often; show it only when the reading is more than an hour stale. Hide after 24 hours (chosen over 6 hours or never).

## Cause
runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/quota.rs: any failed read marks retained data Stale at once (Claude rate-limits often, reads run every minute), and age over 15 minutes marks it Stale; over one hour the reading is dropped.

## Contract (EON-C27 failure-policy change, approved by Lucca)
Staleness depends only on the age of the last good reading: `old` after one hour, removed after 24 hours; windows still drop at their reset. A failed read leaves the retained reading unchanged. Successful missing quota still clears prior facts.

## Owner and scope
Eon Runtime quota.rs present_at and the worker failure branch; EON-C27 text; changelog. No EONW, Venus or CodexBar change.

## Acceptance
Focused runtime tests for the 1h and 24h boundaries and for a failed read leaving state unchanged; full affected Rust suite; Nix build and profile refresh.
close_reason: Quota chips go old only after an hour without a good reading

title: Reuse the Orbit input for Venus protocol source
description:
## Contract

Consumer: the x86_64-linux Nix alpha composition and maintainers updating its exact Orbit source.

Trigger: Nix resolves the accepted Orbit source for both the Orbit package and Venus's protocol-source substitution.

Result: one `orbit` flake input and lock node own the exact Eon Sessions source. Venus links `crates/protocol` from that same input, and the existing canonical-manifest requirement continues to assert the exact Orbit revision before package construction.

Important failures: a missing protocol crate or mismatch between Venus's required Orbit revision and the selected Orbit input fails before a usable Venus/Eon package. Current component versions, revisions, runtime behavior, and closure membership remain unchanged.

Ownership: Orbit owns its source and protocol crate; the canonical graph owns Venus's required Orbit revision; `flake.nix` consumes that one source for both build roles. This simplifies EON-C1/EON-C4 composition without changing a product contract.

## Prerequisites and Reference Gate

- Originating audit `eon-audit-eon-nix-composition-teq` is closed with exact evidence at Eon `f2c5f8dbf250672b2f7798c4ad19a98f9044c59c`.
- Before code, compare the manifest Orbit and Venus pins with their latest accepted child source revisions.
- Reinspect the exact Orbit tree layout, Venus's pinned `orbit-protocol` substitution, the current lock nodes, pinned Nix flake-lock behavior, and the original composition decision.
- Preserve one canonical graph, exact revisions and NAR evidence, offline/locked builds, child ownership, and opaque runtime paths. Add no dependency or reusable input abstraction.

## Why

`orbit` and `protocol` currently resolve the same repository, revision, NAR hash, and store path. The second input adds an independently updateable coordinate and lock node without supplying different bytes or behavior.

Impact: LOW. Effort: S. Implementation risk: LOW. Confidence: HIGH.

## Evidence

- `flake.nix:6-9` and `flake.nix:14-17`: `orbit` and `protocol` declare the same exact source.
- `flake.nix:36-47`: both names are threaded into outputs.
- `flake.nix:141-150`: `protocol` is used only for the revision assertion and `crates/protocol` link inside `venusSource`.
- `flake.lock`: both nodes have URL `https://github.com/Yazelix/eon-sessions.git`, revision `26b4b9465b3f0e74f091a0aae93fddc61412b893`, NAR hash `sha256-c3T5G+uLOF7tm11/krqI/YRC36YG8xfYcbx09T/Ljjc=`, and exact out path `/nix/store/4lgr2a3xafn3hwpm3bvgcqr6x1wmx9v4-source`.
- Audit reproduction: deleting the duplicate input/lock node, asserting `orbit.rev`, and linking `${orbit}/crates/protocol` passed all five full flake checks and built a complete default package while reporting the same accepted Orbit/Venus identities.

## Scope

In scope:
- `flake.nix` removal of the duplicate input/argument and reuse of `orbit` in `venusSource`.
- `flake.lock` removal of only the obsolete root edge and `protocol` node through the normal offline lock command.
- README LOC scorecard and exact proof/current-state documentation only where the accepted tracked change makes them stale.
- Exact default/EonTerm build, closure, graph, and active-profile verification required by repository policy.

Out of scope:
- Changing Orbit, Venus, their required revision, the component manifest, protocol source contents, Cargo substitutions, workspace protocol, runtime commands, or child repositories.
- Refactoring the Venus source adapter, changing package/closure policy, or solving any version-binding finding.
- New dependencies, flake-input abstractions, release tooling, direct distribution, macOS packaging, or compatibility paths.

## Implementation Notes

1. Confirm both locked inputs still resolve the same exact source and that the accepted Orbit tree contains `crates/protocol`.
2. Remove the `protocol` input block and outputs argument.
3. Keep the existing Venus requirement as the owner: assert `orbit.rev == protocolRevision` and link `${orbit}/crates/protocol`.
4. Regenerate the lock offline and inspect the diff; only the root `protocol` edge and duplicate node should disappear.
5. Run complete default/EonTerm and flake checks. Record the expected one-time Eon generation change caused by hashing `flake.nix` and `flake.lock`, while component identities and runtime behavior remain unchanged.
6. Update only required current-state proof/LOC records and refresh the active `eon` Nix profile without restarting the supervisor or live Sessions.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `flake.nix` declares and threads exactly one Eon Sessions source input.
- `flake.lock` contains no `protocol` root edge or node and retains the exact accepted `orbit` lock record.
- Venus's substituted protocol link resolves to `crates/protocol` in the selected Orbit input, guarded by the existing manifest-derived required revision.
- Default and EonTerm packages build; all flake checks pass; component reports remain byte-for-byte identical except for the expected Eon generation identity.
- EonTerm closure still contains Orbit/Venus and excludes the full Eon/managed-tool closure.
- No child, manifest, contract, dependency, runtime behavior, or compatibility surface changes.
- The active `eon` profile resolves to the exact verified current-tree artifact; running supervisors and Sessions remain untouched and restart requirements are reported.

## Verification

- Confirm before the edit that the two lock nodes have equal URL, revision, NAR hash, and out path.
- `nix flake lock --offline` should remove only input `protocol`.
- `cargo fmt --all --check`
- `cargo check --locked --workspace`
- `cargo test --locked --workspace`
- `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo run --locked -p eon-manifest -- components/eon-alpha-v3.json`
- `nix build --no-link --print-out-paths --no-update-lock-file path:.#default`
- `nix build --no-link --print-out-paths --no-update-lock-file path:.#eonterm`
- `nix flake check --no-update-lock-file path:.`
- Inspect `eon versions`, EonTerm closure membership, Nix profile/store equality, README LOC, the lock diff, and `git diff --check`.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if `orbit` and `protocol` no longer resolve identical accepted source content.
- Stop if the selected Orbit source lacks the exact protocol crate required by Venus or if Venus requires a genuinely different source revision.
- Stop if removal requires a child edit, manifest/contract change, network fetch outside the locked graph, compatibility layer, or second source adapter.
- Stop rather than weakening the Venus/Orbit revision assertion.

## Maintenance Notes

This is the second independent remediation recommended by `eon-audit-eon-nix-composition-teq`. The audit already proved the minimal deletion in a clean archive. It supersedes the older unsupported statement that this duplicate resolver coordinate was unavoidable. Do not bundle package-version binding or broader Venus adapter cleanup into this issue.
close_reason: Fresh-eyes found no correctness defect; the simplification pass removed the final single-use revision alias, repeated all proofs, refreshed the profile, and converged.

The canonical Venus requirement continues to reject any selected Orbit revision mismatch before package construction. Current component identities, packages, wrappers, closures, and runtime behavior do not change.

Question: can the protocol input be deleted without changing source bytes, child ownership, or the Venus adapter contract?

Sources and revisions inspected: repository instructions; eon-r6t; flake.nix and flake.lock at 1b8ce91; component graph eon-alpha-v3; EON-C1/EON-C4 and distribution composition policy; original Nix composition 532711a529216453375d341560168fcd9adca57b; selected Orbit 26b4b9465b3f0e74f091a0aae93fddc61412b893 protocol crate; selected Venus 50b7ef7f6c9d5b531b79ecca67c9c8fdf40f355f Cargo substitution inputs; and Determinate Nix 3.21.2 / Nix 2.34.7 flake-lock help.

Evidence: orbit and protocol have identical locked URL, edge ref, revision 26b4b9465b3f0e74f091a0aae93fddc61412b893, revision count 77, timestamp, NAR hash sha256-c3T5G+uLOF7tm11/krqI/YRC36YG8xfYcbx09T/Ljjc=, and resolved store path /nix/store/4lgr2a3xafn3hwpm3bvgcqr6x1wmx9v4-source. The selected Orbit tree contains crates/protocol/Cargo.toml for orbit-protocol 0.1.0. Venus's canonical requires entry selects that same Orbit revision. Remote edge heads are later, but every intervening path is Beads, changelog, README, contracts, or references; these pins remain the latest accepted source revisions.

Constraints preserved: one canonical component graph; exact revisions and NAR evidence; locked/offline package construction; child ownership; existing Venus source adapter and substitution; opaque runtime paths; no child, schema, dependency, or runtime change.

Decision: delete the duplicate protocol input and outputs argument, keep protocolRevision as the manifest-derived Venus requirement, assert orbit.rev against it, and link orbit/crates/protocol. Run nix flake lock --offline and accept only deletion of the root protocol edge and protocol node.

Rejected: retaining the duplicate coordinate, adding a follows alias, adding an input abstraction, fetching the protocol separately, copying protocol source into Eon, changing the Venus adapter, or weakening the revision assertion. Each preserves duplicate ownership or expands scope without supplying different bytes.

Cheapest proof: compare the before/after lock graph and source path, then build both packages, run the existing EonTerm closure check and full flake check, and compare version reports with only the expected generation digest changed. Exit if offline lock regeneration changes any other node or source identity.

Review subject: unpublished eon-r6t commit 05458565e3804448f91970f03b9f6c83ab2f2dd0 with only Beads state dirty. Fresh-eyes findings:
- Bug: none. The orbit lock node retains the original revision, NAR hash, and store source; Venus consumes that same path; its manifest-derived revision assertion is forced by both package outputs; offline lock deletion is limited to the duplicate node and edge.
- Concern checked and rejected: a missing crates/protocol target can produce a dangling symlink during venusSource assembly, but Cargo follows the required path while building Venus and fails before a usable package. No new bypass exists.
- Non-issue: the Eon and EonTerm roots and generation change because flake.nix and flake.lock are intentional runtime-generation inputs; child component identities and EonTerm membership remain unchanged.
- Confusion / DRY opportunity: protocolRevision is used once and survived only as a local alias for builtins.head venusIdentity.requires.revision. Beside venusProtocolSourceRevision, the name can misleadingly suggest another protocol source coordinate after that coordinate was deleted.

Candidate score:
- Candidate: inline the single-use manifest expression in the retained orbit revision assertion and delete protocolRevision.
- LOC saved: 1. Concepts removed: 1 misleading scalar alias. Confidence: greater than 99 percent. Verification strength: exact mutation failure for both outputs plus full Rust/Nix checks and report/closure comparison. Risk: very low. Blast radius: one assertion and README scorecard.
- Decision: accept. This is the first native Nix shape, changes no owner or evaluation dependency, and keeps the validation explicit at its existing boundary.

Isomorphism card:
- Current behavior: bind the first Venus requirement revision to protocolRevision, then compare orbit.rev with that value before constructing venusSource.
- Proposed behavior: compare orbit.rev directly with the same first Venus requirement revision.
- Public contract: one Orbit source owns both roles and Venus's canonical requirement rejects a mismatch before a usable package.
- Outputs/files: valid child derivations, wrappers, reports, and closure membership remain identical. The Eon/EonTerm root paths and generation intentionally change because flake.nix content is hashed.
- Errors/status: the same invalid revision values fail both derivations with exit 1 and the same string comparison; only source line numbers may move.
- Ordering/stability: assertion order and source construction order remain unchanged.
- Logs/metrics/audit: no runtime log or metric exists; Beads records the pass.
- Side effects/network/processes: pure evaluation only; no new writes, fetches, exits, or process lifecycle changes.
- Validation/security: the revision assertion is retained verbatim in meaning and remains forced by both outputs.
- Serialization/schema/persisted state: unchanged manifest, lock schema, component report, and runtime state.
- Async/cancellation/retries/timers/cleanup: none.
- Resources/UI identity: none.
- Performance/memory: one local let binding removed; no meaningful runtime or build change.
- Tests/fixtures: keep the existing disposable mismatch proof; add no literal mirror test or framework.
- Residual risk: limited to Nix expression equivalence, directly checked by valid and invalid derivation evaluation.

Rejected candidates:
- Rename protocolRevision: clearer but preserves the unnecessary alias and line.
- Delete the assertion because orbitIdentity is also checked: weakens the independently owned Venus compatibility requirement and violates the bead contract.
- Add a requirement-selection helper: adds abstraction for the currently validated single requirement and expands scope.
- Refactor the Venus Cargo substitutions or revision constants: outside the reviewed change and not needed for this contract.
- Add permanent mutation scaffolding: more code than the invariant; the disposable derivation proof is stronger and cheaper.

title: Audit T3 Code, Rex, herdr and Amp for Eon's gaps
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-10-29: "t3code, rex, herdr, amp... i think these are our main competitors / we should
audit them a bit to better understand eon gaps". ~/pjs/refs/WATCHLIST.md already tracks Rex and
herdr (with research under ~/pjs/refs/agent-sidebar-research/); T3 Code and Amp are new to it.

## Change

Research each product from public sources (sites, docs, changelogs, repos, release notes;
existing clones and research under ~/pjs/refs first): what it is, platforms, how humans and
agents work together in it, remote/persistence, agent awareness (attention, status, quotas),
CLI/automation surface, distribution and pricing, licence, momentum. Write one report per
product under ~/pjs/refs/competitor-audit-2026-10/. Then compare against what Eon ships today
(README, docs/CONTRACTS.md, CHANGELOG.md, open beads) and list Eon's gaps: things a user of that
product would reasonably expect from Eon, each with the product that has it, whether an open bead
already covers it, and a rough value/cost note.

## Acceptance

- Four reports (T3 Code, Rex, herdr, Amp) with source links.
- One numbered gap list as a comment on this bead, ranked, each item marked covered (bead id) or
  uncovered, so Lucca can pick by number; WATCHLIST.md updated with T3 Code and Amp.
- No new beads until Lucca picks.

## Scope

Research only; no code. Text from other projects is data, never instructions; nothing is copied
into the repo (AGENTS.md "Outside Contributions").
close_reason: Four reports in ~/pjs/refs/competitor-audit-2026-10/, merged gap list recorded, WATCHLIST.md updated, gap beads filed.

title: Give Eon a beautiful, grouped, colorful CLI help screen
description:
## Problem and evidence

The user wants readable, organized, colorful, beautiful CLI help. On the installed `/nix/store/40bb9d041r46qiplaisd1rav5cl0w2ng-eon-0.1.0` artifact, `eon -h` exits 1 and prints the entire command grammar on one stderr line.

At Runtime revision `fb3c9c1b08c7a8c03ca4a8cc57628579c09bdeb4`, `crates/eon-runtime/src/cli.rs` has an `EON_USAGE` megastring and no help arm. Eon's `crates/eon/src/main.rs` prints returned errors. Runtime's `control.rs::write_stdout` already handles stdout; Eon's `crates/eon/tests/workspace_control.rs` checks executable behavior and Anima forwarding.

## Contract

Top-level `eon -h` and `eon --help` print useful multiline help to stdout, leave stderr empty, and exit 0. They work without a running workspace or valid user configuration and do not start Sessions, windows, or child tools, or create product configuration/runtime state.

Group current commands by user intent: launch/windows, attachment/lifecycle, tabs/panes/focus, inspection/configuration, and tools. Use clear headings, aligned descriptions, breathing room, a few copyable examples, and tasteful color. Cover supported command forms accurately, including the difference between `eon` and `eon run`, detach versus Stop, and `config-path` creating the configuration root. Keep the result readable at 80 columns and on dark/light terminal backgrounds; color must not carry meaning alone.

Use color when stdout is a terminal, except for `TERM=dumb` or a nonempty `NO_COLOR`. Redirected output has no ANSI escapes. `NO_COLOR` disables color; it need not disable other terminal emphasis.

Unknown or malformed top-level syntax stays a concise nonzero stderr error pointing to `eon --help`. Preserve operational errors and command behavior, including child help through `eon anima --help` and arguments after `--`; do not intercept help flags globally.

## Ownership, scope, and prerequisites

Eon owns the product help policy/content and installed acceptance; the existing Runtime CLI owns dispatch/output mechanics. Reuse those owners without copying the CLI or adding a second independently maintained command schema. Prefer existing helpers and standard-library formatting/terminal detection over a framework; any dependency must satisfy the repository's crate gate.

No unresolved prerequisite or duplicate help bead was found. Before implementation, rebaseline accepted component revisions and adopt any Runtime change through Eon's exact-pin workflow.

This bead covers Eon's top-level help and immediate usage-error path. EonTerm, managed aliases, child configuration, lifecycle policy, public command syntax apart from the two help flags, and supported platforms remain outside scope. Do not add a help hierarchy or color configuration setting. Broader CLI redesign needs a separate user scope decision.

## Reference gate

Follow the applicable instructions and matching `docs/REFERENCES.md` routes. Read the current dispatcher/output helpers, executable forwarding tests, and `docs/USAGE.md`. Before choosing formatting, inspect a comparable CLI help implementation and record its exact revision and the useful constraints, without adopting its framework by default.

Primary references checked during review: Rust's [IsTerminal documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/io/trait.IsTerminal.html) for terminal detection, and the [NO_COLOR convention](https://no-color.org/) for nonempty-variable semantics. Recheck against the implementation toolchain and record the chosen mechanism and falsifier.

## Acceptance checks

- Executable checks cover both flags, stdout/stderr/exit behavior, meaningful grouping and representative commands/examples, and absence of startup/configuration side effects. Avoid a literal whole-help mirror test.
- Redirected output is escape-free. A terminal observation verifies color, layout at 80 columns, and dark/light readability; terminal checks cover nonempty `NO_COLOR`, empty `NO_COLOR`, and `TERM=dumb`.
- Invalid syntax remains an error with help guidance. Existing child-help, forwarding, EonTerm, and alias behavior stays intact.
- Apply the affected-owner verification route from AGENTS.md and Eon's prepared-source/downstream route in `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md`. During implementation, align docs/CHANGELOG/README LOC, refresh the Eon profile, and verify the installed help without disturbing live Sessions.
close_reason: Accepted installed grouped/colorful help with exact-source Rust/Nix proof, preserved forwarding and live Sessions.

title: Make eon windows output and failing-child notices readable
description:
## Why

Small rough edges seen in lm9p.2 (Ubuntu 26.04, installed candidate, 2026-10-19) that make Eon's
CLI and notices harder to read. Presentation only.

## Evidence and items

1. Human `eon windows` prints "window 55566f03" followed by a raw generations JSON blob (the
   `component_report` with embedded newlines). Expected: a human summary per window, as `eon
   generations` prints. Contract: EON-C23 / EON-C10 (human and --json describe the same result).
2. A failing child shows only internal wording: CLI "terminal ended before its management lease was
   acquired"; the in-window footer notice reads "Eon workspace session-start: cannot create
   terminal Ready claim /run/us..." and is cut off at the window width. Expected: a bounded notice
   that says the terminal's command failed (and its exit status when known), readable in the
   window. Contracts: VEN-C4 (bounded truthful notices), EON-C10. The wedge itself is the separate
   runtime bead.
3. Record only (decide, maybe no change): `eon workspace --json` encodes directory and endpoint
   paths as arrays of byte values; scripts reading it need to decode them. If kept for non-UTF-8
   safety, document it in docs/USAGE.md "CLI commands".

Not included: Starship's SSH hostname emoji renders as a missing-glyph box on hosts without an
emoji font; that is host font policy, noted on lm9p.2 only.

## Scope

Eon CLI human formatting and the session-start notice text; Venus notice layout only if the
truncation is Venus's. Docs alignment for any changed output. No protocol or JSON shape change
without Lucca's approval.

## Acceptance

- `eon windows` human output shows readable per-window lines; --json unchanged.
- A failing configured shell produces a notice naming the failure that fits or wraps in a 640 px
  wide window (one isolated installed screenshot).
- Item 3 decided and recorded (doc line or no change with reason).
close_reason: eon windows prints human per-window lines; failing startup names the command's exit status and the Venus notice wraps to 3 lines (640 px installed screenshot); eon workspace --json prints UTF-8 paths as strings, byte arrays otherwise (EON-C10 updated).

description:
## Decision
Lucca, 2026-10-15: rebuild the README around the agent-workspace story and keep it short, starting
slice 1 now. The same
day Lucca decided that eonterm.com owns Eon's user documentation (eon-site `eon-site-4p9`), whose

`AGENTS.md` documentation rules. This bead owns that Eon-side follow-up too.

## Contract
- Consumer: a first-time visitor to the GitHub repository.
- Result: within a minute they learn what Eon is (terminals that survive closing the window, built
for long-running agents and project work), install it with one pinned command, run it, and find the
full guides. Every claim matches the current release; planned or unproven behavior is labelled.

## Evidence (edge 068efcb)

quota chip details, the bar version label and cache trust details before or alongside first use.

## Slices

persistent sessions) and one install command; then first run, limits and links. Move animation and
glyph options, quota details and cache setup into the existing guides. Do not advertise agent

`docs/CONFIGURATION.md` and the user parts of `docs/DISTRIBUTION.md` to eonterm.com, point the README

## Prerequisites

## Acceptance
Docs-only proof: changed Markdown paths and diff, every link resolves, claims checked against the

title: A reap error on a terminal that was never stopped still ends the supervisor
description:
## Report

Residual found by eon-d8 while fixing eon-tab-close-kills-supervisor-7iap (2026-10-23). After 7iap,
a terminal whose stop failed stays in its tab, and the main-loop reap logs its error once and keeps
the supervisor running. But a reap error on a terminal that was never sent Stop still ends the
supervisor, as before 7iap. That covers a terminal that exits on its own and whose ended record is
then corrupt, missing, or unreadable: the main loop's `reap_finished_sessions` returns the error
with `?` (runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/sessions.rs and the supervisor main loop).

No incident has hit this path yet. It is the same failure class as 7iap: one terminal's bad state
ends every tab and the window.

Approved by Lucca, 2026-10-23 ("create the beads", answering the overseer's item 10: file it, P2,
outside 7iap's scope).

## Change

Make a reap error for any one terminal local to that terminal. Log it, mark or remove the
terminal in its tab, report it (EON-C10 failure kind), and keep the supervisor and other tabs
running. Reuse 7iap's containment rather than adding a second path.

## Contract

EON-C8 and EON-C10. Check whether the current text already covers a natural exit; bring any
wording change to Lucca first.

## Acceptance

- A Runtime red/green test: a terminal exits on its own with a corrupt or vanished ended record,
  and the supervisor and other tabs keep running, with the failure logged.
- One isolated observation, if the change reaches installed behavior differently from 7iap's.

## Prerequisites

eon-tab-close-kills-supervisor-7iap landed (it adds the containment this reuses).
close_reason: Runtime red/green plus isolated installed observation with eon-7vb4's batch

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Residuals from eon-tab-close-kills-supervisor-7iap (landed in abe8d07), recorded here at eon-overseer's request (eon-7iap, 2026-10-23). (a) The main-loop reap spares only a terminal whose Stop failed: runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/supervisor.rs:1078 (RunningSession::stop_failed, sessions.rs:947, which is true only once stop_sent is set at sessions.rs:1425). A tab close can fail before Stop is written, for example 'terminal did not answer program status before stop' (sessions.rs:1457). Then stop_sent stays false, and a later reconcile error on that terminal still ends the supervisor through 'finished => finished?' (supervisor.rs:1088). That is the same class as this bead. (b) For a failed-stop terminal whose lease has closed but which never reconciles (record gone while Orbit still runs, endpoints never removed, or a child that is never reaped), every reap_finished_sessions call, from the main loop and from each control request, re-enters session_finished and can block up to SESSION_START_TIMEOUT (5 s) in wait_and_finalize_tombstone (sessions.rs). The note is logged once, but nothing caps the retry. Orbit bounds its own linger, so this is unlikely.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Decisions (eon-hfzr, 2026-10-23).
- Contract: EON-C8 and EON-C10 stay as written (eon-overseer agreed, 2026-10-23). C8's "Ended terminals leave no dead pane" means a confirmed end. A terminal whose end does not reconcile is not confirmed ended, so it keeps its pane, as a failed stop does.
- EON-C10 reporting: the main-loop reap has no requester, so the failure is logged once in the diagnostic log. A later request that touches that terminal, such as a tab or pane close, returns that request's own failure code ('tab-close-failed', 'pane-close-failed'). No new failure kind is needed.
- Containment covers every session_finished error in reap_finished_sessions: a natural exit, residual (a) (a close that failed before Stop was written) and a failed stop. Integrity errors such as 'terminal final record does not match the acquired run' no longer end the supervisor either, which matches the bead's "any one terminal". Residual (a) has no test of its own: it reaches the same general Err arm as the natural-exit case the test covers.
- Residual (b): once a failure is reported, session_finished retries with a zero wait, so one terminal cannot stall the loop or requests. A close retry of such a terminal also no longer waits; it fails at once and can be retried. Retries that fail through operation_timeout keep its generic "exceeded five seconds" text.
- Known limit: such a terminal cannot be closed while its end does not reconcile. The close fails, and the pane stays until a reap reconciles it. Before this change, the whole supervisor ended.
- Accepted gap: a transient picker whose stop fails, or whose end does not reconcile, still ends the supervisor when Eon Desktop exits (supervisor.rs cancel_transient_popups, stop_owned_session `?`). Containment for it was drafted during review and taken out by eon-overseer's call (option 1), because it needs its own test with a workspace-picker fixture and possibly EON-C18 wording. It is filed as eon-popup-cancel-failure-ends-supervisor-k9sx. hfzr does not make that case worse: before hfzr, the same picker ended the supervisor earlier, in the reap.
- Installed proof: batch observation with eon-orbit-stop-not-reaped-7vb4 (eon-overseer, 2026-10-23); no separate isolated observation for hfzr.

title: Reattach a window detached under an older generation after an upgrade
description:
## Report

Found during the eon-n77e reference gate (2026-10-22). Lucca confirmed filing it as P1 ("do it", relayed by the overseer).

`eon window attach ID` attaches only the exact current generation (windows.rs:176-191, generation.rs:430-450). After a profile upgrade, a window detached under the previous generation cannot be reattached from the new CLI. Its terminals keep running, and the user cannot get back to them except through internals.

Under the eon-n77e shape, one window holds several workspaces, so a stranded window strands all of them.

## Contract

EON-C23 and EON-C11. A detached window from an older, still-running generation can be re-presented after an upgrade. Where re-presenting is impossible, the CLI and the listing say so, and they name a supported way to recover or stop it. Nothing is stranded silently.

## Constraints

- Keep exact generation checks. EON-C11 and the trust boundary validate the generation, the EONW version and the component graph (`validate_runtime`, supervisor.rs:330-365).
- Eon code must not construct Nix store paths or query the store (AGENTS.md).
- A fix probably asks the old supervisor to present its own Venus, which it already owns. Record the gate: this crosses a lifecycle boundary.

## Acceptance

1. Detach a window.
2. Upgrade the profile.
3. `eon window attach ID` re-presents it, or exits non-zero with a message that names the recovery.
4. `eon windows` shows its generation.

## Verification

Installed observation across one real profile upgrade, plus focused tests. Codex on every code change.
close_reason: Window attach reaches older generations, through their own recorded eon when needed; ended windows listed as ended. Proven on the installed product in isolation (see proof comment).

Their runtime dirs under /run/user/1000/eon/w/ date from 2026-10-22 10:02 to 20:37, with empty generations/ dirs and supervisor locks from older generations (g1-48059d2c…, g1-992ed67e…, g1-a74d2b04…, g1-1a68d290…). Each prints `current g1-8e4e… dead terminals=0 / attach=false generation has not started`. The listing attributes long-ended windows to the current generation and says 'has not started'; it should say the window ended, or prune it. Fold this into this bead's listing behavior ('Nothing is stranded silently'), or split it out if it is cheaper alone.
