comments.text:
Reference gate (eon-90, 2026-10-23, edge 6ee477a). Behavior: after an upgrade, `eon window attach ID` re-presents a window started by an older build, or names how to recover it; the listing does not show ended windows as current. Owners: Eon Runtime owns generation selection, discovery and Present (EON-C11) and window identity (EON-C23). The old supervisor owns its Venus and terminals.

Read: runtime windows.rs window_action/list_windows, generation.rs attach_generation/inspect_generation, supervisor.rs probe_supervisor/validate_runtime/present_at, control.rs protocol_endpoint_failure, EON-C11, EON-C23, EON-C28 Upgrades/Boundary. Live: window afacc679 runs g1-8e4e (EONW 18). The profile eon (EONW 19) attach fails with "generation g1-f501… has not started", exit 1. The v18 CLI sees the generation as attach=true, but `window attach` targets only the CLI's own generation. Supervisor exe is .eon-wrapped. Its environment comes from the bin/eon wrapper, so a recorded `eon` must be the wrapper (session bin `eon`, d56c373), never /proc exe.

Comparables:
- tmux 3.8 7f2a35ad: PROTOCOL_VERSION 8 per message (tmux-protocol.h:23, proc.c:134-177). On mismatch the client prints "protocol version mismatch (client N, server M)" and exits 1 (client.c:659-667). ls, attach and kill-server all fail. Nothing records or execs the old binary. Recovery is the old binary or killing the PID by hand (CHANGES:2608).
- zellij v0.45.1 efd8fd5a: the socket dir is versioned by contract (consts.rs:26,90-91). Same-contract sessions interoperate across versions (CHANGELOG 0.44 #4439). ls only probes the current contract dir and silently omits the rest (sessions.rs:19-44). No mismatch message.
- wezterm e2a98e1b: the server reports executable_path in its codec version response (codec/src/lib.rs:617-622, sessionhandler.rs:864-870). On a codec mismatch the client says to install the same version on both ends (wezterm-client client.rs:64-77). It does not re-exec the old binary.

Kept constraints: exact generation/EONW/graph checks; no store-path construction or store query; no PID kill fallback.
Rejected: silent omission like zellij (violates "nothing stranded silently"); a bare mismatch error like tmux (names no recovery); deriving bin/eon from /proc exe (constructs a store-layout path).
Decision: pending Lucca on choices 1-5 (relayed via overseer). Candidate: record the build's own `eon` like wezterm's executable_path, but as a runtime-dir record, not an EONW field, so older-EONW CLIs can read it, and optionally delegate attach to it. Check: focused tests plus one installed observation across a real profile upgrade.

comments.text:
Accepted gaps (eon-90, 2026-10-23), from slice 2 review round 1:
- Trust: any process running as the same user can replace a generation's `eon` record and redirect delegated attach. The record lives in the user's 0700 runtime directory, and the check requires a symlink owned by that user with an absolute target. A same-UID process can already change the user's shell startup files or the profile, so the record grants no new privilege. Ownership is not build provenance.
- Rollback: an Eon build from before this change removes a dead generation's directory with a plain remove_dir. That fails on a directory holding the `eon` record, so after a rollback the older `eon` keeps listing a crashed newer generation as dead. The newer build and the generation's own supervisor do remove it. This only matters across versions.
- Loop guard: a delegated attach carries EON_ATTACH_DELEGATED=<generation>, and it never delegates that generation again. Otherwise an unwrapped dev build started inside an Eon terminal would inherit the outer build's EON_SESSION_BIN and record the outer build's `eon`.

title: Restore workspaces after a machine restart
description:
## Decision
Lucca, 2026-10-15: plan restoring a workspace after a machine restart, honestly labelled as a
restore with fresh processes, not terminal survival. Design and contract are not chosen yet.

## Contract (provisional)
After a machine restart, a full-Eon user can restore their last workspace: tabs with their launch
directories, pane order and the tab popups, started as new terminals. Agent popups restart through
the client's own resume command. The product never presents this as process, scrollback or terminal
state survival.

## Open design decisions
Automatic or opt-in restore; what is saved (layout and directories only, never arbitrary pane
commands); where and when it is written and how stale or partial state fails; privacy of saved
paths; how it interacts with generations and independent windows.

## Evidence (edge 5ae4e0f)
- Restarting the machine ends live terminals (README "Status and limits"; EON-C15 at
`docs/CONTRACTS.md:867` and `:894` claims no machine-restart recovery).
- `docs/REFERENCES.md:150-156` (TUIOS route) keeps the distinction between live detach, crash,
reboot and metadata reconstruction with fresh processes, and rejects presenting a restored layout as
survival. It does not reject a labelled restore.
- Agent defaults already resume: `codex resume` and `claude --resume`
(`eon/crates/eon/src/product.rs:101-105`).

## Owners
Eon Runtime owns saved workspace state and restore (persist only required recovery state,
AP-FAILURE-001); Eon owns the product contract and defaults; Orbit and Venus are unchanged.

## Prerequisites and reference gate
Consequential (new contract, persisted state, lifecycle). Read the affected contracts and
`docs/REFERENCES.md` routes, and inspect at exact revisions tmux-resurrect/continuum and Zellij
session resurrection. Record kept constraints, rejections, the design and its cheapest falsifier.
Stop for Lucca's design and contract approval before code.

## Acceptance
Design approved; then an isolated installed check restores a multi-tab workspace after its
terminals end as they would at reboot, with honest labelling and stale-state failures. Full affected
Rust and Nix surfaces.

## Stop boundary
No process checkpointing, scrollback persistence or remote state.

comments.text: Lucca, 2026-10-20: in 1.0 scope (eon-igae), accepted as recommended. Design decisions above remain open; settle them with Lucca before code.

title: Refresh Eon to accepted ORBS v3-compatible terminal children
description:
## Contract routing

This Eon composition refresh hardens EON-C1, EON-C2, and EON-C4 by consuming the newest mutually compatible accepted ORBS v3 child sources. It preserves EON-C3 and EON-C8 through EON-C12, adds no Eon runtime behavior or child contract activation, and keeps ORBF v1, ORBS v3, EONW v1, component IDs, and compatibility policy unchanged.

Consumer: new x86_64 Linux Eon and EonTerm launches from the canonical Nix alpha package.

Trigger: Eon validates, builds, installs, or reports the canonical component graph.

Result: the graph, Nix inputs, package, and `eon versions` agree on Orbit source `6de95296d252c119d4fdba2d9b03cec1a09355ae` and Venus source `74ab5a0b661210f0afec94086f5358fe50b01f05`. Orbit uses ORB-C1/ORB-C2 proof `9bc87191dd90fd3d7db939127f1ebedfccd2b48d` and ORB-C3 through ORB-C11 proof `6de95296d252c119d4fdba2d9b03cec1a09355ae`. Venus uses VEN-C1 proof `74ab5a0b661210f0afec94086f5358fe50b01f05`, retains VEN-C2 proof `846daf8fb7846b0e8dc227e533aa8d51a691f76f`, and retains every unrelated proof. Canonical ORBF v1 proof `9d6d2bb37f20ab4ad9e186c7bc715eabef43e757`, ORBS v3 proof `3ee7c80005f3d2bbe81e539799327803716f6174`, and EONW v1 remain exact.

Important failures: an unaccepted or incompatible child revision, inconsistent graph/input/lock/report, failed child build, mismatched Venus requirement, or interrupted profile refresh leaves the rollout incomplete and existing live generations untouched.

## Freshness decision

Orbit current edge has advanced to accepted source `2e41997cbec202afc5222f084ffb98973a01b0f0` and ORBS v4. Venus `74ab5a0b661210f0afec94086f5358fe50b01f05` consumes canonical ORBS v3 at `3ee7c80005f3d2bbe81e539799327803716f6174`; therefore Orbit v4 is not mutually compatible and cannot enter this refresh without a separately accepted Venus adoption. Orbit `6de95296d252c119d4fdba2d9b03cec1a09355ae` is the newest accepted ORBS v3 runtime and contains the stale-readiness, transient PTY EIO, serialized stale-socket claim, and truthful-capability fixes. This issue selects that exact compatible frontier rather than adding an adapter, dual protocol, or speculative consumer API.

Venus source `74ab5a0b661210f0afec94086f5358fe50b01f05` is published and accepted. With no opacity flag it is equivalent to `1.0`, so this pin preserves Eon presentation while making the exact VEN-C11 child available for the separate EON-C13 issue. VEN-C11 is not activated or consumed by this refresh.

## Reference gate

Required evidence: current Eon instructions, graph, flake and lock owner, exact version report, current-state documentation, prior exact-pin rollout, Orbit contracts at the accepted ORBS v3 state, Venus VEN-C1/VEN-C2/VEN-C11/VEN-C14 contracts, exact locked Orbit and EONW dependencies, and current installed profile and process identities.

Adopted mechanism: update the single canonical graph first, then matching exact Nix inputs, affected lock nodes, exact report expectation, and current proof metadata. Add no dependency, schema, adapter, compatibility window, or runtime code.

Rejected scope: Orbit ORBS v4, Venus consumer work, Eon opacity configuration, Eonova rollout, child edits, branch pins, a second graph, live restart, or unrelated component changes.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The canonical graph, flake inputs, affected lock nodes, package, and `eon versions` select Orbit `6de9529` and Venus `74ab5a0` exactly.
2. Orbit contract proofs advance only as named above; Venus VEN-C1 advances to `74ab5a0`, VEN-C2 remains `846daf8`, and all unrelated proofs and interface versions remain exact.
3. Venus requires selected Orbit source `6de9529` with unchanged ORBF v1 and ORBS v3 proofs; no adapter or second decoder exists.
4. The selected sources build together through the canonical Nix alpha package; manifest/report, locked Rust, Nix check/build, and diff checks pass.
5. No Eon runtime code, dependency, component ID, schema, interface version, or unrelated pin changes.
6. README, CONTRACTS, CHANGELOG, and LOC describe the accepted package without claiming EON-C13 or ORBS v4.
7. The active Eon profile resolves to the exact published proof artifact while recorded live supervisors and Sessions retain PID/start identities.

title: Remote Eon workspaces over SSH
description:
## Decision
Lucca, 2026-10-15: SSH is a good match for Eon. Remote workspaces reach the server through the
user's existing OpenSSH (config, aliases, keys, jump hosts). Eon opens no network listener and owns
no authentication, encryption or login; it does not replace SSH (unlike Superlogical's Rex, which
claims to). This decision authorizes planning only; each child below still needs its own contract
approval. It is the explicit user direction `orbit/AGENTS.md` requires before any remote use of
Orbit, limited to SSH-carried Unix sockets with Orbit unchanged.

## Outcome
A user keeps Eon's window on their local Wayland desktop while terminals, editor, Git and agents run
on a headless server. Closing the window or losing the connection leaves the remote work running;
reconnecting returns to it; disconnecting stays distinct from stopping.

## Source
GitHub issue Yazelix/eon#1 (bioinformatist, 2026-10-15) describes the full experience: remote
Project browsing, tabs and panes inheriting the remote target, remote Git and Agent popups,
Machine -> named workspace -> tabs -> panes, and disconnect versus stop. Recovery after a server
reboot is explicitly separate.

## Plan (children)
1. `waypipe` spike: run the whole Eon remotely and forward only its window with Waypipe over SSH;
zero Rust. Decide whether a documented recipe suffices.
2. Remote work survives the SSH session: supervisor and terminals outlive SSH logout and the login
session's runtime directory. Needed by every path.
3. Only if the spike falls short: local Venus with a remote supervisor and Orbit over SSH-forwarded
Unix sockets, measured first.
The issue's machine switcher and named workspaces are decided after the spike, inside child 3 or a
later child.

## Related
`orb-permanent-ssh-terminal-access-hd6` (reach a session from any SSH terminal, such as a phone);
`eon-az9` (isolated execution targets); `eon-pxn` (execution-target references);
`eon-next-expansion-0wfb` (remote is a third expansion competing for the same attention).

## Stop boundary
No own transport, listener, login or crypto; no Mosh/QUIC path unless measured latency demands it
and Lucca chooses it; no multi-client attachment; no macOS client in this epic.

title: Spike: run Eon remotely with waypipe over SSH
description:
## Contract
- Consumer: a user with a local x86_64 Linux Wayland desktop and a headless Linux server reachable
by OpenSSH.
- Trigger: `waypipe ssh HOST eon` (and `waypipe ssh HOST eon attach` to return).
- Result: Eon runs entirely on the server and its native window appears locally, with no desktop
environment on the server. The Project picker, tabs, panes, Git and Agent popups all act on the
server automatically. The spike decides whether this is enough to document as the supported first
remote path, or what is missing.

## Why this first
Waypipe (in the pinned nixpkgs, 0.11.0) forwards Wayland applications over SSH: `waypipe server`
gives remote applications their own compositor socket, buffers travel lz4/zstd-compressed or as
h264/vp9/av1 video for DMABUF, and the whole thing rides the user's OpenSSH (6.7+ Unix socket
forwarding). Eon is already Wayland-only, and Venus can render with Mesa lavapipe on a server
without a GPU. If it is good enough, remote Eon costs documentation, not thousands of lines.

## Measure and record
Typing latency and full-screen update bandwidth on a LAN and on a slower link (`waypipe bench`,
compression and video options); server CPU for lavapipe; clipboard and primary selection;
IME; accessibility (AT-SPI does not cross Waypipe, a likely gap); blur protocol pass-through;
cursor trail smoothness; window close and connection loss behavior (does the remote supervisor and
its terminals survive? see the survival bead); reattach.

Known Waypipe caveats to weigh: no reconnection (a dropped link closes the window; reattach starts a
new window); the man page disclaims strong security guarantees against untrusted servers and its
packet timing is observable; buffers may hold screen contents (encrypted swap advised).

## Acceptance
A recorded comparison with exact revisions, hosts, link conditions and numbers, plus a go/no-go
recommendation for Lucca: document `waypipe ssh` as the remote path (with any small Nix packaging),
or proceed to the local-Venus design bead with the specific failures that justify it. No contract
claims remote support until Lucca approves one.

## Stop boundary
No Rust changes. Read-only and disposable test hosts; never disturb Lucca's live sessions.
close_reason: Superseded by eon-remote-workspaces-52i4 (Lucca 2026-10-27, relayed by eon-overseer, 'ssh: okay'): local Venus with a remote supervisor over SSH-forwarded sockets is decided; Waypipe rejected.

title: Keep remote Eon work alive after the SSH session ends
description:
## Contract (provisional; changes EON-C15's boundary, needs Lucca's approval)
- Consumer: a user who starts Eon on a server over SSH, by any path.
- Trigger: the SSH session ends: window closed, network lost, or logout.
- Result: the Eon supervisor and its Orbit terminals keep running and stay reachable by a later
`eon attach` or `eon generations` from a new SSH session. `eon stop` still ends them.

## Evidence (edge 7d97dee)
- EON-C15 excludes "logout/reboot survival" (`docs/CONTRACTS.md:867`, `:894`).
- Only independent windows detach with `setsid` (`runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/windows.rs:133`);
the default supervisor's session and SIGHUP behavior under an SSH session end is unverified.
- Sockets live under `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` (`/run/user/<uid>`), which systemd-logind removes when the
user's last session ends unless lingering is enabled; `KillUserProcesses=yes` would also kill the
work. Eon must stay independent of any init system (root `AGENTS.md`, Platform Discipline), so the
design cannot require systemd, but must behave correctly with it.

## Open decisions
Whether the supervisor detaches from the login session itself, where sockets live when the login
runtime directory disappears (EON_RUNTIME_DIR already exists as an override), and what Eon reports
when logind policy would kill or clean up its work.

## Acceptance
Contract approved and indexed first. Then an isolated two-host (or VM) check: start Eon over SSH,
end the SSH session in each way, reconnect, attach, and stop; with and without lingering. Full
affected Rust surfaces via `eon-test`.

## Stop boundary
No reboot recovery (`eon-reboot-restore-im8y`), no systemd unit or service-manager requirement.

title: Design local Venus with a remote supervisor over SSH-forwarded sockets
description:
## Activation
Only if the `waypipe` spike shows that forwarding the whole window is not good enough, and Lucca
chooses this path. Design first.

## Contract (provisional)
Venus runs on the local desktop and renders locally; the Eon supervisor and Orbit run on the server;
the workspace (EONW) and terminal (ORBS) Unix sockets are carried over the user's OpenSSH
connection. The window shows which machine it is attached to and distinguishes disconnected from
stopped; reconnecting reattaches without restarting remote terminals.

## Lowest-code mechanism to evaluate first
OpenSSH stream-local forwarding (`ssh -L /local.sock:/remote.sock`, `StreamLocalBindUnlink`) with a
ControlMaster connection, adding forwards for terminal sockets as the workspace announces them
(`ssh -O forward`). Venus already connects to socket paths (`venus/src/transport.rs`), so most of
the work is path mapping, a headless supervisor start, and reconnect. Compare with a single stdio
multiplexer over `ssh HOST eon proxy` (Zed and VS Code Remote style) only if forwarding fails.

## Open design decisions
- Bandwidth: Orbit sends complete frames per revision; measure over a slow link first. If needed,
Orbit's planned revisioned row patches (`orbit/docs/PROTOCOL.md:80-85`) become a prerequisite
(an `orbit-protocol` change needing Lucca's approval; consumers Venus, Eon Runtime, Eon,
bend-orbit).
- Version skew: presentation requires the exact same build on both ends; decide how the remote build
is provisioned (for example `nix copy`) and how mismatch is reported.
- Headless supervisor: today the supervisor spawns Venus itself.
- The issue's Machine -> named workspace -> tabs model, machine switcher, and workspace naming
(windows have only random IDs today).
- Where quota collection runs (local or remote credentials).

## Prerequisites and reference gate
Blocked by the `waypipe` spike and the survival bead. Consequential (contracts, lifecycle, possibly
protocol). Inspect at exact revisions: Zed remote development, VS Code Remote-SSH, WezTerm SSH and
TLS domains, and Mosh's state synchronization. Stop for Lucca's design and contract approval.

## Acceptance
Design approved; then installed two-host dogfood: start, work, drop the link, reconnect, stop; with
recorded latency and bandwidth.

## Stop boundary
No own transport, listener or authentication; no Mosh/QUIC path without measured need and Lucca's
choice; no multi-client attachment.

title: Remote workspaces: local Venus, remote Runtime and Orbit over OpenSSH
description:
## Why

GitHub issue #1 (Yu, bioinformatist, a Yazelix member) asks for Eon's window on a PC while terminals, Git, editors and agents run on a headless server, with work surviving window close and connection loss. PR #2 is Yu's working prototype (9.2k lines, two-machine proof, base no longer merges).

## Decisions

- Lucca, 2026-10-23 ("2 ok" to the overseer's item proposing a reply that agrees on the direction and slicing): Venus stays local; Runtime and Orbit run remote; they connect over OpenSSH-forwarded Unix sockets; no new protocol in v1; land in slices on current edge; the remote supervisor must not require systemd (AGENTS.md keeps Linux contracts service-manager independent; systemd user service and linger are optional help for hosts with KillUserProcesses=yes). Reply posted on PR #2: https://github.com/Yazelix/eon/pull/2#issuecomment-6368463120
- Proposed slice order (to settle with Yu): contracts and IDs; one workspace model shared with EON-C33 (eon-workspace-switching-shn4); transport; remote supervision without systemd; recovery; incremental frames and history paging.
- Yu's four overlap questions (identity, Stop, discovery, protocols) are open in the PR thread; the overseer's leaning is recorded in the reply.

## Competitive context

Superlogical's Rex (macOS, public beta) uses the same server/client split, a custom binary screen frame, a Mosh-inspired responsive protocol for low-latency typing, and acts as a full SSH replacement with system logins. Eon deliberately reuses OpenSSH for authentication. OSC 7501, which Eon's agent sidebar reads, is Rex's published generic protocol.

## Scope

Children are filed after Yu and Lucca settle the four questions. Yu ports the slices as a Yazelix member through the normal bead, contract, review and proof loop.

## Acceptance

- Issue #1's recovery goal on two machines: close, connection loss and supervisor restart keep remote tabs, panes and popups running and reattachable, with disconnect distinct from stop.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
SSH owner and first slice: Lucca's decisions (2026-10-27, relayed by eon-overseer).

A coordinator research agent compared eon-remote-ssh-x7dr and this epic (both epics, their children, docs/CONTRACTS.md, docs/REFERENCES.md, Yu's PR #2 and issue #1). Lucca was asked nine numbered decisions, each with the recommendation yes, and replied "ssh: okay":

1. Owner epic: keep eon-remote-workspaces-52i4. Move x7dr.2 ("Keep remote Eon work alive after the SSH session ends") under it as its remote-supervision slice; close x7dr, x7dr.1 (Waypipe spike) and x7dr.3 (local Venus with remote supervisor) as superseded by the 2026-10-23 decision; carry x7dr's recorded decision (OpenSSH owns the connection; Eon opens no listener, owns no auth or crypto; Orbit used remotely only through Unix sockets carried over SSH, Orbit unchanged) and its Related list here; point eon-igae's exclusion at 52i4.
2. First slice: `eon attach --host HOST` = SSH transport plus a detached supervisor with no display on HOST, keeping today's EON-C33 model (one remote supervisor shows as one local window). The workspace registry, persistent IDs and the machine switcher (Yu's Q1-3) move to slice 2. This reorders the 2026-10-23 plan.
3. Surviving logout: setsid, plus sockets in a private per-UID directory when logind manages the login runtime directory (tmux precedent). A host with KillUserProcesses=yes is reported; Eon never enables linger.
4. Versions across machines: exact build match for now, failing closed and naming both builds.
5. Configuration split: local configuration decides presentation; HOST's configuration decides what its supervisor launches.
6. Host visibility: an Eon Bar host label (amends VEN-C21), not only the window title.
7. On disconnect: the window stays, shown disconnected with input off; no automatic reconnect yet.
8. Approve the EON-C34 draft text below, with 1-7 applied.
9. eon-remote-workspaces-52i4.1 (Mosh-style prediction) stays P3, after incremental frames.

Adopted contract text (EON-C34; the next free ID; implementation lands it in docs/CONTRACTS.md):

EON-C34 — Remote workspace over SSH
- Consumer: A full-Eon user on local x86_64 Linux Wayland whose work runs on an x86_64 Linux host they reach by OpenSSH. That host needs no display.
- Trigger: `eon attach --host HOST`, closing the window, losing the connection, ending the remote login, or Commands > Quit this window.
- Result:
  - Eon runs the user's `ssh` with their config, keys, host-key checks and ProxyJump. On HOST it starts or finds one supervisor with no display, detached from the SSH session, and Orbit runs there.
  - Venus runs locally and reaches HOST's workspace and terminal sockets only through forwards that this window owns, each with mode 0600.
  - The local configuration decides presentation; HOST's configuration decides everything its supervisor launches.
  - The Eon Bar shows HOST.
  - Closing the window or losing the connection only disconnects: Venus shows the window as disconnected with input off, and HOST's terminals keep running.
  - Reattach shows the same terminals. Quit stops them under EON-C11/EON-C15.
- Important failures:
  - A different EONW version or component graph on HOST is refused, naming both builds, without stopping anything.
  - Connecting never installs or upgrades software and never enables linger.
  - A host whose logind policy would kill the work at logout is reported, not changed.
- Owner: Eon Runtime owns the SSH launch, the forwards and the supervisor with no display; Venus owns presentation; Orbit owns terminals; OpenSSH owns the connection and authentication.
- Boundary:
  - No Eon listener, login or crypto.
  - No workspace registry or names surviving a supervisor restart.
  - No mixed-host windows, multiple clients or Waypipe.
  - No reboot recovery or service-manager requirement.
  - The x86_64 Linux limit applies to both ends.

Amendments the slice needs (their exact text still comes to Lucca with the implementation): EON-C11 drops "remote runtime" from its Boundary; EON-C15's Boundary allows logout survival for the supervisor with no display; EON-C7: the remote host needs no Wayland; VEN-C14: Venus presented by a local launcher; VEN-C21: the host label. No ORB change.

First-slice acceptance (proposed): two x86_64 Linux hosts or a VM over SSH with the same Eon build: panes run on HOST (`hostname`; the picker browses HOST); close the window, kill the SSH master, end every SSH login with linger off, and a counter in a pane keeps advancing on HOST after each; reattach shows the same terminals; Commands > Quit this window ends them; a mismatched build is refused, names both builds and stops nothing; `nix develop -c eon-test` passes.

Reference gate additions (route docs/REFERENCES.md:143 already covers OpenSSH stream-local forwarding and ControlMaster, Zed, VS Code Remote-SSH, WezTerm SSH domains, Mosh): tmux's per-UID socket directory (logout survival), the kitty ssh kitten (rejected: installs on the remote), Zellij (rejected as owner), Ghosthub and Unpeel (reconnect), the trust boundary (local socket mode; Orbit's SO_PEERCRED UID check sees sshd as the remote user), and the version policy (exact build now; Yu's protocol/build compatibility split as the exit condition).

Yu's PR #2 is reference only for Yazelix-org work (Yu is inside the org): it needs porting off systemd+linger, off the EON-C29 ID (now the clock) and from EONW 13 to the current EONW.

title: Make remote typing feel local with Mosh-style prediction
description:
## Why

Lucca approved filing this on 2026-10-23 ("yeah" to the overseer's item: "Add a responsive remote typing (Mosh-style prediction) bead to the future remote epic, measured after incremental frames"). Over SSH, every keystroke in a remote Eon workspace waits for a full round trip before it shows. Superlogical's Rex, Eon's closest competitor, advertises a Mosh-inspired responsive protocol for low-latency remote typing. On a slow or distant link, Eon will feel worse than Rex until it hides that latency.

## Scope

In scope, after incremental frames land in this epic:
- Measure first (AP-PERF-001): keystroke-to-glyph latency over representative RTTs (for example 20, 80 and 200 ms, with loss), against a local baseline.
- Research Mosh's speculative local echo and its confidence and undo rules, Eternal Terminal, and whatever Rex publishes. Decide where prediction lives. Venus showing tentative echo over Orbit frames is the likely owner, since Orbit stays the sole authority on terminal state.
- Bring the contract and any protocol change to Lucca before code.

Out of scope: replacing SSH, UDP roaming (a separate decision), and changes to local workspaces.

## Acceptance

- At 200 ms RTT, typed characters in a shell prompt appear within one frame locally, and mispredictions are corrected without corrupting the screen; measured and recorded.

## Verification

The measurement harness under realistic RTT and loss, plus the proof route that the eventual contract change requires.

title: Attach to a remote host's workspace with eon attach --host HOST
description:
## Why

First slice of `eon-remote-workspaces-52i4` (GitHub issue #1): a person on local x86_64 Linux
Wayland runs `eon attach --host HOST` and gets an Eon window whose terminals run on HOST. Lucca
chose this first slice on 2026-10-27 (relayed by eon-overseer, "ssh: okay" to nine numbered
decisions recorded on 52i4): SSH transport plus a supervisor with no display on HOST, keeping
today's EON-C33 model (one remote supervisor shows as one local window). Workspace registry,
persistent IDs and a machine switcher are slice 2 (not filed).

Owner: Yu (bioinformatist), a trusted Yazelix-org member (AGENTS.md "Outside Contributions" does
not apply to him), ports this through the normal bead, contract, review and proof loop. His PR #2
is reference only: port it off systemd and linger, off the EON-C29 ID (now the clock) and from
EONW 13 to the current EONW.

## Contract

EON-C34 "Remote workspace over SSH", adopted text recorded verbatim on 52i4's 2026-10-27
comment; this bead lands it in `docs/CONTRACTS.md` (next free ID; EON-C33 is the last at edge
01f5e3c). Amendments this slice needs, whose exact text still goes to Lucca with the
implementation: EON-C11 drops "remote runtime" from its Boundary; EON-C7: the remote host needs
no Wayland; VEN-C14: Venus presented by a local launcher. (EON-C15's logout amendment belongs to
`eon-remote-ssh-x7dr.2`; VEN-C21's host label to the presentation sibling.) No ORB change.

## Scope

In scope (Eon Runtime owns the SSH launch, the forwards and the supervisor with no display):
- `eon attach --host HOST`: runs the user's `ssh` with their config, keys, host-key checks and
  ProxyJump; on HOST starts or finds the supervisor with no display delivered by
  `eon-remote-ssh-x7dr.2`; never installs or upgrades software and never enables linger.
- Forwards owned by this window (OpenSSH stream-local forwarding) of HOST's workspace and terminal
  sockets to local sockets with mode 0600; Venus runs locally and reaches HOST only through them.
- Configuration split: local configuration decides presentation; HOST's decides what its
  supervisor launches.
- Exact-build check: a different EONW version or component graph on HOST is refused, naming both
  builds, without stopping anything.
- Reattach shows the same terminals; Commands > Quit this window stops them under EON-C11/EON-C15.
- Humans and Agents: the attach and quit paths are CLI paths; record any window action this slice
  adds and its CLI path.

Out of scope: the disconnected window state and the Eon Bar host label (presentation sibling);
logout survival (x7dr.2); workspace registry, mixed-host windows, multiple clients, Waypipe,
reboot recovery, automatic reconnect, any Eon listener, login or crypto (EON-C34 Boundary).

## Reference gate (consequential: lifecycle, trust boundary, contract)

Record on this bead before code: route `docs/REFERENCES.md:143` (OpenSSH stream-local forwarding
and ControlMaster, Zed, VS Code Remote-SSH, WezTerm SSH domains, Mosh) plus 52i4's additions
(kitty ssh kitten rejected: installs on the remote; Zellij rejected as owner; Ghosthub and Unpeel
for reconnect), the trust boundary (local socket mode; Orbit's SO_PEERCRED UID check sees sshd as
the remote user), and the version policy (exact build now; Yu's protocol/build compatibility
split as the exit condition).

## Acceptance

- Two x86_64 Linux hosts, or a VM, over SSH with the same Eon build: panes run on HOST
  (`hostname`; the picker browses HOST); close the window and kill the SSH master, and a counter
  in a pane keeps advancing on HOST; reattach shows the same terminals; Commands > Quit this
  window ends them; a mismatched build is refused, names both builds and stops nothing.
- EON-C34 and the approved amendments land in `docs/CONTRACTS.md`; `docs/USAGE.md` and
  CHANGELOG.md updated.
- `nix develop -c eon-test` passes; Codex review per AGENTS.md.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop for Lucca's approval of each amendment's exact text before editing contracts.
- Stop if the slice needs a new protocol or EONW change (52i4: no new protocol in v1).
- Stop if HOST needs anything installed beyond the same Eon build.

comments.text: Order change, Lucca 2026-10-28 (decision on eon-remote-workspaces-52i4): this bead is part of slice 3 (minimal SSH attachment and portable hosting), together with 52i4.2 / x7dr.2. It now waits for the persistent workspace ID and registry (52i4.5) and for recovery into the original groups (52i4.6), so it attaches to a workspace identity instead of the flattened model. The compatibility rule changes from exact-build matching to identical wire protocol versions (slice 1, 52i4.4). Yu ports the slice as a PR.

title: Show a remote window's host and its disconnected state in Venus
description:
## Why

Part of the first slice of `eon-remote-workspaces-52i4` (EON-C34, adopted 2026-10-27): a person
must see which host a window's terminals run on, and losing the connection must look like a
disconnect, not like the terminals ending. Lucca's decisions 6 and 7 (52i4 comment, 2026-10-27,
"ssh: okay"): an Eon Bar host label (amends VEN-C21), not only the window title; on disconnect the
window stays, shown disconnected with input off, with no automatic reconnect yet.

Owner: Yu (bioinformatist), a trusted Yazelix-org member, through the normal bead, contract,
review and proof loop.

## Contract

EON-C34 Result: "The Eon Bar shows HOST" and "Closing the window or losing the connection only
disconnects: Venus shows the window as disconnected with input off, and HOST's terminals keep
running." VEN-C21 amendment for the host label: exact text to Lucca before editing. If the
disconnected state needs VEN-C4 or VEN-C14 text, bring that wording too.

## Scope

In scope (Venus owns presentation; Eon Runtime passes resolved values, Venus parses no
configuration):
- The Eon Bar host label for a remote window, from a value the Runtime passes (a launch argument,
  like `--animate-working-badge`, unless the gate shows it must ride EONW; then stop: EON-C34 v1
  has no new protocol).
- A disconnected window state: when the forwarded workspace socket is lost, the window stays,
  says it is disconnected, and takes no terminal input; `eon attach --host HOST` restores it.
- Accessibility: the label and the disconnected state are in the accessible tree.
- Configurability: record whether the label is configurable or fixed, and why.

Out of scope: SSH launch and forwards (transport sibling), logout survival (x7dr.2), automatic
reconnect, Mosh-style prediction (52i4.1).

## Acceptance

- Venus tests for the label and the disconnected state (input refused, window kept).
- One isolated installed observation on the two-host or VM setup: the bar names HOST; killing the
  SSH master shows the disconnected state with input off; reattach shows the same terminals.
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings` for Venus;
  `nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-venus`; Codex review per AGENTS.md; CHANGELOG.md entry.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop for Lucca's approval of the VEN-C21 (and any VEN-C4/VEN-C14) text before editing.
- Stop if the label or state needs an EONW change.

title: Settle the remote workspace contracts: fresh IDs, compatibility rule, acceptance matrix
description:
## Why

Slice 1 of the remote-workspace plan Lucca adopted on 2026-10-28 (decision comment on eon-remote-workspaces-52i4; PR #2 thread). Yu (bioinformatist) ports it as a PR on current edge.

## Goal

Contract text, approved by Lucca before any code, for the whole remote-workspace feature:
- **Fresh contract IDs.** EON-C29 is the clock's; check the beads for an EON-C34 reservation and reuse it if it fits, otherwise take the next free ID.
- **Amendments to EON-C33, EON-C15 and EON-C11:** persistent workspace identity and registry, recovery into the original groups, targeted Stop, the empty window after the last Stop, offline no-replay, Forget only after confirmed stop.
- **The compatibility rule:** builds are compatible exactly when their wire protocol versions match (EONW, Orbit management, ORBS/ORBF). An incompatible attach fails clearly and stops nothing.
- **Portable and managed hosting:** each with its own startup owner and proof. Managed is opt-in, never inferred, and never a silent fallback. Linux contracts stay service-manager-independent.
- **One active client per workspace:** a second client gets a busy result.
- **Remote identity:** the UID, PID, start-time, inode and lease checks stay.
- **Nix store:** retention through GC roots or profiles; the runtime never queries or records store paths.
- **CLI parity** for every new action, and cached remote state labelled as cached.
- **The acceptance matrix:**
  - simultaneous bootstrap attempts;
  - a wrong host key;
  - stale or replaced sockets;
  - PID reuse;
  - corrupt or unknown snapshots;
  - SSH loss and window close;
  - supervisor normal exit and crash;
  - the last logout;
  - reconnecting without SSH masters piling up.

## Acceptance

- Lucca approves the exact text.
- docs/CONTRACTS.md and orbit/docs/CONTRACTS.md carry it with status Planned.
- Review loop, plus Codex because it changes contract text.

## Scope boundary

Contract text and the acceptance matrix only. No code.

title: Give every workspace a persistent host ID and registry
description:
## Why

Slice 2a of the remote-workspace plan Lucca adopted on 2026-10-28 (decision comment on eon-remote-workspaces-52i4). Yu ports it as a PR.

## Goal

Every workspace, local or remote, gets a persistent host-owned ID and a versioned host registry entry (name, run membership, layout). Window `wN` values become local handles. Directories stay attributes, not identities. Eon Runtime owns the registry and is its only writer. Snapshots are written atomically and never replace live process, socket and lease validation.

## Contract

The slice 1 amendments to EON-C33 and EON-C15.

## Acceptance

- The registry survives a supervisor restart.
- A corrupt or unknown registry fails without stopping unrelated work.
- The CLI lists workspaces by persistent ID.
- Affected Rust suites pass, plus an installed isolated observation.
- Review loop and Codex.

## Reference

PR #2's atomic snapshot and exact-run reconciliation code, as specification only: pr2.diff:9710 and :14783 in /home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-overseer/pr2/.

## Scope boundary

No SSH and no recovery into groups (that is 2b).

title: Recover workspaces into their original groups and layout after a supervisor restart
description:
## Why

Slice 2b of the remote-workspace plan Lucca adopted on 2026-10-28. Yu ports it as a PR.

## Goal

After a supervisor restart, Runtime recovers live Orbit runs into their original workspaces, groups and layout from the registry, instead of one unnamed `w1`. Runs that are missing become stopped slots. Recovery never replays commands or input.

## Contract

The slice 1 amendment to EON-C33's recovery clause.

## Acceptance

- After a normal exit and after a crash restart, the original workspaces come back with the same terminals (the same PID and start identity).
- A stale or mismatched run is refused.
- An installed isolated observation.
- Review loop and Codex.

## Scope boundary

Local only. No SSH.

title: Add opt-in managed hosting: a host service and a Home Manager module
description:
## Why

Slice 4 of the remote-workspace plan Lucca adopted on 2026-10-28. Yu ports it as a PR.

## Goal

Opt-in managed hosting. An explicitly configured host service owns starting the remote supervisor: a systemd user service, and a Home Manager module for Nix users. SSH asks that owner to start it, then performs the same readiness and compatibility handshake as portable hosting. A service failure never silently falls back to an unmanaged launch. Orbit lifetimes stay outside the supervisor's service, so restarting the service never kills terminals. Logout-policy problems (logind KillUserProcesses, linger) are diagnosed and documented, never changed silently.

## Contract

The slice 1 hosting text. Portable hosting (eon-remote-ssh-x7dr.2) stays independent of this slice.

## Acceptance

- Home Manager switch and rollback, and a compatible upgrade, keep live work.
- The service failure path is shown.
- Proof on a systemd host. Portable hosting's own proof stays separate.
- Review loop and Codex.

## Reference

PR #2's independent Orbit scope approach, as specification only.

## Scope boundary

No change to the portable path. No service required anywhere.

title: Send incremental terminal frames with bounded backpressure over remote attach
description:
## Why

Slice 6 of the remote-workspace plan Lucca adopted on 2026-10-28. Yu ports it as a PR.

## Goal

Over a remote attach, terminal updates travel as incremental frames with bounded backpressure, and resynchronize with a full snapshot when they fall behind. Correctness is checked against the full-frame baseline.

## Acceptance

- The same screen content as the full-frame path across a test corpus.
- Measured wire bytes, CPU, input latency and queue memory under constrained RTT and bandwidth, against the baseline, per AP-PERF-001.
- Review loop and Codex.

## Scope boundary

No history paging (slice 7), no prediction (eon-remote-workspaces-52i4.1).

title: Page terminal history in bounded chunks and prove remote performance
description:
## Why

Slice 7 of the remote-workspace plan Lucca adopted on 2026-10-28. Yu ports it as a PR. It closes GitHub issue #1.

## Goal

Scrollback history pages in bounded chunks with stable reading anchors and explicit invalidation. The end-to-end remote performance proof covers RTT and bandwidth limits.

## Acceptance

- The reading position survives new output.
- The memory bound holds.
- The end-to-end measurements are recorded per AP-PERF-001.
- Review loop and Codex.

## Scope boundary

No prediction.

title: Remove inert component launch selection
description:
## Contract routing

Harden EON-C2 after eon-authoritative-component-launch-declarations-iam. Consumers are Eon manifest validation, raw generation identity, Nix composition, and Rust launch policy. When a canonical graph is validated, it must contain no launch declaration that Nix and Rust ignore. Schema 3 removes component.launch; non-library roles must still declare at least one file artifact. An obsolete launch field must fail validation before generation selection, runtime state, or child spawn.

## Confirmed defect

On the current schema-2 graph, changing Orbit launch.artifact from executable to terminfo validates. Renaming the executable artifact and its launch reference together also validates. Nix reads neither launch nor artifacts for program selection; Rust launches EON_ORBIT with hardcoded serve. The exact production digest changed from g1-ce32c5dc7d666f554a285d8565af9d03 to g1-62d75c6ec347f316f6d1a5d98ced7d8f and g1-b441f19b7638ef7df08fa342d78aaebf respectively. This violates the prior Bead acceptance that inert graph edits cannot select a false fresh generation.

## Reference gate and decision

Read the complete prior Bead and explicit schema-2 approval, current EON-C2 proof, canonical manifest, complete validator, every launch/artifact reference, Nix component resolution and package wiring, Rust generation hashing/version reporting/program launch, and architecture/distribution ownership text. Architecture assigns launch policy to Rust and physical paths to Nix; the graph owns abstract artifact identity and compatibility. The user has now authorized the recommended deletion, superseding the prior decision to retain Launch.artifact.

Adopt schema 3 with no schema-2 compatibility path: delete Launch and every launch object, preserve abstract Artifact id/kind, and replace launch-plan validation with the existing role-level requirement that each non-library component has a declared file artifact. Reject Nix assertion plumbing, generic launch translation, path metadata, dependencies, and child changes.

## Scope

In scope: canonical manifest schema/file name, eon-manifest types/validation/focused rejection test, embedded/runtime and Nix references, EON-C2 current-state proof wording/status, architecture/distribution/README current-state paths, changelog, LOC, generation preflight, exact build/profile proof.

Out of scope: artifact path restoration, general launcher schemas, changing actual Orbit/Venus or managed-tool argv, direct distribution, schema compatibility/migration, dependencies, component revisions, child repositories, or other contracts.

## Acceptance

- Schema 3 contains no Launch type or launch field and rejects any launch object as unknown.
- Every service, client, and tool still declares at least one file artifact; libraries remain non-launch policy.
- The prior terminfo swap and coordinated rename cannot be expressed as a launch selection.
- Nix and Rust retain their current single owners and exact program/argv behavior.
- Invalid old launch bytes fail before generation identity or runtime effects.
- Abstract artifact identity, compatibility, version reporting, generated-runtime coverage, and live Sessions remain intact.

## Verification

TDD the old launch object rejection; focused eon-manifest tests; locked workspace fmt/check/test/clippy; canonical manifest validation; invalid embedded graph command matrix; exact Nix build and flake check; git diff check; LOC; active profile and installed versions/dogfood without restarting supervisors.

## Stop conditions

Stop before adding a dependency, compatibility path, generic launcher, physical artifact metadata, child change, or launch behavior change. Stop if removing Launch would weaken the non-library file-artifact invariant or if any independent consumer of schema 2 is found.

title: Rename EonTerm to eonbase
description:
## Outcome
The standalone exact-command product is named eonbase. Its command is `eonbase`, with the
same CLI EonTerm has today, and `eonterm` is gone from product, package and docs.

## Decision (user, 2026-10-15)
- Name: eonbase. "eonterm" reads as Eon itself, and the site is eonterm.com. The product is
  the base layer: Orbit terminals, Venus windows and the runtime lifecycle, with Eon adding the
  workspace and managed tools on top (flake.nix eontermPackage, cli.rs LaunchMode::Terminal).
- Command: `eonbase`, a separate binary, not `eon base`. The slim closure must exclude the eon
  package and every managed tool (eonterm-closure check), so a subcommand would defeat it.
- No `eonterm` alias. One alpha tag shipped it and stays usable at its pin. One spelling per
  product (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md naming boundary).
- No short `eb` command: the AWS Elastic Beanstalk CLI (nixpkgs awsebcli) installs `eb`. User
  docs may suggest `alias eb=eonbase` as an optional shell alias.
- Rejected names: eonlet, eonling, eontiny, eonlite, eonmini, eonslate, eonplate, eonboard,
  eonb, beon. eonbase was absent from nixpkgs, PATH and a web search on 2026-10-15.

## CLI contract
eonbase [--no-decorations] [--application-id ID] -- COMMAND...
eonbase generations [--json]
eonbase attach [GENERATION]
eonbase stop GENERATION [--json]

## Scope
- runtime/crates/eon-runtime: argv[0] dispatch (cli.rs `eonterm` check), EONTERM_USAGE,
  lifecycle hints and errors, LaunchMode::Terminal display name, runtime namespace directory,
  default application ID, sessions.rs and supervisor.rs messages, test names.
- flake.nix: package pname, bin rename, license paths, `eonterm` package/app outputs,
  `eonterm-closure` check, EONTERM_BIN; .github/workflows/cachix.yml build target.
- demo/record.rs features take, docs/DEVELOPMENT.md.

title: Repair Stop completion and owned picker cleanup
description:
## Contract

Under EON-C11, C15, C18 and C23, an explicit Stop of a selected disposable window or generation completes its owned terminal and transient-helper cleanup, reports an accurate bounded result, and preserves peer and older-generation work. Orbit retains process/PTY containment; Runtime retains lifecycle policy, inventory and action-result ownership.

## Evidence and prerequisites

The completed eon-qualify-nix-linux-beta-bxoh is No-Go for Eon 92e0d7b379a14d003f37e5c2df9c468cb43e74b7. An independent-window Stop returned exit 2 with an action-result read timeout even though its intended terminals subsequently ended. A later generation Stop returned success and inventory reported dead while its Orbit directory picker, helper and fzf remained live; bare Eon recovery plus another owner Stop was needed. These are observed failures, not an established shared root cause. See /home/lucca/.local/state/eon/proofs/eon-beta-bxoh-2026-10-07-1845/qualification.json and observations; the compact qualification.txt preserves the exact component graph and environment.

## Reference gate

Read the governing contract sections and the retained observations. Trace Runtime control, supervisor, generation and sessions callers, transient-picker cleanup and Orbit management/containment at the exact accepted revisions. Inspect crates/eon/tests/workspace_control.rs, especially lost-result, failed-picker-Stop and independent-window coverage. Resolve the owner before choosing a fix; route any child mechanism correction to that child and consume only its accepted revision.

## Acceptance

- Reproduce or explain both failures with retained exact evidence and identify their responsible owner(s).
- The installed independent-window Stop completes without the observed spurious result timeout and leaves its peers unchanged.
- A successful generation Stop with an active picker leaves no test-owned managed Orbit/helper/fzf process or endpoint. Genuine partial cleanup remains diagnosable and retryable; inventory and result do not falsely imply completion.
- Preserve bounded shutdown, exact process authority and the existing exception for deliberately detached processes. Add the cheapest meaningful regression check at the changed owner; verify affected Rust/Nix surfaces and one isolated installed observation at the accepted graph.

## Scope boundary

Repair these two Stop failures only; if diagnosis finds independent causes, record them without assuming one patch fixes both. No process-wide kill, blanket timeout increase, cgroup/service dependency, new lifecycle guarantee or protocol framework. Preserve live user terminals and desktop focus. EonTerm package build failures are separately tracked.

title: Report invalid focus actions before supervisor connection
description:
## Contract routing

Harden EON-C10 while preserving EON-C8. The consumer is the canonical local `eon` CLI; the trigger is a syntactically valid `eon focus ID` command whose ID cannot be encoded by the shared EONW owner; the result is a bounded local `malformed-action` failure before any supervisor connection attempt. Valid focus actions and genuine missing, unreachable, incompatible, or corrupt supervisor failures retain their current behavior.

This is a defect correction. It adds no EONW value, validation rule, public command, dependency, compatibility window, Venus behavior, or workspace policy.

## Why

`send_action` connects before `send_action_on` encodes the request. An empty or longer-than-128-byte focus ID is therefore reported as `supervisor-unavailable` with advice to run Eon even when a healthy endpoint accepted the connection. The same invalid action is classified differently when the socket is absent. The command sends no request bytes and mutates no workspace, but its diagnosis points at the wrong owner.

Impact: LOW. Effort: S. Implementation risk: LOW. Confidence: HIGH.

## Evidence

- Closed audit `eon-audit-eonw-boundary-k3y`, comments 285-286, records the exact `57d7acc22f9f01c7f15d9d381845318b67f760e1` snapshot, reproduction, reference gate, and verification.
- `crates/eon/src/main.rs:121-123`: `send_action` connects before delegating request encoding.
- `crates/eon/src/main.rs:184-204`: `send_action_on` encodes only after it owns a stream and classifies encoding failure as endpoint corruption.
- `crates/eon/src/main.rs:1352-1368`: `control` maps every non-dead local client failure to `supervisor-unavailable` and appends `run eon first`.
- `crates/eon/src/main.rs:1387-1414`: focus IDs become `Action::FocusId` without duplicating protocol limits.
- `crates/eon-workspace-protocol/src/lib.rs:168-197` and `:570-580`: the shared encoder correctly owns the nonempty and 128-byte FocusId constraints.
- `crates/eon/src/main.rs:2110-2116`: `malformed-action` is already Eon's bounded EONW failure code for an invalid action; reuse it instead of creating another public token.
- Audit reproduction with an owned mode-0600 Unix listener: `eon focus '' --json` exited 2 with `supervisor-unavailable`, told the user to run Eon, connected, and sent zero bytes. A 129-byte ID behaved identically.

## Prerequisite and reference gate

- No implementation prerequisite.
- Rebaseline the cited symbols and read EON-C8, EON-C10, the complete EONW request encoder, all `send_action`/`send_action_on` callers, and the focused workspace-control test before editing.
- Existing EONW and CLI failure owners completely define the correction. No external reference or dependency comparison is required unless those owners have materially changed.
- This Bead blocks the final cross-subsystem integration audit: applying this client-path correction afterward would invalidate that audit's unchanged-snapshot convergence.

## Scope

In scope:
- The smallest request-preparation/send boundary in `crates/eon/src/main.rs` that encodes ordinary actions before endpoint connection and preserves the already connected, identity-checked presentation path.
- One deterministic real CLI/socket regression in `crates/eon/tests/workspace_control.rs`.
- EON-C10 current-state proof metadata, `CHANGELOG.md`, and the README LOC scorecard as required by the accepted behavior correction.

Out of scope:
- Changing EONW framing, tags, bounds, validation rules, or the `Failure` schema.
- Duplicating FocusId length or emptiness checks in CLI parsing.
- Changing valid focus behavior, direction keywords, workspace state, supervisor-side rejection, Venus, Orbit, runtime discovery, or connection security.
- A generic transport framework, new error hierarchy, protocol dependency, or broader `main.rs` refactor.

## Implementation notes

1. Write the real-process regression first using the existing test helpers and an owned mode-0600 Unix listener. Prove both empty and 129-byte focus IDs return exit 2, structured `malformed-action` JSON, empty stderr, and no `run eon first` guidance; prove the listener receives no connection and the workspace cannot mutate.
2. Prepare and encode the request through `eon_workspace_protocol::encode_request` before `send_action` calls `connect_control`. Keep one shared encode/send path for path-based and already-connected callers where practical, without weakening the socket-identity check in `present_at`.
3. Distinguish local encoding failure from endpoint failure only as much as needed to route `control` to the existing bounded `malformed-action` result. Do not copy protocol constants or semantic validation into the CLI.
4. Preserve `missing-supervisor` and `supervisor-unavailable` plus their launch guidance for genuine endpoint failures.
5. Update current-state EON-C10 proof evidence after the proof-bearing commit, refresh the installed profile, and leave running supervisors and Sessions untouched.

## Acceptance

- `eon focus '' --json` and a 129-byte focus ID exit 2 with bounded `malformed-action` JSON, write nothing to stderr, and do not advise starting Eon.
- Neither invalid command attempts a Unix connection or sends request bytes; no workspace or Session state changes.
- The result is independent of whether a supervisor socket exists.
- A valid focus ID still reaches the current supervisor and returns its complete accepted snapshot.
- A valid workspace command with no supervisor still returns `missing-supervisor`; genuine endpoint failures retain their current classification and guidance.
- EONW remains the sole owner of FocusId validation. No new public failure code, protocol value, dependency, child change, or compatibility promise is introduced.
- The owner-bound `present_at` flow still revalidates socket identity before sending its valid presentation action.

## Verification

- `cargo test --locked -p eon --test workspace_control invalid_focus_is_rejected_before_supervisor_connection` should exit 0 and prove the exact failure shape plus absence of a connection.
- `cargo test --locked -p eon --test workspace_control missing_supervisor_is_a_structured_workspace_failure` should exit 0.
- `cargo fmt --all --check`
- `cargo check --locked --workspace`
- `cargo test --locked --workspace`
- `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo run --locked -p eon-manifest -- components/eon-alpha-v1.json`
- `nix build --no-link --print-out-paths --no-update-lock-file path:.#default`
- `nix flake check --no-build --no-update-lock-file path:.`
- `git diff --check`
- After the proof-bearing commit, refresh the active `eon` profile from the working tree without stopping live supervisors; verify it resolves to the just-built artifact and report that existing generations require restart for changed installed behavior.

## Stop conditions

- Stop if EONW validation, CLI failure projection, or the owner-bound presentation send path has materially changed.
- Stop if the correction requires a new failure code, protocol/schema change, duplicated validation, dependency, Venus/Orbit edit, or weakening socket ownership.
- Stop if the regression cannot prove absence of a connection deterministically.
- Stop if the same verification failure repeats twice after a reasonable correction.

## Maintenance notes

Reuse the existing encoder and `malformed-action` code. Reject CLI-side length checks, preflight-by-double-encoding, a generic request framework, or a broader endpoint taxonomy redesign.
notes: Implemented at source proof d0c2208d628fa0dc1e186899b45e0b73534ff9bc. EONW encode_request remains the only FocusId validator; send_action prepares once before connect, while the owner-checked present_at path keeps its connect and identity order. Local preparation failure alone maps to existing malformed-action. The regression covers empty and 129-byte IDs with absent and listening sockets and proves no connection; genuine missing-supervisor behavior remains covered. No dependency, protocol, manifest, Orbit, or Venus change. The current canonical manifest is components/eon-alpha-v3.json; it replaces the stale v1 path in the issue verification list.
close_reason: Invalid FocusId actions are now rejected locally before any supervisor connection, with exact source, regression, Nix, and installed-runtime proof.

title: Return committed workspace action results within the client deadline
description:
## Contract

Harden EON-C10: when `eon tab create` or `eon pane create` starts an Orbit Session within the supervisor's accepted work bound, the original CLI request returns the committed typed workspace snapshot. It must not report `supervisor-unavailable` after the Session has been accepted, and one request must create at most one Session.

Consumer: the local `eon` CLI and agents consuming its structured action results. Trigger: Session startup completes after the current client control timeout but before the supervisor's Session-start timeout. Result: the initiating client receives the single truthful committed result within one bounded deadline. Important failures: a pre-commit startup failure preserves the prior workspace; a response failure never encourages an unsafe retry after an unknown commit; unrelated actions remain bounded.

## Steps to Reproduce

The final pass of `eon-audit-eon-runtime-lifecycle-wqz` at exact edge revision `88a57f066e426cb2882c4969b9036c4e358fc48b` reproduced the defect with a delayed Orbit substitute: `eon pane create --json` exited 2 after about 2.048 seconds with `supervisor-unavailable`, while the supervisor completed inside its five-second bound and a later workspace snapshot showed the new `session-2` live. Current edge `d8cf277731f112c898843354edb941d02d04cb21` still defines a two-second `CONTROL_TIMEOUT` and five-second `SESSION_START_TIMEOUT`; no existing Bead owns this defect.

Impact HIGH; effort S; implementation risk LOW/MEDIUM; confidence HIGH. A user or agent may retry after the false failure and create another unwanted Session, which has no individual stop action.

## Prerequisites and reference gate

The lifecycle audit and independent replacement-socket correction are closed. Before code, reread EON-C10, the action request/response path, workspace dispatch commit ordering, the delayed-Session audit reproduction, and the matching `docs/REFERENCES.md` route. Keep one Eon-owned bounded deadline policy across client wait and maximum server work, or use the smallest action-aware equivalent. Preserve the private EONW control boundary and Orbit/Venus ownership.

Reject a retry framework, request journal, deduplication protocol, new dependency, child change, public timeout setting, asynchronous action API, or compatibility surface unless the smallest deadline-owner correction cannot satisfy the contract.

## Scope

In scope: the shared action-response deadline invariant in `crates/eon/src/main.rs`, one deterministic real-process regression with Session startup strictly between the old client and server bounds, required EON-C10 proof/current documentation, CHANGELOG and README LOC updates when runtime behavior changes, locked Rust/Nix/profile verification, and a post-change fresh-eyes/simplification pass.

Out of scope: socket cleanup, supervisor replacement, retry or idempotency infrastructure, individual Session stop, durability across supervisor or machine loss, configurable deadlines, child behavior, new contracts, dependencies, compatibility windows, or interruption of live supervisors.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A deterministic red/green check delays CreatePane or CreateTab startup beyond the old client deadline but within the accepted server bound; the original command returns the accepted typed snapshot and exactly one new Session exists.
- A startup failure before commit returns one bounded failure and leaves the accepted workspace and Sessions unchanged.
- The client cannot report `supervisor-unavailable` solely because accepted server work is still inside its owner-approved bound.
- One owner defines the complete request/work/response deadline relationship; the correction remains bounded and adds no retry, journal, protocol field, dependency, or public setting.
- Existing workspace actions, malformed-action handling, control framing, concurrent startup, lifecycle, and replacement-socket checks remain green.
- Locked format, check, tests, Clippy, Nix build/check, LOC, and `git diff --check` pass.
- The active Eon profile resolves to the exact working-tree artifact without restarting running supervisors or Sessions.
- A complete post-change correctness and simplification pass finds no further in-scope correction.
notes: Published Eon proof source a390fc5c007900c3fc8c9c49df85f9b8acc06d4a and Eonova rollout source 247265c44f759f8142783af7dfd5415c25211c5c on origin/edge. EON-C10 is Proven. The named eon, eonterm, and eonova profile elements resolve the verified artifacts recorded in the acceptance comment. Existing live Eonova generations were not restarted.

Reference gate

Question: how should Eon's private action client bound a request when the authoritative supervisor may legitimately spend five seconds starting an Orbit Session before committing and replying?
Contract: EON-C10 is hardened; no contract, protocol, compatibility surface, or child behavior changes.

Options compared:
1. Relate the existing client connection deadline directly to the existing Session-start bound, leaving a small bounded response allowance.
2. Add action-specific timeout plumbing.
3. Retry, journal, or deduplicate requests.

title: Scale the review loop by risk
description:
## Decision
Lucca, 2026-10-15: scale the per-slice review loop by risk instead of repeating fresh-context
passes until one finds nothing.

## Contract
- Consumer: the implementing agent and its reviewers.
- Result: review depth follows the Verification table's change classes. Docs, planning and agent
policy get one fresh-eyes pass; a pass converges when it has no blocking findings (incorrect claims,
lost information, broken links, scope breaches), while style nits are optional. Code that touches a
contract, protocol, lifecycle, security or trust boundary keeps the full loop.

## Evidence
`eon-readme-agent-workspace-06m3` slice 1 (a 100-line README) took four fresh review passes, about
270k subagent tokens; each new reviewer surfaced different wording nits, and only the fourth found
nothing actionable. The current rule is in `AGENTS.md` "Proof and Review" (rendered from
`.agent-protocols.local.md`).

## Prerequisites
Agent policy is Lucca's: get approval for the exact wording. Coordinate with
`eon-slim-agent-instructions-jr9k`, which edits the same file. Validate directly with structural
checks (recorded AP-TEST-001 exception).

## Acceptance
`.agent-protocols.local.md` states the tiers and the convergence rule; render and check pass; the
rendered `AGENTS.md` diff is recorded. Policy proof only.

## Stop boundary
No change to proof requirements, contract rules or the Verification table's routes.
close_reason: Review rule and AP-PROOF-001 exception applied

title: Show the cursor color and its name in the Eon Bar
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-10-21: show the cursor color's name in the Eon Bar, with the color itself as a filled
circle next to the name (for example `● ice`). When `cursor_trail_color` is omitted, each workspace
picks a random preset, so today a user cannot tell which preset they got, or name it to keep it.

## Evidence

- `venus/src/launch.rs:15-24`: `CURSOR_COLOR_PRESETS`, the eight named presets (magma, solar, lime,
  forest, ice, ocean, nebula, bubblegum) and their colors.
- `venus/src/launch.rs:298-337`: `parse_cursor_color_choice` and `endpoint_cursor_color` /
  `cursor_preset_from_entropy`. `random` always resolves to one of the presets, chosen per live
  endpoint so `eon attach` keeps it. `LaunchArguments.cursor_tail` (`launch.rs:39`) keeps only the
  `Color` and duration; the preset name is dropped there.
- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/supervisor.rs:373`: Eon passes `[terminal] cursor_trail_color`
  to Venus as `--cursor-trail-color random|preset:NAME|custom:#RRGGBB`; Venus owns the random pick.
- `docs/CONFIGURATION.md` (cursor_trail_color paragraph): values, presets, random lifetime.
- Pattern to follow: the CPU label, `eon-cpu-widget-eon-bar-acxs`, VEN-C28 in
  `venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md` with its Eon twin EON-C30 in `docs/CONTRACTS.md`; the clock VEN-C27 /
  its EON twin. Eon Bar text and geometry live in Venus Scene (`venus/src/scene.rs`, Eon Bar
  layout near `LocalClock`), drawing in `venus/src/render/chrome.rs`.
- `venus/src/render/chrome.rs:706`: `push_rounded(visual, visual.height / 2.0, fill)` already draws
  pill shapes; a square rect with radius half its side is a filled circle, with no new primitive.

## Contract (draft; show Lucca before code)

New Venus contract (next free `VEN-C` ID) plus its Eon twin (next free `EON-C` ID), mirroring
VEN-C28/EON-C30:
- Consumer/trigger: a person using a Venus surface controlled by a full Eon workspace; the surface is
  presented.
- Result: one read-only label in the Eon Bar's top row: a filled circle in the cursor trail color,
  then the preset name (`● ice`), or the hex for a custom color (`● #12ABCF`). Hover and a static
  AccessKit label say, for example, `Cursor color ice, picked at random for this workspace` or
  `Cursor color ice, from configuration`. It uses only spare drag-region space and yields under
  width pressure (position and yield order: see open decisions).
- Failures: no cursor tail (`--cursor-effect-v1 none`) shows no label. The label has no action,
  focus target or drag behavior and never resizes terminals.
- Owner: Venus launch keeps the resolved choice (name or hex, and whether it was random) next to the
  color; Scene owns text and geometry; chrome draws the circle. No EONW, runtime or configuration
  change.

## Open decisions (recommendations)

1. Position: just left of the CPU label, so it yields before CPU and clock when the window narrows.
   Recommend this; the cursor name is the least time-sensitive item.
2. Hide option: none for now, like CPU and clock. Recommend no new setting.
3. Explicit cursor color from Orbit (a program set OSC 12): the label still shows the trail color,
   which is what the setting controls. Recommend keeping it tied to the setting.

## Scope

In scope:
- `venus/src/launch.rs` (keep the resolved name/hex and random flag), `venus/src/scene.rs` (label
  text, geometry, yield order, hover/accessibility text), `venus/src/render/chrome.rs` (circle),
  `venus/src/accessibility.rs` if the label needs a node, VEN/EON contracts, `docs/CONFIGURATION.md`
  or `docs/USAGE.md` mention, `venus/CHANGELOG.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`.

Out of scope:
- Clicking to change or cycle the color, a new preset, configuration keys, eonbase-specific chrome,
  any EONW or runtime change.

## Acceptance

- Lucca approves the contract wording before code.
- In a full Eon workspace, the Eon Bar shows a filled circle in the cursor trail color and the preset
  name (or hex for a custom color); it survives `eon attach` with the same name; it yields under
  width pressure in the approved order; hover and AccessKit give the label text.
- A Venus test covers label text for preset, random and custom choices, and the yield order.
- One isolated installed observation (headless Sway capture) of the label for a random and a
  configured preset; profile refresh.

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-venus`; `cargo fmt --check` and
  `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings` for venus.
- Isolated installed capture as in `eon-nlcy`'s proof comment (private headless Sway, fresh HOME,
  `[anima] enabled = false`, `wdotool prime`).
- Review per AGENTS.md (parallel Claude + Codex on the candidate tree).

## Stop Conditions

- Stop for Lucca's approval before adding the contracts or writing code.
- Stop if keeping the preset name requires a protocol or runtime change.

## Maintenance Notes

- Keep one owner for the preset table (`CURSOR_COLOR_PRESETS`); do not copy names into Scene.
- Portability: neutral (Venus Scene and launch).

title: Roll refreshed Eon runtime into Eonova
description:
## Contract Routing

This is the explicitly chosen Eon planning owner for the trackerless Eonova repository. It changes no EON, ORB, VEN, or Nova product contract. It consumes the exact published Eon proof produced by the prerequisite refresh and preserves Eonova's current one-surface x86_64 Linux composition.

Consumer: a local user launching Eonova from its named Nix profile.

Trigger: Eonova evaluates, builds, installs, or launches its exact Eon input.

Result: Eonova pins and packages the refreshed accepted Eon artifact, while retaining the exact current Nova source, Mars-free boundary, one private runtime namespace, wrapper, desktop entry, and existing live generations.

Important failures: an unpublished or unproved Eon source, changed Nova identity, Mars/Rio closure entry, failed package/profile verification, or interrupted live process leaves the rollout incomplete.

## Why

Eonova has no tracker and currently pins Eon `a390fc5c007900c3fc8c9c49df85f9b8acc06d4a`. After Eon accepts the child-source refresh, new Eonova launches must consume that exact immutable Eon proof through the repository's existing pin-only update path. Keeping this as a dependent Bead prevents the Eon implementation run from editing two code-owning repositories.

## Evidence

- Eonova `AGENTS.md`: the repository owns only exact Eon/Nova pins, package, namespace, wrapper, desktop entry, and current-state docs; later work requires an explicitly chosen planning owner.
- Eonova `flake.nix:6-29`: the Eon input and assertion both pin `a390fc5...`.
- Eonova `flake.nix:11-31`: Nova is independently pinned and must remain unchanged.
- Eonova `flake.nix:34-94`: the wrapper, Mars-free package, namespace check, desktop entry, license, and app are existing proof owners.
- Prior closed `eon-refresh-clipboard-runtimes-0pt` shows the accepted exact-pin, lock, build, profile, and live-process-preservation workflow.
- Prerequisite Eon refresh produces the only acceptable new Eon source identity for this rollout.

## Prerequisites and Reference Gate

Required before editing:

- Current Eonova `AGENTS.md`, this complete Bead, `flake.nix`, `flake.lock`, README, LICENSE, desktop/package checks, and current profile/process state.
- The exact published Eon proof from the prerequisite Bead, its graph report, package identity, and accepted child revisions.
- The exact current Nova pin and Mars-free package proof, only to establish preservation.
- The prior Eonova pin refresh mechanism, without copying superseded identities.

Rejected scope:

- Eon, Orbit, Venus, or Nova edits; a second runtime protocol; Eon workspace mode; an updater/channel; new package surfaces; macOS; restarting live supervisors; or changing Eonova identity.

No crate/tool decision is involved.

## Scope

In scope:

- Eonova `flake.nix` exact Eon input/assertion, affected `flake.lock` nodes, current-state README/LOC only if the accepted pin changes documented facts, and the named active `eonova` profile.
- Exact Nix evaluation/build, Mars/Rio closure exclusion, desktop/license/wrapper inspection, installed artifact comparison, and isolated native smoke where needed.
- Preserve the current exact Nova revision and every other package/runtime boundary.

Out of scope:

- Any child repository mutation, Eon implementation, Nova update, new wrapper behavior, workspace mode, runtime protocol, packaging channel, or contract change.

## Implementation Notes

1. Begin only after the Eon refresh publishes and records one immutable accepted proof.
2. Record baseline Eonova HEAD, instruction hash, current Eon/Nova pins, profile artifact, and all live Eonova process PID/start identities.
3. Verify the accepted Eon source and package report, then advance only the Eon input/assertion and affected lock nodes.
4. Run the exact package and boundary checks.
5. Refresh the named profile without stopping or restarting live supervisors, verify the installed artifact, and record that existing generations remain immutable.
6. Update only current-state documentation and LOC if required.

Portability disposition: isolated x86_64 Linux Nix composition; no macOS claim.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Eonova's input, assertion, lockfile, build, and installed profile consume the exact published Eon proof from the prerequisite.
2. The Nova revision and Mars-free package identity are unchanged.
3. The default package/app, wrapper, namespace, desktop entry, icon, and license remain valid.
4. The built closure contains neither Mars nor Rio.
5. The active `eonova` profile resolves to the exact verified artifact.
6. Recorded live Eonova supervisors, Orbit Sessions, and Venus processes retain their PID/start identities through the profile refresh.
7. No child code, runtime semantics, contract, dependency, updater, or unrelated pin changes.
8. README LOC and `git diff --check` pass if documentation changes.

## Verification

- `nix flake check --no-update-lock-file` should exit 0.
- `nix build .#default --no-link --print-out-paths --no-update-lock-file` should produce the exact Eonova artifact.
- Inspect the realized closure for forbidden Mars/Rio paths.
- Validate the desktop entry when `desktop-file-validate` is available; inspect installed licenses and exact wrapper argv.
- Compare the installed profile artifact and embedded Eon identity with the prerequisite proof.
- Compare recorded live process PID/start identities before and after refresh.
- Verify README LOC if changed and run `git diff --check`.
- `br lint <this-id>` and `br sync --flush-only` should pass in the owning Eon tracker.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if the prerequisite Eon proof is not published, accepted, or exact.
- Stop if the current Nova pin changed or the update would pull Mars/Rio into the closure.
- Stop if another active run owns Eonova's flake, lock, profile, or docs.
- Stop rather than interrupting a live supervisor or Session.
- Stop if the update needs behavior beyond an exact child pin and package refresh.

## Maintenance Notes

Eonova remains a thin trackerless composition. This Bead owns only this one rollout; future pin changes need a newly selected planning owner.

title: End the popup card on the sidebar's and columns' bottom edge
description:
Contract: VEN-C18 (a selected popup draws over the column area and preserves its outer side and bottom bounds). No contract text change in this bead.

Problem (Lucca, 2026-10-26, screenshot): with the Agent popup open, the popup card's bottom edge sits below the sidebar card's bottom edge. Column cards and the sidebar already share one painted bottom; only the popup differs.

Cause: column and sidebar paint use `WorkspaceScene::card_rect`, whose bottom is `painted_bottom(...)` (an inset from the allocated bottom, kept clear of the visible grid). The popup outline (render/chrome.rs) and its fill (`card_fill`, scene.rs) use `popup_card_rect`, which runs to the allocated bottom. `scene::tests::popup_outer_chrome_reuses_the_pane_stack_rectangle` even asserts that popup bottom equals `chrome.bottom()`.

Change: the popup card keeps `popup_card_rect`'s top (including its rise on short windows) and takes `card_rect`'s painted bottom, so its outline and fill end on the same edge as the column cards and the sidebar. Presentation-only: no wire, contract, dependency or configuration change. Portability: neutral.

Acceptance: at default and small geometries and scales, the popup card's bottom equals the painted bottom of the column card it replaces and of the sidebar card; the scene test asserts that equality in place of the old chrome-bottom one. Installed check: one isolated dogfood capture showing the popup and sidebar bottoms on one line.

Scope boundary: removing the `[popup]` margin settings is a separate bead (contract change, needs Lucca's approval).
