title: Define Eon's concrete runtime library and assembly contract
description:
## Contract and prerequisite
Sequence step 1 for eon-runtime-extraction-l4wh. No open functional prerequisite. The fourth-repository/library direction is chosen; resolve only the minimum input and ownership details needed for extraction.

Consumer: Eon's actual executable and Nix packager. Trigger: assembling/invoking the selected runtime library. Result: explicit product inputs select existing Eon/EonTerm behavior while runtime has one owner for state and mechanisms. Preserve graph-validation timing, bounded startup errors, exact component compatibility and generation isolation.

## Evidence
Eon baseline cda9662c2cfac092d98a998b3a54c9b0fb4f2b7a, 2026-10-04.
- crates/eon/src/main.rs:1-25 already delegates to nine modules; it owns exit/error projection and directory-picker failure delay.
- supervisor.rs:37/:320/:647/:1423-1425 embeds/queries the graph and reports Eon product version.
- cli.rs:380 uses CARGO_PKG_VERSION; moving it unchanged would report the library version.
- generation.rs:24-53 hashes runtime/protocol/validator/Cargo/graph/Nix bytes; eon-generated-runtime-identity-h4g protects generated managed behavior.
- managed_environment.rs:29-160/:317-346 combines chosen defaults with strict parsing/popup validation.
- eon-manifest's parse_and_validate/version_report/component_revision stay Eon's sole graph authority.

## Scope and design
Document one concrete invocation boundary and necessary immutable inputs: Eon version, validated component report/exact Orbit revision, generation contributions, chosen defaults/popup/provider values, opaque launch inputs. Package version plus exact source pin selects the runtime API; promise no compatibility with arbitrary releases. EONW has its own exact package identity/proof within the same repository, independently selected from the runtime implementation.

Eon keeps canonical graph/validator/schema, chosen policy/default values, packaging and actual executable. Runtime owns workspace/generation transitions, Sessions/control/supervisor/windows/quota mechanisms, CLI mechanics and one strict user-config parser/override owner. Move the nine existing modules together without exposing private operations.

Shell/terminal/Anima defaults, popup catalog, ANSI palette, program fallbacks and Agent preference order are Eon values. Deadlines, wire limits, grammar, permissions and validation bounds stay runtime constraints. Preserve absent/partial config semantics and reread shell config per new Session and terminal config on surface open/reopen; add no merge framework/tuning API.

One generation owner combines runtime/EONW contribution with Eon assembly/default/validator/graph/Cargo/Nix inputs. No reverse source includes, graph copy, store/path identity, mutable config or live state. Retain g1 grammar and historical lifecycle codecs. Define graph-error delivery at the existing required preflight before directories/sockets/children; help/tool/picker paths get no blanket graph requirement. A precomputed validation result is sufficient; no callback framework.

Future edit scope: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, narrowly affected EON-C1/C2/C4/C10/C11 ownership/input entries, necessary development/README links/LOC, local instruction source/render only if ownership conflicts. Label split planned until acceptance. Preserve all existing IDs/guarantees/phases. Do not perform eon-canonical-contract-index-6lck's broad cleanup.

## Package and consumer update contract
Represent runtime library and EONW as distinct logical library components/artifacts in the existing graph, preferably using schema 3. Their source URLs can match while exact revisions differ. Venus depends on EONW, not runtime implementation revision; keep both package versions independent and do not bump either solely for unrelated code or repository relocation.

For the unchanged-package case, require equality of the complete EONW crate content and relevant manifest/dependency/build inputs, plus the accepted package/API/wire proof. Exact pins remain exact. Current eon-manifest Requirement/Interface validation in crates/eon-manifest/src/lib.rs:330-342 compares the named component revision and interface proof; preserve that invariant by targeting the protocol component rather than weakening checks for all components.

Define narrow Nix/Cargo provenance handling: the graph selects the exact codec artifact; any translation from a consumer Git pin to that artifact proves package equivalence before substitution. Do not silently replace it with newer unproved codec content or use SemVer/EONW labels as the oracle.

Document the falsifiers: accepted runtime A -> B with identical EONW package keeps Venus source, Cargo EONW pin and proof unchanged while composition passes and generation changes; changing codec/package inputs under the same labels fails the identity gate. Future codec changes need new owner evidence and explicit affected-consumer acceptance, not automatic compatibility assumptions. Initial provider relocation still requires this plan's one-time rebind.

## Reference gate and dependency decision
Required: full instructions, current contracts and docs/REFERENCES.md composition/generation/managed-environment routes, complete affected callers/config/test paths, closed eon-v28/eon-5rp/eon-validate-component-graph-before-launch-1jd/eon-generated-runtime-identity-h4g/eon-6ux. Comparable direct crate boundary: exact current Orbit protocol consumers and eon-manifest consumer.
Required Cargo shape sources: https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/workspaces.html and https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/specifying-dependencies.html. They inform layout, not product policy.

Use owned Rust library and existing dependencies/toolchain. Reject runtime binary/daemon, generic traits/services, second parser/graph and prolonged incubation. Representation/type names remain implementation choices.

## Acceptance and checks
1. Each retained behavior/input has one owner and current consuming check; source DAG has Eon -> runtime/Orbit/Venus, Venus -> runtime EONW/Orbit, no runtime -> Eon.
2. Interface/generation inputs need no private-operation API, graph copy/parser or library-derived Eon version.
3. Docs distinguish planned/current state; proof phases remain truthful; old-generation presentation limits and exact prior-executable reattachment are explicit.
4. Following tasks have falsifiers for defaults, graph ordering, versions, generation contributions and package identity, including runtime-only advancement with unchanged Venus/EONW pins and rejection of codec drift under unchanged version labels.

Reread br show eon-runtime-extraction-l4wh and this issue; verify changed Markdown paths/contract IDs and README LOC; git diff --check. Render imports only if their sources change. No runtime suite/profile refresh or proof from this documentation stage.

Stop/rebaseline for material owner/contract drift; new feature/protocol/process/dependency/platform/public config requires chosen scope. Effort M; risk LOW-MED; confidence HIGH.

Documentation-only acceptance; extraction remains planned.

title: Separate Eon runtime into a fourth repo and keep Eon assembly thin
description:
## Current disposition — 2026-10-06
Completed and accepted. All seven sequence children are closed. Eon retains product assembly, its canonical component graph and Nix distribution; the independent Eon Runtime repository owns runtime mechanisms and canonical EONW. The accepted cutover is Eon `51666e2fcb925a7d2abde204ac402ecf83d1769f`; later runtime evolution and child adoption remain separately owned.

The current working-tree graph selects Runtime `a57e105a5da87d9c65402c1c4c8ea8b5dc8adc45` independently of EONW `b8f18b4374ca0818a64d9cac6a3fcd02d9f2f2aa`, Orbit `6bc269c40b18f08b95778939518f77556ba91c67`, and Venus `c7a0d07612e710854275a31500aaec651cc50a6f`. The existing uncommitted Venus adoption is separate from this metadata-only closure. Native platform and distribution limits are unchanged.

## Chosen outcome
On 2026-10-04 the user chose a fourth repository after evaluating the thin-orchestrator direction and authorized this planning-only batch. The accepted fourth repository is Yazelix/eon-runtime, with separate eon-runtime and eon-workspace-protocol packages. This is an extraction program, not another decision about whether to split.

The installed Eon and EonTerm products keep their existing commands and behavior. Eon becomes product assembly: its small actual executable supplies product defaults/version, selects components, validates its sole canonical graph, and owns Nix distribution. eon-runtime supplies the cohesive Rust runtime library and EONW package. Orbit retains PTY/session/terminal authority; Venus retains native client authority. No additional daemon or process/wire boundary is introduced.

## Historical evidence and planning baseline
Inspected Eon edge cda9662c2cfac092d98a998b3a54c9b0fb4f2b7a, Venus edge 4b5cc0cf8e5c3567f83d94ac0862adbf0c0e23d1, and Orbit edge 68ad73ff2e466f8d028f664c1079468348eb9949 on 2026-10-04. Rebaseline before implementation; discovery is not runtime proof.
- crates/eon/src/main.rs:1-25 is already thin; closed eon-v28 and eon-5rp established internal modules. Repeating thin-main refactoring would not deliver a thin repository.
- Nine runtime modules still compile in Eon; supervisor.rs:37 embeds its graph and generation.rs:24-53 reaches across runtime, protocol, validator, Cargo, graph and Nix sources.
- Venus Cargo.toml:10 pins EONW from Eon f41a41c9aecc4c436edfa2f394b832aa6d8711ad. Its protocol tree equals current Eon's: 8409c419a3496d6f01eeef65295f5d95b943313e.

## Ownership and fixed constraints
Eon keeps components/eon-alpha-v3.json, eon-manifest implementation/schema/validation, product version and chosen defaults, actual executable/error exit handling, assets, Nix graph translation and distribution. Runtime receives explicit validated facts and immutable product inputs, with no dependency back on Eon.

Move cli, codex_quota, control, generation, managed_environment, sessions, supervisor, windows and workspace together; retain internal invariant owners. Runtime owns their mechanisms and strict user-config parsing, not a second product graph or defaults owner. EONW moves with runtime, retaining package identity and v2-v7 exports/bytes. Product diagnostics report Eon's supplied version separately from the runtime component version.

One generation owner covers immutable runtime/EONW inputs plus Eon assembly/defaults/graph/validator/Cargo/Nix projection inputs. Store paths, mutable user config and live state are not identity. Moving source intentionally changes generation. Exact graph comparison can refuse new-client presentation of old generations; keep historical discovery and owner-routed Stop, and preserve old work with its exact prior executable.

## Independent package acceptance
On 2026-10-04 the user approved this refinement: runtime implementation changes that leave EONW unchanged do not require a new Venus source revision or EONW pin. The initial provider move still requires the one-time Venus rebind in this sequence.

Treat eon-runtime and eon-workspace-protocol as separate logical package identities in the existing canonical graph, with one fourth-repository owner. Exact source pins/proofs remain mandatory; runtime source R1 and Venus's codec source P0 may be different commits of that repository. Record package name/version, exact provenance, EONW wire/API proof and unchanged package content including manifest and relevant dependency/build inputs. Matching version labels alone is insufficient.

Prefer existing schema-3 library component records for these package identities; keep exact requirement checks scoped to the named package. Do not weaken revision equality globally, duplicate the graph, create a fifth repo, invent a compatibility resolver or force coupled version bumps. Nix supplies the graph-selected exact codec artifact; any source substitution must prove package equivalence before compiling it.

Acceptance includes an A/B composition: advance only the accepted runtime implementation revision while retaining Venus source and its exact EONW pin/proof; unchanged codec identity permits the build and runtime generation changes. Package drift under unchanged version labels fails closed. This does not relax exact old-generation Present, add protocol negotiation, promise mixed-version compatibility or eliminate composed runtime/package proof.

## Completed sequence
1. eon-runtime-contract-26eu — Define Eon's concrete runtime library and assembly contract.
2. eon-runtime-product-inputs-1dbd — Make the current runtime consume Eon-owned product inputs.

## Independent producer identities

description:
## Contract and prerequisite
Sequence step 2 for eon-runtime-extraction-l4wh, blocked by eon-runtime-contract-26eu.
Consumer: Eon's current real executable. Trigger: invocation of existing runtime modules. Result: one Eon assembly owner supplies concrete product facts/defaults to the existing runtime, preserving commands, config semantics, graph-error timing and generation isolation. This proves the semantic seam before changing crates or repositories.

## Evidence and scope
At Eon cda9662c2cfac092d98a998b3a54c9b0fb4f2b7a, supervisor.rs:37/:320/:647/:1423-1425 owns graph queries/product-version reporting, generation.rs:24-53 includes both owners' sources, and managed_environment.rs:29-160/:317-346 combines product defaults with strict parsing. main.rs is already 25 lines; do not repeat its earlier modularization.

Keep all nine runtime modules in crates/eon for this task. Implement the accepted concrete invocation inputs within the current crate, not a new library, adapter or generic host API. Eon assembly owns eon-manifest/graph validation, product version, immutable product-generation contribution and chosen values. Runtime receives the validated report/exact Orbit revision, supplied Eon version, immutable contribution, concrete defaults and opaque launch inputs.

Move shell/terminal/Anima defaults, popup catalog, palette, program fallbacks and Agent preference order to the Eon assembly owner. Runtime retains its single strict config parser, override application, popup validation and per-Session/surface rereads. Missing files/sections/fields inherit the supplied defaults; unknown fields and invalid overrides still fail. Deadlines, wire limits, grammar, permissions and validation bounds stay runtime constraints.

Remove graph parsing/querying and reverse Eon assembly/graph/validator/Cargo/Nix source includes from runtime modules. One runtime generation owner combines its runtime/EONW contribution with the Eon-supplied contribution, including actual executable/defaults/validator/graph/Cargo/Nix and generated shell/private-command behavior. Exclude store/path identity, mutable config and live state; retain g1 grammar. Deliver graph errors at existing required preflight before owner directories, sockets or children; help/tool/picker paths get no blanket validation. Precomputed validation results are sufficient.

EONW remains the unchanged local package, including v2-v7. No new crate/repo, component selection, child revision or library-version claim here. Necessary owner docs/README LOC follow current implementation; broader contract-index cleanup is independent.

## Reference and dependency gate
Read accepted eon-runtime-contract-26eu, all affected callers/config/tests, docs/REFERENCES.md composition/generation/managed-environment routes, current affected EON-C1-C4/C8-C23 phases, and closed eon-v28/eon-5rp/eon-validate-component-graph-before-launch-1jd/eon-generated-runtime-identity-h4g/eon-6ux. ## Acceptance and proof
1. Actual Eon/EonTerm commands consume supplied product facts/defaults; runtime modules contain no graph/schema/parser copy or reverse assembly source include. Product values have one assembly owner; parser/state/invariants have one runtime owner.
2. Existing actual-binary process checks preserve graph failure before effects, native/terminal rejection before Session creation, alias/window/picker ordering and existing lifecycle behavior.
3. Consuming checks cover absent/partial config, overrides, unknown-field errors, popup validation and Session/surface rereads. Test supplied non-default values through the parser/launch effects rather than mirroring literals.
4. Disposable assembled A/B artifacts retain stable generation for identical inputs and change generation plus consuming behavior for Eon-default-only and generated-shell/private-command-only changes. Runtime/EONW inputs stay fixed. Source movement may change generation; do not promise identity continuity.
5. CLI and EONW snapshots use the supplied Eon product version. Unequal library/product versions and runtime-only generation changes are proved after the library exists in eon-runtime-seam-2tes.

Use the full affected Rust and Nix route once per unchanged candidate: existing workspace checks/process suite, graph validator, both default/eonterm builds and flake checks. Add only missing assembly-boundary falsifiers with TDD where deterministic. Refresh the active eon profile from the accepted current-tree artifact, verify store equality and one isolated installed native Linux Wayland observation of the changed inputs covering both products; preserve live supervisors/Sessions and focus. Record exact revisions/artifact/environment/result/phase; metadata follow-ups reuse proof. Profile failure leaves this task incomplete.

Scope excludes library/source relocation, producer creation, wire/API feature changes, generic configuration, platform/channel work and unrelated runtime improvements. Stop/rebaseline for material contract drift or needed live interruption. Effort M; risk MED-HIGH; confidence HIGH.

title: Remove separate-repository residue from Eon Runtime
description:
## Decision
Lucca, 2026-10-15: keep the `eon`/`eon-runtime` crate split (chosen in `eon-monorepo-2oko` for agent
legibility) and remove what is left over from Runtime being a separate repository.

## Contract
Generation identity has one owner for its source inputs, and the architecture doc describes the
current runtime boundary rather than its extraction history. Users see no change except that the
next build selects a new generation, as any build change does.

## Evidence (edge 068efcb)
- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/generation.rs:28-47` hand-lists Runtime and EONW source files with
`include_bytes!`, while `eon/crates/eon/build.rs` already digests every in-tree source file into the
assembly contribution. In the monorepo the hand list is a duplicate that can silently go stale when
a module is added.
- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:262-375` ("Runtime library boundary") is largely extraction and cutover
history; its acceptance table cites closed extraction beads. `docs/CONTRACTS.md` says history
belongs in Beads and Git.
- `runtime/README.md` describes the self-hash and transfer provenance.

## Slices
1. Make the assembly digest the only source-input hash; keep Runtime as owner of the generation
algorithm and `g1-` format. Update `runtime/README.md`, the architecture text and any contract text
naming the self-hash (check EON-C3 and EON-C11; a contract edit needs Lucca's approval).
2. Reduce `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` "Runtime library boundary" to current-state facts.

Not included unless Lucca chooses: removing `eon-runtime` from `components/eon-alpha-v3.json`
(component graph, EON-C2), and moving `json_escape` out of `workspace.rs`.

## Acceptance
Slice 1 touches the generation and lifecycle boundary: full affected Rust and Nix surfaces in the
isolated sandbox; prove stable identity for identical inputs, a new identity after a Runtime-only
change, and that an older generation stays discoverable and stoppable; refresh the active Nix
profile without restarting live work. Slice 2 is docs-only proof.

## Stop boundary
No change to the crate split, EONW, Orbit or Venus.

title: Move the proved runtime behind Eon's local Rust library

title: Publish an Eon config schema and edit configuration with Ratconfig

## Why

Approved as "configurable later" (`eon-configurability-audit-twdr`, Lucca, 2026-10-23). Ratconfig
is pinned (`eon-v4.json:332-347`, `flake.nix:26`, `:650`), but no crate uses it, and there is no

and defaults (`runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/managed_environment.rs:23-135`,
`eon/crates/eon/src/product.rs`).

## Shape

Runtime generates one schema from its own config table, for example `eon config schema --json`
with key, type, default, bounds and doc. Ratconfig reads it, and validation stays in Runtime. The
same schema serves agents under the Humans and Agents rule. Contract owners: EON-C4 (Thin orchestrator ownership, which lists Ratconfig as a consumer)
and a new configuration-editing contract.

## Why deferred

It is a consequential shape (dependency and integration). It follows the docs coverage test
child, which first proves the key enumeration.

title: Add one sandboxed test command for humans and agents
description:
## Decision
Lucca, 2026-10-15: give humans and agents one checked-in command that runs Eon's Rust test suites
in the isolated sandbox `AGENTS.md` requires.

## Contract
- Consumer: a maintainer or coding agent, including one working inside a live Eon terminal.
- Trigger: one documented command from the repository root, accepting extra cargo arguments.
- Result: the suites run with private PID, network, `/dev` and `/tmp` namespaces, an empty
`XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` with no Wayland or D-Bus, a cleared environment keeping only toolchain variables,
and `FONTCONFIG_FILE` set to the packaged Venus font configuration. Live Eon windows and terminals
are unaffected.
- Important failures: missing user-namespace support or toolchain reports a clear error and runs
nothing outside the sandbox.

## Evidence
- `AGENTS.md` (Testing Discipline) describes the sandbox only in prose; flake apps are `default`,
`eonterm` and `record-demo` (`flake.nix:615-627`).
- 2026-10-14 incident: running `cargo test --locked --workspace` from a live Eon terminal coincided
with the live Venus window and the agent dying. A working bubblewrap recipe passed all 339 tests:
`--die-with-parent --new-session --unshare-all --ro-bind / / --dev /dev --proc /proc --tmpfs /tmp
--tmpfs /run/user/<uid>`, read-write binds for only the repository and `~/.cargo`, `--clearenv`
with PATH, HOME=/tmp/home, CARGO_HOME, RUSTUP_HOME, USER, LANG and XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/tmp/run.
- Nix package builds already run selected tests in the Nix build sandbox (`cargoTestFlags` at
`flake.nix:211,252,422`); that path is slower and is not the edit-test loop.

## Owner and shape
Nix owns the command (a flake app or dev-shell command); the bubblewrap call is irreducible process
glue, so a small shell wrapper is acceptable under the language rules. bubblewrap comes from the
pinned nixpkgs: record it under the dependency gate. x86_64 Linux only; name the platform limit.

## Acceptance
- From inside a live Eon terminal, the command runs the full workspace suite (and the installer
suite) green while the live window and its terminals stay up.
- `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md` and the Testing Discipline rule (via `.agent-protocols.local.md` and a
render) point to the command instead of describing the sandbox.

## Stop boundary
No hosted CI change and no test-harness framework.
close_reason: nix develop -c eon-test runs the workspace and installer suites in bubblewrap; 347/0/7 from inside a live Eon terminal with the session untouched; docs and AGENTS.md point to it.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
## Implementation record (2026-10-15)

Shape: `nix/test-sandbox.nix` owns `eon-test`, a writeShellApplication on the default dev shell, run as `nix develop -c eon-test [cargo test args]`. The dev shell now shares Orbit's and Venus's existing build environment through single bindings (`ghosttyBuildEnv`, `venusBuildInputs`, `venusFontsConf`) and adds Zig, ncurses and pkg-config, so builds use the pinned Ghostty source instead of cloning it. `cargo fetch --locked` (workspace and installer) runs first outside the sandbox; it builds nothing. The sandbox: `--unshare-all`, read-only `/`, private `/dev` and `/proc`, empty `/tmp` and `/run`, writable repository, CARGO_HOME and any target directory, HOME and a 0700 XDG_RUNTIME_DIR under the private /tmp, `--clearenv` plus a toolchain allowlist, and a PATH without Eon's managed `*/libexec/eon/bin` wrappers. Guards stop with a clear error outside the dev shell (no GHOSTTY_SOURCE_DIR/FONTCONFIG_FILE/cargo) or without user namespaces. `AGENTS.md` Testing Discipline (via `.agent-protocols.local.md`, rendered and checked with Starcompass at the pinned 4af5a32) and the development docs point to the command; `nix/test-sandbox.nix` owns the isolation.

Dependency gate: capability is unprivileged namespace isolation for one process tree. bubblewrap 0.11.2 from the pinned nixpkgs (567a49d1913ce81ac6e9582e3553dd90a955875f), no new flake input. Rejected: the Nix build sandbox (already runs selected package tests, but rebuilds from scratch and forbids set-ID chmod Orbit's suite needs), `unshare(1)` (needs hand-built mounts, more shell), systemd-run scopes (systemd dependency the platform rules forbid), containers/firejail (heavier, extra daemon or setuid). Replacement cost: one small file. Exit: drop it if a Rust-owned harness or upstream test isolation replaces it. Platform: x86_64 Linux; proved on a non-NixOS host (Pop!_OS kernel 7.1.5); on NixOS the hidden /run hides /run/current-system and /run/wrappers (documented). Portability disposition: isolated Linux dependency.

Refactor check: `nix derivation show` gives identical `yazelix-orbit` (qh46awyq…) and `yazelix-venus` (hmchvhcg…) derivations at HEAD f916b56/e11bbef and in the working tree; `eon`/`eonterm` change only because `flake.nix` is in their source set.

Proof (revision = this commit; x86_64 Linux, run from inside Lucca's live Eon terminal, Venus pid 4639 with six Orbit processes): final tree `nix develop -c eon-test` passed 347, failed 0, ignored 7 across 21 targets (workspace and installer) in 1m16s; `eon-test -p eon-manifest` and `eon-test --manifest-path installer/Cargo.toml` (7 passed) green; the live Venus process and all Orbit PIDs were unchanged after every run. A sandbox probe showed empty /run, no system D-Bus socket, private PID 1, no network, zero EON_/WAYLAND/DBUS variables and plain /usr/bin/bash. The guard outside the dev shell toolchain prints its error and exits 1.

Observed flake (not caused by this change): one intermediate full run failed `yazelix-orbit` `platform::tests::management_ready_claim_has_one_winner_and_survives_record_removal` with WouldBlock. 30/30 isolated runs and 5/5 Orbit binary suite runs then passed, and four later full runs passed. Likely cause: a parallel test forking while `RecordGuard::publish` holds its O_CLOEXEC flock claim, so the child briefly shares the lock. A separate Orbit bead is proposed to Lucca (pending decision), including whether the server path shares the race.

Review ledger: 7 passes; findings 7, 5, 5, 3, 4, 1, 0. Fixed: /run masking for the system D-Bus socket, guards before fetching, target-dir binds and relative paths, env values ending in `=`, Eon wrapper PATH, coreutils input, installer fetch, toolchain guard, TERM dropped, one sandbox owner in docs, display-test exception, stale doc pointers. Declined: filtering by EON_SESSION_BIN (only set in Eon terminals; the glob covers both), editing proof commands in contract indexes (historical evidence), Nix daemon socket reachability (outside the contract; no Eon socket lives there).

title: Record a scripted native Wayland Eon demo
description:
## Outcome

Consumer: a visitor to Eon, Eon Sessions, or Eon Desktop project documentation. Trigger: opening the README demo. Result: a real, scripted recording of the current Nix-only Linux alpha on an isolated native Wayland display, with a readable poster and links from the three READMEs. The recording shows the composed product; child captions identify Orbit as terminal authority and Venus as renderer. No product contract changes.

The recipe must be reproducible from pinned tools and the canonical Eon package, avoid the live desktop and Sessions, use a clean temporary home/runtime, and contain no account, credential, or private terminal content. Kinestra may gain the minimum native Wayland display, input, and capture support needed; it remains a recording-time tool outside the installed alpha.

## Scope and references

Kinestra source at its accepted revision, its recorder API and Nix mkRecorder pattern, and local headless Sway/grim/wf-recorder observations are required references. Keep the Eon component manifest and exact Orbit/Venus pins unchanged. Add one source-owned recipe, one video/poster pair, and concise README entry points; do not add product behavior, a release channel, or screenshots of the live user desktop.

## Acceptance

Run the recipe against the built Eon package under a private headless Wayland compositor. Verify video decodes, has the expected frame size and useful action sequence; visually inspect poster and representative frames; verify all three README links resolve, media contains no private state, LOC scorecards reconcile, and git diff --check passes. Preserve unrelated Eon Beads work. Package or profile refresh is required only if the installed Eon artifact changes.

title: Send at most one outstanding scroll preview while output keeps arriving
description:
## Problem

During an active Venus terminal scroll (wheel, trackpad or momentum), every frame Venus drains rebases the scroll and clears its preview (venus/src/scroll.rs:216-224, 266; venus/src/model.rs:333). `drive_terminal_scroll` (venus/src/application.rs:3479) then sends a new `PreviewVertical` for that frame revision. `preview_pending` only suppresses a resend for the same revision, so while a program prints, Venus sends one preview request per frame and several can be outstanding. Orbit answers each with a `VerticalPreview` between its frames. Found while diagnosing eon-10qt. That bead made a full event queue apply backpressure, so this flood no longer drops the attachment, but it still wastes round trips and queue slots during output bursts.

## Expected

At most one outstanding preview per scroll gesture or batch. A newer frame supersedes a pending preview without sending a new request per revision, and scroll feel stays the same.

## Contract

VEN-C7 (authoritative history and selection interaction). Keep the existing scroll behavior; no contract text change is expected. If one turns out to be needed, stop for Lucca's approval.

## Prerequisites

eon-10qt landed.

## Scope

In scope: Venus scroll preview request pacing in venus/src/scroll.rs and application.rs, plus a focused regression. Out of scope: Orbit wire or Orbit queue changes, and the eon-10qt queue.

## Acceptance

- A Venus suite check: a scroll active across N frame revisions sends at most one outstanding PreviewVertical.
- Existing scroll tests stay green.
- One isolated installed observation: wheel scrolling while a program prints a burst feels unchanged.

## Portability disposition

neutral.
close_reason: Venus keeps one scroll preview outstanding across frames, with a 50 ms retry after a frame that may have replaced its answer; tests, review loop and installed A/B recorded

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Design (2026-10-27, implementing session in worktree /home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/hhzy at base db378f4).

Cause: TerminalScroll::preview_pending named the frame revision the request was sent for, and every plain Frame called rebase(), which cleared it. While output kept arriving, drive_terminal_scroll sent one PreviewVertical per frame revision until an answer landed. ORB-C8 says a lagging preview resolves against current authority and its answer "names the current authoritative revision whose state it inspected", so answers rarely matched the per-revision marker either. Under DEC 2026 Orbit holds at most one unresolved vertical request and fails a second with InvalidInput ("vertical interaction is already deferred"), which Venus treats as a scroll failure and resets the gesture.

Fix (venus/src/application/scroll.rs, venus/src/application.rs):
- preview_pending becomes a bool: set when PreviewVertical is written, cleared only by its answer (any VerticalPreview; at most one is outstanding and Orbit answers in order) or by reset() (send failure, server Failure, reconnect, lost attachment).
- next_request sends nothing, preview or ScrollVertical, while a preview is outstanding, so a newer frame never adds a request. When the answer lands, a stale-revision answer that the model drops leaves exactly one fresh request for the current revision.
- cancel() keeps the outstanding flag, like the written batch it already preserves, so a new gesture after a cancel waits for the old answer.
- rebase() and its plain-frame call are removed; accept_batch no longer clears the flag (a batch and a preview are never outstanding together now).
- active() no longer counts the outstanding preview: pixels, velocity and a pending batch already cover a live gesture, and a cancelled gesture must stay inactive while its answer is in flight (link surface, redraw and model preview clearing keep their behaviour).

Reference gate: not consequential under AP-REFERENCE-001 as AGENTS.md defines it. No dependency, protocol or wire format, contract, lifecycle, security or trust boundary changes; it only paces Venus's requests within the existing ORBS v13 vertical exchange. VEN-C7 text unchanged. Portability: neutral.

Regression: venus unit test terminal_scroll_keeps_one_preview_outstanding_across_frames (10 frame revisions send one PreviewVertical; a stale answer leaves one fresh request; cancel keeps the hold; reset clears it). The existing coalescing test asserted one preview per revision (9, then 10 after rebase); it now asserts the second waits for the answer.

Known residual (unchanged): a server Failure that answers some other request resets the scroll and clears the flag while the preview answer is still in flight, so one extra request can overlap briefly.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Review record (2026-10-27).

Converge after the plan change: round 1 (fresh Claude) deleted a duplicated segment of the old coalescing test, which the new regression already covers; checks green. Round 2 (fresh Claude) was clean on fixed tree 184ed264e6ea39af93f563666d105310e8933863: no edits, Venus suites 221 passed / 5 ignored, fmt and clippy -D warnings clean, tree unchanged.

Narrow Codex re-check (f0f91c02 -> 184ed264): it found the replaced-answer recovery sound (including output stopping right after), no busy loop at the deadline, and the opposite-direction late answer handled. One finding [P2], accepted as a residual and corrected here:

Correction to the plan-change comment. The 50 ms retry is not limited to output backpressure. A frame already in flight when Venus writes the preview can start the grace. If Orbit then holds the request under DEC 2026 synchronized output for more than 50 ms, the retry overlaps it. Orbit fails the retry with InvalidInput "vertical interaction is already deferred", and Venus shows the Orbit notice and resets the gesture, losing its distance and momentum. Base Venus had the same exposure on the very next frame, without the 50 ms wait, so this change narrows it and does not add it.

Why it stays here: Venus cannot tell a replaced answer from a held one, because Orbit's OutputQueue may drop an unsent preview answer for a newer frame. venus/AGENTS.md says to report an insufficient Orbit contract to Orbit instead of compensating in the client, and this bead excludes Orbit queue changes. Follow-up: eon-preview-answer-survives-frames-u979, which keeps unsent preview answers across frames so Venus can drop the timer.

Accepted residuals, complete list:
- A DEC 2026 hold of more than 50 ms after an in-flight frame can make the retry fail and reset the gesture. Base had this sooner. Follow-up 4ry3.
- A server Failure or a local InvalidInput for some other message, or a same-direction late answer from a retained column, can release the hold early. Each costs one extra request at most.
- If an answer really was replaced, a gesture's first preview can start up to about 50 ms later than in base.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Review round 1 on candidate tree f0f91c02fb3d3ea4e82958e1a73be696bdf77d84 (2026-10-27): fresh Claude reviewer reported nothing blocking (checks green, tree unchanged). Codex (gpt-6.1-sol, xhigh) reported two blocking findings, both accepted:

1. [P1] Orbit's client OutputQueue (orbit/src/socket.rs:215-266) lets a newer Frame or ScrollOutcome replace a VerticalPreview it has not started writing. Under output backpressure an answer can vanish while the attachment stays healthy, so the candidate's hold (cleared only by an answer or a reset) could stay set forever and stop all scrolling. The design comment's claim "Orbit answers each PreviewVertical once" was wrong. This is also why the base code re-armed on every frame.
2. [P2] A terminal still visible in another column keeps its transport when the selected pane moves (set_orbit_attachment keeps the outgoing connection; owes_viewport looks only at pending_viewport). Switching away and back before an old preview answer lands let that late answer release a newer request in the other direction.

Change of plan (relying on Lucca's standing approval, relayed by eon-overseer: Lucca, 2026-10-26, "everything is pre-approved. autonomous." and "also pre-aprove changes of plan if a clearly better alternative appears"; applied here to the pacing mechanism within this bead's scope, venus/src/application/scroll.rs and application.rs; no contract text adopted or changed, VEN-C7 and ORB-C8 unchanged):

Venus cannot tell from a frame whether Orbit dropped the answer, and the wire stays as is (out of scope). So the hold is released by the answer in the requested direction, by reset(), or by a fixed grace after the first frame that follows the request:
- preview_pending is Option<(direction, first frame after the request)>.
- frame_arrived(now) records the first frame-class message (Frame, WheelOutcome::Viewport, ScrollOutcome::Viewport) after the request.
- PREVIEW_ANSWER_GRACE = 50 ms after that frame, retry_preview(now) drops the hold. about_to_wait checks it each loop turn and drives the scroll, and preview_retry_at() joins the event-loop deadlines, so a dropped answer is retried even if output stops after the replacing frame.
- preview_arrived(direction) releases only for an answer in the requested direction (fixes the P2 scenario); a same-direction late answer from a retained column can still release early, which costs at most one extra request and never a stuck hold.

Effect: while output keeps arriving, Venus sends at most one PreviewVertical per answer or per 50 ms grace, instead of one per frame revision. If an answer really was replaced, a gesture's first preview can start up to ~50 ms later than base, which re-asked on the next frame; this only happens under Orbit output backpressure.

Configurability: PREVIEW_ANSWER_GRACE stays fixed. It is internal request pacing within the ORB-C8 exchange, felt only as a start latency under backpressure, and a setting would cost more support than users could gain by differing.

Regression extended: terminal_scroll_keeps_one_preview_outstanding_across_frames now also covers frames inside the grace (no resend), the grace retry after a frame (exactly one new request), the direction-mismatched late answer, cancel keeping the hold, and failure/reset clearing it.

Accepted residuals: a server Failure or local InvalidInput for some other message, or a same-direction late answer from a retained column, can release the hold early; each costs one extra request at most.

title: Square the sheet's bottom corners and thicken its top border
description:
## Decision
Lucca, 2026-10-17, looking at the installed round corners: 'make the top borders of the main area thicker' and 'fix the bottom corners, they should be flush instead of this' (screenshot: the footer's rounded lower-left corner left a wedge inside the window corner). The sheet's bottom corners become square, flush with the window's bottom corners (the footer, and the sheet itself when hints are hidden); only the top corners stay rounded. The sheet's top border, including its rounded corners, becomes 2 px; seams, separators and side edges below the corner curves stay 1 px. The popup frame reuses the sheet and follows both changes.

## Contract (edits approved by this decision)
EON-C8, VEN-C8, EON-C24, VEN-C24, VEN-C18 if needed, PRESENTATION.md and changelogs: square lower corners on the window's bottom corners; 2 px top border. Footer hints return to the plain edge padding (no bottom corner to clear); header labels clear only the top corners.

## Acceptance
Venus suites, fmt, clippy, nix build; isolated capture with hints shown and hidden and a popup; review loop; profile refresh.

## Scope boundary
Bottom corner shape and top border weight only; no color, radius or tab change.
close_reason: Bottom corners square and flush on the window corners; 2 px top edge and curves; popups follow. Proof and ledger in comments.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Proof (x86_64 Linux, nix develop): eon-test -p yazelix-venus lib 91 / 1 ignored, bin 51 / 4 ignored, canonical_scene 18; the footer hint test asserts the plain edge padding again; cargo fmt --check and clippy --locked --all-targets -D warnings green for yazelix-venus; nix build .#default -> /nix/store/lanlbz378q4iazvvlk0cs6a3x2yq0xrr-eon-0.1.1 (code identical to this commit; later edits were comments, a test message and docs). Isolated capture on that artifact (private headless Sway 1.12, 1280x720): the footer's bottom-left pixel and both edges at x=0 and y=719 are border color (square, flush corner); the top edge rows 34 and 35 are both border color (2 px) with the curves thickened, also on the Project popup frame. Mechanism: WorkspaceScene::sheet_shape extends the sheet below the window so only its top corners round; RectangleBatch::push_sheet_border draws the outline, a second inner stroke clipped to the top band and a square bottom edge; the footer draws square. Review ledger: 2 passes (Codex gpt-6.1-sol read-only). Pass 1: frameless clause still promised a rounded footer; stale lower-curve wording in a scene comment, REFERENCES.md, a test message and C24 (fixed, text). title: Round the workspace sheet's outer corners to the header height
description:
## Decision
Lucca, 2026-10-17 ('yeah, i love it', after the schematic mockup): the workspace sheet's outer corners use a radius equal to the pane header height, so the top curve meets the window's side edge exactly at the first header's bottom separator. The bottom corners use the footer height (with hints hidden too, for symmetry). The first header's label and the footer hints move right enough to clear the curve (about 8 px at default typography). Rule kept: objects round, dividers straight; the sheet, as the outermost container, carries the largest radius.

## Contract (edits approved by this decision)
- Sheet outer corners: top radius = pane header height, bottom radius = footer height; they scale with typography. Seams, separators and inner header edges stay straight.
- Header fills, the pane-focus outline where it touches an outer corner, the popup outer frame and the footer follow the same corners.
- The outer columns' first header label and the footer hints inset clear of the curve; terminal grids, hit targets and other headers are unchanged.
- pane_frames = false keeps its current inset shapes.
- Wording: VEN-C8, EON-C8 (and C24 where they name the footer corners), PRESENTATION.md, USAGE.md and INTERACTION.md, plus changelogs.

## Prerequisites
After eon-flush-sheet-bottom-f68t (same frame code).

## Acceptance
Venus suites, fmt, clippy and nix build green; one isolated installed capture at one and several columns, hints shown and hidden, with a popup; review loop; profile refresh.

## Scope boundary
Corner radii and the label/hint insets they require only; no color, typography or configuration change.
close_reason: Sheet corners rounded to the first header's height with the first tab pill centered over the top-left curve; labels, pill and hints clear the curves; one clamped radius owner. Proof and 7-pass ledger in comments.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Decision addition, Lucca 2026-10-17 ('maybe it's worth aligning the first tab position and roundness to be somewhat symmetrical to the pane round border'), shaped by the main session after a mockup: the first tab's pill arc is centered over the sheet's top-left corner arc (first tab left edge = sheet corner radius - tab pill radius, about 16 px at default typography, which also matches the inset header label). Proposed alongside, pending Lucca's objection: mirror it on the right so the rightmost header control's arc is centered over the top-right corner arc.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Scope, Lucca 2026-10-17: 'we just need to align the first tab pill'. The right-side control mirror is dropped; only the first tab pill moves so its arc is centered over the sheet's top-left corner arc.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Implementation note (main session, 2026-10-17): the first capture showed only p1's label inset, out of line with p2 and the terminal text. Label clearance is now measured at the text's vertical middle (the line box's ascender space overlapped the curve while the glyphs cleared it), so at default and normal padding no header label moves; tight padding still insets the corner header. The popup label uses the same rule; footer hints keep the stricter text-box rule because their modifier badges are filled boxes.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Review pass 1 (Codex gpt-6.1-sol read-only + Claude), all fixed in code: (1) focus outline top/bottom strokes crossed the curves when a focused header scrolled into a corner (now the column's sheet shape cut to one row, like separators); (2) in tiny windows fills, outlines and the footer clamped to different radii than the sheet (now one owner, WorkspaceScene::corner_radius, clamps once, and seam_extended/footer bar extend by twice the radius so no shape clamps further); (3) the tab offset ignored tab_max_width and fitting, overflowing a max-width tab by about 9 px (tab_lead now feeds tab_max_width, and narrow strips without room for the offset plus a minimum tab keep the old gap); (4) long popup labels could cross the top-right curve (both sides now clear it); (5) the filled scrollback pill could cross the top-right curve at large typography (it uses box-based clearance, header_corner_insets extent = half the header). Text: changelog said the tab sits under the curve (now 'centered over'); hint test now asserts the exact side inset; frameless footer and popup radius documented; rewraps. Numbers corrected: radius = pane header height - pane_inset/2 (25 px at default; top curve meets the window side at the first header's bottom); first tab offset about 13 px; footer hints move about 1 px; header labels do not move at default padding. Accepted: every tab shifts right with the first one; footer and popup outlines keep the sheet radius when pane_frames = false.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Review pass 2 (Codex gpt-6.1-sol read-only + Claude), fixed in code: (1) a long label could overlap the scrollback pill moved off the top-right curve (the label now reserves the pill's corner inset when the pill shows; the pill uses its own half height, metrics.height/2, for clearance); (2) columns narrower than the radius (shrunk windows, large typography) let curves leave the outer column (the scene now computes one corner_radius clamped to half the sheet and the narrowest column, stored on WorkspaceScene); (3) first-tab alignment used undrawn radii (it now uses the stored corner radius and the pill's drawn, clamped and floored radius; tab_max_width keeps an estimate that is never smaller than the laid-out lead). Accepted: the framed pane-focus outline is square except where it touches the sheet's outer corners, matching the header fills, which are square at seams (it was a separate padding-radius rounded rectangle); with pane_frames = false every tab still shifts with the first, since scene geometry does not depend on frames; the footer hint inset uses the unclamped radius (only more conservative).

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Review pass 3 (Codex gpt-6.1-sol read-only + Claude). Fixed in code: in short windows the top curves ran into the footer (the stored corner radius is also clamped to the space above the footer); a tab-width estimate could disagree with the drawn pill at unusual line heights (tab_max_width is back to its original formula, which supersedes the pass-2 estimate; the first tab aligns only when it fits beside the offset, else keeps the old gap). title: Make the workspace sheet's top corners straight
description:
## Decision
Lucca, 2026-10-17, after seeing the installed result: 'the rounded corners of the top border of the main area actually look bad; lets give up for now and just make it straight'. The sheet's top corners become square like its bottom corners; the 2 px top edge stays. With the radius at zero, the first tab returns to the ordinary gap and no label, pill or popup label needs corner clearance.

## Contract (edits approved by this decision)
EON-C8, VEN-C8, VEN-C18 if it mentions corners, PRESENTATION.md, LAUNCH.md and changelogs drop the rounded top corners, the first-tab alignment and the corner-clearance and scrollback-pill exceptions.

## Mechanism
WorkspaceScene's single corner radius becomes 0; the drawing, clearance and first-tab paths keep following it, so nothing else changes. The rounded-radius computation is deleted (git history keeps it for a later revisit).

## Acceptance
Venus suites, fmt, clippy, nix build; isolated capture; review; profile refresh.
close_reason: Sheet top corners square; 2 px top edge kept; first tab back at the ordinary gap. Proof and ledger in comments.

title: Fill the sidebar row of the agent terminal that has keyboard focus
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-10-23, looking at the agent sidebar's popup markers: "it was supposed to highlight the
row of the agent my keyboard is focused on?". Today no row marks the agent whose terminal has
keyboard focus. VEN-C30's row highlight (venus/src/scene.rs ~130, "The keyboard-focused row's target
while the sidebar holds focus") only follows the sidebar's own F6 or arrow navigation, plus mouse
hover. The tab heading's "popup shown" glyph (from eon-agent-sidebar-yx8.16) is the only
current-state mark, and it is small and a line away from the row it concerns.

Approved by Lucca, 2026-10-23 ("yes to everything", answering the overseer's items 1 and 2):
replace the heading's popup-shown glyph with a "you are here" fill on the row of the agent terminal
that has keyboard focus, panes and popups alike; keep the always-on popup glyph on rows
(eon-popup-marker-always-52rk). File now; start after eon-orbit-stop-not-reaped-7vb4 and
eon-reap-error-unstopped-hfzr.

## Change

- The sidebar row whose source terminal has keyboard focus in the active tab (a pane or the shown
  popup) gets a "you are here" fill: a faint accent (mint) tint, about 10-15% of
  `accent`, distinct from the navy `selected` fill used for hover and sidebar navigation. Hover and
  sidebar-focus highlight and outline draw over it unchanged. Rows in other tabs never get it.
- If that terminal has several records, the one row it leads carries the fill.
- The tab heading no longer ends with the popup-shown glyph, and its accessible label drops
  "popup shown". The current row's accessible label adds a state such as "current" (pick the word
  with the AccessKit convention used elsewhere in Venus; record it).
- Rows keep the popup glyph after their catalog label, as 52rk made them.

## Contract (VEN-C30; wording to Lucca through the overseer before code)

Replace the heading half of the "Popup marker" bullet, and add a "Current row" bullet. Draft the
exact text in the bead.

## Configurability

The tint derives from the theme's accent. It becomes themeable through eon-eon-themes-or3q; record
that as the configuration route rather than adding a separate setting.

## Acceptance

- A Venus scene test: with keyboard focus on a pane agent's terminal, its row carries the
  current-row state and no other row does; with the Agent popup shown and focused, the popup's row
  carries it; the heading carries no popup glyph; sidebar F6 focus on another row keeps both states
  distinct. It fails on today's code.
- Venus fmt and clippy, `nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-venus`, Codex review.
- One installed observation after the profile refresh: focus a pane agent, then open the Agent
  popup, and the fill follows.

## Scope

Venus sidebar only. Not the Eon Bar tab pills, the glyph's shape, or light-theme colors (or3q).
close_reason: Done: the outline marks the focused terminal's sidebar row on the installed product (f6ff36e); outline over a hover highlight is checked only by review, as VEN-C30 Open proof records.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Contract approval (2026-10-23 ~18:20 -03): Lucca approved the VEN-C30 wording drafted by eon-e4, relayed by eon-overseer ("go ahead"): (1) the Popup marker bullet loses its heading half ("...its accessible label adds "popup". Tab headers carry no marker."); (2) a new Current row bullet, tint ~12% of accent; (3) the accessible word "current" appended to the row's label, as rows already append "popup" and "status stale", with no AccessKit aria-current (Venus marks no row state through AccessKit properties; tabs keep set_selected); (4) the Status line notes this bead, and the earlier heading-marker proofs stay as written. Lucca was also shown that no row is tinted while focus is in a non-agent pane or the Git/Files popup, and that a popup shown in a background tab is no longer marked anywhere; he kept the design.

Design: the current row is the one whose target equals model::focused_terminal(snapshot) (moved from application.rs, which keeps using it), so it is derived from the snapshot only and needs no new SidebarView input. One row per terminal already, so "several records" needs nothing more. The tint is the accent at alpha CURRENT_ROW_TINT = 0.12 (render/chrome.rs), drawn under the focused/hovered highlight; RectangleBatch gains push_rounded_alpha for a translucent rounded fill, so the card's terminal-opacity background and blur still show through.

Configurability: the tint derives from the theme accent; its configuration route is eon-eon-themes-or3q, no separate setting.

Portability: neutral.

comments.text:
Exact approved VEN-C30 text, as sent to eon-overseer and relayed to Lucca with items (1)-(4) of the approval comment above:

(1) **Popup marker.** A row whose source terminal is a popup always shows the popup marker glyph after its catalog label, and its accessible label adds "popup". Tab headers carry no marker.

(2) **Current row.** The row whose source terminal is the active tab's focused terminal (its shown popup, else its selected pane) takes a faint tint of the theme accent over the card background. The opaque highlight of a focused or hovered row draws over it, so both stay distinguishable, and the row keeps the tint while the sidebar holds keyboard focus. Rows in other tabs never take it. Its accessible label adds "current".

The Status line names this bead and, until the installed observation is recorded, lists the current row's tint as the second open gap besides compositor blur.

title: Move panes sideways with Ctrl+Alt+H/L and tabs with Ctrl+Alt+Shift+H/L
description:
## Decision
Lucca, 2026-10-17: Ctrl+Alt+H/L moves the selected pane sideways between columns, so Ctrl+Alt+H/J/K/L moves the selected pane in every direction, matching Alt+H/J/K/L navigation. Tab moves go to Ctrl+Alt+Shift+H/L, and `eon tab move left|right` stays the CLI route. Compared and rejected: a column move that falls through to a tab move at the edge (the same keys sometimes move the whole tab); a separate column chord (awkward, and leaves the pane-move grid incomplete); a tab mode with an entry key (new mode state, an indicator, exit rules and focus edge cases, and it breaks EON-C8/VEN-C8's "without a mode" rule for a rarely used action). Fallback if Ctrl+Alt+Shift+H/L is unavailable: Ctrl+Alt+H/L (or Shift+Left/Right) moves the tab while F6 focus is on the tab strip.

## Contract (to draft and show Lucca before code)
- Ctrl+Alt+H/L moves the selected pane into the neighbouring column of its tab, at the same position or the end of that column's stack (exact rule to propose), and it stays selected. Moving a column's only pane out removes that column, which also reorders columns. At the tab's outer edge: open a new column with that pane if the tab has fewer than four (proposed), otherwise stop quietly, like other moves. In a popup-covered or picker-bound tab, unavailable, as moves are today.
- Ctrl+Alt+Shift+H/L sends today's tab Move left/right, non-repeating, without a mode.
- Failures: a fifth column, an unknown or stale identity, or an invalid transition leaves the accepted topology unchanged.

## Changes needing approval
- EON-C8: drop "cross-column … pane movement" from the Boundary and add the move rule; the key mapping text changes.
- EONW: a new revision or action carrying a cross-column pane move (the v10 WorkspaceAction is v3's and stays unchanged; follow the slice 2 CreateColumn precedent of a top-level action). Historical revisions stay unchanged.
- VEN-C8: Ctrl+Alt+H/L and Ctrl+Alt+Shift+H/L mappings; shortcut viewer, hints, USAGE, README, INTERACTION, CHANGELOG (Ctrl+Alt+H/L changes meaning during the 0.x beta).
- Runtime reserves Ctrl+Alt+Shift+H/L from popup keybindings.

## Prerequisites and first check
After eon-splits-opwv (closed). First check, before drafting code: whether COSMIC and Sway (and their default configs) bind Ctrl+Alt+Shift+H/L, and whether Venus receives the chord with exact modifiers; a conflict switches to the F6 fallback, which needs Lucca's choice. Reference gate: consequential (contract, EONW wire). Record inspected references (for example Zellij move-pane and tmux join-pane at exact revisions) before code.

## Acceptance
- Runtime tests: a cross-column move keeps identities and selection, removes an emptied column, refuses a fifth column, and leaves topology unchanged on failure; codec tests for the new action; a Venus mapping test for both chords.
- One isolated installed dogfood observation: moving a pane across columns and reordering a tab with the new chords.

## Scope boundary
No vertical splits, column resizing, drag and drop, a tab mode, or cross-tab pane moves.
close_reason: Ctrl+Alt+H/L moves the selected pane into the neighbouring column and Ctrl+Alt+Shift+H/L moves the tab over EONW v12; eon pane move left|right; covered tabs refuse. Full suite, flake check, isolated dogfood of the profile's store path, graph at EONW 12. Proof and ledgers in comments.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Open decisions raised by Lucca 2026-10-17, with recommendations (not yet chosen). (1) Outer-edge move: block quietly; move into the neighbouring tab's stack (conflicts with tabs as launch-directory groups and EON-C8's no cross-tab moves; needs popup, picker and emptied-tab rules); as a vertical split (out of scope, rejected); or open a new column at that edge while the tab has fewer than four columns, else block. Recommended: the new-column rule; a pane alone in its column stops quietly at the edge. (2) Landing: join the neighbour column's stack, inserted just below its expanded pane and becoming expanded and selected; or always create a new column beside it (no way to merge into a stack without another key, and the four-column cap refuses it quickly). Recommended: join the stack. Resulting model: Ctrl+Alt+K/J reorders within a stack (existing); Ctrl+Alt+H/L moves to the neighbouring stack and splits out into a new column at the outer edge; an emptied column disappears, so columns reorder by moving their panes. Cross-tab pane moves stay out of the first cut.

comments.text: Reference pass on layout switching (Lucca 2026-10-17; inspection only). Zellij 16beceaa0afcdb559316909ed87b84d487356fa6 (zellij-utils/assets/layouts/default.swap.kdl, zellij-server/src/tab/swap_layouts.rs): per-tab swap layouts over the same panes (vertical, horizontal, stacked, plus BASE), picked by pane-count constraints and cycled with Alt+[ and Alt+]; a manual change marks the layout damaged. Nova dcaa0df6b5e0c45f1094b4948061e2a05a73203d (defaults/zellij/layout.swap.kdl, config.kdl, runtime/yzx-menu.rs): two content layouts, single (one stack) and columns (one main pane beside a stack), crossed with sidebar and hints variants; Alt+[ and Alt+] toggle; switching keeps pane order and focus; new tabs inherit. tmux (man page, openbsd.org): seven presets over one pane list (even-horizontal, even-vertical, main-horizontal(-mirrored), main-vertical(-mirrored), tiled); next-layout on prefix Space; break-pane and join-pane for structural moves. kitty (sw.kovidgoyal.net/kitty/layouts): seven layouts (stack, tall, fat, grid, splits, horizontal, vertical); next_layout ctrl+shift+l; enabled_layouts limits the cycle. niri (resources/default-config.kdl, main as fetched 2026-10-17, unpinned): no layout switching; scrollable columns that each stack windows, optionally tabbed; consume-or-expel-window-left/right on Mod+[ and Mod+] (a lone window is consumed into the neighbouring column, a stacked one is expelled to its own column); move-column on Mod+Ctrl+H/L, move-window on Mod+Ctrl+J/K; preset column widths. WezTerm 577474d89ee6 and Ghostty 45db2c2551ec: split trees with zoom and equalize, no layouts. Design note: layout switching keeps one ordered pane list per tab plus a layout choice, so geometry is Venus's function of (layout, order) and moves stay one-dimensional; niri's consume and expel are the comparable answer if the two-dimensional columns model stays.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Layout decision, Lucca 2026-10-17: columns of accordions stay Eon's split model. Rows (one accordion whose open pane splits side by side) and layout presets (Zellij swap layouts, tmux and kitty layouts, Nova's families) were considered and not chosen; the reasons are recorded in eon-zoom-selected-pane-e2pv. This resolves the conditional in the 19:23 reference pass: the two-dimensional columns model stays, so niri's consume and expel remain the comparable reference for this bead's edge and landing rules. Zoom (eon-zoom-selected-pane-e2pv) leaves zoom before a sideways pane move.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Lucca, 2026-10-20: contract approved (agent's recommendations accepted).
First check: COSMIC (cosmic-settings-daemon 1.10.0, /usr/share/cosmic/com.system76.CosmicSettings.Shortcuts/v1/defaults, empty user custom) and Sway 1.12 default config bind H/L only with Super; no Ctrl+Alt+Shift+H/L conflict, F6 fallback not needed. Venus matches the physical key with exact modifiers (shortcuts.rs matches_key), so the chord is distinct from Ctrl+Alt+H/L; live receipt is observed in the installed dogfood.
Reference: niri aee25c9efcfa85b6029d5d1a2b7aaac7d87ae9d1 src/layout/scrolling.rs consume_or_expel_window_left: a lone window joins the end of the neighbouring column (no-op at the edge); a stacked window is always expelled to a new column beside its source, with no column cap. Kept: one-press, selection-following moves, emptied column removal. Rejected: niri's expel-from-stack as the landing rule (moving a stacked pane one column over takes two presses, and the four-column cap refuses it often).
Decisions:
1. Landing: the pane joins the neighbouring column's stack directly below that column's expanded pane and becomes expanded and selected. In the source column the following pane expands, otherwise the preceding one. An emptied column disappears.
2. Outer edge: a stacked pane opens a new column at that edge while the tab has fewer than four columns, under Alt+Shift+M's 40-terminal-column refusal notice; a lone pane at the edge, or a fifth column, stops quietly.
3. Wire: EONW v12 adds one top-level action, MovePaneSideways { direction }, on the selected pane (v11 ClosePane precedent); v4 Move and older revisions keep their bytes.
4. Keys: Ctrl+Alt+H/L moves the pane sideways; Ctrl+Alt+Shift+H/L moves the tab; both non-repeating, no mode. Runtime reserves Ctrl+Alt+Shift+H/L from popup keybindings.
5. Added scope: eon pane move left|right sends the same v12 action.

comments.author: lucca

The runtime refuses it before any change with 'close the popup before moving a pane sideways', as Alt+W does; it does not dismiss the popup the way Ctrl+Alt+K/J does today. Raised by the Codex review round against the approved contract text; the implementation had first copied K/J's dismiss-then-move.

title: Simplify Eon's proof and planning ceremony
description:
## Chosen outcome — Lucca, 2026-10-14
Simplify Eon's proof and planning ceremony. Scope narrowed by Lucca on 2026-10-14: only Eon's policy changes. It becomes the root policy of the consolidated repository. Eon Sessions, Eon Desktop and Eon Runtime are frozen until consolidation and their policies are not rewritten. Their subsystem rules are rewritten once, already simplified, as subsystem instructions during `Consolidate Eon into one repository`. Keep exact identities at acceptance, installed proof before handoff, live-terminal preservation and ownership rules. Remove per-iteration bookkeeping. On the same date Lucca also approved the isolated-candidate workflow in rule 2.

Evidence, 30 days to 2026-10-14: about 80 of Eon's 193 commits begin Record/Accept/Consume, and about 64 of Venus's 139–178 do (counts vary by method). The shortcut-hints bar took about ten rounds, each a Venus commit, an Eon "Select/Consume" pin and an installed-proof commit. The version badge and footer followed the same Consume → Accept pattern. The cause is policy granularity: "exact accepted revisions" applies to every iteration, and Venus proof requires a separate metadata commit. The repository split multiplies that cost.

## Rules (contract)
1. **Batch proof.** Iterate freely. Do one installed proof per accepted batch. Intermediate rounds produce candidate observations, not accepted proof.
2. **Authorized isolated candidates.** Use a disposable Eon source snapshot that changes only `components/eon-alpha-v3.json`, `flake.nix`/`flake.lock` and, when needed, `crates/eon/Cargo.toml`/`Cargo.lock`, pointing at exact child candidate commits. Revision assertions and build gates stay unchanged. Clean commits only, no dirty trees. Never commit the snapshot. Observe in isolated runtime and configuration roots. Record candidate evidence separately. Refresh the normal profile only after batch acceptance. Limited to changes that preserve accepted protocol contracts; protocol evolution needs its own authorization.
3. **One commit per change.** The proof record (revision, check, environment, result) lives in the owning bead and references the commit. `CONTRACTS.md` holds the contract, its checks and its status, not the latest proving SHA. This removes the rule that a source commit must be followed by a metadata commit.
4. **Tiered gates.** Execution baseline, Reference gate and Crate gate comments are required only for: new or changed dependencies; protocol or wire changes; new or changed contracts; lifecycle, security or trust boundaries. Presentation-only changes need one dogfood observation.
5. **Mechanize or delete.** Generate Eon's LOC scorecard or drop it. Enforce dependency direction with a check. Delete prose rules that can't be checked and add no judgment.
6. **Current protocol import.** Eon renders from the current `Yazelix/starcompass` commit. Consolidation leaves a single import.

## Owners
Eon's `.agent-protocols.local.md` and `.agent-protocols.exceptions.json`, re-rendered with Starcompass. Child repository policies are out of scope. If a canonical protocol conflicts, change Starcompass or record an AP-EXCEPTION-001 exception approved by Lucca. Never resolve a conflict silently.

## Prerequisites
None. This precedes `Consolidate Eon into one repository`, so that consolidation doesn't run under the old ceremony.

## Reference gate
Read Eon's current overlay and the canonical AP-PROOF-001, AP-PLAN-001, AP-TEST-001 and AP-GIT-001 text at the chosen Starcompass commit, plus Starcompass's README render/check contract. No external references needed.

## Scope boundary
Eon policy and repository tooling only. No edits to child repository policies. No product behavior or contract changes. No renumbering. No rewrite of existing proof records or history: existing indexed proofs stay valid as written.
acceptance_criteria:
- Eon's overlay expresses rules 1–5, and its rendered AGENTS.md passes `starcompass check` at the current `Yazelix/starcompass` commit.
- No surviving Eon rule requires a separate metadata commit or a child pin and installed proof per iteration.
- The retained guarantees are still stated: exact identities at acceptance, installed proof before handoff, live terminals preserved, single ownership.
- The rendered AGENTS.md is within Starcompass's size budget. Eon's recorded AP-TEST-001 exception covers validation.
- `git diff --check` passes, Eon's scorecard follows rule 5, and `br sync --flush-only` has run.
notes:
Proof (policy-only route), recorded in the same commit as the change per rule 3.
- Check: Starcompass `check` at Yazelix/starcompass f7ff2a64101618b39e7ee71ece0710ef2d7d10b9 (clean clone; no protocol source changes since the previous pin fe1b71f) -> valid. Profiles greenfield + orchestrator; all 15 protocol versions and SHA-256 values unchanged; only the source commit and overlay hash changed.
- Size: AGENTS.md 26,232 bytes (was 24,925), within the 30,720-byte budget and Codex's 32 KiB loader limit.
- `git diff --check` clean. No dangling references to the removed LOC scorecard or old gate section names.
- Validation: Eon's recorded AP-TEST-001 exception (2026-08-09) covers this instruction change; no agent trials run.
Implementation: rules 1, 3 and 7 are in a new Proof and Review section; rule 2 is the Isolated Candidates section; rule 4 defines an Eon 'consequential code shape' under AP-REFERENCE-001 (an overlay, not an exception) and merges the old Reference and Crate gate lists, which duplicated canonical AP-CONTRACT-001/AP-REFERENCE-001/AP-DEPENDENCY-001, into Contract-Driven Method; rule 5 deletes the README LOC scorecard and its rule; rule 6 renders at current Starcompass. docs/CONTRACTS.md: the 'advance the proof revision' rule now records results in the owning bead and edits the index only when a contract, its checks, status or gap changes. Status section records the child freeze. Refinement: the bead proof travels in the change's own commit, which avoids a commit referencing its own SHA.
Ledger: 1 review pass by the implementing agent in its own context, 0 findings. Not a fresh-context pass; Lucca may run one.

title: Create a five-minute new-user path through Eon docs
description:
## Why

A first-time user must currently cross maintainer-level lifecycle, wire, geometry, and subsystem detail before understanding the product and completing the first durable-session workflow. The documentation is rigorous, but its entry path is too dense.

Contract: a first-time x86_64 Linux Wayland user opens `README.md`, understands what Eon does and its support boundary, installs it, starts work, closes and reopens the window without losing the Session, finds shortcut help, and knows how to report a problem within about five minutes. The path must not require reading the contract ledger or learning Orbit and Venus names first.

## Evidence

- Baseline `18f1874f3357aa7f082db004c735a10347fac646`: `README.md` is 602 lines and `docs/CONTRACTS.md` is 1,503 lines.
- `README.md:7-31` leads with component-graph, EONW, generation, process, and platform-proof detail before a newcomer task.
- `README.md:93-115` contains installation, but current credentials and support constraints are separated from the first-use lifecycle at `README.md:125-149`.
- `README.md:184-540` places detailed workspace, picker, popup, rendering, configuration, and protocol behavior in the main entry document.
- `README.md:562-580` already routes maintainers to architecture, contracts, distribution, references, and Beads.
- `README.md:582-602` records the required LOC scorecard.

Impact: HIGH onboarding and evaluation friction. Effort: M. Risk: LOW if claims retain one canonical owner. Confidence: HIGH.

## Scope

In scope:
- Reshape `README.md` into a concise public entry: promise, supported platform, prerequisites, install, first launch, detach/reconnect, F1 shortcut discovery, limitations, troubleshooting/reporting, and links for deeper use.
- Move maintainer-only explanations to the existing owning documents when they are not already there; link instead of copying.
- Keep `docs/CONTRACTS.md` as the complete proof ledger, but give it a compact orientation/index if navigation remains poor after README routing.
- Put public product terms before Orbit, Venus, EONW, manifest, or generation internals.

Out of scope:
- Runtime, package, configuration, keybinding, platform, or product-contract changes.
- Removing proof evidence, weakening support limitations, duplicating truth, creating a documentation framework, adding a build dependency, or implementing `eon-yvw`.
- Claiming credential-free installation before its separate alpha-source task is accepted.

## Implementation Notes

1. Write the shortest newcomer journey first, against the exact accepted product revision.
2. Retain one owner for each detailed fact. Prefer links into existing architecture, contracts, distribution, benchmark, and reference documents over new files or repeated prose.
3. Keep exact support and private-input limitations prominent next to installation.
4. Preserve a clearly labeled maintainer section and the LOC scorecard. Target a README below roughly 300 lines; exceed that only when the newcomer journey is demonstrably clearer and no detailed fact is duplicated.
5. If the 1,503-line contract ledger needs easier lookup, add navigation only; do not split it or rewrite proof history without evidence that navigation is insufficient.

## Verification

- `wc -l README.md docs/CONTRACTS.md` records the before/after size without treating line count alone as quality.
- `rg -n "Project status|Install|attach|F1|Supported|Troubleshoot|Report|Maintainer|LOC scorecard" README.md` finds the complete newcomer and maintainer routes.
- `rg -n "EON-C[0-9]+|Status:|Evidence" docs/CONTRACTS.md` confirms the proof ledger remains present.
- `git diff --check` exits 0; the changed Markdown links resolve to tracked files; the README LOC scorecard matches all tracked handwritten surfaces.
- A clean reader walkthrough can answer: what Eon is, whether their platform is supported, how to install and launch it, what survives window close, how to reconnect, where keys are shown, and where to report a failure without opening `docs/CONTRACTS.md`.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if shortening would delete unique accepted proof, obscure a material limitation, or make README and canonical docs disagree.
- Stop for user choice before adding a site, generator, dependency, durable non-Rust tooling, or public deployment.
- Stop if current product behavior has materially drifted from the cited baseline; refresh claims before editing.

## Maintenance Notes

This fixes documentation hierarchy, not contract rigor. The contract ledger remains maintainer evidence. The deferred interactive explainer `eon-yvw` is optional presentation work and does not replace this entry path.
close_reason: README provides the verified five-minute newcomer path and keeps detailed proof with its existing owners.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Implemented docs-only candidate from Eon base c42e920. README.md is 297 lines (606 before this slice) and leads with the public promise, supported x86_64 Linux native-Wayland boundary, private-input prerequisite, install/launch flow, detach and eon attach lifecycle, Alt+/ global shortcut help, accurate F1 picker help, limitations, troubleshooting/reporting, maintainer routes, and the refreshed 19,947-line scorecard. Detailed ownership and proof remain in the existing architecture, contracts, distribution, references, and benchmark documents; docs/CONTRACTS.md needed no navigation rewrite. Mechanically verified on 2026-09-17 America/Sao_Paulo with wc/rg route checks, tracked local-link resolution, exact LOC recomputation, current-state-language scan, and git diff --check. No runtime, package, configuration, contract, changelog, or profile change.

title: Update eonterm.com text for the release that ships workspaces and popup keys
description:
## Why

AGENTS.md "Website": site text follows every release that changes what a person can do or see,
in that release's bead or its own site bead. The next Eon release ships workspaces (several
workspaces in one window, EON-C33) and configurable popup keys, and the workspace beads each left
the eonterm.com text undone on purpose. This is that site bead: text only, no media.

Source: the site notes on eon-workspace-switching-shn4.5 (comment 4246), shn4.6 (comment 4278),
shn4.7 (comment 4303) and shn4.8 (comments 4340 and 4341), each saying eonterm.com text must
follow in the release that ships the feature, and eon-configurability-qkq8.1 (landed 15134ee,
Eon 0.1.4). Approved by Lucca 2026-10-27 (morning report question 9): "9. ok", accepting the
recommendation "one site bead at release". Relayed by eon-overseer.

## Contract

No contract change: the site describes behavior that EON-C33, EON-C10, EON-C20, EON-C31,
VEN-C8 and VEN-C21 already define at the release tag. If writing the guides shows that an EON-C
text is wrong or missing, record it here and bring the wording to Lucca for approval first, as
AGENTS.md requires. Do not change contracts from this bead.

## Prerequisites

- The Eon release that ships workspace switching (shn4.4-shn4.9, Eon 0.1.5 on edge at
  cf6dc25) and qkq8.1's popup keys is tagged. No release bead exists yet for it; do not start
  before the tag.
- Related, in the eon-site repository's own beads: eon-site-qmt ("Update eonterm.com text for
  the v0.1.2 release", open; the site's src/site.ts still names linux-alpha-2026-10-14). If it
  is still open at this release, do both in one pass against the newer tag and close it with a
  note.

## Scope

In scope (the eon-site repository, ~/pjs/eon/eon-site):

- Workspaces (shn4.4-shn4.8): `eon workspaces [--json]` (fields incl. attention and recency),

  stays in Alt+/ as "overridden by" its holder; `keybinding = ""` unbinds any popup; each

Out of scope:

- Anything unreleased at the tag: Kitty graphics (orb-j2i) and any behavior behind a staging
  switch.
- Pushing the site: pushing eon-site's main publishes eonterm.com and stays on Lucca's explicit
