- Eon repository code or docs.

## Acceptance

- Every claim on the changed pages traces to Eon's source, CHANGELOG.md and docs at the release
  tag; planned or unproven behavior is labelled.
- The site's own checks pass.
- The commit is ready, and the push waits for Lucca.

## Verification

- The eon-site repository's documented build and check commands exit 0.
- `git -C ~/pjs/eon/eon show <tag>:docs/USAGE.md` and `:docs/CONFIGURATION.md` agree with each
  changed guide (commands, keys, fields).

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if the tag does not exist yet.
- Stop if a guide needs a claim the tagged docs do not support.

title: Push agent attention to the person's phone
description:
## Why
All four competitors reach the person away from the desk: push notifications to a phone and a mobile
client (Rex iOS TestFlight, T3 Code iOS/Android, Amp apps, herdr via Moshi). Eon covers desktop
notification and sound (eon-2kvr, eon-iwmz); mobile only through frozen beads
orb-native-mobile-access-bwg and orb-permanent-ssh-terminal-access-hd6. Source: competitor audit
eon-r6yt (2026-10-29), reports in ~/pjs/refs/competitor-audit-2026-10/. Lucca, 2026-10-29: "file the
beads". Filing only; no work is approved yet beyond planning.

## Scope of this bead (narrowed 2026-10-29, prime-beads pass)
Push only: send "agent needs you / finished" to the person's phone through a channel they already
use, off by default. The mobile client scope stays where it already lives: orb-native-mobile-access-bwg
(native mobile client), orb-permanent-ssh-terminal-access-hd6 (any SSH terminal, including a phone)
and eon-remote-workspaces-52i4 (remote host). This bead does not unfreeze them.

## Contracts
EON-C31 (Agent attention) amendment for the trigger, or a new EON-C for push delivery. Consequential:
trust boundary (attention data leaves the machine; agent-authored `title` and `msg` may hold
sensitive text) and possibly a dependency (HTTP client). Lucca approves the text before code.

## Design options for the reference gate
1. Built-in channel: Runtime POSTs to an ntfy or Pushover endpoint from `[attention]` settings.
2. Command hook: Eon runs a configured argv on each raise (the person's `ntfy publish`, `curl`, or
   anything), so Eon adds no HTTP client and no third-party trust.
3. Recipe over the event stream (eon-ciwn.1): a documented script subscribes and pushes; Eon ships
   nothing new for push.
Compare ownership, dependency weight (AP-DEPENDENCY-001), privacy defaults (which fields leave the
machine; default to state and pane only), and failure behaviour (never blocks the Runtime).
References: docs/REFERENCES.md cmux route (notifications) and the cross-device route; ntfy and
Pushover APIs; how Rex and T3 Code push, at recorded revisions.

## Prerequisites
Blocked by eon-2kvr: it settles the shared trigger (new EON-C31 raise and needs input, never while
`background`), the quiet rule and the `[attention]` setting family that push must reuse (one owner
of the trigger). Related: eon-ciwn.1 (option 3).

## Acceptance
- With push configured, an attention raise reaches the configured endpoint within the bound the
  contract sets (seconds), observed in an isolated installed run against a local test endpoint, not
  a third-party service.
- With push off (the default), no network connection is made, shown by a focused test of the
  trigger path.
- Defaults documented in docs/CONFIGURATION.md; contract and mechanism approved by Lucca before code.

## Verification
- Focused trigger and privacy test in the owning crate via `nix develop -c eon-test -p <crate>`.
- Installed runtime route: profile refresh plus one isolated installed observation.

title: Halve the always-loaded agent instructions
description:
## Decision
Lucca, 2026-10-15: cut the always-loaded agent instructions roughly in half. The root `AGENTS.md`
becomes a short, practical page; the full protocol text loads on demand.

## Contract
- Consumer: any coding agent starting work in this repository.
- Result: the root `AGENTS.md` is about half its current size and still states who owns what, the
build and sandboxed test commands, the Git rules and when to stop and ask (contracts, scope,
dependencies, publishing). The canonical protocol text stays available in a file the root page
names and loads only when needed. No rule silently changes meaning.

## Evidence (edge 068efcb)
- `AGENTS.md` is 28,730 bytes and 552 lines. The import record with its SHA-256 table (lines 8-41)
and the canonical protocol text (lines 42-268) are about half; the local rules rendered from
`.agent-protocols.local.md` (14,271 bytes) are the rest.
- With `venus/AGENTS.md` the loaded chain is 31,788 bytes, near the 32 KiB Codex default that
`eon-monorepo-2oko` set as a limit.
- Local rules repeat protocols: Core Rule vs AP-SCOPE-001, Testing Discipline vs AP-TEST-001,
Proof and Review vs AP-PROOF-001, Git Workflow vs AP-GIT-001.
- `AGENTS.md` is generated from Yazelix/starcompass at a pinned commit; never edit it by hand.

## Approach (choose in the first step)
- Trim duplication in `.agent-protocols.local.md` and the subsystem overlays.
- Move canonical protocol text out of the default context: a starcompass renderer option that emits
it to a separate file (upstream change in Yazelix/starcompass, then repin), or a recorded
AP-EXCEPTION-001 exception if the renderer cannot.
Record the choice and its reasons here.

## Prerequisites
Agent policy is Lucca's: get approval for the final text and for any upstream starcompass change.
Per the recorded AP-TEST-001 exception, validate directly with structural checks and repository
evidence, not another agent.

## Acceptance
- Rendered root `AGENTS.md` is at most about 14 KiB; the root plus any subsystem file stays well
under 32 KiB.
- A mapping shows where every removed rule now lives, or that Lucca chose to drop it.
- The import render and check pass; the diff and changed paths are recorded. Docs/policy proof only.

## Stop boundary
No behavior, contract or tooling change in Eon code. Changing a rule's meaning needs Lucca's
approval.

title: Source trustworthy Codex quota for the Eon Bar
description:
## Outcome and routed contract

Create the source half of `EON-C22 — Trustworthy Codex quota in the Eon Bar` after the native Eon Bar is proved.

Consumer: one installed full-Eon user who already has a compatible authenticated `codex` executable on the inherited user `PATH`.

Trigger: full Eon starts with that compatible provider available, then the bounded provider refresh becomes due.

Result: one Eon-owned Codex provider adapter talks only to Codex's stable app-server JSON-RPC surface, reads `account/rateLimits/read`, selects the current Codex rate-limit bucket, and normalizes at most the primary and secondary windows into an optional typed EONW snapshot field. Each window carries duration, remaining percentage, reset time when supplied, observation time, and explicit freshness. Backend `ordinaryUsageAllowed = false` becomes an explicit blocked state; null never becomes inferred recovery. No credential, transcript, token-history, plan, credit, account identifier, upsell, or provider-private payload crosses EONW.

Important failures: missing or incompatible Codex, no authenticated account, malformed or oversized JSON-RPC, changed account, timeout, EOF, provider crash, network loss, out-of-order response, absent bucket, invalid percentage/time, or Eon shutdown leaves the quota absent or explicitly stale, never guessed, and never delays product startup, workspace actions, terminal attachment, or shutdown.

Impact: HIGH from direct user dogfood (“I do miss the quota widget quite a bit”). Effort: M. Risk: MEDIUM at the provider/auth/process boundary. Confidence: HIGH in the selected source boundary; MEDIUM in its exact lifecycle until the pinned implementation gate.

## Evidence

- `crates/eon-workspace-protocol/src/v5.rs:92-98` has one complete workspace `Snapshot` and no provider facts; a truthful native projection needs an explicit versioned owner boundary.
- `crates/eon/src/workspace.rs:173-221` is the single Eon snapshot constructor. `../eon-desktop/src/transport.rs:214-333` already polls complete EONW snapshots, so Venus does not need a provider poller or event bus.
- `crates/eon/src/managed_environment.rs:512-589` already discovers user-installed agent executables on Eon's inherited Session/user path without making them product components.
- Installed Codex CLI `0.154.0` (`codex app-server generate-json-schema`) exposes non-experimental `account/rateLimits/read`, `GetAccountRateLimitsResponse`, `RateLimitSnapshot`, `RateLimitWindow`, `accountId`, `ordinaryUsageAllowed`, and sparse `account/rateLimits/updated` notifications. The read request can exclude reset-credit details and decline Luna Reserve support.
- Nova Bar exact source `bfbf8a7be28b69f9d822c0843bf2dd5066dd49e3` demonstrates the value of one-minute official quota refresh, explicit stale output, reset-aware retention, and bounded backoff, but obtains data through `tokenusage` and a command-widget/cache layer that Eon must not copy.
- `eon-deliver-native-eon-bar-w4d` owns the prerequisite product surface. This bead owns facts only; `eon-desktop:ven-render-codex-quota-eon-bar-wfe` will own native presentation after this source is accepted.

## Prerequisites and reference gate

Hard prerequisite: `eon-deliver-native-eon-bar-w4d` is closed with exact EON-C21/VEN-C21 proof. No other Eon/Orbit/Venus implementation frontier is active unless the user explicitly changes it.

Before code:
- Regenerate the stable schema from the exact selected Codex release and inspect its source, release identity, license, initialization, shutdown, account switching, response ordering, size limits, `account/rateLimits/read`, and notification behavior. Record whether Eon consumes a user-installed executable or must ask the user to approve a pinned product tool; do not silently add Codex to the component graph.
- Compare a dedicated bounded `codex app-server --stdio` child using standard process/I/O plus the workspace's already locked `serde_json`, the Codex daemon/proxy, Nova's `tokenusage` mechanism, direct HTTP, and no feature. Prefer the dedicated official app-server child if the exact gate confirms it: it owns auth and account semantics without Eon reading tokens or adding a generic service.
- Request no reset-credit details, advertise no Luna Reserve support, and perform no provider mutation. Treat notifications as hints to refetch; do not merge sparse values into a second semantic owner.
- Record EON-C22 as Candidate and seed the smallest EONW v6 typed field before implementation. Preserve explicit v5 incompatibility rather than adding a compatibility window.

## Scope

In scope:
- One optional, fail-closed Codex quota provider adapter owned by Eon's existing supervisor lifecycle.
- Exact JSON-RPC initialization, bounded framing/queues/timeouts, one in-flight read, one-minute-or-slower refresh, failure backoff, child cleanup, account-change invalidation, and in-memory-only last-good state.
- Eon-owned normalization of the selected Codex bucket into at most two bounded windows, explicit fresh/stale/blocked/unknown state, and an optional EONW v6 snapshot field.
- The smallest source/configuration-free default: try the existing authenticated `codex` when available; otherwise publish no quota. No widget registry or order setting.
- EON-C22 Candidate text, EONW codec/failure tests, provider-substitute integration checks, current docs/changelog/LOC alignment, and affected Rust/Nix proof.

Out of scope:
- Venus rendering, bar geometry, installed visual acceptance, attention/sidebar state, other providers, token counts, cost estimates, credit purchase/reset actions, provider login/logout, account selection, or provider configuration UI.
- Reading Codex auth/config/history files, direct undocumented HTTP, terminal/process/screen inference, `tokenusage`, Nova Bar code, persistent disk caches, arbitrary command widgets, generic provider/event/status frameworks, plugins, or a second row.
- Bundling Codex, adding a daemon, changing Orbit, macOS support/proof, remote accounts, or any provider compatibility claim beyond the exact accepted evidence.

## Implementation notes

1. Add the bounded optional quota data to the canonical EONW snapshot and validator first. Carry only presentation-safe normalized facts; never carry raw JSON or `accountId`.
2. Resolve `codex` through the existing inherited executable path. Start at most one dedicated child, complete the required app-server initialization, continuously drain bounded JSON-RPC messages, and match replies by request id.
3. Read at startup and no faster than once per minute. On an update notification, schedule a normal refetch rather than interpreting sparse provider state. Use bounded exponential or fixed backoff after failure and never overlap reads.
4. Keep last-good facts only in memory. A failed refresh marks them stale immediately; each window expires no later than its provider reset time. A changed private account identity discards all prior facts before publishing another snapshot.
5. Prefer no new crate. If direct JSON parsing is required, evaluate a direct use of the exact `serde_json` already locked in the workspace against handwritten parsing; do not add a JSON-RPC framework for this one method.
6. Protect one codec boundary and one provider-substitute lifecycle test covering fresh, stale, blocked/unknown, account change, malformed/oversized input, crash/backoff, and clean shutdown.

## Acceptance criteria

- A compatible authenticated Codex yields an optional EONW v6 quota snapshot containing at most two normalized windows with 0–100 remaining percentage, duration, provider reset when present, observation time, and explicit freshness; the current account id and raw provider fields never cross the boundary.
- `ordinaryUsageAllowed = false` publishes blocked. Null or absent permission remains unknown; Eon never derives availability from percentages or reset time.
- Eon requests `excludeResetCreditDetails = true`, does not advertise Luna Reserve support, and performs no provider mutation, login, logout, credit, or account-selection action.
- Missing executable, unauthenticated account, unsupported schema, malformed/oversized response, timeout, provider crash, network loss, and absent quota keep full Eon usable and quota absent or stale with bounded retry work.
- Refresh is no faster than once per minute, only one read is in flight, notifications trigger refetch rather than duplicate interpretation, and failure backoff prevents a hot loop.
- Last-good values are process-memory-only, become stale on the first failed refresh, expire by their provider reset, and are discarded immediately when the private account identity changes or Eon restarts.
- No auth token, account id, plan, balance, credit/reset detail, upsell, transcript, token count, command output, or raw JSON appears in EONW, logs, diagnostics, cache/state files, or documentation.
- EONW v6 bounds and validates every new field, rejects invalid percentages/times/counts/trailing bytes, and remains explicitly incompatible with v5; Orbit protocols and terminal authority are unchanged.
- Focused red/green protocol and provider-substitute checks plus complete affected locked Rust/Nix checks, README LOC, and `git diff --check` pass on one unchanged candidate.
- EON-C22 remains Candidate until the exact Venus child and installed full-Eon delivery are accepted.

## Stop conditions

- Stop if the selected exact Codex release lacks a stable machine-readable rate-limit read or requires Eon to read credentials, use undocumented HTTP, scrape terminal/history, or mutate provider state.
- Stop for explicit user choice before adding Codex, `tokenusage`, a daemon, a new runtime crate/tool, persistent cache, provider login UI, another provider, or a general widget/provider framework.
- Stop if safe integration requires copying the Codex protocol/schema wholesale, publishing account identity, or making provider availability a product-startup dependency.
- Stop while another implementation frontier is active and before Venus/UI or platform-support work.

## Maintenance notes

This first slice is deliberately Codex-only and conditionally present by default. It creates neither a general widget configuration surface nor a multi-provider promise. A disable/order setting is deferred until at least two proved first-party fact chips create real configuration pressure.

title: Specify Helix-like modal editing semantics for an Eon editor
description:
## Contract Routing

This is a planning and research decision. It changes no EON product contract and implements no editor behavior. EON-C4 continues to preserve Helix as the sole owner of editing and language integration. If `eon-ofb` later selects an Eon-native editor, that owner must receive an explicitly approved indexed contract before code.

## Why

The user requires any eventual Eon editor engine to retain Helix-like modal editing regardless of whether it reuses `helix-core`. The modal model is behavior, not a crate choice: normal, select, and insert modes; selection-first operations; multiple selections; command composition; and undo grouping must be specified independently from rendering and physical key assignments. Without this contract, a native editor could reuse Helix data structures while losing the editing model users actually rely on.

## Evidence

- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:16` assigns editing, language integration, and editor state to Helix; `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:69` forbids Eon from duplicating editor behavior under the current contract.
- Official Helix revision `079a789e8cb08ead67f19e1971a1b7438b37354b`, `docs/architecture.md`: `helix-core` supplies functional Rope, Selection, and Transaction primitives, while Document, History, editor lifecycle, and commands live above core.
- The same revision, `helix-core/src/selection.rs` and `helix-core/src/transaction.rs`: multiple selections and invertible transactions are core primitives.
- The same revision, `helix-term/src/keymap/default.rs`: Normal, Select, and Insert are distinct modes, with Select derived from Normal through extension semantics.
- The same revision, `helix-term/src/commands.rs`: user-visible command semantics and undo checkpoints are substantially implemented in the terminal frontend rather than supplied by `helix-core` alone.
- CodeMirror 6 System Guide, https://codemirror.net/docs/guide/, is comparison evidence for an immutable transaction core and derived editor state; it is not a modal-compatibility source.

## Scope

In scope:
- Define the editor-owned modes and transitions required for a Helix-like mental model.
- Define selection-first cursor/range semantics, multiple selections, motion versus extension, operator application, transaction and undo grouping, registers, yank/paste, search/find, text objects, repeat, macros, shell filters, and language-aware command disposition.
- Classify each behavior as required in the first editing proof, required before Helix replacement, or explicitly deferred.
- Assign each accepted behavior to the future editor owner, Venus, Eon workspace policy, or an external language/tool process without duplicate authority.
- Define a deterministic behavioral corpus: initial text, selections and mode plus semantic command sequence produce exact final text, selections, mode, and undo boundaries.

Out of scope:
- Choosing `helix-core`, copying or adapting Helix code, creating a repository, adding dependencies, or implementing an editor.
- Physical key assignments; the separate keybinding-continuity decision owns those after this semantic vocabulary is stable.
- Venus rendering, Eon workspace shortcuts, user keymap configuration syntax, Helix plugin or Steel compatibility, terminal emulation, CRDTs, multiplayer, remote access, or cloud persistence.
- Promising complete Helix feature parity; unsupported behavior must be explicit rather than silently reinterpreted.

## Decision Work

1. Inspect the exact accepted Helix revision required by `eon-ofb`, including the complete default command inventory and the state each command reads or mutates.
2. Produce a semantic command matrix grouped by navigation, selection, transformation, insertion, history, search, registers, macros, shell/tool interaction, language intelligence, views, and application UI.
3. Separate the core modal contract from Helix terminal-frontend and widget behavior.
4. Define the minimum behavioral corpus and how an independent implementation can compare observable results against the pinned Helix reference without sharing editor authority.
5. Record the owned-LOC and maintenance consequences for reusing `helix-core`, using an upstream semantic boundary, and implementing the accepted primitives independently.
6. Obtain an explicit user decision on the required-before-replacement and deferred sets. Do not implement during this Bead.

## Acceptance

- Normal, Select, and Insert modes and every accepted transition have one editor owner and deterministic failure behavior.
- Selection-first and multiple-selection semantics are explicit, including head/anchor direction, overlapping range normalization, empty selections, and mapping selections through transactions.
- The record defines transaction and undo boundaries for insertion, command sequences, repeat, macros, formatter or LSP edits, and rejected or stale external edits.
- Every inspected Helix command family has a required, before-replacement, deferred, or rejected disposition with rationale; absence is never silently replaced by different behavior.
- A small reference corpus covers all accepted core editing families and compares exact text, selections, mode, and undo/redo outcomes at pinned Helix revision `079a789e8cb08ead67f19e1971a1b7438b37354b`.
- The result names the smallest first proof and its owner but creates no implementation, repository, dependency, compatibility claim, or EON contract.

## Verification

- `git -C /home/lucca/pjs/yazelix-dir/helix rev-parse HEAD` must report the inspected revision, or the Bead must record and justify a newly inspected exact revision.
- `rg -n "Mode::Normal|Mode::Select|Mode::Insert|Transaction|Selection|undo" /home/lucca/pjs/yazelix-dir/helix/helix-core /home/lucca/pjs/yazelix-dir/helix/helix-view /home/lucca/pjs/yazelix-dir/helix/helix-term` must route each accepted semantic family to source evidence.
- The final Bead state must contain the command matrix, owner map, corpus shape, option comparison, negative results, and explicit user decision.
- No source, test, manifest, contract index, dependency, generated artifact, or ambient configuration changes during this decision.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if the desired behavior requires copying or adapting Helix source before license and dependency gates are approved.
- Stop if a proposed semantic operation duplicates Orbit terminal authority, Venus presentation authority, or Eon workspace policy.
- Stop if the behavioral corpus would require a second production editor backend or a public compatibility protocol.
- Stop for user choice if preserving Helix semantics makes the recommended editor shape materially different from `eon-ofb`'s current candidates.

## Maintenance Notes

Effort M, implementation risk HIGH, confidence HIGH that modal semantics must be explicit before selecting an engine. `helix-core` is a candidate mechanism, not proof of Helix-like behavior: keymaps and much command behavior currently live in `helix-term`. The keybinding-continuity decision follows this Bead. Helix remains Eon's accepted editor throughout.
notes: Deferred editor decision. The former core Venus lifecycle-hardening gate is complete, but this horizon remains unactivated until the user selects it and product dogfood supplies a concrete editor need. The Helix modal requirement is preserved; this planning batch authorizes no editor contract or implementation.

title: Draw the working badge as Nova's braille dots at 10 Hz, with a setting to keep it still
description:
## Problem

Lucca, 2026-10-27: "i dont like our spinner too much / because of the fps. it ticks too slowly".
Venus's working badge (VEN-C21 "Attention badges"; also the agent sidebar's working row) is a
270° arc with 8 phases (venus/src/render/chrome.rs `SPINNER_PHASES`, `push_arc`) turned every
200 ms (venus/src/application.rs `SPINNER_INTERVAL`): 45° steps, 1.6 s per turn, which reads as
choppy. VEN-C21 caps it at 5 Hz.

## Decision (approved)

Approved by Lucca 2026-10-27, relayed by eon-overseer. Asked: "1. Style: braille dots, like Nova
(⠋⠙⠹⠸⠼⠴⠦⠧⠇⠏, nova-zj-radar crates/core/src/status.rs), drawn as 8 small dots. 2. Speed: 10 per
second (100 ms per frame, one second per cycle); changes VEN-C21's 'at most five times a second'.
3. Settings: one option to turn the animation off (accessibility); style and rate stay fixed.
4. One small Venus bead, after orb-j2i.11 lands." Lucca: "ok".

- Style: the 10-frame braille "dots" sequence ⠋⠙⠹⠸⠼⠴⠦⠧⠇⠏, drawn by Venus as dots in a 2x4 cell
  grid (rectangle quads, as the arc is now; no font dependency), in ATTENTION_WORKING.
- Rate: 100 ms per frame (10 Hz), only the badge repaints, only while shown, as today.
- Software (CPU) adapters keep a still badge that never repaints (a fixed dots frame instead of the
  still arc), as VEN-C21 requires now.
- One configuration value turns the animation off (a still badge on every adapter). Eon Runtime
  parses it and sends the resolved value; Venus parses no configuration. Default: animated.
  Document it in docs/CONFIGURATION.md. Style and rate stay fixed; record that reason (support cost
  of several styles; the dots match Nova, Claude Code and Codex titles) on this bead.

## Contract

VEN-C21 "Attention badges": the working-badge clause changes from "a still open arc ... the arc
turns, repainting at no more than 5 Hz under AP-PERF-001" to braille dots turning at no more than
10 Hz, still on software adapters or when the setting turns animation off. Record the exact adopted
text on this bead. The setting crosses EONW (Runtime to Venus): if it needs a wire field, that is
an EONW version bump (memory: never amend EONW in place); keep it inside this bead only if small,
otherwise stop and ask. Any other contract change needs Lucca's approval.

## Prerequisites

- Start after orb-j2i.11 lands (both touch venus/src/render).
- Read VEN-C21, venus/AGENTS.md, AP-PERF-001, docs/CONFIGURATION.md.

## Acceptance

- Replace `spinner_phases_rewrite_only_alpha_in_place` and
  `spinner_turns_at_most_five_times_a_second_and_only_while_shown` with their dots / 10 Hz
  equivalents; keep `software_adapters_draw_working_badges_still_and_never_tick` and add the
  setting-off case.
- AP-PERF-001: measure Venus CPU over 20 s with and without a working badge on the GPU adapter, as
  VEN-C21's proof did (11 ticks of 10 ms at 5 Hz); record the numbers.
- One isolated installed observation (headless Sway on the Intel GPU): captures 100 ms apart show
  successive dots frames; with the setting off, identical captures.
- CHANGELOG.md, venus/CHANGELOG.md and docs/CONFIGURATION.md updated.
- Review per AGENTS.md (converge plus Codex); cargo fmt and clippy for yazelix-venus.

## Scope boundary

Only the working badge's glyph, rate and the animation toggle. Not: the other badge glyphs, the
Finished-versus-Working rule (eon-eon-attention-working-hides-finish-7df0), sidebar layout.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Portability disposition: neutral. The change reads only `wgpu::DeviceType` (already used for the software-adapter rule) and draws rectangle quads through the shared renderer; no Linux, Wayland or Darwin mechanism is added.

Adopted VEN-C21 text (venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md, Attention badges):

```

    corner badge (◆, ✕, ✓, or braille dots), the active tab included. A stale
    tab's badge is dimmed;
  - the working badge's dots step through ⠋⠙⠹⠸⠼⠴⠦⠧⠇⠏, repainting at no more
    than 10 Hz under AP-PERF-001, and only the badge. On a software (CPU)
    graphics adapter, or when Eon passes `--animate-working-badge false`, it
    is the still frame ⠋ and never repaints to animate;
```

and the Boundary's exceptions sentence now ends: "..., the label and its badge from its `workspace` and `workspaces`, and the `--animate-working-badge` launch argument."

Question for Lucca (numbered, with recommendation):
1. Grid: the Decision says "a 2x4 cell grid" / "8 small dots", but the approved sequence ⠋⠙⠹⠸⠼⠴⠦⠧⠇⠏ never lights braille dots 7 and 8. Venus draws the six positions the sequence uses as a 2x3 grid centred in the badge (2 px dots, 1 px gaps at the default size), so the lit dots match each character exactly. Recommendation: keep the centred 2x3, because a 2x4 cell would only add an always-empty bottom row that pushes the dots above the badge's centre. Answer "2x4" to keep that empty row instead, as a font draws it.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Reference gate (AP-REFERENCE-001; consequential because it changes VEN-C21 and adds a Runtime-to-Venus launch input).

User-visible behavior: the working badge (tab corner badge and the agent sidebar's working row) is drawn as braille dots that step through Nova's 10-frame sequence ⠋⠙⠹⠸⠼⠴⠦⠧⠇⠏ every 100 ms (one cycle per second). On a software (CPU) adapter, or with `[workspace] animate_working_badge = false`, it is the still frame ⠋ and never repaints to animate.

Owners: Eon Runtime parses `[workspace] animate_working_badge` (bool, default true) and passes the resolved value to Venus as `--animate-working-badge true|false`, as it does `warning_close_last_tab` / `--warning-close-last-tab`. Venus parses no configuration and owns the dots' geometry, phase and repaint. No EONW field, no EONW version bump, no change to runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/attention.rs.

References read:
- Nova, /home/lucca/pjs/nova/nova-zj-radar at 0b1672606ca118f6241df687889142c8b52d03fe, crates/core/src/status.rs `working_spin` (FRAMES ⠋⠙⠹⠸⠼⠴⠦⠧⠇⠏, frame % 10) and its plain still glyph ⠋ for Running. - Venus's current arc (venus/src/render/chrome.rs `push_arc`, `Spinners`; venus/src/application.rs `SPINNER_INTERVAL`). Kept: a tick rewrites only the badge's own vertex bytes, the same length in every phase, so only alpha changes; ticks stop while no turning badge shows.
- docs/REFERENCES.md has no route for badge glyphs; none applies.

Geometry decision: the 10 frames use only braille dots 1-6 (⠋=1,2,4 ⠙=1,4,5 ⠹=1,4,5,6 ⠸=4,5,6 ⠼=3,4,5,6 ⠴=3,5,6 ⠦=2,3,6 ⠧=1,2,3,6 ⠇=1,2,3 ⠏=1,2,3,4); dots 7 and 8 are never lit. Checks: chrome.rs dots-phase test (same byte length per phase, only alpha differs, each frame lights exactly its braille dots); application.rs 10 Hz tick test; software-adapter and setting-off still tests; launch.rs argument test; runtime config parse and defaults tests; CPU measurement; isolated installed captures.

The agent proposes drawing a 2×3 grid, which looks identical and is more compact. I recommend 2×3." Lucca: "ok". Venus keeps the centred 2x3 grid.

title: Compare readable working-badge spinners at real size
close_reason: Research done: Lucca picked C2 (an antialiased 270° arc) and approved the VEN-C21 wording, both relayed by eon-overseer on 2026-10-23. The eon-overseer files the implementation bead.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Research result (eon-fd, 2026-10-23). Research only: nothing changed on edge except this bead.

Method: a throwaway local harness, not committed, at
~/.cache/eon-agents/eon-fd/harness/spinners.py. It ports Venus's badge drawing from edge 8a25211:
push_badge, push_badge_glyph, and RectangleBatch push/push_quad/push_rounded/push_span. It keeps
Venus's rasterization: one sample per pixel (MultisampleState::default), so a pixel is lit when its
centre is inside, and alpha blending in linear light on the sRGB target. Geometry uses the default
metrics: font 16, cell height 18, padding 12. That gives a 12 px badge with a 10 px glyph at scale 1,
and 24 px with 20 px at scale 2, in both the tab corner and the sidebar row. Shape candidates are
drawn the way Venus draws other badges: quads, plus 1x1 coverage quads for antialiasing, which is the
same technique as push_span. Braille is text in DejaVu Sans, a font Venus ships (DejaVu Sans Mono
has no braille). The harness approximates the real renderer: text uses FreeType through Pillow, not
glyphon/swash. It is not an installed capture.

Venus has no light theme: chrome is dark and fixed. "Light" therefore means the sidebar card at Eon's
default 0.80 opacity over a white desktop, the only place a light backdrop shows through. There,
every badge and the row text lose contrast equally. That comes from the card's opacity, not from
any candidate, and it doesn't change the ranking.

Images in ~/.cache/eon-agents/eon-fd/spinner/:
- contact-sheet.png: every candidate at real size. For each: the scale-1 tab strip, the scale-1
  sidebar dark and light, the same at scale 2, and zoomed frame strips at x8 and x4 with the still
  form first.
- contact-sheet-x3.png: the scale-1 tab strip and sidebar row, x3, one row per candidate.
- compare.gif: all candidates animating together at 5 Hz, at real size, x2 and scale 2.
- <key>/: per-candidate stills (tab-s{1,2}-still.png, sidebar-s{1,2}-{dark,light}-still.png),
  GIFs (tab-s{1,2}.gif, sidebar-s{1,2}-dark.gif) and frames-s{1,2}-zoomed.png.

Why today's spinner is hard to read: the 8 segments are aliased quads. At a 10 px glyph each one
rasterizes to a 1-2 px blob, so the ring reads as a gear or a dotted circle. The trail fades by 0.11
alpha per segment, which is too faint to show direction at that size. A2, the same ring
antialiased, is smoother but still a blurry donut at scale 1.

Candidates against the constraints (frozen = reads as working when still; distinct = differs from
idle ring, ◆ ✕ ✓; Claude = doesn't look like Claude's ◐ title spinner; cost = ≤5 Hz, badge only;
s1 = legible at scale 1):
- A, today's ring: frozen weak (a gear), distinct yes, Claude yes, cost yes, s1 poor.
- A2, the same ring antialiased: frozen weak (a donut), distinct borderline (close to the idle ring
  in shape), Claude yes, cost yes, s1 fair.
- B, braille ⠋⠙⠹ (still ⣿): frozen poor (⣿ is a dot block), distinct yes, Claude yes (it's Codex's
  look instead). Cost is a problem: a font glyph lives in the text layer, so each turn
  re-prepares text, which breaks today's vertex-only rewrite. s1 poor: the dots are 1 px and the
  glyph is half the badge wide.
- C1, a 120° arc on a faint track: frozen weak (a ring with a dark patch), distinct borderline
  (the track reads as the idle ring), Claude yes, cost yes, s1 fair.
- C2, a 270° arc with no track (still: the same arc): frozen good (it's the universal loading
  glyph), distinct yes (an open blue arc vs a closed thin grey ring, ◆ ✕ ✓), Claude yes, cost yes,
  s1 good.
- D, half-circles ◐◓◑◒ (still ◐): frozen fair, distinct yes, Claude no (it's Claude's own title
  spinner, side by side in rows that show the Claude splat), cost yes, s1 good.
- E, a pulsing dot: frozen poor (a plain dot, which reads as status, not progress; close to the
  unavailable dot), distinct borderline, Claude yes, cost yes, s1 good.
- F (extra), a dot orbiting a faint track: frozen fair, distinct borderline, Claude yes, cost yes,
  s1 poor (it smears at 10 px).

Recommendation: C2, an antialiased 270° arc with no track, turning in 8 steps of 45° at 5 Hz (1.6 s
a turn); on CPU adapters the still arc. Reasons:
1. It's the only candidate that reads as "working" when frozen, which the CPU-adapter still badge
   needs.
2. At scale 1 it stays a clean C. Its open gap shows rotation even at 5 Hz.
3. Blue, open and thick, it can't be confused with the thin grey closed idle ring or with ◆ ✕ ✓.
4. It doesn't echo Claude's ◐ or Codex's braille, so Eon's badge stays distinct from the agents'
   own titles.
5. It keeps today's cost model. Each phase emits the same fixed grid of 1x1 coverage quads over the
   glyph box: 100 at scale 1, 400 at scale 2, with zero-alpha pixels kept so the length never
   changes. Only alpha changes, so spinner_phases_rewrite_only_alpha_in_place and the 5 Hz,
   badge-only tick still hold. Per tick that is about 600 to 2400 vertices per badge instead of
   48. The implementation bead should measure it against the yx8.2 baseline.

VEN-C21 wording draft (for Lucca's approval, landed only with the implementation):
- current: "on a software (CPU) graphics adapter the working badge is a still segmented ring that
  never repaints to animate; otherwise its spinner turns, repainting at no more than 5 Hz under
  AP-PERF-001, and only the badge;"
- proposed: "on a software (CPU) graphics adapter the working badge is a still open arc that never
  repaints to animate; otherwise the arc turns, repainting at no more than 5 Hz under AP-PERF-001,
  and only the badge;"
The other mentions ("corner badge (◆, ✕, ✓, or a spinner)", the EON-C31 proof text) stay as they
are. Existing proof records keep their wording.

Decision (relayed by eon-overseer, 2026-10-23): Lucca picked C2. The overseer asked him "1. Pick
C2, the antialiased 270° arc whose frozen form is the same arc", and he replied "1. approve". The
VEN-C21 wording approval is pending until Lucca confirms the exact text above. The eon-overseer
files the implementation bead, which lands the arc in chrome.rs push_badge_glyph together with the
VEN-C21 edit and installed dogfood.

title: Add split support to Eon workspaces
description:
## Decision
Lucca, 2026-10-15: Eon will support splits, so a user can see more than one terminal at once. The
design is not chosen yet. This bead first produces a design for Lucca to approve, then implements it.

## Contract (provisional)
A full-Eon user can view and use more than one pane's terminal at the same time in a workspace,
create and close that arrangement with the keyboard, and move focus between the visible panes.
Terminals stay persistent and independent; detach and reattach preserve the arrangement the design
chooses to persist. The exact shape, persistence and controls are open decisions below.

## Open design decisions
- Shape: arbitrary split tree, fixed layouts, side-by-side expanded panes inside the existing
accordion, or another model. How splits relate to tabs, the accordion stack and pane frames.
- Controls: creating, closing, resizing, focusing and moving splits; which shortcuts, without
breaking existing Alt/Ctrl+Alt bindings.
- Persistence: whether the arrangement survives detach/attach, profile refresh and same-boot
recovery (EON-C15).
- Resize: how each visible terminal's grid is sized and when Orbit receives resizes.
- Accessibility: how the visible panes appear to screen readers and keyboard focus.
- Scope of the first slice and what stays out (for example, popups inside splits).

## Current boundary this changes
Splits contradict accepted contracts and directory rules, so each needs Lucca's approval before it
changes:
- `docs/CONTRACTS.md` EON-C8: "exactly one pane is expanded" and the Boundary excluding arbitrary
split trees and simultaneous expanded panes.
- `venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md` (pane accordion around exactly one expanded pane) and
`venus/docs/PRESENTATION.md` (excludes split trees and simultaneous expanded panes).
- `venus/AGENTS.md`: arbitrary split trees and simultaneous expanded panes are outside Venus. Change
its `.agent-protocols.local.md` and re-render; do not edit the generated file.

## Owners
Eon owns product defaults and the shortcut/configuration policy. Eon Runtime owns workspace state,
the arrangement model and its EONW representation (likely a new EONW revision; historical revisions
stay unchanged). Venus owns geometry, rendering, input, focus and accessibility for several visible
Orbit surfaces. Orbit keeps one terminal per session with one attachment; any Orbit change is a
separate `orbit-protocol` decision with its consumers named.

## Prerequisites and reference gate
No unmet dependency. This is consequential (contract, wire protocol and Venus scope changes). Before
implementation, read the affected `AGENTS.md`, contracts and `docs/REFERENCES.md` routes, and inspect
at least two comparable implementations at exact revisions (for example Zellij, tmux, WezTerm or
Ghostty splits). Record inspected revisions, constraints kept, rejected approaches, the chosen design
and its cheapest falsifying check here. Stop for Lucca's design and contract approval before code.

## Acceptance
- Design phase: Lucca approves a recorded design, the contract changes and the first slice.
- Implementation: installed Eon shows several terminals at once per the approved design; keyboard
create/close/focus work; terminals keep running across detach and reattach; existing tab, pane and
popup behavior still works. Prove with the owners' existing harnesses plus one isolated installed
dogfood observation, then refresh the active Nix profile without interrupting live workspaces.

## Stop boundary
No implementation, contract edit, EONW revision or Orbit protocol change before the design is
approved. Adds no platform promise.
close_reason: Columns of accordions shipped and dogfooded: up to four live side-by-side columns per tab, Alt+Shift+M with Venus width refusal and Eon capacity refusal, column/tab traversal, click selection, per-column resize, persistence across detach/attach. Proof and ledgers in comments.

Evidence at edge 0fd606c: Application (venus/src/application.rs) has 57 fields; about 20 are singleton state for the one attached terminal: transport, model, presentation, active_endpoint/active_endpoint_live, orbit_retry, retry_suppressed, last_resize, deferred_selection, selection_gate, links/link_opener, terminal_scroll, selection_scroll, pending_viewport, pending_return_to_live, scrollback_press. set_orbit_attachment (application.rs:1090) clears and re-attaches all of it on every pane or popup switch. Renderer (venus/src/render.rs) has 40 fields mixing window/GPU state with one terminal's draw state: content_key, text, cursor_animation/cursor_handoff/last_cursor_frame, hyperlink, scrollback_label/rect. Largest bodies: window_event 493 lines (pointer arms), handle_transport 221, Renderer::build_workspace 337, rebuild_if_needed 288.
Decision: after the split design is approved, the first implementation slice is a behavior-preserving extraction of per-terminal state (a TerminalView in Application, a per-terminal draw layer in Renderer) with one instance, proved by the existing Venus suites; later slices add more instances. Do not extract before the design: which state is per-terminal vs per-window depends on design choices (whether unfocused splits stay live, whether scroll/selection/links are per pane, focus model). Rejected: splitting impl Application/Renderer into per-concern impl files now (navigation only; every file still touches the same fields, and splits reshape those methods).

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Reference gate and design proposal (2026-10-16, awaiting Lucca's approval; no code).
Question: how should full Eon show several terminals at once without a second terminal or layout owner?
Contract (proposed): a tab is an ordered row of 1..=4 columns; each column is today's accordion (ordered panes, exactly one expanded). Every column's expanded pane is a live, visible, independently sized terminal. One column is focused; its expanded pane receives keyboard input. A one-column tab behaves exactly as EON-C8 today.
Sources and revisions (inspection only, nothing copied): Zellij v0.45.1 efd8fd5a (MIT); tmux 3.8 7f2a35ad (ISC); WezTerm 20240203-110809-5046fc22 5046fc22 (MIT); Ghostty v1.3.1 332b2aef (MIT); Rio/Canario 3e41b8b1 (MIT, REFERENCES.md route).
Findings that shape the design: Zellij's default stack-list mode is Eon's accordion placed inside a split layout (hidden members keep the expanded member's size, so switching costs no resize). Canario uses a fixed two-level grid (columns of panels), not a tree. tmux/WezTerm/Ghostty use id-keyed split trees with one top-down size owner; WezTerm's client-computed sizes reconciled on the server is a two-owner anti-pattern. All coalesce or debounce PTY resizes; Zellij documents shells mishandling resize bursts. Directional focus: edge-touching and overlapping candidates, tie broken by most recent focus. Zellij Alt+h/l moves focus across panes and falls through to tabs at the edge.
Constraints preserved: Orbit keeps one terminal per session and one attachment; N visible terminals are N ordinary attachments to N sessions (no ORB change). Runtime owns topology/focus/EONW; Venus owns geometry, sizing, input, accessibility; Eon owns defaults.
Options compared: (A) columns of accordions [proposed]; (B) split tree with accordion leaves (Zellij-like, most general); (C) split tree of single panes with the accordion as a zoom view (Ghostty-like; discards the accordion).
Proposed decisions: columns only, equal widths, max 4, refuse below a minimum column width; Alt+Shift+M opens a new column to the right of the focused one with a new pane in the tab directory; Alt+M still adds a pane to the focused column; Alt+H/L move focus between columns and fall through to tabs at the outer edges; Alt+K/J traverse the focused column's accordion; Ctrl+Alt+H/L keep moving tabs; closing a column's last pane removes the column (focus: following column, else preceding); popups stay tab-wide overlays; focused column shown by the existing frame/selection treatment, no dimming; arrangement lives in runtime topology so it survives detach/attach; EON-C15 same-boot recovery still projects into one column of synthetic t1.
Out of first cut: column resize, moving panes between columns, nested/vertical splits, zoom, popups inside columns, restoring arrangement after supervisor loss.
Contract changes needing approval: EON-C8 (one expanded pane per column; boundary drops 'simultaneous expanded panes', keeps 'no arbitrary split tree'), VEN-C8, venus/docs/PRESENTATION.md, venus/AGENTS.md via .agent-protocols.local.md + re-render, a new EONW revision (v10: Tab carries columns), CHANGELOG at delivery.
Slices: (1) Venus per-terminal state extraction, one instance, no behavior change; (2) EONW v10 + runtime column model and actions; (3) Venus N attachments and column layout; (4) installed dogfood and profile refresh.
Cheapest falsifying checks: runtime test that adding then closing a column returns the exact one-column snapshot; Venus headless test that two columns yield two terminal rects with independent grids and one resize each; installed dogfood showing two live terminals side by side updating.

title: Stop a sub-row wheel step from drawing a stale history row over live output
description:
## Problem

Seen in both base Venus (Lucca's profile package /nix/store/dkdls8mz83nscb6flyc7184d69lk4v05-eon-0.1.3, built 2026-10-27 02:00 -03 from the main checkout) and the eon-scroll-preview-per-frame-hhzy candidate, in an isolated headless Sway (pixman, 1600x900, wdotool wlr-protocols wheel). While a program prints a continuous burst, `wdotool scroll 0 -3` over the terminal leaves the pane in a partial-row scroll state. The top edge shows part of an old history row ("burst line 6197"), taken from the first preview answer, above live rows that keep advancing (7709, then 10762, then 15749). The scroll never commits into history while output runs. When the burst ends, the pane is back at live output.

Likely mechanism, not yet verified: the wheel accumulates less than one row of pixels, so `next_request` never commits. The model keeps a compatible Viewport preview across frames (venus/src/model.rs, Frame arm), so `offset()` keeps drawing that old preview's rows above the newest frame.

Evidence: /home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/hhzy-work/base1/{burst,up1,up2,up3,up4,back1,back2,live1,live2,done}.png (base) and /home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/hhzy-work/obs2/ (candidate). Driver: /home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/hhzy-work/run.sh with obs.sh and burst.sh beside it.

## Expected

A wheel step during output either moves into history and holds there, or leaves the view at live with no stale row drawn. Decide which by checking what wdotool's axis event delivers to Venus (LineDelta or PixelDelta, and its size), and how a one-click wheel behaves with no output.

## Contract

VEN-C7 (authoritative history and selection interaction). If the fix changes contract text, stop for Lucca's approval.

## Prerequisites

None. eon-scroll-preview-per-frame-hhzy touches the same module; land it first to avoid conflicts.

## Scope

In scope: Venus scroll preview offset and commit thresholds in venus/src/application/scroll.rs, plus preview retention in venus/src/model.rs. Out of scope: Orbit.

## Acceptance

- A Venus test reproducing the stale preview row drawn over a newer frame.
- One isolated installed observation with the run.sh driver: no stale row, and a wheel step during a burst behaves as decided above.

## Portability disposition

neutral.

comments.text:
Plan note (2026-10-27): this bead was taken up tonight under Lucca's change-of-plan pre-approval, relayed by the coordinator eon-overseer, because lane B's planned beads are done or waiting on orb-j2i.5. Lucca, 2026-10-26, to eon-overseer: "focus on finishing the worspace-switching beads, but try to advance on kitty-graphics too / everything is pre-approved. autonomous. / and sprinkle the ones the subagent listed that are important." and "also pre-aprove changes of plan if a clearly better alternative appears". It applied to taking up this bead. No contract text was adopted: the fix implements VEN-C7 as written.

Diagnosis (by source, before code):
- wdotool 0.5.3's wlr-protocols `scroll 0 -3` (wdotool-core/src/backend/wlr_protocols.rs, do_scroll) sends one zwlr_virtual_pointer_v1.axis of 3.0 with no axis_discrete and no source, then a frame. So Venus gets a PixelDelta of 3 logical pixels, which VEN-C7's precision rule presents as 6 pixels. That is a sub-row nudge, not a wheel click. A physical wheel sends discrete steps, which Venus maps to LineDelta at three rows per click, and those commit at once. With no output, the nudge holds a 6 px offset over a fresh preview, as VEN-C7 intends.
- During output, the model keeps a compatible Viewport preview across frames (venus/src/model.rs, Frame arm), as VEN-C7 requires: "Venus keeps only that bounded revision-bound preview until Orbit supplies its replacement instead of presenting the remainder as zero or freezing finger movement." But TerminalScroll::next_request (venus/src/application/scroll.rs) asks for a preview only when it holds none in the gesture's direction, so it never asks for that replacement. Base before eon-scroll-preview-per-frame-hhzy had the same branch. The first answer's rows ("burst line 6197") then stay drawn above every later frame.

Decision: a sub-row step at live during output keeps its offset (VEN-C7) and draws current history. When the retained preview names an older revision than the current frame and no row was crossed, next_request asks for one replacement PreviewVertical at the current revision, under hhzy's one-outstanding hold. A crossed row still commits first, because the scroll outcome carries the next preview. Residual: until the replacement arrives (one Orbit answer, normally the message right after the frame), the sub-row band shows the row that was above the previous frame. Two alternatives were rejected because each contradicts VEN-C7's text: committing an uncrossed row ("commits crossed rows"), and presenting the remainder as zero ("instead of presenting the remainder as zero").

Not consequential under AGENTS.md's definition: no dependency, protocol, contract, or lifecycle change. No Orbit change is needed. Configurability: no new value. Portability: neutral.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Decision revised after the first review round (a fresh Claude reviewer and Codex, on candidate tree 3b7d4caabb7c3b8bb9c5258be7893d663e3a6442). Both reported the same blocking finding. The one-outstanding hold limits concurrency, not rate: with a sub-row remainder held, every answered frame re-armed a replacement request. That happened both at live and while scrolled into pinned history, where the rows never change. The Claude reviewer also noted that it multiplied hhzy's accepted DEC 2026 residual (a retry under a held synchronized update fails with InvalidInput).

The replacement is now bounded in two ways:
- Gate: Venus asks for a replacement only while the accepted frame is at live (`rows_from_live == 0`, new `VenusModel::at_live` in venus/src/model.rs). VEN-C7: "after history entry, later output leaves the authoritative viewport pinned", so a preview retained in history still shows current rows.
- Pacing: at live, a replacement is sent at most once per PREVIEW_ANSWER_GRACE (50 ms), and it still goes through hhzy's one-outstanding hold. The pacing deadline (`replace_after`) joins `preview_retry_at`, which is already an event-loop deadline, so a stale preview left by the last frame of a burst is still replaced after output stops. When `retry_preview` reaches that deadline it clears it, so the loop does not spin.

So at live during output, with a held sub-row remainder, Venus sends at most about 20 previews per second. In history, and with no output, it sends none. title: Choose every new Eon tab directory before its first pane
description:
## Outcome

Every newly created full-Eon tab chooses its launch directory before Eon starts that tab's first durable pane.

Smallest observable contract:
- Consumer: a person starting a fresh full-Eon workspace or creating a tab with Ctrl+T.
- Trigger: Eon needs the first pane for a new tab.
- Result: Eon creates one active pending tab and one transient packaged Zoxide/fzf picker before any durable pane exists in that tab. Accepting a valid directory atomically commits the tab directory and starts exactly one normal pN Session there. The picker never becomes a pane.
- Important failures: cancelling the first workspace picker starts p1 at Eon's validated launch directory; cancelling a later new-tab picker abandons that pending tab and restores the prior tab and focus. Picker start, helper, selection, target, or presentation failure follows the same respective fallback without a partial tab, durable Session, or transient residue. Existing generations attach without an automatic picker.

Alt+Z remains available on a tab that already has panes and keeps its current retarget-only behavior. Eon never injects cd, restarts an existing pane, or changes a running process working directory.

Impact: HIGH in current dogfood. Effort: L across EONW, Eon Desktop, and Eon. Implementation risk: MEDIUM. Confidence: HIGH in the pending-tab shape.

## Approved interaction and geometry

User decision on 2026-08-26:
- Picker-first applies to the initial tab of a fresh workspace and every newly created tab.
- No shell or other durable pane starts behind the picker.
- The first-tab picker keeps t1 visible in the tab bar. A later pending tab is appended and active while its picker is open.
- Existing picker geometry remains: tab bar visible; picker is the only tab-body terminal; one-cell inset on every side when the grid permits it.
- Accept creates and focuses the first pane at the selected directory.
- First-tab cancel falls back to the validated Eon launch directory. Later-tab cancel removes the pending tab and restores the exact prior workspace focus.
- Attach, recovery, EonTerm, and existing-tab Alt+Z do not auto-open a picker.

## Ownership

- Eon owns pending-tab creation, fallback policy, exact picker command, target validation, first-pane startup, atomic commit, rollback, and cleanup.
- Venus owns pending-tab projection, tab-bar context, modal focus/input, geometry, rendering, notices, accessibility, and exact focus restoration.
- Orbit owns the transient picker PTY and each committed durable pane Session. No Orbit change is expected.
- Zoxide owns ranked directory history; fzf owns selection UI.

## Frontier and protocol order

1. Eon publishes the smallest EONW v4 seed that explicitly represents a pending tab with no selected pane and requires its picker endpoint. EONW v3 remains unchanged.
2. Eon Desktop changes VEN-C18 under its own implementation Bead and accepts one exact v4 consumer revision.
3. Eon pins that exact Venus revision, implements the bootstrap/new-tab lifecycle, refreshes the installed profile, and completes native dogfood.

One frontier moves in that order. Do not build Eon runtime behavior against a speculative Venus consumer.

## Evidence and reference gate

Required:
- Eon source 9f6599d103162061ee666126c2eddce03383afb6 and EON-C17/EON-C18.
- Exact Venus picker source df88b2867d50c59a316418471abd000da02940bc and current VEN-C18 model, scene, focus, accessibility, and transport owners.
- Exact Orbit 70861097a825c2fbfaea53a8ca9437f45e8602eb startup, exit, attachment, and Stop contracts.
- Existing EONW v2/v3 codecs and version-rejection tests.
- Existing Zoxide/fzf dependency decision and packaged helper.

Adopt:
- A versioned pending-tab state, not an empty-string sentinel, placeholder pane, hidden shell, injected cd, restarted Session, or generic modal.
- One transient picker Session followed by one durable pane Session; they never overlap as pane topology in the pending tab.

## Acceptance criteria

- Fresh Eon publishes t1 plus its picker before session-1 exists. Accept starts p1/session-1 exactly once at the selected directory.
- Ctrl+T publishes one appended active pending tab and picker before allocating or starting its first pN/session-N. Accept commits one pane with the next canonical identities.
- First-tab cancel/failure starts p1 at the original validated launch directory. Later-tab cancel/failure restores the previous tab/focus and consumes no pane or Session identity.
- No picker outcome changes or restarts existing pane CWDs or processes.
- Alt+Z on an existing tab retains explicit retarget-only behavior.
- Pending state is impossible without exactly one picker bound to the active pending tab; durable tabs retain exactly one selected pane and at least one pane.
- Venus preserves the existing tab bar, inset, input, focus, narrow-grid, notice, and accessibility behavior without inventing a popup framework.
- Recovery stops stale transient pickers and never restores pending tabs.
- Full affected Rust, EONW, manifest, Nix, lifecycle, accessibility, and installed native Wayland surfaces pass on exact revisions. Profile refresh preserves live Sessions.

## Scope boundary

No generic popup, zero-pane durable tab, placeholder shell, pane replacement, shell integration, cd injection, arbitrary command, Yazi path, persisted pending tab, recovery of pending topology, EonTerm behavior, compatibility window, other platform, or automatic picker on attach. Starting each tab with Yazi remains separate.

## Stop conditions

- Stop before Venus production edits until its own implementation Bead is selected and baselined.
- Stop before Eon runtime edits until exact accepted Venus v4 proof exists.
- Stop if the design requires an Orbit protocol change, simultaneous picker and durable-pane presentation in a pending tab, or a second workspace schema owner.

title: Fix the flaky startup-anima picker test
description:
## Defect
One full `nix develop -c eon-test` run (run 8 of 18 during eon-orbit-ready-claim-flake-3si2, 2026-10-17, x86_64 Linux, eon-test sandbox) failed `failed_or_stuck_startup_anima_reports_and_continues_to_picker` (eon/crates/eon/tests/workspace_control.rs:396): exit code 1 where 0 was expected. The other 17 runs passed it. Not caused by that bead's test-only Orbit change.

## Contract
The test passes deterministically under the full parallel workspace run, or its failure exposes a real startup-anima or picker defect that is then fixed at its owner.

## Acceptance
Root cause named with red/green evidence; the fix at the owner (test or product); repeated full eon-test runs pass. Scope: this test and its owner only.
close_reason: ETXTBSY from a concurrently forked child holding the test's script writer; the helper now writes scripts from a child process. Red/green and proof in comments.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Root cause: ETXTBSY. executable() wrote each fake script with fs::write in the test process. A concurrent test in the same workspace_control process can fork while that write descriptor is open; the child keeps it until its exec, and exec of a file with an open writer fails with ETXTBSY. Exit 1 at line 396 is directory_picker failing to spawn the fake zoxide or fzf. Red (temporary stressor, not committed: 16 threads spawning `true` with a 30 ms pre_exec while 1000 iterations write fresh zoxide/fzf scripts and run `eon __startup-anima` with a missing Anima): 8/1000 and 12/1000 failures, stderr 'cannot launch packaged directory history: Text file busy (os error 26)' and the same for the directory picker. Fix at the owner, the test helper: a short-lived sh child writes and chmods each script, so the test process never holds a writer that a fork can inherit. Green: same stressor 0/1000. Product unaffected: pinned zoxide/fzf are never written at runtime. Out of scope, not changed: other test binaries (eon-runtime, orbit, installer) write exec'd scripts with the same pattern and may share the latent race.

Review ledger: 1 pass (Codex gpt-6.1-sol read-only): nothing blocking, no nits.

title: Stop previous or all Eon generations with eon stop
description:
## Contract
Consumer: Eon users cleaning up generations. Trigger: `eon stop previous [--json]` or `eon stop all [--json]`. Result: previous attempts every non-dead generation except installed current. Previous does not require current to be live; each previous target remains explicit and validated. Fixed-namespace legacy reports its own unavailable reason. All attempts every non-dead generation, with current last. Each target uses validated, version-aware supervisor Stop and human confirmation; declining one reports no Stop for that target while prior outcomes remain and later targets continue. JSON mode is noninteractive like single Stop. While the caller remains running, continue after an unavailable or failed target and exit nonzero if any Stop attempt fails. Stopping the caller's own Session can terminate the CLI before later targets or a complete JSON result. Fixed-namespace legacy and unknown EONW remain unavailable. No PID, systemd, or process-name fallback.
Owner: EON-C11 in docs/CONTRACTS.md. No wire change or dependency.

## Evidence and reference gate
Question: how can one invocation stop selected generations while preserving supervisor authority and live work after a profile refresh?
Primary: Eon generation discovery, selected inspection, and per-generation Stop in crates/eon/src/generation.rs; CLI dispatch in crates/eon/src/cli.rs; EON-C11; Orbit ORB-C12/C13 accepted management Stop at 0233f4d34b294a50c5bc7f373859cf4ec04d2414.
Comparable: local tmux 3.4 manual distinguishes kill-session -a and kill-server; its server-wide mechanism is not copied.
Child pins: Orbit f8ad14e5195109ba8cb421f30e5ae4a9619a1419 and Venus f6c1ebdb16df2960077dbd88ab6728a921b789d8 match latest accepted code revisions. Baseline Eon ed4d09b82e6105fbf3e0c64b34f18b6281aefe63.
Adopt: compose discovery with existing Stop; select previous independently of current's live state; retain per-target validation and confirmation.
Reject: process kill, systemd control, duplicate Stop implementation, automatic eviction, silently skipping unavailable targets, and a current-live prerequisite that blocks explicit previous Stop.

## Acceptance
Private runtime with two previous and one current proves previous preserves current, all includes current last, and one failed target does not suppress another. Previous attempts an older versioned generation while current is unstarted. Verify help, docs, LOC, locked Rust, Clippy, Nix flake, profile identity, installed private-runtime behavior, and preservation of live user Sessions.

title: Streamline dense documentation across Eon repositories
description:
## Observable outcome

Consumer: a human or coding agent reading canonical engineering documentation in Eon, Eon Sessions, Eon Desktop, or Eonova.

Trigger: the reader needs one ownership boundary, dependency decision, reference route, proof case, or status entry.

Result: the reader can find and understand that item without horizontally parsing paragraph-sized Markdown table cells. Tables remain for compact repeated fields and real comparisons; dense records use stable headings with short labeled fields or bullets.

Important failures: no contract, proof identity, accepted revision, source link, owner, rejection, status, scope boundary, or current limitation may disappear or change meaning. This repository-tooling and documentation task changes no EON, ORB, or VEN product contract, runtime behavior, dependency decision, component revision, platform promise, or compatibility boundary.

## Why and evidence

The current table shape compresses long-form decision records into raw Markdown rows that are hard to scan, review, diff, and maintain. This is one coordinating P1 task because the user chose a consistent pass across all four repositories. Effort M; risk LOW-MEDIUM because most edits are structural documentation, with one narrow repository-governance parser update.

Inspected baselines:

- Eon Sessions at `1f90809d9141b4faff110ec54c4e886aaa3bb193`: `docs/CRATES.md` stores six-field dependency decisions in rows up to 3,329 characters; `docs/CONTRACTS.md` has conformance rows up to 456 characters.
- Eon at `9a56aeb18fc83dccbcf8887f63cc17a08d3cbf53`: `docs/REFERENCES.md` has routing rows up to 1,942 characters, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` ownership rows up to 459, and `docs/DISTRIBUTION.md` conditional routes up to 530.
- Eon Desktop at `d3dea8868f5b841be56d149f31457a7acf77609f`: `docs/CRATES.md` decision rows reach 661 characters. Its measured-comparison table is genuinely tabular and is not a conversion target without a concrete readability failure.
- Eonova at `f4717efe7c68f6061209a225c2a551031da82060`: the only table is a compact README LOC scorecard, so review is expected to produce no change.
- Eon Sessions `tools/governance/src/main.rs` currently parses the exact `docs/CRATES.md` six-column table and rejects malformed status, missing exact version or commit, missing credible alternatives, missing evidence Beads, and unknown contract references. `README.md` documents that row-shape contract. A document-only scope would therefore make the main rewrite unimplementable.
- Closed Eon Beads `eon-tighten-reference-routing-g0h` and `eon-contract-index-current-state-iuh` own the accepted routing and current-state decisions. This task changes presentation, not those decisions.

## Prerequisites and reference gate

Before implementation, reread each repository `AGENTS.md` and the exact target documents. In Eon Sessions, also read the governance description in `README.md`, `check_crates`, the shared Markdown helpers, and the existing governance fixtures in `tools/governance/src/main.rs`.

Adopt the repository-native heading-plus-labeled-field pattern already used for `docs/CONTRACTS.md` where it fits. Keep Markdown itself as the source of truth. Reject a generator, documentation framework, general Markdown parser, new dependency, universal template, or separate lint script: none removes an owned responsibility here.

## Scope

In scope:

- Handwritten Markdown in the Eon, Eon Sessions, Eon Desktop, and Eonova repositories, addressed by repository name and repository-relative path.
- Inventory every non-generated table containing multi-sentence rationale, conditional routing, evidence history, or paragraph prose.
- Convert confirmed dense records to the smallest readable shape: stable headings plus only the labels each record needs, with a compact index only when it materially improves navigation.
- Retain compact matrices, version maps, scorecards, dependency counts, and short ownership mappings when comparison across columns is clearer.
- In Eon Sessions only, update `tools/governance/src/main.rs` and its co-located tests so the governance command validates the new canonical `docs/CRATES.md` section shape. Update the corresponding README governance description.
- Refresh relative links, heading references, and README LOC scorecards where repository policy requires them.

Out of scope:

- Generated `AGENTS.md`, protocol imports, Beads storage other than this task, source code or tests outside the Eon Sessions governance owner, manifests, lock files, Nix, runtime profiles, and CHANGELOG behavior records.
- Product-contract edits, proof promotion, dependency decisions, reference selection, content expansion, or factual corrections hidden inside reformatting.
- A documentation generator, framework, renderer, new dependency, compatibility layer, summary mirror, or second source of truth.

## Implementation notes

1. Record the exact repository revisions, dirty paths, table candidates, record headings, contract IDs, Bead IDs, 40-hex revisions, and external URLs before editing.
2. Start with Eon Sessions `docs/CRATES.md`. Replace the paragraph-cell table with one section per decision using the same six owned fields: boundary, selected shape, status, credible alternatives, rationale, and evidence. Add a compact index only if the headings alone are insufficient.
3. Adapt the existing governance parser and fixtures to that section structure, preserving every current rejection. Do not build a generic Markdown parser.
4. Apply the same prose-versus-comparison test to the named Eon, Orbit, and Venus documents. Review Eonova and leave its scorecard unchanged unless a concrete failure appears.
5. Compare the semantic inventory after each repository. Keep repository commits independently reviewable and follow each repository Git and LOC policy.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every handwritten Markdown table row currently longer than 300 characters is reviewed. No remaining table cell contains multi-sentence rationale, conditional routing, evidence history, or paragraph prose.
- A row longer than 300 characters may remain only when its cells are compact parallel data and the table is clearer than separate records; retained candidates and the reason are recorded in this Bead.
- Every converted record has a stable heading and remains reachable from its document or a compact index.
- Per-record owners, statuses, selected shapes, alternatives, rationale, evidence, contract IDs, Bead IDs, exact 40-hex revisions, source links, and scope boundaries retain their meaning. Baseline and final identifier and URL inventories are identical unless the user separately approves a current-state correction.
- Eon Sessions governance accepts the new canonical crate-decision structure and still rejects malformed canonical decision structure, unknown contract references, invalid decision status, missing exact version or commit, missing credible alternatives, and missing existing evidence Beads.
- The existing governance tests are adapted rather than mirrored; no new dependency, generator, general parser, or standalone linter is added.
- Repository-local documentation and LOC policies are satisfied. No runtime or Nix artifact build, profile refresh, product proof, or behavior claim is made.

## Verification

- Use a read-only `awk` inventory of long Markdown table rows as a review list, not as a zero-row formatting quota.
- Compare sorted `rg` inventories for contract IDs, Bead IDs, exact 40-hex revisions, and `https://` URLs, then review each converted record field-for-field.
- Resolve changed relative links and headings locally, check changed external targets, and preview representative converted documents.

Prefer deleting table syntax and separating independent records. Do not replace compact scorecards or true comparison matrices with repetitive prose. The goal is lower cognitive and diff complexity, not a character-count score.

title: Persistent bounded diagnostic log for Eon supervisors and Venus
description:
## Why

eon-jqxr: a Venus window exited after Alt+Shift+W while its supervisor and terminals lived on, and
nothing recorded why. A COSMIC launch runs `eon` with stdout/stderr on /dev/null, the supervisor
runs in that process, and Venus inherited its stderr, so panics and supervisor diagnostics vanished.
Lucca, 2026-10-21: "maybe we could improve our logging and wait for it to happen again?"; chose a
persistent, bounded log over a runtime-directory one.

## Contract (no stable ID; documented in docs/USAGE.md troubleshooting and CHANGELOG)

Consumer: the user or an agent diagnosing a window that ended unexpectedly.

- Every Eon supervisor (workspace and eonbase) that holds its generation's lifecycle lock writes
  one diagnostic log, `$XDG_STATE_HOME/eon/logs/<generation>-<unix-seconds>-<pid>.log`
  (`$HOME/.local/state/eon/logs` when XDG_STATE_HOME is unset or relative). The file is 0600; the
  logs directory must be owned by the user and not a symlink, and is set to 0700.
- Each line carries a local ISO 8601 timestamp. It records: supervisor start (generation, mode,
  pid) and its final result (exit status or error, including configuration errors before
  launch); each Eon Desktop (Venus) start with its pid and each Venus exit with its exit code or
  signal, once, on every reap path (observed exit, admission failure, supervisor shutdown); each
  terminal that ends on its own (its program exited, or Orbit exited without a result) with its
  status; each tab close's terminals, duration and outcome, also when it fails; and the supervisor
  diagnostics that used to go only to stderr. Per-terminal lines cover terminals the supervisor
  reaps on their own. A terminal stopped by a pane, popup or tab close or by `eon stop`, including
  one that exits by itself while that stop runs, gets no per-terminal line. For a tab close, the
  close's record stands for it.
- Venus's stderr goes through a pipe that the supervisor copies verbatim into the log and onto
  its own stderr. Before recording a Venus exit, the supervisor waits up to 1 s for that copy to
  drain. Venus runs with RUST_BACKTRACE=1 unless the environment already sets it.
- Bounds: copied output stops 64 KiB short of 1 MiB, with one marker line. That reserve keeps
  room for the supervisor's own lines, which stop at 1 MiB. At start, a supervisor creates its
  own log, which it holds locked, and then deletes all but the newest 20 regular files named
  `<valid generation>-<seconds>-<pid>.log`. Logs locked by running supervisors are never deleted.
  Anything else in the directory is left alone, and symlinks are never followed.
- Failure: if the log cannot be created, Eon warns on stderr (best effort) and starts without it.
  If the copy thread cannot start, that Venus launch fails like any other start failure.
- Accepted gap: if the supervisor's own stderr stops draining (e.g. a suspended terminal), the
  copy blocks and Venus's stderr writes then block. Before this change Venus wrote to that same
  stderr directly, so it blocked the same way. Bytes already read land in the log first.
  Supervisor death by signal leaves no end line.

## Owner

Eon Runtime supervisor (`runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/diagnostics.rs`, used by `supervisor.rs`).
Out of scope: Orbit's stderr, which stays on /dev/null, and Eon CLI clients.

## Reference gate

- Routes: docs/REFERENCES.md has no logging route, so I inspected comparable implementations
  instead.
- WezTerm `20240203-110809-5046fc22`, `env-bootstrap/src/ringlog.rs`: one
  `<exe>-log-<pid>.txt` per process in its runtime dir, still logging to stderr, and pruning logs
  older than a week when the GUI starts. Kept: one file per process, stderr kept, prune at start.
  Changed: a persistent state dir (Lucca's choice: a log must outlive the window and a reboot),
  and count/size bounds instead of age, with live logs protected by a lock.
- Ghostty `8c425a7bd57d`: logs to stderr (and the macOS unified log) via GHOSTTY_LOG; no Linux file
  log. Rejected: it relies on the launcher keeping stderr, which COSMIC does not.
- No dependency change: timestamps use libc localtime_r/strftime (libc is already pinned). Turning
  on `time` formatting features was rejected as a dependency change for one format call.

## Acceptance

- Focused tests through `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime -p eon` (the eon crate's
  `workspace_control` suite asserts a real supervisor's log has a failed and a successful tab close):
  - real log names round-trip through pruning;
  - live and foreign files survive;
  - modes are 0600 and 0700;
  - the bound and its marker hold, with the reserve keeping room for records;
  - Venus stderr is copied ahead of its exit signal line, exactly once;
  - an admission failure records the exit.
- Installed dogfood (isolated headless Sway): launch the built package, kill its Venus, and find
  the start and exit lines in the log.

## Scope boundary

No log viewer, no `eon` subcommand, no Orbit stderr, no log levels or config. Prerequisite for
eon-jqxr's diagnosis.

title: Fix the intermittent supervisor Orbit-stderr test (ETXTBSY)
description:
## Why

A flaky eon-runtime test fails suites at random and costs reruns for every agent that runs `eon-test -p eon-runtime`.

## Evidence

- On 2026-10-27, during eon-agent-parity-a9g0.8 (worktree base 872f00a), `supervisor::tests::orbit_stderr_is_logged_and_owner_loss_names_the_file` failed once with `Text file busy (os error 26)` (ETXTBSY). The rerun passed.
- Same class as eon-ven-new-window-test-flake-66gm (landed abdbfd0) and eon-1fxc (landed 1869c19). In both, the test process wrote an executable script while parallel tests forked, so a child inherited the write descriptor and exec failed with ETXTBSY. Both were fixed by having a child `/bin/sh` write each script to a fresh path.

## Scope

- Confirm the cause in this test: a bounded loop or a standalone repro, and print the error.
- Fix the test only, following the pattern already used in quota.rs's tests (1869c19), as a local helper.
- Out of scope: production code, unless the cause turns out to be there.

## Acceptance

- Red/green evidence: a repro that fails before the fix and passes after it.
- A bounded loop of `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime --lib -- --test-threads=4` (30 runs) with no failure of this test.
- eon-runtime fmt and clippy -D warnings clean.

Filed by eon-overseer on 2026-10-27 from eon-57's report (eon-agent-parity-a9g0.8).

Plan (eon-2f, 2026-10-27, base a5a819f). Not a consequential code shape: test-only, no dependency, protocol, contract, or lifecycle change, so no reference gate.

A child forked meanwhile by a parallel test inherits the write descriptor until it execs, so the exec can fail with ETXTBSY. Same class as eon-1fxc and eon-ven-new-window-test-flake-66gm.
- Fix: a local `script` helper in supervisor.rs `mod tests`, following quota.rs's (1869c19): a child `/bin/sh` writes the file (`printf '%s' "$1" > "$0"`) and the test process only chmods by path. The launcher already runs under `#!/bin/sh`, so the writer uses `/bin/sh` too. The two nested `use std::process::Command` imports in later tests become redundant with the module import and go.
