title: Switch to another Eon window from an in-Eon picker (Alt+Shift+S)
description:
## Why

eon-n77e: inside Eon, the only way to see other windows is Commands > List windows, which prints read-only text. Every reference has an in-app picker over detached work:

- tmux `C-b s` and `S-Tab`
- the Zellij session-manager
- WezTerm's launcher
- kitty's `goto_session`
- Rex's "Change Session…"
- the tuios switcher

Eon keeps one workspace per OS window, so a switch attaches or raises that window (kitty's "natural" shape). It does not swap content in place.

## Contract (proposed; bring the exact EON-C23, EON-C10 and Venus shortcut wording to Lucca before code)

Alt+Shift+S, and a Commands entry "Switch window" that replaces the read-only "List windows", open an Eon-owned fzf popup (VEN-C18: no native Venus picker). It lists every other Eon window from the listing bead:

- the name, or else the tab summary;
- open or detached;
- the tab count.

Choosing a row acts as follows:

- **Detached:** attaches it, which opens its OS window.
- **Open:** asks the compositor for attention, the only thing Wayland allows (VEN-C14). The docs say so plainly.
- **Not attachable:** the row says why and does nothing.

Esc closes the popup without acting. The current window is not listed. The popup never stops a window.

## Reference gate

This adds a shortcut and a popup, with no EONW change.

- Read docs/REFERENCES.md:200 (pickers: Eon-owned fzf popups, Kitty overlays and Zellij in-place commands; reject a generic popup protocol).
- Read the session-switching route that the listing bead adds.
- Check that Alt+Shift+S is free once m798 has taken Alt+Shift+D.

## Scope

In scope: the popup command, the shortcut, the Commands entry, the hints and Shortcuts help text, USAGE and contract text, CHANGELOG.

Out of scope:

- in-window swapping;
- create or rename from the picker, since New window stays in Commands;
- next, previous and last-window keys;
- attention badges (the next bead).

## Acceptance

From an installed Eon, with one other window open and one detached:

- Alt+Shift+S lists both.
- Choosing the detached one opens it.
- Choosing the open one raises an attention hint, without stealing focus beyond what the compositor grants.
- Esc does nothing.

## Verification

Installed route: profile refresh plus one isolated dogfood observation for the batch. Codex on every code change.

title: Add T3 Chat and ChatGPT desktop as visual references
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-10-23: "do we have t3chat and chatgpt-desktop as references? we should", then
"search more about them or delegate to an agent, and only them add to references". Neither
product appears in docs/VISUAL-REFERENCES.md, docs/REFERENCES.md or ~/pjs/refs.

## Contract

None. Discovery notes only; no dependency, source reuse or product scope is authorized.

## Scope

- Research T3 Chat (t3.chat, Theo / T3 Tools; whether any source is public and its license) and
  the ChatGPT desktop apps (macOS and Windows: companion window/launcher, conversation sidebar,
  task and agent progress, notifications) with web search.
- Record concrete, verifiable UX lessons for Eon (agent sidebar, attention, switching between
  agents, launching, perceived speed), with sources and access dates, as a comment here.
- Add one short entry for each to docs/VISUAL-REFERENCES.md in its existing style and caveats,
  naming exactly which Eon questions each informs.

Out of scope: any code, contract, or other doc change; filing follow-up beads.

## Acceptance

- Research comment on this bead with sources and dates.
- Two entries in docs/VISUAL-REFERENCES.md; one fresh Claude review pass finds nothing blocking.
- Proof route: docs-only (beads state, changed Markdown path, diff). No profile refresh.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
## Research (accessed 2026-10-23; two web-research subagents, key claims spot-checked by the implementer)

Evidence tags: [v] fetched and checked by the implementer on 2026-10-23; [s] subagent report only; [inf] inference.

### T3 Chat (https://t3.chat)

- Source: no public T3 Chat repository. GitHub user pingdotgg lists no T3 Chat repo [v, API]; the FAQ does not mention open source [s]. T3-Content/t3-cloneathon is an MIT starter for a 2025 contest, last pushed 2025-07-09, not T3 Chat [v]. pingdotgg/t3code is MIT, pushed 2026-10-23, and is a separate coding-agent app [v]. So T3 Chat is proprietary; only its public behaviour is reference material.
- Speed: Theo's build video (2025-01-20, https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QLvIoi2s1zY) describes client-side routing ("I didn't want the server to be involved in navigation"), streaming into a local Dexie/IndexedDB store read through live queries, and memoized finished markdown blocks so only the streaming block re-renders [s]. Moved to Convex as sync engine (Theo, 2025-06-01, https://x.com/theo/status/1929264138544615464) [s]; Convex postmortem (2025-06-03, https://news.convex.dev/how-convex-took-down-t3-chat-june-1-2025-postmortem/): "every online user is subscribed to the first 20 messages for preloading" [s].
- Sidebar: date groups, pins synced across devices, archive and temporary chats (Theo, 2026-02-19) [s]. Cmd/Ctrl+K search, Cmd+Shift+O new chat, Cmd/Ctrl+B sidebar; recent chats removed from Cmd+K as duplicating the sidebar (https://feedback.t3.chat/p/cmd-k, 2025-12-16) [s]. Branching makes each branch a new chat; users say it clutters history (https://feedback.t3.chat/p/branching-chats) [s].
- In-progress marker: "Show Loading Spinner in sidebar on actively generating threads" is Completed; its request says users in other threads otherwise had to check each thread by hand while long responses streamed (https://feedback.t3.chat/p/show-loading-spinner-in-sidebar-on-actively-generating-threads, undated) [v].
- Attention gap: "Notification when request is complete" (tab title/favicon, optional notification) is still "Gathering Interest" (https://feedback.t3.chat/p/notification-when-request-is-complete, undated) [v]. No verified done/unread signal found; only the working spinner [s].
- Launch: `/new?q=&model=&effort=&search=&search_limit=&profile=&temporary=` opens a fully configured new chat; only `q` is required (https://t3.chat/faq, undated) [v]. A choosable default model vs last-used is an open request; users report wasted premium credits when the last-used model carries over [s].
- Limits: the app pages sit behind a Vercel bot checkpoint, so nothing was observed in-app [s]. Board statuses are not in-app proof that a feature shipped.

### ChatGPT desktop apps (macOS, Windows)

- Product line: on 2026-07-09 OpenAI turned the Codex desktop app into the new ChatGPT desktop app with Chat, Work and Codex modes; the old app became "ChatGPT Classic" (macOS release notes https://help.openai.com/en/articles/9703738; https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001276) [s]. Linux preview 2026-08-11 [s]. Current docs at learn.chatgpt.com are undated. Proprietary: no public source found [s, inf]; the Codex CLI is separately open source.
- Launcher: Option+Space (macOS) / Windows+Alt+P show floating "pets" and focus Quick Chat; a pet "can float above other app windows"; clicking a thread opens it in the main app (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/pets) [v]. Classic companion window "stays in front of all other windows" (Aug 2024 notes) [s]. Windows Classic Alt+Space fails silently when another app holds it (https://help.openai.com/en/articles/9982051) [s].
- Statuses and priority: Needs input > Blocked (failed or system error) > Ready (finished with unread activity) > Running (pets doc) [v].
- Activity view: bell in the sidebar or Cmd+Option+U / Ctrl+Alt+U lists chats that are "unread, running, or waiting for your response", with filters and "Mark all as read" (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/notifications) [v].
- Shortcuts (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/reference/commands) [v]: new chat Cmd/Ctrl+N; toggle sidebar Cmd/Ctrl+B; go to chat 1-9; next/previous chat Ctrl+Tab / Ctrl+Shift+Tab; mark unread Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+U; clear all unread Shift+Esc (Codex only); next chat needing attention Cmd+Option+A / Ctrl+Alt+A (Codex only).
- Notifications: turn completion "never, only while ChatGPT is in the background, or always"; permission and question requests have separate toggles (notifications doc) [v].
- Long work: `/goal` progress row with pause, resume, edit, clear; side chat for status without interrupting (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/long-running-work) [s]. Agent mode narrates on screen and lets the user take over (https://openai.com/index/introducing-chatgpt-agent/, 2025-07-17) [s].
- Work with Apps (Classic, macOS): reads Terminal, iTerm, Warp via Accessibility, sending the last 200 lines of open panes, with a banner naming what is attached (https://help.openai.com/en/articles/10119604) [s]. Windows Computer Use "take[s] over the foreground" (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/computer-use) [s].
- Criticism: closing the Companion "no longer returns focus to the previous app" (forum, 2026-07-25; support 2026-07-29 called the old behaviour undocumented but said closing should return focus) (https://community.openai.com/t/companion-window-no-longer-returns-focus-to-the-previous-app/1388206) [v]. Option+Space repointed from ChatGPT to Codex without a choice (2026-07-10, https://community.openai.com/t/companion-window-should-stay-available-for-chatgpt-not-only-codex/1386295) [s]. Companion position settings removed (2026-07-17) [s]. New windows do not focus the input (2026-10-05) [s].

### Lessons for Eon (inference from the above)

1. Attention states: ChatGPT's four ranked states (needs input > blocked > ready-unread > running) and T3 Chat's spinner-only gap both argue for distinct waiting, error, done-unseen and working states, ranked, with a "next agent needing attention" key.
2. Unread as state: mark-unread, clear-all and an activity filter; per the Humans and Agents rule each needs an `eon` CLI path.
3. Notifications: never / background-only / always for completion, separate toggles for permission requests.
4. Focus: a transient launcher or popup must return focus where it came from, and must focus its input when the user opened it; users noticed the loss within weeks.
5. Launch: T3 Chat's one-URL fully parameterized launch maps to `eon pane create`; an explicit default profile beats "last used".
6. Speed: switch from locally held state, preload, render only what changes.
7. Grouping: forks as new top-level rows clutter the list; keep spawned agents under their parent.

The 'next chat needing attention' key is Codex-mode only. T3 Chat's client-side routing and Dexie streaming come from 2025 sources that predate or straddle its Convex move.

title: Venus AccessKit focus may name a hidden Shortcuts header button
description:
## Defect (suspected, found while fixing eon-accesskit-orphan-content-9nbd; not reproduced)

`Snapshot::tree` (`venus/src/accessibility.rs`, focus match) maps `WorkspaceFocus::Header(control)`
to `control_node_id(control)`, but the header-control loop skips any control whose
`rect.width <= 0.0`. Only Shortcuts can have zero width: `scene.rs` hides it when the hints bar
is complete and `keep_shortcuts` is false. If the accessibility snapshot's `workspace_focus` is
`Header(Shortcuts)` while its scene hides Shortcuts, the update's focus names a node that is not in
the tree, and accesskit_consumer 0.38.0 unwraps it in `State::focus` (`tree.rs:546`) while the
host is focused, so Venus exits.

The scene keeps Shortcuts while focus is on it (`keep_shortcuts`, `scene.rs:812`), so this needs
the snapshot focus and the scene's focus to diverge. Whether any path sets
`Snapshot::workspace_focus` without rebuilding the scene with that focus is unverified.

## Contract

Venus accessibility (VEN-C18 workspace header controls): Venus must not exit.

## Acceptance

First establish reachability: trace every writer of `Snapshot::workspace_focus` and of the scene
passed to `set_workspace`. If reachable, add a red/green test through accesskit_consumer's Tree
(the dev-dependency eon-accesskit-orphan-content-9nbd added; its `IgnoreChanges` handler) and make
focus fall back to the selected tab when the control is hidden. If unreachable, record the proof
and close.

## Scope boundary

Only header-control focus. No change to hints or header layout.

title: A failed tab close ends the supervisor and the whole window
description:
## Report

Lucca, 2026-10-23 ~13:22 -03: "last window crashed when i tried close tab 2". The window was supervisor g1-f1f6b48b14309a0f4484891c8b29f1b5 (PID 3357673, profile r18mya95…-eon-0.1.1, EONW 18, started 06:28).

## Evidence (supervisor log ~/.local/state/eon/logs/g1-f1f6b48b14309a0f4484891c8b29f1b5-1792743714-3357673.log)

```
13:22:03.882 closing tab t3: stopping session-31, session-32
13:22:08.005 tab t3 close failed after 4122 ms: session-32: session-32: ended terminal record /run/user/1000/eon/generations/g1-f1f6…/session-32.sock.record disappeared; cannot reconcile terminal after failed stop: …
13:22:08.518 Eon Desktop exited: exit status: 0
13:22:08.519 supervisor failed: ended terminal record …/session-32.sock.record disappeared
```

So one terminal whose stop did not confirm, and whose ended record then vanished, turned a tab close into a supervisor failure. Venus exited and the whole window ended. Other tabs' terminals (Claude agents in tab t1) survived as orphaned Orbit hosts, still running, but with no supervisor or window to reach them.

## Expected

Closing a tab never ends the supervisor or other tabs. A terminal that can't be reconciled after a stop is reported (a VEN-C8 notice and a log line) and removed from the tab, or the tab stays with that terminal marked, but the workspace keeps running.

## Related

eon-jqxr (Closing tab 1 closed the whole window, 2026-10-21, EONW 13): same symptom, which was undiagnosed then because the supervisor logged nothing. This log is the first evidence of a mechanism; check whether jqxr is the same bug and fold it in. Contract owners: EON-C8 (tab close) and EON-C10 (failure kinds).

## Scope

Reproduce in an isolated session: close a tab whose terminal's stop times out or whose ended record disappears, for example by making the stop exceed its grace or removing the record mid-stop. Make the failure local to that tab. Add a red/green test at the Runtime level.

## Acceptance

- A Runtime test: an unreconcilable terminal during tab close leaves the supervisor running and other tabs intact, and reports the failure.
- An installed observation of the same in an isolated window.
close_reason: Failed tab close stays local; Runtime red/green and isolated installed observation recorded

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Diagnosis (eon-7iap, 2026-10-23). Orbit's host failure path (orbit/src/host.rs run, Err arm: failed host, dead or stalled Bend worker) drops its RecordGuard, which removes the Live record and publishes no tombstone (orbit/src/management.rs Drop for RecordGuard). wait_and_finalize_tombstone failed on a missing record ('ended terminal record ... disappeared'). The failed stop left the terminal tracked, and the main loop's reap_finished_sessions returned the same error with '?', which ended the supervisor. Fix (Runtime sessions.rs): a vanished record whose recorded Orbit process is dead reconciles as owner-lost (endpoints checked and removed, child reaped), the same as a dead process with a Live record. While that Orbit still runs, the Runtime waits within the deadline. A tab close then prunes the terminal (status 1) and succeeds. No EON-C8/C10 wording change: EON-C8 already keeps a failed close local (eon-overseer agreed, 2026-10-23). eon-jqxr is a different bug: there the supervisor survived. Orbit's stderr gap (no trace of why its host failed) is out of scope; eon-overseer will raise it with Lucca. Red/green: supervisor::tests::a_terminal_whose_orbit_fails_during_a_close_ends_only_that_terminal kills one leased Orbit's worker, then runs the tab close's per-terminal stop. Red on 0ca4a64 failed with the incident's exact error; green: eon-runtime 85 passed, 1 ignored; fmt and clippy clean.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Evidence (eon-overseer found it; eon-7iap checked it, 2026-10-23). Lucca's windows run Orbit through a stderr-logging wrapper. ~/.local/share/eon/orbit-window/logs/675175.log (Orbit /nix/store/7vv3pwvpyir2r0vgmjczf90gw3ji2fbg-yazelix-orbit-0.1.0, started 16:21:57Z, 6 s before the 13:22 -03 close) ends with 'PTY child was not reaped after canonical session exit', which is the Bend worker's IO.die at orbit/src/main.bend:56. A dead worker takes Orbit's host failure path (orbit/src/host.rs run, Err arm): Orbit contains the child and drops its RecordGuard, removing the Live record without a tombstone. That matches the diagnosis above. The red/green test reproduces the same path by SIGKILLing a leased Orbit's worker. Why the worker found its PTY child unreaped during Stop is an Orbit defect outside this bead (reported to eon-overseer). Codex review round 1 (gpt-6.1-sol xhigh) on candidate tree abe1cf52: nothing blocking.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Proof (eon-7iap, 2026-10-23). Change: (1) sessions.rs wait_and_finalize_tombstone reconciles a vanished record whose recorded Orbit process is dead as owner-lost; while that Orbit still runs, it waits within the deadline. (2) supervisor.rs reap_finished_sessions no longer ends the supervisor for a tracked terminal whose Stop failed (RunningSession::stop_failed). The terminal stays in its tab for a retry, as EON-C8 says, and the log gets one note: 'terminal <id> stays in its tab after a failed stop: <error>'. CHANGELOG entry added. Test supervisor::tests::a_terminal_whose_stop_fails_during_a_close_ends_or_stays_only_in_its_tab covers three leased Orbits. One's worker is SIGKILLed: its close stop now returns Ok(Some(1)); red on 0ca4a64 with the incident error. One has a mode-0644 record, so its stop fails: two reaps return Ok, with exactly one note. Red with the containment disabled: reap returned Err(record must be mode-0600). The third terminal still stops normally. Checks on tree d68e57c3: nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime gave 85 passed, 1 ignored; cargo fmt --check and clippy -D warnings are clean. Installed: build /nix/store/3q4g5b92q200xhp8dh2jnc7ds1ppyhsy-eon-0.1.1 from that tree, in an isolated headless Sway (pixman), x86_64 Linux, with ~/.cache/eon-agents/eon-7iap/iso/check.sh. Two tabs. Run A SIGKILLed t2's Orbit worker: the reap logged 'terminal session-2 ended with status 1; Orbit exited without publishing a terminal result' and pruned t2; the supervisor, Venus and t1 survived. Run B SIGSTOPped t2's worker, then ran eon tab close t2: 'closing tab t2: stopping session-2', then 'closed tab t2 in 2044 ms', exit 0. The supervisor's stderr shows the owner-lost line. The supervisor, Venus and t1 survived, with t1 active. Review ledger: 2 Claude rounds (round 1: 1 blocking, the missing containment, fixed; round 2: clean); Codex 2 passes (full: clean; narrow re-check abe1cf52..d68e57c3: clean, 1 nit not taken). Residuals sent to eon-overseer, who will put them to Lucca: a close that fails before Stop is written leaves stop_sent false, so a later reap error there still ends the supervisor; a failed-stop terminal whose lease closed and that never reconciles can make each reap wait up to 5 s; reap errors on never-stopped terminals still end the supervisor; the Orbit worker's 'PTY child was not reaped' defect. eon-jqxr is a different bug and stays open.

title: Create a tab with a directory and command, without the picker
description:
## Why

Eon is used with one tab per project. An orchestrating agent (the overseer) cannot start an agent in another project's tab. `eon tab create` always opens a pending tab with its directory picker, which waits for a person (EON-C18 Picker-first tab directories). `eon pane create -- COMMAND` adds a pane only to the caller's own tab (or the active tab). On 2026-10-23 the overseer moved nova's Claude session into Lucca's window and could put it only in a pane of the eon tab. Lucca asked "why not a new tab? it's a tab per project, normally" and then had to create the tab and type `claude --resume ...` by hand. Lucca asked for this bead the same day ("create the new bead").

## Goal

From an Eon terminal, one command creates a new tab with a given directory and, optionally, runs a command as that tab's first pane, with no picker and without moving the user's active tab or desktop focus. A sketch to settle at the contract step: `eon tab create [--json] [--no-focus] [--directory DIRECTORY] [-- COMMAND...]`.

## Contract (draft at the reference gate; Lucca approves the exact text before code)

- EON-C18 (docs/CONTRACTS.md:1443) amendment: a tab created with a directory skips the picker. The picker stays the default for a bare `eon tab create` and for the UI's new-tab action.
- EON-C8 (docs/CONTRACTS.md:357) and the CLI and EONW sections: the request carries the directory and the optional command. EONW v18 `WorkspaceAction::CreateTab` takes no payload (runtime/crates/eon-workspace-protocol/src/v18.rs:79), so this probably needs a new action or field and an EONW bump. Coordinate the version with the other EONW changes in flight (yx8.11 takes EONW 19).
- `--no-focus`: the user's active tab, selected pane, shown popup and desktop focus stay as they are, mirroring `pane create --no-focus`.
- Failures: a missing or unreadable directory, and a call from outside an Eon terminal, are each refused with a defined exit code, as for `pane create -- COMMAND`.
- The command runs exactly as given (no shell) at the tab's directory, as `pane create -- COMMAND` does.

## Reference gate

Consequential: the CLI, an EONW request and a contract change. Before code, record on this bead: the owner of each step (CLI → EONW → Runtime tab creation → Orbit terminal), the docs/REFERENCES.md routes read, and comparable implementations at inspected revisions: tmux `new-window -d -c DIR [cmd]`, WezTerm `cli spawn --new-window/--cwd`, kitty `@ launch --type=tab --cwd`, Zellij `action new-tab --cwd --layout`. Note what was kept and what was rejected.

## Scope

In scope: the contract text for Lucca's approval, the CLI, the EONW request, Runtime tab creation with a directory and an optional first-pane command, docs/USAGE.md, CHANGELOG.md, and focused tests.

Out of scope: sending text to existing panes (eon-pane-send-research-fo4p), naming tabs, Venus UI changes beyond rendering the new tab, and moving a live terminal between tabs.

## Acceptance

- A Runtime or CLI test: `tab create --no-focus --directory D -- cmd` yields a new non-pending tab at D whose only pane runs cmd, while the active tab and selected pane are unchanged.
- Bare `eon tab create` still opens the picker.
- One installed observation: from the overseer's popup, launch `claude` into a new `~/pjs/nova` tab; Lucca's view and focus stay where they were.

## Verification

Shared wire route: the affected Rust and Nix surfaces, converge plus Codex, the profile refresh, and one isolated installed observation.

Split before implementing if the EONW change and the CLI and Runtime work don't fit one fresh session (small-beads rule).

title: Park a live Agent in a pane when the tab folder changes
description:
## Decision (Lucca, 2026-10-21)

Eon and Yazelix Nova share one policy for a tab-folder change. The Nova twin of
this bead implements the same policy; keep both texts aligned.

Shared policy:
- When a tab's folder changes explicitly, a live Agent popup terminal is
  **parked**: it leaves the popup and becomes an ordinary pane in the same tab,
  keeping its process, conversation and old directory. Its pane label names that
  old folder.
- The next Agent invocation starts a fresh agent at the new tab folder.
- Git keeps today's rule (restart at the new folder on next invocation); its
  state is cheap. A Yazi popup, when present, is kept as is (Nova already does
  this).
- No agent from the old folder ever appears as the tab's current Agent, and no
  agent is ever stopped by a folder change.

Why: Nova's `yazelix-5vl-f69` rejected keeping the old agent in the popup
("permits an agent from the old workspace to masquerade as current"). Both
products then restart it, which silently ends a live conversation. Parking keeps
both guarantees, and matches how running panes already keep their old folder.
Rejected: keep the old instance with a cue (masquerade), confirm on invocation
(modal friction), footer warning only (still destroys the session).

## Evidence

- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/workspace.rs:420`: on invocation, a keep-alive
  popup whose `launch_directory` differs from the tab directory is stopped and a
  replacement started.
- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/workspace.rs:2112`
  `popup_identity_reuses_hides_and_replaces_only_after_retarget` pins that rule.
- `docs/CONTRACTS.md` EON-C10 "Runtime policy" (~line 688): "explicit
  retargeting changes no process until the next invocation, which stops the
  exact old terminal before starting a fresh one at the new directory."
- `docs/USAGE.md:159`: user text for Project/Git/Agent directory behavior.
- Tab folder changes today come from the Alt+Z Project chooser and
  `eon tab directory TAB -- DIR`. The Yazi popup epic (Alt+Shift+Y, Alt+Enter)
  adds another route and retires Alt+Z; this policy applies to every route.

## Scope

In scope: EON-C10 runtime-policy text; runtime popup/pane topology for the
parked transition; its tests; Venus only if a parked terminal cannot already
render as a pane; `docs/USAGE.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`.

Out of scope: Git and custom popup policy beyond keeping today's restart;
transient popups (Anima, Project); the Yazi popup itself; agent provider
selection; moving any process's cwd or injecting `cd`.

## Proposed contract (stop for Lucca's approval before code)

- Parking happens when the folder change commits, so the Agent popup is never
  stale. The parked pane goes into the active tab's selected column, reusing the
  same Orbit terminal (no restart, no new process).
- If the agent terminal has already exited, nothing is parked.
- If the tab cannot take another pane (column/pane bounds), the folder change is
  refused with a clear error and changes nothing, rather than stopping the agent.
  Confirm this fallback with Lucca.

## Acceptance

- Lucca approved the contract text; EON-C10 states it.
- Start Agent, change the tab folder, then: the old agent is a normal pane with
  its conversation intact and its old folder visible; Alt+Shift+L opens a fresh
  agent at the new folder; no agent terminal was stopped.
- Git still restarts at the new folder on its next invocation.
- A refused park leaves tab folder, Agent popup and panes unchanged.

## Implementation Notes

1. Read EON-C10, EON-C18 and `workspace.rs` popup/pane topology; check whether a
   popup terminal can become a `pN` pane without an EONW change. An EONW change
   is a protocol change: record the reference gate (AGENTS.md) and stop for
   approval.
2. Replace the stop-and-restart branch for the Agent entry with park-on-commit;
   keep Git's branch.
3. Update the pinned test to the new policy, plus one test for the refused park.
4. Update USAGE.md and CHANGELOG.md.

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime` passes.
- If Venus changes: `nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-venus`, `cargo fmt
  --check`, `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings`.
- Refresh the `eon` profile, then one isolated installed observation of the
  acceptance flow; never restart the live supervisor.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop before code until the contract text is approved.
- Stop if parking needs an EONW version change the user has not approved.
- Stop if verification fails twice for the same reason.

title: Report a lost Orbit or signalled program's real end status instead of status 1
description:
## Why

When a terminal's Orbit dies abnormally, the supervisor records a status that hides what
happened. In eon-orbit-worker-exit-reason-ztcq's installed check, SIGKILL to a terminal's Orbit
worker made the Orbit host exit 137, but the supervisor log said "terminal session-1 ended with
status 1; Orbit exited without publishing a terminal result; Orbit log: ...". With its only
terminal gone, the isolated supervisor then exited with status 1. A person or agent reading the
log or the exit status cannot tell a killed terminal from a program that exited 1.

Source: eon-orbit-worker-exit-reason-ztcq, comment 4282 (2026-10-27, its proof record, "Side
observation, unchanged by this bead"; landed in 872f00a). Approved by Lucca 2026-10-27 (morning
report question 6): "6. ok", accepting the recommendation "one bead for the exit-status
mapping". Relayed by eon-overseer.

## Evidence

- runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/sessions.rs:1498-1501 (`session_finished`):
  `SessionEnd::Managed(_, ProcessOutcome::Signal(_)) | SessionEnd::OwnerLost => 1`. Both a
  signalled program and an Orbit that exited without publishing a result become 1.
- runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/sessions.rs:1359 (`owner_lost`): the OwnerLost end keeps no
  Orbit exit status or signal.
- runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/supervisor.rs:1117 (`session_end_line`): formats "terminal {id}
  ended with status {code}".
- runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/supervisor.rs:1191-1192 and 989/1015: session-1's code becomes
  `initial_status`, which the supervisor returns as its own exit status when no terminals remain.
  That is why the isolated supervisor exited 1.
- Installed evidence: ~/.cache/eon-agents/ztcq-work/obs1/ (eon.log, steps.txt), package
  /nix/store/fcd9grzqv5ka19iqccbnkd0ixldxy1fv-eon-0.1.3.
- Tests that pin today's text: supervisor.rs:2189 and :2486 assert "ended with status 1; Orbit
  exited without publishing a terminal result".

## Contract

Check EON-C8 (durable tab and pane workspace, terminal end), EON-C10 (typed workspace control,
`eon stop` statuses) and EON-C28 (1.x stability: documented exit statuses must not change
silently) for text that fixes these statuses, and docs/USAGE.md for the supervisor's exit status.
If the change needs any EON-C text added or changed, stop and bring the exact wording to Lucca
for approval first, as AGENTS.md requires.

## Prerequisites

None. eon-orbit-worker-exit-reason-ztcq (closed) already writes why the worker died to Orbit's
log.

## Scope

In scope:
- Decide and implement one mapping for a terminal's end status: a signalled program reported as
  128+signal (shell convention) or by signal name, and an Orbit lost without a result reported
  distinctly (for example naming Orbit's own exit status or signal when the supervisor reaped it)
  rather than as 1.
- Decide whether the supervisor's own exit status when its last terminal ends should follow
  session-1's status, and document the answer.
- The supervisor log line and the tests that pin it.

Out of scope:
- Orbit's worker-exit stderr line (done in ztcq).
- The EONW wire format; if the status must cross EONW, stop (protocol change, needs an EONW bump
  and Lucca's approval).

## Acceptance

- A runtime test: a terminal whose Orbit is lost without a result, and one whose program dies by
  signal, each produce the decided status in the supervisor log line, and the test fails on
  today's code.
- docs/USAGE.md (and contracts, if approved) state the supervisor's exit status when the last
  terminal ends.
- One isolated installed check: SIGKILL a scratch terminal's Orbit worker; the supervisor log
  shows the decided status (not a bare 1).

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime` passes.
- `cargo clippy --locked -p eon-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.
- The installed check above, in isolated headless Sway with a private HOME and runtime dir, never
  against Lucca's running Eon.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if any EON-C text must change (Lucca's approval).
- Stop if the status must travel over EONW or ORBS.

## Maintenance Notes

ztcq's proof driver ~/.cache/eon-agents/ztcq-work/installed.sh shows how to SIGKILL the exact
worker PID; never use pkill patterns (Orbit hosts carry prompts in argv).

title: Expose terminal typography and initial geometry configuration
description:
## Outcome

Preserve the non-opacity portion of the former broad EonTerm presentation plan as a separate later slice. After background opacity is proved, let Eon own bounded configuration and lifecycle policy for primary monospace family, ordered fallback families, font size, line-height multiplier, and initial columns and rows, then pass exact values to the accepted Venus owner.

The user approved EON-C19 and the original pre-child startup guarantee on 2026-09-08. Extend VEN-C19 with the required startup-admission boundary, prove and publish Venus first, then consume that exact source in Eon. EON-C13 and EON-C14 retain their opacity and blur contracts.

- Consumer: a local Eon or EonTerm user and an approved Nova composition.
- Trigger: create or reopen a Venus surface with accepted typography/geometry fields in the canonical Eon configuration root, or no overrides.
- Result: Eon validates one canonical terminal configuration and passes exact values to Venus. Full Eon and EonTerm agree. Absence preserves current accepted defaults.
- Failures: invalid or unavailable values fail before new child creation and identify the field. A presentation-only failure never kills an existing Orbit Session or PTY child.

Impact: MED/HIGH. Effort: L. Implementation risk: MED. Confidence: HIGH. EON-C19 schema and the original pre-child failure policy were approved on 2026-09-08; the accepted source and installed proof are recorded below.

## Evidence

- `crates/eon/src/managed_environment.rs` contains the existing strict `EonConfig` serde/TOML owner.
- `crates/eon/src/supervisor.rs` contains the single Venus argv owner and the supervisor reopen path that can preserve Orbit while replacing Venus.
- Current `eon-eonterm-presentation-e4f` now owns only approved background opacity and establishes the minimal `[terminal]` section, exact launch boundary, validation pattern, and apply-on-reopen lifecycle.
- Venus `ven-terminal-typography-geometry-settings-ojv` preserves the matching materialization outcome and one authoritative grid.
- The user approved splitting these fields behind opacity on 2026-08-14.

## Scope

In scope:
- Accepted Eon field names, types, bounds, defaults, descriptions, diagnostics, apply timing, and exact Venus argv encoding for primary family, fallbacks, size, line height, columns, and rows.
- Existing strict config parser, launch, supervisor, attach/reopen, help, manifest where required, focused tests, contract proof, README LOC, and accepted user-visible docs/changelog.
- One exact Eon inventory for approved consumers without a handwritten Nova mirror.

Out of scope:
- Background opacity, themes, terminal colors, blur, images, cursor effects, font packaging, live reload, settings service, generic profile framework, arbitrary Mars parity, Orbit state, or Eon workspace protocol changes.
- Ratconfig implementation, Nova persistence, or user-state migration; those remain Nova-owned.

## Implementation notes

1. Wait for `eon-eonterm-presentation-e4f` and exact Venus `ven-terminal-typography-geometry-settings-ojv` proof; record the compatibility order with no adapter.
2. Index the approved EON-C19 fields and original pre-child failure policy before code; do not adopt the withdrawn weaker failure proposal.
3. Extend the existing `TerminalConfig` and direct Venus launch boundary. Avoid a generic serialized profile, environment-variable-per-setting boundary, watcher, or second parser.
4. Validate before initial process creation and reread only at the existing Venus reopen boundary. Preserve live Orbit and child identity.
5. Publish the smallest authoritative field inventory through existing docs/help/manifest ownership. Stop if a new schema service appears necessary.
6. Test configuration and exact argv first, then dogfood one installed Eon/EonTerm pair against the exact Venus proof.
7. Follow the source candidate then proof-metadata/closure workflow.

## Acceptance

- Absent fields preserve current typography and geometry.
- Each accepted field has one Eon-owned name, type, bound, default, description, and apply time.
- Invalid values fail before initial child creation; invalid reopen values preserve the live Session and child.
- Full Eon and EonTerm pass identical exact values to Venus and retain distinct workspace/managed-environment policy.
- Reopening Venus applies changed typography/geometry without restarting Orbit or replacing the PTY child; a live Venus remains unchanged until reopened.
- Exact installed dogfood covers primary/fallback choice, missing glyphs, size, line height, columns/rows, scale factors, resize, selection, cursor, IME, accessibility, reconnect, and long-running child survival.
- Contract/help/inventory docs, package/manifest checks, locked Rust checks, LOC, and `git diff --check` pass on one immutable candidate.

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --check`
- `cargo check --locked`
- `cargo test --locked`
- `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo run --locked -p eon-manifest -- components/eon-alpha-v3.json`
- `git diff --check`

Run exact repository Nix/package checks required by the changed surface. Focused tests must prove defaults, bounds, exact argv, initial ordering, reopen reread, and process preservation.

## Stop conditions

- Prove and accept the Venus startup-admission boundary before Eon consumes it; the EON-C19 contract approval is recorded.
- Stop before a dependency, generic profile/inventory service, environment-variable-per-setting boundary, watcher, live mutation, font package, Orbit restart, PTY replacement, or compatibility window.
- Stop if another active issue owns the same config, launch, supervisor, manifest, or child revision surfaces.

## Maintenance notes

This issue deliberately excludes opacity and all settings beyond typography and initial geometry. Do not use the existence of `[terminal]` as permission to grow a Mars-compatible schema.
notes: User approved continuing with EON-C19 and validation before user-command creation on 2026-09-08. This single cross-repository issue owns the necessary Venus startup-admission slice first, then exact Eon consumption/configuration and installed proof. No second issue is claimed. Preserve live Sessions and the existing typography/partial proof limits.

No dependency is proposed.

Contract gap: current Venus has no validation-only or startup-ready boundary. Eon starts Orbit/the picker before spawning Venus; Venus alone resolves installed fonts and validates native/workspace geometry. Therefore the draft promise that unavailable fonts and every impossible native size fail before any child starts cannot be implemented solely by projecting the accepted Venus options. EonTerm can already have its command running when Venus rejects a font; full Eon cancels its startup picker and can start the fallback initial Session. A replaced surface's failure preserves existing durable Sessions. No code will silently weaken this promise or duplicate font/native checks in Eon.

Proposed EON-C19 — Terminal typography and initial geometry configuration (awaiting user approval):

Consumer: every Eon/EonTerm Venus surface, including a composition consuming the same EonTerm contract. Trigger: create/reopen Venus after reading one canonical config.toml [terminal] snapshot. Fields: font_family optional UTF-8 string; font_fallbacks ordered array of at most eight strings (empty by default); font_size optional finite f32 in 6..=96; line_height optional finite f32 in 1..=3; columns and rows optional integers in 1..=65535, with a supplied pair at most 100000 cells. Family names are nonempty, trimmed, at most 128 UTF-8 bytes and contain no controls. Omitted fields emit no matching override and retain accepted Venus font selection, nominal 16 px / 1.125 line height and 960x600 logical default window. Each omitted dimension retains its existing initial window dimension. Supplied columns/rows request terminal cells including existing workspace chrome; native compositor policy may override them.

One direct argv owner emits --font-family, ordered repeated --font-fallback, --font-size, --line-height, --columns and --rows before the endpoint. Eon validates schema/type/name/scalar/pair bounds before initial child creation and at the existing reopen boundary; errors name the field. Venus owns font availability, monospace admission, shaping and physical/native/workspace size checks. Proposed failure-policy clarification: unavailable/nonmonospace fonts or impossible native layouts reject the Venus surface with its bounded diagnostic, while durable Orbit Sessions remain alive (including a Session already created during initial launch). This is a deliberate clarification requiring approval, not an already accepted equivalence to the draft's stronger pre-child guarantee. Strict pre-child font/native rejection would require a separately approved and proved Venus admission capability first.

A live Venus retains its snapshot; reopen reads current settings without restarting Orbit or replacing the PTY child. Existing opacity, blur, cursor defaults, topology, native input/clipboard, session lifetime, product roots, protocol versions, and Linux Wayland-only scope remain unchanged. No fonts are installed, no fallback silently substitutes a missing requested family, no glyph-completeness promise or live reload. Canonical user inventory belongs in the existing README contract table, not a new schema service.

Cheapest falsifiers after approval: configuration consumed by exact argv in both modes, invalid initial configuration creates no test child, invalid reopen preserves process identities, absent options are omitted, and native installed Eon/EonTerm reopen yields the requested real PTY grids with unchanged Orbit/PTy identities. Final native checks cover the changed presentation surfaces; earlier rendering/IME/accessibility and fractional/compositor qualifications remain bounded to exact exercised evidence. Required Rust/Nix lifecycle checks and profile refresh follow the accepted source candidate. The source candidate precedes proof metadata/closure.

title: Zoom the selected pane alone across the tab, like a popup
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-10-24: "create a bead to fix zoom. zoom in a pane instead a stack should not show the other
stacked panes, but go full width, just like a popup".

Today (VEN-C8, venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md:574-589) Alt+Shift+Z zooms the active tab's selected column:
Scene lays out only that column, its pane cards spanning the area all the tab's columns cover at
unchanged heights, so the column's other stacked panes still show as collapsed rows. In a one-column
tab the key is refused with a notice.

## Behaviour wanted

- Zoom applies to the selected pane, not its column: the zoomed pane alone fills the area all the
  tab's columns cover, as one rounded card like a popup's, with its label in the top edge and the
  focus frame (eon-e8hh). No other stacked rows and no other columns are drawn, hit-tested or listed
  to accessibility while zoomed; their attachments stay open at their last size, unresized.
- Open questions for the contract (wording to Lucca before code): does zoom work in a one-column tab
  with several panes (it should, since hiding the stack is now the point)? What ends the zoom (the
  selected pane changes, the pane closes, a structural change)? Do Alt+K/J move to the neighbouring
  pane and keep it zoomed, or end the zoom? The ` · zoom` marker and the accessible names
  ("Zoomed column N of M" becomes a pane name).
- Window-local, no workspace action, as today. Popups cover it as today.

## Contract

VEN-C8's zoom clause (and EON-C8 if it describes zoom). Wording to Lucca before code; check
`eon` CLI parity (AGENTS.md "Humans and Agents"): zoom is Venus-local view state, an allowed exception.

## Acceptance

- Scene test (fails first): zooming a pane in a stack of three lays out only that pane over the whole
  column area of the tab; the other panes are not drawn, hit-tested or in AccessKit; unzoom restores
  sizes, resizing only what changed.
- Isolated capture: a 3-pane column zoomed and unzoomed.

Portability: neutral.
close_reason: Alt+Shift+Z zooms the selected pane alone across the tab; proof in comments

comments.text: Approval of behaviour (Lucca, 2026-10-24, direct to the overseer, "do it"): zoom shows only the selected pane as one rounded card over the whole tab area, like a popup; works in one-column tabs; any Alt+H/J/K/L move, closing the pane, or a layout change ends the zoom; the tab keeps its " · zoom" marker and the accessible name becomes "Zoomed pane <label>". Rejected: Alt+J/K carrying the zoom to the neighbouring pane. Exact VEN-C8 wording goes to Lucca for sign-off before code.

title: Keep a terminal alive when its title or OSC 7 directory is invalid UTF-8
description:
## Report (eon-63 during yx8.11, 2026-10-23; filed by the overseer)

`orbit/src/host.rs` `flags()` (around line 509) calls libghostty's `title_and_directory()?` whenever a metadata observer, such as an attached Venus, is present. The pinned libghostty-vt cuts titles at 1024 bytes and can split a multi-byte character. It then returns Err for that title, and also for an OSC 7 working directory that isn't valid UTF-8. The `?` turns that into a host error, and the terminal ends.

Result: a program that sets a title of 1023 ASCII bytes followed by a 2-byte character (OSC 0/2), or a non-UTF-8 OSC 7 directory, ends its own terminal while a Venus is attached. The terminal and its program are lost to a cosmetic metadata value. Users are not happy losing a terminal to a title.

eon-63 confirmed the Err with a throwaway probe against the pinned libghostty. yx8.11 fixed the same pattern on its new ProgramStatus reply path (empty title on error, with a real-PTY step that sends 1023 ASCII bytes plus é). The observer path predates that and is untouched.

## Expected

Invalid or cut title and directory metadata never ends a terminal. The observer gets an empty, or lossily decoded, title or directory, and the terminal keeps running.

## Scope

In scope: one fallback at the libghostty boundary (orbit/src/pty.rs or wherever `title_and_directory` is wrapped), shared by the observer path and yx8.11's reply path, so there is one owner. Lossy decode (U+FFFD) or empty: decide at the boundary and keep the result sanitized as today. Add a real-PTY regression with a Venus-style metadata observer attached: the 1023+é title and a non-UTF-8 OSC 7 directory each leave the terminal alive.

Out of scope: changing libghostty's 1024-byte cut.

## Contract

The ORB-C contract for terminal metadata and observers (find the owner in orbit/docs/CONTRACTS.md). Add "invalid metadata never ends a terminal" to its failures. Approved under the overseer's 2026-10-23 approvals; record the exact text as relayed.

## Prerequisites

After eon-agent-sidebar-yx8.11 lands (it touches the reply path and adds the first fallback); reuse its helper.

## Acceptance

The red/green real-PTY regression; orbit fmt, clippy and the orbit-* Nix checks.

Portability disposition: neutral.
close_reason: Done in the commit that carries this close, on edge 11146c4. Proof is in the bead's comments.

comments.text:
## Decisions (eon-3f, 2026-10-23)

Contract approval, relayed by the overseer on 2026-10-23 under Lucca's approval that day: "i give you auto-approval to everything, until 700k / but the focus is landing the sidebar / our mission is: happy users" (recorded on eon-agent-sidebar-yx8; the handoff limits it to user-owned decisions in eon-* beads, relayed quoted). Approved: add to ORB-C3 Important failures exactly: "Invalid UTF-8 terminal metadata, such as a title libghostty cuts inside a character or a non-UTF-8 OSC 7 directory, reaches the client and observer as empty and never ends the terminal." With an orbit/CHANGELOG.md line.

Scope found: the frame path (orbit/src/frame.rs, `terminal.title()?`/`pwd()?` in FrameExtractor::frame) has the same failure for an attached client, so the one fallback covers the frame, observer and ProgramStatus paths.

Empty, not lossy: libghostty-vt's binding returns only `Result<&str>` for title and pwd, so the raw bytes a lossy decode needs are not reachable at the boundary. Empty matches yx8.11's ProgramStatus fallback.

Regression: two gated steps in the existing late-observer real-PTY check (client and observer attached): a 1023-byte ASCII + é title, then a non-UTF-8 OSC 7 directory with a new title. No new Nix check entry.

title: Unify tab-scoped tool popups and the project chooser
description:
## Outcome
One tab-scoped popup surface hosts terminal tools and the existing Alt+Z project chooser. Popups cover the whole pane stack without adding stack entries; the user returns to ordinary work after dismissal. Lazygit is the first useful tool, followed by the configured agent. This is a product container; execute its sequenced children, not the epic as one implementation.

## Agreed product model (2026-09-10)
Panes hold ongoing work; popups are tools visited briefly; the independently scoped sidebar shows cross-project attention. Use one popup presentation/lifecycle owner rather than a separate popup system for every command.

Alt+Z remains “choose this tab's project”: quick Zoxide/fzf search and Yazi directory browsing stay together, with Tab switching between them. Its chooser command owns selecting/cancelling and submitting the existing validated tab-directory action. The popup host need not interpret search/browser modes or gain a generic result-callback framework. Ordinary entry dismissal policy can close the chooser. App-owned Enter/Esc/Ctrl+C and Yazi's nested-dialog behavior remain intact; the host does not globally intercept those keys.

Startup and new-tab creation use the same chooser and surface. Eon still owns pending-tab acceptance and cancellation: first-tab cancellation uses the validated launch-directory fallback; later-tab cancellation removes the pending tab. Do not replace this with placeholder panes, durable hidden pending work, or a different startup workflow.

Full file management is a different optional tool. If configured, plain Yazi/file-manager browsing does not retarget the tab. Keep search and browsing inside the project chooser; do not split them into separate popups or promote full Yazi to another default without a user choice. No dedicated file-manager feature is required for the core popup work.

## Coverage and visual starting point
- Agreed: cover almost the entire active tab body, including all collapsed and selected pane headers and the terminal. Keep tabs visible. When the independently implemented sidebar is open, leave its rail visible and size within the remaining body; reserve no empty rail when closed.
- Preserve ordinary stack membership/order and a valid return target. No live background terminal composition is promised.
- Proposed for visual review: fixed outer margins of 8 logical pixels per side and 4 above/below; rounded corners matching pane frames; a thin, slightly brighter border with a small integrated tool label instead of a full extra header row.
- Keep the exposed margins' background/opacity and existing blur request continuous. Respect best-effort compositor blur. Resize without restarting tools; choose usable tiny-window geometry before implementation. Exact margins, border contrast and label fit remain unproved.

## Agreed Agent/Lazygit cwd lifecycle
A fresh launch uses the tab's authoritative directory, independent of the selected pane's process cwd. The remembered launch cwd determines reuse. Matching cwd reopens the existing Session. After a mismatch, the next popup shortcut invocation stops the old tool Session and launches a replacement in the tab's current directory; this check precedes ordinary same-cwd show/hide behavior.

Retargeting alone does not stop or change a tool. The later invocation intentionally ends the previous running Agent/Lazygit instance rather than retaining hidden old-project work. Same-cwd hiding preserves it; application exit removes its surface. Preserve unrelated pane Sessions. Stop/start failures must not create duplicates or falsely report that replaced work survived.

## Settled contract and optional follow-ups
eon-tool-popups-e13.1 is complete and owns the detailed lifecycle/configuration contract: one instance per entry/tab, one chosen popup per tab, automatic Agent selection, Alt+Z retention across tab switches, app-owned terminal keys, bounded configuration and exact-instance directory acceptance. It also defines detach/recovery, lost return targets and partial failures. Read that decision before implementation; these are no longer unresolved candidates.

The default core shortcuts are Alt+Shift+J for Git and Alt+Shift+L for Agent; Alt+Z remains Project. Agent selection follows the inspected Nova provider order without installing providers or hooks. Tools launch from the authoritative tab directory and retain the agreed next-invocation cwd replacement.

Anima remains the proposed third default (candidate Alt+Shift+A), behind eon-anima-popup-7zp and eon-anima-startup-5el. Its own decision must prevent invisible playback on dismissal, displacement and tab deactivation without changing chooser retention. It does not block core popups. Startup autoplay and eon-agent-sidebar-yx8 remain independent; full Yazi remains an optional configured tool.

## Ownership and reference gate
Eon owns entries, launch/tab/Session identity, lifecycle policy, validated directory updates and configuration; Venus owns geometry, native focus/input/accessibility; Orbit owns PTYs and terminal state. title: Settle the shared popup lifecycle and configuration contract
description:
## Outcome
Resolve only the choices needed to implement eon-tool-popups-e13 coherently: one shared popup host for tool commands and the existing Alt+Z project chooser, with Eon-owned lifecycle and a usable Venus consumer boundary. The parent records the agreed coverage, Agent/Lazygit cwd replacement and preserved chooser outcomes; do not reopen those decisions without new user direction.

## Prerequisites and references
Planning-only, deferred until the user selects it; no implementation prerequisites. Read the parent and its exact reference route, current EON-C8/C10/C11/C17/C18, VEN-C8/C18, Eon cli.rs::directory_picker/browse_directory and pending-tab lifecycle, and Nova/Zellij Popup configuration and replacement sources. Current code and accepted revisions, not historical guesses, decide what can be reused.

## Acceptance
- State consumer, trigger/result and failures for open, focus, hide/displace, process exit, same-cwd reuse and next-invocation cwd replacement; settle one-per-tool/tab and one-visible-surface candidates, tab switching, return-target loss and hidden-work discovery.
- Specify a bounded user configuration contract for default/custom argv commands, key collisions, labels, disabling, dismissal lifetime and shared geometry. Decide when edits take effect and how missing/invalid commands fail. Ask the user for the default Agent/provider choice if still unresolved; do not infer authorization for provider setup.
- Keep Alt+Z search and browsing within its chooser command. Decide ordinary-popup displacement/dismissal for existing tabs without introducing a chooser-only global lock. Preserve Eon-owned first/new-tab acceptance, cancellation and target validation; do not broaden simultaneous pending-tab scope incidentally.
- Specify detach/reconnect, supervisor loss, tab/generation stop and partial-failure behavior without orphaning hidden work or guessing lost associations. Distinguish tool Session preservation from transient chooser/Anima cleanup.
- Name the minimum versioned Eon-to-Venus data/actions and an executable producer-to-consumer transition. The Eon producer must be verifiable before Venus changes without activating an incompatible installed product. Do not mandate a wire version, duplicate schema or speculative compatibility layer here.
- Map any intentional EON/VEN contract changes for approval at the owning implementation frontier and name the cheapest falsifiers. Record adopted/rejected mechanisms and remaining optional Anima/full-file-manager choices; closure is a decision, not runtime proof.

## Scope
No production code, new dependency, runtime refresh, provider/sidebar implementation, file-manager default, popup plugin framework or reworked startup experience. Metadata may refine only this decision's contract; later implementation belongs to the sequenced producer, consumer and delivery children.
design:
## Decision — 2026-09-10
This is the chosen implementation contract, not an implemented or accepted runtime proof. It resolves the remaining candidates in eon-tool-popups-e13. The user explicitly chose Nova-style automatic Agent selection and keeping Alt+Z open across tab switches. Earlier agreed stack coverage, command-owned chooser modes and next-invocation Agent/Lazygit cwd replacement remain in force.

### Observable contract and owners
For a person using full Eon, a configured tool shortcut opens or returns to that tab's tool in one popup covering the stack. Repeating it while the same popup has terminal focus dismisses it; a visible but unfocused popup first receives focus. Normal panes retain their membership, order and selected return target. Eon owns definitions, tab/instance/launch-cwd identity and lifecycle; Venus owns the one terminal presentation, geometry and native input/focus; Orbit owns the PTY, terminal state and bounded process stop. No second emulator, result-callback framework or copied child state.

### Open, hide, switch and exit
- At most one live instance per entry per tab, and one chosen popup per tab; only the active tab's chosen surface is displayed. Selecting another tab deactivates its presentation without dismissing its chosen popup. Returning restores the same instance, including a pending tab's chooser. This is the user's explicit tab-switch decision.
- On invocation, validate the target and entry first. For an existing matching-cwd instance: hidden becomes shown, visible/unfocused becomes focused, and visible/focused is dismissed. No focus/history stack is required.
- Showing a different entry dismisses the current entry using its configured lifetime: keep_alive=true hides without stopping; false stops and reaps. Resolve invalid/missing launch inputs before displacing a working surface. If launch later fails, restore a still-live prior tool or the ordinary selected pane; never fabricate restoration of a stopped transient.
- Retarget alone changes no running Session. Before show/focus/hide on the next invocation, compare Eon's remembered launch cwd to the tab directory. A mismatch stops the old instance, then launches one replacement in the current tab directory. Apply this simple policy to configured terminal tools as well as Agent/Lazygit; no process-cwd/title guessing or hidden old-project instance. A failed stop retains tracked ownership and prevents replacement; a failed start after successful stop reports failure without claiming the old tool survived.
- Application exit removes that instance; an active exit returns to the selected pane, while a hidden exit must not steal focus. Explicit pane navigation/creation in an established tab dismisses the popup before selecting the requested pane. A missing return pane uses the workspace's surviving selection policy.
- Ordinary pane exit must not destroy a tab that still owns a live durable popup. Such a tab may have no selected pane: show its chosen popup, or a minimal empty body with the existing create-pane and live-tool shortcuts. Do not spawn a placeholder shell. Remove it through normal lifecycle once it has no ordinary or durable work and no pending chooser.
- Extend existing human-readable and JSON workspace inspection to list each live popup's tab, entry/instance identity, label, shortcut and chosen/hidden state. Every enabled configurable entry has a usable shortcut, so hidden work remains reachable without a new sidebar or popup browser.
- Esc, Ctrl+C, Tab and Enter remain application input. Eon shortcuts act at the existing workspace shortcut boundary; clicking outside a popup does not replay a click into the covered terminal. No desktop activation is added.

### Project chooser and pending tabs
Alt+Z invokes the same host with the Eon-owned chooser command. Quick search and Yazi browsing, their Tab mode switch and contextual Yazi Esc behavior remain app-owned. Repeat-shortcut dismissal or displacement in an established tab cancels the chooser without retargeting. Acceptance performs the existing validated tab-directory operation; it does not change any ordinary pane's cwd.

Each chooser result must be bound to its exact live invocation and tab. A late result after cancellation, replacement or tab removal must fail unchanged; preserve raw Unix path bytes, validation-before-mutation and request deduplication. This can extend the existing typed directory action with expected chooser identity; it does not authorize a generic completion callback API.

A chooser in one established tab does not block another tab's tools or chooser. Keep at most one pending new tab: another new-tab request focuses that pending chooser rather than creating another. Pending tabs cannot launch project tools before accepting a directory; keep the chooser visible and return a concise choose-directory-first failure. This is pending-tab admission policy, not a global chooser lock. Tab switching retains pending selection as explicitly chosen by the user.

Startup, acceptance and cancellation retain EON-C18 outcomes: one first pane after valid acceptance; first-tab cancellation uses the validated inherited launch-directory fallback; later-tab cancellation removes the pending tab and restores a surviving prior/nearest tab. Ordinary dismissal, presentation loss and explicit close use that same cancellation owner. Existing final-tab close safeguards remain.

### Configuration contract
Use the existing strict Eon TOML owner and direct argv launch pattern; no new dependency or shell-string interpretation. Snapshot popup configuration once when the supervisor starts. Edits apply to the next supervisor/workspace; do not restart a live supervisor or mutate running entries implicitly.

Use shared [popup] geometry and [popups.<id>] entries:
- side_margin=8 and vertical_margin=4, in logical pixels, are the initial defaults. Accept finite values from 0 through 128. Geometry has no per-tool override or manual sidebar offset.
- Entry fields: command (nonempty argv array), keybinding (one chord), label, enabled and keep_alive. Omitted built-in fields inherit defaults in memory; do not rewrite the user's file. Custom entries require command and keybinding; label defaults to id and enabled/keep_alive to true.
- Built-ins: git -> ["eon-lazygit"], label Git, Alt Shift J, keep_alive=true; agent -> command="auto", label Agent, Alt Shift L, keep_alive=true. enabled=false removes a tool and its shortcut from the next workspace.
- command="auto" is only the Agent default selector; explicit argv overrides it. Choose the first executable on the launch environment's PATH in the inspected Nova order: codex resume, grok, opencode, pi, claude --resume. Resolve only for a fresh Agent Session; a hidden running Session keeps its provider. No additional remembered-provider file: explicit argv supplies a stable preference. Do not silently fall through to another provider after the chosen executable fails. No installed provider yields an actionable error. No agent installation, authentication change, hook setup or sidebar integration.
- The reserved project entry has the packaged chooser command, label Project, Alt Z and transient lifetime. Its command, required availability and completion semantics are Eon-owned; its label/shortcut may be customized. Uniform hosting does not make startup's project-selection function replaceable with an arbitrary command.
- Bound to 32 definitions including Project, 64-byte ASCII ids, 128-byte labels, 128 argv elements and 64 KiB total command bytes per entry; reject NUL, empty executables, invalid/unknown fields and conflicting normalized chords. Chords use explicit modifiers and one physical key, consistent with Venus today. Reject collisions among enabled entries and existing workspace/native shortcuts; never intercept bare Esc/Tab/Enter or terminal cancellation keys. One shared normalized key representation owns collision semantics; Venus maps native events to it.
- Bad configuration fails validation before new workspace processes launch, with the offending field; unavailable executables fail on invocation without breaking ordinary panes or other tools. Missing optional tools do not make Eon startup fail. Failures use the existing bounded error/notice path, without notices for successful toggles/navigation.

The proposed Anima default remains behind eon-anima-popup-7zp and eon-anima-startup-5el. Do not ship an enabled nonexistent command or reserve its candidate Alt Shift A binding in the core slice. Its own decision must prevent invisible playback, including on tab deactivation; that must not change the accepted chooser retention rule. Full Yazi remains an optional custom terminal tool; browsing it does not retarget the tab. No new file-manager default or special navigation-preservation policy is selected here.

### Presentation and lifecycle
Cover the entire pane stack, including all pane headers, while keeping tabs and any separately implemented sidebar visible. With no sidebar, reserve no rail. Render only the selected terminal surface, without compositing the underlying terminal. Use pane-frame corner styling, a thin slightly brighter border and a compact integrated label. Preserve continuous background opacity and best-effort blur through margins. On tiny windows reduce margins first, then omit label ornament before sacrificing a usable grid; resizing never relaunches tools. The 8/4 margins and exact contrast are starting values for visual review, not measured visual acceptance.

Presentation exit/detach dismisses transients through the existing cancellation/cleanup path and preserves durable tools plus normal Sessions. Reattachment to the same live supervisor restores its surviving workspace state; attach does not manufacture a chooser. Explicit tab/generation teardown includes every owned popup and reports partial stop failure without forgetting a live owned process or stopping unrelated Sessions.

After supervisor loss, reuse existing exact-generation management-record recovery: durable tool Sessions recover as ordinary panes in the synthetic recovered tab. Their popup roles, old tab associations and launch cwd are lost just like current workspace topology; do not guess them or add a persistent popup registry. They remain visible/reachable, and a later tool shortcut creates a separate new popup. Transient identities must remain distinguishable in management records for validated stop/reap on recovery, as the picker is today. No reboot persistence or stronger process-stop guarantee is introduced.

### Minimum shared boundary and executable sequence
Extend the versioned workspace contract with an enabled entry catalog (id, label, normalized shortcut), live instances (entry, tab, unique invocation, Session and endpoint) and each tab's chosen popup. Keep argv, provider selection, lifetime and launch cwd exclusively in Eon. Existing selected-pane state supplies the ordinary return target. Extend validity to tabs containing durable popups without ordinary panes.

Use a typed entry invocation action, stable tab/instance targeting for dismissal/focus and chooser commit, plus existing tab/pane actions. Reuse request deduplication and polling snapshots; no new event transport, Venus-supplied commands or duplicated configuration policy. Focus-only versus focused-toggle intent must be explicit enough that a visible unfocused popup is not accidentally dismissed. Replacements have distinct identity even if polling misses the intermediate absence.

Retain bounded identities/paths and the current 2 MiB envelope. Cap combined ordinary and popup Sessions at 256 and reject capacity exhaustion before displacement/launch. The protocol seed must prove the largest legal catalog/tab/instance snapshot fits; keeping command arrays and repeated launch directories out of the wire avoids unnecessary pressure. Exact enum/field encoding belongs to that seed, not a second schema in this decision.

The current split needs resequencing before implementation. Eon control.rs and the pinned Venus runtime both unconditionally consume EONW v4, so activating a breaking producer before updating Venus would produce an unusable composed package. Adopt the repository's previous protocol-only seed method:
1. Publish and verify an additive next-version protocol module while Eon's active runtime and installed composition continue using v4.
2. Venus consumes that exact accepted seed, proves the new surface with bounded fixtures/process substitutes and records its exact accepted source.
3. Eon activates popup configuration/lifecycle against that accepted consumer and updates exact composition/generation inputs in the same coherent runtime slice.
4. Delivery proves the installed product and advances acceptance only for exercised behavior.

A new version is indicated by replacing the current picker-specific v4 snapshot; do not redefine v4 or invent runtime negotiation/feature gates merely to preserve the old task order. Prior seeds 96119f29ca2e3ec4ad19bbe272708b07d588429a (v3) and aaafc9127c054e683abfceb3c8fcaae201a7a763 (v4) demonstrate the additive method. No speculative child API, incompatible default package or automatic supervisor restart.

Before claiming an implementation child, a separate planning-only reconciliation must split the seed from eon-tool-popups-e13.2, place ven-shared-popup-surface-ehk between seed and Eon runtime activation, and preserve delivery's dependencies on both accepted implementations. This owned run changes only .1; its closure does not certify the current sibling graph ready for implementation.

### Evidence, contract mapping and falsifiers
Inspected baseline: Eon f512f00919a17f487b6714a859534f616d1344e0; Venus 26df2168ee79acfaf491e4bcad8a7e7d16648cad. Eon/Venus Beads already had authorized planning edits; Nova Beads had unrelated dirty work. No source edits or reference code incorporation.
- Eon workspace.rs, cli.rs::directory_picker/browse_directory, managed_environment.rs, supervisor.rs::reap_presentation, sessions.rs recovery and protocol v4 establish existing ownership, pending-tab behavior, direct argv, detach cleanup and recovery limits. Adopt those owners; reject a second durable registry or chooser-mode host.
- Nova 6575ae476a8d4b2fa8b4aa8d0f3839bdba6467e1, runtime/yzx-agent.rs, defaults/config.toml and crates/yzx-config/src/{root_config,custom_popups}.rs establish provider ordering and configured commands/chord conflicts. Adopt bounded direct argv and automatic detection; reject automatic Radar setup, cached provider truth and copied full-manager policy.
- Zellij Popup f9424823b01e5223dadff9e6c5b87c0131a902f8, README and show_popup/should_restart_popup_for_cwd, demonstrates hide versus stop and next-invocation replacement. Adopt explicit remembered launch cwd; reject its process-cwd fallback and plugin dependency.
- Kitty 54416498c89e1d07e5079c49d15470dd0d947ce7, kitty/launch.py and kitty/tabs.py (GPL source, read-only comparison), demonstrates explicit overlay target identity and reuse of ordinary terminal presentation. Adopt that separation; reject per-pane coverage, extra PTY ownership and copied implementation.

Owning implementations must intentionally update EON-C8/C10/C17/C18 for popup-bearing tabs, actions and removal of the global chooser lock; preserve EON-C11 exact generations/recovery limits. Venus updates VEN-C8/C18 while preserving VEN-C1/C2/C3/C4/C11/C15/C19. Existing proof records remain historical and qualified.

Cheapest falsifiers: deterministic transition checks with a stop/start spy for same-cwd process identity, retarget-only preservation, replacement ordering/failure, displacement and last-pane exit; exact chooser acceptance/cancellation with stale invocation rejection and tab switching; protocol roundtrip/invalid-boundary and maximum-envelope checks; consuming config/shortcut validation with controlled executable PATH; one isolated installed Wayland slice exercising real Lazygit/Agent, startup/new-tab/Alt+Z, detach/recovery and ordinary/narrow geometry. Shared runtime/protocol changes require the affected Rust/Nix surfaces and profile refresh under repository policy. Do not claim sidebar, fractional-scale or compositor blur acceptance from fixtures or a different environment.

This task's proof is source/decision and Beads inspection only. No runtime behavior, pin, indexed contract, README/LOC, changelog or active profile changes are claimed.
close_reason: Decision complete: recorded user-approved automatic Agent selection and picker retention, shared lifecycle/configuration/recovery contract, source evidence and falsifiers. Implementation remains pending; reconcile protocol seed -> Venus -> Eon activation -> delivery ordering before claiming an implementation child.

title: Activate configurable popup Sessions and the project chooser in Eon
description:
## Outcome
Implement the accepted eon-tool-popups-e13 policy in Eon's existing workspace/lifecycle owners: configured terminal popups for Lazygit and Agent, with Alt+Z's combined search/browser command using that same host. Activate the accepted shared protocol against the exact accepted Venus consumer and update composition coherently. This issue does not implement native presentation or reseed the wire contract.

## Prerequisites and references
Blocked on eon-tool-popups-e13.4, the additive protocol seed, and eon-desktop:ven-shared-popup-surface-ehk, its exact accepted Venus consumer; eon-tool-popups-e13.1 is the completed policy decision. Before code, recheck child-source freshness and read the accepted parent/decision, EON-C8/C10/C11/C17/C18, workspace/CLI/supervisor/session owners and existing process tests. Complete the parent's Nova/Zellij and dependency gates for any newly selected mechanism. The seed and Venus consumer come first. Activate Eon's runtime and its exact accepted Venus pin together; update canonical manifest/locks and generation source inputs as required. Do not point the installed product at a speculative or incompatible client.

## Acceptance
- One Eon owner loads and validates accepted default/custom argv entries and owns their tab/Session association, launch cwd, semantic actions and dismissal lifetime. Invalid configuration or stale targets cannot mutate another tab or leave duplicate/residual Sessions.
- Agent/Lazygit use authoritative tab launch cwd. Same-cwd reopen and ordinary hiding retain identity; tab retarget alone does nothing to the process; the next popup invocation after mismatch stops the exact old Session and launches in the new cwd. Exercise stop/start failure without duplicate instances or false preservation claims.
- Reuse the existing project chooser command and validated directory action. Search/Yazi mode switching and app-owned cancellation stay inside it; remove redundant popup-specific ownership rather than duplicating a picker host. Ordinary popup dispatch must not require knowledge of its internal modes.
- Preserve fresh/new-tab pending lifecycle, first-tab fallback, later-tab cancellation, opaque path validation, no placeholder pane and no retargeting of ordinary pane processes. Implement picker/popup coexistence only as settled by the prerequisite decision.
- Expose only accepted versioned workspace data/actions for native projection, with bounded framing and stable identities. Apply the decided focus, exit, detach/recovery, hidden-work inspection and tab/generation stop policies through Orbit's existing authority.
- Use focused red/green owner/process checks and full affected Rust/Nix lifecycle/protocol proof, once per unchanged candidate. Record the exact active producer/consumer sources and qualifications. Refresh the affected Eon profile and make one isolated outermost check of activated popup launch and chooser admission without stopping user Sessions or taking desktop focus. Comprehensive composed tool/visual acceptance belongs to delivery; do not repeat unchanged owner proof there.

## Scope
Eon runtime/configuration, activation of the already accepted shared wire contract, and exact component composition only; no Venus rendering, Orbit mechanisms, agent-status producer, Anima implementation, full file-manager integration, callback registry, second terminal emulator or copied Nova plugin. All required dependency/contract decisions precede implementation. Deferred and unclaimed until the seed and consumer are accepted. Wire gaps return to the seed owner; do not compensate with a second schema.

Publish the additive shared-popup workspace protocol needed by Venus, while Eon's active runtime and pinned installed client keep using EONW v4. This is the first implementation frontier of eon-tool-popups-e13, not runtime popup activation.

## Prerequisites and reference gate
