Required local comparisons: protocol-only seeds 96119f29ca2e3ec4ad19bbe272708b07d588429a and aaafc9127c054e683abfceb3c8fcaae201a7a763. Reuse existing bounded framing and validation; preserve old-version semantics. The decision records the Nova/Zellij/Kitty behavioral evidence; inspect any reference again before adopting a materially different mechanism. No new dependency is selected.

## Acceptance
- Define the next version in the Eon-owned wire crate. Represent the enabled entry catalog/normalized shortcuts, shared presentation values needed by Venus, exact popup instances and tab association, selected popup and ordinary return selection. Valid states include pending tabs and tabs whose only durable work is a popup.
- Define bounded semantic invocation/focus/dismissal and exact chooser-completion targeting. A stale instance cannot become a command for its replacement or another tab. Carry raw Unix path bytes without lossy reconstruction. Keep argv, provider selection, launch cwd, lifetime and pending-tab policy in Eon.
- Prove roundtrip, invalid identities/references, focus-versus-toggle intent, replacement identity, pending/popup-only topology and maximum legal framing. The largest allowed catalog/tab/pane/popup snapshot must fit the existing 2 MiB envelope under the decision's combined Session bound. Use a few strong red/green protocol checks rather than mirrors of every field.
- Leave Eon's CLI/control/supervisor active protocol and the installed composition on their accepted v4 behavior. No runtime negotiation, compatibility adapter or popup feature flag. Exercise the existing v4 consumer through the affected Rust/Nix checks to falsify accidental activation or breakage.
- Update the indexed contract to distinguish a mechanically verified protocol seed from unimplemented runtime policy. Align relevant docs/LOC, record the exact source candidate and proof environment, and make it available as an exact accepted source before Venus pins it. Do not label fixture or codec proof as installed popup acceptance.

## Scope and next boundary
Owned shared wire crate, protocol tests and necessary contract/reference/LOC documentation only. No command launching, user config parser, chooser lifecycle refactor, Venus renderer, new Orbit API, manifest activation, sidebar or Anima. Source publication follows the repository Git workflow; no push/promotion is authorized merely by this planning record.
Next: eon-desktop:ven-shared-popup-surface-ehk consumes this exact seed; eon-tool-popups-e13.2 activates Eon's runtime only after that consumer is accepted; eon-tool-popups-e13.3 owns composed installed acceptance.

## Completion
Implemented and mechanically verified at published source 0cc8f477298681ae3945903e8fdb5852d487c5ab. EONW v5 is an additive inactive module; active Eon and Venus remain on v4. All 76 Rust workspace tests, fmt/check/strict Clippy, Nix flake checks and both product builds pass. Refreshed profiles resolve to those exact builds, and installed Eon reports v4 with the accepted unchanged Orbit/Venus pins. No desktop focus or running supervisor was disturbed.

The exact shared source is available for ven-shared-popup-surface-ehk. Its external prerequisite may be reconciled only after that consumer verifies this source and contract. This closes the protocol seed, not popup runtime, configuration, geometry or native visual acceptance.

title: Allow tab traversal while a directory picker is open
description:
## User-visible acceptance contract

Consumer: one local Eon workspace user with a directory picker open in a live tab.

Trigger: the user invokes the existing semantic focus-left or focus-right action through the CLI or accepted Venus Alt+H/L while that picker remains open.

Result: Eon selects the adjacent or wrapped live tab using EON-C8 traversal. The picker remains live and bound to its original tab. Another active tab presents its selected pane; returning presents the identical picker, which can still be accepted or cancelled normally. Focus-up/down, pane focus by identity, creation, a second picker, and other topology mutations retain picker-active failure.

Important failures: singleton traversal remains unavailable without mutation. Removed picker tabs, picker Session exit, stale identity, duplicate request, invalid workspace state, or failed attachment changes no accepted topology and leaves bounded cleanup.

Ownership: Eon workspace dispatch owns action admission and topology. EONW owns one picker bound to a live but not necessarily active tab. Venus owns shortcut and active-tab presentation. Orbit owns Session lifetime.

## Prerequisites and reference gate

Blocked on local EONW owner Bead eon-allow-inactive-picker-snapshot-2u0 and external Venus consumer Bead ven-traverse-tabs-during-picker-e9i in Eon Desktop. Consume only their exact accepted proof revisions. Then reread EON-C8/EON-C18, workspace dispatch and tests, supervisor picker lifecycle, CLI action routing, component manifest/pins, installed profile workflow, exact accepted Venus contracts, and original picker-first Bead eon-start-tabs-with-yazi-picker-1az.

Preserve circular EON-C8 traversal, one picker, exact tab binding, duplicate-request bounds, Session lifecycle, active component graph, and live Sessions. Reject an Eon copy of Venus behavior, a new action/keybinding, picker relocation, concurrent pickers, generic modal, configuration, new dependency, or platform expansion.

## Scope boundary

Only Eon producer dispatch, focused process proof, exact accepted Venus pin, EON-C8/EON-C18/current docs, changelog after acceptance, README LOC, profile refresh, and isolated installed native Wayland dogfood. EONW and Venus production work remain in their prerequisite Beads; Orbit and Eon Sessions are unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

The structured acceptance criteria field is canonical.
design:
1. Wait for exact accepted EONW and Venus proof revisions; update manifest/source pins only to those revisions under the freshness gate.
2. Update EON-C8/EON-C18 acceptance wording before producer code.
3. Add one focused Workspace::dispatch red check covering left/right ordinary and wrapped movement, durable and pending picker retention, return, singleton failure, and unchanged rejection of unrelated actions.
4. Admit only Action::Focus(Left|Right) through the existing picker gate and reuse focus_direction unchanged. Add no helper, state, action, or dependency.
5. Prove the process control path, complete affected Rust/Nix surfaces, refresh the active eon profile without restarting live supervisors, and dogfood native Alt+H/L plus CLI traversal, picker survival, acceptance, and cancellation.
acceptance_criteria:
1. With a picker open and at least two live tabs, CLI and Venus Alt+H/L select adjacent or wrapped tabs exactly as EON-C8 specifies.
2. The picker stays live and bound to its original tab across traversal; another active tab presents its selected pane, and return presents the exact picker endpoint for normal acceptance or cancellation.
3. Durable-tab and pane-free pending-tab pickers both survive traversal without moving, duplicating, starting a durable pane, consuming an identity, or changing launch directories.
4. Singleton left/right returns unavailable without mutation. Up/down, focus by identity, creation, duplicate picker, and unrelated topology mutations retain picker-active failure.
5. Duplicate requests, removed picker tabs, picker exit, stale identities, failed transitions, and cleanup remain atomic and bounded.
6. Eon consumes exact accepted EONW and Venus revisions through the canonical component graph. No new action, keybinding, protocol field/version, dependency, configuration, Orbit change, or platform surface is introduced.
7. Focused red/green owner and process proof, complete affected locked Rust/Nix verification, installed profile refresh, isolated native picker dogfood, EON-C8/EON-C18/current docs, changelog, README LOC, Beads state, and final diff pass succeed on one immutable candidate without restarting live Sessions.
notes: User authorized the required cross-repository expansion on 2026-08-27. The original Eon-only design was rejected because EONW v4 required the picker tab to be active and accepted Venus bdd8b36 both suppressed all shortcuts and unconditionally presented any picker. Work is sequenced as EONW owner eon-allow-inactive-picker-snapshot-2u0, Venus consumer ven-traverse-tabs-during-picker-e9i, then this Eon producer and installed acceptance slice.

title: Fill the gaps around pane cards with the bar color
description:
## Decision
Lucca, 2026-10-18: with pane frames on, everything below the tab bar that no card covers takes the
bar's color, so the top bar, the gaps between and around the cards and the hint row read as one
frame. Cards keep their terminal's background. Recommendation accepted with "implemnt it": the
exact bar color (DEFAULT_BACKGROUND, #0a0d14) and an opaque frame like the bar; only cards stay
translucent under `background_opacity`. Retune the color only after Lucca sees it.

## Contract
- Consumer: a full-Eon or eonbase user with pane frames enabled (the default).
- Result: the frame (gaps, card surroundings including outside the rounded corners, and the hint
  row) is opaque bar color; each card (column, or the popup card) fills with its terminal's
  background at `background_opacity`. Card outlines, separators, header fills, geometry and
  terminal sizing are unchanged.
- Frameless (`false`) is unchanged: column strips keep the terminal background across the window.
- Edits (approved by Lucca's go): EON-C24 and VEN-C24 gap-color clauses, their check name, USAGE or
  PRESENTATION text that names the gap color, both changelogs' unreleased card entries.

## Prerequisites
eon-gapped-rounded-cards-txco (closed).

## Acceptance
Focused Venus test for the frame-and-card coverage; yazelix-venus fmt and clippy; Venus suites via
`nix develop -c eon-test`; nix build; isolated headless-Sway captures at one, two and four columns,
hints shown and hidden, a popup and frameless; review loop; profile refresh. Lucca's installed look
is the final acceptance.

## Scope boundary
Gap and frame color only. No geometry, outline, header, tab-strip, typography or configuration
change. Portability: neutral.

title: Give tab pills and Eon Bar widgets one centred height, widgets outlined instead of filled
description:
## Why

eon-i2m3 decision (Lucca, 2026-10-24): Eon Bar widgets and tab pills get one height, the widgets
told apart by a thin rounded outline instead of a fill (frame OUTLINE in
~/.cache/eon-agents/i2m3/research/mock/png/). Lucca then: "id like the tabs to change their height
instead", "we should also make tab and widget pills automatically center vertically, with equal
gap between top edge of the window and top edge of the sidebar/project line", and on today's
centring (widgets 4..36, line at 50): "current doesnt work. look at this. it's so uneven ... figure
it out", allowing "a 'middle path'". The overseer chose H30 (mock:
~/.cache/eon-agents/i2m3/research/mock/png/centre-zoom.png, centre-strips.png; script
~/.cache/eon-agents/i2m3/centre-mock.py). Research: ~/.cache/eon-agents/i2m3/research/*.md.

## Behaviour

- One height and one centre line for tab pills and the quota, CPU, RAM and clock widgets: each
  spans from half the card title height (text_height / 2) below the window's top edge to the top
  of the allocated card areas, so the space above equals the space between it and the cards'
  shared top line. At default typography, scale 1: 30 px pills at y 10..40 (tabs grow from 24,
  widgets shrink from 32), shared top line at 50. Scene derives it from its existing title metric
  and card-area top; no second constant.
- Tabs keep their fills, text, attention badge, hover and keyboard-focus outline (re-centred).
- Widgets draw no fill: each is a rounded outline (radius half its height) at the pane cards'
  neutral border width (`[terminal] border_width`) and outline colour, text and provider icons on
  the opaque bar background.
- The version label stays plain text; New tab (+), Keyboard shortcuts (?) and Close centre on the
  same line (header button width unchanged).
- Bar height, allocated card areas, terminal rects and grids unchanged. Hover and AccessKit
  rectangles, item order, width fitting, narrow hiding and the blank drag region unchanged. On a
  short window the extra inset yields before the pills do, as today.
- Configurability: no new setting. border_width (1 to 3, default 1) also sizes the widget
  outlines; docs/CONFIGURATION.md says so.

## Contract (approved wording, see the Approval comments)

- VEN-C21 Result, after "The existing workspace tab strip remains one row at its existing
  height.", add: "Tabs keep their filled pills. Tab pills and the quota, CPU, RAM and clock widgets
  share one height and centre line: each spans from half the card title height below the window's
  top edge to the top of the allocated card areas, so the space above it equals the space between
  it and the cards' shared top line. The widgets draw no fill: each is a rounded outline at the
  pane cards' neutral border width and outline color, with its text and icons on the opaque bar
  background. The version label stays plain text, and New tab, Keyboard shortcuts and Close centre
  on the same line. Hover and accessibility rectangles, order, width fitting and the blank drag
  region stay unchanged."
- VEN-C8: "the tab pills keep the gap from the window's top and left edges" becomes "the tab pills
  keep the gap from the window's left edge"; "Pill size, the gap between pills and header button
  width stay as before" becomes "Pill height follows VEN-C21; the gap between pills and header
  button width stay as before"; "from the tab pills above" is dropped from the card-gap list.
- EON-C8 (docs/CONTRACTS.md ~391-396): the matching sentences change the same way: card areas keep
  the gap from the window's sides and from each other; "The tab pills keep the same gap from the
  window's top and left edges, in both modes." becomes "The tab pills keep the same gap from the
  window's left edge, in both modes, and are centred with the Eon Bar widgets as VEN-C21
  describes."
- VEN-C27 and VEN-C28: "on the quota chips' rounded fill" becomes "in the quota chips' rounded
  outline". Proof records stay as written.

## Acceptance

- Venus scene/paint tests (fail first): tab pills and widgets share height and centre; top gap ==
  gap to the shared top line (within snapping) at scales 1 and 1.3 and line_height 1.125/2; no
  widget fill pixels; outline at border_width 1/2/3; version label and controls centred on the
  same line; tabs keep fill; bar height, card areas and terminal grids unchanged.
- Isolated capture with Lucca's opacity and the six default widgets.

Portability: neutral.

- Treat this evidence as a reason to lead with Yazelix Eon and to perform package, command, domain, and trademark clearance before public release; it is not legal clearance.

Decision:
- Public product: Yazelix Eon, shortened to Eon after first mention.
- Platform labels, only after those surfaces exist: Eon for desktop, Eon for mobile, and Eon for the web.
- User-facing capability: Sessions.
- Technical roles: the Eon orchestrator, Venus client, and Orbit session runtime. Role words remain lowercase descriptors, not three public product names.
- Promote a component name publicly only if users can independently install, choose, configure, or use that component.

Acceptance checks:
- README distinguishes public names, future platform labels, user-facing capabilities, and technical roles without implying unimplemented surfaces exist.
- Architecture documentation records the same naming boundary and uses semantic role labels in the composition diagram.
- Contract IDs and ownership remain unchanged.
- README LOC scorecard, Markdown paths, Beads state, and git diff checks pass.

Scope boundary:
Documentation and mutable Eon planning metadata only. No runtime, command, repository, package, domain, contract, proof-state, child-repository, or historical Bead-ID rename is included.
close_reason: Documented the approved hybrid naming model in README.md and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md: Yazelix Eon is the public product, Sessions is the user-facing capability, and Eon orchestrator, Venus client, and Orbit session runtime are technical role descriptions. No reboot recovery (separate bead), no change to generation identity, no stale-generation notice.

title: Report an unmarked eon-install prefix as not owned instead of os error 2
description:
## Why

lm9p.1 found that `eon-install` gives a misleading message when the prefix is an existing
user-owned 0700 directory without the `.eon-install` marker. The behavior is right (exit 1,
contents untouched, nothing adopted), but the message is "eon-install: No such file or directory
(os error 2)" instead of "prefix is not owned by eon-install".

Cause: installer/src/main.rs:123 checks the marker with `fs::symlink_metadata(&marker)?`; the
NotFound error returns through `?` before the intended `invalid("prefix is not owned by
eon-install")`.

## Contract

docs/INSTALLER.md's prefix ownership rule: an existing prefix that eon-install did not create is
refused with a message naming the ownership problem. No behavior change beyond the message.

## Prerequisites

None. Reference gate: not consequential (no dependency, protocol, contract or trust-boundary
change; the refusal itself stays).

## Acceptance

- An existing 0700 prefix without `.eon-install` exits 1 with "prefix is not owned by
  eon-install", contents untouched. Falsifier: a focused red/green test in installer/src/tests.rs
  if it adds coverage beyond the existing prefix tests, else a red/green reproducer recorded here.
- Installer crate builds; `nix develop -c eon-test` for the installer suite passes.
- Codex and converge review per AGENTS.md (code change).

## Scope boundary

Message only. Any published Nix-free candidate built after this lands differs from lm9p's
6379a43c and needs the re-run named in lm9p's 2026-10-21 harness comment; this bead does not
build or publish a candidate.
close_reason: Unmarked existing prefix now refuses with 'prefix is not owned by eon-install'; red/green and installer checks recorded

title: Modularize Eon runtime by orchestration ownership
description:
## Contract routing

This planning container reorganizes Eon's internal Rust ownership without changing any user-visible contract. Eon remains the thin product orchestrator defined by EON-C1 through EON-C15; Orbit retains Session and terminal lifecycle ownership, Venus retains native presentation ownership, and the component manifest remains the sole composition graph.

## Why

`crates/eon/src/main.rs` is 3,677 lines and currently owns several independent concerns: CLI projection, generation discovery and lifecycle, EONW control transport, the Orbit management adapter, and supervisor composition. The file is harder to review because those owners are interleaved. The desired end state is a genuinely thin `main` that parses/invokes concrete repo-owned modules, not a forwarding layer over arbitrary helper files.

## Scope

In scope:
- the dependency-ordered child issues under this epic
- moving existing behavior into concrete modules named for their invariant owner
- preserving public behavior, wire bytes, filesystem layout, component pins, and error projection

Out of scope:
- implementing any child in this planning run
- changing EON contracts, CLI behavior, EONW, Session topology, component pins, dependencies, or distribution
- traits, service containers, factories, generic frameworks, or compatibility shims
- splitting files solely to meet a line-count target

## Success Criteria

- Every child identifies one concrete owner, affected contracts, and the cheapest falsifying checks.
- `crates/eon/src/main.rs` ends as CLI/process composition and top-level error reporting only.
- Existing `workspace.rs` and `managed_environment.rs` remain the owners of their current invariants.
- The current `eon-g3k` Ready-claim lifecycle work is completed before any overlapping extraction begins.
- The completed sequence preserves all EON-C1 through EON-C15 behavior and passes the repository's required Rust, Nix, installed-profile, and dogfood proof for the touched runtime surfaces.

## Reference Gate

Use the current Eon contracts, tests, and accepted Orbit/Venus revisions as normative evidence. Comparable thin-main layouts are shape evidence only. Prefer direct concrete modules already implied by the code; reject new abstraction layers or dependency additions.

## Stop Conditions

Stop if a proposed extraction needs a new public surface, duplicates a child component's ownership, changes a contract, or cannot be proved as a behavior-preserving move.
close_reason: All five ownership-extraction children are accepted; main.rs is the thin executable boundary and the complete Rust, Nix, profile, and installed proofs passed.

title: Extract Eon generation lifecycle from main
description:
## Contract routing

Preserve EON-C10 command/lifecycle projection and EON-C11 runtime generation semantics. This is an internal ownership move only: generation identity, discovery, classification, selection, and cleanup retain identical observable behavior and paths.

## Why

`crates/eon/src/main.rs` lines 44-1000 contain the generation data model, filesystem discovery, current-generation selection, lifecycle transitions, and generation command output. This is a coherent state owner independent of CLI dispatch and supervisor mechanics.

## Scope

In scope:
- extract the generation value types and lifecycle/discovery operations to `crates/eon/src/generation.rs`
- move their directly coupled unit tests with the owner
- keep configuration/runtime root inputs explicit and concrete

title: Extract Eon EONW control transport from main
description:
## Contract routing

Preserve EON-C10 producer/CLI error projection and EON-C11 supervisor lifecycle behavior. EONW bytes and framing remain unchanged. The module owns transport and request/response projection; workspace and Session policy remain with their existing concrete owners.

## Why

`crates/eon/src/main.rs` contains both client-side control discovery/send/probe logic and server-side listener, framing, response serialization, and dispatch plumbing. Keeping the protocol seam together makes the trust boundary reviewable while avoiding a second schema or generic RPC layer.

## Scope

In scope:
- extract EONW client transport, listener setup, request framing, response framing, and bounded error projection to `crates/eon/src/control.rs`
- invoke concrete supervisor/workspace operations without copying their policy
- move directly coupled protocol unit tests with the owner

Out of scope:
- changing EONW bytes, commands, timeouts, paths, CLI text, or trust validation
- moving workspace topology or Orbit lifecycle policy into control transport
- introducing async runtimes, traits, middleware, or dependencies

## Implementation Notes

Complete `eon-g3k` first. Keep one schema owner and use concrete callbacks/method calls already required by the supervisor; do not create an interface hierarchy for one server. Policy decisions must remain above transport framing.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `control.rs` is the sole owner of EONW connection, framing, parsing, serialization, and transport failures.
- Supervisor and workspace owners retain command semantics and state transitions.
- Existing EONW bytes, paths, timeouts, and user-facing error projection are unchanged.
- Existing control protocol tests and affected Eon crate build pass; the final integrated sequence satisfies required runtime/profile proof.

## Verification

Run the narrow EONW/control tests that exercise both client and listener framing, then the affected crate checks. Reuse the full integrated proof after all children converge.

## Stop Conditions

Stop if extraction requires a second schema, changes wire behavior, moves product policy below the transport boundary, or adds a runtime/dependency.

title: Extract Eon supervisor runtime from main
description:
## Contract routing

Preserve EON-C1 composition, EON-C10 control behavior, EON-C11 generation lifecycle, and EON-C15 rollback. The supervisor owns Eon's composition and lifecycle policy while delegating generation state, EONW transport, workspace topology, managed environment, and Orbit mechanisms to their concrete modules.

## Why

After the generation, control, and Session-adapter seams are extracted, `crates/eon/src/main.rs` still contains Programs/LaunchMode/PresentationProcess, launch/reap flow, and the central supervision loop. Those form the concrete product-runtime owner.

## Scope

In scope:
- extract Programs, LaunchMode, PresentationProcess, supervisor state, launch/reap operations, and the supervision loop to `crates/eon/src/supervisor.rs`
- consume `generation`, `control`, `sessions`, `workspace`, and `managed_environment` directly
- move directly coupled tests with the owner

Out of scope:
- altering launch ordering, retry/recovery, signals, child ownership, Session/workspace behavior, or error text
- adding a service locator, trait graph, event bus, dependency injection framework, or dependency
- moving CLI parsing into the supervisor

## Implementation Notes

Begin only after the generation, control, and Session-adapter children are complete. Prefer a concrete state object and direct calls. Keep platform/process details behind the smallest existing functions rather than inventing interfaces.

## Acceptance Criteria

- One concrete supervisor module owns product composition and process lifecycle policy.
- Generation, EONW, workspace, managed-environment, and Orbit adapter invariants are consumed rather than reconstructed.
- `main.rs` contains no supervision loop or child lifecycle policy.
- Existing workspace-control/lifecycle tests and affected build pass; final integrated Rust/Nix/profile proof passes.

## Verification

Run existing supervisor/workspace-control tests and the affected crate build, then reuse one unchanged-candidate full integrated proof for the completed modularization sequence.

## Stop Conditions

Stop if prerequisite module ownership is unsettled, if behavior changes are needed, or if the extraction adds indirection without removing duplicate responsibility.

title: Reduce Eon main to CLI composition
description:
## Contract routing

Preserve every existing Eon CLI command, default, output, exit status, and EON-C1 through EON-C15 behavior. This final child proves that `main` is a thin executable boundary, not a new policy owner.

## Why

Once the concrete runtime owners are extracted, the remaining CLI parsing and command selection can live in `crates/eon/src/cli.rs`. `src/main.rs` should only invoke that owner and project the top-level result to process exit.

## Scope

In scope:
- move CLI argument parsing, command selection, eon/eonterm entry dispatch, and directly coupled tests to `crates/eon/src/cli.rs`
- leave `crates/eon/src/main.rs` as minimal executable composition and error reporting
- remove obsolete imports, forwarding helpers, and duplicated tests exposed by the move

Out of scope:
- changing commands, flags, defaults, help, output, exit status, launch policy, or binary packaging
- a public library API, command framework, trait, factory, or new dependency
- enforcing an arbitrary line-count ceiling

## Implementation Notes

Begin after the supervisor child. Prefer one concrete `cli::run`-style entry over wrappers for every command. Thin means few responsibilities, not merely few lines.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `main.rs` owns only executable startup, invocation of the concrete CLI/runtime owner, and top-level error-to-exit projection.
- All CLI behavior and help remain byte-for-byte or observably equivalent where environment paths vary.
- No one-use abstraction or forwarding layer is introduced to make the file appear thin.
- The complete Eon test/build surface, Nix check, refreshed profiles, and installed outermost dogfood observation pass as required, preserving live Sessions.

## Verification

Run focused CLI parsing/projection checks, then one complete unchanged-candidate Eon Rust/Nix/profile proof after all modularization children land.

## Stop Conditions

Stop if thinning `main` requires public API growth, behavior changes, new dependencies, or wrappers that do not own an invariant.

title: Validate the canonical component graph before child launch
description:
## Contract routing

Harden EON-C1 and preserve EON-C2 through EON-C4. The consumer is a local Eon launcher; the trigger is creation of a new supervisor from an invalid embedded canonical component graph; the result is a bounded validation failure before Eon creates runtime ownership state or starts Orbit, Venus, or another child. A valid graph retains the current launch, attach, and version-report behavior.

This correction adds no component, schema, launcher framework, compatibility window, distribution channel, child behavior, or public configuration.

## Why

The existing canonical validator is not on the new-supervisor launch path. A locally built or future non-Nix artifact can therefore start a child before discovering that its embedded graph is invalid. The current official Nix package rejects the audited malformed graph indirectly because an Eon test reaches version reporting; this Bead fixes the runtime failure order rather than adding another packaging gate.

Impact: MEDIUM. Effort: S. Implementation risk: LOW. Confidence: HIGH.

## Evidence

- Closed audit `eon-audit-eon-component-graph-g5x`, exact subject `1b8836e616222f29c57ac697916872010db14685`, finding 1.
- `launch_current` reaches `supervise`; `supervise` creates the control listener and starts Orbit before any call to `eon_manifest::parse_and_validate` or the existing validated version-report owner.
- On an exact disposable archive, duplicate Orbit artifact IDs made `eon-manifest` exit 1 and `cargo test --locked -p eon` fail, but `cargo build --locked -p eon` succeeded. Running that binary with bounded fake children wrote the Orbit spawn marker before exiting on child startup.
- The later endpoint-byte commits through `57d7acc22f9f01c7f15d9d381845318b67f760e1` did not change the graph, validator, launch owner, flake, or EON-C1 through EON-C4 evidence.

## Prerequisite and reference gate

- Rebaseline the cited launch and validation owners at the execution baseline and read the complete closed component-graph audit, EON-C1 through EON-C4, `components/eon-alpha-v1.json`, the complete `eon-manifest` crate, the launch path, and the focused runtime tests.
- Reuse the audit's exact Nova `124308bfa128203f843839346c88296cd266568a` comparison only for immutable revisions and resolution assertions; its component set and runtime remain rejected surrounding scope.
- The existing `eon-manifest` validation/report path is the required owner. No external reference, dependency, crate feature, or schema change is expected. Stop for the applicable gate and user approval before any manifest or dependency change.
- Platform classification: neutral preflight policy with the current Nix packaging isolated; no new macOS blocker.

## Scope

In scope:
- The smallest shared new-supervisor preflight in `crates/eon/src/main.rs` using the existing canonical validator/report owner.
- One focused regression or exact disposable build proof that an invalid embedded graph starts no child and creates no durable runtime owner.
- EON-C1 current-state proof metadata, `CHANGELOG.md`, and README LOC only as required after acceptance.

Out of scope:
- A second validator, `build.rs` policy, Nix-only validation, generic launch abstraction, new manifest field, compatibility window, direct distribution, or child-repository change.
- Revalidating the trusted graph before every command, deriving package paths, changing launch arguments, or resolving the separate inert-declaration finding.
- Broad `main.rs` refactoring or changes to attach, stop, workspace, shell, or generation-selection policy.

## Implementation notes

1. Write the cheapest check that fails when fake Orbit is started from an invalid embedded graph; avoid a production injection framework solely for the test.
2. Invoke the existing canonical validation owner once before the first runtime-directory, socket, or process side effect for a new supervisor.
3. Preserve the current valid-graph launch and diagnostics; return the validator's bounded error rather than reconstructing it.
4. Keep attach to an already validated current supervisor unchanged unless exact evidence proves it also needs the same check.

## Acceptance

- An invalid embedded graph fails before a control socket, child process, or child spawn marker exists.
- The failure uses the existing canonical validator and identifies the graph defect.
- A valid graph starts exactly the same accepted Orbit and Venus pair and retains current attach, version-report, lifecycle, and workspace behavior.
- The official Nix build remains green; no duplicate packaging validator or second schema is introduced.
- No new product contract, dependency, component identity, public configuration, or compatibility promise is added.

## Verification

- The focused invalid-graph launch check exits 0 and proves the fake-child marker remains absent.
- `cargo fmt --all --check`
- `cargo check --locked --workspace`
- `cargo test --locked --workspace`
- `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo run --locked -p eon-manifest -- components/eon-alpha-v1.json`
- `nix build --no-link --print-out-paths --no-update-lock-file path:.#default`
- `nix flake check --no-build --no-update-lock-file path:.`
- `git diff --check`
- After the proof-bearing commit, refresh the active Eon profile without stopping live supervisors and report whether a restart is required for existing generations.

## Stop conditions

- Stop if graph acceptance has moved away from `eon-manifest` or the launch owner has materially changed.
- Stop if the correction requires a new schema, dependency, build-time code generator, child change, or public distribution promise.
- Stop if the check can prove only validator behavior and cannot prove child-spawn ordering.
- Stop if the same verification failure repeats twice after a reasonable correction.

## Maintenance notes

Use the validator that already exists, once, at the first side-effect boundary. Do not create another graph owner.

title: Adopt a session-restart rule for context compaction
description:
## Chosen outcome — Lucca, 2026-10-14
Adopt option C: restart chats at each bead boundary, and inside a bead after the second compaction or at the first sign of lost context. If the restarts cost too much, Lucca may switch to option E later (same chat until the second compaction, then finish the current bead).

Evidence (web research, 2026-10-14):
- Task-level loss per compaction is small: SWE-bench methods land within 2.6 points of each other.
- Side constraints are lost often: at best about 55% are retained.
- User corrections spike after a compaction: 41.9% vs 17.7% in one case study.
- Loss compounds across rounds.
The guardrails target chat-only decisions and the period right after a compaction.

## Contract
Instructions only, as an agent-neutral root rule.

## Acceptance
- starcompass check passes.
- Every chain stays at or under 32,768 bytes.

Switching to E later means editing this one paragraph. Rendered from Starcompass 0e1b9c6 (public edge). Proof (policy route): starcompass check is valid with 3 directory files. title: Fix the intermittent new-window shortcut test in Venus
description:
## Why

A flaky test fails package builds at random. Lucca approved filing this on 2026-10-22.

## Evidence

- On 2026-10-22, eon-78's `nix build .#default` on tree d4007e6 failed in Venus's in-build test run with:
  `application::tests::new_window_shortcut_invokes_the_supplied_eon_command` panicked at
  venus/src/application.rs:6084, `assertion failed: run_new_window(&script).is_ok()`.
- 53 of the 54 binary tests passed.
- The identical rebuild passed, and the test passed in two `eon-test -p yazelix-venus` runs.
- The machine was heavily loaded at the time.

## Likely cause (to confirm)

- The test writes a shell script, makes it executable and runs it. It then rewrites the same file
  with `fs::write` and runs it again.
- Other tests in the same process spawn children in parallel. A child forked while the write fd is
  open inherits it, and exec of the script then fails with ETXTBSY ("Text file busy"). This is the
  classic Rust test race.
- The assertion hides the error text.
- Same class as `eon-p8cq` (closed; the cause there was fork inheritance of open file descriptions)
  and the open `eon-1fxc` (quota worker test, ETXTBSY suspected). Check whether one shared
  test-helper pattern fixes both; if so, say so on `eon-1fxc` rather than fixing it here.

## Scope

- Confirm the cause: run the test in a loop under parallel spawning, or print the error.
- Fix the test only, for example:
  - write each script to a fresh path and never rewrite an executable in place;
  - and assert on the error so a future failure names its cause.

Out of scope: `run_new_window` itself, unless the cause turns out to be there.

## Acceptance

- The test passes many repeated runs under load. Record the loop count.
- `nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-venus`, fmt and clippy green for Venus.
- Review loop per AGENTS.md (test-only change).
close_reason: Cause confirmed (ETXTBSY from fork inheritance); test-only fix proven and reviewed; see proof comment

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Seen again 2026-10-25 ~02:20 -03 (overseer): the eon-x7l8 implementer's nix build failed once in the Venus package checks on the new-window shortcut test, unchanged tree; the retry passed (~/.cache/eon-agents/x7l8/report.md, build-round2-retry logs).

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Seen again 2026-10-25 ~13:05 -03 (overseer nix build of the shn4.3 landing tree e572c519): application::tests::new_window_shortcut_invokes_the_supplied_eon_command panicked at venus/src/application.rs:7348 in the Venus package checks; unrelated change. Third sighting in two days.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Proof and review (2026-10-27, x86_64 Linux, nix develop shell). The commit carrying this comment is the proof's revision: base 6a3ee78, code tree 5db9f6c58ddcf2b4efdaa54effe7ebc08b06a7ca (the commit adds only this bead record).

Cause confirmed: ETXTBSY from fork inheritance. Evidence is a disposable standalone reproduction (~/.cache/eon-agents/66gm-work/repro/main.rs, outside the repository). Four threads fork `/bin/sh -c :` in a loop, while the main thread writes a script to a fresh path, chmods it 0700 and execs it.
- Old pattern (`fs::write` in the test process): 162/2000, 758/10000 and 177/2000 (reviewer's run) rounds failed with "Text file busy (os error 26)", and nothing else failed.
- Fix pattern (a child `/bin/sh` writes the file): 0/2000, 0/10000, 0/10000 and 0/2000 (reviewer's run).
- The descriptor that a concurrently forked child inherits stays open until that child execs or exits. A fresh path alone does not help, and the first exec in the old test was exposed too, not only the in-place rewrite.

Fix (test only, venus/src/application.rs, new_window_shortcut_invokes_the_supplied_eon_command):
- A local closure has a child `/bin/sh` write each script to a fresh path with `printf '%s' "$1" > "$0"`. The test process never opens the file for writing; it only chmods by path.
- The assertions now print the error: `assert!(error.contains("window|new"), "{error}")` and `assert_eq!(run_new_window(&succeeding), Ok(()))`.
- run_new_window is unchanged.

Checks:
- `nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-venus`, CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4, on the same change based at c56372f: exit 0.
- After moving the uncommitted change onto 6a3ee78 (no overlap; the Venus diff is byte-identical apart from line offsets), the review round re-ran these on tree 5db9f6c, all exit 0:
  - `eon-test -p yazelix-venus`: lib 140 passed, 1 ignored; bin 61 passed, 4 ignored, including this test; canonical_scene 18 passed; doc-tests 0.
  - `cargo fmt --check -p yazelix-venus`: clean.
  - `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -p yazelix-venus -- -D warnings`: clean.
  - The checks left the tree unchanged.
- Loop: `eon-test -p yazelix-venus --bin yazelix-venus -- --test-threads=4`, 30 consecutive runs, 30/30 passed at 1-minute load 7.7-10.9, with the standalone reproduction running alongside for part of it. The bin suite finishes in about 0.01 s and the old test almost always passed, so the loop is weak evidence alone; the reproduction's red/green is the cause and fix proof.

Review ledger: 1 pass, on candidate 5db9f6c. A fresh Claude reviewer (it also ran the checks) and Codex (gpt-6.1-sol, xhigh, read-only) ran in parallel, and both found no code findings. The Claude reviewer's one blocking item was this proof record, written here, and its nits were left as they are: scripts are removed only on success, as before; the comment could add that the inherited descriptor outlives fs::write. A narrow Codex re-check covers this record. An earlier Codex run on the c56372f-based candidate was stopped unfinished when the base moved.

title: Keep an idle blinking cursor from reshaping the whole Venus grid
description:
## Why

When a program asks for a blinking cursor, Venus flips `blink_visible` every 500 ms, and
`blink_visible` is part of the full-rebuild key, so an idle window reshapes every visible cell
twice a second although the selected column's cursor is drawn in the separate dynamic layer.
Nobody has measured the idle cost. This bead measures it first (AP-PERF-001) and then keeps a
blinking cursor from rebuilding the grid.

Source: Venus GPU audit, eon-overseer, 2026-10-27
(`/home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-overseer/gpu-audit-2026-10-27.md`). Lines below re-checked on
edge `4e705bc`.

## Evidence

- `venus/src/scene.rs:3542-3552` `has_blinking_content`: true for a visible blinking cursor or any
  visible SGR-blink cell.
- `venus/src/application.rs:61` `BLINK_INTERVAL` 500 ms; `:4229-4237` toggles `blink_visible` and
  requests a redraw; `update_blink` at `:4303-4318`.
- `venus/src/render.rs:216-235` `ContentKey` includes `blink_visible` (`:222`, set at `:1404`), so
  each toggle reruns `rebuild_if_needed` (`:1382-1698`): `build_scene_text` and `push_cell_text`
  reshape every visible cell, glyphon prepares (`:1255-1282`), all vertices upload.
- `blink_visible` is used in the rebuild by blinking text cells (`render.rs:1935`, `:1980`) and by
  the static cursor drawn for non-selected columns and when there is no trail
  (`build_scene_rectangles` at `:1556-1564`); the selected column's cursor is drawn by
  `rebuild_dynamic_cursor` (`:1243`, `:1700-1760`).
- Blink is application-requested: Orbit publishes libghostty's canonical blink state, steady by
  default (`ven-stable-cursor-blink-v4o`, closed). A workload must request it, for example
  `printf '\e[1 q'` (DECSCUSR blinking block).

## Contract

Expected none. VEN-C1 keeps the cursor's authoritative shape, visibility and blink, and the
500 ms cadence stays. If the change needs any VEN-C* text change, stop and ask Lucca with the
proposed text.

## Relation to the per-row cache

Independent of the per-row text cache beads (linked as related) and may land first. Both change
`ContentKey` and `rebuild_if_needed`; whichever lands second rebases. With the row cache, a
blink-only change would already be cheaper; this bead still removes the rebuild entirely for a
blinking cursor.

## Prerequisites

- `orb-j2i.11` has landed or is rebased onto (both touch `venus/src/render.rs`).
- Read `AP-PERF-001`, `venus/AGENTS.md`, VEN-C1.

## Scope

In scope:
1. Baseline first, recorded on this bead before any code change: idle Venus CPU over 20 s
   (`utime+stime` ticks of 10 ms from `/proc/<pid>/stat`, as the VEN-C21 proofs did) with a
   blinking cursor and with a steady one, at 1 and 4 columns of dense text, on lavapipe (pixman
   Sway) and on the Intel GPU (Vulkan Sway on `renderD129`), three runs each; exact revision,
   store path, window size and workload recorded. Stop and report to Lucca if a blinking cursor
   costs no material CPU over a steady one.
2. Take the cursor's blink phase out of the full-rebuild trigger: draw the blinking cursor (and
   the static cursors of other columns) in the dynamic layer, or key the rebuild on blink only
   while a visible SGR-blink cell exists. Choose and record the shape.
3. Focused tests that a cursor-only blink does not rebuild the scene text and that blinking cells
   still blink.

Out of scope:
- The per-row text cache, scroll, adapter choice, image upload.
- Changing the blink interval or default (`BLINK_INTERVAL` is a timing a person sees; changing it
  is a configuration question for Lucca under AGENTS.md Configurability).
- Blinking SGR text cells beyond keeping them correct.

## Acceptance

- The baseline and after numbers, on the same workload and environments, are recorded here; with a
  blinking cursor at 1 and 4 columns, idle CPU drops to near the steady-cursor figure.
- Cursor shape, visibility, blink phase and cadence, and SGR-blink cells look the same: installed
  capture bursts over two blink periods match the pre-change build.

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-venus` exits 0.
- `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings` for `yazelix-venus`.
- Refresh the `eon` profile and record one isolated installed observation (do not restart a live
  supervisor).

## Stop Conditions

- Stop and report if the baseline shows no material cost.
- Stop if the cited code has drifted materially.
- Stop if verification fails twice for the same reason after a reasonable fix attempt.

## Review

Code change: converge rounds plus the Codex round (AGENTS.md "Codex on every code change"), with
the ledger line on this bead.

## Approval

Lucca, 2026-10-27, relayed by eon-overseer. Asked: "1. Cache prepared text per row, and move it
instead of re-preparing it when scrolling; first record a baseline (scroll frame time, idle CPU
with a blinking cursor), as AP-PERF-001 requires. 2. Stop cursor blink from re-preparing the whole
window; measure first too. 3. Choose the GPU on purpose: prefer the low-power one, log which one
Venus picked, and slow the cursor-trail animation when there's no GPU. 4. Move the image upload
wait off Venus's main thread, a small follow-up after orb-j2i.11 lands. Should I file 1–4 as beads,
with 1 and 2 each starting from a recorded baseline?" Lucca: "go ahead".

The approval is to file this bead. Any VEN-C* contract text change or new configuration value it
needs still needs Lucca's approval during implementation: stop and ask with the proposed text.

comments.text: Stale-fact fix, 2026-10-27 (prime-beads review at edge 01f5e3c): orb-j2i.11 landed (7dc3509, closed), so that prerequisite is met; lines drifted: ContentKey venus/src/render.rs:218 (blink_visible :224), rebuild_if_needed :1429, BLINK_INTERVAL venus/src/application.rs:64. Measurement hazard new since 4ae8a21: the working attention badge now animates at 10 Hz (VEN-C21 braille dots). Keep any working agent out of the measured window, or launch with [workspace] animate_working_badge = false, and record which, so badge repaints do not pollute the idle-CPU baseline.

title: Choose Venus's GPU adapter deliberately, log it, and slow the cursor trail on software adapters
description:
## Why

Venus takes whatever GPU adapter wgpu enumerates first. It asks for no power preference and
ignores the `WGPU_*` environment overrides, so on a hybrid laptop it can wake the discrete GPU, and
nobody can tell which adapter it picked without reading `/proc`. On a software adapter (lavapipe)
only the working spinner adapts; the 16 ms cursor-trail timer and full redraws still run there,
and software rendering made the spinner cost 738 vs 51 CPU ticks per 20 s before
`eon-agent-sidebar-yx8.15` stilled it. This bead chooses the adapter deliberately, logs the
choice, and slows or stops the cursor trail on a software adapter as the spinner already does.

Source: Venus GPU audit, eon-overseer, 2026-10-27
(`/home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-overseer/gpu-audit-2026-10-27.md`). Lines below re-checked on
edge `4e705bc`.

## Evidence

- `venus/src/render.rs:948-950`: `Instance::new(InstanceDescriptor::new_with_display_handle(..))`,
  not built from the environment.
- `venus/src/render.rs:954-960`: `request_adapter(&RequestAdapterOptions { compatible_surface,
  ..Default::default() })`, so `PowerPreference::None`; wgpu-core 30 then takes the first
  compatible adapter.
- `venus/src/render.rs:961`: `spinners_turn = adapter.get_info().device_type != DeviceType::Cpu`,
  the only software-adapter adaptation (passed to `Spinners::new` at `:1121`).
- `venus/src/application.rs:66` `ANIMATION_FRAME_INTERVAL` 16 ms; `:4249-4261` schedules cursor
  animation frames while `cursor_animation_active()`; `update_animation_deadline` at `:4340-4355`
  is a fixed timer, not frame callbacks.
- `venus/src/application.rs:4430-4432` `report` writes `venus: ...` to stderr, which the
  supervisor relays into its diagnostic log (`runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/supervisor.rs:509-528`).
- Precedent: VEN-C21 `venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md:1331` (still badge on a software adapter) and its
  proofs at `:1409-1437` (CPU ticks over 20 s; lavapipe identified by `llvmpipe-N` threads, the
  Intel GPU by `drm-engine-render` time on `renderD129`).
- On Lucca's machine `renderD128` is NVIDIA and `renderD129` Intel; the Nix Venus loads only Mesa
  ICDs (intel, lvp, dzn) and lands on Intel: correct, but by accident.

## Contract

- VEN-C1 (cursor trail, `venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md:208-221`): slowing or stopping the trail on a
  software adapter adds a clause like VEN-C21's still badge. VEN-C16 (native platforms) may name
  the adapter policy. Both are contract text changes: stop and ask Lucca with the proposed text
  before editing them.
- Configurability: adapter preference and the software-adapter trail rate are values a person
  feels. Either record on this bead why they stay fixed (recommendation: low power is right for a
  terminal and the software-adapter rate is a performance budget; wgpu's own environment
  overrides cover debugging), or propose a configuration key to Lucca; a new key needs his
  approval and an entry in `docs/CONFIGURATION.md`. WezTerm exposes `webgpu_power_preference`;
  weigh that in the decision.

## Humans and Agents

Adapter choice is not something a person sees in the window, so AGENTS.md "Humans and Agents" does
not require an `eon` CLI path; the log line is the diagnostic, and an agent can read the
supervisor's log. Record whether an agent-readable surface (for example a field in a future
`eon` diagnostics command) is warranted; recommendation: not now. `eon-gpu-widget-eon-bar-ri16`
(GPU chip in the Eon Bar) is the place if one is ever shown.

## Reference gate

Record on this bead before code:
- wgpu 30.0.0 source (the pinned version, `venus/docs/CRATES.md` "GPU and text"): how
  `PowerPreference::LowPower` ranks adapters in wgpu-core; which environment helpers exist in 30.0.0
  (`util::power_preference_from_env`, `WGPU_ADAPTER_NAME` adapter selection, instance backends and
  flags from the environment) and what each overrides. Verify exact names in that source.
- Comparable: WezTerm at `e2a98e1` (`~/pjs/refs/wezterm`): `wezterm-gui/src/termwindow/webgpu.rs:237`
  (preferred adapter), `:294-298` (power preference), `config/src/frontend.rs:48-56` (default
  `LowPower`).
- Decision: `LowPower` fixed, or `LowPower` as the default with wgpu's `WGPU_*` overrides honoured
  (recommended: honour `WGPU_POWER_PREF`/`WGPU_ADAPTER_NAME` so users can debug without a key), the
  rejected alternatives and the check.

## Portability disposition

`neutral`: power preference, `AdapterInfo` and `DeviceType::Cpu` are wgpu API on every backend;
on Apple Silicon there is one GPU and the choice is a no-op. The lavapipe/pixman and
`renderD129` observations are Linux evidence only.

## Prerequisites

- `orb-j2i.11` has landed or is rebased onto (it touches `venus/src/render.rs` and the renderer's
  construction).
- Read `venus/AGENTS.md`, VEN-C1, VEN-C16, VEN-C21, `AP-PERF-001`.

## Scope

In scope:
- Adapter request with `PowerPreference::LowPower` (and the environment overrides if the gate
  chooses them).
- One `venus:` log line at startup with the adapter's name, backend, device type and driver.
- On `DeviceType::Cpu`, slow the cursor-trail animation (a longer frame interval) or skip it
  (draw the cursor without a trail), chosen with numbers; keep the spinner's existing behaviour.
- Focused tests in the existing Venus test modules for the software-adapter animation policy.

Out of scope:
- Frame-callback pacing, damage tracking or present-mode changes.
- A configuration key or an `eon` CLI field unless Lucca approves one.
- Text caching and blink (their own beads), image upload.

## Acceptance

- Isolated installed observation on lavapipe (pixman Sway): the log names a CPU adapter;
  `llvmpipe-N` threads present; Venus CPU over 20 s while the cursor moves (typing) is lower than
  the pre-change build, with numbers for both; the cursor still lands exactly on Orbit's position.
- Isolated installed observation on the Intel GPU (Vulkan Sway on `renderD129`): the log names the
  Intel adapter; `drm-engine-render` time on `renderD129`; the trail animates as before.
- Optional: with the host NVIDIA Vulkan ICD added (`VK_ADD_DRIVER_FILES`), `LowPower` still picks
  Intel, and the override (if chosen) can select NVIDIA.

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-venus` exits 0.
- `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings` for `yazelix-venus`.
- Refresh the `eon` profile and record both installed observations (do not restart a live
  supervisor).

## Stop Conditions

- Stop and ask before any VEN-C1/VEN-C16 text change or new configuration key.
- Stop if the cited code has drifted materially.
- Stop if verification fails twice for the same reason after a reasonable fix attempt.

## Review

Code change: converge rounds plus the Codex round (AGENTS.md "Codex on every code change"); a
contract text change also gets its Codex review. Ledger line on this bead.

## Approval

Lucca, 2026-10-27, relayed by eon-overseer. Asked: "1. Cache prepared text per row, and move it
instead of re-preparing it when scrolling; first record a baseline (scroll frame time, idle CPU
with a blinking cursor), as AP-PERF-001 requires. 2. Stop cursor blink from re-preparing the whole
window; measure first too. 3. Choose the GPU on purpose: prefer the low-power one, log which one
Venus picked, and slow the cursor-trail animation when there's no GPU. 4. Move the image upload
wait off Venus's main thread, a small follow-up after orb-j2i.11 lands. Should I file 1–4 as beads,
with 1 and 2 each starting from a recorded baseline?" Lucca: "go ahead".

The approval is to file this bead. Any VEN-C* contract text change or new configuration value it
needs still needs Lucca's approval during implementation: stop and ask with the proposed text.

comments.text: Stale-fact fix, 2026-10-27 (prime-beads review at edge 01f5e3c): orb-j2i.11 landed (7dc3509). Lines drifted: request_adapter is venus/src/render.rs:962; the software-adapter rule is now venus/src/render/chrome.rs:235 spinners_turn(device_type, animate), called at render.rs:968 with the new [workspace] animate_working_badge setting (4ae8a21, eon-spinner-braille-dots-hmg0), so a still badge has two causes: a CPU adapter or the setting. VEN-C21 now words it 'On a software (CPU) graphics adapter, or when Eon passes --animate-working-badge false, it is the still frame ⠋'. title: Move Venus's image-upload GPU waits off the event-loop thread
description:
## Why

`orb-j2i.11` uploads Orbit images into Venus's GPU cache with two blocking GPU waits on the
event-loop thread: one before allocating (so freed textures are released and the VEN-C31 budget is
never exceeded) and one on the staging copy. While the GPU works, Venus cannot paint, read input
or answer the compositor, so a large image (up to 4096x4096, 64 MiB) can hitch the window. This
small follow-up moves those waits off the event-loop thread, after `orb-j2i.11` lands.

Source: Venus GPU audit, eon-overseer, 2026-10-27
(`/home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-overseer/gpu-audit-2026-10-27.md`).

## Evidence

These lines are from the unlanded `orb-j2i.11` worktree (`/home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/j2i11`,
uncommitted on `4e705bc`). Re-locate them on edge after `orb-j2i.11` lands before starting:
- `venus/src/render/images.rs:791-795`: `device.poll(PollType::wait_indefinitely())` before
  `allocate`, to let a frame in flight release freed textures.
- `venus/src/render/images.rs:889-894`: `queue.submit` of the staging copy, then
  `device.poll(PollType::Wait { submission_index, timeout: None })`.
- `venus/src/application.rs:1760-1767`: `ModelEffect::Resource` calls
  `renderer.upload_image(..)` on the event-loop thread.
- `venus/src/render/images.rs:725-726`, `:829`: linear min/mag filter, `mip_level_count: 1`.

## Contract

VEN-C31 (Static terminal images, `venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md:2183-`): its budget (256 MiB at 4 bytes
per pixel, checked before allocating), validation, refusal markers and resync behaviour must stay
exactly as written. Expected no contract text change; if one is needed, stop and ask Lucca with the
proposed text.

## Prerequisites

- `orb-j2i.11` closed (blocking dependency).
- Read `venus/AGENTS.md`, VEN-C31, `AP-PERF-001`.

## Scope

In scope:
- Replace the blocking waits with non-blocking completion: submit the copy, keep the upload
  pending, and poll without blocking (or use `map_async`/`on_submitted_work_done` callbacks) from
  the event loop; draw the image once its copy completes, a marker or nothing until then as
  VEN-C31 allows. Keep the budget exact: count textures freed but possibly still in flight against
  the budget until the GPU has released them, instead of waiting for it.
- A worker thread only if non-blocking polling cannot keep the budget exact; record why.
- Focused tests for the pending-upload state and budget accounting in the existing image tests.

Out of scope:
- Budget size, eviction policy, validation and resync (VEN-C31).
- Mipmaps for heavily downscaled images: optional note for a later bead, not this one.
- Text, blink, adapter choice.

## Acceptance

- Baseline and after, recorded here (AP-PERF-001): the largest frame-to-frame gap while a
  4096x4096 Kitty image uploads (for example `kitten icat` of a fixed PNG in an isolated installed
  Eon, with continuous output in another pane to keep frames coming), on lavapipe and on the Intel
  GPU, several runs each with exact revisions and store paths. After the change, no frame gap
  during upload exceeds the no-image baseline's spread materially.
- VEN-C31 behaviour unchanged: the existing image tests pass, the budget refusal still shows
  markers, and the ignored live test `images_draw_in_panes_and_popups_and_refusals_keep_the_renderer`
  (`venus/docs/DEVELOPMENT.md`) still passes on its isolated display.

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-venus` exits 0.
- `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings` for `yazelix-venus`.
- Refresh the `eon` profile and record one isolated installed observation (do not restart a live
  supervisor).

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if `orb-j2i.11` landed a different upload shape that already avoids these waits; close this
  with the evidence.
- Stop if keeping the budget exact requires a VEN-C31 change.
- Stop if verification fails twice for the same reason after a reasonable fix attempt.

## Notes

- Optional, not scope: images shown much smaller than their pixels sample with a single level and
  a linear filter (`images.rs:725-726`, `:829`), which can alias; mipmaps would fix that at a
  memory cost against the budget.

## Review

Code change: converge rounds plus the Codex round (AGENTS.md "Codex on every code change"), with
the ledger line on this bead.

## Approval

Lucca, 2026-10-27, relayed by eon-overseer. Asked: "1. Cache prepared text per row, and move it
instead of re-preparing it when scrolling; first record a baseline (scroll frame time, idle CPU
with a blinking cursor), as AP-PERF-001 requires. 2. Stop cursor blink from re-preparing the whole
window; measure first too. 3. Choose the GPU on purpose: prefer the low-power one, log which one
Venus picked, and slow the cursor-trail animation when there's no GPU. 4. Move the image upload
wait off Venus's main thread, a small follow-up after orb-j2i.11 lands. Should I file 1–4 as beads,
with 1 and 2 each starting from a recorded baseline?" Lucca: "go ahead".

The approval is to file this bead. Any VEN-C* contract text change or new configuration value it
needs still needs Lucca's approval during implementation: stop and ask with the proposed text.

title: Decide named-key encoding for remapped and virtual keyboards in Venus
description:
## Why

Venus sends Orbit the physical key code for every key event (venus/src/input.rs:151,
`physical_key(code)`), by design under VEN-C2 ("maps_layout_independent_physical_keys"). Keys
without text (Return, Escape, Tab, arrows) and shortcuts are then decided by the physical code,
not the keysym the keymap produces. lm9p.2 (2026-10-19) saw this break input from a keyboard whose
keymap differs from the evdev layout: with wtype's virtual keyboard, Return reached the terminal as
a lone ESC (raw pane bytes), Alt+Shift+J did nothing and some printable characters dropped. Real
users likely affected: on-screen keyboards and remote-desktop input that use virtual-keyboard
keymaps, and possibly xkb remaps such as caps:escape (unverified).

## Evidence

- lm9p.2 proof comment (raw bytes: "ab", Return -> `a b 033`; QMP scancodes through libinput work).
- VEN-C2 (owner: Venus native input; Orbit encodes, ORB-C5 via ORBS v13).

## Scope

Step 1 (no code): verify which real setups break. In an isolated headless session, check
caps:escape (or another xkb option remap) and one virtual-keyboard client (wtype as stand-in), and
read how Ghostty's own apprt chooses the key for named keys. Record results here.
Step 2: if a real user setup breaks, propose the smallest VEN-C2/ORB-C5 change (for example, derive
named keys from the logical keysym while keeping physical keys for layout-independent shortcuts) and
stop for Lucca's contract approval before code. If only synthetic tools break, record that and close
with a note in VEN-C2's boundary.

Out of scope: IME, macOS (VEN-C16), Eon shortcut policy.

## Acceptance

- Step 1 results recorded with the exact setups observed.
- If changed: an approved contract update, a focused Venus test for a remapped named key, and one
  isolated installed observation that Return/Escape/Alt chords work from the affected keymap while
  ordinary layouts keep working; fmt/clippy clean for venus.

## Portability

Disposition to record in the bead: neutral expected (keysym vs physical choice exists on both
Wayland and macOS).
close_reason: Step 1 found a real-user break (caps:swapescape/caps:escape drop Escape; virtual keyboards turn named keys into ESC). Step 2 landed the approved VEN-C2 change: named keys outside the numpad follow the keymap for terminal input and Venus's own key handling, with per-press pinning; proof recorded in VEN-C2 and this bead. Gap eon-lihr accepted.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Step 1 results (eon-48, 2026-10-21, no code). A real setup breaks.

Setup: installed /nix/store/qr5a1z10c5k5icmpj3p0a15rc9zk79lz-eon-0.1.1 (generation g1-fd445623a32b91dc47ef97dfefafe4ca; venus/src/input.rs unchanged on edge since 2586d7c). Private headless Sway 1.12 (WLR_BACKENDS=headless, pixman, no libinput devices), isolated HOME/XDG. Keys from wdotool 0.5.3's wlr virtual keyboard, whose keymap comes from xkbcommon names (XKB_DEFAULT_LAYOUT/OPTIONS), so it reproduces what a compositor forwards for a physical keyboard with that layout and those options. The pane ran `stty raw -echo; timeout --foreground 15 cat > FILE`. The test sent a, Escape, b, Return, c, Tab, d, BackSpace, e, Up, f. Raw bytes from od -c:

- base (us): `a 033 b \r c \t d 177 e 033 [ A f`, correct.
- caps:swapescape (Escape's keysym is on the physical CapsLock key, xkb keycode 66): `a b \r c \t d 177 e 033 [ A f`. The Escape is lost, with no byte and no notice. Venus sends PhysicalKey CapsLock with no text, and Orbit encodes nothing for it. caps:escape puts the same keysym on the same keycode, so it breaks the same way (inferred, not run separately). Helix and Vim users commonly use this remap, and GNOME/KDE expose it in their keyboard settings, so this is a real-user break, not only a synthetic-tool one.
- wtype 0.4 (custom keymap, keysyms on low keycodes): `a 033 b 033 c 033 d 033 e 033 f`. Return, Tab, BackSpace, Up and Escape all arrive as ESC. This confirms lm9p.2. On-screen keyboards that upload their own keymaps (e.g. wvkbd) are inferred to behave the same; not run.
- An unrelated observation that did not reproduce: in the first run (before the capture script was fixed), every `m` and one `i` were dropped from a 90-character `wdotool type` command line. Two later runs typed `echo m1 mm2 Mm3 nmn4` correctly. Not pursued.

Venus also matches its own named keys on the physical code, so these break under the remap too: Escape returns focus to the terminal (shortcuts.rs:148), the shortcut viewer handles Escape and the arrows (application.rs:3923), the header handles Tab and Enter (application.rs:1788, :1802), and Arrow keys traverse chrome (shortcuts.rs:155-176).

Ghostty reference (a887df42c56f6de86c0fe6da9c4eeca37931e083, read by a subagent): the GTK apprt maps the XKB keycode through the evdev table, and maps the keyval with gtk key.zig keyFromKeyval. If either result is a non-writing-system key (input/key.zig shouldBeRemappable: everything except letters, digits and punctuation), the keyval-derived key wins (apprt/gtk/class/surface.zig:1361-1381, from PR #9454 "fix xkb mapping not working in Linux"). The doc comment names caps:swapescape. The encoder and bindings then use that key. Letters stay physical, so layout-independent letter shortcuts keep working. Known weak spot: keysyms that keyFromKeyval does not know (e.g. Cyrillic letters from wtype) fall back to the physical key.

Portability: neutral. winit exposes the keymap's logical key on Wayland and macOS alike.

Proposed contract change (step 2; needs Lucca's approval before code). VEN-C2 only. ORB-C5 and ORBS are unchanged: the key field already carries a canonical key, not a promise about which physical key was pressed.
- VEN-C2 Result, add: "Venus resolves each native key event to one key. When the active keymap's key or the physical key is a non-writing-system key (anything other than a letter, digit or punctuation key), and the keymap's key has a canonical Orbit key, Venus uses the keymap's key. Otherwise it uses the physical key. Venus's terminal input and its own named-key actions (focus return, chrome traversal, the shortcut viewer, header activation) use the resolved key."
- VEN-C2 Boundary, add: "Letter, digit and punctuation keys stay physical, so letter shortcuts stay layout-independent, and keymaps that place letters on unrelated keycodes (some virtual keyboards) remain unsupported for chords."
- Evidence to add: a Venus unit test that the resolver maps physical CapsLock with logical Escape to Escape, keeps physical KeyA with logical 'q' (AZERTY) as A, and keeps NumpadEnter as NumpadEnter. Plus one isolated installed observation (this script): swapescape Escape gives 033, wtype Return/Tab/BackSpace/Up give \r, \t, 177 and ESC [ A, and the us baseline is unchanged.
- Implementation shape: one resolver in venus/src/input.rs that maps winit's KeyEvent.logical_key (Key::Named plus location) to a KeyCode, used by InputState::key and the native-shortcut and viewer matching. No Orbit change.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Lucca, 2026-10-21: approved the proposed VEN-C2 Result and Boundary text, evidence and implementation shape as written in the step 1 comment (named keys follow the active keymap, writing-system keys stay physical; Venus-only, no ORB-C5/ORBS change).

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Lucca, 2026-10-21: approved the revised VEN-C2 Result wording to match the implementation: 'When the active keymap produces a named key (such as Escape, Return, Tab, an arrow, a function or modifier key) outside the numpad and Orbit has a key for it, Venus uses that key; otherwise it uses the physical key, so letter, digit, punctuation and numpad keys stay physical.' Why: the earlier wording taken literally would drop numpad identity (NumLock-off 7 -> Home, NumLock-on 1 -> Digit1, breaking Kitty reporting) and needed a character-to-key table for letters on non-writing keys. Boundary text unchanged.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Progress (eon-48, 2026-10-21): implementation in detached worktree /tmp/claude-1000/-home-lucca-pjs-eon-eon/aee87891-bf19-4fb0-a5cc-d862c34c3cd6/scratchpad/wt on edge 9f972e5, candidate tree 1acfa397. Shape: InputState::resolve_key at the top of the KeyboardInput arm (venus/src/application.rs) overwrites event.physical_key with the resolved key; resolved_key/named_key_code apply the approved VEN-C2 rule; pin_key pins each press's resolution per native key (level changes while held), lets every press through, consumes a release while another live key holds the same resolved key, drops repeats of retired pins, marks pins retired only when their key was pressed or captured, and when a press meets a capture held by another key it ends that capture and retires the other key. paste_shortcut matches the resolved Paste key. Checks on 1acfa397: cargo fmt --check, eon-test -p yazelix-venus (101+53+18 pass), clippy -D warnings all green; red/green for each pin behavior. Installed observation on the 7d94c0a build: base, caps:swapescape and wtype all give a 033 b \r c \t d 177 e 033 [ A f, viewer closes on the scenario's Escape, Alt+Shift+T opens a tab under swapescape; red on qr5a1z10 (0.1.1): swapescape drops Escape and the viewer stays open. Review ledger so far: Codex rounds 5, findings 2+2+2+1+1 (pairing, table gaps, retired pins, paste identity, shared presses, retired repeats, capture overlap x2); Claude rounds 7, findings 2 (pairing, proof record), 0, 0, 1 (held-arrow regression), 1 (focus-loss test gap), 0, 0. Out of scope, for Lucca: orbit/docs/PROTOCOL.md:17 still says 'Keys retain physical identity'.

comments.text: Lucca, 2026-10-21: accepted as a recorded gap (recommended), rather than another review cycle: with caps:backspace and a configured Alt+Backspace popup, hold physical Backspace (sent to the terminal), then Alt+CapsLock starts a Backspace capture; if the popup request fails and the attachment stays, one Backspace release never reaches Orbit until the next attachment retirement or native focus loss. Why accepted: needs a remap, a popup on a named key and a failed invoke at once; the Claude reviewer rated it optional. Follow-up bead filed.

title: Split Venus's large source files into cohesive modules
description:
## Decision
Lucca, 2026-10-15: refactor Venus's oversized source files into smaller, cohesive private modules so
humans and agents can navigate and change them cheaply. This is a structure-only change: no
user-visible behavior, contract, wire, dependency or platform change.

## Contract
- Consumer: maintainers and coding agents working in `venus/`.
- Result: each concern has one private module that can be read on its own; `application.rs` keeps
event dispatch, focus and action execution, and `render.rs` keeps GPU rendering. Existing behavior,
public items and tests are unchanged, and tests move with the code they cover.
- Important failures: behavior drift, a second owner for any moved policy, a new framework or trait
hierarchy introduced "for modularity", or lost test coverage.

## Evidence (inspected at edge 068efcb)
- `venus/src/application.rs`: 8,036 lines (production 1-4857, tests 4858-8036). `impl Application`
spans about 1472-3424 and `impl ApplicationHandler` about 3438-4139.
- `venus/src/render.rs`: 5,970 lines (production 1-3785, tests 3786-5970). `impl Renderer` spans
about 736-2768.
- `venus/src/scene.rs` (2,780) and `accessibility.rs` (2,340) are next largest; leave them unless a
slice shows a concrete structural problem.
- `eon-monorepo-2oko` (2026-10-14 Codex discussion, spot-checked by Claude) proposed the first two
slices below; neither has been done.

## Slices (one commit each, in order)
1. Shortcut policy out of `application.rs`: `NativeShortcutAction`/`Trigger`/`NativeShortcut`, the
catalog, matching, platform labels, and help and hint projection (about lines 626-1226) into one
private module. One catalog, no keymap framework. Its existing tests are the oracle.
2. Font resolution and fallback out of `render.rs`: `FontSettings`, `OrderedFallback`, `FontSetup`
(about lines 117-400). Keep one `CellMetrics` owner and the existing shaping.
3. Then reassess with Lucca. Candidates seen, not chosen: terminal scroll and selection autoscroll
(`application.rs` about 79-460), link handling and clipboard (about 554-650 and 1227-1330, 4540-4680),
and cursor-trail geometry in `render.rs` (about 478-680, 3505-3740). Add slices only on evidence that
the split makes the code easier to read and change.

## Owners and boundary
Venus owns all of this. Keep modules private to the crate; keep one protocol validator, model, scene,
draw-input, renderer, accessibility and semantic-action path (`venus/AGENTS.md`). A new Venus module
is product scope under `venus/AGENTS.md`; this bead is Lucca's approval for the modules named in
slices 1 and 2 only. Not consequential under the root `AGENTS.md` (no dependency, protocol, contract,
lifecycle or trust change), so no reference gate.

## Acceptance
- Per slice: no behavior change; the moved tests and the rest of the Venus suite pass unchanged in
the isolated sandbox; `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings`
are green for Venus; `nix build --no-link .#default` builds. No new tests, since no behavior changes.
- Each slice gets the fresh-eyes and simplification review loop; record one ledger line per slice
here.

## Stop boundary
Stop for Lucca if a slice would change behavior, a public item, the wire schema or another owner, or
if the right cut is unclear. No Orbit, Runtime or Eon changes in this bead.
close_reason: All four approved slices landed as pure moves with unchanged tests: shortcuts and scroll out of application.rs (8036 -> 6390 lines), fonts and cursor trail out of render.rs (5970 -> 5350). Link handling and clipboard stay by Lucca's 2026-10-16 decision. Further shrinking impl Application and impl Renderer needs its own design decision.

Kept in application.rs: link_hint_for/link_copy_shortcut (link handling, slice-3 candidate), shortcut_viewer_command, sends_workspace_shortcut, dispatch call sites. Kept in render.rs because other renderer code shares them: CursorPoint and rect_corners (RectangleBatch::push_quad), valid_rect, cursor_bounds and push_cursor (static cursor), cursor_outline and contrast helpers (colour policy). Renderer still owns the one cursor_animation. pub(super): CursorAnimation, reset, is_active, target (read by suspend_cursor_animation), build_tail_cursor, inset_cursor_quad (render.rs tests).
