title: Recreate Venus's renderer after non-destroyed GPU device loss so images resync
description:
## Why

When the GPU device is lost without being destroyed, Venus today treats it as VEN-C4's terminal
renderer failure: the window stops rendering for good. Once Kitty images ship (orb-j2i.11), every
image texture dies with the device too, and VEN-C31's resync (reattach to recover images) can only
run "once the renderer works again", which never happens today. Recreating the renderer after
such a loss lets the window, and its images, recover.

Source: orb-j2i.2, comment 4263 (2026-10-27), "Questions for Lucca", question 1 ("Device loss:
should Venus gain renderer recreation after non-destroyed device loss, so that VEN-C31's resync
can recover images? Recommendation: yes, as its own small bead under VEN-C4, after orb-j2i.11"),
listed as question 2(a) in eon-overseer's morning report of 2026-10-27. Approved by Lucca
2026-10-27 (morning report question 2): "2 yes. yes.". Relayed by eon-overseer.

## Evidence

- venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md:384 VEN-C4 (Bounded explicit failure UX): device loss blocks surface
  recovery; its evidence names `uncaptured_errors_remain_fatal_until_device_loss` and
  `device_loss_blocks_surface_recovery_but_destroy_does_not`.
- venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md:2258-2262 VEN-C31 Resync: "after device loss, once the renderer works
  again ... Today non-destroyed device loss keeps VEN-C4's terminal renderer failure, so this
  applies only to recoveries VEN-C4 allows". :2300: Venus keeps no CPU copy of an uploaded image,
  so recovery reattaches instead of re-uploading.
- venus/src/render.rs:848, :966-975: the `device_lost` flag set by
  `device.set_device_lost_callback`; :993-995 `ensure_device_available` fails rendering after it.
- Earlier work: ven-distinguish-device-from-surface-loss-d96 and
  ven-expose-persistent-renderer-failures-4xj (closed).

## Contract

VEN-C4 (owner of renderer lifecycle and failure UX) and VEN-C31 (its Resync clause and "Today
..." sentence). Both texts change: each contract-text change in this bead needs Lucca's approval
per AGENTS.md. Draft the exact VEN-C4 and VEN-C31 wording, stop, and bring it to him before
editing venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md; the change also takes AGENTS.md's Codex review. Changing the
renderer lifecycle is a consequential code shape (AP-REFERENCE-001): record the reference gate
(venus/docs/REFERENCES.md routes, a comparable wgpu device-loss recovery, rejected approaches)
on this bead before coding.

## Prerequisites

- orb-j2i.11 (Venus uploads and draws images under a GPU budget) lands first (blocks dependency),
  so recovery can be proved with images.

## Scope

In scope:
- Venus renderer lifecycle: on non-destroyed device loss, drop the renderer, request a new
  adapter and device, rebuild pipelines and surfaces, and resync every attached terminal by
  reattach (VEN-C31), with a bounded retry and VEN-C4's notice while it recovers.
- A destroyed device, and recreation that keeps failing, stay VEN-C4's terminal failure.

Out of scope:
- Orbit, the ORBS/ORBF wire, and Eon Runtime.
- Keeping CPU copies of images (VEN-C31 rejects it).
- Surface-loss handling that already recovers.

## Acceptance

- Lucca has approved the VEN-C4 and VEN-C31 wording; the approval is quoted here.
- A Venus test drives a simulated non-destroyed device loss and shows the renderer recreated and
  terminals resynced; it fails on today's code. The existing VEN-C4 tests are updated to the new
  rule, not deleted.
- If a real device loss can be forced (for example a GPU reset or wgpu's test hooks), one
  isolated observation shows a window with a Yazi image preview recovering; otherwise record the
  gap with its reason.

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-venus` passes.
- `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --locked -p yazelix-venus --all-targets -- -D warnings`
  clean.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop before editing VEN-C text until Lucca approves.
- Stop if recovery needs a wire or Orbit change.

## Maintenance Notes

Portability disposition: neutral (wgpu device-loss callback and adapter request on every
backend; macOS Metal recovery stays unproved until the Apple Silicon work resumes).

title: Cache Venus's shaped text per row and translate it when scrolling
description:
## Why

Scrolling a dense grid re-shapes every visible cell on every frame, because `scroll_offset` is in
Venus's full-rebuild key and every rebuild builds a fresh cosmic-text `Buffer` per cell. Caching
prepared text per terminal row and translating it by the scroll offset should make a scroll frame
cost a translation plus the rows that newly enter the viewport, not a whole-window reshape. This
bead builds that cache, only if the baseline bead that blocks it shows a material cost and
supports a cache shape.

Source: Venus GPU audit, eon-overseer, 2026-10-27
(`/home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-overseer/gpu-audit-2026-10-27.md`). Lines below re-checked on
edge `4e705bc`; re-locate them before starting.

## Evidence

- `venus/src/render.rs:216-235` `ContentKey`, with `scroll_offset` at `:220`.
- `venus/src/render.rs:1382-1698` `rebuild_if_needed`; `build_scene_text` at `:1927`,
  `build_preview_text` beside it (`:1586`, `:1642` call sites), `push_cell_text` at `:2187-2254`.
- `venus/src/render.rs:1255-1282`: glyphon `prepare_with_custom` over `text_areas(...)`.
- `venus/src/render.rs:1242-1246`: the dynamic cursor layer is rebuilt only at `scroll_offset ==
  0.0`; scrolling resets the cursor animation.
- The baseline, attribution and chosen cache shape: recorded on the blocking baseline bead.

## Owner and invariants

- Owner: the Venus renderer (`venus/src/render.rs` and its `venus/src/render/` modules). Orbit,
  Eon Runtime and the wire protocols are untouched; Venus still materializes only the Orbit
  frame it has (`venus/AGENTS.md` Boundary).
- Identical rendered output: for the same Scene, scroll offset, preview and window state, the
  cached path draws exactly what the full rebuild draws. Checked by a comparison of the renderer's
  text and rectangle inputs (cached vs uncached) in unit tests, and by pixel-identical captures of
  the installed build against the pre-change build at fixed scroll positions.
- Invalidation: a cached row is reused only while its content, style, selection, hyperlink hover,
  blink phase (for blinking cells), column width, font metrics, scale and clip are unchanged.
  Font, scale or geometry changes drop the cache. Memory stays bounded by the rows visible plus a
  stated margin.

## Contract

Expected none: this keeps VEN-C1 (presentation), VEN-C7 (history and kinetic scroll) and VEN-C19
(typography) behaviour as written. If the change needs any VEN-C* text change, stop and ask Lucca
with the proposed text.

## Prerequisites

- The baseline/spike bead that blocks this one is closed with a "go" and a cache shape.
- `orb-j2i.11` has landed or is rebased onto (both touch `venus/src/render.rs`).
- The blink bead (linked as related) is independent; whichever lands second rebases onto the other's
  `ContentKey` change.

## Scope

In scope:
- A per-row cache of prepared text (shaped buffers and their glyphon text areas) in the Venus
  renderer, reused across frames and translated by the scroll offset; only rows that change or
  enter the viewport are shaped.
- Taking `scroll_offset` out of the full-rebuild trigger for terminal text, in the shape the
  baseline bead chose.
- Focused unit tests for reuse and invalidation in the existing Venus test modules.

Out of scope:
- Blink handling (its own bead), adapter choice, image upload.
- Chrome text (Eon Bar, headers, popups) unless the baseline shows it matters.
- SDF/instanced shaders, sRGB in the vertex shader, `wl_surface` damage or incremental present
  (not pursued, Lucca 2026-10-27).
- Any configuration value. If a size or margin needs to be user-visible, stop and ask (AGENTS.md
  Configurability); otherwise record why it stays fixed (performance budget).

## Acceptance

- On the baseline bead's exact workload and environment, the frame-gap and rebuild-time
  distributions beat the recorded baseline, with the before/after numbers and revisions recorded
  here (AP-PERF-001).
- Cached and uncached renderer inputs are identical in the new tests; installed captures at fixed
  scroll positions are pixel-identical to the pre-change build.
- Kinetic scroll, preview rows, selection and hyperlink hover behave as before in one isolated
  installed observation.

## Implementation Notes

1. Re-read the baseline bead's attribution and chosen cache shape; re-locate the cited lines.
2. Add the row cache and its key; translate cached rows by the offset; shape only new or changed
   rows.
3. Add reuse and invalidation tests; compare cached vs full-rebuild inputs.
4. Re-run the baseline reproducer; record the after numbers.

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-venus` exits 0.
- `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings` for `yazelix-venus`.
- Refresh the `eon` profile from the tree and record one isolated installed observation
  (AGENTS.md Local Runtime Synchronization; do not restart a live supervisor).

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if the baseline bead closed no-go.
- Stop if the cited code has drifted materially.
- Stop if identical output cannot be kept (for example shaping that depends on neighbouring rows);
  report the case instead of accepting a visual change.
- Stop if verification fails twice for the same reason after a reasonable fix attempt.

## Review

Code change: converge rounds plus the Codex round (AGENTS.md "Codex on every code change"), with
the ledger line on this bead.

## Approval

Lucca, 2026-10-27, relayed by eon-overseer. Asked: "1. Cache prepared text per row, and move it
instead of re-preparing it when scrolling; first record a baseline (scroll frame time, idle CPU
with a blinking cursor), as AP-PERF-001 requires. 2. Stop cursor blink from re-preparing the whole
window; measure first too. 3. Choose the GPU on purpose: prefer the low-power one, log which one
Venus picked, and slow the cursor-trail animation when there's no GPU. 4. Move the image upload
wait off Venus's main thread, a small follow-up after orb-j2i.11 lands. Should I file 1–4 as beads,
with 1 and 2 each starting from a recorded baseline?" Lucca: "go ahead".

The approval is to file this bead. Any VEN-C* contract text change or new configuration value it
needs still needs Lucca's approval during implementation: stop and ask with the proposed text.

title: Record a Venus scroll and text-rebuild baseline and spike a per-row shaped-text cache
description:
## Why

Every change to Venus's content key reshapes every visible non-blank cell, and scrolling puts
`scroll_offset` in that key, so kinetic or wheel scrolling reruns the whole text rebuild on every
frame. Nobody has measured what that costs: no scroll frame time, rebuild time per frame or idle
blink cost is recorded anywhere. AP-PERF-001 requires a fixed workload, a baseline and a measured
attribution before redesigning for speed. This bead records that baseline and decides whether the
per-row cache (the implementation bead this one blocks) is worth building, and in what shape.

Source: Venus GPU audit, eon-overseer, 2026-10-27
(`/home/lucca/.cache/eon-agents/eon-overseer/gpu-audit-2026-10-27.md`). Lines below re-checked on
edge `4e705bc`.

## Evidence

- `venus/src/render.rs:216-235`: `ContentKey` holds `scroll_offset` (`:220`) and `blink_visible`
  (`:222`) beside the column revisions; any change rebuilds.
- `venus/src/render.rs:1382-1698` `rebuild_if_needed`: key built at `:1396-1415`; on a change it
  calls `build_scene_text` per column (`:1554`, `:1585-1586`, `:1641-1642`), uploads all vertices
  and re-prepares images (`:1690-1695`).
- `venus/src/render.rs:1927` `build_scene_text` and `:2187-2254` `push_cell_text`: one new
  cosmic-text `Buffer` per visible cell and layer, shaped each time; no shape cache.
- `venus/src/render.rs:1255-1282`: glyphon `prepare_with_custom` over every text area each
  rebuild.
- `venus/docs/REFERENCES.md:630-655` (kinetic scrolling): `request_redraw` with
  `pre_present_notify` paces frames; FIFO with frame latency two "until installed measurements
  justify a change" (`:644-647`).
- Prior measurement: `eon-investigate-anima-performance-vs-nova-g92d` found 70.31% of CPU in
  cosmic-text font fallback via `build_scene_text`/`push_text`, fixed for half-blocks (`bac1d8d`,
  `ven-render-anima-half-blocks-k2c`) and font order (`eon-accelerando-font-order-performance-qc6a`).
  `venus/docs/benchmarks/venus-memory-2026-09-08.md` is the prior Venus benchmark record.

## Contract

Touches no contract: this is measurement. VEN-C1 (authoritative presentation), VEN-C7 (history and
kinetic scroll) and VEN-C19 (typography) must stay unchanged by anything it recommends.

## Prerequisites

- None to measure. `orb-j2i.11` is changing `venus/src/render.rs`; the measurement can run on the
  installed or edge build now, but note the exact revision.
- Read `AP-PERF-001` (`docs/AGENT-PROTOCOLS.md`), `venus/AGENTS.md`, VEN-C1 and VEN-C7.

## Scope

In scope:
- A fixed, reproducible workload: an isolated headless Sway (pixman/lavapipe and Vulkan on the
  Intel GPU, `renderD129`), a fixed window size (for example 2560x1440 and 1280x720), four columns
  of dense text with colors and some wide/CJK and Nerd Font glyphs (record the exact generator,
  for example a fixed file `cat` into each pane), scrolled through retained history by a recorded
  input driver (synthetic wheel steps, and a touchpad-style pixel stream if one can be driven).
- Measurements, each with a distribution (median, p95, max) over repeated runs: frame-to-frame
  gap while scrolling; wall time of `rebuild_if_needed` and of the glyphon prepare per frame;
  Venus CPU ticks over a fixed scroll; and a `perf record -g` attribution of where the rebuild
  time goes (cosmic-text shaping, font fallback, glyphon prepare, vertex upload).
- A temporary, uncommitted timing probe is fine for this; keep the reproducer script and raw
  numbers under `~/.cache/eon-agents/<session>/` and record their paths.
- A short spike, if the numbers warrant it, that prototypes the cheapest cache shape (shaped
  `Buffer` per row keyed by the row's content and style, reused across frames and translated by
  the scroll offset) far enough to measure its effect on the same workload. Spike code is not
  committed.

Out of scope:
- Committed renderer changes (the implementation bead owns them).
- Blink (its own bead, linked as related), GPU adapter choice, image upload.
- SDF/instanced shape shaders, sRGB in the vertex shader, `wl_surface` damage or incremental
  present: Lucca chose not to pursue these (2026-10-27).

## Acceptance

- The bead records: the workload (exact generator, sizes, columns, input driver), the environment
  (repository revision, installed or built store path, Sway renderer, adapter, CPU, governor if
  known), the baseline distributions above, the `perf` attribution, and a go/no-go.
- Go: a material cost (state the threshold used, for example rebuild time that misses the 16.7 ms
  frame budget or a large CPU share on Intel) plus the cache shape the spike supports, its
  invalidation rules and its expected gain. The implementation bead's scope is updated to match.
- No-go: the baseline shows no material cost on either adapter. Record the negative result here
  (AP-PERF-001 keeps it), and stop and report to Lucca before closing the implementation bead.

## Verification

- Re-running the recorded reproducer on the same revision reproduces the baseline within the
  recorded spread.
- No tracked file changes (`git status` clean apart from bead state).

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if the cited code has drifted materially (re-locate after `orb-j2i.11` lands).
- Stop and report if the baseline shows no material cost.
- Stop if measuring needs a committed harness: the Testing Discipline rule forbids bespoke
  scaffolding; keep the reproducer outside the repository and report the gap.

## Review

Planning and measurement only: Review loop on the bead record. No Codex round unless code or a
contract changes. Ledger line on this bead.

## Approval

Lucca, 2026-10-27, relayed by eon-overseer. Asked: "1. Cache prepared text per row, and move it
instead of re-preparing it when scrolling; first record a baseline (scroll frame time, idle CPU
with a blinking cursor), as AP-PERF-001 requires. 2. Stop cursor blink from re-preparing the whole
window; measure first too. 3. Choose the GPU on purpose: prefer the low-power one, log which one
Venus picked, and slow the cursor-trail animation when there's no GPU. 4. Move the image upload
wait off Venus's main thread, a small follow-up after orb-j2i.11 lands. Should I file 1–4 as beads,
with 1 and 2 each starting from a recorded baseline?" Lucca: "go ahead".

The approval is to file this bead. Any VEN-C* contract text change or new configuration value it
needs still needs Lucca's approval during implementation: stop and ask with the proposed text.

title: Version Eon by number: 0.x is beta, 1.0.0 leaves beta
description:
## Decision
Lucca, 2026-10-16: drop the alpha/beta stage words in favour of version numbers. Every 0.x release
is beta; 1.0.0 means out of beta. Installing without Nix is a delivery milestone inside 0.x, not a
stage. Releases are tagged `vX.Y.Z` after bumping Eon's product version; date tags stop.

## Contract
- Product text calls Eon beta and names the 0.x/1.0.0 meaning; no document presents "alpha" as the
current stage or "public beta" as the Nix-free milestone.
- Eon's product version in `eon/crates/eon/Cargo.toml` is the one user-facing number. Orbit, Venus,
Eon Runtime and EONW keep their own package versions as compatibility identities.
- Platform and channel claims are unchanged: Nix-only, x86_64 Linux on native Wayland.
- `linux-alpha-2026-10-14` was version 0.1.0; the next release is `v0.1.1`.

## Scope
Docs, agent overlay and planning wording, plus retitling `eon-qualify-nix-free-linux-public-beta-lm9p`
and reframing `eon-next-expansion-0wfb`. The manifest file and its `eon-alpha` graph ID keep their
names until the next graph version, because renaming them changes the component report that live
generations compare. The `v0.1.1` version bump, tag and profile refresh are a separate release step.

## Acceptance
No product or policy text uses alpha or public beta as a stage; rendered `AGENTS.md` passes
`starcompass check-consumer`; changed Markdown paths and diff reviewed.
close_reason: Versioning policy and wording applied; v0.1.1 release is a separate step

title: Control Eon workspaces by voice
description:
## Contract
A user can control Eon with spoken commands: open a window, create a tab or pane, and navigate tabs/panes without using physical shortcuts. Provide a discoverable, bounded command vocabulary, an explicit listening state, and pause/cancel. Unrecognized or ambiguous speech produces visible feedback without acting. Closing work or stopping terminals requires explicit confirmation tied to the intended target.

## Prerequisites and reference gate
Choose and verify a voice-input provider on Eon’s supported Linux Wayland environment, including microphone permissions, activation, recognition quality, resource use, licensing and any external-service/data requirements. Compare an existing desktop voice-control tool with a local speech-recognition component before considering owned recognition code. Read their current primary documentation and inspect a comparable command-mapping integration. Inspect EON-C8, EON-C10, EON-C18 and EON-C20 and the actual Eon CLI/EONW/native-action surfaces before selecting mappings. Record exact references, decisions and limits; no recognition engine or cloud service is selected by this bead.

## Ownership and implementation boundary
Keep audio capture and recognition with the selected provider. Eon owns the product command vocabulary, activation/configuration and installed integration; Eon Runtime owns existing typed workspace actions and target validation; Venus owns native interaction, focus and feedback. Prefer a thin integration with existing controls. Resolve the intended window/tab/pane explicitly and revalidate it before execution so delayed recognition cannot affect a different workspace. Do not parse screen text or treat recognized speech as arbitrary shell code. Decide terminal dictation separately from command recognition before adding a text-input path; it must not implicitly execute commands.

## Acceptance
1. Document the chosen input system, platform, activation method, vocabulary and data handling. Listening is opt-in, visibly indicated, and can be paused or cancelled.
2. In an installed Eon, actual microphone speech opens a window, creates a tab/pane and navigates them; record exact component/provider revisions and the observed environment. Synthetic transcripts alone do not prove voice usability.
3. Ambiguous speech, silence, unavailable recognition, cancellation and stale/missing targets cause no unintended action. Duplicate recognition does not repeat a non-idempotent command. Confirmed close/stop affects only the identified work.
4. Ordinary keyboard/pointer input and live terminals remain usable when voice control is off or fails. Add the smallest checks for any new mapping/dispatch logic and one installed end-to-end voice workflow.
5. Document setup, supported commands and known recognition limits. Use existing dependencies and action owners where sufficient; no generic voice assistant, autonomous command execution, new platform promise or unrelated input framework.

## Scope
One voice-control integration for core Eon workspace actions. Independent of Neuralink support; no dependency on that bead. Implementation remains unclaimed until this work is selected.

title: Build Eon's public website
description:
Goal and observable contract
A visitor evaluating Eon can understand what it does, see the real product, learn its current availability and limitations, and reach the canonical documentation, source, and supported installation instructions. Deliver a focused public product website with a coherent Eon visual identity and a clear path from discovery to trying the product.

Initial scope
Explain the terminal workspace and durable work across window close/reconnect using concise copy and real screenshots or a short demo of accepted behavior. Describe Eon and EonTerm accurately where relevant. Keep platform, installation, release-status, and durability claims aligned with the current README and proven contracts; distinguish planned capabilities from supported ones. Start with the smallest useful landing/onboarding surface rather than a general content platform.

Ownership and prerequisites
Eon owns website content and composition. README, docs/CONTRACTS.md, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, and distribution documentation remain the authorities for product behavior and installation. The user purchased eonterm.com and selected it as the website domain (2026-10-12, America/Sao_Paulo). The selected approach is a neutral Yazelix/site-starter repository extracted from Nova's website, then a separate Yazelix/eon-site seeded from that template. Reuse Nova's Astro static-site foundation and Bun/Node development tooling, with TypeScript limited to website components, configuration, and checks. This website toolchain remains separate from Rust-owned Eon runtime and repository policy. Hosting remains undecided. Website work does not activate public beta, distribution graduation, or unsupported platforms. Publishing requires an explicitly chosen destination and authorization.

Starter extraction decision
The user accepted this approach after source inspection of /home/lucca/pjs/yazelix-dir/nova-site at 5917e42b31db6c746c82a3295ada69a9448d31bc (clean working tree). Inspected README.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, Astro configuration, components, styles, browser tests, and the Nix development shell. This is source evidence only; the extracted starter and Eon site have not been built or browser-verified.

- Extract the static build/development setup, responsive shell and navigation, metadata/canonical URL handling, accessible media components, and applicable browser checks. Retain Starlight docs/search only if the initial Eon site consumes it.
- Keep customization small: site identity, navigation, metadata, and CSS tokens. Preserve direct Astro composition rather than adding a generator, plugin framework, or generic page-schema system.
- Replace hardcoded Nova identity, repository links, social imagery, and content assertions with neutral examples or explicit site inputs. Keep Nova release claims, articles, compatibility redirects, product pins, screenshots, and recording recipes out of the generic starter. The base development shell must not require Nova's recording machinery.
- Eon owns its copy, visual identity, screenshots, installation guidance, product evidence, and deployment configuration. Do not transfer Nova's website-owned canonical-guidance policy into Eon; Eon's existing canonical documents remain authoritative.
- Use a starter template rather than a shared runtime package. Generated sites evolve independently, and later template fixes do not propagate automatically. Reconsider a shared component package only after repeated maintenance across real sites demonstrates a common owner is worthwhile.
- Prove the extracted starter by using it to seed Eon's site. Do not migrate or refactor Nova as part of this issue. Establish appropriate source/asset licensing for the extracted repository before redistribution.

Reference gate
Before design or code shape, read the current canonical product and distribution docs and the relevant docs/REFERENCES.md routes. Inspect primary sources and at least one comparable product website for product explanation, onboarding, accessibility, and visual hierarchy; record inspected identities/dates, adopted mechanisms, rejected alternatives, and the simplest sufficient build/hosting option in this bead. Consider eon-yvw (the deferred public interactive explainer) as optional related work; do not make it a prerequisite or reactivate it. Preserve source-license boundaries and avoid copying branding or unapproved source.

Acceptance
- A neutral starter builds independently, and Eon's site can be seeded from it without Nova-specific content, product dependencies, or recording tools. Preserve applicable accessibility, navigation, metadata, and overflow behavior in browser verification of the generated Eon site.
- Visitors can identify Eon's purpose and main benefit, inspect real product imagery, and find documentation, source, and the current supported installation path.
- Claims and examples match accepted product behavior and current platform/release status; website links point to canonical installation and release authorities rather than creating a second distribution graph.
- The site works at desktop and narrow mobile widths, with semantic structure, keyboard navigation, visible focus, readable contrast, and reduced-motion behavior if motion is used.
- Verify the built site in a real browser at both widths and exercise navigation and installation links. Record the revision, environment, and observations; document how to reproduce the chosen build and deployment.

title: Protect EON-C15 recovery failure paths
description:
## Contract Routing

This hardens EON-C15 same-boot recovery proof without changing recovery policy or workspace projection.

Consumer: a replacement Eon or EonTerm supervisor targeting the same exact generation.

Trigger: recovery enumerates retained live or tombstone management records after supervisor loss.

Result: Eon either acquires the complete bounded, valid Session set and publishes it once, or fails closed without partial topology, duplicate launch, unsafe cleanup, or alternate process authority. Matching tombstones are reconciled before reuse.

## Why

The 2026-08-28 audit found `recover_sessions` at cyclomatic complexity 37, cognitive complexity 24, 62.61% coverage, and CRAP 108.57. Unlike exhaustive codecs, this is genuine multi-stage lifecycle complexity. Current integration coverage proves successful adoption and stale initial-picker handling, but important rejection and tombstone branches remain unexecuted. Strong failure-path proof should precede any structural refactor.

Impact HIGH, effort M, implementation risk MEDIUM, confidence HIGH.

## Evidence

- `crates/eon/src/sessions.rs:607`: `recover_sessions` owns bounded record enumeration, ordering, live/tombstone validation, dead residue cleanup, duplicate rejection, picker cleanup, and lease acquisition.
- `crates/eon/src/sessions.rs:632`: the record-count limit failure is uncovered.
- `crates/eon/src/sessions.rs:653`: retained tombstone reconciliation and endpoint-object checks are uncovered.
- `crates/eon/src/sessions.rs:684`: wrong presentation identity path rejection is uncovered.
- `crates/eon/src/sessions.rs:708`: duplicate numeric Session, duplicate picker, and EonTerm cardinality rejection branches are uncovered.
- `crates/eon/tests/workspace_control.rs:2035`: replacement with only a stale initial picker proves the successful cleanup/fallback path.
- `crates/eon/tests/workspace_control.rs:2103`: replacement adopts exact live runs and rejects selected corrupt record identity, but does not cover the remaining equivalence classes.
- `docs/CONTRACTS.md:508`: EON-C15 requires bounded enumeration, exact identity, no partial workspace, no duplicate run, and tombstone reconciliation.

## Scope

In scope:
- Recovery-focused tests in `crates/eon/tests/workspace_control.rs` and, only when cheaper and behaviorally equivalent, focused tests beside `crates/eon/src/sessions.rs`.
- A few data-driven cases covering the distinct uncovered recovery failure classes.
- Existing test process/record helpers.
- Before/after cargo-crap evidence for `recover_sessions`.

Out of scope:
- Mechanical decomposition of `recover_sessions`, new recovery behavior, topology persistence, machine-restart recovery, PID/signal fallback, dependencies, mock frameworks, arbitrary coverage targets, or CI thresholds.
- A separate test for every source line or error string.
- Orbit or Venus source changes.

## Implementation Notes

1. Re-read EON-C15, the complete recovery and tombstone flows, and existing recovery integration helpers at the implementation revision.
2. Partition failures by distinct authority/invariant, not by branch count. Prefer one table-driven rejection test plus one tombstone lifecycle test.
3. Prove at minimum: bounded record count; wrong record/endpoint identity path; EonTerm's one-live-Session bound; and tombstone cleanup that waits for both exact endpoints and refuses replaced objects. Record why duplicate numeric and picker identities are unreachable after canonical path validation instead of fabricating fixtures.
4. Assert the outer contract: no partial control socket/workspace publication, no duplicate Orbit launch, and no deletion of an unowned replacement artifact.
5. Reuse current record and managed-Orbit helpers. Add production seams only if a case is otherwise impossible to exercise and the seam reduces ownership; stop before refactoring for the metric.
6. Rerun identical coverage-aware diagnostics and record remaining uncovered equivalence classes without making a global threshold.

## Verification

- `cargo test --locked -p eon --test workspace_control` should exit 0 and prove successful adoption plus the added adversarial recovery cases.
- `cargo test --locked -p eon` should exit 0.
- `cargo clippy --locked -p eon --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` should exit 0.
- `cargo llvm-cov --workspace --all-features --lcov --output-path /tmp/eon-quality.lcov` should exit 0.
- `cargo-crap --workspace --lcov /tmp/eon-quality.lcov --format json --output /tmp/eon-crap.json` with cargo-crap 0.4.3 should show that `recover_sessions` exercises the newly selected failure classes without source/LCOV mismatch diagnostics.
- `git diff --check` should exit 0.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if a proposed test needs weaker identity, ownership, deadline, endpoint, or cleanup validation.
- Stop before changing EON-C15 behavior, Orbit authority, wire contracts, runtime limits, or workspace projection.
- Stop before a filesystem/mock abstraction or dependency.
- If a test exposes a production defect, record the exact failing contract and obtain scope for the fix rather than hiding it in coverage work.

## Maintenance Notes

Do not chase a numeric score by splitting one lifecycle owner into helpers. After these failure classes are protected, reassess cognitive complexity from the new evidence and create no follow-up unless a concrete owner boundary emerges.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A few strong, preferably data-driven tests cover the bounded record limit, wrong record/endpoint identity path, EonTerm's one-live-Session bound, and retained tombstone reconciliation; the unreachable duplicate identity guards are justified from canonical path invariants instead of fabricated fixtures.
- Adversarial cases prove no partial workspace/control publication, no duplicate Orbit launch, and no deletion of a replacement or otherwise unowned endpoint/record.
- Existing successful live-run adoption and stale initial-picker recovery remain green.
- Production recovery policy and EON-C15 remain unchanged; if a real defect appears, the failing contract is recorded and implementation stops for explicit scope.
- Focused eon integration tests, package tests, Clippy, and the repeated cargo-crap 0.4.3 observation pass without a new dependency, mock layer, threshold, or mechanical recovery refactor.
close_reason: EON-C15 recovery rejection and exact tombstone lifecycle proof is complete; all selected outer contracts pass without production changes.

title: Show each window's agent attention in the window list and picker
description:
## Why

eon-n77e: Rex marks sessions with completed or blocked tasks in its picker. herdr rolls agent state up per workspace, and tuios lists the agents that need a human. EON-C31 already derives attention per window in the runtime (commit e87b9f8), but nothing shows another window's attention.

## Contract (proposed; bring the exact EON-C31 and EON-C23 wording to Lucca before code)

`eon windows --json` and the window picker show each window's attention rollup: its most urgent normalized EON-C31 state, such as needs input, error or finished. The picker sorts windows that need input first. Showing attention never marks it seen; seen still needs an attached Venus and focus on that exact terminal (EON-C31). Showing it never moves focus.

## Prerequisites

- The window picker bead.
- eon-agent-sidebar-yx8.7, which puts attention on EONW.

## Scope

In scope: the rollup in the listing and the picker, the sort, contract and USAGE text.

Out of scope: notifications, sidebar changes, attention for the default workspace beyond what the listing exposes.

## Acceptance

A detached window whose agent asks for input shows "needs input" in `eon windows` and at the top of the picker. Viewing the picker does not clear the raise.

## Verification

Focused runtime tests plus one installed observation. Codex on every code change.

title: Keep slow workspace actions from showing Eon as unavailable
description:
## Defect
Once, right after `eon attach`, opening the Project popup (Alt+Z) over a multi-column tab showed "Cannot read Eon workspace response header: Resource temporarily unavailable (os error 11)" in the status line; pane headers fell back to "unavailable" and the popup did not render. The next 250 ms poll recovered, and a repeat opened normally. Seen in the `eon-splits-opwv` slice 4 isolated dogfood (2026-10-17) on installed /nix/store/86755wd8yc9b63j6lwvic6grpslyg6kk-eon-0.1.1, private headless Sway 1.12.

Evidence: `venus/src/transport.rs` `workspace_exchange` connects per request and sets a fixed 2 s read and write timeout; EAGAIN is what a receive timeout returns, so the supervisor most likely took over 2 s to answer InvokePopup while starting the picker terminal. The transport and popup-start paths predate the splits work.

## Contract
A slow but successful supervisor action must not surface as workspace loss: Venus shows no "unavailable" state or failure notice for an action Eon is still completing, and a genuinely unresponsive supervisor still fails within a bound (VEN-C3 transient client recovery, VEN-C4 bounded failure UX, EON-C8 workspace actions). The fix belongs to one owner: Venus's workspace transport bound, or the supervisor's action latency (for example, answering before slow terminal start completes). Decide from measurements.

## Prerequisites
None. First measure InvokePopup and CreateTab latency at the supervisor in an isolated session, cold and warm, and record the distribution.

## Acceptance
- Measured latency with environment and a stated bound, plus the chosen owner and mechanism recorded here.
- A deterministic check where the owner's harness allows it (for example, a fake slow supervisor in the Venus transport tests), plus one isolated installed observation that opening a popup right after attach shows no unavailable state.

## Scope boundary
Workspace action latency and its failure presentation only. No EONW wire change, retry framework, or second state owner; an EONW change needs a user decision.
close_reason: Venus waits Eon's five-second terminal-start deadline plus one second, like Eon's control clients, so a slow single terminal start no longer reads as workspace loss; queued and stop-then-start cases remain bounded at 6 s. Measurements, red/green, installed observation and 3-pass ledger in comments.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Measurement (2026-10-17, installed /nix/store/ivv9a03r11f5r8zkag88f2fnd11z04jd-eon-0.1.1, private headless Sway 1.12, isolated HOME and runtime root, eon CLI against the live supervisor, wall time per call). Quiet machine (load ~7): workspace inspect 23-48 ms; pane create 49-59 ms (5); tab create 54-59 ms (6). Busy machine (load ~19-26, other sessions' nix builds): pane create 65-645 ms; tab create 56-443 ms, and one tab create ran 5,040 ms and failed (the supervisor's five-second terminal-start deadline, SESSION_START_TIMEOUT). Owner and mechanism: actions that start a terminal answer after Orbit Ready, bounded by the supervisor's shared five-second start deadline; Eon's own control clients wait CONTROL_TIMEOUT = start deadline + 1 s, but Venus's workspace_exchange cut every exchange at 2 s, so a start between 2 and 5 s surfaced as 'Cannot read Eon workspace response header: Resource temporarily unavailable (os error 11)'. Chosen: Venus's workspace exchange bound becomes 6 s (the shared five-second deadline plus one second, matching Eon's control clients); the supervisor keeps sole ownership of the start deadline and still reports a start failure itself. Rejected: answering before Ready (a pending-terminal lifecycle and likely EONW change, out of scope); retries (would repeat non-idempotent actions). Red/green: transport::tests::slow_successful_workspace_action_is_not_reported_as_loss (fake supervisor answers after 2.5 s) fails with the dogfood's exact error under the 2 s bound and passes under 6 s.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Review pass 1 (Codex gpt-6.1-sol read-only + Claude). Codex: 6 s does not cover every slow success; the supervisor serves clients serially and each terminal start gets its own five-second deadline, so a popup queued behind another slow action, or a stop-then-start action (popup replacement; pane or column creation that first dismisses a popup), can exceed it (accepted narrowing, decided by the main session under Lucca's delegation: the guarantee is one slow terminal start within the shared deadline, the same rule Eon's control clients use; a complete guarantee needs an unbounded wait or a supervisor progress protocol, out of scope; comment and changelog now say so). Both: InvokePopup cold/warm not measured separately (answered: eon tab create starts the Project picker popup terminal, the same start InvokePopup performs; the first call after launch is the cold case, 56 ms quiet and 56 ms busy, later calls 54-443 ms) and the installed popup-after-attach observation is pending. Claude: nothing blocking; comment and changelog overstated (fixed, text). Accepted costs: a genuinely silent supervisor is reported after 6 s instead of 2 s, and the single workspace worker holds polls and queued workspace actions for that long; terminal input and rendering use separate Orbit transports. Retained risk: the bound is a socket inactivity timeout, not an absolute exchange deadline, and blocking connect stays outside it (unchanged).

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Proof (x86_64 Linux, nix develop): transport::tests::slow_successful_workspace_action_is_not_reported_as_loss red under the old 2 s bound with the dogfood's exact 'Resource temporarily unavailable (os error 11)' error, green under 6 s; eon-test -p yazelix-venus lib 91 / 1 ignored, bin 51 / 4 ignored, canonical_scene 18; cargo fmt --check and cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -D warnings green for yazelix-venus; nix build --no-link .#default -> /nix/store/663kjij0bdmzpvcc1z5i5dgiqrqgf23h-eon-0.1.1 (tree before the last changelog wording fix). Installed observation on that artifact (private headless Sway 1.12, isolated HOME and runtime root, wdotool prime): three columns, window killed (detach), eon attach, Alt+Z pressed 1 s after attach; screenshots at 0, 2 and 5 s show the Project popup over the tab with no unavailable notice and live pane headers; eon workspace lists popup u2 (directory-picker-2) chosen. Review ledger: 3 passes (pass 1 Codex gpt-6.1-sol read-only + Claude; passes 2-3 Codex). Pass 1: guarantee narrowed (see the pass 1 comment); comment and changelog overstated (fixed, text). Pass 2: changelog omitted the queued and stop-then-start exceptions (fixed, text). Pass 3: nothing blocking; nits left: the changelog's 'waits up to six seconds' is a per-I/O socket timeout, not a total deadline; the test can miss the old cutoff if the client stalls more than 500 ms before reading.

title: Define a declarative workspace profile over Eon actions
description:
## Origin
Split from closed `eon-pxn` on 2026-10-16 (its configuration boundary and acceptance item 15).

## Contract (provisional)
A user can describe a workspace (tabs, launch directories, panes, keybindings and named action
sequences) in one versioned Eon-owned file and apply it. Applying routes through the same action
owner as the CLI; failures are deterministic and leave the prior workspace intact. Ratconfig may edit
the file but does not own its meaning.

## Relation
Distinct from `eon-reboot-restore-im8y`, which restores saved state; settle whether they share a
format when either activates.

## Prerequisites and reference gate
Consequential (new schema and contract). Depends on a settled action surface
(`eon-cli-action-discovery-ogzi`). Stop for Lucca's schema and contract approval before code.

## Acceptance
Focused tests apply a valid profile and reject invalid ones without touching live state; one
installed observation applies a two-tab profile.

## Stop boundary
No loops, variables, callbacks, arbitrary code, widget trees, raw child-protocol access or ambient
environment capture.

title: Fix shn4.9's leftovers: EON-C10's EONW v20 note, Quit counting the Commands popup, and EON-C31's proof pointer
description:
## Why

The installed proof of workspace switching found three small out-of-scope problems: a stale
protocol version in EON-C10, a Quit prompt that counts a terminal the person does not think of as
theirs, and a missing proof pointer in EON-C31.

Source: eon-workspace-switching-shn4.9, comment 4351 (2026-10-27), "Out of scope, reported to
the coordinator, no bead filed", items 1, 3 and 4 (the morning report's (a), (c) and (d)).
Approved by Lucca 2026-10-27 (morning report question 11): "11 ok", accepting the recommendation
"one small follow-up bead for (a), (c) and (d)". Relayed by eon-overseer. Item 2, (b), is filed
separately under eon-agent-parity-a9g0.

## Evidence

- (a) docs/CONTRACTS.md:899-903, EON-C10's nested "Several workspaces in one window (EON-C33)"
  Status: "implemented on EONW v20, with their CLI front end (...shn4.5), the Workspaces picker
  and the Commands entries (...shn4.6)". The protocol is EONW v22 (shn4.8, 57718ae), and the
  Eon Bar label and attention (shn4.7, shn4.8) are not named.
- (c) Commands > Quit this window runs `eon stop GENERATION` (runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/
  cli.rs:128), whose prompt is built at runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/generation.rs:888 ("Stop
  generation {target} and {n} live terminal{s} [...]? [y/N]"). In shn4.9's run it said 5 live
  terminals for 4 workspace terminals plus the Commands popup's own terminal
  (~/.cache/eon-agents/shn4.9-work/results.md:62-63).
- (d) docs/CONTRACTS.md:2543, EON-C31's "Across workspaces" clause has no pointer to shn4.9's
  installed cross-workspace Alt+G observation; only EON-C33's Proof block cites it.

## Contract

(a) and (d) change EON-C10 and EON-C31 text, and (c) may change EON-C10 wording of `eon stop`'s
prompt. Each contract-text change in this bead needs Lucca's approval per AGENTS.md: draft the
exact wording, stop, and bring it to him before editing docs/CONTRACTS.md. Changing a contract's
text, status or proof record also needs the Codex review that AGENTS.md requires.

## Prerequisites

None.

## Scope

In scope:
- (a) EON-C10's nested EON-C33 Status: name EONW v22 and the beads that implement the label and
  attention, or point to EON-C33's Status instead of repeating it (prefer the pointer: one owner).
- (c) Decide whether `eon stop`'s count and list leave out the calling popup's own terminal, or
  name it as the Commands popup; implement the decision with a runtime test that fails on today's
  code. Docs/USAGE.md follows.
- (d) Add a pointer from EON-C31's "Across workspaces" clause to the installed observation
  recorded in EON-C33's Proof (shn4.9, cf6dc25).

Out of scope:
- `eon workspace switch --json`'s reply (the separate a9g0 child).
- Any EONW change; stop if (c) needs one.
- EON-C33's status or proof block.

## Acceptance

- Lucca has approved the exact EON-C10 and EON-C31 wording (and any EON-C10 `eon stop` wording)
  before it lands; the approval is quoted on this bead.
- Quit from Commands no longer reports a count that surprises a person (as decided), proved by
  a runtime test that fails on today's code.
- CHANGELOG.md gets an entry only if the Quit prompt's user-visible text changes.

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime` passes; clippy clean for eon-runtime.
- Changed Markdown paths and contract IDs listed on this bead with the diff.
- One isolated installed observation of the Quit prompt from Commands if (c) changes behavior
  (never in Lucca's running Eon).

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if (c) needs an EONW change.

title: Switch between workspaces in one Eon window
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-10-22 (eon-n77e): Eon 1.0 lets one window switch between several workspaces ("do it", approving shape D). The comparison and the reference gate are on eon-n77e. Read both before starting any child.

## Shape

- One supervisor holds N workspaces. Each workspace is a tab set with its own tabs, panes, popups and Orbit terminals.
- Venus shows one workspace at a time; switching swaps the shown workspace.
- Venus already attaches only what is visible (model.rs:173-215), so a switch looks like a tab switch to it.
- Independent windows (EON-C23) stay, and each window holds N workspaces.
- The user noun is "workspace". Jumping to the next agent that needs attention crosses workspaces.

## Contracts

EON-C8, EON-C10, EON-C11 (wording), EON-C23, EON-C28 (fields freeze at 1.0), EON-C31, VEN-C8, VEN-C21.

Unchanged: VEN-C14, VEN-C18, VEN-C23.

The first child brings the exact wording to Lucca.

## Children, in order

1. Contracts.
2. Runtime workspace layer.
3. The next EONW version (after eon-agent-sidebar-yx8.7).
4. Close semantics and the CLI, in parallel.
5. Picker.
6. Venus bar label.
7. Attention across workspaces.
8. Batch proof.

## Known risk, accepted

One supervisor crash closes the window and flattens every workspace into one tab, because recovery projects everything into `t1` and the terminals survive through EON-C15. `eon stop` and Quit this window stop every workspace.

## Acceptance

All children closed. The batch proof shows three workspaces in one installed window: switching between them, closing them, and attention across them.

title: Approve the workspace-switching contracts and CLI spelling
description:
## Why

The epic's first child. Lucca approved shape D (eon-n77e). AGENTS.md requires his approval of the exact contract wording before any code.

## Work

1. Draft the exact amendments under the epic's shape and the eon-n77e comparison:
   - **EON-C8:** a workspace layer above tabs. Traversal, tab moves and the final-tab rule work per workspace. A workspace's final close switches to the most recently shown other workspace; only the last workspace's final close ends the window. Recovery collapses everything into `t1`.
   - **EON-C10:** workspace requests (new, switch, rename, close); replies scoped to the caller's workspace through `EON_TERMINAL` (supervisor.rs:1230-1252); `CreateTab` targeting; stale cross-workspace IDs fail with exit 3; Commands entries. "Quit this window" stops every workspace.
   - **EON-C11:** Present shows the last shown workspace.
   - **EON-C23:** a window holds N workspaces.
   - **EON-C28:** the frozen `eon workspace --json` fields.
   - **EON-C31:** focus means the shown workspace's active tab; a rollup per workspace; the jump crosses workspaces and switches.
   - **VEN-C8:** shows only the shown workspace's tabs.
   - **VEN-C21:** a workspace label in the bar.
2. Fix the CLI spelling, for example `eon workspaces`, `eon workspace new|switch|rename|close`, and `--workspace` targeting, and the Alt+Shift+S key. Workspace names are display text; the ID is the identity, and an ambiguous name fails without acting (Rex reference on eon-n77e).
3. Add the docs/REFERENCES.md route for workspace and session switching, citing the pins on eon-n77e.
4. Bring the wording to Lucca. Record his approval here.
5. Land the contract text as Planned in the same commit as the route. The ARCHITECTURE.md naming boundary gains this meaning of workspace.

## Scope

Docs and planning only, with no code. Out of scope: restore across reboot (eon-reboot-restore-im8y owns it and must later save workspace membership).

## Acceptance

Lucca's approval is recorded. The contract text and the route have landed. Every later child cites the approved wording.

## Verification

Docs route: changed contract IDs plus the diff. The Review loop applies; Codex reviews the contract text.
close_reason: EON-C33 approved by Lucca and landed as Planned with the naming line and the REFERENCES route

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Draft 1 of the contract wording (2026-10-22), awaiting Lucca's approval. Shape: one new contract EON-C33 owns the workspace set and lists what it later amends in EON-C8/C10/C11/C23/C28/C31 and VEN-C8/C21. Proven contracts are left untouched until each child folds its part in. The ARCHITECTURE naming line and the REFERENCES route follow the contract.

## EON-C33 — Several workspaces in one window

- **Status:** Planned. Approved by Lucca on <date> (`eon-workspace-switching-shn4.1`, shape D from `eon-n77e`). The children of `eon-workspace-switching-shn4` implement it and fold each part into the contract named under **Amends**.
- **Consumer:** One full-Eon user, or an agent working for them, who keeps several separate sets of work in one Eon window.
- **Trigger:**
  - Alt+Shift+S, or Commands > Switch workspace;
  - Commands > New workspace, Rename workspace or Close this workspace;
  - `eon workspaces`, or `eon workspace new|switch|rename|close`;
  - the final close or last exit in one workspace;
  - an attention jump to a terminal in a hidden workspace;
  - detach, attach and recovery of the window.
- **Result:**
  - **Model.**
    - A window holds an ordered list of 1 to 32 workspaces and shows exactly one.
    - Each workspace has its own tabs, panes, popups, focus and terminals, exactly as EON-C8 describes for a workspace.
    - Each workspace has a stable `wN` identity, unique for the life of the window's supervisor and never reused in it.
    - A workspace may have an optional name: 1 to 64 characters, no control characters. Names are display text, not identity, and need not be unique.
    - Tab, pane and popup identities are unique across all of the window's workspaces. A tab or pane action never reaches another workspace.
  - **Showing.**
    - Venus renders only the shown workspace's tabs and terminals.
    - Terminals in hidden workspaces keep running. Only Venus's view of them is detached, as with a background tab.
    - Switching never starts, stops or restarts a terminal.
    - A new window, and a window that has never been split into workspaces, holds exactly one workspace, `w1`. It looks and behaves as today, with no label.
  - **The window list of workspaces.**
    - `eon workspaces [--json]` lists this window's workspaces in order. Each entry gives `id`, `name` (null when unnamed), `shown`, and `tabs` (the tab count).
    - The window means the caller's window inside Eon, and otherwise the default namespace or `EON_WINDOW_RUNTIME_DIR`, as for `eon workspace`.
    - `eon workspace [--json]` keeps its meaning for the caller's workspace. Inside an Eon terminal that is the terminal's workspace; outside Eon it is the shown one.
  - **New.**
    - `eon workspace new [--name NAME] [--no-focus]` and Commands > New workspace add a workspace after the shown one.
    - It opens with one pending tab and a fresh directory picker, as a new window does (EON-C23).
    - It becomes the shown workspace unless `--no-focus` is given, the same convention as `pane create --no-focus`.
    - The reply names its `wN`.
  - **Switch.**
    - `eon workspace switch WS` shows WS, where WS is a `wN` or a name.
    - Switching to the shown workspace returns the unchanged snapshot (EON-C10 no-op).
    - The shown workspace keeps its own active tab, selected pane and popups across switches. Zoom ends, as with any tab change (EON-C8).
  - **Rename.** `eon workspace rename [WS] NAME` and Commands > Rename workspace set the name. An empty NAME clears it. Without WS it renames the caller's workspace.
  - **Close.**
    - `eon workspace close WS` and Commands > Close this workspace stop every terminal of that workspace, as closing each of its tabs does (EON-C8), and then remove it.
    - Each one first lists the terminals and asks for confirmation, as `eon stop` does. `--json` asks nothing.
    - Closing the last workspace is the final close of the window (EON-C8): it ends the window.
  - **A workspace that empties.**
    - When a workspace's final tab closes, or its last terminal ends, and other workspaces remain, the workspace is removed and the most recently shown remaining workspace is shown.
    - Only the last workspace's final close or last exit ends the window (EON-C8).
    - The final-close prompt says "Close the last tab? This closes workspace NAME and stops N terminals." while other workspaces remain. With one workspace it keeps the existing "This quits the window" wording.
  - **Targeting.**
    - Run from an Eon terminal, every workspace-scoped command acts in that terminal's workspace, found through `EON_TERMINAL`. EON-C10's per-tab rules apply inside that workspace.
    - Run outside Eon, commands act on the shown workspace.
    - WS resolves an exact `wN` first, then an exact name. A name that matches more than one workspace refuses with `ambiguous-workspace` (exit 1) and names the matching IDs.
  - **Picker.**
    - Alt+Shift+S and Commands > Switch workspace open an Eon-owned fzf popup over the shown tab (VEN-C18).
    - Rows show the name, or `wN` when unnamed, and the tab count. They are ordered most recently shown first, with the shown workspace last and marked. Alt+Shift+S then Enter returns to the previous workspace.
    - Enter shows the selected workspace.
    - Enter on a query that matches no row creates a workspace with that name and shows it.
    - Esc, Ctrl+C or an empty query runs nothing.
  - **Eon Bar.**
    - While the window holds two or more workspaces, or its one workspace has a name, the Eon Bar shows a leading label before the tabs: the shown workspace's name or `wN`, plus `N/M` when there are several.
    - Clicking the label opens the picker.
    - Its accessible name reads "Workspace NAME, N of M".
  - **Attention.**
    - Each workspace carries the most urgent normalized EON-C31 state of its terminals. `eon workspaces --json` gives it as `attention`, and the picker shows it.
    - The picker sorts needs-input workspaces first, then by recency.
    - The bar label shows a badge while a hidden workspace needs input.
    - The Alt+G queue (EON-C31) spans every workspace of the window. A jump to a terminal in a hidden workspace shows that workspace first.
    - A raise becomes seen only while its terminal's workspace is shown, under EON-C31's existing rules.
    - The sidebar lists the shown workspace's terminals only.
  - **Detach, attach and recovery.**
    - Closing the window, or Alt+Shift+D, detaches every workspace together. Attach shows the last shown workspace.
    - `eon stop` and Commands > Quit this window stop every workspace of the window.
    - Same-boot recovery projects every recovered run into one workspace `w1`, as EON-C8 does into `t1`. Names and workspace membership are not recovered.
- **Important failures:**
  - In each of these cases nothing changes, and the reply is EON-C10's typed failure:
    - an unknown or stale `wN`, or a name that matches nothing (exit 3);
    - an ambiguous name (exit 1);
    - a 33rd workspace (exit 1, `workspace-limit`);
    - a malformed name (exit 2);
    - a tab, pane or popup identity that belongs to another workspace (exit 3).
  - A repeated request ID never repeats a switch, create or close.
  - A failed stop while closing a workspace keeps the workspace and its remaining terminals, as a partial tab close does (EON-C8).
  - Switching never moves desktop focus.
- **Owner:**
  - Eon Runtime owns the workspace list, identities, the shown workspace, names, removal and the per-workspace attention rollup.
  - Eon owns the picker, the Commands entries and the CLI projection.
  - Venus renders the shown workspace and the bar label (VEN-C8, VEN-C21).
  - Orbit owns every terminal.
- **Consumes:** EON-C8, EON-C10, EON-C11, EON-C15, EON-C23, EON-C31, the next EONW version, VEN-C8, VEN-C18 and VEN-C21.
- **Amends, when implemented:**
  - EON-C8: the final-close and empty-workspace rules above.
  - EON-C10: the workspace requests, caller targeting and exit codes.
  - EON-C11: attach shows the last shown workspace.
  - EON-C23: a window holds 1 to 32 workspaces.
  - EON-C28: the `eon workspaces --json` fields, frozen at 1.0.
  - EON-C31: focus means focus in the shown workspace; the queue spans workspaces; the rollup.
  - VEN-C8: the shown workspace only.
  - VEN-C21: the label.
- **Boundary:** All of the following are out of scope:
  - showing another window's or generation's workspace in this window (Venus never changes supervisor);
  - moving a workspace, tab or pane between workspaces or windows;
  - a window with zero workspaces;
  - keeping names or membership past the supervisor's end or across a reboot (`eon-reboot-restore-im8y`);
  - unique names, or names as identity;
  - next, previous or last-workspace shortcuts beyond the picker's recency order;
  - per-workspace detach;
  - per-workspace configuration;
  - eonbase, which keeps one workspace and no picker.
- **Proof:** None yet. `eon-workspace-switching-shn4.9` is the batch proof.

## ARCHITECTURE.md naming boundary: add after the workspace sentence

> An Eon **window** holds one or more workspaces and shows one at a time; switching the shown workspace keeps every terminal running. A workspace may have a user-set name; its `wN` identity, not its name, identifies it.

## docs/REFERENCES.md: new route, in the workspace/picker area

> ### How should one Eon window let a user find and switch between several workspaces?
>
> - **Owner:** Eon Runtime workspace set (EON-C33); Eon owns the picker
> - **Read first:**
>   - tmux 3.8 `7f2a35ad3321` `cmd-switch-client.c` and `window-switch.c`;
>   - Zellij v0.45.1 `efd8fd5a89a2` `default-plugins/session-manager`;
>   - Rex docs `llms-full.txt` (sha256 `fc17b069…8ffe6`), session targeting.
> - **Read additionally only if:**
>   - window-level behaviour is in scope: kitty v0.49.2 `b2cb871254fb` `kitty/session.py` and WezTerm `e2a98e1b8af1` `wezterm-gui/src/frontend.rs` `reconcile_workspace`;
>   - persistence is in scope: herdr `143bf5fd4781` and tuios `0047c409185f` `docs/SESSIONS.md`.
> - **Preserve / reject:**
>   - Preserve: a picker that lists every workspace by recency, with its marker; create from an unmatched query; a stable ID separate from the name, where an ambiguous name acts on nothing; agents that create without moving the user.
>   - Reject:
>     - Venus re-targeting another supervisor (shape B), or WezTerm-style OS-window reconciliation;
>     - name-as-identity (Zellij's rename moves its socket, and kitty's basenames collide);
>     - presenting restored structure as survival.

title: Hold several workspaces in one supervisor with one shared ID allocator
description:
## Why

Epic child 2. The supervisor holds a single `Workspace` (supervisor.rs:980-994) with per-workspace ID counters (`next_tab`, `next_pane`, `next_session`, `next_popup`: workspace.rs:124-135). Socket names (`session-N.sock`, `kN.sock`: workspace.rs:660-670, :959-965) and tab IDs would collide across workspaces.

## Contract

The approved EON-C8 wording (from the contracts child). This child changes no user-visible behaviour, and with one workspace everything is identical.

## Work

- Add a workspace-set owner in the supervisor over N `Workspace`s, with one shown.
- Use one ID allocator shared by all workspaces for tabs, panes, sessions, popups and sockets.
- Make the 256-terminal cap and request de-duplication span the supervisor.
- Map `EON_TERMINAL` and endpoint to the owning workspace.
- The snapshot stays the shown workspace's tabs.
- Recovery still projects into one workspace with `t1`.
- No EONW change.

## Portability

Neutral.

## Acceptance

Focused runtime tests: two workspaces created in-process never share an ID or socket path, and a request carrying another workspace's tab ID is refused. The existing suites pass unchanged.

## Verification

`nix develop -c eon-test` with the affected crate tests, plus the build. Codex on every code change.

title: Carry workspaces and workspace requests on the next EONW version
description:

The runtime workspace layer, and eon-agent-sidebar-yx8.7, so that the two EONW bumps don't collide.

- A Venus on the new version renders an unchanged single workspace.

title: Close a workspace without ending the window, and detach every workspace together
description:
## Why

Epic child 4a. Today the window ends when no terminals remain (supervisor.rs:899), and closing the final tab warns that it quits the window (m798). With N workspaces, closing one workspace's last tab must not end the window.

## Contract

The approved EON-C8 and EON-C11 wording.

- Closing a workspace's final tab removes that workspace and shows the most recently shown other workspace.
- Only the last workspace's final close follows the m798/fwnp end-of-window path.
- Detach (window close, Alt+Shift+D) detaches every workspace.
- Present shows the last shown workspace.

## Prerequisites

The EONW child, and eon-final-close-prompt-and-detach-key-m798 landed.

## Acceptance

- Runtime tests: closing workspace 2's last tab while 3 workspaces exist shows the most recent one, and the window stays alive.
- The last workspace's final close ends the window.
- After detach and attach, the window shows the same workspace.

## Verification

Focused tests plus the build. Codex on every code change.
close_reason: Close and detach semantics proven by the e2e and Venus tests; EON-C8/C10/C11/C18 and VEN-C8 folded under the relayed 2026-10-26 approval; installed proof is shn4.9

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Reference gate (eon-84, 2026-10-26, before code; consequential because it changes the EON-C8, EON-C10, EON-C11 and VEN-C8 text).

Behavior and owners: with several workspaces, closing a workspace's final tab or last pane, or its last terminal exiting, removes only that workspace and shows the most recently shown remaining one; only the last workspace's final close or last exit ends the window; detach (window close, Alt+Shift+D) detaches every workspace and attach/Present shows the last shown workspace. Eon Runtime's WorkspaceSet owns removal, recency and the shown workspace (workspace.rs prune_empty/show, landed with shn4.3); the supervisor owns Ended (closed_response, and the main loop's end when no session remains) and presentation (Present hands Venus state.workspace_snapshot(), the shown workspace; reap_presentation leaves the set untouched). Venus owns only its final-close prompt decision (application.rs final_close_tab), which today checks for one tab and ignores the workspace list, so it would claim "This quits the window" for a close that only removes one workspace; the CLI already skips its prompt with several workspaces (cli.rs final_close_terminals). The workspace-worded prompt stays with shn4.7.

Investigation found the runtime half already implemented by shn4.3 (it kept pruning as the minimum shared-owner operation). This slice therefore: (1) adds an end-to-end test in eon/crates/eon/tests/workspace_control.rs that fails if a non-last workspace's final close ends the window or shows a positional rather than most-recent survivor, if detach and attach reset the shown workspace, or if the last workspace's final close fails to end the window; (2) makes Venus's final_close_tab return None while the snapshot lists more than one workspace, matching the CLI, with a unit case; (3) folds EON-C33's final-close, emptying and detach/attach rules into EON-C8, EON-C10's close sentence, EON-C11's Present line and VEN-C8's final-close clause.

Routes read: docs/REFERENCES.md "How should one Eon window let a user find and switch between several workspaces?" (the EON-C33 route). Comparable implementation: tmux 3.8 7f2a35ad3321 server-fn.c server_destroy_session (:486-528) with detach-on-destroy (options-table.c:822): "off" moves each client to the remaining session with the newest activity time (server_newer_session); the default detaches. Kept: removal moves the viewer to the most recent survivor, and the server never ends while sessions remain. Rejected: tmux's default detach-on-destroy (EON-C33 approves switching) and index order (previous/next) as the survivor rule. Decision check: the e2e test orders history w1 -> w2 -> w3 -> w2, so closing w2 must show w3, which neither a previous-index rule nor a first-workspace fallback gives.

Portability: neutral (runtime logic and the Venus prompt decision). No dependency, wire or EONW change (stays v20). Not user-visible yet, since no CLI or picker front end creates a second workspace, so no CHANGELOG entry.

I relied on it for the contract text below, which folds EON-C33's approved final-close, emptying and detach/attach rules (shn4.1) into the contracts EON-C33 names. No new rule was added. The interim "asks nothing yet" clauses describe the behaviour the CLI already had, and Venus now matches it. The workspace-worded prompt stays planned under shn4.7 (plan-change note on that bead).

Adopted text:

EON-C8, final-tab close: "Closing the final tab of the window's last workspace (EON-C33) ends the window. [...] The reply is EONW `Ended`, and Venus then exits. While other workspaces remain, closing a workspace's final tab stops that tab's terminals as above and removes the workspace; if it was shown, the most recently shown remaining workspace is shown. The reply is that snapshot, and the window stays."

EON-C8, prompt: "When the setting is false, a final close quits at once. Closing a workspace's final tab while other workspaces remain asks nothing yet; EON-C33's workspace-worded prompt is planned."

EON-C8, detach: "Closing the window itself, or Alt+Shift+D, detaches every workspace together without asking; attach then shows the last shown workspace (EON-C11)."

EON-C8, pane close: "Closing the final tab's last pane acts as final-tab close does, stopping that tab's popups with it."

EON-C8, ended terminals: "A workspace left empty while other workspaces remain is removed, and if it was shown, the most recently shown remaining workspace is shown (EON-C33); the last workspace left empty closes Venus and the supervisor."

title: List, create, switch, rename and close workspaces from the CLI
description:
## Why

Epic child 4b. Users and agents need to list, create, switch, rename and close workspaces from the CLI. This supersedes eon-name-eon-windows-1opf: names now belong to workspaces.

## Contract

The approved EON-C10 and EON-C28 wording and the CLI spelling from the contracts child, for example:

- `eon workspaces [--json]`
- `eon workspace new [--name N]`
- `eon workspace switch ID|NAME`
- `eon workspace rename [ID] NAME`
- `eon workspace close ID|NAME`

`eon workspace` alone keeps showing the caller's workspace.

Rules:

- Inside Eon, commands target the caller's workspace through `EON_TERMINAL`. Outside it, they target the shown workspace or `--workspace`.
- An ambiguous name fails without acting.
- `new` leaves focus where it is, unless the user asks to switch (agents open work without moving the user; Rex and herdr references on eon-n77e).

## Prerequisites

The EONW child.

## Acceptance

Using only the CLI: create 3 workspaces, name them, switch, and close one. `eon workspaces --json` reflects every step. An ambiguous name exits non-zero and changes nothing.

## Verification

Focused CLI tests through `nix develop -c eon-test`, plus the build. Codex on every code change.
close_reason: CLI lists, creates, switches, renames and closes workspaces; created names the new wN against old and new v20 supervisors; EON-C10/EON-C33 folded under the relayed 2026-10-26 approval; installed proof is shn4.9

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Reference gate (shn4.5 implementer, 2026-10-27, before code; consequential because it changes EON-C10 and EON-C33 text and the reply of an EONW request, with no wire change: EONW stays v20).

Behavior and owners: `eon workspaces [--json]` lists the targeted window's workspaces (id, name, shown, tabs); `eon workspace new [--name NAME] [--no-focus]`, `switch WS`, `rename [WS] NAME` and `close WS` send v20's NewWorkspace, SwitchWorkspace, RenameWorkspace and CloseWorkspace. Eon Runtime's WorkspaceSet keeps sole ownership of resolution (wN first, then exact name, ambiguous-workspace naming the IDs), the shown workspace, names and removal; the CLI (runtime cli.rs, the "CLI projection" EON-C33 assigns to Eon, implemented in the runtime crate like every other control command) only parses, prompts and prints, and never resolves WS itself. Targeting reuses the existing control path: EON_TERMINAL inside Eon, otherwise the shown workspace, and --generation/--window as for `eon workspace`.

Findings that shape the slice:
1. The approved EON-C33 says "The reply names its wN", but today's supervisor projects every reply into the caller's workspace (supervisor.rs reply_workspace), so `new` from inside Eon, or `new --no-focus` outside it, never names the new workspace. Fix at the owner: the supervisor's NewWorkspace reply describes the new workspace, whose ID WorkspaceSet's allocator reports. v20's snapshot already separates `workspace` (projected) from `active_workspace` (shown), so no wire change.
2. v20's WorkspaceInfo has no attention rollup; shn4.8 owns adding it (its bead: "Each workspace in the snapshot carries its most urgent normalized attention state"). `eon workspaces --json` ships without `attention` and shn4.8 adds it; EON-C28 lets 0.x add fields before the 1.0 freeze.
3. v20 cannot inspect the terminals of a workspace other than the caller's (inside Eon) or the shown one (outside), so `close WS` cannot list WS's terminals as EON-C33's "list the workspace's terminals" says without a new EONW request. Plan change (pre-approved, relayed 2026-10-26; clearly better than an EONW bump for prompt text, which would also collide with shn4.8's bump): the prompt names the workspace and says it stops every terminal in it, and that it quits the window when it is the last one; it asks exactly when `eon stop` asks (without --json) and cancels on anything but yes.

Routes read: docs/REFERENCES.md "How should one Eon window let a user find and switch between several workspaces?" (EON-C33 route), EON-C10, EON-C28, EON-C33, beads shn4.1, shn4.3, shn4.4, shn4.6, shn4.8. Comparable implementation: tmux 3.8 7f2a35ad3321 cmd-new-session.c (-d at :165/:358 creates without switching the client; -P at :348-350 prints NEW_SESSION_TEMPLATE "#{session_name}:") and cmd-list-sessions.c LIST_SESSIONS_TEMPLATE (:31-36: name, window count, attached marker). Kept: create-without-switching that still prints the new identity (our reply's `workspace`), and a list of identity, count and shown marker. Rejected: tmux's name-as-target addressing (EON-C33: wN identity, names are display text) and a separate print flag (the reply always names it).

Decision check: an end-to-end test in eon/crates/eon/tests/workspace_control.rs that drives only the eon CLI: creates workspaces with and without --no-focus (the reply names the new wN both times), names them, switches by ID and by name, renames from inside a terminal through EON_TERMINAL, refuses an ambiguous name with exit 1 and an unchanged `eon workspaces --json`, cancels a close without --json on a non-yes answer, and closes one with --json; `eon workspaces --json` is checked after every step. CLI parser cases in cli.rs cover the argument forms and usage errors.

Portability: neutral (CLI and runtime logic). No dependency, wire or EONW change. User-visible: new CLI commands, so CHANGELOG.md, docs/USAGE.md and help change, and the final-close wording that shn4.4 left for the first front end (docs/USAGE.md, docs/CONFIGURATION.md, venus/docs/INTERACTION.md).

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Review round 1 on candidate tree 91b3b518 (base 6a3ee78), and a change of plan (2026-10-27).

Change of plan, made with eon-overseer: the CLI names the new workspace instead of the supervisor reply. eon-overseer pointed out the mixed-version case: Lucca's terminals run the profile `eon` CLI against his running v20 supervisor, which keeps answering NewWorkspace with the caller's workspace. A CLI that read the reply's `workspace` as the created wN would then report the wrong workspace. I chose a CLI-side fix over an EONW bump. It is correct against both reply meanings, adds no wire change, and does not collide with shn4.8's EONW bump.

- The supervisor's NewWorkspace reply change is reverted, so supervisor.rs and workspace.rs's allocator are unchanged from base, and the reply stays caller-projected (EON-C10).
- The CLI prints the new wN as `created` (JSON) and `created wN` (human). It takes the highest wN in the reply's `workspaces`.
  - Why this cannot pick another client's workspace: the supervisor serves one control client at a time on its main loop. supervisor.rs:1010-1012 calls `control_listener.accept(|request| dispatch_control_request(request, &mut state, ...))`, and control.rs:479-484 accepts one stream and runs `handle_client(stream, dispatch)` to completion.
  - Inside that one call, the generic branch of dispatch_control_request runs `workspace.dispatch(...)` (supervisor.rs:1985) and then builds the reply with `state.workspace_snapshot_in(reply_workspace)` (supervisor.rs:2025), so no other request can create a workspace in between.
  - WorkspaceSet allocates wN from a counter that only increases (workspace.rs:238, insert_pending), and EON-C33 guarantees a wN is never reused, so the new workspace has the highest number in that list.
  - Today's v20 supervisors run the same code, so the rule holds against them too.

Round 1 findings:
- Codex (gpt-6.1-sol, xhigh) found 3 blocking issues, all fixed:
  1. The close prompt came before target resolution, so an unknown or ambiguous WS was asked about and then cancelled with exit 0, and a rename during the prompt could redirect the close. Now the CLI asks only when WS names exactly one workspace (an exact wN, else one exact name, as Runtime resolves it), then sends that wN. A WS that names no workspace or several goes to Runtime unasked and fails with exit 3 or exit 1.
  2. The new test removed its root while mock Orbit helpers were alive. It now closes every workspace through the CLI until the reply is Ended and waits for the supervisor to exit.
  3. `--name --window` lost its operand to the target-flag parser. The target parser now passes the argument after `--name` through, and the parser test runs the whole pipeline.
- Codex also reported a nit, which I took: the test no longer requires exactly four fields.
- Codex also flagged a new-surface item, name trimming. The trimming is now in EON-C10's Rename sentence.
- The fresh Claude reviewer found 1 blocking issue, fixed: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md still said the CLI front end was planned.
- The Claude reviewer's nits that I took:
  - the EON-C33 Close line was not wrapped, and it now includes the last-workspace clause;
  - the help shows `[--no-focus]` on the `workspace new` line;
  - USAGE says "never reused by the window's supervisor";
  - the test covers the last-workspace prompt.
- The Claude reviewer's checks were green on 91b3b518, and the tree was unchanged after them.
- Not taken: the bead body's "new leaves focus where it is" disagrees with the approved EON-C33 ("becomes the shown workspace unless `--no-focus`"). The code follows the contract, which Lucca approved on shn4.1. docs/USAGE.md:387-388's older use of "default workspace" for the namespace predates this change, so I left it.

Adopted contract text: see the approval comment that follows.
