comments.text:
Contract wording approval, relayed by the coordinator (eon-overseer). On 2026-10-26 Lucca wrote to eon-overseer, as the standing approval for the overnight run: "focus on finishing the worspace-switching beads, but try to advance on kitty-graphics too / everything is pre-approved. autonomous. / and sprinkle the ones the subagent listed that are important." He added: "also pre-aprove changes of plan if a clearly better alternative appears". The coordinator states that the approval covers this bead, including the EON-C and VEN-C wording it needs.

I relied on it for the following, in docs/CONTRACTS.md:
- folding the CLI front end into EON-C10's EON-C33 block;
- two changes of plan against EON-C33's approved text:
  - the new wN is reported in `created`, not as the reply's projected workspace (mixed-version safety, round-1 comment above);
  - the close prompt names the workspace and does not list its terminals, because v20 cannot inspect a workspace other than the caller's or the shown one without an EONW bump;
- recording two things the shipped CLI does: name trimming, and that a WS naming no workspace or several fails without asking.

Adopted text:

EON-C10, Status: "The workspace requests and targeting below are implemented on EONW v20, with their CLI front end (`eon-workspace-switching-shn4.5`); the Commands entries remain planned."

EON-C10, new Listing item: "`eon workspaces [--json]` lists this window's workspaces in order, each with `id`, `name` (null when unnamed), `shown` and `tabs` (the tab count), after the `generation`, `window` and caller's `workspace` that every result names. This window means the caller's window inside Eon, and otherwise the window `eon workspace` targets. EON-C33's per-workspace `attention` is planned (`eon-workspace-switching-shn4.8`)."

EON-C10, New (replacing "The reply names its `wN`."): "The reply names the new `wN` in `created`, whether or not it is shown, alongside the caller's projected `workspace`."

EON-C10, Rename (appended): "The CLI trims surrounding whitespace from NAME and from `--name`, as for pane names, so a blank NAME clears the name and a blank `--name` is malformed (exit 2)."

EON-C10, Close (prepended): "`eon workspace close WS` first asks for confirmation, as `eon stop` does, when WS names exactly one workspace: the prompt names its `wN` and name, says that closing stops every terminal in it, and that it quits the window when it is the last workspace. Any answer but yes changes nothing, and a yes closes that `wN` even if names change meanwhile. `--json` asks nothing, and a WS that names no workspace or several fails unasked."

EON-C33, New (replacing "The reply names its `wN`."): "The reply names the new `wN` in `created`, whether or not it is shown."

EON-C33, Close (replacing "list the workspace's terminals and ask for confirmation, as `eon stop` does; `--json` asks nothing."): "ask for confirmation, as `eon stop` does, naming the workspace and saying that closing stops every terminal in it, and that it quits the window when it is the last one; `--json` asks nothing."

No EON-C28 text change: its general rule already freezes, at 1.0, the commands and JSON fields that `eon --help` and docs/USAGE.md list.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Converge and Codex re-check after round 1 (2026-10-27).

Converge rounds, fresh Claude, base 6a3ee78:
- Round 2: one code simplification. `inspect` and `final_close_terminals` take `&Path`; the `Result` wrapper was a leftover.
- Round 3: one doc-comment fix on `inspect`.
- Round 4: clean on tree 151aba0f.
- Each round's checks were green: eon-test -p eon --test workspace_control workspace, eon-test -p eon-runtime cli::, fmt, and clippy -D warnings.

Narrow Codex re-check of 91b3b518..151aba0f found 2 blocking races in the interactive close. Both are fixed.
1. A WS that resolved to no workspace or several was sent unasked. A rename by another client before the send could then make it close a workspace without confirmation. Now the CLI refuses such a WS before sending anything, with Runtime's own failure (exit 3 or 1).
2. After a yes, the CLI sent the confirmed wN. If another client had closed that workspace meanwhile, Runtime's resolver would have read the wN as another workspace's name (ID-shaped names are allowed). Now the CLI inspects again after the answer and sends the wN only if it is still live; otherwise it fails with unknown-workspace (exit 3).
   - Residual gap, accepted: the window between that second inspection and the send is one control round trip, the same as every other check-then-act in the CLI.
   - Closing it fully needs an ID-only close request on a later EONW version. It is out of scope here, since this slice adds no wire change.

To keep one owner of the selector rule, Runtime's WorkspaceSet::resolve_workspace now calls a crate function, workspace.rs `resolve_selector`, over (wN, name) pairs. The CLI applies the same function to the snapshot's `workspaces`. Runtime's failures and messages are unchanged.

The round-1 claim "a yes closes that wN even if names change meanwhile" overstated this. EON-C10's Close item now reads (adopted under the relayed approval recorded above, replacing that item's first sentences):
"`eon workspace close WS` first asks for confirmation, as `eon stop` does. The prompt names the `wN` and name that WS resolves to, says that closing stops every terminal in it, and that it quits the window when it is the last workspace. A WS that resolves to no workspace or several fails before asking, with the failures below. Any answer but yes changes nothing. A yes closes that `wN` if it is still live, and otherwise changes nothing and exits 3. `--json` asks nothing."

Test additions in workspace_cli_lists_creates_switches_renames_and_closes:
- an ambiguous close without --json exits 1 without prompting;
- a close confirmed with "yes" on stdin closes the resolved workspace.

title: Switch workspaces from an Alt+Shift+S picker
description:
## Why

Epic child 5. This supersedes eon-switch-window-picker-i92k. Every reference on eon-n77e has an in-app switcher:

- tmux `C-b s` and `S-Tab`
- the Zellij session-manager
- WezTerm's launcher
- kitty's `goto_session`
- Rex's "Change Session…"
- the tuios switcher

## Contract

The approved EON-C10 and EON-C23 wording.

Alt+Shift+S, and a Commands entry "Switch workspace", open an Eon-owned fzf popup (VEN-C18 holds, with no native Venus picker). The popup lists this window's workspaces with name, tab count and the shown marker.

- Enter switches.
- Typing a name that matches nothing creates a workspace with that name and switches to it (Zellij and tuios).
- Esc does nothing.

Commands also gains "New workspace" and "Rename workspace". Check Alt+Shift+S against the key map when this child starts.

## Prerequisites

The close-semantics child and the CLI child.

## Acceptance

From an installed Eon with three workspaces: Alt+Shift+S lists them, Enter switches, a new name creates one, and Esc changes nothing.

## Verification

Installed route, run once in the batch proof. Codex on every code change.

Reference gate (shn4.6 implementer, 2026-10-27, before code; consequential because it changes EON-C10's popup catalog and EON-C33 text, with no dependency, wire or EONW change: EONW stays v20).

Behavior and owners:
- Alt+Shift+S opens a new built-in transient popup, `[popups.workspaces]` (label "Workspaces", argv `eon-workspaces`), so its key, label and enablement are configurable through the existing popup catalog (Runtime parses, Venus only matches `snapshot.entries`; eonbase gets no entries and so no picker). Its default is documented in docs/CONFIGURATION.md's generated defaults block. Popup over the shown tab, VEN-C18 unchanged, no Venus code.
- `eon-workspaces` is a libexec name of the `eon` binary, as `eon-commands` is (flake symlink plus an argv0 match in runtime cli.rs). It inspects the caller's window over v20 (snapshot.workspaces, active_workspace), lists one row per workspace (name or wN, tab count, the shown one last and marked), runs the packaged fzf (`packaged_fzf`, exact match on the label only, `--print-query` with `enter:accept-or-print-query`), and then runs the existing CLI in-process as the popup's caller: `workspace switch wN` for a row, `workspace new --name QUERY` for a non-empty query that matches no row, nothing for Esc/Ctrl+C or a blank query. The CLI keeps owning validation, targeting and failures; a failure stays on screen until Enter, as in Commands.
- Commands (RUNNER_COMMANDS) gains "Switch workspace" (runs the same picker in the Commands popup), "New workspace" (`workspace new`), "Rename workspace" (a name text box like Rename pane, then `workspace rename -- NAME` for the caller's workspace; empty clears) and "Close this workspace" (`workspace close <the popup's own wN>`, keeping the CLI's confirmation).
- Owners: Eon Runtime's WorkspaceSet keeps resolution, the shown workspace, names, creation and removal; the picker and Commands entries only call the CLI (the "Eon owns the picker, the Commands entries and the CLI projection" of EON-C33, implemented in the runtime crate like Commands). Humans and Agents: every picker action already has its CLI path by ID (`eon workspaces`, `eon workspace switch|new|rename|close`, shn4.5).

Plan change (pre-approved changes of plan, relayed 2026-10-26; recorded in the approval comment that follows): the picker orders rows in window order with the shown workspace last and marked, not most recently shown first, and shows no needs-input marker. Recency order and the marker move to eon-workspace-switching-shn4.8.
- Evidence: v20's WorkspaceInfo carries only id, name and tab_count (runtime/crates/eon-workspace-protocol/src/v20.rs:425-430); recency lives only in WorkspaceSet.recent_workspaces inside the supervisor (workspace.rs:185). Putting it on the wire needs an EONW bump, and the last bump (11905dd, v19 -> v20) touched 37 files including Venus, the component manifest and every runtime consumer, and each bump makes the profile CLI refuse older running supervisors. shn4.8 must bump EONW anyway to put per-workspace attention on WorkspaceInfo, so carrying recency in that same bump costs one bump instead of two.
- Interim effect: with two workspaces, Alt+Shift+S then Enter still returns to the other one (it is the first row). With three or more, the first row is the first other workspace in window order, not the previous one.

Routes read: docs/REFERENCES.md "How should one Eon window let a user find and switch between several workspaces?" (EON-C33 route); EON-C10 (popup catalog and Commands paragraph, docs/CONTRACTS.md:1024-1041), EON-C33; beads shn4, shn4.1, shn4.4, shn4.5, shn4.7, shn4.8.

- tuios 0047c40 internal/input/session_switcher_input.go:46-60: Enter switches to the highlighted session, else a non-empty query creates and switches to a session of that name; internal/app/render_session_switcher.go:48-51 says "No match, Enter to create '<query>'". Kept: Enter on a match switches, Enter on an unmatched non-empty query creates; the footer names the create case. Rejected: name-as-target (tuios switches by name; Eon switches by the row's wN).
- Zellij v0.45.1 efd8fd5 default-plugins/session-manager: creation is a separate "New session" screen (main.rs:70, ActiveScreen::NewSession). Rejected for the picker: a second screen; Eon keeps creation in one Enter and in Commands > New workspace.
Decision check: an end-to-end test in eon/crates/eon/tests/workspace_control.rs that runs `eon-workspaces` (and the new Commands entries) as a popup caller with a scripted fzf, against a supervisor with three workspaces: the rows list every workspace with the shown one last and marked; a row switches; an unmatched query creates and shows a named workspace; a cancel changes nothing (checked with `eon workspaces --json`); Rename workspace renames the caller's workspace; Close this workspace closes the popup's own workspace after a yes. The runtime catalog test covers the new default entry and the defaults block test covers its documentation. Installed observation in an isolated headless Sway: Alt+Shift+S lists three workspaces, Enter switches, a new name creates one, Esc changes nothing.

Configurability: the key, label and enablement are `[popups.workspaces]` settings. The picker's footer and row wording, the exact match mode and the packaged fzf look stay fixed, as for Commands and the Project picker (packaged_fzf deliberately ignores user fzf options so the packaged pickers look and behave alike).
Portability: neutral (runtime CLI logic and a libexec symlink).

title: Show the shown workspace in the Eon Bar and word the final-close prompt by workspace
description:
## Why

Epic child 6. The user must see which workspace is shown. The OS title is the terminal's title (venus application.rs:3898-3902).

## Contract

The approved VEN-C21 and VEN-C8 wording.

- The Eon Bar shows a leading label with the shown workspace's name, or its number when unnamed, and the workspace count when there are several.
- Clicking the label opens the picker.
- The m798 final-close prompt says "closes this workspace" while other workspaces exist, and keeps "quits the window" otherwise.

## Portability

Neutral, Venus rendering only.

## Prerequisites

The picker child.

## Acceptance

Installed observation in the batch proof: the label tracks switches and renames, and the prompt wording follows the workspace count.

## Verification

`cargo fmt --check`, plus clippy for venus. Installed route in the batch. Codex on every code change.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Reference gate (shn4.7 implementer, 2026-10-27, before code). Consequential because it changes the text of VEN-C8, VEN-C21, EON-C8, EON-C10 and EON-C33. No dependency, wire or EONW change: EONW stays v20, and Venus reads only `workspace` and `workspaces`, which it already receives.

Behavior and owners:
- Eon Bar label (VEN-C21). The label shows while the window holds two or more workspaces, or while its one workspace has a name. It is a leading item at the bar's left inset, before the tab strip. It reads the shown workspace's name, or its wN, followed by " N/M" when M >= 2. N is the shown workspace's 1-based position in window order. The name is clipped to a tab's maximum width, and " N/M" always stays visible.
- The label looks like the bar widgets (an outline with no fill), so it does not read as a tab. It uses existing palette tokens, plus the header controls' hover, pressed and focus states.
- A click, or Enter or Space after header-focus traversal, invokes the popup entry `workspaces` from `snapshot.entries`. This builds the same InvokePopup that its key does. The tooltip comes from that entry's label and chord. With no `workspaces` entry (the user disabled it), the label is inert, with no focus and no actions.
- AccessKit gives the label a new fixed node, ordered first, named "Workspace NAME, N of M". Its role is Button when the label is clickable and Label otherwise.
- Width pressure: the widgets yield before the label. The label is dropped before the tab region falls below its one-pill minimum.
- Repaint: a change to the label's inputs (the shown workspace's name, N or M) re-measures and repaints the bar. EON-C33's rule stays: a change confined to hidden workspaces disturbs none of the shown workspace's navigation, scroll, attachments or rejected-action notice.
- The badge for a hidden workspace that needs input stays with shn4.8, because v20 has no per-workspace attention.
- Venus prompt (VEN-C8). A final close shows the m798 prompt whatever the workspace count. Until now it showed only with one workspace. With two or more workspaces, the subtitle is "This closes workspace NAME and stops N terminals.", the footer is "Enter Close · Esc Cancel", and the AccessKit description says "Press Enter to close it". The text is rebuilt from the current snapshot on every frame, so an open prompt re-words when the workspace count changes, which settles shn4.4's review note. Enter still sends the held close, and Runtime decides whether it ends the window or removes the workspace.
- CLI prompt (EON-C10). `final_close_terminals` also asks while other workspaces remain: "Close the last tab? This closes workspace NAME and stops N terminals [..]. [y/N]". A cancel prints "cancelled; workspace NAME stays open". The single-workspace wording is unchanged.
- Owners: Runtime keeps the workspace list, names and close semantics. Venus owns the label's geometry, paint, hit, input and AccessKit, and the prompt's presentation. Eon's popup catalog owns the picker's key and label. Venus derives the tooltip from that catalog and parses no configuration.

Routes read:
- venus/docs/REFERENCES.md "Native Eon Bar workspace header". Kept: tab-first priority and the existing Scene, renderer, EONW-action and AccessKit owners. Rejected: a second row, a widget tray, configuration in Venus, any protocol change.
- docs/REFERENCES.md "How should one Eon window let a user find and switch between several workspaces?" (the EON-C33 route).
- EON-C8, EON-C10, EON-C33, VEN-C8 and VEN-C21, and beads shn4, shn4.1, shn4.4 and shn4.6.

Comparable implementations (pins checked against the ~/pjs/refs clones):
- tmux 3.8 7f2a35ad3321. options-table.c:1068-1071 shows the session name at the left of the status line by default (`status-left` "[#{session_name}] "). key-bindings.c:548 opens a session menu on a right-click of status-left. The full switcher is the `s` key (choose-tree, key-bindings.c:439). Kept: a leading name label, shown by default, that leads to switching. Rejected: right-click only, and a menu separate from the picker. Eon uses a left click that opens the same picker its key opens.
- Zellij v0.45.1 efd8fd5a89a2. default-plugins/tab-bar/src/line.rs:270-274 prints "(session) " ahead of the tabs, only when it fits. A click on it does nothing (main.rs:136-152). Kept: the leading position, dropped under width pressure. Rejected: an inert label, since VEN-C21 and EON-C33 make it a way to reach the picker.
- WezTerm e2a98e1b8af1 shows the workspace only through user Lua (`window:active_workspace()`, docs/config/lua/window/active_workspace.md:13-14). Rejected: off by default. In Eon the label is the only sign of which workspace is shown.
- None of the references shows an N/M position. Eon keeps it because EON-C33, as Lucca approved it, requires it.

Configurability: the label's format, its visibility rule and its look stay fixed. EON-C33, approved by Lucca on 2026-10-22, requires the label while two or more workspaces exist. It is also the only on-screen sign of which workspace is shown, since the OS title is the terminal's. It appears only after the user creates or names a workspace. Its key, label and enablement come from `[popups.workspaces]`. The prompt's wording is fixed, as m798's is.
Portability: neutral (Venus scene, rendering and input, plus runtime CLI text).

Decision checks:
- Venus scene and AccessKit unit tests for the label: absent with one unnamed workspace; present with "NAME N/M" and the right accessible name; inert without the entry; tabs, hits and controls stay disjoint under width pressure.
- An application test that a click builds the `workspaces` InvokePopup.
- A model test that a label-input change repaints while a hidden-only change keeps navigation.
- The prompt test opening with two workspaces and re-wording when the count changes.
- A cli.rs unit test for both CLI wordings.
- An installed observation in isolated headless Sway (shn4.7 acceptance; shn4.9's batch proof repeats it): the label tracks switches and renames, a click opens the picker, and the prompt wording follows the count.

title: Carry agent attention across workspaces
description:
## Why

Epic child 7. This supersedes eon-window-attention-rollup-vgfx. Lucca chose attention that spans workspaces (eon-n77e).

## Contract

The approved EON-C31 wording.

- Each workspace in the snapshot carries its most urgent normalized attention state.
- The picker shows that state and sorts needs-input first.
- The bar label shows a badge when a hidden workspace needs input.
- The Alt+G jump (eon-agent-sidebar-yx8.8) walks agents across workspaces and switches to the target's workspace.
- A hidden workspace's raises stay unseen until it is shown and the exact terminal has focus.
- Showing attention never moves OS focus.

## Prerequisites

The picker child, the bar-label child, eon-agent-sidebar-yx8.7, and eon-agent-sidebar-yx8.8.

## Acceptance

- Runtime tests: the rollup per workspace; the jump crosses workspaces; a hidden raise stays unseen.
- Installed observation in the batch proof.

## Verification

Focused tests plus the build. Codex on every code change.
close_reason: Attention spans workspaces on EONW v22 (Eon 0.1.5): per-workspace rollup and recency, picker recency order with needs-input marker, Eon Bar badge, Alt+G across workspaces; proof and ledger in comments

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Plan change from eon-workspace-switching-shn4.6 (2026-10-27, under the pre-approved changes of plan relayed by eon-overseer; evidence on shn4.6's reference gate): this bead also carries the picker's recency order. v20's WorkspaceInfo has no recency, and putting it on the wire needs an EONW bump, which this bead makes anyway for per-workspace attention. So the same bump also tells the CLI each workspace's recency (for example, by listing workspaces most recently shown first in a new field, or with a per-workspace rank), and the `eon-workspaces` picker (runtime cli.rs) then orders rows most recently shown first, with the shown workspace last and marked, and shows a needs-input marker (EON-C33 Picker). Until then the picker lists rows in window order with the shown workspace last. Acceptance gains: with history w1 -> w3 -> w2, the picker's first row is w3.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Reference gate (AP-REFERENCE-001; consequential: EONW wire format v22, lifecycle of attention across workspaces). Base 07414f7; EONW v22 lands on top of eon-configurability-qkq8.1's v21.

Behavior and owners
- Eon Runtime (attention.rs) owns polling, seen, the per-tab and per-workspace rollup, the queue and its cursor, now over every workspace of the window. Today follow_attention builds targets from the shown workspace only (supervisor.rs:1083-1091) and Attention::retain drops every other terminal (attention.rs:226), so a hidden workspace's records and unseen raises are discarded and re-raised on return; this bead fixes that.
- Eon Runtime (WorkspaceSet, workspace.rs) owns the shown workspace and its recency (recent_workspaces, workspace.rs:185, front = most recent, a permutation of the live workspaces) and performs the cross-workspace jump: FocusAttention in the target's workspace, then show it. Sidebar FocusAttention stays scoped to the caller's workspace (EON-C33: another workspace's identity is exit 3).
- EONW v22 (eon-workspace-protocol) carries, per WorkspaceInfo, `attention: Option<AttentionState>` (the rollup, validated against the projected workspace's tab rollups) and `recency: u8` (0 = shown, 1 = previously shown, ..., validated as a permutation with 0 on active_workspace). One owner of each: Runtime computes both; the CLI picker and Venus only read them.
- Eon CLI (runtime cli.rs) owns the picker rows: most recently shown first, shown last and marked, ` · needs input` on a workspace whose rollup is needs input. `eon workspaces [--json]` gains `attention` (EON-C33 Listing, EON-C10).
- Venus owns the Eon Bar label badge (VEN-C21) while any hidden workspace's rollup is needs input; it reads, never computes, the rollup. It reuses the EON-C31 tab marker primitive (scene.rs TabBadge::corner at the pill's top-right, drawn by chrome.rs Spinners::push_badge with the needs-input diamond in palette::ATTENTION_NEEDS_INPUT), so the label's width and the tabs' geometry do not move, and it shows whether or not the sidebar is open (the sidebar lists only the shown workspace). The label's accessible name gains ", another workspace needs input". A hidden-only attention change repaints the bar through the content path (model.rs attention_only_change) and still disturbs nothing in the shown workspace (EON-C33 Showing).

Routes read (docs/REFERENCES.md)
- "How should one Eon window let a user find and switch between several workspaces?" (220-247): keep one picker listing every workspace by recency with the shown one marked.
- "How should shared popups extend the workspace wire contract without breaking the installed client?" (249-265): bounded framing, one schema, protocol before consumer; no negotiation.
- "How should Eon expose agent-readable actions and source-labeled attention" (383-400) and "How should Venus direct human attention across many agent-bearing workspaces" (459-468; cmux a35880b1031e is the named first read, not cloned in ~/pjs/refs, so the comparables below stand in).

Comparables (evidence, file:line@rev)
- tmux 7f2a35ad3321: alerts raise only when the window is not shown (alerts.c:202,238,274); session rollup is derived, not stored (format.c:602 format_cb_session_alert); flags clear on select (session.c:521 -> window.c:2467-2478); `switch-client -l` keeps one last_session slot (cmd-switch-client.c:128-130, server-client.c:455-456); choose-tree's activity sort changes on any input (sort.c:176-184).
- herdr 143bf5fd4781: Workspace::aggregate_state is the max-priority pane state (src/workspace/aggregate.rs:50-74), unseen finish above working; seen marks the whole tab on switch or agent focus (src/workspace.rs:451-459, src/app/agents.rs:75-82); agent list status then recency (src/client/shell/aggregate_navigation.rs:159-170).
- Zellij efd8fd5a89a2 session manager sorts by creation time, not recency (single_screen.rs:77-88,140-142).
- In-repo bumps: 11905dd (v19->v20, workspaces), 4b150d5 (v18 attention).

Kept: herdr's max-priority rollup, computed once at the owner (Runtime) and derived per snapshot as tmux derives session_alerts; tmux's "raise only while hidden, clear on showing" as the shape of seen; a full shown-recency rank (tmux keeps one slot; activity order would reshuffle rows on input).
Rejected: tmux/herdr coarse clearing (whole window or tab) — Eon keeps EON-C31's exact-terminal rule, so showing a workspace sees only its focused terminal; Zellij creation order as recency; a picker sorted needs-input first (Lucca, shn4.1 2026-10-23: "picker order is pure recency ... with needs-input as a row marker; Alt+G covers urgency"; the bead body's "sorts needs-input first" predates that decision and the approved EON-C33 text wins); a second recency list on the snapshot (a per-entry rank validates locally and keeps window order intact); Venus or the CLI recomputing rollups from tabs (they only see the projected workspace).

Decision check: runtime tests — the per-workspace rollup; a jump to a hidden workspace's terminal shows it and walks the queue across workspaces; a hidden workspace's raise stays unseen until it is shown with that exact terminal focused; history w1 -> w3 -> w2 puts w3 first in the picker. Codec round-trip and rejection of a bad rank or rollup. Venus badge test. Installed observation in isolated Sway.

Configurability: the picker marker text ` · needs input` stays fixed beside shn4.6's fixed ` · shown`: it names the EON-C31 state the CLI already spells, not a user preference. The badge reuses the existing needs-input tab marker's colour token, which theme configuration already owns.
Portability: neutral (no platform mechanism).
No new dependency.

comments.text:
Plan change (2026-10-27, under the pre-approved changes of plan relayed by eon-overseer: Lucca, 2026-10-26: "also pre-aprove changes of plan if a clearly better alternative appears"). Raised by review round 1 (Codex and fresh Claude, both blocking).

1. `eon workspaces [--json]` also gives each workspace's `recency` (text `recency=N`, JSON `"recency":N`, 0 for the shown workspace). Why: the picker now shows people the recency order, and AGENTS.md (Humans and Agents) requires "Everything a person can see about that workspace, an agent can read from the CLI as data"; without it, histories w1->w3->w2 and w3->w1->w2 list identically while the picker's first row differs. Adopted text, EON-C33 Listing: "Each entry gives `id`, `name` (null when unnamed), `shown`, `tabs` (the tab count), `attention` and `recency` (0 for the shown workspace, then 1, 2, ... from the most recently shown, the picker's order, so an agent reads what a person sees there)." EON-C10 Listing: "... `attention` (...) and `recency` (EON-C33's rank, 0 for the shown workspace, which orders the picker) ...". EON-C28's freeze (eon-igae.11) has not listed these fields yet; it now has `attention` and `recency` to freeze.

title: Use workspace and terminal consistently in Eon product terminology
description:
## Contract
Use workspace for the collection of tabs and panes, tab for a directory-based grouping, pane for the visual view, and terminal for one persistent Orbit-backed PTY/process/terminal-state instance. Product README, guides, launcher copy, help, human CLI output and Eon-owned diagnostics use this vocabulary consistently. Closing a native window detaches; Stop ends its terminals.

## Ownership and scope
Eon owns product vocabulary and documentation; the existing private Runtime CLI/output owners project it. Preserve session-N IDs, socket paths, JSON session/sessions keys, EONW/ORBS/management fields, symbolic error codes, existing lifecycle and Eon Sessions repository/component identity. Record this technical-to-product mapping explicitly rather than adding aliases, migrating live state or inventing a larger Session namespace. Child protocol names and historical proof identities stay exact. No feature, platform expansion, repository rename, beta release or supervisor interruption.

## Prerequisites and reference gate
User selected workspace/tab/pane/terminal on 2026-10-07 after comparison. Eon baseline 8578cf81275a2a61eefdc0d4cc5a72cb1485f904; Runtime 9780ccff908a7e5e506351ad017f219697e17681. Orbit pin 6bc269c40b18f08b95778939518f77556ba91c67 and Venus a27aad23822d3bd0b0e467ffc32c578bbde8b00d remain the latest accepted source revisions; child HEADs add only proof/planning/docs. No duplicate terminology bead or active implementation frontier found.
References inspected: Eon architecture Naming boundary and EON-C1/C8/C10/C15/C23, Runtime help/human workspace/generation output and Orbit launch identity. Primary Herdr concepts https://herdr.dev/docs/concepts/ (session=server namespace; workspace/tab/pane), Rex CLI https://www.superlogical.com/rex/docs/automate/cli (session/window/block; immutable IDs vs labels), and Zellij https://zellij.dev/tutorials/basic-functionality/ (session contains tabs and panes), accessed 2026-10-07. Web docs identify terminology, not adopted mechanism or source reuse. Prefer current owners and text-only corrections; no dependency.

## Acceptance
- Public prose and human Eon/EonTerm output identify Orbit-backed instances as terminals and explain workspace/tab/pane/view ownership.
- Help remains aligned/readable at 80 columns; attach/Stop, generation listing, workspace output and representative failure text use terminal wording.
- Existing technical IDs, JSON fields and exact wire/codec bytes remain unchanged. One consuming regression covers terminology alongside actual identity preservation, without mirroring every string.
- Exact producer acceptance, downstream pin/build checks, profile synchronization and isolated installed observation pass; live user terminals and desktop focus survive.
- Current docs, changelog, LOC and generated local agent overlay agree. Historical IDs/revisions/proof quotations are preserved; proof is stamped with exact candidate and scope.

title: Wrap directional tab and pane traversal at workspace edges
description:
## User-visible contract

Consumer: one local Eon workspace user.

Trigger: the user invokes semantic focus left, right, up, or down through the CLI or the existing Venus shortcuts while the selected tab or pane is at that ordered axis edge.

Result:
- With at least two tabs, left from the first tab selects the last tab and right from the last tab selects the first.
- With at least two panes in the active tab, up from the first pane selects the last pane and down from the last pane selects the first.
- Non-edge movement keeps its current adjacent-target behavior.
- Moving between tabs preserves each tab own selected pane.

With only one target on an axis, the direction remains unavailable and does not report a successful self-focus. A pending tab with no pane, modal directory picker, unknown identity, or invalid workspace state retains its existing bounded failure and last accepted topology.

The user selected circular edge traversal on 2026-08-26. This changes EON-C8 current direction-without-target and non-wrapping behavior; it creates no new EONW version, action, keybinding, or child contract.

## Ownership and evidence

Eon workspace focus policy is the sole owner. Venus continues to emit the existing semantic directional actions and render the resulting authoritative EONW snapshot. Orbit Sessions, PTYs, terminal state, pane lifetime, and working directories are untouched.

Current crates/eon/src/workspace.rs uses checked subtraction and explicit upper-bound failures in focus_direction. README documents traversal "without wrapping", and the original eon-pxn.1 proof explicitly rejected wrapping. The new behavior belongs at that shared Eon owner rather than in CLI or Venus callers.

## Reference gate

Required before code: current AGENTS.md; EON-C8; eon-pxn.1 historical decision/proof; focus_direction, dispatch, CLI parsing, process-level action checks, pending-tab picker rules, and exact current Venus VEN-C8 shortcut consumer. Inspect exact current Zellij directional-focus wrapping only as a comparable interaction; copy no code or broader layout behavior.

Rejected: per-caller wrapping, Venus-owned topology, configurable wrap policy, cross-axis traversal, arbitrary layout graphs, focus history, new keybindings, protocol changes, and dependencies.

## Scope boundary

In scope: Eon directional focus transition policy, focused deterministic and process-level proof, EON-C8/current docs/changelog, README LOC, exact Nix build/profile refresh, and one installed native observation.

Out of scope: focus-by-ID behavior, pane/tab creation or deletion, picker modal policy, reordering, split trees, simultaneous panes, new shortcuts, Orbit/Venus code, configuration, persistence, or platform expansion.

## Acceptance Criteria

The structured acceptance_criteria field is authoritative. Both axes wrap only when at least two targets exist, ordinary movement and failure atomicity remain intact, and the existing CLI/Venus action path is proved without a protocol or keybinding change.
design:
1. Write one deterministic red check at the existing Workspace action owner covering both axes, both edges, ordinary adjacent movement, remembered per-tab pane selection, and the one-target failure.
2. Change only focus_direction. Use the existing ordered vectors and selected indices directly; add no abstraction, configuration, or dependency.
3. Preserve dispatch atomicity and current errors for empty/pending axes, modal picker restrictions, unknown IDs, duplicate request handling, and invalid state.
4. Prove the existing control/CLI projection returns the wrapped authoritative snapshot. No EONW or Venus protocol change is expected.
5. Update EON-C8 and current user documentation, build the exact Nix candidate, refresh the active eon profile without restarting live supervisors, and dogfood the existing Venus shortcuts on a fresh isolated surface.
acceptance_criteria:
1. With at least two tabs, left from index zero selects the final tab and right from the final tab selects index zero. Intermediate left/right movement remains adjacent and every tab retains its selected pane.
2. With at least two panes in the active tab, up from index zero selects the final pane and down from the final pane selects index zero. Intermediate up/down movement remains adjacent and no other tab changes.
3. With exactly one tab or one pane, directional focus on that axis returns the existing unavailable failure and leaves the topology byte-for-byte unchanged.
4. Pending tabs with no pane, an active directory picker, unknown/stale identities, duplicate requests, invalid transitions, and malformed actions retain bounded failures with no partial mutation.
5. Focus movement never starts, stops, detaches, replaces, or changes an Orbit Session, pane directory, tab directory, picker, or child process.
6. CLI human and JSON output plus the existing Venus shortcuts consume the same wrapped Eon action result. No new keybinding, action value, EONW version, compatibility adapter, configuration, dependency, or child-repository edit is introduced.
7. The focused red/green transition check, affected process-level workspace control check, locked Rust checks, manifest check, Nix build, installed profile refresh, fresh native dogfood, README LOC, EON-C8, changelog after acceptance, and git diff pass on one immutable candidate.
8. Profile refresh preserves live supervisors and Sessions; no running Eon process is restarted without explicit user authorization.
notes: Priority P1: high-frequency workspace ergonomics, but lower urgency than the P0 continuous-output scrollback regression. Independent of the scrollback fix; no false dependency is added.

title: Restore link hover highlight and target preview in Eon
description:
## Why

Lucca reported on 2026-10-19 that hovering a link in Eon no longer highlights it, while Ctrl+click
still opens it. Lucca sees this in the installed `eon` and in their Eon build with a modified Orbit
("eon-bend"/"eon-bead"), which they are using now. VEN-C5 (venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md) requires "The
hovered link is highlighted and its escaped target is shown with Open and Copy actions", and
venus/docs/INTERACTION.md says the same. Ctrl+click opens only the current hovered target, so hover
detection still works; only the hover presentation is missing.

## Evidence (edge d4960d4, source reading only, not reproduced yet)

- Hover focus: application.rs `pointer_link`, `inspect_pointer_link`, `focused_link`. The highlight
  is `highlighted_link = self.focused_link()` and is passed to `Renderer::set_hyperlink`
  (application.rs ~2694, ~2724), which is the same focus Ctrl+click uses.
- Drawing: render.rs `build_hyperlink` draws a 1px hollow rectangle (137,180,250) around the link in
  the workspace path, after the scene rectangles and before the card separators and outlines.
- Target preview: `link_status` becomes the status line through `status()`.
- Recent candidate causes, all on 2026-10-18: ab697a2 (panes drawn as gapped rounded cards, with the
  shortcut hints moved bare below the cards) and the flush-sheet commits before it (00e282d,
  cca9f14). Hypotheses to test: the status line or notice that carried the target preview is no
  longer drawn in workspace mode; the outline is clipped or covered under the new card geometry;
  hover no longer triggers a redraw.
- First step: find out whether the outline, the target preview, or both are missing, then bisect
  with ab697a2^ if needed.

## Contract

VEN-C5, unchanged. This restores existing behavior; no contract edit.

## Acceptance

- In an installed Eon workspace on Linux, hovering an OSC 8 link draws its highlight and shows its
  escaped target. Ctrl+click and Ctrl+Shift+C still work.
- This also holds with pane frames on and in a non-first column.

## Verification

- A focused render or application test that would have failed on the regression, if the cause is
  deterministic logic (AP-TEST-001: name the failure it catches).
- One isolated installed dogfood observation of hover, highlight and target preview (for example
  `printf '\e]8;;https://example.com\e\\link\e]8;;\e\\\n'`), plus the profile refresh.

## Scope boundary

Restore VEN-C5 hover presentation only. Heuristic URL detection, new schemes and restyling the
highlight are out of scope. The "eon-bend" variant is not in this repository; confirming it there
is a dogfood note, not a change.

Portability: neutral (Venus rendering).
close_reason: Not a regression: VEN-C5 OSC 8 hover, highlight, preview and actions work in stock Eon (isolated reproduction, see comments). The real gap is plain-text URLs, which Lucca decided should highlight; tracked in eon-nlcy.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Narrowed (Lucca, 2026-10-19): hovering a link changes nothing. The outline and the target preview are both missing, while Ctrl+click still opens the link. Source reading (edge d4960d4, not reproduced): CursorMoved calls inspect_pointer_link, which sets links.focus from pointer_link() and calls refresh_client_view; the Ctrl press path calls the same pointer_link(). So both use the same hit test, and the likely break is between hover focus and presentation: hover does not trigger a redraw or presentation update, or focus is cleared before the frame (refresh_client_view clears it when focused_link() is None; the CursorMoved over-scrollback branch sets it to None). First check: log links.focus and highlighted_link on hover in an isolated session before bisecting from ab697a2^.

The text inside the OSC 8 link is not drawn at all, so there is nothing to hover. Nushell emits a correct sequence (checked: ESC ]8;;https://example.com ESC \ example ESC ]8;; ESC \). title: Clear a ProgramStatus request whose reply header fails to decode
description:
## Report

A reviewer on eon-agent-sidebar-yx8.6 (eon-b6, 2026-10-22, edge e87b9f8) found this outside that
diff, in code eon-agent-sidebar-yx8.10 landed (7267b8a, "Read ProgramStatus replies on Runtime
leases without misreading Stop or EOF"). Lucca approved filing it (2026-10-22).

## Defect (reviewer finding; confirm first)

If a ProgramStatus reply header fails to decode, `advance_program_status` (eon-runtime) leaves the
request in flight. That terminal's program status then stays stale, because no new request is
sent, and a later Stop drain on that lease returns the decode error instead of stopping cleanly.

## Expected

A malformed or undecodable ProgramStatus reply ends that request: it's logged, the request
clears, and the terminal's status becomes "unknown" or keeps its last value under the EON-C31 rule.
Status polling resumes on a later poll. Stop is never blocked or failed by an old bad reply.
If the lease itself is no longer trustworthy after a framing error, it's retired the documented
way, not left half-open.

## Contract

EON-C31 (agent attention, Runtime model) and the lease and Stop rules yx8.10 relies on. Check
whether the intended failure behavior is already stated. If not, bring Lucca the exact wording
before code.

## Scope

In scope: confirming the path with a focused unit test (red first), the fix in
`advance_program_status` and its Stop drain interaction, and the contract text if needed.
Out of scope: the ProgramStatus wire format, and sidebar presentation (yx8.7 and yx8.3).

## Acceptance

- A Runtime unit test feeds an undecodable reply header. The request clears, the next poll sends a
  fresh request, and Stop on that lease succeeds.
- No change to well-formed replies.

## Verification

`nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime`, plus fmt and clippy.
close_reason: An Orbit that stops on its own signal, and any unsolicited, undecodable or unexpected bytes on a terminal's lease, now affect only that terminal; the supervisor no longer fails (EON-C15 text approved by Lucca 2026-10-22). Proven by eon-test (eon-runtime, eon) and the eon and eonbase package builds on tree cdf3d2d.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Escalation (Lucca, 2026-10-22 ~22:15 -03): raised to P1 and widened. At 22:06:58 Lucca's supervisor g1-caca13d0 (installed ckisr53k, EONW 15) failed with 'supervisor failed: terminal sent an unsolicited management result' (~/.local/state/eon/logs/g1-caca13d0b514d3f810ccd8ca773d498b-1792695618-251291.log). That error comes from session_finished (runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/sessions.rs:1356), whose `?` carries it up to the supervisor loop. The window closed (VEN-C14), and the terminals were orphaned in Orbit with no supervisor. The trigger: the overseer sent SIGTERM to a Claude agent (eon-a2) in one terminal; about ten earlier SIGTERMs that day didn't crash it, so it's a race. Inference, unconfirmed: a ProgramStatus reply was in flight, or arrived after the request state cleared, when the terminal ended. Widened goal: no per-terminal management anomaly (undecodable header, unsolicited or late reply, framing error) ever fails the supervisor. It's confined to that terminal: logged, status unknown, lease retired the documented way, terminal end still reaped and reported. Acceptance gains a deterministic Runtime test that writes an unsolicited reply byte before EOF on a terminal's lease and asserts the supervisor keeps running and the other terminals stay unaffected. Contract check: EON-C31 and the EON-C11/EON-C14 failure rules. If the 'fatal' behavior is contracted anywhere, bring Lucca the wording. Runs before yx8.7 and shn4.2.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Trigger confirmed (overseer, 2026-10-22). The 22:06:58 kill was `kill -TERM $(pgrep -f 'claude prime, then continue eon-agent-sidebar-yx8.7' | head -1)`. pgrep -f matches full command lines, and the Orbit host's ends with `-- claude prime, then continue ...`. pgrep lists PIDs in ascending order, so head -1 picked the Orbit host (the parent), not claude. The earlier kills that day took claude's PID from ~/.claude/sessions and logged 'ended with status 143'. Mechanism (source, edge 6edf631): under ORB-C12, Orbit takes a host SIGTERM as an explicit stop. orbit/src/host.rs finish_management(ExplicitStop) writes an ExplicitStop tombstone and calls reply_stopped (orbit/src/management.rs:387), which writes an unrequested Stopped(tombstone) on the held lease. Runtime's EOF probe (session_finished, sessions.rs:1356) reads that as 'unsolicited management result' and its ? fails the supervisor. Even with no Stopped bytes, the probe finalizes with NaturalExit, and wait_and_finalize_tombstone rejects the ExplicitStop tombstone ('final record does not match'), which is also fatal. Separately, a ProgramStatus header that fails to decode makes advance_program_status return Err with the request left in flight, so every later EOF probe or Stop drain on that lease errors (the original finding). Deterministic repro: SIGTERM the Orbit host of a leased_orbit test run.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Red (edge 6edf631 plus two new tests only; nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime ends_only_its; x86_64 Linux): an_orbit_stopped_by_a_signal_ends_only_its_terminal fails with 'terminal sent an unsolicited management result' after SIGTERM to a real leased Orbit host, which is the production error. an_undecodable_or_unsolicited_result_ends_only_its_request fails with 'invalid terminal program status result: invalid management magic' from session_finished. Proposed EON-C15 wording is with Lucca (Result: an Orbit that stops on its own termination signal is reconciled like a natural exit; Important failures: lease anomalies fail only that terminal's in-flight request, and the lease is kept). The fix waits for approval.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Decision (Lucca, 2026-10-22): 'approve' accepts all four recommendations. (1) The EON-C15 wording as proposed, Result plus Important failures. (2) After an anomaly the lease is kept, not retired: dropping it would orphan a live run (ORB-C13), and Stop already waits for the tombstone. (3) No separate log line; the terminal's end is already logged. (4) One CHANGELOG line.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Review ledger (candidate tree 034b89a on edge 6edf631): pass 1 converged. Claude found 0 blocking and 4 nits, not applied: a stricter is_err assert in the undecodable test; the tests drive session_finished, not the supervisor loop; a leftover-garbage Stop reads 'wrong stop result' and fails without waiting for the tombstone; Orbit's reply_stopped can interleave with a partly flushed reply. Codex gpt-6.1-sol xhigh found 0. The repro of the 22:06:58 trigger is an_orbit_stopped_by_a_signal_ends_only_its_terminal, which SIGTERMs a real leased Orbit host: red before the fix with the production error, green after. Final proof after rebase (overseer, AGENTS lifecycle route): nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime -p eon, plus nix build #default #eonbase (the package check runs the release-Orbit Stop-under-load test).

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Proof, tree cdf3d2d, the eon-wt6l change rebased onto edge be5273a8; x86_64 Linux, sandboxed nix develop, CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=6. (1) nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-runtime -p eon passes: eon-runtime 80 passed, 1 ignored; eon workspace_control 39 passed. Includes both new tests, red before the fix (see the red comment). (2) nix build path:<tree>#default #eonbase passes: eon-0.1.1 /nix/store/j283p7l9paw4cjkjchbabjf8kws7i1r9 and eonbase-0.1.1 /nix/store/3npi3gnrdnmac3s6xx3lsw1apvck96qy. The eon package check ran all 81 eon-runtime tests, including the release-Orbit stop_waits_only_orbit_answer_time_for_an_in_flight_reply_under_pty_load: median 86us, p99 802us, max 1.23ms. (3) Earlier on the same code: cargo fmt --check and clippy -D warnings for eon-runtime are clean. The checks left the tree unchanged. Not run: the profile refresh (Lucca runs it after landing) and installed dogfood of a signalled Orbit in a live window, which is not to be triggered there.

title: Copied wrapped text loses characters at row joins
description:
## Why

Lucca, 2026-10-21: text copied from an Eon terminal and pasted elsewhere came
out corrupted. Copy silently changes what the user copied, so pasted prompts,
commands and notes can be wrong without anyone noticing.

## Evidence

Lucca copied a four-bullet message (wrapped across several rows in the
terminal) and pasted it. The original and the paste differ at row joins:

- "It is a record of one issue's investigation, not a pattern guide" pasted as
  "It is a record of one isstern guide": 29 characters gone.
- "the smallest way to reuse the queries, as the issue asked" pasted as
  "the smallest way to reussked": 29 characters gone.
- "Some scenarios may be tested twice" pasted as "Swice": 29 characters gone.
- "has no description" pasted as "has nodescription", and "a quick check for"
  as "a quick checkfor": the space at a row join is gone.
- Every pasted line also starts with two spaces, the indentation as drawn.

Both patterns sit at points where one terminal row continues on the next, so
the copied text likely joins wrapped rows wrongly. The exact source program,
terminal width and selection gesture (drag, triple or quadruple click) are not
yet recorded.

Owners: Orbit owns selection boundaries and copied text through libghostty
(ORB-C9, "Authoritative bounded selection and copy"; spans and logical lines
cross soft wraps). Venus owns the selection gesture and clipboard delivery
(VEN-C7, VEN-C13).

## Scope

In scope: reproduce in an isolated Eon with text that wraps across rows
(including a program that redraws, such as Claude Code); find which layer
drops the text (the program's own drawing, libghostty's text extraction,
Orbit's frozen copy, or Venus's clipboard delivery); fix it at that owner, or

than lost characters; rich-text copy.

  owning layer if one exists, else a retained reproducer.

title: Make the EON-C11 cgroup gate directly testable
description:
## Contract Routing

This hardens EON-C11's existing Linux cgroup launch gate without changing its observable policy.

Consumer: Eon immediately before it spawns an Orbit Session.

Trigger: Eon inspects its current unified cgroup-v2 membership within the shared launch deadline.

Result: launch proceeds only when the resolved cgroup directory is safe, user-owned, not writable by group or others, and contains Eon's exact PID. Missing, malformed, unsafe, foreign, or stale evidence fails explicitly. Retry timing remains owned by `wait_for_orbit_parent_cgroup`.

## Why

The 2026-08-28 audit found `current_cgroup_is_inheritable` at cyclomatic complexity 11, cognitive complexity 4, 0% coverage, and CRAP 132. The function is skipped under `EON_TEST_MANAGED_ORBIT`, so existing integration tests prove retry behavior but none of the security-sensitive membership, pathname, ownership, mode, or PID checks.

Impact HIGH, effort S/M, implementation risk MEDIUM because this is a launch trust boundary, confidence HIGH.

## Evidence

- `crates/eon/src/sessions.rs:746`: `current_cgroup_is_inheritable` directly reads `/proc/self/cgroup`, resolves beneath `/sys/fs/cgroup`, checks path components and directory metadata, then checks `cgroup.procs`.
- `crates/eon/src/sessions.rs:784`: retry policy is already separately injectable through `wait_for_orbit_parent_cgroup`.
- `crates/eon/src/sessions.rs:825`: managed-Orbit tests bypass the real cgroup inspection.
- `crates/eon/src/sessions.rs:1223`: current focused tests cover retry success and deadline failure only.
- `docs/CONTRACTS.md:389`: EON-C11 requires the exact user-owned, non-writable-by-others directory and own-process membership gate.

## Scope

In scope:
- `crates/eon/src/sessions.rs`.
- The smallest deterministic validation seam needed to test membership parsing, safe path resolution, directory ownership/mode, and exact PID membership.
- Focused unit tests for accepted and rejected evidence.
- Unchanged Linux filesystem observation and unchanged launch retry/deadline behavior.
- Required locked Rust/Nix proof and local profile refresh if production source changes.

Out of scope:
- A filesystem trait, mock framework, cgroup library, dependency, service-manager integration, cgroup creation/delegation, platform abstraction, macOS/X11 support, or wider lifecycle policy.
- Weakening validation so tests are easier.
- Splitting helpers solely to lower a score.

## Implementation Notes

1. Re-read EON-C7, EON-C11, the launch call path, and the complete existing cgroup gate.
2. Separate observation from deterministic validation at the smallest existing boundary. Prefer plain values or a direct helper; add no trait or generic provider.
3. Cover unified-hierarchy selection, required absolute path, unsafe components, directory kind/UID/mode, and exact line-based PID membership, including lookalike PIDs.
4. Keep `/proc/self/cgroup`, `/sys/fs/cgroup`, effective UID, and current PID observation in the Linux adapter that already owns them.
5. Preserve exact user-facing failures unless a current message is demonstrably misleading.
6. Rerun coverage-aware diagnostics, then the lifecycle-required Rust and Nix proof. Refresh the active `eon` profile from the working tree without restarting live supervisors.

## Verification

- `cargo test --locked -p eon sessions::tests` should exit 0 and exercise every deterministic cgroup validation class plus retry behavior.
- `cargo fmt --check` should exit 0.
- `cargo test --locked --workspace` should exit 0.
- `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` should exit 0.
- `cargo run --locked -p eon-manifest -- --check` should exit 0.
- `nix flake check --no-update-lock-file` should exit 0 for the unchanged component graph.
- `nix profile upgrade eon --flake .#default` should refresh the active profile from this working tree if production source changed; verify `nix profile list --json` resolves `eon` to the just-built store path.
- `git diff --check` should exit 0.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if a testable seam would duplicate cgroup policy or require a trait/dependency.
- Stop before changing the accepted ownership, mode, containment, deadline, or failure semantics.
- Stop before adding cgroup creation, delegation, service-manager, or portability behavior.
- Preserve live Sessions; do not restart the running supervisor without explicit user authorization.

## Maintenance Notes

The production owner should remain one small Linux adapter plus deterministic validation, not a reusable cgroup subsystem. cargo-crap is diagnostic only; no score threshold or CI policy is part of this issue.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Deterministic tests accept a valid unified cgroup-v2 membership and reject missing hierarchy, non-absolute or unsafe paths, wrong file kind/UID/mode, absent exact PID membership, and lookalike PID lines.
- The production observer still reads only the current Linux `/proc/self/cgroup`, resolved `/sys/fs/cgroup` directory, `cgroup.procs`, effective UID, and current PID, and `wait_for_orbit_parent_cgroup` retains its deadline/retry ownership.
- EON-C11's fail-closed ownership, mode, containment, and diagnostic behavior is unchanged; no validation is weakened or duplicated.
- Focused and complete locked Rust/Nix checks pass. If production source changes, the active `eon` profile resolves to the just-built working-tree artifact without restarting live supervisors.
- No filesystem trait, mock framework, cgroup dependency/subsystem, service-manager requirement, or platform expansion is introduced.
close_reason: Obsolete, not implemented: accepted eon-uj7 source 76b9f5635d9ae545dadb0326976f309afae8fd25 removed the entire cgroup preflight and retained the installed cgroup-free launch regression. EON-C11 no longer requires membership or delegation. Reintroducing this gate or its tests would contradict the current contract. User authorized backlog reconciliation on 2026-09-08.

title: Build a public interactive explainer for Eon
description:
## Why

Eon's defining behavior is easy to lose in architecture prose: a person can close the native window while the Orbit-owned Session keeps running, then reopen Eon and reconnect to the same work. One small interactive explainer can show that lifecycle before introducing subsystem names.

## Evidence

- `README.md:28-37` defines Eon and EonTerm as products, Sessions as the user-facing durability concept, and Orbit and Venus as engineering subsystems.
- `README.md:109-142` documents exact-generation launch, detach-only window close, surviving Sessions, and later presentation through `eon attach`.
- `docs/VISUAL-REFERENCES.md:8-17` pins System Atlas at `6b3c91bc54e638ff58699b04199d994369ba7e3c` as the preferred visual reference and records the ownership, reuse, narrow-screen, keyboard, and reduced-motion constraints.
- System Atlas uses progressive chapters and inspectable flows from one authored data model. Its MIT source includes a 104-line Node build script and a 396-line HTML renderer, but the current template is desktop-first and loads Google Fonts.

Impact: MEDIUM for onboarding and product explanation. Effort: M. Implementation risk: LOW if kept as a static documentation artifact. Confidence: HIGH.

## Scope

In scope:
- One release-stamped interactive explainer derived from accepted Eon documentation and exact component revisions.
- A short user-first sequence: open Eon; start work in a durable Session; close the window while work continues; reopen and reconnect; organize Sessions in the workspace; then inspect Eon, Orbit, and Venus ownership.
- Public product language before engineering names. The final technical chapter may expose the owner boundaries.
- One shareable static artifact with keyboard navigation, useful narrow-screen behavior, a reduced-motion mode, readable text alternatives, and no telemetry or required network assets.
- A source-reuse and toolchain gate comparing a small Eon-owned artifact with bounded reuse of the exact MIT System Atlas renderer.

Out of scope:
- Changing Eon, Orbit, Venus, EONW, ORBS, runtime behavior, installation, or product contracts.
- Creating Eon for the web, a website framework, a documentation platform, analytics, live product state, or remote access.
- Treating generated `SYSTEM.md`, atlas decisions, or atlas question IDs as canonical. Eon contracts, README, architecture docs, and Beads retain ownership.
- Adding Node, npm, a bundler, durable JavaScript, copied MIT source, an external font, or a publishing service without the required user and toolchain decision.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. One release-stamped static artifact explains open, durable work, detach, reconnect, workspace organization, and the Eon, Orbit, and Venus owner boundary without claiming behavior beyond the cited accepted Eon revision.
2. The default chapter order uses public product language; engineering subsystem names appear only in the final technical chapter or an explicit detail view.
3. A real-browser check passes on a wide desktop and narrow viewport with keyboard-only navigation, reduced motion, readable text alternatives, and offline loading.
4. Eon contracts, README, architecture docs, and Beads remain canonical. The artifact contains no duplicate decision store, question tracker, generated `SYSTEM.md` authority, telemetry, required network asset, runtime state, or Eon Web scope.
5. The issue records the selected implementation shape, exact source and license identity, user approval for any source reuse or non-Rust toolchain, build and validation command, owned LOC, replacement cost, revision label, and any approved publishing location. Canonical documentation links and the README LOC scorecard match the accepted files.

## Implementation Notes

1. Re-read the accepted Eon contracts, naming model, and exact component proofs. Record the release or proof revision represented by the explainer.
2. Inspect System Atlas at exact commit `6b3c91bc54e638ff58699b04199d994369ba7e3c`. Record its MIT terms, useful interaction mechanisms, rejected planning machinery, owned LOC, toolchain cost, and replacement cost.
3. Stop for user approval before source reuse, a durable non-Rust language, a build tool, or public hosting. Prefer an existing approved documentation surface and no package dependency.
4. Author the smallest chapter set that explains Session durability and workspace composition. Keep representative payloads hidden from the default public path.
5. Generate or author one artifact, verify it with a real browser, and link it from canonical docs only after its revision label and hosting location are stable.

## Verification

- `git diff --check` exits 0.
- `rg -n "Eon|EonTerm|Sessions|Orbit|Venus" README.md docs/ARCHITECTURE.md docs/CONTRACTS.md` confirms that the explainer's nouns and owner boundaries map to canonical text.
- The selected build or validation command recorded at the source-reuse and toolchain gate exits 0 and produces one self-contained static artifact.
- Manual browser checks cover a wide desktop, a narrow viewport, keyboard-only navigation, reduced motion, and offline loading. Every user-visible lifecycle claim cites the exact accepted Eon revision it represents.
- The README LOC scorecard and changed documentation links match the final tracked files.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if Eon's product naming or detach and reconnect behavior changes before authoring completes.
- Stop if the artifact would become another owner for contracts, decisions, questions, or runtime state.
- Stop for user choice if implementation requires a new language, dependency, copied source, external service, or public deployment.
- Stop if the explainer cannot communicate the user outcome without exposing speculative behavior.

## Maintenance Notes

Treat the explainer as a release-stamped projection, not a live architecture database. Update it when a public release changes one of its shown flows. Skip System Atlas's generated `SYSTEM.md`, question tracker, and decision table. No runtime dependency or Eon contract changes are expected.

title: Check that Venus picks up a Wayland output scale of 2 on Linux
description:
## Why

While proving kz4p.17 (a36f243), Venus's ignored live test ran on a private headless Sway 1.12
(pixman, 1600x900) with the output at scale 2. Venus logged only `venus: window scale factor 1` at
window creation and no change line within the test's 4 s. Either the test is too short to see the
compositor's scale arrive, or Venus on Linux does not pick up a Wayland output scale. The second
would mean blurry or wrongly sized rendering on HiDPI Linux displays, which is Eon's only proved
platform. No user has reported it.

## Contract

Venus renders at the window's scale factor (VEN contracts on presentation; see
venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md). This bead decides whether that holds on Wayland at scale 2; it changes
no contract by itself.

## Investigation

- Rerun the live test (or an isolated full Eon) on headless Sway with `output * scale 2` set before
  Venus starts, and long enough to see a `window scale factor` change line. The kz4p.17 recipe is
  on that bead's comments (eon-f2 livetest.sh, own user+PID namespace).
- If Venus stays at 1: check winit's Wayland scale path (wl_output scale, fractional-scale-v1,
  preferred_buffer_scale) against what headless Sway sends, and whether the surface ever enters the
  output.
- Record the observation and the cause on this bead.

## Acceptance

An isolated observation that names the scale Venus reaches on a scale-2 Wayland output, and either
"works, the test was short" or a filed fix bead with the cause.

## Scope

Investigation only; no Venus code change in this bead. Read venus/AGENTS.md first. Never use
Lucca's running Eon or desktop session.

title: Let eon pane create add a pane without taking focus (--no-focus)
description:
## Why

On 2026-10-22 the orchestrating agent, running in Lucca's Agent popup, started two agents with `eon pane create --json -- claude "..."` (eon-n6ga). Each launch dismissed the popup and selected the new pane, which took Lucca away from the conversation he was in. He asked: "should it steal focus, or mantain the popup? the current behaviour steals focus". Then he approved the recommendation below ("yeah").

## Decision (Lucca, 2026-10-22)

Add `--no-focus` to `eon pane create`, for both the plain and the `-- COMMAND` form. It adds the pane, but the caller's popup stays shown and the tab's selected pane does not change. The default stays as it is: the new pane is selected and a calling popup is dismissed. That matches Alt+M, today's EON-C10, and all four reference tools: tmux `-d`, Zellij `--no-focus`, kitty `--keep-focus`, and WezTerm, which always focuses. Orchestrating agents always pass `--no-focus`. Rejected: never focusing when a command is given. It differs from every comparable tool and from plain `pane create`, and users would have to switch to the pane by hand. Ship it on its own EONW bump (v16), but hold the profile refresh so that one restart covers it together with whatever lands alongside. Sharing yx8.7's bump was rejected because it would wait behind yx8.6/yx8.7.

## Evidence (edge 7849484)

- `docs/CONTRACTS.md` EON-C10 (calling-terminal bullet): "so `pane create` selects the new pane and dismisses the tab's popup".
- `runtime/crates/eon-runtime/src/workspace.rs`: `dispatch` selects the target pane before `apply`; `create_pane(target, called, ...)` and `dismiss_for_pane_action` do the dismissal.
- `runtime/crates/eon-workspace-protocol/src/v15.rs`: `WorkspaceAction::CreatePane` has no payload, and `Action::CreateCommandPane { argv }` (tag 27) has no focus field. Carrying the option needs an EONW change (v16).
- Reference evidence for the four tools at pinned revisions is on eon-n6ga (comment "Reference evidence").

## Scope

In scope: the EON-C10 text change (Lucca approves the exact wording before code); EONW v16 carrying a keep-focus flag on both pane-create requests; the Runtime behavior (no selection change, no popup dismissal, and the new pane placed exactly as now); CLI parsing of `--no-focus` in either flag order alongside `--json`; `eon --help`; `docs/USAGE.md`; `CHANGELOG.md`; `venus/CHANGELOG.md` (rename only); the component graph in a second commit, as eon-n6ga did (0c066f1 then 6c582e3).

Out of scope: Alt+M and the Commands popup "New pane" entry (they keep focusing); `eon edit`; focus flags on other commands.

## Acceptance

- From the Agent popup, `eon pane create --no-focus -- sh -c 'sleep 30'` adds a pane in the tab's selected column. The popup stays shown and `selected_pane` is unchanged in `eon workspace --json`.
- Without `--no-focus`, the behavior is identical to today.

## Verification

- Codec wire bytes and bounds tests, a Runtime unit test for popup and pane callers, and the end-to-end CLI test in `eon/crates/eon/tests/workspace_control.rs`, all through `nix develop -c eon-test -p eon-workspace-protocol -p eon-runtime -p eon`.
- Full affected Rust and Nix surfaces for the wire change, plus one isolated installed observation on headless Sway, with a popup caller.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop for Lucca's approval of the EON-C10 wording and the v16 bump timing.
- Stop if the cursor or selection model cannot add a pane without selecting it. Record why and ask.

Observation (2026-10-22, window g1-934c7cca): the overseer launched the eon-be, eon-77 and eon-ff agents with 'eon pane create --no-focus --json -- claude ...' from the Agent popup, and Lucca's focus stayed on the popup. comments.text:
Decision (Lucca, 2026-10-22 ~16:25 -03, "Approve as drafted"; confirmed to the coordinator as "1. ok"): EON-C10 gains this Result bullet after `pane create -- COMMAND`:

"`eon pane create --no-focus [--json]`, with or without `-- COMMAND`, adds the same pane in the same place but takes no focus: the tab's selected column and pane stay as they were, a shown popup stays shown, and the new pane joins the end of its column collapsed. In a tab without panes it becomes the tab's only, selected pane, and a shown popup still stays shown. Without `--no-focus`, `pane create` selects the new pane and dismisses the tab's popup, as above."

title: Benchmark Eon and EonTerm terminal memory
description:
## Outcome

Measure the Linux system-memory footprint of one idle and loaded terminal Session in full Eon and EonTerm against two controls on the same COSMIC Wayland machine:

- Foot: the lean independent full-terminal baseline. The installed package is foot 1.16.2 +pgo; upstream describes it as fast, lightweight, minimal, and Wayland-native.
- Ghostty: the same-engine full-GUI control. The installed snap is Ghostty 1.3.1 using the GTK runtime and OpenGL renderer.

This benchmark changes no EON product contract, runtime behavior, dependency, package, or platform promise. It is evidence for later optimization decisions only.

## Why both controls

EonTerm already uses libghostty inside Orbit. Ghostty is a useful related-engine GUI control, though its different engine revision, packaging, and renderer prevent isolating the cost of Eon's supervisor + Orbit + Venus split, while Foot tests whether the complete product is competitive with a deliberately lean independent terminal. Comparing only Alacritty or only libghostty would not answer either product question.

Mitchell Hashimoto's 2026-07-27 library benchmark is comparison evidence, not an Eon result: at 120×40 and 10,000 history rows, compressed libghostty reports 2.65–5.41 MiB versus alacritty_terminal 34.09–36.91 MiB; uncompressed libghostty reports 12.19–13.98 MiB. It measures terminal state in one shared Rust harness on macOS, not Linux GUI/process-tree cost.

Sources:
- https://x.com/mitchellh/status/2081788657078505732
- https://codeberg.org/dnkl/foot
- https://codeberg.org/dnkl/foot/src/branch/master/doc/benchmark.md
- https://github.com/ghostty-org/ghostty

## Contract and owner

Consumer: Eon product development.
Trigger: evaluate idle or scrollback memory cost before choosing optimization work.
Result: one reproducible table reports Eon, EonTerm, Ghostty, and Foot under identical workloads, with process-level attribution for Eon supervisor, Orbit, and Venus.
Important failures: do not compare RSS sums that double-count shared pages, different grid/font/scrollback settings, different child workloads, warm versus cold processes, or GUI memory against a terminal-state-only library number.

Eon owns this cross-product measurement. Orbit and Venus remain unchanged; a confirmed owner-specific problem must be separately chosen and routed before implementation.

## Method

- Use the installed COSMIC Wayland session and record kernel, compositor, GPU/backend, scale, exact executable/package revisions, configuration files, and environment.
- Recorded grid: 120×30, deviating from the planned 120×40 because of COSMIC startup geometry. Use 16 logical-pixel text, 18 logical-pixel row, opacity 1, and the same inert child. Orbit and Ghostty have 16 MiB history budgets; Foot requests 10,000 rows. Retained row counts are unmeasured; loaded labels describe emitted content.
- Measure empty, full-screen, and 10,000-row plain, styled, Unicode, and mixed workloads matching the published libghostty categories closely enough to state differences explicitly.
- Run at least 10 fresh processes per terminal after a fixed settle interval. Recorded cohort: 55 each for Eon, EonTerm and Foot, 54 for Ghostty; n=9 per workload except n=10 plain for Eon/EonTerm/Foot. The expanded 240-run plan was interrupted at 219; no ten-per-cell completion claim. Report median and empirical p05–p95 with actual counts.
- On Linux, sum proportional set size from /proc/*/smaps_rollup across each owned process tree; report unique/private memory when available. Report RSS only as secondary data. Exclude the identical child workload or show totals both with and without it.
- For Eon and EonTerm, report supervisor, Orbit, Venus, and total separately. Include all Ghostty/Foot descendants under the same rule.
- Keep any harness disposable unless repeated measurement proves a checked-in owner is worth maintaining. Do not add a benchmarking dependency.
- Do not count Nix closure size as runtime memory. Do not claim GPU memory unless a reliable backend-specific measurement is recorded separately.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. One table reports median and p05–p95 PSS for all four products and every workload under one recorded environment.
2. Eon and EonTerm process totals are attributable to supervisor, Orbit, Venus, and identical child; Foot and Ghostty use the same process-tree rule.
3. Grid, typography, opacity, scrollback, payload, child command, settle time, run count, warm/cold policy, and cleanup are identical or every unavoidable mismatch is explicit.
4. The result distinguishes terminal-state evidence from complete GUI/process memory and does not extrapolate Mitchell's macOS result to Linux.
5. Repeated runs leave no benchmark supervisors, Sessions, sockets, windows, or temporary configuration behind and do not stop existing Eon/Eonova Sessions.
6. Record raw observations or a lossless table, exact commands, summary, uncertainty, and whether any product-owned optimization is justified. Create no remediation bead without separate user approval.

## Scope boundary

No runtime edit, optimization, benchmark framework, CI job, dependency, child-repository change, terminal feature comparison, throughput claim, GPU-memory claim without evidence, or cross-platform conclusion. Stop if matching workloads would require changing user configuration or interrupting existing Sessions; use isolated temporary roots instead.
notes: Completed report: docs/benchmarks/eon-zlf-2026-09-08.md; lossless numeric observations: docs/benchmarks/eon-zlf-2026-09-08.csv (658 process rows, SHA256 f9477a676657e1744f213b382ab428a4b5eb22b4ed9d73b6eba3af5cc671cd24). Mechanically verified installed cohort: 219 runs, 55 Eon/EonTerm/Foot and 54 Ghostty, n=9 per cell except n=10 plain for Eon/EonTerm/Foot. Original minimum ten launches per terminal is met; expanded 240-run plan remains interrupted, with no ten-per-cell completion claim. Baseline edge dd74bacfdee000aa109f2bea855aa4651a7c04e7; installed runtime 0b0b6312531229270c157df31ba49800a6daef03, Venus ec80e36625dec73544c0cb64becf4b135c932a63, Orbit 91999d79546422b49bdbc124166a65859d0bd872. Exact COSMIC/Linux/artifacts/configs in report. Ghostty snap 820 is 1.3.1 ReleaseFast stable; official release list checked 2026-09-08 confirms latest stable, so no Home Manager change was needed. Installed packaging/renderer differences remain qualified. Summed PSS medians excluding identical child: empty Foot 11.21, EonTerm 71.05, Eon 71.20, Ghostty 182.61 MiB; mixed 24.73, 97.44, 97.40, 187.87 MiB. Venus is largest owner, but no waste or optimization is proved. Limits: 120x30 instead of planned 120x40, emitted history rather than measured retained rows, warm active host and uncontrolled focus/occlusion, related but unequal engine revisions/font bytes, no GPU-memory/long-term-growth claim. Three stray-input Foot runs flagged; exclusion sensitivity leaves ordering unchanged. Validation: offline analyze.py checks all scheduled labels, raw smaps fields, process identities/roles, geometry/barrier/settle, zero SwapPss and cleanup; independent CSV calculation verifies all 360 distributions.
