title: Zoom the selected pane across a tab's columns
description:
## Decision
Lucca, 2026-10-17: keep the shipped columns of accordions (`eon-splits-opwv`) as Eon's split model
and add zoom. Rows (one accordion whose open pane splits into up to four side-by-side terminals) was
considered and not chosen: it gives new panes full width, but hides everything outside the open pane
while switching, and costs another EON-C8/VEN-C8 change, an EONW revision and a conversion of saved
column workspaces. Layout presets (tmux `select-layout`, kitty `enabled_layouts`, Zellij swap
layouts, Nova's stacked/split families) were rejected for now: they add a second owner of the
arrangement beside the workspace structure (Nova needed eight named swap layouts plus
`zellij-pane-orchestrator`; Zellij leaves overflow placement unspecified). Revisit rows or presets
only with dogfood evidence that narrow column panes still hurt with zoom.

## Contract (provisional; approve before code)
- Consumer: a full-Eon user in a tab with one or more columns.
- Trigger: one zoom toggle shortcut (proposed Alt+Shift+Z: tmux's `z`; Alt+F would take the
  shell's forward-word) and its `eon` command if the design adds one.
- Result: the selected pane's terminal fills the tab's whole content area; other columns are hidden
  but their terminals keep running. Toggling again restores the same columns, widths and selection.
  The zoomed state is visible (header or Eon Bar indicator) and announced to accessibility, which
  lists only the zoomed column's panes while zoomed. The frame follows the flush workspace sheet of
  `eon-flush-workspace-sheet-5779` with no seam.
- Important failures: a hidden column's terminal stops or loses state; unzoom restores a different
  arrangement; keyboard input reaches a hidden terminal; a zoomed grid keeps the column-sized grid.

## Open design decisions (recommendation first)
- Persistence: transient Venus view state, not persisted across detach/attach (recommended: no
  EONW change), or Eon Runtime state in a new EONW revision.
- Actions while zoomed: Alt+H/L, Alt+K/J, Alt+M, Alt+Shift+M, Ctrl+Alt+K/J, close, and the
  sideways pane move (Ctrl+Alt+H/L) and tab move (Ctrl+Alt+Shift+H/L) of
  `eon-sideways-pane-moves-k9ca`. Recommended: any action that changes the selected column, moves a
  pane across columns or creates a column leaves zoom first; Alt+K/J and Ctrl+Alt+K/J within the
  zoomed column stay zoomed. Ghostty's default unzooms on any focus or layout change
  (`split-preserve-zoom`).
- Hidden columns' attachments: keep each attached at its column size (recommended: no Orbit resize
  churn on toggle) or detach while hidden.
- One-column tabs: zoom is a no-op with a notice, or still hides pane headers (recommended: no-op).
- Popups and pickers over a zoomed tab keep their current geometry.

## Owners
Eon owns the shortcut default and EON-C8's product text. Venus owns geometry, rendering, input,
focus and accessibility for the zoomed view (VEN-C8, VEN-C20 shortcut viewer, VEN-C24 hints). Eon
Runtime and EONW are unchanged: the 2026-10-22 approved design leaves the zoom chord unreserved,
so a user popup on it takes it as with other fixed bindings (EON-C20). Orbit is unchanged (one
resize per zoomed terminal through the existing path).

## Reference gate
Consequential: changes EON-C8 and VEN-C8, and possibly EONW. Before code, read the affected
`AGENTS.md`, both contracts and `docs/REFERENCES.md` routes, and inspect at exact revisions at least
Ghostty `toggle_split_zoom` (`~/pjs/yazelix-related/ghostty` 45db2c255) and WezTerm
`TogglePaneZoomState` (`~/pjs/yazelix-related/wezterm` 577474d); Zellij fullscreen
(`~/pjs/yazelix-related/zellij` 16beceaa0) is optional. Record constraints kept, rejected approaches,
the chosen design and its cheapest falsifying check here. Stop for Lucca's design and contract
approval before code. Portability: neutral.

## Prerequisites
After `eon-flush-workspace-sheet-5779`, so the zoomed frame is designed once on the decided sheet
and the two do not edit `venus/src/render/chrome.rs` in parallel (`eon-7rk3` closed 2026-10-17).

## Acceptance
- Design phase: Lucca approves the design, the EON-C8/VEN-C8 changes and the shortcut.
- Implementation: installed Eon zooms and unzooms the selected pane in a multi-column tab; hidden
  terminals keep running and reappear unchanged; input reaches only the zoomed terminal; shortcut
  viewer, hints, `docs/USAGE.md` and CHANGELOG list the binding; a user popup on the zoom chord takes
  it and Alt+/ lists zoom as overridden. Prove with the owners' existing harnesses plus one isolated
  installed dogfood observation; Venus fmt and clippy green; refresh the active Nix profile without
  interrupting live workspaces.

## Scope boundary
No rows, layout presets, column resizing, arbitrary split trees or Orbit protocol change. Adds no
platform promise.
close_reason: Alt+Shift+Z zooms the selected column across the tab as Venus view state; hidden columns keep running and attached; EON-C8/VEN-C8 updated. Venus suite, fmt and clippy green; isolated installed dogfood; profile refreshed. Proof and ledger in comments.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Design approved by Lucca, 2026-10-22 (eon-43 session).

Reference gate. Read root, venus/ and runtime/ AGENTS.md, EON-C8, VEN-C8, EON-C20 (reserved popup keys), docs/REFERENCES.md "Terminal workspace experience", venus/docs/REFERENCES.md "Rounded pane frames" and "Required for shared popup presentation".
- Ghostty 45db2c255 (local checkout ~/pjs/refs/ghostty-7501/repo): the per-tab split tree holds `zoomed: ?Node.Handle` (src/datastruct/split_tree.zig:59-62). A single leaf refuses zoom (apprt/gtk/class/application.zig:2689-2691). A new split resets zoom (split_tree.zig:566-567). goto_split unzooms unless `split-preserve-zoom = navigation` (Config.zig:1089-1103, 8681-8683). Only the zoomed subtree is laid out, so hidden surfaces get no size updates. The tab title gets a 🔍 prefix (gtk/class/tab.zig:529-532). No zoom-specific accessibility.
- WezTerm e2a98e1 (the only local clone, shallow; 577474d unavailable): per-tab `zoomed` plus `size_before_zoom` (mux/src/tab.rs:40-49). `resize` resizes only the zoomed pane, and unzoom re-runs layout at the current size (891-912, 1139-1147). `unzoom_on_switch_pane` defaults true, and with it off the switch is silently dropped (1439-1453, config.rs:835). Splitting while zoomed is refused or unzooms (1925-1927, 1966-1968; issue #723). `[Z]` title prefix. A single pane can be zoomed, so an indicator shows with no effect.
- Zellij 16beceaa0 (~/pjs/nova/nova-zellij): per-tab `fullscreen_is_active` (tiled_panes/mod.rs:71). Hidden panes keep their geometry and are not rendered. Navigation moves the fullscreen along (2591-2596). A new split, close or relayout exits. A single pane is a no-op. "(FULLSCREEN)" on the tab bar.
Constraints kept: one zoom reference per tab, not per pane; hidden terminals are not resized while zoomed; structural change ends zoom; refuse a one-column zoom; an indicator at tab level. Rejected: move-the-zoom navigation (Zellij, Ghostty `navigation`), because it needs more rules; WezTerm's silently dropped switch; persisting zoom (WezTerm's wire field, Ghostty's macOS restore path), because it needs an EONW revision for view state; reserving the chord from popups (would change EON-C20's reserved set; every other fixed binding is popup-overridable and listed as overridden in Alt+/).

Approved design (EON-C8 and VEN-C8 gain a zoom bullet; VEN-C20 and VEN-C24 list the binding):
- Alt+Shift+Z toggles zoom of the active tab's selected column. Not reserved: a user popup on that key takes it and Alt+/ lists zoom as overridden (existing EON-C20 rule). No Runtime, EONW, Orbit or `eon` command change. CHANGELOG records the binding (not as a breaking change).
- Zoomed: the selected column's card covers the tab's whole card area (the area a popup card covers) and shows that column's headers and terminal at full width. It is one gapped rounded card (`ab697a2` replaced the flush sheet this bead assumed). Other columns stay attached at their last column size and keep running. They are not drawn, hit-tested, resized or listed to accessibility while zoomed. Unzoom restores the same columns, widths and selection at the current window size.
- Zoom is transient Venus view state: not persisted, and not restored by a new window or attach.
- Zoom lasts while the active tab, its column count and its selected column index stay the same. Any change ends it: Alt+H/L (unzoom, then move), tab focus, column creation, sideways moves, or closing the zoomed column's last pane. Alt+K/J, Ctrl+Alt+K/J, Alt+M, and closing a pane that leaves the column non-empty stay zoomed.
- A one-column tab consumes the shortcut without zooming and shows a rejected-action notice. While a popup or picker covers the tab, the toggle is consumed without effect. A popup over a zoomed tab keeps its usual geometry, and the zoomed view returns when it hides.
- Indicator: the active tab pill shows a zoom marker while zoomed, and its accessible name says zoomed. The tab panel is named "Zoomed column N of M" and lists only that column's panes.
- Cheapest falsifiers: Scene tests (the zoomed geometry spans the card area; hidden columns are absent from draw, hit and accessibility), a model/application test of the end-of-zoom rule, and one isolated installed dogfood observation.
Portability: neutral.

title: Make the Nix-free Linux bundle namespace-free
description:
## Why

The Nix-free Linux bundle is a No-Go as built. Evidence is on eon-qualify-nix-free-linux-public-beta-lm9p (comment of 2026-10-18; candidate ef238be, archive sha256 5f08ec4d...):
- Stock Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS (kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=1) cannot start it. `eon --help` and `eon versions` exit 1 with "bwrap: setting up uid map: Permission denied", denied by AppArmor's unprivileged_userns profile. Only a root-installed per-path AppArmor profile makes it run.
- On every host, the user namespace and bwrap's PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS reach every Orbit terminal: sudo, su, pkexec and setuid helpers fail, root-owned files show as nobody:nogroup, and supplementary groups collapse to nogroup. orb-prove-no-survivor-session-shutdown-btg already rejected unmapped root as "not an acceptable Orbit terminal contract".

User decision (Lucca, 2026-10-18): open this redesign. Lucca accepted the recommended direction, namespace-free relocation, as the starting hypothesis; the mechanism itself is still decided by the first child.

## Outcome

A user-owned extracted Eon bundle starts on stock Ubuntu 26.04 LTS without root, AppArmor changes, or user namespaces. Every Orbit terminal it spawns behaves like a native host terminal (no NoNewPrivs, real uid/gid/groups, sudo works where the host allows it). Nix and direct delivery keep consuming the one canonical component graph (EON-C2, EON-C6), and EON-C5's install/upgrade/rollback/remove lifecycle and eon-install stay intact.

## Acceptance

- On a fresh stock Ubuntu 26.04 LTS VM with no Nix, verify plus extract plus `eon versions`, `eon --help`, and the eon-install dry run and install all succeed with no root step.
- Inside an Eon terminal from the bundle, /proc/self/status shows NoNewPrivs 0, `id` matches the host, `stat -c %U /usr/bin/sudo` shows root, and `sudo -n true` behaves as on the host.
- The candidate is ready for lm9p's qualification matrix (Ubuntu 26.04 and 24.04, Fedora Workstation).

## Children

Mechanism decided on eon-zti4.1 (closed 2026-10-18): host-glibc relink, GLIBC_2.42 floor first, host Vulkan driver, approved EON-C6 host-input statement, new installer layout only. In order:
1. eon-zti4.2 Make Eon shell integration location-neutral (after eon-8olu).
2. eon-zti4.3 Relink the eon closure for the host glibc as a Nix check.
3. eon-zti4.4 Replace bundle makeWrapper scripts with a static launcher env table.
4. eon-zti4.5 Relocate compiled-in data roots for the relinked bundle.
5. eon-zti4.6 Switch manual-bundle and eon-install to the relinked layout.
6. eon-zti4.7 Update bundle docs and the EON-C6 host-input statement.
7. eon-zti4.8 Lower the bundle glibc floor to 2.39 for Ubuntu 24.04 (after eon-8olu).
8. eon-zti4.9 Prove the namespace-free bundle on Ubuntu 26.04 and 24.04 (last; hands the candidate to lm9p).

## Scope boundary

No release, tag, signing anchor, publication, new distribution channel (deb, rpm, Flatpak, Snap, AppImage), or support expansion. No change to Orbit's terminal contracts except removing the namespace from the bundle's launch path. macOS is out of scope.
close_reason: All children closed; acceptance met by eon-zti4.9 (stock Ubuntu 26.04.1 and 24.04.5 VMs, no root step, no namespace). Candidate b396b4a2... handed to lm9p. Closed by Lucca's decision, 2026-10-19.

title: Decide the namespace-free relocation mechanism for the Linux bundle
description:
## Why

The bundle must leave user namespaces, but a Nix closure is full of absolute /nix/store references, so the mechanism that replaces bwrap's /nix projection is a consequential code shape (AGENTS.md reference gate: dependency, lifecycle and trust boundary). That choice needs evidence before any implementation slice. Parent epic and No-Go evidence: see the parent and eon-qualify-nix-free-linux-public-beta-lm9p.

## Evidence

- bundle/src/main.rs:8-16: entrypoint execs libexec/bwrap --unshare-user with the host root bound and the bundle's nix/ ro-bound at /nix, then runs EON_BUNDLE_PROGRAM.
- nix/linux-bundle.nix:3,9,11,31-41: static pkgsStatic.bubblewrap helper; the closure of eonPackage copied whole via closureInfo.
- flake.nix:616-620: manual-bundle consumes eonPackage plus components/eon-alpha-v3.json and flake.lock.
- docs/MANUAL-BUNDLE.md "Execution and host boundary": the current bwrap /nix projection and its "no ELF/config path rewriting" decision, which this bead may supersede.
- Prior candidate: 488 MB archive, about 1.8 GB unpacked closure.

## Scope

In scope:
- An inventory of /nix/store references in the candidate closure, split by kind: ELF PT_INTERP, RUNPATH, dlopen targets (Vulkan ICD and loader, Wayland, xkbcommon, fontconfig), script shebangs, wrapper scripts, and text or config references (Nushell, Helix runtime, Yazi, LazyGit, Anima, terminfo, fonts, CA certificates). Name which components run inside Orbit terminals and which only in Venus.
- A comparison, with sources and inspected revisions, of: (a) a static launcher invoking the bundled ld.so with --library-path (Exodus pattern; fzakaria 2026-06-21 "Nix needs relocatable binaries"); (b) static or musl builds for eon, Orbit, eon-install and the managed CLI tools; (c) install-time prefix rewriting with padded placeholders (the conda pattern, which needs a long storeDir and a world rebuild); (d) a hybrid where only Venus is relocated and terminals run fully static tools; (e) rejected references: bwrap or userns (this No-Go), PRoot (nix-portable fallback; ptrace overhead, and it would also wrap terminals), and Guix -RR packs (userns by default).
- A throwaway prototype of the chosen mechanism on the riskiest piece (Venus rendering through the host or bundled Vulkan on Wayland), plus one terminal tool, run from an extracted directory with no /nix.

Out of scope:
- Changing the shipped bundle, docs/MANUAL-BUNDLE.md, docs/CONTRACTS.md or installer code. Those belong to later children after acceptance.
- Distribution channels, signing, publication.

## Acceptance

- The bead records the inventory counts by kind, the chosen mechanism, rejected alternatives with reasons, its dependency and version policy and exit condition, the effect on EON-C2/C5/C6 and on the MANUAL-BUNDLE decision, and the GPU stance (host driver or bundled lavapipe).
- The prototype shows red/green evidence: on a stock Ubuntu 26.04 VM (cloud image, no Nix), the prototype Venus window or headless render plus the terminal tool run without userns, and NoNewPrivs is 0 in the spawned shell.
- It proposes ordered implementation children for the epic, each sized for one session. They are not filed until Lucca accepts.

## Implementation Notes

1. Build `nix build .#manual-bundle --out-link <scratch>/mb` and inventory references with `readelf -l/-d`, `file`, and `grep -rl /nix/store` over the extracted nix/ tree.
2. Read the reference sources and record the inspected revisions.
3. Prototype in scratch space only. VM recipe: lm9p's 2026-10-18 comment (official cloud image, cloud-init NoCloud seed via cloud-localds, qcow2 overlay, QEMU -display none, SSH on a forwarded port, QMP socket under a path shorter than 108 bytes).

## Verification

- The VM run outputs (`eon`-equivalent prototype exit 0, `grep NoNewPrivs /proc/self/status` showing 0 inside its child shell) are recorded in the bead with the image sha256, kernel and prototype source revision.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop and ask Lucca if every viable mechanism needs root, a new distribution channel, or a contract change beyond EON-C5's bundle mechanism.
- Stop if the inventory shows a component that cannot be made relocatable without forking it.

## Maintenance Notes

- Desktop focus: run GUI checks headless (VM or isolated compositor), never on Lucca's desktop.
- Run tests only through `nix develop -c eon-test`.
close_reason: Mechanism decided and accepted by Lucca (host-glibc relink, GLIBC_2.42 floor first, host Vulkan driver, EON-C6 host-input statement approved, new installer layout only). Inventory, references, red/green prototype on stock Ubuntu 26.04 and the ordered children are recorded in comments; children await a separate go-ahead to file.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Reference gate, inventory, prototype and recommendation (2026-10-18). Repo edge 7f56e37 (untracked review-corners.md is not part of this work). Candidate eon package /nix/store/sqlb0nca8h6bs8c48xrnv3k0is6898kl-eon-0.1.1 (same manual-bundle /nix/store/qb3svi8f...-eon-0.1.1-x86_64-linux-bundle as lm9p's No-Go). No repository code changed; the prototype lived in session scratch only.

INVENTORY (412 store paths, 2.11 GB, 15,103 regular files; scanned every file):
- ELF: 1,224. 250 executables carry PT_INTERP, all the same nixpkgs glibc-2.42-61 ld-linux-x86-64.so.2; 962 shared objects; 12 static. 929 have /nix/store RUNPATHs. 104 contain other compiled-in store paths (data roots): glibc gconv/locale/ld.so.cache, helix-runtime (hx), zsh fpath/module dir/zshenv, bash and bash-interactive lib dirs, fish (python3, awk, vendor dirs), ncurses default terminfo, libxkbcommon XKB and Compose roots, openssl etc/ssl and engines, krb5 config, libX11 locale, mesa drirc, libdrm/libpciaccess id tables, man-db/groff, and inert nixpkgs tzdata/iana-etc fallbacks in Go binaries (lazygit, fzf, carapace).
- dlopen targets: Venus loads libwayland-client, libvulkan and libxkbcommon by name through the makeWrapper LD_LIBRARY_PATH; vulkan-loader finds Mesa ICD manifests via XDG_DATA_DIRS (mesa share) whose library_path is an absolute store path; fonts come from FONTCONFIG_FILE, a store fonts.conf with absolute <dir> entries.
- Scripts: 58 with store shebangs (24 with further store refs in the body). The runtime-relevant ones are all makeWrapper scripts: eon, yazelix-venus, CodexBarCLI and every libexec/eon/bin session wrapper (eon-nu, eon-bash, ..., hx, yazi, lazygit, nu, bash, zsh, fish). The rest are zsh function files, jemalloc and fzf-share.
- Symlinks with absolute store targets: 314 (including the whole libexec/eon/bin farm).
- Text with store refs: 263 (.la 71, .fish 39, .nu 30, .pc 25, .json 20 incl. Vulkan ICDs, X11 Compose 14, Eon-owned shell init: eon.bashrc, eon-zsh-config, eon.fish, eon-nu-vendor-autoload, eon-shell-init/*, eon-directory-picker-config). Non-ELF binary with refs: 2,407 (2,253 fish/python .pyc, ~150 compiled terminfo entries pointing at ncurses tabset); inert.
- Where they run: Venus only: yazelix-venus, wayland, vulkan-loader, xkbcommon, Mesa 26.1.2 (265 MB) plus llvm-21.1.8-lib (541 MB), libdrm/pciaccess/X11 libs, dejavu/nerd-symbols/accelerando fonts. Inside Orbit terminals: bash-interactive, zsh, fish (pulls python3 134 MB, coreutils, man-db, groff, gettext, util-linux), nushell, starship, zoxide, fzf, atuin, carapace, helix (+ runtime and grammars), yazi/ya, lazygit, anima, the directory picker, Orbit terminfo. Supervisor side: eon, Orbit, CodexBarCLI (262 MB Swift runtime), and bash as the makeWrapper interpreter.
- glibc symbol floor of what actually runs: eon, Orbit, Venus, nu, starship, zoxide, atuin, anima <= GLIBC_2.39; carapace 2.34; fzf static; Venus's wayland/vulkan/xkbcommon <= 2.38. ncurses 6.6 (so bash-interactive, zsh, readline) and coreutils 9.11 (from fish) need GLIBC_2.42 through the new cfgetospeed/cfsetospeed/cfgetispeed/cfsetispeed versions. No closure object uses GLIBC_PRIVATE. Bundled libgcc_s (gcc 15.2) and Ubuntu 26.04's (gcc 16) both top out at GCC_14.0.0.

MECHANISMS COMPARED (sources and revisions below):
(f) CHOSEN: host-glibc relink. At bundle build time every ELF gets PT_INTERP = /lib64/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2 (the x86-64 psABI loader path every glibc distribution ships) and every store RUNPATH entry becomes $ORIGIN-relative inside the bundle's own nix/store tree; glibc entries are dropped and glibc leaves the payload; absolute store symlinks become relative. No namespace, no ptrace, no install-time rewrite, no launcher in front of each ELF; /proc/self/exe stays the real program; host NSS, locales and GPU drivers work natively. Cost: a declared host glibc floor equal to the newest symbol version the shipped executables need, enforced at build time.
(a) Exodus-style bundled ld.so --library-path: works on any host glibc, but /proc/self/exe becomes ld.so (breaks self-re-exec and exe-relative data lookup, e.g. fish, nu and helix fallbacks), needs a launcher per ELF, and keeps Nix glibc, so host GPU drivers cannot be loaded and Venus is stuck on bundled lavapipe. Rejected as the primary path.
(b) static/musl builds of eon, Orbit, eon-install and the managed tools: removes the loader question for those, but Venus cannot be static (it must dlopen host Vulkan and Wayland), many managed tools need per-package static work, and a second build of the components is a separate artifact set that would need to be reconciled with EON-C6. Kept only as a fallback lever for lowering the glibc floor (bash and zsh).
(c) conda-style padded-prefix install-time rewriting: needs a long storeDir world rebuild with no binary cache plus install-time binary patching, and eon-install and manual extraction would both have to own a rewrite step. Rejected.
(d) Venus relocated, terminals static: subsumed by (f), which needs no static rebuild for terminals.
(e) bwrap or userns (this epic's No-Go), PRoot (nix-portable fallback: ptrace overhead, and it would wrap every terminal child), Guix -RR packs (user namespaces by default, PRoot fallback): rejected for the same reasons as the No-Go.

GPU STANCE: host driver. In the prototype, the bundled vulkan-loader under the host glibc enumerated and loaded the host Mesa ICDs (/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libvulkan_lvp.so and libvulkan_nouveau.so) and rendered. Recommendation: drop bundled Mesa and LLVM (806 MB unpacked) and declare a host Vulkan driver as a prerequisite (Ubuntu Desktop and Fedora Workstation ship Mesa Vulkan, including lavapipe). Take libwayland-client from the host (the AppImage excludelist does the same because of a Mesa conflict). The bundled vulkan-loader may stay, since it loaded host ICDs here. libxkbcommon comes either from the host or from the bundle with its data roots set: the bundled copy logged "No Compose file for locale C.UTF-8" because its Compose root is compiled in. Child 4 decides with evidence. Venus's RUNPATH should carry no bundled gcc runtime, so host drivers never inherit an older libgcc_s/libstdc++.

PROTOTYPE (throwaway relink.py in session scratch: copy the closure minus glibc, Mesa and LLVM; patchelf 0.15.2 sets the interpreter on 246 ELFs and rewrites RUNPATH on 899, dropping 897 glibc entries; 314 symlinks made relative; 73 scripts and 51 Eon-owned text files rewritten to ${EON_BUNDLE_ROOT}; fonts.conf <dir> -> prefix="relative", which fontconfig-parser 0.5.8 supports; a /bin/sh top-level eon). Archive eon-proto.tar.zst sha256 726c0dcd847e3778d2c956620a140e8d050c0c4f6925145eae3bdcc27e46e8de, 1.2 GB unpacked versus 2.1 GB.
VM: official ubuntu-26.04-server-cloudimg-amd64.img sha256 8800651811af9a85465ad1d552add729947bb16488dddb4a9b5305a3d97332b2 (same image as lm9p), Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS, kernel 7.0.0-34-generic, glibc 2.43-2ubuntu2.4, kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=1, no /nix, QEMU 11.1.1/KVM with a cloud-init NoCloud seed. Stand-in desktop packages: sway 1.11 headless (pixman), grim, wtype, mesa-vulkan-drivers 26.0.8, libvulkan1 1.4.341. User eon in groups adm, sudo, video with NOPASSWD sudo.
- RED, same VM: the ef238be bwrap bundle `eon versions` -> "bwrap: setting up uid map: Permission denied", exit 1.
- GREEN: `eon versions` exit 0 and `eon --help` exit 0. `eon run -- eon-bash -c ...` opened the Venus window (sway app_id eon, title Venus); Venus NoNewPrivs 0 on host libc with the host lvp ICD. After the picker was confirmed by Enter from a held wtype virtual keyboard, the bundled bash ran in pane p1 while Venus was alive and recorded: NoNewPrivs 0; Uid/Gid 1000; Groups 4 27 44 1000; id matches the host; user ns user:[4026531837], the same as the SSH login; /usr/bin/sudo root root; /etc/shadow root shadow; `sudo -n true` exit 0; exe = bundled bash-interactive; libc = /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6; bundled nu 0.113.1, helix 25.07.1 and lazygit 0.62.2 ran from $EON_SESSION_BIN. The grim screenshot shows the bash pane under Venus chrome.
- Prototype failures (design inputs, not blockers): (1) Eon does not forward arbitrary environment to terminals, so eon.bashrc's rewritten ${EON_BUNDLE_ROOT} paths expanded empty and Starship/Zoxide/Atuin/Carapace init warned "cannot initialize" (EON-C9's warn-and-continue path). Eon-owned shell init must name managed artifacts through variables Eon itself supplies. (2) An env-bash shebang resolved `bash` through the terminal's private PATH to Eon's own bash wrapper and recursed; host-shell shebangs are unsafe, so the bundle needs a static launcher, not rewritten scripts. (3) fonts.conf absolute dirs -> "terminal font family is unavailable: Symbols Nerd Font Mono" until made relative. (4) The xkbcommon Compose root (above).

CONTRACT EFFECT: EON-C2 unchanged (same manifest and lock bytes, same `eon versions`). EON-C3 unchanged and better served: the bundle launcher supplies bundle-relative opaque component paths; runtime code still never constructs store paths. EON-C5: lifecycle and eon-install unchanged; only the bundle mechanism changes, and payloads stay relocatable while stopped. EON-C6: needs one explicit statement in its proof text that the direct bundle takes libc, NSS, locales and the Vulkan driver as declared host inputs (the bwrap bundle already treated resolver, user, timezone and desktop services as host inputs); component identities are unchanged. MANUAL-BUNDLE "Execution and host boundary" is superseded: no bwrap, no /nix projection, build-time ELF relink plus launcher env table instead of "no ELF/config path rewriting"; host prerequisites become glibc >= floor, a Vulkan driver, and native Wayland. No contract change beyond EON-C5's mechanism and the EON-C6 host-input statement, so no stop condition is triggered; both texts change only after Lucca accepts.

DEPENDENCY AND VERSION POLICY: patchelf (build-time only, from the flake-locked nixpkgs; no runtime dependency) and the existing static Rust bundle entrypoint, which becomes the env-table launcher. The relinker itself is Rust repository tooling, not Python. The glibc floor is declared in the bundle builder and enforced by a build gate that fails if any shipped ELF needs a newer GLIBC_x or any GLIBC_PRIVATE; a nixpkgs glibc bump that raises it fails the build rather than shipping silently. bubblewrap and its vendored source leave the payload. Exit condition: drop the relinker if nixpkgs gains relocatable outputs (the fzakaria proposal) or if Eon's terminal set becomes fully static, and revisit if any supported target ships a glibc below the floor.

OPEN DECISION FOR LUCCA (glibc floor): with today's closure the floor is GLIBC_2.42 (Ubuntu 26.04 LTS 2.43, Fedora 43/44, Debian 14+; not Ubuntu 24.04's 2.39 or Debian 13's 2.41). Recommendation: ship floor 2.42 for the first namespace-free candidate and move Ubuntu 24.04 to a follow-up that lowers the floor to 2.39 (static musl bash and zsh, and fish's coreutils/man-db chain). eon, Orbit, Venus, nu, hx, yazi, lazygit and the other tools already meet 2.39.

PROPOSED CHILDREN (not filed; each one session):
1. Location-neutral Eon shell integration: Eon-owned init (bash, zsh, fish, nu autoload, shell-init, directory picker config) resolves managed artifacts through an Eon-supplied input such as EON_SESSION_BIN, not absolute store paths, in both channels. EON-C9 behavior unchanged; Nix dogfood plus the existing EON-C9 tests.
2. Relinking bundle builder: nix/linux-bundle.nix replaces bwrap with a Rust relink step (interpreter, $ORIGIN RUNPATH, relative symlinks, glibc/Mesa/LLVM excluded), the glibc-floor gate and the static-bootstrap check, and drops bubblewrap from payload, licenses and provenance.
3. Static launcher env table: the bundle entrypoint becomes a multi-call launcher that applies the makeWrapper env (EON_*, TERMINFO_DIRS, FONTCONFIG_FILE and so on) relative to its own directory and execs the real binary; the table is generated from the same Nix wrapper definitions so one owner holds the env list; no host-shell shebangs.
4. Third-party data roots: helix runtime, zsh fpath and modules, fish data and helpers, ncurses terminfo, CA certificates (host /etc/ssl), relative fonts.conf, and Venus on host libwayland/libxkbcommon/libvulkan with no bundled gcc runtime; check each inside an Orbit terminal.
5. Docs and contract text after acceptance: MANUAL-BUNDLE execution boundary and host prerequisites, the EON-C5 mechanism wording and the EON-C6 host-input statement (user approval of the contract text first), then the Ubuntu 26.04 VM proof of verify, extract, `eon versions`, eon-install install/upgrade/rollback/remove and the terminal NoNewPrivs/id/sudo checks; hands the candidate to lm9p.
6. (If Lucca wants Ubuntu 24.04 in the matrix) lower the glibc floor to 2.39.

REFERENCES READ (2026-10-18; inspected revisions):
- Exodus github.com/intoli/exodus @ ef3d5e92c1b6: one launcher per executable that runs `exec "${linker}" --library-path ... --inhibit-rpath "" "${executable}"` (templates/launcher.sh:9); copies ld.so beside each binary so /proc/self/exe yields the right directory (bundling.py:800-802), i.e. /proc/self/exe is the linker; Known Limitations (README:469-492): isolated from host driver libraries, shebangs not rewritten. Kept: the per-ELF relocation idea. Rejected: bundled-loader invocation (host GPU and self-exec).
- fzakaria "Nix needs relocatable binaries", 2026-06-21: $ORIGIN/../../<hash>-pkg RUNPATHs; the kernel cannot expand $ORIGIN in PT_INTERP or shebangs; options are a kernel change, a static self-locating wrapper, or language-level relative paths. Kept: $ORIGIN RUNPATH and the static wrapper for env/shebang cases; PT_INTERP is solved by the host psABI loader instead. Unshipped proposal.
- conda-build @ 6ab6f8e74ed1 / conda @ 4604464d9c3c: 255-char padded placeholder prefix (config.py:107), NUL-padded binary rewrite with _PaddingError (portability.py:253-305), install-time and fixed thereafter. Rejected.
- nix-portable @ 91122e3d94ba: runtimes nix, bwrap (host or bundled), proot (host or bundled); falls back to proot without userns, with "significant performance overhead" (README 159-166, 194-195). Rejected.
- Guix manual "Invoking guix pack" (1.5.0 dev): -R needs userns; -RR falls back to PRoot (ptrace overhead per syscall) or Fakechroot ("erratic behavior"). Rejected.
- AppImage docs @ b29179c8f913 and pkg2appimage excludelist @ 19e30b276ffe: build on the oldest supported base (best-practices.rst:23,82-84); ld-linux, libc, libGL/EGL/GLX, libdrm, libgbm and libwayland-client come from the host (excludelist :9,:14,:38-46,:90); libvulkan and libxkbcommon are bundled. This is the closest shipped comparable to (f): host glibc and graphics, everything else bundled, with a glibc floor.
- patchelf @ 382d8bc12db9: --set-rpath '$ORIGIN/...' documented (patchelf.1:171-176); --set-interpreter takes a literal path. psABI x86-64 @ e1ce098331da dl.tex:404-421: Linux interpreter /lib64/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2.
- glibc-2.42 d2097651cc57: NEWS:25-27 termios arbitrary baud rates, speed_t redefined; x86_64 libc.abilist:2752-2760 adds GLIBC_2.42 cf{get,set}{i,o}speed and cfsetspeed.
- Vulkan-Loader @ 3aba6aeb8786 docs/LoaderDriverInterface.md:736-742 (relative library_path resolves against the manifest), :381-452 (Linux search through XDG dirs, /etc and /usr/share vulkan/icd.d).
- Distro glibc: Ubuntu 24.04 2.39-0ubuntu8.9, Ubuntu 26.04 2.43-2ubuntu2.4, Debian 13 2.41-12+deb13u4, Fedora 43 2.42-17.fc43, Fedora 44 2.43-2.fc44.

comments.text: User decision (Lucca, 2026-10-18), answering the open choices in the record above: (1) mechanism accepted: host-glibc relink (psABI interpreter, $ORIGIN RUNPATH, glibc out of the payload, static launcher env table); (2) glibc floor: GLIBC_2.42 for the first namespace-free candidate (Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, Fedora 43/44); Ubuntu 24.04 and Debian 13 move to a later child that lowers the floor to 2.39; (3) GPU stance: host Vulkan driver, bundled Mesa and LLVM dropped. The proposed children are still unfiled pending a separate go-ahead to file them.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Corrections after fresh-eyes review pass 1 (supersede the matching parts of the record above):
1. EON-C5 effect was wrong. eon-install requires libexec/bwrap when it installs a payload (installer/src/main.rs:388) and when it validates a selected version (installer/src/main.rs:200), and its fixture creates the file (installer/src/tests.rs:77). Removing bubblewrap breaks install and selection, so an installer child is required. It validates the new layout and keeps retained bwrap-era payloads selectable for rollback, so live work under either layout is preserved. EON-C5's text names no mechanism, so the earlier "EON-C5 mechanism wording" edit is withdrawn. The contract text is unchanged and the installer's validation code changes.
2. The glibc floor against the epic: eon-zti4 Acceptance names Ubuntu 24.04 in lm9p's matrix. Lucca's "2.42 now, 24.04 later" is applied inside the epic without amending it. The first candidate targets Ubuntu 26.04 and Fedora 43/44, and the floor-2.39 child is mandatory before eon-zti4 closes.
3. Inventory addendum: zoxide 0.9.9 has a compiled-in store path to fzf (a nixpkgs patch), so `zi` breaks without /nix, and child 4 covers it. A looser scan counts 116 ELFs with extra store strings against the 104 above. The other additions are inert: lazygit's mailcap, libpsl's publicsuffix list and the wayland-cursor icons.
4. Inventory precision: only 6 of the 20 libexec/eon/bin entries are absolute store links. The rest are relative links to bin/eon-*, which point to the single bin/eon makeWrapper script that dispatches on argv0, so the launcher must keep the `exec -a "$0"` dispatch and replace that in-closure wrapper too. The GLIBC_2.42 users also include python3's termios module (fish) and util-linux agetty, sulogin and ldattach (man-db chain). The floor gate either scopes to reachable executables or the floor-2.39 child covers these as well. CodexBarCLI is a statically linked binary with debug info; only its wrapper's SSL_CERT_FILE store default matters.
5. Bundled-loader evidence: VM run 4's Venus maps list /home/eon/t/eon-proto/nix/store/d6vnmfmcz5b299180issiaad4m96wh8k-vulkan-loader-1.4.341.0/lib/libvulkan.so.1.4.341 next to host /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libvulkan_lvp.so and libvulkan_nouveau.so, so the bundled loader, not the host's libvulkan1, loaded the host ICDs.
6. Prototype source revision: relink.py sha256 8208ab32140c8022b36a50301a3510a17cca6a756f5812c48b3705fd3f35167f and run-proof.sh sha256 fceb78c11cef649948e3c351e7646840407d29644e642870ae170b0ff48dc885; both are kept in the next comment as the runnable reproducer. A fresh relink.py run reproduces the proven tree except 5 inert files: fzf-tmux, fzf share/update.sh and helix's hx.bash completion. Their upstream `#!/usr/bin/env bash` shebangs were also changed to /bin/bash by the manual shebang fix before archive 726c0dcd....

Revised proposed children (still unfiled; each one session):
1. Location-neutral Eon shell integration (as above).
2. Static launcher env table (the multi-call entrypoint keeps argv0 dispatch and replaces the makeWrapper scripts in the bundle). It lands before or with child 3, because the bundle is not runnable with only one of them.
3. Relinking bundle builder with the glibc-floor gate; drops bubblewrap from payload, licences and provenance.
4. Third-party data roots, now including zoxide's fzf path.
5. eon-install layout validation: install and select the new layout, keep bwrap-era payloads selectable, and update the installer tests.
6. Docs and contract text: MANUAL-BUNDLE's execution boundary, receipts (absolute symlinks), licence and userns copy, and the EON-C6 host-input statement after Lucca approves the text.
7. Final installed proof on the Ubuntu 26.04 VM: verify, extract, `eon versions`, and eon-install install, upgrade, rollback and remove with two archives, plus the terminal NoNewPrivs/id/sudo checks. Hands the candidate to lm9p for Ubuntu 26.04 and Fedora.
8. Lower the floor to GLIBC_2.39 for Ubuntu 24.04 and Debian 13 (bash, zsh, fish's coreutils, python termios and man-db chain). Required before eon-zti4 closes.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Runnable reproducer for the prototype (disposable investigation tooling, not checked-in policy). Usage: nix path-info -r <eon package> listed into closure.txt; python3 -I relink.py closure.txt <out>/eon-proto <patchelf>; tar the tree; in the VM, run-proof.sh with eon-proto.tar.zst and the ef238be archive in $HOME.

=== relink.py (sha256 8208ab32...)
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Disposable prototype: relocate a Nix closure to run on the host glibc, no namespace.

ELF: PT_INTERP -> /lib64/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2 (psABI path), store RUNPATH entries ->
$ORIGIN-relative, glibc entries dropped. Absolute store symlinks -> relative.
Shell wrappers and eon-owned shell text: /nix/store -> ${EON_BUNDLE_ROOT}/nix/store
(prototype only; the proposed design replaces this with a launcher env table).
"""
import os, re, shutil, stat, subprocess, sys

closure_file, out, patchelf = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3]
EXCLUDE = re.compile(r"-(glibc-2\.42-61|mesa-26\.1\.2|llvm-21\.1\.8-lib)$")
GLIBC = re.compile(r"^/nix/store/[0-9a-z]{32}-glibc-2\.42-61(/|$)")
INTERP = "/lib64/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2"
store_out = os.path.join(out, "nix/store")
os.makedirs(store_out, exist_ok=True)
paths = [l.strip() for l in open(closure_file) if l.strip()]
kept = [p for p in paths if not EXCLUDE.search(p)]
for p in kept:
    dst = os.path.join(out, p.lstrip("/"))
    if not os.path.lexists(dst):
        subprocess.run(["cp", "-a", "--reflink=auto", p, dst], check=True)
subprocess.run(["chmod", "-R", "u+w", store_out], check=True)

def inbundle(abs_store_path):
    return os.path.join(out, abs_store_path.lstrip("/"))

stats = dict(interp=0, runpath=0, symlink=0, script=0, text=0, dropped_glibc_rp=0)
for p in kept:
    root = inbundle(p)
    for dirpath, dirnames, filenames in os.walk(root):
        for name in dirnames + filenames:
            f = os.path.join(dirpath, name)
            if os.path.islink(f):
                t = os.readlink(f)
                if t.startswith("/nix/store/"):
                    os.unlink(f)
                    os.symlink(os.path.relpath(inbundle(t), dirpath), f)
                    stats["symlink"] += 1
                continue
            if not os.path.isfile(f):
                continue
            with open(f, "rb") as fh:
                head = fh.read(4)
            if head == b"\x7fELF":
                ro = subprocess.run(["readelf", "-ldW", f], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
                args = []
                if "Requesting program interpreter" in ro:
                    args += ["--set-interpreter", INTERP]
                    stats["interp"] += 1
                m = re.search(r"\((?:RUNPATH|RPATH)\)\s+Library r(?:un)?path: \[([^\]]*)\]", ro)
                if m and "/nix/store/" in m.group(1):
                    new = []
                    for e in m.group(1).split(":"):
                        if GLIBC.match(e):
                            stats["dropped_glibc_rp"] += 1
                            continue
                        if e.startswith("/nix/store/"):
                            e = "$ORIGIN/" + os.path.relpath(inbundle(e), dirpath)
                        new.append(e)
                    args += ["--set-rpath", ":".join(new)]
                    stats["runpath"] += 1
                if args:
                    subprocess.run([patchelf, *args, f], check=True)
                continue
            data = open(f, "rb").read()
            if b"/nix/store/" not in data:
                continue
            owner = p.split("/")[3].split("-", 1)[1]
            is_script = data.startswith(b"#!") and os.access(f, os.X_OK)
            if not (is_script or owner.startswith("eon")):
                continue
            text = data.decode("utf-8", errors="surrogateescape")
            if is_script:
                first, rest = text.split("\n", 1)
                interp = first[2:].strip().split()
                prog = os.path.basename(interp[0])
                first = "#!/bin/" + prog if prog in ("bash", "sh") else first
                # makeWrapper bodies are bash; run them with the host bash.
                if "/nix/store/" in first:
                    first = "#!/usr/bin/env " + prog
                text = first + "\n" + rest
                stats["script"] += 1
            else:
                stats["text"] += 1
            text = text.replace("'/nix/store/", "\x00Q")
            text = text.replace("/nix/store/", "${EON_BUNDLE_ROOT}/nix/store/")
            text = text.replace("\x00Q", "\"${EON_BUNDLE_ROOT}\"'/nix/store/")
            mode = os.stat(f).st_mode
            open(f, "w", encoding="utf-8", errors="surrogateescape").write(text)
            os.chmod(f, mode)

# fonts.conf sits directly in nix/store, so its store dirs become prefix="relative".
for p in kept:
    if p.endswith("-fonts.conf"):

title: Make Eon shell integration location-neutral
description:
## Why

The namespace-free bundle (epic eon-zti4; mechanism accepted on eon-zti4.1) moves the payload away from /nix. Eon-owned shell init files embed absolute store paths at build time. In the eon-zti4.1 Ubuntu 26.04 prototype, eon.bashrc's Starship, Zoxide, Atuin and Carapace sources failed ("eon: cannot initialize Starship" and the rest). Eon does not forward arbitrary environment to terminals, so a bundle-root variable never reached the shell. The init must name managed artifacts through an input Eon itself supplies, in both the Nix channel and the bundle.

## Evidence

- `nix/shell-environment.nix:5-60`: the `eon-shell-init` store directory (starship-*, zoxide-*, atuin-*, carapace-*).
- `nix/shell-environment.nix`: the bash rc, the nu vendor autoload and the directory-picker config `source` ${shellInit}/... as absolute store paths.
- `flake.nix:493-511`: the eon wrapper sets EON_BASH_RC, EON_NU_VENDOR_AUTOLOAD, EON_DIRECTORY_PICKER_CONFIG and EON_SESSION_BIN as store paths.
- `eon/crates/eon/src/product.rs:115-125`: Eon reads those inputs as opaque paths (EON-C3).

## Scope

In scope: Eon-owned Bash and Nushell init, the shell-init directory, the directory-picker config, and the inputs that carry them. Resolve artifacts through one Eon-supplied input (for example a shell-init root next to EON_SESSION_BIN) that Eon passes into the child environment.
Out of scope: Zsh and Fish (removed by eon-8olu, which lands first); EON-C9 semantics; bundle builder changes.

## Acceptance

- No Eon-owned shell init or picker config contains an absolute /nix/store path; each resolves through the Eon-supplied input.
- In the Nix channel, EON-C9 behavior is unchanged for Nushell and Bash, including Starship, Zoxide, Atuin and Carapace activation and warn-and-continue on failure.

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test` exits 0; `nix build .#default` exits 0.
- `grep -r /nix/store` over the built eon-shell-init, the bash rc, the nu autoload and the picker config finds only references Eon resolves through the input. List any that remain.
- Refresh the `eon` profile and make one isolated installed observation that a new Bash and a new Nushell terminal initialize all four integrations. Do not restart the live supervisor.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if this needs an EON-C3 or EON-C9 contract change.
- Stop if the child environment cannot carry the input without changing Orbit.
close_reason: Shell init resolves through a relocatable tree; proof recorded

- eon.bashrc captures its directory from ${BASH_SOURCE[0]} before sourcing ~/.bashrc and sources shell-init files and calls tools from bin/ relative to it. Nu files use `const ... = path self ...` for both the source paths and the tool paths (^$const in defs and closures).

Alternative rejected for now: a new child env variable naming the root. It adds an input that the runtime must forward, touches runtime launch enforcement, and may need an EON-C3/EON-C9 change.

title: Relink the eon closure for the host glibc as a Nix check
description:
## Why

Mechanism accepted on eon-zti4.1 (epic eon-zti4): relink the Nix closure to run on the host glibc. Every ELF gets PT_INTERP=/lib64/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2 (the x86-64 psABI path) and $ORIGIN-relative RUNPATHs inside the bundle's own nix/store tree. glibc, Mesa and LLVM are excluded, and absolute store symlinks become relative. Build it first as a standalone Nix check, so manual-bundle keeps working until the switch child.

## Evidence

- eon-zti4.1 inventory: 1,224 ELFs, 250 with PT_INTERP (all nixpkgs glibc-2.42-61), 929 with store RUNPATHs, 314 absolute store symlinks. The prototype relinked 246 interpreters and 899 RUNPATHs with patchelf 0.15.2; the reproducer relink.py is in an eon-zti4.1 comment.
- `nix/linux-bundle.nix:1-45`: the current builder (closureInfo copy plus bwrap).
- Remaining ELFs NEED glibc sonames: libdl (17), libpthread (22), libresolv (18), librt (5), ld-linux (21).

## Scope

In scope: a Rust relink step (repository tooling must be Rust; Python is disposable only) that runs patchelf as a subprocess and readelf for inspection, with no new ELF crate (any crate goes through AP-DEPENDENCY-001); a Nix check, e.g. `checks.x86_64-linux.bundle-relink`, producing the relinked tree; and two gates:
1. The floor gate: every shipped ELF needs GLIBC_x <= 2.42 and no GLIBC_PRIVATE, with an explicit reviewed exclusion list for executables Eon never runs.
2. The NEEDED-resolution gate: each NEEDED soname resolves inside the bundle via RUNPATH, or is on the declared host set (every glibc soname, libgcc_s, and libwayland-client for Venus).
Out of scope: changing manual-bundle or eon-install, the launcher, and data-root fixes.

## Acceptance

- The check builds a relinked tree with no PT_INTERP other than the psABI path, no RUNPATH entry outside $ORIGIN, no absolute store symlink, and no glibc, Mesa or LLVM store paths.
- Both gates pass on the current closure, and each fails on a seeded violation.

## Verification

- `nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.bundle-relink` exits 0, and its gate output lists counts by kind.
- A red/green check of both gates on a deliberately bad input (for example an ELF that needs GLIBC_2.43, and a NEEDED with no provider). Keep it in the supported harness.
- `nix develop -c eon-test` exits 0 for the relink crate's unit tests.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if a needed object cannot be relinked by patchelf (for example a Go or static-PIE edge case) without forking a component.
close_reason: bundle-relink check builds the host-glibc relinked tree; both gates pass on the current closure and fail on seeded violations

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Reference gate and code shape (2026-10-19, repo edge b1c374e, untracked review-corners.md not part of this work; eon package /nix/store/7ps5hzi0fizmgfqphyi6mc767xi3861v-eon-0.1.1, nixpkgs 567a49d1913c, patchelf 0.15.2).
Question: how should the eon closure be relinked for the host glibc and gated, as a standalone Nix check?
Contract: no contract change; check-only. Consumers are eon-zti4.4/.5/.6, which take the relinked tree.
Owners: nix/bundle-relink.nix owns policy: the root (eon package), the host-provided store paths excluded (pkgs.glibc, pkgs.mesa), the glibc floor (2.42) and the declared host libraries (every soname in the excluded glibc's lib/, libgcc_s.so.1, libwayland-client.so.0). A standalone std-only Rust crate relink/ (eon-relink) owns the mechanism: closure pruning from closureInfo's registration, copying, the psABI interpreter, $ORIGIN RUNPATHs, relative symlinks, and the gates. patchelf and readelf run as build-time subprocesses from the flake-locked nixpkgs.
Sources and revisions: eon-zti4.1's record (patchelf @ 382d8bc12db9 patchelf.1:171-176; psABI x86-64 @ e1ce098331da dl.tex:404-421; AppImage excludelist @ 19e30b276ffe for host glibc and libwayland-client; fzakaria's $ORIGIN RUNPATHs); nixpkgs 567a49d1913c pkgs/build-support/closure-info.nix:70 (registration: path, narHash, narSize, empty deriver, reference count, references).
Inventory of that closure, excluding glibc, Mesa, libgbm and LLVM: 651 ELFs, 59 with PT_INTERP, 645 with RUNPATH, 0 with DT_RPATH, 3 with an empty RUNPATH; 640 RUNPATH entries name glibc; 306 absolute store symlinks, none into an excluded path; GLIBC needs above 2.39 come only from ncurses libncursesw and tset, python3's termios module and util-linux sulogin (all 2.42); there is no GLIBC_PRIVATE and no non-numeric GLIBC_ name; every NEEDED resolves through RUNPATH or the host set.
Decision: exclude glibc and Mesa, and ship only what eon reaches without passing through them. That also prunes 41 paths (186 MB) referenced only through Mesa or glibc: llvm-21.1.8-lib, mesa-libgbm, python3, util-linux-minimal (lib, login), libdrm, elfutils, curl, openssl and others. With python3 and sulogin gone, only ncurses stays above 2.39, which narrows eon-zti4.8.
Failure conditions: the relinker exits 1 on a stale exclusion (path not in the closure), a RUNPATH entry or symlink naming a store path the tree does not ship, or a readelf or patchelf failure. The gates reject an interpreter other than /lib64/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2, a RUNPATH entry outside $ORIGIN, DT_RPATH, a rewritten symlink that does not resolve inside the tree, any GLIBC_ need that is non-numeric (GLIBC_PRIVATE) or above the floor, and a NEEDED that neither resolves inside the tree through RUNPATH nor is a declared host library.
Rejected: (1) copying the closure minus only the excluded directories, as the prototype did, which ships 186 MB that nothing reaches and keeps 2.42 objects Eon never runs. (2) A workspace-member crate: crateSource would include it, so a relinker edit would rebuild Orbit, Venus and eon and change eon's generation identity. It stays standalone like installer/ and bundle/. (3) An ELF crate (goblin or object): readelf suffices, and the bead forbids one without AP-DEPENDENCY-001. (4) A floor exemption list: it would be empty at 2.42 on this closure, so none is added; eon-zti4.8 adds one if it chooses exemption over a fix.
Cheapest proof: nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.bundle-relink with the gate counts; unit-test red/green that seeds a GLIBC_2.99 need into a real ELF and adds a NEEDED with no provider, run by nix develop -c eon-test --manifest-path relink/Cargo.toml and in the relinker's Nix build.
Exit condition (from eon-zti4.1): drop the relinker if nixpkgs gains relocatable outputs or Eon's terminal set becomes fully static.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Gate rules and accepted gaps (2026-10-19), from glibc 2.42's elf/dl-load.c (glibc-2.42.tar.xz in the pinned nixpkgs 567a49d1913c):
Gate rules. A RUNPATH entry must begin with $ORIGIN as a whole path component and resolve step by step (each symlink before a later "..", as the kernel does) without leaving the tree. A missing directory holds nothing to search. fillin_rpath searches the working directory for an empty entry inside a nonempty RUNPATH, so such an entry fails. decompose_rpath ignores an entirely empty RUNPATH, which 2 shipped objects (anima, gcc libgcc_s) keep. A NEEDED library counts as in the tree only if it resolves to a shipped ELF shared object ("DYN (Shared object file)"): glibc refuses a PIE executable as a dependency. A library found through a symlink from another directory takes that directory as its $ORIGIN, so such a provider fails if it has a RUNPATH. Version needs declared in the dynamic section (VERNEEDNUM) that readelf cannot list, for example because the section headers are stripped, fail the floor gate. Only an interpreter from an excluded path is replaced; any other stays for the gate to report. readelf runs with LC_ALL=C because the parser matches its untranslated messages.
Accepted gaps, with reasons:
1. LLVM and libgbm leave through pruning, not an explicit exclusion. If a kept path ever references LLVM directly, LLVM ships because something kept needs it; the check prints the pruned count, and the host-driver stance is enforced where Venus's environment changes (eon-zti4.4, eon-zti4.5).
2. No floor exemption list: at GLIBC_2.42 it would be empty. eon-zti4.8 adds one only if it chooses exemption over fixing ncurses.
3. eon-test with no arguments does not run the relinker's suite; the suite runs in the relinker's Nix build, which the check requires, and with eon-test --manifest-path relink/Cargo.toml, as docs/DEVELOPMENT.md says. Adding it to the default run would also mean re-rendering AGENTS.md, whose text lists the suites.
4. The GLIBC_PRIVATE and DT_RPATH rejections have no seeded test: no same-length edit seeds GLIBC_PRIVATE, and neither occurs in the closure. Both are one-condition rules beside seeded ones.
5. The declared host set holds every glibc soname, including ones some distributions split out (libnsl.so.1, libnss_db, libnss_hesiod, libc_malloc_debug.so.0). This follows the bead's policy, and no shipped object NEEDs them.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Gate rules, addendum (2026-10-19): the NEEDED gate follows the loader's search order. The first RUNPATH candidate that exists decides, and it fails unless it is a shipped shared object; glibc stops with an error there rather than searching on. Each step of a search path must be a directory, because the kernel answers ENOTDIR for file/... Every symlink in the tree, not only the rewritten ones, must resolve inside the tree. The relinker's Nix source is a fileset of Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock and src, as in nix/installer.nix.
Accepted gaps, continued:
6. Any non-numeric GLIBC_ need fails the floor gate, including public markers such as GLIBC_ABI_DT_RELR that every host at the floor satisfies. None occurs in the closure. If one appears, the gate fails loudly; the fix then maps the marker to the glibc release that introduced it.
7. The "found away from its $ORIGIN" rule is conservative: it also rejects a same-depth cross-directory library link with a RUNPATH, which would resolve the same way. None occurs today.

title: Replace bundle makeWrapper scripts with a static launcher env table
description:
## Why

Mechanism accepted on eon-zti4.1 (epic eon-zti4). The Nix closure's makeWrapper scripts have /nix/store shebangs and absolute env values, so a relocated bundle cannot run them. In the prototype, rewriting them to a host shell failed: an `env bash` shebang found Eon's own `bash` session wrapper first on the terminal's private PATH and recursed. The bundle needs a static launcher that applies the same env relative to its own directory and execs the real binary.

## Evidence

- `flake.nix:493-511`: the eon wrapper (EON_ORBIT, EON_VENUS, EON_* tool paths, EON_SESSION_BIN, TERMINFO_DIRS). `flake.nix:289`: the Venus wrapper (FONTCONFIG_FILE, LD_LIBRARY_PATH, XDG_DATA_DIRS). `flake.nix:183`: CodexBarCLI (SSL_CERT_FILE).
- libexec/eon/bin: 6 of 20 entries are absolute store links; the rest point to bin/eon-*, which point to the single bin/eon makeWrapper script that dispatches on argv0 via `exec -a "$0"`.
- `bundle/src/main.rs`: the current static Rust entrypoint (it execs bwrap).

## Scope

In scope: a multi-call static launcher (an evolution of bundle/src/main.rs) that keeps the argv0 dispatch, plus an env table generated from the same Nix wrapper definitions so one owner holds each env list (refactor the wrapper args into a shared Nix attrset if needed). The launcher replaces the in-closure wrapper scripts inside child 2's relinked tree. Check it against that tree in a Nix check.
Out of scope: shipping it in manual-bundle (switch child), eon-install, third-party data roots.

## Acceptance

- In the relinked tree, every former wrapper entry (eon, eon-* commands, yazelix-venus, CodexBarCLI, session bin) runs through the launcher with bundle-relative values and no host shell.
- The Nix channel's wrappers and the bundle table derive from one definition.
- Moving the tree to another directory keeps it working.

## Verification

- A Nix check runs `eon versions` and `eon --help` from the relinked tree at two different paths, with no /nix lookups. Use env -i and strace or LD_DEBUG to show that no /nix/store path is opened.
- `nix develop -c eon-test` exits 0.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if generating the table needs a second hand-maintained copy of the env lists.
close_reason: Static launcher env table replaces the relinked tree's makeWrapper scripts; one definition for both channels; bundle-launch check

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Design and reference gate (2026-10-19, edge b85d82f).
Owner: flake.nix defines each wrapper environment once (eon, yazelix-venus, CodexBarCLI) as {set, setDefault, prefix}. One renderer turns it into makeWrapper args for the Nix channel; nix/bundle-relink.nix renders the same attrsets into the launcher's compiled-in table. The eon environment takes its own out path: placeholder "out" for makeWrapper, the real path for the table. The closure has exactly these three makeWrapper scripts (scan of every file for 'exec -a "$0"'); there are no makeBinaryWrapper binaries.
Launcher: a new static std-only crate, launcher/, built with pkgsStatic.rustPlatform like the current entrypoint. A copy replaces each wrapper script in the relinked tree. It finds its own entry by the suffix of /proc/self/exe, so the tree root is whatever precedes the wrapper's store path. It prefixes every value with that root and execs wrapProgram's .NAME-wrapped with argv[0] passed through. bundle/ (the bwrap entrypoint) stays as it is, so manual-bundle keeps building until eon-zti4.6 switches it and deletes bundle/.
Semantics: --set, --set-default and --prefix follow shell makeWrapper, which the Nix channel runs: drop the first equal element, then prepend; a set-but-empty value counts as unset. Values inside the tree's excluded paths drop out of the table. Today that is only Mesa's share in Venus's XDG_DATA_DIRS, per eon-zti4.1's host Vulkan decision. A gate requires every other value to exist in the tree.
References: nixpkgs 567a49d makeWrapper output (the three scripts in the closure) and pkgs/by-name/ma/makeBinaryWrapper/make-binary-wrapper.sh. Its wrapProgram uses --inherit-argv0, so argv[0] is passed through; the launcher does the same. Rejected: its set_env_prefix semantics, which differ from shell makeWrapper on set-but-empty values (it yields 'value:').
Check: a new Nix check runs the tree as a host without Nix would. bwrap binds a stand-in host glibc (nixpkgs glibc) and its loader at /lib64/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2, the tree at two locations and nothing else from /nix, with --clearenv. Probe: nested bwrap inside this host's Nix sandbox works (userns-probe-2). The bundle itself stays namespace-free; only the check needs nested user namespaces, so it cannot run on hosts that restrict them.

title: Relocate compiled-in data roots for the relinked bundle
description:
## Why

Mechanism accepted on eon-zti4.1 (epic eon-zti4). Several components read data from store paths compiled into the binaries, so they misbehave without /nix even after the relink and launcher. The prototype hit fonts.conf (Venus refused to start: "terminal font family is unavailable") and the xkbcommon Compose root ("No Compose file for locale C.UTF-8").

## Evidence (eon-zti4.1 inventory)

- helix-term: compiled-in helix-runtime path; HELIX_RUNTIME overrides it.
- zoxide 0.9.9: compiled-in fzf store path (a nixpkgs patch), which breaks `zi`.
- ncurses: default terminfo dir. bash-interactive: lib dirs. openssl: etc/ssl; use the host CA store via SSL_CERT_FILE/SSL_CERT_DIR, or the host default.
- The fonts.conf store `<dir>` entries become `prefix="relative"` (supported by fontconfig-parser 0.5.8, which Venus uses through fontdb).
- Venus: take libwayland-client from the host (as the AppImage excludelist does). Keep the bundled vulkan-loader, which loaded host ICDs in the prototype. libxkbcommon comes from the host or the bundle with XKB and Compose roots set. Venus's RUNPATH must carry no bundled gcc runtime, so host GPU drivers never get an older libgcc_s.

## Scope

In scope: launcher env and build-time relative rewrites in the relinked tree for the items above; the launcher table from the launcher child.
Out of scope: Zsh and Fish (gone after eon-8olu); manual-bundle shipping; installer.

## Acceptance

- Inside an Orbit terminal started from the relinked tree with no /nix: hx finds its runtime (`hx --health` shows the runtime dir), `zi` runs fzf, the terminfo lookup for Orbit's TERM succeeds, and an HTTPS fetch from a managed tool verifies certificates.
- Venus starts with the bundled fonts and logs no xkbcommon Compose error.

## Verification

- An isolated headless run with no /nix, either a VM (recipe on eon-zti4.1) or a Nix check where possible, recording each item above. Desktop focus rule: never on Lucca's desktop.
- `nix develop -c eon-test` exits 0.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if a component cannot be pointed at relocated data without forking it.
close_reason: Compiled-in data roots relocated for the relinked bundle (helix fallback link, zoxide fzf from PATH, ncurses terminfo, relative fonts.conf, host libwayland-client and gcc runtime for Venus, xkb roots); bundle-launch checks and Ubuntu 26.04 VM proof recorded

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:

Inventory changes: openssl is no longer in the tree (it left with Zsh and Fish). nu and atuin verify TLS through rustls-platform-verifier, and lazygit through Go crypto/x509; all three read the host CA store (/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt, /etc/pki/tls/certs/ca-bundle.crt, ...). CodexBarCLI keeps its SSL_CERT_FILE default. So the CA item needs no change, only the HTTPS proof. Inert: Go tzdata, iana-etc and mailcap fallbacks (carapace, fzf, lazygit); bash's loadables dir, locale and bashdb.
Decisions (owner, mechanism, rejected):
- Helix (helix 817dcbc helix-loader/src/lib.rs:50-86): after the config dir, HELIX_RUNTIME and the compiled HELIX_DEFAULT_RUNTIME, it falls back to <canonical exe dir>/runtime. The tree gets helix-term/bin/runtime, a relative link to helix-runtime (a "fallback" in nix/bundle-relink.nix). Rejected: HELIX_RUNTIME, which Eon strips from managed hx on purpose (runtime managed_environment.rs:701).
- zoxide (nixpkgs 567a49d pkgs/by-name/zo/zoxide/package.nix: withFzf patches "fzf" to nixpkgs's own fzf store path): zoxidePackage sets withFzf = false in both channels, so zoxide runs fzf from PATH. Eon puts its session bin first on every terminal and managed-shell PATH (sessions.rs orbit_command, managed_environment.rs command); the directory picker already runs "fzf" that way (cli.rs:178). The closure loses the second, unmanaged fzf. Rejected: patching the binary.
- ncurses 6.6: its only compiled terminfo dir is its own store path. Orbit sets TERM=eon (orbit/src/platform.rs:72), and the eon wrapper's TERMINFO_DIRS already resolves that. The bundle adds the bundled ncurses database after Orbit's, for other terminal types (for example inside tmux). It is bundle-only, so host programs in Nix-channel terminals keep their own lookup.
- Fonts: venusFontsConf rewrites makeFontsConf's store dirs to prefix="relative" in both channels (one file; relative to /nix/store under Nix). Venus parses it with fontdb 0.23.0 / fontconfig-parser 0.5.8 and links no libfontconfig. A build gate fails if any store path remains.
- Venus libraries: libwayland-client comes from the host (pkgs.wayland joins the excluded paths, so its LD_LIBRARY_PATH entry and libffi drop out). Only xkbcli helpers inside libxkbcommon NEED it, and it is already a declared host library. This matches the AppImage excludelist (eon-zti4.1 references). The bundled vulkan-loader stays. libxkbcommon stays bundled; the bundle environment sets XKB_CONFIG_ROOT and XLOCALEDIR (as set-default, the env names in libxkbcommon 1.13.1) to the bundled xkeyboard-config and libx11 data. The new eon-relink --host-runtime removes its RUNPATH, so the gate requires each of them on the host, and a host driver never meets the bundled gcc 15 libgcc_s.
- Ownership: wrapper environments stay single-sourced. A wrapper's new `relocated` attrset holds environment for the bundle only (data roots that only the relocated tree misses). The launcher table and the bundle-launch makeWrapper comparison both use the merged environment.
Checks: bundle-launch in its no-/nix stand-in host runs hx --health bash (parser and highlight queries found), tput -T eon and -T xterm-256color through eon-bash (compared with the Nix product), and zoxide query --interactive through fzf on PATH (--filter). The store-lookup trace gate exempts only the fallback targets. Venus fonts and xkb, Orbit-terminal checks and HTTPS go to the Ubuntu 26.04 VM. Dependency effect: zoxide loses its fzf edge; nothing is added.

title: Switch manual-bundle and eon-install to the relinked layout
description:
## Why

Mechanism accepted on eon-zti4.1 (epic eon-zti4). This child ships it: manual-bundle switches from the bwrap /nix projection to the relinked tree and launcher, and eon-install changes in the same commit, because it rejects any payload without libexec/bwrap. User decision (Lucca, 2026-10-18): eon-install accepts only the new layout, with no bwrap-era compatibility (those candidates were never published).

## Evidence

- `nix/linux-bundle.nix:1-45`: the bwrap helper, the closure copy, provenance (bubblewrap fields at :13-24) and closure-paths.txt (:42).
- `installer/src/main.rs:200` and `:388`: `executable(libexec/bwrap)` checks. `:63-70`: accepts absolute /nix/store symlinks because they "resolve through the bundle's private /nix" (:64). `installer/src/tests.rs:77`: the fixture creates libexec/bwrap.

## Scope

In scope:
- manual-bundle ships the relinked tree plus launcher; bubblewrap and its vendored source leave the payload, licences and provenance.
- provenance.json and closure-paths.txt describe the relinked, partial payload: glibc, Mesa and LLVM excluded, bytes patched.
- eon-install validates the new layout, rejects absolute symlinks in it, and its tests and fixture are updated.
Out of scope: docs and contract text (next child); the glibc floor change; the final VM proof.

## Acceptance

- `nix build .#manual-bundle` produces an archive with no bwrap, no absolute store symlink and no glibc/Mesa/LLVM. The bundle's `eon versions` matches the Nix product's (EON-C2/C6: same manifest and lock bytes).
- eon-install's tests cover installing the new layout and rejecting an absolute symlink.

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test` exits 0, including the installer suite.
- `nix build .#manual-bundle` exits 0. Extracting outside /nix and running `env -i ./eon versions` exits 0 on this host.
- Shared lifecycle/trust boundary route: full affected Rust and Nix surfaces (`nix flake check`).

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if eon-install needs an EON-C5 contract change, not only validation code.
close_reason: manual-bundle ships the relinked tree with a relative eon entry link and schema 2 provenance; bubblewrap and bundle/ are gone; eon-install rejects absolute symlinks and requires the linked entrypoint; end-to-end install, eon-test and flake check pass

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Design and reference gate (2026-10-19, edge f973ce0, clean apart from the unrelated untracked review-corners.md).
Contract: nix build .#manual-bundle yields eon-<version>-x86_64-linux.tar.zst and SHA256SUMS. The archive root holds eon (a relative symlink to the tree's eon launcher), nix/store (the bundle-relink tree as built), closure-paths.txt, component-manifest.json, flake.lock, provenance.json and licenses/eon. No bwrap, no absolute symlink, no glibc, Mesa, Wayland or what only they reach (LLVM).
Owners: nix/bundle-relink.nix keeps the relink policy and exports its excluded roots and glibc floor (the floor becomes one let binding read by --glibc-floor and by provenance). nix/linux-bundle.nix keeps archive assembly and receipts. eon-install keeps install-time validation.
Entrypoint: the launcher finds the tree root from /proc/self/exe, so the top-level eon must be a link; a copy or hard link reports its own path and matches no wrapper. Reference: Exodus ef3d5e92c1b6 src/exodus_bundler/bundling.py:503-517 makes each bin/ entry a relative symlink to its launcher, and templates/launcher.sh:3 resolves the launcher's real directory with readlink -f. Kept: the relative link. Rejected: a top-level launcher copy with its own table row (a second match rule in the launcher), and the prototype's /bin/sh entry script (host shell glue).
Receipts: provenance.json schema 2 drops bubblewrap and adds relink {glibc_floor, excluded: the glibc, Mesa and Wayland store paths}. closure-paths.txt lists exactly the shipped store paths (the tree's nix/store entries), so what the package's closure lacks is excluded or pruned with them. The bytes are patched, so the store paths name origins, not NAR contents.
Installer: extraction rejects every absolute symlink. The relative-link depth check already rejects a root component, so the /nix/store exception just goes. The payload's eon must be a symlink resolving to an executable file, and the libexec/bwrap checks go. A bwrap-era payload (regular-file eon, absolute store links) is then neither installable nor selectable by rollback, per Lucca's 2026-10-18 decision, with no bwrap-specific code.
Deletions: bundle/ (the bwrap entrypoint crate), pkgsStatic.bubblewrap and licenses/bubblewrap-source. Dependency effect: bubblewrap leaves the payload; nothing is added.
Docs here: docs/DEVELOPMENT.md (bundle/ gone, relink adopted) and docs/INSTALLER.md's symlink sentence, which describe code this commit changes. MANUAL-BUNDLE, INSTALLER.md's userns prerequisite, CONTRACTS and CHANGELOG stay with eon-zti4.7.
Checks: installer tests (absolute link rejected at extraction; the fixture uses the new layout; a regular-file entry is not selectable); nix build .#manual-bundle plus an archive listing; extract outside /nix and env -i ./eon versions compared with the Nix product; a local end-to-end eon-install install of that archive over a throwaway HTTPS server and signing key (candidate observation, not lm9p proof); nix develop -c eon-test; nix flake check.

title: Update bundle docs and the EON-C6 host-input statement
description:
## Why

After the switch (epic eon-zti4), docs and contracts still describe the bwrap bundle. User decision (Lucca, 2026-10-18, on eon-zti4.1): EON-C6 gains a statement that the direct bundle takes libc, NSS, locales and the Vulkan driver from the host as declared inputs, while the Nix channel pins them. Component identities and the graph stay unchanged. Lucca approved this in principle; the exact wording must be shown to him before it is written.

## Evidence

- `docs/MANUAL-BUNDLE.md` "Execution and host boundary" (around :14-40): the bwrap /nix projection, "No ELF/config path rewriting", the userns host requirement, and the bundled Mesa software driver. Its receipts section explains absolute /nix/store symlinks resolving within the bwrap view. The licence text covers bubblewrap.
- `docs/CONTRACTS.md:285-305` EON-C6; `:251-283` EON-C5, which names no mechanism and stays unchanged.

## Scope

In scope: MANUAL-BUNDLE execution boundary and host prerequisites (glibc >= the declared floor, a host Vulkan driver, native Wayland, no userns), receipts, licence and userns copy; the EON-C6 host-input statement; a CHANGELOG entry if user-visible bundle requirements change.
Out of scope: EON-C5 text; runtime code.

## Acceptance

- No doc claims bwrap, a /nix projection or a userns requirement for the bundle; host prerequisites match the builder's declared floor and the GPU stance.
- The EON-C6 text Lucca approved is in docs/CONTRACTS.md.

## Verification

- Planning/docs route: changed Markdown paths and contract IDs listed in the bead, and a grep showing no stale bwrap/userns claims in docs/.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop for Lucca's approval of the exact EON-C6 wording before editing CONTRACTS.md.
close_reason: MANUAL-BUNDLE, INSTALLER, DISTRIBUTION and CHANGELOG describe the relinked bundle and its host inputs; EON-C6 carries Lucca's approved host-inputs text; no doc claims bwrap, a /nix projection or a userns requirement for the bundle
