comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Result (eon-c4, 2026-10-26/27 overnight). Verdict: GO. Every required lifecycle state is available through upstream's render-state ImageIterator plus Graphics::image. Upstream Uzaaft/libghostty-rs 9ede35b8 is enough for orb-j2i.6 without fork changes, once eon-9rtt.4 moves the pin.

The pointer-lifetime stop condition does not fire. A pixel slice cannot outlive the next mutating call, but Orbit never needs it to. `FrameBuilder::frame` takes `&Terminal` and returns an owned `Frame` (orbit/src/frame.rs:36-55). Copying the pixels during that same extraction ends the borrow before carry-out (see 4). One correctness condition: orb-j2i.4 must land before orb-j2i.12 (see 3).

## Revisions and environment

- Eon tree: edge 2556829 (this bead's base). Observed package: the installed `eon` profile element, /nix/store/bmnw2kag1yx800zrg6n560yfk69fzas6-eon-0.1.3. It was built from path:/home/lucca/pjs/eon/eon, so the store path is its only exact identity. Its Orbit is /nix/store/y2bpij3kgp0jhy0jxpni5ihfvb2778vg-yazelix-orbit-0.1.0, still on fork libghostty-rs 6313a9b and Ghostty 8c425a7bd. Its Yazi is aa526434 (`Yazi 26.5.6 (Nixpkgs 2026-05-05)`), /nix/store/4sx3b1rmic8rs5paq48f4yxhx5mgz7zg-yazi-26.5.6.
- Isolation: a private headless Sway (pixman) at 1600x900, private HOME and XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, driven over wdotool. The driver is ~/.cache/eon-agents/j2i1-work/obs/drive.sh, a copy of eon-overseer/batch/proof.sh. It never touched Lucca's Eon, and the eon profile was not refreshed.
- Scratch program: ~/.cache/eon-agents/j2i1-work/scratch (main.rs sha256 3b14c644…bae05) against upstream libghostty-rs 9ede35b8ea94a55ed3608408d67e102883129f1e (safe crate, default `kitty-graphics` feature), which builds Ghostty 521cf2c5d30bd48028ca61546c64e7913764073d. Built in upstream's own devshell (zig 0.17.0, rustc 1.90.0), `cargo build --release --jobs 4`. It replays Yazi's captured output byte for byte. The capture is obs/run1/w/kgp.log, sha256 5d16b30d…cb226, 4,005,469 bytes.
- Machine: i5-13450HX, 16 threads, 31 GiB. eon-test from eon-9rtt.4 was running throughout. Only obs/out-bench.txt saves its load with the output. The load averages read by hand just before the scenario runs (5.49 1-minute before S1-S3, 1.66-2.09 before the Sway run) appear only in this session's shell output.

## 1. What Yazi does in Eon today (observed)

The pane is 127x43 cells, first pane of a 1600x900 window with the sidebar.
- TIOCGWINSZ: rows 43, cols 127, xpixel 1296, ypixel 801. That is the whole surface including padding. Venus's cell is 10x18, so the text area is 1270x774.
- Replies (perl probe, 1 s per query): XTVERSION `\eP>|libghostty\e\\`; DA1 `\e[?62;22c`; DA2 `\e[>1;0;0c`; Kitty `a=q` `\e_Gi=31;OK\e\\`; CSI 14t, 16t and 18t give no reply; `CSI ? u` `\e[?0u`.
- `yazi --debug` in the pane: `Emulator.detect: Emulator { kind: Left(Ghostty), version: "libghostty", light: false, csi_16t: (0, 0), force_16t: false }`, `Adapter.matches: Kgp`, `Dimension.available: Dimension { rows: 43, columns: 127, width: 1296, height: 801 }`. Yazi on PATH is libexec/eon/bin/yazi, which links to eon. TERM=eon. The Files popup was observed in a second isolated run (obs/run2, with YAZI_LOG=debug inherited from the supervisor). About 79 ms after Alt+Shift+Y, its Yazi logged a WARN "Failed to detect background color" that quotes the replies it received: `\e_Gi=31;OK\e\\\eP>|libghostty\e\\\e[?62;22c` (run2/yazi-state/yazi.log). That reply contains "ghostty", which selects Kgp, and it drew the same placeholder rows. A probe popup (custom `[popups.probe]` on Alt+Shift+O) ran `yazi --debug` and got `Adapter.matches: Kgp`, `Dimension.available: Dimension { rows: 42, columns: 125, width: 1280, height: 797 }`, with the same replies (run2/w/yd-popup.txt, replies-popup.txt). The Files popup's own `Dimension` line is not recorded, because `--debug` cannot run inside it. The perl probe that ran first in the popup saw winsize 24x80 with 0x0 pixels, a moment before the popup was sized. A program that reads pixel size at startup in a popup can miss the real size until SIGWINCH. orb-j2i.4 should check this at popup start. Inside a nested script(1) pty the replies, winsize and Yazi's detection are identical, so the capture is faithful.
- Yazi's stream (a 1200x900 RGB PNG and a 900x1200 RGBA PNG, both downscaled by Yazi):
  - Startup probe: `\e7\e_Gi=31,s=1,v=1,a=q,t=d,f=24;AAAA\e\\\e[>q\e[16t\e]11;?\a\e[0c\e8`.
  - Each preview is `q=2,a=T,C=1,U=1,f=24|32,s=479,v=359|639,i=2464929,m=1` (id = Yazi's pid), sent in 4096-byte base64 chunks. Then come 47-column U+10EEEE placeholder rows with fg `38;2;37;156;161`, the id as RGB, plus row and column diacritics.
  - Leaving a preview overwrites the placeholder cells with spaces, then sends `\e_Gq=2,a=d,d=A\e\\`. Moving to the next image retransmits under the same id.
- What Venus draws: rows of missing-glyph boxes where the preview belongs, in both the pane and the Files popup. No image appears. Captures: obs/run1/pane-rgb.png, pane-rgba.png, popup-rgb.png, popup-rgba.png. This confirms the plan's premise: Eon advertises Kitty graphics (`a=q` OK plus the ghostty brand) and draws only placeholder glyphs.

## 2. Iterator results per lifecycle step (scratch program, terminal 127x43, cells 10x18)

Every placeholder entry reports: protocol Kitty, layer BelowText, z -1, kind Virtual, placement id 0, one entry per placeholder row (grid Nx1), id = 2464929, and the image generation. Unicode-placeholder placements arrive as one entry per row. orb-j2i.6 must either carry per-row entries or merge them; per-row is what libghostty and ghostling_rs do.
- Transmit (`a=T,U=1`), no placeholders yet: 0 entries, placements_generation 0. Storage holds the image (479x359 Rgb, compression None, 515,883 decoded bytes, image gen 1, storage gen 2) and one virtual placement.
- Placeholders printed: 20 entries at cell (79,1..20), each px 470x18, src (0, about 18k, 469x18), image gen 1, placements_generation 1.
- Placeholder cells erased with spaces: 0 entries. The image and its virtual placement stay in storage.
- `a=d,d=A`: no change. Kitty's d=a/A deletes only visible placements, and Ghostty skips virtual placements there (src/terminal/kitty/graphics_storage.zig:1473-1490). Not exercised: `a=d,d=A` while placeholders are still visible (by the same source the outcome is the same), and an image deleted (d=I) while its placeholders remain. Yazi sends neither; orb-j2i.6/.8 should cover the second. The image stays until it is replaced, the screen's storage is reset, or the storage limit evicts it.
- Replacement with a new image under the same id: image gen 1 to 4 (to 7 on the next send), storage gen 2 to 5, a new storage placement number, and a new data pointer. The same holds when replaced while the old placeholders are still on screen (S2.5): the entries keep their cells and switch to gen 4 with the new image's geometry.
- RGBA 479x639: 35 entries. The first is px 470x14 with offset (0,4) (vertical centring); the rest are px 470x18.
- Scroll (CSI 3 S on the alternate screen; line feeds into scrollback on the primary screen): the entries move up with their cells and the source rects shift (src y 36 onward). Entries scrolled out of the viewport disappear, and 0 entries remain once all rows are off (S3.4).
- Viewport scrolled back into scrollback (primary screen, viewport -3): entries return for the visible rows.
- Resize to 100x30: the runs clip to 21 columns (src width 210). The terminal's own reflow also drops the top 13 rows, leaving 5 of 18 placeholder rows; that is not image behaviour. Resize to 12x22 cells: geometry is recomputed (px 252x22). Rows whose diacritics index past the image's height at the new cell size yield no entry (2 entries for 5 placeholder rows).
- Alternate screen exit: active storage switches to the primary screen's (storage gen 0, 0 entries). Re-entering the alternate screen gives back the alternate storage with the RGBA image still stored (1,224,324 bytes). Each screen's storage outlives the program that filled it.
- Fresh render state (the reattach equivalent): the same entries and geometry; placements_generation starts again at 1. This value is only comparable within one render state, so a reattach must resend the full list, which is already the plan.
- Default storage limit at Ghostty 521cf2c: `kitty_image_storage_limit()` returns 10,000,000 on a new terminal. The safe crate's module docs say Kitty graphics are off until a limit is set; that doc is wrong at this pin. Orbit should set its limit explicitly (orb-j2i.6 or .7). S0 ran on the default; S1-S3 set 10,485,760, a stand-in the scripts mislabel as "Orbit's 10 MiB limit" (Orbit sets none today; the fork's default was 10 MB). The scratch terminal's own replies (XTVERSION, DA1, a=q, DECRQSS, DECRQM, CSI ? u; out-s0.txt) match what the installed fork answered in Eon.

## 3. Placeholder grid versus Yazi's grid when the PTY pixels include padding: they do not match

Yazi derives its cell size from the PTY pixel fields: 1296/127 = 10.2 and 801/43 = 18.63. It prints 47x20 placeholders for the 479x359 image and 47x35 for 479x639. libghostty knows the real 10x18 cell and computes 48x20 and 48x36. Result: libghostty crops the right 10 px of every image (src width 469 of 479) and the bottom 14 px of the tall one. The last source row ends at 625 of 639. The image is not misplaced, only cropped by about 2%. orb-j2i.4 removes this by reporting the text area (cols x cw, rows x ch) in the PTY pixel fields. Plan change (pre-approved route, relayed below): orb-j2i.12 now also depends on orb-j2i.4, because the installed proof cannot show a correct image without it.

## 4. Pointer lifetime, decoded bytes, cost, peak

- `Image::data()` returns `&'t [u8]` borrowed from `Graphics<'t>`, which is borrowed from `&Terminal`. The compiler forbids holding it across `vt_write`, `resize` or any other `&mut Terminal` call. The pointer was in fact stable across scroll and resize and changed on replacement, but that is not a promise. Orbit must copy the pixels out while it holds `&Terminal` during frame extraction. It needs to copy only when (id, image generation) is new, which is how ghostling_rs keys its texture cache (example/ghostling_rs/src/main.rs:711-737; the placement queue it reads is built at :401-467). The pixels are always decoded and uncompressed (Rgb or Rgba here, compression None), ready to send as they are.
- Per frame, 2000 frames, 3 runs (obs/out-bench.txt; load average 11.82 / 7.41 / 4.42 over 1, 5 and 15 minutes, so these are upper bounds):
  - render_state.update with nothing changed: 0.5-1.4 us.
  - Image list walk with all getters: 2.6-3.3 us for 20 entries, 4.3-5.4 us for 35.
  - Lookup plus copying the pixels: 25.9-30.2 us for 0.49 MiB RGB, 97.3-121.8 us for 1.17 MiB RGBA.
  - The 500-frame runs inside S1 (out-s1.txt; 1-minute load 5.49 read just before, not saved with the output) gave 0.1/1.1/12.9 us (RGB) and 0.2/2.1/58.7 us (RGBA).
  - The copy is paid only on a generation change.
- Ingest: `vt_write` of a whole 1.6 MB chunked RGBA transmit takes 0.42-0.73 ms, and 0.57-1.03 ms for the 0.69 MB RGB stream with Yazi's UI.
- Peak bytes, counting allocator, with libghostty on `Allocator::GLOBAL`; the replay's 3.82 MiB input buffer is subtracted:
  - RGB transmit: peak 0.63 MiB for a 0.49 MiB image.
  - RGBA transmit while the old RGB was still stored: peak 1.96 MiB for a 1.17 MiB image. The largest peak seen was 2.04 MiB, when the RGBA was resent while the RGBA was stored (S1.8).
  - Steady state retains one decoded image per screen per Yazi process, because Yazi reuses its pid id. That image stays after Yazi hides the preview or exits (see 2).
  - The worst case is libghostty's per-screen storage limit times two screens. Orbit's own retained copies must stay within a bound of the same kind (orb-j2i.7). Each copy briefly peaks at about twice its size: the bench measured 1.05 MiB transient for a 0.49 MiB copy (out-bench.txt).
  - Page memory is mmap'd by libghostty and not counted; it is unrelated to images.
  - Yazi's default caps (600x900) bound one RGBA image at 2.16 MB.

## Inputs for orb-j2i.2 and the later children

- Wire entries: per-row virtual entries with (id, generation, layer, z, viewport cell, grid size, cell offset, pixel size, source rect, placement id, kind).
- Resources: keyed by (epoch, id, generation). A replacement under the same id yields a new generation.
- Per-screen storage persists across alternate-screen exit, so resources must outlive the primary/alternate switch.
- Yazi hides by erasing cells, so frames stop referencing an image while it stays in storage. Venus can evict by reference, and Orbit must not resend unreferenced images.
- Orbit sets the storage limit explicitly.
- eon-9rtt.4 is a hard prerequisite for orb-j2i.6 (the dependency exists). No fork change is needed.

## Approval relayed by the coordinator

eon-overseer relayed Lucca's words, 2026-10-26: "focus on finishing the worspace-switching beads, but try to advance on kitty-graphics too / everything is pre-approved. autonomous. / and sprinkle the ones the subagent listed that are important." And: "also pre-aprove changes of plan if a clearly better alternative appears". The coordinator applied them to this lane: orb-j2i.1, then drafting, indexing and adopting orb-j2i.2's contracts on a go verdict, plus clearly better plan changes. Not covered: push, promotion, GitHub or site posts, touching his running Eon, deletion.

Used here only for the orb-j2i.12 -> orb-j2i.4 dependency (evidence in 3).

## Process note

The main checkout's beads.db still shows orb-j2i.1 as in_progress. The coordinator said to leave main alone; landing this commit's issues.jsonl row reconciles it.

Run in the detached worktree, `br` resolves .beads to the main checkout through the git common dir. My first claim (`br update orb-j2i.1 --status in_progress`) therefore went to /home/lucca/pjs/eon/eon/.beads/beads.db. Everything else used BEADS_DB=<worktree>/.beads/beads.db. The coordinator has been told.

Evidence (disposable, not a harness): ~/.cache/eon-agents/j2i1-work/{obs,scratch}.
- Scenario scripts: obs/s0-s3.txt and bench.txt; outputs: obs/out-s*.txt and out-bench.txt.
- Captures: obs/run1/*.png and run2/*.png.
- Popup observation: obs/run2 (drive2.sh).

Review ledger: 3 passes. Pass 1 found 3 blocking issues: unsaved bench output, the Files popup detection not recorded, and the GO not addressing the pointer-lifetime stop rule. It also found 8 nits. All are fixed in this text; the popup detection and the bench were re-observed. Pass 2 found 1 blocking issue, load figures not saved with their output (fixed), and 8 nits. Pass 3 found nothing blocking and 5 nits, applied. No Codex round: the slice changes no code, tests, scripts or contract.

title: Validate and assemble image resources in Venus
description:
## Why

Venus must validate and assemble resources per attachment before any GPU allocation and carry
placements into the scene, without a Kitty parser or placeholder reading.

## Evidence

- Transport reader and bounded `EventQueue` (256 events, 2 frames, about 24 MiB, frame coalescing):
venus/src/transport.rs:451-585, 704-724.
- `SessionModel::apply` -> `FrameReducer::push` -> `Scene::from_frame`: venus/src/model.rs:346-455,
venus/src/scene.rs:2961.
- Each visible terminal has its own transport and `SessionModel` (venus/src/application.rs:461-531);
hidden tabs keep no attachment.

## Prerequisites

orb-j2i.1, orb-j2i.5 (codec).

## Scope

In scope:
- Queue treatment of resource messages (counted against the queue's bytes, never coalesced away).
- In `SessionModel`: validate announce metadata against VEN-C31 and ORB-C16 limits before buffering,
assemble chunks, reject malformed, oversized, duplicate, out-of-order and stale input with an
explicit failure, scope resources to the attachment epoch.
- Carry placements (resolved geometry, id, generation, pending marker) on `Scene` with the terminal
identity the renderer needs.
- CPU-only tests in the existing model and canonical-scene tiers.

Out of scope:
- GPU upload, cache, drawing (orb-j2i.11); any Kitty or placeholder interpretation.

## Acceptance

- Valid streams produce complete resources and scene placements; every invalid case fails
deterministically before allocation.

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test`; fmt and clippy for venus; converge plus Codex.
close_reason: Validation and assembly landed; proof recorded in the bead's comment

comments.author: lucca
lucca
comments.text:
Implemented and proved (2026-10-27). The code was written on base b7aec03 and rebased onto edge de270de; the code tree this bead's commit records is the rebased one.

What landed:
- venus/src/model.rs: `SessionModel` validates resource messages under VEN-C31 and assembles them. It keeps one attachment's order state: the last announced identity, at most one assembly, and the set of complete, unretired identities.
  - An announcement is refused, before any reservation, when no frame has been accepted in the attachment, when its identity is not greater than every earlier one, when another resource is incomplete, when 1,024 resources are complete and unretired, or when its metadata differs from what `ResourceAnnounce::new` derives. Only then is the buffer reserved, at exactly the byte length.
  - A chunk must name the incomplete resource at the next index, with exactly 262,144 bytes, or exactly the rest for the last chunk.
  - A retirement must name a complete, unretired resource.
  - Any violation returns `ModelError::Resource(detail)` and drops the assembly. Both application callers already route errors to `mark_lost`, so the attachment fails (VEN-C1, VEN-C3).
  - `apply` now returns `Option<ModelEffect>`, with `ModelEffect::{Clipboard, Resource}`. The last chunk moves the pixels out as `ImageResource { attachment, resource, format, width, height, pixels }`, so the model never holds a completed resource.
  - Each attachment takes a process-unique number, assigned in `new` and `prepare_reconnect`. `prepare_reconnect`, `Exited`, `mark_lost`, `mark_lost_preserving_constraining_notice` and `mark_incompatible` discard the resource state.
- venus/src/application.rs: both callers handle `ModelEffect::Clipboard` as before and drop `ModelEffect::Resource`, which counts as refused, until orb-j2i.11 uploads. ORB-C16's switch is off in the shipped build, so Orbit sends no resources.
- venus/src/scene.rs: `Scene.graphics: SceneGraphics { attachment, placements, placements_omitted }`. Each `ScenePlacement { resource, state, source, target }` keeps the protocol's `PlacementState` and `SourceRect`, and its target is in cells from the grid's top-left: the cell plus pixel offset and size, divided by the frame's stated cell size. Entries keep frame order; layer and z are dropped (one band). `Scene::from_frame(frame, attachment)`. Test-only `Scene` literals gain `graphics: SceneGraphics::default()`.
- venus/src/transport.rs: no production change. The existing reduction test now also shows that a frame is not coalesced across a resource message (it uses a retirement; the gate comment said "a chunk", and every non-frame message takes the same path).
- No contract, doc or changelog change. VEN-C31 stays Planned, and its proof belongs to orb-j2i.11 and orb-j2i.12. The behavior is unreachable in the shipped build until ORB-C16's switch turns on.

Proof on the rebased code tree (x86_64 Linux, sandboxed `eon-test`, CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4):
- `nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-venus`: lib 144 passed / 2 ignored, bin 64 passed / 4 ignored, canonical_scene 20 passed. That includes `resource_streams_assemble_complete_pixels_and_frames_carry_placements` and `invalid_resource_streams_fail_deterministically` (14 invalid sequences plus the pre-attachment, pre-frame, metadata and 1,024-cap cases) in venus/tests/canonical_scene.rs, and `frame_reduction_preserves_message_and_revision_order`.
- `cargo clippy --locked -p yazelix-venus --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean. `cargo fmt --check -p yazelix-venus`: clean.
- The same three checks passed on the pre-rebase candidate tree ca491d70566779a111ee4974d3439b021739a84b, run by me and again by the round-1 Claude reviewer; the tree was unchanged after them.
- Not run: an installed or GUI observation. None is needed, since no shipped path reaches this code until orb-j2i.11. No profile refresh (Venus behavior in the shipped build is unchanged).

Portability disposition: neutral.

Review ledger (orb-j2i.10 slice):
- First round, on candidate tree ca491d70566779a111ee4974d3439b021739a84b (base b7aec03), with two reviewers in parallel:
  - A fresh Claude reviewer, who also ran the checks: 0 blocking. It noted three nits. The queue test uses a retirement where the gate said "a chunk"; this is recorded above. `ImageResource` derives Clone; it is left. The cap and oversized cases bypass the codec, which is unavoidable for the oversized case.
  - Codex: 0 findings, 0 nits.
- The first round converged on that tree. Rebasing onto edge de270de needed one conflict resolution (accessibility.rs test imports, v21 plus `SceneGraphics`).
- One Claude round on the rebase (range-diff b7aec03..897cc58 against de270de..8e2858e, checks rerun, tree unchanged): 0 code findings. It found one tracker-metadata item: the worktree's comment id 4320 collides with an id in the main database, so bead writes are replayed through br at landing rather than copied from this jsonl.
- Narrow Codex re-check of the rebase: 0 findings.
- Totals: 2 Codex passes (0 findings), 2 Claude passes (0 blocking code findings).
- Before review, one check of my own failed and was fixed. My first queue-test edit pushed a third uncoalescable frame into a two-frame queue, and the test blocked until the eon-test timeout. The assertion now runs in its own drained segment.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Reference gate and plan (2026-10-27, base b7aec03). This slice adds Venus's validation of untrusted resource messages and the per-attachment resource lifecycle, a trust and lifecycle boundary, so it is consequential. The contracts (VEN-C31 and ORB-C16 as adopted in orb-j2i.2) govern; no contract text changes.

- Behavior and owners:
  - `SessionModel` alone validates resource order and assembles. On each announcement it checks, before reserving anything: a frame has been accepted in this attachment; the identity is greater than every earlier one in the attachment; no resource is incomplete; fewer than 1,024 are complete and unretired (freed ones included); and the metadata equals what `orbit_protocol::session::ResourceAnnounce::new` derives. That function stays the one owner of the format, side, length and chunk-count rules, which the codec already enforces on decode. Only then does it reserve the buffer, sized exactly to the byte length. Each chunk must name the incomplete resource at the next index and carry exactly 262,144 bytes, or exactly the rest when it is the last. A retirement must name a complete, unretired identity. Any violation returns `ModelError::Resource`, which the existing callers already route to `mark_lost`, failing the attachment (VEN-C1, VEN-C3). The failing arm drops the assembly at once.
  - The last chunk moves the pixels out of the model as a new `apply` effect: the return value becomes `ModelEffect::{Clipboard, Resource}`. The model therefore never holds a completed resource, and the caller must upload or refuse it before it handles the next message. That is VEN-C31's "uploaded or refused before the next announcement is accepted". Until orb-j2i.11 uploads, the application drops the effect. Orbit's graphics switch is off, so nothing produces resources in the shipped build.
  - Resource state is scoped to one attachment. `prepare_reconnect`, `Exited`, `mark_lost` and `mark_incompatible` discard it. Each attachment takes a process-unique number. The completed resource and the scene carry that number, so orb-j2i.11 can key textures across terminals, and a scene kept across a reconnect (VEN-C3) names an attachment whose resources are gone.
  - `Scene::from_frame` carries the frame's placement entries in frame order: Orbit's identity, the entry state (ready, pending or unavailable, using the protocol's own type), the source rectangle in resource pixels, and the target in cells from the grid's top-left (cell, plus pixel offset and size divided by the frame's stated cell size). It also carries `placements_omitted`. Layer and z are dropped because VEN-C31 draws one band in frame order. Clipping the source to the resource bounds, converting it to `Scene.images` and drawing markers stay with orb-j2i.11, which holds the resource sizes.
  - Transport queue: no change. Resource messages already count their full framed bytes against the queue's byte bound, and only frame-bearing events are ever replaced. One assertion is added to the existing reduction test so a chunk between frames survives in order.
- References read:
  - VEN-C31 (venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md:2158) and ORB-C16 (orbit/docs/CONTRACTS.md:1049), including Orbit's 1,024 cap and its one-transfer-at-a-time rule.
  - orbit-protocol session codec (`validate_announce`, `validate_chunk_bytes`): the codec checks metadata and chunk size bounds, but not order, exact chunk sizes, identities or retirements.
  - Comparable implementations: kitty `b2cb871254fbdac19a085188813c8dfb258b95cd`, kitty/graphics.c `load_image_data` (one `currently_loading` buffer per terminal; raw RGB/RGBA past the size computed from its dimensions is refused with EFBIG; completion checks for insufficient data). Ghostty `8c425a7bd57de848aa83cb9b003b1ecd6037c56a` (Orbit's libghostty pin), src/terminal/kitty/graphics_image.zig `LoadingImage` (expected size derived from format and dimensions, max size checked before reading).
  - Kept: one in-progress assembly per terminal; a buffer sized from validated metadata; an exact-length check at completion.
  - Rejected: kitty's buffer growth by doubling, since the length is known and validated up front; and soft per-image errors, since VEN-C31 fails the attachment instead.
  - docs/REFERENCES.md has no graphics route.
- The 1,024 cap is a local Venus constant that cites ORB-C16. The protocol crate has no constant for it, and moving Orbit's into that crate is out of scope.
- Check: CPU tests in venus/tests/canonical_scene.rs over the wire codec:
  - a valid RGB and RGBA stream yields complete pixels and scene placements;
  - every invalid case (before the first frame, a non-increasing identity, a second incomplete resource, the 1,025th unretired resource, an unannounced, out-of-order, wrong-size or excess chunk, a bad or repeated retirement) fails deterministically with `ModelError::Resource`, and the model frees its assembly;
  - a reconnect resets identities.
  Then `nix develop -c eon-test -p yazelix-venus`, cargo fmt --check, clippy -D warnings, converge plus Codex.
- Portability disposition: neutral (platform-independent Rust in the model and scene; no native mechanism).
- Approval relied on: Lucca's standing approval, relayed by eon-overseer on 2026-10-27: "focus on finishing the worspace-switching beads, but try to advance on kitty-graphics too / everything is pre-approved. autonomous." and "also pre-aprove changes of plan if a clearly better alternative appears" (Lucca, 2026-10-26). It applies to this bead's implementation under the VEN-C31 text adopted in orb-j2i.2, which this slice implements unchanged: the validation list quoted in orb-j2i.2's comment on this bead ("the identity is greater than every identity announced before in this attachment; no other resource of this terminal is still incomplete; the format is RGB or RGBA; each side is 1 to 4,096 pixels; the byte length equals width times height times bytes per pixel and is at most 10,000,000; the chunk count is the byte length divided by 262,144, rounded up; fewer than 1,024 resources of this terminal are announced and not retired, counting resources Venus freed"). The plan changes it applies to: Scene entries carry the identity and the three states instead of a Kitty id, generation and pending marker, as orb-j2i.2's comment records, and the completed resource leaves the model as an effect.

title: Upload and draw Orbit images in Venus under a GPU budget
description:
## Why

This bead makes images visible: Venus uploads assembled resources into one window-wide GPU cache and
draws the frame's placements in the band orb-j2i.9 built. Lucca chose (2026-10-23): resources the
current frame references are never evicted; over budget or on device loss Venus draws a
missing-image marker and resyncs by reattach; no request message.

## Evidence

- One `Renderer` and device per window; renderer receives `&Scene` without terminal identity today
(venus/src/application.rs:461-531); `ContentKey` triggers full rebuilds (venus/src/render.rs:869-900).
- Frames in flight after a scale change carry geometry for the old cell size.

## Prerequisites

orb-j2i.7 (Orbit sends resources), orb-j2i.9 (pipeline), orb-j2i.10 (store).

## Scope

In scope:
- Window-wide texture cache keyed by attachment namespace, image id and generation, under the
VEN-C31 budget, with retain-while-referenced and release of unreferenced entries; namespace release
on reattach, tab switch and popup close.
- The application hands completed resources to the renderer; the renderer reports budget refusal or
device loss so the application shows the marker and resyncs that terminal by reattach.
- Draw placements with their resolved geometry; handle scale change (placements carry Orbit's
assumed cell size); add a resident-set version to `ContentKey`.

Out of scope:
- Kitty z-bands other than the chosen one; animation; a request message.

## Acceptance

- In an isolated Eon, Yazi's preview draws at the right place in a pane and a popup; a forced budget
refusal shows the marker and recovers by reattach; no panic.

## Verification

- CPU tests through `nix develop -c eon-test`; one isolated-display observation; fmt and clippy;
converge plus Codex.

## Stop Conditions

- Ask eon-overseer before any isolated Sway session or nix build.

Lucca accepted (2026-10-27, relayed by eon-overseer, "ok") the one unmet acceptance item as a recorded gap: a forced budget refusal recovering by reattach in a running Eon cannot be triggered without a hidden setting; CPU tests and the live image regression cover it (proof comment).

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Contract text adopted in orb-j2i.2 (VEN-C31) replaces parts of this bead's plan; where they differ, the contract governs.
- Venus keys resources by Orbit's identity number within one terminal's attachment, not by Kitty image id and generation.
- It draws any entry whose resource it holds, clipped to the resource, and scales by the frame's cell size during geometry changes.
- It draws the missing-image marker at once for unavailable and refused entries, and after 250 ms for pending ones. The marker's look and the omitted-placements notice fall under the configurability rule.
- This bead turns on Orbit's internal graphics switch in the shipped build, in the same change that makes Venus draw images.
- A texture allocation that fails within the budget is captured, not left to the uncaptured-error panic, and is treated as a budget refusal.
- Budget: 256 MiB window-wide at 4 bytes per pixel, checked before allocation. Revisit it with measurements.
- Configurability: decide whether to expose the 250 ms marker delay, which would change VEN-C31 to state 250 ms as the default, or record one of the rule's reasons for keeping it fixed.
- Resync by reattach after a freed reference, or a refused one once the budget has room again. After device loss it applies only once the renderer works again; question 1 on orb-j2i.2 asks about renderer recreation.

Only Orbit's own checks set it (the real-PTY check in Orbit's env; unit tests through FrameExtractor::new(true)); Eon, Runtime and Venus never set or parse it. This bead removes it when it turns graphics on in the shipped build: make the switch a constant on, or default it on and delete the variable, and update orb-j2i.6's checks to match.

comments.text:
Implemented and proved (2026-10-27). Code tree dd18b8729dbd2b98c10a9eacd0f48f494c72ddc3, rebased onto edge 4e705bc (orb-j2i.8). After the final proof only the proof record changed: this comment, plus ORB-C16's proof sentence naming how the checks ran.

What landed:

- Venus renderer (render/images.rs):
  - `ImageStore` keys entries by (attachment, identity): Held, Freed (evicted for budget while unreferenced) or Refused (budget, or a captured allocation failure).
  - The 256 MiB budget is checked before allocating. Eviction takes unreferenced textures, smallest key first. A refusal frees nothing, and a retired texture is forgotten.
  - The upload writes rows straight from the assembly into one MAP_WRITE | COPY_SRC buffer, adding alpha to RGB as it copies, and drops the assembly. It then copies to the texture inside error scopes and returns once the GPU has finished. It waits for released textures before allocating, so the budget holds on the GPU.

- Venus application:

  - Sweeps dead attachments and retired, unreferenced textures before an upload, after a retirement, when a view's attachment changes, in `reconcile_column_views` and before each redraw.
  - Reattaches a terminal whose frame needs a Freed resource, or a Refused one as `RefusalResync` allows. It allows one resync per refusal across attachments, renewed when placement count or sizes change (positions ignored) or when resident bytes fall below the reading at the next refusal.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Reference gate and plan (2026-10-27, before code).

Consequential: it turns ORB-C16's switch on in the shipped build (the shipped ORBS v14 wire starts carrying graphics state and resources), adds a GPU resource lifecycle and budget, and edits VEN-C31's text. No new dependency, no wire format change.

Authority: Lucca's standing approval, relayed by eon-overseer on 2026-10-27. Lucca, 2026-10-26, to eon-overseer: "focus on finishing the worspace-switching beads, but try to advance on kitty-graphics too / everything is pre-approved. autonomous. / and sprinkle the ones the subagent listed that are important." and "also pre-aprove changes of plan if a clearly better alternative appears". Applied here to: the switch removal, the VEN-C31 and ORB-C16 text edits recorded in this bead's proof comment, and the configurability dispositions below. It does not cover push, promotion or GitHub.

Behavior and owners:
- Orbit: ORB-C16's internal switch becomes a constant on. `cli::kitty_graphics()` and `ORBIT_KITTY_GRAPHICS` are deleted; the host passes `true` to `Orbit::spawn`. `FrameExtractor::new(false)` stays for unit tests only. Chosen over "default on, keep the variable" because the contract says the switch is not configuration, and a variable that can turn it off would be a hidden setting.
- Venus renderer (`render/images.rs`) owns textures, the 256 MiB budget, eviction, refusals and the image and marker draw list. Entries are keyed by (attachment number, Orbit identity): Held, Freed (evicted for budget while unreferenced) or Refused (budget, or a captured allocation failure). The budget is checked before allocation; a refusal frees nothing; RGB expands to RGBA on the CPU; the upload returns only after the GPU copy completes.
- Venus model owns validation (orb-j2i.10) and now reports retirements as an effect and the attachment whose resources are live (attached only).
- Venus application glues them: it uploads completed resources, forwards retirements, sweeps dead attachments and retired unreferenced textures before each redraw, and reattaches a terminal whose frame references a Freed resource, or a Refused one once it would fit. A refusal allows one resync across attachments, spent until the placements' cell targets change or the resident bytes fall.
- Marker: drawn in the image band over the entry's target when the entry is unavailable, refused, freed, or ready but not held (including identities Venus never saw), and over every entry of a scene whose attachment is not live (VEN-C3 reconnect). It is also drawn over pending entries after 250 ms, or at once in an attachment started by an image resync, until a resource of that attachment arrives, so the markers do not blink off for 250 ms after reattach (orb-j2i.2's open note; its recommendation adopted). A source rectangle clipped to the resource shrinks the destination proportionally, so the visible part keeps its scale and place.
- ContentKey gains the derived per-terminal image and marker lists instead of a version counter: any upload, eviction, free or marker coming due changes the key, with no counter to keep in step.

References read (docs/REFERENCES.md has no route for GPU image caches; comparable implementations):
- Ghostty `8c425a7bd57de848aa83cb9b003b1ecd6037c56a` (src/renderer/image.zig): one texture per Kitty image id with a generation; pending/ready/unload states; RGB converted to RGBA on the CPU; no GPU budget; failed or not-ready images draw nothing; no device-loss handling. Kept: CPU RGBA expansion and an sRGB RGBA8 texture; freeing only images that are no longer live. Rejected: drawing nothing when an image is missing (VEN-C31 requires a marker), and per-frame retries of a failed upload (VEN-C31 allows one resync).
- kitty v0.49.2 `b2cb871254fbdac19a085188813c8dfb258b95cd` (graphics.c, shaders.c): eager upload on transmission completion, refcounted textures, a 320 MiB CPU storage quota that can evict referenced images, and GL OOM fatal or unchecked. Kept: eager upload on completion. Rejected: evicting referenced images, and uploading RGB directly (wgpu has no RGB8 texture format).
- WezTerm `e2a98e1b8af156988ad0ac778658ac27b60a55fb` (glyphcache.rs, termwindow/render/paint.rs): images packed into the glyph atlas, which is rebuilt or grown on overflow and then downscales images. Rejected: one shared atlas (it would make images a second owner of glyph atlas space, and downscaling changes what the program asked to show).
- None of the three has a GPU-side budget or a missing-image marker. VEN-C31's budget, marker and resync are Eon's own choices from orb-j2i.2.
- Check: CPU unit tests of the budget plan, the draw and marker derivation, and the resync allowance; the existing ignored live image regression updated to the cache; an isolated-display observation of Yazi (orb-j2i.12 owns the installed acceptance; see the proof comment for which this bead ran).

Configurability dispositions (AGENTS.md Configurability):
- 250 ms marker delay: kept fixed. It is a contract bound (VEN-C31 states it), and it exists only to hide the protocol's frame-before-chunks order. It is not a preference a person tunes, so a setting would cost support with no user benefit.
- Marker look: no new value. It is drawn in the terminal's own foreground colour (an outline at 50% alpha and a 12% fill), so the terminal's colour theme, which Eon already exposes, governs it.
- Omitted-placements notice: a fixed English Venus notice like the existing local notices (input, queue, resize, clipboard), none of which is configurable.
- 256 MiB budget: stays fixed as orb-j2i.2 recorded: a performance and safety budget for every pane of the window. Not revisited: there are no measurements yet to revisit it with (orb-j2i.12 can).

Device loss: unchanged. VEN-C4's terminal renderer failure still owns non-destroyed device loss, so VEN-C31's resync-after-device-loss stays unreachable until renderer recreation exists. orb-j2i.2's question 1 to Lucca stays open; this bead does not decide it.

Portability disposition: neutral. wgpu textures, error scopes and the queue wait are the same on Vulkan and Metal; no Linux or Wayland assumption is added.

title: Prove Yazi image previews on the installed Eon
description:
## Why

The user-visible outcome is Yazi image previews in Eon (Lucca, 2026-10-23). This bead proves it on
the installed product, replacing the former Eonova / Nova Zellij acceptance path, and moves the
contracts to Proven.

## Prerequisites

orb-j2i.8 and orb-j2i.11.

## Scope

In scope:
- Build and refresh the `eon` profile from the accepted tree; installed, isolated dogfood (never the
user's live session): Yazi (Eon's pinned revision) image previews in the Files popup and in an
ordinary pane, across scroll, resize, delete, alternate screen, detach, and reattach; RGB and RGBA
images.
- Proof record: exact repository and component revisions, platform, artifact, extraction cost,
transfer bytes, peak Orbit decoded-image storage, peak Venus GPU memory, queue pressure, unsupported
Kitty features, portability disposition, LOC.
- ORB-C16 and VEN-C31 proof records and status, ORB-C6 restated; CHANGELOG.md entry (user-visible).
- Refresh the active `eon` profile; report that a restart is needed (do not stop the running
supervisor).

Out of scope:
- New features; Zellij or tmux inside Eon (record as unproven).

## Acceptance

- Every lifecycle step shows the preview correctly or removes it, with captures as evidence.

## Verification

- Installed, isolated dogfood per AGENTS.md (one outermost observation per accepted batch); Codex
narrow re-check of the proof record.

## Stop Conditions

- Ask eon-overseer for the build, profile refresh and Sway slot, and to freeze edge for the final
proof.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Reference gate and plan (2026-10-27, eon-5d, before the contract edits).

Consequential only as a contract change: ORB-C16 and ORB-C6 become Proved and VEN-C31 Proven, with proof records. title: Draft and index the static graphics contracts (ORB-C6, ORB-C16, VEN-C31)
description:
## Why

Lucca approved (2026-08-12) changing ORB-C6 and adding one static-graphics resource contract, and
asked (2026-10-23) that contract text come to him before code. Orbit and Venus children cannot start
production code until the text is approved and indexed.

## Evidence

- ORB-C6 (orbit/docs/CONTRACTS.md:232-282), Proved, Boundary "Kitty graphics remain explicitly
unsupported" (:252). ORB-C7 output room (:284-321). Highest IDs at edge ed78d5b: ORB-C15, VEN-C30.
- Venus contracts touched: VEN-C1, C3, C4, C7, C8, C11, C16, C18, C19 (venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md).
- orb-j2i notes hold the seven 2026-10-23 decisions this text must encode.

## Prerequisites

orb-j2i.1 closed with a go verdict and its measurements.

## Scope

In scope:
- Draft, for Lucca: the ORB-C6 change (graphics supported through ORB-C16 instead of unsupported);
ORB-C16 static graphics resource plane: capability, epoch-scoped identity plus generation, resource
announce and chunk shape, placement references with resolved geometry, pending marker and re-send,
blanked placeholder cells, exact limits (filled from orb-j2i.1 measurements), failure behavior, the
one z-band and the recorded gaps; VEN-C31: validation before allocation, window-wide GPU budget,
retain-while-referenced, missing-image marker and resync by reattach, drawing band and clipping;
any ORB-C7 restatement for the new queue class, and ORB-C2 only if CSI 14t/16t/18t answers need it.
- Choose and record the exact Kitty graphics specification revision used as reference.
- Decide whether scrollback previews carry placements; record it in the text.
- After approval, index the contracts as Planned in orbit/docs/CONTRACTS.md and
venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md and add orbit/CHANGELOG.md and venus/CHANGELOG.md entries only if those
files record planned contracts.

Out of scope:
- Code, tests, the protocol crate. Changing contracts other than those named.

## Acceptance

- Lucca's approval of the exact text is recorded on this bead (direct or relayed with his words).
- The indexed text matches the approved text; contract IDs are not reused or renumbered.

## Verification

- Markdown diff plus `br` state; Codex review of the contract-text change per AGENTS.md.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop for Lucca on any change to the seven 2026-10-23 decisions.
close_reason: ORB-C6 change, ORB-C16 and VEN-C31 adopted under Lucca's relayed standing approval and indexed as Planned (ORB-C6 Partially proved); exact text and decisions in comments for his morning review

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Adopted (eon-c4, 2026-10-27): the ORB-C6 change, ORB-C16 and VEN-C31, indexed as Planned (ORB-C6 Partially proved; ORB-C7 unchanged), plus an orbit/CHANGELOG.md entry. venus/CHANGELOG.md records contracts only when they ship, so it gets no entry.

## Where the adopted text is (for the morning review)

- orbit/docs/CONTRACTS.md:
  - the preamble sentence after "Each contract below states the current ORBS v13 behavior";
  - "ORB-C6 — Rich presentation without silent degradation": Status, Boundary and Open proof;
  - "ORB-C16 — Static graphics resource plane", which is all new.
- venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md:
  - the preamble sentence about VEN-C31;
  - "VEN-C31 — Static terminal images", which is all new.
- orbit/CHANGELOG.md: the "ORB-C16 enters the index as Planned" entry.

The exact text is this commit's diff of those files (`git show <this commit> -- orbit/docs/CONTRACTS.md venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md orbit/CHANGELOG.md`).

## Approval relayed by the coordinator

eon-overseer relayed Lucca's words, 2026-10-26: "focus on finishing the worspace-switching beads, but try to advance on kitty-graphics too / everything is pre-approved. autonomous. / and sprinkle the ones the subagent listed that are important." He added: "also pre-aprove changes of plan if a clearly better alternative appears". The coordinator applied this to orb-j2i.2: draft, index and adopt the ORB-C6 change, ORB-C16 and VEN-C31 without stopping, and record the exact text for his morning review. The epic's 2026-10-27 02:31 comment records the same approval.

The seven 2026-10-23 decisions are encoded, with the refinements below.
- Decision 1, the placeholder path: ORB-C16 resolves placements in libghostty and blanks placeholder cells.
- Decision 2, the fork iterator: superseded by eon-9rtt.4's upstream pin, which was Lucca's own decision. orb-j2i.1 proved the upstream iterator suffices.
- Decision 3, no stopgap.
- Decision 4: one band between backgrounds and text, other layers a recorded gap.
- Decision 5: referenced resources are never evicted; the budget is checked before allocation; the marker and resync by reattach; no request message. Its device-loss half becomes reachable only with renderer recreation (question 1).
- Decision 6: pending and re-send; resource messages never cause ORB-C7's disconnect, and every other message keeps it.
- Decision 7: ORBF v3 in ORBS v14.

## Choices made in the text, and why

- **Kitty reference:** kovidgoyal/kitty b2cb871254fbdac19a085188813c8dfb258b95cd (2026-10-01), docs/graphics-protocol.rst. It is the local reference clone's head, and its Unicode-placeholder and deletion sections match what orb-j2i.1 observed (virtual placements are deleted only by d=i/I/r/R/n/N).
- **Scrollback previews carry no placements** and blank their placeholder cells; ORB-C8 and ORB-C9 already exclude graphics. A viewport scrolled into history is a live frame, and orb-j2i.1 S3.2 showed the iterator gives its entries, so it carries them.
- **The PTY text-area pixel size and the CSI 14t/16t/18t answers go into ORB-C16**, not ORB-C2. ORB-C2 already covers terminal-generated replies. The text-area rule exists for placeholder geometry (the orb-j2i.1 §3 crop), so the graphics contract owns it and orb-j2i.4 implements it.
- **Limits** come from orb-j2i.1's measurements:
  - Storage of 10,000,000 bytes per screen: the observed libghostty default, set explicitly because the safe crate's docs disagree with the pin.
  - At most 4,096 pixels per side: over 4.5 times the long side of Yazi's default cap (600x900), and half wgpu's default 8,192-pixel texture limit.
  - Decoded bytes at most 10,000,000: the storage limit.
  - Chunks of 262,144 bytes: a 2.16 MB Yazi image is 9 chunks, which interleave with frames.
  - At most 4,096 entries and 256 resources per frame: Yazi uses 20 to 35 per-row entries per image.
  - A queued resource allowance of 1,048,576 bytes (four chunks), separate from ORB-C7's 12,587,045-byte frame and scroll room, so ORB-C7's guarantees stay intact. A local socket drains four chunks quickly, so a Yazi image completes within a few frames.
  - A window-wide Venus budget of 256 MiB at 4 bytes per pixel: about 20 to 26 maximum-size images (10 MB decoded; RGB grows by a third as a texture).
- **One transfer at a time from one copy.**
  - Orbit copies a resource once when it starts it and sends one resource at a time. Its retained copies (at most 10,000,000 bytes per attachment) and Venus's assembly (one incomplete resource per terminal) are therefore bounded without a cancel message.
  - A replacement mid-transfer finishes the old copy, then retires it.
  - The cap of 1,024 unretired resources per attachment, enforced on both sides, bounds the count of tiny images that the byte budget alone would not.
- **Fixed-size chunks** (all but the last are exactly 262,144 bytes), so both sides derive the same chunk count.
- **Pending to ready.**
  - Orbit publishes a new complete frame when a pending resource's last chunk is sent.
  - Venus draws any entry whose resource it holds, so a resource that arrives just after its frame shows at once.
- **Frame geometry.**
  - Frames state the cell size their placement geometry uses, and Venus scales by the ratio during font or scale changes.
  - Placement entries sit outside ORB-C6's cell-and-link frame budget, with their own ORBF v3 bound. ORB-C6's degradation order is therefore untouched. orb-j2i.5 owns growing the ORBF v3 frame maximum, Orbit's worker output bound and Venus's event-queue bound together (its note says so).
- **Drawing order** follows the Kitty specification: layer, then z-index, then lower Kitty image id, then libghostty's order. Orbit sorts before truncation, so Venus draws in frame order.
- **Device loss.** VEN-C4 still owns renderer failure. Non-destroyed device loss is terminal today: `record_device_loss` never clears, and nothing recreates the renderer.
  - VEN-C31 keeps decision 5's rule (resync by reattach after device loss), but it applies only once the renderer works again.
  - Making that reachable needs renderer recreation, which no bead owns. See question 1.
- **Identity.** Each resource gets its own identity number, strictly increasing within an attachment, so a replaced image gets a new one. The libghostty generation travels in the announcement. Venus checks only that a new identity is greater than the last, so it keeps no growing set. This realizes the epic's "opaque epoch-scoped image identity and libghostty generation" without a pair key. Each chunk carries its identity and index.
- **Inactive screen.** libghostty's storage handle sees only the active screen, so resources of the inactive screen are retired when it is active again or when the attachment ends. The 1,024 cap bounds them meanwhile.
- **Copy gap.** ORB-C9's copy uses libghostty's formatter, which keeps U+10EEEE. Copying across placeholder cells puts it in the clipboard; this is recorded as a gap, not fixed here.
- **Resync and Busy.** Venus's own resync reattach follows VEN-C3: it retries Busy under Eon supervision, and Busy stays terminal in standalone mode. A standalone resync can lose the release race and end its terminal; this is a recorded gap rather than an exception to VEN-C3, since Eon windows are supervised.
- **Retirement order.**
  - Retirements travel in the resource queue, in order with announcements, so Venus's count check never sees an announcement overtake the retirement that frees room.
  - Orbit writes a retirement only after writing a frame without the reference, and never writes a later frame with it.
  - A resource replaced mid-transfer is finished, then retired.
- **Exit and the row flag.** Queued resource messages are dropped before `Exited`. ORBF v3 rows drop ORBF v2's `kitty_virtual_placeholder` flag, since placeholder cells are blanked.
- **Owner split.**
  - The host assigns identities and applies the fixed limits that make entries unavailable.
  - Bend decides when resources start (so entries stay pending until then), retirement and pressure.
  - So orb-j2i.6 needs no Bend change.
- **Bounded refusal recovery.** A refusal (budget or a failed texture allocation) allows one resync in total, across attachments. After that the marker stays until the referenced placements change, the budget gains room, or the renderer recovers. This prevents a reconnect loop when allocation keeps failing.
- **Upload completion.** Venus admits the next announcement only after the previous resource's GPU copy has finished and released its staging. This bounds staging at one resource per terminal (at most 13,333,334 bytes for RGB expanded to RGBA).
- **Smaller rules.** Identities are 64-bit. Frames carry no overscan rows. A displayed image that the storage limit evicts disappears unmarked; this is a recorded gap in ORB-C16.
- **Capability switch.**
  - An internal Orbit switch, not user configuration, gates ORB-C16. While it is off, frames state false, carry no entries and keep placeholder cells as today.
  - Orbit's real-PTY checks turn it on from orb-j2i.6, so .6 to .8 can prove their parts. orb-j2i.11 turns it on in the shipped build together with Venus's drawing, so edge never blanks previews before Venus draws them.
  - ORB-C6's rule ("true exactly when a frame carries ORB-C16 state") holds throughout.
- **Marker delay (a clearly better alternative, under the plan-change pre-approval).** A pending entry shows the marker only after 250 ms pending. Without the delay, every new Yazi preview would flash the marker, because frames go ahead of resource chunks. Unavailable and refused entries show it at once.
- **Child beads superseded in part.** This commit adds a comment to each of orb-j2i.4, .5, .6, .7, .8, .10 and .11 naming where ORB-C16 and VEN-C31 replace their earlier plan text. The changes: opaque identity instead of the Kitty id on the wire; format and dimensions in the announcement; entries outside the frame budget; the copy at transfer start; three entry states; Venus's cache keyed by identity.
- **ORB-C7 unchanged.** The resource allowance and its "never ORB-C7 pressure" rule live in ORB-C16, so ORB-C7's proved text and status stand.
- **Retirement message:** Orbit tells Venus when a sent resource leaves libghostty storage. Venus memory then follows storage instead of waiting for budget pressure, and Venus never has to guess.
- **Pending versus unavailable entries:** unavailable is the explicit "never sent" state for images over the limits, so "no visible placement silently dropped" (acceptance 2) holds.

## Reference gate (consequential: contract and wire revision)

- **Behavior and owners:** Orbit, alone, owns Kitty parsing, image storage, placement resolution and the resource plane (ORB-C16). Venus, alone, owns validation, GPU textures, the budget and drawing (VEN-C31). libghostty owns the image data structures, and Orbit only reads them.
- **Routes read:**
  - orbit/docs/REFERENCES.md:342-354, the Unpeel Surface entry (Yazi RGBA through Kitty graphics as a layering oracle). It names libghostty extraction and the Orbit-to-Venus resource contract as this work's owners, and it is not used for this slice's shape;
  - the epic's Selected references:
    - Ghostty a887df42c56f6de86c0fe6da9c4eeca37931e083: adopt its split of storage, decoded pixels, resolved placements and generation invalidation; reject its renderer and app architecture;
    - Unpeel Surface a3004c88a8b871837dac4820f48cf8a184a7276d: the same entry, kept as a later layering oracle;
  - venus/docs/REFERENCES.md has no route for image textures or a GPU budget, so ghostling_rs below is VEN-C31's comparable implementation;
  - docs/REFERENCES.md:86-91, the Monstar route, which says to study its graphics among other areas. It was read, but its single-process renderer is rejected there and gives nothing for a split Orbit/Venus plane;
  - the Kitty specification at kovidgoyal/kitty b2cb8712 (see above).
- **Comparable implementation:** upstream ghostling_rs at Uzaaft/libghostty-rs 9ede35b8 (example/ghostling_rs/src/main.rs).
  - It reads the render-state image list only when `image_placements_generation` changes (:401-467).
  - It keeps one texture per image id, and re-reads the pixels when that id's generation changes (:711-737).
  - Kept: generation-keyed caching, one per-row entry list, sorting by layer and z, and clipping to the grid.
  - Rejected: its in-process draw from the borrowed slice. Orbit and Venus are separate processes, so Orbit copies and transfers.
- **Rejected approaches:** a client-side Kitty parser or placeholder reader; pixels in every frame; content addressing; a missing-resource request message; a second socket or shared memory for pixels; a cancel message (made unnecessary by one transfer at a time from one copy).
- **Decision and its check:** the shape above, checked by orb-j2i.1's replay of Yazi's real byte stream through upstream libghostty (entries, generations, lifetimes and costs), and later by orb-j2i.8 (real PTY) and orb-j2i.12 (installed Eon).

## Configurability (repository rule)

The 250 ms marker delay is not settled here. A reasonable user could differ, so orb-j2i.11 decides: expose it, changing VEN-C31 to state 250 ms as the default, or record one of the rule's reasons. Until then it is the value VEN-C31 states.

These values stay fixed, for these reasons:
- the per-screen storage limit: a memory and safety budget for Orbit, which only Orbit applies;
- the side and byte limits, the chunk size, the per-frame entry and resource caps, and the queued allowance: protocol bounds that ORB-C16 and VEN-C31 must agree on;
- the 256 MiB GPU budget: a performance and safety budget for every pane in the window. orb-j2i.11 may revisit it with measurements.

The missing-image marker's appearance and the omitted-placements notice are values a person sees. VEN-C31 leaves both to orb-j2i.11 under the configurability rule.

## Questions for Lucca (numbered, with a recommendation)

1. **Device loss:** should Venus gain renderer recreation after non-destroyed device loss, so that VEN-C31's resync can recover images? Recommendation: yes, as its own small bead under VEN-C4, after orb-j2i.11. Until then, device loss stays VEN-C4's terminal renderer failure, which is today's behavior. Not filed tonight.
2. **Agent parity:** should the `eon` CLI let an agent read a terminal's image placements (rectangles, sizes, states) as data, through the owner's authorization for terminal contents? Recommendation: yes, as an entry under eon-agent-parity-a9g0 after orb-j2i.11, reading Orbit's entries; pixels are not needed. Not filed tonight.

## Humans and agents

Images are terminal contents. An agent cannot read image placements through the `eon` CLI today, and this slice adds none. See question 2.

## Recorded nits (left for the implementing beads)

- ORB-C8's Boundary still says graphics are excluded. Frames scrolled into history do carry placements under ORB-C16, which is a cross-reference to add when orb-j2i.6 touches ORB-C8.
- The orbit/CHANGELOG.md entry says behavior is unchanged "until orb-j2i.4 to orb-j2i.7 land". Shipped image behavior changes only at orb-j2i.11, when the switch turns on; orb-j2i.4's PTY pixel size changes earlier.
- "Skipped" (ORB-C16 Resources) means a resource whose start Orbit passed over because no current frame referenced it.
- "Room returns" (Pending) also requires that no transfer is in progress, since one transfer runs at a time.
- When a pending resource completes, the frame it triggers is a revision change with no PTY output, and the ORB-C3 metadata observer sees it.
- With the switch off, previews keep placeholder cells as frames do.
- VEN-C31 does not say what Venus does with an entry whose identity it never saw (it draws the marker, as for any resource it does not hold), or whether clipping a source rectangle shrinks the destination. orb-j2i.11 settles both in VEN-C31's spirit.
- VEN-C31's Trigger does not list `Exited`, although Retention handles it.
- Markdown lazy continuation: in ORB-C16's Entry states and Placements, and in VEN-C31's Validation and Resync, a paragraph follows a nested list without a blank line, so it renders inside the last bullet. Fix with a blank line, as ORB-C15 does, when a child next edits these contracts.
- VEN-C31's 13,333,334-byte staging figure ignores wgpu's 256-byte row alignment (813x4096 RGB stages 13,631,488 bytes). orb-j2i.11 states "plus row alignment" or uploads in strips.
- Marker sequence after reattach: the retained scene shows markers, then the new first frame's pending entries show nothing for up to 250 ms. orb-j2i.11 decides which rule wins; the recommendation is that markers stay until a resource arrives.
- "Starts resources in identity order" skips unavailable identities, which never start. Frame-versus-chunk scheduling must not starve chunks; orb-j2i.7 states its progress rule.
- The internal switch is a build-time setting, not a runtime environment variable or flag, so it cannot become hidden configuration (orb-j2i.6 and .11).
- The PTY pixel size and the CSI 14t/16t/18t answers are host mechanics that ORB-C16's Owner does not name. orb-j2i.4 records it, and ORB-C5 is unchanged.
- orb-j2i.5's bound change reruns the proofs; it shows Lucca a law only if a law's text changes.
- Orbit lowers its unretired count when it queues a retirement, which is why a retirement ahead of the next announcement keeps both sides' 1,024 counts equal.
- After a failed copy, Orbit retries only when a later frame that references the image is queued for other reasons, never by publishing frames just to retry. The realistic cause is libghostty reporting no pixels yet.
- "Before the next announcement is accepted" (VEN-C31) means Venus holds that terminal's later messages until the upload finishes. An early announcement is not malformed.
- ORB-C6's "its recorded gaps" means ORB-C16's.

## Checks

- `orbit-governance` (`nix develop -c cargo run --locked --quiet -p orbit-governance`):
  - base edge abdbfd0: 9 errors, ORB-C15's status line plus eight beads referencing the unknown ORB-C16;
  - this tree: 1 error, ORB-C15's status line, which predates this change. The new status lines are bare words, and their adoption notes sit in Proof and Open proof.

## Review ledger

orb-j2i.2: round 1 had Codex (8 blocking) and Claude (7) in parallel on be5a5b8. Claude rounds 2-13 found 7, 5, 3, 3, 4, 5, 1, 1, 2, 1, 0 and 0 blocking; text-only restarts used: 2. Narrow Codex re-checks from be5a5b8: ef78e67 had 1 blocking (upload staging), f9e918d had 1 (refusal loop), and 40f21d9 is in the next comment. Rebased onto abdbfd0 without conflict.
