### orbit/docs/CONTRACTS.md: preamble (sentence changed)

in this repository. Each contract below states the current ORBS v13 behavior,
except ORB-C16, which is Planned and states the ORBF v3 in ORBS v14 behavior it
enters with; its PTY pixel size rule needs no wire change.

### orbit/docs/CONTRACTS.md: ORB-C6 (changed fields; the rest is unchanged)

- **Status:** Partially proved
- **Boundary:** A frame states `kitty_graphics` true exactly when it carries
  ORB-C16's graphics state; one that does not, such as every ORBF v2 frame,
  declares Kitty graphics unsupported. Kitty features outside ORB-C16 are its
  recorded gaps, and ORB-C16's Boundary names each, including those nothing
  marks.
- **Open proof:** Static graphics joined this contract on 2026-10-27 under
  Lucca's standing approval of 2026-10-26, relayed by eon-overseer
  (`orb-j2i.2`), and the proof above predates them. ORB-C16 is Planned.
  Today frames state `kitty_graphics` false while libghostty stores Kitty
  images and answers their queries, so a program such as Yazi prints
  placeholder cells that Venus shows as missing glyphs (`orb-j2i.1`).

### orbit/docs/CONTRACTS.md: ORB-C16 (new)

## ORB-C16 — Static graphics resource plane

- **Status:** Planned
- **Consumer:**
  - a program in an Orbit terminal that shows static images through the Kitty
    graphics protocol, directly or with Unicode placeholders, such as Yazi
    image previews;
  - the one attached client, Venus, which draws them under VEN-C31.
- **Trigger:**
  - PTY output transmits, places, replaces or deletes a Kitty image, prints or
    erases Unicode placeholder cells, scrolls, clears, resets or switches
    between the primary and alternate screens;
  - the client attaches, resizes, scrolls the viewport, reads slowly, detaches
    or reattaches;
  - the child exits.
- **Result:**
  - **Storage.** libghostty alone parses Kitty graphics and stores images.
    Orbit sets its storage limit to 10,000,000 decoded bytes for each screen,
    accepts only the direct transmission medium, and installs no PNG decoder.
    A stored image is therefore 8-bit RGB or RGBA.
  - **Capability.** An internal Orbit switch, which is not user configuration,
    gates this contract. While it is on, every complete frame states
    `kitty_graphics` true and carries the graphics state below. While it is
    off, frames state false, carry no entries and keep placeholder cells as
    they are, and Orbit sends no resources. Orbit's real-PTY checks turn it
    on from `orb-j2i.6`; `orb-j2i.11` turns it on in the shipped build, in the
    same change that makes Venus draw images. The PTY pixel size rule below
    does not depend on it.
  - **Placements.** Each frame lists the placements that libghostty's render
    state resolves for the viewport, with no overscan rows: fixed, relative and
    Unicode-placeholder placements, the latter as one entry per run of
    neighbouring placeholder cells in a row. Each entry gives:
    - the resource identity and libghostty's layer and z-index;
    - the viewport cell of its top-left corner, which for fixed and relative
      placements can lie above or left of the viewport;
    - its grid size in cells;
    - its pixel offset from that cell's top-left corner, which can exceed one
      cell when libghostty centres an image in its placeholder cells;
    - its drawn pixel size and its source rectangle in image pixels.
    The frame states the cell width and height in pixels that this geometry
    uses. Entries are listed in drawing order: by layer, then z-index, then
    Kitty image id, lower first (the specification's order for equal
    z-indexes), then libghostty's order.
  - **Entry states.** Each entry also carries a state:
    - **ready**, when its resource's last chunk has been written to the
      socket in this attachment;
    - **pending**, while that has not happened;
    - **unavailable**, when the image breaks the resource limits below and is
      never sent.
    When a pending resource's last chunk is written, Orbit publishes a new
    complete frame at the next revision (ORB-C4), after any synchronized
    output hold ends, so its entries become ready without further PTY output.
  - **Placeholder cells.** Rows no longer carry the ORBF v2
    `kitty_virtual_placeholder` flag. Frames and previews carry Unicode
    placeholder cells (U+10EEEE and their diacritics) as blank cells that keep
    only their background, so a client never draws or interprets placeholder
    codepoints or their decorations.
  - **Resources.** A resource is one image's decoded pixels at one libghostty
    image generation. Orbit assigns a resource its 64-bit identity number when
    it first queues a frame that references it. Numbers strictly increase
    within an attachment and are never reused, and Orbit starts resources in
    identity order, so announcements carry increasing identities. A resource
    that is skipped and later referenced again gets a fresh number. Replacing
    an image's pixels, even under the same Kitty image id, makes a new resource
    with a new identity.
    - **Sending.** Orbit sends a resource as one announcement, giving identity,
      libghostty generation, format (RGB or RGBA), width, height, byte length
      and chunk count, followed by its chunks in order. Each chunk names its
      resource's identity and its index, counting from 0. Every chunk except
      the last carries exactly 262,144 bytes, and the last carries the rest.
      Orbit sends one resource at a time: all of one resource's chunks precede
      the next announcement. Frames and other messages may arrive between
      chunks.
    - **Order and copies.** Orbit sends each resource at most once per
      attachment, and none before the attachment's first complete frame. After
      that it starts a resource before the first frame that references it when
      the resource queue below has room. It copies the pixels out of libghostty
      storage once, when it starts the announcement, and finishes the transfer
      from that copy even if storage later replaces or drops the image.
    - **Pending.** While the resource queue is full, Orbit sends frames with
      the entry pending. Once room returns it starts the resource from
      libghostty storage if a current frame still references it, and starts
      nothing if storage has dropped that generation or no frame references it.
    - **Retirement.** When a sent resource leaves the storage of the screen
      that holds it, including when a new generation replaces it, Orbit retires
      it with one message. If that happens during its own transfer, Orbit
      finishes the transfer first. A retirement travels in the resource queue,
      in order with announcements and chunks. Orbit writes it only after it has
      written a complete frame that no longer references the resource, and
      writes no later frame that does. Orbit sees a screen's storage only while
      that screen is active, so a resource of the inactive screen stays
      unretired until the screen is active again or the attachment ends.
  - **Screens.** A frame references only the active screen's images. Each
    screen keeps its own storage, which survives switching away, so returning
    to a screen can reference images again that were sent earlier in the same
    attachment.
  - **PTY pixel size.** The PTY's pixel fields hold the text area, columns
    times cell width by rows times cell height, and Orbit answers CSI 14t,
    16t and 18t from the same measurements. A program that derives its cell
    size from them, such as Yazi, then sizes its placeholder grid to
    libghostty's cells.
  - **Limits.**
    - A resource is 1 to 4,096 pixels on each side and at most 10,000,000
      decoded bytes.
    - A frame carries at most 4,096 placement entries referencing at most 256
      resources. Entries do not count toward ORB-C6's frame budget for cells
      and links; ORBF v3 bounds them separately.
    - Per attachment, Orbit holds at most one resource copy outside
      libghostty storage, the one transfer in progress, whose queued chunks
      count toward the resource queue below.
    - Resource messages (announcements, chunks and retirements) wait in their
      own resource queue, apart from every other message. They never take
      ORB-C7's frame and scroll-outcome room. A frame waits at most for the
      rest of the one resource message already being written. At most 1,048,576
      bytes of chunk payload are queued per attachment, besides announcements
      and retirements, which the count below bounds. This bound is internal to
      Orbit; Venus does not check it.
    - At most 1,024 resources are announced and not retired per attachment. A
      resource that would pass that count is not started until one retires, so
      its entries stay pending.
- **Important failures:**
  - An image outside the limits stays in libghostty storage and is never
    sent. Its entries are unavailable, so the client marks them instead of
    dropping them silently.
  - Placements beyond 4,096 entries or 256 resources: the list stops at the
    first entry, in drawing order, that would pass either cap, and the frame
    states that placements were omitted.
  - A full resource queue makes entries pending. Resource messages never cause
    ORB-C7's disconnect, block PTY processing or grow the queue; every other
    message keeps ORB-C7's behavior unchanged.
  - Failed extraction publishes no partial frame; the frame fails as ORB-C6
    already requires. A failed copy starts no resource, so its entries stay
    pending; when Orbit tries again, the resource takes a fresh identity.
  - Detach discards every per-attachment identity and copy. The next
    attachment starts with no resources sent: its first complete frame lists
    every visible placement as pending or unavailable, and the resources
    follow as above.
  - On child exit, Orbit drops the resource messages it has not started
    writing, finishes the one it is writing, and then sends `Exited`. Exit ends
    the run and its images; nothing persists across an Orbit or machine
    restart.
- **Owner:** Orbit.
  - Its Bend session policy decides when resources start, which keeps entries
    pending until then, and decides retirement and pressure, within budgets
    that a law bounds.
  - Its Rust host reads libghostty's render-state image list and storage. It
    assigns identities, applies the fixed resource limits that make entries
    unavailable, copies pixels out of storage when the policy starts a resource
    (which needs no PTY output), and writes resources. Pixel bytes never cross
    the worker pipe.
  - Canonical `orbit-protocol` values and codecs own the wire.
- **Consumes:**
  - libghostty-vt's render-state image iterator and Kitty graphics storage
    at the upstream `Uzaaft/libghostty-rs` commit that CRATES.md records;
    `orb-j2i.1` proved the interface at
    `9ede35b8ea94a55ed3608408d67e102883129f1e`;
  - the Kitty graphics protocol as specified at `kovidgoyal/kitty`
    `b2cb871254fbdac19a085188813c8dfb258b95cd`,
    `docs/graphics-protocol.rst`.
  - The wire is ORBF v3 in ORBS v14, a breaking, exact-version revision with
    no adapter or compatibility window. Venus, Eon Runtime and Eon consume it
    in this repository. Orbit lands first, then Venus, in one Eon build.
- **Boundary:**
  - Static images only. Orbit does not drive libghostty's animation tick, so
    an animated image shows whichever frame libghostty holds as current;
    animation playback and frame composition are not presented.
  - Clients draw every layer in one band, between cell backgrounds and text
    (VEN-C31). Kitty's other layers are a recorded gap: an image placed above
    text draws below it, and one placed below cell backgrounds draws above
    them.
  - Scrollback previews (ORB-C8) carry no placements and blank their
    placeholder cells. A viewport scrolled into history is a live frame and
    carries its placements.
  - A displayed image that libghostty's storage limit evicts disappears with
    its placements, and nothing marks it. This is a recorded gap.
  - Placeholder cells whose image libghostty cannot resolve, for example
    after the image is deleted, are blanked like any other placeholder cell
    and carry no entry, so nothing marks them. This is a recorded gap.
  - ORB-C9 copies text from libghostty, which keeps placeholder codepoints,
    so copying across placeholder cells yields U+10EEEE and its diacritics.
    This is a recorded gap.
  - At the cap of 1,024 unretired resources, entries of further resources
    stay pending until one retires. This is a recorded gap for programs that
    keep many images stored.
  - File, temporary-file and shared-memory transmission, PNG, Sixel, iTerm2
    images, a client request for a missing resource, content addressing and
    restart persistence are excluded.
- **Proof:** Not proved. Adopted on 2026-10-27 under Lucca's standing
  approval of 2026-10-26, relayed by eon-overseer (`orb-j2i.2`).
  `orb-j2i.4` sizes the PTY; `orb-j2i.5` adds the wire revisions;
  `orb-j2i.6` and `orb-j2i.7` extract placements and send resources;
  `orb-j2i.8` proves the lifecycle.

### venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md: preamble (sentence added)

VEN-C31 is Planned and names the ORBF v3 in ORBS v14
revision it will enter with.

### venus/docs/CONTRACTS.md: VEN-C31 (new)

## VEN-C31 — Static terminal images

- **Status:** Planned
- **Consumer:** A person viewing an Orbit terminal in an Eon window, in a pane
  or a popup, whose program shows static images (ORB-C16), such as Yazi's
  image previews.
- **Trigger:**
  - Orbit sends a resource announcement, chunk or retirement, or a frame whose
    placement entries change;
  - the terminal resizes, scrolls, detaches or reattaches, or Venus's cell
    geometry changes;
  - the window's image budget is reached, or the renderer recovers from GPU
    device loss.
- **Result:**
  - **Validation before allocation.** Venus checks each announcement and
    reserves nothing until it passes:
    - the identity is greater than every identity announced before in this
      attachment;
    - no other resource of this terminal is still incomplete;
    - the format is RGB or RGBA;
    - each side is 1 to 4,096 pixels;
    - the byte length equals width times height times bytes per pixel and is
      at most 10,000,000;
    - the chunk count is the byte length divided by 262,144, rounded up;
    - fewer than 1,024 resources of this terminal are announced and not
      retired, counting resources Venus freed.
    Chunks must arrive in order for the one incomplete resource: every chunk
    but the last carries exactly 262,144 bytes, and the last fills it exactly.
    A retirement must name a completely received resource that is not yet
    retired, and no resource message may precede the attachment's first frame.
    Anything else is a malformed ORBS value and fails the attachment as any
    other does (VEN-C1, VEN-C3). Venus assembles and uploads one resource per
    terminal at a time: a completed resource is uploaded, meaning the GPU has
    finished the copy and released its staging, or refused, before the next
    announcement is accepted. It therefore holds at most one resource per
    terminal outside textures: 10,000,000 bytes of assembly plus that
    resource's staging, at most 13,333,334 bytes when RGB is expanded to RGBA.
  - **Drawing.** Venus draws every entry whose resource it holds complete and
    uploaded, whatever state the entry carries, clipping the entry's source
    rectangle to the resource's bounds. It draws the source rectangle, scaled
    with linear filtering
    to the entry's pixel size, at the entry's cell plus pixel offset. When the
    frame's stated cell size differs from Venus's current cell size, as during
    a font or scale change, Venus scales the entry's position and size by the
    ratio of the two, so entries stay on their cells until a frame in the new
    geometry arrives. All entries draw in one band, above every cell background
    and below text, text decorations and the cursor, in the frame's order.
    Images move with their rows under VEN-C7's precision translation. VEN-C11's
    background opacity does not apply to them; their own alpha blends over what
    lies beneath, including a selection highlight, which an image can therefore
    cover. Images are clipped to the terminal's grid area and drawn under
    anything Venus stacks above that terminal: overlays, notices, hints and
    popup cards.
  - **Missing-image marker.** For an entry whose resource Venus does not hold,
    Venus draws a marker over the entry's rectangle and never leaves the area
    silently blank for long. This covers unavailable and refused resources at
    once, and a pending entry that has stayed pending for 250 ms, so a
    resource that promptly follows its frame never flashes the marker. A
    frame that states omitted placements also raises a bounded notice for
    that terminal.
  - **Retention.** Resources and their identities belong to one terminal's
    attachment. Venus never frees a resource that terminal's current frame
    references while the attachment lasts. It frees a resource:
    - once Orbit has retired it and the current frame does not reference it;
    - when the current frame does not reference it and the budget needs room;
    - on detach or `Exited`, which discard all of that terminal's resources and
      its incomplete assembly. A scene that Venus keeps showing after detach,
      as VEN-C3 does during a reconnect, draws the marker over every image
      until the next attachment's frames and resources arrive.
  - **Budget.** Image textures across the whole window are limited to 256 MiB,
    counted at 4 bytes per pixel. Venus checks the budget before allocating. A
    resource that would exceed it, after freeing unreferenced ones, is not
    uploaded, and its entries show the marker. A texture allocation that fails
    within the budget is treated the same way: Venus captures the error instead
    of failing the renderer, and the entries show the marker.
  - **Resync.** Venus reattaches the terminal to recover:
    - after device loss, once the renderer works again, since every image
      texture is lost. Today non-destroyed device loss keeps VEN-C4's
      terminal renderer failure, so this applies only to recoveries VEN-C4
      allows;
    - when a frame references a resource Venus freed, or one it refused for
      budget once the budget has room again.
    Busy keeps VEN-C3's rule: under Eon supervision the reattach retries it,
    and in standalone mode Busy stays terminal. A standalone resync can
    therefore lose the race in which Orbit has not yet released the attachment
    Venus just left, and end that terminal. This is a recorded gap; Eon windows
    are supervised. Until the new attachment's first frame, the terminal shows
    what VEN-C3 shows during a transient reconnect, with markers over its
    images. Venus reattaches at most once for each such event. A refusal, for
    budget or because a texture allocation failed, allows one resync in total,
    across attachments: if the resync is refused again, the marker stays
    without further reattaching until the terminal's referenced placements
    change, the budget gains room, or the renderer recovers. While the renderer
    cannot draw, VEN-C4's failure handling applies unchanged.
  - Venus never parses Kitty graphics commands, reads placeholder cells or
    reconstructs image state. Orbit's frames and resources are its only image
    input.
- **Important failures:**
  - Malformed metadata, oversized dimensions or length, a second incomplete
    resource, a resource message before the first frame, a bad retirement,
    and out-of-order, wrong-size, duplicate, unannounced or excess chunks
    fail the attachment. A failed announcement reserves nothing, a failed
    chunk frees its assembly, and no partial image is ever drawn.
  - A budget refusal shows markers, never a stale or half-uploaded image, and
    resyncs as above.
  - An image cannot draw outside its terminal's grid area or over the window
    chrome or another terminal.
- **Owner:** Venus: protocol validation, the resource store, GPU textures, the
  budget and drawing. Orbit (ORB-C16) owns which images exist and where they
  are.
- **Consumes:** ORB-C16 through ORBF v3 in ORBS v14 from the in-tree
  `orbit-protocol` crate.
- **Boundary:**
  - One drawing band. Kitty's above-text and below-background layers are
    drawn in it (ORB-C16's recorded gap).
  - Besides textures, Venus holds at most one resource's assembly and upload
    staging per attached terminal, outside the GPU budget.
  - Venus keeps no CPU copy of an uploaded image, so device-loss recovery
    reattaches instead of re-uploading.
  - No image request message, animation, scrollback-preview images, image
    selection or copy, accessibility description of images, or persistence.
    The marker's and notice's appearance is chosen in `orb-j2i.11` under the
    repository's configurability rule.
- **Proof:** Not proved. Adopted on 2026-10-27 under Lucca's standing
  approval of 2026-10-26, relayed by eon-overseer (`orb-j2i.2`).
  `orb-j2i.9` adds the drawing band; `orb-j2i.10` validates and assembles
  resources; `orb-j2i.11` uploads and draws them; `orb-j2i.12` proves Yazi
  previews on the installed Eon.

### orbit/CHANGELOG.md (entry added)

- ORB-C16 enters the index as Planned: static Kitty images and Unicode
  placeholder placements will reach the client as decoded RGB or RGBA resources
  and per-frame placement entries on ORBF v3 in ORBS v14, a breaking revision
  for Venus, Eon Runtime and Eon. ORB-C6 becomes Partially proved: a frame that
  carries ORB-C16's state states Kitty graphics supported, and one that does
  not still declares them unsupported. Behavior and wire are unchanged until
  `orb-j2i.4` to `orb-j2i.7` land (`orb-j2i.2`).

title: Add a safe render-state image iterator to the libghostty-rs fork
description:
## Why

Yazi's placeholder path needs libghostty's render-state image iterator, which the safe
libghostty-vt wrapper at 6313a9b does not expose. Lucca approved (2026-10-23, relayed) adding it to
the Yazelix/libghostty-rs fork, with no Ghostty change, offered upstream with the #111 series.

## Evidence

- C API: Ghostty include/ghostty/vt/render.h:205-356, 1451-1535 (image iterator, `get_multi`).
- -sys symbols: libghostty-vt-sys src/bindings.rs:4407-4430; safe handles keep raw pointers
`pub(crate)`, so Orbit cannot reach them without a fork change.
- Model to follow: the fork's existing `RowIterator` and `kitty::graphics` `PlacementIterator`.
- Fork record: orbit/docs/CRATES.md:16-38; retirement bead eon-9rtt.3.

## Prerequisites

orb-j2i.1 go verdict (it confirms the iterator gives what Orbit needs).

## Scope

In scope:
- In Yazelix/libghostty-rs: a safe `render` image iterator (`update(&Snapshot)`, lending `next()`,
an image-placement value read in one `get_multi` call, enums for protocol, layer and placement kind),
with tests in the crate's own harness. Estimated 200-350 LOC plus about 150 LOC of tests.
- Bump orbit/Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock to the new fork commit; update orbit/docs/CRATES.md (fork
delta now five commits) and widen eon-9rtt.3's exit to a release that also contains the iterator.

Out of scope:
- `animation_tick`, memory usage, a global PNG decoder (not needed for the static slice).
- Any Ghostty change, any Orbit use of the iterator (orb-j2i.6), opening an upstream PR (Lucca
opens upstream PRs).

## Acceptance

- Orbit builds against the new pin with no behavior change; the fork's tests cover the iterator on a
placeholder image.

## Verification

- Fork tests; Orbit's suites through `nix develop -c eon-test` green on the bumped
lock; Codex review per AGENTS.md (Cargo manifests and lockfiles included).

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if the wrapper needs a Ghostty change or an unsafe lifetime that cannot be expressed safely.
- Ask eon-overseer for a build slot.

title: Report the text-area pixel size and answer CSI 14t, 16t and 18t
description:
## Why

Yazi sizes images from the PTY pixel fields divided by cols and rows. Orbit fills those fields with
the whole surface, padding included, and answers no CSI 14t/16t/18t, so previews can be up to about
one cell off and programs that ask for cell size get no reply. This needs no wire change.

## Evidence

- orbit/src/pty.rs:360-372: `ws_xpixel`/`ws_ypixel` = `screen_width`/`screen_height` (padding
included); `terminal.resize(cols, rows, cell_w, cell_h)` already gets cell pixels.
- Venus sends cell and padding pixels in `SurfaceSize`
(orbit/crates/protocol/src/session/mod.rs:574-587; venus/src/application/geometry.rs:153-187).
- The safe wrapper offers `on_size`; Orbit installs none (orbit/src/pty.rs:177-217).
- Yazi cell-size logic: yazi-adapter reads TIOCGWINSZ pixels and uses a 16t reply only on mismatch.

## Prerequisites

orb-j2i.1 go verdict (it records whether padding causes visible misalignment) and orb-j2i.2 (it records whether ORB-C2 wording changes).

## Scope

In scope:
- PTY pixel fields carry the text area (cols x cell width, rows x cell height).
- Install libghostty's size callback so CSI 14t, 16t and 18t are answered from authoritative state.
- Real-PTY checks for both, and orbit/docs/BEHAVIOR.md claims naming those checks.

Out of scope:
- Any ORBF/ORBS change; Venus.

## Acceptance

- A program in an Orbit terminal reads text-area pixels from TIOCGWINSZ and gets correct 14t/16t/18t
answers after resize.

## Verification

- Focused real-PTY checks through `nix develop -c eon-test`; `cargo fmt --check` and clippy for
orbit; converge plus Codex per AGENTS.md.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop for Lucca if ORB-C2 (query answers) or ORB-C5 wording must change; the decision on whether
it does is recorded in orb-j2i.2's text.
- If the answers decision touches the Bend worker (query answering policy), stop and re-scope.
close_reason: Text-area PTY pixel size and CSI 14t/16t/18t answers landed with the orbit-pixel-size check; proof in comments

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: From orb-j2i.1 (2026-10-26), for this bead: in a popup terminal the first program saw winsize 24x80 with 0x0 pixels, a moment before the popup was sized. ORB-C16 adopts the text-area PTY pixel size and the CSI 14t/16t/18t answers as this bead's rule, independent of Orbit's graphics switch. ORB-C2 does not change, since it already covers terminal-generated replies. Check the size a popup's first program reads.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Plan and reference gate (eon-53, 2026-10-27, worktree at edge 9e2fc14).

Contract: ORB-C16's PTY pixel size rule as adopted in orb-j2i.2 (orbit/docs/CONTRACTS.md, ORB-C16 Result): "The PTY's pixel fields hold the text area, columns times cell width by rows times cell height, and Orbit answers CSI 14t, 16t and 18t from the same measurements. A program that derives its cell size from them, such as Yazi, then sizes its placeholder grid to libghostty's cells." ORB-C2 does not change (orb-j2i.2's comment). No contract text changes in this bead.

Consequential? No: no dependency, wire or protocol, contract, lifecycle, security or trust boundary change. It sets the PTY winsize Orbit already sets and installs one libghostty callback the pinned wrapper already exposes. Reference read anyway: Ghostty 521cf2c5d30bd48028ca61546c64e7913764073d (the libghostty-vt-sys pin at libghostty-rs 9ede35b8), src/terminal/size_report.zig:35-96 (14t = ESC[4;rows*cell_h;cols*cell_wt, 16t = ESC[6;cell_h;cell_wt, 18t = ESC[8;rows;colst, 19t = ESC[9;rows;colst, mode 2048 = ESC[48;rows;cols;h_px;w_pxt), stream_terminal.zig:1821-1875 (no callback or a None answer sends nothing; setting ?2048h reports at once through the callback), :511-537 (a resize with mode 2048 set reports from the resize arguments without the callback), Terminal.zig:4157-4168 (resize stores width_px = cols*cell_w, height_px = rows*cell_h).

Shape:
- orbit/src/pty.rs resize: ws_xpixel = cols x cell_width, ws_ypixel = rows x cell_height (u16, saturating), instead of the padded screen size.
- orbit/src/pty.rs spawn: install Terminal::on_size, answering from libghostty's own cols, rows, width_px/cols and height_px/rows, so the answers and Kitty geometry share one owner (libghostty's stored size) and agree with the PTY fields. Rejected: a second copy of the size in an Rc<Cell> (a second owner of the same state).
- Before any client size, Orbit starts the child at 80x24 (host.rs:448) and libghostty knows no cell size: the PTY pixel fields stay 0 and the pixel answers say 0, which is the convention for unknown. Rejected: reporting Orbit's placeholder 10x18 cell before a client says so (a guess presented as a measurement). The popup observation from orb-j2i.1 (first program sees 24x80 with 0x0) is this startup state; it is fixed only by giving Orbit the size before it spawns the child, a launcher and Orbit command-line change outside this bead's scope: filed as a follow-up bead.
- Also answered as a side effect of the same callback: CSI 19t and mode 2048's report on set. Both are checked.
- Check: new real-PTY check orbit-pixel-size (orbit/tests/real_pty/pixel_size.rs, nix/orbit-checks.nix): reads TIOCGWINSZ from the child's own terminal (path from tty(1), opened O_NOCTTY), before any client size and after a padded 50x20 surface of 9x17 cells, and the child's 14t/16t/18t/19t/2048 answers at both points. BEHAVIOR.md "PTY pixel size" names it.

Portability disposition: neutral. TIOCSWINSZ stays behind platform::set_window_size; the callback is libghostty's; the check opens the tty path tty(1) prints, which works on Linux and Darwin.
Bend worker: untouched (libghostty answers the queries as it answers the other terminal replies; no policy decision is involved), so the stop condition does not fire.

comments.text:
Shape correction (eon-53, 2026-10-27), superseding the "Rejected: a second copy of the size in an Rc<Cell>" line of the plan comment above.

The size answers do not read libghostty's grid. A program can resize libghostty's grid itself: with mode 40 set, DECCOLM (CSI ?3h/l) resizes it to 132 or 80 columns with no cell size, keeping width_px (Ghostty 521cf2c src/terminal/Terminal.zig:4057-4081), so width_px/cols gave 3-pixel cells and a 396-pixel text width while TIOCGWINSZ still said 50 columns and 450 pixels (found by the Codex review; reproduced by the pixel-size check). The answers' owner is therefore the size Orbit gives the PTY: Orbit keeps it in one Rc<Cell<SizeReportSize>> (orbit/src/pty.rs `pty_size`), set at spawn to the 80x24 start with zero-pixel cells and in `resize` to the client's cols, rows and cell size, and the callback returns it. The PTY fields and the answers both come from that value, which is what ORB-C16's "from the same measurements" requires; libghostty's grid is a separate state that DECCOLM may move away from the PTY, as before this bead.

The pixel-size check gained a third round after the child's own DECCOLM switch (answers and TIOCGWINSZ keep 50x20, 450x340, 9x17), and now waits for a title the child prints after turning mode 2048 off before the client resizes, so libghostty's unsolicited mode-2048 resize report cannot be read as an answer.

title: Carry graphics on the next ORBF and ORBS revisions
description:
## Why

Static graphics need new wire shapes: placement references in frames and a separate resource plane.
Lucca chose (2026-10-23) that graphics takes the next ORBF and ORBS revisions, breaking and
owner-first, with no adapter or compatibility window.

## Evidence

- ORBF v2: orbit/crates/protocol/src/lib.rs:15-24 (4 MiB, 100,000 cells); `Capabilities`
(:131-138), validator requiring `kitty_graphics == false` (:729-737), test
`orbf_v2_capabilities_are_truthful_at_every_acceptance_boundary` (:1281); row placeholder flag
(:249, :584, :615); `FrameReducer` (:366-382).
- ORBS v13: orbit/crates/protocol/src/session/mod.rs:16-35, message enums (:127-197), tags
(session/codec.rs:8-36), exact-version header check (codec.rs:59-73).
- Consumers that break: Orbit (frame.rs, socket.rs, real-PTY test harness) and Venus (transport,
application, render, cells, scroll, tests/canonical_scene.rs). Eon Runtime and Eon recompile only.

## Prerequisites

orb-j2i.1 (gate) and orb-j2i.2 (approved and indexed contract text, which fixes the shapes and the
limits).

## Scope

In scope:
- orbit-protocol: next ORBF revision with placement references (epoch-scoped image id, generation,
source rect, cell and pixel geometry, pixel format and dimensions, pending marker) and size
accounting inside the frame budget; next ORBS revision with resource announce and chunk messages
as ORB-C16 states. Strict decoder and canonical corpus: old, malformed, truncated, trailing,
oversized, stale, duplicate, and out-of-order values fail deterministically.
- Update Orbit and Venus to compile and pass on the new revisions with `kitty_graphics` still false
and no placements emitted or drawn.
- orbit/CHANGELOG.md and venus/CHANGELOG.md protocol entries; orbit/docs/CRATES.md codec entry.

Out of scope:
- Extraction (orb-j2i.6), resource sending (orb-j2i.7), Venus storage or drawing (orb-j2i.10,
orb-j2i.11). eon-orbf-link-dedupe-4w4c (follows on the revision after).

## Acceptance

- Codec tests cover every new message and bound; Orbit and Venus suites pass on the new revisions.

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test`; `cargo fmt --check` and clippy for orbit and venus crates; converge
plus Codex per AGENTS.md (shared wire protocol route: full affected Rust and Nix surfaces).

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if the approved contract text cannot be encoded without a shape change; return to Lucca.
close_reason: ORBF v3 in ORBS v14 landed with the codec, consumers and proof; see the proof record comment

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Contract text adopted in orb-j2i.2 (ORB-C16, VEN-C31) replaces parts of this bead's plan; where they differ, the contracts govern.
- Placement entries reference a resource by Orbit's identity number. The number is assigned at first reference, strictly increases within an attachment and is never reused. Entries do not carry the Kitty image id.
- Format, width, height, byte length, chunk count and libghostty generation travel in the resource announcement, not in entries.
- Entries carry layer, z-index, cell, grid size, pixel offset (which can exceed a cell), drawn size, source rectangle and one of three states: ready, pending or unavailable. Frames add the cell size their geometry uses and an omitted-placements flag.
- Entries sit outside ORB-C6's cell-and-link frame budget, with their own ORBF v3 bound of 4,096 entries and 256 resources.
- This bead owns the frame-size consequence. ORBF v3's maximum frame is the 4 MiB cell-and-link budget plus the entry block.
  - In the same change, raise Orbit's worker output bound (orbit/src/main.bend, now 12,587,045) and Venus's frame event-queue bound to match. ORB-C7's maximum-frame check (`worker_bound_admits_a_maximum_scroll_outcome_behind_a_started_maximum_frame`) must stay true.
  - The Bend bound change needs its law check, shown to Lucca as orbit/AGENTS.md requires.
  - Update the index preamble's "Existing 4 MiB/100,000-cell bounds remain" line.
- Chunks carry identity and index, are all exactly 262,144 bytes except the last, and arrive one resource at a time. A retirement message exists.
- ORBF v3 rows drop the `kitty_virtual_placeholder` flag.
- The v3 codec accepts `kitty_graphics` true or false. A false frame carries no entries, and no resources are sent with it.
- An entry's cell can be negative, above or left of the viewport, for fixed and relative placements.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Reference gate (eon-j2i5 session, 2026-10-27), recorded before code. This is a consequential shape: it changes the ORBF and ORBS wire formats.

## Behavior and owners

- ORBF v3 frames carry ORB-C16's graphics state; ORBS v14 carries resource announcements, chunks and retirements. Canonical `orbit-protocol` values and codecs own both encodings and their stateless validation. Orbit (orb-j2i.6, .7) owns what is sent; Venus (orb-j2i.10) owns per-attachment resource sequencing (identity order, one incomplete resource, chunk order, retirement of a completed resource, the 1,024 cap), as VEN-C31 assigns it.
- In this bead the switch stays off: Orbit emits frames with no graphics state and no resource messages, and Venus draws no placements.

## Routes read

- docs/REFERENCES.md "Orbit and terminal architecture" -> orbit/docs/REFERENCES.md "Attachment and terminal state".
- Source shape: libghostty-rs `9ede35b8ea94a55ed3608408d67e102883129f1e`, crates/libghostty-vt/src/render.rs `ImageIteration` (layer: BelowBackground/BelowText/AboveText; z i32; viewport_col/row i32; grid_cols/rows u32; cell_offset_x/y u32; pixel_width/height u32; source x/y/width/height u32) and src/kitty/graphics.rs (generation u64, width/height u32, formats RGB/RGBA/PNG/Gray/GrayAlpha; only RGB and RGBA reach the wire under ORB-C16's storage rule). Wire field widths follow these types, so no value narrows.
- Comparable implementation: WezTerm `e2a98e1b8af156988ad0ac778658ac27b60a55fb`, codec/src/lib.rs `SerializedImageCell` and `GetImageCell`/`GetImageCellResponse` (~/pjs/refs/wezterm). Kept: frames carry placement references and geometry without pixels; pixels travel separately. Rejected: its 32-byte content hash as identity and its client pull request (ORB-C16 excludes content addressing and a request message); per-cell texture coordinates (libghostty already resolves placements, so entries carry its geometry).
- Kitty graphics protocol at kovidgoyal/kitty `b2cb871254fbdac19a085188813c8dfb258b95cd` docs/graphics-protocol.rst, as ORB-C16 consumes it (layers, z order).

## Decision

- The 4 MiB budget keeps its role as ORB-C6's frame budget for the header, cells and links (renamed `FRAME_BUDGET_BYTES`); `MAX_FRAME_BYTES` becomes the largest encoded ORBF v3 frame, budget plus the largest graphics block. Every queue and decoder bound that means "largest frame" therefore grows with it, and the three ORB-C6 degradation sites keep the 4 MiB budget explicitly.
- `Frame.graphics: Option<Graphics>` replaces `Capabilities.kitty_graphics`; the wire's capability byte is `graphics.is_some()`, so ORB-C6's "true exactly when it carries ORB-C16 state" holds by construction.
- Graphics block after the rows: cell width and height in pixels (u32, nonzero), omitted flag, entry count (u16, at most 4,096), entries of 70 bytes. Codec checks: tags, caps (4,096 entries, 256 distinct resources), (layer, z) drawing order, nonzero cell size.
- ORBS v14 server messages: announce (identity u64, generation u64, format, width, height, byte length, chunk count; the codec checks sides 1..=4,096, length = w*h*bpp <= 10,000,000, chunk count = ceil(length/262,144)), chunk (identity, index u32, 1..=262,144 payload bytes), retire (identity).
- Rejected: a dual decoder or adapter (Lucca 2026-10-23: no compatibility window); keeping both `kitty_graphics` and an optional block (two sources of truth); a stateful resource reducer in orbit-protocol (VEN-C31 makes Venus own sequencing; orb-j2i.10 adds it).

## Check

Protocol codec tests for every new message and bound, plus the existing ORB-C7 test `worker_bound_admits_a_maximum_scroll_outcome_behind_a_started_maximum_frame` against the raised worker bound; full `nix develop -c eon-test` and the Nix build on the final tree.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Live generation across the ORBF v3 / ORBS v14 bump, portability and approval (eon-j2i5 session, 2026-10-27).

## A running Eon after a profile refresh

Checked by source reading of this tree (3f90cad plus this change):

title: Put libghostty's image placements into Orbit frames
description:
## Why

Orbit must put libghostty's resolved placements into frames and stop showing Unicode placeholder
cells as text, so Venus never interprets them (approved direction, 2026-08-12).

## Evidence

- Frame extraction: orbit/src/frame.rs:36-221 (`frame_within`, `RenderState::update`), the
frame-budget degradation rule (frame.rs:44-48, 130-195; ORB-C6 text) and commit 8a25211 (overflow
must degrade, never end the terminal).
- Row placeholder flag filled at frame.rs:168-170, 289-291.
- Render-state image iterator: added to the fork by orb-j2i.3.
- libghostty handles die on the next mutating terminal call, so everything a frame needs is read in
the same carry-out.

## Prerequisites

orb-j2i.1, orb-j2i.3 (iterator), orb-j2i.5 (codec).

## Scope

In scope:
- In frame extraction: walk the render-state image iterator for the active screen's viewport and
emit placement references with the fields orb-j2i.5 defines; blank placeholder cells in the frame
(as Ghostty's own shaper does); account their bytes in the frame budget and degrade explicitly
(marked as omitted per ORB-C16) when they do not fit.
- Set the frame capability as ORB-C16 defines it whenever placements are emitted, so frames stay
truthful (orbit/src/frame.rs:201-204 and the codec validator).
- Unit and real-PTY checks: Yazi's Kgp stream produces placements with the right geometry and no
placeholder text in the frame.

Out of scope:
- Sending pixel resources (orb-j2i.7); Bend worker changes; Venus drawing (orb-j2i.11).

## Acceptance

- A frame after Yazi's stream carries the expected placement references and blank cells; overflow
degrades without ending the terminal.

## Verification

- Focused tests through `nix develop -c eon-test`; fmt and clippy for orbit; converge plus Codex.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if extraction needs a Bend decision (that belongs to orb-j2i.7) or a frame-budget rule the
contract text does not state.
close_reason: Placements, identities, caps and blank placeholder cells land behind ORB-C16's switch; proof on tree c7e6871c

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Contract text adopted in orb-j2i.2 (ORB-C16) replaces parts of this bead's plan; where they differ, the contract governs.
- Placement entries do not count toward ORB-C6's frame budget. ORBF v3 bounds them separately: at most 4,096 entries and 256 resources per frame. Past either cap the list stops in drawing order and the frame states that placements were omitted.
- Entries are listed by layer, then z-index, then lower Kitty image id, then libghostty's order. Unicode placeholder entries are one per run of cells in a row.
- Placeholder cells are blanked to their background in frames and previews.
- In the Rust host, this bead assigns 64-bit identities at first reference and marks entries over the fixed limits unavailable. ORB-C16's Owner gives both to the host. Every other entry stays pending: no resource starts until orb-j2i.7's Bend policy starts resources. This bead needs no Bend change.
- Frames list placements without render-state overscan.
- Frames state their cell size. An internal Orbit switch, not user configuration, gates graphics. While it is off, frames state `kitty_graphics` false, carry no entries and keep placeholder cells unblanked. Orbit's real-PTY checks turn it on from this bead; orb-j2i.11 turns it on in the shipped build.
- The prerequisite orb-j2i.3 (the fork iterator) is superseded: eon-9rtt.4 moved the pin to upstream 9ede35b8, whose safe ImageIterator orb-j2i.1 proved.
- ORB-C16's Storage rules fall to this bead: set libghostty's storage limit to 10,000,000 bytes per screen, accept only the direct medium, and install no PNG decoder.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Correction to the reference gate above (j2i6 session, 2026-10-27, from review round 1).
- Wrong: "Frames are extracted only inside the client's send closure, so extraction is queueing". The Frame decision does extract inside `send_server`'s closure. Wheel (host.rs `orbit.wheel`), scroll (`orbit.scroll`), the selection tick (`orbit.tick`, pty.rs) and return to live (`orbit.return_to_live`) extract their frame first and then call `send_server`. `send_server` (socket.rs) drops a message without queueing it when the session is Disconnected or Pressured, or when the push fails. Identities are therefore assigned at extraction. This still meets ORB-C16 ("when it first queues a frame that references it"): a frame goes unqueued only on an attachment that is ending, and the next attach resets the numbers. orb-j2i.7 must not treat extraction as queueing when it starts resources. It should start them from frames actually queued.
- Storage: libghostty already defaults to the direct medium and a 10 MB limit. Orbit's setters make those rules explicit and change no behavior. The orbit CHANGELOG now says so.
- Blanking also drops a placeholder cell's link. The unit test now covers this in the frame and in a preview row (red with the link kept).

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Decision on ORB-C16's internal switch (j2i6 session, 2026-10-27, answering eon-overseer's design question).

`ORBIT_KITTY_GRAPHICS=1` is a temporary staging switch, not a user toggle. ORB-C16 says the switch "is not user configuration" and that "`orb-j2i.11` turns it on in the shipped build, in the same change that makes Venus draw images". So it does not belong in Eon configuration (AGENTS.md Configurability). No person should ever choose it.
- Who sets it: only Orbit's own checks. The real-PTY check `kitty_placements` sets it in Orbit's environment, and the unit tests build `FrameExtractor::new(true)` directly. Eon, Eon Runtime and Venus never set or parse it. No launch path passes it, and `docs/CONFIGURATION.md` does not name it. Orbit reads it once at start (`cli::kitty_graphics`), like `ORBIT_GUARDIAN_FAULT`.
- Who removes it: orb-j2i.11. That bead turns graphics on in the shipped build, either by deleting the variable and making the switch a constant on, or by having Orbit default it on. It records which. Until then, a shipped Orbit states `kitty_graphics` false and keeps placeholder cells as they are.
- Why an environment variable: the real-PTY checks run the built Orbit, which rules out a Cargo feature. A command-line option would add to Orbit's command-line surface, which its consumers parse and the contract excludes.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Reference gate (j2i6 session, 2026-10-27). The change is consequential: it changes what Orbit writes on the wire while ORB-C16's internal switch is on, and it sets libghostty's Kitty storage and transmission-medium rules, a trust boundary.

## Behavior and owners
- With the switch on, every complete frame carries ORBF v3's graphics block: libghostty's cell size, the viewport's placements in drawing order, each pending or unavailable, and the omitted flag past 4,096 entries or 256 resources. Placeholder cells (U+10EEEE) are blanked in frames and previews. With it off, frames are as at 44e92c5. Owner: Orbit's Rust host, in `orbit/src/frame.rs` (extraction, identities, limits, blanking). No Bend change: no resource starts, so every entry within the limits stays pending (ORB-C16 Owner).
- Storage rules (always, not gated): Orbit sets libghostty's per-screen limit to 10,000,000 bytes, turns the file, temporary-file and shared-memory mediums off, and installs no PNG decoder. Owner: `Orbit::spawn` in `orbit/src/pty.rs`. libghostty owns parsing and storage.
- Per-attachment identities: the extractor numbers each resource, keyed by libghostty's image generation, when a frame first references it; numbers increase and are never reused; the host resets them when a client attaches. Frames are extracted only inside the client's send closure, so extraction is queueing.

## References read
- libghostty-rs `9ede35b8ea94a55ed3608408d67e102883129f1e` (the pin): `render.rs` ImageIterator/ImageIteration docs and getters (iteration order is not drawing order; only drawable placements; partly visible entries have negative viewport cells; no cell size means an empty list); `kitty/graphics.rs` Graphics::image, Image::{width,height,format,generation,data}, the storage and medium setters, `set_png_decoder` (Orbit calls none).
- Ghostty (refs `~/pjs/refs/ghostty-7501/repo`, 8c425a7, same code paths as the pin's vendored 521cf2c5 per orb-j2i.1): `src/terminal/render.zig:1829-1830` computes the placement geometry's cell as `width_px / cols` and `height_px / rows`; `src/font/shaper/run.zig:264-267,326-333` shapes a placeholder cell as a blank; `src/terminal/Terminal.zig:305-325,4241-4248` (libghostty's defaults are already 10 MB and the direct medium; the alternate screen inherits the primary's limits); `src/terminal/c/terminal.zig:1559-1610` (setters apply to every initialized screen).
- Comparable implementation: Ghostty's own renderer (above) and ghostling_rs's placement queue (example/ghostling_rs/src/main.rs:401-467, 711-737, read in orb-j2i.1): sort by layer then z, key textures by (image id, generation).

## Decisions and rejected approaches
- Switch: the environment variable `ORBIT_KITTY_GRAPHICS=1`, read once at start, as `ORBIT_GUARDIAN_FAULT` is. Rejected: a command-line option (Orbit's command line is a consumer surface; the contract says the switch is not configuration) and a Cargo feature (the real-PTY checks run the built Orbit).
- Cell size: the frame states libghostty's own `width_px / cols` and `height_px / rows`, the values its geometry uses, or 1 when no client size has arrived (the list is then empty). Rejected: Orbit's surface size, which can differ from libghostty's after a program's DECCOLM.
- Identity map: kept only for resources the latest frame references (at most 256). A resource that no frame references any more was never started, so it is skipped and a later reference takes a fresh number, as ORB-C16 states. orb-j2i.7 extends it for started resources.
- Unavailable: a side outside 1..=4,096 pixels, more than 10,000,000 decoded bytes, a format other than RGB or RGBA, or an image the storage cannot look up. Unavailable entries still take an identity and count toward the 256 resources.
- Order: stable sort by (layer, z, Kitty image id), so libghostty's order breaks ties.
- Blanking keeps the cell's width, its background, foreground and inverse (which decide the background a client paints), selection and protection; it drops text, link, underline, underline colour and the other text attributes. Rejected: a space with the full style (Ghostty's shaper), because ORB-C16 forbids drawing placeholder decorations.
- No dependency is added. Portability disposition: neutral (no platform mechanism changes).

## Checks
- Unit tests in `orbit/src/frame.rs`: a placeholder stream gives per-row entries with libghostty's geometry, stable pending identities and blank cells, and nothing with the switch off; ordering, the 256-resource and 4,096-entry caps with the omitted flag; an image over 4,096 pixels is unavailable.
- Real-PTY check `kitty_placements` (Nix `orbit-kitty-placements`): with the switch on, a Yazi-shaped Kitty stream after a client size gives the expected entries and blank cells; a file-medium transmission stores nothing.

title: Send image pixels to the client through a bounded resource plane
description:
## Why

Venus needs the decoded pixels each placement refers to, sent once per attachment epoch and
generation, bounded, and never blocking PTY processing. Lucca chose (2026-10-23) that a resource that
does not fit is marked pending and re-sent when room returns, while frame overflow keeps
Pressured -> Detach.

## Evidence

- Output queue and classes: orbit/src/socket.rs:193-353 (`replaceable_suffix` :246-268, room checks
:284-323, pressure :619-638).
- Bend bounds: `Bounds{1000, 1000, 1000, 12587045}` (orbit/src/main.bend:17-18; schema
src/boundary.schema:317); Pressured -> Detach (src/session.bend:560-564); ORB-C7 promise check
(src/socket.rs:1178-1195).
- Nearest precedent for per-turn host output decided before the frame: clipboard writes
(src/boundary.schema:45-48, 358; docs/HOST.md "Decisions").
- Bend cost: proof/ is generated by tools/step-proof.rs; a new flag that gates a decision splits the
proof search (the `metadata_changed` precedent grew it from 7,800 to 12,300 cases).
- Pixel bytes must never cross the worker pipe (facts are one line under PIPE_BUF).

## Prerequisites

orb-j2i.6.

## Scope

In scope:
- Copy decoded pixels out of libghostty storage during the frame carry-out for placements the
attachment has not received at that generation; enqueue announce and chunk messages in a queue class
frames never replace; per-attachment sent record keyed by epoch-scoped id and generation.
- A resource budget chosen by the Bend worker (a new `Bounds` field), with boundary.schema change,
regenerated src/boundary.rs and src/boundary.bend via tools/boundary.rs, step-proof reruns, and one
new accounting law in LAWS.bend with its proof and sensitivity check. Show the law text to Lucca
before relying on its proof (orbit/AGENTS.md).
- Pending marker for placements whose resource did not fit; re-send when room returns.
- Exact limits from ORB-C16; docs/HOST.md and docs/BEHAVIOR.md updates.

Out of scope:
- A missing-resource request message (rejected for the first slice); Venus.

## Acceptance

- A slow client never makes Orbit block PTY processing or detach for resources; frames still detach
on overflow as before; each resource is sent at most once per epoch and generation absent pressure.
- `ALL PROOFS CHECK` with the new law, and its sensitivity check fails a broken policy.

## Verification

- Focused real-PTY and socket checks through `nix develop -c eon-test`; Orbit proof run; fmt and
clippy; converge plus Codex (gate code: include the scope line for corner cases).

## Stop Conditions

- Stop for Lucca on the law text. Stop and split if the Bend change and the Rust resource plane do
not fit one session; the split point is the Bounds field and law versus the Rust queue work.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Contract text adopted in orb-j2i.2 (ORB-C16) replaces parts of this bead's plan; where they differ, the contract governs.
- Orbit copies a resource's pixels once, when it starts the announcement, which needs no PTY output. The copy belongs to the transfer start, not to every frame's carry-out.
- One transfer runs at a time per attachment, from that copy, and finishes even if storage replaces the image. The copy plus at most 1,048,576 queued chunk bytes is all Orbit holds outside storage.
- Resource messages wait in their own queue, never take ORB-C7's room, and never cause its disconnect. A frame waits at most for the one resource message being written.
- Entries are pending until a resource's last chunk is written. Orbit then publishes a new frame at the next revision, after any synchronized-output hold ends.
- Identities are assigned at first reference, strictly increase and are never reused. Pending resources start in identity order, and a skipped resource gets a fresh number if referenced again.
- A retirement is written only after a frame without the reference, and no later frame references the resource.
- At most 1,024 resources are unretired per attachment. On exit, unstarted resource messages are dropped, the one being written is finished, and then `Exited` follows.
- The PTY text-area pixel size belongs to orb-j2i.4.
- The frame published when a pending resource completes is a Bend publication decision, as ORB-C4 has Bend decide each publication.

comments.text:
Correction to the reference gate above (j7 session, 2026-10-27): the boundary gains one decision, not two. `decision 43 Transfer start:bool retire:bool` replaces the gate's `StartResource` and `RetireResources`. Bend answers fact `Resources` with exactly one `Transfer`, and its fields carry the policy: `retire` when the run is live and a retirement is due, `start` when it is live, the plane is idle and not capped. The host retires first, then starts.

Why: with two decisions whose presence depends on `idle`, `capped` and `due`, those flags split every proof leaf that reached them. The full PROOF.bend peaked at 5.1 GB (HEAD 2.3 GB), and the lifecycle step-proof search took 30.5 minutes. With the fields, the Resources trees roughly halve (lifecycle 3,936 → 1,956 leaves, view 5,016 → 2,420, management 4,440 → 2,204), and the proof peaks at 2.7 GB in about 21 s. The adopted law's text is unchanged; `Resource.starts` reads the `start` field. Plan change under Lucca's relayed pre-approval of "changes of plan if a clearly better alternative appears" (2026-10-26).

comments.text:
Law text adopted (j7 session, 2026-10-27) under Lucca's standing approval, relayed by eon-overseer. Lucca, 2026-10-26, to eon-overseer: "focus on finishing the worspace-switching beads, but try to advance on kitty-graphics too / everything is pre-approved. autonomous." and "also pre-aprove changes of plan if a clearly better alternative appears". Applied to: orbit/AGENTS.md's rule that Lucca sees a new law before its proof is relied on, for this bead's one new law.

```
# ORB-C16: Orbit starts a resource exactly when the child runs, no transfer
# is in progress and fewer than 1,024 resources are announced and not
# retired, so it holds at most one copy outside storage and never passes the
# cap.
law resource_starts_stay_within_budget:
  for live: Bool
  for idle: Bool
  for capped: Bool
  for due: Bool
  {Resource.starts(Resource.answer(Resource.Plane{live, idle, capped, due})) == Bool.and(live, Bool.and(idle, Bool.not(capped))) : Bool}
```

Before: "After that it starts a resource before the first frame that references it when the resource queue below has room."
After: "After that it starts a resource once it has queued the first frame that references it, when the resource queue below has room."

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Reference gate (j7 session, 2026-10-27). The change is consequential: it changes the host/worker boundary (a new Bounds field, fact and two decisions), adds a Bend law, and adds a per-attachment resource queue that writes decoded pixels to the client while ORB-C16's internal switch is on. The shipped wire is unchanged while the switch stays off (orb-j2i.11 turns it on).

## Behavior and owners
- Bend (src/session.bend plus a pure policy module src/resource.bend) decides when resources start and when retirements are queued, from fact `Resources`, and publishes the frame at the next revision when a resource's last chunk is written (after any synchronized-output hold, through the existing `publish`). It chooses the resource queue's bound, `Bounds.resource_bytes` = 1,048,576 chunk payload bytes.
- Rust host: `frame.rs` keeps the per-attachment resource records (identity by libghostty image generation, which libghostty never reuses across images, screens or terminals; sent, delivered, gone) and marks entries ready, pending or unavailable. `socket.rs` keeps a second lane beside ORB-C7's output queue: announcements, chunks and retirements, the one transfer's copy, and the chunk payload count under Bend's bound. The writer finishes whichever message it started; otherwise it writes the output queue first, so a frame waits at most for the rest of one resource message. Resource messages never count against `output_bytes` and never make the client Pressured. `host.rs` reports `Resources` from its wake when the plane changed, and carries out `StartResource` and `RetireResources`.
- Candidates come only from frames actually queued (the relay from orb-j2i.6): a frame's pending references become startable when its push succeeds, not at extraction.
- Retirement: when a frame extraction finds a sent resource missing from the active screen's storage at its generation (only for resources copied from that screen), it is gone after that extraction's serial; it becomes due once a frame-bearing message with that serial or later is fully written. Retirement waits while its own transfer still queues chunks.
- Exit: unstarted resource messages and the transfer copy are dropped; the partly written message finishes before `Exited`. Detach drops the lane with the peer; attach resets the records.

## References read
- ORB-C16 (orbit/docs/CONTRACTS.md, adopted in orb-j2i.2) and the relays on this bead; orb-j2i.6's gate and its correction (identities at extraction).
- libghostty-rs 9ede35b `kitty/graphics.rs`: `Image::generation` is never reused by another image, screen or terminal; `Image::data` is None while pixels are pending and valid only until the terminal is next mutated, so the copy is taken in the carry-out of `StartResource`.
- orbit-protocol ORBS v14 codec (orb-j2i.5): `ResourceAnnounce::new`, `ResourceChunk`, `ResourceRetire`, `RESOURCE_CHUNK_BYTES`.
- Precedents in this repository: the clipboard writes (a host-held per-turn output that Bend orders before the frame), the metadata observer's queue (a second bounded queue whose pressure Bend decides), and ORB-C7's single output bound (socket.rs, the bound unit test).
- Comparable implementation: Ghostty's renderer and ghostling_rs (read in orb-j2i.1/orb-j2i.6) key uploaded textures by (image id, generation) and drop them when storage no longer holds that generation; adopted for retirement detection. Rejected: their in-process upload, since Orbit's client is across a socket.

## Decisions and rejected approaches
- Bend holds no copy of the plane's counts; the host reports `idle`, `capped` and `due` and Bend decides from them, so each count has one owner. Rejected: Bend tracking queued bytes and unretired count itself (a second owner, and a fact per chunk).
- One fact `Resources` reported from the wake only when something changed, so a failed copy or a start with nothing to start cannot loop.
- Writer priority to the output queue, as ORB-C16 states; resources move whenever frames are not waiting.
- The law: Bend starts a resource exactly when the child runs, no transfer is in progress and fewer than 1,024 resources are unretired (text recorded on this bead before its proof is relied on).
- No dependency is added. Portability disposition: neutral (socket writes and libghostty reads only).

## Checks
- Unit tests in socket.rs (lane priority, chunk budget, no pressure from resources, exit drop) and frame.rs (ready after delivery, retirement after a written frame, fresh number after a failed copy).
- The real-PTY check `kitty_placements` extended: a Yazi-shaped image arrives as one announcement and its chunks, and a later frame lists it ready without further PTY output.
- `ALL PROOFS CHECK` with the new law, its sensitivity check, regenerated proof lemmas, orbit-boundary.

title: Prove Orbit's image lifecycle on a real PTY
description:
## Why

ORB-C16 must be proved across terminal lifecycle, not only on a single transmit. Kitty images change
with replace, delete, clear, scroll, resize and screen switches, and attachments come and go.

## Prerequisites

orb-j2i.7.

## Scope

In scope:
- Real-PTY checks (Orbit's existing harness, canonical wire only) feeding Yazi's Kgp stream and
asserting frames and resource messages across: replacement (new generation), `a=d,d=A` delete,
clear, scroll, resize, primary and alternate screens, detach and reattach (re-send from libghostty
storage on the new epoch), pressure (pending then re-sent), and process exit. No stale placement,
no reference to an unsent resource without a pending marker, no false success.
- orbit/docs/BEHAVIOR.md claims naming each check; ORB-C16 checks listed in its index entry.

Out of scope:
- Venus; installed dogfood (orb-j2i.12).

## Acceptance

- Every lifecycle step above has a passing real-PTY check named in BEHAVIOR.md.

## Verification

- `nix develop -c eon-test` for the focused checks; converge plus Codex.

## Stop Conditions

- A lifecycle defect in orb-j2i.6 or orb-j2i.7 code: fix it here only if small and owned by the
same code; otherwise file a bug under orb-j2i and stop.

title: Draw images between cell backgrounds and text in Venus
description:
## Why

Venus cannot draw images at all: it has one rectangle pipeline and one glyphon text pass, and each
row interleaves background and foreground rectangles, so there is no place for an image band
between cell backgrounds and text (Lucca's 2026-10-23 z-order choice). This bead builds that
drawing path with a local test image and no wire dependency.

## Evidence

- Rectangle pipeline: venus/src/render.rs:495-565 (24-byte position+color vertices); one render
pass, glyphs last in one `text_renderer.render` call (render.rs:806-844).
- Row rectangles interleave backgrounds then block/underline/strike/overline per row:
venus/src/render/cells.rs:259-392.
- Text above overlays only by clipping around one `text_overlay` rect: render.rs:1928-1977.
- Uncaptured wgpu errors panic via `assert!` in `handle_uncaptured_gpu_error` (render.rs:2318);
device uses default limits (render.rs:463; 2D textures max 8192).
- VEN-C15 rejected a "second GPU pipeline" for blur; this bead adds one for images, which
VEN-C31 (orb-j2i.2) authorizes. wgpu has no RGB8 format, so RGB expands to RGBA (4/3 bytes).

## Prerequisites

orb-j2i.1, orb-j2i.2 (VEN-C31 text: band, budget, sampling).

## Scope

In scope:
- A textured-quad pipeline (WGSL) for RGBA images; per terminal, emit all cell backgrounds first,
then images, then foreground rectangles and text, so images sit in the chosen band; clip to the
terminal surface and under anything stacked above (popups, dialogs, notices).
- Texture creation inside an error scope after checking device limits and a budget, so a bad
allocation is a reported failure, never a panic.
- A test-only image source to exercise the band in the existing CPU-side vertex/scene tests, plus
one isolated-display observation.
- venus/docs/CRATES.md "GPU and text" line for the image pipeline.

Out of scope:
- Protocol, resource store (orb-j2i.10), cache and real placements (orb-j2i.11).

## Acceptance

- With the test source, an image draws above a cell background and below text in a pane and in a
popup, clipped correctly; an oversize allocation is refused without a panic.

## Verification

- CPU vertex/scene tests through `nix develop -c eon-test`; one isolated-display observation as
venus/docs/DEVELOPMENT.md describes; fmt and clippy for venus; converge plus Codex.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if the band needs a second text renderer or atlas change beyond VEN-C31's text.
- Ask eon-overseer before any isolated Sway session or nix build.
close_reason: Image band, pipeline and scoped uploads landed; CPU tests, fmt, clippy and the isolated lavapipe observation pass on tree 5a5c86d

title: Keep scrollback usable during continuous terminal output
description:
## User report and observable contract

Consumer: one healthy exact-version attached client, including Venus inside Eon.

Trigger: the client has presented frame revision N and sends PreviewVertical or ScrollVertical while PTY output advances Orbit before that request is handled.

Result: the user can enter and continue retained-history scrolling without a continuous-output TUI starving the gesture. Orbit applies any committed relative movement exactly once against one coherent authoritative state, returns rows and frames tied to the state actually used, and keeps the viewport pinned after entry while later output continues.

Important failures: Orbit must not expose a partial synchronized-output update, mix rows from different revisions, apply a batch twice, route from stale terminal modes, hide queue pressure, or weaken stale-revision protection for selection and unrelated semantic input.

Dogfood report, 2026-08-26: Codex and possibly other updating TUIs can make scrolling fail visibly with "Orbit rejected input: scroll frame revision is stale"; the same race also produces "preview frame revision is stale". This blocks normal scrollback during active output.

## Contract routing and ownership

This intentionally changes the ORB-C8 rule that preview and signed scroll commit require the exact current complete-frame revision and that every stale request fails. It preserves Orbit as the sole terminal, history, viewport, routing, revision, and PTY owner. Preserve ORB-C1 through ORB-C7 and ORB-C9 through ORB-C11.

Prefer a compatible ORBS v10 semantic hardening with unchanged wire bytes and no Venus retry policy. Known consumers are Eon Desktop Venus and Eon. Stop for explicit user choice if correctness requires a wire change, compatibility window, second terminal snapshot, or client-owned history.

The user selected the product outcome and planning work on 2026-08-26. Contract-index and implementation edits begin only after this Bead is claimed under the repository execution and reference gates.

Portability disposition: neutral above the existing terminal owner.

## Evidence and root-cause hypothesis

Current src/interaction.rs rejects both requests whenever their frame_revision differs from Presentation.revision. Venus sends the revision it presented, exposes InvalidInput as a notice, and resets its terminal-scroll gesture after any server failure. Continuous output can therefore advance Orbit between preview and commit indefinitely.

The existing authoritative_viewport_survives_detach_and_slow_reader_pressure proof already shows that, after one successful upward commit, libghostty keeps the viewport pinned across later PTY output. The missing contract is starvation-free admission into and movement within that already-owned viewport, not a second freeze subsystem.

## Scope boundary

In scope: the smallest Orbit-owned ORB-C8 admission rule that removes the observed preview and commit races; exact revision/result semantics; synchronized-output coherence; terminal-routing changes; selection cancellation; pressure; detach; and one real continuous-output regression.

Out of scope: Venus string matching or blind retries, a client history cache, arbitrary history queries, a second terminal state, new gesture fields, pixels, kinetic policy, public tuning, search, graphics, persistence, unrelated stale semantic inputs, dependencies, or platform expansion. Downstream Venus acceptance `ven-accept-continuous-output-scrollback-a1s` and Eon profile rollout `eon-adopt-continuous-output-scrollback-umf` remain separate repository-owned Beads.

## Steps to Reproduce

Run a retained-history terminal under repeated full-screen TUI updates, present revision N in Venus, then begin or continue scrolling after Orbit advances its presentation revision. The current owner rejects PreviewVertical or ScrollVertical as stale, Venus displays the corresponding notice, resets the gesture, and repeated output can prevent entry into scrollback.

## Acceptance Criteria

The structured acceptance_criteria field is authoritative. In summary, both stale races must be reproduced first, continuous output must no longer starve authoritative scrollback, and revision coherence, synchronized output, routing, pressure, and unrelated stale-input rejection must remain intact.
design:
1. Start with one deterministic red check for each observed race: obtain a valid frame, advance Presentation through terminal output before PreviewVertical or ScrollVertical is handled, and prove the current code returns InvalidInput.
2. Compare only the minimum credible shapes: safely resolve the relative request against the current authoritative state; retain one bounded pending scroll intent until a coherent frame exists; or retain the current failure. Prefer unchanged ORBS v10 and no new state only if the resulting rows, routing, ordering, and synchronized-output behavior are coherent.
3. A preview response names the authoritative revision whose rows it describes. A commit mutates the native viewport once, advances authority at most once, and returns one atomic frame-bearing outcome from that resulting state.
4. Evaluate terminal mouse tracking, alternate-screen mode 1007, and synchronized output from the current authoritative terminal state. Never expose an intermediate synchronized frame. If the continuous-output regression cannot be fixed without a new pending-interaction lifecycle or wire field, stop for user choice.
5. Keep stale selection and other coordinate- or phase-bound input strict. Add no generic stale-request framework.
6. Prove Orbit first. Venus then accepts the exact producer revision; Eon pins the accepted pair and dogfoods the installed profile.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A deterministic regression advances Orbit after a client frame, then sends both PreviewVertical and ScrollVertical from that previously presented revision. Neither observed stale-frame notice is returned, and every response is coherent with the authoritative revision and viewport actually used.
2. One real PTY fixture emits a bounded Codex-like stream of repeated screen updates while an attached client enters history and continues scrolling. The request completes within a bounded time, applies exactly once, and later output does not pull the pinned viewport back to live.
3. Preview remains read-only. A signed commit calls the native viewport once, clears selection under the existing policy, advances authority at most once, and returns exact requested/applied rows, one complete frame, and its matching next preview.
4. Terminal mouse tracking, alternate-screen mode 1007, synchronized output, resize, semantic-key return to live, detach/reattach, client loss, exit, malformed distances, and output pressure retain explicit coherent outcomes with no partial mutation or invented PTY input.
5. Stale selection and every unrelated revision-bound semantic input remain rejected. No client string matching, blind retry loop, second terminal/history owner, unbounded queue, or new dependency is introduced.
6. ORBS v10 bytes and public values remain unchanged, or implementation stops before a breaking protocol change for explicit user approval and a revised consumer plan.
7. ORB-C8, contracts, changelog after acceptance, reference evidence, LOC, focused red/green checks, canonical locked Rust/governance/Clippy checks, and git diff all agree at one proof revision.
8. Closure names the exact compatible producer proof and Venus acceptance `ven-accept-continuous-output-scrollback-a1s`; it does not claim installed Eon resolution before the downstream pin rollout.
notes:
Accepted owner proof: 4e03fe280a714c3f3e29d31d0ec6374eaaf4ecea changes ORB-C8 under unchanged exact-version ORBS v10.

Orbit semantic interaction remains the sole owner. Lagging relative PreviewVertical and ScrollVertical requests resolve against current terminal modes and authoritative presentation state; preview reports the revision inspected, while commit applies one native delta and returns one atomic frame-bearing outcome. Future revisions, stale selection, synchronized output, malformed distance, pressure, and unrelated revision-bound input retain their strict failures.

Rejected alternatives: Venus string matching or blind retry, pending-scroll state, a second terminal snapshot or history owner, a generic stale-request abstraction, protocol fields or version change, and a new dependency.

Exact proof: focused red/green unit and real-PTY regressions; cargo fmt --all --check; cargo check --locked --workspace; cargo test --locked --workspace; orbit-governance; pinned Starcompass check-consumer; cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings; and git diff --check, all green on the unchanged candidate before commit. Product Rust is 13,830 lines; governance Rust 729; total owned Rust 14,559; total owned implementation 15,266. Dependency footprint and wire bytes are unchanged.

Remaining scope: exact Venus acceptance ven-accept-continuous-output-scrollback-a1s, then Eon rollout eon-adopt-continuous-output-scrollback-umf. This Orbit closure does not claim either downstream result.
close_reason: Accepted Orbit owner proof 4e03fe280a714c3f3e29d31d0ec6374eaaf4ecea keeps relative preview and signed scroll usable while output advances; Venus acceptance and Eon rollout remain downstream.

title: Encode Kitty Space release without duplicate text
description:
## Contract and observed regression

Harden preserved ORB-C5 without changing ORBS v4.

- Consumer: a terminal application such as Codex CLI 0.149.0 running under Orbit.
- Trigger: Kitty keyboard event reporting is active and Venus sends one semantic Space press followed by one Space release; both events may carry associated text U+0020.
- Result: Orbit writes one literal Space for the press and a Kitty release sequence for the release. A release never becomes a second text insertion.
- Important failures: unsupported physical keys and encoder failures remain explicit terminal failures without partial admission.

Observed on 2026-08-23 in a disposable Venus and Orbit session on x86_64 Linux Wayland. Venus emitted exactly one Press and one Release for PhysicalKey SPACE. strace of the actual Codex TTY reader showed two separate reads of 0x20. Letter releases in the same session were correctly encoded as Kitty release sequences. A virtual-key Space whose physical identity was Escape produced one literal Space plus an Escape release sequence, isolating the defect to Orbit key encoding for the physical Space release.

## Ownership and references

Orbit semantic interaction remains the sole ORB-C5 encoder owner. Venus must not coalesce or discard valid native key transitions to compensate.

Required before code: current ORB-C5 contract and proof; libghostty-vt 0.2.1 and pinned Ghostty a887df42c56f6de86c0fe6da9c4eeca37931e083 key encoder source and tests; Kitty keyboard protocol release and associated-text rules; one comparable terminal encoder when useful. No dependency or protocol change is authorized.

## Acceptance

1. A focused red-green check reproduces Space release with associated text under Kitty event reporting and expects the canonical Kitty release sequence rather than U+0020.
2. The existing real-PTY ORB-C5 conformance check and canonical Rust suite pass.
3. Venus wrong-owner Space timing and IME coalescing compensation is removed in its own correction before Eon integration.
4. Eon consumes exact accepted Orbit and Venus revisions; the installed profile is refreshed without restarting live Sessions.
5. An outermost disposable Venus, Orbit, and actual Codex CLI reproduction shows one TTY read of 0x20 per hardware Space press and a distinct Kitty release sequence.
6. ORBS v4, dependencies, and unrelated input behavior remain unchanged. Portability disposition: neutral.
