title: Stream live terminal title and CWD to pane chrome
description:
## Outcome

Give Venus a bounded, read-only stream of Orbit-authored terminal title and working-directory metadata for pane chrome while preserving the sole interactive presentation attachment.

Smallest observable contract:
- Consumer: the exact Venus workspace client selected by Eon.
- Trigger: Venus observes a live Orbit Session for a pane, including a pane that is not currently selected.
- Result: Orbit publishes coalescible title, working-directory, revision, and lifecycle metadata as authoritative terminal state changes. A Codex OSC-title animation therefore continues to update in an inactive pane header.
- Failures: incompatible, malformed, excess, slow, or disconnected observers fail deterministically without disturbing the PTY, child, interactive Venus attachment, or Session cleanup.

Orbit remains the sole title/CWD authority. Observers never infer provider state from title text and never gain terminal input, resize, selection, clipboard, raw PTY, full-frame, process-control, or lifecycle authority.

This requires a user-approved product contract and a scoped amendment to ORB-C3 before code. Do not reserve or choose an ORB-C number during planning.

Impact: HIGH for multi-pane agent dogfood. Effort: M/L. Implementation risk: HIGH at the attachment boundary. Confidence: HIGH that a live owner-authored channel is needed; MEDIUM on whether it should reuse the presentation socket, extend the private management exchange, or use one new endpoint.

## Evidence

- Current Orbit source at bb1df102220577cd1f2647d47502d7a7c86cdabc already extracts libghostty title and pwd together in src/presentation.rs and carries both in canonical ORBF v1.
- crates/protocol/src/session/mod.rs and src/attachment.rs enforce one input-capable ORBS v4 client; a simultaneous connection receives Busy before a role can be negotiated.
- ORB-C3 proves exactly one local attachment. ORB-C4, ORB-C6, and ORB-C7 prove coherent bounded presentation and pressure behavior.
- Venus currently attaches only the selected Eon pane. A Venus last-seen cache would freeze Codex's animated title after focus moves and would not satisfy live per-pane chrome.
- Deferred epic orb-p92 already proposes broader authorized agent observation including visible text. This issue is its minimum reusable metadata subset, but it does not activate or expose the agent observer contract.

## Scope

In scope:
- One versioned local read-only metadata role or equivalent narrow boundary for title, working directory, terminal revision, and lifecycle only.
- A fixed observer-count bound, bounded/coalesced output, handshake/version failure, disconnect, child exit, and shutdown behavior.
- Concurrent proof with the existing one input-capable presentation client.
- Exact protocol documentation, contract index, changelog at acceptance, and focused real-PTY checks using OSC title and working-directory changes.
- Neutral wire values with Linux local-socket mechanics remaining in the existing platform seam.

Out of scope:
- Visible terminal text, rows, history, graphics, hyperlinks, cursor, selection, clipboard, raw ORBF, raw PTY, input, resize, process inspection/control, remote access, MCP, agent authorization, transcripts, provider-status inference, redaction claims, or multiple interactive clients.
- Venus rendering, Eon topology, pane naming, tab launch-directory policy, or user configuration.

## Reference gate before code

Required:
- Complete current ORB-C3, ORB-C4, ORB-C6, ORB-C7, ORB-C13 owners and their exact checks.
- Current runtime, attachment, presentation, management, protocol codec, pressure, and lifecycle paths.
- Exact pinned libghostty title/pwd behavior and update semantics.
- Exact Zellij pane-title/CWD mechanism as comparison evidence for the user-visible result.
- The complete orb-p92 planning contract, separating reusable metadata from its broader security surface.

Compare and record:
1. A role negotiated on the existing presentation endpoint.
2. A bounded extension of the existing private management request.
3. A separate metadata endpoint.
4. Venus last-seen caching only.

Choose the first shape that preserves one interactive client, live inactive updates, bounded pressure, lifecycle cleanup, and exact component identity with the least new state. Last-seen caching is rejected if it freezes inactive animations. A new dependency requires the crate gate; the expected solution uses existing Rust and local transport.

## Acceptance

- With one interactive Venus client attached, at least one simultaneous read-only observer receives the initial exact title/CWD metadata without Busy and cannot send any mutating message.
- Split and rapid OSC title updates coalesce to the latest complete metadata revision; an inactive Codex-style animation remains live without selecting the pane.
- OSC working-directory changes publish the exact Orbit-authored value. Empty or unavailable values remain explicit and bounded.
- Slow or non-reading observers cannot delay PTY reads, terminal mutation, interactive frames, child observation, or shutdown; memory and observer count stay within fixed documented bounds.
- Malformed, oversized, wrong-version, excess, and post-exit observation fail deterministically without leaking full frames or disturbing the active presentation client.
- Interactive input/resize/selection/clipboard semantics and ORB-C1 through ORB-C13 remain preserved except for the explicitly approved ORB-C3 wording.
- Focused protocol and real-PTY red/green checks pass, followed once by cargo fmt --check, cargo check --locked, cargo test --locked, cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings, and git diff --check.
- Closure records exact accepted source revision, consumer update order, observer bounds, dependency footprint, portability disposition, LOC, and remaining exclusions.

## Stop conditions

- Stop before code until the user approves the new/changed contract and exact compatibility/update order.
- Stop if the design grants a second input-capable attachment, exports full presentation state, makes Eon or Venus author terminal metadata, weakens bounded pressure or cleanup, or silently activates orb-p92's agent-observation surface.
- Stop before a new endpoint, dependency, compatibility window, or public/remote protocol unless its lifecycle cost is explicitly accepted.
- Stop if exact source/reference evidence shows live inactive metadata cannot be delivered without materially broader architecture; report that choice instead of falling back to misleading stale UI.

## Maintenance notes

This is pane-chrome metadata, not a general observer API. Manual pane rename is a separate Eon workspace-state decision because it is user-authored policy, not terminal state.

title: Structure Eon-family contracts for human review
description:
Documentation/tooling-only contract: humans, agents, and the Orbit governance validator consume the canonical Eon-family contract indexes. When any index is read or validated, each stable ORB-C*, VEN-C*, or EON-C* contract appears once as a named Markdown section with small semantic fields for status, consumer, trigger, result, important failures, ownership, consumed boundaries, scope boundary, current proof, and open proof. Existing behavior, ownership, statuses, IDs, proof revisions, and proof claims remain unchanged. Missing or duplicate required metadata and invalid proved revisions continue to fail deterministically.

Scope: migrate docs/CONTRACTS.md in eon-sessions, eon-desktop, and eon; update only the eon-sessions governance parser/tests that own contract-index validation; update affected README LOC scorecards. This changes no ORB, VEN, EON, wire, runtime, package, dependency, platform, or user-visible product contract. No YAML/JSON source, generator, compatibility parser, new dependency, or per-contract files.

## Acceptance Criteria

The canonical completion criteria are stored in this issue's acceptance_criteria field.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Every existing ORB-C*, VEN-C*, and EON-C* ID remains present exactly once with unchanged status, ownership, normative behavior, proof revisions/evidence, consumed boundaries, and limitations.
2. Contract prose is represented by one heading per contract and fixed semantic Markdown fields; long table rows and duplicated chronological proof narration are absent.
3. The current accepted proof is concise; historical execution detail remains in Beads/Git and user-visible chronology remains in CHANGELOG.md.
4. Orbit governance validates unique IDs, recognized statuses, required fields, full proof commits for proved contracts, named evidence, and unknown references against the new format.
5. Focused governance tests, all required documentation/diff checks, Beads flush, and affected README LOC scorecards pass.
6. No runtime source, protocol, manifest, dependency, package, or product behavior changes.
notes:

title: Upstream erased-row loss for libghostty tracked references
description:
Low-priority external correctness work in Ghostty. This Bead changes no product contract, does not block orb-j0m, and must not create an Orbit fork or private adapter.

Known failure:
External tracked grid references can silently change semantic identity after erased scrollback is removed. CSI 3 J reaches PageList history erasure; affected pins are remapped to retained storage rather than marked garbage. Later output can move the replacement cell into history, allowing an old external reference to resolve to the wrong row.

Outcome:
Confirm the failure against current Ghostty main, obtain the required human contribution access, and propose the smallest upstream correction if maintainers accept the issue. The native Orbit viewport and selection design does not expose long-lived history references, so this work is independent maintenance rather than product-path work.
design:
Exact prior proof:
- Pinned Ghostty a887df42c56f6de86c0fe6da9c4eeca37931e083 reproduced the clear-and-repopulate semantic remap.
- A disposable candidate changed three Ghostty files by +42/-2; 32 added lines were regression tests and production code was net +8.
- The candidate added an internal Pin.invalidate_on_erase bit, enabled it only for C-created external tracked pins, and marked those pins garbage when their row was erased.
- Internal viewport and selection pins retained existing remapping behavior, Pin remained 16 bytes, and focused tracked-grid-reference tests passed.
- No public C API, Rust wrapper, dependency, or Orbit change was required.

Submission discipline:
Rebase the proof onto current Ghostty before proposing code. Follow current CONTRIBUTING and AI rules exactly: the user writes any vouch request personally, discloses the extent of Codex assistance, and understands every submitted line. Open or obtain an accepted issue before a pull request when policy requires it. Treat the prior patch as evidence, not as a shape maintainers must accept.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Current Ghostty main is checked for the clear-and-repopulate failure with exact revision and focused reproducer.
2. The accepted issue states external tracked-reference semantic loss precisely and does not claim Orbit needs client-side paging.
3. Current contribution and AI rules are followed; the human author writes the vouch request and can explain the patch and tests.
4. Any patch preserves ordinary append and pruning behavior for surviving references, invalidates externally tracked references whose semantic row is erased, and preserves dependency-owned internal viewport and selection behavior.
5. Focused regression tests cover erased-reference loss and unaffected-reference stability; the required upstream checks pass.
6. No public API, new dependency, Orbit fork, private adapter, or libghostty-rs pin change is added unless separately chosen.
7. Closure records the upstream outcome: merged, rejected, superseded, or no longer reproducible. A later Orbit dependency update is a separate user-approved Bead only if the product needs it.

Priority P3 and deferred by user choice on 2026-08-06. Do not activate during the native orb-j0m path.

title: Validate canonical ORBF cell-width topology
description:
## Contract routing

Hardens existing `ORB-C4` and `ORB-C6` and preserves `ORB-C3`, `ORB-C5`, and `ORB-C7` through `ORB-C11`; it adds no product capability and does not authorize a new ORBF/ORBS wire revision. The canonical `orbit-protocol` frame validator remains the sole owner of accepted ORBF v1 cell-width topology.

The preceding shared-validator hardening `orb-harden-orbf-capabilities-6v9` closed at accepted proof `6de95296d252c119d4fdba2d9b03cec1a09355ae`. This Bead starts from that immutable ORB-C4/C6 owner revision; the historical Venus audit used package `3ee7c80005f3d2bbe81e539799327803716f6174`, and Venus must consume the resulting owner-first proof separately.

## Why

Consumers: Orbit's authoritative presentation producer and every canonical ORBF v1 decoder/reducer, including Venus.

Trigger: code encodes, decodes, or directly reduces a complete ORBF v1 frame containing `Wide`, `SpacerTail`, or `SpacerHead` roles.

Result: the canonical owner accepts only width-role layouts that preserve the selected libghostty terminal-grid topology. At minimum, ordinary wide cells and their tails must be contiguous and correctly ordered, spacer tails cannot be orphaned, and wrapped spacer heads must occur only in the exact edge/wrap sequence selected by the accepted producer. Invalid topology fails before a reducer or consumer materializes it.

Important failures: no partial frame acceptance, no silent normalization, no Venus compensating validator, and no over-restrictive rule inferred without checking exact libghostty wrap/viewport semantics.

Venus audit `ven-audit-venus-scene-renderer-2db` found the gap at Venus `4f799fef1c3e10e86d70b708708f7c2702d7aee8`. Impact MED. Effort S-M. Implementation risk MED because validation hardening and exact consumer pins/proofs must advance. Confidence HIGH in the canonical gap; confidence LOW that the accepted producer emits an invalid topology.

## Evidence

- `crates/protocol/src/lib.rs:223-239`: ORBF exposes four cell-width roles.
- `crates/protocol/src/lib.rs:553-582` at accepted proof `6de95296...`: `validate_frame` checks capabilities, dimensions, row/cell counts, cursor bounds, and encoded size, but not width-role topology.
- `crates/protocol/src/lib.rs:643-659`: raw decode validates only the width tag, so any ordering of valid tags is canonical.
- `crates/protocol/src/lib.rs:972-1039`: the rich codec fixture itself arranges `Wide` at a row end, `SpacerTail` at the next row start, and `SpacerHead` afterward; it proves tags/round-trip, not a producer-valid grid.
- `src/presentation.rs:110-155,194-200`: the accepted producer maps exact libghostty width roles directly into the canonical frame.
- Pinned Ghostty `a887df42c56f6de86c0fe6da9c4eeca37931e083` `src/terminal/page.zig:510-555`: page integrity requires a SpacerTail to follow Wide and requires SpacerHead at the last column of a wrapped row.
- The same Ghostty source `src/terminal/Terminal.zig:1187-1220`: an ordinary wide character emits Wide followed by SpacerTail; wrapping at the real edge first emits SpacerHead, then wraps and emits the wide pair.
- Venus `src/scene.rs:435-535` at `4f799fef...`: Scene documents a validated-frame precondition, treats Wide as spanning two columns, and skips spacer roles. Adjacent Wide heads or a missing tail can therefore omit content; a maximal malformed run can overflow debug arithmetic.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Starting from an otherwise valid ORBF v1 frame, replace one row with adjacent `Wide` cells, a `Wide` not followed by `SpacerTail`, or an orphan `SpacerTail`.
2. Call canonical frame encoding; observe success because `validate_frame` checks no role adjacency.
3. Mutate valid encoded cell-width tag bytes into the same malformed ordering; observe canonical decode success.
4. Push the typed frame directly into `FrameReducer`; observe acceptance when its revision is newer.
5. Project the canonical-valid result through the exact Venus Scene consumer and observe skipped columns or invalid run arithmetic.

Expected: the canonical owner rejects producer-invalid width topology before reducer/consumer acceptance. Actual: valid individual tags are unconstrained.

## Reference classification

Required before code:
- Current `AGENTS.md`, this complete Bead, closed predecessor `orb-harden-orbf-capabilities-6v9` and accepted proof `6de95296d252c119d4fdba2d9b03cec1a09355ae`, `docs/CONTRACTS.md`, `docs/REFERENCES.md`, `docs/RATIONALE.md`, and `docs/CRATES.md`.
- Exact accepted `ORB-C4`/`ORB-C6` proof and canonical `orbit-protocol` source at the execution baseline.
- Exact libghostty-vt/libghostty-vt-sys 0.2.1 and pinned Ghostty `a887df42c56f6de86c0fe6da9c4eeca37931e083`: public `CellWide`, RenderState row/cell iteration, page integrity, wide printing, wrap, resize/reflow, and viewport-boundary behavior.
- Exact current Orbit producer and every canonical frame fixture/reducer caller.
- Exact Venus consumer revision and Scene width-role interpretation, only to prove the independently released boundary and required consumer update order.

Conditional:
- A focused real-libghostty corpus for viewport top/bottom boundaries, resizing, or reflow if source semantics do not uniquely determine whether a cross-row SpacerHead sequence may be truncated at a complete-frame boundary.

Comparison-only:
- No second terminal implementation is required unless exact selected libghostty behavior remains ambiguous after the focused corpus.

Rejected:
- Per-consumer validation, normalization/repair, a second schema, a new error framework, dependency, general grid validator framework, or new wire revision.

No Crate gate is expected. Platform disposition: neutral.

## Scope

In scope:
- `crates/protocol/src/lib.rs` existing frame validation and the fewest strong co-located encoder/raw-decoder/direct-reducer tests.
- Correction of existing protocol fixtures that are contract-invalid once exact topology is established.
- `src/presentation.rs` only if a focused producer check is required to prove emitted topology, not to normalize it.
- `README.md` LOC scorecard and `docs/CONTRACTS.md` proof lifecycle metadata.
- Exact cross-repository compatibility classification and owner-first/consumer-second update order.

Out of scope:
- Editing Venus in this Bead, changing public width variants/tags, new frame/session revision, compatibility adapter/window, graphics, shaping, grapheme-width calculation, terminal repair, dependency, or broader codec cleanup.

## Implementation notes

1. Rebaseline the exact accepted validator at `6de95296d252c119d4fdba2d9b03cec1a09355ae` and rerun duplicate and consumer searches.
2. Use TDD: require encoder, raw decoder, and direct reducer rejection plus non-mutation of an already accepted reducer frame.
3. Derive the smallest exact topology rules from selected libghostty, including ordinary same-row pairs and wrapped SpacerHead sequences; do not guess across viewport boundaries.
4. Put the invariant in the existing shared frame-validation owner so encode, decode, and reducer cannot drift. Reject rather than coerce.
5. Correct only fixtures proven invalid; retain accepted producer bytes byte-for-byte for valid frames.
6. Classify this as compatible hardening of contract-invalid ORBF v1 bytes only if every accepted producer and known consumer agrees. Otherwise stop for the user's breaking-change decision.
7. Commit/verify the Orbit source candidate first, then update proof metadata and close. A separate Venus Bead adopts the exact accepted Orbit proof and reruns consumer proofs; no compatibility window.

## Acceptance criteria

- Encoder, raw decoder, and direct reducer reject every locally malformed Wide/SpacerTail pair and every invalid SpacerHead placement selected by the exact producer contract.
- A rejected newer typed frame cannot replace the reducer's prior valid current frame.
- Focused valid cases cover narrow cells, ordinary wide pairs, a real wrapped SpacerHead sequence, relevant viewport boundaries, and producer-derived resize/reflow cases.
- Accepted Orbit producer frames remain byte-for-byte unchanged and pass the canonical validator.
- Venus needs no compensating validator or schema mirror.
- The change is explicitly classified compatible or stopped for a user compatibility decision; known consumers and owner-first update order are recorded.
- No direct dependency, new protocol version, adapter, or compatibility window is introduced.
- ORB-C4/ORB-C6 and every touched proof row are current at closure.

## Verification

- `cargo test --locked -p orbit-protocol` must pass focused width-topology, canonical codec, and reducer checks.
- Run the cheapest focused `src/presentation.rs` producer corpus selected at the Reference gate.
- `cargo fmt --all --check`
- `cargo check --locked --workspace`
- `cargo test --locked --workspace`
- `cargo run --locked --quiet -p orbit-governance -- .`
- `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `git diff --check`
- `br lint <this-id>`

All commands must exit 0 on one materially unchanged candidate; record exact test counts and environment.

## Stop conditions

- Stop if selected libghostty permits a topology that cannot be validated from one complete ORBF frame without an additional producer field or changed wire semantics.
- Stop if an accepted producer or consumer relies on the malformed layouts; ask the user to choose compatibility/versioning.
- Stop before a new dependency, wire revision, adapter, compatibility window, cross-repository edit, or second validator.
- Stop if another active issue owns canonical frame validation.

## Maintenance notes

The canonical protocol owns trust-boundary topology; Orbit owns producer truth; Venus consumes validated roles. Keep the correction one shared validator plus few strong cases, not a grid framework.

title: Record VT and Unicode baselines through Orbit and Venus
description:
Cross-repository verification task with no new user-visible behavior, terminal compatibility promise, or product contract. After orb-bi4.6 proves the first composed dogfood path, record one reproducible VT and Unicode baseline through the actual pinned Orbit server, PTY child, ORBS and ORBF bridge, and Venus native renderer.

Use a focused VTTEST scorecard plus ucs-detect and ucs-browser. The purpose is not to re-prove the complete libghostty terminal engine. It is to detect whether terminal modes, replies, input, structured presentation, Unicode cell semantics, glyph shaping, and native rendering survive the boundaries Eon owns.

Contract routing:
- Changes no EON-C, ORB-C, or VEN-C contract or proof status by itself.
- Exercises the exact accepted ORB-C2 and ORB-C4 through ORB-C6 boundary, later accepted history and selection contracts where relevant, and VEN-C1 through VEN-C4 plus VEN-C7 when accepted. Reconfirm IDs and exact proofs at activation.
- Routes every discrepancy to one Orbit, Venus, Eon, upstream, tool-expectation, or unsupported-capability owner. It repairs none of them.

Out of scope:
- An Eon terminal-emulation profile, xterm compatibility guarantee, exhaustive conformance claim, copied or vendored external suite, esctest integration, upstream libghostty testing, automated screenshot farm, per-push or scheduled CI, product code, protocol changes, new runtime dependencies, performance benchmarking, macOS support, or feature expansion.
design:
Verification plan:

1. Start only after orb-bi4.6 closes with exact accepted Eon, Orbit, and Venus revisions and a reproducible composed launch path. Record a planning and evidence baseline; this is a no-code acceptance run unless a minimum local command is later approved as necessary.
2. Pass a Reference and tool gate before tracked test, script, workflow, Nix, fixture, or documentation edits. Required evidence: the exact VTTEST source and release, applicable DEC manuals and xterm control-sequence documentation, the exact ucs-detect and ucs-browser release with its wcwidth and Unicode data identities, exact pinned libghostty and Ghostty behavior, and the accepted Orbit and Venus contracts. Compare focused direct use, esctest, owned synthetic cases, and no external suite. Keep esctest rejected unless a later exact review shows a maintained profile that removes rather than adds expectation ownership.
3. Launch the exact accepted pair through the existing Eon dogfood path. VTTEST and ucs-detect must run as real PTY children owned by Orbit while the real Venus client renders and supplies input. Do not substitute standalone Ghostty, a fake frame source, the diagnostic text client, raw PTY replay, or a handwritten protocol consumer.
4. Select the smallest VTTEST menu set that crosses owned boundaries: cursor movement and save or restore, margins and scrolling regions, erase behavior, SGR and colors, origin and wrap modes, alternate screen where covered, device status and attributes, resize-sensitive behavior, and representative keyboard sequences. Record pass, deviation, unsupported, ambiguous, and not-run outcomes; never report a blanket conformance score.
5. Run ucs-detect with a saved machine-readable report for bounded representative wide, zero-width, combining, grapheme, emoji ZWJ, variation-selector, regional-indicator, and language cases. Run ucs-browser visually for alignment and glyph quality using the actual Venus font stack. Distinguish Orbit and libghostty cursor-position or cell-width semantics from Venus shaping, fallback, atlas, and visual alignment.
6. Treat the ucs-detect wcwidth model as one comparator rather than product law. Classify every delta against the exact Unicode versions, accepted libghostty behavior, advertised terminal modes, actual glyph result, and prior Eon baseline. Unsupported graphics or terminal modes are not failures merely because a probe exists.
7. During a focused stateful case, resize once and detach then reattach Venus once to check that the observed state remains coherent across the accepted bridge. Do not repeat the broader lifecycle and application matrix already proved by orb-bi4.6.
8. Record exact Eon manifest and component commits; operating system, display backend, GPU and driver, locale, TERM and capability declarations, geometry, font and fallback stack; tool and Unicode versions; commands, menu items, generated report hashes or locations, screenshots where needed, elapsed time, and every classified result.
9. A regression in a claimed supported capability or an Orbit to Venus boundary invariant blocks closure and names one owner. A tool expectation mismatch or unsupported feature remains recorded evidence. Product fixes, protocol changes, renderer changes, new capabilities, and upstream work require separately authorized owner Beads.
10. The initial baseline is manual Linux evidence. Rerun after relevant libghostty, Unicode, font, shaping, input, presentation, or renderer changes and before releases carrying them. A future accepted macOS client consumes the method in its own platform proof rather than inheriting this Linux result.

Do not add a CHANGELOG entry. README LOC changes only if tracked handwritten verification text is later required; generated logs and screenshots remain evidence artifacts, not product source.
acceptance_criteria:
1. orb-bi4.6 is closed with exact accepted Eon, Orbit, and Venus revisions, and the baseline records the EON-C, ORB-C, and VEN-C implementations exercised without changing or promoting any contract.
2. A pre-edit Reference and tool gate records exact VTTEST, DEC or xterm references, ucs-detect, wcwidth, Unicode data, libghostty, Ghostty, Eon, Orbit, and Venus identities and licenses. It compares direct focused use with esctest, owned synthetic checks, and no external suite.
3. VTTEST and ucs-detect run inside the real Orbit-owned PTY while the real pinned Venus client renders and sends input through canonical ORBS and ORBF. Evidence identifies the actual processes and rejects standalone-emulator or fake-frame substitution.
4. One focused VTTEST scorecard covers the selected cursor, scrolling-region, erase, style or color, origin or wrap, terminal-reply, resize, and keyboard surfaces. Every item is classified as pass, deviation, unsupported, ambiguous, or not run with no blanket xterm or DEC conformance claim.
5. One saved ucs-detect report covers bounded representative width, combining, grapheme, emoji ZWJ, variation-selector, regional-indicator, and language cases. One ucs-browser pass visually checks alignment, shaping, fallback, and glyph quality in Venus.
6. Results distinguish authoritative Orbit and libghostty state, replies, and cell semantics from Venus presentation, shaping, fallback, and visual rendering. No client-side terminal model or alternate expectation owner is introduced.
7. One selected stateful result remains coherent across a real resize and Venus detach and reattach. This does not duplicate or replace the orb-bi4.6 application and lifecycle matrix.
8. Every deviation names one exact owner: Orbit, Venus, Eon composition, pinned upstream, external-suite expectation, environment, or explicitly unsupported capability. A regression in accepted behavior blocks closure; no product repair occurs in this Bead.
9. Evidence records exact commits, tools, platform, display, GPU, locale, TERM, geometry, fonts, Unicode data, commands, selected cases, report or screenshot locations, duration, and classified outcomes so a later run can compare deltas.
10. No external test source is copied or vendored; no esctest profile, compatibility layer, runtime dependency, product mode, protocol surface, CI job, schedule, screenshot farm, or full upstream conformance suite is added.
11. The recurring trigger is recorded as after relevant engine, Unicode, shaping, input, presentation, renderer, or platform changes and before releases that carry them. Linux evidence makes no macOS claim.
12. Any tracked planning or minimal verification surface passes governance and git diff checks. Closure records limitations and one result: accepted integration baseline, or held open with one named owner regression.

title: Adopt a qualifying libghostty release
description:
## Contract

- Consumer: Orbit and terminal applications using its authoritative terminal encoder.
- Trigger: crates.io publishes `libghostty-vt` and `libghostty-vt-sys` releases whose embedded Ghostty revision contains upstream fix `bd647035e97da4aadfe1003877ecf64a3a655059` or an accepted equivalent.
- Result: Orbit consumes that exact released dependency, Kitty releases never fall back to inserted text, press and repeat fallback text remains intact, and the local release adapter is reduced to only metadata normalization still required by the released API.
- Important failures: unpublished Git pins, unknown embedded source identity, API or ABI drift, Zig or Nix build drift, lost alternate-key metadata, missing Space release identity, or a wider terminal regression blocks adoption.

## Why

Orbit is current on the published Rust binding but not on Ghostty source. `Cargo.toml` pins crates.io `libghostty-vt` 0.2.1, and `docs/CRATES.md` records its embedded Ghostty `a887df42c56f6de86c0fe6da9c4eeca37931e083`. Upstream Ghostty fix `bd647035e97da4aadfe1003877ecf64a3a655059` prevents text fallback on release and is assigned to Ghostty 1.4.0. The binding master currently pins `22d13172cde98a0a4dda05d3d6a3fcb0dd8ed018`, which also predates the fix, so adopting an unpublished branch now adds churn without removing Orbit ownership.

`src/interaction.rs::encode_input` currently supplies canonical U+0020 metadata for physical Space and withholds fallback text from unidentified releases. The first responsibility may remain necessary after the dependency update; the second should be deleted only when the released encoder proves it owns that invariant.

## Prerequisites And Reference Gate

Before implementation:

1. Read current `AGENTS.md`, ORB-C2 and ORB-C5 in `docs/CONTRACTS.md`, the authoritative-terminal decision in `docs/CRATES.md`, and the complete key encoder call path and tests.
2. Inspect the exact published crate archives, embedded Ghostty revision, release notes, safe-wrapper API changes, C ABI changes, Zig requirement, license, dependency graph, and Nix prefetch implications.
3. Confirm by Git ancestry or exact source inspection that the embedded revision contains upstream Ghostty PR #13861, including release suppression and repeat preservation.
4. Compare the qualifying released dependency with no update and an unpublished Git pin. Select the release only if it removes more lifecycle ownership than it adds.
5. Keep the active integration frontier and Eon component graph unchanged until Orbit has an immutable accepted source revision.

## Scope

In scope:

- `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock`, and existing libghostty integration in `src/interaction.rs`.
- The focused Kitty release regression and only tests needed for changed dependency behavior.
- `docs/CRATES.md`, `docs/CONTRACTS.md`, `README.md` dependency identity and LOC accounting, and `CHANGELOG.md` only if observable behavior changes.
- Existing Nix downstream build proof against an immutable Orbit candidate.

Out of scope:

- Unpublished Git dependencies, a libghostty fork, copied Zig source, a second terminal engine, protocol changes, Venus input compensation, unrelated Ghostty features, automatic dependency updates, platform expansion, Eon graph edits, profile refresh, or live Session restart.
- Removing Space U+0020 normalization unless the qualifying release and exact regression prove another existing owner supplies the required release identity.

## Implementation Notes

1. Add no production change until the prerequisite release exists and its embedded revision is verified.
2. Update both exact crate versions and the lockfile together; retain the existing sole terminal owner.
3. Run the focused Kitty regression before simplifying `encode_input`. Delete only the release-text guard proven redundant upstream; retain the smallest remaining Space metadata normalization if required.
4. Recheck all libghostty API consumers and regenerate no binding locally.
5. Record exact dependency, Ghostty, Zig, license, graph, and replacement-cost evidence in this Bead and `docs/CRATES.md`.
6. Accept an immutable Orbit source before opening a separate Eon composition bead for the exact pin and profile rollout.

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo check --locked --workspace`
- `cargo test --locked --workspace`
- `cargo run --locked --quiet -p orbit-governance -- .`
- pinned Starcompass `check-consumer`
- `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `git diff --check`
- Focused Kitty checks prove release suppression with and without report-all, preserve repeat fallback, and preserve canonical Space release encoding.
- An existing Eon Nix consumer build resolves the exact immutable Orbit candidate and all vendored Ghostty and Zig inputs without network access during the build.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if no published crate contains the upstream fix.
- Stop if the crate does not expose its exact embedded Ghostty identity.
- Stop if adoption needs a fork, copied binding, protocol change, second terminal owner, or speculative Eon graph edit.
- Stop and retain the current adapter if removing any part loses Space releases, alternate-key metadata, press or repeat text, or existing terminal behavior.
- Stop for a new user decision if the release adds a materially broader dependency, toolchain, license, platform, or ownership cost.

## Maintenance Notes

Priority P2, effort M, risk MED, confidence HIGH. The current adapter is small and accepted, so this is release-triggered maintenance rather than an urgent bug. Ghostty 1.4.0 is a signal, not sufficient proof: the independently published Rust crate must embed the qualifying source. Eon adoption remains a later owner-first composition task after Orbit acceptance.
close_reason: Subsumed by eon-9rtt.3 (same outcome: pin an exact crates.io libghostty-vt release; 9rtt.3's Exit already says it 'settles orb-ze3'). ze3's text was stale (crates.io 0.2.1, src/interaction.rs; Orbit now pins upstream libghostty-rs 9ede35b8 via c56372f). Its bd647035 Kitty-release check and adapter-reduction rule were carried into eon-9rtt.3's 2026-10-27 comment.

Its spike eon-a9tr.1 must put this bead's 'no unpublished Git dependency / no copied binding' stop conditions to Lucca; if eon-a9tr lands a revision containing bd647035, this bead's purpose is covered there.

title: Match Nova's 16 px terminal typography
description:
## Observable contract

Consumer: a local user opening an unconfigured Venus terminal through Eon or EonTerm.

Trigger: Venus creates its default terminal grid at any supported display scale.

Result: terminal text uses a nominal 16 logical-pixel font size, matching Nova's selected size. The default row remains 18 logical pixels at 1x, giving an effective 1.125 line-height ratio—the integer-grid equivalent of Nova's configured 1.12 (16 × 1.12 = 17.92). Rendering, resize, pointer mapping, selection, cursor placement, IME, and accessibility consume the same scaled cell metrics.

Important failures: the horizontal fitting path must not silently reduce the selected face back to the current 14 px result; complete glyph ink must remain inside its row; adjacent rows must not overlap; grid capacity and cursor alignment remain coherent.

## Contract routing

Harden proved VEN-C1 and VEN-C2 while preserving VEN-C3, VEN-C4, VEN-C7, VEN-C8, VEN-C9, and VEN-C13. Consume the current accepted Orbit presentation contract unchanged. This changes only Venus's no-profile fallback; it adds no public setting, protocol value, dependency, or Eon/Orbit behavior.

## Evidence and ownership

- Venus currently hardcodes CellMetrics at 9 × 18 logical pixels with nominal font_size 14 in src/render.rs.
- Nova defaults/mars/config.toml selects JetBrains Mono size 16.0 and line-height 1.12.
- Venus fitted_cell_font may reduce font size to preserve the fixed cell width, so changing only the 14 literal is not sufficient proof of the requested result.
- Venus owns native font fitting and grid materialization. Eon owns future product configuration and persistence.

Existing deferred bead ven-terminal-presentation-settings-5y7 owns configurable font family, size, and line-height materialization. Eon bead eon-eonterm-presentation-e4f owns the matching persisted product configuration. This issue does not duplicate or activate those broader settings surfaces.

## Minimum implementation

1. Write one focused metric/font-fit regression that fails on the current 14 px fallback and proves the selected default is actually laid out at 16 logical pixels at 1x, 1.25x, 1.5x, and 2x.
2. Keep the row height at 18 logical pixels. Adjust the default cell width only if the packaged monospace face otherwise forces fitted_cell_font below 16; use the smallest coherent metric change.
3. Reuse CellMetrics, fitted_cell_font, and every existing geometry consumer. Add no setting parser, profile type, module, dependency, font package, or second metric owner.
4. Reprove complete regular/bold/italic descenders, box and Braille alignment, wide/combining cells, cursor/input/selection geometry, resize, IME, accessibility, and canonical scenes.
5. Dogfood installed EonTerm/Eonova beside Nova on the same display scale and obtain user acceptance.

## Acceptance

- Default Venus uses an effective 16 logical-pixel terminal font at 1x and scales consistently at 1.25x, 1.5x, and 2x.
- Default row height remains 18 logical pixels at 1x; no separate line-height setting or approximation layer is added.
- Horizontal fitting does not undo the requested size. Any width change is derived once in CellMetrics and shared by rendering and interaction geometry.
- Complete glyph ink stays within row and pane clips with no overlap; existing typography, cursor, input, resize, IME, accessibility, and scene checks remain green.
- Native side-by-side Eon/EonTerm and Nova dogfood confirms the requested perceived size.
- Update VEN-C1/VEN-C2 proof metadata after an immutable source commit, CHANGELOG for the accepted visual default, and README LOC accounting.
- cargo fmt --check; cargo check --locked; cargo test --locked; cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings; git diff --check all pass.

## Scope boundary and stop conditions

No configurable typography, family change, font packaging, live reload, opacity, geometry preference, renderer replacement, dependency, Orbit/Eon edit, or macOS claim. Stop for user approval if correct 16 px rendering requires a font-package change, a public setting, a new dependency, weakened clipping, or a contract beyond the stated hardening. Rebaseline if another active issue changes src/render.rs or CellMetrics.

Existing CellMetrics and fitted_cell_font remain the single geometry and font-fit owners: 10x18 logical cells, nominal 16 px text, and shared rendering/input/resize/IME/accessibility metrics. Rejected settings, font-package or dependency changes, a second metric owner, weakened clipping, and renderer replacement. Dependency footprint unchanged; Rust diff is +48/-18 across the existing renderer and host regression surfaces. Exact checks: cargo fmt --check; cargo check --locked; cargo test --locked; cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings; git diff --check. Native isolated EonTerm with exact packaged Fontconfig passed, and user visual acceptance was received 2026-08-12. Remaining limits: configurable typography stays deferred; fractional/HiDPI native compositor quality and macOS remain unproved.

title: Modularize Venus native host behind a thin main
description:
## Contract routing

This planning container reorganizes Venus internal Rust ownership without changing any current contract: VEN-C1 through VEN-C4, VEN-C7 through VEN-C11, and VEN-C13 through VEN-C16. It preserves canonical ORBS v4 at Orbit proof `7f067b30e97d0b4787a7c6c0bbe3dd8a80a61c2c`, EONW v1 at Eon proof `4af395aea06c230ee6b18cf0755ae25915c0b88d`, and Linux native-Wayland/Vulkan-only VEN-C16 at Venus proof `e033efadf023492ae02eb1e9036de98ad93d2f98`. This is an internal ownership move, not a contract, protocol, platform, or packaging change.

## Current source map

At accepted edge `fa96d8159511019f273b1cc32cf9e8661cab0d78`, `src/main.rs` is 2,411 lines:

- Launch values and validation are `DEFAULT_CURSOR_TAIL` and `USAGE` at lines 52-60, `LaunchArguments`, argument parsing, cursor-color parsing, and default socket selection at lines 1541-1653 and 1674-1685, with the focused launch test at lines 1734-1900.
- The concrete native host is `OrbitRetry`, presentation/window/application state, `UserEvent`, `Application`, `ApplicationHandler`, and directly coupled host helpers at lines 62-1524.
- Supervised presentation-control mechanics are at lines 1655-1672 and their focused test is at lines 1961-1975; they emit application-owned `UserEvent` values.
- Executable orchestration is at lines 1526-1538.

These line anchors document the current baseline; named owners and behavior govern if lines drift.

## Selected ownership and sequence

1. `ven-12v.1` extracts CLI values, validation, default socket/color policy, and the private supervision activation decision to `src/launch.rs`. It does not move the stdin reader or winit event routing.
2. `ven-12v.2` extracts the concrete winit application, event loop, native host helpers, and presentation-control mechanics to `src/application.rs`, consuming the validated launch value.
3. `src/main.rs` retains only module declarations, the crate result boundary, Linux-only compile guard, argument collection, and one call composing launch with application run.

Presentation-control mechanics stay with the application because they emit `UserEvent::Present` and `UserEvent::Exit`. Putting them in launch would require a reverse dependency or a second command abstraction. Keep one concrete application and one concrete validated launch value.

## Scope

In scope:
- the dependency-ordered child issues
- moving existing behavior and directly coupled tests to the two concrete owners
- preserving all arguments, environment semantics, defaults, errors, native event ordering, clipboard behavior, protocol bytes, rendering, input, accessibility, and lifecycle
- updating module declarations, internal visibility, proof metadata, and README LOC only as required by the moves

Out of scope:
- behavior changes, new contracts, public modules, dependencies, platform work, Eon or Orbit edits, and packaging
- opportunistic Linux-only cleanup unrelated to the move
- splitting `render.rs` or another established subsystem solely by size
- traits, factories, service containers, event buses, command adapters, or compatibility layers

## Success criteria

- `launch.rs` solely owns validated startup values and supervision selection.
- `application.rs` solely owns native application/window state, winit event composition, and presentation-control mechanics.
- Existing subsystem modules remain authoritative; neither new module copies their policy.
- `main.rs` is a thin executable composition boundary.
- Each child closes against an immutable source commit and the final sequence passes one complete unchanged-candidate Rust proof plus bounded native Wayland and absent-Wayland outer observations. Eon owns any later Nix/profile/package acceptance; this repository does not claim that proof.

## Reference gate

Required before each child: current `AGENTS.md`, this batch, affected VEN contracts, exact current `src/main.rs` and tests, and the accepted ORBS/EONW revisions above. Exact winit `fb45fbf901fbe70cc9a877b5d651d0b60c206b08` is required for the application child because it defines the event-loop owner. Monstar `71e4babde8e47e0739abd610f2afe202c8e99c00` remains comparison-only and is explicitly rejected as thin-main, PTY, terminal, renderer, or application-owner authority. No crate gate is expected.

## Stop conditions

Stop if a split changes observable behavior, requires a public surface or dependency, duplicates an existing subsystem owner, weakens VEN-C16, or only improves a line-count metric.
notes: Completed by accepted child source proofs `bab89d1a31bdb7a6a5985f12443f1ace3b0d7f18` and `8e506a247af7ce031798e198e691ca64671b5c27`, with proof metadata through `c0a1813b54daecda8fe9f1d085edd289eddbc301`. Fresh-eyes and ruthless isomorphic simplification review found no source correction that clears the ownership and behavior-preservation gates. The final 19-line main, private launch owner, private application owner, complete locked Rust proof, and bounded native observations satisfy every success criterion.

## Scope

## Acceptance criteria

## Reference gate and verification

title: Reduce Venus sustained complete-frame CPU below the acceptance ceiling
description:
## Why

Orbit acceptance Bead orb-bi4.5.4 found one confirmed pre-graduation no-go at Orbit 847cab1ca37495c5cd45454623bd81909b488564 and Venus 8149002c7275a00db1c08fded171e09f249dd977. Release builds at a 929x976 window and authoritative 100x52 grid ran timeout 20s sh -c "while :; do seq 1 20000; done". Combined Orbit plus Venus CPU p95 was 240 percent, above the predeclared 200 percent ceiling. A same-shape attribution sample measured Orbit p95 101 percent and Venus p95 141 percent, making Venus the larger process-level cost. RSS and final convergence passed: 8.2 MiB growth and 116 ms after output quiesced.

Effort: M. Risk: MED. Confidence: HIGH that Venus owns the larger observed share; the internal limiting stage is not yet identified.

## Evidence

- src/model.rs:141-144 materializes every accepted protocol frame into a fresh Scene.
- src/scene.rs:104-146 clones the complete frame into Venus draw rows and cells.
- src/main.rs:113-170 applies every server message, refreshes accessibility and window state, and requests redraw.
- src/render.rs:302-408 prepares text, records a complete render pass, submits, and presents.
- src/render.rs:411-434 rebuilds all scene text and rectangles whenever the revision changes.
- orb-bi4.5.4 records exact revisions, environment, ceilings, workload, and process-level measurements.

## Scope

In scope:
- Venus-owned complete-frame materialization, scene rebuild, glyph preparation, and presentation costs.
- Private, bounded profiling sufficient to identify the dominant Venus stage.
- The smallest Venus-only correction that brings the accepted complete-frame path below the existing envelope.
- Preserve VEN-C1 through VEN-C4 and canonical ORBS v1.

Out of scope:
- Orbit code, tests, manifests, or ownership.
- A protocol revision, delta schema, dirty-row extraction, snapshot-plus-row-patch, public trace, alternate backend, or second terminal authority.
- History, ordered effects, graphics-resource expansion, remote transport, macOS support, or persistence.
- A direct crate unless a repository Crate gate selects it.

## Implementation Notes

1. Reproduce the exact release workload and segment Venus CPU among Scene::from_frame, refresh and accessibility, rebuild_if_needed, glyph preparation, submission, and presentation without changing the public boundary.
2. Identify the dominant measured stage before choosing code shape.
3. Apply the smallest Venus-owned correction and retain complete canonical frames plus snapshots as the resynchronization fallback.
4. Rerun the exact envelope and every canonical proof check for contracts touched.
5. If the measured cause requires an Orbit or protocol change, stop and report the compatibility decision instead of adding an adapter.

## Verification

- cargo fmt --check should exit 0.
- cargo check --locked should exit 0.
- cargo test --locked should exit 0.
- cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings should exit 0.
- The orb-bi4.5.4 sustained-output condition should report combined CPU p95 <= 200 percent, RSS <= 192 MiB, RSS growth <= 32 MiB, and final convergence <= 1 second.
- Shell, Neovim, Yazi, resize, and reattachment observations should preserve their accepted results.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if the complete-frame flow has drifted materially from the cited revision.
- Stop if a correction requires changing ORBS v1, Orbit ownership, or another repository.
- Stop before adding a dependency, public instrumentation surface, dirty-row extraction, or patch protocol without the required gate and explicit user choice.
- Stop if the exact workload cannot reproduce the result; record the negative result rather than optimizing a guess.

## Maintenance Notes

This Bead hardens VEN-C1 and must preserve VEN-C2, VEN-C3, and VEN-C4. It consumes compatible ORB-C1 through ORB-C7 proofs through Orbit 847cab1. Complete frames remain accepted unless measured evidence and a separate user decision change the boundary.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The exact orb-bi4.5.4 release workload is reproducible and attributes the dominant Venus CPU stage with observed data.
2. A Venus-only correction brings combined Orbit plus Venus CPU p95 to <= 200 percent at 929x976 and 100x52 while RSS remains <= 192 MiB, growth <= 32 MiB, and final convergence <= 1 second.
3. VEN-C1 is hardened and VEN-C2 through VEN-C4 remain behaviorally preserved; canonical checks pass on the resulting exact revision.
4. ORBS v1, complete canonical frames, snapshot resynchronization, Orbit ownership, and the one-client boundary do not change.
5. No direct crate, public trace, dirty-row extraction, snapshot-plus-row-patch, adapter, or cross-repository change is introduced without its required gate and explicit user choice.
notes: Accepted state: Venus source proof 8929c9f9d151641a343813ddeb6005cb9c771286 and proof metadata cea6b00e122968fa5bd3f92ffb6b9d8bf54c2b4c harden VEN-C1 and preserve VEN-C2 through VEN-C4 against Orbit runtime 847cab1ca37495c5cd45454623bd81909b488564 and unchanged canonical protocol c905bf9610581747f1b07565814b501ca66cfaa6. Venus keeps one bounded native event queue. Complete frames are replaced across ordered Accepted acknowledgements only when the queued candidate is strictly newer than every previously delivered or queued frame and the incoming frame is strictly newer again; otherwise original order reaches FrameReducer, which remains the sole revision validator. Failures, invalid data, connection loss, and other semantic barriers retain ordering and first-cause behavior. ASCII uses basic shaping; non-ASCII retains advanced shaping. Exact Xwayland acceptance at 929x976 and 100x52 measured active combined CPU p95 167 percent, Orbit maximum 101 percent, Venus maximum 67 percent, peak combined RSS about 55.3 MiB, and 13.6 ms final convergence. Fifty fullscreen cycles returned coherently to 929x976 within 500 ms, and current state reattached in 122 ms while Orbit and its PTY survived client loss. Shell, Unicode, Neovim, and Yazi evidence remains preserved. Simplification retained one strong frame-reduction test for message barriers, delivered high-water, and non-increasing revisions. Container replacement, derived frame counting, notifier inlining, and batch refresh were rejected because they increased code or runtime work, moved rather than removed the concurrency concept, or risked observable accessibility/failure behavior. No protocol, dependency, public trace, Orbit, or cross-repository change was introduced. Platform disposition: isolated existing native-render dependency; no new macOS blocker. Material constraints remain: redraw cadence alone failed, a 33 ms scheduler remained above the ceiling, Accepted cannot be a coalescing barrier during resize storms, and reduction must never hide a revision failure.

title: Provide native history scrolling, selection, and copy
description:
Contract routing:
- Creates VEN-C7 when implementation is explicitly activated.
- Consumes ORB-C8 at `840a67c0cb32b334ed54888321d5ca77e58117b0` and ORB-C9 plus the breaking ORBS v2 replacement at `9d6d2bb37f20ab4ad9e186c7bc715eabef43e757`.
- Preserves VEN-C1 through VEN-C4 and keeps Orbit as the sole terminal, retained-history, viewport, selection, selected-presentation, and copied-text authority.
- Planning this Bead changes no product contract, protocol, manifest, or runtime behavior.

Goal:
Prove the minimum useful native-terminal interaction in Venus against the exact accepted Orbit owner. Venus captures native gestures, maps them to the last accepted complete frame, presents Orbit-authored selection, and performs the explicit native clipboard side effect. It does not cache or reconstruct terminal history.

Accepted compatibility order:
1. Orbit has proved ORBS v2 and ORB-C9 at `9d6d2bb37f20ab4ad9e186c7bc715eabef43e757`.
2. After Orbit `orb-j0m.5` closes, activate this Bead as the next single implementation frontier.
3. Update the exact `orbit-protocol` pin from the ORBS v1 consumer revision `c905bf9610581747f1b07565814b501ca66cfaa6` to the accepted Orbit proof.
4. Prove Venus, then let Orbit `orb-j0m.4` accept the real pair.

This is a breaking owner-to-consumer update. There is no ORBS v1 adapter, dual-version support, feature probe, compatibility window, second decoder, or handwritten schema.

Implementation shape:
- Wheel and trackpad input use the existing canonical semantic mouse message. Venus owns only bounded native scroll normalization: line deltas accumulate in line units, while pixel deltas normalize against the current rendered cell dimensions, and either source emits only whole semantic wheel steps. It keeps at most a sub-step remainder, drops non-finite input, caps emissions per native event, and clears residual state on focus loss, scale or geometry change, and reconnect. Orbit alone resolves authoritative application mouse tracking, DEC 1007 alternate scroll, primary-history viewport movement, clamping, no-op framing, and byte-producing-key return to live.
- Pointer gestures are mapped against the last accepted complete-frame revision and current viewport cells. Venus sends canonical ORBS v2 Begin, Update, Finish, and Copy actions in order.
- Orbit-authored complete frames remain the only source of cells, selected styling, cursor, title, and reconnect state. Venus keeps only transient native gesture state and the accepted frame required to render and hit-test it.
- Orbit returns exact bounded CopiedText only after an explicit Copy action. Venus writes that result to the native clipboard and never extracts terminal text from rendered cells.
- A non-selection terminal mutation cancels active selection. After Finish, terminal output, resize or reflow, and active-screen transitions clear selected presentation without changing the frozen copy candidate. A newer valid Begin, client loss, or exit clears it.
- Accessibility derives viewport and selection from the same accepted complete frame and reports interaction failures without inventing missing terminal state.

Explicit non-owners:
Venus has no history page cache, epoch, stable row anchor, row token, page request, gap repair, cache eviction, client-owned viewport, client-owned terminal selection content, or text reconstruction. Search, semantic command regions, richer word/line/rectangle selection, drag autoscroll, auto-copy, rich clipboard formats, terminal clipboard-write effects, restart persistence, tabs, panes, and workspace topology remain outside this Bead.

References before code:
- Required: exact Orbit ORB-C8/ORB-C9 proof and canonical ORBS v2 package; current Venus Scene, renderer, input, accessibility, lifecycle, and failure owners; exact winit and AccessKit surfaces already selected by the repository; and the repository's native clipboard path or a triggered native-platform decision.
- Comparison only: one mature native terminal interaction at an exact revision, limited to gesture precedence, accessibility, and clipboard UX.
- Rejected scope: client-side VT parsing, page caches, stable anchors, replay protocols, copied terminal implementations, and compatibility adapters.

Cheapest proof:
Use deterministic protocol-faithful tests against the exact canonical Orbit package for scroll-delta normalization, gesture-to-cell mapping, action ordering, stale revision rejection, authoritative selected frames, frozen copy behavior, mouse-mode precedence, reconnect, and bounded failure. Then dogfood the real Linux Orbit/Venus pair through shell history, rapid wheel movement, key return to live, wrapped Unicode and wide graphemes, forward and reverse selection, explicit copy, resize/reflow, alternate-screen Neovim and Yazi, mouse mode, DEC 1007, detach, reattach, client loss, oversized copy, and stopped-reader pressure.

Acceptance:
1. VEN-C7 and the exact ORB-C8/ORB-C9 proof revisions are indexed before implementation; the manifest pins the accepted ORBS v2 `orbit-protocol` revision.
2. Native wheel and trackpad deltas become a bounded count of canonical semantic wheel steps: fractional line movement accumulates in line units, sub-cell pixel movement accumulates against current cell dimensions, emission is capped, and residual state resets at native lifecycle boundaries. The resulting steps traverse Orbit-owned retained history and return to live without client history state or duplicate PTY bytes.
3. Application mouse reporting and DEC 1007 behavior remain Orbit-owned and take correct precedence over host scrolling.
4. Selection begins only against the exact last accepted complete-frame revision; stale revisions, invalid cells, invalid phase order, oversized work, and pressure fail deterministically without partial client state.
5. Venus renders authoritative selected styling from complete frames and never reparses or mirrors terminal text.
6. Explicit Copy places only Orbit-returned bounded CopiedText on the native clipboard. Output, resize/reflow, and screen transitions preserve the finished frozen candidate exactly as ORB-C9 specifies.
7. Resize/reflow, alternate-screen transitions, mutation cancellation, detach/reattach, client loss, and reconnect converge without a cache, stable-anchor, or second terminal owner.
8. Accessibility exposes the same accepted viewport, selected styling, copy success or failure, and reconnect state used visually.
9. Deterministic checks and real Linux dogfood cover the stated boundary; canonical locked Rust checks and git diff checking pass.
10. Closure records exact Orbit and Venus revisions, VEN-C and ORB-C IDs, breaking update order, commands, environment, bounds, latency, memory, queued output, dependency disposition, portability, LOC, and remaining limitations.
11. Orbit `orb-j0m.4` can accept the exact real pair for Eon dogfood without an adapter or client-side compensation.

Dependency decision:
No dependency is selected. Reuse the accepted Venus stack and native platform facilities. Any new crate or architecture-shaping native choice requires the repository gate and user approval.

Portability disposition:
Neutral gesture and protocol flow with clipboard and window-system effects isolated at existing platform seams. Linux is the proof target; macOS remains credible but unproved.

External gate:
This is the sole Venus consumer Bead for the pre-graduation native-interaction baseline. Keep it deferred until Orbit `orb-j0m.5` closes, then activate it as the next single implementation frontier. Orbit `orb-j0m.4` and Eon dogfood wait for the accepted VEN-C7 proof.

Capability and contract: Venus must place only the bounded UTF-8 ServerMessage::CopiedText returned by accepted ORBS v2 onto the native default clipboard, report failure without losing the terminal scene, and keep the Linux clipboard owner alive while the process runs. Venus does not read the clipboard for this feature, generate copy text, expose image or rich formats, or take terminal ownership.

Existing orbit-protocol dependency: update the current exact Git pin c905bf9610581747f1b07565814b501ca66cfaa6 to accepted Orbit proof 9d6d2bb37f20ab4ad9e186c7bc715eabef43e757. Probe result: the commit exists and is fully inspectable in the sibling Eon Sessions repository, but that edge branch is three commits ahead of origin and Cargo cannot fetch 9d6d2bb from the configured Git URL. The exact scratch cargo check failed at dependency fetch with revision not found. The remote commit must be published before a locked Venus proof can exist; no local-path or compatibility substitute is accepted.

Native clipboard candidates:

1. Standard library, winit 0.30.13, and existing dependency graph: rejected because none owns a native clipboard write. External wl-copy, xclip, or xsel commands are rejected as undeclared runtime and process-lifetime dependencies with inconsistent X11, Wayland, Nix, and macOS behavior. Handwritten X11, Wayland, and AppKit integration is rejected because it would add unsafe and substantial platform ownership beneath a forbid-unsafe crate for one bounded text operation.

2. arboard 3.6.1, exact crates.io release, MIT OR Apache-2.0, recommended with default features disabled and wayland-data-control enabled. It owns set_text, X11 fallback, Wayland data-control, macOS AppKit, clipboard hosting, and typed failure. A scratch locked cargo check passed with the existing Venus stack. The all-target lock adds 12 packages: arboard 3.6.1, wl-clipboard-rs 0.9.3, os_pipe 1.2.3, tree_magic_mini 3.2.2, nom 8.0.0, petgraph 0.8.3, fixedbitset 0.5.7, hashbrown 0.15.5, foldhash 0.1.5, clipboard-win 5.4.1, error-code 3.3.2, and objc2-app-kit 0.3.2. Active Linux reuses the existing Wayland, x11rb, parking_lot, log, percent-encoding, and Rust build stack; it adds no separately managed native library or Nix package. Image support is disabled. Expected Venus-owned cost is one retained Clipboard field and one bounded write/error path, about 15 to 25 handwritten lines; exact LOC will be recorded after implementation. Upgrade burden is one direct version and feature selection. Removal or replacement is isolated to that field and write path.

Linux behavior: arboard first attempts the optional Wayland data-control protocol and falls back to X11. This covers the accepted Linux/Xwayland slice and wlroots-style data-control compositors; native Wayland environments without data-control and without Xwayland may reject initialization and remain an explicit unproved platform gap. macOS feasibility is credible through its native AppKit backend but remains unproved. Input and accessibility ownership are unchanged; success and failure are exposed through the existing Venus status and AccessKit alert path. A future browser client would replace this isolated native effect with the browser clipboard API rather than carry arboard across the boundary.

3. copypasta 0.10.2, exact crates.io release, MIT OR Apache-2.0: rejected. Its generic Unix ClipboardContext is X11-only; correct Wayland use requires selecting a separate provider from a raw display pointer through an unsafe constructor, which conflicts with the repository forbid-unsafe boundary and adds Venus-owned runtime dispatch. Alacritty uses that larger integration because it already owns those platform handles; Venus does not.

Security, data, and proof: pass at most the canonical 1 MiB ORBS v2 CopiedText directly to set_text, enable no reads or image formats, retain no second text copy, and surface initialization or write failure. First crate check after approval is locked compile against the published 9d6d2bb pin; focused model and clipboard-side-effect checks follow. title: Make Eon workspace navigation direct and pane headers visible
description:
## Contract routing

Change and harden VEN-C8 under the user-approved 2026-08-09 contract. In Eon workspace mode, Alt+H/L selects the previous/next tab, Alt+K/J selects the previous/next pane, Alt+M creates one pane, and Ctrl+T creates one tab through existing EONW semantic actions. Creation ignores key repeat; direct traversal may repeat. Standalone Venus passes these keys to Orbit unchanged. F6/arrow/Escape focus navigation remains available.

Every pane in the active tab has one visible ordered header whenever the headers plus a useful terminal body fit. Exactly the selected pane exposes its terminal body immediately after its header. When they do not fit, bounded pane scrolling preserves the existing overflow mechanism and reveals the selected pane without hiding otherwise fitting siblings.

Important failures: unavailable workspace transport reports the existing bounded failure and preserves accepted state; rejected Eon actions preserve the accepted scene; tiny windows remain bounded; no shortcut creates duplicate requests from key repeat.

Preserve VEN-C1 through VEN-C4 and VEN-C7, Orbit ownership, Eon topology/action ownership, the exact EONW schema, accessibility order/actions, pointer behavior, and one expanded terminal. No new dependency, protocol, configuration surface, split model, or module.

## Evidence and references

Required before code: AGENTS.md, this Bead, VEN-C8 and its proof, current workspace scene/render/input/application owners and tests, exact Eon/EONW producer proof 4af395aea06c230ee6b18cf0755ae25915c0b88d, exact Orbit/ORBS proof 9d6d2bb37f20ab4ad9e186c7bc715eabef43e757, and the user-named Nova project at an exact commit for shortcut behavior only. Existing Canario/Rio 3e41b8b19a1cad9cd9bdfc8f7900cf61ce5a9098 remains comparison-only for accordion geometry. Reuse no reference source.

## Acceptance

A deterministic failing-then-passing check proves all four direct directions, the two creation actions, modifier gating, creation repeat suppression, standalone passthrough, and retained F6 navigation. Accordion checks prove two and three pane headers are simultaneously visible around the selected expanded body at ordinary sizes, selected-body adjacency, bounded tiny/overflow geometry, hit testing, and stable order. Accessibility derives the same order. Locked Rust format, check, tests, clippy, git diff check, and focused native Linux dogfood pass. README, CHANGELOG, contract proof state, agent policy if affected, and LOC are accurate. No commit, push, Eon pin, runtime replacement, or distribution is included without separate user direction.

title: Accept Orbit continuous-output scrollback in Venus
description:
## Outcome and contract routing

Consumer: one Venus terminal user, including a Venus surface launched by Eon.

Trigger: Orbit publishes an accepted exact ORB-C8 proof for orb-keep-scrollback-usable-during-output-rgi, and Venus previews or commits retained-history movement while terminal output continues to advance frames.

Result: Venus consumes that exact compatible Orbit revision and preserves its existing fractional, kinetic, wheel, selection, and rendering behavior while the user can enter and continue scrollback during continuous TUI output. The stale preview/scroll notices from the dogfood report do not appear, the gesture is not starved, and an entered viewport remains pinned as output continues.

This hardens VEN-C7 and consumes the new exact ORB-C8 proof. Preserve every other VEN-C contract. If Orbit changes ORBS bytes or version, stop before consumer edits and require an explicitly approved breaking rollout; this Bead assumes unchanged ORBS v10.

## Ownership and sequencing

Orbit remains the sole terminal, history, viewport, routing, revision, and PTY owner. Venus owns native input accumulation, one in-flight scroll batch, fractional/kinetic presentation, rendering, and truthful notices. Venus must not compensate with failure-detail string matching, a blind retry loop, cached history, or a second revision policy.

Sequence:
1. orb-keep-scrollback-usable-during-output-rgi proves the producer and records the exact compatible revision.
2. This Bead pins that revision, proves the current Venus interaction path against it, and publishes one exact consumer revision.
3. Eon adoption `eon-adopt-continuous-output-scrollback-umf` selects the accepted Orbit/Venus pair and refreshes the installed profile.

Status is deferred until the Orbit proof exists. Native Linux Wayland remains the only product surface.

## Evidence

Current application.rs sends PreviewVertical and ScrollVertical from the last presented revision, allows one batch in flight, exposes Orbit InvalidInput through the model, and resets terminal scrolling after a server failure. Current VEN-C7 treats stale presentation as a cancellation. The Orbit defect makes that valid client behavior user-visible under continuous output.

The Orbit lifecycle proof already establishes that a successfully entered authoritative viewport stays pinned across later PTY output. This consumer slice should need no new terminal or freeze state.

## Scope boundary

In scope: exact Orbit source/protocol pin, VEN-C7 contract/proof refresh, focused model/application/transport coverage needed for the compatible producer, native dogfood, documentation, changelog after acceptance, and LOC accounting.

Out of scope: Eon component/profile updates, client-owned history, generic retry, string matching on failure details, a new protocol version, gesture redesign, public tuning, new renderer/input module, dependencies, or platform expansion.

## Acceptance Criteria

The structured acceptance_criteria field is authoritative. Venus must accept the exact compatible Orbit proof, retain its existing scroll/input/render owners, pass focused and native continuous-output checks, and publish one exact consumer revision without a retry workaround.
design:
1. Consume accepted Orbit source a65e199e16e97330175e314cacf791fa00f53069, which preserves ORBS v10 and ORBF v1 while hardening ORB-C7/C8 queue admission.
2. Update only the existing exact orbit-protocol manifest/lock and durable current identities. Add no adapter, dual protocol, retry, or client behavior.
3. Prove the unchanged compatible-frame and lagging-batch owners through their existing focused regressions and the full locked Venus suite. Any required Venus runtime change returns the gap to Orbit.
4. Preserve one pending preview, one in-flight batch, frame ordering, fractional and kinetic input, selection gating, pressure, and truthful failures.
5. Reuse the accepted optimized native evidence only for unchanged Venus client behavior. The exact corrected Orbit/Venus pair receives the higher-boundary installed native pressure observation in downstream Eon adoption.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Every authoritative current Orbit identity resolves to accepted source a65e199e16e97330175e314cacf791fa00f53069; ORBS v10, ORBF v1, orbit-protocol source, dependency set, and bytes remain unchanged.
2. Existing deterministic checks prove compatible advancing frames retain bounded previews and lagging signed batches complete without duplicate requests, lost distance, invented rows, or stale notices.

5. Venus adds no failure-string match, blind retry, history cache, second terminal/revision owner, dependency, protocol value, or platform surface.
6. VEN-C7, current Orbit identities, README LOC, locked Rust checks, Clippy, Bead state, and diff agree at one immutable Venus proof revision; changelog records the accepted pin without claiming Eon.
7. Closure names downstream Eon adoption eon-adopt-continuous-output-scrollback-umf and does not claim the installed Eon profile changed.

title: Accept Venus on Apple Silicon with Orbit
description:
## Outcome and contract

Accept the complete native Venus Apple Silicon slice against exact Orbit authority and hand a proof-bearing Venus revision to Eon composition.

- Consumer: standalone Venus diagnostics and the existing Eon Apple Silicon composition epic.
- Trigger: launch the final aarch64-darwin Venus candidate against accepted native Orbit, and exercise its workspace client with the exact accepted Eon workspace protocol.
- Result: one native Venus process renders and controls the authoritative Orbit Session through the shared model/scene/renderer/action path, preserves workspace and popup behavior through an exact protocol substitute, survives reconnect and owned failures, and leaves a complete VEN-C16 proof record for Eon to consume.
- Important failures: identity mismatch, attach/reconnect loss, stale frames, Orbit exit, Venus exit, invalid workspace state, renderer recovery, clipboard/input/accessibility/presentation regression, or missing proof fails explicitly without moving PTY, workspace, lifecycle, or composition ownership into Venus.

This is the final Venus acceptance child. It may mark the Apple Silicon portion of VEN-C16 Proven only after the preceding four children and this exact native dogfood are accepted. It changes no Eon contract and does not prove full Eon on macOS.

## Ownership and sequencing

Require accepted opaque host, interaction/pasteboard, accessibility/lifecycle/identity, and Metal transparency/blur children at exact revisions. Retain Orbit ORB-C14 native source 0233f4d34b294a50c5bc7f373859cf4ec04d2414 as the scoped historical baseline. At resumption, select the exact accepted Orbit candidate and canonical orbit-protocol package, record their actual ORBF/ORBS versions, and identify native proof still valid for unchanged behavior versus changes requiring fresh proof. The earlier ORBS v11 planning value is not a pin requirement; the current Linux consumer is on ORBS v13. Do not infer native acceptance of a changed wire/runtime from the historical baseline alone. Orbit owns PTY, Session, terminal state, copied text, and attachment. Venus owns native presentation and semantic interaction. Eon owns component graph, Nix composition, managed tools, launch/update policy, and full-product dogfood.

Use the exact canonical eon-workspace-protocol package owned by Eon Runtime with fixtures or a bounded substitute to prove Venus-owned tabs, panes, shared popups, shortcut viewer, picker projection, failure handling, and caller inputs. Do not require an unproved full Eon macOS build before Venus can close; that would create a cycle. After acceptance, update the external handoff to eon-prove-full-eon-apple-silicon-macos-t8o, which owns Nix packaging and complete product proof.

## Reference gate

Read this bead and parent, every preceding child and accepted proof, complete current VEN-C contract index and touched checks, accepted ORB-C14 contracts/proof and exact current protocol source, exact Eon workspace protocol/fixtures, current Venus transport/model/application/render/accessibility/launch owners, and relevant docs/REFERENCES.md and docs/CRATES.md routes. Inspect official macOS behavior only for a concrete unresolved native failure from the dogfood. Reuse exact preceding reference decisions; do not repeat them or widen claims. Record exact candidate identities, dirty state, preserved contracts, unresolved limitations, and first outermost check.

## Scope and verification

In scope: exact native Orbit launch/attach/reconnect/loss; authoritative rendering, input, resize, selection/copy/paste, links, accessibility, tabs/panes/popups, shortcut viewer, configured presentation, surface recovery, Venus close/quit with Orbit survival, workspace-protocol failure UX, Linux regression proof, VEN-C16 evidence/status, changelog and LOC, and the Eon handoff identity.

Out of scope: modifying Eon composition or Orbit behavior; Nix package graph; Helix/Yazi/Ratconfig availability; installer, signing, notarization, Homebrew, direct bundles, public release, Intel macOS, remote transport, another protocol, compatibility window, or broader platform support.

## Acceptance Criteria

Cheapest proof of the native outcome, preserving the scope of preceding accepted owner checks:

1. Run the complete locked Venus Rust route once on the unchanged final source for Linux and the accepted Apple target; reuse lower proof already subsumed by exact native observations.
2. On real Apple Silicon, exercise one retained Orbit Session through launch, authoritative Unicode output, keyboard/IME/pointer/trackpad, resize/scale, history selection and copy/paste, link Open/Copy, accessibility actions, opacity values and truthful blur behavior, surface recovery, detach/reconnect, Orbit loss, Venus close/quit, and reattachment.
3. Exercise exact workspace protocol state for tabs, panes, shared popups, shortcut viewer, picker projection, caller identity, malformed/lost workspace input, and recovery without claiming Eon composition.
4. Record exact source, Orbit/protocol revisions, hardware, macOS/Rust identities, commands, artifacts, observations, failures, limits, dependency/LOC delta, proof phase, and Eon handoff. Update docs/CONTRACTS.md only from the accepted proof-bearing source commit.

If native acceptance needs unavailable interactive hardware, user action, a change in Orbit/Eon ownership, Nix composition, or a new dependency, stop and ask the user. Do not substitute compilation, an opaque screenshot, or full-Eon assumptions for this proof.
