- Trigger and user evidence: accepted Venus kinetic source f13dc7ac2e9a24c5cff5bb7e618436783ec76dbf and installed Eon dogfood at b44d968e38474fc5b75a41bcde2ad750da0d1e3e established responsive pixel tracking, bounded fling, immediate interruption, discrete wheel behavior, and stable lifecycle on supported COSMIC native Wayland. The user accepted scrolling as really good. Strong-fling power remains a non-blocking tuning observation, not a reproduced input-fidelity defect. No stationary-fingers continuation or high-resolution-wheel loss was reproduced.
- Adopted: keep winit 0.30.13 pinned to chiyuki0325/winit-0.30 commit fb45fbf901fbe70cc9a877b5d651d0b60c206b08. Its Wayland path maps discrete axes to LineDelta, continuous axes to PixelDelta, and available stop to Ended; it exposes neither AxisSource nor hardware event time. The fork commit changes only the accepted ext-background-effect blur path, not scrolling. Cargo resolves one winit shared by Venus and accesskit_winit 0.33.2.
- Current candidate scan: upstream master remains 874a1e31f194d11313c1ac133b28037b99db3e19. Winit 0.31.0-beta.2 is a prerelease at f98ccf8efc5e3f6dd3e31b705178603f6556d316; it preserves the line/pixel/phase model and adds fractional axis_value120 line deltas, but its public event API does not include HoldGesture. Master adds Wayland HoldGesture and the broader pointer-source overhaul, but MouseWheel still carries no AxisSource or hardware timestamp and Wayland device_id remains None. Exact source remains Apache-2.0.
- Rejected: no backport because there is no bounded reproduced defect to patch; no stable upgrade because no accepted stable release supersedes the selected 0.30.13 behavior and blur requirement; no beta or unreleased pin because optional hold/value120 capability does not justify prerelease API, AccessKit compatibility, lock, native, and regression cost without a hardware gap.
- Replacement cost if reopened: one exact winit source and lock change, AccessKit shared-version compatibility, accepted blur mechanism, exhaustive native event matches, full locked Rust checks, and installed Wayland dogfood.
- Cheapest falsifier: reproduce either continued kinetic motion while fingers remain stationary or lost fractional movement from a high-resolution discrete wheel, capture the exact winit delta and phase sequence, and show that beta/stable behavior fixes it without weakening blur, AccessKit, or lifecycle proof. Otherwise the exact pin stays selected.

title: Deliver macOS input, pasteboard, and link actions
description:
## Outcome and contract

Complete the native macOS interaction seams without branching Venus semantic policy.

- Consumer: a person using an opaque aarch64-darwin Venus window after the AppKit/Metal foundation is accepted.
- Trigger: keyboard, IME, pointer/trackpad, paste, copy, terminal clipboard-write, or visible-link Open/Copy input.
- Result: macOS conventions become the same existing Venus/Orbit semantic actions; Command shortcuts work where macOS expects them, committed text and pointer phases stay ordered, all Orbit clipboard locations map explicitly to the general macOS pasteboard, and link Open/Copy use bounded native mechanisms.
- Important failures: repeat/modifier confusion, partial IME text, stale pointer geometry, missing/non-text/oversize/invalid UTF-8 pasteboard data, subprocess failure, or opener failure produces the existing bounded notice and never sends partial or invented terminal input.

This advances the interaction portion of VEN-C16 while preserving VEN-C2, VEN-C3, VEN-C7, VEN-C8, VEN-C10, VEN-C13, VEN-C18, and the Linux Ctrl/Wayland behavior. Protocol, InputState, selection, paste-size validation, link validation, model, and renderer remain shared. Native pasteboard and URI-dispatch mechanics stay behind the existing application-level seams.

## Ownership and decision gate

The accepted opaque foundation is required first. Existing input mapping owns physical/logical keys, modifiers, IME, and pointer phases. Existing Application shortcut dispatch owns platform convention before it emits shared semantic actions. Existing read_native_clipboard and write_native_clipboard own native text transfer; one platform-neutral internal destination may express Standard, Selection, or Both, with Linux mapping to wl-clipboard-rs and macOS mapping all three Orbit locations to the general pasteboard. Existing LinkOpener owns URI process lifetime; Linux keeps gio and macOS needs one native dispatcher.

Before selecting pasteboard code, test standard macOS pbcopy/pbpaste on the real host for Unicode, empty/non-text data, bounded reads, GUI-launch environment, exit status, and fixed executable availability. Compare: no dependency via platform commands; already-present APIs; maintained arboard with default features disabled; and direct AppKit bindings. Prefer the standard-library subprocess path only if it passes the contract. Direct unsafe AppKit ownership is rejected by the repository unsafe-code boundary; wl-clipboard-rs is not a macOS implementation. Any crate, native binding, helper service, entitlement, or fork change triggers the dependency gate and user approval.

Before selecting link dispatch, inspect official macOS open/NSWorkspace behavior and prove exact URI argument and completion semantics. Prefer the native command through std::process if it safely accepts one validated URI and returns after dispatch. Do not own the browser lifetime, URL discovery, templates, shell parsing, or another launcher.

## Reference gate

Read this bead and parent, the accepted foundation proof, all touched Venus contracts/checks, current input/application/clipboard/link owners, docs/REFERENCES.md and docs/CRATES.md, exact winit macOS keyboard/IME/pointer event behavior, official Apple pasteboard and URI-opening behavior, and the accepted Orbit clipboard/location and input contracts. Rio and Ghostty are comparison-only for exact macOS shortcut/IME/pointer questions. Record exact identities, adopted and rejected mechanisms, and the first checks before code.

## Scope and verification

In scope: Command equivalents for current Venus shortcuts, shared modifier translation, committed IME text, pointer/trackpad button/motion/scroll phases, macOS general-pasteboard read/write and location collapse, visible hyperlink Open/Copy, bounded child-process ownership, notices, and cancellation/focus behavior.

Out of scope: configurable keymaps, new shortcuts, primary-selection emulation, rich clipboard formats, drag-and-drop, URL discovery/navigation modes, browser lifetime, VoiceOver proof, application/bundle identity, transparency/blur, Orbit protocol changes, Nix/Eon composition, new dependencies without approval, and a macOS support claim.

Cheapest proof:

1. Deterministic tests show identical semantic actions from Linux Ctrl and macOS Command conventions, committed-only IME, bounded pointer phases, location collapse, exact paste limits/errors, and safe URI dispatch arguments.
2. Linux locked route and current Wayland clipboard/link behavior remain green.
3. Real observation on an exact physical Apple Silicon host, with the chip and macOS build recorded, covers Unicode and empty/non-text/oversize pasteboard cases; Command copy/paste and link Open/Copy; ordinary text, IME, click/drag, trackpad scrolling, focus loss, repeat, and failure notices.
4. No native mechanism leaks into protocol/model/scene/render ownership, and no compatibility or support claim is added.

If standard platform commands cannot satisfy the bounded contract or native input events require a new owner, stop and ask the user before widening the shape.

title: Distinguish GPU device loss from surface loss
description:
## Contract routing

Hardens existing `VEN-C4` bounded client-visible failure behavior and preserves `VEN-C1`, `VEN-C2`, `VEN-C7`, and `VEN-C8`; it adds or changes no product contract. It uses the selected wgpu 30.0.0 device-loss signal and routes failure through prerequisite ven-expose-persistent-renderer-failures-4xj after that Bead proves an independently visible non-GPU diagnostic. Transparent device recreation is not authorized.

Implemented and mechanically verified at source commit `e6326b2578beff0932fe51504935b7296070b0ba`; the closure record retains the exact proof and native-fault limitation.

## Why

Consumer: a local user whose GPU device is reset or otherwise lost while Venus owns a native surface.

Trigger: wgpu reports whole-device loss, possibly alongside `CurrentSurfaceTexture::Lost`.

Result: Venus observes the device-loss state, stops treating it as recoverable by recreating only the surface, and enters the bounded explicit renderer-failure path proved by ven-expose-persistent-renderer-failures-4xj. Ordinary surface-only loss continues to recreate and configure the surface.

Important failure: never report `Recovered` while retaining a lost Device, Queue, pipelines, buffers, and glyph resources; never spin indefinitely on an invalid GPU owner.

Audit `ven-audit-venus-scene-renderer-2db` found this at Venus `4f799fef1c3e10e86d70b708708f7c2702d7aee8`. Impact HIGH. Effort M. Implementation risk MED. Confidence HIGH in the missing required branch; native hardware-fault occurrence was not exercised.

## Evidence

- `src/render.rs:147-168`: Renderer owns Device, Queue, surface, pipelines, buffers, glyph atlas, and text resources together.
- `src/render.rs:384-410`: every `CurrentSurfaceTexture::Lost` recreates only Surface and configures it with the existing Device.
- wgpu 30.0.0 `src/api/surface_texture.rs:44-73`: whole-device loss requires recreating the device and all resources; only surface-only loss permits surface recreation.
- wgpu 30.0.0 `src/api/device.rs:680-686`: `set_device_lost_callback` is the explicit notification owner.
- wgpu 30.0.0 `src/backend/wgpu_core.rs:285-305`: `ErrorType::DeviceLost` is routed through that callback rather than uncaptured-error handling.
- Exact locked wgpu 30.0.0 checksum `6d8f4bd44d92da5270f03409dba9f952dab24f128e05d6a554926101d1bf9114` reports actual loss as `DeviceLostReason::Unknown` and explicit destruction as `Destroyed`. In the selected core backend, a HAL device error invokes the loss callback but `Surface::get_current_texture` returns the API-level `Validation` result, while an ordinary HAL surface loss returns `Lost`; the loss check therefore cannot live only in the `Lost` arm.
- No current Venus owner installs the callback or retains observable device-loss state.
- `src/main.rs:708-748`: `RenderError` stores a GPU-drawn status, invalidates presented input, and updates AccessKit, but a persistent failure cannot render its own sighted diagnostic.
- Host audit `ven-audit-venus-host-lifecycle-8jl` comment 310 proved that visibility gap; prerequisite `ven-expose-persistent-renderer-failures-4xj` owns the non-GPU title/stderr projection.

## Scope

In scope:
- `src/render.rs` observation of device loss, redraw/failure notification, and the decision between surface-only recovery and bounded renderer failure.
- `src/main.rs` only to consume the already-proved failure projection from `ven-expose-persistent-renderer-failures-4xj`; this Bead must not duplicate title, stderr, AccessKit, or diagnostic policy.
- Focused deterministic recovery-decision tests and the cheapest feasible wgpu lifecycle proof.
- `docs/CONTRACTS.md` proof metadata for hardened VEN-C4 and preserved visual/input contracts after a committed source candidate, README LOC scorecard, and CHANGELOG only for accepted visible behavior.

Out of scope:
- Transparent recreation of Device, Queue, pipelines, buffers, glyph atlas, or all renderer resources.
- A general GPU recovery framework, renderer replacement, process supervisor restart, crash reporting, telemetry, new backend, dependency, or macOS support promise.
- Treating all surface loss as fatal.

## Reference and dependency gate

Required before code:
- This Bead; audits `ven-audit-venus-scene-renderer-2db` and `ven-audit-venus-host-lifecycle-8jl`; and completed prerequisite `ven-expose-persistent-renderer-failures-4xj`.
- Current `AGENTS.md`, `docs/CONTRACTS.md`, `docs/REFERENCES.md`, and `docs/CRATES.md`.
- Exact locked wgpu 30.0.0 Device lost callback, `CurrentSurfaceTexture::Lost`, callback delivery, Device polling, and thread/wakeup semantics.
- Current Renderer initialization/render/surface-recovery path and Application renderer-error/presentation invalidation path.

Conditional: exact winit 0.30.13 cross-thread redraw semantics only if the wgpu callback needs to wake an otherwise idle event loop.

Comparison-only: no external renderer is required to classify the selected dependency's loss states.

Rejected: transparent full-device reconstruction, a generic resource factory, backend switch, compatibility layer, or new dependency. No Crate gate is expected; stop before a manifest edit.

Platform disposition: isolated platform dependency. Linux is the proof target; Metal/macOS remains unproved.

## Implementation notes

1. Use TDD for the recovery decision: surface Lost plus no device-loss signal selects current surface recreation; surface Lost plus device loss cannot select surface-only recovery.
2. Install the selected wgpu callback at Device creation and retain one `Arc<AtomicBool>` as Renderer-owned loss state. Treat `DeviceLostReason::Unknown` as real loss, ignore `Destroyed`, discard the callback detail, and emit one fixed owner-authored `RenderError`; the callback string has no declared bound and is not needed to classify recovery.
3. Check retained loss before GPU work, before surface-only recovery, and after submit/present before returning `Presented`. Request redraw through the existing `Arc<Window>` so asynchronous loss reaches the prerequisite `RenderError` path while idle; add no `UserEvent` or second lifecycle owner unless an exact selected-stack check disproves that existing wake path.
4. Preserve normal Outdated, Suboptimal, Timeout, Occluded, and surface-only Lost behavior.
5. Do not reconstruct GPU resources unless the user separately chooses transparent recovery under a contract decision.
6. Follow the source-commit then proof-metadata/closure workflow.

## Acceptance criteria

- Whole-device loss is observable by the Renderer and, once the callback fires, cannot return `PresentOutcome::Presented` or `Recovered` through the stale device or surface-only recreation.
- The prerequisite non-GPU renderer-failure path clears presented input identity, exposes the bounded notice without a successful GPU frame, and remains bounded without redraw or error loops.
- Surface-only Lost still recreates/configures the surface and requests the existing recovery redraw.
- Other `CurrentSurfaceTexture` outcomes remain unchanged.
- Dropping Renderer does not create a false user-visible device-loss failure.
- No GPU resource-rebuild framework, dependency, product contract, or second lifecycle owner is introduced.

## Verification

- A focused deterministic test must prove both device-lost and surface-only recovery decisions.
- Exercise callback/wakeup behavior with the cheapest feasible selected-stack check; explicitly retain the limitation if real GPU reset injection is unavailable.
- `cargo fmt --check`
- `cargo check --locked`
- `cargo test --locked`
- `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `git diff --check`

All commands must exit 0 on the materially unchanged source candidate. Native proof may claim only the surface actually exercised.

## Stop conditions

- Stop if exact wgpu semantics require Device polling or host lifecycle behavior outside the existing Renderer/Application owners.

- Stop before a dependency, manifest edit, renderer/backend redesign, product contract change, or platform framework.

## Maintenance notes

One loss signal and the prerequisite RenderError projection are sufficient. Full transparent recovery is a separate product choice only after measured need. Cheapest falsifier: inject device-lost=true with surface Lost and assert surface-only recovery is impossible.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Inject `DeviceLostReason::Unknown` into the recovery decision, and use the cheapest feasible selected-backend loss trigger if available.
2. Observe that Venus installs no callback, retains no loss state, and schedules no redraw when loss is reported asynchronously; a loss raised during submit/present can therefore leave the current call reporting `Presented` until another unrelated redraw reaches the API-level `Validation` path.
3. Separately inject surface-only `CurrentSurfaceTexture::Lost` and confirm the current recreation path. The candidate must keep that recovery, route `Unknown` through the existing bounded renderer failure before returning `Presented` or `Recovered`, and ignore `Destroyed`.

title: Expose persistent renderer failures without GPU rendering
description:
## Contract routing

Hardens existing VEN-C4 bounded explicit client failure UX and preserves VEN-C1, VEN-C2, VEN-C3, VEN-C7, VEN-C8, VEN-C12 planning, and Orbit-authored terminal title state after recovery. It adds or changes no product contract, dependency, popup surface, crash-reporting policy, or transparent GPU recovery promise.

The prior Eon terminal-child refresh frontier is closed. This issue is open and unclaimed; before claiming, reconfirm that no other implementation owns the active cross-repository frontier.

## Why

Consumers: a local user whose Venus renderer has failed and the local launch/supervision environment that captures process diagnostics.

Trigger: Renderer::render returns a persistent RenderError from glyph preparation, surface recreation/validation, or glyph rendering.

Result: Application immediately projects the existing bounded renderer-failure notice through non-GPU owners: native window title metadata and stderr, while retaining the AccessKit alert and invalidating presented input identity. If rendering later succeeds, Venus restores the authoritative Orbit title through the existing refresh path.

Important failures: the diagnostic must not depend on another successful GPU frame, spin redraws, create a popup, replace application identity, permanently overwrite an Orbit title, expose unbounded backend data, or imply transparent device recovery.

Audits ven-audit-venus-host-lifecycle-8jl and ven-audit-venus-scene-renderer-2db found the ownership gap at Venus 4f799fef1c3e10e86d70b708708f7c2702d7aee8. Impact HIGH. Effort S/M. Implementation risk LOW/MED. Confidence HIGH.

## Evidence

- src/main.rs:708-753 computes status before Renderer::render; on Err it stores render_notice, clears presented_revision, and updates only AccessKit.
- src/main.rs:673-705 makes render_notice the highest-priority status, but that status becomes pixels only through a later successful renderer call.
- src/main.rs:518-546 already owns native title projection and restores either the accepted Orbit scene title or Venus fallback.
- src/render.rs:357-381 can return persistent glyph-atlas preparation failure.
- src/render.rs:400-410 can return surface recreation or validation failure.
- src/render.rs:440-442 can return glyph rendering failure.
- Host audit comment 310 records that a static nonblinking scene can remain stale or blank with no ordinary sighted diagnostic.
- Existing ven-distinguish-device-from-surface-loss-d96 assumes this path is visible; this Bead must prove that prerequisite before device loss routes into it.
- ven-caller-application-identity-dcb explicitly separates native application identity from Orbit-authored window title, so a bounded failure-title override must not mutate app ID/class/bundle identity.

## Scope

In scope:
- src/main.rs renderer-error handling, native title metadata, stderr diagnostic, AccessKit alert preservation, presented_revision invalidation, and successful-render restoration.
- The smallest existing-host policy helper needed for deterministic failure/recovery testing; no renderer interface or module.
- Focused host tests, one persistent-error injection at the cheapest existing seam, and native observation that does not require successful GPU presentation.
- docs/CONTRACTS.md proof metadata for hardened VEN-C4 and preserved contracts after a committed source candidate, README LOC scorecard, and CHANGELOG for the accepted visible correction.

Out of scope:
- Transparent Device/Queue/resource reconstruction, device-loss classification, renderer replacement, process restart, supervisor protocol, popup/dialog/notification UI, telemetry, crash reporting, log framework, new module, dependency, application identity, or macOS support promise.
- Changing Orbit title ownership or retaining the failure title after successful recovery.

## Reference and dependency gate

Required before code:
- Current AGENTS.md, this Bead, audits ven-audit-venus-host-lifecycle-8jl and ven-audit-venus-scene-renderer-2db, docs/CONTRACTS.md, docs/REFERENCES.md, and docs/CRATES.md.
- Current Application status, refresh, render, accessibility, title, and presented-input paths plus Renderer error sources.
- Exact locked winit 0.30.13 Window::set_title behavior for current Linux backends.
- Beads ven-distinguish-device-from-surface-loss-d96 and ven-caller-application-identity-dcb only to preserve their device-loss and app-identity ownership.

Conditional:
- Eon launch stderr capture only if implementation evidence tries to claim supervisor-visible diagnostics. The native title remains the direct non-GPU user surface.

Rejected:
- A popup, notification system, logging dependency, renderer trait, recovery framework, process restart, or second status owner.

Platform disposition: neutral host policy over isolated native title behavior. Linux is the proof target; title visibility under undecorated windows and macOS runtime remain explicitly bounded proof surfaces.

## Implementation notes

1. Use TDD for one failure/recovery transition: a persistent RenderError immediately produces native-title and stderr effects without a successful present; a later Presented outcome clears render_notice and restores the accepted Orbit title.
2. Reuse the single existing notice string for pixels, AccessKit, title, and stderr. Do not add a second error taxonomy or status owner.
3. Keep presented_revision invalidation and AccessKit update exactly at the renderer-error boundary.
4. Set only window title metadata; do not touch Wayland app ID, X11 class/instance, bundle identity, or Eon policy.
5. Avoid redraw or retry loops. Recovery remains whatever current render scheduling already provides.
6. Make ven-distinguish-device-from-surface-loss-d96 depend on this proved failure surface rather than duplicating diagnostics.
7. Follow the source-commit then proof-metadata/closure workflow.

## Acceptance criteria

- A persistent RenderError on a static nonblinking scene immediately changes native title metadata to the bounded Venus renderer-failure notice and emits the same notice to stderr.
- The result is observable without a later successful GPU frame.
- AccessKit receives the same alert and presented_revision remains invalidated.
- A later successful presentation clears render_notice and restores the current accepted Orbit title or Venus fallback.
- Application identity, terminal attachment, transport state, and GPU recovery policy remain unchanged.
- Repeated failures remain bounded and do not create redraw, retry, popup, notification, logging, or allocation loops.
- No new module, dependency, product contract, or second diagnostic owner is introduced.

## Verification

- A focused deterministic host regression must prove immediate non-GPU failure projection and successful-title restoration.
- Inject a persistent RenderError at the cheapest existing seam for a static nonblinking scene and assert that no successful present is needed for the title/stderr result.
- Native Linux observation should confirm title metadata changes even when GPU presentation is unavailable; retain title-bar/compositor limits honestly.
- cargo fmt --check
- cargo check --locked
- cargo test --locked
- cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings
- git diff --check

All commands must exit 0 on the materially unchanged source candidate. Record exact stdout/stderr capture and native backend details.

## Stop conditions

- Stop if current renderer-error, title, or refresh ownership has materially changed.
- Stop if bounded explicit UX requires a popup, notification service, supervisor protocol, application-identity mutation, new dependency, or product contract.
- Stop if the existing error text can contain unbounded or sensitive backend data; resolve the bounded notice owner before projecting it.
- Stop if another active issue owns Application render failure or native title state.

## Maintenance notes

One existing notice projected through title, stderr, AccessKit, and the renderer status is sufficient; do not introduce a diagnostic subsystem. Cheapest falsifier: force RenderError forever and require title plus stderr to change before any successful present.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Inject or force Renderer::render to return RenderError persistently while the accepted scene is static and nonblinking.
2. Observe Application store render_notice, clear presented_revision, and update AccessKit.
3. Observe that native title and stderr do not change and stale or blank pixels remain; the notice cannot become visible pixels until the same renderer later succeeds.

title: Ship selectable cursor colors with random default
description:
## Outcome and contract

Ship one Venus-owned cursor-tail color choice with built-in presets, custom colors, a random default, and an automatic contrast-aware outline.

- Consumer: a person launching Venus directly or through Eon.
- Trigger: Venus starts without a color choice, or the caller chooses random, a named preset, or a custom RGB color.
- Result: one launch selector accepts random, preset:<name>, or custom:#RRGGBB. The absent selector defaults to random. Venus resolves exactly one solid color once per process launch and keeps it for that process lifetime. Every animated tail receives a one-logical-pixel outline derived automatically from the resolved color. Orbit remains authoritative for the actual terminal cursor body, color, shape, visibility, blink state, and destination.
- Important failures: unknown presets, malformed custom colors, duplicate selectors, conflicts with the existing explicit scalar profile, unavailable geometry, hidden cursors, resize, pane changes, occlusion, or renderer recovery cannot invent a color, modify the Orbit cursor body, leave animation active, or create stale draw state.

This changes the VEN-C1 omitted-profile default from one fixed blue tail to one launch-stable random built-in color. It preserves VEN-C2, VEN-C3, VEN-C7, VEN-C8, VEN-C19, the existing tail motion, and the accepted none and explicit duration behavior.

## Color choices

The single choice model is:

- random: uniform selection from the eight presets below, once per Venus process launch
- preset:<name>: one exact built-in color
- custom:#RRGGBB: one caller-supplied validated solid color

The built-in presets are:

- magma: #FF3B30
- solar: #FFD23F
- lime: #B7F34A
- forest: #35C978
- ice: #7DDCFF
- ocean: #5271FF
- nebula: #A970FF
- bubblegum: #FF5DA2

Colors are solid. There are no split palettes, gradients, families, shader assets, mode effects, glow, or cursor-body overrides.

## Automatic outline

Every built-in, random, custom, or accepted legacy explicit color receives the same automatic outline policy. Compute the resolved fill relative luminance, choose the higher-contrast direction toward black or white, and retain as much of the source color as possible while reaching at least a 3:1 fill-to-outline contrast ratio. Very light colors therefore receive a darker shade; very dark colors receive a lighter tint.

The outline is one logical pixel, shares the tail geometry, clipping, opacity, animation, reset, and recovery lifecycle, and has no user-facing option. It never outlines or recolors the Orbit-authored cursor body.

## Ownership and minimum shape

Venus owns the fixed preset names and RGB values, custom-color validation, random default selection, outline derivation, launch validation, and tail materialization. Resolve the color choice at the existing launch boundary into the existing tail presentation owner; do not carry preset or random policy into Application, Scene, Orbit protocol, or Eon workspace state.

Use one narrow selector/value surface for random, preset:<name>, and custom:#RRGGBB. Preserve cursor-effect-v1 none and explicit duration. Preserve the accepted complete scalar profile as a lower-level explicit input for now, but reject combining it with the new selector; do not add any other compatibility surface. Eon passes no cursor profile today and therefore consumes the random default automatically.

Use the standard library for cosmetic launch entropy and one private deterministic selector for proof. Add no dependency, config file, registry, child repository, serialization schema, runtime reload, compatibility adapter, or generic palette abstraction. Yazelix Cursors is not an owner, dependency, compatibility target, or reference requirement.

Use the existing rectangle batch, clipping, cursor animation, and redraw owners for the outline. Derive its color once per resolved fill, not per frame.

## Reference gate

Before code, inspect current VEN-C1 and its accepted cursor proofs; launch parsing and help; Renderer cursor animation, rectangle batching, clipping, recovery, and native checks; README, CHANGELOG, docs/CONTRACTS.md, and docs/REFERENCES.md. External cursor registries and shader implementations are rejected scope. Consult wgpu documentation only if the existing rectangle path cannot express the outline.

Record the exact current Orbit proof and protocol revision. Platform disposition is neutral shared renderer and launch behavior; native Linux Wayland remains the proof environment and macOS support is not widened.

## Acceptance

- With no selector, repeated deterministic selections cover all eight presets and each launch resolves exactly one stable color at duration 1.0.
- random, every preset:<name>, and representative custom:#RRGGBB values resolve exactly; unknown, malformed, duplicate, or conflicting inputs fail before window creation.
- Existing none, explicit duration, and complete scalar profiles remain exact.
- Random selection creates no dependency and no state outside launch resolution.
- For every preset plus black, white, and mid-luminance custom controls, the derived outline reaches at least 3:1 contrast against the fill by tinting or shading it. The calculation is deterministic and occurs once.
- The tail renders the selected solid fill with its one-logical-pixel outline using the same clipping and animation lifecycle. The terminal cursor body remains byte-for-byte driven by Orbit color and shape.
- Focused checks cover the choice table, deterministic random indexing, parser conflicts, custom validation, outline contrast and geometry, wide cursors, clipping, disable/reset, pane changes, resize, occlusion, and recovery without mirroring implementation trivia.
- Run the locked Rust route and the existing native cursor-tail dogfood. Update current docs, VEN-C1 proof/status only from accepted evidence, CHANGELOG, and README LOC.
- Publish the exact Venus source for Eon composition; no Eon, Orbit, or Yazelix Cursors source changes belong to this issue.

## Scope boundary

No split colors, gradients, per-segment colors, user-defined preset registry, live reload, configurable border, animation settings, new motion effects, shader ABI, dependency, cursor-body recoloring, per-pane policy, Cursors compatibility, Eon configuration work, Orbit change, or broader platform claim.

## Planning decision

The user finalized the product on 2026-09-17: Venus owns eight understandable solid presets; people choose random, preset, or custom color; random is the default; and every resolved color receives an automatic contrast-aware outline. The prior fixed darker-outline rule is superseded because it fails for very dark custom colors. This planning update authorizes the contract, not implementation.

## Prerequisites and reference gate

Coal, Cloud, Fire and Earth are absent from the default inventory.
Compare a bounded successor target with a sufficient existing child API. No exact v2 name or field schema is approved by this planning record.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The requested named presets are present in the child registry, preserving existing names and user definitions; choose distinct coherent palettes for missing names.
- A versioned native profile retains all agreed mono/accent or split colors, divider/transition information and any separately agreed cursor-body presentation value needed to render the preset faithfully.

## Scope boundary
No Eon schema/launch edits, Venus renderer changes, generated Ghostty shaders in Venus, general effects engine, live reload, per-pane policy, new toolchain or dependency without its gate. Motion remains tail/none; glow, warp, sweep and mode effects are separate scope.

Recorded in the user-authorized planning-only batch on 2026-09-09. No implementation, contract-index edit, dependency adoption, runtime refresh or proof advancement is authorized by this record; select the issue and settle its named contract choices before implementation.

title: Keep AccessKit workspace identities stable
description:
## Contract routing

Hardens proved VEN-C8 accessible workspace topology and semantic action routing while preserving VEN-C1 through VEN-C4, VEN-C7, EONW v1, ORBS v4, and Eon topology ownership. It adds or changes no product contract, dependency, Eon/Orbit protocol, reorder behavior, or compatibility promise.

Consumes Eon EON-C10, EONW v1, and eon-workspace-protocol 0.1.0 at exact proof 4af395aea06c230ee6b18cf0755ae25915c0b88d. Existing terminal presentation remains pinned to Orbit 7f067b30e97d0b4787a7c6c0bbe3dd8a80a61c2c.

The prior Eon terminal-child refresh frontier is closed. This issue is open and unclaimed; before claiming, reconfirm that no other implementation owns the active cross-repository frontier.

## Why

Consumer: an assistive-technology user activating an Eon tab or pane in Venus.

Trigger: AccessKit has published workspace nodes, then Eon removes an earlier tab or pane before the queued Click or Focus action is handled.

Result: each present Eon identity retains one stable AccessKit NodeId for the lifetime of that logical node, and action lookup uses the exact current identity-to-node mapping. An action for a removed node resolves to no target; it can never select a sibling that inherited the same vector index.

Important failures: keep Eon as the sole topology/selection owner, preserve Eon vector order in the tree, do not reuse retired NodeIds during one adapter lifetime, and do not replace stable allocation with collision-prone string hashing.

Audit ven-audit-venus-accessibility-p2h found this at Venus 4f799fef1c3e10e86d70b708708f7c2702d7aee8. Impact HIGH. Effort M. Implementation risk MED. Confidence HIGH.

## Evidence

- Exact Eon 4af395aea06c230ee6b18cf0755ae25915c0b88d docs/CONTRACTS.md:23-42 defines stable ordered tab and pane identities, identity actions, and Venus accessibility ownership.
- src/accessibility.rs:91-123 enumerates current vectors to publish workspace nodes.
- src/accessibility.rs:284-290 derives tab and pane NodeIds solely from vector indices.
- src/accessibility.rs:235-255 resolves an action NodeId against the latest snapshot by those current indices.
- src/main.rs:1009-1036 handles AccessKit action events after delivery through the event loop.
- AccessKit 0.24.1 src/lib.rs:705-715 defines NodeId as stable node identity; lines 2829-2849 say a node with the same ID overwrites the prior node.
- accesskit_winit 0.33.2 src/lib.rs:97-109 queues ActionRequest through EventLoopProxy.
- Audit comment 316 records the complete removal/action trace and all-status duplicate search.

## Scope

In scope:
- src/accessibility.rs workspace NodeId allocation, current identity lookup, tree focus mapping, and focused transition tests.
- src/main.rs AccessKit action routing only if the existing target API needs the smallest call-site adjustment.
- Existing workspace scene fixtures for deterministic insertion/removal transitions.
- docs/CONTRACTS.md VEN-C8 proof metadata after a proof-bearing source commit, README LOC accounting, and CHANGELOG for the accepted user-visible correction.

Out of scope:
- Eon identity generation, topology, reordering, protocol/schema changes, adapters, compatibility windows, a general object registry, terminal row identity, spatial bounds/clipping, selection text units, other accessibility features, or macOS support.

## Reference and dependency gate

Required before code:
- Current AGENTS.md, this Bead, audit ven-audit-venus-accessibility-p2h, VEN-C8, docs/REFERENCES.md, and docs/CRATES.md.
- Exact Eon producer proof and EONW identity/action semantics.
- Exact AccessKit 0.24.1 NodeId/TreeUpdate/ActionRequest behavior and accesskit_winit 0.33.2 queued handler delivery.
- Current Accessibility snapshot/tree/action owner and Application event routing.

Comparison-only: no external UI implementation is needed; selected APIs and exact producer contracts determine the invariant.

Rejected:
- Hashing Eon strings into NodeId, retaining index IDs, reusing retired IDs, an unbounded historical identity registry, changing Eon identity format, or adding a dependency.

Platform disposition: neutral accessibility identity state behind the selected native adapter. Linux is the proof target; macOS remains unproved.
design:
## Implementation notes

1. Use TDD for [a,b] to [b]: b must retain its NodeId, while a retained action must resolve to none after a disappears.
2. Keep allocation inside the existing Accessibility/Snapshot owner shared by activation and action lookup. Do not add a module or global registry.
3. Allocate from one disjoint workspace NodeId range with checked monotonic IDs. Retain assignments only for current identities, but never recycle a retired numeric ID during one adapter lifetime.
4. Key tab and pane identities distinctly even though EONW currently validates a shared focus-ID namespace; preserve that producer validation rather than relying on it for internal type safety.
5. Build children in the accepted Eon vector order. Maps own identity only, never ordering or topology.
6. Resolve queued actions only through the current reverse map. Removed or unknown NodeIds are bounded no-ops; current nodes route the exact Eon FocusId.
7. Preserve direct activation freshness, fixed root/content/status IDs, text-run IDs, and existing action vocabulary.
8. Run locked checks and focused native Linux AT-SPI dogfood across pane exit, tab removal, external refresh, and subsequent activation.
9. Follow the source-commit then proof-metadata/closure workflow.

Dependency decision: standard-library collections inside the existing owner are sufficient. No crate or manifest edit is expected.

## Stop conditions

- Stop if EONW identity stability or current namespace guarantees differ at the exact consumed proof.
- Stop before an Eon/Orbit change, new module, dependency, global registry, persisted identity state, product contract, or reorder feature.
- Stop if stable action routing requires retaining removed topology or reconstructing Eon state.
- Stop if another active issue owns workspace accessibility identity or action routing.

title: Activate safe native hyperlink interaction
description:
Contract routing:
- Implements the user-activated VEN-C5 contract.
- Consumes Orbit ORB-C6 and the exact accepted ORBF/ORBS proof revision current at activation.
- Preserves VEN-C1, VEN-C2, and VEN-C4; exact proof scope is recorded in docs/CONTRACTS.md.

## Why

Before implementation, Orbit emitted explicit OSC 8 hyperlink URIs and Venus preserved each URI in its immutable scene, but Venus offered no native hyperlink action. Users therefore saw linked text without a safe way to inspect, copy, or open the authoritative target.

## Activation evidence (before implementation)

- `src/scene.rs:42-48` stores the Orbit-authored hyperlink on each DrawCell.
- `src/scene.rs:285-297` materializes the URI directly from the canonical frame without reparsing terminal text.
- `docs/CONTRACTS.md:8-11` proves scene materialization and semantic input but indexes no hyperlink interaction.
- Orbit `docs/CONTRACTS.md:27` proves ORB-C6 and identifies rich presentation as an owned cross-repository boundary.

## Scope

In scope:
- Pointer hit testing against only the last successfully presented scene.
- Clear hover/focus affordance, target inspection, copy-link, and an explicit modifier-click or equivalent open action.
- A narrow scheme and length policy with bounded failure UX.
- Linux native Wayland proof; macOS APIs are comparison evidence only under the current VEN-C16 platform boundary.

Out of scope:
- Parsing URLs or file paths from ordinary terminal text.
- Silently opening a target, hiding the actual URI, or bypassing terminal mouse-reporting semantics.
- Workspace file navigation, custom schemes, shell integration, or any Orbit protocol/schema change unless a confirmed owner gap is reported back to Orbit.
design:
## Implementation Notes

1. Before code, add the user-approved VEN-C5 row to docs/CONTRACTS.md and record the exact consumed Orbit proof and compatibility classification.
2. Complete the Execution baseline and Reference gate. Required before code: the current OSC 8 specification or Ghostty VT documentation, the exact winit pointer/cursor APIs already selected, and official Linux/macOS external-open behavior. Compare only the native/standard-library path and credible opener crates if an opener dependency is actually needed.
3. Specify the interaction so terminal mouse reporting and selection retain priority; prefer an explicit modifier or context action rather than stealing ordinary clicks.
4. Derive link spans and hit targets from the accepted Scene. Do not add a second parser or mutable hyperlink model.
5. Apply URI size and scheme policy before invoking a native action. Opening and copying remain user-triggered.
6. Add one strong deterministic scene/hit/action-policy test and focused native dogfood.

Dependency decision: no crate is selected. A direct crate or architecture-shaping feature requires the Venus Crate gate and user approval before manifest edits.

Portability disposition: isolated platform dependency for external opening; scene identity, hit testing, and URI policy remain neutral.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if ORBF no longer carries one unambiguous target for the presented link.
- Stop if the design requires reparsing text, changing terminal authority, or adding a protocol adapter.
- Stop for user choice if safe platform opening requires a new dependency or materially different Linux/macOS policy.
acceptance_criteria:
1. VEN-C5 is approved and indexed before implementation, with the exact consumed ORB-C6 proof revision.
2. Hover, keyboard/context inspection, copy, and explicit open operate only on the last successfully presented scene and never on stale or unpresented geometry.
3. Links spanning multiple cells resolve to the exact Orbit-authored URI; resize, reconnect, revision replacement, wide cells, and renderer recovery cannot activate a stale target.
4. Ordinary clicks continue to follow terminal mouse and selection policy; opening is explicit and never silent.
5. Unsupported schemes, oversized or malformed targets, and native-open failure produce bounded, accessible UX.
6. Deterministic checks cover target identity, geometry invalidation, policy, and failure. Manual Linux dogfood covers hover, copy, open, terminal mouse mode, and keyboard access.
7. Canonical locked Rust checks and git diff --check pass, and every touched proved contract advances to an accepted proof commit or retains an explicit gap.
8. Closure records compatibility, dependency disposition, portability, owned LOC, and remaining platform limitations.
notes:
Accepted VEN-C5 source cf3a9169f2cd95d42c689134a52d51d9147ff37c; accepted Eon/EonTerm integration 07867f99d176012a9d34a61aa37b5de9ce0888af. The user activated this direction on 2026-09-07 America/Sao_Paulo after the graduation gate orb-bi4.7 closed. Orbit owns OSC 8 targets, Scene owns spans, existing presentation/input/render/accessibility/clipboard owners project them, and host GIO dispatches bounded explicit HTTP/HTTPS activation. Copy preserves bounded target text. The Eon launch owner preserves host XDG preferences and supplies product EON_CONFIG_HOME separately.

Compatibility: additive native interaction; ORBF v1, ORBS v10 and EONW v4 unchanged. Native Linux Wayland only. Fractional scale, broader compositor quality and non-systemd installed support remain unproved. Missing GIO or handlers produces a bounded failure; browser content loading is outside dispatch proof. Existing live user supervisors are preserved and need a user-directed restart to adopt the refreshed artifacts.

Owned LOC after source and acceptance docs: Desktop 17,330 (14,318 Rust source including unit tests; 898 Rust integration tests), Eon 17,160. Rejected alternatives and their failure conditions remain in the reference gate comment.

title: Identify Venus as Eon on native Wayland
description:
Contract routing:
- Consumes and hardens EON-C1 application identity for the Venus graphical consumer.
- Preserves VEN-C1 through VEN-C4 and VEN-C7; changes no Orbit contract or terminal behavior.
- Adds no new Venus contract because Eon already owns the desktop application identity and packaging metadata.

Consumer, trigger, result, failures:
A local Eon user launches the Venus window under native Wayland. The compositor receives application ID eon, matches eon.desktop, and displays the canonical Eon icon for the running application. X11/Xwayland retains the existing yazelix-venus WM_CLASS. Wrong or absent application identity must not leave a generic running-app icon or break the accepted X11 match.

Scope:
One Venus-owned winit window-identity correction and focused proof. No icon asset, desktop file, package, renderer, terminal, protocol, workspace, dependency, or configuration change.
design: Use winit 0.30.13's existing Wayland window-attribute extension before window creation. Set app ID eon only when the active event loop is Wayland; leave X11 attributes untouched so argv[0] continues producing WM_CLASS yazelix-venus. Keep the backend distinction at the existing native-window creation seam. First check: compile and locked tests, then launch the resulting Venus through the installed Eon desktop identity on COSMIC Wayland and inspect the running-app icon.

1. Native Wayland xdg_toplevel app_id is eon before the window is mapped and resolves eon.desktop.
2. X11/Xwayland retains WM_CLASS yazelix-venus and the existing Eon StartupWMClass contract.
3. VEN-C1 through VEN-C4 and VEN-C7, Orbit protocols, window title, rendering, input, lifecycle, dependencies, and packaging remain unchanged.
4. cargo fmt --check, cargo check --locked, cargo test --locked, cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings, README LOC accounting, and git diff --check pass.
5. One focused native COSMIC Wayland observation confirms the running window uses the canonical Eon icon.

Chosen owner and code shape:
- Eon remains the desktop application identity owner. Venus supplies that identity at its existing native-window seam.
- On Linux native Wayland only, create_window applies winit WindowAttributesExtWayland::with_name with general app ID eon. X11/Xwayland attributes remain untouched, retaining executable-derived WM_CLASS yazelix-venus.
- No helper, test fixture, icon asset, configuration, protocol, manifest, lockfile, dependency, or packaging surface was added.

Contract and platform disposition:
- Consumes and hardens EON-C1. Preserves VEN-C1 through VEN-C4 and VEN-C7. Changes no Orbit contract.

title: Preserve shifted punctuation through Kitty keyboard mode
description:
## Contract Routing

This bug hardens proved `VEN-C2`; it does not add, change, replace, or retire a Venus, Orbit, Eon, Eonova, Nova, or Zellij contract. Venus remains the owner of native interaction collection and sends only canonical Orbit semantic input. Consume `ORB-C5` at accepted Orbit proof `c905bf9610581747f1b07565814b501ca66cfaa6` and canonical ORBS v2 / `orbit-protocol` 0.1.0 at `9d6d2bb37f20ab4ad9e186c7bc715eabef43e757`. Advance the exact `VEN-C2` proof revision after implementation and proof.

Smallest observable contract:
- Consumer: a local Eon terminal user, including when the child is Nova's Zellij with Kitty keyboard mode enabled.
- Trigger: the native keyboard layout produces printable text using Shift, such as `Shift+/` producing `?`.
- Result: the child receives the exact layout-derived printable text while Orbit still receives truthful physical-key, active-modifier, consumed-modifier, composition, and unshifted-codepoint fields.
- Important failures: unsupported platform metadata must not be guessed from a US keyboard table; Ctrl/Alt/Super behavior, IME/dead-key composition, releases/repeats, and non-Kitty input must not regress.

## Why

In Eonova, `Shift+/` reaches the shell as `/`; the same key produces `?` in vanilla Eon. Eonova adds Nova's Zellij between Eon and the shell and enables Kitty keyboard mode, exposing incorrect consumed-modifier metadata at the Venus native-input boundary.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start the pinned Eonova composition with Nova/Zellij Kitty keyboard support enabled and focus an ordinary shell pane.
2. Press `Shift+/` on a layout where that chord produces `?`; observe `/` reaches the shell.
3. Start vanilla Eon with a direct shell under the same layout and press the same chord; observe `?` reaches the shell.
4. Capture or probe the semantic key and encoder boundary: empty consumed modifiers produce `CSI 47;2u`, which pinned Zellij downgrades to `/`.

Impact: HIGH because a common printable character is corrupted in the accepted Eonova dogfood composition, and the same defect can affect other Shift-produced punctuation or layouts.

Effort: M. Implementation risk: MED because winit's public cross-platform event surface may not expose an exact consumed-modifier mask. Confidence: HIGH in the diagnosed byte path.

## Evidence

- Current Venus `src/input.rs:85-97` forwards active modifiers, layout-derived text, and the layout-derived unshifted codepoint, but hardcodes `consumed_modifiers: Modifiers::empty()` for every native key event.
- Current Venus `src/input.rs:554-561` accepts a single layout-derived unshifted codepoint; focused tests cover that helper but not shifted printable metadata or Kitty-mode behavior.
- Eonova pins Eon `2d7c080aaafaca519d5f99e0ef7f4fdf3d14f1a7`, which pins Venus `90988f6ebcde68338e202a9c637c59398aafe93d`, Orbit `64db581445bafca1a08a6530f8e44f9c1edbc169`, and canonical protocol `9d6d2bb37f20ab4ad9e186c7bc715eabef43e757`; it pins Nova `6c7174b4efca5f139a461d204186c5001d6457bd`.
- Pinned Nova `defaults/zellij/config.kdl:4` enables `support_kitty_keyboard_protocol true`; pinned Zellij `bbccdea6eda81f314151160f9b3f8882a26478ec` requests Kitty disambiguation with `CSI > 1 u`.
- Pinned Orbit `src/main.rs:748-769` forwards Venus's semantic key fields unchanged into libghostty-vt 0.2.1 and derives encoder options from the child's current terminal modes.
- A focused libghostty-vt 0.2.1 probe for physical Slash, active Shift, text `?`, and unshifted `/` produced literal `?` in legacy mode but `CSI 47;2u` under Kitty disambiguation when consumed modifiers were empty; setting consumed modifiers to Shift produced literal `?` in both modes.
- Pinned Zellij parses `CSI 47;2u` as Shift plus `Char('/')`; its `zellij-utils/src/vendored/termwiz/input.rs:359-368` removes Shift from ASCII punctuation without translating `/` to `?`, and a focused probe confirmed `serialize_non_kitty()` returns `Some("/")`.
- Eon Desktop HEAD `47a07cdcf00b7fe50bf9a34474e668386b642b8d` still contains the hardcoded empty field. This is diagnosis evidence, not implementation proof.

## References Before Code

Required:
- Complete Bead and comments, `AGENTS.md`, `docs/CONTRACTS.md` for `VEN-C2`, `docs/REFERENCES.md`, and `docs/CRATES.md`.
- Exact winit 0.30.13 `KeyEvent`, Linux XKB translation, `KeyEventExtModifierSupplement`, text, and modifier semantics. Determine whether the accepted public API can truthfully supply consumed modifiers across supported layouts.
- Exact Orbit proof/source revisions above, `ORB-C5`, the canonical `KeyEvent` validation rules, and the libghostty-vt 0.2.1 / Ghostty `a887df42c56f6de86c0fe6da9c4eeca37931e083` consumed-modifier and Kitty encoder behavior.
- Exact Eonova, Eon, Nova, and Zellij revisions above for the reproduced composition and Kitty-to-legacy conversion. These are boundary evidence only; reuse no source.

Rejected surrounding scope:
- Disabling Kitty keyboard support in Nova or Eonova.
- Patching Nova keybindings, maintaining a Venus punctuation lookup table, assuming a US layout, or teaching Venus about Zellij.
- Moving PTY or terminal encoding authority into Venus.

First meaningful check: a deterministic shifted-printable event must carry truthful semantic fields and the accepted Orbit encoder must emit the layout-produced text under Kitty disambiguation.

License: winit, Ghostty/libghostty, and the pinned Zellij fork are primary behavior references. Inspection does not authorize copying or dependency selection; record exact licenses and independently adopted mechanisms at the Reference gate.

## Scope

In scope:
- `src/input.rs` native key-event translation and the minimum focused tests.
- Existing protocol values only; no local schema or terminal encoder.
- `docs/CONTRACTS.md` proof maintenance for `VEN-C2`, README LOC scorecard, and `CHANGELOG.md` after accepted user-visible proof.
- Native Linux Eon and Eonova dogfood, with a macOS-credible ownership assessment.

Out of scope:
- Nova/Eonova configuration changes, Zellij changes, Orbit terminal-encoder changes, new keybindings, a keyboard-layout subsystem, macOS implementation, or any new dependency without a separate approved Crate gate.
- Changes to workspace topology, rendering, selection, clipboard, or terminal authority.

## Implementation Notes

1. Before edits, claim this Bead and add the required Execution baseline with current HEAD, `git hash-object AGENTS.md`, Bead `updated_at`, `VEN-C2`, consumed Orbit proofs, intended surfaces, dirty paths, and agent identity.
2. Complete and record the required Reference gate before code. Name one owner for consumed-modifier truth and the cheapest falsifying check.
3. Use the first sufficient existing winit/native mechanism. Keep one translation path for press, repeat, and release; do not infer shifted punctuation from physical keys or a fixed layout.
4. Add a few strong tests covering shifted printable punctuation and preservation of non-US/layout-derived text, unshifted codepoints, active versus consumed modifiers, composition, and non-Shift modifiers. Avoid per-key tables and duplicate protocol tests.
5. Prove the exact semantic event through the accepted Orbit encoder with Kitty disambiguation, then dogfood both direct Eon and the pinned Eonova Nova/Zellij path.
6. Rerun a fresh-eyes correctness pass and a separate simplification pass after the material change; repeat after any actionable correction before claiming convergence.

Dependency decision: add no dependency. If exact winit cannot expose sufficient information, stop for user choice rather than adding XKB/platform bindings or a heuristic.

Platform disposition: prefer neutral native-event translation. If the correct solution needs Linux-specific consumed-modifier access, classify it as an isolated platform dependency, name the macOS replacement seam and removal cost, and stop for the required user/dependency decision.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `Shift+/` produces `?` in both vanilla Eon and the pinned Eonova Nova/Zellij composition.
- A compact representative set of other Shift-produced punctuation behaves identically in direct and Kitty-requesting paths.
- Layout-derived non-ASCII text, dead-key/IME composition, Ctrl/Alt/Super combinations, key releases/repeats, workspace shortcuts, and unmodified text remain correct.
- Venus reports consumed modifiers truthfully without a fixed-layout punctuation map, second key schema, or terminal-aware special case.
- No Nova, Eonova, Zellij, Orbit protocol, or dependency file changes are needed.

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --check`
- `cargo check --locked`
- `cargo test --locked`
- `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `git diff --check`
- Native Linux dogfood records exact Eon/Eonova/Nova/Zellij revisions, keyboard layout, compositor path, observed characters, and Kitty-mode state.
- Update README LOC accounting, record accepted user-visible behavior in `CHANGELOG.md`, and advance `VEN-C2` only at the exact proof-bearing commit.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if exact winit/native evidence cannot provide truthful consumed modifiers without a new dependency, backend-specific API, unsafe access, or layout heuristic.
- Stop if the observed semantic event is already truthful at the implementation revision; route the remaining gap to Orbit or Zellij instead of compensating in Venus.
- Stop for user approval if fixing the defect changes a contract, dependency, public surface, platform boundary, or requires edits in another repository.
- Stop if another active implementation owns `src/input.rs` or materially changes an in-scope surface; rebaseline only after coordination.
- Stop if the Eonova reproduction pins drift materially before implementation.

## Maintenance Notes

This Bead is independently reviewable and has no prerequisite. The open whole-subsystem input audit is not a blocker and should audit whichever accepted input implementation exists when it starts.

title: Paste native clipboard text through Orbit semantic input
description:
## Outcome and contract

Add the missing native clipboard-read path required for EonTerm to replace Mars without regressing ordinary terminal paste. This implementation creates `VEN-C10` after that contract is approved and indexed before code.

- Consumer: a local user focused on an attached Venus terminal surface.
- Trigger: the platform Paste key or the accepted native `Ctrl+Shift+V` shortcut on Linux.
- Result: Venus reads plain text from the native clipboard once, submits one canonical Orbit semantic Paste message, and Orbit alone applies bracketed-paste and terminal-mode encoding under proved `ORB-C5`.
- Failures: unavailable or non-text clipboard data, oversized input, queue pressure, attachment loss, and platform errors produce bounded visible failure without partial or repeated paste.

This consumes `ORB-C5` at the exact accepted proof current at activation, creates `VEN-C10`, hardens `VEN-C2`, and preserves `VEN-C1`, `VEN-C3`, `VEN-C4`, `VEN-C7`, `VEN-C8`, and `VEN-C9`. Terminal-originated clipboard effects remain separate work under Orbit `orb-ll1` and are not part of this contract.

## Ownership and minimum shape

Venus owns only the explicit native clipboard read, shortcut precedence, size admission, and client-visible failure. Orbit remains the sole terminal/input-mode authority and semantic paste encoder. Reuse the existing native clipboard owner and canonical protocol; add no second clipboard library, terminal parser, keymap table, Eon wrapper, Nova workaround, or hidden fallback.

Read and queue the clipboard only after explicit user action. Use the existing canonical message and queue bounds; reject over-limit text explicitly rather than truncating it. Preserve IME composition, terminal mouse reporting, selection/copy, ordinary `Ctrl+V`, application key modes, reconnect, and accessibility.

## References before code

Required: current `AGENTS.md`; `VEN-C2`, `VEN-C4`, and `VEN-C7`; exact accepted `ORB-C5` semantic-paste proof and canonical message bounds; the current Venus input, queue, notice, and arboard paths; exact winit Paste-key and modifier behavior; and pinned Mars `Ctrl+Shift+V` behavior as comparison evidence only.

Conditional: official platform clipboard behavior when a reproduced Linux/macOS distinction affects the seam. A crate gate is required before changing the existing clipboard dependency or features.

Rejected: reading on focus, primary-selection substitution for the clipboard shortcut, direct PTY bytes from Venus, terminal escape parsing, silent truncation, repeated retries, Nova/Eon key translation, or terminal-generated clipboard effects.

## Acceptance

1. `VEN-C10` is approved and indexed before implementation with the exact consumed `ORB-C5` proof.
2. `Ctrl+Shift+V` and the native Paste key each read one plain-text clipboard value and cause exactly one canonical semantic Paste action.
3. Normal and bracketed paste reach a real Orbit-owned PTY exactly as authoritative terminal modes require; multiline and Unicode text remain exact.
4. Empty, unavailable, non-text, oversized, disconnected, and queue-full cases are bounded, visible, and never send partial or duplicate text.
5. Shortcut precedence preserves ordinary text, IME, Kitty key reporting, selection, copy, mouse modes, workspace shortcuts, and reconnect.
6. Deterministic tests cover admission, dispatch, precedence, and failure; native Linux dogfood covers shell, Zellij, Helix, Yazi, multiline text, and reconnect.
7. The accepted proof records dependency disposition, canonical bounds, portability, exact revisions, owned LOC, locked Rust checks, and remaining platform limitations.

Portability disposition: neutral semantic flow with an isolated native clipboard effect. Linux is proved first; macOS remains unclaimed until exercised.

title: Build the native Eon Bar workspace header
description:
## Outcome and routed contract

Create and prove `VEN-C21 — Native Eon Bar workspace header` by evolving Venus's existing full-workspace tab strip into one restrained native header without adding another row.

Consumer: one person using a Venus surface controlled by a full Eon workspace.

Trigger: the person points at, activates, focuses, or scrolls the header; activates New tab, Shortcuts, or the active tab's Close control; or presses the empty header background to move an undecorated window.

Result: the current one-row tab strip keeps its height and tab-first overflow behavior, adds fixed native New tab and Shortcuts controls, exposes Close only for the active tab, and leaves a bounded empty background region for native window dragging when width permits. New tab and Close send the existing EONW actions; Shortcuts toggles the existing VEN-C20 viewer locally; only empty-background left press invokes the locked winit window-drag mechanism. Tooltips and AccessKit names include the accepted shortcuts.

Important failures: narrow or tiny surfaces retain the active tab identity and reachable controls without overlapping the terminal; stale snapshots keep existing stable-target rejection; a drag failure does not crash, mutate workspace state, or leak input; buttons, tab gaps, terminal content, pane chrome, popup/picker focus, and the shortcut viewer never become drag targets.

Impact: HIGH for native usability and discoverability. Effort: M. Implementation risk: MEDIUM at layout/input/accessibility boundaries. Confidence: HIGH.

## Evidence

- `src/scene.rs:440-510` gives the tab viewport the full window width and owns shaped tab widths, overflow, and active-tab reveal.
- `src/scene.rs:655-676` currently hit-tests tabs, panes, and terminal content; unused header background has no semantic target.
- `src/application.rs:540-541`, `693-700`, and `3604-3607` already route Create tab and stable active-tab Close actions.
- `src/application.rs:1438-1517` and `3573-3590` already own the local VEN-C20 shortcut viewer.
- `src/accessibility.rs:269-291` exposes the current tab strip as a native horizontal TabList with stable Tab nodes.
- `docs/CONTRACTS.md:589-720` defines VEN-C8 tab geometry, scrolling, stable identity, input, and accessibility; `docs/CONTRACTS.md:1227-1266` defines VEN-C20.
- `Cargo.toml:29` pins winit source `7c209ec5bebbd2963f75a39f79b320af6b03f72c`; its `Window::drag_window` contract requires an immediately preceding left press and, on Wayland, the cursor inside the window.
- Eon EON-C8 omits the native title bar for current full-Eon surfaces, so the existing tab row is the correct single owner for native workspace chrome.
- Nova Bar at exact source `bfbf8a7be28b69f9d822c0843bf2dd5066dd49e3` supplies comparison evidence for tab-first width priority and secondary-information yielding. Its Zellij, zjstatus, WASM, command polling, widgets, colors, and notification controller are rejected.
- Official GNOME header-bar/tabs, Apple toolbar, VS Code status-bar, and Ghostty titlebar/tab guidance inspected on 2026-09-17 support few controls, responsive priority, alternate keyboard access, and preserving draggable space; they are UX guidance, not dependencies or copied implementation.

## Prerequisites and reference gate

- This bead is approved and open, but do not claim it while another Eon/Orbit/Venus implementation frontier is active. At activation, confirm the current frontier is accepted or the user explicitly authorizes a change.
- Record the exact accepted EON-C8, EON-C20, EONW, Orbit, and Venus revisions before code. Stop on a stale or speculative consumer.
- Inspect the locked winit drag implementation and event-order assumptions at the exact selected source.
- Inspect Nova Bar's exact tab/status fitting only for priority behavior and recheck the official UX references above.
- Adopt the existing Scene rectangles, renderer batches, input owner, action descriptors, shortcut viewer, AccessKit tree, and locked native window API.
- Add no crate, framework, protocol field, compatibility adapter, timer, generic toolbar, or second UI owner.

## Scope

In scope:
- Venus-owned workspace scene geometry, rendering, hit testing, hover/focus, pointer routing, tooltips, and AccessKit projection.
- One-row header containing existing scrollable tabs, a small empty drag region when width permits, and fixed New tab and Shortcuts controls.
- One Close affordance for the active tab only, routed through the existing exact active `tN` action.
- VEN-C21, focused deterministic checks, current README/changelog/LOC alignment, and isolated native Linux Wayland proof.

Out of scope:
- A second status row, Nova Bar code or compatibility, CPU/RAM/clock/shell/editor/Git/version/quota widgets, configurable widget trays, plugin APIs, and polling.
- Transient notice relocation, agent status, per-tab attention markers, cursor-color-derived chrome, settings, branding, tab drag reorder, tab overview, or inactive-tab close.
- EONW or Orbit changes, a new action, Eon topology policy, native-decoration policy changes, arbitrary window-control replacement, or macOS support/proof.

## Implementation notes

1. Record VEN-C21 as Candidate before production edits, extending VEN-C8 only where the shared tab geometry must remain explicit.
2. Keep the current header height. Reduce the scrollable tab viewport only by the fixed controls and a bounded drag target; preserve active reveal, shaped labels, number retention, wheel scrolling across tab gaps, and terminal/picker geometry.
3. Render controls with the existing restrained navy/mint palette and existing primitives. Use the full header height as the pointer target, concise glyphs, hover/press/focus states, and shortcut-bearing tooltips.
4. Route New tab and active Close through existing common/EONW actions. Toggle the existing local shortcut viewer directly. Do not reconstruct Eon pending-tab, final-tab, stale-target, or close policy.
5. On immediate left press over only empty header background, call the existing native window drag API. Preserve wheel scrolling and all nonempty targets.
6. Extend the existing accessibility tree with Button nodes and stable activation; keep tab semantics and terminal focus deterministic.
7. Protect one layout/hit/action/accessibility boundary check, then run the complete unchanged-candidate Rust/Nix route and one isolated native Wayland dogfood.

## Acceptance criteria

- Full workspace mode has one header row at the previous tab-strip height; standalone and popup geometry remain unchanged and no terminal row is lost to a second bar.
- Tabs retain current labels, middle ellipsis, maximum width, scrolling, active reveal, selection, hover path preview, focus outline, hit identity, and accessible path context.
- New tab is fixed outside tab scrolling and sends exactly the existing CreateTab action once. Existing picker-first and pending-tab policy remains Eon-owned.
- Shortcuts is fixed outside tab scrolling and toggles the existing VEN-C20 viewer without terminal bytes or EONW traffic.
- Close is exposed only for the active tab, names its exact accepted `tN`, and sends exactly the existing CloseTab action once. Rejection and partial-stop behavior remain Eon-owned; inactive tabs gain no close path.
- Empty-background left press starts compositor-owned window movement through locked winit. Tabs, controls, tab gaps used for scrolling, pane chrome, terminal, popup/picker, tooltips, and viewer do not start a drag.
- Ordinary, overflow, narrow, and tiny layouts neither overlap nor conceal the active tab identity and controls. Secondary empty drag space yields before required interaction.
- Tooltips and AccessKit expose “New tab — Alt+Shift+T”, “Keyboard shortcuts — Alt+/”, and “Close tab — Alt+Shift+W”; every control is keyboard/screen-reader activatable and visible focus is not color-only.
- Existing workspace traversal/reorder, pointer focus, tab wheel scrolling, popup/picker behavior, shortcut capture, terminal input, native notices, accessibility, resize/scale, and application lifecycle remain intact.
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo check --locked`, `cargo test --locked`, `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings`, the affected Nix package build/check, README LOC, and `git diff --check` pass on one unchanged candidate.
- Isolated native Linux Wayland proof records exact source, package, EONW/Orbit revisions, compositor/scale, tab counts, narrow/overflow interaction, drag, pointer/keyboard/AT-SPI activation, and cleanup without disturbing live user Sessions.

## Stop conditions

- Stop if another implementation frontier is still active without explicit user authorization.
- Stop if safe behavior requires an EONW/Orbit change, inactive-tab close, new dependency, generic toolbar/widget system, second row, or copied Nova mechanism.
- Stop if the locked winit contract cannot initiate a Wayland drag from the immediate empty-background press without stealing other input.
- Stop before claiming macOS, other compositors, native titlebar replacement, or installed full-Eon acceptance.

## Maintenance notes

This is a Venus presentation contract, not a Nova compatibility surface. The active-tab-only close is deliberate: current Eon policy accepts only the exact active `tN`; focusing then closing an inactive tab would be a racy two-action reconstruction. The public product may call the row “Eon Bar”; the implementation remains the existing Venus workspace header, not a new module or repository.
notes:
Quota reconciliation — 2026-09-17: quota remains out of scope for VEN-C21 itself, but the chosen later presentation is now `ven-render-codex-quota-eon-bar-wfe`, downstream of this bead and Eon's accepted typed facts. Keep VEN-C21's header geometry/render/hit/accessibility ownership direct and extensible by that one later child; do not add speculative slots, a widget trait/registry, timers, polling, configuration, or provider logic to the core bar.

Platform classification: isolated Wayland dependency for native empty-background window drag; header geometry, controls, hit testing, and accessibility remain shared. This bead proves only native x86_64 Linux Wayland; macOS remains unproved and out of scope.

title: Keep pane headers focused on pane identity
description:
## Why

Pane headers currently expose both the user-facing pane identity and the underlying Orbit Session identity, producing labels such as `pane-1  session-1`. The Session value is useful for Eon diagnostics but is redundant implementation detail in the visual accordion. The user explicitly chose pane-focused headers while retaining Session identity in Eon human and JSON diagnostics.

Smallest observable contract:
- Consumer: a local user or assistive-technology user viewing an Eon workspace in Venus.
- Trigger: Venus materializes a live or offline pane header from an accepted EONW snapshot.
- Result: the header identifies the pane and lifecycle only: `pane-1` when live and `pane-1 offline` when offline. It does not present the mapped Session ID.
- The EONW snapshot and Eon CLI/JSON retain the exact pane-to-Session mapping; Venus does not rewrite or remove protocol data.

Contract routing:
- Intentionally updates the pane-header presentation governed by proved VEN-C8; update that contract before implementation.
- Preserves VEN-C1 through VEN-C4 and VEN-C7, EONW v1, EON-C10, Orbit Sessions, endpoints, topology, selection, actions, and lifecycle.
- Changes no Eon or Orbit contract.

## Evidence

- `src/render.rs:662-666` constructs live and offline visual labels from both `pane.id` and `pane.session`.
- `src/accessibility.rs:114-126` repeats the same combined identity in the AccessKit button label.
- `src/scene.rs:55-63` retains Session identity in `WorkspacePane`; `src/scene.rs:172-180` copies it from EONW for those presentation consumers.
- Repository search finds no other `WorkspacePane.session` consumer. The EONW model and transport still retain the authoritative mapping independently.
- `docs/CONTRACTS.md:13` assigns pane-header materialization and accessible focus to VEN-C8.
- `tests/canonical_scene.rs:13-150` proves pane order, geometry, hit testing, and selected content but does not constrain the displayed label.

Impact: MED for workspace clarity.
Effort: S.
Implementation risk: LOW.
Confidence: HIGH.

## Scope

In scope:
- Visual pane-header labels in `src/render.rs`.
- Matching AccessKit labels in `src/accessibility.rs`.
- Remove `WorkspacePane.session` from the native scene projection if it becomes unused.
- Focused tests for live and offline labels plus existing workspace accessibility and geometry assertions.
- VEN-C8 current-state wording/proof, README user-facing description if necessary, and LOC accounting.

Out of scope:
- EONW or ORBS schema changes; Eon human or JSON output; Session, endpoint, pane, or tab identity changes.
- Pane renaming, terminal-title or working-directory labels, AgentRun metadata, new settings, tab-label changes, or workspace restyling.
- Hiding offline state or weakening accessible selection, expansion, action, order, or bounds.

## References Before Code

Required:
- Current workspace scene, renderer, AccessKit projection, canonical workspace tests, VEN-C8, and exact EONW v1 producer proof `4af395aea06c230ee6b18cf0755ae25915c0b88d`.
- Exact AccessKit 0.24.1 and accesskit_winit 0.33.2 label/action behavior already selected in `docs/CRATES.md`.

Comparison only:
- Canario/Rio at `3e41b8b19a1c`, limited to concise labeled-row activation and distinct selected state. Copy no source or terminal ownership.

Rejected:
- Removing Session identity from EONW, changing Eon diagnostics, retaining different visible and accessible names, introducing configurable label templates, or replacing pane IDs with guessed shell/process text.

## Acceptance and Verification

- A live header visibly and accessibly reads `pane-1`; an offline header reads `pane-1 offline`.
- Neither visual nor AccessKit pane labels contain the mapped Session ID.
- EONW decoding, endpoint switching, and Eon-owned pane-to-Session mappings remain byte- and behavior-identical.
- Pane order, selection, expansion, pointer hit testing, F6 focus, arrow traversal, scrolling, and offline styling remain unchanged.
- Remove the native scene Session field if repository-wide search proves it unused after label cleanup.
- `cargo fmt --check`
- `cargo check --locked`
- `cargo test --locked`
- `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `git diff --check`
- Native Wayland dogfood shows concise live/offline headers and unchanged pointer/keyboard behavior.
- Advance VEN-C8 to the exact proof-bearing revision; keep Eon and Orbit proof pins unchanged.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if Session identity is required by a current Venus behavior beyond header presentation; do not reconstruct it elsewhere.
- Stop for user choice if removing it would make two visible pane labels ambiguous under accepted Eon identity rules.
- Stop and route to Eon if the requested result requires changing EONW or Eon diagnostics.
- Stop if source or proof revisions drift materially before implementation.

## Maintenance Notes

Use one shared pane-label projection for visual and accessibility consumers if that reduces duplicated policy without creating a new abstraction. Preserve pane identity as the user-facing workspace handle and leave Session diagnostics with Eon.
