title: Keep Venus text and cursor on one cell grid
description:
## Why

Venus does not keep every rendered terminal glyph on the authoritative cell grid. The accumulated horizontal drift already appears as a growing gap between text and the Orbit cursor. Current Eon dogfood also shows ordinary Nushell `ls` and `which` tables with box borders, separators, and junctions landing at inconsistent horizontal positions. This is a confirmed Venus presentation defect, not Nushell configuration and not an Orbit cursor-coordinate defect.

Contract routing:
- Hardens proved VEN-C1 structured-presentation materialization.
- Preserves proved VEN-C2 input and resize geometry, VEN-C3 lifecycle, VEN-C4 failure UX, VEN-C7 history and selection ownership, and VEN-C8 workspace composition.
- Consumes unchanged canonical Orbit cell widths and cursor columns from ORBS v2 at proof `9d6d2bb37f20ab4ad9e186c7bc715eabef43e757`.
- Changes no Orbit or Eon contract.

## Evidence

- `src/render.rs:65-85` defines the shared physical cell metrics, including a fixed 9 px width and 14 px font at scale 1.
- `src/render.rs:709-735` anchors each Orbit-authored glyph run at `column * cell_width` and bounds it to `columns * cell_width`.
- `src/render.rs:817-892` shapes the complete styled run through glyphon/cosmic-text with a nominal monospace width.
- `src/render.rs:929-934` uses advanced shaping for Nushell box-drawing characters while plain ASCII uses basic shaping.
- `src/render.rs:751`, `src/main.rs:424`, and `src/scene.rs:437-451` place the cursor and IME from the unchanged canonical Orbit column.
- `src/render.rs:1445-1474` checks combining-mark width and shaping selection but does not prove exact per-cell advances or aligned box-drawing junctions.
- 2026-08-09 focused measurement against the exact locked cosmic-text build: `lucca@pop-os:~$ d` contains 17 narrow cells, whose grid width is 153 px, but shapes to 142.8 px with origins advancing about 8.357 px. The approximately 10.2 px accumulated difference matches the native cursor gap.
- 2026-08-10 native Eon dogfood: Nushell `ls` and `which yazi` tables visibly render horizontal borders and vertical separators at inconsistent columns even though Orbit supplies a regular cell grid.

Impact: HIGH for basic terminal credibility.
Effort: M.
Implementation risk: MED because the same metric participates in text, cursor, resize, IME, selection, and pointer geometry.
Confidence: HIGH.

## Scope

In scope:
- The existing text-layout and cell-metric owner in `src/render.rs`.
- A failing-then-passing deterministic regression for narrow text, style boundaries, and Unicode box-drawing tables using the exact selected text stack.
- Existing scene and canonical tests only where needed to preserve combining and wide-cell behavior.
- Native COSMIC Wayland dogfood at representative scale factors.
- `docs/CONTRACTS.md` proof/check updates for touched proved contracts and README LOC accounting.

Out of scope:
- Orbit cursor or frame correction, ORBS/EONW changes, terminal parsing, Nushell configuration, font settings UI, renderer replacement, an owned glyph atlas, dependency upgrades, workspace topology, or unrelated visual restyling.
- Changing semantic input, resize, selection, accessibility, or clipboard behavior.

## References Before Code

Required:
- Current `src/render.rs`, `src/scene.rs`, input/resize geometry, tests, `docs/CONTRACTS.md`, and the selected seam and rollback condition in `docs/CRATES.md`.
- Exact locked glyphon 0.12.0 and cosmic-text 0.19.0 source.

Comparison only:
- COSMIC Terminal at `7daf10e3b540f612cbc48973469656ecd1635dfc`, limited to measured monospace width, shape-run caching, and cell projection. It is GPL-3.0-only; inspect mechanisms but copy or adapt no source.
- Ghostling at `f9034e43a50a2f3a8101e35497f486090c1ddd6e` and libghostty-rs at `72ac98f292879bf9f788fcbb11238c562a1eebe6`, limited to cell-placement and render-loop ownership.

Conditional:
- Newer glyphon/cosmic-text or another text renderer only if focused proof shows the selected versions cannot preserve exact cell advances. That requires the crate gate and explicit user approval before manifest edits.

Rejected:
- Cursor-only offsets, per-prompt or Nushell compensation, changing canonical Orbit coordinates, separate text and interaction grids, disabling Unicode shaping globally, or an ASCII-only workaround.

## Acceptance and Verification

- A deterministic test fails before the fix and proves after it that N adjacent narrow cells occupy exactly N authoritative cell widths with no accumulated cursor-boundary drift.
- A representative multi-row Nushell-style box table keeps every vertical separator and intersection on the same authoritative columns across plain, bold, colored, and Unicode runs.
- Existing combining graphemes, wide head/tail cells, spaces, preedit, cursor shapes, selection, and hit testing retain their accepted geometry.
- `cargo fmt --check`
- `cargo check --locked`
- `cargo test --locked`
- `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `git diff --check`
- Native COSMIC Wayland dogfood with short and long prompts plus Nushell `ls` and `which` tables at scale 1 and the active HiDPI scale shows no length-dependent gap, overlap, disconnected border, or shifted junction.
- Advance the exact VEN-C1 proof revision and any other touched proved owner; record the exact accepted Orbit proof unchanged.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop for the crate gate and user decision if the selected glyphon/cosmic-text versions cannot provide exact grid alignment without brittle compensation.
- Stop for explicit contract choice if the fix changes terminal column counts, ORBS, semantic input, resize semantics, or another repository owner.
- Do not weaken shaping, fallback, combining-mark, wide-cell, IME, accessibility, or selection behavior to satisfy one screenshot.
- Stop if source or proof revisions drift materially before implementation.

## Maintenance Notes

One metric owner must govern terminal text placement, cursor and background rectangles, IME, input hit testing, selection, and resize. Prefer the smallest robust correction inside the selected stack. The scene-renderer audit remains blocked on this issue so that it audits the corrected grid rather than a known defect.

title: Refine pane-stack appearance with rounded frames enabled by default
description:
## Outcome
Eon's accordion pane stack has rounded borders around each pane by default, alongside the accepted pill-shaped tabs, while every fitting pane stays discoverable and selectable. pane_frames defaults to true; false removes the decorative frames. Investigate compact labeled headers/separators within that chosen design instead of full-width filled header bars.

## Contract routing and ownership
VEN-C8 presentation change; preserve its ordered headers, one expanded terminal, selected-body adjacency, overflow, keyboard and AccessKit contracts. Venus owns geometry, draw, hit testing and accessibility. Eon owns product configuration, launch serialization and installed delivery in eon:eon-pane-stack-delivery-jfo; a new setting requires an accepted Venus startup contract before that downstream implementation. Platform: isolated Wayland dependency.

## Prerequisites and reference gate
User decision on 2026-09-09: pane_frames is included and defaults to true, with rounded borders around each pane. Exact radius, spacing and header treatment remain visual-design choices; enabling frames and their default are settled. Activated by the user on 2026-09-09.
Required before code: current scene::WorkspaceScene, header_heights, render::build_workspace, input/accessibility paths, VEN-C8/VEN-C19, accepted ven-599, ven-rounded-adaptive-tabs-vdf and ven-pill-workspace-tabs-rg4. Discovery Venus source 8211e8f773140429398154ca3f2230bd09fed1df retains full-width pane fills and header height of 1.5 cell heights. Compare Nova's current stack/frame behavior at an exact revision; existing Canario route is comparison-only. Use existing captures or an isolated surface without taking desktop focus.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Compare current bars and compact labeled headers/separators within rounded pane frames on one, three and overflowing panes; choose and record radius, spacing and header treatment before implementing. Frame each pane's visible bounds, including collapsed pane headers and the expanded pane's header/body, without changing the one-expanded-terminal model.
- Preserve readable pane identity/cwd, selected versus keyboard-focus distinction, usable pointer hit areas, hover feedback and full accessible labels. Thin drawn lines do not imply one-pixel click targets.
- Keep the selected terminal immediately after its header, bounded tiny-window geometry, long-label handling and all otherwise fitting sibling headers.
- Prove pane_frames = true draws rounded borders around each pane. pane_frames = false removes decorative frames while preserving collapsed-pane handles, selection, keyboard focus and usable hit areas. Preserve terminal content and grid accounting at rounded edges.
- Verify keyboard/pointer/AccessKit alignment and the Venus candidate's actual appearance at ordinary and narrow sizes. Publish the accepted exact Venus source and visual decision for eon:eon-pane-stack-delivery-jfo, which owns installed Eon acceptance. Retain fractional-scale and screen-reader qualification where unproved.
- Admit and prove the pane_frames startup boolean in Venus, including invalid values before window creation and both rendering modes. eon:eon-pane-stack-delivery-jfo owns the persistent product setting and default-on launch policy; this Venus issue never writes Eon configuration.

## Scope boundary

title: Consolidate in-flight viewport request ownership
description:
## Outcome and preserved contract

Consumer: one attached Venus terminal surface. Trigger: an ordinary signed ScrollVertical commit, a synthetic upward-selection tick, gesture cancellation, its ordered Orbit response, or ReturnToLive. Result: one local owner records which commit/tick is outstanding and the cancellation information needed to reconcile its response; an ordinary commit and a selection tick cannot be represented as concurrently outstanding. Queue rejection leaves no phantom pending request. Cancellation retains correlation until response or attachment retirement. Preserve existing VEN-C7 behavior, including ReturnToLive ordering and rejected-tick wheel-input preservation. This is an internal ownership refactor, not a confirmed runtime bug or behavior expansion.

Effort M; implementation risk MED; confidence HIGH in the shared invariant, MED in maintenance payoff. Platform classification: neutral shared interaction state, proved through native x86_64 Linux Wayland/Vulkan. Preserve the partial VEN-C16 status and existing macOS limits.

## Current evidence

Inspected clean edge HEAD 4b5cc0cf8e5c3567f83d94ac0862adbf0c0e23d1 on 2026-10-04; rebaseline before implementation.

- src/application.rs:78-88: TerminalScroll owns in_flight plus batch_cancelled.
- src/application.rs:339-344: SelectionAutoscroll separately owns in_flight.
- drive_terminal_scroll (:1529) and drive_selection_autoscroll (:1572) implement mutual exclusion by examining the other controller.
- handle_transport (:2337-2385) infers response origin from those flags. Ordinary upward scroll and a selection tick may both carry requested_rows == -1, so the wire distance is insufficient correlation.
- send (:2793) and handle_transport (:2482) gate/release ReturnToLive by checking both representations.
- TerminalScroll::cancel (:194) and SelectionAutoscroll::cancel (:410) intentionally retain sent-request correlation after gesture cancellation.
- src/transport.rs:390: send means bounded queue admission (Full/Closed), not encoding or successful wire delivery; asynchronous InvalidInput is a separate event.

Closed ven-12v/.2 already established the thin native host and rejected splitting by file size. This bead removes independently mutable representations of one exchange instead of repeating that extraction.

## Ownership and scope

Use one private concrete typed pending state for an ordinary signed commit, including cancellation correlation, or a synthetic selection tick. Remove the old independent in-flight/cancelled-batch truth. An enum or equally small existing-code representation is sufficient; it may remain inside application.rs.

Keep TerminalScroll arithmetic/kinetics and SelectionAutoscroll edge, cadence, and required-presentation logic separate. Keep preview_pending and its existing response semantics separate: preview traffic is not covered by commit/tick exclusivity. The existing pending_return_to_live action flag may remain; its wait/release condition consumes the single pending owner.

Application retains native focus/occlusion, selection readiness, geometry and settled resize, actual send admission, SessionModel application and notices, successful-presentation observations, redraws, and event-loop deadlines. SessionModel and Orbit retain canonical frame/terminal authority.

Likely implementation surface: application.rs controllers, drive/send/response/cancellation paths and their existing tests; necessary VEN-C7 proof metadata and README LOC under repository rules. No Orbit/Eon implementation, new contract, wire/schema or pin change, dependency, module/crate requirement, history cache, physics change, generic controller/effect framework, renderer change, selection queue/gate extraction, platform expansion, packaging, or downstream promotion.

## Prerequisites and reference gate

No blocking open Bead found. Implement serially under the one-active-frontier rule; this work has no functional dependency on Eon's documentation bead.

Before code, record the required Execution baseline and Reference gate. Required: current VEN-C7 and touched VEN-C1/C2/C3/C4/C8/C16 boundaries; complete current application/model/transport paths and cited tests; closed ven-selection-upward-autoscroll-161.1 and ven-scrollback-return-to-live-j8u; routed REFERENCES sections for scrolling, native selection, continuous output and live-output acceptance; exact Orbit b6cecf8f2ee35570b41cfdc578b095889d917fe2 request/outcome and pending-publication behavior. Orbit src/runtime.rs::Presentation::deferred_vertical and defer_vertical retain one canonical typed request; inspect that producer boundary as an admission/correlation comparison, not a client implementation to copy or a reason to merge Venus preview state.

Consumed producer proof mapping from the canonical Orbit index: ORB-C4 and ORB-C6 -> ea9fd28ce0908f218cf65d4e6df368f0a4e565f5; ORB-C5 -> aed0bcb7e9ad08c8e3e086c7dad0a0eb3ef16672; ORB-C8 and ORB-C9 -> b6cecf8f2ee35570b41cfdc578b095889d917fe2. Venus consumes their preserved behavior through ORBF v2/ORBS v13 at exact b6cecf8f2ee35570b41cfdc578b095889d917fe2; current upward-selection consumer proof is 773c6bab7d3e21e0b0d7d942c9bba72260a08b42. Revalidate these identities against the current index and pins.

Pinned winit 7c209ec5bebbd2963f75a39f79b320af6b03f72c event/redraw guidance is comparison-only while native scheduling stays unchanged; required if scheduling changes become necessary, which requires re-evaluating scope first. GTK/Kitty physics and other terminal histories are comparison-only historical evidence; their algorithms and surrounding systems are outside this bead. No new crate/tool capability is needed; use owned Rust state and the standard library.

## Acceptance and cheapest falsifiers

1. One authoritative pending representation distinguishes ordinary signed commits from selection ticks, including the identical -1 wire-distance case. The two origins cannot coexist. Response classification and ReturnToLive waiting no longer combine independent controller in-flight flags.
2. Gesture cancellation retains the sent request's origin. A later rejected selection tick preserves wheel input accumulated after release. Attachment/lifecycle retirement clears correlation; unsolicited/mismatched outcomes keep the existing protocol-order failure.
3. Full/closed send admission leaves no phantom pending exchange. Preserve asynchronous encoding-failure handling separately.
4. Existing native observation still sends zero ReturnToLive messages while a commit/tick is outstanding, then exactly one after the applicable ordered result or rejection, and none for the queued action after local encoding failure.
5. Numerical physics, preview eligibility, cadence, presentation gates, native input, wire bytes and exact pins retain their behavior. Report the ownership simplification; file splitting or a LOC target is not acceptance.

Reuse/adapt existing tests rather than creating a parallel suite:
- cargo test --locked --bin yazelix-venus terminal_scroll_coalesces_one_signed_batch_without_losing_distance
- cargo test --locked --bin yazelix-venus rejected_selection_tick_preserves_wheel_input_after_release
- On an isolated Wayland display with Vulkan and disposable XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/WAYLAND_DISPLAY/TMPDIR: timeout 30s cargo test --locked --bin yazelix-venus live_output_keeps_application_input_admitted_before_repaint -- --ignored

The native regression at application.rs:5309-5412 observes actual encoded ReturnToLive messages. Preserve those scenarios when moving pending-state setup to its new owner. Add only missing focused coverage for origin/admission transitions.

Finish with the required Rust route in docs/DEVELOPMENT.md once per unchanged candidate (fmt/check/test/clippy, locked where documented), diff/LOC checks, and the touched owner's indexed native proof. Record exact candidate/environment/results and advance proof metadata only after source acceptance; leave unexercised macOS gaps explicit. Downstream Eon adoption remains a separate accepted-revision integration step.

## Stop and rejected alternatives

Stop/rebaseline if the shared pending invariant or cited code has materially changed, producer/pins conflict, a new contract/dependency is required, or the refactor needs to absorb model, transport, presentation, native scheduling, or terminal ownership. Reject a full ViewportController: it would need most of Application's legitimate integration context. Reject a forwarding facade that keeps the old flags, a general message dispatcher, or collapsing preview and commit/tick traffic into one restriction.

Planning evidence only: no runtime checks were run during issue creation.

title: Place New tab beside the Eon tab strip
description:
## Contract
Consumer: a full Eon user creating tabs from the native one-row bar.
Trigger: tabs fit, overflow, or the window narrows.
Result: New tab sits immediately after the last tab when all tabs fit, and remains pinned at the tab-region edge during overflow. Quota, Shortcuts, and active-tab Close retain their existing priority and behavior. Keyboard focus, hit testing, tooltip, and AccessKit use the same button rectangle.
Failures: no overlap or inaccessible active tab at narrow widths; tab gaps and the button never become drag targets or terminal input.

## Prerequisites and reference gate
Preserve VEN-C21 and EON-C21. Consume accepted Orbit f8ad14e5195109ba8cb421f30e5ae4a9619a1419 and the current EONW v6 contract without changing either. Read docs/REFERENCES.md native Eon Bar routing. Required before code: current Venus Scene, renderer, input, and AccessKit owners; Nova Bar bfbf8a7be28b69f9d822c0843bf2dd5066dd49e3 as comparison; GNOME header-bar and Apple toolbar guidance for grouping and width priority. Conditional on changing drag semantics: patched winit drag contract. Comparison only: VS Code status-bar and Ghostty titlebar guidance. Rejected scope: Nova code reuse or a new UI dependency.

## Scope
Change Venus-owned header geometry and the smallest meaningful regression checks. Update VEN-C21 proof after acceptance; consume the exact accepted Venus revision in Eon, align EON-C21 and user-facing docs, build and refresh the active Eon profile without restarting live Sessions. No protocol, Orbit, Eon tab policy, new control, second row, configuration, or platform promise.

## Acceptance
At ordinary width the plus button directly follows the rightmost tab. With overflow it stays visible at the tab-region edge as tabs scroll. At 960, 320, and 100 pixels, the active tab and required controls remain reachable and disjoint. Pointer, keyboard, tooltip, focus, and AccessKit activation still invoke only CreateTab; drag and terminal hit exclusions hold. Focused Venus and affected Eon Rust/Nix checks pass; one isolated installed native Wayland observation proves the layout and action. Existing live supervisors are preserved.

## Stop conditions
Stop if the layout requires an EONW change, duplicate geometry ownership, another native control, or weakening active-tab priority.

title: Show positional tab numbers and add direct Alt-digit focus
description:
## Outcome and contract

Consumer: a person using the Venus Eon workspace. Trigger: Eon supplies an ordered tab snapshot, the order changes, or the person presses physical Alt+1 through Alt+9 or Alt+0. Result: each visible and accessible tab name uses its current one-based position while the existing stable tN remains the action and AccessKit identity; Alt+1 through Alt+9 focuses positions 1 through 9 and Alt+0 focuses position 10 through the existing FocusId action. A position absent from the current snapshot is consumed without a workspace action or terminal input. Alt+H/L remains available beyond position 10.

This changes VEN-C8 only. It consumes unchanged EONW v5 at Eon 0cc8f477298681ae3945903e8fdb5852d487c5ab and unchanged Orbit presentation/input contracts at accepted Orbit ea9fd28ce0908f218cf65d4e6df368f0a4e565f5. No wire, topology, lifecycle, Session, or platform contract changes.

## Scope

In scope: Venus scene labels, AccessKit names, native physical-key shortcut dispatch, current documentation, and the smallest focused regression coverage. Resolve position from each accepted snapshot; do not persist an index.

Out of scope: changing EONW, stable tab IDs, tab limits, multi-digit chords, shortcut configuration, a mode, new dependencies or modules, Orbit/Eon production changes, macOS support work, or native acceptance claims.

## Reference gate

Required before code: current VEN-C8, workspace scene/application/accessibility/input owners, exact EONW v5 Snapshot and FocusId definitions at Eon 0cc8f477298681ae3945903e8fdb5852d487c5ab. Comparison only: Nova 57b0c8621894c59d058d7ba7d91464864b7c4917 positional tab labels and direct Alt-digit bindings. Existing winit physical KeyCode mapping is an already-selected mechanism; inspect exact locked source only if its digit identity is ambiguous.

## Acceptance

1. A reordered snapshot proves visible and accessible positions derive from order, not tN, while hit testing and actions retain stable IDs.
2. Focused shortcut proof covers Alt+1, Alt+9, Alt+0, a reordered stable ID, and an unavailable position consumed without action; non-Alt digit input remains terminal input.
3. Focused and complete locked Rust checks pass; README, VEN-C8 and LOC stay current. Native installed acceptance and Eon pin adoption remain separate after an immutable Venus candidate.

title: Present the Eon tab directory picker modal
description:
## Contract routing

Introduces candidate VEN-C18 and consumes Eon EON-C18 through dependency-free EONW v3 at exact pushed Eon source 96119f29ca2e3ec4ad19bbe272708b07d588429a. Preserves VEN-C1, VEN-C2, VEN-C3, VEN-C4, VEN-C7, VEN-C8, VEN-C16, and exact Orbit ORBS v10 proof 59975e9176f5caf8b78dc3273e88d9ecbb75dc3f.

## Observable contract

Consumer: one person using terminal, tab, or pane focus in a live full-Eon Venus workspace.

Trigger: press Alt+Z when the EONW v3 snapshot has no directory picker.

Result: Venus captures the physical shortcut and sends one PickTabDirectory action. When Eon publishes a picker endpoint bound to the active tab, Venus attaches that endpoint, keeps the tab bar visible, hides pane headers and the prior selected terminal, and renders the picker in the tab body with a one-cell inset on every side when the grid permits it. Input and accessibility focus enter the picker while the local prior workspace focus is retained; removing picker state reattaches the selected durable pane and restores that focus.

Important failures: standalone Venus keeps raw Alt+Z; repeated or modified shortcuts do not create extra actions; invalid v3 state is rejected by EONW; endpoint loss remains visible and bounded; gutters receive no terminal pointer input; narrow grids collapse the inset rather than produce invalid geometry; no stale picker remains after Eon removes it.

## Ownership and scope

Venus owns physical shortcut precedence, modal projection, effective focus/input, rendering, hit testing, accessibility, and attachment selection. Eon owns picker creation, command, tab binding, lifecycle, mutation, cleanup, and notices that require product action. Orbit owns the terminal Session and PTY.

In scope: advance the one exact EONW pin to v3; use v3 directly in the existing model/transport; add the one shortcut; project the explicit directory_picker through the existing workspace scene, renderer, input, and AccessKit owners; focused deterministic checks; docs and LOC after source proof.

Out of scope: Eon runtime implementation, fzf/zoxide packaging, Yazi, generic popup/modal/floating-pane APIs, simultaneous surfaces, animation, dimming, transparency, configurable geometry, arbitrary commands, another protocol/schema, Orbit changes, EonTerm behavior, or another platform. Platform disposition: neutral protocol/scene/input logic inside the already isolated Linux Wayland host; no new platform dependency.

## Reference gate

Required before code: current AGENTS.md and this issue; VEN-C1/C2/C8/C16; exact Eon 96119f2 EONW v3 source, EON-C18, LICENSE, and reference route; current Venus workspace model/transport/scene/render/input/accessibility owners; exact locked winit, wgpu, glyphon, AccessKit, and Orbit contracts already selected by this repository.

Comparison only: Nova f1beb34fe6060cfa2c0201d7f8095f6ef707f467 for the accepted Alt+Z outcome and margin comparison; Zellij 910339e219b17f4e2ffd4a2cb6e35cccc7246493 and Kitty 54416498c89e1d07e5079c49d15470dd0d947ce7 for terminal-backed in-place/overlay lifecycle. No source reuse.

Rejected scope: WezTerm native InputSelector, Yazi picker plugins, native Venus ranking or fuzzy matching, copied Nova code, generic modal framework, second socket, and inferred picker state.

## Dependency gate

Capability: consume Eon-authored semantic picker action and authoritative tab-bound endpoint. Selected: advance the existing dependency-free Apache-2.0 eon-workspace-protocol 0.1.0 pin from exact Eon 7bb50873 to exact pushed Eon 96119f2 and consume v3 directly. No dependency is incapable because v2 lacks both values. A Venus-owned schema or adapter duplicates trust-boundary validation; an in-place v2 extension breaks exact consumers. Lock/native/build/transitive cost remains unchanged. Replacement remains one exact pin edit. User approval is the 2026-08-25 continue direction after the v3-only state was explained.

## Acceptance

- Alt+Z in full-Eon workspace mode sends exactly one PickTabDirectory on initial press from any workspace focus and consumes repeat/release; standalone mode retains Orbit input.
- A picker snapshot selects its endpoint for presentation, forces effective terminal input/IME/accessibility focus without overwriting prior workspace focus, and returns to the durable selected endpoint/focus when removed.
- The tab bar remains visible; pane headers and prior content are absent; the picker terminal uses one cell of horizontal and vertical inset within the tab body, collapsing safely to zero on undersized grids.
- Rendering, hit testing, pointer coordinates, resize, clipping, cursor, notices, and accessibility use that same geometry. Picker mode exposes no actionable pane nodes.
- Existing v3 validation rejects wrong-tab and aliased endpoints; Venus adds no duplicate validator or inferred state.
- Exact locked Rust checks pass on one source candidate. Native Wayland dogfood proves shortcut capture, open/close endpoint switching, geometry, focus restoration, and raw Alt+Z preservation outside workspace mode once an Eon producer exists.

## Stop conditions

Stop if the slice requires a generic modal abstraction, dual v2/v3 compatibility, copied protocol schema, new dependency, Orbit change, simultaneous surface composition, or Eon runtime behavior in this repository. Native end-to-end picker dogfood remains blocked until Eon implements the producer.

title: Preserve authoritative Orbit completion across writer loss
description:
## Contract routing

Hardens proved VEN-C3 and VEN-C4 without adding or changing a product contract. Preserve VEN-C1, VEN-C2, VEN-C7, VEN-C8, and canonical ORBS v4 consumption. Consume Orbit ORB-C3, ORB-C4, and ORB-C7 at accepted proof and exact pinned package revision 7f067b30e97d0b4787a7c6c0bbe3dd8a80a61c2c.

Consumer: the Venus attachment lifecycle and client-visible connection status.

Trigger: Orbit has flushed an authoritative terminal ServerMessage such as Exited and closed its socket while the independent Venus writer observes a socket error before the reader drains the buffered message.

Result: the authoritative decoded server terminal outcome wins exactly once. A writer-side socket observation may become the final loss only when no authoritative terminal message is available. Important failures: completion must not hang, leak a worker, reorder ordinary effects, admit late events after final completion, or turn invalid local input into transport loss.

This issue is open and unclaimed. Before claiming, reconfirm that no other implementation owns the active cross-repository frontier and rebaseline against the exact accepted Orbit proof.

Audit ven-audit-venus-transport-model-w0s found this at Venus 4f799fef1c3e10e86d70b708708f7c2702d7aee8. Impact HIGH. Effort M. Implementation risk MED. Confidence HIGH.

## Evidence

- src/transport.rs:395-421 starts independent writer and reader workers that publish into one EventQueue.
- src/transport.rs:424-440 publishes writer-side socket loss before Shutdown::Both.
- src/transport.rs:261-320 stops on the first RetryableLoss, Lost, Busy, Incompatible, or Exited and rejects every later event.
- src/transport.rs:565-590 tests first-terminal-event-wins but does not distinguish a writer observation from an authoritative buffered server terminal message.
- src/main.rs:449-514 converts a winning RetryableLoss into Lost and may schedule retry; src/model.rs:251-254 would preserve an authoritative Exited code.
- Exact Orbit 3ee7c80005f3d2bbe81e539799327803716f6174 src/main.rs:159-165 queues Exited and flushes before teardown.
- Audit comment 321 records a Linux socketpair reproduction where the client write returned BrokenPipe errno 32 and a later read still returned the already-buffered EXITED bytes.
- ven-separate-transport-loss-state-retry-policy-iqe owns the downstream no-transport model transition and retry policy. It does not own this upstream transport-completion arbitration.

## Scope

In scope:
- src/transport.rs Orbit reader/writer completion ownership, EventQueue terminal admission, and focused deterministic transport tests.
- src/main.rs or src/model.rs tests only if needed to prove that the delivered authoritative event reaches the existing owner unchanged; do not change their retry or connection-state policy here.
- docs/CONTRACTS.md proof revisions for hardened VEN-C3 and VEN-C4 after a proof-bearing source commit, README LOC accounting, and CHANGELOG only for the accepted user-visible correction.

Out of scope:
- Orbit or Eon changes, protocol fields, compatibility adapters, timeout policy, retry/backoff policy, connection-state redesign, remote transport, alternate transports, new modules, and dependencies.
- The Failure then Accepted then RetryableLoss state defect owned by ven-separate-transport-loss-state-retry-policy-iqe.
- Queue byte accounting, owned separately by audit finding F2.

## Reference and dependency gate

Required before code:
- Current AGENTS.md, this Bead and comments, audit ven-audit-venus-transport-model-w0s comments 320-322, docs/CONTRACTS.md, docs/REFERENCES.md lifecycle and transport entries, and docs/CRATES.md.
- Current src/transport.rs, direct Application and SessionModel consumers, and all focused transport/lifecycle tests.
- Exact pinned Orbit package 3ee7c80005f3d2bbe81e539799327803716f6174, especially session framing and Client finish_session, plus accepted proof 9d6d2bb37f20ab4ad9e186c7bc715eabef43e757.
- Rust 1.96 standard-library UnixStream clone and shutdown documentation or source for the relied-on completion behavior.

Conditional:
- Exact Linux socket documentation only if the deterministic test exposes behavior not specified by Rust std.
- The downstream retry-policy issue only when its source candidate has changed the same caller assertions.

Rejected:
- Async runtimes, a new coordinator module, protocol acknowledgements, sleep-based race tests, arbitrary grace periods, and producer changes. No manifest edit is expected; stop for the crate gate and user approval before one.

Platform disposition: isolated platform dependency. The owner is the existing Unix local transport. Linux is the required proof environment; the code shape must remain credible for macOS Unix sockets, but no macOS behavior is proved and no new blocker is introduced.

## Implementation notes

1. First add one deterministic regression using UnixStream pairs and synchronization barriers, not sleeps: encode and send Exited, close the peer, force a client write failure before reader drain, then require the authoritative Exited outcome.
2. Give reader and writer completion one existing transport-level owner. Treat a writer socket error as an observation until the reader either delivers an authoritative server terminal message or establishes that none can be decoded.
3. Preserve prompt bounded loss when no server terminal message exists. Do not wait indefinitely for a peer that remains open, and do not add a third worker or general state machine.
4. Preserve ordinary server-message FIFO, frame coalescing, one wake transition, invalid-input behavior, and rejection of events after the final outcome.
5. Coordinate but do not combine with ven-separate-transport-loss-state-retry-policy-iqe; that issue owns Application and SessionModel policy after a loss is delivered.
6. Commit and verify the source candidate first. Then advance VEN-C3 and VEN-C4 proof metadata, update LOC and any applicable changelog, close against the source commit, and commit metadata plus closure together.

## Acceptance criteria

1. When Orbit bytes for Exited are buffered before peer close and the Venus writer observes BrokenPipe first, Venus delivers exactly one Exited with the exact code and does not let RetryableLoss or Lost win.
2. A write failure with no complete authoritative terminal message still produces exactly one existing bounded loss promptly, wakes the application, and terminates the workers.
3. Busy, Incompatible, closing Failure, EOF, malformed or partial messages, invalid local input, action-channel closure, and explicit Transport drop preserve their existing semantics except for authoritative-message precedence.
4. Ordinary Accepted, Frame, CopiedText, ClipboardWrite, and Failure ordering and frame coalescing remain unchanged.
5. No deadlock, wall-clock race test, worker leak, second completion owner, new module, dependency, protocol change, or retry-policy change is introduced.
6. The deterministic regression fails on the audited implementation and passes on the source candidate without relying on scheduler luck.
7. Locked Rust checks, Clippy, diff check, LOC accounting, exact proof metadata, and Beads flush pass.

## Verification

- A focused deterministic transport test for buffered Exited versus writer failure should fail before and pass after.
- Focused tests should also prove write loss without a server terminal result and current first-final-event behavior.
- cargo fmt --check
- cargo check --locked
- cargo test --locked
- cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings
- git diff --check

All commands must exit 0 on the materially unchanged source candidate. Record test counts, environment, exact Orbit identities, and Linux-only proof limits.

## Stop conditions

- Stop if the exact accepted Orbit lifecycle or package pin has changed; rebaseline and reread the producer before code.
- Stop if correctness requires an Orbit field, acknowledgement, compatibility window, timeout contract, new dependency, or new Venus module.
- Stop if prompt loss and authoritative-message precedence cannot both be proven without a new contract choice.
- Stop if another active issue owns src/transport.rs completion or EventQueue terminal behavior.
- Stop rather than folding in Application retry/model work from ven-separate-transport-loss-state-retry-policy-iqe.

## Maintenance notes

Transport completion has one invariant: a decoded authoritative server terminal outcome outranks a concurrent local writer observation, while absence of such an outcome still fails promptly and visibly. The cheapest falsifier is the barrier-controlled buffered-Exited and BrokenPipe regression. No external implementation reference or source reuse is selected.

Adopted mechanisms:
- Orbit 7f067b30 queues Exited, flushes the ordered output queue, and then closes the accepted Unix socket after child completion. A terminal closing Failure is likewise flushed without appending a later Exited.
- Rust UnixStream::try_clone duplicates the same socket, and Shutdown::Both makes pending/future I/O on both halves return. The recorded Linux socketpair reproduction confirms that a writer BrokenPipe can occur while the reader clone still has a complete buffered Exited.
- Ownership consequence: the reader is the sole owner of peer/socket completion after the writer is spawned. A non-encoding writer failure ends only the writer; it neither publishes a competing terminal event nor shuts down the shared read half. The existing reader then drains complete server messages in wire order and classifies the eventual EOF/reset. Dropping the client input sender retains the existing explicit Shutdown::Both cancellation path.
- The focused deterministic UnixStream-pair regression will buffer an exact Exited, force the writer failure, and prove that no writer loss is queued and the reader still decodes the exact code. Existing full-close-without-message coverage remains the prompt bounded-loss proof.

- No EventQueue arbitration redesign, timeout/grace period, protocol acknowledgement, third coordinator, async runtime, dependency, module, retry-policy/model change, schema mirror, producer change, compatibility window, or platform promise.
- Ordinary Failure is not distinguished as terminal by ORBS v4, so this work preserves its existing ordering/notice semantics rather than inventing a closing-failure heuristic.
- The solution is isolated Unix transport behavior and remains Linux-proved; it introduces no additional macOS blocker.

Ownership, license, and code shape:
- Venus owns local transport arbitration; Orbit remains the terminal/session authority and protocol owner. No source is copied.
- Rust standard-library evidence is under the Rust project's MIT/Apache terms. Orbit is inspected as the exact project-owned internal source dependency; its existing missing public-distribution license metadata remains unchanged and no distribution claim is widened.

title: Keep kinetic scrolling alive across presentation timeouts
description:
Contract: for one focused visible Venus surface, a transient presentation-texture timeout may skip one visual frame but must not cancel an active precision gesture, kinetic velocity, accumulated distance, preview request, or authoritative Orbit viewport movement. An occluded surface and existing lifecycle, input, authority, transport, recovery, and error boundaries retain explicit cancellation.

Prerequisites: proven VEN-C7 ownership; exact accepted Orbit ORBS v10; locked wgpu 30 and winit 0.30.12 surface/event contracts. No protocol or child behavior change.

Reference gate: inspect VEN-C7, every PresentOutcome producer and consumer, TerminalScroll cancellation caller, the locked wgpu CurrentSurfaceTexture contract, locked winit Wayland occlusion support, and comparable terminal viewport behavior.

Scope boundary: Venus presentation-outcome handling plus aligned VEN-C7 proof, changelog, LOC, and Beads state. Explicit user authorization later expanded delivery to the exact immutable Venus revision, Eon component pin, lock, manifest, proof metadata, and active eon profile refresh. No emulator, replay framework, renderer abstraction, physics setting, dependency, wire change, client history, other component pin, process restart, or platform expansion.

Acceptance: the existing deterministic elapsed-time regression and complete outcome/source inspection prove skipped cadence and timeout preserve motion; timeout still requests redraw; the distinct occluded outcome and all existing lifecycle/error paths cancel. Complete locked Venus and Eon checks pass, optimized continuous-output dogfood is user accepted, immutable proof and exact installed profile agree, and live supervisors remain untouched.
design: Treat presentation as a fallible observer of scroll state. Keep the existing elapsed-time TerminalScroll integrator and renderer-owned timeout retry. PresentOutcome::Deferred remains the retryable timeout; the distinct PresentOutcome::Occluded preserves cancellation because locked winit does not supply that event on Wayland. Add no timer, persistent visibility state, renderer abstraction, or protocol.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The existing deterministic elapsed-time physics regression proves skipped cadence does not alter total fling integration, and timeout handling contains no scroll-cancellation side effect.
2. CurrentSurfaceTexture::Timeout skips the frame, requests redraw, and preserves logical scroll state; CurrentSurfaceTexture::Occluded maps distinctly and cancels it.
3. Presented cadence, elapsed-time decay, distance accumulation, one in-flight Orbit batch, compatible-frame preview retention, lifecycle cancellation, renderer recovery, and errors remain unchanged.
4. Optimized native continuous-output dogfood confirms hard flings decay naturally without an abrupt presentation-driven stop, and VEN-C7 names the immutable accepted proof.
5. VEN-C7, changelog, LOC, Beads, exact Eon component pin and lock, complete affected Rust/Nix checks, installed profile identity, and preserved live supervisors agree. No dependency, module, protocol value, configuration surface, replay system, or platform promise is added.

title: Preserve authoritative cell placement while shaping terminal graphemes
description:
## Problem

Fix the Venus native renderer regression proven by orb-vt-unicode-baselines-i32 comments 478 and 479. Wide, grapheme, and emoji ZWJ rows preserve correct Orbit cell widths but later cell delimiters drift because adjacent same-style cells are concatenated into one shaped string and only the run start plus aggregate width survive.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Launch ucs-browser 2.3.5 as the real PTY child of the exact installed Eon composition with terminal grapheme mode 2027 enabled.
2. Render `--wide 2`, `--graphemes`, and `--zwj` through native Venus.
3. Capture only the uniquely titled Venus toplevel with `grim -T` and inspect the repeated vertical cell delimiters. Later delimiter pairs shift after affected glyphs; ZWJ components also expand across later cells. Comment 479 records exact native captures, hashes, and connected-component measurements.

## Contract Routing

Hardens proved VEN-C1 and preserves VEN-C2, VEN-C3, VEN-C4, VEN-C7, VEN-C8, VEN-C11, and VEN-C15. Consumes canonical ORBF v1 proof 9d6d2bb37f20ab4ad9e186c7bc715eabef43e757, ORBS v3 proof 3ee7c80005f3d2bbe81e539799327803716f6174, and Orbit ORB-C4 through ORB-C6. Adds or changes no product contract.

## Scope

Eon Desktop Venus owns native materialization. Work only in the existing scene-to-render text placement path and its focused tests. Retain each Orbit-authored cell position while allowing shaping inside its complete grapheme, or use an equivalently constrained existing shape. Do not change Orbit widths or wire formats, create a second terminal grid, disable advanced shaping globally, add a dependency or module, or fold in the separate protocol-validation adoption bead.

This is a successor regression to closed ven-ogd, not a reopening of its published proof. ven-ogd covered ordinary accumulated monospace advance and simple tables; it did not prove multi-scalar, fallback, bidi, or ZWJ placement.

## Acceptance Criteria

The canonical criteria are stored in this Bead acceptance_criteria field.
design:
Before the first edit, claim this Bead, record its execution baseline, and pass the Eon Desktop reference gate. Required before code: the exact installed and current Venus scene/render sources; locked glyphon and cosmic-text source for shaping and placement behavior; closed ven-ogd evidence and proof; canonical Orbit frame schema and ORBF/ORBS proofs; and orb-vt-unicode-baselines-i32 comments 478 and 479 with their capture hashes. ucs-browser 2.3.5 and wcwidth 0.8.2 are comparison tools only.

Start with one deterministic failing test at the existing scene/render boundary: adjacent cells containing narrow, width-two, combining, multi-scalar grapheme, emoji ZWJ, RTL or bidi, fallback, and delimiter text must retain their canonical x positions. Then make the smallest root-cause change in the shared placement path. A new direct crate, feature, module, protocol field, or compatibility surface is a decision gate and stops this Bead.

After local checks, run only the focused ucs-browser wide, grapheme, and ZWJ pages through the real composed stack on isolated Xvfb and native Wayland. Identify the unique Venus toplevel and capture it with grim -T. Use a connected-component or equivalent pixel check for delimiter collinearity so the result does not depend on judging glyph outline width. Keep existing sessions and desktop focus untouched.

Portability disposition: neutral placement policy with Linux native proof; no macOS claim.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A deterministic regression test fails on the old behavior and proves that every authoritative cell start remains exact across narrow, wide, combining, multi-scalar grapheme, emoji ZWJ, RTL or bidi, fallback, and delimiter cases.
2. Venus preserves Orbit-authored cell boundaries while shaping each complete grapheme; joined sequences may render joined or fall back, but they cannot displace later cells. No second terminal model or client-side width policy is introduced.
3. Focused wide, grapheme, and ZWJ pages pass through the real pinned Orbit/ORBF/ORBS/Venus path on isolated Xvfb and native Wayland. Machine-inspectable captures show collinear cell delimiters; no human inspection is required.
4. Existing style, fallback, bidi, cursor, selection, input, accessibility, resize, detach, and reattach behavior remains green under the canonical checks for VEN-C1 and preserved contracts.
5. cargo fmt --check, cargo check --locked, cargo test --locked, cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings, repository governance, and git diff --check pass. README LOC scorecard is refreshed for Rust changes.
6. docs/CONTRACTS.md records VEN-C1 as hardened at the accepted proof revision and the exact checks; CHANGELOG.md records the accepted renderer correction. No dependency or contract surface is added.
notes: Recommended first implementation frontier from the 2026-08-14 baseline because the failure affects many Unicode rows and has a local owner with no expected crate decision. Expected implementation risk: medium. Main trap: preserving run-level shaping convenience after it has discarded authoritative per-cell placement.
close_reason: Second fresh-eyes pass completed without source changes; the only further simplification is correctly deferred until canonical Orbit topology validation is adopted.

title: Attribute Venus memory and reduce confirmed avoidable retention
description:
## Outcome and contract

For Eon and EonTerm users starting Venus and rendering terminal text, attribute the client's baseline and first-output memory, then remove the largest confirmed avoidable allocation or retained copy that fits the existing owner. Preserve presentation, ordered font fallback, authoritative cell geometry, input, accessibility, and bounded renderer failures. No numerical reduction is promised before attribution; a measured finding that no worthwhile local optimization exists is a valid outcome.

This preserves VEN-C1, VEN-C4 and VEN-C19; it creates no new product contract. Preserve VEN-C2, VEN-C7, VEN-C8, VEN-C11, VEN-C14 and VEN-C18 where exercised. Fractional native scale, VEN-C8's partial proof, and broader compositor coverage remain qualified. Platform classification: isolated Wayland dependency; x86_64 Linux, native Wayland and Vulkan only.

## Why and evidence

User approved creating this one bead on 2026-09-08 after eon-zlf. Effort M; implementation risk MED; confidence HIGH in the profiling target, unknown in achievable savings.

- Eon's closed eon-zlf report at Eon commit 418c3889b7a79808c05e6b7ead9d27d30337f496, docs/benchmarks/eon-zlf-2026-09-08.md:40-65, measures Venus at approximately 67 MiB idle and 78-79 MiB after printable output. Orbit starts around 1.8 MiB; the supervisor stays around 2 MiB. Venus is the first attribution target, not proven waste.
- Durable baseline report and raw process rows: https://github.com/Yazelix/eon/blob/418c3889b7a79808c05e6b7ead9d27d30337f496/docs/benchmarks/eon-zlf-2026-09-08.md and adjacent eon-zlf-2026-09-08.csv.
- The baseline used accepted Venus ec80e36625dec73544c0cb64becf4b135c932a63 and Orbit 91999d79546422b49bdbc124166a65859d0bd872. It covers 219 launches across four products at actual 120x30; the expanded 240-run plan stopped for desktop focus theft. It does not measure GPU allocations, long-term growth, or equal retained-history row counts. PSS depends on shared mappings and this warm host.
- At inspected Venus HEAD 9d72b9fce3ef274bce5c2663175c12ffc88ed67e, src/render.rs:173 FontSetup owns FontSystem; :644 Renderer owns SwashCache, TextAtlas, shaped text and vertex buffers; :834 initializes text caches/atlas; :1084 already trims the atlas after presentation. These are attribution sites, not diagnosed leaks. docs/CRATES.md:79 records the existing GPU/text owners.

## Scope and prerequisites

In scope: attribution of anonymous allocations versus file/library/driver mappings; font and glyph caches, shaped text and CPU/GPU staging or rendering buffers in the existing renderer. Investigate src/render.rs and its direct Scene/Application callers only as needed to identify the real owner. Prefer removing duplicate work or unnecessary retention to adding a cache policy, configuration or abstraction.

The benchmark prerequisite is complete; no unresolved blocker or parent epic is needed. Before implementation, claim this bead and record the required Execution baseline and Reference gate. Reconfirm accepted runtime identities and preserve unrelated work and live Sessions.

Consume unchanged ORBF v1 / ORBS v10 through Orbit 91999d79546422b49bdbc124166a65859d0bd872 and EONW v4 through Eon c305453bba4fe50c29f65e829b9cd65af31ced8a. Relevant inherited proof mappings in docs/CONTRACTS.md: ORB-C4/C6 at 9d6d2bb37f20ab4ad9e186c7bc715eabef43e757; ORB-C3/C4/C7 via ORBS v4 at 7f067b30e97d0b4787a7c6c0bbe3dd8a80a61c2c; ORB-C5/C8/C9 via ORBS v10 at 91999d79546422b49bdbc124166a65859d0bd872. Preserve their recorded limits; no protocol change.

Out of scope: Orbit history/engine optimization, supervisor optimization, replacing the renderer or text stack, dependency upgrades, new modules or product settings, a general benchmark framework, platform expansion, Eon manifest/profile rollout, and benchmarking all competing terminals again. A later Eon rollout requires its own selected integration work after an accepted Venus source.

## Reference gate

Required before code: relevant entries in docs/REFERENCES.md, docs/CRATES.md and docs/CONTRACTS.md; the frozen eon-zlf report; exact locked glyphon 0.12.0, cosmic-text 0.19.0/fontdb 0.23.0 and wgpu 30.0.0 source for the attributed owner. Inspect allocation, cache lifetime and release semantics rather than assuming trim frees process memory.

Required comparison before choosing a cache/font code shape: COSMIC Terminal 7daf10e3b540f612cbc48973469656ecd1635dfc, routed terminal.rs/terminal_box.rs, limited to independently useful text/cache lifetime mechanisms. GPL-3.0-only inspection does not authorize copying or incorporation.

Conditional: authoritative documentation/source for any profiler actually needed, at an exact version, and Linux proc accounting definitions when interpreting mappings. Prefer existing native/disposable tools; no runtime dependency or manifest edit is selected. Follow the crate gate if a dependency becomes necessary. Foot/Ghostty benchmark rankings are comparison evidence only, not an architecture or savings target.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Retain reproducible attribution with exact source/artifact, tool and environment identities, workloads and raw evidence. Explain the idle cost and roughly 11 MiB first-output increase as far as measurement permits; name unresolved mappings rather than labelling them heap waste.
2. If avoidable retention is established, state the owned cause and meaningful savings threshold before changing it; implement the smallest correction. Otherwise close with the measured reason no worthwhile local change was justified.
3. For a correction, compare unchanged baseline and candidate under the same fixed workload/environment with repeated fresh-process PSS and USS samples, distributions and controlled or explicitly recorded mapping sharers. Include idle, first screen and a representative loaded Unicode workload. Do not infer GPU-memory savings from PSS or history efficiency from emitted row counts. Do not rerun the 219-launch cross-product matrix.
4. Preserve actual glyphs/fallback, Nerd Font regular/bold geometry, cursor and interaction for the changed surface. Reuse existing corpus and renderer checks; add only the cheapest falsifier for a confirmed regression. Follow the repository Rust route when Rust changes: cargo fmt --check; cargo check --locked; cargo test --locked; cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings. Record exact native evidence needed for the changed owner; deterministic/headless checks do not prove visual quality.
5. Preserve desktop focus. Prefer background, isolated or non-activating observations. Take focus only if no workable alternative exists or alternatives give materially worse results, and explain why beforehand. Never rerun the old active-desktop harness as-is or terminate live user Sessions. Any different compositor/device measurement is a distinct baseline, not a drop-in continuation of eon-zlf.
6. Record the attribution or accepted correction and all remaining limits. Validate Beads state, cited paths/contracts, LOC and git diff --check; do not advance unrelated contract proofs.

## Stop conditions

Stop at evidence-backed attribution if no useful local reduction exists. Return for a scope decision if the result requires a new owner, contract, module, renderer, runtime dependency or cross-repository change. Reject arbitrary memory targets, indiscriminate cache clearing, reduced fallback coverage and a bounded startup-name allocation as speculative megabyte optimizations. Do not broaden into long-running leak or multi-window scaling work without separate selection.

Report and raw proof retained; Eon rollout remains separate.

title: Prove macOS accessibility, lifecycle, and identity
description:
## Outcome and contract

Complete the macOS accessibility, application lifecycle, and caller-identity boundary on the accepted opaque/input-capable native host.

- Consumer: a person, including a VoiceOver user, launching Venus directly or from an approved caller on aarch64-darwin.
- Trigger: native activation, focus, accessibility query/action, caller identity, attention request, close, or application quit.
- Result: the existing scene-derived AccessKit tree is exposed through the AppKit adapter with correct focus and actions; caller identity reaches the strongest honest pre-distribution native surface; close/quit terminates Venus while the Orbit Session survives and can be reattached.
- Important failures: accessibility activation before scene availability, stale focus/action routing, denied accessibility access, invalid identity, repeated resume/close, renderer failure, or Orbit loss remains bounded and cannot create another tree, terminate Orbit, or claim bundle identity that is not present.

This advances VEN-C16 and hardens VEN-C1, VEN-C4, VEN-C14, VEN-C17, VEN-C18, and VEN-C20 on macOS while preserving their Linux behavior and every shared semantic/accessibility owner.

## Ownership and platform decision

The accepted opaque foundation and macOS interaction child are prerequisites. Existing Accessibility owns one scene-derived tree, node identity, actions, focus, alerts, and popup projection. accesskit_winit owns AppKit adaptation. Existing Application/ApplicationHandler owns resume, focus, attention, close and exit policy. The caller-supplied application ID remains one validated product identity input; platform mapping belongs at the existing native window/application boundary.

First determine what identity is honestly available to an unsigned, Nix-first native executable versus an application bundle. Preserve the caller value where winit/AppKit exposes a stable title, accessibility application name, activation identity, or equivalent. Do not fabricate a bundle identifier, add packaging/signing, or silently reduce distinct Eon/EonTerm identities. If durable macOS identity requires an app bundle owned by Eon distribution, record the exact gap and hand it to the existing Eon Apple Silicon epic instead of copying that policy into Venus.

Close and quit act only on the Venus process. Orbit owns its Session/process lifecycle; the proof must reattach another client to the same accepted Session after Venus exits. No PTY/process supervision, application delegate, second event loop, second accessibility tree, or compatibility layer is selected.

## Reference gate

Read this bead and parent, accepted foundation/input proofs, VEN-C1/C4/C14/C16/C17/C18/C20 and their checks, current Accessibility and Application lifecycle owners, docs/REFERENCES.md and docs/CRATES.md, exact AccessKit/accesskit_winit macOS source, exact winit AppKit lifecycle/attention/activation behavior, and official Apple VoiceOver accessibility, application activation, close/quit, process identity, and bundle identity documentation. Inspect Rio and Ghostty only as exact comparisons for unresolved lifecycle or accessibility-host questions. Record identities, honest identity ceiling, adopted/rejected mechanisms, and first falsifying checks. Stop before a native binding, entitlement, new module, packaging surface, or dependency.

## Scope and verification

In scope: AppKit AccessKit activation/update/action/focus behavior, scene and popup accessibility, native focus and attention, repeat resume, create/show/close/quit, caller identity mapping available before distribution, bounded failures, Orbit survival, and reattachment.

Out of scope: changing accessibility semantics/tree ownership, new screen-reader commands, global shortcuts, pasteboard/input mechanics, transparency/blur, Eon composition or bundle policy, signing, notarization, installer metadata, Intel macOS, dependency additions, and a support claim.

Cheapest proof:

1. Existing deterministic accessibility, lifecycle, popup, identity, and failure tests remain the shared oracle; add only macOS-specific policy checks that can fail independently.
2. Linux locked route and current AT-SPI/application identity behavior remain green.
3. Real Apple Silicon observation covers initial VoiceOver discovery, terminal and workspace order/names, focus, representative Click-backed Open/Copy and shortcut-viewer actions, alerts, close/quit, repeat launch, attention, and successful reattachment to the same Orbit Session.
4. Record the exact native identity exposed and any bundle-owned limitation without widening VEN-C17.

If VoiceOver proof or honest caller identity cannot be exercised on available hardware, stop and ask the user; compilation or AccessKit tree inspection alone is not acceptance.

comments.text:
Reference gate — 2026-09-17. Inspected this issue and parent ven-prove-venus-apple-silicon-macos-nm7; accepted foundation and input children; VEN-C1/C4/C14/C16/C17/C18/C20; docs/REFERENCES.md and docs/CRATES.md; current Accessibility, Application, launch identity, attention, focus, close, quit, and reattachment owners; exact AccessKit 0.24.1 checksum d3b7f7f8, accesskit_winit 0.33.2 checksum d5b41e63, accesskit_macos 0.26.3 checksum ce02dc63; and winit fork 7c209ec5bebbd2963f75a39f79b320af6b03f72c. AccessKit already supplies the complete native seam: Venus creates the adapter before first show, its direct activation handler synchronously returns the latest complete scene-derived tree, accesskit_macos subclasses the existing NSView to expose children/focus/hit testing, winit forwards native focus before Venus handles the event, and native actions return through the event-loop proxy to the one existing target owner. Adopt this unchanged; reject a second tree, AppKit binding, native module, entitlement, or dependency.

Exact winit AppKit source sets Regular activation policy for an unbundled executable, emits CloseRequested from windowShouldClose, closes native windows and emits Destroyed during application termination, builds the default Quit menu from NSProcessInfo.processName, and maps request_user_attention to NSApplication.requestUserAttention. Venus already creates at most one window across repeated resumed callbacks, exits its event loop on CloseRequested or Destroyed, and never owns Orbit lifetime. Apple documents that regular apps appear in the Dock; requestUserAttention is inert while active and is cancelled by activation; close removes one NSWindow while app termination is an NSApplication lifecycle; VoiceOver must be tested with VoiceOver or Accessibility Inspector. Sources: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appkit/nsapplication/activationpolicy-swift.enum, https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appkit/nsapplication/requestuserattention(_:), https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appkit/nswindow/close(), https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appkit/nsapplicationdelegate, and https://developer.apple.com/documentation/accessibility/integrating-accessibility-into-your-app.

Identity ceiling: Apple defines CFBundleIdentifier as the system-wide app identity stored in the bundle Info.plist, and bundle name/spoken-name keys as the user-facing and accessibility names. Winit explicitly observes no bundleIdentifier for this unbundled Nix executable and falls back to regular activation. NSProcessInfo.processName is non-unique and Apple warns that mutating it can affect defaults and is not thread-safe. Therefore the honest pre-distribution native identity is only the yazelix-venus executable/process/default-menu identity plus the current Venus or terminal window and AccessKit labels. The validated caller --application-id cannot distinguish Eon from EonTerm on macOS without an Eon-owned app bundle or separate packaged executable identity; do not fabricate or mutate one in Venus. Sources: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/bundleresources/information-property-list/cfbundleidentifier, https://developer.apple.com/documentation/bundleresources/bundle-configuration, https://developer.apple.com/documentation/foundation/processinfo/processname, and https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appkit/nsrunningapplication. This exact bundle-owned gap is retained for the existing Eon Apple Silicon epic; VEN-C17 remains Linux-only. Rio and Ghostty were not inspected because exact selected-stack and Apple primary sources resolved every code-shape question. First local falsifiers are the existing accessibility/action/focus and launch-identity tests; native falsifier remains VoiceOver discovery/actions plus close, Quit, attention, relaunch, same-Orbit reattachment, and observed process/bundle identity on physical Apple Silicon. No production or test change is justified before that observation.

title: Prove Metal transparency and macOS blur behavior
description:
## Outcome and contract

Prove the existing shared renderer presents correct terminal transparency on Metal and resolve the bounded macOS behavior of the existing blur request.

- Consumer: a person launching accepted native Venus with the current background-opacity and background-blur inputs on Apple Silicon macOS.
- Trigger: create or recover the native surface at opacity 1.0, 0.88, or 0.0, optionally with the boolean blur request.
- Result: Metal uses one shared renderer and a correct native alpha mode so text, cursor, selection, explicit cell backgrounds, workspace chrome, hit testing, IME, and accessibility remain usable at all three opacities. Blur is either visibly accepted by the existing native path or truthfully reported as unsupported without launch failure.
- Important failures: unavailable premultiplied alpha, wrong color conversion, opaque native backing, stale/recovered surface state, click-through, unreadable content, or unsupported blur fails or degrades explicitly and never creates a second renderer or silent false claim.

This advances VEN-C11, VEN-C15, and the presentation portion of VEN-C16 on macOS while preserving the accepted Linux Vulkan/Wayland behavior and all shared scene/render owners.

## Ownership and simplification boundary

The first three Apple Silicon children are prerequisites. Existing window_attributes owns transparent/blur requests. Existing Renderer surface configuration, surface_alpha_mode, clear color, text/rectangle encoding, presentation, loss recovery, and redraw scheduling own alpha materialization. Scene and model continue to supply the same colors and geometry.

Opacity is required. Native blur is best effort. Qualification found no Apple delta in the selected winit fork and did not prove a macOS blur implementation. First inspect the exact winit/AppKit behavior. If the existing dependency cannot provide native blur, keep macOS blur unsupported with one bounded truthful outcome; do not add an AppKit binding, visual-effect view, blur strength, fallback tint, shader imitation, dependency, entitlement, or second setting. Linux keeps its accepted compositor-owned blur path unchanged.

## Reference gate

Read this bead and parent, accepted preceding child proofs, VEN-C1/C4/C8/C11/C14/C15/C16 and their checks, current window/render/clear/surface recovery owners, docs/REFERENCES.md and docs/CRATES.md, exact wgpu 30 Metal surface/alpha behavior, raw-window-handle and winit AppKit window/transparency/blur source, and official Apple window opacity/compositing behavior. Inspect current Rio and Ghostty only for exact native alpha/backing-layer questions that remain unresolved. Record exact identities, whether blur is supported, adopted/rejected mechanisms, and first falsifying checks before code. Any direct native binding, dependency, fork change, or new rendering owner stops for user approval.

## Scope and verification

In scope: native window transparency request, Metal surface alpha selection, premultiplied clear/presentation, recovery, controlled opacity values 1.0/0.88/0.0, truthful boolean blur capability, and preservation of visible/interactive/accessibility surfaces.

Out of scope: blur strength, animations, materials, vibrancy, fallback tint, click-through windows, per-pane opacity, separate shaders/renderers, palette changes, packaging, Eon composition, signing/notarization, Intel macOS, and a support claim.

Cheapest proof:

1. Existing deterministic alpha/clear/geometry tests remain shared; add only a macOS policy check that can fail independently.
2. Linux locked route and accepted Wayland opacity/blur behavior remain green.
3. Controlled real-M1 captures at 1.0, 0.88, and 0.0 prove background composition while preserving text, cursor, selection, explicit cell backgrounds, workspace chrome, hit testing, IME, accessibility, resize, and surface recovery.
4. The same environment proves visible blur acceptance or the exact bounded unsupported result; docs and contracts make no stronger claim.

If correct Metal transparency requires another renderer, unsafe native ownership, or an unapproved dependency, stop and ask the user. Unsupported native blur alone is an acceptable simplified outcome.
