title: Render compositor-paced pixel and kinetic scrollback
description:
## Outcome and contract routing

Intentionally revise `VEN-C7` after exact accepted Orbit proofs from `orb-orbit-history-byte-budget-ykn` and `orb-orbit-signed-scroll-batch-x12`. Venus makes retained-history scrolling direct, pixel-smooth, compositor-paced, and interruptible while Orbit remains the sole authority for routing, cells, viewport state, edges, and presentation revisions.

Consumer: one attached Venus user on supported native Linux Wayland.
Trigger: native `MouseWheel` input arrives while the terminal surface is eligible for retained-history scrolling.
Result:

- `PixelDelta` moves the presented history directly at 2.0 presented pixels per native input pixel. Venus keeps a fractional vertical remainder strictly smaller than one cell height and clips/translates only an accepted complete Orbit frame plus its revision-bound adjacent preview.
- Crossing whole-row boundaries produces one coalesced bounded signed Orbit commit. At most one commit is in flight; Venus installs the atomic authoritative frame/next-preview result and retains exact unapplied pixel distance.
- A phase-complete precision/continuous sequence may fling on `Ended`. Release velocity comes from a bounded recent 150 ms delivery-time sample, is clamped from hardware evidence, and decays by actual elapsed time: `v1 = v0 * exp(-4 * dt)`, `dx = (v0 - v1) / 4`. Stop when less than one pixel of theoretical distance remains.
- `LineDelta` accumulates fractional logical lines and moves three rows per whole logical step with no Venus-generated post-release inertia. Rapid turns accelerate through their native event count.
- Redraw is compositor-paced: input requests redraw immediately; active direct or kinetic motion advances on `RedrawRequested`, calls `pre_present_notify` immediately before presentation, retains FIFO, and requests another redraw only while motion remains active.

The constants above are private measured starting points, not public compatibility promises. When two safe candidates preserve responsive low-speed control, exact distance, bounded stopping, and routing, prefer the livelier response.

## Input and failure semantics

Pinned winit does not expose Wayland `AxisSource`, hardware event time, or useful per-device identity. Therefore Venus must not claim universal finger detection, physical input-to-screen latency, or per-device state.

- Phase-complete `PixelDelta`: two presented pixels per native input pixel; eligible for release momentum.
- `PixelDelta` without a usable `Ended`: direct pixels only; no fling and no permanent redraw loop.
- `LineDelta`: three rows per logical step; no synthetic inertia.
- Terminal-owned mouse tracking or alternate-screen alternate-scroll: use Orbit's existing preview route gate, forward only the physical event through the canonical semantic mouse path, and cancel synthetic motion.
- libinput button scrolling may arrive as continuous pixel input. Add no middle/right-button binding or source guess; dogfood the existing platform translation.

Cancel motion and pending preview state on a new gesture, opposite-direction input, keypress, mouse-button/selection start, cursor leave, focus loss, occlusion, resize, pane/session or endpoint change, reconnect/loss, stale or incompatible authority, and transition to terminal-owned routing. Stop firmly at history edges without bounce.

Background PTY output does not itself cancel history motion or jump live. Venus installs the newer authoritative frame, preserves only valid pending distance/velocity, reacquires its adjacent preview, and resumes without rendering stale rows. A semantic key that Orbit accepts cancels motion and returns to the live bottom under existing `ORB-C8`.

## Reference gate

Inspected 2026-08-24:

- Venus `082ecb7e9e2a8dde009db28e481a68bee2d3ace6`: whole-row input currently expands movement into repeated Orbit wheel work; FIFO presentation and glyphon 0.12 are already accepted owners.
- Eon Sessions `bad068a775140a1a4c4a157a0b9b64fba46f8202`: ORBS v5 already supplies a revision-bound one-row `PreviewVertical`; `orb-orbit-signed-scroll-batch-x12` owns the required atomic batch extension.
- Patched winit 0.30.13 `fb45fbf901fbe70cc9a877b5d651d0b60c206b08`: on Wayland, discrete axes map to `LineDelta`, continuous axes to `PixelDelta`, axis-stop maps to `Ended`, source/time are discarded, and one constant device identity is reported.
- Wayland pointer semantics: finger axis-stop is guaranteed; wheel/continuous stop may be absent: https://wayland.app/protocols/wayland
- Winit redraw/presentation API: https://docs.rs/winit/0.30.13/winit/window/struct.Window.html
- WGPU FIFO/latency contract: https://docs.rs/wgpu/latest/wgpu/enum.PresentMode.html and https://docs.rs/wgpu/latest/wgpu/type.SurfaceConfiguration.html
- GTK main `04275027fc556b1b0f3935e2f502fc356e88227b`: compositor frame clock, 150 ms velocity capture, elapsed-time exponential friction at 4 s^-1, and hold cancellation informed the small physics model.
- Kitty `7f71461` demonstrates per-pixel scrolling and precision-only momentum, but its fixed 8 ms timer, per-tick 0.96 decay, velocity stacking, and reported hold/long-tail behavior are rejected.
- Glyphon 0.12 accepts fractional text-area positions and reuses its atlas, but still prepares and uploads visible vertices each redraw. Reuse it first and measure before changing renderer architecture.

The unreleased-winit question is deliberately outside this slice and tracked separately after installed dogfood. Core behavior must work without the optional Wayland hold protocol.

## Acceptance

1. Deterministic checks cover fractional accumulation across both directions and cell boundaries, `LineDelta` fractions and three-row gain, phase-complete versus incomplete `PixelDelta`, the 150 ms estimator, velocity cap/threshold, exact elapsed-time decay at different frame cadences, the sub-pixel stop rule, reversal, every cancellation, and history edges.
2. One in-flight batch plus coalescing preserves signed distance under fast input. Atomic batch responses install matching frames/previews; stale responses, routing changes, partial edge movement, reconnects, and background-output rebasing never show invented or stale rows.
3. Slow precision movement visibly follows sub-row distance rather than whole-row steps. Stronger releases produce faster/longer bounded movement; no runaway tail, bounce, oscillation, lost distance, or motion after an incomplete phase sequence.
4. Terminal-owned physical scroll preserves exact existing PTY routing and receives no synthetic momentum. Discrete wheel, continuous button-scroll if present, touchpad, selection, live-output return, focus/occlusion, resize, pane changes, and endpoint loss are exercised on real supported Wayland hardware.
5. Motion is driven by compositor redraw callbacks rather than a nominal 16 ms scroll timer. Compare wgpu desired frame latency 1 versus 2 and adopt 1 only if evidence improves event-delivery-to-present-submit latency without worse completion/cadence or instability.
6. Record event-delivery-to-redraw/present-submit time, redraw cadence/missed callbacks, requested/applied pixels and rows, Orbit batch/frame time, glyphon prepare/GPU-submit time, outstanding/coalesced distance, fling duration, and stopping distance. Do not label these measurements physical-input or visible-presentation latency.
7. Prove the fixed 120×40 workload on available 60 Hz and 120+ Hz displays. If glyphon preparation, Orbit batching, or the one-row preview cannot sustain controlled compositor-paced motion, record the measured bottleneck and stop before adding a renderer, timer, thread, or multi-row protocol.
8. `VEN-C7`, crate/reference records, changelog, exact Orbit import, focused checks, and all affected locked Rust surfaces agree at one accepted revision.

## Scope boundary and stop conditions

In scope: existing winit events, one adjacent preview, fractional presentation, one coalesced Orbit batch, minimal private physics, compositor-paced FIFO redraw, and acceptance instrumentation.

Out of scope: multi-row overscan, offscreen/shader renderer architecture, refresh-rate discovery, guaranteed 60/120/144 Hz, actual presentation-feedback protocols, Wayland input-timestamp protocols, device/source heuristics, velocity stacking, bounce, repeated-flick acceleration, public tuning, new mouse bindings, worker threads, physics dependencies, X11/Xwayland, macOS, and additional architectures.

Stop and return to the user before adding any out-of-scope mechanism, if one-row preview correctness fails, if hardware needs per-device policy, or if the first measured bottleneck cannot be fixed within the existing owners.

Reference gate — implemented candidate evidence, 2026-08-24
- Exact owner consumed: Eon Sessions ORBS v6 source 780f5d746175b4a9b71df57c51ed4bfcc4c4c375. Venus will not reconstruct Orbit routing, edges, cells, revisions, or history.
- Exact native source: patched winit 0.30.13 fb45fbf901fbe70cc9a877b5d651d0b60c206b08. Its Wayland pointer adapter prefers discrete axes as LineDelta, maps continuous axes to physical PixelDelta, maps axis stop to Ended, and documents that discrete wheels may have no Ended. request_redraw plus pre_present_notify is the existing native compositor-paced path. Axis source, Wayland event time, and useful device identity are unavailable, so no source/device claim or heuristic is added.
- Platform semantics: wl_pointer axis-stop terminates sources that supply it and permits kinetic scrolling; discrete/value120 is wheel-step data. Pinned winit has already made the only units available to Venus, so Venus consumes those values rather than adding a Wayland protocol owner.
- Existing graphics owners: wgpu 30.0.0 retains guaranteed FIFO; default desired maximum frame latency 2 remains unchanged until dogfood measures 1 versus 2. glyphon 0.12 accepts fractional TextArea positions/bounds and the existing rectangle batch clips geometry, so the candidate translates/clips the existing scene plus one accepted preview row before considering renderer work. No crate gate is activated because no dependency or capability owner changes.
- Comparisons inspected at exact revisions: GTK main 04275027fc556b1b0f3935e2f502fc356e88227b uses a 150 ms recent delivery-time history, frame-clock ticks, and 4 s^-1 exponential deceleration; adopt those three small mechanisms. Reject GTK overshoot/bounce, velocity accumulation, hold timer, general scroll widget, and public tuning. Kitty 7f71461a9de44f71f631db29d50bcb3e866988b8 demonstrates sub-row presentation and precision momentum; reject its fixed timer, frame-dependent 0.96 decay, shared/global momentum machinery, velocity stacking, source-specific platform code, and configuration surface. Comparison source is not copied.
- One owner/flow: a single private Venus terminal-scroll state owns fractional pixels, phase history, kinetic velocity, pending signed rows, one in-flight commit, and the revision-bound preview. Input events add distance; RedrawRequested advances time; Orbit responses atomically rebase the state; renderer only consumes an offset and resolved adjacent row. Cancel at the accepted lifecycle/input boundaries.
- First falsifiers: focused tests for accumulation/physics/coalescing and a renderer check that exactly one adjacent row covers every remainder |y| < cell height. If conversion or clipping needs a second frame/schema, multi-row overscan, another renderer, timer/thread, device heuristic, or unreleased winit, stop and return to the user.

The scroll driver no longer schedules frames; each native input requests one redraw, transport refresh already requests one, and render requests continuation only while kinetic velocity is nonzero. The corrected isolated release build was launched against the same Orbit session, CPU dropped, and the user confirmed the problem is fixed.
- Two focused red checks exposed and now protect additional bugs: release after a pause reused samples older than the 150 ms window (2400 px/s instead of zero), and an invalid atomic next-preview could install its frame before returning UnexpectedMessage. Ended now records its zero-distance timestamp to expire stale samples; batch preview conversion/validation completes before FrameReducer mutation.
- Cancellation now always clears non-visible gesture/sample/fractional state even when no redraw is needed. This prevents a zero-distance Started phase or sub-line remainder from surviving focus/input lifecycle cancellation.
- Isomorphic simplifications: removed the full DrawRow clone from every scroll drive; append glyph runs into one scene allocation instead of allocating once per terminal row; removed two private one-line state accessors; removed redundant transport redraw scheduling; updated the stale README ORBS v5 identity and wording. No contract, wire value, ordering, errors, side effects, security, lifecycle, or visible scroll gain changed by these refactors.

title: Route native selection gestures and automatic copy
description:
## Outcome and contract

Change `VEN-C7` so one presented Venus surface provides native text selection without taking terminal semantics from Orbit:

- Uncaptured left press and drag select cells.
- Double press and drag select words.
- Triple press and drag select logical lines.
- When the terminal captures mouse input, ordinary pointer events remain terminal-owned; Shift forces the same host-selection gestures.
- Successful release copies Orbit's exact frozen text to both the ordinary Wayland clipboard and primary selection.
- `Ctrl+Shift+C` continues to copy explicitly to the ordinary clipboard.

Venus owns native surface hit routing, event delivery, modifiers, and Wayland clipboard effects. Orbit owns terminal-versus-host routing, click classification, boundaries, selected presentation, and copied text.

## Evidence and references

Current source and accepted prerequisite:

- Venus candidate `1034817bbe2352fb4b1026bce6b1f02eedd67e37` sends every native left-pointer sequence through Orbit, preserves ordered completion, and applies automatic release copy to both Wayland targets.
- Accepted Orbit source `59975e9176f5caf8b78dc3273e88d9ecbb75dc3f` owns ORBS v10 terminal-versus-host routing, cell/word/logical-line gestures, frozen copied text, and authoritative `SelectionFinished` revisions.
- Winit 0.30.13 supplies button state and native event delivery; it supplies neither click count nor a physical event timestamp.
- Existing winit and wl-clipboard-rs dependencies cover native delivery time and both Wayland clipboard targets.
- Reference-gate comments record the exact WezTerm, Kitty, Alacritty, Zellij, Ghostty, winit, and Orbit comparisons.

Adopt established cell, word, and line gestures, Shift bypass of mouse reporting, ordered authoritative completion, and automatic release copy. Reject local word or line inference, a second click recognizer, a new dependency, unreleased winit, and copied terminal code.

Impact: HIGH. Effort: M after the Orbit routing prerequisite. Risk: MED at input routing and clipboard failure boundaries.

## Implementation

1. Consume one exact accepted Orbit revision that owns terminal-versus-host left-pointer routing and host gesture semantics; add no compatibility adapter.
2. Update `VEN-C7` before production code.
3. Map native left-button phases, viewport position, presented revision, modifiers, and bounded event-delivery monotonic time into that Orbit contract.
4. Let Orbit decide terminal capture versus host selection; Shift forces host selection.
5. On successful release, write Orbit's returned frozen text to both Wayland clipboard targets. Preserve explicit ordinary clipboard copy as a separate effect.
6. Cancel through existing state ownership on focus or cursor loss, resize, pane or session change, reconnect, stale presentation, terminal-routing transition, and endpoint failure.

## Acceptance

- Single, double, and triple press-drag gestures visibly select cells, words, and logical lines in both directions.
- Mouse-reporting Yazi, Neovim, and tmux receive ordinary clicks unchanged; Shift performs host selection.
- Paths, URLs, punctuation, wrapped lines, wide cells, and combining graphemes display the exact Orbit result without Venus reconstruction.
- Release makes the selection available through Wayland primary paste and ordinary `Ctrl+V`; `Ctrl+Shift+C` remains an explicit ordinary-clipboard copy.
- Clipboard refusal, stale revision, invalid ordering, focus loss, resize, reconnect, and endpoint loss leave no partial or stale local gesture.
- Focused native-event, routing, rollback, and clipboard-target checks pass, followed by the unchanged-candidate Venus Rust and Nix route and installed Wayland dogfood.
- Closure records exact Venus, Orbit, ORBS, winit, compositor, package, and profile revisions plus remaining limits.

## Scope and stop conditions

In scope: `VEN-C7`, native left-pointer surface routing, Shift override, release clipboard effects, exact Orbit consumption, focused checks, contracts, references, changelog after acceptance, and LOC.

Out of scope: terminal boundary or capture inference in Venus, custom separators or thresholds, settings UI, middle-click paste, right-click extension, block selection, drag autoscroll, OSC 133 command-output selection, hyperlinks, search, other display systems, and other operating systems.

Stop if the exact accepted Orbit revision no longer owns terminal-versus-host left-pointer routing, if Venus would need local click or terminal-semantic inference, if correct Wayland clipboard delivery requires a new dependency or winit upgrade, or if another active frontier owns `VEN-C7`.

- Accepted Orbit source/proof d9b22eb294f8f42b4f49324fd5467eab239c2917 and acceptance metadata 93e38b35dd378b9a189f1ff0b1a61ea33682446f: ORBS v8 SelectionAction carries frame revision, surface position, press time, and cancel/copy; handle_selection always applies the host libghostty gesture. Mouse tracking is consulted only in Orbit's separate ordinary mouse/wheel path. ORBF frames carry no mouse-routing state and ORBS returns no typed routing outcome for left buttons.
- Pinned winit 0.30.13 plus Venus patch fb45fbf901fbe70cc9a877b5d651d0b60c206b08: WindowEvent::MouseInput carries state/button/device only, so Venus can supply delivery time with std::time::Instant but cannot discover terminal capture or a native click count.
- Pinned wl-clipboard-rs 0.9.3: the existing Regular/Primary mapping is sufficient; no dependency or upgrade is needed for release-to-primary.
- Current behavior comparisons: WezTerm f93d90350075d3e42566e0557ca36e82ffdcbec1 bypasses application mouse reporting with Shift before native mouse assignments; Kitty 479872838f7536ab87b8133471eb49d06804951b maps left selection only when ungrabbed and Shift bypasses grabs; Alacritty 7dd7b5b09e06ca58daadfb12bd45a9aa8fa716f2 separates host selection/copy from terminal mouse modes; Zellij b0bd3e1e7f530db8879e8cbde79de245e6101a8a documents Shift as the escape from its mouse handling; current Ghostty 8867c37c55b578b9eb4cfaba41cb9023e557176d and pinned mechanism a887df42c56f6de86c0fe6da9c4eeca37931e083 decide mouse reporting versus selection at the terminal-state owner, then apply the gesture and copy on release. These were behavior comparisons only; no source is copied.

Adopted: Orbit remains the terminal-state/routing and selection-semantics owner; Venus remains native event/timing and clipboard-effect owner. std::time::Instant and the installed clipboard dependency cover their portions.

Rejected:
- Always send SelectionAction: breaks Yazi/Neovim/tmux mouse capture.
- Keep Shift-only selection: fails the chosen uncaptured-selection contract.
- Infer capture from prior wheel outcomes or UI state: stale, incomplete duplicate terminal semantics.
- Send both Mouse and Selection and undo one later: invents terminal input or visible selection.
- Add a Venus click recognizer, dependency, unreleased winit, or ORBF mouse-mode guess: violates the contract and stop conditions.

Blocker: the accepted ORBS v8 boundary cannot express one left-pointer sequence that Orbit authoritatively routes to either terminal input or host selection. The minimum correct prerequisite is an Orbit-owned routed left-pointer gesture carrying native phase, position, modifiers, revision/time on press, and Shift-forced host intent; Orbit pins/routes the sequence from current terminal state and reuses its existing mouse encoder or libghostty Gesture. That is a breaking cross-repository contract change and is not authorized by this Venus-only implementation run. No production, test, manifest, contract, or dependency edit was made.

title: Request compositor-owned background blur
description:
## Contract routing

This issue proposes new product contract `VEN-C15`: compositor-owned background blur requests for one Venus surface. Before any production, test, manifest, or generated edit, the executing agent must obtain user approval for the exact contract text and index it in `docs/CONTRACTS.md`. It preserves `VEN-C1` through `VEN-C14`, canonical ORBS v3 at `orbit-protocol` revision `3ee7c80005f3d2bbe81e539799327803716f6174`, and EONW v1 at `eon-workspace-protocol` revision `4af395aea06c230ee6b18cf0755ae25915c0b88d`. Orbit and Eon workspace protocols remain unchanged.

The user selected Plan A on 2026-08-14 America/Sao_Paulo: retain winit, temporarily pin the exact v0.30.13 backport of `ext-background-effect-v1`, and prove native COSMIC Wayland behavior. This planning decision does not waive the repository contract, reference, or crate gates.

Candidate observable contract:

- Consumer: Eon, EonTerm, or a direct caller launching one Venus surface.
- Trigger: launch with `--background-blur`; absence preserves the current no-blur request.
- Result: Venus asks the selected native window backend for full-surface background blur before showing the window. On the required COSMIC Wayland proof target, winit selects `ext-background-effect-v1`; translucent terminal-default pixels reveal compositor blur while explicit cell backgrounds, selection, inverse video, workspace chrome, notices, focus borders, text, cursor, input, IME, and accessibility remain unchanged.
- Limits and failures: Venus does not own blur radius, strength, algorithm, or compositor policy. The selected winit API does not expose compositor capability or acceptance, so non-COSMIC compositors are a best-effort request rather than a visible-blur guarantee. X11 and macOS behavior are unproved. Launch parsing retains current bounded rejection of unknown or excess arguments.

Impact: MED/HIGH visible product value. Effort: M including dependency gate and native proof. Implementation risk: MED because the source pin affects the full native host even though the Venus code change is small. Confidence: HIGH for COSMIC Wayland and dependency fit.

## Evidence

- `Cargo.toml:16` pins crates.io winit 0.30.13 with X11, Wayland, dynamic Wayland loading, and raw-window-handle 0.6.
- `src/main.rs:184-217` owns pre-show window attributes, transparency, AccessKit creation, renderer creation, IME enablement, and visibility. Blur belongs on this existing creation boundary.
- `README.md:149-158` currently excludes blur and names winit as the native host.
- `docs/CRATES.md:15` makes winit the sole window, event-loop, native input, IME, resize, recovery, and scheduling owner; replacing or bypassing it would duplicate that boundary.
- Closed `ven-terminal-presentation-settings-5y7` proves `VEN-C11` background opacity and explicitly stopped before blur. Its accepted layer policy already makes translucent terminal-default pixels and opaque explicit/workspace layers deterministic.
- Exact winit 0.30.13 documents Wayland blur only through `org_kde_kwin_blur_manager`, which does not satisfy COSMIC.
- winit PR 4580 commit `fb45fbf901fbe70cc9a877b5d651d0b60c206b08` is exactly one commit above tag v0.30.13 and backports upstream merged, verified commit `c4afadbfabf7b1e7989b40b493db1a4c7bd8ff4e`. It prefers `ext-background-effect-v1`, retains the KDE fallback, and changes 200 additions / 30 deletions across eight winit files without changing the public blur API.
- The original upstream PR 4553 passed its complete CI matrix. The backport stable and nightly Wayland jobs pass; its red aggregate includes unrelated current Clippy, dependency-MSRV, and cargo-deny drift. The backport has no peer review or automated compositor integration test.
- A disposable Venus evaluation at HEAD `27af57690cf79b1f4a04b6a71eeb17cd05c9b3e1` applied `[patch.crates-io]` at exact `fb45fbf`, resolved one shared winit through `accesskit_winit`, and passed `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo check --locked`, 46 library + 19 host + 12 canonical tests, and `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings`. The lock source changed winit and the workspace `dpi` package from crates.io 0.1.2 to exact fork revision 0.1.1; no second winit was introduced.
- Installed COSMIC compositor 1.0.0 at exact commit `091583ac84abac02967ae358cf9570ddfef63b31`, as well as current upstream `3b8bac8335ed017a70f1ffe865c86d1ffe07c0cb`, implements Smithay `ExtBackgroundEffectHandler`, advertises `Capability::Blur`, and applies a surface-local blur region.
- `ext-background-effect-v1` version 1 defines a compositor capability event and a double-buffered, surface-local blur region; the algorithm remains compositor policy.
- An all-status Beads search found no existing blur implementation issue. The typography issue mentions blur only as excluded scope.

## Scope

In scope:

- Candidate `VEN-C15` contract indexing and proof metadata.
- `Cargo.toml` and `Cargo.lock`: keep the existing exact winit dependency and use `[patch.crates-io]` for `https://github.com/chiyuki0325/winit-0.30.git` at exact revision `fb45fbf901fbe70cc9a877b5d651d0b60c206b08`.
- `src/main.rs`: one bounded launch boolean and `WindowAttributes::with_blur` before window creation.
- Existing launch tests and the cheapest checks proving default parity and requested blur plumbing.
- `docs/CRATES.md`, `docs/REFERENCES.md`, README current-state behavior and LOC scorecard, and CHANGELOG for accepted visible behavior.
- Native COSMIC Wayland proof with compositor frosted-window policy enabled, standalone and Eon workspace surfaces, existing background opacity, decorations, and resize.

Out of scope:

- Blur radius, strength, algorithm, per-cell or configurable regions, live toggling/reload, background images, click-through, shaders, offscreen passes, or renderer changes.
- A Venus Wayland protocol module, direct `wayland-client` ownership, unsafe code, winit replacement, SDL, Tao, GTK, libcosmic, or a new event loop.
- Eon persistence/schema/defaults and Nova/Yazelix mapping; create their independently reviewable consumer issues only after the Venus contract and source proof are accepted.
- Orbit or EONW fields, compatibility adapters, arbitrary split layout, X11 blur guarantees, or macOS implementation/proof.
- Compositor configuration UI or a promise that every compositor applies the request.

## Reference and crate gate

Required before code:

- Current `AGENTS.md`; this issue and all comments; `docs/CONTRACTS.md`, `docs/REFERENCES.md`, and `docs/CRATES.md`; current `VEN-C1`, `VEN-C9`, `VEN-C11`, and `VEN-C14` owners and checks.
- Complete current launch parsing, window creation, transparency, renderer surface setup/recovery, AccessKit, input/IME, workspace layering, and relevant tests.
- Exact crates.io winit 0.30.13 source and exact fork commit `fb45fbf901fbe70cc9a877b5d651d0b60c206b08`; exact upstream source commit `c4afadbfabf7b1e7989b40b493db1a4c7bd8ff4e`; PR 4580 and upstream PR 4553 histories and CI.

Conditional:

- KDE protocol behavior only if regression proof is extended beyond COSMIC.
- A newer stable winit release only if it contains the same upstream mechanism before implementation begins; if so, rerun the crate gate and prefer crates.io.
- Non-COSMIC compositor sources only after a named native failure or user-selected portability expansion.

Rejected:

- Direct protocol plumbing around winit, replacing winit, SDL3, Tao/GTK, a generic presentation profile, a blur amount, or a second window owner. These add ownership without improving the selected COSMIC contract.

License and dependency disposition:

- winit and the fork retain the upstream Apache-2.0 license; COSMIC compositor source is evidence only and is not copied or incorporated.
- Before manifest edits, append a `Crate gate` comment comparing exact sources, 200/30 upstream delta, direct/transitive/native/build/Nix cost, the git-sourced `dpi` change, Linux/COSMIC behavior, macOS feasibility, input/IME/accessibility preservation, upgrade burden, and replacement cost. Stop for user approval as required by repository policy.
- Exit condition: replace the fork patch with the first accepted stable crates.io winit release containing the upstream mechanism, rerun all native-host proofs touched by the upgrade, and remove fork-specific documentation.

Platform disposition: isolated platform dependency. COSMIC Wayland is required proof. Existing X11 behavior without the new flag remains preserved; macOS remains architecturally credible but unproved.

## Implementation notes

1. Reconfirm the one active cross-repository frontier and that no issue owns `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock`, or the window-creation path. Obtain approval for the exact `VEN-C15` contract and index it before implementation.
2. Claim this issue and append the required Execution baseline with current HEAD, AGENTS hash, issue revision, contracts, exact Orbit/Eon proofs, intended surfaces, dirty paths, and agent identity.
3. Complete the required reference gate. Then append the crate matrix and stop for dependency approval before manifest edits.
4. Keep `winit = "=0.30.13"` as the dependency contract and add only the exact `[patch.crates-io]` revision. Update the lock deterministically. Require `cargo tree -i winit -e normal` to show one winit shared by Venus and `accesskit_winit`; inspect the exact `dpi` source change.
5. Extend the existing launch parser and `Application` state with one boolean. Apply `.with_blur(background_blur)` on the existing pre-creation attributes. Add no module, adapter, capability cache, or platform abstraction.
6. Test no-flag parity, flag parsing, bounded invalid arguments, and that the selected creation attributes receive the boolean through the smallest deterministic seam. Do not test winit internals.
7. On exact COSMIC Wayland with frosted-window policy enabled, compare flag off/on over a visually discriminating background at opacity 0.88 and 0.0. Cover standalone/workspace, decorated/undecorated creation, resize, active Orbit background changes, opaque explicit cells/selection/inverse/workspace chrome, cursor/text/IME/input/accessibility, reconnect, and bounded loss notice.
8. Commit and verify the source candidate first. Then advance contract and crate metadata, README LOC, accepted changelog text, and issue closure against that source commit in the required follow-up commit.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The exact approved `VEN-C15` row states request semantics, COSMIC proof scope, compositor-owned policy, and the lack of portable capability reporting without widening `VEN-C11`.
2. No flag produces byte-for-byte-equivalent launch configuration and current accepted rendering/input/accessibility behavior.
3. `--background-blur` is accepted exactly once through the existing parser and requests blur before the hidden window becomes visible. Unknown and excess arguments retain bounded failure.
4. Blur does not modify scene colors, alpha, draw inputs, surface blend modes, render pipelines, or workspace layer ownership. At opacity 1.0 it may be visually occluded; the flag remains independent rather than inventing coupling.
5. Cargo resolves one exact winit shared with `accesskit_winit`, records fork revision `fb45fbf901fbe70cc9a877b5d651d0b60c206b08`, and contains only reviewed expected lock changes including git workspace `dpi` 0.1.1.
6. Native COSMIC Wayland visibly distinguishes blur off from on at opacity 0.88 and 0.0. Standalone and workspace terminal areas blur while opaque explicit cells, selection/inverse, workspace chrome, notices, focus borders, text, and cursor retain their accepted appearance.
7. Decorations, resize, dynamic terminal background changes, IME, keyboard, pointer, selection, accessibility, reconnect, and failure presentation preserve current contracts.
8. Unsupported or policy-disabled compositors are documented as best effort; Venus makes no false guarantee or owned blur-algorithm claim.
9. The locked Rust suite, focused tests, dependency tree check, diff check, LOC accounting, exact proof metadata, and Beads flush pass on one materially unchanged candidate.
10. Closure records exact winit/fork/upstream/COSMIC/protocol identities, commands, test counts, native environment and policy, observations, lock delta, license disposition, proof limits, and the stable-release exit condition.

## Verification

- Focused launch tests for default and `--background-blur` behavior should fail before and pass after implementation.
- `cargo tree -i winit -e normal` should show exactly one winit used by Venus and `accesskit_winit`.
- `cargo tree -p winit --depth 2` and reviewed `Cargo.lock` diff should match the accepted crate gate.
- `cargo fmt --check`
- `cargo check --locked`
- `cargo test --locked`
- `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings`

- `br sync --flush-only`

All commands must exit 0 on one materially unchanged source candidate. Native proof must name COSMIC version/commit, Wayland rather than Xwayland, frosted-window policy, GPU/backend, opacity, and observed scope.

## Stop conditions

- Stop before code until the exact new contract is user-approved and indexed.
- Stop before manifest edits until the crate gate is recorded and the dependency change is approved.
- Stop if stable winit already contains the mechanism; prefer the stable release through a fresh gate instead of retaining the fork.
- Stop if the fork revision is unavailable, differs from the reviewed one-commit v0.30.13 delta, introduces a second winit, or changes dependencies beyond the reviewed `dpi` source/version.
- Stop if COSMIC at the exact proof revision does not advertise and visibly apply `Capability::Blur`, or if correct output requires renderer, shader, surface-alpha, or compositor-setting ownership changes.
- Stop if implementation requires direct Wayland registry/event-queue access, unsafe code, another module, another event loop, winit replacement, a public capability guarantee, or an Eon/Orbit protocol change.
- Stop if another active issue owns the launch parser, window lifecycle, manifest, lockfile, opacity owner, AccessKit adapter, or renderer surface setup.
- Stop rather than adding Eon persistence, Nova mapping, blur strength, live reload, X11 guarantees, or macOS proof.

## Maintenance notes

The invariant is deliberately small: Venus owns one boolean request at its existing native-window boundary; winit owns protocol selection and lifecycle; COSMIC owns the visual algorithm and policy; Eon may later own persistence and defaults. The cheapest removal path is deleting the patch when stable winit carries upstream commit `c4afadbf`.

The selected patch is preferable to direct Wayland code because it preserves one native-host owner and one AccessKit-compatible winit instance. Reconsider replacing winit only after multiple independently required native protocols are blocked and upstream extension is no longer viable.

title: Expose a Venus-native target from Yazelix Cursors
description:
## Outcome and boundary

Consumer: Eon at launch time.

Trigger: Eon resolves the active Yazelix Cursors configuration for a Venus window.

Result: the child library returns one typed, versioned native cursor presentation containing only `tail` or `none`, one resolved trail color, and the duration multiplier. For both mono and split definitions, this target projects the first resolved palette color; Eon and Venus never receive family, accent, secondary color, divider, transition, or cursor-color override data. Orbit-authored cursor color remains unchanged. Yazelix Cursors remains the sole owner of preset lookup, palette lookup, target projection, validation, and random selection.

Important failures: an unknown preset or palette, malformed color, invalid duration, or explicit unsupported movement effect returns a bounded child-owned error. Eon and Venus must not parse the child configuration, duplicate its registry, infer unsupported effects, or consume generated Ghostty shaders.

This tracker owns the work because `/home/lucca/pjs/yazelix-dir/cursors` has no Beads store. Implementation belongs only in that repository. This issue changes no `VEN-C*`, `EON-C*`, Orbit protocol, Eon workspace protocol, or Venus source.

## Evidence and decision

The user accepted the narrow consumption boundary on 2026-08-11 America/Sao_Paulo. Exact inspected child revision: `e0f8bc9492dbfaaf498cef47d543010f4abb2b8f`. `CursorRegistry`, `CursorSettings`, `CursorDefinition`, and `ResolvedCursorRegistryState` already own configuration and selected registry values. `CURSOR_TARGET_CONTRACTS` already documents consumer-specific targets, but no Eon/Venus target exists. The Rio target describes a shader ABI and is not the native Venus contract.

Adopt the existing registry, resolver, target-contract table, error style, and CLI target validation. Reject a second schema, Eon-owned preset interpretation, a subprocess boundary, generated shader reuse, a general capability-negotiation system, and copying the 3,331-line child into Eon. Apache-2.0 remains compatible with direct exact-revision dependency use; preserve notices.

## Minimum scope

- Add one explicit `eon-venus-native-v1` target contract.
- Add the smallest typed output and resolver needed by an exact-revision Rust consumer: `None` or `Tail { color, duration }`. Reuse the existing registry selection, first resolved palette color, duration, and errors.
- Project both mono and split definitions to `colors[0]` inside Yazelix Cursors. Do not expose a palette, family, accent, secondary color, split metadata, or cursor-color override through v1.
- Resolve `trail_effect = random` only across effects supported by this target; with the v1 set it resolves to `tail`. Accept explicit `tail` and `none`. Reject explicit `warp`, `sweep`, or any later unsupported movement effect with a target-specific error.
- Treat mode-change effects, glow, shader uniforms, and shader file generation as outside this target. The target documentation must not imply that Venus consumes them.
- Preserve all existing Ghostty, Rio-compatible-config, Mars, Ratty, and protocol-position target behavior.
- Update current README/API documentation and the existing focused registry, resolver, CLI, and target-contract tests.

Out of scope: Eon persistence or defaults, Eon launch policy, Venus CLI encoding, spring physics, GPU drawing, cursor-color override, multiple trail colors, arbitrary shaders, live reload, a new config format, a new dependency, or target discovery.

## Acceptance Criteria

- One child-owned API returns a versioned native presentation with only `None` or `Tail { color, duration }`; the color is exactly the selected definition`s first resolved palette color.
- Existing preset and palette validation remains the source of truth. No consumer must reconstruct registry rules.
- `tail`, `none`, target-scoped effect `random`, mono projection, split first-color projection, and the shipped default have deterministic tests. Unsupported explicit movement effects fail with a stable bounded error.
- The default shipped configuration resolves successfully for the native target.
- Target metadata and CLI validation report the v1 capability without claiming mode effects, glow, shader ABI, or generated assets.
- Existing target output and tests remain unchanged.
- README states the ownership split and exact unsupported fields in present tense.

## Verification

Use TDD at the resolver boundary. Run `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo test --locked`, `nix build`, `nix run .#yzc -- --help`, focused target validation, and `git diff --check`. Record the exact source revision and API surface for the Eon and Venus follow-ups.

## Stop conditions
